Research published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences demonstrates that harnessing competition among pathogens inside a patient could extend the usefulness of existing drugs and prevent the emergence of drug resistance. Drug-resistant pathogens often acquire certain resources less efficiently than drug-sensitive ones, and competition with sensitive pathogens normally limits their spread.

Researchers led by Nina Wale and Andrew Read of Penn State manipulated a nutrient in the drinking water of mice infected with malaria parasites, alongside traditional drug treatment. When the nutrient was available, treatment failed in 40 percent of mice due to drug-resistant strains emerging. When the nutrient was limited, infections did not rebound. Additional tests confirmed the effect was due to competition: limiting the nutrient stopped resistant parasites from growing only when sensitive parasites were also present.

The authors suggest researchers identify resources that resistant strains need more than sensitive strains and incorporate resource-limiting interventions into drug development. The work was funded by the Institute of General Medical Science.

The London-St. Thomas unemployment rate rose slightly to 5.5 per cent in September, while the labour force dropped by 3,000 and is down 9,300 from a year ago. Only about 75 per cent of the area's population aged 25-54 are working, the lowest among 15 major Ontario cities. A new Poverty Research Centre study at King's University College, led by Prof. Joe Michalski, found only half of working adults have full-time permanent jobs with benefits, while the rest hold precarious positions. Michalski said precarious work is linked to increased stress, poorer health and reduced family quality of life, affecting young people and minorities most. He suggested middle-class frustration fuels support for populist politicians. Nationally, unemployment held at 6.2 per cent with a net gain of 10,000 jobs, while Ontario's rate fell to 5.6 per cent, its lowest since 2000.

The present application is a continuation of prior U.S. patent applications relating to an invention made with government support under a Department of Navy contract.

LIDAR (light detection and ranging) is used for applications including altimetry, imaging, and collision avoidance, providing finer range resolution than microwave systems like RADAR. Optical range detection techniques include direct ranging (based on pulse travel time), chirped detection (based on frequency differences between transmitted and returned signals), and phase encoded detection. Direct long-range LIDAR uses short high-power pulses that can degrade optical components, while chirped LIDAR uses longer pulses with lower peak power and achieves range accuracy based on chirp bandwidth. Heterodyne and homodyne detection methods combine reference and returned signals at a detector to produce beat frequencies. Data from LIDAR systems is often represented as 3D point clouds.

The inventors recognized challenges in real-time automatic classification of objects represented by 3D point clouds, particularly at long range. In one embodiment, a method includes obtaining a 3D point cloud of an object's external surface, extracting a surface normal at a point to define a translational and rotational invariant coordinate system, and extracting feature variable values. Two classification statistics are computed and matched against sets corresponding to N classes to estimate first and second classes. If these classes differ, a third classification statistic is computed based on closest fit between the point cloud and models for only the first and second classes, assigning the object accordingly in near real time. The first statistic may be a spin image, the second a covariance matrix, and the third an iterative closest point (ICP).

Another embodiment describes an apparatus with a laser source, splitter, optical coupler, optical detector, and processor configured to perform the method steps. The classification uses k-d trees and nearest neighbor searches to assign objects to classes based on trained data. Experimental results demonstrated high accuracy in classifying objects including cones, cubes, pipes, boxes, pistols, and similar-shaped toy guns.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended April 1, 2017. As of April 21, 2017, approximately 5.21 billion shares of common stock were outstanding. For the three months ended April 1, 2017, net sales were $52.9 billion (up 5% year-over-year), with net income of $11.0 billion and diluted EPS of $2.10. Six-month net sales reached $131.2 billion with net income of $28.9 billion. Gross margin was 38.9% for the quarter. Services, Mac, and Other Products drove growth, while Greater China sales declined 14%. iPhone net sales rose 1%, iPad fell 12%, and Mac grew 14%. Total assets were $334.5 billion, with $257.1 billion in cash and marketable securities. The Company issued $11.0 billion in long-term debt, repurchased $7.0 billion in shares, and paid $3.0 billion in dividends during the quarter. Apple had $10.0 billion in commercial paper outstanding and $88.9 billion in term debt. Regarding the European Commission's State Aid Decision, Apple has appealed the ruling, which could require recovery of up to €13 billion plus interest. Gross margin for Q3 2017 is projected between 37.5% and 38.5%.

The GeForce RTX 50 Series, based on NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture, introduces FP4 support in its fifth-generation Tensor Cores, reducing model memory requirements by over half compared to FP16 and doubling performance over the previous generation. For example, FLUX.dev drops from 23GB to under 10GB VRAM.

The fourth-generation RT Core doubles ray-triangle intersection throughput and supports new features including Mega Geometry, which enables ray tracing of highly detailed geometry through Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) and Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures (PTLAS). Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) accelerate rendering of hair and strand-like objects, being 2x faster than DOTS while using 5x less VRAM. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 is twice as efficient as the Ada version.

The AI Management Processor (AMP), a dedicated RISC-V processor, offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU. Blackwell adds 4:2:2 hardware encode/decode, a ninth-generation NVENC with 5% quality improvements, sixth-generation NVDEC with 2x faster H.264 decoding, and DisplayPort 2.1b (80 Gbps).

Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating, accelerated frequency switching (1000x faster), and deep sleep entry 10x faster than Ada, yielding up to 50% power savings.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation (up to 3 generated frames per rendered frame), is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and transitions from CNN to transformer-based models for improved image quality.

Neural shaders, accessed via the new Cooperative Vectors API, enable RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (3x+ memory savings), Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin (subsurface scattering), and RTX Neural Faces.

GPU variants include the GB202 (RTX 5090, 92.2B transistors, 24,576 CUDA Cores), GB203 (RTX 5080/5070 Ti), and GB205 (RTX 5070, 6,400 CUDA Cores).

Sara Zaske's daughter showed little interest in owning a cell phone while living in Germany, where about 51% of children ages 6-13 own mobile phones, but wanted one after moving to California, where she was the only fourth-grader without a smartphone.

Across Europe, a 2015 study found 46% of children ages 9-16 owned smartphones, with usage patterns varying by country due to school restrictions and economic factors. In the US, a Nielsen report showed 45% of children ages 10-12 have smartphones with service plans, and 42% of children 8 and younger own tablets.

Outside the US and Europe, children typically get phones later. In South Korea, 72% of children ages 11-12 own smartphones. In Taiwan, ownership rises from 45% at age 11 to 71% at 15. Turkish parents disagreed on ideal age, with most suggesting ages 12-17. In African nations, ownership rose significantly between 2007-2014, reaching 50.8% in South Africa, 16.2% in Ghana, and 8.4% in Malawi. An Australian study found the median age for first phone use was 8.

The American Academy of Pediatrics states there is no "right" age for cell phone ownership but recommends limiting screen time, particularly for young children.

The passage describes the development of a new classical embedded atom method (EAM) interatomic potential for the ternary tungsten-hydrogen-helium (W-H-He) system, intended for simulating radiation damage in fusion reactor plasma-facing components. Tungsten is a candidate material, but irradiation causes defects such as vacancies, voids, and gas bubbles that degrade performance and increase tritium retention.

Existing W-H-He potentials have limitations, particularly in accurately representing defect relaxation volumes and tungsten surface energies. The authors extend the Mason W-H potential to include helium interactions, using a generalized Finnis-Sinclair formulation that permits negative electron densities.

The fitting process minimizes a loss function based on differences from DFT data for defect formation energies, relaxation volumes, binding energies, and gaseous configurations, with greater weight assigned to defect properties. A custom global optimization algorithm using Gaussian Mixture Models is employed, followed by local Simplex minimization.

DFT data were sourced from literature and supplemented with new calculations using VASP. Each potential component was parameterized with physics-informed priors, including ZBL stopping for short-range interactions, constraints reflecting helium's weak interaction with metal surfaces, and a modified embedding function preventing attraction to negative electron densities. The He-He potential incorporates high-pressure hcp data to better represent helium bubbles. Charge density analysis indicates non-negligible electronic interactions for helium in tungsten, contrary to assumptions in prior potentials.

New energy assessors from diesel-powered Alaskan villages are being trained to conduct affordable household energy assessments. The program, run by the Renewable Energy Alaska Project (REAP) in partnership with Southeast tribes, invited residents from Kake, Angoon, Hoonah, Yakutat, and Metlakatla. While private energy audits can cost thousands of dollars, these assessments cost $25. Trainees like Alexis Wagner and Austin Pajak learn to inventory appliances, lighting, and other energy factors in homes. Suggestions include replacing bulbs with LEDs and swapping glass coffee pots for insulated ones, which could lower electric bills by about 10 percent. Jennifer Hanlon of Yakutat Tlingit Tribe says such fixes help residents afford to stay, though they don't replace diesel power. The Home Energy Leader Program runs through July 31.

NAB executive Andrew Hagger described financial advisers' falsification of superannuation beneficiary documents as "sloppy and unprofessional." The royal commission has exposed widespread misconduct within the financial planning divisions of major banks and AMP, prompting apologies from those who previously opposed the inquiry. This follows years of reporting on issues including trailing commissions, conflicted advice, vertical integration, and insurance rorts. Among those affected was Joe Hockey's mother-in-law, who lost significant savings through a CBA financial planner and initially received a low compensation offer.

Commercial property owners in Southern Nevada have been paying trash fees to Republic Services that were never approved by local lawmakers, despite municipal ordinances requiring council or commission approval for fees not covered in ordinances or franchise agreements. The Las Vegas City Council plans to introduce an ordinance codifying several such fees, including container delivery, removal, exchange, and industrial dry run fees. Republic is the sole waste collector in Clark County, Las Vegas, North Las Vegas, and Henderson. Elected officials in these areas said they do not recall approving such fees. Republic representatives stated the fees appear on an annual "supplemental services" list provided to municipalities. City spokespeople largely declined to comment beyond referencing the ordinances, while Henderson said it would investigate and Clark County said commissioner approval was not required.

This study used Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis on GWAS-derived data from European populations to investigate causal relationships between gut microbiota, plasma metabolites, and fibromyalgia (FM).

The analysis identified six gut microbial taxa with causal effects on FM: four protective (family Enterobacteriaceae, genus Butyricicoccus, genus Coprococcus1, and order Enterobacteriales) and two risk factors (genus Eggerthella and genus Ruminococcaceae UCG005).

Additionally, 82 plasma metabolites were associated with FM, primarily involved in caffeine metabolism, α-linolenic acid (ALA) metabolism, and GLP-1/incretin synthesis, secretion, and inactivation pathways. In caffeine metabolism, AFMU was protective while 7-Methylxanthine and 1-Methylxanthine were risk factors. In ALA metabolism, EPA and SDA were protective. In the GLP-1 pathway, EPA was protective while Oleoyl-EA was a risk factor. Oxalate was suggested as a potential FM risk factor.

Mediation analysis revealed that 2,3-dihydroxypyridine and palmitoylcholine mediated the effects of Enterobacteriaceae and Enterobacteriales on FM, with mediation proportions of 14.91% and 12.34%, respectively.

The authors proposed dietary recommendations including limiting caffeine, increasing omega-3 intake, adopting a low-GI diet, and reducing high-oxalate foods. Limitations included lack of demographic subgroup data, European-only ancestry in datasets, and the need for experimental validation.

Guinness has partnered with former Arsenal footballer Thierry Henry for its Made of Black campaign, marking the first time the brand has collaborated with a footballer. Henry will work with Guinness in Nigeria and across Africa to highlight individuals who embody the Made of Black spirit. Henry expressed enthusiasm about the partnership and Nigeria's football passion, while Guinness Nigeria Marketing Director Adenike Adebola described him as an inspirational ambassador. The Made of Black campaign, launched in August 2014 on MTV Base, features African performers and promotes "black" as an attitude representing the best of Africa. This season, Guinness will host Fanzone activations combining live football and music, and will continue sponsoring EPL broadcasts on DStv.

This patent application, a continuation of multiple prior applications claiming priority to a 2015 provisional application, relates to implantable medical devices with magnets, particularly hearing prostheses such as cochlear implants compatible with MRI environments.

The background describes two types of hearing loss (conductive and sensorineural) and various hearing prostheses including conventional hearing aids, bone conduction devices, and cochlear implants, which convert sound into electrical stimulation applied to the cochlea.

The invention provides implantable medical devices comprising a magnet within a body, where structural components are configured to move away from each other upon initial magnet rotation when subjected to external magnetic fields (such as MRI fields of 0.2T to 7T or more), thereby limiting further rotation. Embodiments include plates sandwiching the magnet within an elastomeric housing (e.g., silicone). When external magnetic fields impart torque on the magnet, the plates separate, stretching the elastomeric material, which generates counter-forces resisting further rotation.

Alternative embodiments use springs, rails, extended plates, or curved plate surfaces to provide reaction forces. The magnet may be housed in a container permitting revolution but limiting rotation. Plates may include holes for interlocking with elastomeric material, bumpers, or tracks to guide magnet movement. The body may include a slit allowing magnet insertion or removal.

Various figures illustrate cochlear implant configurations, functional block diagrams, transceiver arrangements, magnetic coupling schematics, and different plate and magnet assemblies.

Activist hedge fund TCI Fund Management stated on Wednesday that Zodiac Aerospace shares are worth 7-10 euros each, down from its previous 10 euros valuation on March 24. TCI is pressuring Safran to drop its bid for Zodiac, arguing any offer above 10 euros destroys value. The revised valuation follows Zodiac's reported first-half 2017 loss and what TCI called "unrealistic" forecasts of a return to mid-teen margins.

Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell stated that demand for AI computing power remains "tremendous," though he acknowledged that eventually "there'll be too many" AI data centers built, while noting no current signs of oversupply. Dell's server networking business grew 58% last year and 69% last quarter. The company's stock rose over 3% Tuesday after it raised long-term financial targets, increasing expected annual revenue growth to 7%-9% (from 3%-4%) and diluted EPS growth to 15% (from 8%). Dell plans to ship $20 billion in AI servers in fiscal 2026, double the prior year.

The Agreement specifies that quantities listed in the first Schedule are minimums and additional purchases are permitted. Prices are to be mutually agreed between the Belgian Government and the UK or US Governments. Payment follows standard procedures, and the UK will ensure customs duties do not disadvantage Congo products relative to British colonial products. The RSI, ADX, and IBS are considered among the best indicators for short-term trading, collectively referred to as the "Big Three." RSI and IBS are suited for mean-reversion strategies, while ADX is effective for trend-following strategies.

The RSI, developed by Welles Wilder in 1978, is a momentum indicator oscillating between 0 and 100, with values above 70 indicating overbought conditions and below 30 indicating oversold conditions. Backtesting suggests shorter timeframes (2-3 days) work best for stocks.

The ADX, also developed by Wilder, measures trend strength without indicating direction. Backtesting indicates a 5-10 day period and threshold values of 30-40 work best.

The IBS indicator measures the closing price's position relative to the High and Low, oscillating between 0 and 1, with low values signaling bullish conditions.

Backtests on Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 showed:
- IBS strategy: 0.78% average gain per trade, 12.1% CAGR, 32% risk-adjusted return.
- RSI strategy: 0.98% average gain, 7.5% CAGR, 18% risk-adjusted return.
- ADX strategy: 6.5% CAGR, 10.3% risk-adjusted return.

Combining two indicators on SPY produced 270 trades with 0.86% average gain and 56% risk-adjusted return; results were even stronger on QQQ.

The passage describes an autonomous vehicle management system (AVMS) that uses artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques to control autonomous vehicle operations safely. The system receives sensor data to generate and maintain an internal 3D map representing the vehicle's state and environment, which is used alongside goals and safety considerations to create plans of action.

Key features include:

1. **Dynamic sensor control**: The AVMS can send instructions to sensors to modify what data is captured, when, and how it is communicated, enabling efficient resource use and improved safety.

2. **What-if simulations**: The system creates multiple internal map instances to simulate possible future scenarios (e.g., different speeds or paths of surrounding vehicles) to determine the safest sequence of actions.

3. **AI confidence scoring**: The system generates a confidence score measuring how similar inferring data points are to training data, allowing predictions with low confidence to be overridden.

4. **User interface transparency**: Information about planned actions and reasons for them is displayed to users and potentially to those in the environment, increasing trust and enabling manual override.

5. **Reinforcement learning safety**: A Safety Sanity Index (SSI) and interruptible commands override unsafe actions selected by RL agents prioritizing reward maximization.

The AVMS comprises subsystems including sensors interface, localization, perception, planning, controls, and information subsystems. The internal map uses a multilayered graph data structure for efficient querying and storage. The system applies to various autonomous machines beyond vehicles, including construction and mining equipment.

The application is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 16/258,265, filed January 25, 2019, which claims priority to U.S. Provisional Application Ser. No. 62/667,188, filed May 4, 2018. It relates to wireless communication systems, specifically ACK/NACK feedback in networks with multiple transmission reception points (TRPs), applicable to 5G New Radio (NR).

A base station may send a UE information indicating PDCCH monitoring occasions for each of multiple TRPs, whether ACK/NACK feedback across TRPs is allowed, rules for ACK/NACK feedback bundling, and a downlink assignment index (DAI) definition indicating whether DAIs transmitted by the TRPs are independent or joint. An independent DAI includes a count of PDCCH grants from a single TRP across all scheduled carriers, while a joint DAI includes counts across all TRPs and carriers. Joint DAIs suit tight coordination with fast backhaul; independent DAIs suit loose coordination or non-ideal backhaul.

Multi-TRP transmission supports two modes: a single DCI granting one transport block with layers from different TRPs, or multiple DCIs each granting one TB. ACK/NACK codebooks may be semi-static (type 1) or dynamic (type 2), with size determined based on PDCCH monitoring occasions, timing values, and DAIs.

When bundling is enabled, the UE may transmit a joint ACK/NACK in a PUCCH based on the rules—for example, a joint ACK when at least one TRP's data is received (same payload case), or a joint NACK if any TRP's data fails (different payload case). Alternatively, the UE may transmit multiple individual PUCCHs to each TRP, either via TDM, concurrently on different resources, or concurrently from multiple uplink antenna arrays/beams.

The disclosure includes methods, computer-readable media, and apparatus for both base stations and UEs implementing these features.

The C-BerryTrans code is a C++ based program that computes Berry curvature (Ω), anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC), and anomalous Nernst conductivity (ANC) directly from WIEN2k outputs using the Kubo formula. Unlike Wannier-based methods that depend on interpolation and high-quality Wannier functions, this approach uses DFT eigenvalues and momentum-matrix elements directly from the FP-LAPW basis set, ensuring greater accuracy.

The code parallelizes Ω calculations over k-points using OpenMP and stores band-resolved results in binary files, enabling efficient post-processing of AHC/ANC across various temperatures and chemical potentials in a single run. Spin-orbit coupling must be included, as transverse responses vanish without it.

Key modules include klist_gen_div for generating k-meshes in the full Brillouin zone, modify_calc_window for adjusting energy windows, and berryTrans_plot.py for visualization. Input parameters control crystal structure, energy windows, temperature ranges, threading, and RAM management via batch processing of k-points. The code has been validated on Fe, Pd, Fe3Al, and Co2FeAl, and can be adapted to other DFT packages like ELK and Quantum Espresso.

The Single/Double Offense uses double and down screens to free a shooter, requiring defenders to disrupt both screen types.

In the NBA, "Show and Recover" is preferred over switching, since switching creates post mismatches. The defense dictates the shooter's direction away from their preferred side while pressuring the ballhandler toward the sideline. On double screens, the screener's defender steps out to force the shooter wide, then recovers to deny the post. Similar principles apply to single screen options, with weakside defenders packing in toward the ball. Post mismatches may be trapped using weakside defenders.

Total disruption ("All Out SOS") is achieved by initiating action and trapping the shooter on the wing, forcing offensive players into freelance situations. This involves sequential switches on screens, with defenders assuming Snuggle denial positions. Wing traps are executed when the ball reaches the shooting guard, with rotations into Triangle "I" positions to deny reversal passes. Closeout rotations must occur as the ball leaves the passer's hands. Baseline drives and post mismatches trigger specific trap and rotation schemes.

The lecture restates the Weierstrass M-test and applies it to power series, proving that a power series with radius of convergence ρ converges uniformly on any closed interval strictly inside its radius of convergence. From this, it follows that power series can be differentiated and integrated term by term within their radius of convergence, and that the differentiated power series has the same radius of convergence as the original. Iterating this result shows that every power series equals the Taylor series of the function it defines.

The lecture then introduces the Weierstrass Approximation Theorem: every continuous function on [0,1] is the uniform limit of a sequence of polynomials. The proof reduces to the case where f(0) = f(1) = 0, allowing f to be extended by zero. A sequence of polynomials qₙ(x) = cₙ(1−x²)ⁿ is constructed, which behaves as an approximation to the identity (concentrating mass at zero while integrating to 1). Using the bound cₙ < √n, it is shown that qₙ converges uniformly to 0 outside any interval around zero. The approximating polynomials pₙ(x) are defined by convolving f with qₙ, and using uniform continuity of f and boundedness on [0,1], pₙ is shown to converge uniformly to f.

The lecture concludes by mentioning that more powerful interchange-of-limits results appear in Lebesgue integration theory, and offers closing remarks about the remote teaching experience.

The case of Single-Track Overhead Ry. Mfg. Co. v. Roden, decided January 31, 1895, concerned alleged infringement of patent No. 285,116, granted to Benjamin S. Curtis and John A. Cook in 1883 for an improvement in portable elevated railroads.

Defense witness Joseph H. Haynes, who built the defendant's railway, testified that a substantially similar single-track overhead railway had been in use at the Camden Iron Works since 1866. This uncontradicted testimony led Judge Acheson to rule that the first, second, and third claims of the patent failed due to anticipation.

However, regarding the fourth claim—which covered a main overhead track combined with branch tracks, a switch, and a traveler—Haynes admitted he had no knowledge of such a combination prior to September 1883, and acknowledged the defendant's structure contained these elements. The court found the fourth claim was infringed and that the presumption of patentability had not been rebutted. A decree was entered for the plaintiff on the fourth claim.

The invention provides automated object sortation systems and methods using programmable motion devices (e.g., robotic arms) that dynamically assign intermediate containers (collection bins) to object destinations, rather than relying on fixed pre-assigned relationships.

Conventional sortation systems rely heavily on human labor or costly automated diverts (e.g., tilt-tray conveyors), with limitations in throughput, number of diverts, space, and operating costs. Manual parallel cells reduce divert costs but cannot expand the total number of system bins because each cell must share identical bin designations.

The disclosed systems include one or more sorting stations with robotic arms, perception units (cameras/scanners) for identifying objects, input conveyors or buffers (including circulating conveyors), collection bins, and output conveyors, all coordinated by a central controller. Objects are acquired from a disorganized input, identified, and dynamically assigned to an intermediate bin associated with a destination. When bins are full or unlikely to receive further matching objects, they are forwarded for further processing, and the bin can be reassigned.

Bin-to-destination mapping may be optimized using heuristics such as historical trends, current system state, physical characteristics, and network-wide cost considerations.

Certain embodiments use shuttle carriages that travel along tracks between rows of bins, including multi-wing configurations (two, four, or eight wings) fed by a primary shuttle and picking robot. A drop camera unit with multiple cameras captures images as objects fall through it for identification. Non-sortable objects are routed to a separate chute.

The systems offer scalability by adding robots and wings, dynamic allocation of high-volume bins to minimize cycle time, and reduced space, labor, and capital costs compared to prior sortation methods.

The GHCB MSR protocol defines request/response pairs exchanged between an SEV-ES/SEV-SNP guest and hypervisor for operations including AP reset hold, preferred/registered/unregistered GHCB GPA handling, page state changes, Run VMPL requests, hypervisor feature queries, and guest termination requests.

GHCB GPA registration is required for SEV-SNP guests. A guest may query the hypervisor's preferred GHCB GPA, register a chosen GPA (making it shared/hypervisor-owned), or unregister it. Mismatched GPAs cause guest termination. Under the Multi-VMPL feature, each VMPL level may register its own GHCB GPA.

GHCB negotiation examples are provided for SEV-ES (protocol version 1, encryption bit 47) and SEV-SNP (up to version 2, encryption bit 51) guests, involving VMCB offset 0x00a0, #VC exception handling, CPUID queries, page table setup, and GHCB page allocation marked as shared.

Non-Automatic Events (NAE) trigger a #VC exception in SEV-ES guests. Guests populate GHCB fields (SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1/2, VALID_BITMAP) and invoke VMGEXIT. Hypervisors can return error codes via SW_EXITINFO1 indicating exceptions, malformed input, unregistered GHCB, invalid scratch, missing valid bits, or invalid input.

Specific NAE handling is defined for IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access (requiring a decrypted scratch buffer), Page State Change (supporting private/shared assignments, PSMASH/UNSMASH hints, with per-entry progress tracking), and SNP Guest Requests (requiring separate shared request/response pages, sequence-number synchronization, and optional rate limiting via retry codes).

Additionally, the SEV-SNP secrets page includes a 96-byte guest-reserved area holding VMPL message sequence numbers (extended to 64 bits) and an AP Jump Table address, and an EFI configuration table GUID is defined for communicating secrets and CPUID pages to the OS.

Collagen is a protein providing structural support to skin, tendons, and bones, accounting for around 30% of the body's natural protein. The body has approximately 28 collagen types, with types I, II, III, IV, and V being most common, each serving different functions.

Collagen supplements come in three main forms: hydrolysed, undenatured, and gelatin. Hydrolysed collagen may be the most effective due to easy absorption. Supplements are typically sourced from marine animals, cows, pigs, or chickens, and generally contain types I, II, and III.

Potential benefits include improved wound healing, reduced wrinkles, stronger nails, better bone and joint health, and muscle support. Limited research suggests possible hair growth benefits.

Recommended dosages vary by purpose, ranging from 2.5g daily for joints and skin to 15g for muscle mass. Manufacturers typically recommend 12 weeks for noticeable results. Experts advise choosing third-party tested products.

A balanced diet rich in protein, vitamin C, and gelatinous foods can also support natural collagen production.

The Midline Option is a play where the Quarterback reads an interior Defensive Lineman to decide between handing off to a dive back through the A-gap or keeping the ball through the B-gap. Its main strength is eliminating the need to block one defender and complementing veer-based option offenses by using motion as a decoy. Its primary weakness is exposing the Quarterback to frequent hits, requiring a durable player at the position.

Against a 3-4 odd front, linemen focus on reaching interior defenders and climbing to linebackers, while the Fullback runs the midline and the Quarterback reads the first defender on or outside the right guard. Against a 4-3 even front, assignments shift to account for the Nose Tackle and Middle Linebacker, but Quarterback and Fullback responsibilities remain similar.

Common variations include the Flexbone Midline, which replaces the Tight End with a receiver to spread the defense, and Midline "Follow," where the Wingback becomes a lead blocker for the Quarterback, often used by service academies in short-yardage situations.

P. falciparum modifies infected erythrocyte surfaces through Variant Surface Antigens (VSAs), primarily PfEMP1, encoded by ~60 var genes classified into groups A, B, C, and E. These genes undergo mutually exclusive expression linked to pathogenesis severity. Parasites evade host immunity through intrinsic switching and immune-driven turnover of var expression.

A Controlled Human Malaria Infection (CHMI) study in The Gambia involved 19 semi-immune adult males classified as sero-high or sero-low based on pre-existing antibodies against six P. falciparum antigens. All were inoculated with NF54/3D7 sporozoites and monitored for parasitaemia, var expression, and immune responses.

Sero-low individuals showed higher peak parasitaemia, more symptoms, and shorter latency than sero-high individuals. Whole transcriptome analysis identified var genes as the primary differentially expressed genes. Sero-high "controllers" exhibited restricted var expression (low entropy), while sero-low "non-controllers" showed diverse var expression, consistent with findings from a Gabon CHMI.

In vivo var turnover rates were high (69-97% per generation), with group A showing highest transition rates. In vitro culturing revealed sero-low isolates rapidly converged to a high-entropy steady state, while sero-high isolates retained memory of initial states longer, suggesting epigenetic imprinting from immune pressure.

Protein microarray analysis showed sero-high individuals recognized significantly more PfEMP1 domains. Sero-low individuals doubled their antibody breadth post-infection, while sero-high showed minimal change. Pre-existing PfEMP1 antibodies moderately correlated negatively with subsequent var expression, particularly for groups A, B, and B/C. However, antibody acquisition post-infection did not correlate with var expression intensity during infection, suggesting some PfEMP1 domains are poorly immunogenic.

The findings suggest intrinsic var switching maintains diverse repertoires as a bet-hedging strategy, while negative selection in immune hosts favors stable, less immunogenic variants.

Sharded services distribute data across replicas, each handling a subset of requests, suitable for stateful services with large datasets. Riverton Investment Corporation (RIC) sued the United States for a tax refund after the IRS disallowed deductions RIC claimed for payments made in the 1990s to buy back stock from management stockholders. The IRS characterized the payments as non-deductible stock redemptions, while RIC reported them as deductible compensation expenses.

The dispositive issue was whether RIC "transferred" the stock to employees in the 1980s under Treasury Regulation 1.83-3(a)(1). If the Management Stockholder's Agreement (MSA) restrictions were "non-lapse" (permanent), no transfer occurred, and RIC would prevail. If they were "lapse" restrictions, the payments were non-deductible redemptions.

The Magistrate Judge recommended judgment for the United States, finding that Paragraph 9 of the MSA caused the restrictions to lapse upon liquidation, merger, acquisition, or reorganization. RIC objected, arguing Paragraph 9 was ambiguous.

The court found Paragraph 9 ambiguous because its sentences admitted multiple interpretations and conflicted with other MSA provisions. It therefore admitted parol evidence, which showed the parties intended only the timing restriction to lapse, while permanent restrictions remained on who could buy the stock and the maximum/minimum sale price (60% of book value, but no less than original purchase price).

Because the management stockholders never bore the risk of substantial value decline and could not receive fair market value, no "transfer" occurred in the 1980s. The United States produced no contrary evidence. The court sustained RIC's objections, rejected the Report and Recommendation, denied the motion to strike, and granted summary judgment for RIC.

Containers establish boundaries for resources, ownership, and separation of concerns. Even single-machine applications benefit from being split into multiple containers for resource isolation, team scaling, and modular reuse. Containers tightly grouped on one machine form a "pod" in Kubernetes.

The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a sidecar that augments functionality, such as adding HTTPS to legacy services or synchronizing configurations. Successful sidecars require parameterization (preferably via environment variables), well-defined APIs, and documentation through Dockerfile directives like EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL.

The ambassador pattern uses a container to broker interactions between the application and external world, useful for sharded service routing (e.g., twemproxy for Redis), service brokering across environments, and request splitting for experiments (e.g., using nginx for 10% traffic redirection).

The adapter pattern modifies an application's interface to match expected standards, useful for monitoring (e.g., Prometheus exporters), normalizing logging formats (e.g., fluentd), and adding health checks (e.g., for MySQL).

Multi-node distributed patterns are loosely coupled via network calls. Microservices architectures decouple components for reliability, agility, and independent scaling, though they complicate debugging and design.

Replicated load-balanced services use identical stateless servers behind a load balancer, requiring at least two replicas for high availability and readiness probes for proper load balancing. Session-tracked services route specific users to the same replica via consistent hashing. Caching layers (e.g., Varnish) improve performance and should be deployed as separate tiers with fewer, larger replicas. Additional layers like nginx provide SSL termination and rate limiting.

Sharded services distribute data across replicas, each handling a subset of requests, enabling larger state storage. Sharded caches increase effective cache capacity but make individual shard failures more impactful. Replicated sharded caches combine both patterns for resilience and scalability, allowing safe rollouts and hot sharding during peak traffic.

At Lakers media day, LeBron James, entering his 23rd NBA season in an expiring contract year, said his contract status "doesn't bother" him and will not affect his performance. James, 40, exercised his $52.6 million player option in June. He expressed excitement about the Lakers' roster additions and continuity with the coaching staff and Luka Doncic. James said a successful season requires being "detailed every day" in the tough Western Conference, while Doncic stated the goal is winning a championship. Recovering from a Grade 2 MCL sprain suffered in last season's first-round playoff loss to Minnesota, James indicated he may be limited in training camp as he works to get his body closer to 100 percent. Regarding retirement, James said his decision will not depend on his son Bryce and will come when he falls out of love with the preparation process.

Facebook announced on Tuesday it has acquired the team behind Bloomsbury AI, a London-based start-up founded in 2015 that specialises in natural language processing. Bloomsbury AI developed "Cape," an AI that reads documents and answers questions about their contents. Facebook stated the team's expertise will strengthen its natural language processing research. The deal is an "acquihire," meaning Facebook is only acquiring the talent, not the product. TechCrunch previously reported the deal was valued at up to $30 million and that Facebook was interested in using the software to combat fake news. The future of Bloomsbury AI's operations remains unclear.

Patrick Cullen, 33, of Courtbrack, Dock Road, has been jailed for three years after pleading guilty to robbing a 21-year-old woman on Wolfe Tone Street on July 11. Limerick Circuit Court heard Cullen approached the victim from behind shortly before midnight, pushed her, and grabbed her handbag, causing her to fall and cut her finger. Gardai located Cullen nearby, and he directed them to the discarded handbag at Vizes Court. His counsel, Aaron Desmond BL, said Cullen acted out of desperation to fund a drug habit, made immediate admissions, and is engaging with the Probation Service. Judge Tom O'Donnell described the victim as an "easy and defenceless target" and the offence as opportunistic. He imposed a four-year sentence with the final 12 months suspended, backdated to July 12.

Ida C. Scott, a married woman, brought action to enjoin enforcement of a judgment against her real estate. John R. House had obtained a justice court judgment against her for $61.50 for goods sold and delivered, and levied execution on 80 acres of her land. The parties stipulated that the debt was for necessaries furnished to Scott and her husband, and that no prior judgment had been obtained against the husband.

Defendants argued the wife was concluded by the judgment from raising defenses, including the absence of a prior judgment and unsatisfied execution against the husband, since these should have been pleaded in justice court.

The court, citing section 1, ch. 53, Comp. St. 1911, held that a married woman's property is not liable for debts contracted for family necessaries until an execution against the husband has been issued and returned unsatisfied. This is a condition precedent to liability. The court held that where a judgment does not show it was rendered for necessaries, the statutory protection may be raised before sale of the wife's property. Since the condition precedent was not met, Scott was entitled to an injunction.

The judgment of the district court was affirmed.

The convergence of digital technology and education has transformed higher education, particularly following COVID-19, making it essential to evaluate digitalization's impact on educational quality. While prior research has examined online learning platforms, digital tools, and accessibility, a systematic framework to rank these impacts has been lacking. This study applies the Spherical Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (SFAHP) to assess and prioritize key criteria affecting online higher education quality in Vietnam.

The literature distinguishes digitization, digitalization, and digital transformation, with digitalization focusing on integrating digital tools into existing educational processes. Key evaluation criteria include technological infrastructure, digital resource accessibility, pedagogical integration, student engagement, and adaptability and innovation.

Using SFAHP with input from nine education experts, pairwise comparisons were conducted through hierarchical construction, fuzzy comparisons, weight derivation, and result synthesis. The analysis ranked pedagogical integration highest (23.6%), followed by student engagement (21.2%), accessibility of digital resources (20.3%), adaptability and innovation (18.4%), and technological infrastructure (16.5%).

These findings challenge traditional prioritization of infrastructure, emphasizing that teaching methodologies are central to successful online learning. Strategic recommendations include fostering collaboration between educators and technologists, prioritizing interactive learning experiences, ensuring equitable digital access, supporting innovation, and investing in professional development for digital pedagogy. Limitations include reliance on expert evaluations, suggesting future research incorporate broader stakeholder perspectives.

A Reuters table dated February 2 displays exchange rates for Asian currencies against the U.S. dollar at 0134 GMT, comparing the latest bids to the previous day and end-2017 values. Daily movements were mixed, with the ringgit and yuan gaining most, while the peso and won declined. Year-to-date in 2018, most currencies strengthened against the dollar, led by the ringgit, baht, yen, and yuan, while the peso, rupee, and won weakened.

Ottawa Senators winger Mike Hoffman scored the winning shootout goal using a Peter Forsberg-style move to defeat the Philadelphia Flyers 4-3 at the Wells Fargo Center. Coach Guy Boucher praised Hoffman's high-risk approach. Rookie Colin White earned his first NHL point with an assist on Matt Duchene's goal. Goalie Craig Anderson is backing the Philadelphia Eagles in the Super Bowl, while Mike Condon and Colin White support the Patriots. Defenceman Johnny Oduya collected a $250,000 bonus for reaching Game 41. Boucher praised Flyers centre Sean Couturier, whom he previously coached in junior. Calgary Flames scout Don Maloney attended the game, with reported interest in Senators Zack Smith and Jean-Gabriel Pageau ahead of the February 26th trade deadline.

The Mets had a disappointing season despite offseason signings of Juan Soto and Pete Alonso, losing the final NL Wild Card spot due largely to pitching struggles. GM David Stearns criticized Kodai Senga for two inconsistent seasons, including injuries in 2024 and a Triple-A demotion this year. Stearns acknowledged Senga's potential but declined to guarantee him 30 starts next season.

SCDNR biologists in St. Helena Sound have satellite-tagged "Harry-Etta," an 820-pound, 12-foot pregnant female tiger shark, to track her movements and gather data on the species' lifespan, reproduction, and migration patterns. Sponsored by the Harry Hampton Wildlife Fund, the SPOT tag sends signals to a satellite when the shark surfaces. Harry-Etta is the fifteenth tiger shark tagged by Frazier's team in South Carolina and the first confirmed pregnant, offering insight into gestation habitats. Previous research suggests South Carolina's southern sounds may serve as important foraging, nursing, and reproduction areas for tiger sharks. Her movements can be followed on the OCEARCH Global Shark Tracker.

Offensive linemen play a selfless, grueling position with no statistical recognition, focused on protecting teammates and enabling offensive success. The unit of five players lines up together at the line of scrimmage, responsible for run-blocking to create rushing lanes and pass-blocking to give quarterbacks time to throw. Their role requires communication, physicality, technique, and football IQ to counter defensive blitzes, stunts, and varying alignments.

Typically standing 6'2"-6'8" and weighing 300-340 pounds, linemen need skills in run-blocking, pass-blocking, athleticism, strength, awareness, and technique. Body types vary across center, guard, and tackle positions. Notable historical players include Jim Otto (center), John Hannah (guard), and Anthony Munoz (tackle).

While often overlooked, the offensive line is frequently blamed during struggles and is considered the primary factor in offensive success, enabling skill position stars to perform effectively.

Sarah Sajedi, inspired by plastic waste observed on Thailand's Phi Phi islands, returned to Concordia University for a PhD examining health risks of single-use plastic water bottles. Reviewing over 140 scientific articles, she found that people ingest 39,000 to 52,000 microplastic particles annually, with bottled water drinkers consuming 90,000 more than tap water drinkers.

Microplastics range from one micron to five millimeters, while nanoplastics are smaller. Particles shed from bottles during production, storage, transport, and exposure to sunlight and temperature changes. Once ingested, they can enter the bloodstream and organs, potentially causing inflammation, oxidative stress, hormonal disruption, impaired reproduction, neurological damage, and cancer. Long-term effects remain understudied due to limited testing and inconsistent measurement methods.

Sajedi notes that existing plastic-waste legislation rarely targets single-use water bottles and emphasizes education, stating bottled water should be reserved for emergencies rather than daily use. The concern centers on chronic, not acute, toxicity.

Following reports of unrest along the northern U.S. frontier due to the civil war in Canada, President Martin Van Buren received information that, despite prior proclamations and the presence of civil officers, U.S. citizens continued to supply arms and had organized an armed force at Navy Island under a U.S. citizen's command. Van Buren urged these citizens to return home peaceably and warned that those violating U.S. neutrality by interfering in British Provinces would face arrest and prosecution under U.S. law, and would receive no government support. Issued January 5, 1838.

A University of Pennsylvania study, published in the Journal of Neuroscience, found that electrical stimulation of the prefrontal cortex may reduce intentions to commit aggression and enhance moral judgement. Researchers applied transcranial direct-current stimulation to 81 healthy adults averaging 20 years old, with one group receiving 20 minutes of stimulation and a control group receiving only 30 seconds. The next day, participants read accounts of physical and sexual assault and rated their likelihood of committing such acts. The stimulated group reported a 47 percent lower likelihood of physical assault and 70 percent lower likelihood of sexual assault, and judged the acts as more morally wrong than the control group. Paul Appelbaum of Columbia University, not involved in the study, noted the data suggest no impact on actual aggressive behaviour. Lead author Olivia Choy suggested repeated sessions might produce behavioural changes. Penn psychologist Adrian Raine described the procedure as minimal risk.

A fossil discovered by elk hunter David Bradt in 2010 at Montana's Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge has been identified as a new species of elasmosaur, a 70-million-year-old marine reptile. Detailed in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, the find is notable for its unusually short neck of about 7½ feet with roughly 40 vertebrae, compared to the typical 18-foot necks with up to 76 vertebrae. According to co-author Danielle Serratos, its coexistence with longer-necked elasmosaurs challenges the theory that the species gradually evolved longer necks. Co-author Patrick Druckenmiller noted that marine reptile fossils from the region's former inland sea are understudied compared to land dinosaurs.

The lecture introduces Chapter 7 on algebra, aiming to cover finite fields in a compressed form to prepare students for Reed-Solomon codes. Guest lecturer Ralf Koetter will teach the following week.

The professor reviews integers mod n (Zn) and groups, emphasizing the permutation property as a useful group axiom. All finite cyclic groups are isomorphic to Zn.

Subgroups are defined as subsets that are themselves groups under the same operation. Examples include {0,5} and even elements in Z10, and nZ in the integers. Cosets (translates H+G) either coincide or are disjoint, forming a partition of G. This yields Lagrange's theorem: |H| divides |G| for finite groups. Cosets themselves form a quotient group G/H under coset addition; Z/nZ is isomorphic to Zn.

Fields are sets with two operations (addition and multiplication) where elements form an abelian group under addition, non-zero elements form an abelian group under multiplication, and distributivity holds. Examples include real, complex, and binary fields.

Prime fields Fp (integers mod p with p prime) are finite fields. Primality ensures non-zero elements remain closed under multiplication. Every finite field with p elements is isomorphic to Fp, and every finite field contains a prime subfield whose size p is the field's characteristic. For any element β, adding β to itself p times yields 0. In characteristic 2 fields, addition equals subtraction.

Polynomials over a field F, denoted F[x], treat x as an indeterminate (placeholder), not a field element. Addition is component-wise; multiplication follows standard polynomial rules, with degree of products equaling the sum of degrees. The zero polynomial's degree is defined as minus infinity. Polynomials form an abelian group under addition but not under multiplication, as only non-zero degree-0 polynomials (units) have multiplicative inverses.

A webinar hosted by the presidents of Middle States, SACSCOC, and WASC addressed credit transfer policies, but concrete changes were unclear. MSCHE president Heather Perfetti stated accreditors should not be barriers to credit transfer and are urging a shift in the burden of proof from yes to no, though "urging" falls short of requiring. Historically, departments resist transferring credits due to economic self-interest, changing only under pressure from administration or legislatures like MassTransfer in Massachusetts. Accreditors' leverage has weakened since the first Trump administration broke regional monopolies, allowing colleges to shop for alternative accreditors. The new preference suggests defaulting to yes on transfer credits absent contrary evidence, though what constitutes such evidence remains unclear. AI could help by enabling faster transcript assessments, ideally alongside admission and financial aid decisions, though concerns about AI hallucinations exist. The author views the direction as positive but lacking a concrete plan.

A security aide to Ebonyi State Governor David Umahi allegedly slapped an FRSC officer identified as Soji at a checkpoint near Eagle Square, venue of the PDP convention. The checkpoint, manned by police, FRSC, and VIO personnel, was set up to restrict unauthorized access. The altercation reportedly began when the governor's aides demanded passage for the convoy. Soji was restrained by colleagues from retaliating and left the scene. FRSC spokesman Bisi Kazeem said no official report had been filed. Separately, security personnel at the venue were observed collecting money from individuals without accreditation in exchange for passage.

Coach Sutter reflects on a closely contested game, noting his team had a strong first period despite a goal allowed on what he considered a marginal call. He emphasizes the importance of finishing opportunities and limiting the opposition to one goal. Sutter states the home team faces pressure due to their regular-season points total and explains that seven-game series exist because of how close matchups can be. He identifies scoring the first goal as the key factor, noting his team did so in the first three games. On the opposing goal, Sutter describes it as a screened soft wrister and says the winger needed to block the shot, adding that a tired player couldn't change in time.

The 7th annual Julia's Hope Cup and Carnival, a pond-hockey tournament, will take place on Feb. 17 at Chippawa Park in Welland. Organizer Paul Turner created the event in memory of his daughter Julia, who died of cancer in 2011, to raise money for The Hope Centre, which addresses homelessness. The event has expanded to include food, kids' games, a silent auction, and a mini-tournament for children aged six to 12. It is being held on Family Day weekend for the first time. The main tournament starts at 11:30 a.m. and costs $100 per person or $50 for students, while the mini-tournament begins at 10 a.m. with a $25 registration fee. Last year's event raised $20,000 and drew around 1,000 attendees. Registration forms are available at several local businesses, and more information can be found at juliashopecup.ca.

Led by Isaiah Roth (Elliot Gould), the firm includes transgender lawyer Cameron Wirth (Laverne Cox) and former inmate Nick Brady (Kobi Libii). Jersey played defensively well after taking the lead, limiting offensive opportunities. Two teenagers, aged 14 and 17, are in custody after stealing a 15-passenger van from the Smoky Mountain Children's Home and leading multiple law enforcement agencies on a high-speed chase across East Tennessee. The pursuit ended near Highway 153 when the van struck another vehicle and hit a barrier wall at the Chickamauga Dam. No serious injuries were reported. The Children's Home stated it will conduct an internal investigation and cooperate with authorities.

The HID AMDI0095 enables the OS to bind a driver to the TMPM device in the ACPI namespace, with resources declared via resource objects. A page migration driver must enable the PAGEMIGRATION_EN bit in the IOMMU_MMIO_CNTRL_1 register across all IOMMUs, a one-time initialization that is harmless if repeated.

The TMPM function provides a single interface to the OS through mailbox registers, supporting parallel command execution via a ring buffer (RB). The firmware controls the Read pointer (initialized to the RB start), while the driver controls the Write pointer. Command execution order is not guaranteed; completion is indicated when the firmware advances the Read pointer past the command. The PM_COMMAND_STATUS field should be zero when sent, as firmware uses non-zero values.

The PM_Status register contains a TOGGLE bit; its state should be noted before sending a command to RB_Ctl. A change in TOGGLE indicates command completion and valid PM_Status contents. TOGGLE applies only to RB_Ctl register changes.

Cirque du Soleil announced it will donate US$1 million following the deadly shooting in Las Vegas. Half will go directly to victims' families, while the other half will be distributed as 5,000 tickets to police officers, firefighters, and paramedics for eight permanent Cirque shows on the Las Vegas Strip. The company also plans to participate in a benefit show to raise additional funds. Vice-president Jerry Nadal expressed condolences, and spokesperson Marie-Hélène Lagacé noted Las Vegas has been the company's second home for 20 years. None of its 1,500 local employees were injured.

President Ram Nath Kovind delivered his first address to the nation on the eve of Independence Day, marking 70 years of India's freedom. He paid tribute to freedom fighters and soldiers, and called August 15, 1947 the culmination of a dream rather than merely a transfer of power. Kovind urged citizens to participate in government initiatives like Swachh Bharat and Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao, and to make India open-defecation free. He called for building a "New India" before the 75th anniversary of Independence in 2022, emphasizing collective responsibility in abiding by laws, adopting GST, and paying taxes. He noted that demonetisation supported efforts toward an honest society and praised over one crore families who gave up LPG subsidies. Kovind envisioned New India as having housing for all, better infrastructure, and modern railways, while being both rapidly developing and sensitive. He urged citizens to educate at least one underprivileged child and aim for a fully educated society. Kovind was elected on July 17, defeating Opposition candidate Meira Kumar.

Zoë Schiffer and Leah Feiger discuss five news stories. First, Mark Bray, a Rutgers professor who wrote a book on antifa, is attempting to flee to Europe after death threats, though his flight reservation was mysteriously canceled. This follows Trump's September 22nd executive order designating antifa affiliates as domestic terrorists. Second, ICE is planning a 24/7 social media surveillance team, hiring around 30 analysts and seeking AI-enabled contractors across two centers. Third, a Harvard study found AI companion apps use emotional manipulation 37 percent of the time when users try to say goodbye. Fourth, an FDA announcement approving leucovorin calcium for autism symptoms has spawned a chaotic Facebook group filled with misinformation and grifters. Finally, an OpenAI blog post about internal tools caused DocuSign stock to drop 12 percent and affected HubSpot and Salesforce, while Figma's stock rose after being mentioned at OpenAI's Dev Day. Schiffer discusses whether AI infrastructure spending, projected at $500 billion for 2026-2027 against roughly $12 billion in consumer spending, indicates a bubble.

Former Southport MP John Pugh has expressed concerns that the closure of Homebase in Southport, and Sefton Council's approval of a 60,000 sq ft Sainsbury's store at Meols Cop retail park, could lead to further job losses in the town centre. Although Sainsbury's plans to create 400 jobs, Pugh argues the store will sell comparison goods and compete directly with town centre shops, potentially causing larger stores to relocate to Meols Cop. He criticised Sefton Council for encouraging the development and urged them to prepare a plan for Lord Street.

Web hosting company GoDaddy announced on Sunday that it had given The Daily Stormer, a neo-Nazi website, 24 hours to move its domain elsewhere for violating its terms of service. The action followed the site's article denigrating Heather Heyer, 32, who was killed at a white nationalist rally in Charlottesville, Virginia, allegedly struck by a car driven by a man with white nationalist views.

Lexus has announced UK pricing for its 2017 LC flagship coupe, with both the V8-powered LC500 and hybrid LC500h starting at £76,595. Over a third of the UK's allocation has been pre-ordered. The LC500 features a 467hp 5.0-litre V8 with a 10-speed automatic, while the LC500h produces 354hp through a hybrid powertrain with a four-speed automatic. The V8 accelerates from 0-60mph in under 4.5 seconds, with the hybrid half a second slower. Optional Sport and Sport+ packages add features such as 21-inch alloys, a carbon-fibre roof, sports seats, four-wheel steering, a limited slip differential, variable steering, and a retractable rear spoiler.

Research published in the Journal of Human Nutrition and Dietetics, involving over 24,000 Slimming World members with a BMI of at least 30, found that dieters setting ambitious weight-loss goals lost around 19 per cent of their body weight in a year, roughly double the 11 per cent lost by those with more modest aims. The findings challenge current NHS and NICE guidance, which recommends a "realistic" target of 5-10 per cent weight loss to avoid disappointment. Professor Amanda Avery of Nottingham University said encouraging slimmers to aim for their "dream weight," alongside regular support, could improve motivation and success. Participants who set their own personal targets were ten times more likely to succeed. Hollie Barrett, 30, who lost 8st 6lbs after setting a high target, was cited as an example.

WIRED editors tested carry-on bags for air travel, updated October 2025 with new additions including the Away softside suitcase and Travelpro Platinum Elite.

Top picks include: a preferred stylish suitcase with hidden pockets, interior stabilizer, three handles, and water-resistant nylon; Peak Design's Roller Pro, a hybrid hardshell/softshell with a "drawbridge" opening and expandable capacity, though heavier and pricier; the Travelpro Maxlite 5, a lightweight, durable option around $100; and the Rimowa aluminum case, known for durability and patina.

Other recommendations include Antler's roller bag with smooth, silent wheels and padded sleeves; State's Logan bag for children; Briggs & Riley for its lifetime warranty and soft expandable design; Yeti's Crossroads 35L; Beis weekender with removable bottom compartment; and a mini Take Off suitcase with removable wheels for budget airlines.

For backpacks, testers recommend the Tom Bihn Aeronaut 45, Six Moon Designs travel backpack, and Aer Travel Pack 3.

Guidance includes the TSA 3-1-1 liquids rule, comparison of softshell versus hardshell suitcases (hardware quality matters most), and advice to verify airline size requirements. Testing involved at least two flights per bag, assessing materials, wheels, handles, straps, and zippers.

The Colorado Prescription Drug Affordability Board voted to cap payments for Amgen's arthritis drug Enbrel, marking the first such action in the U.S. The limit, set at $600 per unit (about $30,350 annually per person), applies to government agencies and commercial health plans covering state residents. This compares to the roughly $53,000 paid per person by the average state insurance plan in 2023 and matches the upcoming Medicare maximum fair price. The move may prompt other states to adopt similar cost-containment strategies.

Long snappers hold a specialized role in football, responsible for snapping the ball to holders on field goals and extra points (about 7 yards) and to punters on punts (about 15 yards). Precision is essential, as inaccurate snaps can result in missed field goals or blocked punts, the latter correlating with a roughly 90% win rate for the blocking team. Long snappers are typically 6'1"-6'3", 230-250 pounds, with a build similar to a linebacker, requiring accuracy, consistency, balance, athleticism, and physicality. They must also cover downfield on punts and make tackles. NFL rosters reserve one spot for this position. Notable long snappers include Zak DeOssie, a two-time Super Bowl champion and Pro Bowler with the Giants, and Don Muhlbach, a two-time Pro Bowler who ranks second in Lions franchise history for games played. Alternate names include LS, deep-snapper, and short-snapper.

Brown shares quotes from OU coach Bob Stoops, who noted his team is more mature and confident at 4-0, acknowledged turnovers were a factor in last year's loss, and said OU needs to win after three straight losses to Texas.

The Biloxi Shuckers saw a 21 percent increase in attendance during their opening series at MGM Park compared to last year, drawing 2,500 more fans. Saturday's Jackie Robinson Day celebration set a record with 4,006 fans. A catch by center fielder Johnny Davis was named SportsCenter's top play, gaining 767,000 views on Instagram. The team plays in Chattanooga before returning April 22, when a jersey designed by Matt Stebly will be auctioned to benefit March of Dimes. New promotions include All-You-Can-Eat Wednesday and Thirsty Thursday.
