The study addresses the need for early identification of language comprehension deficits in young children, noting that existing assessments (PPVT-4, EVT-2, PLS-5, Token Test, CELF-5, TROG) are either vocabulary-focused or unsuitable for children aged 2-4. Building on prior research identifying three language comprehension phenotypes in autistic individuals (Command, Modifier, Syntactic), the authors developed the 15-item Language Phenotype Assessment (LPA), a 10-minute clinician-administered tool using toy-animal manipulatives, and a parallel parent-reported Language Phenotype Evaluation Checklist (LPEC).

The LPA was administered to 116 neurotypical children aged 1.5-7 years and 79 children diagnosed with ASD aged 2-8 years. Results showed 50% of neurotypical children attained the Command Phenotype by 1.6 years, Modifier Phenotype by 3.0 years, and Syntactic Phenotype by 3.7 years. All neurotypical children achieved the Syntactic Phenotype by age 5, compared to only 39% of ASD participants. The LPA demonstrated excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.92), test-retest reliability (r = 0.96), and inter-observer agreement (Kappa = 0.97). LPA and LPEC scores correlated strongly (r = 0.78).

The authors conclude that the LPA can support early identification of language deficits, improve classification beyond verbal/nonverbal categories, and guide language therapy by shifting focus from vocabulary-building to syntactic development. Limitations include logistical challenges of manipulatives and the need for basic vocabulary knowledge prior to testing.

The Trump administration announced it will largely continue Obama-era nuclear policy but adopt a more aggressive stance toward Russia, warning of "unacceptably dire costs" for any limited nuclear attack in Europe. The 74-page nuclear posture review does not call for a net increase in strategic nuclear weapons and endorses existing arms control agreements, including the New START treaty. It labels North Korea a "clear and grave threat" and identifies China as a potential nuclear adversary. The review supports modernizing the arsenal with new bombers, submarines, and land-based missiles. To counter Russia's "escalate to de-escalate" doctrine, the administration proposes modifying some submarine-launched ballistic missiles with smaller-yield warheads and, longer-term, developing a nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile. Arms control groups criticized the plan, with the Union of Concerned Scientists calling it "reckless." Russian and Chinese officials were briefed before the review's release.

Ministers negotiating with the DUP to form a working administration have said abolishing line dancing may be necessary for progress. The DUP opposes line dancing due to founder Ian Paisley deeming it sinful. David Davis stated other concessions, such as ending Sunday trading or restricting same-sex relationships, were not viable. A Leave voter from the Isle of Wight expressed support for the move if it facilitated Brexit.

A new EducationNext poll shows shifting U.S. opinion on school choice, a priority of President Trump and Education Secretary Betsy DeVos. Support for forming charter schools dropped 12 points in one year, from 51 to 39 percent, across political parties and demographic groups—one of the largest single-year shifts in the survey's 11-year history. Meanwhile, support for universal vouchers rose to 45 percent, and tax-credit scholarships remained the most popular option at 55 percent. The charter decline coincides with disputes over charter expansion, including opposition from the NAACP and Black Lives Matter and battles in Massachusetts, Detroit, and Los Angeles. Partisan divides have reversed on vouchers, with 62 percent of Republicans now supporting them versus 50 percent of Democrats. Pollsters found Trump's net influence on opinion is negligible, unlike Obama's in 2009. However, Republicans and Democrats give local public schools nearly identical approval ratings.

The patent application relates to robotic systems featuring multi-gripper assemblies designed to selectively grip and hold objects. The technology addresses limitations in conventional robots that struggle with gripping objects from groups or handling irregularly shaped items.

The system includes a transport robot with multi-gripper assemblies containing addressable vacuum regions that can operate independently or together to grip single or multiple objects simultaneously or sequentially. Each vacuum region can draw air independently through arrays of suction elements to create pressure differentials that secure target objects.

Key components include: an imaging system for capturing object data, a robotic arm with an end effector, a vision sensor device, a force detector assembly, a manifold assembly fluidically coupling vacuum regions to vacuum sources, and a controller/processing unit. The vision sensor is positioned below the gripping interface plane to maintain an unobscured field of view during operations.

The system operates by receiving image data of objects, identifying target objects, selecting appropriate vacuum regions based on object geometry and weight, gripping objects at calculated vacuum levels, and transporting them via a planned path. The controller measures grip strength against thresholds, executing regripping actions if initial grips are insufficient, and monitors grips during transfer using different thresholds.

A registration data source (RDS) stores object characteristics and vacuum gripper data, enabling dynamic learning and accommodation of different gripper configurations. The system supports various gripper arrangements (1x3, 2x2, etc.) and can be applied in warehousing, shipping, manufacturing, and packaging environments.

The Fraser Institute will release a study on February 16, 2017, titled *Examining the Revenue Neutrality of British Columbia's Carbon Tax*. The study assesses whether B.C.'s carbon tax revenues, introduced in 2008 with a revenue-neutral promise, are offset by other tax reductions. The issue is relevant as the federal government requires provinces to adopt carbon pricing by 2018, with B.C.'s system considered a potential model.

The passage discusses sequences of functions and modes of convergence in analysis.

**Two notions of convergence:** Pointwise convergence requires that for each fixed x in S, f_n(x) → f(x). Uniform convergence is stronger, requiring that for every ε > 0, there exists M such that |f_n(x) − f(x)| < ε for all n ≥ M and all x in S simultaneously. Uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence, but not conversely.

**Example:** f_n(x) = x^n on [0,1] converges pointwise to a discontinuous function (0 on [0,1), 1 at x=1). It converges uniformly on [0,b] for b < 1, but not on [0,1]. Another example is a tent function sequence that converges pointwise to 0 but not uniformly.

**Interchange of limits:** A central question in analysis is whether two limiting processes can be interchanged. Three key questions are posed:
1. Is the limit of continuous functions continuous?
2. Does the derivative of the limit equal the limit of the derivatives?
3. Does the integral of the limit equal the limit of the integrals?

Under only pointwise convergence, the answer to all three is no, demonstrated by counterexamples. Under uniform convergence, the answer to all three is yes.

**Theorems proven:**
- The uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous (proved via an ε/3 argument).
- If f_n → f uniformly on [a,b] with f_n continuous, then ∫f_n → ∫f.
- If f_n are continuously differentiable, f_n → f uniformly, and f_n′ → g uniformly, then f is differentiable and f′ = g (proved using the fundamental theorem of calculus).

**Weierstrass M-test:** If |f_j(x)| ≤ M_j for all x in S and ΣM_j converges, then Σf_j(x) converges absolutely for each x, and the partial sums converge uniformly to the sum. This provides a useful criterion for establishing uniform convergence of series of functions.

The De'Longhi Rivelia, discounted to $1,300, is an automatic latte maker that handles milk-based coffee drinks from start to finish via a touchscreen interface. It features a swappable hopper for using two bean types, a "bean adapt" function for customizing settings per bean, and a built-in milk frother that produces micro-foam, though not as hot as a traditional steam wand. While it may not match the quality of a portafilter machine, it offers consistency and ease of use.

Imran Mohammad, a Rohingya refugee recognised by the UNHCR, recounts spending four birthdays in detention on Manus Island in Papua New Guinea after arriving on October 29, 2013, at age 19. He was first placed in Delta compound, where 300 men shared cramped shipping container rooms, five toilets, and one washing machine, with long queues for basic necessities. He later moved to Mike compound, housing over 400 men in similarly poor conditions, including hot metal containers and limited facilities. Mohammad describes psychological distress, suicidal thoughts, hunger, and restricted communication with family. He avoided crowds, focused on learning and writing, and adopted the motto "the pen is mightier than the sword." He states that detainees face ongoing hardships, including slow internet that prevents phone calls, and expresses that seeking safety in Australia resulted in suffering and, for some, death.

Historically, solar eclipses inspired fear across cultures, including ancient Greeks, Vikings, and Chinese. In his book "American Eclipse," David Baron describes the 1878 eclipse, during which some terrified Americans believed Judgment Day had arrived, leading to one man killing his son and himself. Some Christians today link eclipses to biblical end-times, referencing the darkened sky during Jesus's crucifixion, though astronomers reject that an eclipse occurred then. Sister Mary Elizabeth of a Missouri monastery reassures worried Catholics that the August 21 eclipse is not an omen, and her fellow nuns plan to watch it. In Islamic tradition, Prophet Muhammad taught that an eclipse coinciding with his son Ibrahim's death was merely a sign of God, not of human events. Baron says even non-religious people find eclipses profoundly awe-inspiring, tapping into brain regions associated with religion and evoking humanity's smallness relative to the universe.

The Triangle (1-3-1) Offense attacks a Diamond & One defense by placing the Star player at the high post, isolating them against the Chaser, who is typically skilled in pass denial but weak in post defense. When the Star receives the ball, baseline and wing players form an inside triangle, while two players set up a guard front.

Key options include:
- Driving left or right with drop passes to teammates for layups
- Kick-out passes to perimeter players for open shots or dribble penetration
- Post flashes by O4 into the middle when feeds are unavailable
- A lob exchange when the Star's defender overplays the high post entry

Successful implementation requires execution of high post isolations, back cuts, interior passing, spot-up shots, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, and timing. Recommended preparation includes scouting opponents, identifying weak defenders, and varying alignments to prevent defensive focus.

A funnel-web spider, considered the world's most venomous, was spotted at a home in Springwood, NSW, by resident Bec Sheedy and her mother. Funnel-webs are common along Australia's east coast, from Queensland to New South Wales, with a new species recently discovered in northern Tasmania. Paul Hare, Invertebrate Keeper at Taronga Zoo, said bite symptoms include nausea, cramps, sweating and numbness, and urged immediate hospitalisation. The Australian Museum has recorded 13 deaths, though none since antivenene was developed in 1981 by Dr Struan Sutherland. Hare noted the spiders are defensive rather than aggressive, and their venom is lethal only to insects, other spiders and primates. Sightings are common during mating season when males search for females. Hare advised caution, wearing gloves while gardening, but said the spiders play an important ecological role by killing pests.

The speaker, assuming the presidency, pledges to uphold the Constitution and fulfill his duties. He reflects on the Constitution's success over 36 years, during which the population grew from four to twelve million, territory extended from the Mississippi to the Pacific, new states joined, treaties were established, and commerce and industry flourished.

He acknowledges past dissensions, including those rooted in European revolutionary wars, but notes that ten years of peace have dissolved partisan divisions. He outlines shared political principles: popular sovereignty, limited government, frequent elections, fiscal economy, military subordination to civil power, press and religious freedom, and union.

He warns that geographically based divisions pose greater dangers than ideological ones, emphasizing the federal-national balance between state and Union rights.

Reviewing his predecessor's administration, he cites achievements: debt reduction, repeal of internal taxes, acquisition of Florida, boundary extension to the Pacific, recognition of southern hemisphere independence, naval expansion, and suppression of the slave trade. He commits to continuing internal improvements, citing the national road as precedent, and hopes constitutional objections to such projects will be resolved.

Acknowledging the unusual circumstances of his election and his limited initial public confidence, he pledges honest intentions and devoted service, committing his fate to divine providence.

KGI analyst Ming-Chi Kuo reports that the 2017 Apple Watch will retain the same form factor as previous models, marking three generations with the same design. The new model will reportedly include LTE connectivity and be available in 38mm and 42mm sizes, in both LTE and non-LTE versions. Since the original 2014 release, the only design change has been a slight thickness increase. Ben Lovejoy speculated that a non-LTE version could either offer improved battery life or a thinner design, with the latter being more likely given Apple's priorities. A significant form factor change would require substantial effort from Apple and app developers.

A recent college graduate with a music education degree wrote seeking advice about their mother demanding $480 monthly for rent and phone while they earn minimum wage at a three-month job. The graduate also faces tuition debt, certification exam fees, and wants to save for a car and apartment. They described their mother imposing rent after conflicts, including allegedly keeping $2,000 from a past refund check.

The advice columnist offered four suggestions: 1) Budget carefully, noting $500-$1,000 monthly could remain after expenses to address debts and savings; 2) Consider additional jobs during off-hours, sharing a personal example of working multiple jobs to pursue golf; 3) Use this post-college period to explore different experiences, such as waiting tables, which builds transferable skills; 4) Be honest about the situation, questioning whether the graduate has fully disclosed their role in the conflicts with their mother.

Following the enemy's invasion of the nation's capital, during which public edifices and archives were destroyed, and the subsequent plundering of Alexandria after the loss of a nearby fort, the British commander has declared his intent to destroy assailable coastal towns, citing alleged retaliation for actions in Upper Canada. Deeming these acts a disregard of civilized warfare amid ongoing peace negotiations, President James Madison issues this proclamation on September 1, 1814, urging all citizens to unite in defense, directing civil and military officers to perform their duties, and authorizing military district commanders to call upon local militia, whether or not part of federal quotas, to protect threatened areas. The proclamation is attested by Secretary of State James Monroe.

The team suffered a tough loss after giving up a two-goal lead in the third period, allowing too many chances and failing to execute in the final ten minutes. Detroit is credited for battling hard. Despite the frustrating downer, the speaker believes the team showed tenacity and will rebound in the playoffs.

The speaker describes a goal sequence involving blocked shots and a puck deflecting off Fleury's leg. He discusses a physical altercation where he struck an opponent with a two-hander after trash talk. He mentions an unusual play where the puck rested on Osgood's back and a player covered it with his hand, uncertain if it warranted a penalty shot. He defends a coaching decision to give defensemen a breather, noting the team had chances to clear the puck. Despite conceding goals early and late, he emphasizes the game remained close, scoring opportunities were generated, and bounces favored the opponent. Insufficient sleep is prevalent among children, yet pediatric clinicians lack effective tools to address it at the point of care. Using the Multiphase Optimization Strategy (MOST) framework, researchers developed a mobile health platform combining behavioral sleep promotion and behavioral economic incentives to increase weeknight sleep duration in children aged 9-12 years with insufficient sleep.

In this optimization phase, 97 participants from PA and NJ were randomized using a 2⁵ factorial design to test five candidate components: sleep goal (guideline-based vs. personalized), child-directed loss-framed incentive, caregiver-directed loss-framed incentive, screen time reduction messaging, and daily routine messaging. All participants received core components of sleep tracking (via Fitbit) and weekly performance feedback. The optimization criterion was a ≥30-minute increase in average weeknight sleep duration.

No single component setting achieved the optimization criterion independently. However, two component combinations did: (1) core intervention plus caregiver-directed incentive, screen time messaging, and routine messaging (+39.6 minutes); and (2) core intervention plus caregiver-directed incentive and routine messaging (+32.0 minutes). Either sleep goal setting was equally effective in these combinations. The child-directed incentive was found redundant.

Limitations include a single site, predominantly non-Hispanic White sample, fewer data captured from Black participants, a brief two-week follow-up, and use of a single-sensor sleep tracker. The next step is evaluating the optimized intervention in a randomized controlled trial.

The Gorakhpur BRD Hospital tragedy, which killed at least 30 children, has been linked to severe overcrowding, with the facility accommodating 10 times its capacity, according to a central team's findings reported by Indian Express. Infant warmers were shared by multiple babies, raising concerns about Special Newborn Care Units (SNCUs) in the region. An SNCU typically has 12-20 beds, requires four doctors and 10-12 nurses, costs Rs 41 lakh to set up, and Rs 10 lakh annually to operate. Although 700 SNCUs were reportedly functional nationwide as of July 28, 2017, those in nearby districts like Basti and Ballia are non-existent or non-functional, causing referrals to BRD Hospital. The hospital also faced oxygen supply issues, relying on standby cylinders. Union Health Minister J P Nadda, along with Anupriya Patel and C K Mishra, visited Gorakhpur and announced a Rs 85 crore regional medical centre for research on children's diseases.

This paper addresses deontic argumentation, focusing on the challenge of formalizing weak permission—the idea that an action is permitted if the obligation to its contrary cannot be derived.

The authors argue that standard argumentation semantics, such as grounded and stable semantics, fail to support weak permission when conflicts between obligations arise. They formally prove (Theorem 1) that in conflictual theories, weak permissions for conflicted literals cannot be justified under these semantics, meaning conflicted literals cannot be deemed weakly facultative.

To address this limitation, the paper introduces a Deontic Argumentation Theory built from literals, deontic literals (obligation, permission, weak permission), and rules. Arguments are classified as either natural or imaginary (weak permission arguments). A new "wp-semantics" is defined through a fixed-point construction that iteratively builds sets of wp-acceptable and wp-rejected arguments, treating weak permission as failure to derive the contrary obligation.

The authors prove the wp-extension is unique, conflict-free, that no argument is simultaneously justified and rejected, and that it extends grounded semantics. Crucially, weak permissions for conflicted literals are justified under wp-semantics, enabling weakly facultative conclusions in conflict scenarios.

The discussion justifies this treatment by appealing to legal principles against ad hoc adjudication and retroactivity. Related work is reviewed, noting that prior approaches—including ASPIC+ extensions, Defeasible Deontic Logic, and various argumentation frameworks—have largely neglected weak permission or cannot handle unresolved conflicts. Future work includes integrating ambiguity blocking and propagation, and extending the approach to neighbourhood semantics.

The global aluminum foil packaging market is expected to grow at approximately 4.5% CAGR during the forecast period. Growth drivers include innovation in packaging, expansion in pharmaceutical and cosmetic industries, changing consumer lifestyles, and rising spending power. Aluminum packaging offers corrosion resistance, chemical neutrality, hygiene, and non-toxicity, protecting beverages, food, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics. Companies are adopting sustainable, active, and intelligent packaging technologies. Market restraints include the lack of proper recycling processes in several countries. A key trend involves manufacturers focusing on profitable production locations and short-distance supply to reduce costs. Regionally, the market is segmented into North America, Europe, Asia Pacific, and RoW, with Asia Pacific expected to be the fastest-growing region due to rising per capita income and purchasing power.

MyWorld is a new gaming platform that allows users to create their own games across any genre. Players can build objects, choose genres and scenes, set rules, and determine play modes (single-player, PvP, or Co-Op). Games can be saved locally or shared with the MyWorld community.

Game creation occurs in two settings: design mode, where players place and remove objects, and constructor mode, where objects are designed in a model editor. Designs can be functional, including turrets, sensors, and robots. Players level up through building and playing, unlocking pre-built materials. Avatars are also customizable.

MyWorld has launched a Kickstarter crowdfunding campaign to fund its next development phase, offering exclusive materials to early backers.

Novice Forex traders often believe success requires exceptional talent or following others' opinions, but Australian traders demonstrate this is false. Traders should avoid being misled by the market's apparent ease and wait for profitable trade setups rather than forcing trades.

Mental stability is crucial, as inexperienced traders often take large risks after losses. Developing a strong mentality requires mastering three elements: technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis.

Traders should rely on themselves rather than copying others. While learning from experts is valuable, decisions should be independent. Active traders who develop judgmental skills outperform passive ones who imitate others.

Beginners can seek expert advice but should start small and think critically before applying it, as their experience level differs.

At Tesla's 2021 Annual Meeting of Stockholders on October 7, 2021, stockholders voted on nine proposals. James Murdoch and Kimbal Musk were elected as Class II directors. Management proposals to reduce director terms to two years (Proposal 2) and eliminate supermajority voting requirements (Proposal 3) were not approved, as they failed to reach the required 66 2/3% threshold. The ratification of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as the independent auditor (Proposal 4) was approved. Non-binding stockholder proposals regarding one-year director terms (Proposal 5) and diversity and inclusion reporting (Proposal 6) were approved. Stockholder proposals on employee arbitration reporting (Proposal 7), human capital management oversight (Proposal 8), and human rights reporting (Proposal 9) were not approved.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC announcing that on February 5, 2019, Angela Ahrendts, Senior Vice President of Retail, would depart the company effective April 15, 2019. Deirdre O'Brien succeeded her, assuming the role of Senior Vice President, Retail + People, effective February 5, 2019. The report was signed on February 6, 2019 by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary.

The NTSC and CSA have partnered to improve cloud vendor security by promoting the CSA's Security, Trust & Assurance Registry (STAR) and related tools as recommended practices for vendor evaluations. The collaboration aims to streamline vendor security reviews and encourage best practices. The organizations will develop a STAR-based questionnaire mapped to common compliance frameworks, along with a joint whitepaper explaining the program's implementation for CISOs and vendors. Additionally, the CSA and NTSC will participate in each other's events, engage in working groups, and collaborate on cloud security research.

Consumer Electricals Ltd (CGCEL) submitted a bid on September 20, 2017, as an expression of interest for the Kenstar business and brand, a Videocon group subsidiary that makes kitchen appliances, TVs, air conditioners, air coolers and health appliances. The bid followed an invitation letter from Videocon Industries dated September 6. The bid price was not disclosed, results have not been announced, and no binding documents or negotiations have taken place. Videocon, burdened with over Rs 40,000 crore in debt, has been selling assets, including a 10 per cent stake in Offshore Area 1 to ONGC Videsh and Oil India in June 2013 for USD 2.475 billion, merging its direct-to-home business, and selling spectrum in six circles for Rs 4,428 crore.

Daniella Teutsch and Sara Wolf founded HydroChic in 2007 to provide modest swimwear for women, initially inspired by their needs as religious Jewish women seeking less revealing options. They soon discovered another underserved market: women with medical conditions such as mastectomies, bariatric surgeries, skin cancer, and psoriasis. The New Rochelle, N.Y. company now designs athletic wear addressing these needs, including swim tops with mastectomy bras, compression workout gear, and skin-protective suits. Previously educators who met working at a women's hat business, the founders were inspired during a 2006 beach outing to create more flattering swimwear, building a business that has succeeded both financially and personally.

The Supreme Court's new term is expected to significantly impact higher education, though only two college-related cases—both concerning transgender rights—appear on the main docket. Many consequential rulings are instead occurring through the "shadow docket," an emergency process that allows rapid interim decisions without full briefings or oral arguments. Legal experts note this has already affected higher education, as the court has overturned lower-court rulings on Department of Education staffing cuts and other issues.

The two main docket cases, West Virginia v. B.P.J. and Little v. Hecox, involve transgender athletes barred from women's sports. Hecox recently requested dismissal of her case, though B.P.J. is likely to proceed, potentially affecting Title IX interpretations beyond sports, including bathrooms and locker rooms.

Experts anticipate additional shadow docket cases involving First Amendment rights, visa policies, academic freedom, and federal funding. Trump v. Orr, concerning transgender passport identification, could also affect university operations. Former Brandeis president Fred Lawrence warned that shadow docket rulings often cause irreversible harm before full merit reviews occur.

Riley Oil Company in Paoli, Indiana, is one of the few remaining full-service gas stations in the area, where attendants pump gas, wash windshields, and check oil at no extra cost. Opened in 1971 by Glendon Riley, the business is now run by family members Jo Ann and Jeff Riley, along with four other relatives. Employee Daniel McCabe and customers like Loretta Brown appreciate the old-fashioned service and personal interactions. The owners emphasize their commitment to customers and family, noting that great-grandchildren are being born into the business, suggesting it will remain family-operated for years to come.

Oklahoma City Taco Bell employees called police early Tuesday after 52-year-old Zette Madden allegedly chased them with a tire iron, demanded money, and destroyed cash registers, glass doors, the drive-thru window, and menu, causing thousands in damages. Officer Phillip Paz ordered her to drop the weapon seven times before using a taser, fearing she would threaten employees again. Madden was treated at a hospital for cuts and jailed on charges including destruction of property, first-degree robbery, and robbery with a dangerous weapon. Employees said she had previously trespassed and attempted to steal soda.

This study presents the first coupling of atomistic nanoindentation simulations with orientation-resolved Schmid factor mapping to examine how slip system activation in single-crystalline α-titanium depends on temperature and crystallographic orientation.

Molecular dynamics simulations were performed using LAMMPS with an EAM potential on three orientations ([0001], [10̅10], and [2̅110]) at 10, 300, and 600 K. A rigid spherical indenter was applied to depths of 4 nm, and dislocations were analyzed using OVITO and the Dislocation Extraction Algorithm.

Load–displacement curves showed Hertzian elastic responses followed by pop-in events, most pronounced for [0001]. Contact pressure decreased with increasing temperature due to enhanced atomic mobility. For [0001], intense stress induced a martensitic HCP→BCC transformation, most prevalent at low temperatures, while a-type dislocations dissociated into Shockley partials at 300 K. Dominant defects were basal a-type dislocations, accompanied by c-type, prismatic, and pyramidal ⟨c+a⟩ dislocations.

Schmid factor mapping linked high resolved shear stress regions to plastic zones beneath the indenter. The [10̅10] orientation exhibited a characteristic "lasso" mechanism producing prismatic loops and dual-lobe pile-up morphology, while [2̅110] showed asymmetric pile-ups from direct subsurface loop nucleation. Surface morphologies agreed with AFM observations.

Dislocation density was highest in [0001] and increased with temperature, while prismatic orientations showed lower densities that decreased with temperature due to enhanced recovery. The results provide a mechanistic framework for interpreting temperature-sensitive deformation in HCP titanium.

Falkland Islands Senior Fisheries Scientist Alexander Arkhipkin has contributed to international efforts addressing the challenges of high seas fishing on stock assessments. He noted that in areas lacking regional fisheries management organisations, fishing is largely unregulated, with limited data on vessel numbers, catch amounts, species, and sizes. In the Southwest Atlantic, over 250 jiggers and trawlers annually catch substantial quantities of squid, hake, and rock cod, complicating stock assessments and increasing overfishing risks. Similarly, nearly 300 foreign jiggers now fish jumbo squid in the Eastern Pacific high seas, raising concerns for Mexico, Peru, and Chile. In September 2017, Peru's IMARPE hosted an international workshop in Lima, which Arkhipkin attended, producing recommendations on acoustic surveys, stock structure analysis, and assessment techniques to improve squid management.

The application relates to physical layer preambles and signaling for wireless communications, particularly for WLAN protocols including IEEE 802.11be and future versions. As new wireless protocols enable enhanced features and greater bandwidth (up to 320 MHz), new preamble designs are needed to support signaling for features and resource allocations.

The disclosure describes a physical layer convergence protocol data unit (PPDU) containing a preamble with legacy fields (L-STF, L-LTF, L-SIG, RL-SIG) followed by a universal signal field (U-SIG) and version-specific fields such as EHT-SIG. The U-SIG contains version-independent fields (version identifier, UL/DL indicator, BSS color, TXOP duration) and version-dependent fields (format information, additional signaling). The U-SIG indicates PPDU format (trigger-based, single-user, multi-user, or unified SU/MU), bandwidth, puncturing, and content channel structures.

The EHT-SIG, which follows the U-SIG, carries overflow signaling and additional information including resource unit (RU) allocations, spatial stream configurations, and per-user signaling, supporting up to 16 spatial streams. Different EHT-SIG formats accommodate various PPDU types, compression modes, and OFDMA/MU-MIMO transmissions.

The design supports puncturing indications, parallelization of signaling across subchannels or subbands, and flexible RU allocations, while aiming to minimize preamble length and maintain compatibility with legacy devices.

Nintendo's Labo line of cardboard accessories will include a Toy Con Garage, a kit allowing users to build their own cardboard creations, as confirmed at a New York event reported by Kotaku. The toolkit features basic inputs, actions, and if-then statements. Nintendo demonstrated possibilities including a cardboard electric guitar and electronic tennis. It is unclear whether accessing the app requires purchasing a Labo set, though this is assumed. The virtual mech accessory launches April 20th.

Darren Till won a controversial unanimous decision over Stephen Thompson at UFC Fight Night 130 in Liverpool on May 27, 2018. Critics suggested the decision favored Till due to the fight's location. Till has offered to rematch Thompson in America as soon as possible, expressing confidence in the same outcome, possibly by knockout. The fight had limited action aside from a knockdown by Till in the final round, and many disputed judges' scoring that gave Till four rounds.

The Department of Justice has called on the Education Department to investigate the University of Nevada at Reno's UndocuPack program, which supports undocumented students through referrals, aid, and career services. UNR President Brian Sandoval defended the program, stating it uses no federal funds, serves all students regardless of citizenship, and complies with federal and state law. He said the university will respond through legal channels.

Advocates view the investigation as an escalation of the Trump administration's broader crackdown on higher education benefits for undocumented students, following lawsuits against states over in-state tuition policies and investigations into scholarship programs. The DOJ cited the 1996 Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act, though Diego Sánchez of the Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration noted no court has interpreted the law to bar university support offices.

A report identified at least 59 undocumented student resource centers nationwide. Advocates, including Gaby Pacheco of TheDream.US, fear institutions may pre-emptively scale back programs, and expect continued federal targeting of undocumented student supports.

The patent describes a system and method for processing mobile payments when a user device or merchant payment system is disconnected from payment servers. A user device with an enabled "offline payment mode" can receive an offline payment request from a merchant payment system via local communications (e.g., PAN, NFC, LAN, or QR code scanning), approve the payment, and provide payment information without requiring a connection to payment servers.

Key features include:
- Only one user device per e-wallet can have offline mode enabled at a time to prevent account overdrawing.
- The offline mode can be transferred between user devices, either online through a payment server or offline through local communications using a handover process with suspended states and confirmation messages.
- A pre-authorized reserve amount is set aside from a payment account for offline transactions.
- Both the user device and merchant payment system store transaction details and transmit them to the payment server once connectivity is restored.
- Each transaction has a unique ID, and the payment server refrains from processing duplicate IDs to prevent double-processing.

The system is useful in situations like natural disasters or network congestion when connectivity is unavailable, and may be implemented in cloud computing environments.

The High Post Split Offense is a simple, long-standing basketball system effective at all levels, built on quick high post splits, down screens, and back cuts. Its 2-3 alignment frees the baseline for cuts, creates scoring opportunities for all five players, eliminates weakside defensive help, and supports strong offensive rebounding.

The offense has four phases: (1) High Post Split, where a guard passes to the high post and splits with the other guard, with counters including handoffs, fake splits, back cuts, and two-same-side cuts; (2) Down Screens, set by wings for guards, with counters like double splits and back screens; (3) High Post Isolation, where the post assumes a triple-threat position with no weakside help; and (4) Strong Post Ups against smaller defenders.

Down screen counters address defenders who chase, cheat, switch, or show-and-recover, using curls, fades, back cuts, screen-and-rolls, and slips. Entry variations include Flop/Back Cut, Wing Pass, Wing Double Away, and Post Single/Double.

Success depends on spacing, execution, coordination, non-verbal communication, and aggressive offensive rebounding with box-outs.

The passage describes a tonneau cover for pickup truck beds, continuing from prior patent applications dating to 2015. The cover spans the bed's side walls and includes multiple panel sections, a non-movable base panel, and features such as latching assemblies, vertical support gussets, a buckle securement system, hinge assemblies with seal spacers and rods, and side rails.

Each panel section has a latching assembly with two pinch latch assemblies, one on each side wall. Each pinch latch assembly includes a latch handle portion with a latch, spring pockets, and guide tabs, plus an inner pinch handle portion with slots receiving the guide tabs. Springs bias the latches into a latched condition. A longitudinally extending connector links both pinch latch assemblies so activating one simultaneously releases the opposing latch, enabling single-side operation. Springs return latches to the latched position when force is released.

Additional features include integrated lights near the latches, D-shaped seals on rails to prevent water entry, adjustable rail brackets and clips, a removable gusset assembly that pivots between stowed and upright positions to support folded panels, hinge seals with spacers and rods for sealing between panels, and a channel bracket with buckle straps to secure folded panels vertically on the base panel.

The Bank of England's executive director for prudential policy, Vicky Saporta, stated that British banks should not anticipate further major changes to capital or liquidity requirements following the implementation of Basel III reforms. Speaking at a London conference, Saporta said the BoE's focus would shift to new risks and unintended consequences of existing regulations, including cyber-attack resilience and research indicating post-crisis leverage rules have discouraged central clearing of over-the-counter derivative trades. The BoE has also indicated it will not lower regulatory standards after Britain leaves the EU in March 2019.

Aaron Judge suffered an elbow injury in late-July, causing him to miss 10 days and serve primarily as a DH for nearly a month before returning to the outfield in September with diminished arm strength. Despite the injury, he batted .331 with 53 home runs and 114 RBIs in the regular season, and .500 in the playoffs. Microsoft Corporation, headquartered in Redmond, Washington, filed its Form 10-K annual report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021. As of December 31, 2020, the aggregate market value of common stock held by non-affiliates was $1.7 trillion, with 7,514,891,248 shares outstanding as of July 26, 2021.

Microsoft develops software, services, devices, and solutions, including cloud-based offerings, operating systems, productivity applications, server applications, and gaming products. The company operates through three segments: Productivity and Business Processes (Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products, Enterprise Services), and More Personal Computing (Windows, Devices, Gaming, Search Advertising). In June 2021, Microsoft announced Windows 11, and in March 2021 acquired ZeniMax Media Inc. An agreement to acquire Nuance Communications was entered in April 2021.

As of June 30, 2021, Microsoft employed approximately 181,000 people (103,000 in the U.S.). The company committed to be carbon negative by 2030 and pledged initiatives addressing racial inequity and digital skills training. Microsoft faces significant competition across all markets from firms including Apple, Google, Amazon, Oracle, IBM, and others, and is increasingly focused on cloud-based services, which presents execution and competitive risks. The COVID-19 pandemic continues to impact business operations.

The disclosure describes a semiconductor device and method of manufacture addressing coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch issues that cause delamination between semiconductor die layers, particularly involving copper and low-k dielectrics.

The method involves arranging a plurality of pre-tested interconnect structures (or a single universal interconnect structure) on a carrier substrate using an adhesive film, then encapsulating them in a first encapsulant to form a reconstructed wafer. The encapsulant is thinned via CMP to expose external connectors. Packaged semiconductor devices, such as processor dies (xPU) and memory cubes with memory controllers, are bonded to the interconnect structures using either direct Cu-to-Cu bonding (at 150-250°C) or solder bonding. An underfill material (CUF or MUF) is provided, followed by a second encapsulation and thinning. The carrier substrate is de-bonded, and external contacts are formed.

Embodiments include configurations where semiconductor dies bridge adjacent interconnect structures or share a universal interconnect structure, with series of redistribution layers (URDLs) formed between them.

The approach enables super large package components (>70 mm by 70 mm) for high performance computing (HPC) applications, including AI, networking, and servers. Benefits include reduced CTE mismatch stress, lower bonding temperatures, improved component and board-level reliability through pre-testing of known-good components, and a simplified wafer-form process flow.

Enron's stock fell to a 14-year low on November 26, 2001, trading below one-third of its book value amid mounting doubts that Dynegy's $23 billion acquisition would be completed on original terms. Enron's 6.4% notes due 2006 dropped to 48 cents on the dollar. Concerns centered on Enron's financial disclosures, a $690 million loan (extended to December 14), and efforts to raise $500 million to $1 billion in additional capital through J.P. Morgan Chase and Citigroup.

Dynegy's board declined to comment on the deal's status, though management reiterated commitment while conducting due diligence. The merger contains a "material adverse change" clause that could allow Dynegy to withdraw. Dynegy's own bonds fell on concerns the acquisition would harm its credit rating.

Citigroup reportedly reduced its Enron exposure by $2.38 billion through credit default swap transactions involving several trusts.

Enron faced a third class-action lawsuit over its 401(k) plan, with plaintiffs seeking $850 million, alleging the company sold stock to employees at artificially inflated prices without a prospectus. Employees were barred from selling shares during an October-November administrative lockdown.

Separately, Petrobras reportedly neared approval to purchase Enron's stakes in Brazilian gas distributors CEG and CEG Rio, while India's AV Birla group denied interest in Enron's Dabhol Power stake.

Martin Colin Hodder, 45, of Parr Street, Macclesfield, has been jailed for 18 weeks after admitting two charges of assault at Stockport magistrates' court. The January attack occurred after Hodder consumed one and a half bottles of vodka while drinking with his ex-partner and her daughter. Prosecutor Robert Jones said Hodder retrieved a butter knife from the kitchen, held it to his own throat, then slashed his ex-partner's arms when she raised her hands to protect herself. He threatened to take the daughter's life, and she was cut on the wrist while trying to take the knife from him. Magistrates described it as a "sustained attack with a weapon in a domestic setting whilst in drink" and imposed a year-long restraining order. The older victim criticised the sentence as a "disgrace." Defending, Anthony Gardener noted Hodder had not been in trouble for six years.

Coach Julien declined to provide updates on an injured player, stating evaluation is ongoing. He praised the replacement's performance in Bergeron's spot despite limited chemistry, and noted his team played better in the third period after sitting back early. Julien emphasized that depth scoring from players like Shaw and Paille is expected, not surprising, and stressed that his team cannot afford passengers in a do-or-die game. He defended captain Zdeno Chara against criticism, calling him one of the league's best defensemen and noting none of the five goals were his fault. Julien explained he is tinkering between Daugavins and Soderberg due to Campbell's injury, and uses Peverley on faceoffs as his hot hand. He acknowledged both teams have had strong starts and momentum swings, often driven by penalties, and said he and opposing coach Joel are constantly making adjustments. Julien predicted the next game is unpredictable but expects it to be close, noting the team has been good at home and plans to bounce back without panic.

The Low-Frequency Sub-System (LFSS_B) combines peripherals clocked by a 32kHz LFCLK, including RTC_B and an Independent Watchdog Timer (IWDT). RTC_B provides timekeeping with counters, alarms, periodic interrupts, and calibration for crystal offset and temperature drift. IWDT_B generates a POR reset if not serviced within programmable periods (2ms to 2hr). WWDT supervises code execution with selectable timer periods.

The device includes general-purpose timers (TIMGx) and advanced timers (TIMAx), supporting various counter modes, prescalers, synchronization, and DMA/interrupt triggers. TIMAx adds complementary PWM output with dead-band insertion and fault handling.

A serial wire debug interface enables debug access. The bootstrap loader (BSL) supports UART or I2C programming, protected by a 256-bit password, and can be invoked via pin condition, blank device state, or runtime command.

Application guidelines recommend 10µF and 0.1µF decoupling capacitors near VDD/VSS, a 47kΩ pullup with 10nF pulldown on NRST, a 100kΩ resistor on ROSC for the SYSOSC frequency correction loop, a 0.47µF tank capacitor on VCORE, and pullup resistors for 5V-tolerant open-drain IOs. Development tools include LaunchPad kits, MSPM0 SDK, SysConfig, and IDEs such as Code Composer Studio, IAR, and Keil MDK. The revision history documents updates from November 2024 to April 2025.

The speaker, a hockey coach, discusses his team's recent win that kept their series alive. He emphasizes that skating better and becoming more involved improved their performance, though it was only one period of progress. He credits a player for scoring by stopping in front of the net rather than flying past, and notes that matchups against Madden have been effective because his team was more physical through skating.

He rejects the perception that New Jersey only plays defense, explaining his team tries to attack with four people in the rush. Ben Bishop states he feels better after a couple of days of recovery, making it easier to play. He reflects on his career, noting that with limited starting goalie positions in the NHL, it doesn't always work out with the drafting team. Researchers at the University of Michigan, led by associate professor Anish Tuteja, have developed an "omniphobic" coating capable of repelling nearly every known liquid. Inspired by Tuteja's desire to ease cleanup after his young child, the clear and durable coating can be applied to surfaces such as tables, floors, walls, and phone screens to prevent grime buildup. Published in ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces, the coating combines fluorinated polyurethane, a bonding agent, with a molecule called F-POSS, which rises to the surface to form the repellent layer. The team is now testing the coating for toxicity, as polyurethane-containing products have previously been linked to health concerns.

Paula Norrell sued Waste Away Group, Inc. under Title VII, alleging gender discrimination based on failure to promote and disparate impact employment practices. Norrell, hired in 1996 and promoted multiple times, was not selected in 2001 for the combined Montgomery-Opelika district sales manager position, which went to Terry White, a male candidate. Waste Away offered her a Temporary Construction Representative position, which she declined after maternity leave.

The court found Norrell established a prima facie case of discrimination, but Waste Away articulated a legitimate, non-discriminatory reason: White was more qualified, having previously held the same combined position and possessing outside sales experience. Norrell's pretext arguments—being asked to train White, allegedly discriminatory remarks by Malphrus, and a comment by Johnson—were rejected. The court found Malphrus was not a decisionmaker, his remarks were stray, and Johnson's isolated comment was unrelated to the employment decision. Norrell abandoned her disparate impact claim.

The court granted summary judgment for Waste Away on all claims, entered judgment for the defendant, and taxed costs against the plaintiff.

The Triangle Post Offense, developed by Tex Winter, is a defensive-recognition system rather than a set-play offense, built on principles, court spacing, and fundamentals. It consists of three components: an entry, a sideline triangle on one side, and a two-man game on the weakside.

Proper spacing (15-20 feet between players) spreads the defense, discourages double-teaming, and enables one-on-one post play, cuts, and drives. The offense uses multiple entries—including outside cut, inside cut, dribble clear, off guard cut, post pop, base screen, ball reversal, and dribble weave—making it difficult to disrupt.

The sideline triangle creates post split actions, post isolations, corner splits, and screen-and-roll options. The weakside two-game offers pass and dribble series with counters (drive, jumper, roll, cut opposite, lob) based on defender reads.

Automatic counters address defensive overplays such as post fronts (over-the-top pass, flop), wing sags (dribble penetration), post double-teams (weakside spot-ups), and reversal or back-door denials (back cuts, lob passes).

Success depends on execution, scouting opponents, recognizing defensive reads, and teaching through breakdown drills progressing from 2-on-2 to 5-on-5.

Bollinger Bands, developed by John Bollinger in the 1980s, are a technical indicator used to analyze asset volatility and potential trend changes. They consist of a central moving average with standard deviations plotted above and below it, where the upper band adds a multiple of the standard deviation and the lower band subtracts it.

Disadvantages include false signals, reduced effectiveness in range-bound markets, signal delays due to reliance on historical data, and sensitivity to time period settings. By default, they use a 20-period moving average, though settings can be adjusted.

In TradingView's Pine Script, Bollinger Bands can be built using the ta.sma() function for the moving average and ta.stdev() with a multiplier for the deviations. A breakout strategy focuses on capitalizing on band breaches. Testing on the H4 timeframe with adjusted parameters produced notable returns but significant drawdown. Overall effectiveness depends on the trading rules applied, and Bollinger Bands can serve in breakout, mean reversion, or squeeze strategies.

The speaker accepts the presidential oath as a sacred trust from the people, emphasizing that the government belongs to its citizens. The TPS7H500x-SP is a family of radiation-hardness-assured PWM controllers with a 0.613 V voltage reference (+0.7%/-1% accuracy) and configurable switching frequency from 100 kHz to 2 MHz. The family includes four devices: TPS7H5001-SP (dual output, current mode, optimized for Si and GaN DC-DC converters), TPS7H5002-SP (single output with configurable dead time and leading edge blank time), TPS7H5003-SP (single output with fixed 50 ns dead time and blank time), and TPS7H5004-SP (dual output for non-synchronous push-pull and full-bridge topologies).

The controllers operate with an input voltage of 4 V to 14 V and feature three switching frequency modes: internal oscillator, external synchronization, and primary-secondary. Key functions include soft-start, enable/UVLO, current sensing, hiccup-mode overcurrent protection, external fault protection, programmable slope compensation, and thermal shutdown at 175°C. Maximum duty cycle is configurable (50%, 75%, or 100%) depending on the device via the DCL pin.

The devices use fixed frequency peak current mode control and support topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. A design example for a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices is provided, along with layout guidelines emphasizing proper grounding, bypass capacitor placement, and noise isolation of feedback signals.

Jane Goodall, who died on October 1 at age 91, was known for studying chimpanzee behavior in Tanzania's Gombe National Park for nearly 30 years. Beyond observing living chimps, she assembled a unique collection of chimp skeletons, retrieving bodies shortly after death and cleaning the bones. Each skeleton was linked to a known individual's sex, age, weight and life history, allowing researchers to study how development shaped skeletal features—information unavailable to those studying ancient hominid fossils.

In a 1990 interview, Goodall spoke humbly about the implications of her collection, saying, "We just don't know." She explained her motivation simply: "When you're working in the field, you shouldn't waste anything."

The collection yielded notable findings, including the skeleton of Flo, a dominant matriarch who died in 1972. Flo's skeleton was larger than most at Gombe, yet she weighed less than a stockier male named Charlie, illustrating the difficulty of estimating body weight from bones. Her bone loss pattern differed from human osteoporosis, and her skeletal strength aligned with evidence she gave birth near age 50. As Goodall shifted to environmental activism and writing in later years, her skeletal collection continued contributing to science.

The author describes the second week of motherhood as the most difficult phase of new parenthood, surpassing other challenges like the first night home or a baby's first illness. Unlike the first week, which is buoyed by endorphins, visitors, and pain medication, the second week brings the full weight of sleep deprivation, which the author compares to torture and says intensifies every emotion and worry. Additional struggles included painful breastfeeding with raw, bloody nipples; babies failing to gain weight, which made her feel like a failure; loneliness after family left and visitors stopped coming; inability to interpret a crying baby experiencing a growth spurt; frequent fights with her husband due to emotional rawness; and a baby who wouldn't sleep and wanted constant feeding or holding. The author notes that conditions eventually improved and she came to enjoy the fourth trimester.

A follow-through day, developed by William J. O'Neil, is a market-timing concept used to identify a shift from a downtrend to a new uptrend. It occurs when a major index closes significantly higher than the previous day on greater volume, typically on Day 4 or later of a rally attempt.

The process begins with Rally Day 1, marked by a higher close or a "pink rally day." During Days 2 and 3, the index must not fall below Rally Day 1's low. From Day 4 onward, a follow-through day can occur, ideally between Days 4 and 7.

A backtest on the S&P 500 (using SPY) showed poor short-term results, as the market tends to be mean-reverting, making buying on strength less effective. Adding a filter like a 25-day RSI below 55 slightly improved results. O'Neil originally applied the concept to individual stocks, not indexes.

Early failure signs include weak follow-through or the index falling below previous lows. A complete failure occurs if the index makes a new low. Despite imperfections, no bull market since the early 1900s has begun without a follow-through day, making it useful for long-term investors, though less so for short-term traders.

The double top chart pattern is a bearish reversal formation consisting of two swing highs at approximately the same level, with a swing low between them forming a neckline. It typically appears at the end of an uptrend or prolonged pullback in a downtrend. The two peaks create a resistance level, while the neckline acts as support. A break below the neckline signals a potential downward reversal, prompting long position closures or short entries.

Traders estimate profit targets by measuring the pattern's height and projecting it downward from the neckline. Stop losses can be placed mid-pattern or above it.

Coding and backtesting this pattern is difficult. Research by Thomas Bulkowski in *The Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns* (2000), based on 500 stocks over 5 years, found only 39% of double top formations reach their target, compared to 68% for double bottoms. This difference is attributed to the stock market's upward bias from inflation and productivity gains, making shorting strategies generally challenging and profitable only during sharp market declines.

Enron Corp.'s stock fell to near seven-year lows on October 29, 2001, following Moody's Investors Service downgrading the company's senior unsecured long-term debt to Baa2 (two levels above junk) from Baa1, with further downgrades possible. A heat wave affecting the northeastern United States is expected to move westward after July 4th, reaching southern California by Friday, according to the National Weather Service. Amid the 2024 political cycle and lingering pandemic-related learning loss, education policy faces heightened political pressures. Despite polarization, cross-partisan education reforms are being enacted across states, offering a contrast to federal gridlock.

Analysis of successful state-level initiatives reveals five key factors that support cross-partisan progress:

1. **Easy communication and broad appeal**: Policies framed around widely shared values gain momentum. Examples include the science of reading movement, catalyzed by the *Sold a Story* podcast, which led 15 states to pass reading laws, and efforts to address teacher shortages through apprenticeship programs in 16 states.

2. **Responsiveness to local context**: Policies rooted in local needs gain traction. The Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact, addressing military spouse licensure issues, has 11 participating states. Career and technical education initiatives in Idaho and North Carolina also exemplify this.

3. **Political cover**: Policymakers need protection when taking risky positions. Virginia's history standards revision succeeded partly because a legal deadline forced board members to compromise, resulting in a 9-0 vote.

4. **Both sides claiming a win**: Teacher pay raises coupled with school choice in Arkansas, and civics education legislation in 43 states, allow differing political philosophies to claim victories.

5. **Media as an accelerant**: Credentialed journalism can drive policy change, as demonstrated by *Sold a Story* and parent empowerment movements post-COVID.

Additional considerations include understanding the political landscape, establishing shared problem definitions, gauging urgency, minimizing threats to frontline staff, and framing policies as expansive. Advocates should avoid mission creep, prioritize focus, and remain open to opposing viewpoints.

The paper concludes that meaningful cross-partisan education policy change is achievable through realistic expectations, inclusive framing, and strategic collaboration.

This systematic review and meta-analysis examined the seroprevalence of Chikungunya in Ethiopia, following PRISMA guidelines and registered with PROSPERO (CRD42023271579). Literature searches across Medline/PubMed, Science Direct/Scopus, Google Scholar, and Web of Science identified 40 articles published between 2016 and November 2023, with five meeting eligibility criteria. Included studies were predominantly cross-sectional (4/5) with one case-control, using ELISA (4/5) or RT-qPCR (1/5) diagnostic methods.

The pooled seroprevalence of Chikungunya was 12.35% (95%CI: -0.57, 0.81). The highest regional prevalence occurred in SNNPR (43.6%) and the lowest in Dire Dawa (~12%). At district level, Debub Ari had the highest rate (51.58%) and Lare the lowest (6.25%). Prevalence varied by occupation, with farmers most affected; by age, generally higher in adults aged 31–40; by education, higher among those with formal education; and inconsistently by sex across studies. Subgroup analysis showed significant heterogeneity (I²=97.72%, p=0.00), particularly among ELISA-based studies, while RT-qPCR studies showed no variability. Begg's and Egger's tests indicated no publication bias.

The review concluded that Chikungunya remains a public health concern in Ethiopia, with variation attributed to sample size, test type, location, demographics, and community practices. Limitations include the small number of included studies, predominance of cross-sectional designs, and absence of molecular studies identifying circulating viral strains. The authors recommend enhanced operational readiness, collaboration, and public awareness campaigns.

The Indianapolis Colts enter the 2018 NFL Draft with nine picks, including the No. 6 overall selection, as GM Chris Ballard continues his rebuild. Three top prospects stand out for the first-round pick: Bradley Chubb (NC State, EDGE), who could address the Colts' weak pass rush; Quenton Nelson (Notre Dame, IOL), considered one of the safest prospects and capable of protecting Andrew Luck while boosting the run game; and Saquon Barkley (Penn State, RB), potentially the most talented player in the class, though he may not be available at No. 6.

Sharded services distribute requests across replicas (shards), each handling only a subset of requests, with a root node routing traffic. Unlike replicated stateless services, sharded services are typically stateful and used when data exceeds what a single machine can serve. Sharding scales a service based on state size. Key design considerations include the need for sharding and the cache's architectural role. A sharded cache sits between user requests and frontend implementations, and can be distributed using an ambassador pattern.

The Piotroski F-Score strategy, developed by Stanford professor Joseph Piotroski, is a stock selection method that uses nine financial criteria related to profitability, liquidity, and efficiency to evaluate a company's fundamentals. Each criterion receives a score of 0 or 1, with totals of 8-9 indicating strong financials and 0-4 indicating weak financials. It is commonly used to identify undervalued value stocks but can also apply to growth stocks.

Several backtests support the strategy. Alpha Architect tested F-scores on large NYSE stocks (1974-2014), finding the Piotroski score returned 12.6% annually versus 11.2% for the S&P 500, with similar standard deviation. Applied to the cheapest 20% of stocks with scores above 6, annual returns rose to 15.2%. ValueSignals tested European stocks (1999-2011), and Alexander Eriksen studied Norwegian and Swedish stocks (1997-2011), comparing Piotroski, contrarian, and combined strategies.

Patrick McCaffery, a 6-foot-8 wing/forward and consensus four-star prospect, committed to play basketball for Iowa, coached by his father Fran McCaffery. Carton, Trace Jackson-Davis, and Tyrell Terry to join him. He is Iowa's first 2019 commit, with two slots remaining.
