Drug repurposing, identifying new therapeutic uses for existing drugs, is especially valuable for rare diseases where treatment options are limited and patient populations are small. Knowledge graphs, which represent biomedical entities and their relationships, are increasingly used for drug repurposing by integrating data from scientific literature and databases.

This study analyzed the Elsevier Biology Knowledge Graph (EBKG), built via proprietary AI NLP technology from both open access (OA) and controlled access (CA) publications, to compare their contributions to drug repurposing for rare diseases.

Key findings:
- OA and CA publications contribute roughly equally to knowledge graph relations, though CA yielded 1.5 times more NLP assertions.
- OA contributions grew significantly after 2006; now over 50% of rare disease-related relations are in OA.
- Rare diseases with more than 100 relations tend to have over 50% of relations in OA; no such bias was found for drug-target relations.
- Approximately 50% of all relations in EBKG are supported by a single reference, distributed equally between OA and CA.
- Citation rates and first-citation times are similar between OA and CA publications.
- CA journals had a higher article retraction rate (68.3%) than OA.
- Uncited relations are accumulating exponentially, primarily from original research articles lacking follow-up rather than from fraudulent research or high-throughput experiments.

The authors suggest developing additional confidence measures beyond reference counts, including epistemic discourse analysis, citation indices, and alignment scores. They propose training large language models on different literature subsets stratified by credibility to assist peer review and verify low-confidence findings.

The lecture covers upcoming course logistics, including a quiz scheduled for the following week that will be closed-book but allow one page of notes and a calculator, with statistics tables provided.

The main content reviews statistical process control concepts. Control charts function as running hypothesis tests, where alpha (false alarm probability) determines control limits and beta (missed alarm probability) depends on sample size. Average run length (ARL) is defined as the inverse of the relevant probability: ARL0 relates to false alarms under the null hypothesis, while ARL1 relates to detecting an actual shift. Increasing sample size tightens the sampling distribution, narrowing control limits while maintaining alpha, and reducing beta.

The lecture distinguishes control limits (based on statistical false alarm rates) from specification limits (based on design requirements), noting these are often incorrectly conflated. Process capability is introduced through CP (ratio of spec limit range to six sigma) and CPK (which also accounts for mean offset from target). Higher CP/CPK values reduce nonconforming parts: CPK of 1 yields about 3 per 1,000, while CPK of 2 yields approximately one per billion, providing robustness against small mean shifts. Quality loss functions, typically quadratic, penalize deviations from target and encourage both centering and variance reduction.

When alarms occur, operators should first verify measurements, then review historical data for trends, and investigate process changes. Multivariate situations require adjusted control limits to prevent excessive false alarms across many charts.

The lecture concludes by introducing alternative control charts for sample size of one, including running/moving averages, and previews upcoming topics: exponentially weighted moving average and cumulative sum charts designed to detect small shifts more rapidly.

The PGA848 is a monolithic, high-voltage, high-bandwidth, precision programmable gain instrumentation amplifier with single-ended output, combining a current-feedback input stage with a matched gain resistor network and differential amplifier output stage. It offers eight binary-gain settings (0.5V/V to 100V/V) via three digital pins (A0, A1, A2), targeting factory automation, data acquisition, and semiconductor test applications. Its linear input range extends within 3V of either supply.

In a typical application, the PGA848 drives the ADS8860 16-bit, 1MSPS SAR ADC, using ±15V input supplies and a 5.3V output supply to prevent ADC overload. The REF6250 provides the 5V ADC reference, while an OPA192 buffer drives the PGA848 REF pin at mid-scale (2.5V). Three filters manage EMI/RFI, bandwidth (nominal 318kHz f–3dB), and ADC charge kickback.

Supply voltages above 40V cause permanent damage. Recommended layout practices include symmetrical input paths, 0.1µF bypass capacitors near supply pins, minimizing leakage on DA_IN pins, separating input from supply/output traces, and minimizing thermal junctions. TINA-TI and PSpice simulation tools are available for design verification.

Tungsten (W) is a leading candidate for plasma-facing material in fusion reactors due to its high melting point and favourable thermal properties, but it readily oxidises above 500°C, raising concerns for accident, maintenance, and detritiation scenarios. This study examines W oxidation behaviour across 400–1050°C and WO3 sublimation in synthetic air, addressing gaps regarding long-duration spalling behaviour and oxide microstructure.

Using thermogravimetric analysis, differential scanning calorimetry, XRD, Raman spectroscopy, SEM, and EBSD, the authors measured oxidation kinetics and characterised the oxide scale. Oxidation showed a transition from parabolic to linear kinetics, with activation energies of 180.4 kJ/mol and 117.5 kJ/mol, respectively. WO3 sublimation had an activation energy of 335.8 kJ/mol. Preferential oxidation occurred at specimen edges, increasing with higher perimeter-to-area ratios, and edge oxides spalled easily during handling.

Raman mapping identified three oxide layers: a thin inner WO2 layer (30–50 nm), a middle WO2.72 layer (10–20 µm), and an outer WO2.9/WO3 layer. Cracks and voids formed above 600°C, attributed to volume expansion (Pilling-Bedworth ratios 2–3.4), thermal expansion mismatch, and grain-orientation-dependent oxidation rates. The WO2 layer's presence may explain the low detritiation efficiency previously reported for JET W tiles.

Matroid theory abstracts linear independence to connect algebraic, geometric, and topological methods. This survey examines algebraic invariants (Orlik–Solomon algebra, holonomy Lie algebra, holonomy Chen Lie algebra), algebro-geometric invariants (resonance varieties, Koszul modules), and combinatorial structures (multinets), focusing on their interplay and dependence on the matroid versus its realization.

Section 2 introduces matroids, which generalize linear independence via a ground set and independent sets satisfying an exchange axiom, with structure captured by the lattice of flats. Key examples include uniform and graphic matroids. Multinets are partitions of a matroid's ground set with multiplicity functions satisfying specific conditions on base locus flats. Special cases include reduced multinets and k-nets. For realizable matroids, a Riemann–Hurwitz type inequality holds, though its validity for non-realizable matroids remains open. Realizable 3-nets correspond to Latin squares and can encode finite groups; questions remain about whether all 3-nets in CP² are algebraic.

Section 3 introduces the Orlik–Solomon algebra A(M), defined as a quotient of an exterior algebra by an ideal generated by circuit relations. This graded algebra's Betti numbers depend only on the lattice of flats, and it decomposes tensorially under direct sums of matroids. The algebra is quadratic with a Gröbner basis precisely when M is supersolvable.

Researchers at Albert Einstein College of Medicine, publishing in PLOS Biology, report that intense exercise may temporarily suppress appetite through heat-sensitive neurons in the brain's hypothalamus. Senior author Young-Hwan Jo investigated whether proopiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons in the arcuate nucleus (ARC) respond to exercise-induced warming.

The team found that about two-thirds of ARC POMC neurons in mice possess receptors similar to TRPV1, which detect heat and capsaicin. Infusing capsaicin into the ARC reduced food intake for 12 hours, an effect eliminated by blocking or silencing the TRPV1-like receptors. Forty minutes of treadmill exercise raised body and ARC temperatures and cut food intake by roughly 50 percent, but had no effect on mice lacking these receptors.

Jo suggests body temperature can act as a biological signal regulating feeding behavior, potentially informing new appetite-suppression approaches.

**Managing Hull:** The coach describes a compromise with Hull, allowing creative freedom with the puck but requiring physical, structured play without it. He compares this to his past relationship with Rob Brown, emphasizing differentiating personality from performance.

**Keane:** Given the option to skate only once due to heavy minutes and his smaller size.

**Scoring Plays:** Nieuwendyk, Fleury, and Sakic are cited as rare players who remain composed in tight scoring situations.

**Mental Preparation:** The team feels it did not sacrifice enough in a prior overtime loss in Colorado and wants to commit more fully, including blocking shots.

**Containing Peca:** Viewed as a dangerous offensive and physical player who must be kept away from their net.

Intel is reportedly in early talks with AMD to manufacture chips through its foundry business, according to Semafor. Intel shares rose 7% on the news, while AMD shares gained over 1%. Securing AMD as a customer would be significant for Intel's foundry, which is seeking major clients, and would indicate AMD's confidence in using its competitor for manufacturing. The extent of potential manufacturing is unclear. Intel has recently added several notable investors as it attempts a turnaround under CEO Lip-Bu Tan, with shares up nearly 77% in 2025. Intel declined to comment, and AMD said it does not comment on rumors.

Saudi Arabia announced the selection of international oil companies for three major natural gas projects requiring approximately $25 billion in investment, marking the first significant reopening of its energy sector to foreign investors since nationalization in the 1970s.

Exxon Mobil, Royal Dutch/Shell, BP and Phillips Petroleum were chosen for Core Venture 1 (South Ghawar), estimated at $15 billion, with no leader yet announced. Exxon Mobil will lead Core Venture 2 (Red Sea project), with Enron and Occidental Petroleum holding stakes. Shell, TotalFinaElf and Conoco were selected for Core Venture 3 (Shaybah), with no leader named. Leaders for ventures 1 and 3 are expected to be announced by June 5, along with the signing of memoranda of understanding. Chevron, ENI and Marathon were dropped from participant lists.

Separately, a Dow Jones column reported that California's long-term power contracts, totaling $43 billion signed in March, have declined in value by approximately 15% ($6.5 billion) as forward power prices in the western U.S. have fallen. Electric usage in the state is down 9% from projected levels due to conservation and economic slowing. Enron was described as having sold aggressively for two months.

An options report noted that Enron's June options were active, with an institutional investor buying over 5,000 June 55 call contracts and selling a similar number of June 50 puts, suggesting a bullish outlook. Enron stock rose $2.02 to $54.24.

The U.S. Energy Department welcomed the Saudi awards, stating they align with the Bush administration's energy plan supporting foreign investment in Middle Eastern energy sectors.

Steven Kean writes to James Hughes regarding Enron's role in the Export-Import Bank lobbying campaign, suggesting the company's involvement is smaller than a Wall Street Journal article indicates. Kean notes that headcount and expenditures for related efforts were reduced in the 2001 budget, and John Hardy has joined Linda Robertson's DC office organization. Kean believes Hardy still has substantial project finance work related to existing projects, pursued projects, and asset sale transfers.

The forwarded message from John Hardy clarifies that Enron is not leading the battle with OMB but needs to show support for Ex-Im and OPIC programs, as Enron is negotiating with both agencies on Electrobolt and needs their support on problem projects. Rebecca McDonald serves on Ex-Im's private sector advisory committee.

The attached news compilation includes Wall Street Journal coverage of major U.S. exporters—including Boeing, Caterpillar, Enron, and Halliburton—launching a lobbying campaign to oppose the White House's proposed 25% cut to the Ex-Im Bank's $865 million operating budget. Enron received $135 million in Ex-Im financing in fiscal year 2000. Additional articles cover Dutch gas market competition involving Enron Europe, Southern California Edison's financial troubles and lawsuits from suppliers including Enron Wind, doubts about SEC approval of Sierra Pacific's acquisition of Enron's Portland General Electric, unfinalized California power contracts involving Enron and other suppliers, and U.S. natural gas price movements.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on July 18, 2019, reporting that it had issued a press release announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2019. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration; Chief Accounting Officer. Microsoft's securities registered under Section 12(b) include its common stock (MSFT) on NASDAQ and three notes listed on the New York Stock Exchange.

The Stack Offense compacts players into two stack alignments just outside the free throw line, allowing ballhandlers to maneuver sideline to sideline while reducing turnovers by limiting ball possession to three handlers. Two post players serve as stationary screeners. When the ballhandler dribbles to a wing, the same-side ballhandler pops out off the post screen for a pass.

Key options include:
- **Basket Roll**: If defenders overplay the pop-out or show to disrupt passes, the popping player or post rolls to the basket.
- **Dribble Penetration**: If defenders fail to protect the basket, the ballhandler drives hard; if post defenders sag, the post rolls for a drop pass.
- **Back Cut**: If passing lanes are denied, the receiver back cuts while the post may set a back screen or step out as a pressure release.

Players should back cut against overplays rather than fight pressure, and ballhandlers must avoid offensive fouls when driving.

This cross-sectional study used a "secret shopper" methodology to assess the accessibility of electronically prescribed, nameless Expedited Partner Therapy (EPT) at 335 retail pharmacies in New York City. Trained pseudopatients called pharmacies using a standardized script, inquiring whether an EPT prescription for chlamydia could be filled under the profile "Expedited Partner." Researchers also examined whether accessibility varied by neighborhood socioeconomic vulnerability using the CDC's Social Vulnerability Index (SVI).

Only 40% of pharmacists were aware of EPT, and 30% were willing to dispense nameless prescriptions. Awareness was significantly higher at national chain pharmacies (aOR 2.58) than at non-chain pharmacies. Contrary to the researchers' hypothesis, higher socioeconomic vulnerability was associated with greater EPT awareness but not with willingness to dispense. Only 46% of dispensed prescriptions adhered to New York State guidelines. The most common reasons for refusal were unfamiliarity with EPT (62%) and the belief that a patient name was legally required (28%). Neighborhood chlamydia incidence was not significantly associated with awareness or willingness.

The authors conclude that pharmacy-level barriers—limited awareness, low willingness to dispense nameless prescriptions, and poor guideline adherence—hinder EPT implementation. They recommend targeted pharmacist education, policy interventions, and improved electronic prescribing systems. Study limitations include the hypothetical nature of the prescriptions, potential interaction variability, and focus on a single metropolitan area.

The principal of Horace Maynard Middle School in Union County, Greg Clay, said he was unaware of repeated bullying against sixth-grader Keaton Jones and stated the incident described in a viral video had been resolved weeks ago, with action taken against the other children involved. The video, posted on Facebook by Keaton's mother Kimberly Jones, showed him describing having milk poured on him and ham put in his clothes at lunch. It gained widespread attention from celebrities and athletes using #StandWithKeaton. The school planned an anti-bullying assembly and had already scheduled a related talk for January. Other parents acknowledged occasional bullying but did not consider it worse than at other schools.

The passage describes a Machine Learning Model Swapping (MLMS) system designed to address limitations in conventional machine learning model design and Neural Architecture Search (NAS) techniques, which are time-consuming, resource-intensive, and often not optimized for diverse hardware platforms.

The MLMS system selects and interchanges ML models (subnets) in an energy and communication-efficient manner while adapting to real-time changes in hardware constraints. It uses a similarity-based subnet selection process, choosing replacement models with maximum pre-trained parameter overlap from the currently deployed model to minimize memory write overhead.

Key components include an MLMS engine (with an interface and subnet selector), an ML model adaptation decision maker, and a performance auditor. Users provide an ML configuration including a reference supernet, application quality metrics, system constraints, and performance auditor settings. The supernet contains smaller subnets optimized for different operational conditions.

The performance auditor monitors inference results, quality metrics, and context information including mode of operation, system state, physical environment, and networking environment. When status changes occur, it triggers the subnet selector to find replacement subnets using NAS algorithms.

The subnet search and swap algorithm operates in two stages: discovering candidate subnets meeting performance and constraint criteria, then selecting the optimal replacement with minimum data transfer cost.

Use cases include autonomous vehicles, IoT devices, remote sensor arrays, drones with limited battery, and edge computing nodes. The system is hardware-agnostic and supports various AI/ML applications including image recognition, segmentation, and language translation.

Globalization, though often ill-defined, represents an interconnected global society requiring cooperation to address shared challenges in health, environment, economics, and security. International organizations such as the UN, WHO, and WTO facilitate this cross-cultural collaboration, with English serving as the primary tool for international communication.

This study argues that English curricula, particularly in Taiwan, should incorporate global issues to prepare university students for participation in the international community. Suggested topics include HIV/AIDS, global warming, and war, tailored to students' academic disciplines. Pedagogies include online resources, films, discussions, and cross-cultural interaction.

Research was conducted with 372 non-English major students across three Taiwanese universities over 18 weeks, covering topics such as global warming, cultural festivals, food, technology, sports, animals, energy, and environmental protection. Data was gathered through surveys, Facebook discussions, and classroom activities.

Results indicated strong student support: 95% affirmed the importance of globalization education, 96% said it motivated English learning, and 87% found it interesting. Students identified global warming, energy, and environmental protection as top priorities and suggested additional topics like international trade, welfare systems, and human rights. Travel, films, music, guest speakers, and news readings were recommended as effective teaching methods.

The study concludes that integrating global issues into English education equips students with knowledge, confidence, and cultural awareness necessary to function as competitive, cooperative global citizens in the third millennium.

Skinimalism is a skincare trend focused on simplifying routines to a few high-quality, multitasking products rather than layering numerous items. According to Dr Hazel Parkinson, this approach protects the skin barrier, reduces irritation, and benefits those with sensitive or ageing skin. Benefits extend to mental wellbeing, sustainability, and cost savings.

While most people can adopt skinimalism, those with conditions like acne, eczema, rosacea, hyperpigmentation, or menopausal skin may still require targeted actives such as retinoids, azelaic acid, or niacinamide, used alongside gentle cleansers, moisturisers, and SPF. Parkinson recommends tailoring routines to individual skin needs, age, and lifestyle, and transitioning gradually by removing one or two products at a time over 2–4 weeks. Consulting a professional is advised when uncertain.

This case study examined smartphone touchscreen interactions in a man in his late twenties with refractory right temporal lobe epilepsy to assess the effects of anti-seizure medication (ASM) changes and seizures on day-to-day behaviour. Over 185 days, 718,357 touchscreen interactions were recorded via the TapCounter app, alongside a seizure diary and a five-day video-EEG monitoring admission during which ASMs (lamotrigine and perampanel) were withdrawn.

Joint-interval distributions (JIDs) of inter-touch intervals were calculated and compared across pre-tapering, tapering, and post-tapering periods using cluster-based permutation testing. ASM tapering was associated with faster next-interval dynamics, which reversed upon medication reinstatement. Conversely, the day of a focal to bilateral tonic-clonic convulsion showed slower next-interval dynamics compared to the three preceding days, likely reflecting post-ictal effects.

The authors suggest smartphone-based monitoring may objectively track medication- and seizure-related behavioural fluctuations, potentially explaining accelerated behavioural ageing observed in epilepsy. They note limitations including the single-case design and acknowledge that cohort studies are needed to confirm generalisability.

Market Basket, a New England supermarket chain founded in 1917 by Greek immigrant Athanasios Demoulas, became the center of a significant corporate conflict in 2014. The chain, led by CEO Arthur T. Demoulas since 2008, operated 71 stores with 25,000 non-unionized employees and generated $4.6 billion in revenue by 2014.

The company's business model emphasized low prices, high sales volume, employee loyalty, and customer service. Market Basket paid above-industry wages, contributed 15-20% of annual pay to a profit-sharing plan, promoted from within, and maintained low turnover. It operated with a lean management structure and had strong relationships with suppliers, many of whom were long-term partners.

A longstanding family feud between Arthur T. and his cousin Arthur S. Demoulas culminated in June 2014 when the board, controlled by Arthur S., fired Arthur T. along with other senior executives. This triggered an unprecedented six-week protest by employees, vendors, and customers demanding his reinstatement. Warehouse workers, drivers, and office staff walked out, essentially shutting down operations, while store employees and customers boycotted the chain. Sales dropped over 90%.

On August 27, 2014, an agreement was reached for Arthur T. to purchase the 50.5% stake held by Arthur S.'s family for $1.6 billion, financed through mortgage loans and syndicated debt. Arthur T. was reinstated with full operational authority, and employees returned to work. However, the acquisition left the company with substantial debt, raising questions about whether Market Basket could maintain its low prices, generous employee benefits, and growth trajectory.

The 2022 NFL draft featured a record 6 wide receivers selected in the first 20 picks, reflecting the position's growing importance as offenses become more pass-oriented. Wide receivers complete the passing game by running precise routes, creating separation, and catching passes, requiring high football IQ and toughness. Their secondary role is run blocking, which helps extend runs into longer gains. The name derives from their alignment "wide" near the sideline and their role of "receiving" passes. Key skills include route-running, speed, strong hands, and agility, with body types varying from tall and strong to small and elusive. Notable all-time greats include Jerry Rice, Randy Moss, and Steve Largent. Elite wide receivers force defenses to adjust their alignments, giving offenses strategic advantages.

PerovSegNet is a lightweight deep learning segmentation framework based on YOLOv8-seg, designed for SEM image analysis of perovskite and lead iodide films in solar cell research. It introduces two novel modules: the Adaptive Split-Dilated Convolution with Shuffle Block (ASDCB) for multi-scale feature fusion, and the Separable Adaptive Downsampling (SAD) module for capturing both fine-scale textures and large-scale structures. To address annotated data scarcity, the authors constructed the PerovData dataset containing 10,994 images augmented from 40 manually labeled samples, with UMAP analysis confirming class separability.

Ablation experiments showed the combined modules achieved 87.25% mAP@0.5 and 79.96% mAP@0.5:0.95, while reducing parameters and GFLOPs by 24% and 25% compared to the baseline. Defect segmentation accuracy notably improved from 33% to 64%. PerovSegNet outperformed baselines including Mask R-CNN variants and Cascade InternImage-XL, producing sharper boundaries and fewer missed detections across varying SEM magnifications.

Beyond segmentation, the framework extracts quantitative descriptors (area, count, shape complexity) linked to photovoltaic performance. Correlation analysis across ~25 peer-reviewed studies revealed perovskite area strongly correlates with PCE (r=0.78), lead iodide area shows mild positive correlation (r=0.23), and defect metrics correlate negatively (r=-0.27 to -0.32). Limitations include observational (non-causal) correlations, sensitivity to imaging conditions, and the need for further inference acceleration for in situ applications.

A University of Connecticut study suggests that vaping nicotine-based e-cigarette liquids may cause DNA damage comparable to smoking unfiltered tobacco cigarettes, potentially leading to cancer-causing cellular mutations. Researchers used a 3D-printed electro-optical screening device, costing under a dollar, which mimicked a lung using human metabolic enzymes and DNA. Samples taken at 20, 60, and 100 puffs showed DNA damage increased with the number of puffs and depended on vapor quantity and additives. Researcher Karteek Kadimisetty expressed surprise at the findings, published in ACS Sensors, and noted plans to explore further 3D-printed platforms for toxicity screening.

This article explains how to backtest a momentum trading strategy in Python. Momentum is an investing factor that benefits from ongoing trends—rising stocks have positive momentum, while falling stocks have negative momentum.

The backtest uses select sector SPDR ETFs, with historical data downloaded via the yfinance library, alongside pandas, numpy, and matplotlib. Adjusted close prices are resampled monthly to capture dividends and calculate percentage changes.

Momentum is defined as the rolling 9-month performance, calculated using a custom `get_rolling_ret()` function. Two additional functions, `get_top()` and `portfolio_ret()`, identify the top 3 ETFs by 9-month performance each month and compute returns for an equally-weighted portfolio, rebalanced monthly.

Results are plotted against the SPY for comparison. The strategy achieved a 9.89% CAGR versus the SPY's 9.46% CAGR, indicating minimal alpha. The strategy can be customized with different ETFs or assets.

The Evening Star is a bearish reversal candlestick pattern formed by three candles: a tall bullish candle, a small candle gapping above the first, and a bearish candle closing below the midpoint of the first. Traders use this pattern to identify potential price reversals and profit from downtrends.

Reliability increases when the gap between the first and second candles is significant and when the bearish third candle is longer than the first. The pattern is more dependable when it forms near a downward trendline or resistance level.

Traders often confirm the pattern with additional technical tools such as trendlines, resistance levels, RSI, stochastic oscillators, and Bollinger Bands before entering short positions. Exit methods include profit targets, technical signals, and stop-loss orders.

The strategy's success depends on accurate pattern identification, confirmation, and solid risk management. Timeframes vary based on trading style and risk tolerance, and the strategy can be adapted to different market conditions. Risks include false signals, volatility, over-reliance on technical analysis, and insufficient diversification. Backtesting the pattern requires defined rules and settings.

A 92-year-old Arizona woman, Anna Mae Blessing, has been charged with first-degree murder, aggravated assault, and kidnapping after allegedly shooting her 72-year-old son at their Fountain Hills home, according to the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office. Authorities said Blessing concealed two pistols in her robe and shot her son in his bedroom because he wanted to place her in an assisted living facility. His girlfriend, who was present, struggled with Blessing and disarmed her of both weapons. Blessing reportedly told deputies, "You took my life, so I'm taking yours." She had moved in with the couple approximately six months prior.

US public education has historically adopted business models, from Horace Mann's factory-oriented framing to bureaucratic structures categorizing students by age, grade, and IQ. Reports like *A Nation at Risk* (1983) and *A Nation Prepared* (1986) led to teacher professionalization efforts, though these failed to improve teacher pay, security, or student test scores. The No Child Left Behind Act (2001) introduced competition, standardized testing, and accountability measures, with failing schools facing interventions including conversion to charter schools. However, research shows charter schools have produced mixed results, increased segregation, and no broad academic gains.

The "medical model" of education, rooted in eugenicist thinking, diagnoses students as having inherent deficits, reinforcing fixed mindsets, stigma, and stereotype threat that impair learning. An alternative approach reframes education as problem-solving, engaging students in self-discovery rather than labeling them.

Problem-solving is presented as a universal cognitive process underlying perception, learning, and scientific inquiry. Research including Levin's scale-free cognition, Deutsch's theory of explanation, and the child scientist theory suggests humans naturally develop theories, test them, and refine understanding through environmental interaction. Cognitive heuristics and metacognition develop through interaction and reflection, paralleling the teacher-student relationship and scientific peer review.

Declining student performance is attributed to reduced metacognitive support from parents, mentors, and tutors, compounded by technology-driven disengagement. The author proposes restructuring education around problem-solving at student, teacher, and administrative levels, promoting self-directed learning, one-to-one mentoring, and assessment measured against individual progress rather than norms—replacing the business-modeled, commoditized system with one supporting lifelong learner development.

Minister Richard Bruton announced that 12 Autism Units will be built across Sligo, Leitrim, and Donegal during the 2018/19 school term, comprising five Primary and seven Post-Primary ASD classes. In Leitrim, ASD special classes have grown from two in 2011 to five, located in schools including St Patrick's NS and Mohill Community College. Responding to Deputy Marc MacSharry, Bruton noted that nationally since 2011, SNA numbers have risen by 3,545, resource teachers by 3,660, and special classes by 712. A professional report is required for placement in a special class, and selection processes must be non-discriminatory where demand exceeds places. The NCSE advises parents to apply in writing early.

Hartman argues that INF deployment, originally initiated by Europeans like Chancellor Schmidt to address regional imbalances and prevent "decoupling," has become divisive and unlikely to succeed given European sentiment. He recommends trading deployment for a Soviet arms control agreement. The author disagrees, arguing the INF decision has become a test of NATO's viability, and non-deployment would embolden anti-American forces in Europe. The author reads European support as stronger than Hartman suggests, citing Mitterrand and Italian positions. The recommendation is to maintain the zero-zero option, deploy as scheduled if Soviets don't shift position, and only consider alternatives if Soviets seriously restructure their stance.

In a separate memorandum, Secretary Shultz and Soviet Ambassador Dobrynin met for lunch with aides, agreeing to meet regularly on arms control, regional, and bilateral issues. They discussed a possible Foreign Ministers' meeting before the next UNGA and agreed a U.S.-Soviet summit should produce concrete results. Dobrynin emphasized that the Shultz-Gromyko channel was necessary to resolve major arms control problems beyond negotiators' flexibility.

The passage discusses legal precedents for calculating damages when vessels are unjustifiably detained or damaged. In the Costa Rica Packet case, losses to owners, officers, and crew from precautionary detention were recognized, establishing that loss of catch may be considered when assessing damages to a whaling vessel.

In the Potomac case, Justice Gray of the U.S. Supreme Court held that owners of an injured vessel are entitled to recover for loss of use during repairs, measured by market price or, absent one, by evidence of lost profits.

In Williamson v. Barrett, Justice Nelson affirmed that damages should indemnify the injured party for losses, including repair costs and loss of the vessel's service during repairs. Citing the English case of the Gazelle (1844), the court noted damages should reflect the vessel's earning capacity during detention.

This rule was applied to whaling ships James Maury, General Pike, Mile, and Nile, captured by the Confederate cruiser Shenandoah, by the Court of Commissioners of Alabama Claims.

This study investigates chemical etching (polishing) of Cd1-xZnxTe1-ySey (CZTS) quaternary semiconductor crystals using a 5% bromine-methanol solution. Samples with fixed zinc content (x ≈ 0.1) and varying selenium concentrations (y = 0, 0.02, 0.06, 0.1) were cut, mechanically polished, and then chemically etched at +19°C in stages totaling 8 minutes, with geometric dimensions measured between stages to determine etching trajectories and rates.

A thermodynamic model was developed predicting that the CZTS etching rate should be lower than that of CZT, proportional to the excess Gibbs energy of solid solution formation. Experimentally, average etching rates decreased from 24 μm/min (CZT) to 18, 15, and 13 μm/min for CZTS2, CZTS6, and CZTS10 respectively. Even a small selenium addition (y ≈ 0.02) produced an approximately 24% reduction in etching rate, closely matching the theoretical prediction (~22%). At higher selenium concentrations, differences between etching rates gradually diminished.

The authors interpret the reduced etching rate as direct evidence of crystal lattice hardening caused by selenium incorporation, contrasting with zinc, which weakens the structure. Etching uniformity was affected by surface roughness, damaged layer depth, temperature, and solution stirring (which increased rates 1.5–2 times). The findings are relevant for optimizing processing of CZTS-based radiation detector elements.

Vanuatu's Reserve Bank may be investigating AFIC, a savings and loan scheme managed by Barnabas Tabi that promises 50% interest. Despite claims of 25,000 fully vested depositors, three of four commercial banks deny doing business with AFIC. Meanwhile, the Ambae volcano's alert has been lowered from level 4 to 3, with activity confined to Lake Voui. The Ambae Port Vila Disaster Committee has collected essentials for evacuees. New teacher salary scales will take effect from 2018, and 21 retired teachers received medals from President Moses Tallis for 35 years of service.

Crystal Palace will host Newcastle United at Selhurst Park, with neither Rafael Benítez nor Roy Hodgson satisfied with their transfer window dealings. Islam Slimani may feature for Newcastle, while Hodgson faces the loss of Bakary Sako to a broken ankle, his sixth long-term absentee, potentially forcing him to rely on three young new signings. Last year, Sunderland won 4-0 at the same venue, a result Newcastle hope to replicate.

The second edition of The New Zealand Land and Food Annual, edited by Massey University AgriFood Director Professor Claire Massey and published by Massey University Press, was launched at the National Field Days in Mystery Creek. The book compiles views from 31 contributors on how New Zealand can address sustainability challenges in food production. Professor Massey notes all food production impacts the planet, and addressing this is a shared responsibility. The land and food sector contributes $33 billion to New Zealand's economy, with aims to treble this by 2025. Contributor Professor Ralph Sims states current agri-food practices are unsustainable and New Zealand could, but does not currently, lead by example.

Small-body reservoirs in planetary systems are remnant populations orbiting stars after gas disc dispersal, and serve as sources of exocomets. In the Solar System, these reservoirs span from near-Sun asteroids to the Oort cloud, with trans-Neptunian populations being the most massive and numerous, exhibiting icy compositions with various volatiles.

Stars form in dense molecular clouds, evolving through classes 0–III, with protoplanetary discs serving as sites of planet formation. The stellar cluster environment can affect discs via flybys and photo-evaporation, influencing planetesimal formation. Disc composition is controlled by thermal conditions and snowlines, whose locations depend on stellar luminosity.

Exocomets require both a source reservoir and massive perturbing bodies. While exocomets are predominantly detected around A-type stars due to observational biases, planet formation occurs around stars of varied masses. Debris discs, found around ~20% of nearby AFGK stars, are likely primary exocomet sources.

Planetesimal formation proceeds from micron-sized dust to ~100 km bodies, though bouncing and fragmentation barriers inhibit simple collisional growth. The streaming instability, combined with particle trapping in vortices and pressure bumps, enables gravitational collapse of pebble clouds into planetesimals. Evidence from Solar System bodies, including Arrokoth's bi-lobed structure and TNO binary fractions, supports this formation pathway.

Protoplanetary disc lifetimes depend on stellar mass, ranging from 1–4 Myr for A-type stars to 5–10 Myr for M/K-type stars. After dispersal, debris discs remain, with masses potentially reaching 0.3–300 Earth masses, depleting over time through collisional grinding.

Solar System observations, including sample returns and missions like Rosetta, constrain planetesimal formation and composition. The Oort cloud, source of long-period comets, may have formed during Solar System formation or been modified by the Sun's birth cluster environment. Exo-Oort clouds are theoretically possible but observationally unconfirmed.

Open questions include the role of stellar environment, the dominant exocomet source reservoir, debris disc masses and formation locations, and Oort cloud structure, which future facilities like LSST, JWST, and ELT may address.

This Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) for trial ZEA-DNK-02170 outlines analyses for plasma concentration, plasma glucose, pharmacokinetic (PK), pharmacodynamic (PD), and safety data by treatment group.

PK/PD analyses include summary statistics, change from pre-dose, and mean/individual concentration-versus-time plots (original and log scale) for dasiglucagon and GlucaGen; placebo samples are not analyzed. Plasma glucose is measured at specified timepoints after dosing, with AUE0-30min calculated using SAS.

Safety analyses (based on the safety set) cover insulin administration, hypoglycemia induction, trial medication, rescue glucose infusion, local tolerability, adverse events (AEs), laboratory parameters, vital signs, ECG, and immunogenicity. AE summaries focus on treatment-emergent AEs (TEAEs), coded using MedDRA v21.0+, with categories including AESIs, injection site reactions, drug-related TEAEs, SAEs, and deaths. Causality is classified on a 0–3 scale, with missing values set to related. Severity is graded mild/moderate/severe.

ECG analyses include QTcF thresholds (>450, >480, >500 ms) and change-from-baseline categories (>30, >60 ms). ADA incidence covers treatment-induced and treatment-boosted patients.

Changes from the protocol include rewording of the primary efficacy analysis and terminology updates for secondary variables. Appendices detail programming standards, QC requirements, and the list of tables, figures, and listings following ICH E3 guidelines.

The State Department clarifies that passports may be issued to applicants who do not state an intent to return to the U.S. within two years, though passports remain valid for only two years, renewable upon new application.

Regarding Article 19 of Instructions to Diplomatic Officers, "the secretary" refers to the actual first secretary, who assumes charge as chargé d'affaires ad interim in the head of mission's absence. Leaves of absence should be arranged so the secretary is present when the head is away. If a second or third secretary must take temporary charge, the Department must be consulted first.

An Executive order dated April 25, 1902, prohibits diplomatic and consular officers from publicly attacking, preferring charges against, or criticizing other officers in either service, except through confidential communication to the Department of State.

Sixteen Miami Valley seniors participated in seminary graduation exercises on May 20 at The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Huber Heights, receiving certificates for completing a course on the Book of Mormon. Over 100 attended. Mark Skouson of the Dayton Ohio East Stake presidency addressed students, and graduates Stephanie Tullis, Mark Hastriter, and Hannah Campbell spoke about their experiences. The four-year seminary program, taught this year by 11 volunteers, covers the Old Testament, New Testament, Book of Mormon, and Church History, and is open to all high school students.

The passage details design considerations for a push-pull converter using the TPS7H500x-SP controllers.

Leading edge blank time was initially set to ~50 ns using a 49.9 kΩ RLEB resistor, though optimization may be needed based on PCB parasitics and gate driver propagation delay. A 33 nF soft-start capacitor yields a ~7.5 ms soft-start time.

For the transformer, a 35% maximum duty cycle was targeted to provide margin below the 50% controller limit, resulting in a turns ratio of 2.5. Magnetizing current was set at 6% of output current, with primary inductance calculated as 33 μH but implemented as 40 μH.

Primary-side GaN FETs were rated at 170 V (for 36 V max input), while synchronous rectifier FETs were rated at 80 V. A Schottky diode in parallel with the SR FETs reduces soft-start current and reverse conduction losses. An RCD clamp circuit limits switch node voltage.

This study investigates ultrafast magnetization fluctuations in the canted antiferromagnet Sm0.7Er0.3FeO3 using femtosecond noise correlation spectroscopy (FemNoC). By varying temperature across the spin reorientation transition (SRT) and applying external magnetic fields, the authors examine how spin fluctuations relate to the free energy landscape and quasi-ferromagnetic (qF) magnon properties.

The experimental setup employs two femtosecond laser pulse trains with different wavelengths, measuring polarization rotations via the Faraday effect to detect out-of-plane magnetization fluctuations. Results are compared with atomistic spin model simulations using the stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation and phenomenological Monte Carlo simulations.

Key findings show that picosecond-scale spin fluctuations are governed by the free energy potential, with fluctuations amplified where the energy landscape softens. Near the lower critical SRT temperature, qF magnon variance increases sharply while its resonance frequency softens, accompanied by random telegraph noise. External magnetic fields suppress these fluctuations and increase the qF magnon frequency by stiffening the potential. These trends are confirmed by both simulation methods.

The authors conclude that FemNoC enables direct characterization of magnetization potentials and demonstrates tunable ultrafast spin fluctuations, relevant for developing high-frequency, low-noise spintronic devices.

David Hardt guest lectures on manufacturing process control from a mechanical engineering perspective, covering process definitions, control taxonomy, and sources of variation.

He frames manufacturing processes as involving an interaction between equipment and material through a directed energy exchange (mechanical, electrical, thermal, or chemical) that changes geometry. Four fundamental geometry-change modes are identified: removal, addition, deformation, and formation.

A key taxonomy distinguishes serial processes (localized energy interaction moved over time, e.g., machining, laser cutting) from parallel processes (energy applied everywhere simultaneously via shaped tooling, e.g., stamping, injection molding, CVD). Serial processes generally offer greater flexibility since changes require only reprogramming trajectories, while parallel processes are faster but require costly tooling changes. Some processes, like rolling, combine both modes. Energy source type affects rate, quality, repeatability, and diffusivity (side effects).

Hardt divides process parameters into four categories: equipment properties (e.g., stiffness, thermal expansion), equipment states (e.g., forces, speeds, temperatures), material properties (e.g., yield strength, elasticity), and material states (transient conditions during processing).

Regarding variation sources: equipment states are highly controllable thanks to modern CNC and active control; equipment properties are generally stable but degrade over time; material properties are typically variable and a major source of uncertainty; material states are knowable but often expensive to measure directly. Consequently, manufacturing control primarily manipulates equipment states to compensate for variability originating in material properties and states.

The passage discusses interactions between neutral atoms separated by a distance R. Classically, neutral atoms exhibit no attraction because creating a dipole moment costs more energy than is gained from dipole interaction. However, quantum mechanics introduces zero-point fluctuations, resulting in a non-zero expectation value for the squared dipole operator, which enables attractive forces between atoms.

Three interpretations of the van der Waals force are presented: perturbation theory yielding a 1/R⁶ potential for two ground-state atoms; the ground state of two coupled LC oscillators where first-order coupling cancels but quadratic terms remain; and spontaneous dipole fluctuations inducing correlated dipoles in neighboring atoms via polarizability.

When electromagnetic field vacuum fluctuations are considered, correlated dipole moments arise between distant atoms, producing a 1/R⁷ interaction. The dominant contribution comes from modes with wavelengths comparable to the interatomic distance, as shorter wavelengths average out and longer ones are suppressed by density-of-states considerations.

The 1/R⁶ short-range van der Waals potential applies when propagation effects are negligible, while the 1/R⁷ long-range Casimir-Polder potential accounts for retardation. The transition occurs at distances comparable to the resonant atomic wavelength.

Using fourth-order perturbation theory and Feynman-like diagrams, the interaction is shown to arise from virtual photon pair exchange. At short range, photons are exchanged sequentially (intermediate states involve atomic excitations); at long range, both photons are emitted nearly simultaneously (intermediate states involve photonic excitations), yielding the additional 1/R factor.

The lecture introduces risk preferences from the perspective of expected utility theory, the classical economic framework for analyzing choices involving risk. Most important life decisions—education, housing, investments, health, and farming—involve uncertainty, and people often use risk-mitigation strategies like insurance.

Three stylized facts are presented: (1) people are generally risk averse, as evidenced by widespread insurance purchases; (2) risk reduction has a price, meaning people accept risk for sufficiently high returns; and (3) in some contexts, such as lotteries and casinos, people willingly take on risk despite negative expected returns.

Economists model risk aversion through diminishing marginal utility of wealth, represented by a concave utility function. Expected utility is calculated by weighting the utility of each final outcome by its probability. Key assumptions are that only final outcomes matter and that probabilities enter linearly. This model ignores factors like anxiety, regret, loss aversion, and disappointment.

Risk aversion is measured using the coefficients of absolute risk aversion (r) or relative risk aversion (gamma), typically via certainty equivalents, gamble choices, or insurance decisions. Large-scale choices suggest gamma values between 0 and 2, while small-scale gamble rejections imply implausibly high gamma values (e.g., above 18).

Rabin's (2000) theorem demonstrates that, under minimal assumptions, rejecting modest small-scale gambles implies absurd risk aversion over large stakes, revealing a fundamental limitation of expected utility theory in reconciling small- and large-scale risk behavior. This motivates alternative models like reference-dependent preferences and loss aversion.

Finally, Sydnor's study of home insurance deductible choices provides real-world evidence for estimating risk aversion from observed decisions.

The U.S. government has granted over $55,000 to Cambodia to preserve personal belongings of prisoners from the Khmer Rouge's Tuol Sleng (S-21) prison. The United States' objectives regarding dependent areas included promoting self-governance, economic advancement, security, and non-discriminatory treatment. On March 9, 1943, a "Draft Declaration by the United Nations on National Independence" distinguished between mandated territories (to be placed under international trusteeship) and colonial territories (to receive progressive self-government on a fixed timeline). The draft was discussed with the British at Quebec (August 1943), with the British and Russians at Moscow (October 1943), and during the Stettinius Mission in London (April 1944), where British objections were noted. Proposals were refined before the Dumbarton Oaks Conversations, but the trusteeship chapter was deleted at the Joint Chiefs of Staff's request to avoid territorial disputes, though Britain, the USSR, and China expressed interest.

In Document 5 (January 1945), Leo Pasvolsky acknowledged British acceptance of the President's December 5, 1944 proposal on Security Council voting.

In Document 6, Secretary of War Stimson argued that fundamental issues should first be settled among the great powers before convening a general assembly. He opposed raising territorial questions during the war, particularly before Russia committed to the Pacific war, warning that discussions of trusteeships would inevitably involve contested specific territories and jeopardize wartime unity.

The NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture introduces hardware-based real-time ray tracing through dedicated RT Cores, which accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing. This offloads work from the SM and enables approximately 10x faster ray tracing than Pascal GPUs, which performed these operations in software. Turing works with APIs including NVIDIA RTX, Microsoft DXR, OptiX, and Vulkan.

Turing also incorporates NVIDIA NGX, a deep learning technology stack powered by Tensor Cores. NGX features include Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS), which uses neural networks trained on 64x supersampled reference images to produce high-quality output at reduced rendering cost; InPainting, which intelligently replaces removed image content; AI Slow-Mo for frame interpolation; and AI Super Rez for image upscaling. NGX requires Turing or newer architectures.

Additional Turing features include Mesh Shading (introducing Task and Mesh Shaders to reduce CPU draw call bottlenecks), Variable Rate Shading (VRS) for fine-grained shading rate control enabling Content Adaptive, Motion Adaptive, and Foveated Rendering, Texture Space Shading (TSS) to decouple visibility and shading sampling, and Multi-View Rendering (MVR) supporting up to four views per pass.

Turing enhances VR through USB Type-C/VirtualLink support, MVR, Foveated Rendering via VRS, and ray-traced audio in VRWorks Audio. The TU104 and TU106 GPUs share Turing's core features, used in products including GeForce RTX 2080/2070, Quadro RTX 5000, and Tesla T4.

A Hybrid Rendering model combines rasterization, ray tracing, and AI. The RTX-OPS metric measures performance based on typical workload distribution: Tensor operations (20%), CUDA cores (80%), RT cores (40%), and INT32 pipes (28%). Ray tracing enables improved shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections compared to traditional techniques, with denoising algorithms reducing the required ray count per pixel.

The ambassador pattern uses a dedicated container to broker interactions between an application container and external services, enabling modular, reusable designs. Common applications include client-side sharding (e.g., using twemproxy with sharded Redis or memcache), service brokering for portability across environments, and request splitting for experimentation (e.g., using nginx to direct 10% of traffic to a beta version).

The adapter pattern modifies an application container's interface to conform to a standardized one, useful for monitoring (e.g., Prometheus exporters for Redis), normalizing logs (e.g., fluentd for Redis SLOWLOG or Apache Storm), and adding rich health checks (e.g., custom MySQL query probes) without modifying the original container.

Multi-node patterns build distributed systems through networked microservices. Replicated load-balanced services provide redundancy and horizontal scaling for stateless applications, requiring readiness probes and sometimes session tracking via consistent hashing. Caching layers (e.g., Varnish) and SSL termination (e.g., nginx) can be added as additional replicated tiers.

Sharded services split data across replicas, each serving a subset of requests, useful when state exceeds single-machine capacity. Sharded caches improve memory utilization but make shard failures more impactful. Replicated sharded caches add resilience. Sharding functions must be deterministic and uniform, with carefully chosen keys; consistent hashing minimizes remapping during resizing. Hot shards can be replicated dynamically to handle uneven load.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing across replicas or shards, with a root combining partial results. It enables time-based scalability but suffers from overhead and straggler problems, making 99th percentile latency critical. Replicating shards improves reliability and scale.

Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) enables event-driven, serverless computing, simplifying deployment and auto-scaling. However, it complicates debugging due to strong decoupling, is unsuitable for long-running background processing, and struggles with applications requiring significant in-memory data.

AT&T announced it will activate LTE-M technology nationwide by the end of June, enabling everyday objects to connect to the internet. Designed for the Internet of Things, LTE-M uses less energy than standard LTE, allowing devices to last up to 10 years on a single charge, and can penetrate walls 8 inches thicker than standard cellular signals. Coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery is performed on patients with ischemic heart disease, either on-pump or off-pump, and is associated with various postoperative complications. A retrospective cohort study analyzed data from 290 surgically treated patients (2017-2021) from Mordovian Republic Hospital, aged 41-80 years, including 46 females and 244 males. Most patients (95.86%) underwent on-pump CABG.

Risk factors observed included diabetes mellitus (22.76%), dyspnea (18.97%), arrhythmia (23.79%), progressive angina (38.62%), and post-myocardial infarction sclerosis (61.38%). Shunt numbers varied, with three shunts being most common (41.03%), and 65.86% of patients had one internal thoracic artery used.

Postoperative complications included arrhythmia (10.73%), psychosis (4.95%), stroke (1.41%), myocardial infarction (0.71%), hydrothorax (12.01%), re-sternotomy (3.18%), and dyspnea (3.89%). Mortality was 1.72%.

Key findings: Elderly patients had higher risks of psychosis, arrhythmia, stroke, and longer hospitalization. Low BMI and prolonged aortic cross-clamp time were associated with hydrothorax, which increased CPB time. Progressive angina and post-myocardial infarction sclerosis increased complication risk. The number of complications was not correlated with the number of shunts or internal thoracic arteries used but was associated with age, CPB time, aortic cross-clamp time, and hospitalization duration.

Lewis Roberts sued David B. Prosser and Charles R. King for false imprisonment after they, as attorneys for a judgment creditor, issued an execution against his person and had him jailed. The underlying judgment arose from an action against Roberts and Myers, assignees of insolvent debtor Mills, seeking an accounting and distribution of assigned property among creditors.

The court held that although assignees for the benefit of creditors hold property in a fiduciary capacity, the action against them was not "an action for money received" in a fiduciary capacity under subdivision 2 of section 179 of the Code. That provision contemplates only actions primarily and simply for the recovery of money, akin to suits for money had and received against factors, agents, or brokers. It does not extend to suits requiring an accounting and pro rata distribution among multiple creditors, nor to executors, administrators, guardians, or similar trustees.

Because the execution against Roberts's person was unauthorized, it provided no justification for the defendants. The judgment for plaintiff was affirmed with costs.

This review protocol aims to evaluate published data on infectivity assessment in immunosuppressed solid organ or hematopoietic stem cell transplant patients infected with SARS-CoV-2, and to estimate the relationship between viral culture results and rt-PCR Ct values or other viral burden measures. LitCovid, medRxiv, Google Scholar, and the WHO Covid-19 database will be searched from November 2019 to December 31, 2021, without language restrictions. Screening and data extraction will be performed in duplicate, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Only studies employing viral cell culture on respiratory samples will be included; post-mortem-only studies, non-respiratory-only studies, reviews, and abstract-only reports will be excluded. Quality will be assessed using five criteria covering case definition, patient characteristics, follow-up duration, and PCR and viral culture methods. Results will be reported narratively following PRISMA standards, without data pooling, due to laboratory variability. Subsequent reviews will address other immunosuppressed populations.

Lincolnshire County Council has approved a new care leavers strategy to support vulnerable young people leaving care. Corporate Parenting Manager Andrew Morris said the council has a legal responsibility to act as a parent, offering support beyond age 18.
