A fossil discovered in southwestern China shows that Dinocephalosaurus, a fish-eating marine reptile from the Triassic Period 245 million years ago, gave birth to live young rather than laying eggs. According to paleontologist Jun Liu, this makes it the first known member of the archosauromorph vertebrate group—which includes birds, crocodilians, dinosaurs, and pterosaurs—to reproduce this way, altering scientific understanding of vertebrate reproductive evolution. The reptile measured about 13 feet long, with a 5-1/2-foot neck, paddle-like flippers, and teeth suited for catching fish. Researchers confirmed the specimen was an embryo, not prey, due to its curled posture and forward-facing orientation. Live birth suggests Dinocephalosaurus was fully marine. Evolutionary biologist Chris Organ noted the creature determined offspring sex genetically.

The Farmers State Bank of Craig sued Samuel J. Lydick to recover on a $3,000 promissory note. Lydick's answer and cross-petition alleged the note was partial payment for an original $5,000 note given to purchase stock in the Missouri Valley Cattle Loan Company, which he claimed he was fraudulently induced to buy through misrepresentations by Everett J. Martin, then cashier and later president of the bank. Lydick sought to defeat recovery and obtain damages from Martin and the bank.

The trial court directed a verdict for the bank on Lydick's cross-petition claim against the bank, and submitted to the jury whether the bank was a holder in due course and whether Martin made the alleged fraudulent representations. The jury found for the bank and for Martin. A second count regarding a subsequent stock purchase was withdrawn for lack of evidence.

On appeal, Lydick argued the bank could not be a holder in due course because it was the original payee. The court rejected this, citing Bank of Commerce & Savings v. Randell, 107 Neb. 332, which held a payee receiving a negotiable instrument in good faith, for value, before maturity, and without notice from a holder other than the maker or drawer is a holder in due course. The jury's finding that Martin was not party to fraud resolved the argument regarding imputed knowledge. The judgment was affirmed.

PenFed Credit Union President and CEO James Schenck was named Large Business Philanthropist of the Year at the 20th annual Volunteer Alexandria Business Philanthropy Summit. Accepting on behalf of PenFed's 2,500 employees, Schenck highlighted the organization's "People Helping People" philosophy. Recent PenFed charitable contributions include $300,000 to Serve our Willing Warriors, $125,000 to the Kennedy Center, $100,000 to DC Habitat for Humanity, $75,000 to the Military Officers Association of America, and $15,000 to Bunker Labs. PenFed also supports the Gary Sinise Foundation and launched the Veteran Entrepreneur Investment Program. Since 2001, the PenFed Foundation has provided over $30 million to military members and families. Schenck, a West Point and Harvard Business School graduate and former Blackhawk pilot, was named 2017 National Credit Union Hero of the Year. Jen Walker was named Small Business Philanthropist of the Year.

Amazon Prime Day 2 runs October 7-8, 2025, with early deals already available. The WIRED Reviews team has compiled discounts on hand-tested gear, updated September 30, 2025 with 10 new deals. Highlighted offers include the Apple iPad (2025, A16) for $299 ($149 off), Apple MacBook Air (M4, 2025) for $799 ($200 off), Amazon Kindle Scribe (2024) for $300 ($100 off), Arlo Pro 5S Security Camera for $100 ($80 off), and Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K) for $70 ($20 off). Additional deals cover earbuds, power banks, keyboards, fitness trackers, and smart home devices. The Ultrahuman Ring Air is also discounted, though FTC restrictions will end US sales after October 21.

China has pursued military modernization for roughly 20 years, seeking hard power to match its economic and diplomatic influence, defend regional interests such as South China Sea claims and sea lanes, support global economic initiatives like the AIIB and One Belt One Road, and counter US presence in the Indo-Pacific. Since the late 1990s, the PLA has transformed significantly, resulting in a more assertive China willing to use military force to advance national interests. The ultimate outcome of this modernization remains uncertain.

North Korea's rarely traded defaulted debt may become further inaccessible following new sanctions imposed this week on Pyongyang. The country has syndicated loans with a face value of around $1 billion, in default since the 1980s, which were repackaged in 1997 into NK Debt Corporation by BNP. Total accumulated debt was estimated at $3 billion in 2013. Securities traded regularly from around 2000, rising to 14-18 cents on the dollar after Kim Jong-un took power in 2011, but trading froze in early 2013 due to sanctions. Exotix Capital has not seen the loans trade in three to four years. Holders include the Franklin Emerging Markets Debt Opportunities Fund, which held $15.5 million in principal of zero-coupon bonds maturing in 2020. Fresh U.N. sanctions target North Korean exports of coal, iron, lead, and seafood. Debt expert Charles Blitzer estimates interest arrears are 4-5 times the outstanding principal and compared the situation to Cuba's.

Latin American stocks rebounded on Monday from last week's selloff as tensions eased between the United States and North Korea, with U.S. officials downplaying the prospect of imminent war. Mexico's S&P/BVM IPC rose 1.1 percent, while Brazil's Bovespa reached its highest level since May, led by gains in Cia Paranaense de Energia SA. Currency movements were more subdued, with the Mexican peso firming 0.3 percent ahead of NAFTA negotiations, and the Brazilian real fluctuating ahead of an expected revision to the government's fiscal goal. Analysts at Scotiabank warned some risk remained if North Korea resumed missile testing.

Researchers developed a modular framework at NSLS-II integrating AI agents with the Bluesky software suite to orchestrate multi-modal, multi-beamline synchrotron experiments combining X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) spectroscopy. The system uses Bayesian optimization-based agents for data processing, dimensionality reduction via K-means clustering, model construction through Gaussian process regression, and measurement selection, while human-controlled adjudicators moderate AI measurement requests to maintain safety and user autonomy.

The framework was demonstrated through synchronous mapping of identical Al-Ni-Pt thin film combinatorial libraries on the PDF and BMM beamlines. EXAFS modeling revealed compositional gradients (Al: 18.2-44.3%, Ni: 21.8-50.9%, Pt: 21.8-53.6%), while XRD analysis identified coexisting face-centered cubic and face-centered tetragonal phases with position-dependent lattice parameters.

A digital twin simulating an Al-Li-Fe oxide combinatorial library was used to benchmark AI-driven mapping against conventional geometric grids and random sampling. After collecting 5% of total measurements, the AI-driven approach achieved 98.9% model accuracy compared to 95.9% for geometric series and 96.6% for random sampling, with superior resolution of phase boundaries and localized features.

The framework supports operating modes ranging from manual to fully autonomous across four automation levels, accommodates FAIR data principles, and enables plug-and-play integration of domain-specific agents for diverse characterization techniques.

Let's Grow Kids, a Vermont advocacy organization founded by Rick Davis in 2015, officially sunset on Oct. 3 after a decade of work improving the state's child care infrastructure. Led by Aly Richards, the group raised over $70 million in private philanthropy and grew to 40 staffers, driving passage of Act 76 in 2023, which established Vermont's near-universal child care program. Since implementation, more than 100 new child care programs have opened, creating over 1,000 spaces and 230 educator jobs, with 4,000 additional children qualifying for tuition assistance.

Leaders say the planned 10-year timeline was critical to success, sharpening focus, attracting talent, and encouraging philanthropic investment. The organization spent years preparing for the transition, building partnerships with permanent groups that will continue the work on financing, workforce, data, and advocacy. Many former staffers have moved into related roles across Vermont, while remaining staff transition to the Let's Grow Kids Action Network, a 501(c)(4) focused on protecting Act 76's funding.

Though 80–90% of Vermont families in child care programs qualify for subsidies, the system is not fully universal. Richards has been consulted by child care advocates in other states and emphasizes the sunset provision as key to effective campaigning.

Jennifer Bartell, 39, was shot and killed outside her Portsmouth, Va. home on March 14. Court documents state Joshua Bowen shot Bartell multiple times, while his girlfriend Albany Pierce, her mother Shaunicka Cooley, and Shyrayno Jackson face accessory charges. The incident reportedly stemmed from a Facebook argument between Pierce and Bartell's daughter and friend, which escalated into a planned meeting at a church. When Bartell's daughter and friend did not appear, the four went to Bartell's home, where a fight occurred. Bowen claims Bartell appeared armed, though investigators say no firearms were recovered from the scene. Neighbors expressed shock but noted the shooting was not random.

A U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin ruled Tuesday that the 1991 Nirvana album cover depicting a naked baby floating toward a dollar bill does not constitute child pornography. The judge dismissed a 2021 lawsuit by Spencer Elden, who was photographed at 4 months old and sued under a federal law providing civil remedies for victims of certain crimes as minors. Olguin evaluated factors including genitalia focus, suggestive setting, nudity, and intent to elicit sexual response, finding only nudity applicable. He compared the image to a family photo of a nude child bathing, deeming it insufficient to establish lasciviousness.

A Florida Museum of Natural History study examined the coevolution of blood-sucking lice and their vitamin-producing bacterial symbionts, which lice require to survive on a blood-only diet. Researchers Bret Boyd and David Reed found that lice parasitizing primates and humans have maintained the same endosymbionts for at least 20 to 25 million years, contradicting prior research suggesting repeated symbiont replacement. By sequencing endosymbiont genomes from human, chimpanzee, gorilla, and red colobus monkey lice, the team found the bacterial genomes were small (530,000–570,000 base pairs) and had undergone extensive remodeling, positioning symbiosis-critical genes near one another. Much of the genome is dedicated to producing B-vitamins. The researchers note that studying lice symbionts offers insights into bacterial genome evolution, mutualistic relationships, and primate and human evolutionary history.

A study led by Dr. Valentin Bickel from the University of Bern found that Martian winds and dust devils can reach speeds of up to 160 km/h, far exceeding previous estimates of 50-100 km/h. Using deep learning, researchers analyzed over 50,000 satellite images from ESA's CaSSIS and HRSC cameras, and examined stereo images of around 300 dust devils to measure their movement. The findings suggest these strong winds lift significantly more dust into the Martian atmosphere than previously thought, influencing the planet's weather, climate, and dust cycle. The research, conducted with the Open University and the German Aerospace Center (DLR), provides global wind data spanning two decades and could improve planning for future Mars missions, atmospheric modeling, and studies of surface processes like dune formation.

This study investigated whether resting-state functional connectivity (FC) patterns of the nucleus accumbens (NAc) could predict the course of ADHD symptoms in newly diagnosed adults. Fifty-four adult ADHD patients underwent baseline fMRI scans and clinical evaluation using the Wender-Reimherr-Interview (WRI) at diagnosis (t1), with follow-up approximately three years later (t2). At t2, 34 patients were still taking stimulants while 20 had discontinued medication as non-responders.

Results showed that higher symptom load at t1 correlated with decreased FC between the NAc and the right paracingulate gyrus, a region of the default mode network (DMN). Symptom improvement over time correlated with decreased FC between the NAc and the right anterior insular cortex, part of the salience network (SN). When medication status was considered, treated patients showed that higher FC between the NAc and right posterior insular cortex corresponded with symptom improvement, while non-responders showed the opposite pattern.

The authors conclude that FC patterns between the reward system and the DMN and SN correlate with the clinical course of ADHD symptoms and medication response, suggesting potential use as a biological marker. Limitations include small sample size, technical constraints of rs-fMRI, and lack of task-based behavioral paradigms. Further research with larger samples and extended follow-up is recommended.

A state audit found the Utah Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control overcharged business customers nearly $1,200 and lost $186 due to incorrect price markups on seven items. The errors occurred when the Legislature raised the required markup from 86 to 88 percent last July, and prices were entered incorrectly in the department's computer system. DABC executive director Sal Petilos said the department will refund overpayments and has implemented a program to flag incorrect markups. The audit also found that the department failed to transfer $4.6 million in revenue to state school lunch and public safety programs in November 2017, an error later corrected. Commission member Neal Berube said nothing in the report was overly alarming.

The Aedes aegypti mosquito, currently known for spreading Zika, also caused a deadly yellow fever epidemic in Philadelphia in 1793, killing about 5,000 people. At the time, physicians like Benjamin Rush tried ineffective treatments, as the mosquito's role in transmission was not discovered until over a century later. The last North American outbreak occurred in New Orleans in 1905. Today, concerns about yellow fever's resurgence are growing due to climate change and deforestation, with Brazil experiencing its worst outbreak in decades, including 326 confirmed cases and 220 deaths since December 2016. According to Dr. Pablo Tebas of Penn's Perelman School of Medicine, prevention advice remains similar to historical recommendations. A highly effective yellow fever vaccine, available since 1939, is 99 percent effective and serves as a foundation for developing vaccines against Zika and Dengue. Penn researchers are developing two Zika vaccine candidates using DNA and mRNA technology, with the goal of accelerating availability compared to traditional vaccines.

Rachael Caplan, 29, suffers from Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS), a rare neurological disease that has left her bedridden in her parents' Thornhill home. Once an athletic law graduate, Caplan began experiencing symptoms seven years ago after a hip injury, with pain intensifying following acupuncture treatment in 2012. It took 18 months to receive a diagnosis from Dr. David Shulman in 2013.

According to Helen Small, co-founder of patient advocacy group PARC, CRPS affects over 9,000 Canadians yearly. Early diagnosis is critical, with an 80-90% treatment success rate within the first three months. After six months, the disease typically becomes irreversible. Symptoms include intense burning pain, swelling, skin changes, and deterioration of bodily systems.

Conventional treatments including physiotherapy and opioids have worsened Caplan's condition, though recent green light therapy has helped her sleep. Her friends launched a social media campaign using #AceThisFire, sharing videos of participants submerging hands in ice water to simulate CRPS pain. The videos have garnered over 20,000 views, aiming to raise awareness and promote earlier diagnosis.

Gulf Island Fabrication (GIFI), a builder of offshore platforms, vessels, and steel structures, trades at a significant discount to book value following a sharp share price decline. The company operates three divisions: Fabrication, Shipyards, and Services. It faces challenges from an oversupplied offshore support vessel market in the Gulf of Mexico and muted demand for new offshore platforms. In Q4, technical problems with two multi-purpose support vessels built for Hornbeck Offshore caused a $23.9 million loss and delayed delivery to 2019, contributing to a quarterly loss of $24.3 million on $37.3 million revenue.

Positive factors include the company having essentially no debt and a backlog shifting toward non-offshore work, including tugs, research and icebreaker vessels, and a potential large contract with SeaOne Caribbean. Gulf Island is also selling non-core Texas facilities, with a $55 million purchase option agreement executed with Buckeye Pipe Line for the South Yard, and the North Yard also for sale. These facilities are booked at roughly $100 million, leaving the remaining business valued at about $30 million against a market capitalization of approximately $120 million. The author views the shares as attractive based on valuation, with potential contracts offering additional upside.

QoCGM is an open-source MATLAB tool for processing Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) data, addressing a gap in MATLAB-based analytical tools. It processes CSV input files containing timestamps and glucose values through two stages: preprocessing (removing duplicates, identifying missing periods, and interpolating gaps using Piecewise Cubic Hermite Interpolating Polynomial) and deriving metrics.

The tool calculates metrics across six domains: basic descriptive statistics, Time-in-Range (TIR) metrics, glycemic risk indicators (GRI, LBGI/HBGI, GRADE), glycemic variability metrics (CONGA, MAGE, Mobility, DTpM), glycemic control indicators (fasting glucose proxy, GMI, hypoglycemia events), and entropy/complexity measures (Multiscale Entropy). Several metrics are computed separately for daytime, nighttime, and day-to-day variations.

The tool was demonstrated using CGM data from 324 participants with insulin-treated Type 2 Diabetes from the DiaMonT trial. Coefficient of determination (R²) analysis revealed that most metrics overlap significantly, though some—including day-to-day standard deviation of TIR and mean, MCI, Mobility, and DTpM—showed low R² values, indicating they capture unique information. Differences between diurnal and nocturnal TIR metrics were also observed. The source code is available on GitHub.

European statesmen at the upcoming conference will be primarily concerned with obtaining means for recuperation, as failure will lead to revolutionary discontent during demobilization. Both slow and quick demobilization pose risks unless raw materials, transportation, markets, and credit are available. The Allies' control of outer communications and sea-borne materials will be a powerful negotiating tool, particularly because the disputed belt from the Baltic to the Persian Gulf will likely remain under German control at war's end.

German supremacy in the Near East represents its victory thus far, though the blockade creates difficulties, as Middle Europe cannot function as a closed economic system and requires outside supplies. Two schools of German imperialism exist: the Kühlmann-Helfferich group, which seeks access to outer markets through accommodation with western nations, and the Fatherland Party, which insists on military power and retention of Belgium. Belgium has become the pivot of German policy because its control would prevent England from landing armies in France, leaving France vulnerable.

Dunkin' Donuts will launch its fall-inspired menu on Aug. 28, returning pumpkin spice offerings while introducing maple and pecan flavors and bacon items. According to Paul Racicot, director of research and development for Dunkin' Donuts US, seasonal products evoke nostalgia for customers. New items include pumpkin cream cheese, maple pecan coffees and lattes, and a maple sugar bacon breakfast sandwich. Releasing the pumpkin beverage ahead of McDonald's and Starbucks could offer Dunkin' a sales advantage. The company has posted better-than-expected earnings for seven consecutive quarters, aided by limited-time products, strong breakfast sandwich sales, cold brew coffee, and fruited iced tea.

Sarasota County petitioned for writ of certiorari seeking review of a declaratory statement issued by the Department of Administration. The County sought to have a proposed crude oil splitter in Manatee County classified as a development of regional impact (DRI) under Chapter 380, Florida Statutes. The Department determined the DRI definition was limited to projects described in Fla.Admin.Code Rule 22F-2, which did not include the proposed project.

The court denied the petition, holding the County lacked standing. The court reasoned that Section 380.06 designates specific entities—developers, local governments with zoning authority, regional planning agencies, and the state planning agency—to initiate the DRI process, and the County did not fall within any of these categories. Issuance of an unfavorable declaratory statement alone does not confer standing under the Administrative Procedure Act.

Chief Judge Boardman concurred specially, noting the County could pursue relief through its regional planning agency under Section 380.06(3) or through the Florida Environmental Protection Act under Section 403.412.

Judge Scheb dissented, arguing the declaratory statement constituted final agency action subject to judicial review under Section 120.68. He contended the Department incorrectly concluded that administrative guidelines in 22F-2 were exclusive, thereby improperly limiting the state land planning agency's discretion to determine whether unlisted projects qualify as DRIs under Section 380.06(1).

The speaker confirms a player is fine and was given a day off. He acknowledges that second periods in two Boston games were problematic and emphasizes the need to improve each shift. Regarding two key players, he notes they are self-demanding and playing better than their point totals suggest, crediting the opposing goaltender and defensemen for shutting them down. He expects their performance to turn around soon. The team remains focused on a one-game-at-a-time approach, planning to execute their best. He is satisfied with the last game's play. He acknowledges that winning the trophy is physically taxing and travel-heavy, but states the group has been ready since day one.

ICICI Bank announced its mortgage loan portfolio has crossed Rs 1.5 trillion, making it the largest private player in the segment, with a target to reach Rs 2 trillion by FY20 at a 15% annual growth rate. According to executive director Anup Bagchi, the mortgage book represents half of the bank's Rs 3 trillion retail assets. Growth is primarily driven by tier II and III towns, with an average ticket size slightly above Rs 30 lakh. To achieve its target, the bank is expanding digitisation, having approved 2,000 housing projects online and creating a repository of 30,000 approved projects across 40 cities. It also plans to increase loan processing centres by 50% from the current 1,050.

SARS-CoV-2 vaccines have reduced COVID-19 cases, hospitalisations, and deaths, but the emergence of variants like Omicron has decreased vaccine effectiveness against infection. Bivalent Omicron-specific vaccines now demonstrate higher immunogenicity against Omicron subvariants.

The authors developed a model of immune waning and boosting fitted to vaccine effectiveness data from England for three vaccines (AZD1222, BNT162b2, mRNA-1273) against Delta and Omicron BA.1/BA.2 variants. They used a biphasic exponential decay function for immunity levels and a logistic relationship between immunity and protection against mild disease, hospitalisation, and death, fitted via Bayesian MCMC methods.

Results showed mRNA-1273 generated the highest immunity levels, followed by BNT162b2 and AZD1222. A 6.5-fold immunity reduction was estimated for Omicron versus Delta. Initial decay half-life was 33 days, followed by 580 days. At 180 days post-boost, effectiveness against Omicron hospitalisation was 49.5% (AZD1222), 63.7% (BNT162b2), and 69.8% (mRNA-1273), declining further at one year.

Applying a 1.61-fold NAT increase from bivalent mRNA-1273.214 data, the model predicted the bivalent vaccine sustains higher protection over time, with approximately double the prevented severe disease episodes compared to the original booster over one year.

Limitations include inability to separate infection- from vaccine-induced immunity, absence of immunological measurements, and difficulty distinguishing COVID-19-caused hospitalisations. The authors conclude that immunogenicity-based models will be increasingly important for evaluating future booster strategies.

Research reveals the average Brit wakes three times nightly, with one in 10 waking 7-10 times. The top 10 reasons include: needing the toilet (47%), discomfort or aches (19%), snoring partners (41%), being edged out of bed (25%), tossing and turning (10.5%), partners talking in their sleep (10%), phone light (10%), partners watching TV or reading (4.6%), nightmares (11%), and anxiety (6%).

Psychologist Robert Stewart said sleep quality depends on sleep hygiene and sleep cycles. Good pre-bed routines include avoiding heavy food, drink, and screens, and keeping consistent sleep times. People pass through five sleep stages, with REM being lightest and most prone to disturbance. While sleep cycles can't be controlled, optimising the environment with earplugs or a comfortable mattress can help.

Larry Connors' R3 strategy, from Chapter 4 of his 2009 book "High Probability ETF Trading," is a mean-reversion strategy tested on 20 liquid ETFs. The rules require the close to be above the 200-day moving average, the 2-day RSI to drop three consecutive days (with the first drop from below 60), and entry when the 2-day RSI is below 10. Exit occurs when the 2-day RSI exceeds 70.

When backtested, roughly 50% of the strategies performed worse than in Connors' original tests. For SPY, the win ratio was 90% across 79 trades since 1993. Applied as a portfolio across 25 ETFs from 2000 to December 2020 (max five positions, 20% equity each), the strategy produced 992 trades, a 75% win ratio, 0.68% average gain per trade, a profit factor of 2.08, CAGR of 6.47%, and a maximum drawdown of -16% during August 2011. A QQQ/SPY-only allocation yielded a 3.37 profit factor but only 2.69% CAGR due to limited market exposure (4.5%). The strategy works best on equity markets.

Treasury bills worth N62.4 billion and an OMO maturity of N168.1 billion are expected in the market this week, according to Afrinvest West Africa Limited. Analysts expect CBN's liquidity mop-up to keep OBB and overnight rates in check. Last week, system liquidity remained negative due to primary market issuances and a Retail SMIS auction, with the CBN mopping up N28.6 billion via OMO sales. OBB and overnight rates closed at 55.8% and 59.3% on Friday.

The Federal Executive Council approved issuing dollar-backed treasury instruments internationally to restructure Nigeria's debt and extended maturity from 91-364 days to two-three years. The treasury bills market closed bearish, with average yield rising 61 basis points to 18.5%.

In the forex market, the CBN auctioned $100 million SMIS. The naira remained flat at N305.55/$1 officially, appreciated to N365.91/$1 on NAFEX, depreciated to N365.20/$1 on NIFEX, and stayed at N367/$1 at the parallel market. Bond market performance was bearish with average yield at 16.8%.

Finance Minister Kemi Adeosun said the initiative would reduce government borrowing to $3 billion and lower interest rates. The FEC also approved the 2018-2020 MTEF with oil benchmark at $45. The Bankers' Committee disclosed that the I&E forex window attracted $4 billion between April and August.

Six Texas public university systems have ordered reviews of their curricula, syllabi, and course descriptions amid pressure from conservative politicians targeting faculty who teach about gender identity. The reviews were prompted by an incident at Texas A&M, where administrators were demoted and the president was pushed out after backlash over a gender identity lesson in a children's literature course. System leaders cite state directives asserting only two sexes exist, though no current laws prohibit teaching about transgender identity at public universities.

Faculty critics, including Brian Evans of the Texas AAUP, argue politicians should not dictate course content. Conservative groups have located targeted faculty through publicly accessible syllabi, including those posted on the third-party platform Simple Syllabus, used by over 500 institutions. Texas House Bill 2504 requires public syllabi access, complicating faculty privacy efforts. University of Houston lecturer Andrew Joseph Pegoda was targeted by a conservative news site after his queer theory course materials were found via Simple Syllabus. It remains unclear whether the reviews will result in courses being censored or removed.

The Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals denied Earl Ringo's petitions for rehearing en banc and rehearing by the panel in his case against Donald Roper. Judge Bye dissented, favoring en banc rehearing, while Judge Benton did not participate.

Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder affecting approximately 10% of the global population, predisposing individuals to complications including cardiovascular disease, neuropathy, and nephropathy. Diabetic patients face increased risks of severe COVID-19 outcomes, and vaccination has been shown to reduce hospitalization and mortality in this population.

In a longitudinal clinical trial of 155 adults receiving the BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, immune responses (spike protein, IgG antibodies, neutralizing abilities) increased similarly across healthy, pre-diabetic, and diabetic subjects. However, pre-diabetic and diabetic patients showed elevated HbA1c, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, and TyG index after booster shots, while fasting blood glucose and insulin remained unchanged. HOMA-IR positively correlated with immune response markers.

In mice, weekly mRNA vaccination over multiple doses impaired glucose tolerance, elevated triglycerides, reduced insulin-induced Akt phosphorylation, and decreased insulin sensitivity without affecting insulin secretion. Metformin at clinically relevant dosages alleviated vaccine-induced insulin resistance and restored insulin signaling in mice without diminishing vaccine-induced immune responses.

The authors suggest potential mechanisms involving SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binding to TLR4 and estrogen receptors, and systemic immune responses affecting insulin signaling. They recommend pre-diabetic and diabetic individuals monitor glucose control after vaccination and propose metformin as adjunctive treatment.

Love in the Time of Chasmosaurs is a website dedicated to dinosaurs and prehistoric life, combining educational content with humor. It features factual reports from scientists, links to scientific papers, and paleoart in various styles ranging from fine art to cartoons. The site is known for its snarky, entertaining book reviews, particularly of older children's books, as well as reviews of toys, films, TV shows, and museum exhibits. Active since 2009, it posts weekly with monthly news round-ups. Its name references Gabriel Garcia-Marquez's novel, and a Chasmosaur is a dinosaur formerly called Triceratops.

Olivia Munn, 45, was diagnosed with stage 1 breast cancer at 43 despite negative mammograms, ultrasounds, and genetic testing. Her OB/GYN, Dr. Thaïs Aliabadi, had her take a two-minute lifetime risk assessment, which showed a 37% risk. A subsequent MRI revealed the cancer. Munn's mother later took the same assessment and was also diagnosed with stage 1 breast cancer in July 2025. The assessment asks about factors like family history, age, and first menstruation. The recommended screening age for the assessment has been lowered to 25, with those scoring 20% or higher encouraged to pursue further testing. Munn advocates for the assessment to become standard care.

Hugh Jackman, 48, announced on Twitter and Instagram that he is being treated again for basal cell carcinoma, the most common and rarely fatal form of skin cancer. Sharing a photo with a bandage on his nose, he credited frequent body checks and his doctors, and urged fans to wear sunscreen. Jackman has been treated for the condition at least four times previously, starting in November 2013 after his wife Deborra-Lee Furness urged him to have a mole examined. The diagnosis has not impacted his work, with Logan set for a March release and The Greatest Showman on Earth due later this year.

Doug Ford, the newly-elected Progressive Conservative leader, launched his election campaign at the Toronto Congress Centre with a rally-like event. Entering to "Eye of the Tiger," he was greeted by enthusiastic supporters chanting his name. Ford aimed to unify the party after a divisive leadership contest, with former rivals Christine Elliott, Caroline Mulroney, and Tanya Granic Allen in attendance. Kory Teneycke is reported to be his campaign manager, with Jeff Silverstein as communications manager. Ford targeted Premier Kathleen Wynne and the Liberals, vowing to end wasteful spending and bring prosperity to all Ontarians. Supporters, including PC candidates and councillors, expressed confidence in Ford's ability to win, though acknowledged the campaign would be challenging. Family members, including nephew Michael Ford, referenced the late Rob Ford's spirit at the event.

Comic book creator Stan Lee, 95, was recently rushed to Cedar-Sinai hospital after experiencing shortness of breath and an irregular heartbeat at home. According to his representative, Lee has since been discharged and is doing well, though he will need to return periodically for monitoring. Lee himself told ABC News on Feb. 1 that he "feels great." His condition remained stable throughout the incident, with hospitalization taken as a precaution. Lee's most recent public appearance was at the Jan. 30 Hollywood premiere of "Black Panther," a character he co-created with Jack Kirby in 1966. The film releases Feb. 16.

Valeant Pharmaceuticals, J. Michael Pearson, Pershing Square Capital Management, and William Ackman entered into a litigation management agreement concerning a putative class action pending in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California. The agreement will terminate on November 1, 2017 if a stipulation of settlement has not been executed by that date. Under the agreement, the first $10 million in legal fees and litigation expenses for the Allergan litigation will be split 50/50 between Valeant and Pershing Square. Pershing Square also agreed to forbear from commencing related actions. Pershing Square funds beneficially owned 7.8% of Valeant's common stock as of February 13, 2017. The parties also entered into a mutual release of claims.

The speaker reflects on preparing for and winning a Stanley Cup Final game. Before the game, he emphasized relying on routine, teamwork, and not putting individual pressure on himself, noting most players opted for the morning skate. He recalled formative experiences from minor hockey, including the Joe Lamontagne tournament.

After winning, he described it as a dream come true, crediting sacrifices from parents, coaches, and teammates, and mentioning veterans like Bill Guerin and Sergei Gonchar who had long awaited a championship. He explained a knee injury sustained when Franzen hit him, jamming his knee against the boards, which limited him to brief shifts despite numbing treatment and pain medication. He acknowledged opposing fans' reactions to his injury but said it didn't concern him.

He praised Pittsburgh's loyal fanbase, noting this was the team's fourth road series-clinching win, and expressed satisfaction at rebounding from the previous year's loss.

Severe storms and tornadoes struck the Southeast on Monday night, with forecasters warning over 29 million people of potential powerful tornadoes, damaging winds, and large hail. Northern Alabama reported power outages and at least three confirmed tornadoes, with homes damaged in Limestone County and significant damage at Jacksonville State University. Tornado warnings extended into southern Tennessee, and a watch was issued for northern Georgia. Officials, including Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey, urged residents to prepare and seek safety. Schools dismissed early, and the University of Alabama suspended evening operations.

This study investigated the relationship between inflammatory markers, oxidative stress indicators, and NT-proBNP in cardiomyopathy patients. The researchers examined 202 cases, comprising 101 cardiomyopathy patients (43 with dilated cardiomyopathy and 58 with other types) and 101 healthy controls. Blood samples were analyzed for C-reactive protein (CRP), TNF-α, IL-6, NT-proBNP, malondialdehyde (MDA), and glutathione peroxidase (GPX) using ELISA kits and spectrophotometric methods.

Results showed that cardiomyopathy patients had significantly higher concentrations of CRP, TNF-α, MDA, GPX, and NT-proBNP compared to controls. TNF-α positively correlated with GPX and MDA, while NT-proBNP correlated with both MDA and GPX. IL-6 did not significantly correlate with GPX.

The authors concluded that inflammatory and oxidative stress indicators are correlated in cardiomyopathy patients but not in healthy individuals, suggesting complex interactions between these cellular processes in late-stage cardiomyopathy.

Chinese Premier Li Keqiang announced on Tuesday that China will further open its economy, granting foreign and domestic firms equal competitive footing. Li pledged increased access to services and manufacturing sectors, lower import tariffs, no forced technology transfers, and better intellectual property protection. The announcement comes amid global trade war concerns, following US President Trump's tariffs on steel and aluminium and expected new tariffs on Chinese goods. Trump has accused Beijing of forcing US companies to transfer intellectual property, a claim China denies.

Amadeus FiRe AG issued a correction on 15.02.2017 to a voting rights notification originally published on 10.02.2017, under Article 26, Section 1 of the German Securities Trading Act (WpHG). Research indicated that transfusions reduced long-term patient survival rates. The project sought to cut blood product utilization by two-thirds within a year, saving an estimated $2.5 million annually and 125 lives per year over a decade.

Young faced significant challenges, including HUH's complex organizational structure, where medical team members reported through separate chains of command and surgeons held no formal authority over nurses or perfusionists. Physician compensation was largely volume-based, fostering competition over collaboration. Appointed by the Chief Medical Officer to lead the initiative, Young proposed techniques like autologous blood harvest and retrograde autologous priming. While he had support from administrators, nurses, anesthesiologist Anil Gupta, and some colleagues, veteran surgeons resistant to altering long-standing routines remained skeptical. The Statistical Analysis Plan outlines a study comparing dasiglucagon to placebo, with GlucaGen® as a reference. With 20 patients on dasiglucagon and 10 on placebo, a log-rank test provides 90% power to detect differences in plasma glucose recovery time. Analyses use SAS 9.4+ and Phoenix WinNonlin 6.4+, with two-sided testing at 0.05 significance. Three analysis sets are defined: Safety, Full Analysis Set (FAS), and Per Protocol Set (PPS). The primary efficacy endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery (≥20 mg/dL increase within 45 minutes), analyzed via stratified log-rank test on the FAS, with sensitivity analyses and Cox proportional hazards modeling. Secondary endpoints include recovery rates and glucose changes at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes, tested hierarchically. Pharmacokinetic parameters are calculated via non-compartmental analysis. Safety analyses cover exposure, local tolerability, treatment-emergent adverse events (coded via MedDRA), laboratory values, vital signs, ECGs, and immunogenicity (ADA). No interim analyses are planned. Appendices detail presentation standards, QC requirements, and table/figure/listing specifications.

Soccer passing directions terminology describes the path a ball takes when passed, generally from the perspective of a player facing the attacking goal. Passes may travel on the ground or in the air, and terms apply regardless of the passer's orientation.

Clockwise around the player, directions include Forward, Angled Right, Right, Back and Right, Back, Back and Left, Left, and Angled Left. Each category contains related terms:

- **Forward**: ahead, deep, downfield, down the line, long, parallel, short, straight, upfield.
- **Angled Right/Left**: angled, corner, diagonal, line, post.
- **Right/Left**: center/centering, flat, lateral, square, wide.
- **Back and Right/Left**: angled, diagonal, reverse.
- **Back**: behind, straight back.

Additional terms include angle of a pass, back heel, center, far/near post, horizontal and vertical axis, interface, outlet, parallel, passing angle, possession, reverse field, straight lines, and switch fields.

Phlogopite (KMg3(AlSi3O10)(OH)2) is a layered dark mica used in electrical/heat insulation, construction, radiation dating, radionuclide waste storage research, and 2D optoelectronics. Its response to ionizing radiation is governed by electronic excitation, cascades, electron-phonon coupling, and nonthermal effects that existing ab-initio or classical MD methods cannot fully capture.

This study uses the hybrid XTANT-3 code, combining tight-binding molecular dynamics, transport Monte Carlo, and Boltzmann collision integrals, to simulate phlogopite irradiated by a 92 eV, 10 fs FWHM laser pulse at varying doses. The calculated bandgap (7.5 eV ideal, ~6.5 eV at room temperature) agrees with prior studies.

Key findings:
- At ~0.17 eV/atom (Te~11,000 K), hydrogen detaches and migrates, matching the experimental damage threshold of ~0.2 eV/atom.
- Electron-phonon coupling counteracts nonthermal damage, raising the threshold relative to Born-Oppenheimer simulations.
- At ~0.4 eV/atom, Mg becomes liquid-like while other sublattices remain stable (superionic state).
- At ~0.5 eV/atom, the full lattice disorders; at ~0.9 eV/atom, the bandgap collapses, creating a liquid metallic state.
- At ~2 eV/atom, nonthermal heating selectively accelerates O and K atoms within femtoseconds.

Results qualitatively match swift-heavy-ion irradiation experiments showing distinct damage mechanisms in hydroxyl versus silicon sublattices. Damage threshold fluences are provided to guide future X-ray experiments.

Lecture 16 of 14.13 reviews utility from beliefs and learning. Anticipatory utility can motivate people to delay consumption and reject negative information (e.g., Huntington's disease testing), particularly when outcomes cannot be altered. In a model where beliefs must be correct given received information, information aversion occurs when the utility function f(p) is concave and information-loving when convex. When belief manipulation is possible, people would choose p=1 unless beliefs affect future actions or cause disappointment through reference-point effects.

Evidence of overoptimism is widespread. Weinstein's study found students rate positive life events as more likely and negative events as less likely for themselves versus peers. Similar patterns appear among couples, small business owners, smokers, drivers, and professors. MIT students, however, tend to be under-confident, especially female students, possibly due to frequent feedback and biased perceptions of averages. Ego utility and the "depressive realism" literature suggest overconfidence may support mental health.

Experimental evidence (Eil and Rao, Mobius et al., Zimmermann) shows asymmetric updating: people incorporate positive feedback in a Bayesian manner but discount negative feedback, and remember positive signals better over time. Real-world evidence includes overconfident male investors (Barber and Odean) and managers engaging in value-destroying mergers (Malmendier and Tate).

Bayesian updating is cognitively demanding, leading people to use heuristics that produce systematic biases: the gambler's fallacy, the hot-hand fallacy (both explained by belief in the law of small numbers), and base-rate neglect. Kahneman and Tversky identified the representativeness heuristic (illustrated by the Linda problem, violating the conjunction law) and the availability heuristic.

Policy implications depend on the cause of misinformation: making information salient helps with attention failures or wrong theories, but may not work when people have motivated beliefs, and correcting beliefs may reduce welfare when people derive utility from them.

Topological insulator lasers combine topology with lasers to address common problems such as defects, unstable output power, and unwanted color variations at higher power levels.

In crystalline materials, electrons form two energy bands separated by a gap. Insulators have a large gap, making the top band nearly empty, except at the surface where electrons can conduct. In some materials, surface states are "protected": electrons moving along the surface have spin tied to direction, so reversing direction requires a difficult spin flip, allowing electrons to flow past defects with minimal resistance.

Researchers applied this concept to lasers by using rings of optical waveguides arranged so light leaks between them. Exciting only the outer rings confines light to the edge, while intermediary rings shift the light's phase to create a protected state. Light not in this state is scattered out, leaving protected light to be amplified.

Experiments comparing protected and unprotected edge states showed the protected laser remained functional despite removed rings, was more efficient, and did not produce unwanted colors at higher power. Such lasers could benefit applications like 5G networks and space-based interferometers.

Researchers recorded medical problems in participants who received at least one dose of a study vaccine, noting these could be unrelated to the study, caused by a vaccine or medication, or of unknown cause.

**Phase 1 blood test results:** A few participants had a temporary drop in lymphocyte count 1–3 days after Dose 1 of BNT162b1 or BNT162b2, which returned to normal by 6–8 days.

**Injection site reactions (Phase 1 and 2/3):** Reactions within 7 days of BNT162b1 or BNT162b2 were well tolerated, mostly mild or moderate, and short-lived. Pain was the most common reaction.

**Systemic events (Phase 1 and 2/3):** Fever, tiredness, headache, chills, vomiting, diarrhea, and muscle or joint pain within 7 days were well tolerated and short-lived, mostly mild or moderate. Tiredness and headache were most common.

**Medical problems within 1 month after Dose 2 or booster:** All tested BNT162b1 and BNT162b2 doses in Phase 1 were well tolerated except BNT162b1 at 100 µg, which was stopped after Dose 1. BNT162b2 at 30 µg was selected for Phase 2/3. No participants left Phase 1 due to medical problems. In Phase 2/3, fewer than 1% of participants in either the BNT162b2 or placebo groups left due to medical problems; most problems were mild or moderate.

**Serious medical problems:** Few serious problems occurred across phases, and researchers generally did not believe they were related to the vaccine, with a few exceptions in the 16-and-older group.

**Deaths:** No participants died in Phase 1. In Phase 2/3, 85 of 23,141 BNT162b2 recipients, 62 of 21,371 placebo-then-BNT162b2 recipients, and 23 of 23,141 placebo recipients died from various causes; researchers do not believe the deaths were caused by BNT162b2.

Neutral particle diagnostics are used to measure the ion distribution function f_i(V_i) in the core of a plasma, such as a tokamak, where confined ions cannot easily be observed. Alternative diagnostics like electron cyclotron emission, laser-induced fluorescence, and Thomson scattering are unsuitable because they measure electron properties or require bound electrons absent in the fully ionized core.

The technique relies on core ions becoming neutrals, which can escape confinement and be detected externally. Two key issues are neutral production and neutral transport. Neutrals can be produced via charge exchange with edge neutrals or with neutral beam injection (NBI). Radiative recombination is negligible.

Neutral transport is limited by electron impact ionization, ion impact ionization, and charge exchange (which dominates due to resonance). For a 10 keV, 10^20 m^-3 plasma, the mean free path is ~10 cm, so low-density devices (line-integrated density < 10^19 m^-2) are required.

In passive charge exchange, neutrals from the core pass through a stripping cell, are ionized, and separated by a magnetic field onto a binned detector to measure the distribution function, revealing T_i from the slope and fast-ion tails. This method is line-integrated.

Active diagnostics using neutral beams provide localized measurements:
- **Charge Exchange Recombination Spectroscopy (CXRS/CHERS)**: Measures impurity density, ion temperature, and flow velocity via Doppler effects on light emitted after impurities charge-exchange with the beam.
- **Beam Emission Spectroscopy (BES)**: Detects intensity fluctuations proportional to electron density fluctuations, useful for turbulence studies, but requires accounting for beam attenuation.
- **Motional Stark Effect (MSE)**: Beam particles experience an effective electric field E = -V×B, causing linear Stark splitting of energy levels (typically using the H-alpha Balmer transition). The splitting is ~10× larger than Zeeman splitting, and polarization analysis of the split lines determines the magnetic field angle, enabling reconstruction of the poloidal field and current profile.

In late 2004, Walt Bernstein, Toyota Motor Manufacturing's Macon, Georgia (TMMGA) production control director, expressed frustration to ChassisCo plant manager David McDonald about persistent quality and production problems with rear suspension cradles for the Suprima crossover vehicle built at ChassisCo's Athens, Georgia plant.

Toyota's production approach relied on the Toyota Production System (TPS), built on jidoka and Just-in-Time principles, emphasizing continuous improvement, respect for people, problem-solving, and long-term supplier partnerships.

ChassisCo's relationship with Toyota began in 1993 when Toyota outsourced rear suspension cradle assembly for the 1997 Suprima. That launch and the subsequent 1999 Responsa launch at ChassisCo's St. Louis plant were successful, leading Toyota to expand ChassisCo's responsibilities for the 2003 Suprima to include parts sourcing, logistics, and project management.

However, the 2003 Suprima launch revealed significant capability gaps at ChassisCo, including weak project management, inadequate supplier oversight, insufficient engineering resources, lack of tuning expertise, and an unrealistic target price. ChassisCo's 2000 decentralization dispersed experienced staff, while multiple concurrent launches stretched resources thin. Increased automation (102 robots versus 13) introduced new welding challenges without real-time feedback.

The Suprima launched on time in September 2003 but at 60% of target production rate, having failed three high volume production trials. Throughout 2004, defects, scrap rates, downtime, and overtime remained high. A November 2004 arc welding audit scored only 13%, and external defects rose from 565 to 2,845 per week year-over-year.

By late 2004, ChassisCo sought a price increase while Bernstein insisted on addressing underlying quality issues, acknowledging TMMGA's resources were also taxed and a breakthrough was needed.

Radiotheranostics enables personalized cancer treatment through radiopharmaceutical therapies (RPTs), exemplified by FDA-approved [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-PSMA-617. Current RPT regimens remain standardized despite interpatient variability, prompting development of computational nuclear oncology (CNO) and theranostic digital twins (TDTs). Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models are advantageous for estimating absorbed doses and responses by incorporating patient physiology and drug characteristics.

PBPK models comprise computational, anatomical-physiological, and radiopharmaceutical frameworks, and can be built using bottom-up, top-down, or middle-out approaches, the latter being well-suited for data-limited RPT settings.

Due to sparse clinical data and modeling variability, verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification (VVUQ) are essential. Verification ensures correct model implementation through structural and computational checks. Validation includes internal goodness-of-fit assessment, model selection (via AIC, BIC, or F-tests), sensitivity analysis (local or global), and external validation using data splitting or resampling. Uncertainty quantification assigns statistical distributions, propagates variability through sampling methods, and evaluates accuracy using metrics like RMSE and MAPE.

Extending PBPK to dynamic TDTs introduces additional VVUQ challenges, requiring iterative validation against evolving imaging and physiological data. Regulatory standards for PBPK in RPTs remain undeveloped compared to pharmaceutical applications. Establishing VVUQ frameworks and collaboration with organizations like SNMMI, EANM, and IAEA will support clinical translation.

The paper addresses challenges in measuring and advancing the persuasive capabilities of large language models (LLMs). While frontier LLMs demonstrate human-comparable persuasive abilities across domains like health, marketing, and politics, existing evaluations suffer from inconsistent metrics, subjective human judgment, and limited systematic methods.

To address this, the authors propose a theory-driven framework grounded in Bayesian persuasion, which conceptualizes persuasion as a Sender strategically revealing information to shift a Receiver's beliefs. They repurpose existing human persuasion datasets to construct environments where both Sender and Receiver are LLMs, validated through a 45-participant human study. They measure persuasiveness using persuasion gains and conditional mutual information signals.

Key findings include: (1) stronger models like DeepSeek-R1 achieve higher persuasion gains and exhibit more sophisticated adaptive information revelation; (2) reinforcement learning can train small LLMs (Llama3.2-3B-Instruct) to reach persuasive capabilities comparable to larger models; and (3) these learned strategies transfer across Receiver architectures.

The contributions are a principled Bayesian-persuasion-inspired framework, concrete evaluation environments, and empirical evidence that LLM persuasive capabilities can be scaled via reinforcement learning. The paper also formalizes opinion-change tasks with utility functions, posteriors, and target action supports.

The Clock Zone Offense is a simple, easy-to-teach offense effective against both person-to-person and zone defenses. It combines a 1-3-1 free-lance passing attack with basic rotation rules, relying on sharp ball movement to create open shots, basket cuts, and post rolls.

The offense is named for its clockwise and counterclockwise outside-player rotations. Key actions include:
- **Corner Pass**: The wing passes to the corner and cuts to the basket for a possible return pass; if the defender helps, the corner feeds the open post.
- **Ball Reversal**: When the defense adjusts, the ball is swung quickly to attack the weakside.
- **Dribble Clear**: The wing may dribble to the corner, prompting the corner player to back-cut, swapping roles.
- **Continuity**: Movement continues via corner passes, dribble clears, or reversal passes.

The offense exploits weaknesses along the baseline of a 1-3-1 zone and in the middle/corners of a 1-2-2 zone.

Against traps, the "Cat" 2-1-2 alignment uses sharp passes without dribbling to counter double teams. Specific rules include post rolls on baseline corner passes and back cuts when the ball enters the middle.

Crunch-time specials include "Vegas" (a double screen away play) and "Back" (a weakside lob play), both with options transitioning into standard Clock action.

The NVIDIA Turing TU102 GPU is the flagship of the Turing line, featuring 6 GPCs, 36 TPCs, 72 SMs, 4608 CUDA Cores, 576 Tensor Cores, 72 RT Cores, and a 384-bit GDDR6 memory interface with 6MB L2 cache. Each SM contains 64 CUDA Cores, 8 Tensor Cores, one RT Core, and 96 KB configurable L1/shared memory, and supports concurrent FP32 and INT32 execution, delivering roughly 36% additional throughput and a 50% performance-per-core improvement over Pascal.

Turing introduces hardware-accelerated real-time ray tracing via RT Cores, which handle BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, achieving over 10 Giga Rays/sec—ten times faster than Pascal's software-based approach. Tensor Cores add INT8 and INT4 precision for AI inferencing and power NVIDIA NGX features like DLSS, InPainting, AI Super Rez, and AI Slow-Mo.

Other innovations include GDDR6 memory (14 Gbps, 20% more power efficient), second-generation NVLink (100 GB/s bidirectional on TU102), Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. The display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, HDR, and VirtualLink via USB-C for VR headsets. Enhanced NVENC/NVDEC support HEVC 8K encoding and VP9 decoding.

The scaled-down TU104 (13.6B transistors, 3072 CUDA Cores) powers the RTX 2080, Quadro RTX 5000, and Tesla T4, the latter delivering up to 260 TOPS INT4 for inferencing with 50× better energy efficiency than CPUs. The TU106 (10.8B transistors, 2304 CUDA Cores) powers the RTX 2070 without NVLink. Turing enables a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization, ray tracing, and AI, measured by the new RTX-OPS metric (78 for RTX 2080 Ti).

Vehicles use communication buses (e.g., CAN bus) connecting computing nodes, sensors, and actuators, accessed through data link connectors such as diagnostic ports. Although manufacturers use standardized hardware connectors, pinout configurations vary, traditionally requiring different cables for compatibility.

The disclosed system addresses this with an external device containing a variable multiplexer that can be electronically configured to match different pinout configurations, enabling use of a single standardized cable across vehicles.

The device determines the correct pinout configuration through several methods:
1. Transmitting a vehicle identifier (e.g., VIN) via a network gateway to a remote computing system that maintains a vehicle data index and returns the appropriate pinout configuration.
2. Using a listening mode to gather data transmitted across the bus, then comparing enabled and disabled pins against known pinout configurations to find a match.
3. Using checksum values transmitted with data blocks to validate which known pinout configuration produces matching checksums.

Key components include a connection detection component, pinout configuration determination component, pinout configuration modification component, network gateway, and data storage holding known pinout configurations. Once the configuration is identified, the modification component reconfigures the variable multiplexer to map pins correctly between the data link connector and the external device.

The disclosure also describes general software architecture and machine hardware components (processors, memory, I/O, communication modules) supporting the implementation.

Equality, shaped by historical economic, legal, political, and sociological discussions, has become enriched with principles like equality of opportunity and is considered a superior value. Cevizci (1999) defines it as a moral and social ideal where people hold the same position and value. The education system plays a key role in implementing equality of opportunity.

Equality of opportunity, a central democratic concept, is interpreted differently across countries, referring to education, culture, economy, or gender equality. Resources should be accessible to all segments of society based on knowledge and talent rather than origin.

Education is variously defined as a system ensuring social continuation (Buluç, 1997), a process of developing skills and positive behaviors (Aydın, 2015), and intentional behavioral change (Ertürk, 1998).

Equality of opportunity in education emerged with 18th-century Prussian compulsory education, with foundational studies by James S. Coleman (1968). Definitions emphasize providing educational services that allow each individual to develop their abilities without discrimination, regardless of family or economic background.

Five factors affect educational equality: economic, geographical, political, individual, and social. Economic factors are primary, while geographical conditions, state policies, individual differences, and societal traditions all influence access and success.

In Turkey, the Ministry of National Education shapes education policies, with National Education Councils playing advisory roles. Kaya (2013) identifies inadequate schools, economic difficulties, insufficient equipment, and low student motivation as key issues.

Recommendations include measuring children's abilities early and independently of family background, increasing education quality and access, reducing regional disparities, extending compulsory education, strengthening infrastructure, improving teacher quality through better recruitment to education faculties, and expanding high-standard preschool institutions to ensure early equality of opportunity.

Sharded services differ from replicated services in that each shard handles only a subset of requests, with a load-balancing root distributing requests appropriately. Sharding is primarily used for stateful services when data size exceeds a single machine's capacity.

In sharded caching, sharding increases usable cache storage since each replica holds unique data rather than duplicates, improving memory utilization. However, failure of a shard causes cache misses for mapped users until restored, affecting performance. Cache effectiveness is measured by hit rate, which influences system capacity and request latency. Load testing with and without caches is recommended.

Replicated sharded caches combine replication with sharding, making each shard resilient to failures and enabling independent scaling during peak traffic, at the cost of greater deployment complexity.

A hands-on example demonstrates deploying a sharded memcache using Kubernetes StatefulSets, Services, and twemproxy either as an ambassador or as a shared shard routing service. The shared service reduces complexity but adds latency and requires scaling.

Sharding functions map requests to specific shards, typically using a hash function combined with modulo. Key properties are determinism (same input yields same shard) and uniformity (even load distribution). Selecting the correct sharding key is critical: overly general keys group non-identical requests, while overly specific keys fail to group identical ones. For example, including client IP country with request path can properly group region-specific content.

The NVIDIA Blackwell GPU architecture introduces significant advancements over the Ada generation, with SMs optimized for neural shaders rather than standard shaders. Blackwell unifies INT32 and FP32 cores, enabling up to 2x throughput for many integer operations, and increases texture units from 512 to 680 in the flagship GeForce RTX 5090.

The architecture debuts GDDR7 memory using PAM3 signaling, delivering higher bandwidth and efficiency. The RTX 5090 offers 28 Gbps GDDR7 with 1.792 TB/sec bandwidth, while the RTX 5080 provides 30 Gbps with 960 GB/sec. GDDR7 includes built-in ECC and EDR support.

Fifth-Generation Tensor Cores add FP4 and FP6 support, reducing memory requirements and doubling AI performance versus the previous generation. Fourth-Generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and support new technologies including Mega Geometry (for high-detail ray tracing with cluster-based LOD and PTLAS), Linear Swept Spheres (for efficient hair rendering), and improved Shader Execution Reordering (SER 2.0).

A new AI Management Processor (AMP) offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU. Video capabilities include ninth-generation NVENC with 4:2:2 support, sixth-generation NVDEC, and DisplayPort 2.1b with up to 80 Gbps. Max-Q improvements feature advanced power gating, accelerated frequency switching, and 10x faster sleep-state entry.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation (up to three generated frames per rendered frame) and transitions from CNN to transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA. Neural shaders enable RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

Blackwell GPUs include the GB202 (RTX 5090), GB203 (RTX 5080, 5070 Ti), and GB205 (RTX 5070).

The Reverse Action Offense, introduced by Hall of Fame Coach Pete Newell in the late 1950s, is a guard-around continuity offense known for its precise execution and footwork. Its signature feature is the weakside wing's rub cut off a post screen to the basket, while also providing post-up opportunities, two-player guard-around isolation, and counters against defensive overplays.

The offense relies on patience and off-ball post screens, requiring coordination between passer, screener, and receiver. Multiple entries (weakside, strongside, dribble clear, and back door) make it difficult to disrupt, with defensive deployment dictating the entry used.

Key components include guard around action creating a sideline triangle and post isolation similar to Tex Winter's Triangle Post Offense. Players read defensive post positioning (high side, baseline side, fronting, behind, or double-teaming) and counter accordingly with options like power lay-ups, baby hooks, triple threat moves, lob passes, and pressure releases.

The offense also includes back cut counters against overplays, corner pass reads using screen-and-roll action, and crunch-time specials such as weakside screen and roll, double screens, and back screen lobs.

Defensive wall building in soccer involves placing defenders shoulder-to-shoulder, 10 yards from the ball, to block part of the goal during a free kick near the Penalty Area. This becomes relevant around age 12, when players can shoot accurately from distance. The wall blocks roughly half the goal, allowing the goalkeeper to cover the remaining angle.

Law 13 governs free kicks: the ball must be stationary, defenders must stay 10 yards away (unless on the goal line between posts), and attackers must remain 1 yard from walls of three or more. Referees are not required to delay play for wall building, and defenders blocking quick kicks receive yellow cards.

The goalkeeper calls for the wall, specifying the number of players (typically two to five) based on the ball's location and angle. In traditional wall-building, an "Anchor" player positions on the line from the near post to the ball, directed by the goalkeeper. Alternatively, a "Wall Setter" positioned beyond the ball can direct the Anchor, freeing the goalkeeper to watch the ball.

Players face the ball, stand tightly packed without gaps, may protect sensitive body parts with hands/arms held still, and must not turn or rush the kick. For rare indirect free kicks inside 10 yards, players stand on the goal line between the posts.

Coaches can use ropes to demonstrate angles, mannequins for goalkeeper training, and should prepare players against attacker deception tactics.

The reverse play is a high-risk, high-reward football play designed to deceive the defense by running the ball in one direction before handing it off to another player moving the opposite way. Typically, the quarterback hands off to a running back or wide receiver, who then tosses the ball to another receiver crossing in the opposite direction. Success depends on disguising the play and having offensive linemen form a "seal" to block pursuing defenders.

Several variations exist. A 2018 Carolina Panthers play illustrated a traditional reverse, resulting in a touchdown. A fake reverse, demonstrated by the 2020 Arizona Cardinals, uses motion to draw defenders away before the quarterback keeps the ball. The reverse screen, shown by 2021 Purdue, involves tossing the ball back to the quarterback, who then throws a screen pass behind a wall of blockers. The reverse pass play, often considered the best variation, adds a twist where the quarterback becomes a receiver after handing off, catching a pass from the ball carrier for a touchdown.

Industrial enterprises increasingly rely on IT-based simulation, modeling, and data analysis to support collaborative design, digital twins, and innovation. Modern engineering workstations "as a Service" and digital twins enable new products, services, and business models such as "Product as a Service."

High-Performance Computing (HPC) is viewed as a game changer by 81% of surveyed industry decision makers, enabling complex calculations, higher quality simulations, new usage scenarios, and greater innovation. Currently, 8% report high demand for HPC, rising to nearly 50% expected in two years. While 42% admit simulations are outdated or inaccurate, over a quarter already use HPC and 39% are piloting it.

Most HPC users (87%) prefer external infrastructures, with 74% using colocation. Key challenges include security (72%), energy consumption (58%), costs, computing power, availability, and skills shortages (42%).

Cloud-based HPC and HPCaaS are becoming dominant, offering scalability, flexibility, cost optimization (OPEX vs. CAPEX), access to cutting-edge technology, and a foundation for new business models. Hybrid architectures allow sensitive data to remain on-premises while using public cloud for peak loads. 81% of HPC users plan HPC-based business models.

IDC recommends developing virtual product development strategies, a holistic data strategy with a single source of truth, evaluating suitable HPC operating models, prioritizing scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise.

The findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 decision makers from industrial enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Charles W. Parker, administrator of Melvin Douglas's estate, appealed a district court ruling that Farmway Credit Union could exhaust its security interest in the decedent's personal property without filing a claim in probate or a foreclosure action.

Prior to his death, Douglas had defaulted on obligations to Farmway totaling $111,290.17, secured by farm machinery, crops, livestock, and real estate. Douglas and his wife orally agreed before his death that Farmway could sell the collateral at public sale. After Douglas's death, his heirs cooperated with Farmway, and a public sale was held on May 26, 1984, with notice given to heirs and creditors.

The administrator filed for declaratory judgment seeking sole right to the property. The trial court granted Farmway's motion for summary judgment, finding no conflict between the administrator's rights under K.S.A. 59-1401 and Farmway's self-help repossession rights under K.S.A. 84-9-503.

On appeal, the court held that an administrator's right to decedent's property is not absolute and is affected by contractual arrangements made during the decedent's lifetime. Citing In re Estate of Dahn, the court found secured creditors need not foreclose through district court to exhaust security. Because Farmway had a contractual right to possession upon default and a pre-death agreement authorized the sale, the trial court correctly ruled in its favor.

The court also rejected the argument that summary judgment was premature, noting the material facts were uncontroverted. Affirmed.

The Counter play creates the illusion of Power in one direction before sending the runner the opposite way. The backside Guard pulls to kick out an edge defender, while a Fullback inserts through the created lane to block an Inside Linebacker.

Its main strength is exploiting aggressive, over-pursuing defenses and outnumbering defenders at the point of attack. Its weaknesses include slower development, vulnerability to B-gap penetration, and defenses that spill the play to force lateral runs into pursuing defenders.

Blocking assignments vary slightly against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts, but the core concept remains: down blocks playside, a pulling Guard kick-out, and a Fullback insert, while the Quarterback fakes Power before handing off and booting away.

Variations include GT Counter, where the backside Tackle replaces the Fullback as the inserting blocker, and Gun Split GT Counter Triple Option, which adds triple-option reads for mobile Quarterbacks.

The cubic-to-tetragonal (CT) phase transition in perovskite-based ferroelectrics produces domain microstructures underlying ferroelasticity, piezoelectricity, and shape-memory effects. A key challenge is the lattice mismatch between coexisting C and T phases, which prevents a mismatch-free interface unless addressed through models like the "adaptive state" (AS) or Wechsler–Lieberman–Read (WLR) theory, both assuming domain miniaturization.

This paper presents a mathematical framework for investigating CT coexistence using high-resolution X-ray diffraction 3D reciprocal space mapping, extending prior work on coherent twin relationships in ferroelectrics. The authors model CT coexistence through periodic T-domain assemblages without requiring miniaturization, catalog 24 possible ASC variants, and predict Bragg peak splitting in 3D reciprocal space.

The framework derives orientation relationships between C, AS, and T phases, including Habit Plane Miller indices, transformation matrices, and Bragg peak separations, summarized in twelve tables. Experimental validation was performed on PMN-35PT single crystals at the ESRF ID28 beamline, revealing CT coexistence over a 4K range near 435K. The observed Bragg peak splitting patterns align with predictions, supporting AS-like coexistence without domain miniaturization, with estimated domain sizes of several hundred nanometers. The methodology may extend to other ferroelectric systems and phase coexistence scenarios, such as rhombohedral-tetragonal boundaries.

The design pairs the single-channel, 16-bit ADS8681W SAR ADC with the eight-channel MUX36D08 differential multiplexer. The ADS8681W offers fast settling (1% accuracy under 5µs), 400kHz bandwidth, an internal programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, reference, and safety features like overvoltage protection and alarms, supporting signals up to ±12.288V. The MUX36D08 allows up to eight differential inputs for voltage, current, or temperature sensing, controlled by three digital lines. The Washington Supreme Court affirmed a judgment confirming a local improvement assessment roll for the City of South Bend. The city passed an ordinance in 1911 for filling low lands and tide lands, estimating the cost at $9,500 based on an arrangement to obtain fill material cheaply from a Federal dredging project on the Willapa river. When Federal officials deposited all material within a 1,500-foot limit rather than across the entire district, the city contracted with a private dredging company to complete the remaining work, raising the actual cost to $89,199.92.

The court held that under Rem. & Bal. Code § 7974, the preliminary cost estimate serves only to guide the city council in deciding whether to initiate an improvement, not to protect property owners. Section 7983 permits assessments to reflect the actual bona fide cost, with additional amounts added after due notice and hearing when estimates prove too low. Because the excess reflected the actual cost and was explained by changed conditions, the assessment was valid. The court further held the ordinance was not void for indefiniteness, as it complied with statutory requirements, and found the evidence supported the benefits assessed.
