NeoWorld is a deep learning framework that generates an interactive, infinitely expandable virtual 3D world from a single input image. Inspired by the novel Simulacron-3, it uses on-demand rendering, initially representing scenes in 2D and progressively unfolding them into 3D as users explore or issue prompts.

The framework addresses limitations of prior methods (e.g., WonderJourney, WonderWorld), which support only visual navigation and suffer from artifacts under large viewpoint changes. NeoWorld introduces three key innovations: (i) an object-centric neural scene representation using layered Gaussian Splatting with a compact codebook for instance-level semantics; (ii) a progressive 2.5D-to-3D unfolding mechanism prioritized by object proximity or user prompts, using Amodal3R for image-to-3D reconstruction with coarse and fine alignment; and (iii) a user-interaction module leveraging Gemini-2.5pro to interpret natural language commands for object manipulation and animation.

Experiments on a 112-scene benchmark show NeoWorld outperforms baselines including WonderWorld, WonderJourney, CogVideo-I2V, Wan2.1-I2V, and Matrix-Game2 in 3D consistency, scene quality, object-centric accuracy (IoU), and prompt alignment for dynamic simulation, while maintaining competitive rendering efficiency (18.14s per view).

Limitations include error propagation across its cascaded pre-trained modules, particularly from alignment failures, ambiguous prompts, occlusion during 3D reconstruction, and segmentation errors.

**Clocking and Synchronization:** Requires a free-running sampling clock (differential or single-ended). A SMPL_SYNC signal synchronizes multiple devices.

**Reference:** Includes an internal low-drift voltage reference; an external reference can be used by disabling the internal one.

**Operating Modes:** Supports power-down, reset, and a speed-boost mode enabling up to 8MSPS on a selected channel pair.

**Configuration:** Registers are organized in three banks, accessed via SPI, with support for daisy-chain topology across multiple devices.

**Application:** Suitable for ATE applications, achieving 0.0015% TUE at 25°C post-calibration. Requires three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with decoupling capacitors, and recommends careful PCB layout to separate analog and digital paths.

Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, remains a leading infectious cause of mortality, with extrapulmonary TB (EPTB) accounting for approximately 16% of cases in 2019. Despite its prevalence, EPTB treatment is understudied and typically mirrors pulmonary TB regimens using four first-line drugs: rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol.

The authors developed a whole-body physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model that, for the first time, incorporates pleura and lymph node compartments—major EPTB sites—and simulates tissue concentrations of all four first-line drugs, considering both slow and fast isoniazid acetylators. The model uses 17 perfusion-limited compartments described by 18 ODEs, with parameters derived from literature, Rodgers and Rowland partition coefficient calculations, and fitting to plasma and lung concentration data.

Key predictions include: rifampicin concentrations exceeded critical thresholds in most organs but were over-predicted in pleura (consistent with known poor pleural penetration); ethambutol failed to reach critical concentrations in brain, kidney, bone, and skin; isoniazid exceeded thresholds in all compartments, with slow acetylators maintaining higher levels longer; and pyrazinamide never reached its critical concentration in any compartment.

Limitations include assumptions of no drug-drug interactions, no rifampicin autoinduction, a single consolidated lymph node compartment, and identical pharmacokinetics in TB and non-TB patients. The authors suggest the model could guide optimization of EPTB treatment regimens and serve as a foundation for future PBPK studies of EPTB drug distribution.

The court found the motions to quash were untimely and meritless, as a sheriff's wife serving on a grand jury does not render it illegally constituted. The denial of trial counsel's withdrawal motion was within the court's discretion given its proximity to trial. Severance was not required because the offenses were connected and mutually relevant. Bryson waived objections to the no contest plea's admission, and the plea was admissible to prove his conviction for registration purposes. Finally, Bryson waived his ineffective assistance claim by declining to pursue it at the motion for new trial hearing despite the court's warning.

Image registration is a non-linear inverse problem that finds a coordinate transform to align a moving image to a fixed image, minimizing a dissimilarity function plus regularization. It is fundamental for biomedical applications including multimodal data fusion, cross-subject comparison, and atlas construction.

Recent advances in ultra-high resolution imaging (MRI, CT, PET, microscopy) have produced images requiring up to 11B transform parameters, whereas existing registration methods reliably handle only ~50M parameters due to memory and compute limitations.

This paper applies concepts from large-scale transformer training (IO-awareness, shared memory usage, distributed optimization) to image registration. The contributions are: (1) identifying compute and memory bottlenecks and proposing components fitting problems 64× larger on a single GPU, and (2) Flash Fused Distributed Primitives (FFDP), a framework scaling registration to arbitrary GPU counts.

Key components include: a composite implicit grid sampler reducing memory from O(n) to O(1); implicit Parzen windowing for Mutual Information loss with O(1) HBM overhead; efficient fused cross-correlation reducing memory by 76.5%; Grid Parallel sharding with boundary synchronization; and a distributed Ring Sampler for interpolation across GPUs without allgather operations. Distributed versions of MSE, LNCC, and MI losses are also proposed.

Experiments demonstrate aligning a 250µm in-vivo MRI to a 100µm ex-vivo human brain FLASH volume (11.8B parameters) in approximately one minute using 8 A6000 GPUs. FFDP accelerates traditional pipelines up to 7.48× with 59% less memory, and deep learning pipelines up to 6.14× with 24% less memory. On the synthesized faux-OASIS dataset at 250µm, the method improves Dice by 18.1 points and reduces AvgHD90 by 62.1% compared to baselines, while requiring up to 500× fewer GPU-hours.

This paper investigates the relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data (BD), and Advanced Analytics (AA) within digital business platforms, addressing a gap in managerial research on AI innovation. Using a methodology combining literature review and semi-structured expert interviews with Russian National Technology Initiative members, the author developed a multidimensional, taxonomy-based framework.

The research defines AI as a digital innovation powered by BD and AA that transforms enterprise products, services, and business models. It identifies seven overlapping technological platforms supporting digital business, including Information Systems, Customer Experience, Data and Analytics, IoT, Ecosystems, Trust, and Integration platforms.

Key contributions include: (1) an AI/BD/AA micro-level value chain covering data acquisition, curation, storage, and usage; and (2) a multidimensional data-driven AI enterprise maturity framework with five levels ranging from Human Led/Initial Analytics to Machine Controlled/Advanced Analytics IV, each corresponding to different stages of the AI/BD/AA value chain.

The framework helps organizations identify use cases for AI automation, evaluate human-machine relationships, and plan investments. The author emphasizes the importance of ethical considerations and broad participation in shaping AI development to ensure beneficial outcomes for organizations and society.

The AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 has multiple known issues:

- SSMI events may not be synchronous if an IRQ occurs simultaneously; resolution is to use the Geode GX processor instead.
- PIO access to CD-ROM with UDMA bus master enabled first will fail; normal UDMA procedure must be followed.
- Most wake event inputs (GPIO[27:24]) do not function in ACPI S3 state; PWRBTN# should be used with external OR circuitry.
- RTC CMOS RAM may read incorrect data when extended and legacy ports are accessed in a specific sequence; no resolution.
- Block and demand mode legacy DMA to LPC devices fails; single transfer mode should be used.
- USB Controller clock gating causes register read failures; clock gating must be disabled.
- ATAPI packet commands after bus master enable can fail on certain CD-ROM firmware; no resolution.
- AuxOutputFull bit is incorrectly cleared on Port 60h reads; interrupts should be used for USB PS/2 emulation.
- tACK bits do not affect UDMA IDE_DACK setup timing, which is fixed at 30 ns; no action required.
- ATAC may hang with WORD-aligned PRDs; drivers should use DWORD alignment.
- LPC controller may abort transactions on certain SYNC patterns; a PLD workaround is available.
- NEGACK status bit in the SMB controller behaves incorrectly; two writes to SMB_STS are required.
- GLPCI retry counter counts all PCI retries, not just its own; limit should be increased or disabled.
- Atomic writes to GPIO High Bank Feature Bit Registers after suspend clear non-selected bits; Read-Modify-Write should be used.
- SMBus data hold time is shorter than the 300 ns specification requires.
- LOWBAT_FLAG is not set after abnormal standby; no resolution.
- Sleep_X/Y signals may not deassert if delays exceed PM_SED; delay counters must be programmed to lower values.

Ulysses S. Gandy appealed his second manslaughter conviction following a June 1976 two-car collision that killed three occupants of the other vehicle. Gandy raised four assignments of error: insufficient evidence, refusal of a jury instruction on intoxication factors, improper admission of sketches, and failure to grant a jury recess during deliberations.

The Mississippi Supreme Court rejected each claim. Although testimony conflicted regarding the position of the vehicles after impact and Gandy's intoxication, nine witnesses described signs of intoxication, and evidence suggested Gandy was in the wrong lane on a straight stretch of road. The court held this sufficient to support a jury finding of culpable negligence under Mississippi Code Annotated section 97-3-47, defined as negligence evincing reckless disregard for human life.

The court found the refused jury instruction unnecessary since other instructions adequately addressed intoxication. The admitted sketches were deemed appropriate, as witnesses used them only to illustrate personally observed scenes rather than reconstruct the collision. The recess claim was rejected as unsupported by authority.

The judgment was affirmed.

The authors developed a meta-population model to examine whether Google Community Mobility Reports (GCMR) can explain SARS-CoV-2 transmission dynamics. The model related four GCMR settings (Grocery and pharmacy, Retail and recreation, Transit stations, Workplaces) additively to transmissibility, while temperature and virus variants acted multiplicatively. Residential and Park settings were excluded due to implausible linearity assumptions.

Applied to 11 Norwegian and 21 Swedish regions (Feb 2020–July 2021), the model attributed 60% of infections in Sweden and 39% in Norway to contacts captured by GCMRs, with Transit stations and Workplaces contributing most. A 20°C temperature increase reduced transmissibility by about 40%, the Delta variant roughly doubled transmissibility, and the Alpha variant showed a modest increase in Norway only.

When applied to Bavaria and Berlin (Feb–Dec 2020), GCMRs explained about 65% of infections, but Retail and recreation was the most influential setting, unlike in Norway and Sweden.

Limitations include assumed linearity between activity and contacts, constant relationships over time, and potential GCMR measurement errors. The authors conclude that GCMRs are useful for real-time activity assessment, though more direct contact measurements would be preferable.

Reagan accepts the Republican nomination for the Presidency, thanking Texas and Dallas for their hospitality. He frames the election as a choice between two visions: Republican hope, confidence, and growth versus Democratic pessimism, fear, and limits.

Reagan closes with imagery of the Olympic torch's journey across America and the Statue of Liberty's torch, symbolizing national unity and opportunity.

Grief is an emotional reaction to losing someone or something you care about, and it is a highly personal experience that varies by individual. Grief can also occur in response to significant life changes, such as becoming a carer, retirement, or declining health.

Anticipatory grief may occur before an impending loss, such as a terminal diagnosis, affecting both the person dying and their loved ones. Grief can also arise from leaving a long-term home, particularly following bereavement; major moving decisions should ideally be deferred for several months.

Although grief was once thought to follow sequential stages, it is now understood to be complex and variable. Common reactions include numbness, denial, acceptance and relief, yearning, repeatedly recounting the event, restlessness, disturbed sleep, loss of confidence, guilt, anger, and profound sadness or depression. Support from others often lessens over time, but those closest may continue to struggle. Seeking help from a GP or specialist is advised if depression develops.

There is no set duration for grief. While the pain of loss remains, most people eventually experience more good days than bad. Grieving can be especially difficult for older people.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition device featuring two data averaging modes: simple averaging (which halves output data rate) and moving averaging (which does not affect output data rate). Test patterns (fixed pattern, digital ramp, and alternating pattern) can replace ADC output data for debugging, configured separately for channel groups CH[4:1] and CH[8:5] via registers in bank 1.

The device can be powered down via the PWDN pin or register write, and reset via the RESET pin or register. After power-up or reset, an initialization sequence of register writes is required with a free-running sampling clock connected. A speed-boost mode enables up to 8MSPS sampling for a user-selected channel pair while idling the other six channels.

Registers are organized into three banks accessed via an 8-bit address, with bank 0 always accessible. Writing requires selecting the bank through register 0x03, while reading requires enabling SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE bits. Multiple devices can be connected in a daisy-chain topology, with register operations requiring N × 24 SCLKs per SPI frame, where N equals the number of ADCs.

The ADS9803 has a post-calibration TUE of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C and offers two bandwidth modes: low-noise (up to 22.7kHz) and wide-bandwidth (up to 700kHz), the latter settling to 99.95% full-scale in 7.5µs. It uses three separate power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence, and recommends 0.1μF ceramic bypass capacitors near supply pins.

Researchers led by Joshua Caldwell of Vanderbilt University have improved the quality of hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), an optical material used in hyperlensing, by making crystals from isotopically purified boron. Reported in Nature Materials on Dec. 11, the advance reduces optical losses and triples the lifetime of surface phonon polaritons, enhancing imaging potential tenfold. The purified crystal could theoretically image objects as small as 30 nanometers. Unlike electron or atomic-force microscopes, hyperlenses use low-energy infrared light, making them compatible with living cells in natural environments and capable of providing spectroscopic "fingerprinting." Researchers anticipate further improvements with larger crystals, with potential applications in biology, medicine, communications, and nanoscale optics.

Beating the offside trap in soccer requires attackers to recognize when defenders are moving up rather than retreating, and to adjust their play to avoid being called offside while exploiting the space behind defenders. Recognition comes from scouting or noticing frequent offside calls, while patience prevents unnecessary offside positions.

Several tactics can beat the trap: dribbling through after faking a pass; executing a through pass to an onside receiver; making horizontal, checking, deep-lying, bending, or delayed runs; playing short or back passes; and delaying through possession. For free kicks, a designated "non-runner" can fake a run and return for a short pass.

Fakes may prompt defenders to reveal the trap. If one defender fails to move up, attackers must quickly capitalize. A successful breakthrough typically creates a one-on-one with the goalkeeper, and opponents are less likely to attempt the trap again afterward.

Scientists reporting in Environmental Science & Technology have found that sea snails called periwinkles may adapt to increasingly acidic oceans. As oceans absorb carbon dioxide, pH levels decrease, reducing the carbonate ions needed by calcifying organisms like coral and oysters to build shells and skeletons. Sean D. Connell and colleagues exposed periwinkles to acidity levels predicted for 2100 (pH 7.85, down from today's 8.10). Although the snails' metabolism slowed, they accelerated shell production by creating less-dense inner shells and developed less-soluble shells more resistant to harsh conditions. Researchers suggest periwinkles and potentially other calcifying organisms may be able to adapt to ocean acidification.

China has blacklisted Canadian firm TechInsights and nine subsidiaries, adding them to its "unreliable entity list" after the company published an analysis of Huawei's advanced AI chips. Barron's Jack Hough argues Netflix shares could lose more than half their value due to competition from Disney's upcoming streaming services, Facebook's video content, and Amazon Prime, along with Netflix's cash burn and accounting practices. A study published in Pediatrics found that from 1990 to 2015, nearly 17,000 US children under age 6 were treated in emergency rooms for window blind-related injuries, with about one child dying per month. While most injuries were minor, entanglement—mostly in cords—accounted for nearly 80% of hospitalizations and 94% of deaths. Most incidents occurred at home, unwitnessed, often while children were unsupervised briefly. Dr. Gary Smith, the study's senior author, argues that the voluntary safety standard in place since 1996 is insufficient and advocates for mandatory requirements that window blinds have inaccessible or unexposed cords. In 2014, the US Consumer Product Safety Commission approved developing a mandatory standard, though rulemaking remains in early stages. In 2017, the Window Covering Manufacturers Association proposed revising voluntary standards to require stock products—over 80% of the market—to be cordless or have inaccessible cords, with compliance expected in late 2018. Linda Kaiser of Parents for Window Blind Safety also supports a mandatory rule, stating cords should be eliminated entirely.

Management of hospitalized patients is largely supportive, with only dexamethasone and tocilizumab demonstrating mortality benefits, while remdesivir shows limited impact. Convalescent plasma from recovered donors may provide passive immunization, though a meta-analysis found no mortality benefit amid significant study heterogeneity. The researchers hypothesized that early administration of high-volume, high-neutralizing-antibody-titer convalescent plasma would reduce mechanical ventilation needs. The study's primary objective was evaluating clinical efficacy and safety of convalescent plasma plus supportive care versus supportive care alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, with secondary objectives assessing clinical severity, oxygenation, ventilation, and hospitalization. The NAAIM Exposure Index, compiled by the National Association of Active Investment Managers, tracks the average US equity market exposure reported by its members through a weekly survey, displayed as a two-week moving average. Investing when weekly readings were below the 10-week moving average yielded a CAGR of only 4.4% (2.5% excluding dividends). Varying the moving average length and testing extreme readings did not significantly improve results, suggesting other indicators, such as the VIX, perform better for contrarian strategies.

This study used EEG to investigate whether increased neural noise underlies tic occurrence in Tourette syndrome (TS). Twenty adults with TS and 19 matched neurologically healthy controls received single-pulse median nerve electrical stimulation (MNS) while EEG was recorded. Neural noise was operationalised as trial-by-trial variability in the magnitude and timing of somatosensory evoked potentials (SEPs).

Key findings were: (1) the amplitude, timing, and topography of most early and mid-latency SEP components did not differ between groups, and timing variability was not increased in the TS group; (2) the P2 (P100) SEP component was significantly larger in the TS group and correlated with tic severity, consistent with tactile hypersensitivity in TS; (3) trial-by-trial variability (standard deviation) was substantially higher in the TS group throughout the trial, not only post-stimulation; (4) Power Spectral Density analysis showed flatter 1/f slopes in the TS group at beta and gamma frequencies, indicating increased neural noise; (5) coefficient of variation decreased comparably in both groups following stimulation; (6) inter-trial phase coherence increased post-stimulation in both groups, though alpha-band coherence was less sustained in the TS group, while beta-band coherence was elevated around the P100 window.

The authors conclude that sensorimotor neural recruitment is less stable at rest in TS, likely linked to altered GABAergic inhibition and dysfunctional striatal-thalamic activity, but normalises following stimulation.

Facebook has publicly released a detailed 8,000-word version of its community standards, previously kept internal, outlining rules on topics such as drug use, sex work, bullying, hate speech, and violence. A federal jury cleared retired Little Rock police lieutenant David Hudson of excessive force accusations after about two hours of deliberation. Hudson was filmed in October 2011 punching Jon "Chris" Erwin seven times outside Ferneau restaurant in Little Rock's Hillcrest neighborhood, with the video viewed thousands of times on social media and contributing to national debate over police use of force.

The jury of seven women and four men unanimously found the force reasonable from Hudson's perspective. Hudson testified he was asked by a bartender to remove unruly people who had crashed a private party. He said Erwin approached him demanding to know who complained, became agitated, refused orders, and put his hands on him, prompting the arrest and punches to avoid knocking him down. Witnesses described Erwin's group as appearing intoxicated and disruptive, though Erwin and his friend Blake Mitchell denied drinking much.

Misdemeanor charges against Erwin and Mitchell were later dropped for procedural reasons, though Judge James Moody Jr. did not allow testimony about the dismissal. The city of Little Rock and Ferneau's owner settled Erwin's claims before trial. Former police chief Stuart Thomas testified that officers were permitted to use such force when reasonable. Hudson, now a Pulaski County Circuit Court bailiff, said he felt vindicated, while Erwin maintained he was a victim of excessive force.

Texas Monthly's November 2001 article "How Enron Blew It" by Mimi Swartz chronicles the rise and decline of Houston-based Enron. Founded from the 1985 merger of Houston Natural Gas and InterNorth under CEO Ken Lay, Enron transformed from a pipeline company into a trading powerhouse, with stock prices rising 1,700 percent and revenues reaching $100 billion by 2000.

The transformation was largely engineered by Jeff Skilling, hired as a McKinsey consultant in 1985. Skilling created the Gas Bank, which guaranteed gas supply and prices, and built a trading-based business model. He cultivated an aggressive corporate culture that recruited elite graduates, offered uncapped merit bonuses, and employed a harsh "rank and yank" Performance Review Committee that replaced 15 percent of staff annually.

Enron expanded into electricity, broadband, water, and online commodity trading. The company used mark-to-market accounting and booked long-term profits upfront. Skilling became CEO in February 2001, pushing out rival Rebecca Mark, whose asset-heavy international projects, including a troubled Indian power plant, conflicted with his vision.

Problems emerged in 2001: Enron was blamed for California's energy crisis, its telecommunications division collapsed with the tech bubble, the Blockbuster deal failed, and analysts questioned its accounting. Stock dropped from $80 in January to around $35. Skilling resigned abruptly after six months, citing personal sacrifices. Lay resumed as CEO, promising reforms to the culture and business focus.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2018, with 485,226,904 shares of common stock outstanding as of April 18, 2018. Total net sales increased 43% to $51.0 billion in Q1 2018 from $35.7 billion in Q1 2017, with net income rising to $1.63 billion from $724 million. Key activities included the completion of the Whole Foods Market purchase price allocation and the April 12, 2018 acquisition of Ring Inc. for approximately $900 million. The company continues to contest IRS transfer pricing adjustments and a European Commission state aid decision, having deposited approximately €250 million into escrow in March 2018. This work addresses process modeling in Materials Science and Engineering (MSE), where the processing–structure–properties–performance paradigm requires accurate representation of material transformations. Despite numerous ontologies developed for this purpose, interoperability and reuse remain limited, particularly due to insufficient adoption of Ontology Design Patterns (ODPs).

The authors surveyed relevant ontologies (PMDcore, GPO, WILD, P-PLAN, Metadata4Ing, OPMW) and defined three core requirements: Process Structure, Data and Resources, and Project Goals and Participant Roles. ODPs were manually extracted, reviewed by nine domain experts from the NFDI-MatWerk Linked Open Data Working Group, and mapped to these requirements.

A baseline automated extraction method was proposed using semantic similarity with sentence transformer embeddings (hkunlp/instructor-large), combined with ROBOT's STAR modularization. Evaluation using precision, recall, and F1-score showed P-PLAN performed best for Process and Resource ODPs, while PMDcore uniquely supported all three ODP categories.

Limitations include bias toward ontologies with richer annotations, sensitivity to requirement phrasing, and isolated per-ontology processing. Future work will expand to additional MSE subdomains, integrate cross-ontology mappings, use controlled vocabularies, and develop a platform for publishing extracted patterns.

In July 2021, Public Health Wales investigated a salmonella outbreak following an Eid al-Adha barbecue in Cardiff attended by a North African community. A cohort study of 36 attendees and a nested case-control study using Firth logistic regression identified 22 symptomatic cases, with 12 seeking emergency care and six hospitalised. Consumption of "marrara," a traditional raw liver dish, was the most likely infection vehicle (aOR: 49.99, 95%CI 1.71-1461.54). Whole genome sequencing showed identical Salmonella Typhimurium sequences in human samples, raw lamb from two local butchers, and the supplying abattoir. Contributing factors included hot weather, undercooked lamb, and cross-contamination from raw liver marinade. The investigation linked cases to a broader five-SNP cluster dating to 2018, including individuals with sheep farm contact. Public Health Wales collaborated with the community to develop culturally sensitive food safety messaging, released in multiple languages around World Food Safety Day and Eid al-Adha. The outbreak highlights the need for outbreak investigations to consider culturally specific dishes beyond routine questionnaires.

The Coppock Curve, developed by economist E.S.C. Coppock in 1965 for the Episcopal Church, is a smoothed momentum indicator used primarily to identify long-term stock market swings. It is calculated as a 10-month weighted moving average of the sum of 11-month and 14-month rate-of-change indicators, with periods based on Coppock's estimate of mourning recovery time.

A long entry is triggered when the curve crosses above zero, and an exit when it crosses below. Backtesting on the S&P 500 monthly chart since 1960 produced only 12 trades, all winners. The strategy showed reduced drawdown, less market exposure, and better risk-adjusted returns than a buy-and-hold approach.

The passage describes memory mapping and pin configurations for the TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processor. It references the L4 Fast and L4 Slow Peripheral Domain memory maps, noting that certain regions are decoded internally by the Cortex-A8 Subsystem and reserved for other masters.

The DDR DMM TILER Extended Addressing Map provides an additional 4-GByte range via a 33rd address bit for accessing rotated and mirrored frame buffer views, accessible only to the HDVPSS and ISS subsystems, though other masters can access a single view through the 512-MB TILER region.

The terminal functions tables identify external signal names, pin multiplexing, pin numbers, pin types, internal pullup/pulldown resistors, supply voltages, and pin functions. Several GPMC pins are multiplexed between ARM Cortex-A8 boot mode and GPMC peripheral functions, with BTMODE bits sampled at reset to determine configurations including GPMC_Wait enable, Address/Data multiplexing, Data Bus Width, RSTOUT_WD_OUT behavior, XIP (NOR) options, and Ethernet PHY mode. After reset, these pins function as GPMC multiplexed data/address pins.

This lecture on sustainable real estate finance covers three main topics: the big picture of sustainable finance, mortgages (debt side), and private equity.

The sustainable finance field emerged prominently in 2020 when BlackRock CEO Larry Fink declared climate risk as financial risk, emphasizing fiduciary responsibility to manage future climate risks. Capital flows through a layered system: individuals direct money to institutional investors, who then invest in assets via equity or debt instruments.

The lecture connects capital and space markets using the four-quadrant model, where investors compare weighted average cost of capital against market returns to determine investment viability. Adding green buildings as a fourth asset class (alongside bonds, stocks, and conventional real estate) shifts the efficient frontier northwest, offering higher returns with lower risk. True green assets command higher NOI due to regulations (e.g., Local Law 97) and tenant preferences, while requiring lower discount rates due to reduced risk. Early investors ("frontrunners") capture excess returns before market equilibrium adjusts.

On mortgages, climate risk increases default risk when property values fall below loan values, as demonstrated by Wallace's research on California wildfires showing 1% default increases. Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac face challenges pricing climate risk, creating tension between accurate risk assessment and social equity concerns for low-income borrowers in risky areas.

Green mortgages represent the positive side: banks offer larger loans at lower rates for energy-efficient homes because higher property values improve loan-to-value ratios, and lower energy bills free up income for loan repayment. Research confirms energy-efficient homes have one-third lower default rates, with stronger effects for low-income households. The EU's renovation wave applies similar logic, allowing banks to lend more upfront based on expected post-renovation value appreciation.

The lecture concludes by introducing private equity real estate, noting that firms increasingly incorporate ESG into investment memos, aligning social and business value.

A blitz is a defensive play where five or more defenders rush the quarterback to disrupt the offense, rather than the standard four rushers. Blitzes carry risk because fewer defenders remain to cover receivers, but well-timed blitzes can significantly impact a game.

Defensive coordinators call plays and use blitzes strategically to get off the field quickly. Common types include:

- **Zone blitz**: A linebacker rushes while a lineman drops into coverage, confusing blocking assignments.
- **Safety blitz**: A safety rushes, leaving a gap in deep coverage.
- **Cornerback blitz**: Similar to a safety blitz, using a cornerback.
- **Zero blitz**: No deep safety; used when expecting a run.
- **Run blitz**: Aimed at stopping run plays at the point of attack.

Offenses counter blitzes through quick passes (often to running backs), mobile quarterbacks who evade rushers, or max protection schemes that keep extra blockers in. Quarterbacks must identify blitzes and exploit the resulting weak points in coverage.

- Buying when the bull-bear spread turned negative and holding four weeks returned 0.68% per trade (70% cumulative).

Rapid technological and social changes make lifelong learning essential for Library and Information Science (LIS) professionals in Romania, where libraries are subordinated to the Ministries of Education and Culture and represented by two professional associations.

LIS academic education, ignored during communism, began in 1999 and now exists at four universities. Romanian law recognises three training paths for librarians: (a) a Bachelor's in LIS, whose graduates mostly work in academic libraries but suffer from low prestige and salaries; (b) a Bachelor's in another field plus a post-graduation LIS programme, the most common route, though paradoxically classified as lifelong education while functioning as initial training; (c) a Bachelor's in another field plus competences assessed via occupational standards, favoured by public libraries but criticised for weak certification.

Non-formal training includes library visits, conferences, and mentorship. Although the Law of Libraries requires institutions to allocate 5% of personnel expenses to training, few comply; only 10% of 2016 post-graduates at West University of Timisoara received employer funding.

In 2012, the National Library of Romania developed the Occupational Standard "Librarian (Higher Education)", approved by the National Authority for Qualifications. It defines eight key competences (C1–C8), three general competences (G1–G3), and two specific ones (S1–S2), covering communication, IT, culture, and document management. It also specifies professional activities including collection development, cataloguing, conservation, automation, digitalisation, research, and promotion.

The authors recommend adding competences in internationalisation, multiculturalism, information literacy education, and reading promotion. Negative stereotypes about librarianship deter youth, requiring institutions to update their programmes.

The passage introduces a theoretical and empirical framework for information design that integrates framing effects with the classic Bayesian persuasion model, leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs).

The authors note that traditional Bayesian persuasion, pioneered by Kamenica and Gentzkow, focuses solely on quantitative correlations between signals and world states. However, behavioral economics research, including Tversky and Kahneman's work, shows that human decisions are also shaped by framing—such as phrasing, tangential information, and non-textual cues. LLMs are proposed as tools to address the linguistic complexity of framing.

The proposed model extends Bayesian persuasion by introducing a framing space C, where each framing induces a receiver belief. Three optimization variants are considered: (a) recommendation-only, (b) framing-only, and (c) joint framing and recommendation optimization.

Theoretically, the authors show that framing-only optimization is computationally hard (NP-hard) and discontinuous in induced beliefs, making it sensitive to oracle errors. In contrast, joint optimization yields a continuous utility function and admits a quasi-polynomial-time approximation scheme (QPTAS), making it more tractable.

Empirically, the authors propose a hill-climbing method using LLMs both to optimize framing and act as belief oracles. Two case studies—a realtor pitching to buyers and a clothing brand's advertising campaign—demonstrate the method's effectiveness, validated through human subject studies that confirm directionally correct predictions.

The work contributes a formal integration of behavioral framing into information design, offering a scalable, algorithmic alternative to heuristic-driven persuasive communication design, with potential extensions to non-textual media.

The adapter pattern is a single-node pattern in which an adapter container modifies an application container's interface to conform to a predefined standard, enabling consistent monitoring, logging, or health-checking across heterogeneous applications. Examples include using Prometheus exporters to standardize metrics (e.g., for Redis), fluentd plugins to normalize logs from Redis or Apache Storm, and custom containers to add rich health checks to databases like MySQL. Keeping adapters in separate containers supports modularity, reuse, independent resource allocation, and sharing across teams.

Multi-node distributed patterns are more loosely coupled, communicating via network calls. Microservices architectures split applications into small, independently developed and scaled services with formal APIs, improving agility and scalability but complicating debugging and design.

The replicated load-balanced service pattern uses identical stateless replicas behind a load balancer, requiring at least two replicas for high availability and readiness probes to signal when instances can serve traffic. Session tracked services route a user's requests consistently to the same replica, often via consistent hashing. Caching layers (e.g., Varnish) and SSL termination layers (e.g., nginx) can be added as additional replicated tiers for performance, rate limiting, and security.

Sharded services distribute data across replicas, each serving only a subset of requests, enabling scaling of stateful services beyond single-machine capacity. Sharded caches increase effective cache storage but lose redundancy; replicated sharded caches combine both approaches for resilience. Sharding functions must be deterministic and uniform, with carefully chosen keys; consistent hashing minimizes remapping when shard counts change. Hot sharding dynamically rebalances replicas in response to uneven loads.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing across leaf nodes, with a root aggregating partial responses. It suits embarrassingly parallel problems like distributed document search and can be combined with sharding for large data sets. However, parallelism gains are asymptotic due to per-node overhead and the "straggler problem," where overall latency is bounded by the slowest leaf. Replicating shards improves reliability and scale.

Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) supports event-driven, serverless computing, simplifying deployment and automatic scaling but complicating debugging, background processing, stateful workloads, and cost at sustained load. FaaS patterns include the decorator pattern (transforming requests/responses, e.g., adding defaults), event handling (e.g., two-factor authentication), and event-based pipelines.

The lecture covers the second-order wave equation utt = c²uxx, presented both as a second-order equation and as a first-order system with a symmetric matrix having eigenvalues c and -c, representing waves traveling in both directions.

The professor notes that real-world wave problems involve variable coefficients, forcing terms, and high frequencies that create numerical challenges due to the kΔx error term requiring small Δx.

The general continuous solution combines functions of (x-ct) and (x+ct), with no dispersion since all frequencies travel at the same speed. Dispersion appears in discrete methods, causing oscillating errors.

For the semidiscrete method (method of lines), space is discretized while time remains continuous. Substituting exponentials yields a factor involving 2-2cos(kΔx)/Δx², which equals 4sin²(kΔx/2)/Δx². This sinc function approximates k for small kΔx, confirming second-order accuracy.

For the fully discrete method, substituting ujn = gⁿe^(ijkΔx) produces a quadratic equation g² - 2ag + 1 = 0, where a depends on r² = (cΔt/Δx)². Solving gives g = a ± √(a²-1). When a < 1, the roots are complex with |g|² = 1 (stable); when a > 1, roots exceed 1 (unstable). This reduces to the Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy condition r ≤ 1.

The next lecture will cover staggered grids.

This study demonstrates high-energy (1 MeV) electron beam irradiation as a controlled method for defect engineering in monolayer MoS2. CVD-grown MoS2 samples were irradiated for 30s, 60s, and 120s, and characterized using Raman, PL, XPS, KPFM spectroscopy, and first-principles calculations.

Key findings include:
- Raman spectra revealed shifts in E¹₂g and A1g modes and increased LO(M) mode intensity, indicating sulfur vacancy formation.
- XPS analysis showed the emergence of Mo⁵⁺ and Mo⁶⁺ oxidation states, confirming oxygen incorporation at sulfur vacancy sites.
- KPFM measurements revealed a work function increase from 4.8 eV to 5.24 eV, indicating p-type doping.
- Temperature and power-dependent PL spectra showed defect-bound emissions 200–300 meV below the A exciton, which intensified with irradiation time, accompanied by quenching of free exciton emission.
- Circular polarization-resolved PL measurements showed valley polarization decreased from 62% to 38% with increasing defects.
- First-principles calculations confirmed that oxygen interactions at sulfur vacancies produce acceptor states near the valence band, supporting the observed p-type behavior and defect peak.

The methodology offers precise defect density control and can be extended to other TMDs for optoelectronic and quantum device applications.

The Wing-T is a deception-based offense that uses misdirection, unusual formations, and a diverse run game to exploit aggressive defenders. Developed by Coach Harold "Tubby" Raymond at the University of Delaware between 1966 and 2001, it requires at least two capable running backs, an athletic quarterback, and quick, agile offensive linemen rather than elite passers or large linemen.

Its strengths include slowing down more talented defenses through misdirection and its rarity in modern football. Its main weakness is the lack of a traditional dropback passing game, though coaches often supplement it with shotgun spread formations.

Common formations include the Wing (100/900), Wing-Slot ("Red" or "Doubles 100"), and Unbalanced formations. Signature running plays are the Buck Sweep, Down (Belly G), and Trap. Common pass plays include the Waggle (designed to mimic the Buck Sweep), single receiver option routes, and play action vertical passes.

While largely extinct in major college football, the Wing-T remains popular at the high school level. Coaches like Gus Malzahn have integrated its principles into modern spread offenses.

The ADS868xW device operates across several states including ACQ (acquisition), CONV (conversion), and RESET states, with transitions controlled by RST and CONVST/CS signals. The device offers a low-power NAP mode and deep power-down (PD) mode to reduce consumption.

The device contains nine configuration registers and supports data write and read operations through a multiSPI interface. Data transfer frames begin on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and end on the rising edge. Frames with 32 SCLKs are optimal, while shorter or longer frames are handled differently, with long frames enabling daisy-chain operation.

Input commands include HWORD variants (CLEAR_HWORD, READ_HWORD, WRITE, SET_HWORD) which operate on 16 bits, ignoring the LSB of the 9-bit address. Output data can include appended flags such as device address, range, alarm flags, and parity bits, configured via the DATAOUT_CTL_REG register.

The device supports four SPI-compatible protocols (SPI-00-S through SPI-11-S) for configuration, defaulting to SPI-00-S on power-up. Read protocols include legacy SPI with single or dual SDO-x and source-synchronous (SRC) protocols using internal or external clocks.

Configuration registers include DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG, SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, ALARM_REG, ALARM_H_TH_REG, and ALARM_L_TH_REG, controlling identification, reset/power, interface protocols, data output, input ranges, and alarm thresholds with hysteresis.

Application examples include a 16-bit, 8-channel analog input module for PLCs, combining the ADS8681W with the MUX36D08 multiplexer to handle industrial voltage and current ranges (±2.5V to ±10V, 0-20mA). The device features programmable input and AVDD alarms with hysteresis for noise immunity, useful in temperature sensing applications.

Led by the CEO, COO, and CTO, the GSC oversees later-stage innovation programs, allocates resources across businesses, paces investments, and maintains portfolio balance. The article explores a trading strategy for the Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF (BOTZ), founded in 2016, as a vehicle for gaining exposure to the robotics and AI industry. The strategy combines Donchian Channels as a short-term momentum indicator with an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) filter to reduce false signals. It is a long-only strategy.

Through optimization testing on daily timeframes since September 2016, the author selects a Donchian Channel length of 3 and an EMA of 200, noting that optimization should focus on robustness rather than finding perfect values to avoid curve fitting. Results showed profitability across most settings, with the EMA filter improving performance.

The resulting strategy outperformed Buy and Hold with lower volatility and showed promising results on a 2-hour timeframe as well. However, the author cautions that the low number of trades (87) reduces statistical reliability and increases curve-fitting risk. Out-of-sample backtesting and an incubation period are recommended before live trading, as short-term strategies are particularly challenging to validate.

Fabry-Perot (FP) cavities are widely used optical devices, but traditional high-performance mirrors are too large for compact systems, motivating microfabrication methods. This work presents a simple, scalable fabrication method for visible-wavelength microcavities using buckled dielectric membrane mirrors on silicon wafers. The process involves wet thermal smoothing of a silicon wafer, deposition of 21 SiO2/Ta2O5 quarter-wave stacks by ion beam sputtering, and backside etching to suspend the dielectric coating, which buckles due to compressive strain. The resulting mirrors are rotationally symmetric with radii of curvature from 0.9 to 21 mm and surface roughness ≤90 pm.

Using a swept-ring-down method at 780.24 nm, the authors measured a maximum finesse of 0.89×10⁶ and a maximum quality factor of 2.3×10⁹. Finesse decreased with increasing cavity length due to diffractive losses. Extrapolated to telecom wavelengths, finesse would reach 3.5×10⁶. Compact cavity assemblies (as small as 2 mm³) were created by gluing mirror chips together, achieving linewidths of 5.16 MHz with a 3.18 THz FSR.

The authors conclude these microcavities are suitable for quantum networking with neutral atoms and trapped ions, as well as classical applications such as filters, transfer cavities, and laser stabilization.

The disclosure relates to digital twin simulations, presenting a computer-implemented method, system, and computer program product for executing simulations that can bypass selected input parameters. A digital twin is a virtual representation of a physical asset that mirrors real-time changes captured through sensors and IoT devices.

The method involves capturing real-time data from collection devices connected to a physical asset, creating a digital twin model, and generating multiple versions reflecting changes over time. Users can configure simulations by selecting a specific version, a previous version, or constructing a hybrid model combining components from multiple digital twin versions. Simulations can be customized by bypassing selected components, substituting alternatives, or inputting overriding values for non-simulated portions to serve as intermediate results.

The system architecture includes a host system running a digital twin module containing a creation engine, data collection engine, version management, simulation engine, and reporting engine. It can be deployed in containerized or cloud environments. Augmented reality devices may assist users in building hybrid models and selecting components.

The algorithm processes requests to create or transfer digital twins, collects operational data, detects specification deviations prompting new model versions, configures simulations based on user selections, executes them, and outputs results that can be refined through parameter revisions.

With six defenders missing, Tisdale handed 20-year-old Jordan Storey his first league start, crediting coaches Matt Taylor and Andy Tillson for preparing the seventh-choice centre-back. Tisdale acknowledged Luton deserved the win but disagreed with the referee's decision to disallow Liam McAlinden's late equaliser due to a foul by Robbie Simpson on goalkeeper Marek Stech. He maintained that Exeter's form remained strong ahead of their match against Wycombe Wanderers.

The device's boot state is set by sampling BTMODE[15:0] pins when reset is de-asserted, with values latched into the CONTROL_STATUS register. BTMODE[15:11] configures GPMC CS0 data bus width, wait enable, and address/data multiplexing. BTMODE[4:0] determines boot mode order, executing primary through fourth boot modes sequentially until successful. BTMODE[7:5] are reserved and should be pulled down. BTMODE[9:8] selects Ethernet PHY Mode when EMAC bootmode is active, while BTMODE[10] selects GPMC pin muxing for XIP bootmodes.

WhatsApp, with 94% reach in India, appears to be building an ecosystem of products and services similar to China's WeChat, which offers services from food delivery to gaming. After introducing voice and video calls, payments is its next step. User engagement drives the mobile internet battle, with content—boosted by cheap data from Reliance Jio—being central. WhatsApp's attempt at Instagram-style 'stories' failed; professionally produced content may be a better option. Airtel-backed Hike, though well-placed, trails WhatsApp despite launching payments earlier, but could leverage Airtel TV and Wynk content. Gaming is another engagement tool, exemplified by Gamepind, a JV between AGTech Holdings and Paytm. India's internet is consolidating into an oligopoly backed by global conglomerates, and chat could be a defining battleground.

A security appliance is described that incorporates a local input/output interface, such as a touch screen, enabling command and control over network functionality and configuration without requiring network-based login from another device. During denial of service attacks, commands from the local interface are given priority access to processing resources and memory, allowing mitigating actions like shutting down ports, blacklisting sources, or modifying filter rules without manual reboot or network disconnection.

The appliance may apply packet processing rules via geoprocessing-based analysis, using minimum bounding rectangles (MBRs) and R-tree indexes to accelerate rule searching compared to B-tree searches, with multidimensional filter regions supporting multiple parameters simultaneously.

Rules may be distributed from a management server to security devices according to a statistical model, where mandatory rules for known threats are sent to all devices, while potential rules for inactive threats are randomly distributed to subsets of devices based on likelihood scores. This reduces memory, bandwidth, and CPU usage while enabling early attack detection.

The appliance may automatically quarantine communications from unrecognized devices on the network until a user physically authorizes them through the local interface, preventing unauthorized network-based configuration changes.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC reporting the results of its Annual Meeting of Shareholders held on March 10, 2015. Shareholders voted on six proposals: (1) elected seven directors—Tim Cook, Al Gore, Bob Iger, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Ron Sugar, and Sue Wagner; (2) ratified Ernst & Young LLP as the independent registered public accounting firm for 2015; (3) approved an advisory resolution on executive compensation; and (4) approved an amendment to the Employee Stock Purchase Plan increasing authorized shares by 50,000,000. Two shareholder proposals, "Risk Report" and "Proxy Access for Shareholders," were not approved. The report was signed by D. Bruce Sewell, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary, on March 13, 2015.

The federal government's review of phthalates concluded that none of the more than a dozen studied posed a risk to human health, with only one requiring further environmental study, according to Environment and Climate Change Canada. Phthalates are chemicals used in plastics and numerous commercial products. Muhannad Malas of Environmental Defence criticized the finding, noting the European Union has identified at least four phthalates as risks to human health. He said a key difference is that Europe requires manufacturers to prove products safe, while Canada requires proof that products are unsafe before restricting them. Last June, the House of Commons environment committee recommended modernizing the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, including adopting Europe's approach. Environment Minister Catherine McKenna stated the government is considering the recommendations and will present a plan by June 2018.

Standardized testing monopolies constrain the benefits of school choice by dictating curriculum and teaching approaches. Studies show educators alter instruction to match high-stakes tests, and some states extend this burden to private schools through choice programs. In Wisconsin and Texas, private school choice participants face requirements tied to public school assessments. College admissions tests like the ACT and SAT similarly dominate, with several states mandating them for graduation or scholarships.

These tests have reportedly declined in rigor, with the SAT aligning to Common Core and a 2024 study finding a 71-point drop in SAT math rigor from 2008 to 2023. AP Literature high scores rose 240 percent between 2021 and 2022 despite declining national reading scores.

Rather than banning standardized tests—an approach universities like MIT and Yale abandoned—the author advocates testing choice. The Classic Learning Test offers an alternative grounded in classic texts and correlates strongly (0.89) with SAT scores, enabling comparisons.

The author recommends states offer menus of assessments for school choice participants and accept multiple tests for college admissions and scholarships, citing Arkansas and Florida as examples.

The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments in a challenge to Colorado's 2019 Minor Conversion Therapy Law, which bans mental health professionals from providing conversion therapy to clients under 18. Kaley Chiles, a licensed counselor, argues the law violates her free speech rights because her therapy consists solely of talk, making the ban a content- and viewpoint-based restriction that should face strict scrutiny. She contends the law is not supported by evidence of harm and is neither narrowly tailored nor underinclusive, as it exempts religious ministry and unlicensed individuals.

The federal government, supporting Chiles, argues the law regulates speech as speech and urges remand for strict scrutiny review. Colorado counters that the law regulates a healthcare treatment—not speech—that has been found unsafe and ineffective, and should be reviewed under rational basis. The state argues the ban is narrow, targets only conversion therapy, and would survive strict scrutiny regardless. The 10th Circuit previously upheld the law, though one judge dissented, arguing the majority treated speech as conduct.

A new report by the Canadian Society of Palliative Care Physicians (CSPCP) argues that expanding palliative care services across Canada would improve patient care while reducing costs. CSPCP President Dr. David Henderson states such services would enable more efficient use of health care resources, particularly given Canada's aging population, with research suggesting a quarter of health care costs are spent in the last year of life.

The report cites findings that hospital-based palliative care saves $7,000-$8,000 per patient compared to usual care, and outpatient palliative services reduce costs by about 30%. A 2013 study projected that expanding in-home palliative care in Ontario could avoid $191-$385 million in health costs, while shifting patients to residential hospices could save roughly $600 per day.

The CSPCP has developed recommendations for governments to improve and monitor palliative care access across Canada.

AMP's new chairman David Murray, in a speech to the Australian Centre for Public Affairs, criticised the ASX corporate governance principles for causing declining governance standards in the financial sector. He argued the principles have evolved from broad guidelines into prescriptive, one-size-fits-all regulations, resulting in a "trust deficit." Murray said that despite an "if not, why not?" opt-out, companies simply conform, and institutions should redesign their governance mechanisms.

Gardaí in Louth are appealing for information about the murder of 18-year-old Cameron Reilly, whose body was found at Rivervale, Dunleer, on Saturday morning with neck injuries. He had been socialising with others the previous night. Officers are searching for his iPhone 8 Plus with a black and lime green cover, which they believe may contain relevant messages. Superintendent Andrew Watters stated the focus is on establishing the truth rather than any alcohol or drug use by young people, and urged those with information to come forward.

In a separate operation, gardaí seized a semi-automatic shotgun during a handover in west Dublin, arresting a 31-year-old man and a 53-year-old woman. Follow-up searches uncovered drugs valued at around €1m, including 6kg of heroin and 2kg of cocaine, along with cash and mixing agent. The operation was led by the Special Crime Task Force.

The seventh annual Johnston Press South Business Awards were held at Brighton's Grand Hotel, hosted by Nick Wallis. Chichester's Guardian Angel Carers won both Large Business of the Year and Overall Business of the Year, with managing director Christina Bassadone calling it a boost after a difficult year. Olive and Vine in Midhurst won the Place to Eat or Drink award, while Brandon Relph of Go Creative took Young Achiever. Southsea Bathing Hut won Retailer of the Year, and Talks at Six, which has raised over £7,500 for charity, received the Outstanding Contribution to the Community award. Additional winners spanned categories including Customer Service, Innovation, Green Business, Employer of the Year, and Lifetime Achievement.

In National Sheet Metal Company v. AAA Highway Express Incorporated (decided March 4, 1937), the plaintiff sought damages for injury to its automobile allegedly caused by the defendants' negligent operation of a vehicle at a street intersection. The court held:

1. The trial court adequately conveyed the plaintiff's allegations of negligence, including failure to sound a horn, by reciting them in the charge.

2. Absent a specific pleading or request, the court was not required to charge on right-of-way rules for vehicles approaching from the right.

3. Without allegations regarding failure to reduce speed at intersections, no such instruction was required. Instructing that both parties were lawfully entitled to use the highway was not error, especially given the accompanying ordinary care instruction.

4. Specific instructions regarding statutory and ordinance violations did not preclude consideration of other negligence claims.

5. Charging comparative negligence was proper where evidence supported findings of negligence by both parties, despite no such issue being pleaded.

6. Any error regarding the measure of damages was harmless given the defense verdict.

7. Evidence was conflicting, and the verdict for defendants was authorized.

Judgment affirmed.

The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has introduced FORM X to ease foreign exchange access for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and retail businesses. According to CBN spokesman Isaac Okorafor, the form requires only basic documentation, including a supporting application letter, beneficiary invoice, and bank wire transfer. The initiative aims to remove obstacles for those with forex needs of $10,000 or less, as the CBN continues efforts to ensure adequate forex supply for genuine transactions.

The patent application describes techniques for providing enhanced trick-play modes (fast-forward, rewind, slow motion) for streaming video content delivered from a server to a client.

A media guidance application maintains two types of buffers: a normal buffer window containing continuous video content for standard playback, and a trick-play window that buffers only selected video frames (typically key frames) at spaced intervals, without the intervening frames. This selective frame buffering enables faster-than-real-time playback with frequent frame updates, avoiding the need to stream entire video portions during trick-play operations.

The system uses metadata containing frame address information to identify specific frame locations within streams. Frame selection may be based on streaming performance metrics, playback rate, stream bitrate, and available bandwidth. Multiple trick-play windows of varying sizes and quality can be maintained for different playback rates.

Key components include: a video repository storing content items with potentially multiple bitrate streams; a streaming server (optionally HLS-compatible); an optional proxy server that generates indexes, metadata, and proxy streams for servers lacking native support; a video player; a streaming client; a performance monitor generating network metrics; and a trick-play optimizer that selects which individual frames to request.

The trick-play optimizer can request frames from different bitrate streams adaptively, create trick-play windows in response to user input or predicted jump points, and later expand the normal buffer window by requesting intervening frames without re-requesting already-buffered frames. The system also supports cached content at predefined jump points for discontinuous repositioning.

Breast cancer is the most common cancer in the UK, with around 56,000 new cases annually. Regular self-examination is important for early detection.

Breast lumps vary in feel—some are pea-sized, others larger, hard, and irregular—and can appear in the breast or armpit. Other symptoms include swelling, dimpling, skin changes, nipple discharge, inversion, or rashes.

GP Dr Sarah Cooke recommends self-examining every two weeks to once a month, ideally a week after a period. Examine both lying down and sitting, using circular motions from the collarbone to the nipple, checking both breasts and armpits. Showering can make lumps easier to detect.

Any unusual lumps, nipple changes, or skin puckering should be checked by a doctor, who will review medical history and may refer for examination.

Most breast cancers start in the milk duct lining; ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is the earliest, non-invasive form. Risk factors include alcohol consumption, prolonged combined HRT use, BRCA gene mutations, early menstruation, late menopause, and having children after 30 or not at all. Risk may be reduced through active lifestyle, healthy weight, and breastfeeding.

Men can also develop breast cancer, typically between ages 60-70, and should check for lumps or nipple changes.

Survival rates have nearly doubled in 40 years due to improved treatments and screening, with over 3 in 4 women surviving 10 years after diagnosis. Early detection is critical.

On June 16, 2019, NVIDIA Corporation's Board of Directors appointed Donald F. Robertson Jr., age 50, as Vice President, Chief Accounting Officer and Principal Accounting Officer, effective June 17, 2019. Robertson, who reports to CFO Colette Kress, previously held accounting leadership roles at Western Digital Corporation and SanDisk Corporation. He replaces Michael Byron, who will transition to Vice President, Finance, Merger & Acquisition Integration and Financial Systems.

Robertson's offer letter terms include an annual base salary of $650,000, a $600,000 sign-on bonus (repayable if he departs before his first anniversary), and a grant of 15,000 Restricted Stock Units vesting over approximately four years. He is also eligible for NVIDIA's employee stock purchase plan and benefits programs, and has signed NVIDIA's standard indemnity agreement.

Travis Haydon, 20, was jailed for 18 months after stabbing Liam Brown in the stomach with a flick knife during an argument over a spilt drink at the Newmarket Tavern in Plymouth. Haydon pleaded guilty to assault causing actual bodily harm, possessing an offensive weapon, and cannabis possession. Recorder Paul Grumbar noted Haydon's "appalling record" for violence and weapons offences, and that the attack breached an eight-month suspended sentence for a 2015 affray. The victim received a two-centimetre puncture wound and was kept at Derriford Hospital overnight but suffered no lasting damage. Haydon's barrister, Ali Rafati, said his client feared being punched and noted his father was seriously ill. The judge stated witnesses refused to give statements and the facts suggested malicious wounding.

SPYR, Inc. announced it will issue shareholders of record as of May 19, 2017, a dividend of shares in a new spin-off company, created to divest its restaurant division. Shareholders will receive one share in the new company for each SPYR share owned. Following the spin-off, the new entity will file a registration statement with the SEC to become a separately traded public company with its own ticker symbol. The spin-off will focus on licensing or franchising the Eat at Joe's® brand and concept, and on manufacturing and distributing branded foods, partly through acquisitions. Like SPYR, the new company will be a low float stock.

A Jurassic lizard fossil named Breugnathair elgolensis, discovered in 2016 on Scotland's Isle of Skye, has been described in a study published October 1 in a multinational collaboration led by the American Museum of Natural History. The 167-million-year-old specimen combines snake-like jaws and curved, python-like teeth with the short body and limbs of a lizard. Researchers placed it in a newly defined squamate group, Parviraptoridae, previously known only from fragmentary fossils. The unusual mix of primitive and specialized features suggests either that snake ancestors differed from expectations or that snake-like predatory traits evolved independently in an extinct group. Researchers could not definitively determine whether it is a snake ancestor or a stem-squamate.

The A100 GPU features 40 MB of L2 cache, 6.7x larger than the Tesla V100, improving HPC and AI workload performance by caching more data. The L2 cache, shared across GPCs and SMs, is split into two partitions, delivering 2.3x the bandwidth of V100 while maintaining hardware cache-coherence.

Each partition contains 40 L2 cache slices, with eight 512 KB slices per memory controller. In MIG configurations, each GPU slice includes a group of 10 L2 cache slices. A100 read bandwidth reaches 5120 Bytes/clk versus V100's 2048 Bytes/clk.

The NVIDIA Ampere architecture offers L2 cache residency controls and adds Compute Data Compression, providing up to 4x improvements in DRAM and L2 read bandwidth.

The RTC_B operates on a 32kHz input clock and provides timekeeping with counters for seconds through years, customizable alarm interrupts, interval alarms, periodic wake-up options, crystal calibration (±240ppm), and clock output for calibration.

The IWDT_B is an independent watchdog timer with its own clock source that generates a POR reset if not reset within a programmed time, offering eight selectable periods (2ms to 2hr).

The WWDT is a windowed watchdog that generates resets or interrupts, with eight selectable periods, sleep mode support, and interval timer mode.

The device includes general-purpose (TIMGx) and advanced (TIMAx) timers, with TIMGx as a subset of TIMAx. Features include 16/32-bit counters, 8-bit prescalers, shadow registers, QEI support, complementary PWM with dead band, and fault handling.

Additional sections cover analog connections, IOMUX input/output configuration, serial wire debug interface, bootstrap loader (BSL) via UART/I2C with 256-bit password protection, factory constants in memory-mapped regions, recommended application circuits (decoupling capacitors, NRST pullup, ROSC resistor, VCORE tank capacitor), development tools, documentation, and packaging information.

Chicago faces a major security challenge this weekend with three large sporting events: the Bank of America Chicago Marathon with 40,000 runners and up to 1.7 million spectators, a Cubs playoff game at Wrigley Field, and a Bears Monday Night Football game at Soldier Field. The recent Las Vegas massacre, along with reports that the gunman had booked rooms overlooking Chicago's Lollapalooza festival, has heightened concerns about lone-wolf attackers in high-rise buildings. Saudi Aramco plans to change the formula used to price its long-term crude oil sales to Asia from October, according to trade sources, marking the first benchmark change for its official selling prices (OSP) since the mid-1980s. The new formula will use the average monthly prices of Oman crude futures on the Dubai Mercantile Exchange (DME) and the average cash price for Dubai assessed by S&P Global Platts, replacing the previous average of Oman and Dubai prices assessed by Platts. Sources said Aramco was expected to notify Asian customers, though Aramco, DME and Platts did not respond to Reuters. The DME Oman contract, launched in 2007, is the most liquid physically deliverable Middle East crude futures contract. Iraq's SOMO previously proposed a similar switch but shelved the plan. The change could boost liquidity for DME Oman futures and related derivatives. Aramco's OSPs typically influence Iranian, Kuwaiti and Iraqi pricing, affecting over 12 million bpd bound for Asia, though it remains unclear if other producers will follow.

DoorDash unveiled a new autonomous delivery robot called Dot at an event in San Francisco. Dot is nearly five feet tall, equipped with nine cameras and seven sensors, and designed to operate on sidewalks, roads, and bike lanes. Developed by DoorDash Labs, Dot complements DoorDash's existing partnership with Coco Robotics and supports a hybrid delivery model involving humans, drones, and autonomous vehicles.

Interest in delivery robots peaked during the pandemic but declined as companies like Amazon and FedEx abandoned projects due to technical challenges, particularly navigating unpredictable sidewalk environments. Companies like Starship Technologies have focused on college campuses, which offer simpler infrastructure. Coco Robotics, backed by Sam Altman, operates in Los Angeles using a mix of autonomous driving and human teleoperators.

Concerns raised include competition for limited bike lane space, regulatory complications, and labor impacts. Research from Carnegie Mellon suggests robots often displace rather than eliminate human labor, as workers are still needed for tasks like cleaning robots and final delivery steps. In China, hybrid models exist in hotels, but human delivery workers remain dominant.

The speaker welcomes the visiting chiefs, affirming friendship between their nations and urging lasting peace. He describes the United States as a growing nation of seventeen States that does not seize land but purchases it by mutual consent, and offers a copy of a law protecting the visitors' lands from encroachment.

Responding to the chiefs' request (signed by Puckshanublee and others) to sell lands to pay debts to merchants, he declines the Tombigbee offer but accepts lands along the Mississippi, useful as resting places for boats traveling to New Orleans. Officials will later be appointed to negotiate the boundary on site.

Regarding lands formerly sold to the English, he states that custom, time elapsed, and testimony from living witnesses indicate payment was made; any unpaid debt would belong to the English, not the US.

He encourages the chiefs to adopt farming, livestock-raising, spinning, and weaving, promising assistance. He clarifies that previously sent goods were gifts, and the store was placed on their land at their request without transferring ownership. The Secretary at War will address other matters.

He arranges carriage travel for their tour and land transport home, expresses regret over the mistaken sea voyage to Savannah, and wishes them safe travels.

Genel Altimeaux, a Haitian worker with limited English, was employed by Ocean Construction. After a dispute on September 26, 1997, regarding pay differences between Haitian and other workers, one Haitian worker, Vidieu Tanis, declared the Haitians would no longer work for Ocean. When Altimeaux returned Monday, he was told he was no longer employed and subsequently received unemployment benefits, which the employer appealed.

At the initial hearing held without Altimeaux's presence, supervisor Milliken testified Altimeaux quit. The appeals referee accepted this, but the appellate court remanded after finding Altimeaux had not received notice. At the second hearing, Altimeaux denied quitting, and supervisor Tranowski admitted he never personally heard Altimeaux quit. The referee nonetheless relied on Milliken's earlier untested testimony to find Altimeaux voluntarily quit.

The appellate court reversed, holding that Milliken's testimony was incompetent because Altimeaux had no opportunity to cross-examine him, as required under section 120.569(2)(j). The remaining testimony did not support a finding that Altimeaux voluntarily quit. The court directed reinstatement of Altimeaux's unemployment award.

Parents are raising concerns about Township High School District 113's process for hiring a new principal for Highland Park High School, particularly regarding the inclusion of only two parents on the 18-member stakeholder interview committee. Parent representative Amy Small and board member Julie Gordon cited a lack of transparency and unclear selection criteria for committee members. Superintendent Christopher Dignam, who is using Ray and Associates to screen candidates replacing departing Principal Tom Koulentes, stated the process mirrors last year's Deerfield High School principal search. The stakeholder committee is scheduled to interview finalists on April 25, with the goal of selecting a principal that day.

The Pin and Pull is a popular perimeter run play that creates favorable down block angles while positioning lead blockers in space. Its strengths include versatility, flexibility in blocking assignments based on defensive alignment, and allowing the Tailback to run anywhere from the C-gap to the sideline. Its weaknesses include requiring at least two Guards capable of pulling and running, and being most effective with a speed-oriented Tailback.

Unlike the traditional Buck Sweep, which includes a simultaneous inside run threat, the Pin and Pull is purely a perimeter run. Blocking assignments vary against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts, with Guards typically pulling while other linemen execute down or combination blocks. Variations include the Pin and Pull Toss, which uses receiver motion and a quarterback toss, and the TE-Wing Pin and Pull Toss, which adds a Tight End and Wing to create a 4-man blocking surface.

Researchers have documented how Europe's largest bat, the greater noctule (*Nyctalus lasiopterus*), hunts migrating songbirds mid-flight. A team led by bioacoustician Ilias Foskolos of Aarhus University equipped bats with biologgers containing accelerometers, magnetometers, altimeters, and microphones to track their nocturnal activities, as reported in the October 9 issue of *Science*.

Of 611 recorded hunting events, most involved insects, but two showed bats ascending above 1,200 meters to intercept songbirds. The bats emitted high-frequency feeding buzzes inaudible to birds, then attacked. One bird escaped; the other was consumed during a 23-minute in-flight meal, with audio capturing chewing and possible bone-biting. Evidence suggests the bats remove their prey's wings during feeding. DNA analysis of bite wounds on discarded wings confirmed greater noctule involvement, and captured bats have been found with feathers in their mouths. Bat ecologist Danilo Russo called the findings compelling, though no visual footage exists. Researchers say much remains unknown about the species.

Gold rallied strongly on Friday alongside a decline in the USD Index, but silver, platinum, and mining stocks failed to follow. The VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ) closed below the April high for a third consecutive day, suggesting bearish implications.
