Former Nepali prime minister K.P. Oli appears poised to return to power after winning his parliamentary seat, with his Communist UML party and Maoist allies on track for a majority. The election follows a decade-long transition from monarchy and civil war. Oli, 65, has pledged a stable five-year government, extension of Chinese railways into Nepal, and infrastructure development to attract investment. Analysts suggest Oli will need to balance relations between China and India. Final results are expected within a week.

Research at Brock University, led by associate professor Evangelina Tsiani, found that rosemary extract may reduce lung cancer cell growth. The team, including graduate student Jessy Moore, exposed aggressive lung cancer cells to rosemary extract and observed that it halted cancer cell survival and spread, promoted pre-programmed cell death, blocked the Akt signalling pathway responsible for cancer cell multiplication, and prevented activation of certain proteins. The findings were published in Biomedicine & Pharmacotherapy. Tsiani cautioned it is premature to recommend increased rosemary consumption for cancer prevention. Further research aims to identify which components—potentially the polyphenols carnosic acid and rosmarinic acid—are responsible for the anti-cancer effects.

The 32-mile stretch between London and Theale, Berkshire, will be widened to four lanes in both directions, with 11 bridges demolished and rebuilt and four others widened. Highways England stated the road carries 130,000 vehicles daily and is congestion-prone. Following RAC safety concerns about the absence of a hard shoulder, Highways England confirmed places of relative safety will be situated 1.12 miles apart on average.

JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon, speaking in Washington, D.C., addressed concerns about an AI bubble, stating that while some asset prices are in "bubble territory," AI itself is real and will likely pay off overall, comparing it to the early internet era. Dimon warned that AI will eliminate jobs and urged society, government, and businesses to prepare through retraining, new income models, or early retirement to prevent social unrest.

He distinguished between applied AI, which JPMorgan uses successfully for fraud prevention, risk, and marketing, and generative AI, which he placed in a less proven category due to anecdotal efficiency claims and hallucination issues. Responding to an MIT study finding 95% of generative AI pilots failed to yield ROI, Dimon argued against measuring costs too carefully, emphasizing the importance of properly formatting data first.

Under Dimon, JPMorgan has invested billions in AI since 2012, employing over 2,000 AI staff. He advised executives to adopt AI, invest in training, and called for thoughtful regulation. Days earlier, Dimon estimated a 30% chance of a stock market correction. AI investment reportedly accounts for an estimated 40% of U.S. GDP growth in 2025.

Jane Goodall, who died on October 1 at age 91, was known for studying chimpanzees in Tanzania's Gombe National Park. Less known was her one-of-a-kind collection of chimp skeletons, assembled by retrieving bodies shortly after death and preparing the bones. Because each skeleton came from an individual with documented sex, age, weight, and life history, researchers could study how development shaped skeletal features—an advantage unavailable to those studying ancient hominid fossils.

In a 1990 interview, Goodall explained her motivation simply: field researchers shouldn't waste anything. She was cautious about drawing conclusions, repeatedly saying "we just don't know" regarding implications for human ancestors or variations among Gombe chimps.

One notable skeleton belonged to Flo, a matriarch who died in 1972. Her remains were larger than most at Gombe yet lighter than a stockier male, illustrating the difficulty of estimating body weight from bones. Flo's bone loss pattern differed from human osteoporosis, and she gave birth shortly before dying near age 50—relevant to recent findings of menopause in older female chimps. Goodall's skeletal collection continued yielding scientific insights as she shifted toward activism and writing.

Gold prices may reach a four-year high of $1,400 per ounce by year-end, driven by U.S.-North Korea tensions and demand from China and India, according to Evgeny Ananiev of VTB Capital. Prices could hit $1,360 within three months, with support above $1,200. Gold has risen 12 percent this year amid nuclear conflict fears and subdued U.S. inflation, which reduces the likelihood of interest rate hikes. The passage describes multi-camera imaging systems and methods for detecting faint objects in space or low-light environments using arrays of economical or low-performance cameras that individually cannot image such objects.

Three array configurations are disclosed:

**Common Field Array**: Multiple cameras are positioned so their fields of view share a common region. A computing system co-registers and combines the captured images, producing a combined image with signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at least √N times greater than individual images, where N equals the number of combined images.

**Hybrid Field Array**: Multiple camera arrays each produce a combined image from their common field of view region. These combined images partially overlap and are stitched together to create a composite image with both a wider field of view and enhanced SNR.

**Adaptive Field Array**: Cameras initially form a wide composite field of view for target detection. Upon detecting a target, the cameras automatically reconfigure so their fields of view share a common region containing the target, then generate an enhanced combined image.

Benefits over prior systems (e.g., the DARPA Space Surveillance Telescope) include lower cost, scalability, flexibility, reduced cosmic ray artifacts, and increased bit depth (approximately Log₂(N) additional bits) enabling advanced deconvolution.

The passage details processes for camera calibration (dark frame, flat frame, bias frame, barrel distortion, field calibration), data collection (star matching, pixel mapping, image registration, image combining), and data reduction (streak detection via Hough transform, streak characterization, orbit determination, and catalog searching to identify uncorrelated space objects).

Natural zircon single crystals from the Mud Tank deposit were shock-compressed to 13.6 and 51.3 GPa to investigate trace element behavior during the zircon–reidite transition. The 13.6 GPa sample retained the zircon structure with fracturing, while the 51.3 GPa sample transformed to textured reidite (with (112)R||(200)Zrn orientation) containing relict zircon near fractures.

X-ray diffraction, Raman, IR, cathodoluminescence (CL), and photoluminescence analyses revealed that reidite CL intensity was roughly six times lower than the starting material, with the emission maximum shifted to shorter wavelengths (<450 nm). Splitting and intensity changes in Dy3+ luminescence lines indicated at least two REE3+ positions with different local symmetries.

A notable feature was bright yellow luminescent speckles (2–10 μm), often aligned along crystallographic planes intersecting at ~73°, interpreted as REE3+ segregation on dislocations and planar defects generated during the transition.

Unlike previous studies attributing such segregation to prolonged post-shock annealing, this segregation occurred within seconds, suggesting vacancy-mediated diffusion or transport along defects. The authors propose that the reconstructive zircon–reidite transition causes local charge imbalances, expelling trivalent trace elements into interstitial positions where they diffuse rapidly to defects. This has implications for trace element release during fluid or melt interaction with shocked zircon.

This patent application relates to ladar transmitter technology and claims priority to multiple prior applications dating back to 2014. The invention addresses limitations in conventional ladar systems, which suffer from high cost, size, weight, power requirements, and bandwidth usage, particularly for computer vision applications like vehicle autonomy.

The inventors disclose three main innovations:

1. **Optical Field Splitter/Inverter**: A device positioned downstream from scanning mirrors that splits and inverts the scan area so fast scanning occurs at edges rather than the middle. Embodiments include W-shaped reflectors and triangular prism designs. This allows longer gaze time at desired regions (typically the center) during Lissajous scans, where mirrors naturally scan faster in the middle. Adjustable hinges can control overlap for customized coverage.

2. **Induced Periodic Phase Drift**: A technique where phase is time-varying rather than fixed in Lissajous scan patterns, driving scanning mirrors slightly off-resonance. Using total least squares optimization with singular value decomposition, this reduces scan gaps in targeted regions while preserving periodicity and beam quality. The process runs in milliseconds, enabling frame-by-frame updates.

3. **Ellipsoidal Conjugate Reflector (ECR)**: A reimaging system placing two scan mirrors at the foci of an ellipsoid, with a focusing lens upstream. This enables compact beam scanner assemblies with equally-sized, closely-placed mirrors. A coplanar angle (CPA) constraint formula ensures ray fans remain planar, producing linear scan rows with minimal distortion.

These techniques can be combined to improve ladar transmitter gaze on regions of interest while maintaining scan speed advantages.

The application describes Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) transmission methods for small data transmission in new radio (NR) systems. In LTE, data transmission requires an established RRC connection, which is inefficient for small data transmission (SDT). 3GPP has proposed Control Plane (CP) and User Plane (UP) solutions to reduce signaling overhead.

The disclosed methods enable small data transmission while the UE remains in RRC-IDLE or RRC-INACTIVE states. A network apparatus (gNB) configures contention-based radio resources for a configured grant PUSCH (CFG-PUSCH) and broadcasts configuration information, potentially via a remaining system information block, including NOMA parameters such as DMRS ports, multiple access signatures, and interleavers.

For idle-state transmission, the UE uses NAS security context without requiring AS security establishment. For inactive-state transmission, stored AS security context is used. Multiple CFG-PUSCH resources may be configured for different message sizes, with guard bands or extended cyclic prefixes to mitigate interference from asynchronous transmission.

The NOMA scheme mitigates sequence collision by using UE-specific reference bits generated from a UE-specific ID and multiple access identity. These reference bits are jointly encoded with information bits using a systematic LDPC coder and can serve as preamble or DMRS, enabling UE activity detection, channel estimation, and MA signature indication, thereby reducing collision probability and enhancing decoding performance.

In Pelitsie v. National Surety Corporation (1956), the Wisconsin court addressed whether the plaintiff insured substantially complied with the record-keeping clause in his burglary insurance policies, which required records sufficient for the insurer to accurately determine the amount of loss.

The plaintiff maintained a cash fund of approximately $3,000 for cashing patrons' pay-roll checks, kept in an insured safe. His record-keeping consisted of totaling the cash and checks nightly on an adding machine and writing the sum on a scratch-pad. Following a burglary on February 9, 1954, plaintiff claimed a loss of $2,922, of which $600–$800 was estimated to be in checks. He recovered $182 by remembering details of two checks and having the drawers stop payment.

The court noted that while record-keeping requirements for cash-only losses may be less stringent than for merchandise, substantial compliance still requires sufficient written evidence for a person of ordinary intelligence to determine the loss without relying on an interested party's memory.

The court held that adequate records for stolen checks must list each check's amount along with identifying data (such as drawer name and payee or check number) enabling claims against drawers. Because plaintiff's ability to recoup $182 by memory demonstrated that better records could have further minimized the loss, his record-keeping was insufficient.

The judgment was reversed and the complaint ordered dismissed.

Monte Carlo methods are widely used for neutron transport simulations but suffer from slow convergence, prompting the development of variance reduction techniques (VRTs). While most VRTs were designed for steady-state problems, advances in computing have made time-dependent Monte Carlo simulations more practical, raising questions about how VRTs interact with population control techniques (PCTs) essential for time-dependent work.

This study examines global VRTs—including Implicit Capture (IC), CADIS, FW-CADIS, and Cooper-Larsen (CL) weight windows—alongside PCTs such as uniform combing (UC) and weight-based combing (WC). Testing was conducted using two codes: Shift (coupled with DENOVO for adjoint flux generation) and MC/DC (a fully time-dependent Python-based code).

Three test problems were evaluated: a pulsed slab, the supercritical AZURV1 benchmark, and a 1D SCRAM problem with moving surfaces. Key findings include:

- FW-CADIS slightly outperformed other methods in the pulsed slab, with benefits growing at later time steps.
- CL weight windows combined with UC achieved significant efficiency gains, while time-dependent weight windows outperformed static ones.
- Combining CL weight windows with WC caused memory exhaustion due to excessive particle splitting from weight resetting.
- IC unexpectedly performed poorly when paired with UC across multiple problems.

The results demonstrate that steady-state VRTs can effectively be applied to time-dependent simulations, but method selection is critical. Incompatible combinations (weight windows with WC, IC with UC) degrade performance, while compatible pairings (CL with UC) yield substantial efficiency improvements. Time-dependent adaptations of VRTs show promise for further optimization.

Research suggests imagination can influence performance, behavior, and feelings of connection. This approach was implemented in a yearlong study in two eighth-grade German classrooms in the Northeastern U.S., aimed at boosting retention and preserving the program.

The method requires no extra funding but demands planning time, as no prepackaged curriculum exists. It builds on task-based instruction (TBI), with tasks designed to help students imagine themselves using the target language authentically. Sample scenarios include planning a move abroad, finding apartments, shopping for furniture, navigating transit, and, for older students, drafting résumés and emails to landlords. Students receive scaffolding, realia, and just-in-time instruction.

Implementation guidelines emphasize plausible scenarios, authentic assessments, student autonomy, and curriculum alignment. Reported outcomes included deeper cultural engagement, increased feelings of connection with target-language speakers, and continued language study beyond requirements.

The approach is adaptable to all levels (K–16), contexts, and languages. Sustainability is supported by cataloging materials and collaboration among instructors. The disclosure describes methods, polypeptides, nucleic acids, and genetically modified host cells for producing cannabinoids, cannabinoid precursors, and their derivatives. Host cells may additionally express tetraketide synthase (TKS), olivetolic acid cyclase (OAC), cannabinoid synthases (THCA or CBDA synthase), acyl-CoA-generating enzymes, GPP-generating enzymes, malonyl-CoA-generating enzymes, and mevalonate pathway polypeptides. Suitable hosts include yeast (e.g., Saccharomyces cerevisiae), plant, and prokaryotic cells, cultured in media containing fermentable sugars, cellulosic feedstocks, carboxylic acids, or olivetolic acid.

The broad substrate specificity of these enzymes enables production of non-naturally occurring cannabinoid derivatives. Compared to agricultural or chemical synthesis, microbial fermentation offers faster, more reliable, and economical production of pure cannabinoids with defined stereochemistry.

A New York Times survey of 65 federal judges found widespread dissatisfaction with the U.S. Supreme Court's emergency docket decisions related to President Trump's second term. Only 12 judges agreed the Supreme Court has made appropriate use of the emergency docket, and only 12 felt lower courts received sufficient guidance on applying such orders. Of 54 judges answering the question, just two believed the docket improved public perception of the judiciary, while 42 said it caused harm.

Anonymous judges described the orders as "mystical," "overly blunt," and "demoralizing," though one Trump appointee viewed them positively. The survey was sent to over 400 judges; respondents included 28 Republican and 37 Democratic nominees. At least seven of roughly 20 emergency orders lacked reasoning, and nearly all favored Trump, enabling deportations, military discharges, federal firings, and spending cuts.

The New York Times acknowledged respondents may not represent the entire judiciary. The Volokh Conspiracy critiqued the survey, suggesting unhappy judges were more likely to respond and that sampled districts may skew results.

President Trump's pardon of Scooter Libby, following an FBI raid on his personal attorney Michael Cohen, has raised concerns that Trump may use his pardon power to shield associates in special counsel Robert Mueller's Russia investigation. This paper investigates the social tendencies of Large Language Models (LLMs) in agent-based modeling (ABM), specifically examining whether LLM agents default to egoistic or altruistic behavior when individual and collective interests conflict. The authors argue that existing LLM-driven social simulations overlook the intrinsic dispositions of LLMs in group decision-making, and that current evaluation benchmarks rely on micro-level game theory scenarios that fail to capture emergent social phenomena.

To address this gap, the researchers propose a Schelling-variant urban migration model featuring over 200 agents distributed across a 3×3 grid of residential blocks, with a shared message board mechanism to simulate social influence. They evaluate agent behavior using mixed methods: quantitative metrics including Price of Anarchy (PoA), Residential Gini Index, and a 3×3 behavioral archetype matrix, alongside qualitative analysis using an LLM-as-judge approach inspired by Grounded Theory.

Testing six LLMs (o1-mini, o3-mini, Qwen2.5-7B, Deepseek-V3.1, Deepseek-R1, and Gemini-2.5-pro) across three Guidance on Strategic Deliberation (GSD) levels, the experiments reveal a fundamental bifurcation:

1. **Adaptive Egoists** (o1-mini, o3-mini, Qwen2.5-7B): Default to self-interest, producing sub-optimal equilibria, but demonstrate significantly increased altruism when exposed to social norms via the message board.

2. **Altruistic Optimizers** (Gemini-2.5-pro, Deepseek-R1, Deepseek-V3.1): Consistently achieve system-optimal states (PoA=1.0) regardless of message board presence, displaying inherent altruistic logic.

The authors conclude that selecting an LLM for social simulation constitutes a theoretical choice about the social actor model employed. Adaptive Egoists are better suited for simulating bounded rationality in human societies, while Altruistic Optimizers suit idealized pro-social modeling contexts. Limitations include model simplifications and homogeneous agents, with future directions suggesting human-in-the-loop validation and real-world demographic integration.

This retrospective study investigated the association between resting heart rate (RHR) and all-cause mortality (ACM) in intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) patients in the ICU, using data from the MIMIC-IV database. The cohort included 1,918 adult patients diagnosed with ICH (ICD-9/10 codes) between 2011-2019, divided into four quartiles based on RHR levels. ACM was assessed at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year following ICU admission.

Baseline analysis showed higher proportions of intraventricular hemorrhage, mild liver disease, and diabetes in the higher RHR quartiles (Q3 and Q4), along with greater mechanical ventilation use and higher ACM incidence. Kaplan-Meier survival curves and multivariate Cox regression models (adjusted via three approaches, including directed acyclic graphs) indicated that RHR above 78.5 bpm was significantly associated with increased ACM risk, while Q1 and Q2 showed no significant correlation.

Restricted cubic splines identified a nonlinear J-shaped relationship, with 90.3 bpm as the threshold: RHR below this value appeared protective, while values above it were independently associated with higher ACM risk. Subgroup analyses revealed an interaction with age, though mediation analysis showed the indirect effect through age was minor compared to the direct positive correlation between RHR and ACM.

Limitations include exclusion of blood pressure as a confounder and the need for randomized trials to validate findings. The authors concluded that RHR stratification, particularly using the 90.3 bpm threshold, may inform management strategies and improve clinical outcomes for ICH patients in the ICU.

Sigi Zheng's lecture introduces methods for quantitatively measuring the benefits of green buildings and cities, focusing on the hedonic pricing model. The model decomposes a property's total price into component values (e.g., rooms, subway access, parks, LEED certification) plus a residual, with coefficients estimated via regression using large datasets like Zillow. Taking the log of price allows coefficients to be interpreted as percentage changes.

Willingness to pay (WTP) for non-market goods can be derived through stated preference (surveys) or revealed preference (observed market behavior), with the latter being more reliable. Empirical studies using hedonic regression have found approximately a 6% rent premium and 7.6% price premium for green buildings.

A key challenge is causal inference: comparing green and non-green buildings often constitutes an "apples-to-oranges" comparison due to endogeneity, which arises from omitted variables, reverse causality, and selection bias. Researchers address this by seeking counterfactuals through techniques including OLS with controls, randomized controlled trials (the "gold standard," exemplified by Duflo and Banerjee's Nobel-winning work), geographic matching, propensity score matching, regression discontinuity, instrumental variables, and difference-in-differences.

The methodology extends to valuing locational amenities like schools, transit, parks, and clean air. Case examples include Bryant Park's public-private restoration, which increased nearby property values, and the High Line Park, which illustrates environmental gentrification—where green amenities raise willingness to pay among wealthier residents, displacing lower-income occupants. Zheng emphasized understanding these quantitative methods is valuable for future decision-makers evaluating investments in amenities and infrastructure.

The Turtle Trading Strategy is a trend-following approach developed by Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt in 1983 as part of an experiment to determine whether trading skills are innate or learnable. Dennis recruited 14 novice traders, dubbed "Turtles," and trained them for two weeks using mechanical rules. The experiment proved successful, demonstrating that trading could be taught.

The strategy centers on three key elements: volatility-based position sizing using the ATR indicator, pyramiding (adding to winning positions), and strict stop-loss exits. Turtles identified new uptrends through breakouts of 20-day highs and reversed positions on breakdowns of 20-day lows.

Dennis eventually lost more than half his assets between 1987-1988 and stopped trading, while Eckhardt founded a successful CTA firm in 1991. Notable books on the subject include Michael Covel's "The Complete TurtleTrader" and Curtis Faith's "Way of the Turtle."

Backtests from 2007 onward across multiple futures contracts using strategies like Dual Moving Average, ATR Channel Breakout, and Bollinger Band Breakout show the approach still works but is less effective than in earlier decades. Trend-following indices like the MLM Index and Barclay CTA Index confirm ongoing relevance, with low correlation to stocks. The strategy works best in trending markets but involves frequent whipsaws, low win rates, and long drawdown periods.

Dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) were fabricated using natural dyes extracted from mangosteen peel (MP) and grass jelly leaves (GJL) at varying volume ratios (3:0, 3:1, 2:1, 1:1, 1:2, 1:3, 0:3). TiO2 paste was spin-coated onto cleaned ITO glass, sensitized with the dye mixtures, and assembled with a KI/I2 electrolyte and graphite counter electrode. UV-Vis spectra confirmed complementary absorption from anthocyanin, α-mangostin, and chlorophyll pigments. FESEM showed that the 1:1 mixture produced uniform, crack-free films, while MP-rich films exhibited cracking. The 1:3 MP:GJL ratio achieved the highest power conversion efficiency (3.50%), exceeding pure MP (2.75%) and pure GJL (2.12%). GJL-rich samples also showed better cycling stability, while the 1:1 mixture degraded rapidly. The results indicate that optimizing dye ratios enhances light harvesting and charge collection in DSSCs.

The NVIDIA RTX A6000 contains a GA102 GPU with 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 48GB of GDDR6 memory, scalable to 96GB via NVLink, offering improvements in rendering, HPC, and deep learning over the RTX 6000.

The lecture begins by reviewing the LSZ theorem, which relates scattering amplitudes to time-ordered correlation functions. The scattering amplitude is obtained by taking momentum-space correlation functions in the on-shell limit, after stripping external propagators. Initial state momenta take negative energy roots while final state momenta take positive roots, a convention arising from whether field operators act on initial or final states. Only truncated, connected Feynman diagrams need be considered, as corrections to external propagators are absorbed into a constant Z (=1 at leading order).

The lecture then transitions to fermions and the Dirac equation. Historically, Dirac sought a first-order relativistic wave equation to resolve issues with the Klein-Gordon equation (non-positive probability and negative energy states). He proposed an equation of the form i∂ψ/∂t = (-iα·∇ + βm)ψ, where α and β must be Hermitian matrices rather than constants. Squaring the equation to recover the Klein-Gordon form requires: α_i α_j + α_j α_i = 0 (i≠j), α_i² = β² = 1, and βα_i + α_iβ = 0. These conditions require at least 4×4 matrices, making ψ a four-component spinor.

Introducing gamma matrices (γ⁰ = iβ, γⁱ = iβα_i), the Dirac equation becomes (γ^μ∂_μ - m)ψ = 0, with the Clifford algebra relation {γ^μ, γ^ν} = 2η^μν. Two example representations are given. For massless particles, only 2×2 matrices (Pauli matrices) are needed, indicating massive particles have more degrees of freedom. A conserved current with positive-definite j⁰ can be derived classically. All representations satisfying the Clifford algebra are related by similarity transformations and are physically equivalent, though different forms are convenient for nonrelativistic versus ultrarelativistic limits. Proof of Lorentz covariance of the Dirac equation is deferred to the next lecture.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2017. Phuket Governor Norraphat Plodthong has ordered lifeguards to resume patrols on Phuket's beaches by April 1, according to the National News Bureau of Thailand (NNT). The directive was issued at a March 21 meeting attended by vice governors, administrative officials, and the Phuket Provincial Administration Organisation (PPAO) Acting Chief, with military and police personnel also present.

Previously, the PPAO provided 37 lifeguards across 15 points at six beaches from December 28 to February 26. The Governor stated that local administrative offices must take responsibility for beaches in Muang Phuket and Kathu districts, while a procurement-winning company will cover Thalang district beaches. Local offices lacking budgets may request support from the PPAO, though next year they must fund lifeguards themselves.

This contradicts Norraphat's December 12 order that the PPAO would no longer be involved. The NNT report did not explain this reversal, and questions from The Phuket News to the Governor remain unanswered.

Eric Schmidt, former Google CEO, will fund a project through Schmidt Sciences to deploy uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) in the Southern Ocean to collect data on its carbon cycle. The initiative is part of a $45 million, five-year commitment to global carbon cycle research. The Southern Ocean, surrounding Antarctica, accounts for a significant portion of ocean-based CO2 absorption, but scientists lack data due to its remote location, harsh conditions, and cloud cover that limits satellite observation. Four USVs will operate continuously for five years, including through winter, collecting measurements of CO2 partial pressure in areas inaccessible to crewed vessels or commercial ships. Machine learning will guide their routes, and the data will be publicly available. The project is structured as a public-private partnership involving NOAA. Lead scientists include Galen McKinley of Columbia University. The funding comes amid proposed Trump administration cuts to federal scientific agencies, including a 30 percent reduction to NOAA and a 57 percent cut to the National Science Foundation, increasing reliance on private funding for climate research.

AGESA™ software provides several procedures for processor and memory management:

**Stack Initialization (AmdEnableStack)**: A stackless assembler procedure using register passing that initializes the processor and cache to establish a pre-memory stack region, dividing it among processor cores and configuring MTRRs (x86-64 only). It preserves SS in protected mode and creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance. AARCH64 APUs with PSP do not use this. Returns AGESA_SUCCESS, AGESA_WARNING (stack reentry), or AGESA_FATAL (unknown processor family).

**Stack Removal**: A stackless procedure run once by the BSP when main memory becomes available. It disables CAR mode, flushes caches, and returns the processor to a non-stack state without modifying MTRRs. EBX is preserved for use as a return address.

**AmdCreateStruct**: Allocates and initializes parameter block storage using one of three methods: PreMemHeap (Cache-as-RAM), PostMemDram (post-memory), or ByHost (caller-allocated). Requires release via AmdReleaseStruct.

**Additional Service Procedures** (require an established stack):
- Retrieve DIMM data eye bitmap results (31×32 bits, normalized to 1D Center[+16,-15])
- Obtain APIC address for a specified socket/core (x86-64 only)
- Return available pre-memory execution cache size (x86-64 only)
- Obtain base PCI address for a specified processor die
- Identify the current executing processor core (socket/module/core)
- Map a system memory address to its FRU (socket, channel, DIMM, chip select, bank, row, column) for error location

Most procedures depend on operational coherent HyperTransport™ links.

Chemists have proposed that microsparks of electricity may ignite will-o'-the-wisps, the bluish glowing lights historically reported above swamps and cemeteries. While scientists have long suspected these lights result from burning methane released by decaying matter, the ignition source remained unknown. Researchers led by Richard Zare and Yu Xia, building on prior work showing water droplets can create electrical sparks, tested whether bubbles could do the same. Using a 3-D printed nozzle to produce tiny bubbles of methane and air in water, they detected emitted photons and eventually captured visible microlightning with a high-speed camera when bubbles were made smaller and closer together. Differently charged bubbles apparently allowed electrons to leap between them.

Other scientists, including Antonio Pavão and Luigi Garlaschelli, find the findings intriguing but not fully conclusive, noting that the experiments occurred underwater while will-o'-the-wisps appear in air. Pavão suggests historical lantern flames may have ignited swamp gas. Researchers say the work advances the field of triboelectricity and could potentially be harnessed to trigger chemical reactions, break down pollutants, or improve environmentally friendly technologies.

6.4.1.3 Multiple Devices: Daisy-Chain Topology

In a daisy-chain topology, multiple devices share common CONVST/CS and SCLK inputs controlled by the host. The host's SDO-x connects to device 1's SDI, each device's SDO-0 feeds the next device's SDI, and the final device's SDO-0 returns to the host's SDI.

The host programs identical configuration register values in all devices, setting SDO_CTL_REG bits 7-0 to 00h. Devices sample analog inputs on CONVST/CS rising edges, with data transfers starting on its falling edge. On SCLK launch edges, devices shift MSBs out via SDO-0; on capture edges, they shift SDI data in as the LSB of a unified shift register. The host receives data from device N first, then N-1, and so on in MSB-first order. On CONVST/CS rising edges, devices decode their shift register contents.

An optimal frame uses 32 × N SCLK capture edges for N devices. Shorter frames cause configuration errors; longer frames require the host to align configuration data properly before raising CONVST/CS.

President Taft addresses Congress on conservation of national resources. He notes the public domain has shrunk from 1.05 billion acres in 1860 to 731 million acres, with much land fraudulently obtained under outdated statutes.

Taft urges Congress to validate executive withdrawals of coal and water-power lands and authorize the Secretary of the Interior to make future withdrawals. He recommends classifying public lands by their principal use through the Geological Survey, and separating surface agricultural rights from mineral rights, with minerals leased on royalty terms to prevent monopoly.

For water-power sites, Taft proposes leasing government-adjacent lands for up to 50 years with graduated rentals to prevent monopolistic consolidation. He emphasizes soil conservation as paramount and praises the expanded 320-acre homestead act for enabling dry farming.

Regarding reclamation, Taft recommends issuing up to $30 million in bonds to complete overextended irrigation projects where settlers await promised water. He supports repealing the 1878 timber act and selling timber at public sale.

On forests, Taft notes 190 million acres of federal reserves and supports modest federal appropriations for reforestation at navigable stream headwaters, while leaving private forest regulation to states.

For inland waterways, he prioritizes completing dams on the Ohio River (remaining cost $63 million over 12 years) and improvements on the upper Mississippi and Missouri Rivers, citing European evidence that waterways help regulate railroad rates. He urges Congress not to delay legislation pending ongoing investigations.

NVIDIA RTX IO benefits artists and designers by accelerating data transfer from storage to GPU, reducing bottlenecks in rendering. It works with Microsoft's DirectStorage API to enable GPU-based lossless decompression, offloading work from the CPU and improving I/O performance by a factor of two.

The NVIDIA A40, based on the GA10x Ampere architecture, is designed for data center visual computing. Compared to the Quadro RTX 6000, it delivers up to 2X FP32 throughput, 2X ray-tracing throughput, and 5X (10X with Sparsity) AI training throughput. It includes 48GB of memory (scalable to 96GB via NVLink), PCIe Gen4, three DisplayPort 1.4 outputs, and supports vGPU software and the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz displays, DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1 (first discrete GPUs to do so), and HDCP 2.3. The fifth-generation NVDEC decoder supports multiple codecs including AV1, with GA10x being the first GPUs to offer AV1 hardware decode, enabling 8K60 HDR playback with low CPU usage. The seventh-generation NVENC encoder supports high-quality encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The GA10x Ampere architecture delivers up to 2x performance improvements in shading, ray tracing, and AI, featuring second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity, and GDDR6X memory (up to 19.5 Gbps). The GeForce RTX 3090 includes 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA Cores, and 24GB GDDR6X, offering 1.5x TITAN RTX performance. The RTX 3070 (GA104) exceeds RTX 2080 Ti performance.

New Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology on GDDR6X helps overclockers identify memory limits via plateauing performance rather than crashes.

The NVIDIA RTX A6000 features a GA102 GPU with 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 48GB GDDR6 (expandable to 96GB via NVLink), delivering improved performance across rendering, HPC, and deep learning workloads compared to the RTX 6000.

SEV-ES and SEV-SNP are AMD virtualization features that protect guest virtual machine register state from the hypervisor by encrypting it during world switches. This document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB), a 4KB shared memory page enabling communication between guests and hypervisors during Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs).

The GHCB must be mapped as decrypted and is accessed via MSR 0xc001_0130. A GHCB MSR protocol allows limited communication before the full GHCB is established, supporting functions like SEV information requests, CPUID queries, AP reset hold, page state changes, and termination requests.

Version 2 introduces SEV-SNP support and hypervisor feature advertisement via a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap. Subsequent revisions (2.01–2.04) add: 64-bit guest request message sequence numbers, VLEK certificate support, APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL execution, SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob EFI protocol, SEV trusted IO (SEV-TIO), and Secure AVIC support.

For NAE events, guests populate GHCB fields with required register state and mark them valid in VALID_BITMAP before issuing VMGEXIT. The document specifies handling for IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access, page state changes, SNP guest requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell pages, IPIs, timers, and termination requests.

SMP booting under SEV-ES/SNP requires special handling since register state cannot be modified post-measurement. Solutions include AP reset hold loops, AP jump tables, or the SNP AP Creation NAE event. NMI handling requires intercepting #DB (not IRET) and using "NMI Complete" messages.

Restricted Injection limits host-to-guest communication to #HV exceptions via a doorbell page containing a PendingEvent field and NoEoiRequired flag, emulating APIC behavior for interrupt delivery and EOI handling. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

The University of Michigan Consumer Confidence Index measures economic optimism through monthly surveys. Backtests using OECD US consumer confidence data from 1993 show that stock market performance correlates with consumer confidence levels.

In the first backtest, a $10,000 investment in the S&P 500 (SPY) held only when consumer confidence was above its 12-month moving average grew to $99,000 over 28 years (8.4% CAGR), compared to $159,000 for buy-and-hold (10.4% CAGR). However, the strategy had a lower max drawdown (23% vs. 55%) and was invested only 55% of the time.

The opposite strategy—investing only when confidence was below the moving average—yielded just $15,000, a 1.58% annual return.

The Consumer Confidence Index (CCI), published by The Conference Board, surveys 5,000 US households monthly using five questions answered as positive, negative, or neutral. Changes under 5% are typically considered insignificant. The index depends on the present situation index and expectations index.

Consumer confidence influences manufacturer inventories, bank lending, hiring, and government tax projections. The University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index, developed by Professor George Katona in the 1940s, conducts monthly telephone surveys, releasing preliminary and final reports.

Backtests indicate consumer confidence is a significant predictor of stock market returns relative to its 12-month moving average.

Natalie Grabow, 80, of Mountain Lakes, New Jersey, set a world record as the oldest woman to finish the Kona Ironman World Championship, completing it in 16 hours, 45 minutes, and 26 seconds on October 11, 2025. Growing up before Title IX, she had limited athletic opportunities and focused on studies at Bucknell University before working as a software developer and raising two daughters. She began running in her 40s and competing in 5Ks and 10Ks in her 50s. At 59, she taught herself to swim using books, videos, and YMCA sessions, enabling her to enter triathlons. She qualified for the Kona Ironman at 61. Grabow trains about two hours daily, eats a varied diet including sweets, and takes only multivitamins. She was greeted at the finish by previous record holder Cherie Gruenfeld and plans to continue competing.

Lenovo officially unveiled the ThinkPad 25 at an event at Yamato Labs in Yokohama, Japan. The limited edition laptop is based on the current T470 but draws design inspiration from the 1992 ThinkPad 700C, featuring a rubberized coating, red TrackPoint, seven-row keyboard, and status LEDs. Its modern hardware includes a 14-inch Full HD touchscreen, Intel Core i7-7500U, GeForce 940MX GPU, 16GB DDR4, 512GB SSD, and claimed 18-hour battery life. Available in limited quantities in select countries, prices start at $1,899, compared to the 700C's original $2,375 price.

Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations are used to study nanoscale thermal properties, primarily through the Green-Kubo (GK) and Non-Equilibrium MD (NEMD) methods. Both require calculation of the heat flux (HF) to determine thermal conductivity κ, and the interfacial heat current Q1→2 is needed for Interfacial Thermal Conductance and Spectral Decomposition of the Heat Current (SDHC) calculations. LAMMPS, a widely used MD code, originally implemented an HF formula valid only for pair potentials, leading to incorrect κ results for many-body interactions. Torii et al. previously derived exact HF formulas for arbitrary many-body potentials, and subsequent corrections have been published for specific systems. However, existing implementations remain limited, and SDHC calculations for many-body potentials are lacking. This work extends and implements the Torii et al. formulas in LAMMPS for control volume and control surface heat flux calculations, including SDHC, for arbitrary many-body potentials. The article presents theoretical background, comparative tests using Tersoff and Stillinger-Weber potentials on 2D and 3D systems, and SDHC results for graphene and MoS2.

COPD, a leading cause of death in the US, is a chronic obstructive disease caused almost exclusively by smoking, according to Dr. Jordan Taillon of Lee Health. Symptoms include chronic coughing and shortness of breath, with patients struggling to exhale. Diagnosis involves reviewing smoking history and a pulmonary function test measuring breathing capacity. Treatment options, based on severity, include inhalers, oxygen, or pulmonary rehabilitation. Though COPD has no cure and lung damage cannot be reversed, treatment can halt decline and reduce exacerbations. Quitting smoking is the most important step to prevent the disease.

The passage examines distance education in sports higher education during the COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey. It begins with a historical overview, tracing distance education from Caleb Phillips' 1728 advertisement through its evolution with modern information technologies.

The study employed a qualitative case study approach using descriptive analysis, interviewing 14 lecturers from sports-related departments at various Turkish universities through semi-structured interviews. Data was analyzed using MAXQDA 20, achieving 82% reliability.

Four main themes emerged from the analysis:

1. **Positive aspects**: Independence from time and space (36.11%), access to resources including lesson repetition (30.56%), use of information technologies (19.44%), and socioeconomic benefits (13.89%).

2. **Negative aspects**: Social influences including communication and participation issues (29.52%), psychological influences such as motivation problems (24.59%), educational issues particularly with applied lessons (24.59%), and technology/access issues (21.31%).

3. **Challenges**: Infrastructure issues including connection problems (51.61%), difficulties with lessons and assessment (32.25%), and ineffective communication (16.13%).

4. **Distance education management**: Process management concerns (66.67%) and education management issues (33.33%), with participants noting poor crisis management and decision-making delays.

The discussion compares findings with similar studies, confirming common advantages (flexibility, accessibility) and disadvantages (inequality, communication problems, technical difficulties).

The conclusion emphasizes that distance education in sports sciences requires field-specific design due to applied courses, raises data security concerns regarding personal data protection, and calls for further research on department-specific distance education effectiveness.

This study investigates the tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) effect in Mn3Sn(01¯10)/MgO(110)/Mn3Sn magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) using first-principles calculations. Mn3Sn is a kagome noncollinear antiferromagnet with an inverse triangular magnetic structure that breaks time-reversal symmetry, enabling TMR effects despite lacking net spin polarization. The Mn3Sn(01¯10) orientation was selected because it supports experimentally demonstrated spin-orbit torque switching.

The calculations yield a TMR ratio exceeding 1000% at 12 MgO monolayers, with reasonable resistance-area values for practical devices. Analysis reveals that the TMR effect arises from two factors: the momentum-dependent spin splitting of Mn3Sn (dominated by the x-component along the cluster octupole easy axis) and electron filtering by the MgO barrier, confirmed through complex band structure analysis showing minimal decay rates near k∥=0. Unlike previous theoretical studies using thin or absent barriers, this work ensures genuine tunneling transport, providing a realistic reference for Mn3Sn-based MTJ applications in antiferromagnetic spintronics.

Jeff Bezos has proposed that future data centres could be built in space to address Earth's growing digital demands. Orbital data centres could reduce pressure on land, energy, and cooling resources while using solar power. However, significant challenges remain, including radiation shielding, cooling in a vacuum, low-latency communication, and high launch and maintenance costs. Other aerospace and technology firms are also exploring orbital and lunar infrastructure, supported by falling launch costs and hardware advances. Though speculative, the concept reflects rising competition for computing power driven by cloud services and AI.

A study published in the Journal of Neuroscience found that barn owls, despite having simpler brains than primates, can group moving elements together to distinguish objects from backgrounds—a visual processing ability previously studied only in humans and primates. Researchers led by Yoram Gutfreund showed barn owls screens of moving black dots and tracked their gaze, finding the birds could identify a target dot moving differently from others, particularly when surrounding dots moved uniformly. Recordings from the ocular tectum, a brain region involved in basic visual processing, showed activity varied with dot movement, suggesting this region handles the task. The findings indicate this perceptual ability may be more fundamental than previously thought, possibly evolved to detect prey against moving backgrounds like wind-blown grass.

Strong US jobs data, with 200,000 jobs added last month and 2.9 percent wage growth—the largest 12-month increase in over nine years—heightened expectations of further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. The dollar and US bond yields rose, with the 10-year US Treasury yield reaching a four-year high of 2.84 percent, while stocks declined. Clark County Schools Superintendent Pat Skorkowsky marked his final day after five years in the role and 30 years in the district. He cited the graduation rate increase from 60 to 83 percent and expanded magnet school seats as key accomplishments. Skorkowsky noted the district's $60 million budget shortfall and urged his successor, Dr. Jesus Jara, to prepare for the pivotal 2019 legislative session. He suggested marijuana tax revenue should be directed to education in counties where it is generated. Skorkowsky also addressed school safety measures, including single-entry doorways and the need for more mental health professionals. He advised Jara to engage with the community and plans to work alongside him briefly. Skorkowsky has not determined his next steps.

Lifeline Fiji's program director Jeremiah Merekula states that suicide remains a taboo subject in Fiji. According to NSAAC statistics, 124 suicide cases and 107 attempted suicides were recorded in 2015, while 102 suicide cases and 104 attempted suicides were recorded in 2016. From 2011 to March this year, 627 suicide cases and 694 attempted suicide cases were recorded, including 56 suicides and 97 attempted suicides among children. Merekula attributes the high numbers to a lack of help-seeking behaviour, limited community support, and low awareness of emotional wellbeing. Lifeline Fiji operates a 24/7 helpline and runs programs for preschool and primary school students, as well as parents, to identify warning signs. The helpline number is 132454.

At RSA Conference 2017, Intel Security's Chris Young warned of "data landmines," where attackers manipulate small data feeding big-data analysis, leading to flawed business decisions. He cited the 2016 U.S. presidential election as an example. Young also identified home networks, including IoT devices, as a growing attack surface threatening corporate networks, referencing the Mirai botnet attack.

Microsoft President Brad Smith called on the tech community to act as a "digital Switzerland," committing to defense-only principles, collaboration, and protecting civilians. He proposed a digital Geneva Convention barring attacks on the private sector and civil infrastructure, and urged governments to disclose rather than stockpile software vulnerabilities. Smith suggested forming an international agency, modeled on the Red Cross, to monitor and attribute nation-state attacks. He cited the 2016 U.S.-China agreement against economic cyber espionage and emphasized that private security practitioners, not governments, should lead cyberspace defense.

The disclosure describes a location-sharing system that predicts a user's destination and shares it with the user's friends through a map-based graphical user interface (GUI) used alongside a social media application.

The system receives location information from a location sensor on a first user's client device via wireless communication. Based on this data, it determines the user's current trajectory and accesses historical location information stored in a database. By correlating the current trajectory with historical data, the system identifies a presumed destination, often selected from the user's habitual places (e.g., home, work, school), which are inferred from patterns in historical location data.

The system computes probabilities based on factors such as distance trends, likelihood of arrival within a set time, duration of stay, and behavioral consistency. If a probability exceeds a threshold, the candidate is selected as the presumed destination. Trajectory patterns, extracted by clustering and averaging historical trajectories, help match current movements to recurring routes.

The map GUI displays avatars representing users and their friends, along with icons marking presumed destinations. The system can also estimate and display arrival times, update locations as new data arrives, and infer transport modes to refine predictions. Users can control sharing permissions, select audiences, and interact with friends (e.g., chat or send messages) directly through the interface.

The document also details supporting software architecture, hardware components, APIs, communication networks, and definitions of related technical terms.

The MSPM0 MCU features an ARM Cortex-M0+ CPU supporting 32kHz-80MHz frequencies, with pre-fetch logic, SysTick timer, MPU, and NVIC. It offers five operating modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) across two power domains (PD1, PD0) for power optimization.

Key components include a PMU with brown-out reset, a clock module with multiple oscillators (LFOSC, SYSOSC, SYSPLL), and a DMA controller with 12 channels. The device provides dual-bank flash memory (up to 512kB) with ECC protection, 128KB SRAM split into two banks, and up to 93 GPIO pins.

Analog peripherals include two 12-bit ADCs (4Msps), a temperature sensor, configurable VREF (1.4V/2.5V), comparators, and a 12-bit DAC. Security features include AES-128/256, TRNG, keystore for four keys, and CRC. Communication interfaces support UART, I2C, SPI (up to 32Mbits/s), and CAN-FD (5Mbit/s).

Additional features include timers (TIMGx, TIMAx), RTC_B, watchdog timers (IWDT_B, WWDT), MATHACL accelerator, serial wire debug, and bootstrap loader via UART or I2C. The device requires specific decoupling capacitors and supports development through TI's LaunchPad, MSPM0 SDK, and various IDEs including Code Composer Studio.

Radyr, reportedly the only Cardiff suburb without a pub since the Radyr Arms closed in 2003, could gain one after Vale of Glamorgan Brewery applied to open a micropub called the Radyr Tap on Station Road. The plans follow a Twitter campaign by resident Jamie Grundy. A consultation runs until June 19, after which Cardiff council will decide. Managing director Phil Newbould said the venue would stock local cask ales, craft beers, wines and spirits, along with artisan meats, cheeses, and snacks, but no cooked food.

MIT has rejected the Trump administration's "Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education," becoming the first of nine invited universities to publicly decline. The compact would require campus changes in exchange for preferential federal funding treatment. MIT President Sally Kornbluth stated the proposal would restrict free expression and institutional independence, and contradicts MIT's belief that funding should be merit-based.

Other invited institutions—Brown, Dartmouth, Arizona, Penn, USC, UT Austin, UVA and Vanderbilt—have mostly issued vague statements, though UT Austin expressed enthusiasm. Dartmouth's president emphasized independence without explicitly rejecting the compact.

State officials in California, Virginia and Pennsylvania have threatened to cut funding for institutions that sign. MIT's rejection was praised by the AAUP, Senator Chris Van Hollen, and some academics who suggested it may influence other universities. However, former Trump administration official Kenneth Marcus hinted at potential retaliation, referencing a pending lawsuit against MIT.

Komar Uddin, a 68-year-old spiritual healer, is on trial at Leicester Crown Court, denying charges of sexual assault, assault by penetration, causing a female to engage in sexual activity and two counts of rape against a 19-year-old woman in February 2015. The prosecution alleges Uddin was invited by the woman's father to drive away an evil spirit the family believed was following her after a relative's death. During a candlelit ritual in her bedroom, while her family was downstairs, Uddin allegedly rubbed holy oil on her, sexually touched her, and raped her twice, telling her afterwards not to tell anyone. He also reportedly claimed she was pregnant and offered to help end the pregnancy for £200. An internal swab contained Uddin's DNA. Uddin was arrested, bailed, and left the country before being extradited from Germany in November. The defence claims the woman instigated sexual contact, which Uddin refused. The trial continues.

Amazon.com, Inc.'s Form 10-K for fiscal year 2020 reports net sales of $386 billion, operating income of $22.9 billion, and net income of $21.3 billion. Headquartered in Seattle, Washington, the company operates through three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS), serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators.

As of December 31, 2020, Amazon employed approximately 1,298,000 full and part-time workers, having hired over 400,000 since February 2020 in response to COVID-19. The company incurred roughly $11.5 billion in COVID-19 related costs during 2020, implementing safety measures across its operations.

Cash flow from operations increased to $66.1 billion in 2020 from $38.5 billion in 2019. Cash capital expenditures rose to $35.0 billion, primarily supporting fulfillment operations and AWS technology infrastructure. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $84.4 billion at year-end.

The filing identifies risks including intense competition, international operations, foreign exchange exposure, intellectual property matters, data security, regulatory compliance, tax liabilities, and supply chain dependencies. Amazon uses restricted stock units as its primary equity compensation vehicle, with total shares outstanding plus stock awards reaching 518 million at year-end 2020.

Prosecutors released three cellphone videos found on Nikolas Cruz, the suspect in the February 14 shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida, which killed 17 people and injured 17 others. In the videos, Cruz announces his intention to become "the next school shooter of 2018," stating he plans to kill at least 20 people using an AR-15. He describes logistics, including taking an Uber to the campus, and expresses loneliness, anger, and hatred. Cruz, 19, a former student at the school, faces 17 counts of murder and 17 counts of attempted murder. His lawyers have offered a guilty plea in exchange for life without parole, but prosecutors are pursuing the death penalty. The videos were released under Florida law requiring evidence shared in pretrial discovery to become public record. Cruz previously attended a school for children with emotional disabilities, and his late mother had called 911 on him nearly 20 times.

The Navy requires a thousand additional officers and expanded Annapolis classes, while facilitating retirement of less useful senior officers. Officer shortages have strained lieutenants and junior grades, whose conduct has been commendable. Though no foreign conflict appears imminent, maintaining an efficient navy is essential to prevent disaster.

Michael T. Klare argues that while President Trump is widely viewed as dismantling the liberal world order, he is simultaneously attempting to construct a new one based on energy preferences, dividing nations into fossil-fuel powers and green-energy states.

According to Klare, Trump's worldview differs from both the Wilsonian model (liberal democracies versus autocracies) and Huntington's "clash of civilizations" framework. Instead, Trump supports fossil-fuel-producing nations and opposes those favoring renewable energy.

Klare identifies three steps in Trump's strategy: first, revitalizing the U.S.-Saudi alliance during his May visit to Riyadh, including a $110 billion arms deal and energy cooperation; second, weakening NATO and the EU while attempting to improve relations with Russia, though domestic controversies have hindered the latter; and third, withdrawing from the Paris climate agreement to boost domestic coal, oil, and gas industries.

Researchers led by Omri Yosef and Prof. Michael Berger at Hebrew University, in collaboration with scientists from Philipps University of Marburg and the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, discovered that blocking a protein called Ant2 in T cells reprograms their energy metabolism. This study surveyed 304 Belgian medical students from four universities to assess their knowledge, attitudes, and exposure to global surgery. Despite 95% of students agreeing that global surgery is relevant and 70% supporting more compulsory teaching, only 24.7% reported exposure to the field, primarily through social media. Knowledge was poor: only 24% knew that five billion people lack access to surgical care, and 22% knew approximately 150 million additional procedures are needed annually. Master's students were less interested in further exposure than bachelor's students. Students preferred optional teaching, events, clinical internships, and required teaching over social media. Reported obstacles to pursuing a global surgery career included personal responsibilities, language barriers, lack of established career paths, financial constraints, and limited mentorship. The authors recommend incorporating pre-clinical global surgery seminars and equitable international clinical internships into medical curricula. Limitations include potential selection bias, limited institutional representation, and lack of a validated questionnaire.

Fred Pearce revisits Paul Ehrlich's 1968 book *The Population Bomb*, which opened with a description of Delhi's crowded streets as evidence of overpopulation. Pearce notes that while half the world's population lives in urban areas—projected to reach 66 percent by 2050—cities are not the cause of population growth but part of the solution. Urban women consistently have fewer children than rural ones: 2.7 in Nairobi versus 4.3 nationally in Kenya, and 1.6 in Delhi versus 2.4 across India. Rural-to-urban migrants quickly adopt smaller families.

However, cities drive a "consumption bomb," using three-quarters of the planet's extracted materials despite housing half its people. London, for example, consumes tens of millions of tonnes of construction materials, food, paper, plastic, and water annually, while producing millions of tonnes of sewage and waste.

The passage introduces EchoingECG, a probabilistic student-teacher framework for cardiac assessment that integrates Probabilistic Cross-Modal Embeddings (PCME++) with ECHO-CLIP to model ECGs. It addresses two challenges: the complexity of ECG signals and the scarcity of ECG data labeled with echocardiogram (ECHO) outcomes. Unlike deterministic contrastive learning methods that enforce one-to-one mappings, the probabilistic approach enables many-to-many mappings by modeling both mean and variance of latent representations, capturing uncertainty across modalities. ECHO-CLIP serves as a teacher model to distill cardiac information into ECG representations through ECHO-ECG pairs. The contributions include a probabilistic multimodal ECG model, a knowledge distillation approach reducing reliance on large annotated datasets, and uncertainty-aware downstream evaluation.

This bibliometric study analyzes academic publications on Digital Accessibility in Education from 2013-2024, using data from Web of Science (WoS), Scopus, and ERIC databases, with VOSviewer 1.6.20 software for visualization.

Publications increased significantly from 12 in 2013 to 502 in 2024, with rapid growth beginning in 2020 during the post-pandemic period. Scopus contained the majority of publications, followed by WoS and ERIC.

Key findings include:
- Journal articles (468) were the most common publication type, followed by conference papers (274) and book chapters (105).
- Research spans 15 areas, with "Digital Accessibility and Inclusion," "Education, Higher Education, and Social Sciences," and "Computer Science and Engineering Sciences" leading.
- English dominated publication languages (873), followed by Spanish and Portuguese.
- Higher education (469 publications) was the most studied educational level.
- The USA (236), UK (104), and Spain (74) produced the most publications.
- Highly cited works include Gorriz (2023), Kuc-Czarnecka (2020), and Bong (2024). Chen Weiqin was the most cited author.
- The USA and UK led in citations and research influence, while Norway showed the strongest collaborative links.

The study concludes that digital accessibility has become an increasingly important research area, though citation distribution is uneven and greater international collaboration is needed. Future research should address legal frameworks and educational challenges such as computer literacy for students with disabilities.

This study evaluated Optical Genome Mapping (OGM) with Variant Intelligence Applications (VIA) software as an alternative to standard cytogenetic testing (karyotyping, FISH, microarray) for hematologic malignancies. Current standards have low resolution, rely on subjective interpretation, and require multiple sequential tests, while next-generation sequencing approaches remain limited by cost and complexity.

Ten retrospective myeloid malignancy cases (nine AML, one MDS) were analyzed 5-6 times each by independent technologist-director teams using a streamlined VIA workflow featuring custom views, filters, panels, and classifications. Technologists sequentially reviewed variants using guideline-based panels, then directors finalized classifications and reports.

Results showed OGM detected all variants identified by standard of care (SOC) testing. In five of six positive cases, sentinel variants were unanimously classified as Tier 1A. OGM additionally identified novel findings in five of six positive cases, including complex rearrangements and interstitial deletions undetectable by karyotype or FISH. Technologist review averaged 25.2 minutes for negative cases, 28.5 minutes for simple cases, and 47.3 minutes for complex cases, representing approximately 50% time reduction compared to Bionano Access alone.

The authors conclude that OGM with VIA provides a streamlined, efficient, objective method for cytogenomic variant interpretation and reporting, potentially alleviating cytogenetics labor shortages and standardizing clinical significance assessments.

The Best 6 Months Timing Model strategy, created by Yale Hirsch, is an active market-timing strategy that can be applied to any asset class or portfolio. Unlike passive strategies, it signals when to enter and exit the market, reducing risk exposure.

Yale Hirsch founded the Hirsch Organization and created the Stock Trader's Almanac in 1968, introducing concepts like the "Presidential Election Year Cycle," "January Barometer," "Santa Claus Rally," and "Best Six Consecutive Months."

For backtesting, a portfolio with equal weights across five asset classes was used: stocks, bonds, REITs, and commodities, selected via diversified, liquid ETFs with long histories. Stocks historically deliver the highest returns; bonds reduce volatility and drawdowns; REITs and commodities improve diversification due to low correlation with traditional assets.

Backtest results over 16 years showed the timing strategy produced a maximum drawdown of -27.27%, significantly smaller than the -47.77% drawdown of a buy-and-hold approach using the same portfolio.

This paper examines the normative assumption underlying empirical studies on educational disparities—that such disparities are unfair and should be corrected—through the lens of luck egalitarianism in contemporary political philosophy.

Luck egalitarianism holds that inequalities caused by "brute luck" (uncontrollable factors like socioeconomic status, gender, or ethnicity) are unjust, while those resulting from "option luck" (individual choices) fall within personal responsibility. Applied to education, this justifies correcting disparities tied to social background.

However, the author draws on Elizabeth Anderson's two critiques to highlight problems with pursuing fairness alone:

1. **The harshness objection**: Luck egalitarianism leaves individuals to bear severe consequences of their own choices, as illustrated by a musician who dropped out of high school and later cannot escape poverty.

2. **The humiliation objection**: Compensation policies can stigmatize recipients, as seen when low-achieving students feel embarrassed receiving extra help.

To address these problems, the paper proposes three additional values:
- **Fresh start** (Fleurbaey, Tomlin): Allowing people to revise past choices and receive new opportunities, countering the Matthew effect.
- **Sufficiency**: Guaranteeing all individuals meet an absolute threshold of welfare or educational attainment, ideally combined with luck egalitarianism.
- **Respect** (Wolff): Avoiding "shameful revelations" required by conditional redistribution, potentially through unconditional support or proficiency-based classes.

The paper concludes that empirical research on educational disparities should extend beyond fairness to investigate these additional values, such as through longitudinal studies on second chances, thresholds of educational adequacy, and classroom humiliation. Collaboration between empirical social science and normative philosophy is encouraged to generate new research questions.

The Trustee of the Liquidation Trust, established under the Modified Plan of Reorganization of Southern Industrial Banking Corporation (SIBC), filed suit under 11 U.S.C. § 548(a) to recover alleged fraudulent conveyances from defendants East Tennessee Equity, Ltd., Theodore A. Erck, and James E. Steiner. Defendants moved to dismiss, arguing the Trustee lacked standing and that any recovery would not result in equal distribution among creditors.

The court denied the motion. Under the Modified Plan, impaired unsecured creditors received distributions including stock or stock purchase rights in the successor-in-interest. Recovery of fraudulent transfers would increase the assets and financial health of the successor-in-interest, thereby augmenting the value of creditors' distributions.

Relying on In re Centennial Industries, the court held that as long as unsecured creditors receive some benefit from recovery, the action is permitted. The court further found that 11 U.S.C. § 1123(b) expressly authorizes a representative of the estate to retain and enforce claims, and its legislative history supports a liberal interpretation. Cases cited by defendants, including Texas Consumer Finance and Sapolin Paints, were distinguished as inapplicable. The court concluded that denying the Trustee's action would create a windfall for defendants while depriving creditors of benefit.

Hardin v. White concerns an action to enjoin an execution sale of real estate in Keokuk. The court addressed two issues:

First, regarding the injunction bond: while Code §§ 3396-3397 requires a bond double the judgment amount when enjoining proceedings on a judgment, this rule does not apply when the action seeks only to prevent sale of a particular piece of property under a general execution. The motion to increase the bond was properly overruled.

Second, regarding liability of the property: The execution creditor, White, held a decree foreclosing multiple liens totaling amounts at different interest rates. Rather than taking a single special execution for the full amount, he took execution for part, sold the property, then sought to sell the debtor's statutory right of redemption under a general execution for the balance. The court held that by taking execution for only part of the decree when he could have taken it for the whole, White exhausted his remedy against that property. Sustaining his position would render the statutory right of redemption nearly valueless.

On rehearing, defendant argued the second execution issued from a different decree (chattel mortgage foreclosure) rather than the real estate foreclosure decree, invoking Barnes v. Cavanagh, 53 Iowa 27. The court distinguished that case, holding that where both decrees cover the same indebtedness entitling the creditor to only one satisfaction, they must be treated as identical for this purpose.

Judgment affirmed.

Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a genetic disorder causing the body to produce abnormal, sickle-shaped hemoglobin cells that carry oxygen less effectively and can block blood vessels. It affects people of all backgrounds but is most common among those of sub-Saharan African descent, and impacts about 100,000 people in the United States.

Symptoms include sudden pain episodes (sickle cell crises), acute chest syndrome, anemia, jaundice, organ problems, infections, and strokes. Smoking increases the risk of complications. SCD is diagnosed through a simple blood test, often at birth, and prenatal testing is available.

Management involves regular screenings, vaccinations, antibiotics for children, pain medication, blood transfusions, and medications promoting fetal hemoglobin. Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the only permanent treatment, reserved for severe cases. Lifestyle recommendations include quitting smoking, maintaining a balanced diet, limiting alcohol, resting adequately, and exercising regularly.
