The products were distributed to retailers and distributors across 15 states. According to the FDA, Listeria can cause serious or fatal infections in vulnerable groups, short-term symptoms in healthy individuals, and miscarriages or stillbirths in pregnant women.

Research from the University of Exeter suggests that traditional, "inefficient" fishing methods have sustained the Fal oyster fishery in Cornwall, the only sail-driven commercial fishing fleet in Europe. Scientists found that motorising the fleet would increase fishing activity at least nine-fold, threatening stocks. Using GPS tracking and onboard observers, researchers compared sail-dredging to mechanised methods. The native European flat oyster is threatened by pollution, overfishing, and non-native species, and two of England's three remaining oyster fisheries have faced temporary closures. The study was published in the Fisheries and Aquaculture Journal.

A Gallup poll found that 44 percent of Americans believe Donald Trump is capable of preventing major scandals, compared to 74 percent for Barack Obama in 2009 and 77 percent for George W. Bush in 2001. Gallup attributed the lower confidence partly to declining trust in government. Across all measured categories, including military decisions and working with Congress, Trump scored lower than his three predecessors, with deficits ranging from 15 to 32 percentage points. The poll surveyed 1,028 adults between December 7-11, with a margin of error of plus or minus 4 percent.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended December 30, 2017, reporting net sales of $88.3 billion (up 13% from $78.4 billion year-over-year) and net income of $20.1 billion ($3.89 diluted EPS). The first quarter of 2018 spanned 13 weeks versus 14 weeks in Q1 2017. Growth was driven by iPhone, Services, and Other Products, with gross margin at 38.4%. All geographic segments grew, led by Japan (26%) and Rest of Asia Pacific (17%).

Total assets were $406.8 billion, with $285.1 billion in cash and marketable securities. The Company issued $7.0 billion in term debt, bringing total term debt to $111.0 billion, and had $12.0 billion in commercial paper outstanding.

Following the December 22, 2017 enactment of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, which lowered the U.S. federal corporate tax rate from 35% to 21% and imposed a deemed repatriation tax, Apple recorded a $7.0 billion income tax provision, including a $2.6 billion provisional estimate ($1.8 billion from remeasuring deferred tax balances and ~$800 million from repatriation tax). The effective tax rate was 25.8%.

Apple repurchased $10.1 billion of common stock and paid $3.3 billion in dividends. Regarding the European Commission's State Aid Decision, Apple expects recovery of approximately €13 billion plus €1 billion interest, to be placed in escrow in 2018 pending appeals.

The article explores how to build a "Get Rich Portfolio" designed to generate high returns with minimal risk. Drawing on Jeremy Siegel's research, it notes that stocks have been the most productive asset class over 220 years, vastly outperforming bonds, bills, and gold. Since most wealthy individuals are business owners, the article argues that buying stocks—becoming a co-owner of profitable businesses—is the key to wealth building.

The authors select liquid, diversified stock ETFs ranked by Return/MaxDD ratio to construct the portfolio. While stock ETFs carry high maximum drawdowns, the article emphasizes that drawdowns differ from permanent capital loss and investors must remain patient. A moderately aggressive portfolio combining various stock categories with different weightings is then proposed and backtested to minimize crisis-period drawdowns.

FOX 17 News, a Tribune station in the 40th market (West Michigan), seeks a meteorologist/Multi-Platform Reporter with at least two years of weather forecasting/reporting experience in a commercial TV newsroom. Responsibilities include delivering on-air forecasts, producing weather graphics, covering breaking news, and shooting, editing, writing, and anchoring content across broadcast, social media, and web platforms. Candidates must have strong time management, digital/social media, editing, and shooting skills, and engage with local communities. Applications should be submitted online with a demo reel link and proof of digital journalism skills.

The team had many scoring opportunities but missed the net often, while the opposing goalie made several key saves. Success came in the third period by getting pucks to the net and creating scrambles, a strategy continued in overtime, but the opponents capitalized on a chance to win. The speaker described it as a painful but valuable learning experience and the hardest thing they've been through. They believe the difficult season brought the group closer together.

Heikin Ashi, meaning "average bar," is a Japanese price representation imported to the West in the late 1990s, popularized by trader Dan Valcu in a 2004 article. Unlike traditional candlesticks that show real open, high, low, and close prices, Heikin Ashi uses calculated averages to smooth price movements and highlight trends or consolidation phases. Because the displayed prices are not real, traders cannot execute directly on them, making it a lagging indicator.

The article notes that the standard Heikin Ashi formulas can be simplified: haHigh equals the maximum of H and haOpen, while haLow equals the minimum of L and haOpen. Additionally, haOpen functions as a 3-period exponential moving average of the previous haClose, a parameter that can be customized to filter noise.

A tested strategy on the S&P 500 (1960–present, monthly timeframe) buys when haClose crosses above haOpen and sells when it crosses below, producing a 49.4% win ratio with favorable asymmetric profit distribution typical of trend-following systems. An additional ADX-based mean reversion test yielded a 5.27% CAGR with only 5% market exposure. The author concludes Heikin Ashi works best on long timeframes.

Enron Corp. shares fell 21% on October 22, 2001, after the company disclosed that the Securities and Exchange Commission had requested information regarding related-party transactions involving limited partnerships run by Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow. Enron stated it would cooperate fully with the SEC, noting that its auditors and board had reviewed and approved the arrangements. A shareholder filed a derivative lawsuit in Texas alleging Enron's board breached fiduciary duties by permitting Fastow to run the partnerships, which allegedly cost the company over $35 million. Additionally, Shapiro Haber & Urmy LLP filed a class action suit alleging securities fraud against Enron. Analysts raised concerns about potential dilution and credit rating downgrades, with Salomon Smith Barney estimating dismantling affiliated companies could cost up to $3 billion. AG Edwards downgraded the stock to "hold." Despite Enron's troubles, broader U.S. stock indexes closed higher, buoyed by better-than-expected earnings from companies including American Express, 3M, and U.S. Steel. Separately, UniPrime Capital Corporation announced a Letter of Intent involving a wind park ground lease owned by an Enron subsidiary.

Enron Corp. shares fell approximately 21% on October 22, 2001, after the company disclosed that the Securities and Exchange Commission had requested information about related-party transactions involving limited partnerships run by Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow. Enron stated it would cooperate fully with the SEC, noting its auditors, attorneys, and board had reviewed and approved the arrangements, which were disclosed in SEC filings.

The partnerships, including LJM Cayman LP and LJM2 Co-Investment LP, engaged in transactions with Enron involving company assets. Enron took a $35 million charge and reduced shareholder equity by $1.2 billion after repurchasing 55 million shares to unwind its involvement. Salomon Smith Barney analyst Ray Niles estimated dismantling additional affiliated companies could cost up to $3 billion.

Multiple law firms filed shareholder lawsuits, including a derivative suit alleging Enron's board breached fiduciary duties by permitting Fastow to run the partnerships, and a class action alleging securities fraud during July 13 through October 16, 2001. AG Edwards downgraded Enron stock from "buy" to "hold." Enron shares had declined 75% year-to-date, with CEO Jeff Skilling having resigned in August.

Broader markets rose Monday, with the Dow gaining 1.9% on positive earnings reports from companies including American Express, 3M, and U.S. Steel.

World stocks rose and equity volatility approached record lows on Monday as investors focused on strong economic growth signs ahead of several central bank rate decisions. European stocks climbed, with Britain's FTSE up 0.6 percent. Bitcoin futures debuted on the CBOE, with the one-month contract opening at $15,850 and later trading at $18,600, while bitcoin has surged 1,600 percent this year. Lukas Daalder of Robeco noted the 11 percent premium indicated disconnection between markets. The Federal Reserve is expected to raise rates this week, while the Bank of England and European Central Bank are likely to hold steady. Sterling edged lower to $1.3375, and the dollar index eased 0.1 percent. Ten-year Bund yields dipped below 0.30 percent. Oil prices fell on increased U.S. drilling activity, with U.S. crude at $57.13 and Brent at $63.16.

Fabinho has indicated his intention to leave Monaco, following the departures of Bernardo Silva, Benjamin Mendy, and Tiemoue Bakayoko. Reportedly a Manchester United target, the 23-year-old stated after Monaco's 4-1 win over Dijon that the club is aware of his wishes. However, vice-president Vadim Vasilyev said last month that Fabinho and Thomas Lemar, both considered essential players, would not be sold this transfer window.

Gold rallied strongly on Friday alongside a declining USD Index, but remains below its rising resistance line and mirrors its 2011-2013 price pattern. Notably, silver, mining stocks, and platinum did not follow gold's rally. The VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF closed below the April high for a third consecutive day, suggesting the early stages of a larger decline, as gold stocks typically outperform gold during rally beginnings.

The USD Index is positioned for further gains, having verified an inverse head-and-shoulders breakout by returning to the neck level, with a target of at least 101.3. Stocks are consolidating above 6,250 after declining below their rising support line, signaling potential for significant further drops.

The author compares current conditions—resilient gold, rising USD, falling stocks, and weak miners—to the 2008 market environment.

Trinidad and Tobago won the men's 4x400 metres relay at the World Athletics Championships, ending the United States' streak of six consecutive titles. Lalonde Gordon overtook Fred Kerley on the final straight after the U.S. had led most of the race following a strong third leg by Michael Cherry. Jereem Richards and Machel Cedenio ran the earlier legs, helping Trinidad claim their first world title in the event with a time of 2:58.12, the fastest this year. Britain took bronze, while Jamaica, Bahamas, and Botswana failed to reach the final. It was Trinidad's only gold of the championships. The U.S. last lost this title in Paris in 2003.

FHA loans treat married couples jointly, requiring lenders to pull credit on both spouses even if only one is on the mortgage. A non-applicant spouse's debts count toward the debt-to-income ratio, potentially reducing borrowing power for purchases or refinances. This rule does not apply to single or engaged individuals, only legally married ones. Married applicants whose spouse has poor credit may benefit from switching to a conventional loan, which requires 1.5 percent more down payment but lacks this requirement. Unmarried couples are advised to purchase before marrying. Additionally, a quit claim deed is required when one spouse applies for a mortgage on a separate property.

A resurfaced 2013 YouTube video shows actress Allison Mack praising NXIVM-affiliated women's group JNess, calling it the "most gratifying" work she had done. Mack was arrested on April 20 and charged with sex trafficking and forced labor for allegedly recruiting women as sex slaves in NXIVM. NXIVM founder Keith Raniere was arrested on similar charges a month earlier. A 2017 New York Times investigation revealed women in the organization were called "slaves" and subjected to ritual humiliations and brandings. In the video, Mack also named Lena Dunham and Miranda July as personal heroes.

A 16-year-old girl from Waterloo, Iowa, suffering from severe depression, visited a hair salon before her school portrait with matted hair she could no longer brush. She requested her head be shaved, but 20-year-old student stylist Kayley Olson refused. Instead, Olson spent 13 hours over two days untangling the hair and restyling it into a shoulder-length cut. Olson shared the experience in a Facebook post, which was shared over 75,000 times, urging awareness of mental health issues in children. The teen reportedly told Olson she felt like herself again and would smile for her photos. Commenters praised Olson and shared similar experiences.

The Side Screen is a motion offense using continuous on-ball side screens, forcing defenses to defend quick-hitting options across the full court while hindering box-outs due to constant player movement.

Entries include the High Post Rub (point guard passes to wing and cuts off the post), Dribble Clear (point guard dribbles to wing while the wing back cuts), and Pass & Clear (point guard passes and clears to the opposite corner).

Basic actions involve the wing driving over the on-ball screen, with options to drive, pull up, pass to the rolling or popping screener, or kick out to shooters. Continuity includes ball reversal, back cuts, screen and roll, and dribble hand-offs.

Defensive counters include: slipping the screen against show-and-recover defenses, popping out or posting up against switches to exploit mismatches, and stringing out traps into a 2-1-2 alignment with baseline cuts when the high post receives the ball.

The lecture series addresses nuclear arms control and nonproliferation, with the first lecture focused on India-Pakistan tensions delivered by MIT political science professor Vipin Narang. Professor Aaron notes that nuclear exchange risks remain high despite reduced public attention since the Soviet Union's collapse, and emphasizes the need for technically trained people in arms control.

Narang covers basic deterrence theory, including the concepts of deterrence by punishment versus denial, and the three requirements: capability, credibility, and communication. He explains that nuclear weapons transformed deterrence by enabling massive destruction with minimal risk to the attacker.

India and Pakistan operate fission and boosted fission weapons. India follows an assured retaliation posture with no-first-use policy under civilian control, aimed primarily at deterring China. Pakistan, under military control, adopts an asymmetric escalation doctrine with tactical nuclear weapons to offset India's conventional superiority.

Historically, Pakistan's nuclear program began after the 1971 war, predating India's 1974 test. Pakistan acquired uranium enrichment via AQ Khan's stolen URENCO designs and received Chinese assistance. The US tolerated Pakistan's program during the 1980s Soviet-Afghan war.

Post-1998 nuclearization, Pakistan has sponsored militant attacks (Kargil 1999, Parliament 2001, Mumbai 2008), using nuclear deterrence to shield against Indian conventional retaliation. India has shown restraint in all three crises, but Narang warns future attacks could trigger escalation, making South Asia uniquely dangerous due to the combination of proxy militancy and nuclear weapons.

Kieran Trippier called England's penalty shootout victory over Colombia "the best feeling of my career." The Tottenham wing-back performed strongly during the 1-1 draw in Moscow and converted England's fourth penalty in the shootout. England advanced to the World Cup quarter-finals after Eric Dier scored the winning kick, marking only their second victory in eight penalty shootouts. Yerry Mina's injury-time equaliser had cancelled out Harry Kane's penalty. Trippier said the team blocks out negative expectations and believes in themselves. Dele Alli, who played despite a thigh injury and was substituted late, praised goalkeeper Jordan Pickford for his penalty save from Carlos Bacca, calling him a "top-class keeper."

A three-year study of 195 health facilities in Uganda, presented to the Global Fund Country Coordinating Mechanism, examined the sustainability of HIV treatment programmes. The research, published in BMC Health Services Research, found that the current HIV funding structure favours larger, well-established hospitals, which can attract multiple donor grants, while smaller, rural, and for-profit facilities struggle to sustain services. Barriers include shortages of ART-proficient staff, difficulty meeting donor reporting requirements, and irregular ARV supply. For-profit facilities' goals often conflict with mass HIV treatment access, and patients frequently bypass smaller clinics for larger hospitals. The author recommends mentoring partnerships between large and small facilities, service purchase agreements, and salary support for select for-profit providers. Increased Ugandan government involvement is urged to reduce reliance on external donors.

The socket cover includes a latch mechanism and support tabs to lock the actuation lever in the closed position. Lever actuation force must be less than 3.6 kgf, and package pin displacement during actuation must be under 1.0 mm. The socket must maintain integrity after 50 actuation cycles. Visual inspections at 1X magnification must confirm no missing, damaged, or misaligned solder balls, contacts, gold plating, cover, base, tabs, latch, or lever.

Electrical specifications include: contact current rating of 1.5 A with less than 30°C temperature rise; initial and final LLCR not exceeding 25 mΩ per contact with Kovar pins, measured across 200 daisy-chained pairs; single-pin partial self-inductance under 4 nH; mated-loop and partial-loop inductance of 3 nH ± 10%; capacitance under 1 pF; differential impedance of 100 Ω ± 10%; propagation delay skew under 10 ps plus 3 ps error; dielectric withstanding voltage minimum 650 Vac; and insulation resistance minimum 1000 MΩ. Measurements are taken at 500 MHz and 2 GHz.

Corn futures are contracts with corn as the underlying asset, traded on the CME Globex platform and settled by physical delivery. A corn futures strategy involves techniques for profitable trading, including technical and fundamental analysis, entry/exit signals, position sizing, and risk management.

The corn market is influenced by weather in growing regions, USDA reports (WASDE, Prospective Planting, Grain Stocks, Crop Production), and demand from China. Macro numbers also affect commodity prices significantly.

Corn futures exhibit seasonality, performing better in January, February, April, May, October, November, and December than in summer months. Two seasonal backtests are presented: the first shows a 70% max drawdown due to a 2012 short trade, while the second uses a momentum filter, yielding 1.13% average per trade over 175 trades with low stock market correlation.

Full contracts equal 5,000 bushels (tick size $12.50); mini contracts equal 1,000 bushels (tick size $1.25). The all-time high was $8.3125 (2012) and low was $1.007 (1960). Major risks include leverage-related losses. Alternatives include CFDs and the Teucrium Corn Fund ETF (CORN).

The Supreme Court will hear arguments on whether Delaware's "affidavit of merit" statute, which requires medical malpractice plaintiffs to submit a medical professional's affidavit attesting to negligence, applies in federal court. The case involves Harold Berk, a Florida resident suing a Delaware doctor and hospital over treatment of an ankle injury. Because the parties are from different states, Berk filed in federal court, avoiding immediate dismissal that would have occurred in Delaware state court.

The central issue is whether the statute is "substantive" law that federal courts must apply, or "procedural" and thus superseded by federal rules. Berk argues federal rules define all requirements for federal cases and contain no affidavit requirement. Choy and Beebe argue Rule 11 permits statutory exceptions and that the requirement falls outside federal rules. They emphasize the statutes' purpose of limiting malpractice litigation costs. A professors' brief contends the statutes are procedural and would disrupt federal judicial administration. The justices' views remain uncertain.

AIRSS (Ab-initio Random Structure Search) generates random structures using chemically informed parameters, producing distributions near local minima. Users specify MINSEP (pair-wise minimum separation σij between atomic species) and TARGVOL (target volume Ω). A two-stage optimization satisfies these constraints: first iteratively separating overlapping atoms, then optimizing lattice and ionic degrees of freedom at fixed volume using a truncated Lennard-Jones model.

President Jackson informs Congress that South Carolina, through an ordinance passed by its convention in November and subsequent legislative acts, has declared federal tariff laws of 1828 and 1832 null and void within the state, effective February 1. The state prohibits enforcement of these laws, forbids appeals to the Supreme Court, requires officials to swear oaths upholding the ordinance, and is organizing military forces, including authorization for 2,000 volunteers in Charleston and 10,000 additional state guards.

Jackson reports that his December 10 proclamation and the administration's willingness to modify tariff laws have not altered South Carolina's position. He argues that the state's actions—claiming rights to both nullify federal laws and secede—are revolutionary and subversive of the Union. He rejects the legitimacy of unilateral secession, asserting that constitutional remedies through the judiciary and amendment process must be exhausted first, and notes South Carolina has not pursued these remedies.

Jackson states that existing enforcement mechanisms, including the 1799 collection act, are inadequate against organized state resistance, particularly the state's replevin process and the sheriff's posse comitatus powers. He requests Congress authorize: relocating custom-houses to secure locations within ports; detaining vessels until duties are paid; using military and naval forces to protect customs officers; transferring state court cases against federal officers to federal circuit courts; providing for safekeeping of federal prisoners; and modifying the 1795 act to allow the President to deploy force when states militarily obstruct federal laws.

He concludes by affirming his determination to enforce the laws and preserve the Union.

The speaker praises an opposing player's puck-handling and playmaking, noting he was screened on the winning goal. He suggests his team needs to play lanes better and avoid being too deep defensively. While his team dominated late in the second period, the opponent's power play generated many chances and scored twice, which he identifies as the difference in the game. He was surprised by a late call involving a hit from behind. He notes the referees called the game more strictly than the previous two, requiring more care with sticks and interference. On the road, line matching is harder without last change, but he felt his team handled matchups well. They plan to regroup for Thursday.

This study evaluated the Karius Test, a plasma microbial cell-free DNA (mcfDNA) sequencing test, using results from 19,739 samples collected from 16,172 patients across 39 U.S. states and D.C. between April 2018 and September 2021. The test can identify and quantify mcfDNA from over 1,500 bacteria, DNA viruses, fungi, and parasites.

Key findings include a median turnaround time of 26 hours, with 96% of samples yielding valid results. Performance metrics were consistent with the initial validation study. Of valid reports, 58% identified at least one microbe, representing 701 unique taxa and 22,792 detections. The top 50 taxa included 36 bacteria, 9 viruses, and 5 fungi, with common commensal pathogens predominating.

The test successfully detected diagnostically challenging organisms including Legionella, Nocardia, Mycobacterium species, systemic dimorphic fungi, and zoonotic pathogens—many of which are difficult to identify using standard-of-care methods. Multiple species co-detections within single reports suggested either divergent strains, database gaps, or true polymicrobial infections.

Limitations included lack of orthogonal testing data, limited clinical context (available for only 29% of patients), and inability to analyze repeat testing patterns. The authors conclude that mcfDNA sequencing offers non-invasive pathogen detection with potential clinical and public health benefits, but emphasize the need for diagnostic stewardship and further outcomes studies to optimize its application.

Coach Julien commented that his team did not play their best game, citing poor decision-making, weak puck movement, and deviation from their normal game plan, though the team battled back to force overtime. He described the overall performance as average and noted the opposition outplayed them in the first half. Julien praised Patrice Bergeron for consistent strong play on both sides of the ice, Jaromir Jagr for his playmaking ability, and Johnny Boychuk for his scoring and defensive reliability. He emphasized focusing on the present game rather than looking ahead or dwelling on previous results, noting the series has been tight and either team could win individual games. Julien also discussed maintaining open communication with players like Tyler, praised Jagr's work ethic and conditioning as an example for younger players, and highlighted the importance of role players stepping up in Gregory Campbell's absence.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended April 28, 2019. The company reported revenue of $2,220 million, down 31% year-over-year from $3,207 million, with net income of $394 million ($0.64 diluted EPS), down 68% from the prior year. Gross margin decreased to 58.4% from 64.5%, primarily due to lower gaming margins and portfolio mix shifts. Operating expenses rose 21% to $938 million, driven by employee additions and related costs.

GPU business revenue declined 27% to $2,022 million, reflecting declines in gaming and data center revenue and the absence of cryptocurrency mining processor sales. Tegra Processor revenue fell 55% to $198 million due to lower gaming platform SOC shipments. By market, Gaming revenue dropped 39%, Data Center decreased 10%, Professional Visualization grew 6%, and Automotive rose 14%.

On March 10, 2019, NVIDIA entered a Merger Agreement to acquire Mellanox Technologies for $125 per share (approximately $6.9 billion), subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals, with a potential $350 million termination fee.

NVIDIA adopted the new lease accounting standard on January 28, 2019, recognizing $470 million in operating lease assets and $500 million in operating lease liabilities. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $7.80 billion as of April 28, 2019. The company returned $97 million in dividends during the quarter and intends to return $2.20 billion more to shareholders by fiscal year-end 2020. Ongoing litigation includes securities class actions related to cryptocurrency mining disclosures and lawsuits concerning the Mellanox merger.

Thyroid nodules, which can be benign or malignant, affect a significant portion of the population and traditionally require diagnosis via invasive Fine Needle Aspirations (FNA) or expert-analyzed ultrasounds. This pilot study developed a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to classify thyroid ultrasound images as benign or malignant, using the Thyroid Digital Image Database (TDID) with TI-RADS classifications.

The researchers combined two pre-trained models, VGG-16 and Inception v3, to leverage both general image recognition and medical imaging capabilities. To address the small, imbalanced dataset, they applied image augmentation, early stopping, and class weighting (favoring benign cases 4x). The model used binary cross-entropy loss and was trained for 10 epochs with a batch size of 8 on a GPU-equipped desktop.

The hybrid model achieved 87.5% accuracy and an AUROC of 0.929, indicating strong performance without overfitting. Limitations included the small, skewed dataset. The authors conclude that CNNs can potentially support radiologists in diagnosing thyroid cancer from ultrasounds.

India's Congress party elected Rahul Gandhi as its president on Monday, succeeding his mother Sonia Gandhi, who had led the party since 1998. Gandhi, great-grandson of India's first prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru, was elected unopposed. The move positions him to challenge Prime Minister Narendra Modi ahead of the 2019 national elections. Since Congress's heavy defeat in 2014, Gandhi has struggled to demonstrate leadership, and the party has suffered poor results in local elections. His elevation coincides with state polls in Modi's home state of Gujarat. A November Pew survey found Modi retains a favourability rating 30 points higher than Gandhi's.

Hiscox's eighth annual DNA of Entrepreneur report, based on a survey of over 4,000 small and medium-sized businesses across six countries, examines the state of entrepreneurship. In the U.S., 50 percent of respondents always wanted to be their own boss, with flexibility (68 percent), control (61 percent), and remote work (57 percent) cited as top motivators over money (37 percent). U.S. businesses reported strong performance: 70 percent saw revenue growth, 68 percent profit growth, and 73 percent gained new customers, with financial services, hospitality, and technology leading. Forbes ranked Bend, Oregon as the top small metro for business, citing a 6.6 percent job growth rate. However, 17 percent of U.S. small businesses report difficulty obtaining bank funding, prompting use of personal credit cards (23 percent), venture capital (11 percent), and peer-to-peer lending (15 percent). Oregon offers state-funded programs including OBDF, CAP, CEF, IDB, and EDLF. Only 34 percent of owners feel government policies support entrepreneurs, and 61 percent lack succession plans. Oregon's economy is approaching full employment, with growth expected through 2017.

Interest rates and stocks are generally believed to have an inverse relationship, though since the 2000s, the correlation has become more positive. While interest rate shifts typically take 12 months to affect the economy, the stock market reacts more quickly.

A backtest was conducted using the S&P 500 index (not adjusted for dividends), trading based on whether the SMA is above or below the 10-year yield. Buying when rates were rising produced poor compounded returns, which aligns with the theory that rising rates increase the opportunity cost of investing in stocks, pushing investors toward treasuries.

Conversely, investing in the S&P 500 when interest rates were falling significantly improved CAGR, with slightly less time in the market and similar drawdown. This strategy performed better before the 1990s than during the 2000s and 2010s quantitative easing era.

Overall, holding stocks when rates fall is more profitable than buying when rates rise.

President Barack Obama announced in an email statement that he will deliver a farewell address on January 10 in his hometown of Chicago, referencing George Washington's 1796 farewell address as precedent. Obama said the speech would thank supporters, celebrate changes over his eight years in office, and offer thoughts on the future. Donald Trump, who pledged during his campaign to undo many of Obama's policies, will be sworn in on January 20. Obama has worked to ensure a smooth transition despite policy differences.

The Apple Watch Series 3 has maintained Apple's dominance in the wearable market despite its limited LTE rollout since September 2017. Initially available in countries including the US, UK, Australia, and Japan, it later expanded to Hong Kong and Singapore. Not all carriers in these regions supported the LTE version, and China banned the device after initial acceptance. Starting May 4, pre-orders will open in Denmark, Sweden, and India, with deliveries a week later. Three will be the sole carrier in Denmark and Sweden, while Reliance Jio and Airtel will support it in India. Pricing has not been officially announced.

IFC Films has promoted Mark Boxer to executive vice president of sales and distribution, and Lauren Schwartz to senior vice president of publicity and promotions. Boxer oversees theatrical, non-theatrical, and Canadian distribution for IFC Films, Sundance Selects, and IFC Midnight, having worked on releases such as "Boyhood" and "The Trip" series. Schwartz has led promotional campaigns for films including "45 Years" and "Finding Vivian Maier," and previously served as publicity director at Oscilloscope Laboratories. Co-presidents Jonathan Sehring and Lisa Schwartz praised their contributions to the company's reputation in independent cinema.

Marquez Charter Elementary reopened on a temporary campus nearly nine months after the Palisades fire destroyed much of the site, making it the first public school to return to a campus damaged by the January Palisades and Eaton fires. Roughly 130 students are attending the temporary facility, which includes 19 classrooms, a kitchen, library, and play areas. Enrollment has dropped about 58% since the fire, with three-quarters of students no longer living in the Palisades.

The temporary campus and rebuild will cost approximately $202.6 million, with completion expected by 2028. Rebuilding all three damaged campuses—including Palisades Charter Elementary and Palisades Charter High School—is estimated at $600 million. LAUSD's decision to reopen Marquez first was based on parent surveys and town halls, though some parents expressed concerns about environmental risks and commutes.

Pasadena Unified, the hardest-hit district, has installed portable structures at several campuses but has no rebuild timeline and lacks a construction bond, relying instead on insurance and public funding sources.

The MMA Manifesto's Middleweight Rankings, voted on by a four-member panel, list the top fighters in the division. Michael Bisping retains the #1 spot as UFC Middleweight Champion with 39 points, followed by Luke Rockhold (35) and Yoel Romero (34). Chris Weidman and Ronaldo 'Jacare' Souza are tied at #4 with 25 points each. Gegard Mousasi ranks #6, Robert Whittaker moves up to #7, and Anderson Silva drops to #8. Vitor Belfort holds #9, while Kelvin Gastelum debuts at #10. Derek Brunson dropped off the rankings. Suspended or inactive fighters (12+ months) are excluded.

This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of open education literature to identify key trends, thematic patterns, and future research directions. Using co-citation and co-word analyses via VOSviewer on 402 articles from the Web of Science database, the research addresses gaps left by prior studies that focused narrowly on specific elements like OER or MOOCs.

The co-citation analysis identified five clusters: evolving open education, OER's role in education, adoption of open education, educational paradigms of MOOCs, and implementation of open educational practices (OEP). The co-word analysis revealed five emerging themes: blended learning, openness during COVID-19, challenges of OER adoption, inclusive digital pedagogy, and collaborative online academia.

Findings indicate open education is a dynamic field intersecting pedagogy, technology, and social justice. While OER offer cost savings, accessibility, and flexibility, challenges remain regarding faculty acceptance, institutional support, scalability, and regional disparities, particularly in underresourced areas.

Limitations include reliance solely on the Web of Science database, subjective cluster interpretation, and limited attention to regional variations. Future research should combine bibliometric and qualitative methods, examine contextual factors influencing adoption, and explore potential drawbacks to provide a more balanced understanding of open education.

The OHL (Open, High, Low) trading strategy is an intraday stock trading approach that uses the configuration of open, high, and low prices in the first few minutes of a session to determine trade entries. A buy signal occurs when the open equals the low (suggesting bullish sentiment), while a sell signal occurs when the open equals the high (suggesting bearish sentiment). The strategy is best applied on lower timeframes such as 1-minute, 5-minute, or 15-minute charts. Some traders combine it with CPR (central pivot range) levels, going long only when buy signals occur above CPR levels and short when sell signals occur below.

Backtests on the S&P 500 (ES futures) produced 1,401 trades with an average gain of 0.04% per trade. Results improved to 0.06% when the day's open was above the prior close, and dropped to 0.01% when below. WTI crude oil showed a 0.12% average gain under similar conditions. Reversed rules produced 0.00% average gains for both markets. The backtests suggest the first minutes of trading have some predictive value for the rest of the day.

A multi-patch isogeometric neural solver is proposed to address three key limitations of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) when applied to complex computer-aided design (CAD) geometries: enforcing solution conformity across multi-patch domains, strongly imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions (BCs), and handling geometric variations. The method combines PINNs with isogeometric analysis (IGA), drawing from finite element tearing and interconnecting and mortaring methods. Neural network-based ansatz functions operate on IGA's reference domain, using non-uniform rational B-spline (NURBS) parametrizations to map solutions to the physical domain. Separate ansatz functions approximate solutions within individual patches and on interfaces between neighboring patches, ensuring C0-continuity. A custom output layer with residual connection strongly enforces Dirichlet BCs, while operation on the reference domain naturally normalizes inputs. Training uses the variational PINN framework, minimizing a discretized energy functional. The method is demonstrated on two engineering applications: a 2D magnetostatics quadrupole magnet model and a 3D nonlinear solid mechanics mechanical holder model with hyperelastic material and contact BCs.

Owen Sound Foodland, located in Georgian Bluffs, is among 87 new Ontario stores authorized to sell beer and cider starting in April, bringing the provincial total to 370. Selected through an LCBO bidding process, it will be the first grocery store in the immediate Owen Sound area to offer these products. Owner Bill Graham said the beer and cider will be sold at a new 34,000-square-foot store, tentatively opening March 22 on the former Towers/Zellers site. The new location will emphasize fresh products, expanded catering, delivery, and health-focused items, and include a sit-down eating area. Staffing will grow from 100 to roughly 160 employees.

Machine learning force fields (MLFFs) provide a computationally efficient alternative to first-principles methods like Density Functional Theory (DFT). While graph-based equivariant neural networks (GNNs) represent the state-of-the-art, they face challenges with point-defect computations, including oversmoothing, large supercell demands, and limitations to local interactions.

To address non-local interactions critical to defect formation, the authors introduce ADAPT (Accelerated Deep Atomic Potential Transformer), a coordinate-based Transformer using attention over all atom interactions to predict per-atom forces from Cartesian coordinates and atomic features. Trained on a DFT database of silicon defects, ADAPT uses separate networks for force and energy prediction, avoiding graph structures and inductive biases.

Each atom is tokenized as a 12-dimensional vector containing coordinates and atomic properties (group, period, electronegativity, covalent radius, valence electrons, ionization energy, electron affinity, atomic radius, molar volume), then embedded into a higher-dimensional space via an MLP. ADAPT reportedly outperforms pretrained universal MLFFs like MACE and MatterSim, with training costs two orders of magnitude lower than message-passing architectures.

Nearly 88% of Ireland's publicly-quoted companies met or exceeded market expectations in recent earnings reports, according to a Merrion Capital review of 33 Irish companies. Aryzta, Ryanair, Tullow Oil and IFG Group missed expectations, while 16 companies, including CRH, Kerry Group and Grafton, beat forecasts. Average earnings per share growth was 8%, despite sterling's decline against the euro. The Iseq index reached a 15-month high of 6,750.78 points, 6% above its pre-Brexit referendum level. Merrion Capital's David Holohan cited robust economic growth driven by domestic consumption and employment, though the Iseq has underperformed other European markets due to Brexit concerns. Irish Continental Group leads the Iseq 10 with a 17% share increase, followed by Origin Enterprises, Glanbia, Kerry Group and FBD. Aryzta performed worst, declining 27.2% after a January profit warning and executive departures.

The study examines Turkish parents' experiences, opinions, and suggestions regarding emergency distance education during the COVID-19 pandemic. Following the March 2020 pandemic declaration, Turkey suspended face-to-face education and implemented distance learning through platforms like EBA, TRT EBA TV channels, and ADES.

Using a descriptive survey model, data was collected from 2,371 parents across Turkey's 12 NUTS regions via a 16-question questionnaire distributed through teacher networks between May 2020 and June 2022.

Key findings include:
- 57.7% of parents held positive views on distance education (citing educational continuity and health protection), while 42.3% viewed it negatively (citing inefficiency and adaptation difficulties).
- 86.4% did not arrange private lessons for their children.
- WhatsApp (91.1%) was the primary teacher-parent communication channel.
- 90% agreed internet fees should not be charged for EBA use; 86.5% rejected distance education fully replacing face-to-face education.
- Main criticisms centered on inadequacy (41%), difficulty (17.8%), time problems (17.4%), and technical issues.
- Positive aspects included educational continuity (47.4%), repetition opportunities (42.2%), and health protection (10.4%).
- Suggestions included implementing online exams, continuing distance education as support, enriching content, and extending lesson durations.

The study concludes that economic inequalities, infrastructure problems, and the digital divide were deepened by the pandemic. Recommendations include improving technological infrastructure, providing economic incentives for families, strengthening open-source educational philosophy, and developing digital literacy policies for all citizens.

The Detroit Tigers, currently competing in the ALDS, have been identified as needing a dedicated closer rather than their current closer-by-committee approach. Writer Powell suggests Suarez, expected to opt out this offseason, as a potential fit. Suarez posted a 2.97 ERA, 75 strikeouts, a 0.904 WHIP, and 40 saves over 70 appearances this season. The Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs Commission will be merged with the Ministry of Culture and the Mainland Affairs Council by the end of this year, ending nearly a century of operations. Six of its 49 employees will transfer to the council, with the rest continuing Mongolian and Tibetan affairs work under the ministry. Founded in 1928, the commission serves 472 Mongolians and 648 Tibetans in Taiwan. Calls to abolish it have grown since Taiwan's democratization, as it has no control over those regions. President Tsai Ing-wen prioritized scrapping the commission in October last year, and the Executive Yuan plans to propose abolishing the authorizing act next legislative session. DPP Legislator Tsai Yi-yu opposed merging part of it into the council, arguing the entire commission should join the Ministry of Culture. KMT Legislator Lin Te-fu called it a move toward de jure independence, while NPP Legislator Hsu Yung-ming urged swift abolition.

Manchester United manager Jose Mourinho has urged Marouane Fellaini to sign a new contract amid an ongoing stand-off. Fellaini, substituted shortly after coming on during the Tottenham defeat due to injury, could be sidelined for up to two months with a knee problem. Renewable energy production fluctuates with natural resource variability, and since the grid lacks storage, excess power can destabilize it, sometimes prompting operators to pay consumers to use surplus electricity. Prof. Mahesh Bandi of OIST, in a paper published in Physical Review Letters, used turbulence theory and wind plant data to explain the statistical nature of wind power fluctuations. While it was previously assumed that wind power spectra matched Kolmogorov's 1941 wind speed spectrum due to the power-speed relationship, Bandi showed the match arises for a different reason, since speed is measured across space simultaneously while power is measured at a fixed location over time.

Bandi describes turbulence as eddies of varying time-scales, with shorter high-frequency eddies nested inside larger low-frequency ones. Turbines within the same eddies produce correlated fluctuations. Analyzing data from 20 Texas wind plants and 224 Irish wind farms, Bandi demonstrated that "geographic smoothing"—the averaging of power across dispersed plants—only works at high frequencies, as distant plants may share long time-scale eddies, producing correlated low-frequency fluctuations that cannot be averaged out.

These findings have implications for estimating backup reserve requirements, reducing carbon emissions from standby coal plants, and guiding policy on optimal combinations of renewable energy sources by region.

Merger arbitrage is a trading strategy that exploits price differentials between a target company's stock price and the offer price during mergers or acquisitions. Arbitrageurs buy target shares at market price, expecting convergence with the acquisition price upon deal completion. Success requires analyzing deal completion likelihood, regulatory hurdles, deal terms, and market conditions, alongside strong risk management.

Performance testing showed the IQ Merger Arbitrage ETF had a CAGR of 2.73% since 2010 versus 18.52% for the S&P 500, with volatility of 7.83 vs. 17.27. The Merger Fund returned 4.46% CAGR since 2013 versus 17.37% for SPY, with volatility of 3.81 vs. 17.29.

A Verdad Research study of 835 deals (2000-2020) found an 89% closure success rate, with successful deals averaging 2.0% returns and canceled deals losing 2.8%, producing a blended 1.5% return. The strategy offers uncorrelated, market-neutral returns but requires deep deal-specific analysis.

Oxygen-containing rare-earth hydrides (REHO) exhibit color-neutral photochromism, losing nearly 50% transmittance under illumination, making them promising for smart window applications. This study investigates the kinetics of the photochromic reaction in yttrium oxyhydride (YHO) films produced via reactive magnetron sputtering.

Transmittance measurements during illumination revealed a rapid initial decay (within 2-3 minutes) followed by slower darkening, which could not be described by simple zero-, first-, or second-order reaction kinetics. Electron energy loss spectroscopy showed a plasmon peak shift (14.4 eV vs 15.9 eV) between photochromic and opaque films, indicating higher concentrations of free or mobile hydrogen in photochromic samples.

The authors proposed a two-phase exponential decay model incorporating light-induced hydrogen migration and a non-photoactive volume fraction. This model fit the data significantly better than single-phase models, revealing two distinct rate constants (k1=0.016 s⁻¹ and k2=0.001 s⁻¹). The fast decay is attributed to local processes driven by light absorption and possible loosely bound hydrogen release, while the slow decay is linked to hydrogen migration/diffusion within the film and associated lattice contraction.

The findings suggest that tuning these two processes through microstructure modification could optimize photochromic properties for energy-efficient device applications.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on January 26, 2022, reporting under Item 2.02 that it released its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended December 31, 2021. The Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2021 Update was posted on Tesla's website and attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

The U.S. federal government shut down at midnight Wednesday after Congress failed to pass a funding continuation, adding uncertainty to the education system following months of grant cancellations and funding freezes. The Department of Education stated Title I and special education funds would be distributed as expected, but districts relying on Impact Aid—nearly 1,100 districts serving eight million students—could face cash flow issues. A prolonged shutdown could disrupt Head Start, school nutrition programs, and WIC benefits, though the USDA reports sufficient funds to reimburse September and October school meals. SNAP benefits should continue if the shutdown lasts under a week.

Democrats are seeking to reverse Medicaid cuts and extend ACA tax credits, while Republicans pushed a short-term bill extending funding to Nov. 21. The Trump administration, which blames Democrats, may use the shutdown to pursue further downsizing; the Office of Management and Budget instructed agencies on Sept. 24 to consider mass layoffs, prompting a union lawsuit. During the shutdown, Education Department civil rights investigations, regulatory work, and grant communications will pause.

Chicago wheat prices rose 0.9 percent to $4.54-3/4 a bushel on Tuesday, recovering from a 7.8 percent decline over the previous three sessions—the largest three-day drop since April 2013—after rain and snow brought relief to drought-affected U.S. winter wheat crops in the southern Plains. The storm delivered about 1 inch of moisture to Kansas, Nebraska, and northern Colorado. The USDA rated 11 percent of Kansas winter wheat as good-to-excellent, down from 12 percent the prior week. Corn rose 0.1 percent to $3.75-1/2 a bushel, and soybeans gained 0.2 percent to $10.25 a bushel, following losses in the previous session. Analysts cited rains in Argentina as pressure on corn prices. Australian wheat was offered at $306 a tonne in Iraq's tender for 50,000 tonnes of hard milling wheat.

William Asa Hutchinson III, the 42-year-old son of Arkansas Governor Asa Hutchinson, was arrested by State Police and booked into Washington County jail on charges of DWI, speeding, and violation of implied consent. Billionaire U.S. investor Paul Kazarian, owner of Japonica Partners, has opened his first European office in Lisbon and views Portugal's corporate sector as ripe for investment. He noted Portuguese companies tend to focus on Portuguese-speaking markets like Angola and Mozambique rather than expanding globally, and said his firm can add value by making such businesses globally competitive. The Lisbon office will also consider investments across Europe.

This study investigates degradation mechanisms in commercial NMC/graphite lithium-ion coin cells (3032) cycled at high C-rates, using Lithium Nuclear Reaction Analysis (Li-NRA) alongside XRD, SEM, and EDS characterization.

Cells were cycled between 2.7–4.3 V at 25°C through 278 cycles: 11 at 1C, 67 at 2C, and 200 at 3C. Capacity retention dropped from ~100.3% at 1C to 89.2% at 2C and 51.9% at 3C, while internal resistance at 3C rose from 0.23 Ω to 0.34 Ω. Coulombic efficiency slightly decreased with higher C-rates (99.88% to 99.80%).

XRD revealed a contraction of the cathode c-lattice parameter (14.27878 Å to 14.27442 Å) and expansion of the graphite c-parameter (6.71906 Å to 6.72132 Å), indicating structural degradation and lithium trapping. SEM showed surface decomposition and micro-cavities on cycled cathodes and cracking with SEI formation on cycled anodes. EDS indicated decreased cathode density (4.624 to 4.20 g/cm³) and increased anode density (1.99 to 2.03 g/cm³).

Li-NRA quantified a bulk lithium loss of 1.86 × 10²² atoms/cm³ in the cathode (~19.7% loss) and a gain of 1.38 × 10²² atoms/cm³ in the anode (115.96% increase), confirming irreversible lithium consumption, plating, and trapping. The findings demonstrate Li-NRA's effectiveness for non-destructive, spatially resolved lithium profiling in diagnosing battery degradation.

The Education Department announced it will rewrite two Obama-era rules—Borrower Defense to Repayment and Gainful Employment—that govern student loan forgiveness in cases of university fraud. Secretary Betsy DeVos called the regulations "overly burdensome and confusing," noting colleges complained the definitions of misrepresentation were too broad and lacked due process. Hearings will be held in July, and DeVos said nearly 16,000 pending defense claims will still be processed. Eight states and D.C. filed a motion to retain the rules. The original regulations followed a crackdown on for-profit colleges, including Corinthian Colleges and ITT Technical Institute, which shut down amid fraud allegations. Consumer advocates criticized the revision, warning it would leave students with unaffordable debt and shift costs to taxpayers, while an industry group supported DeVos's actions.

The Carolina Panthers signed defensive tackle Kawann Short to a five-year, $80 million deal, ending a year-long negotiation and removing the franchise tag placed on him in February. The extension reflects GM Dave Gettleman's emphasis on interior linemen and the franchise's win-now approach under 66-year-old Gettleman and 80-year-old owner Jerry Richardson, who seeks a first Lombardi Trophy.

Other win-now moves include signing Julius Peppers to a one-year deal, adding safety Mike Adams, and re-signing cornerback Captain Munnerlyn. The average age of projected defensive starters is 29.45.

Offensive concerns remain, particularly around quarterback Cam Newton's recovery from shoulder surgery. Coach Ron Rivera has indicated the offense must evolve under coordinator Mike Shula. The team replaced receivers Ted Ginn Jr. and Philly Brown with Russell Shepard and Charles Johnson, and signed tackle Matt Kalil to a five-year deal worth up to $55 million.

With the No. 8 pick—their highest since Gettleman's 2013 arrival—the Panthers are expected to target an offensive playmaker such as Leonard Fournette, Christian McCaffrey, or O.J. Howard.

The University of Calgary will host the annual Battle of Alberta chess tournament on February 18–19, 2017, in That Empty Space. According to U of C Chess Club president Riley Workman, 30 to 40 players will compete, including six to eight from the U of C. The tournament follows World Chess Federation rules, including time clocks and the "no touch" rule. The U of C Chess Club, founded in 2015 by Workman and Chinmoy Ayachit, holds weekly meet-ups for players of all skill levels. The event is open to independent players and non-students, with registration fees of $10 for university students and $15 for non-students.

The passage describes methods and systems utilizing a cache coherent switch on chip based on the Compute Express Link (CXL) interconnect standard. The switch enables low-latency memory access, coherent caching, and resource sharing between components such as accelerators, memory, storage, ASICs, and persistent memory without requiring processor involvement as a bottleneck.

Key features include:
- Upstream and downstream ports supporting PCI and CXL protocols, with switched fabric circuitry and processing cores.
- Virtual hierarchies and bridges (PPB, vPPB, SR2MR, SLD2MLD) allowing single-root or single-logical devices to be exposed as multi-root or multi-logical devices.
- Fabric managers for allocating and deallocating resources, managing hot-plug devices, and interfacing with higher-level management software via Ethernet or PCI.
- Memory expansion and pooling across servers, racks, and data centers, including through Ethernet bridging with defined packet formats for reads, writes, and acknowledgments.
- AI/ML-based memory prefetchers, compression/decompression, encryption, and erasure code accelerators integrated into the switch.
- Cache coherency resolution between accelerators and CPUs, enabling accelerator-to-accelerator traffic and reducing CPU bottlenecks.
- Support for computational storage services and chiplet integration.

The passage also details software stack configurations for CXL over Ethernet (including modified L2 layers with configurable interframe gaps), IPSec headers, and various frame formats for CXL 2.5, CXL 3.0, CXLoverMPLS, and L3/L4 layers, along with defined command codes for memory operations, prefetching, and device management.

Sugar futures are derivative contracts traded on ICE and CME exchanges, representing agreements to deliver or receive sugar at a future date and pre-agreed price. On ICE, contracts (symbol SB) settle via physical delivery, while CME's Globex platform (symbol YO) settles financially. One contract equals 112,000 pounds of sugar, with a tick size of $11.20 and minimum price fluctuation of 0.0001 per pound. Contracts follow a March, May, July, and October cycle.

A sugar futures strategy is a method combining technical and fundamental analysis for trading sugar profitably, used for speculation, portfolio diversification, or hedging. Sugar prices are influenced by government subsidies, tariffs, ethanol demand (linked to oil prices), Brazil's currency value, and weather. Historically, sugar performs better in February, June, July, November, and December.

The author considers sugar difficult to trade and does not trade it. A tested ATR channel breakout strategy based on turtle trading rules showed modest positive but random results, with a low win ratio offset by few large winners.

Sugar's all-time high was 66.00 US cents (November 1974) and all-time low was 2.63 US cents (June 1985). Major risks include leverage-amplified losses from adverse price movements. ETFs offering sugar exposure are available, and CFDs provide an alternative without expiry dates.

Prime Day offers discounts on MacBook models, but whether it's a good time to buy depends on the model. All current MacBooks are at least $200 off on Amazon, making the M4 MacBook Air (now $800 with 16 GB RAM and 256 GB storage) the best deal. Despite rumors of an M5 MacBook Air, the performance upgrade is unlikely to justify waiting, and Apple typically discontinues older models after new releases.

The M1 MacBook Air remains available at $600, though Apple may soon launch a new entry-level MacBook, possibly with an iPhone chip and 12.9-inch display, to replace it.

MacBook Pro discounts are smaller (10–13 percent), and rumors suggest M5 MacBook Pros could launch within weeks or months, with one report indicating an M5 model this month without Pro or Max variants. A redesigned, thinner MacBook Pro, possibly with a touchscreen, is reportedly planned for the M6 generation. Buyers seeking maximum power may want to wait.

The Supreme Court heard arguments in a case brought by William Case, a Montana man shot by police who entered his home without a warrant in 2021. Police had responded after Case's former girlfriend reported he threatened suicide and harm to officers. Upon entering, an officer shot Case, believing he had a gun. Case was charged with assault and argued evidence from the warrantless entry should be excluded, but state courts ruled police did not need a warrant in non-criminal matters if entry was reasonable.

During 75 minutes of arguments, justices appeared inclined to reject Case's proposed probable cause standard in favor of giving police more leeway. Justices Thomas, Roberts, and Kagan questioned applying "probable cause" outside criminal contexts, while Alito, Jackson, and Kavanaugh expressed concern that a stricter standard would hinder emergency responses. Montana's Solicitor General argued the Fourth Amendment only bars unreasonable searches, not all warrantless ones.

Justices debated whether to remand the case to the Montana Supreme Court or apply the "objectively reasonable" standard directly. A decision is expected by June or early July.

This proclamation, issued by President Thomas Jefferson on November 27, 1806, addresses reports that citizens and residents of the United States are conspiring to launch a military expedition against Spanish territories by arming vessels in western waters, gathering supplies, and recruiting participants under false pretenses. Jefferson warns misled citizens to withdraw from the enterprise and orders all involved to cease their activities or face prosecution. He directs civil, military, judicial, and executive officers at all levels to search out offenders, seize vessels and military stores, and prevent the expedition by lawful means. He also calls on citizens to assist authorities in identifying and apprehending those involved. The document is signed by Jefferson and countersigned by James Madison.
I am unable to summarize this passage.

Kano Pillars drew 1-1 with Niger Tornadoes in a week 12 rescheduled match of the 2017/2018 Nigeria Professional Football League at the Sani Abacha Stadium. Andrew Ikefe scored for the visitors in the 19th minute, while Junior Lokosa equalised via a penalty in the 81st minute, bringing his season tally to 11 goals. Coach Ibrahim Musa praised his players and fans, and stated the team would prepare for their next match against Kwara United in Ilorin.

A Market Structure Trading Strategy analyzes elements like swing highs/lows, support and resistance levels, and trendlines to interpret price movements. Traders identify three primary market structures: trending (sustained upward or downward movement), ranging (oscillation within a defined range), and consolidating (indecision with narrow ranges).

Key components of analysis include swing highs/lows, support/resistance levels, and trendlines/channels. Supplementary tools include candlestick patterns (e.g., doji, engulfing), volume analysis to validate breakouts, and Fibonacci retracements for identifying potential reversal levels, though Fibonacci is difficult to backtest.

Common entry strategies are breakout trading (entering when price breaks key levels, reportedly more effective in commodities and Bitcoin than stocks) and pullback trading (entering during retracements in established trends).

Risk management involves stop-loss orders based on support/resistance, though these may reduce long-term profitability, and adjusting position sizes according to market conditions. Multiple time frame analysis can confirm market structures, while harmonic patterns like Gartley and Butterfly use Fibonacci ratios to identify reversals but are hard to backtest. The article repeatedly emphasizes the importance of backtesting strategies personally.

The President transmits dispatches from Mr. Wise, U.S. envoy to Brazil, regarding the slave trade. The documents reveal methods used to evade U.S. laws against the traffic, implicating American citizens alongside British subjects. American vessels are nominally chartered but effectively sold to Brazilian slave dealers, with English brokers and capitalists assisting. These ships clear for Britain, load "coast goods," proceed to Africa, exchange merchandise for slaves, and return under a substitute crew to Brazil. The original American crews, often unaware, bear legal penalties while the principal organizers escape punishment.

British factors supply goods and facilitate misuse of the American flag. Mr. Wise's suggestions to British envoy Mr. Hamilton for suppressing the trade are commended for consideration.

The President questions whether additional U.S. measures are needed and criticizes British policy, which transfers captured slaves to West Indian colonies under apprenticeships and pays bounties per captive. These interests, he argues, perpetuate rather than suppress the trade, producing outcomes little different from slavery itself. He urges Britain to adopt more effective measures consistent with returning captured Africans home.

DS, the premium brand from PSA Peugeot-Citroen, is expanding its UK range with a new PureTech 225 petrol engine for the DS7 Crossback SUV. The engine, featuring advanced technologies, delivers 225hp with 6% reduced fuel consumption, and is paired with a new EAT8 automatic gearbox that further improves efficiency via an ECO mode. Eventually, the DS7 Crossback will offer five combustion engines and a 300hp hybrid powertrain. At launch, four Euro 6.2-compliant engines are available: PureTech 180, PureTech 225, BlueHDi 130, and BlueHDi 180. The PureTech 225 is available on multiple trims, starting at £34,990.

President Coolidge reports that the Union is in a state of unprecedented prosperity, domestic tranquility, and international peace. Four revisions of the internal revenue system have reduced taxes while increasing national income to over $90 billion, and one-third of the national debt has been retired. However, with only a $37 million projected surplus, no new appropriations can be made without new revenue, and further tax reductions are not possible.

In foreign affairs, the Sixth International Conference of American States advanced cooperation, 11 arbitration treaties were signed, and a peace treaty renouncing war was signed by 15 nations in Paris. Relations with Nicaragua, Mexico, China, Chile, and Peru have improved. Coolidge recommends settling the Greek and Austrian debts.

On defense, the Army requires no increase, but the Navy needs cruiser replacements. Veterans' relief expenditures approximate $765 million annually and continue to grow.

Agriculture has improved but still faces a surplus problem; Coolidge recommends creating a Federal Farm Board with a revolving loan fund, while opposing government price-fixing and subsidies.

Other recommendations include: continued railroad consolidation legislation, merchant marine support, Inter-American highway assistance, expanded air mail routes, a Colorado River dam leaving power generation to private enterprise, leasing Muscle Shoals for nitrate production, maintaining restrictive immigration, consolidating federal legal activities under the Attorney General, and continued Prohibition enforcement with state cooperation.

Coolidge concludes that prosperity requires continued effort, integrity, and generosity toward other nations.

The author reports that most Hawaiians and foreign residents favor annexation to the United States, particularly anticipating a political crisis upon the death of the current sovereign, who has no heir. American missionary influence over fifty years has made Hawaiians sympathetic to U.S. democratic ideals, and the Fifteenth Amendment has increased annexation's popularity. The native population has declined to 45,000, while foreigners, mostly Americans, control government offices and capital. Strategic arguments for annexation include Hawaii's central Pacific location for a naval and coaling station, its value for protecting growing trade with Asia, and the risk of a hostile European power seizing the islands during wartime. The author suggests annexation could be achieved cheaply, requiring only purchase of Crown lands and annuities for chiefs. The king, aged 41 and in poor health due to obesity, is the last of the Kamehameha line and is unlikely to name a successor.

A mother, Imgur user LauraCorreadaSilva, shared a warning urging parents to keep sick children home after her 3-year-old daughter Chloe was hospitalized following a Christmas dinner. Chloe contracted respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) after playing with a cousin whose father claimed was not contagious despite having a lung infection. Because Chloe has asthma, RSV posed serious risks, requiring antibiotics and a breathing machine. The mother shared the story to warn others that assumptions about contagiousness can have severe consequences.

On June 14, 2017, developer Ed Russo commemorated the groundbreaking of the Annin Lofts project in Verona, converting the historic Annin Flag manufacturing building on Bloomfield Avenue into a 112-unit apartment complex. The ceremony, held on Flag Day, included the Verona Fire Department Honor Guard raising an American flag. The building operated as a flag manufacturing plant from 1919 to 2013. The main building will contain 52 loft-style units with an added penthouse floor, while a new adjacent building will hold 60 more studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom apartments. Architect Kurt Vierheilig said completion is expected in 12 to 14 months. Annin Flag CEO Carter Beard, former plant manager Joe Vallone, and Verona Mayor Kevin Ryan also spoke at the event. Vallone recalled increased production after the September 11, 2001 attacks, including a large flag made for the George Washington Bridge.
