He praises a teammate, described as the heart and soul of New Jersey, for scoring a meaningful goal in a Stanley Cup Final. He recounts making a difficult save on a Modano slapshot, then stopping Brett Hull's rebound. Comparing this series to a previous one, he notes respect for the opposing team, acknowledges lucky bounces contributed to their lead, and emphasizes the next game starts fresh.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 26, 2016. The company reported net sales of $50.6 billion for the quarter and $126.4 billion for the six-month period, decreases of 13% and 5% respectively compared to the prior year, driven primarily by lower iPhone sales and foreign currency weakness. Net income was $10.5 billion for the quarter and $28.9 billion for the six months. Gross margin was 39.4% for the quarter. iPhone unit sales declined 16% year-over-year, iPad 19%, and Mac 12%, while Services net sales grew 20%.

Geographically, Greater China net sales fell 26% and Americas declined 10%, while Japan grew 24%. During the quarter, Apple introduced iPhone SE and the 9.7-inch iPad Pro, issued $15.5 billion in long-term debt, repurchased $7.0 billion of common stock, and paid $2.9 billion in dividends.

Total assets were $305.3 billion and total term debt reached $71.9 billion. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $232.9 billion, with $208.9 billion held by foreign subsidiaries. The effective tax rate was 25.6% for the quarter. Apple also disclosed an ongoing European Commission investigation regarding alleged state aid from Ireland, with potential material but unestimable impact. Apple expects third-quarter 2016 gross margin between 37.5% and 38.0%.

The Foreign Office agreed to update the US Embassy on its discussions with Belgian officials regarding renewal of the Anglo-Belgian purchase agreement on the Belgian Congo, which expired August 31. A memorandum outlined new challenges: Far East developments increased the importance of Congo raw materials (wolfram, tin, copper, palm oil, rubber), and Britain pressed Belgium to boost production. However, competing US offers at significantly higher prices (palm oil at £40-50 vs. UK's £18; rubber at 14 pence vs. 8½ pence) complicated matters, as did the lack of coordinated Belgian supply requirements. Belgium reportedly prefers dollars over pounds.

In response, the UK Ministry of Supply proposed a broad arrangement covering both Congo requirements and UK/US purchases, suggesting joint UK-US negotiations with the Belgian Minister of Colonies. Washington meetings involving the State Department, Board of Economic Warfare, Combined Raw Materials Board, and British Embassy unanimously endorsed this coordinated approach.

Sienna Senior Living Inc. announced a February 2017 dividend of $0.075 per common share, annualized at $0.90, payable March 15, 2017 to shareholders of record as of February 28, 2017. The dividends qualify as eligible dividends under Canadian tax law. Sienna offers a Dividend Reinvestment Plan (DRIP) allowing shareholders to reinvest cash dividends into additional Common Shares issued from treasury at a 3% discount to market price. Participation is optional. Sienna operates 55 residences across Canada with 9,000 employees, providing a range of seniors living services.

Nigeria's Finance Minister, Kemi Adeosun, announced that Nigeria and foreign countries, including the UK, have begun the Automatic Exchange of Tax Information (AETI), which Nigeria joined in January 2018. Data received on overseas assets, bank accounts, property, and trusts held by Nigerians is being used to support the Voluntary Assets and Income Declaration Scheme (VAIDS) and to send "nudge" letters to potential tax defaulters. Adeosun urged users of offshore structures to regularise their taxes before VAIDS expires.

During the presentation of the Progress Report on Tax Laws Reform, NTPIC Vice Chairman Taiwo Oyedele said the Committee aligned reforms with the Economic Recovery and Growth Plan, National Tax Policy, and Ease of Doing Business Plan. Seven key tax areas were identified, including CIT, VAT, CET, PIT, pensions, IDITR, and the Tertiary Education Trust Fund. The Committee's work produced two executive orders and five amendment bills.

Following backlash over Project Maven, a Pentagon contract, Google announced it will create an ethics policy regarding military projects that will reportedly prohibit AI use in weaponry, according to The New York Times. CEO Sundar Pichai promised guidelines incorporating employee feedback, with details expected soon.

Internal emails reveal executive concerns about the project. Fei-Fei Li, chief scientist for Google Cloud, warned against any public mention of AI in connection with the contract, citing potential media backlash. Google chose not to publicize its involvement, but debate spread among employees. A departing engineer renamed a conference room after Clara Immerwahr, a chemist who protested science in warfare. DeepMind executives, including Mustafa Suleyman, joined policy discussions, and AI research head Jeff Dean signed a letter opposing machine learning for autonomous weapons.

Google Cloud CEO Diane Greene and cofounder Sergey Brin addressed employee questions. Greene held an April 11 roundtable featuring Vint Cerf and Meredith Whittaker, though it did not satisfy employees who felt Google had violated its "Don't be evil" principle.

Eleven Ursuline High students and six adults will travel to Nicaragua from April 2-8 during spring break. According to assistant principal Maggie Mattune, participants will help locals with food, housing, home visits, cooking, and playing with children. Parent volunteer Aimee Morrison noted students also help build houses. Mattune stated the trip teaches empathy and compassion while preparing students for a global society.

Dr Chukwuma Agubata, a pharmacist and researcher at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, stated that Irvingia fat from Ogbono nuts can improve the efficacy of the anti-malaria drug Artemether. According to him, Artemether has low water solubility, limiting its absorption, but formulating it with locally-sourced Irvingia fat as microparticles helps the drug reach the bloodstream effectively. He said consuming Ogbono soup while taking Artemether aids the drug's delivery in the body. Agubata called on the government and private organisations to support advancing the research for mass production.

A Nationwide Home Insurance survey found that pet owners spend nearly £3,500 in the first year of ownership. First-year costs average £2,455 for cats, £4,791 for dogs, £12,654 for horses, £1,802 for rabbits, and £769 for fish, covering items such as food, bedding, and equipment. The Association of British Insurers reported a record £706 million in pet insurance claims in 2016. Among those claiming on home insurance for pet-related accidents, 7 per cent reported carpet damage, 5 per cent damage to sofas and chairs, and 5 per cent broken TVs. Nationwide's Rob Angus advised owners to budget ahead to avoid financial difficulties.

On Saturday 9 December, the Palmerston North Rescue Helicopter was dispatched three times. It first transferred a 31-year-old man with a suspected spinal injury from a swimming pool incident to Christchurch Hospital. It was then sent east of Pahiatua to airlift a 57-year-old motorcyclist with a fractured leg to Palmerston North Hospital. That evening, it transported an 11-year-old boy with a back injury from a trampoline fall in Ohakune to Whanganui Hospital. The helicopter is operated by Philips Search and Rescue Trust, a charity reliant on sponsor and community funding.

This study examines the (re)construction of professional identities among language teachers in initial formation, drawing on the author's experience in teacher training and public school English teaching. Guided by Alsup's (2006) concept of "Borderland Discourse," the research explores how preservice teachers integrate their personal selves with professional expectations to form autonomous, reflexive identities.

The theoretical framework draws on Applied Linguistics, Anthropology, and sociocultural theories, treating identity as multiple, transitory, and transformative rather than fixed. Identity construction involves negotiation between "claimed" and "assigned" identities through discourse and social practice.

The study analyzes internship reports from two participants, Laura and Richard, collected over four semesters (2010-2011) during their Supervised Internship in English Language. Both expressed dissatisfaction with the disconnect between university theory and school practice. Laura progressed from apprentice to language teacher, developing a flexible, student-centered professional identity committed to adapting and being different from criticized models. Richard criticized his trainers as disconnected from public school realities and, despite developing a holistic, paternalistic teaching identity, ultimately rejected becoming an English teacher, identifying instead as a mother-language teacher.

The author draws four conclusions: (1) the institutional context provided fertile ground for identity negotiation; (2) four transient identity categories emerged—student/apprentice, internship professor, foreign language teacher, and sociocultural identity—without chronological order; (3) the Supervised Internship discipline is crucial for identity reconstruction; and (4) the Moodle platform served as an emotional scaffold for sharing experiences, making narratives a privileged site for understanding identity construction.

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) finalized rules requiring payday and auto title lenders to verify borrowers' ability to repay loans within 30 days, and limiting repeated debit attempts on borrowers' accounts. CFPB Director Richard Cordray said the rules prevent lenders from trapping borrowers in unaffordable loans. A 2014 CFPB study found over 80 percent of payday loans are rolled over or followed by another loan within two weeks.

The Financial Services Association of America argues the rule would devastate an industry serving 30-40 million customers annually, potentially pushing borrowers toward unregulated lenders. The CFPB estimates loan volume could be halved, forcing many of 16,000 payday stores out of business. Fifteen states have already banned such lenders.

The rule would take effect in 2019 and could be rolled back by Congress. Republican lawmakers, including Sen. Mike Rounds and Rep. Jeb Hensarling, have introduced legislation to weaken the CFPB. A Pew Charitable Trusts poll found 70 percent of surveyed adults want more payday lender regulation.

Ariel Miranda pitched seven shutout innings in the Mariners' 6-1 win over the Marlins at Safeco Field, allowing four hits, striking out five and walking none to earn his first win of the season. Following spring training debate over whether he should serve as a reliever or starter, Miranda began the season in the rotation after Drew Smyly's injury. He aggressively used his fastball, throwing it 63 of 97 pitches, complemented by his changeup. Manager Scott Servais praised the outing, noting Miranda relies heavily on his fastball. Robinson Cano, who had been slumping with a .212 average, hit a 441-foot home run off Tom Koehler in the first inning. Nelson Cruz immediately followed with a 410-foot homer. It marked the sixth time this season a Seattle starter threw seven shutout innings.

Oil prices fell on Thursday as easing Middle East tensions reduced the risk premium on crude markets. Reports of progress toward a Gaza ceasefire boosted investor confidence, with Brent crude dropping around 1.4 percent to $65.07 per barrel and WTI falling to $61.55. Rising U.S. crude inventories and slowing demand in transport and manufacturing added to the decline.

Expectations of potential Federal Reserve interest rate cuts next year produced mixed signals, supporting risk assets but tempering oil demand forecasts. With geopolitical tensions subsiding, analysts said focus has shifted to fundamentals, including rising output from the U.S. and Brazil and weaker demand in Europe and Asia. Analysts forecast relative stability in energy markets barring renewed tensions.

The lecture reviews quantum states of light, focusing on coherent states as eigenstates of the annihilation operator with complex eigenvalue alpha, representing the closest quantum analog to a classical electromagnetic field. Coherent states are minimum uncertainty states, satisfying the Heisenberg limit between position and momentum-like variables.

Three quasi-probability distributions (Q, P, and Wigner W) describe phase space in quantum optics, each with different operator orderings and trade-offs. Q is always positive, P gives delta functions for coherent states, and W projects correctly onto momentum/position distributions but can be negative, indicating non-classical behavior.

The second-order coherence function g2(τ) characterizes intensity fluctuations. Classically, g2 ≥ 1, but quantum states can yield g2 < 1, signaling non-classical light. For single-mode light, g2 is independent of τ and relates to photon number fluctuations via the Fano factor. Coherent states have g2 = 1 (Poissonian), thermal states have g2 = 2 (super-Poissonian), and Fock states have g2 = (n−1)/n (sub-Poissonian), reaching 0 for single photons.

An attenuated coherent state is not a single-photon state. True single photons require single atoms in cavities, either via direct excitation or heralded schemes using many atoms with Raman transitions, where detection of one photon signals readiness to emit another.

The Hanbury Brown Twiss experiment measures g2 using a beam splitter and two detectors with coincidence detection, distinguishing thermal light (g2 = 2) from laser light (g2 = 1) and single photons (g2 = 0).

New research published on October 6 by an interdisciplinary team led by MBARI reveals that marine heatwaves can disrupt the ocean's biological carbon pump, reducing its capacity to transport carbon to the deep sea. Using data from robotic BGC-Argo floats and ship-based plankton surveys, researchers examined two heatwaves in the Gulf of Alaska: "The Blob" (2013–2015) and another in 2019–2020. In both events, shifts in plankton communities caused carbon particles to accumulate near the surface or in the twilight zone rather than sinking to the deep ocean, increasing the risk of carbon returning to the atmosphere. The changes differed between the two heatwaves, with altered phytoplankton populations favoring smaller grazers that produce less sinkable waste. The findings highlight the need for sustained, coordinated ocean monitoring as marine heatwaves grow more frequent and intense.

Yen Bai province plans to develop raw material areas and hi-tech processing facilities to advance its agro-forestry-fishery sector under its industrial development plan to 2020, with a vision to 2025.

The province has 430,000 hectares of forests and 104 wood processing facilities, though most use low-tech production. It aims to attract investment in high-quality furniture production, targeting 300,000 products annually and 850 billion VND in revenue by 2020, doubling by 2025.

Yen Bai also has significant tea (11,000 hectares), cinnamon (40,000 hectares), and cassava (16,000 hectares) cultivation, supported by numerous processing facilities. Van Yen district targets 900 billion VND from industrial production by 2020.

Additional goals include investment in camellia fruit and bamboo shoot processing, aiming for 200 billion VND by 2025, and establishing cattle meat processing facilities with over 3,000 tonnes annual capacity.

In No. 1995—Equity, defendants moved to dismiss on grounds that the action had abated because plaintiff Bill Vassar ceased to be County Attorney of Lincoln County, Oklahoma in January 1939, and his successor, Frank McVey, failed to be substituted as plaintiff within the six-month period required under Rule 25(d) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.

Judge Vaught found that Rule 25(d) is substantially the same as 28 U.S.C.A. § 780, and that the language of both is clear and mandatory. Although plaintiff contended Vassar was merely a nominal party and the State of Oklahoma was the real party in interest, the petition itself identified Vassar as the party bringing the action.

The court held the rule applicable, requiring dismissal without prejudice. The same ruling was applied to equity cases Nos. 1996, 1997, 1999, 2000, 2001, and law cases Nos. 6362 and 6363, with exceptions allowed to plaintiff in each.

The Austro-Hungarian government received, through the United States, the enemy states' reply to its December 12 peace proposal. After joint examination with its allies, it found the enemy governments declined the proposal, alleging it lacked sincerity.

The Imperial and Royal Government disclosed its views to neutral powers, stating the enemy reply avoided discussing how to end the war, instead revisiting pre-war events and military claims. It maintained that responsibility for the war has been established, citing Serbia's hostile actions culminating in the Sarajevo assassination as justification for its ultimatum.

It asserted that Austria-Hungary and its allies sought defensive aims, while enemy states sought territorial conquests including Alsace-Lorraine, partition of Turkey, and dismemberment of Austria-Hungary. It rejected the "stratagem" accusation as unprovable before negotiations, noting the adversaries refused to hear the terms.

Responding to enemy demands regarding nationalities and small states, it cited the treatment of Irish, Finnish, and Boer peoples, North Africa, and Greece. The government disclaimed responsibility for the war's continuation and vowed to fight on until securing a peace ensuring its peoples' existence and honor.

Celebrity chef Mario Batali has stepped away from daily operations of his restaurant empire following reports by Eater New York of sexual misconduct involving at least four women over a 20-year period, three of whom were his employees. Batali acknowledged the complaints "match up" with his past behavior and apologized. His company said an employee first formally reported inappropriate conduct in October, resulting in a reprimand and required training. ABC asked Batali to step away from "The Chew" pending review, and the Food Network paused plans to relaunch "Molto Mario." The allegations follow a wave of sexual misconduct claims affecting figures in politics and entertainment. Batali co-owns restaurants in multiple cities through the Batali & Bastianich Hospitality Group and is a partner in Eataly.

Starbucks (SBUX) stock has been flat since late-2015, disappointing investors who expected stronger growth. U.S. comparable-store sales have fallen below the company's usual 5% benchmark, partly due to congestion caused by its Mobile Order & Pay platform, though management reports comps are rebounding. Promotions like the Unicorn drink and Frappuccino Happy Hour are expected to boost sales, and prior-year Q3 issues involving loyalty program changes and altered transaction reporting will no longer distort comparisons.

Starbucks began paying dividends in April 2010 at 5 cents per share and raised it to 25 cents in November 2016, reflecting a compound annual growth rate above 26%.

In China, Starbucks opens roughly 500 stores annually, with management expecting this pace to continue for decades. Regional comp-store sales grew 7% last quarter, supported by a rapidly expanding middle class. The company's strong workplace culture is also cited as a key strength.

The Grocery Basket Score (GBS) is a model developed to rate the health properties of entire grocery shopping baskets, complementing existing product-level systems like the Nutri-Score. Using NHANES dietary recall data from 2001-2018 linked with 2019 mortality data for 35,462 individuals, researchers constructed "density signals" (nutrient proportions relative to total basket) and "deficiency signals" for essential nutrients, evaluating them through Cox proportional hazard models.

The final GBS combines separate food and beverage models via calorie-weighted averaging. The food model incorporates seven signals: saturated fats, sugar, sodium, fiber (protective), and deficiencies in protein, vitamin C, and iron. The beverage model assesses calorie density. The biggest risk drivers were vitamin C and iron deficiency, followed by high beverage calories, sodium, saturated fats, and sugar.

Validation against 913,298 items from the Open Food Facts database yielded a 0.60 correlation with the Nutri-Score, with cluster correlations ranging from 0.25 to 0.75. Differences arose for dairy products (rated lower by GBS due to missing nutrients) and sweet snacks (rated higher by GBS as it excludes calorie density). Validation against the Alternate Healthy Eating Index (AHEI) using 4,382 NHANES participants showed stronger correlation (-0.62) than the calorie-weighted Nutri-Score (-0.48).

Limitations include development on a U.S. population, reliance on self-reported dietary data, and inability to capture alcohol's non-caloric health effects. Strengths include automated deployment without manual food annotation, compatibility with retailer loyalty programs, and density-based scoring that does not require household size information.

Cam Newton apologized for sexist comments made at a recent press conference, where he told Carolina beat writer Jourdan Rodrigue that it was "funny" to hear a female ask about routes. The Panthers quarterback faced backlash and lost his Oikos Greek Yogurt sponsorship. In a video posted October 5, Newton called his word choice degrading and disrespectful, apologized to those offended, acknowledged his role as a father to two daughters, and asked for forgiveness from reporters, mothers, and women.

The Fifth Circuit reversed a district court judgment that had affirmed the bankruptcy court's dismissal of the Tates' Chapter 7 bankruptcy case for abuse. The issue was whether debtors with above-median income may claim a vehicle ownership deduction under the means test of 11 U.S.C. § 707(b) when they have no loan or lease payment on their vehicles.

The Tates, who owned two vehicles outright, claimed vehicle ownership deductions that brought their monthly disposable income below the threshold for presumptive abuse. The Bankruptcy Trustee moved to dismiss, arguing the deduction was improper.

Courts have split on this issue between the "plain language approach," which permits the deduction regardless of actual payments, and the "IRM approach," which requires an actual debt or lease payment. Adopting the Seventh Circuit's reasoning in In re Ross-Tousey, the Fifth Circuit embraced the plain language approach. The court reasoned that "applicable" refers to geographic region and number of vehicles, not actual expenses; that Congress explicitly required actual expenses in other provisions but not here; that the statute does not incorporate IRS methodology; and that policy considerations support allowing the deduction since vehicle ownership carries costs even without loan payments.

The case was reversed and remanded.

AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine extends the Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) and SEV Secure Nested Paging (SNP) APIs to facilitate page migration—copying page content and updating virtual-to-physical mappings between memory tiers. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement and availability is determined via the ENGINE_READY bit in the PM_Status register.

TMPM enables two capabilities unavailable to x86 CPU software or standard I/O devices: migrating pages that are concurrent DMA targets, and migrating SNP-protected guest pages inaccessible to the Hypervisor/OS. The PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO command migrates pages during concurrent DMA by coordinating with IOMMUs, while PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST handles SNP guest pages, requiring source pages in Guest-Valid/Invalid states and destinations in a new Pre-Migration state.

Commands can move up to 128 pages via a Page Migration List (starting at a 4KB-aligned address), with no order-dependence between entries. PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS status requires checking per-page status; PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE indicates a retry is possible.

Performance is optimized using 16+ pages per command (peak at 128), keeping the ring buffer full, and using interrupts sparingly via NOP commands or low-water marks. Certain structures (IOMMU data structures, ring buffer, argument pages) cannot be migrated.

TMPM firmware can be reloaded via the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol when no operations are in flight; reload requires equal or greater firmware versions. The PM_GET_CAPABILITIES command's FW_VER_Major field identifies the EPYC family (value 71 = Family 19h) to determine the appropriate reload execution path.

Liberty Island was evacuated on July 4th after a person climbed the Statue of Liberty's base, sitting about 100 feet above ground while police attempted to persuade them to descend. Earlier, at least six people were arrested for hanging a banner reading "Abolish I.C.E." from the statue's pedestal, violating federal regulations. The banner's organizing group, Rise and Resist, stated the climber was not connected to their demonstration.

FoodSEM is a fine-tuned open-source large language model (LLM) designed for food named-entity linking (NEL), addressing the lack of semantic resources in the food and nutrition domain compared to biomedical fields. The model links food-related entity mentions in text to entities from three ontologies: FoodOn, SNOMED-CT, and the Hansard taxonomy, supporting FAIR data principles and EU sustainability initiatives.

Built by fine-tuning Meta's Llama 3 8B instruction-tuned model using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), FoodSEM was trained on 21,027 instruction-response pairs derived from the CafeteriaFCD and CafeteriaSA corpora, supplemented with artificially generated samples to balance entity distribution. Evaluation via five-fold cross-validation shows FoodSEM achieves macro-weighted F1 scores up to 98% on artificial samples, 0.827–0.863 on CafeteriaFCD, and 0.654–0.730 on CafeteriaSA across the three ontologies.

FoodSEM significantly outperforms 0-shot, 1-shot, and 5-shot prompting baselines of the non-fine-tuned model. The code, datasets, and model are publicly available. Future work will incorporate scientific datasets and explore retrieval-augmented generation for handling unseen entities.

Checkr, a background check technology startup founded in 2014 by Daniel Yanisse and Jonathan Perichon, became a leading voice in the fair chance hiring movement, which advocates providing equal job opportunities to individuals with criminal records. After noticing that candidates with conviction records—disproportionately Black and Hispanic—were being rejected at high rates, the founders sought to use technology to promote inclusive hiring while maintaining safety standards.

By 2024, the company was valued at $5 billion, employed 1,200 people (4% with records), and completed 30 million background checks annually. Checkr developed AI-powered tools including Candidate Stories, which allows applicants to provide context on their records, and Assess, which filters convictions by type, age, or recency. In 2021, it signed the Pledge 1% and launched a Corporate Social Responsibility division led by Ken Oliver, along with its Checkr.org foundation.

Proponents argue fair chance hiring expands talent pools amid U.S. labor shortages, improves retention (Checkr's fair chance attrition was 5% vs. 22% company-wide), enhances diversity, and reduces recidivism. Approximately 80 million Americans have records, facing over 44,000 collateral consequences and a 27% unemployment rate.

CEO Yanisse emphasized maintaining alignment between Checkr's social mission and its for-profit business model, noting that mission impact depends on business success. As Checkr approached its 10-year anniversary and potential IPO, Yanisse faced questions about making the business case for fair chance hiring to new stakeholders.

The DAWN-plasma trial was a prospective multicenter randomized open-label study evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard of care (SOC) versus SOC alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Between May 2020 and January 2021, 320 patients were randomized to receive 4 units of high-titre convalescent plasma and 163 to the control group (2:1 allocation).

No statistically significant differences were found between groups for any secondary endpoints, with treatment effects near identity values. Adverse event incidence was similar: 28.13% (plasma+SOC) versus 30.06% (SOC). Fatal AEs occurred in 10.31% versus 9.82%, and SAEs in 20.62% versus 20.68%, respectively. Five AEs led to treatment discontinuation, all in the plasma+SOC group. Fourteen AEs and 7 SAEs were considered treatment-related. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 6.0% of intervention patients, with no TRALI cases.

Laboratory parameters (CRP, ferritin, D-dimer) and body temperature showed no clinically meaningful differences. Neutralizing antibody titres increased by Day 6 regardless of intervention; higher baseline and Day 6 titres correlated with better outcomes. The intervention did not alter the natural course of disease.

The TLV321x comparators include internal ESD protection limiting inputs to 0.2V beyond rails; a current-limiting resistor is recommended for low-impedance sources, keeping current under 10mA. A Power-on-Reset circuit holds the output low for up to 32µs after V+ crosses the 1.65V VPOR threshold.

The basic comparator outputs logic high or low based on whether VIN exceeds VREF, with propagation delays (tpLH, tpHL) between input crossing and output response. Smaller overdrive voltages increase propagation delay, especially below 100mV.

Because the TLV321x has only 1.8mV internal hysteresis, external hysteresis via positive feedback can prevent output chatter near the switching threshold. Both inverting (three-resistor network) and non-inverting (two-resistor network with VREF) configurations are described, with equations provided for trip voltages and hysteresis.

A typical application is low-side current sensing, where an amplifier boosts the shunt voltage and the comparator triggers at an over-current threshold. Design guidance emphasizes 0.1µF ceramic bypass capacitors near the V+ pin, solid grounding, minimized input/output coupling, and optional series output resistors to dampen ringing. The device supports split or single supplies.

Three days after Iraqis voted in elections, the President addressed the nation about the war in Iraq. He acknowledged that although weapons of mass destruction were not found, removing Saddam Hussein was justified. He argued that terrorism must be confronted abroad, citing the September 11 attacks as evidence that terrorists do not act only in response to provocation.

The President outlined a three-part strategy: maintaining military offensives while training Iraqi forces, helping establish democratic institutions, and rebuilding Iraq's economy and infrastructure. He reported progress, including over 125 Iraqi combat battalions and more than 10 million voters in recent elections, including Sunni participation.

He warned that withdrawing prematurely would betray Iraqi allies, demoralize troops, embolden terrorists, and damage American credibility. Troop level decisions, he said, would be based on conditions on the ground rather than political timetables. He asked Americans, including those who opposed the war, not to give up on the effort, and acknowledged the sacrifices of military families. He concluded with holiday reflections and prayers for troops serving overseas.

Southeast Asian stock markets rebounded on Wednesday as investors sought bargains after recent losses driven by Sino-U.S. trade war fears. Indonesian shares closed 1.8 percent higher, recovering from a 15-month low, led by financials such as Bank Central Asia and Unilever Indonesia. Indonesia's finance minister announced plans to review capital goods imports to manage its current account deficit. Philippine shares rose over 1 percent for a fourth consecutive session, with real estate and industrial stocks leading, ahead of Thursday's inflation data. Analyst Lexter Azurin noted bargain hunting as valuations fell below historical averages. Singapore shares gained 0.3 percent on financials, while Vietnam rose 1 percent on real estate stocks, and Thai stocks hit a one-week high.

Michael Daniels, 40, of Ashford, was jailed for five years and three months for conspiracy to steal motor vehicles. As head of sales at BMW Berry in Chiswick, he used his position to access customer addresses and provided spare keys to accomplice Alex Tingle. Tingle and Vincent Murphy then drove to the addresses and took the vehicles. Between December 2015 and February 2016, nine cars worth a combined £210,000 were stolen and delivered to a figure known as "Ali" in Alperton. Victims reported significant personal impact, including missing a child's birth and being unable to sell their home. Tingle received a two-year sentence but was released having served 13 months. Murphy was previously jailed for 16 months. Daniels was caught after Tingle confessed upon being identified via CCTV. Judge Simon Davis described the case as a "horrendous breach of trust." Both men had no previous convictions.

Sony's "Baby Driver" has surpassed $100 million at the domestic box office after seven weeks, with an additional $67 million from overseas markets. Made on a $34 million budget, the film exceeded expectations after its June 28 release, earning $39 million in its first week. Directed by Edgar Wright from his own script, the film stars Ansel Elgort, Kevin Spacey, Lily James, Jamie Foxx, Jon Bernthal, and Jon Hamm. It holds a 94% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, and its soundtrack reached No. 1 on iTunes. Wright expressed gratitude to the cast, crew, and studios for supporting an original film amid a franchise-heavy summer. Markets yet to open include Japan, Russia, China, Italy, and South Korea.

Jury selection has begun in the retrial of Isaiah Hagan, accused of killing Halee Rathgeber, after a judge declared a mistrial earlier this month. The court agreed to maintain the motion of limine from the first trial. Ten of 14 jurors, including two alternates, have been chosen from a pool of about 200. Hagan faces four charges, including murder and robbery resulting in serious bodily injury. The remaining jurors will be selected Thursday, with opening statements beginning Monday.

Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) are baskets of securities traded on stock exchanges like individual stocks, offering diversification, liquidity, and relatively low expense ratios. The first ETF, SPY, was launched in 1993 and tracks the S&P 500; ETFs have grown significantly since the 2008/09 financial crisis, reaching over 7,100 globally by 2020.

ETFs can be used for both passive investing and active trading across various asset classes, including equities, bonds, commodities, and currencies. Eighteen ETF trading strategies include trend following, mean reversion, momentum, sector rotation, arbitrage, high-frequency trading, quantitative trading, options trading, volatility trading, statistical arbitrage, pair trading, market-neutral strategies, global macro trading, equal weight strategies, smart beta, currency hedging, fixed income strategies, and commodities trading.

Key benefits include diversification, cost-effectiveness, tax efficiency, and flexibility for margin trading or short selling. Risks involve market volatility, liquidity concerns, and tracking errors. ETFs can be day-traded, swing-traded, or held long-term, though swing trading is generally considered more effective than day trading or scalping.

Popular ETFs include SPY (S&P 500), VTI (Vanguard Total Stock Market), and IEFA (iShares Core MSCI EAFE). Unlike mutual funds, ETFs trade continuously throughout the day at known prices. Successful ETF trading requires diversification across multiple strategies, backtesting, and incubation before live trading.

The Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) Operations Guide describes AMD's extensions to the SEV and SNP Firmware ABI for page migration in tiered memory systems. TMPM offloads page migration by copying page contents between memory tiers while updating IOMMU virtual-to-physical mappings, and requires IOMMU enablement.

TMPM enables two unique capabilities: migration of pages concurrently targeted by DMA operations, and migration of SNP-protected guest pages inaccessible to the hypervisor/OS. Key commands include PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO (for hypervisor-owned pages with concurrent DMA), PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST (for SNP guest pages), PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, and PM_NOOP. A new Pre-Migration RMP state facilitates SNP guest page migration.

Commands are submitted via a ring buffer interface with mailbox registers, supporting up to 128 pages per command, with 16+ pages recommended for better performance. Only 4K-aligned system physical addresses are supported (except 8-byte aligned host PTE addresses). Certain data structures, including IOMMU tables and the ring buffer itself, cannot be migrated.

The firmware can be reloaded while no operations are in flight, using the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol; reload behavior varies by EPYC family (Family 19h uses FW_VER_Major value 71).

Six interrupt sources share one x86 signal for events like completion, errors, queue threshold, and ring buffer errors. Errors are reported via command status fields, the PM_STATUS register, or Machine Check Architecture, with some hardware errors potentially rendering affected pages unrecoverable.

A girl from Bihar, diagnosed with drug-resistant TB in 2012, deteriorated despite treatment at Delhi's Lala Ram Swarup TB Hospital. By October 2016, weighing just 25kg, she was brought to Dr Zarir Udvadia in Mumbai, who recommended Bedaquiline, a new drug he had studied in 2012. However, under the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme, the drug was restricted to select cities and unavailable to non-residents, even in Delhi. After exhausting other avenues, the girl's father petitioned the Delhi High Court, which ordered the drug be administered. Dr Udvadia reports a 70% success rate among his 30 Bedaquiline patients but notes access remains difficult. While authorities restrict the drug due to potential fatal side-effects, the rigid approach forces patients to seek legal recourse. TB's resurgence is concerning, requiring strict 18-month compliance, with no preventive vaccine for drug-resistant TB.

Duncan Keith reflects on maturing as a player and person with experience, noting not everything goes your way. He acknowledges goalie Rask's strong play but expresses confidence in scoring. Document 29: Ambassador Penfield reports a private letter from Hungarian Minister President Tisza, who emphasizes two points from his parliamentary declaration: (1) the enemies' peace conditions would mutilate Germany and dismember Austria-Hungary and Turkey, contradicting President Wilson's views; and (2) the ideal of national self-determination cannot apply to mixed-population regions, and the dual monarchy system best approximates this ideal in southeastern Europe. Tisza requests that these points be conveyed to American statesmen and public.

Document 30: Ambassador Bernstorff conveys Germany's thanks to President Wilson and expresses confidence in him. Germany accepts Wilson's offer to facilitate a peace conference but refuses to publish peace terms publicly while enemies proclaim terms aimed at Germany's destruction, though it will privately share the terms it would have proposed. Germany agrees to join a post-war international conference based on Wilson's Senate message. Germany states the submarine blockade could not be postponed due to preparations, justifies it as a response to Entente violations of international law and destructive war aims, and claims it will end the war quickly. Germany pledges to safeguard American interests and will end the blockade if Wilson's peace efforts succeed, citing the May 4, 1916 note as reserving its freedom of action.

NVIDIA's GA10x Ampere architecture GPUs deliver significant performance improvements over the previous Turing generation, offering up to 2x advancements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI processing.

The architecture features GDDR6X memory (developed with Micron), which uses PAM4 signaling to achieve data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/sec on the RTX 3090. GA102 GPUs include seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, and 84 SMs, with each SM containing 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, and one second-generation Ray Tracing Core.

Key improvements include doubled FP32 throughput per SM, second-generation RT Cores with 2x ray/triangle intersection performance and hardware-accelerated motion blur, and third-generation Tensor Cores supporting new data types (TF32, BF16) and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity for 2x throughput. ROPs are now integrated into GPCs, increasing total count to 112 on full GA102.

Additional features include third-generation NVLink (112.5 GB/sec bidirectional bandwidth), PCIe Gen 4 support, and NVIDIA RTX IO, which works with Microsoft's DirectStorage API to accelerate GPU-based asset loading and decompression by up to 100x.

The architecture powers multiple products: GeForce RTX 3090/3080/3070 for gaming, NVIDIA A40 for data centers, and NVIDIA RTX A6000 for workstations (both with 48GB GDDR6, scalable to 96GB via NVLink). Display support includes DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 for 8K60 and 4K120 resolutions. The GPUs feature fifth-generation NVDEC (first to support AV1 hardware decoding) and seventh-generation NVENC encoders. A new Error Detection and Replay (EDR) feature on GDDR6X assists memory overclocking.

Following the death of President William Henry Harrison, the author addresses the nation as the first Vice President to assume the Presidency through constitutional succession, and outlines his governing principles.

In foreign affairs, he pledges justice to all nations while tolerating injustice from none, emphasizing strong military and naval defenses. Domestically, he warns against the concentration of power in the executive, particularly through patronage, and calls for separating control of the Treasury from presidential appointment powers. He commits to removing officeholders only for misconduct or active partisanship and will seek congressional action to curb these dangers.

He advocates rigid economy in public spending, avoidance of public debt in peacetime, abolition of sinecures, and strict accountability for disbursing agents. On currency, he will enforce existing laws but considers them oppressive, and will support constitutional measures from Congress to restore a sound circulating medium.

He stresses limiting federal power to what the Constitution grants, preserving the balance between federal and state authority, and warns that overreach could lead to disunion or centralized tyranny. He concludes by pledging to preserve free institutions for future generations.

The speaker reflects on a recent game, noting the team played more aggressively and physically in game two compared to the passive first game. He emphasizes the importance of skating, initiating contact, and not giving the opposing team time and space. For over a decade, the U.S. has pursued detente—relaxation of tensions with potential enemies. However, detente requires positive actions from both sides, and one-sided relaxation while the Soviets conduct a major military buildup does not advance peace. Continued negotiation with the Soviet Union is essential, but agreements should not be made for their own sake. The speaker would support verifiable mutual reductions in nuclear weapons but rejects treaties like SALT II that legitimize a one-sided buildup. The 1950s Austrian State Treaty is cited as an example of successful negotiation.

Americans must understand Soviet strategic objectives: dividing NATO, expanding influence in the Arabian Gulf and South Asia, encircling China, and fostering subversion in the Caribbean, where leftist regimes have taken hold in Nicaragua and Grenada. The Soviets prioritize strategic nuclear programs, seeking superiority that would force the U.S. to choose between submission and conflict. Restoring a margin of safety is presented as the path to real peace and potential arms limitation. The U.S. is described as non-belligerent, using strength historically to defend others, while Leninist-Marxist philosophy is characterized as primitive and comparable to feudalism.

Merck has halted a late-stage trial of its Alzheimer's drug verubecestat for mild-to-moderate patients after an independent study found it had "virtually no chance" of working. This follows Eli Lilly's discontinuation of solanezumab three months earlier. Verubecestat is a BACE inhibitor, targeting amyloid plaque build-up linked to the beta amyloid theory of Alzheimer's. Its failure raises concerns about this theory, though other companies including AstraZeneca, Novartis, Janssen, and Biogen continue trialling BACE inhibitors. Around 47 million people worldwide have dementia, with Alzheimer's accounting for 60-80% of cases. No new Alzheimer's drug has been released in over a decade. Merck's trial results for early-stage patients are expected in February 2019, and its shares fell nearly 2% after the announcement.

Edward C. Turner was arrested for driving under the influence and refused a chemical test, resulting in the Commissioner of Public Safety revoking his license for six months under 47 O.S.1971, § 753. After an administrative hearing sustained the revocation, Turner appealed to the District Court, which found the revocation justified but reduced the period to three months based on his driving record. The Department of Public Safety appealed the modification.

The Supreme Court held that the trial court's modification was contrary to State ex rel. Oklahoma Department of Public Safety v. Kopczynski, which established that district courts lack authority under 47 O.S.1971, § 6-211 to modify the six-month suspension. The Court reasoned that the 1975 amendment to § 755, which created a specific limited exception for modification, would have been unnecessary if § 6-211 already granted such authority, and that subsequent amendments do not reflect the original legislative intent. The suspension was affirmed and the modification reversed.

Justices Hodges, Simms, and Doolin dissented, arguing Kopczynski was distinguishable because it involved hardship (not then a statutory ground), while Turner's modification was based on driving record evidence permitted under § 6-211(e). The dissent contended § 6-211 governs implied consent appeals and permits modification when suspension periods are excessive.

Vermont City Electric (VCE), a municipal agency formed in 1905, provides electricity to approximately 16,000 residential, 2,845 small commercial, and 784 large commercial customers across 16 square miles. VCE has pioneered demand-side management (DSM) strategies to reduce energy use and peak demand costs since 2000. Due to the 2008 economic downturn, VCE's Finance Committee limited 2009 DSM direct spending to $800,000, requiring the utility to optimize across its nine DSM programs rather than fund all of them.

VCE sources power from three categories: its own generation facilities (the wood-powered McNeil Station and oil-powered VCE GT), medium-term hydroelectric contracts (NYPA, NYSEG, VEPPI), and the ISO-NE wholesale market. A wind generation facility is expected in 2012. Demand is analyzed through load duration curves divided into five blocks representing varying hours and average loads.

Daniela Shazar, a Citizen's Oversight Board member, was tasked with independently evaluating which DSM programs to retain and assessing their carbon impact. The assignment involves building a mixed-integer optimization model to determine VCE's least-cost electricity supply plan for 2009–2014, with and without DSM activities, while tracking carbon emissions and respecting the $800,000 budget constraint.

The System MMU redirects C674x MDMA port accesses to physical system addresses, protecting ARM Cortex-A8 memory and enabling direct buffer allocation without ARM/DSP translation. EDMA TC0/TC1 accesses can optionally route through it via the MMU_CFG register.

The Media Controller manages HDVPSS and ISS modules. The HDVICP2 is a video encoder/decoder hardware accelerator supporting MPEG1/2/4, H.264, VC-1, RV9/10, AVS-1.0, and ON2 VP6.2/VP7 standards.

The Face Detection module performs face detection/tracking on QVGA 8-bit Luma images stored in DDR, using 51.25KB working memory, providing size, position, angle, and confidence for each face.

The Spinlock module provides 128 hardware semaphores for multi-process synchronization via single read-access locks. The Mailbox module enables inter-processor communication between ARM Cortex-A8, C674x DSP, and Media Controller, with four-message FIFO queues and interrupt notifications.

The device uses a unified memory map across L3 and L4 (Fast/Slow) interconnects. The TILER provides an additional 4GB addressing range for rotated/mirrored frame buffer views, accessible fully only to HDVPSS and ISS.

Boot configuration is determined by sampling BTMODE[15:0] pins at reset release, controlling GPMC settings, boot mode order, Ethernet PHY mode, and XIP muxing options. Device pin multiplexing is controlled via PINCNTL1–PINCNTL270 registers, with default MUXMODE=0x0 placing I/O buffers in 3-state. Some peripheral functions are Multimuxed across multiple pins with distinct timing characteristics.

This lecture introduces Effective Field Theory (EFT) as a framework for isolating physics at specific scales. The course, which has no exams but includes five problem sets and a student presentation, lists quantum field theory 2 as a prerequisite. The first half covers general EFT principles, while the second focuses on soft-collinear effective field theory and its LHC jet physics applications.

EFT operates opposite to how physics is typically taught: rather than building up from classical mechanics to quantum field theory, EFT takes a general theory and derives more specific, computationally tractable versions. The goal is the simplest framework capturing essential physics while retaining the ability to correct results to arbitrary precision through higher-order expansion terms.

Constructing an EFT requires three steps: identifying relevant degrees of freedom, determining symmetries, and establishing power counting (the expansion parameter). Power counting is as fundamental as gauge symmetry. The guiding principle is insensitivity to physics at higher energy scales, though expansions are not always in mass ratios—examples include velocity expansions in non-relativistic QED.

EFTs fall into two categories. Top-down EFTs start from a known high-energy theory and integrate out heavy particles through matching calculations (examples: heavy quark effective theory, NRQCD). Bottom-up EFTs construct low-energy theories from symmetries and degrees of freedom alone, without detailed knowledge of high-energy physics (examples: chiral perturbation theory, the Standard Model, quantum gravity).

The Standard Model is treated as a bottom-up EFT, with expansion parameter epsilon being Standard Model mass scales divided by unknown higher scales (Planck mass, GUT scales). Corrections appear as higher-dimensional operators built from Standard Model fields.

The lecture concludes by redefining renormalizability: rather than requiring finite parameters, an EFT must be renormalizable order-by-order in its expansion parameter, permitting infinitely many parameters overall but finitely many at any fixed order.

DTE Maharashtra has released the MHT CET 2018 exam pattern and syllabus circular on its official website. The exam, scheduled for May 2018, is for admission to first-year degree courses in Engineering and Technology, Pharmacy, and Pharma-D for 2018-2019. The team values fan support but doesn't rely on it, focusing instead on winning rather than individual stats or minutes played. The speaker describes the rivalry as a fight for the cup, noting players would do anything to win it. Hockey is portrayed as an emotional game where high stakes create intense feelings, and opposing teams are disliked for trying to take the cup. The team is described as sore losers, led by captain Jarome, composed of prideful players who hate losing. Playing with collective emotion is essential for winning, requiring all players to contribute, not just one. Regarding a loss, the speaker acknowledges the opponent was better, citing a weak power play, and noted the other team improved their passing and sharpness from the previous game.

The passage describes methods, apparatuses, and systems for multi-user (MU) transmission in wireless local area networks (WLANs), particularly addressing limitations in IEEE 802.11ac's group ID mechanism for downlink MU-MIMO transmissions.

The application is a continuation of prior U.S. patent applications dating back to 2015 provisional applications. Current WLAN standards support limited clusters, users, and MU transmission schemes, while MU control frames contribute overhead that reduces MAC efficiency.

The disclosed embodiments provide new MU clustering and scheduling mechanisms supporting larger numbers of clusters, combinations of OFDMA clusters and OFDM MU-MIMO groups, and flexible per-transmission scheduling. A wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) may receive a frame, determine if it is a null data packet (NDP) MU MAC PPDU based on an NDP condition, process the NDP SIG field containing MU control information, and generate a response.

Two HE NDP MAC PPDU designs are presented: one with a single HE-NDP-SIG field and another with both HE-NDP-SIG-A and HE-NDP-SIG-B fields. Various NDP MU control frame types are described, including MU-RTS, MU-CTS, MU-Poll, ULR, and MU schedule frames, with detailed field structures such as NDP MAC Frame Type, MU mode, AP address, Group ID, duration, response protocol, and synchronization information subfields.

The embodiments enable flexible membership and position assignments updated per transmission, support multiple simultaneous MU transmission schemes in both downlink and uplink directions, and reduce control overhead through NDP-based control frames.

Xenon Pharmaceuticals hosted an investor webinar on its Nav1.7 and Kv7 programs for pain treatment. Defense attorney Darla Palmer has filed a motion alleging that Panola County District Attorney John Champion sought false testimony from an unrelated defendant, Jalen Asir Matthews Caudle, in exchange for leniency in the case against Quinton Tellis. Tellis is accused of killing 19-year-old Jessica Chambers by setting her on fire in 2014; his first trial ended in a hung jury in October. James Patterson has increased his annual donations for classroom libraries from $1.75 million to $2 million, distributing 4,000 gifts of $500 each to teachers across the country.
