Daniel Loeb's Third Point increased its stakes in Alphabet by 120,000 class A shares to 575,000 and in Facebook by 500,000 class A shares to 3.5 million. Leon Cooperman's Omega Advisors took a bearish stance, reducing holdings in Facebook, Netflix, and Amazon, while keeping its Alphabet stake unchanged at 158,835 class A shares. Cooperman told CNBC that Alphabet was his largest position, representing 4-4.5 percent of his fund. Barry Rosenstein's Jana Partners, which held no FAANG stocks, increased its Whole Foods stake by 9 million to 23.3 million shares, later profiting in July after Amazon's $13.7 billion acquisition announcement. Third Point's Facebook and Alphabet positions proved profitable, with Facebook gaining roughly 13 percent in the third quarter and Alphabet up 1 percent.

The U.S. government was on track to shut down at midnight as Republicans and Democrats remained at odds over a funding deal. The Congressional Budget Office estimated a shutdown would furlough about 750,000 federal workers, with daily compensation costs of roughly $400 million.

House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., and Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., blamed Democrats for the impasse, urging passage of a "clean" continuing resolution that would fund the government for seven weeks. Johnson accused Democratic leaders Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries of making irrelevant policy demands, partly to shield Schumer from progressive challengers.

Democrats are insisting that any funding bill include an extension of enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits, which lower insurance premiums and are set to expire at the end of 2025. Jeffries said Democrats would not support a bill that "guts" health care and denied Republican claims that Democrats sought to extend federal health benefits to undocumented immigrants, noting federal law prohibits such coverage.

This application, a continuation of U.S. Patent Application No. 16/371,056, relates to configurable computing circuitry, specifically a heterogeneous computing system with an embedded interconnection network, dynamic reconfiguration, and dynamic control over power consumption.

The invention addresses limitations in existing computing systems regarding speed, energy consumption, and heat dissipation, particularly for compute-intensive applications such as FFTs, FIR filters, synthetic aperture radar, 5G base stations, machine learning, and graph analytics.

Representative embodiments provide a multi-threaded, coarse-grained configurable computing architecture capable of self-scheduling, dynamic self-configuration and reconfiguration, conditional branching, backpressure control, ordered thread execution, loop thread execution with data dependencies, and nested loop execution.

A configurable circuit may include: a configurable computation circuit; synchronous network inputs and outputs; a control circuit with memory control, thread control, and control registers; and a configuration memory comprising an instruction memory storing data path configuration instructions, and an instruction/index memory storing spoke instructions and indices for selecting inputs, current instructions, or next instructions for subsequent circuits.

The system comprises a hierarchical interconnection network with crossbar switches, a processor, host interface, and configurable circuit clusters. Each cluster contains arrays of configurable circuits (tiles) connected via a synchronous network enabling pipelined data flow (forming synchronous domains) and an asynchronous packet network for control messaging, memory access, and bridging synchronous domains.

The architecture uses thread identifiers (TIDs) and transfer identifiers (XIDs) for tracking computations, loops, and nested loops, with control registers storing completion tables, loop tables, and thread identifier pools. Threads queue for execution when completion counts reach zero. Conditional logic circuits enable branching by modifying next instructions based on computation outputs.

Various method embodiments describe configuring circuits and controlling thread execution using these components.

Contrave, an FDA-approved prescription weight-loss pill combining bupropion and naltrexone, is marketed for obese individuals or overweight people with conditions like heart disease or diabetes. While commercials claim users lost two to four times more weight than those who only dieted and exercised, a Consumer Reports analysis of three clinical trials found the additional weight loss was small—only five to nine pounds more than a placebo over 56 weeks. The drug can cause anxiety, insomnia, headaches, and more serious risks including liver damage, seizures, increased blood pressure, and heart problems. Consumer Reports recommends discussing risks with a doctor and pursuing weight loss through diet, exercise, or intensive behavioral programs.

The IOMUX manages peripheral function selection on digital IOs, output driver controls, input paths, and wake-up logic for SHUTDOWN mode. Not all pins support analog functions, wake-up logic, drive strength control, or pull resistors.

A serial wire debug (SWD) two-wire interface via an ARM-compatible SW-DP provides access to debug functions. The boot strap loader (BSL) enables device configuration and memory programming through UART or I2C, protected by a 256-bit password. BSL requires minimum two pins and can be invoked via pin state during boot, automatically when reset vector/stack pointer are unprogrammed, or at runtime via SYSRST.

Devices include a memory-mapped FACTORY region with read-only capability data and trim information. Hardware revision and device ID are stored there and marked on package tops.

For applications, TI recommends 10µF and 0.1µF decoupling capacitors near VDD/VSS pins, a 47kΩ pullup with 10nF pulldown on NRST, a 100kΩ 0.1% resistor for SYSOSC FCL, a 0.47µF tank capacitor on VCORE, and pullup resistors for 5V-tolerant open drain IOs.

TI provides development tools including LaunchPad kits, MSPM0 SDK, SysConfig, Code Composer Studio, IAR Embedded Workbench, Keil MDK, and GNU Arm toolchain. Device prefixes indicate development stage (X for experimental, MSP for production). The revision history lists numerous updates to features, electrical characteristics, and specifications between November 2024 and April 2025.

Penn State and USC are meeting for the 10th time, with USC leading 5-4. YbCu1.14Se2 was synthesized and investigated as a potential disordered quantum spin liquid (QSL) candidate related to YbMgGaO4 and the AYbSe2 series. Single crystal x-ray diffraction revealed a triangular lattice of Yb ions with disordered Cu vacancies (57% occupancy instead of the expected 50%). Magnetic susceptibility indicates antiferromagnetic exchange and a Kramer's doublet ground state. Specific heat measurements show no magnetic ordering transition and sub-linear behavior between 0.5 K and 5 K, inconsistent with typical magnon or Fermi surface models. Ultra-low-temperature AC susceptibility reveals a frequency-dependent freezing transition near 0.1 K, and no 1/3 magnetization plateau characteristic of ideal triangular Heisenberg systems. These findings resemble YbMgGaO4 and theoretical predictions for disordered frustrated magnets, suggesting universal behavior in disordered QSL materials.

Christian Bushman credits CPR with saving her life after an object fell from a closet and struck her chest in May 2014, leaving her unresponsive and without a pulse. Her husband sought help from his sister, Cathy Carson, a CPR instructor, who performed CPR until Bushman was breathing when Life-Force arrived. Introduction
Multivariate count data modeling is needed in applications like non-life insurance claims, where zero inflation and dependence between components are common. Traditional Poisson models are inadequate for zero-inflated data, prompting various univariate and multivariate extensions. This work proposes a bivariate zero-inflated Poisson (BZIP) model using a common Bernoulli inflation factor combined with comonotonic or counter-monotonic Poisson shocks, enabling both positive and negative correlations.

Proposed Model
The model defines X = WT, where W is Bernoulli and T is a bivariate Poisson pair following either BP+ (comonotonic) or BP− (counter-monotonic) shock structures. Joint PMFs, CDFs, and probability generating functions are derived for both positive (BZIP+) and negative (BZIP−) dependence cases.

Dependence Structure
Dependence arises from both the inflation factor ϕ and parameter θ. In BZIP+, correlation increases with θ; in BZIP−, it decreases. The parameter ϕ affects correlation differently across models. BZIP+ attains the Fréchet-Hoeffding upper bound when θ=1, while BZIP− only reaches the lower bound when ϕ=0.

Estimation
Method of moments (MoM) and maximum likelihood estimation (MLE), including an EM algorithm, are presented. MoM estimators are shown to be consistent and asymptotically normal.

Simulations
Across 72 scenarios, MLE methods outperformed MoM in RMSE. Estimation accuracy decreased as ϕ increased. Negative dependence estimation posed more numerical challenges.

Data Illustration
The model was applied to Australian disaster data, fitting BZIP+ to storm-flood pairs and BZIP− to bushfire-flood pairs, confirming significant zero inflation and dependence.

Multivariate Extensions
The positive dependence model extends directly to higher dimensions using the multivariate comonotonic shock model.

In south Los Angeles, literacy is framed as a tool for empowerment for Black youth. Partnership for Growth LA's Read Lead Freedom Schools program combines literacy instruction with civic engagement, culturally relevant books, and small class sizes. A 2023-24 pilot with the California Department of Education showed a 14.5-point increase in English Language Arts proficiency, chronic absenteeism dropping from 47% to 5%, and 88% of families reporting gains in confidence and motivation.

Research indicates children not reading on grade level by third grade are four times more likely to drop out of high school. Despite proven results, federal funding cuts threaten such programs, though $900 million was allocated for California and state lawmakers approved funding for evidence-based literacy instruction.

The authors, including the mayor of Lakewood and an LAUSD Board member, cite former student Anastacia Nwosu—now a field deputy to a California Assemblymember—as evidence that literacy fosters leadership. They call for sustained support of local literacy programs during National Literacy Month.

The President advises maintaining self-protective measures despite pacific policy, recommending systematic development of a defensive navy, completion of seaport fortifications, and continued support of domestic arms manufacturing.

He concludes by urging adherence to established institutions, resistance to dangerous innovations, and pledges cooperation with Congress.

The ADS7828 operates with either a 2.5V internal reference or an external reference. A +5V supply requires an external +5V reference for full dynamic range, while a +2.7V supply allows the internal reference to provide full range. The external reference can go as low as 50mV. Lower reference voltages reduce LSB size (reference voltage divided by 4096), making offset, gain errors, and internal noise appear larger. Internal noise contributes 0.32LSB peak-to-peak at 2.5V reference, increasing to 16LSBs at 50mV. These noise errors are Gaussian in nature.

Zimbabwe's Ministry of Health and Child Care estimates there are approximately 44,586 female sex workers aged 15-49 in the country, with nearly 7,000 in Bulawayo, according to the HIV and Aids Estimates Report. The 10-pound oven cooks at 350°F, feeds five, and uses vacuum insulation to function through clouds and cold weather. Founder and CEO Patrick Sherwin described the product as the result of six years of development. GoSun launched a Kickstarter campaign to promote the Fusion. Russ Tedrake discusses extending temporal difference (TD) learning beyond discrete Markov chains to continuous systems using function approximation. He begins with a crash course on least squares function approximation, comparing neural networks (nonlinear in parameters, requiring gradient descent) to linear function approximators (linear in parameters but allowing nonlinear basis functions), which can be solved analytically. Examples of basis functions include radial basis functions (Gaussians), barycentric interpolators, Fourier decompositions, and polynomials.

He demonstrates linear function approximation applied to system identification, noting that manipulator equations for rigid-body robots are linear in their parameters (though parameters may appear in groups), making system identification tractable via one-shot least squares. Limitations arise with saturations, unmodeled dynamics, or insufficient excitation of system dynamics.

Tedrake then extends TD learning to linear function approximators by replacing the discrete eligibility trace with one defined over parameter vector alpha, weighted by the gradient of the value estimate. Tsitsiklis and Van Roy proved convergence for linear function approximators with lambda between 0 and 1. For lambda equals 1, the update performs gradient descent on Monte Carlo error.

To address data inefficiency in online TD updates, he introduces Least Squares Temporal Difference (LSTD) learning, which accumulates matrices from experienced data and solves directly for alpha, eliminating learning rate selection and initial condition dependence. Incremental LSTD variants exist for non-episodic tasks. Function approximation will later be applied to policy gradient methods and actor-critic algorithms.

AAA Nevada Insurance Company sought declaratory relief regarding its policy limits following a fatal car accident involving its insured, Vinh Chau, and Benjamin Buenaventura. The policy provided bodily injury limits of $100,000 per person. Counsel for the Buenaventuras sent a two-week policy-limits demand letter but failed to identify all heirs, provide a release, or respond to AAA's follow-up inquiries. After the demand expired, the Buenaventuras filed a wrongful death action seeking $999,997.

The court granted AAA's motion for summary judgment, holding that policy liability is limited to $100,000. On the bad faith claim, the court found AAA had a reasonable basis for not settling within the two-week deadline, given counsel's refusal to respond to inquiries about claimants. Citing similar facts in Hicks v. Dairyland, the court concluded AAA's actions did not constitute bad faith as a matter of law. The court denied Interveners' request for a Rule 56(f) continuance and rejected renewed jurisdictional objections.

The Trap play is a quick-hitting, downhill run scheme where a pulling Guard kicks out an interior Defensive Lineman. It works well against aggressive pass-rushers and suits various offensive styles, from power Fullbacks to Spread Tailbacks.

Strengths include its speed, particularly effective from under-center or in deception-based offenses like the Wing-T, and its reliance on angle blocks, which accommodates smaller Offensive Linemen. Its main weakness is difficulty against defensive fronts that squeeze interior gaps, such as a Bear front.

Against a 3-4 Odd Front, the Left Guard pulls to kick out the 4-technique while other linemen execute combination and second-level blocks, with the Fullback bursting through the running lane. Against a 4-3 Even Front, assignments shift to target the 3-tech and corresponding linebackers.

Variations include the Gun Trey Same-Side Trap RPO, which runs Trap from Shotgun with an RPO option, and the Wing-T Trap, paired with the Buck Sweep as a "sister play" using identical backfield action to pressure defensive discipline.

The President addresses Congress to review U.S. foreign relations following prior reports on economic recovery and energy independence. He emphasizes continued American leadership since World War II, citing strong alliances with Europe and Japan, a more stable relationship with the Soviet Union, improved ties with China, and diplomatic efforts in the Middle East, Latin America, and Africa.

Addressing the crisis in Indochina, he describes North Vietnam's violations of the 1973 Paris accords, including the infiltration of 350,000 troops, and South Vietnam's deteriorating military position. He reads a letter from Cambodia's acting President appealing for aid.

He criticizes the Trade Act of 1974 for harming U.S.-Soviet relations and reducing Jewish emigration from 33,000 in 1973.

He announces plans to visit China, addresses global challenges including hunger and energy, defends the CIA against dismantling, and urges approval of his national security budget. He calls for national unity and cooperative executive-congressional foreign policy.

Hillview Middle School is hosting an outdoor family movie night on April 27 at 7:30 pm, screening the PG-rated film "Sing." The event is open to all ages, with a required ratio of one adult per eight children. Baked goods, $2 popcorn, and $1 water will be sold, and the Los Carnalitos food truck will be on site. The passage describes the AGESA™ software interface for host BIOS environments. Errors other than SUCCESS and BOUNDS_CHK are logged in an event buffer holding the 16 most recent events, retrievable via AmdReadEventLog. Support for 16-bit Real Mode is deprecated; the binary module now operates in 32-bit protected mode.

The interface uses a Bridge (host-side call point), Dispatcher (AGESA entry point), Router (call-out re-entry), and CallOut (callback to host BIOS). Host BIOS calls the bridge, which invokes the dispatcher to execute functions; call-outs reverse this flow through the router.

UEFI implementations span SEC, PEI, DXE, and RTP stages using specialized libraries and build tools (MASM, ml, CL compilers). PEI drivers include AmdProcessorInitPeim (publishing PPIs like AMD_PEI_INIT_EARLY_PPI and AMD_PEI_INIT_POST_PPI) and a reset-coordination PEIM. A DXE driver generates ACPI/DMI tables via AmdInitLate.

Key entry points include: AmdInitReset (minimal post-reset initialization with execution cache setup), AmdInitEarly (full processor initialization with platform configuration), AmdInitPost (memory initialization), AmdInitEnv (HOB/artifact data transfer to permanent memory), AmdInitMid (graphics configuration), AmdInitLate (ACPI/DMI table generation), AmdInitRtb (saves context for suspend), AmdInitResume (memory restoration), AmdS3LateRestore, and AmdS3Save.

Stack management uses macros AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK and AMD_DISABLE_STACK for Cache-As-RAM setup/teardown. Service functions include AmdCreateStruct/AmdReleaseStruct for parameter block allocation, AmdGetApicId, AmdGetPciAddress, AmdIdentifyCore, and AmdReadEventLog. Cache region rules require 32-KByte alignment, maximum three regions, and addresses above 0x000D0000. AARCH64 APUs with Platform Security Processor do not use stack macros, as the PSP initializes DRAM.

The passage describes systems and methods for dynamically providing video overlays on video streams. A client device (such as a smart TV) identifies a set-top box that presents information overlaid on a video stream and selects a corresponding template based on the identified box and received video data. Using this template, the client device presents a replacement video stream that mimics the original presentation style, including position, size, speed, and transparency blending.

The replacement video is selected by generating query fingerprints of video frames and matching them against a database of known reference fingerprints maintained by a video identification system. Fingerprints may be single-frame or multi-frame and are generated using techniques like Haar-like features and integral image calculations on selected patches of video frames.

Templates correspond to screen regions generated by the set-top box (e.g., menus, picture-in-picture displays, informational bars) and can be created manually or programmatically by analyzing video data. The system supports detecting channel changes, playback speed modifications (fast-forward, rewind, pause), and semi-transparent overlays, adjusting the replacement stream accordingly.

Data structures include tables for picture-in-picture, menu overlay, menu blend, and template configurations tied to specific device identifiers. The methodologies aim to reduce computational and resource demands while enabling substitution of content (e.g., replacing national commercials with local ones) seamlessly.

The Kiss of Death is a sell signal in the S&P 500 that triggers when the index drops from an all-time high, falls below its monthly 21-EMA, bounces back above it, and then drops below its recent low. A backtest starting in 1967, with re-entry when the S&P 500 closes above its 10-month EMA, showed improved CAGR and nearly halved maximum drawdown compared to buy and hold.

The first trading day of the month effect refers to the tendency of the S&P 500 to perform better on the first trading day of each month than on other days. The first trading day is defined based on trading days, not calendar days, accounting for weekends and holidays.

Mediation analysis examines how interventions influence outcomes through mediator variables, offering insights into treatment mechanisms, refinement opportunities, and early success indicators. Structural equation modeling (SEM) is standard for identifying latent mediators, as it addresses measurement error in self-report data. However, SEM relies on the sequential ignorability assumption, which requires all relevant confounders to be included—a condition rarely met in practice, leading to biased estimates.

To address this, rank-preserving models (RPMs) using g-estimation have been developed in biomedicine, relying instead on a no-effect-modifier assumption that permits omitted covariates if they do not interact with treatment or mediator. Since RPMs have not been extended to latent variable models, the authors introduce the Rank-Preserving Structural Equation Model (RAPSEM), combining RPM with factor score regression to handle both measurement error and omitted confounders.

The paper defines causal effects—controlled direct effect (CDE) and controlled mediation effect (CME)—within the potential outcomes framework for randomized trials. RAPSEM's measurement model includes latent mediator, covariates, and outcome variables, each measured by observed indicators. Subsequent sections present estimation procedures, assumptions, simulation studies comparing RAPSEM's robustness and power to standard SEM, and a discussion of limitations.

A cross-sectional study was conducted from April to August 2021 in Denan district, Somali Region, southeastern Ethiopia, to determine the sero-prevalence, knowledge, attitudes, practices (KAP), associated risk factors of visceral leishmaniasis (VL), and sand fly species abundance. Blood samples from 187 participants across six kebeles were analyzed using the Direct Agglutination Test (DAT), and a structured questionnaire assessed KAP. Entomological sampling used CDC light traps and sticky traps across four habitat types.

The overall VL sero-prevalence was 9.63%. Significant risk factors included being aged 19–36, damp floor housing, outdoor sleeping, and sleeping near animal shelters. Only 53.48% of participants had heard of VL, 42% knew sand flies transmit it, and 36% believed it was preventable. Preventive practices included bed nets (42%), insecticide spraying (32%), smoking tree branches (14%), and environmental cleaning (8%).

A total of 823 sand flies representing 12 species were collected, including five Phlebotomus species and seven Sergentomyia species. P. orientalis, a known VL vector, was the most abundant Phlebotomus species (11.42%), predominantly found in termite mounds and forests, with none collected indoors. Sergentomyia species comprised 74.24% of collections, with S. clydei most abundant.

The authors conclude that VL sero-prevalence is relatively high in this new focus, community knowledge is poor, and P. orientalis likely contributes to transmission. Further epidemiological and vector bionomics studies are recommended.

This study investigates whether transformers can learn transitive relations by inferring connectivity in directed graphs when node-pair connectivity is provided as individual training examples rather than in-context prompts. The authors hypothesize that transformers more easily learn connectivity on graphs embeddable in low-dimensional subspaces, defining grid graphs (k-dimensional graphs where connectivity is inferable from vector differences) and contrasting them with disconnected chain graphs.

Experiments evaluate three research questions regarding transformer performance, the effects of model and graph scaling, and the impact of grid dimensionality and number of chains. Key findings include:

- Transformers achieve near-perfect accuracy on grid graphs but struggle to generalize on disconnected chain graphs.
- Scaling model size improves performance on grid graphs but not on disconnected chain graphs.
- Scaling graph size maintains consistent performance on grid graphs and improves performance on larger disconnected chain graphs with fixed chain count.
- Performance declines with higher grid dimensionality and more chains; increasing graph size helps more than increasing model size in these harder settings.

The authors conclude that data scaling benefits transformers more than model scaling for learning connectivity in higher-dimensional grids or graphs with many chains, and suggest future work examining real-world graphs such as knowledge and causal graphs.

The North Carolina Supreme Court reviewed the case of Roy Allen Whisnant, who was indicted for assault with a deadly weapon with intent to kill. After initially pleading guilty to the lesser offense of assault with a deadly weapon, Whisnant withdrew his plea upon learning it waived certain constitutional rights, and entered a not guilty plea. His requests to continue the case to secure witnesses from West Virginia and Florida, as well as his attorney's request to postpone the trial by a week, were denied. The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on Oct. 7 in Barrett's case, addressing whether Section 924(j) creates a separate crime carrying a separate punishment from Section 924(c) under double jeopardy principles.

Section 924(c) prohibits using a firearm to advance a federal crime of violence or drug-trafficking offense, while Section 924(j) adds liability when such conduct causes a person's death. Barrett was convicted under both provisions for his role in armed robberies that resulted in a fatal shooting.

The analysis applies the nearly century-old Blockburger test, which compares statutory elements to determine whether the legislature intended separate offenses. When one offense requires only a subset of another's elements, courts presume Congress did not intend multiple punishments unless clearly indicated otherwise.

This issue emerged from a decision two years ago holding that Section 924(c)'s sentencing provisions do not automatically apply to Section 924(j) charged alone, though the court did not resolve the double jeopardy question.

Because both Barrett and the government agree separate sentences are impermissible, the court appointed an amicus to defend the 2nd Circuit's contrary ruling. Barrett argues neither statute authorizes cumulative punishment, while the amicus contends Section 924(c)(1)(D)(ii) mandates consecutive sentences sufficient to overcome Blockburger's presumption.

Formative assessment in vocational education and training (VET) requires active teacher-student participation, immediate feedback, and student self-assessment, though it adds workload and involves unplanned teachable moments (De Vos et al., 2024; Sandal, 2023). It identifies student difficulties and can include clear expectations, descriptive feedback, multiple attempts, peer reviews, and self-assessments, often increasing student motivation (Black & Wiliam, 2009; Gulikers et al., 2018).

Vocational teachers must balance academic summative assessments with vocation-based formative ones, as academic tools like written tests often poorly suit VET (Sandal, 2023; De Vos et al., 2024). Competence-based education (CBE) links classroom theory to workplace skills, assessing students' ability to perform industry-standard tasks, and has been shown to improve motivation and engagement (Baartman et al., 2013; Wesselink et al., 2017).

Authentic assessment prioritizes workplace context over strict reliability, developing deeper understanding and relevant skills rather than rote learning (Gulikers et al., 2004). Teachers can reduce subjectivity by clearly communicating procedures, using rubrics, engaging in professional development, and including supervisor feedback from practicums (Baartman et al., 2013; Gulikers et al., 2018).

Because VET integrates theory and practice, a comprehensive assessment program is needed, combining written tests, skills assessments, workplace evaluations, and both summative and formative methods across four competence levels: knows, knows how, shows how, and does (Loo, 2018; Miller, 1990). Overall, effective VET assessment requires authentic, competence-focused approaches that address both theoretical knowledge and technical skills.

The Second Circuit affirmed the district court's grant of summary judgment to Reisdorf Brothers, Inc. on the Georges' federal claims under the Clean Water Act (CWA) and Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA).

Regarding the CWA claim, the court held that the plaintiffs failed to raise a triable issue of fact as to whether Reisdorf engaged in continuous or intermittent discharge of pollutants. Consent orders referenced only a single "catastrophic tank failure" in March 2009, which constitutes a past violation insufficient to support a citizen suit under Gwaltney. Evidence regarding fertilizer, pesticide, and molasses discharges was deemed speculative or inadequate for a reasonable jury to find ongoing violations.

On the RCRA claim, the court found summary judgment appropriate because the plaintiffs failed to allege or provide evidence of violations of the relevant federal regulations defining "open dumping" under 40 C.F.R. pt. 257.

The court also affirmed the district court's decision declining to exercise supplemental jurisdiction over the state law adverse possession claim, consistent with the general rule that state claims should be dismissed when federal claims are dismissed before trial.

Finally, the court upheld the denial of attorney's fees to Reisdorf under 42 U.S.C. § 6972(e), finding no abuse of discretion given that the plaintiffs' claims had some arguable basis in fact and were litigated in good faith.

This study used data from the PREVEND prospective cohort (8,569 participants in Groningen, Netherlands) to model transitions between KDIGO kidney disease risk stages and new-onset heart failure (HF) using a multi-state model accounting for misclassification. Participants were categorized into low, intermediate, or high/very high risk stages based on eGFR and urinary albumin excretion (UAE), with follow-up over a median of 12.6 years.

Key findings:
- Forward transition rates between KDIGO risk stages increased exponentially with age and were generally higher in men; women and younger subjects were more likely to revert from intermediate to low risk.
- Progression to intermediate risk mainly occurred between ages 60–70, and to high/very high risk after age 70.
- More advanced KDIGO stages were associated with increased HF risk. Relative risks decreased with age (e.g., intermediate vs. low: RR=3.4 at 60 years, RR=1.6 at 80), while absolute risk differences increased with age.
- Misclassification probabilities were substantial with creatinine-based eGFR (e.g., 18.4% of intermediate-risk individuals misclassified as low risk) but lower using cystatin C–based eGFR.
- Men had higher mortality than women across all stages.

The authors conclude that kidney disease progresses rapidly in middle-aged populations and that slowing KDIGO stage progression could meaningfully reduce new-onset HF incidence. Limitations include the UAE-enriched, predominantly Caucasian cohort and the Markov assumption.

Backtesting using the EWA ETF as a proxy reveals that mean reversion strategies and classical approaches like the 200-day moving average and Golden Cross are less effective for Australia's commodity-heavy market compared to the US.

This study developed a scale to measure prospective teachers' attitudes toward values education through distance education, addressing a gap in existing literature following the Covid-19 pandemic's shift to online learning.

The research involved 341 prospective teachers (77.3% female) from Gazi University's Faculty of Education. Following DeVellis's (2017) scale development steps, researchers generated an initial pool of 43 items through literature review and student compositions, which was refined to 40 items after expert review and a pilot study. A five-point Likert scale format was used.

Exploratory Factor Analysis yielded a Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin value of .971 and a significant Barlett Sphericity test, confirming sample adequacy. After removing items that did not meet criteria, the final scale consisted of 36 items (21 positive, 15 negative) across two factors: "Necessity and Usefulness" (21 items) and "Feasibility" (15 items), explaining 63.28% of total variance.

Cronbach Alpha reliability coefficients were .97 for "Necessity and Usefulness" and .96 for "Feasibility." Item-total correlations ranged from .656 to .841, and t-values between subgroups were significant, confirming item distinctiveness. Tukey's Test indicated the scale lacks additivity, so subfactors must be evaluated separately.

Limitations include gender imbalance, single-university sampling, and absence of comparable external scales. Researchers recommend future confirmatory factor analyses across multiple universities and additional validity and reliability testing methods.

The Dabhol Power Company (DPC) board, at a London meeting on April 25, 2001, authorized its management—Managing Director Neil McGregor and Enron India MD K Wade Cline—to issue a preliminary termination notice of the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB). Defending skilled tall or wide post players requires a total team effort and special adjustments. Children born to obese parents face significantly higher risks of obesity themselves, with risk doubling when both parents are obese. Research indicates that eggs and sperm carry more than DNA; they contain molecules responsive to parental nutrition that influence offspring development. In obese male mice, non-coding RNAs in sperm differ and, when injected into eggs, produce fatter offspring. Similar alterations occur in obese men. Eggs of obese females contain defective mitochondria, which are maternally inherited and affect offspring metabolism, increasing obesity and diabetes susceptibility. However, embryos also respond to positive signals. Studies show anti-diabetes drugs and exercise improve egg quality in mice, while exercise restores sperm non-coding RNA content and prevents obesity transmission. Human studies are limited, though children conceived after maternal gastric banding were less obese than siblings conceived beforehand. Researchers emphasize pre-conception interventions for both mothers and fathers, supporting policies targeting obesity prevention in adolescents and young adults.

Cornerbacks are defensive players whose primary role is covering wide receivers in man or zone coverage to disrupt the opposing team's passing game. The position is named for its responsibility to protect the outer thirds of the field. Teams typically field two cornerbacks, with a third added in nickel packages to cover slot receivers. Exceptional cornerbacks, known as "lockdown corners" or "DBs," require speed, agility, and the ability to transition from backpedaling to sprinting while mirroring receivers' movements. They also assist in run defense near the boundary. Notable cornerbacks include Deion Sanders, Charles Woodson, Mel Blount, Champ Bailey, Ty Law, and Darrell Revis, with 18 cornerbacks enshrined in the Hall of Fame. Defending goal kicks in soccer involves strategic positioning and pressing to either win the ball in a dangerous area or prevent the opposing team from building up play. Under Law 16, a goal kick is taken from within the goal area after the ball crosses the defenders' end line off an attacking player. The ball is in play once kicked and visibly moved, and opponents must be outside the penalty area until then.

The three main defensive tactics are: positioning defenders using man-to-man and zone coverage, aggressively moving to win the ball, and transitioning to attack or pressing high if the ball is lost. Strikers cut off short passes, midfielders contest aerial balls, and the team maintains options for counters and back-passes.

Coaching varies by age. For players 10 and under, "build-out lines" help teams safely play the ball out from the back, with designated kickers, dribblers, and target receivers used to develop goal-kick plays. Players 11 and above progress to using multiple targets and midfielder options, learning to kick based on defensive coverage. Adults have all options available, typically with the goalkeeper taking the kick.

Key coaching points include recognizing that goal kicks are direct restarts, accounting for field conditions like wind, maintaining awareness of the ball, scouting opponents' tendencies, and drilling defensive goal-kick scenarios thoroughly.

The study analyzes survey data from 147 second-year students at a Hungarian university (engineering and technical management faculties) to examine how they evaluate university education and skills acquisition within the framework of Education 4.0.

1. Both groups ranked Problem Solving as most important, but engineering students prioritized specialization knowledge and technical/mathematical skills, while business students prioritized decision-making and analytical thinking. Hypothesis accepted.

2. Both groups identified individual talents, professional devotion, and networking as key career success factors, with no significant differences. Hypothesis rejected.

3. Students from both faculties valued job-related knowledge and digital literacy from higher education, with significant differences appearing in analytical, teamwork, and self-understanding skills. Hypothesis partly accepted.

Regarding international study experience, both groups valued language improvement most, though engineering students emphasized research opportunities while business students emphasized networking.

Limitations include the small, non-probabilistic sample. The authors conclude that universities must adapt curricula to integrate both hard and soft skills, promote multidisciplinary collaboration, and address the differing needs of engineering and management students to prepare graduates for Industry 4.0.

A cross-sectional study was conducted at the Muhimbili National Hospital Medication Assisted Therapy (MAT) clinic in Dar-es-salaam, Tanzania, between May 2022 and July 2023, to determine the magnitude of lung function decline and associated risk factors among heroin users on methadone therapy. Using systematic sampling, 310 participants aged above 18 were enrolled, with 302 completing spirometry testing. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, substance use, comorbidities, and respiratory symptoms were collected via questionnaire, and lung function was measured using a portable spirometer.

The mean participant age was 42.78 years, with 95.7% male. Cigarette smoking was reported by 83.8%, and 19.9% had injected heroin. HIV prevalence was 9.6%, and 32.8% had a history of pulmonary tuberculosis. Lung function decline was identified in 28.5% of participants, with a mean onset age of 44 years. Being underweight (aOR 4.73), living with HIV (aOR 2.61), and having a history of pulmonary tuberculosis (aOR 2.48) were identified as independent risk factors for lung function decline. The study was limited by the absence of bronchodilator reversibility testing. The authors recommend routine lung function screening at MAT clinics to address undiagnosed lung diseases in this population.

The passage introduces BALLAST (Bayesian Active Learning with Lookahead Amendment for Sea-drifter Trajectories), a methodology for placing Lagrangian ocean drifters. The authors note that while drifters are increasingly used to measure ocean currents due to affordability and sampling capability, existing placement strategies rely on space-filling designs or expert opinion rather than active learning.

Key contributions include: (i) introducing active learning to Lagrangian observer placement, (ii) proposing BALLAST, which simulates hypothetical trajectories using vector fields, and (iii) developing a new Gaussian process (GP) posterior sampling method combining standard GP regression with the stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) approach.

The methodology employs a spatio-temporal, vector-output GP surrogate using a temporal Helmholtz kernel (combining a spatial Helmholtz kernel with a Matérn 3/2 temporal kernel) over two-dimensional, time-dependent vector fields. Placement locations are selected sequentially at predetermined measurement times by maximizing expected information gain, using an equivalent formulation based on mutual information symmetry for computational efficiency. Numerical results indicate benefits on synthetic and high-fidelity ocean current models.

This study examined the relationship between long-term blood pressure (BP) variability and cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) using 1,284 participants from the Kailuan cohort (2006-2022). Systolic BP (SBP), diastolic BP (DBP), and pulse pressure (PP) variability were categorized as low, middle, or high, and MRI identified four cSVD features: white matter hyperintensities (WMH), lacunae (LA), cerebral microbleeds (CMBs), and visible perivascular spaces (PVS).

Results showed cSVD in 69.3% of participants. High SBP variability was associated with moderate cSVD burden and PVS; high DBP variability was associated with LA; and high PP variability showed the strongest risk effects on moderate/severe cSVD burden, LA, and PVS. In participants under 60, only high PP variability was significantly associated with severe cSVD burden, LA, and PVS. Risk effects of SBP and PP variability were significant only in hypertensive participants.

The authors conclude that high long-term BP variability, particularly combined with hypertension, is an independent risk factor for cSVD, and PP variability warrants special attention in younger adults.

In Meola v. Ziman, the New Jersey Superior Court addressed whether an employee's sick time and employer-allowed wages for personal days and family illness constitute collateral sources under N.J.S.A. 2A:15-97, which would entitle a defendant tortfeasor to a credit against a lost wages claim.

The plaintiff, injured as a passenger in an auto accident, sought lost wages from the defendant. The defendant argued that plaintiff's sick pay, personal days, and family illness days should be disclosed to the jury and deducted from any award. The statute aims to prevent claimants from receiving duplicate benefits.

Relying on Bruwelheide v. Garvey and American Jurisprudence, the court reasoned that sick leave and similar benefits are earned as part of employee compensation, and using them due to a tortfeasor's actions diminishes their availability for future use or retirement cash-out.

The court held that sick pay and compensation for personal and family illness days are not collateral source benefits under the statute and cannot offset a lost wages recovery.

The paper concludes that Ontario's education system was structurally designed to exclude disabled and marginalized students, particularly racialized students, who remain undervalued and unplanned for.

Higher education in Pakistan was neglected until 2002, when the government established the Higher Education Commission (HEC) to expand access and improve quality. Enrollment rose from 2% in 2003 to 12.6% in 2021, but growth has been uneven. Universities are concentrated in major cities like Karachi, Lahore, and Islamabad, leaving rural and low-income populations underserved. Private universities, which charge significantly higher fees than public ones, have grown rapidly but primarily serve urban, affluent populations.

Using a distributive social justice framework, this study analyzed secondary data from HEC, AEPAM, PSLM, and PPAF to assess equity in HE access across region, gender, urbanicity, and poverty. Findings show enrollment increased roughly 500% from 2001 to 2021, with the gender gap narrowing (female enrollment rose from 27% to 46%). However, disparities persist: low-poverty zones contain over 70% of universities, while extreme poverty zones have almost none. Female enrollment remains very low in impoverished rural areas, and provinces like Balochistan and rural Sindh lag significantly behind Islamabad, Punjab, and urban Sindh.

The authors conclude that HE growth has not been inclusive and has reproduced structural inequalities. They recommend targeted scholarships, new public universities in rural and high-poverty zones, HEC regulation of private institutions, and expansion of skill-based community colleges. Limitations include the macro-level focus and exclusion of vocational education and cultural barriers. Further research is recommended to support equity-based reforms.

Digital leaders distinguish themselves from digital laggards through four key cultural practices: embracing a learning mindset, ensuring data transparency, using measurement to guide progress, and aligning the organization through shared data-driven goals.

Digital leaders encourage sensible risk-taking, experimentation, and long-term employee development, viewing themselves as learning organizations. In contrast, laggards prioritize short-term optimization, discourage risk, and offer narrow, transactional training. Even in regulated industries, leaders can create localized environments for safe experimentation.

Leaders promote broad access to data, believing good ideas can come from anywhere, while maintaining appropriate governance controls. Laggards hoard data, rely on business judgment or a "culture of genius," and use data mainly to justify pre-made decisions.

Digital leaders ground objectives in measurable data, using metrics to provide teams flexibility and autonomy. Laggards set unrealistic aspirational goals disconnected from data, causing employees to avoid measurement and focus on process adherence.

Leaders use transparent, data-driven objectives developed through top-down and bottom-up processes to align teams around a shared "North Star" vision, though some struggle with over-analysis. Laggards fail to connect goals to strategy, causing misalignment.

Data culture aligns organizations both vertically (individuals to company goals) and horizontally (across teams). Changing entrenched mindsets is the most challenging aspect of digital transformation, but laggards can progress. Organizations typically fit into four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant—and can build from their strengths toward a strong data culture.
