His accomplishments include serving as principal cellist of the Abington Heights Symphony Orchestra and PMEA district 9 and region 4, ranking 11th and 7th at the PMEA state level, participating in a master class with pianist Fei Fei Doug, performing with the Wyoming Seminary Civic Orchestra, receiving the Director Award, playing in "Les Misérables," teaching cello to peers, and being named WVIA artist of the year. He also joined the NEPA Philharmonic mentoring program, performing at the Kirby Center and Marywood University. Beyond music, he participated in scholastic bowl, Envirothon, and the ACS National Olympiad, and also plays violin. Lambert performs classical, pop, and modern music at various events. He plans to study chemical engineering at the University of Delaware while continuing to perform with chamber groups.

Jordan Montgomery, a 6-foot-6 lefty pitcher, threw four perfect innings against the Tigers to complete a combined no-hitter in a 3-0 Yankees victory. Manager Joe Girardi said the 24-year-old could potentially make the Opening Day roster, likely as a reliever, though Montgomery's long-term future is as a starter. After strong performances at Double-A Trenton and Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre last season, Montgomery has remained with the major league team during spring training while others have been reassigned. He faces competition from Luis Severino, Bryan Mitchell, Chad Green, and Adam Warren for rotation spots, alongside veterans Tanaka, Sabathia, and Pineda.

LimeWire, formerly known as a file-sharing tool, has re-emerged as an AI content publishing platform. It allows users to create AI-generated images using models like Stable Diffusion 2.1, Stable Diffusion XL, and DALL-E 2, with various design styles available. Artists including Deadmau5, Soulja Boy, and Sean Kingston use the platform to publish NFT content.

Created content is automatically minted as NFTs on the Polygon or Algorand blockchain, and can be made public or exclusive to premium subscribers. Creators earn a 2.5% royalty on trades and can receive up to 70% of ad revenue, paid in LimeWire's LMWR cryptocurrency, which is tradable on exchanges like Kraken, ByBit, and UniSwap.

Free users receive 10 credits daily and 50% ad revenue share. Premium plans range from $9.99 to $99 per month, offering increased credits, image generation limits, early access to AI models, and higher ad revenue shares. LimeWire plans to expand into AI music and video generation tools.

A Sunshine Coast woman was sexually abused by her stepbrother over eight years, beginning when she was eight and he was 14, after their parents combined households. The abuse included inappropriate touching and five rapes, starting when she was 10 and continuing until age 16, when their parents separated. She reported the abuse in 2011 after joining the Australian Defence Force, and gave evidence to police in 2013. Her abuser, now 33, was arrested in 2015 and pleaded guilty to five counts of rape, three counts of indecent treatment of a child under 12, and one count of maintaining a sexual relationship with a child. Judge Brian Devereaux noted sentencing difficulty as crimes spanned his childhood and adulthood. He was jailed for five years with parole eligibility from August 10, 2015.

This whitepaper is a collaborative effort by the Societal AI team at Microsoft Research Asia (MSRA) and computer and social scientists from various institutions, including Tsinghua University, College of William and Mary, Renmin University of China, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, and Microsoft CELA. Additional contributors include interns from Tsinghua, Peking, Nanjing, and New York Universities. A designer team led by Yang Ou and Scarlett Li, including interns from the University of Washington and Capital Normal University, supported publication. The authors also acknowledge researchers involved in the Societal AI initiative and express gratitude to Lidong Zhou from MSRA for his support and suggestions.

The lecture introduces linearized general relativity as one of three approaches to solving the Einstein field equations, alongside symmetric solutions and numerical methods. Linearized GR considers spacetimes that are nearly flat, expressing the metric as the flat spacetime metric plus a small perturbation h-alpha-beta, with all higher-order terms in h neglected.

Key properties are established: Lorentz transformations leave the background metric unchanged while the perturbation transforms as an ordinary tensor field. Indices are raised and lowered using the flat metric, and the inverse metric equals the flat inverse minus h-alpha-beta to linear order.

Infinitesimal coordinate transformations, called gauge transformations, modify the metric perturbation but leave the Riemann curvature unchanged—analogous to gauge transformations in electromagnetism.

After running the linearized metric through the curvature machinery, the Einstein tensor is simplified by introducing the trace-reversed perturbation h-bar. Choosing Lorentz gauge (where the divergence of h-bar vanishes) reduces the field equations to a simple wave equation: the box operator acting on h-bar equals a constant times the stress-energy tensor.

In the static, non-relativistic limit with a perfect fluid source, this reproduces the Newtonian gravitational potential equation, yielding a metric that describes the Newtonian limit of general relativity. This framework underlies gravitational lensing, post-Newtonian solar system tests, and analysis of many binary systems.

The lecture notes that a rotating body generates additional "gravitomagnetic" effects resembling magnetic fields, and previews upcoming discussions of general dynamic solutions and gravitational radiation.

Executive Pay (Business Week): In 2000, average CEO pay at 365 large U.S. companies rose to $13.1 million, with cash compensation up 18% and total pay up 6.3%—the smallest increase in five years. Despite weak market performance, most boards shielded CEOs from losses through new options grants, loan forgiveness, and repricings. John Reed of Citigroup topped the list at $293 million. Jeffrey Skilling of Enron ranked 20th at $72.5 million, while Enron's Kenneth Lay topped non-CEO earners at $140.8 million. Some companies, like Dana Corp., Coca-Cola, and Oracle, tied pay more closely to performance. Institutional investors have filed over 50 shareholder proposals targeting executive pay.

Enron Payment Dispute (NYT): India's government refused to pay $22 million owed to the Enron-majority-owned Dabhol Power Company, citing a penalty for alleged contractual failures. The dispute will go to conciliation and possibly London arbitration. U.S. diplomats warned this could harm future foreign investment.

Utility Earnings (LA Times): U.S. utilities are expected to post strong Q1 results due to cold weather boosting gas and power demand. Enron, Dynegy, PPL, Entergy, and others are highlighted. Utility profits are projected to grow 11% versus an 8.6% decline for the S&P 500.

Energy Cost Study (LA Times): A confidential Cal-ISO document identifies public agencies—including LA's DWP, Bonneville Power Administration, and BC Hydro's Powerex—alongside private firms as driving up California wholesale electricity prices. Powerex earned $176 million in alleged excess profits, followed by Mirant at $97 million. Enron ranked sixth at $27.9 million. Total alleged excess profits reached $505 million from May to November 2000. Named entities denied manipulation.

French Power Trading (Reuters): A wholesale power trading market is emerging in France despite EdF's 95% generation dominance. About eight companies, including Enron, TXU Europe, and RWE, regularly trade, with roughly 30 deals weekly. EdF plans to release 10% of output to competitors, and a Paris power bourse launches in July.

Brazil's Copel (Reuters): Brazil's integrated power utility Copel is set for privatization in H2 2001, with the government's 31% stake valued at 1.4 billion reais. Potential bidders include Tractebel, AES, Duke Energy, and Enron.

Dabhol Renegotiation (Business Standard): The Godbole committee recommended renegotiating both phases of the Enron-promoted Dabhol project and linking returns to a fixed rupee-dollar rate to lower tariffs. The committee was divided on certain concessions and reportedly lacked powers to fully investigate.

Mexico's higher education system enrolls over 5.2 million students, with online learning growing 150% since 2013-14 compared to 18% growth in face-to-face learning. Despite this expansion, no prior studies have examined online learning's potential to improve access and quality in Mexico. This qualitative study used semi-structured interviews with 32 academic leaders, professors, and students from six Mexican universities, applying the Community of Inquiry framework to analyze responses.

Findings revealed that online learning expands access for non-traditional students but is limited by economic and infrastructural barriers, particularly in rural areas, and challenges neurodivergent students. Quality concerns included insufficient faculty training in online pedagogy, lower student engagement, collaboration difficulties, and increased academic dishonesty. Stakeholders generally viewed online learning as a complement to in-person education rather than a replacement, valuing its flexibility and utility for international collaboration.

The study concludes that while online learning could democratize Mexican higher education, existing digital divides risk deepening disparities without targeted infrastructure investment, teacher training, and support for underserved student populations.

The author shares personal experiences with esthetician Renée Rouleau, who previously diagnosed her melasma (triggered by birth control) and acne cosmetica (caused by oil-based foundation in dry climates). During a recent visit, Rouleau introduced her newest product, the Rapid Response Detox Masque ($61), designed to combat hormonal and premenstrual acne without drying skin. Key ingredients include tea tree leaf oil, Chinese licorice, manuka oil, and a salicylic acid complex, while excluding parabens, synthetic fragrances and dyes, alcohol, and gluten. The author tested it for a month with positive results, using it weekly for about 15 minutes after exfoliating. She reports the lightweight gel mask removes easily and leaves skin glowing.

This specification update document for the AMD Geode™ CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 lists known hardware issues, their implications, and resolutions. Key issues include:

- **PIT deviations**: Read-back commands do not cancel uncompleted counter latch commands, and new count values in mode 3 load immediately rather than after current counting completes.
- **Debug port and GLIU issues**: The GLIU debug port hangs, data pattern detection fails, and MSR unexpected address flags do not activate.
- **DMA/PIC issues**: DMA rotating mode priorities do not rotate correctly; PIC fails if an edge-configured interrupt source remains high after clock gating; AEOI causes duplicate interrupts.
- **UART limitations**: UART registers cannot be accessed during block/demand DMA; clock gating fails in CEIR mode.
- **I/O addressing**: Addresses at 10000h or higher incorrectly claimed, causing hangs.
- **UDMA/ATAC problems**: CRC corruption after device termination, hangs with non-DWORD aligned PRDs, and PIO failures when bus master is enabled first.
- **USB**: Over-voltage protection specification not met; clock gating causes register read failures; KEL emulation cannot distinguish writes to ports 060h and 064h.
- **ACPI/PMC**: Byte accesses to PM1_STS/PM1_EN hang; WORD/BYTE writes to PMC registers cause corruption; most wake inputs fail from S3 state.
- **PCI**: IRDY# and DEVSEL# violate tVAL minimum timing; SSMI may not be synchronous with IRQs.
- **Other**: LPC aborts on certain SYNC patterns, SMB NEGACK bit misbehaves, GPIO High Bank writes fail post-suspend, LOWBAT_FLAG missing after abnormal standby, and SLEEP_X/Y signals not properly de-asserted.

Most resolutions involve avoiding specific operations, disabling features, using workarounds, or employing external circuitry/software traps.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers feature soft-start circuitry controlled by a capacitor between SS pin and AVSS, using a 0.613V reference and 2.7µA charging current. Switching frequency (100kHz-2MHz) can be set via three modes: internal oscillator (RT resistor), external synchronization (clock at SYNC pin), or primary-secondary mode. The controllers offer configurable duty cycle limits, programmable dead times and leading edge blank times, and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) that activate after soft-start. Protection features include cycle-by-cycle current limiting via CS_ILIM, hiccup mode operation, external FAULT pin protection, and thermal shutdown at 175°C. The devices use peak current mode control with slope compensation configurable via RSC pin, and support Type 2A/2B frequency compensation. Applications include buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies, operating from 4-14V input. Layout guidelines emphasize separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switching loops, and placing bypass capacitors close to the controller.

The disclosure relates to a force transmission mechanism for a teleoperated surgical instrument that converts rotary input motion into translational movement of an actuation element to operate an end effector.

The mechanism includes a drive pulley, a driven pulley, and a drive cable operably coupling the two. The drive pulley and driven pulley may have rotational axes oriented in parallel or non-parallel relationships, with a perpendicular orientation described in one embodiment. The drive cable may be a single cable or two separate cables fixed to both pulleys, with the latter configuration facilitating pre-tensioning. Rotation of the drive pulley causes one cable portion to wind while another unwinds, transmitting rotation to the driven pulley.

An actuation element, such as a push-pull rod, is operably coupled to the driven pulley via a ball joint. Rotation of the driven pulley produces translational movement of the rod, which actuates components such as opposing jaws (e.g., forceps, grippers, or clip appliers) through a cam and pin arrangement.

Components may include a chassis, interface disks coupling with a patient-side manipulator, idler pulleys routing the cables, and grooved pulleys. The drive pulley may include independently rotatable upper and lower sheaves locked together via a clamp screw to enable cable pre-tensioning.

The relative diameters of the pulleys and the ball joint's distance from the driven pulley's rotational axis determine mechanical advantage, which can be optimized for specific applications. The disclosure notes that this configuration may provide higher force transmission efficiency and improved reliability compared to toothed gear arrangements.

Clarkson College developed a model for integrating Interprofessional Education (IPE) into higher education, grounded in the Interprofessional Education Collaborative (IPEC) Core Competencies, the Quadruple Aim, and guidance from NCICLE. Formed in 2016, an IPE Committee designed a framework emphasizing community involvement, service, and online learning to accommodate both clinical and non-clinical, on-campus and distance students.

The resulting IPE 301 course, required of all degree-seeking students, consists of five online modules. The first four cover IPEC competencies through didactic content, while the fifth requires participation in real-time IPE events across three categories: knowledge, community, and service. A parallel course is required of faculty and staff.

Student competencies are measured using the Interprofessional Collaborative Competencies Attainment Survey (ICCAS) administered as pre-, mid-, and post-tests, alongside qualitative analysis of reflection journals. Data collected from 428 students between Fall 2018 and Summer 2021 showed that 88.6% reported improved collaboration ability after the first four modules, and 93% of those reported further growth after participating in IPE events. Qualitative findings indicated positive student experiences with teamwork, collaboration, and communication.

The authors attribute the program's success to careful curriculum planning, executive leadership support, faculty engagement, and ongoing monitoring by a four-team microsystem addressing curriculum, outcome assessment, professional development, and clinical application.

Enron Corp. confirmed it is in talks with rival Dynegy Inc. for a possible acquisition valued at approximately $8 billion in stock, potentially backed by a $1.5 billion cash infusion from ChevronTexaco, which owns 27% of Dynegy. The talks follow Enron's severe financial troubles, including a 75% share price decline since mid-October, credit rating downgrades to within two steps of junk status, and an SEC investigation into partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, who allegedly received over $30 million from them.

Enron announced it will restate earnings from 1997 through the second quarter of 2001, reducing net income by hundreds of millions across those years. The company also fired its treasurer and a division lawyer. Trading partners in North American and UK power and gas markets, including Mirant, Aquila, PPL, and Tractebel, have restricted dealings with Enron due to credit concerns, though none have fully withdrawn given Enron's market centrality. A potential further downgrade to junk status would require early repayment of $3.3 billion in bonds. FERC stated it is monitoring the situation but will not intervene in the SEC probe. Enron plans to meet with over 300 creditors on Friday.

The lecture examines the Schwarzschild solution as a vacuum spacetime with mass m, which contains a true tidal singularity at r=0 and a coordinate singularity at r=2GM. Although infalling bodies reach r=2GM in finite proper time, they appear to asymptotically approach it in coordinate time t, indicating the time coordinate is pathological at that surface.

Analysis of light propagation shows that radiation emitted near r=2GM is infinitely redshifted, and pulse intervals stretch to infinity, revealing that the Einstein synchronization procedure breaks down there. Null geodesics in Schwarzschild coordinates show light cones closing up as r approaches 2GM.

To resolve this, tortoise coordinates (r*) and new coordinates v and u (constant on ingoing/outgoing null rays) are introduced, eliminating the dr² term. Kruskal-Szekeres coordinates further demonstrate that light always travels at 45° angles, and r=2GM becomes a pair of lines. Inside r=2GM, all timelike trajectories must move toward r=0, making this surface an event horizon. Such spacetimes are called black holes.

Two other black hole solutions are introduced: the Reissner-Nordström (charged) and the Kerr (spinning, discovered by Roy Kerr) black holes, with Kerr-Newman combining both charge and spin. The No-Hair theorem states that the only stationary spacetimes in 3+1 dimensions with event horizons are Kerr-Newman black holes, characterized entirely by mass, spin, and charge. Price's theorem states that any structure inconsistent with the Kerr-Newman form is radiated away during collapse. Astrophysical black holes are effectively described by the Kerr solution, which has passed all observational tests.

The TMS320DM8127 DaVinci Digital Media processor is a programmable, integrated platform combining an ARM Cortex-A8 RISC CPU with Neon extension, a TI C674x VLIW floating-point DSP core, and high-definition video/imaging coprocessors. The ARM manages control functions separately from A/V algorithms on the DSP and coprocessors, reducing system complexity. The ARM Cortex-A8 includes 32KB instruction cache, 32KB data cache, 256KB L2 cache, 48KB Boot ROM, and 64KB RAM. The C674x DSP, code-compatible with prior C64x/C67x generations, uses 32KB L1 program memory with EDC, 32KB L1 data memory, and 256KB L2 RAM with ECC; accesses are routed through an MMU.

Peripherals include dual-port Gigabit Ethernet MACs supporting IEEE 1588, multiple McASP audio serial ports, a McBSP port, an 8/16-bit asynchronous memory interface, and two DCAN modules. An HDVICP2 coprocessor offloads video/imaging tasks from the DSP. Development tools include C compilers, a DSP assembly optimizer, and a Windows debugger interface.

The document also covers the Media Controller, Face Detect module (supporting QVGA inputs), Spinlock module (128 hardware semaphores), and Mailbox module for inter-processor communication. Memory maps, pin multiplexing, boot modes, power sequencing, clocking, and peripheral timing specifications are detailed, along with revision history tracking changes across SPRS712A, B, and C versions.

The Wisconsin Department of Workforce Development has awarded nearly $480,000 in grants across seven projects to train approximately 600 Milwaukee residents for local jobs. The funding is part of the $4.5 million announced by Gov. Scott Walker in August following unrest in Sherman Park. Recipients include the Milwaukee Area Health Education Center, Word of Hope Ministries, St. Ann Center for Intergenerational Care, Employ Milwaukee, Grant Lakes Community Conservation Corps, Abaxent LLC, and Enoch Solutions. Training areas range from community health work and childcare to construction, CNC operation, and customer service. DWD Secretary Ray Allen stated the grants help employers recruit and train skilled workers.

NVIDIA's A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture and built on TSMC's 7nm process, is the company's 8th generation data center GPU. It contains 54.2 billion transistors, 108 SMs, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, and 40GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth. Key features include third-generation Tensor Cores supporting new data types (TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, binary), fine-grained structured sparsity that doubles throughput, and Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology that partitions a single GPU into up to seven isolated instances for improved utilization and multi-tenant use cases. The A100 delivers up to 2.5x the performance of V100 for mixed-precision workloads and 20x V100's standard FP32 throughput. Additional enhancements include third-generation NVLink (600 GB/sec total bandwidth), PCIe Gen 4, a 40MB L2 cache, asynchronous copy instructions, hardware-accelerated barriers, improved error detection, and a hardware JPEG decoder. CUDA 11 adds programming support for these features, including task graph acceleration. The NVIDIA DGX A100 system combines eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitches to deliver 5 PFLOPS of AI performance for large-scale training and inference workloads.

The documents detail diplomatic correspondence from January 1917 regarding responses to President Wilson's peace note of December 18, 1916.

Ambassador Page reported that the Allies' joint reply, friendly in tone but lacking war aim details, would be sent by Briand pending Russian approval. Minister Droppers reported Greece submitted a conciliatory but vague preliminary reply, while the Italian Minister warned Greece must accept conditions from a December 31 note within 48 hours, with 15 days for execution, or the blockade would continue.

Ambassador Sharp reported that Briand delivered the Allied reply on behalf of the Allied Governments, with Belgium submitting a separate note expressing gratitude to the United States. Briand explained publication could not be delayed and was scheduled for Friday the 12th. The French note praised Wilson's sentiments and endorsed a league of nations concept, but stated peace discussions required first settling the current conflict, securing reparations, restitution, and guarantees from the Central Powers, whom they held responsible for the war.

Mr. Solanko discussed with a U.S. official the travel of Finnish Legation personnel, including Mr. Mikkola and Mr. Wrede, who were in New York and being recalled to Washington. The official clarified that the U.S. note applied to future visits outside Washington. Solanko inquired about Finnish restrictions on American personnel and procedural handling of communications, expressing some surprise at the U.S. terms.

In a separate meeting, the Finnish Minister told Assistant Secretary Long that restrictions in Helsinki applied universally to all diplomats because Helsinki was designated a "war area," and requested relief from restrictions in Washington. Long noted inconsistencies and said the U.S. would respond later.

A telegram from Minister Schoenfeld summarized Finnish public opinion (December 21, 1941–January 4), shaped by U.S. military reverses in the Far East and growing U.S. cooperation with the Soviet Union. Finns reportedly felt satisfaction at U.S. setbacks but alarm over U.S. alignment with the USSR.

The passage lists nine podcasts aimed at improving financial knowledge:

1. **Side Hustle Nation** – Hosted by Nick Loper, focuses on starting side businesses for passive income.
2. **SO Money** – Hosted by Farnoosh Torabi, covers personal/business finance and personal development.
3. **Smart Passive Income** – Hosted by Pat Flynn, teaches wealth-building and starting side businesses with minimal resources.
4. **Adulting Podcast** – Created by Harlan L. Landes and Miranda Marquit, targets financial education for younger audiences.
5. **Money Podcast** – Hosted by Cait Flanders and Carrie S. Nicholson, helps young adults manage money.
6. **Millennial Money** – Hosted by Shannah Compton Game, offers relatable personal finance tips for millennials.
7. **Money Girl** – Provides quick tips on personal finance, real estate, and investing.
8. **Radical Personal Finance** – Hosted by Joshua Sheats, focuses on achieving financial freedom.
9. **Money For The Rest of Us** – Hosted by David Stein, explains money, the economy, and financial markets.

The October 5, 2000 edition of VentureWire, a daily private company business news publication by Technologic Partners, reported several major stories. Broadcom announced it would acquire U.K.-based chip maker Element 14 for approximately $640 million in stock. Sony Broadband Entertainment launched 550 Digital Media Ventures, a subsidiary to incubate, fund, and acquire digital media companies. Andersen Consulting's AC Ventures and Softbank Venture Capital launched GameChange, a network of incubators with up to $100 million in investments. Enterprise Investors raised $200 million in the first closing of its $300 million PEF IV fund focused on Poland and Central Europe. Productopia, a product review site, closed down, and CyOptics secured $57 million in funding for optical networking components.

The issue also covered numerous funding rounds, including Talisma ($31.5 million), Ripcord Systems ($16.5 million), Cyclone Commerce ($31 million), ePartners ($35 million), NetScaler ($35 million), and the Paytrust/PayMyBills merger with $20 million in financing. M&A activity included WatchGuard's $66 million acquisition of Qiave Technologies and Peopleclick's acquisition of Claybrooke & Associates. New executive appointments, board changes, VC fund launches, and corrections to prior reporting were also included.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS ADC with a source-synchronous data interface where clock frequency depends on sampling rate, data rate (SDR/DDR), and number of output lanes (two or four).

The device includes a data output randomizer that performs bit-wise XOR between the conversion result and either the LSB or an appended PRBS bit, reducing correlation between data transmission and analog performance. Two data averaging modes are supported: simple averaging (halves output rate) and moving average (preserves rate).

Test patterns for debugging include fixed patterns, digital ramps, and alternating patterns, configurable separately for channel groups CH[4:1] and CH[8:5]. Power-down is controlled via the PWDN pin or register write, and reset via the RESET pin. An initialization sequence of register writes is required after power-up or reset.

A speed-boost mode enables up to 8MSPS sampling on a user-selected channel pair while other channels are idle. Configuration registers are organized in three banks, accessible via SPI with bank selection through register 0x03. Daisy-chain topology supports multiple devices sharing CS and SCLK, requiring N×24 SCLKs per frame.

The device has three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence. It offers low-noise (up to 22.7kHz) and wide-bandwidth (up to 700kHz) modes, achieving 0.0015% TUE at 25°C post-calibration, suitable for ATE applications.

Stafford Global, based in the Ras Al Khaimah Free Zone, UAE, offers open days and webinars for working professionals interested in online or distance learning programs. Attendees can consult academic and admissions experts online. A University of Northampton MBA Webinar is scheduled for 1 May 2018. Attendees of open days are encouraged to bring a CV and certificates for a free review and eligibility assessment. Partner universities include Leicester, Northampton, Nottingham, Dundee, and Edinburgh Napier. Registration is available via their blog or by requesting a call back.

The December 6, 2000 VentureWire newsletter reports major industry news including Oxygen Media laying off 65 employees and restructuring its online business around four brands while consolidating offices. Softbank reportedly halted investments through two European joint ventures, eVentures U.K. and @visio, though it will continue direct early-stage European investments. Innovance Networks secured $75 million in second-round funding led by Morgenthaler Ventures and Thomas Weisel Partners, bringing total financing to $95 million. Merrill Lynch launched an Internal Venture Capital Fund to support business plans from its employees in financial services technology, planning to seed three to four companies by early next year.

The newsletter also details numerous funding rounds across sectors including wireless, optical networking, semiconductors, B2B applications, and healthcare. Notable closures include Babygear.com filing for Chapter 7 bankruptcy. Pets.com agreed to sell its URL to Petsmart.com. Several companies rebranded, including Gazooba to Qbiquity and TelenComm to Zeevo. Giza Venture Capital closed its third fund at $211 million. The newsletter additionally covers new board appointments, executive hires, mergers such as Fandom acquiring Creation Entertainment, and Qualcomm's new equity-based CDMA licensing program for early-stage companies.

US unemployment claims fell by 12,000 to 260,000 for the week ended Sept. 30, though Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, and Maria continued to affect the data. Economists expect September nonfarm payrolls to show 90,000 jobs added, down from 156,000 in August. Claims have remained below 300,000 for 135 consecutive weeks, the longest stretch since 1970.

Separately, the Commerce Department reported the trade deficit narrowed 2.7 percent in August to $42.4 billion, the smallest since September 2016. Exports rose 0.4 percent to $195.3 billion, the highest since December 2014, with exports to China up 8.8 percent. Imports dipped 0.1 percent to $237.7 billion, though imports from China reached a record high, pushing the US-China trade deficit up 4.0 percent to $34.9 billion. The improved trade data could offset some hurricane-related GDP losses, expected to cut at least 0.6 percentage points from third-quarter growth.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 31, 2021 reports revenue of $7.10 billion for Q3, up 50% year-over-year, and $19.27 billion for the first nine months. Net income was $2.46 billion for the quarter and $6.75 billion year-to-date. Gross margin reached 65.2%, with growth driven by Gaming (up 42%), Data Center (up 55%), and Professional Visualization (up 144%) segments.

On June 3, 2021, shareholders approved a four-for-one stock split, distributed July 19, 2021. In June 2021, NVIDIA issued $5 billion in new notes (2023, 2024, 2028, and 2031) and repaid $1 billion of 2021 Notes in August 2021.

The pending $40 billion acquisition of Arm Limited from SoftBank, announced September 13, 2020, faces regulatory scrutiny from the FTC, China, UK, and EU, with Phase 2 reviews underway in the UK and EU. The transaction may be terminated if not closed by September 2022.

Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $19.30 billion as of October 31, 2021. The company operates in two segments: Graphics and Compute & Networking. NVIDIA paid $298 million in dividends during the first nine months and has $7.24 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization through December 2022. Ongoing securities class action and derivative lawsuits remain pending on appeal.

California lawmakers revived a proposal to set a goal of generating 100 percent of the state's energy from carbon-free sources. A legislative committee advanced the bill to the full Assembly for a vote later this year. Authored by Democratic Sen. Kevin de Leon, the bill would raise California's renewable portfolio standard from 50 percent to 60 percent by 2030, requiring energy from resources such as wind, solar, geothermal and small dams. It would also target 100 percent carbon-free energy by 2045, with specifics to be determined later. Critics, including business groups and utilities, warn the measure could raise prices for industrial users and consumers, and render fossil fuel plants stranded assets. The legislation coincides with Senate consideration of expanding the Independent System Operator regionally, and discussions about reducing utility liability for wildfire damages.

The Soviet leadership favors multi-level dialogues with the U.S. to exploit differences within democratic governments. For two years, U.S. policy has limited political contacts to ministerial and ambassadorial levels, rejecting Soviet attempts to establish direct White House links. Lower-level talks should only occur after Moscow signals willingness to make concessions through Gromyko or Dobrynin, with summits reserved for when issues near resolution. Proposals for a summit and intensified specialist dialogues are deemed premature, as meetings with Gromyko and expert-level talks on Afghanistan and Namibia have shown no Soviet readiness to concede. Another Gromyko meeting is suggested to assess Moscow's position. Creating false expectations through intensified dialogue could pressure the U.S. into concessions long-term.

In an attached memorandum, Paula Dobriansky opposes Ambassador Hartman's argument that the zero-zero arms control option should be abandoned. She contends Hartman's view repeats the failed 1970s approach, and that deterrence requires redressing Soviet strategic-nuclear advantages. Restoring parity at intercontinental and theater levels through arms control and new deployments is presented as the fundamental objective, since a non-zero solution would perpetuate Soviet superiority in long-range Euro-based nuclear systems. Hartman anticipates continued Soviet propaganda and European resistance to U.S. "rigidity," jeopardizing INF deployment.

The University of Ghana has appointed Mary Chinery-Hesse as its first woman Chancellor, making her the first woman to hold such a position in Ghana's public universities. Beginning August 2018, she will replace current Chancellor Kofi Annan, overseeing university operations, graduation ceremonies, and degree issuance.

Chinery-Hesse is Vice-Chairman of Ghana's National Development Planning Commission and holds positions on several boards, including the Centre for Policy Analysis and the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission. She previously served as Deputy Director General of the International Labour Organization (1989-1999) and as UNDP Resident Representative in Sierra Leone, Tanzania, the Seychelles, and Uganda. Earlier, she was Principal Secretary at Ghana's Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning.

She holds a BA in Sociology and Economics and an honorary Doctor of Laws from the University of Ghana, with postgraduate training from the University of Dublin. She is also a member of the AU's Panel of the Wise for West Africa and Board Chairman of Zenith Bank, Ghana.

This paper presents a formalization of constructive nominal sets in the Rocq proof assistant, building towards a nominal framework for reasoning about syntax with binders. The authors follow the approach of Choudhury's Agda formalization but leverage Rocq's typeclass hierarchy and generalized rewriting mechanism to mitigate the burden of working with setoids.

The formalization develops core nominal theory notions: names (as an abstract type with decidable equality and infiniteness), permutations (represented as lists of swaps), permutation actions, nominal sets (as typeclasses), freshness, name abstraction, and finitely supported functions. Since least supports cannot be proved constructively, the authors use "some support" characterized via swaps, and define freshness accordingly. Some/any principles are proved to bridge existential and universal formulations.

Key contributions beyond prior work include formalizations of the Freshness Theorem and the Freshness Condition for Binders (FCB), which were not present in Choudhury's development. The authors discuss implementation challenges, such as representing name abstraction via a dedicated Record type to avoid typeclass resolution issues, and bundling supported functions similar to Lean MathLib's approach.

Related work includes classical formalizations (Isabelle's nominal package), axiomatic approaches in Rocq, and other Agda formalizations. As ongoing work, the authors are developing α-structural recursion and induction principles, currently having derived an α-recursion principle for the λ-calculus, with α-induction posing additional challenges since it would require showing Prop is a nominal set.

A 28-year-old man suspected of shooting two teenagers at a Pasadena birthday party was fatally shot by law enforcement Friday in Duarte. Officers from three agencies, including a U.S. Marshals task force, opened fire after locating the parolee and a 36-year-old woman in a vehicle on Encanto Parkway. The woman was wounded, expected to survive, and arrested on suspicion of narcotics possession. One officer sustained minor injuries. The Thursday Pasadena shooting on North Summit Avenue left a 19-year-old man in critical condition and a 16-year-old girl treated and released.

Netflix evolved from a 1997 DVD rental company into the leading streaming video on demand (SVOD) provider, reaching 167 million subscribers and a $157 billion enterprise value by 2019. It grew by licensing content, producing original series starting with House of Cards (2013), and expanding to 190 countries, spending $15 billion on original content in 2019.

Netflix attributed its success to a distinctive culture outlined in its widely-read "Culture Deck," emphasizing five values: freedom and responsibility, transparency, candor, retaining only highly effective employees (the "dream team"), and avoiding rules. The company paid top-market salaries, used a "keeper test" for retention, and encouraged experimentation and open feedback.

Strategically, Netflix focused solely on streaming, rejected advertising, adopted a "cost-plus" model for original content while retaining global rights, and used a "straight-to-series" approach. It invested $1.5 billion in technology in 2019.

Facing new competition from Disney+, HBO Max, and Peacock, Netflix targeted India as the source of its "next 100 million" subscribers. Entering India in 2016, it had about 2 million subscribers by 2019, compared to Disney-owned Hotstar's 129 million users. Netflix launched a $2.85 mobile-only plan and committed $420 million for local content by 2020.

The Indian SVOD market included 32 players by 2018, with broadcasters, telecoms, international streamers, and local players competing largely on price and regional-language content. Indian consumers preferred mobile viewing, regional languages, and ad-supported freemium models. Netflix faced strategic questions about pricing, advertising, partnerships, acquisitions, and local decision-making authority in pursuing Indian growth.

Senseonics Holdings (NYSE:SENS) received a somewhat positive media sentiment score of 0.19 from Accern Sentiment Analysis, along with an impact score of 43.92 out of 100, suggesting recent coverage is unlikely to affect share price soon. Shares rose 5.03% on Friday to $3.34, with a market capitalization of $411.49 million. The company's 50-day and 200-day moving averages are both $3.12, with a 12-month range of $2.15 to $3.67. Senseonics is a medical technology company focused on glucose monitoring systems, including its implantable CGM system, Eversense.

Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez Bezos, a public couple since 2019, have frequently appeared together at high-profile events wearing coordinated outfits. Notable appearances include Prime Video events, "Lord of the Rings" premieres, fashion shows for Versace, Staud, Dolce & Gabbana, and Chanel, the Vanity Fair Oscars after-parties, the 2024 Met Gala, and a White House state dinner. Bezos typically wears tuxedos or suits, while Sánchez Bezos favors designer gowns from labels such as Tom Ford, Elie Saab, Oscar de la Renta, and John Galliano. Their June 2025 wedding in Venice featured multiple high-end looks, including a lace mermaid-style bridal gown and a pink Atelier Versace dress. They later attended Paris Fashion Week in matching gray ensembles.

The newly elected President affirms he has taken the oath of office and pledges to fulfill its duties to the best of his ability. He states he will share his views with Congress, use the veto when necessary, and faithfully execute all laws, whether he approves of them or not. He emphasizes that bad laws are best repealed through strict enforcement.

He notes that the post-Civil War era presents unprecedented challenges, requiring calm deliberation aimed at the greatest good for the greatest number, including securing personal, property, and religious freedoms nationwide.

On finances, he calls for repayment of the national debt in gold unless otherwise stipulated, a return to specie payments when feasible, faithful revenue collection, and reduced government expenditure. He expresses confidence in the country's future paying capacity, referencing precious metal resources in the West. He urges prudence in contracting future debts and calls for rebuilding commerce and industry.

He appeals to young citizens to uphold national honor and argues that unity on a debt repayment plan matters more than the specific method.

On foreign policy, he advocates treating nations equitably while protecting citizens abroad and demanding mutual respect. He supports policies promoting Indian civilization, Christianization, and citizenship, and endorses ratification of the Fifteenth Amendment to address suffrage. He closes by requesting patience, unity, and prayer.

The DISCARD operation resembles the default ERASE operation, allowing the card to de-allocate discarded blocks partially or completely. Previously written data in discarded regions should be treated as "don't care" by the host and may be partially or fully readable afterward.

To discard multiple write blocks simultaneously, the host uses ERASE_WR_BLK_START (CMD32), ERASE_WR_BLK_END (CMD33), and DISCARD (CMD38) with argument 00000001h. Hosts must verify card support via the DISCARD_SUPPORT bit (b313) in the SD_STATUS register; unsupported cards will execute ERASE instead.

Out-of-sequence commands trigger ERASE_SEQ_ERROR or ERASE_RESET status bits and reset the sequence. Out-of-range addresses cause OUT_OF_RANGE errors and sequence resets. DISCARD is supported only on SDHC and SDXC cards, excluding SPI interface. The card signals DISCARD progress by holding DAT0 low, with a 250ms busy timeout per command.

This documentation describes several AGESA™ software procedures:

**Stack Creation Procedure:** A stackless native assembler routine using register passing that initializes the processor and cache system to establish a pre-memory stack region before main memory is available. It divides stack space among processor cores, maps them to global address space, and sets MTRRs (x86-64 only). It preserves the SS register in protected mode and creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance. AARCH64 APUs with PSP do not use this, as the PSP initializes DRAM. Returns AGESA_SUCCESS, AGESA_WARNING (stack re-entry), or AGESA_FATAL (unknown processor family).

**Stack Removal Procedure:** A stackless routine that returns the processor and cache to a non-stack state, executed once when main memory becomes available. It disables CAR mode, flushes cache, and preserves EBX. Must run on all cores, but invoked only by the BSP.

**AmdCreateStruct:** Allocates storage for AGESA parameter block structures and pre-initializes them with default values. Allocation methods include PreMemHeap (pre-memory, via internal heap), PostMemDram (post-memory), and ByHost (host pre-allocates). Requires a stack and must be paired with AmdReleaseStruct.

**Data Eye Retrieval Procedure:** Returns a data eye bitmap (31 elements × 32 bits) for a specified DIMM by socket and memory channel, for reads or writes, normalized to 1D trained Center[+16, -15]. Requires operational coherent HyperTransport™ links and a stack.

The President opens by invoking the tradition of the inaugural address and pledges to uphold the principles stated during his campaign. He identifies the permanent pacification of the country, particularly the Southern States, as the foremost issue, advocating local self-government that protects the rights of both races and adheres to the Constitution.

He acknowledges the federal government's moral obligation to protect the rights of the 4,000,000 emancipated citizens and calls for cooperation across party and racial lines to restore the South's political stability and material development. He emphasizes that universal suffrage requires universal education, supported by state and, if necessary, national funding, aiming to eliminate the color line and sectional divisions.

The President calls for thorough civil service reform, returning to the founders' principle that public office is not a reward for partisan service, and recommends a constitutional amendment establishing a single six-year presidential term.

On finances, he supports a currency backed by coin and legislation for the early resumption of specie payments. In foreign affairs, he endorses nonintervention and arbitration, following President Grant's example.

Addressing the disputed election, he praises the bipartisan tribunal established to resolve it and celebrates the peaceful, lawful adjustment of the contest as a historic example. He closes by calling for unity, justice, and peace.

Linda Farr, 68, received a 20-month suspended sentence at Stafford Crown Court after admitting gross negligence manslaughter of her 86-year-old mother, Doreen Shufflebotham. Medical experts estimated Shufflebotham had not moved from her chair for 8 to 12 months before dying on September 6, 2016. She suffered a fractured femur, infection, pulmonary embolism, sepsis, deep-vein thrombosis and acute bacterial meningitis. A neighbour reported a fly infestation spreading to her home following the death. Other residents described Farr as reclusive. The suspended sentence prompted outrage on social media from local residents.

In his farewell address in Chicago, President Obama thanked the American people and reflected on his journey, which began as a community organizer in the city. He outlined accomplishments over eight years, including economic recovery, expanded health coverage, marriage equality, the Iran nuclear deal, and counterterrorism efforts.

Obama committed to a peaceful transition to President-elect Trump and focused his speech on the state of American democracy. He identified four threats: economic inequality, racial division, retreat into ideological bubbles that reject shared facts, and taking democracy for granted. He called for a new social compact, anti-discrimination enforcement, empathy across racial and cultural lines, and respect for reason and science, citing climate change as an example.

On foreign policy, he defended American values against extremism and authoritarianism, warning against abandoning constitutional principles out of fear. He urged citizens to strengthen democratic institutions by voting, reducing money in politics, and participating actively in civic life.

Obama thanked Michelle Obama, his daughters, Vice President Biden, his staff, and supporters. He expressed optimism about the younger generation and closed by asking Americans to believe in their own ability to create change, echoing his "Yes, we can" campaign slogan.

Nigel Rothsay, a New Zealand man, was informed by police that he does not legally own the Masterton house he purchased in 2012. The error was discovered in December when police placed a restraining order on his neighbour's property during a methamphetamine investigation, revealing that Rothsay owned the neighbour's house and vice versa. Conveyancing firm First Property Legal denied wrongdoing, attributing the mistake in a February letter to either real estate agent Harcourts or the seller's agent, Public Trust, stating the properties were initially signed over correctly but altered two months later. Rothsay, a builder, said the stress has affected his work. Police acknowledged the situation is taking longer to resolve because multiple parties are involved.

RADAR (Reasoning—Ability and Difficulty-Aware Routing) is a framework for routing queries to optimal reasoning language model (RLM) configurations, balancing performance and cost. It addresses the challenge that always selecting the most expensive RLM is inefficient, as simpler queries can be solved by smaller models with minimal reasoning budgets.

RADAR discretizes RLMs by reasoning budgets and formulates routing as a multi-objective optimization (MOO) problem, using linear or Chebyshev scalarization to target the performance-cost Pareto frontier. It employs a custom Item Response Theory (IRT) 2PL model to jointly estimate interpretable query difficulties and scalar-valued RLM configuration abilities, using frozen query embeddings with linear transformations for low-latency, generalizable predictions. Costs are predicted via a token-based heuristic.

RADAR is lightweight (~7ms latency), treats RLMs as black boxes, and supports plug-and-play integration of new models through adaptive testing on a small query subset. Experiments across benchmarks show superior performance-cost tradeoffs, including matching 90% of OpenAI o4-mini's performance at 1.31% of its cost on MATH-500, with strong out-of-distribution generalization.

Milwaukee has improved its efforts to support African-American boys and young men, according to the Campaign for Black Male Achievement's "Promise of Place" report, which assessed 50 U.S. cities. Milwaukee's score rose from 63 to 71 since 2015, ranking 13th. Contributing factors include the creation of Milwaukee Public Schools' Department of Black and Latino Male Achievement, the MyBlackStory.us website, and the Black Male Achievement Advisory Council. Milwaukee is one of five cities receiving additional CBMA resources due to racial disparities.

However, officials including Ald. Khalif Rainey and MPS director Juan Baez noted that increased engagement has not yet improved graduation rates or reduced crime. MPS four-year graduation rates are 49 percent for African-American males and 57 percent for Latino males. The department has identified five strategies to address disparities, including improving school climate, promoting positive media narratives, expanding manhood academies, and hiring more male teachers of color, as 71 percent of MPS teachers are white.

Forecasters are monitoring an outflow boundary moving slowly southeastward for possible scattered storm development, along with storms forming near Gulf moisture over southeastern Missouri. An MCV to the north and northwest could trigger an organized bow of severe storms, potentially bringing scattered severe gusts to part of the Tri-State, though widespread severe weather is more likely to the northwest. The storm system's longevity is uncertain as it moves from stronger mid-level flow.

Reckitt Benckiser shares are trading at least 15% below their 52-week highs across all markets, with a P/E ratio of 22.79, below both the Household Products industry and S&P 500 averages. Two factors have driven the decline: a South Korean dehumidifier incident causing at least 92 deaths and 530 injuries, and the $17.9 billion acquisition of Mead Johnson, a formula milk company in an unfamiliar sector for the firm.

Despite these concerns, the dehumidifier incident was isolated to one country, and Reckitt Benckiser has strong brand-building expertise across products like Dettol, Durex, Lysol, and Nurofen. Revenue and net income from 2012-2016 show consistent profitability. Though debt rose to a 67.57% debt-to-capital ratio, the $4.2 billion sale of its food business to McCormick eases concerns.

The company is focusing on core health and hygiene products (83% of portfolio) and expanding in developing markets, particularly China via Mead Johnson. Investors can secure a 2.37% dividend yield with a 53% payout ratio. The author concludes current pricing presents a buying opportunity, while noting no personal positions in the stock.

Protesters gathered at Laguna's Main Beach on Feb. 3 for a "Hands Across the Sand" event opposing the Trump administration's proposal to expand offshore oil and gas drilling. The plan would lease 47 coastal areas from 2019 to 2024, including seven in the Pacific Ocean. If enacted, it would mark the first new offshore drilling leases offered in California since 1984. California currently has over 30 offshore platforms off its southern coast, dating to the 1950s.

Baylor NAACP launched a hashtag, #myblackhistory, which features videos of African-American students sharing their perspectives on being black. Press and publicity chair Maryse Bombito created the hashtag to celebrate present-day experiences rather than only historical events. Participant Danielle Sherman emphasized celebrating black culture year-round. The organization also marked the NAACP's 108th founders day with a viewing of "A Raisin in the Sun." President Reginald Singletary expressed pride in the organization's enduring legacy. Baylor NAACP plans to support upcoming events, including the Black Heritage Banquet, the All For One Soiree, and an Asian Student Association fashion show.

The Area Agency on Aging and Preble County Council on Aging are promoting Healthy U, an interactive small-group workshop designed to help people manage chronic diseases. Rather than focusing on a specific illness, the program addresses common challenges such as chronic pain, nutrition, exercise, medication, emotions, and communication with doctors and family. Participants learn coping strategies through action planning, problem-solving, and social support. The six-weekly workshops will be held Tuesdays, March 6 through April 10, from 9:30 a.m. to noon at the Preble County Council on Aging in Eaton. Advance registration is required.

Constable Godknows Dube (36), a police officer stationed at Guyu Police Station and deployed at Gungwe Police Base, was found hanging from a tree at the base on Wednesday morning by a colleague. Dube, who was facing rape charges and due to appear in court on October 26, reportedly used a rope taken from a flag post at Gungwe Primary School, where his girlfriend is a student teacher. He left no suicide note, but sources suspect the pressure from the rape case drove him to end his life. National Police Spokesperson Senior Commissioner Charity Charamba said she had not yet received a report on the incident.

Two insurers disputed priority of coverage after Jill Kearns, an ETS employee, was injured and sued ETS, Essex (the lessor), and Anton (landscaper). The $100,000 settlement was partially paid by Essex ($87,500), with Vigilant (ETS's insurer) and Travelers (Essex's insurer) splitting that cost while reserving rights to sue for contribution. The District Court ruled Vigilant's coverage had priority, making it liable for the full $87,500.

On appeal, Vigilant argued Travelers' policy was ambiguous regarding priority. The court disagreed, finding Endorsement # 0192, titled "OTHER INSURANCE-ADDITIONAL INSUREDS," explicitly subordinated Travelers' policy when the insured is an additional insured under another policy. Since Essex was an additional insured under Vigilant's policy, and no other provisions contradicted this endorsement, the court affirmed the District Court's judgment.

Male cichlids (Pelvicachromis taeniatus) exposed to predator threats grow faster and delay their full breeding coloration to reduce predation risk, according to a University of Bonn study published in The American Naturalist. Researchers raised two groups of fish over two years, regularly adding an extract containing alarm substances from conspecifics to one tank. Males in this group developed larger bodies, bigger eyes, and longer dorsal fin spines, which may help them evade or deter predators. They also displayed duller coloration at the onset of sexual maturity. These differences appeared only in males, likely because they defend territory outside breeding caves while females remain inside caring for eggs. By around one year of age, males from both groups exhibited equally conspicuous coloration, as the ornaments are essential for signaling dominance and attracting mates.

UBS trades at nearly twice the tangible book value of Barclays (1.3 vs 0.7), reflecting investor preference for CEO Sergio Ermotti's focused strategy over Barclays CEO Jes Staley's approach. First-quarter results showed both banks trailed the top five U.S. peers in investment banking, though a fixed income decline hurt Barclays more, as it generates 15 percent of revenue from that segment versus 6 percent at UBS. UBS's wealth management arm posted a 19 percent pre-tax profit increase and attracted 20 billion Swiss francs in net new money, while Barclays' core UK operations were flat. However, excluding a one-off African writedown, Barclays earned a 9 percent return on tangible equity, close to UBS's 10.9 percent. UBS anticipates outflows matching 2016's 14 billion francs, and Deutsche Bank analysts warn sector margins may face pressure. Barclays' valuation discount appears excessive.

Multiple write blocks can be erased simultaneously to improve throughput, identified via ERASE_WR_BLK_START (CMD32) and ERASE_WR_BLK_END (CMD33). The required command sequence is CMD32, CMD33, then ERASE (CMD38); with arguments 00000001h or 00000002h, ERASE may not execute if the card supports DISCARD or FULE.

Out-of-sequence erase or address commands trigger the ERASE_SEQ_ERROR bit and reset the sequence. Other out-of-sequence commands (except SEND_STATUS) set the ERASE_RESET bit, reset the sequence, and execute the last command. Write-protected sectors within the range remain intact, setting WP_ERASE_SKIP. Address fields use byte units, ignoring LSBs below WRITE_BL_LEN. The card signals erase progress by holding DAT0 low, and the host may issue CMD7 to deselect. Post-erase data is '0' or '1' depending on vendor.

Several Moffat County students are graduating through non-traditional educational paths. Casey Copeland is graduating from Monte Vista Online Academy, where he earned National Honor Society and honor roll recognition. Isaiah Harmon, Jessica Johnson, and Macie Schrimsher are graduating from G.O.A.L. Academy; Johnson took art classes at Colorado Northwestern Community College. Colin Jensen is graduating from homeschool and has been accepted to Western State. John Cutler is also graduating from homeschool and received an automotive certificate from Colorado Northwestern Community College. Parents expressed pride in their children's accomplishments.

The speaker comments on a league decision regarding Rome receiving a four-game suspension, which they accept as the league's call. They acknowledge Horton's significant role on the team throughout the season and playoffs, stating he will be missed. The team aimed to win the game for Horton and show support. Regarding the jacket, they explain Horton kept it since he had it previously and wasn't there to pass it on. The speaker expresses comfort playing with Krejci and Lucic if needed, though acknowledges he cannot replace Horton. They also note the arena's heat made conditions chippy, requiring smart puck decisions from both teams.

Winston House, a former Gympie nursing home, has been redeveloped into a dual-purpose facility combining short-term accommodation and medical care. Purchased earlier this year, the project has a budget exceeding $500,000, with two-thirds of the building allocated to medical services and one-third to accommodation. Project manager Richard Hall said funds have been spent upgrading medical facilities and converting rooms into self-contained units. Century 21's Billy Mitchell is managing the 18 new units, which are 95 percent full, with plans to expand to 30 units by December. The accommodation targets workers staying six to 12 months. The medical component's completion date remains unfinalised pending council applications.

Phase 2/3 results compared COVID-19 cases in participants from 7 days after the second dose of BNT162b2 or placebo until 03 December 2020. Two participant groups were assessed: those without prior COVID-19 infection, and those with or without prior infection. BNT162b2 was 95% effective in preventing COVID-19 compared to placebo, with similar results across both groups. Researchers concluded the results were not due to chance, and two 30 µg doses provided protection in participants aged 16 and older.

Moyale Barracks Football Club will host TNM Super League defending champions Be Forward Wanderers in a friendly match on July 6 as part of Independence Day celebrations. Moyale Coach Charles Kamanga expressed honour at participating and said his team is preparing seriously, viewing the match as a strength test before the two sides meet in the league. Wanderers currently sit fourth with 18 points from ten games, while Moyale are tenth with 14 points from twelve games. Silver Strikers lead the table with 26 points, followed by Nyasa Big Bullets and Civil Sporting Club.

The Education Department's Office of Inspector General recommended that the agency resume processing loan forgiveness claims from students defrauded by for-profit colleges, establish timeframes for claim review, and develop controls to meet them. The report noted the processing unit's contracted staff was reduced from 19 to six between November 2016 and September 2017. Education Secretary Betsy DeVos has been criticized for not approving any of over 95,000 pending claims, with critics alleging she favors for-profit colleges. DeVos says she needs time to draft new rules balancing fairness and preventing abuse. The department is reportedly considering partial relief instead of full forgiveness and is rewriting Obama-era rules. Senator Patty Murray urged DeVos to follow the watchdog's recommendations.

President Fillmore's annual message reports that the quadrennial election passed peacefully and the nation enjoys peace and prosperity, while mourning the death of Secretary of State Daniel Webster.

On foreign affairs, he addresses a dispute with Great Britain over fishing rights under the 1818 convention and proposes renegotiation. Tensions with Cuba persist, and he declined a tripartite convention with Britain and France disclaiming designs on Cuba, while stating that annexing Cuba would currently be hazardous. Mexico rejected a Tehuantepec transit treaty, and negotiations continue regarding a Nicaragua ship canal. Treaties were concluded or pursued with Uruguay, Venezuela, and the Argentine Confederation. Peru's sovereignty over the Lobos Islands was acknowledged, and a naval expedition was sent to Japan to seek diplomatic openings.

Domestically, Fillmore recommends reorganizing the State Department, revising tariffs toward specific duties and protective measures, and addressing Indian policy, particularly in California, Oregon, and Texas. He reports Treasury receipts of about $49.7 million and expenditures of $46 million, with continued debt reduction.

He discusses land sales, the Mexican boundary survey, District of Columbia improvements, frontier defense, fortifications, naval reforms including seamen enlistment and Naval Academy reorganization, and reduced postal receipts following lower rates.

Fillmore defends non-intervention in foreign conflicts, warning against filibustering expeditions, and closes by celebrating national progress while urging constitutional preservation.

H. W. Robinson & Co. v. United States, decided December 23, 1946, involved an appeal for reappraisement submitted on a stipulation of counsel. Judge Mollison found the export value, as defined in section 402(d) of the Tariff Act of 1930, to be the proper basis for determining the merchandise's value. Such values were determined to be the appraised values, less additions made by the importer on entry due to the appraiser's advances in similar cases.

Seasonal affective disorder (SAD) is a pattern of recurring depression linked to seasonal change. Winter SAD is most common, while summer SAD accounts for only one-tenth of cases. It affects 1-10% of the global population, particularly those far from the equator, and is more prevalent in women and young adults. Around 10 million Americans are affected.

Though described since ancient times and clinically defined in the 1980s, its cause remains unclear. Many scientists attribute it to reduced sunlight altering serotonin and melatonin levels, though some question whether SAD truly exists.

Winter SAD symptoms include fatigue, oversleeping, cravings, weight gain, and depression, while summer SAD involves insomnia, appetite loss, and anxiety. Untreated, SAD may lead to serious mental health issues. Treatments include light therapy, medication, psychotherapy, and mind-body techniques. Because other conditions mimic SAD, medical consultation is advised. Preventative measures include exercise, outdoor time, balanced diet, socializing, and increased light exposure.

The Big Ten is in discussions about a private capital deal that would infuse at least $2 billion into the league and its 18 schools, according to sources. The plan includes a 10-year extension of the league's grant of rights until 2046, ensuring long-term stability. The proposed structure would create a new commercial entity, tentatively called Big Ten Enterprises, housing revenue streams such as media rights and sponsorships. A private capital company would receive annual distributions proportional to its financial stake, without requiring board seats or decision-making control. Three private capital entities are being considered, and no vote has been taken. Each school would receive an upfront cash payment of at least a nine-figure amount, with larger brands receiving more. The deal, shepherded by commissioner Tony Petitti, aims to better leverage the league's 18 members and counter efforts to form college sports super leagues. A decision is expected in the coming weeks.

The Arms Index (TRIN), created by Richard W. Arms in 1967, is a market sentiment indicator that compares the AD Ratio (increasing vs. decreasing stocks) to AD Volume (increasing vs. decreasing volume) to gauge market strength or weakness.

A reading of 1.0 indicates market balance. Readings below 1.0 are generally bullish, while readings above 1.0 suggest bearish sentiment. Extreme readings above 3.0 may signal oversold conditions and a potential bullish reversal, while readings below 0.50 may indicate overbought conditions.

The AD Volume Line measures market breadth by tracking net volume, helping identify buying or selling pressure and divergences with underlying indices.

Backtests using TRIN data showed that a basic TRIN strategy produced 522 trades with an average gain of 0.39% per trade, which was not tradable on its own. Adding a second trading indicator nearly doubled the average gain to 0.66%, with a 77% win rate and 2.4 profit factor, suggesting TRIN is most effective when combined with other indicators.

Pitt student Trisha Klan, a patient care technician at Jefferson Hospital, will work Christmas from 3 p.m. to 11 p.m., having also worked Thanksgiving overnight. She has observed increased ER visits during the holidays, which co-workers attribute to families seeking to admit elderly relatives, depression-related suicidal ideation among isolated patients, and weather- or alcohol-related car accidents. Sitting with suicidal patients is difficult, but Klan finds hope knowing they are receiving help.

Bethany Peng, a registered nurse at Allegheny General Hospital, will work her first Christmas shift, expecting unpredictability and noting that remaining patients are typically very ill and unable to go home. Nurses often work 12 to 13 hours without breaks. Allegheny General alternates holiday shifts yearly, and nurses receive overtime holiday pay.

Madeline Borsos, a sophomore pre-med student, works as a clinical research assistant at UPMC Presbyterian and UPMC Mercy, primarily in the ER. She noted that hospital units are decorated for the holidays to comfort patients who cannot be home.

This paper proposes PAST (Pilot-and-Adaptive Stable Trading), a framework for resource trading between UAVs and edge servers (ESs) in edge-assisted UAV networks with spatio-temporal dynamism (STD-EUNs). The authors address three challenges: high overhead of online trading, inefficiency of static pre-signed agreements, and the need for adaptive updates under uncertainty.

PAST consists of two modules:
1. **PilotAO**: A futures trading stage using many-to-many stable matching to establish pre-signed pilot agreements with overbooking between UAVs (buyers) and ESs (sellers), based on historical data. It guarantees individual rationality, strong stability, competitive equilibrium, and weak Pareto optimality.
2. **AdaptAO**: A Deep Reinforcement Learning (DDQN-based) module that dynamically updates agreements and overbooking rates in response to UAV mobility, demand fluctuations, and resource variability.

The system models UAV mobility using Markov stochastic processes across Broader Trading Units (BTUs) and Small Trading Units (STUs), incorporating risk analysis for both parties.

Experiments using the Chicago taxi trip dataset compare PAST against five benchmarks (ConSM, ConFM_NoA, ConFM_NoO, GrdM, RandM) across metrics including running time, number of interactions, task completion time, social welfare, resource utilization, and task completion rate. Results show PAST reduces decision overhead while maintaining high social welfare, resource utilization, and adaptability.

Future work includes adding privacy-preserving mechanisms, machine learning for task specification, and extending to heterogeneous multi-UAV, multi-ES networks.

Netflix is raising its subscription prices, with the standard plan increasing from $9.99 to $10.99 per month and the premium plan from $11.99 to $13.99, according to Engadget. New sign-ups will see the updated prices immediately, while current customers will be notified in mid-October. This marks Netflix's first price increase since 2014. Compared to competitors like HBO Now at $15 per month and Hulu Plus at $11.99, Netflix remains relatively affordable.

U.S. per capita meat consumption is projected to hit a record in 2018, but the composition has shifted significantly over five decades. Beef consumption peaked in the 1970s and has declined by about one-third, while chicken consumption has more than doubled and pork has remained steady. This shift reduces environmental impact, as beef production requires seven times more land and greenhouse gas emissions than chicken per gram of protein. The NRDC estimated U.S. diet-related greenhouse gas emissions fell 10 percent from 2005 to 2014, largely due to a 17 percent drop in beef consumption. Factors driving the beef-to-chicken shift include health concerns, more women in the workforce, increased chicken availability, and lower chicken prices. Recent rebounds in beef consumption may reflect post-recession economic conditions. Despite declines, U.S. per capita beef consumption remains four times the world average. Researchers indicate that limiting global warming to 2°C requires further beef consumption reductions in high-consuming countries. WRI plans to release modeling on needed dietary shifts toward plant-based foods by 2050.

Lecture 4 covers empirical work on price discrimination, following a prior theoretical lecture. Empirical work examines whether firms price discriminate, whether pricing matches profit-maximizing models, the magnitude of profit gains, and effects on consumer surplus.

Early papers include Borenstein's analysis of leaded vs. unleaded gasoline pricing and Shepard's study of self- vs. full-serve gasoline, both arguing price differences reflected second-degree discrimination rather than cost differences.

On racial and gender discrimination in car prices, early studies produced conflicting results: Ayres and Siegelman's audit study found large discrimination against women and minorities, while Goldberg found none using survey data, and Graddy found whites paid more at a fish market.

Scott Morton, Zettelmeyer, and Silva-Risso used detailed JD Power transaction data (671,000 purchases) and Autobytel data to re-examine this. They found small discrimination effects (around 1% or less) that shrank further when restricting to cash buyers or trade-in customers, and largely disappeared among Autobytel users, suggesting discrimination reflects differential shopping ability rather than bias.

Shiller used ComScore web browsing data to study Netflix pricing, exploiting known costs to infer demand elasticities without price variation. Using Lasso estimation with 4,600 website variables, he found demographic targeting would increase profits only 0.3%, while web-browsing-based targeting would increase profits 13%, with minimal consumer surplus effects.

Dubé and Misra conducted randomized pricing experiments with ZipRecruiter, finding the firm was underpricing ($99 vs. optimal $327). Personalized pricing would raise profits 8.2% but reduce consumer surplus 25%, decreasing total welfare. A follow-up experiment validated the model's predictions. ZipRecruiter adopted uniform $249 pricing rather than personalization.

Overall findings suggest demographic price discrimination yields small profit gains, while behavioral data enables more substantial discrimination, though often with negative welfare effects.

Research software is increasingly central to modern science, yet research-performing organisations (RPOs) often lack coherent policies to support its development, sustainability, and recognition of its personnel. While data management policies are widespread, equivalent research software policies remain limited, particularly in areas of research assessment reform.

The Policies in Research Organisations for Research Software (PRO4RS) Working Group, a joint ReSA-RDA initiative (2023-2025), examined institutional policies worldwide. It produced a list of existing policies, resources for enabling policy change, analysis of policy gaps, and four institutional case studies. The WG found that although many institutions address software in infrastructure, licensing, or open science policies, few substantively include it in research assessment, despite broader initiatives like DORA, CoARA, and Science Europe advocating for recognition of software outputs. Challenges include the lack of reliable software impact metrics.

Relevant guidelines, frameworks, and examples (e.g., Monash University, Helmholtz Association, OpenAIRE, OPUS) offer operational support where formal policies are absent.

PRO4RS recommends a layered framework: a central research software policy, aligned surrounding policies (open science, IP, hiring), and outer implementation guidelines. Institutions should assess existing policies, sign relevant declarations, highlight their software output volume, advocate for software's research role, and engage stakeholders to integrate software into broader research policies.

Following President Tyler's 1842 recommendation, George Brown was appointed U.S. commissioner to the Sandwich Islands in March 1843. Upon presenting credentials in October, Brown sought equal treatment for U.S. citizens, which the King promised. Tensions arose in 1844 over the John Wiley case, in which an American was denied a jury trial—a right granted to French citizens under an 1839 treaty secured by Laplace and to British citizens under an 1844 treaty. The attorney-general, American lawyer John Ricord, advised against extending this privilege absent a U.S. treaty. Disputes led the King to request Brown's recall, and Anthony Ten Eyck was appointed.

In July 1844, Secretary Calhoun confirmed U.S. recognition of Hawaiian independence. On March 26, 1846, France and Britain signed identical conventions modifying jury and liquor provisions, though without fully recognizing Hawaiian independence. A treaty with Denmark on October 19, 1846, was the first to fully acknowledge Hawaiian independence.

Ten Eyck was instructed to negotiate based on the British treaty but unwisely insisted on the objectionable jury clause despite Buchanan's June 1847 correction. His negotiations failed, and he became embroiled in disputes with the Hawaiian government. Buchanan reprimanded him on August 28, 1848. Ten Eyck resigned in September 1848, and Charles Eames was appointed in January 1849.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, built on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture and TSMC's 7nm process, is an 8th-generation data center GPU designed for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. Powered by the GA100 GPU with 54.2 billion transistors and 108 SMs, the A100 includes 40GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth and a 40MB L2 cache.

Key features include third-generation Tensor Cores supporting new data types (TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, Binary), delivering up to 2.5x the performance of V100, with an additional 2x boost via fine-grained structured sparsity. The new Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) capability allows partitioning a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, benefiting Cloud Service Providers through improved utilization and fault isolation.

Third-generation NVLink doubles per-signal data rates to 50 Gbit/sec and provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth. The A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, hardware JPEG decoding (NVJPG), five NVDEC units, and an Optical Flow Accelerator.

CUDA 11 introduces support for A100 features including Task Graph acceleration, asynchronous copy operations, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, and expanded Cooperative Groups.

The NVIDIA DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs connected via six NVSwitches, delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and supporting up to 56 MIG accelerators for scalable enterprise AI infrastructure.
