The October 2025 U.S. Supreme Court term is expected to be significant, following a summer of activity on the emergency docket in which the court issued several 6-3 rulings favoring Trump administration actions over lower court objections.

Multiple cases will address presidential power. On Nov. 5, the court will consider whether the International Emergency Economic Powers Act authorizes President Trump's tariffs on foreign goods. In December, the court will hear a case concerning Congress's power to limit presidential authority to fire agency heads, potentially overruling a 1935 precedent involving FTC commissioners. The Trump administration has also asked the court to rule on an executive order restricting birthright citizenship, which lower courts have declared unconstitutional under the 14th Amendment.

The court will rehear a Louisiana redistricting case concerning Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, with supplemental briefing on whether creating a second majority-minority district violates the 14th or 15th Amendments. The ruling could affect disparate impact liability across civil rights laws, including Title VII and the Fair Housing Act.

Other cases address social issues, including a challenge to Colorado's ban on conversion therapy (argued Oct. 7) and laws in Idaho and West Virginia prohibiting transgender athletes from competing on teams matching their gender identities. A Fourth Amendment case will examine whether the emergency aid exception requires probable cause for police to enter a home.

The column is written by Erwin Chemerinsky, dean of UC Berkeley School of Law.

The waveguide device includes an optical substrate, light source, light coupler, light extractor, and debanding optic to mitigate banding effects in illuminated pupils, producing substantially flat illumination. Various embodiments achieve spatial non-uniformity below 10-20%.

The debanding optic can take multiple forms: an effective input aperture sized by thickness D and TIR angle U (2D tan U); gratings providing spatial variation of diffraction efficiency, transmission, polarization, or birefringence; stacked or switchable gratings; grating arrays with rolled K-vectors; passive grating layers; refractive index layers (including GRIN media); partially reflecting or polarization-modifying layers; crossed slant gratings with fold grating pupil expanders; microdisplays with variable numerical aperture; tilted microdisplays projecting tilted exit pupils; coupling prisms; or light-absorbing films adjacent to substrate edges.

Color waveguide embodiments stack multiple substrates with input stops containing dichroic portions and phase compensation coatings (e.g., SiO) to mitigate color banding.

The device can be integrated into head-mounted or head-up displays, optionally with eye trackers. Light sources include lasers or LEDs, while couplers include input gratings or prisms. A corresponding method involves producing light, coupling it into the substrate via TIR, and extracting it through a debanding optic to reduce banding in the output illumination.

The center position in football combines mental leadership with physical demands, often compensating for being less naturally gifted than other offensive linemen through high football IQ and grit. Centers direct the offensive line at the line of scrimmage, calling out pass protections, identifying linebackers, and coordinating blocking assignments. Physically, they snap the ball, execute blocks against interior defensive linemen, and occasionally pull as lead blockers or pick up blitzes.

Named for their central position on the line, centers are sometimes called the "quarterbacks of the offensive line." Typical centers stand 6'1"-6'4", weigh 310-325 pounds, and have compact builds. Required skills include football IQ, leadership, agility, strength, run- and pass-blocking, and snapping ability.

Notable centers include Jim Otto (Oakland Raiders, 1960-1974) and Mike Webster (Pittsburgh Steelers, 1974-1990). The center's role is critical for protecting the quarterback and supporting the run game, requiring strong trust and communication with the quarterback for offensive success.

The device's PCIE PHY requires a high-quality, low-jitter AC-coupled differential clock source compliant with PCI Express specifications, with optional LVDS clock exceptions. Optional external clock inputs are available at AUD_CLKIN0/1/2 (max 50MHz) and CLKIN32 (32768 Hz). Two general-purpose clock outputs (CLKOUT0/1) are selectable via the CLKOUT_MUX register. The device contains 12 top-level PLLs and 4 embedded PLLs, referenced mainly from DEV input clock, all starting in Bypass mode after reset. PLL supplies require external filtering, and PLLs must operate within specified frequency limits. SYSCLKs and Module Clocks have maximum frequencies valid for OPP100, with higher limits at OPP120/OPP166.

The ARM Cortex-A8 Interrupt Controller (AINTC) handles up to 128 prioritized requests generating IRQs (FIQs unsupported on General-Purpose devices). The C674x DSP interrupt controller combines up to 128 events into 12 prioritized CPU interrupts, with 24 multiplexed event options.

Timing parameters exclude board routing delays; IBIS models are recommended for analysis, except for DDR2 which uses TI-provided PCB routing rules. Two DCAN interfaces support CAN protocol 2.0 A/B. The EDMA controller supports 64 channels mapped to 512 parameter entries. Debug features include AET, Trace, and IEEE 1149.1 JTAG with an internal TRST pulldown.

The EMAC SW provides a 3-port gigabit switch supporting MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII modes at 10/100/1000 Mbps, conforming to IEEE 802.3-2002, with 3.3-V I/O only. The MDIO module polls 32 addresses to enumerate PHYs. GPIO provides up to 128 configurable 1.8V/3.3V pins across four modules.

The GPMC interfaces glueless to NOR/NAND flash, SRAM, and Pseudo-SRAM with 8/16-bit multiplexed address/data and up to eight chip selects. The ELM supports 4/8/16-bit BCH error location. The HDMI 1.3a transmitter supports up to 1080p with layout requiring 100Ω differential/60Ω single-ended impedance, ESD protection, and specific stackup rules. The HDVPSS provides two display pipelines, HD/SD video encoders, HDMI transmitter, and multiple input/output interfaces. Video DAC outputs support Normal and TVOUT Bypass modes with 75Ω impedance matching.

Four I2C modules support Philips I2C v2.1 at 10-400 Kbps with 7/10-bit addressing and 32-byte FIFO. The Imaging Subsystem includes parallel (CAM) and serial (CSI2) camera interfaces with an ISP supporting lens shading, defect pixel correction, color correction, and 3A data collection.

The DDR2/DDR3 memory controller supports 16/32-bit paths, device capacities from 64Mb to 4Gb, two chip selects, and two independent DDR interfaces. Strict PCB routing rules govern stackup (minimum six layers), placement, keepout regions, bypass capacitors, VREF routing, signal termination, and trace matching for CK, ADDR_CTRL, DQS, and DQ net classes. DDR2 supports up to DDR2-800 x16 devices; DDR3 supports up to DDR3-1600 x8/x16 devices with various mirrored configurations.

High-performance computing (HPC) uses aggregated facilities to process complex calculations in parallel across connected systems. Four out of five surveyed industry decision makers view HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation in discrete manufacturing and process industries for several reasons: it enables completion of highly complex simulations, modeling, and data analysis previously unfeasible; it increases quality and intensity of use by accelerating iterations; it unlocks new usage scenarios previously limited to scientific institutions; and it boosts innovation and agility across value creation departments, enabling new products, services, and business models.

IDC expects HPC environments to replace multicore workstations for many workloads. Over 25% of surveyed enterprises already use professional HPC infrastructures, 39% are planning or piloting deployment, and 15% are not engaging with HPC, citing high investment costs.

The NVIDIA Blackwell GPU architecture introduces developer-created neural shaders, marking an evolution in GPU shading technology. Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing (DLAA) uses AI-based techniques derived from DLSS to improve image quality, temporal stability, and motion detail at native resolution.

Shaders have evolved from fixed-function pipelines through vertex, pixel, geometry, compute, tessellation, mesh, and ray-tracing shaders, culminating in Blackwell's neural shaders. Using the new Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, developed with Microsoft, Tensor Cores can now be accessed by any shader type, enabling neural techniques in graphics applications.

Key neural technologies include:
- **RTX Neural Materials**: Uses AI approximations to render film-quality multi-layered materials in real time.
- **RTX Neural Texture Compression (NTC)**: Compresses textures more efficiently, reducing memory use by over 3x in demos while improving quality; works with Stochastic Texture Filtering (STF).
- **Neural Radiance Cache (NRC)**: Trains neural networks in real-time on path-traced rays to infer multiple light bounces, improving indirect lighting and performance.
- **RTX Skin**: Brings film-style subsurface scattering to real-time ray tracing for translucent materials.
- **RTX Neural Faces**: Uses generative AI to produce more natural-looking faces from rasterized input and 3D pose data, optimized via TensorRT.

The Blackwell family includes multiple GPUs:
- **GB202** (flagship): 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA Cores, powering the GeForce RTX 5090.
- **GB203**: 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA Cores, powering the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti.
- **GB205**: 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA Cores, powering the RTX 5070.

All GPUs feature Blackwell's fourth-generation RT Cores, fifth-generation Tensor Cores, DLSS 4, and SER 2.0 scheduling optimizations.

Matrimonial sites have replaced traditional methods of finding marriage partners, such as consulting priests, relatives, or marriage brokers. These online platforms offer several advantages: they save time and money by eliminating travel and physical exchange of bio-data; provide access to large databases with diverse options; and are easily accessible through user-friendly websites and mobile apps. Many sites offer blogs and live counseling on marriage-related topics. They ensure privacy through anonymous or private profiles, and safety through verified memberships. Users can filter results based on specific criteria like community, profession, or location. Communication is simplified via live text and video chats, and profiles provide detailed, accurate information about potential matches, including marital history and residency status.

Larry Connors' %b strategy, from Chapter 5 of his 2009 book "High Probability Trading," is a mean-reversion strategy based on Bollinger Bands. The %b indicator typically fluctuates between 0 and 1, with values above 1 indicating overbought conditions and below 0 indicating oversold conditions. The strategy buys when the close is above the 200-day moving average and %b is below 0.2 for three consecutive days, exiting when %b closes above 0.8.

Using a 5-day lookback period and two standard deviations, the strategy was tested on 25 ETFs as a portfolio (max five open positions, 20% equity each) from 2000 to December 2020. Results showed 677 trades, a 75% win ratio, 0.76% average gain per trade, 1.9 profit factor, 4.84% CAGR, and 16% max drawdown, with only 17% market exposure. Using a 10-day lookback increased CAGR to 8.2% but drawdown to 24%.

This work presents a coarse-grained rod-sphere model to study the self-assembly of polymer-grafted nanoparticles, particularly those with crystallizing ligands like PiPrOx-grafted silica nanoparticles. The model represents a nanoparticle as a sphere tethered to a rigid rod (made of five beads), with three rod interaction types: lock-and-key, symmetric, and unspecific.

Using molecular dynamics simulations, the authors varied temperature and the sphere-to-rod size ratio (R/r), performing 170 simulations. They classified resulting mesostructures using two parameters: a dimensionality parameter (D), derived from the gyration tensor, and a degree of order parameter (O).

Seven mesostructure classes emerged—bulk assemblies, bilayers, monolayers, fibers, worms, ribbons, stars, and spheres—with dimensionality decreasing as sphere size increased, consistent with surfactant self-assembly theory. Self-assembly proceeded through three stages: aggregation, growth, and consolidation. Ribbons were found to spontaneously twist into double helices due to geometric frustration, with pitch decreasing as sphere radius increased.

The model reproduces experimentally observed structures (fibers, clusters) from PiPrOx-grafted silica nanoparticles and predicts additional mesostructures not yet observed experimentally, offering guidance for designing nanobuilding blocks.

This transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) compared whole blood RNA sequencing data from 194 virally non-detectable people living with HIV (PLWH) on antiretroviral therapy (ART) to 361 HIV-seronegative individuals. The analysis identified 566 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), with 274 up-regulated and 292 down-regulated in PLWH. Enrichment analyses linked these DEGs to immune system processes (cell migration, T cell biology, calcium signaling, PI3K signaling) and cancer-related pathways, including Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/AKT, MAPK/ERK, p53, and TGF-β signaling.

Cell-type deconvolution revealed significant proportion differences by HIV status in five cell types, including elevated CD8+ T cells and follicular helper T cells, and decreased naïve and resting memory CD4+ T cells in PLWH. Approximately 40% of DEGs were classified as ART-affected, with most showing inverse expression changes compared to a pre/post-ART study, suggesting ART partially restores gene regulation toward the uninfected state.

Expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) mapping identified 258 eGenes. Partitioned heritability analysis showed enrichment for inflammatory diseases (Crohn's disease, asthma, rheumatoid arthritis, primary biliary cirrhosis, primary sclerosing cholangitis) but not for cancers or HIV acquisition. Colocalization analyses identified shared genetic signals between some eGenes and immune-related traits, with limited overlap for cancers. Additionally, 111 DEGs were identified as targets of approved drugs or clinical-trial compounds, suggesting potential therapeutic interventions for comorbidities in PLWH.

This study investigated lipid profiles in students with simple dysmood disorder (SDMD) and first-episode SDMD (FE-SDMD) compared to healthy controls, excluding participants with metabolic syndrome (MetS). Of 108 Thai university students recruited, 64 had SDMD (47 with FE-SDMD) and 44 were controls, matched for age, sex, BMI, and education.

Key findings showed that SDMD and FE-SDMD patients had significantly decreased lecithin-cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) activity and elevated free cholesterol and ApoE levels compared to controls. No significant changes were observed in HDLc, ApoA1, reverse cholesterol transport (RCT), or ApoB. Atherogenicity composite scores and Athero/LCAT and Athero/RCT indices were elevated in patients. Psychotropic medications did not significantly affect results.

Subclinical MetS was characterized by lowered HDLc and elevated triglycerides and ApoE, while LCAT and free cholesterol remained unchanged. However, interactions between SDMD and subclinical MetS produced reduced HDLc, ApoA1, and RCT, plus increased ApoB/ApoA1 ratios.

Regression and PLS analyses revealed that LCAT's effects on the depression phenome (including suicidal behaviors) were fully mediated through free cholesterol and brooding. Free cholesterol, brooding, and age explained 62.2% of phenome variance.

The authors conclude that SDMD and FE-SDMD represent pre-proatherogenic states distinct from MDMD, characterized by decreased LCAT and increased free cholesterol and ApoE. These abnormalities may activate neuro-oxidative and neuro-immune pathways. The authors recommend lipid screening (free cholesterol, LCAT, ApoE) for FE-SDMD patients to identify those at risk for recurrent depression, atherogenicity, and MetS, enabling preventive therapy.

The speaker begins his presidency by following the tradition of outlining his guiding principles. He acknowledges that, unlike his predecessors, he was born after the Revolution and cannot claim the same reverence, so he relies on the support of other branches of government, the people, and Providence.

He describes the nation as prosperous, respected abroad, and internally stable. He emphasizes that preserving this condition requires upholding the Constitution, which the framers built on reciprocal concession and compromise, balancing state and federal powers and accommodating diverse regional interests.

Reviewing fifty years of history, he argues that early predictions of the Republic's failure have been disproven. The people have willingly borne taxation and war costs, withstood partisan strife after Washington's death, demonstrated capacity for self-government, shown military resolve when needed, and thrived despite territorial expansion and population growth. Federal-state tensions have been resolved over time.

Regarding slavery, he pledges to oppose any congressional attempt to abolish it in the District of Columbia against slaveholding states' wishes and to resist interference with it in states where it exists. He vows to veto conflicting legislation, believing forbearance on this issue preserves the Union.

He commits to strict constitutional adherence, limiting federal action to national concerns and leaving remaining powers to states and people. In foreign policy, he pledges to cultivate friendships, avoid alliances, pursue equal commerce, maintain neutrality in foreign disputes, and defend national rights.

He closes by praising his predecessor, acknowledging his own limitations, and invoking divine protection for the country.

Over 250 small earthquakes have struck near the California-Mexico border since New Year's Eve, with the largest at magnitude 3.9 beneath Brawley. The swarm occurred in the Brawley Seismic Zone, which connects the San Andreas and Imperial faults. Caltech seismologist Egill Hauksson monitored the swarm for potential triggering of a larger earthquake, though that possibility receded by Sunday night. The Imperial fault previously produced a magnitude-6.5 quake in 1979, which injured 91 and damaged infrastructure, and a magnitude-7.1 quake in 1940 that killed nine. A September swarm in the northern zone previously prompted a USGS warning about increased San Andreas risk. Brawley Mayor Sam Couchman said the earthquakes have unsettled the city's 26,000 residents.

Enron Corp. disclosed on October 22, 2001, that the Securities and Exchange Commission had requested information regarding the company's transactions with partnerships previously run by Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow, specifically LJM Cayman LP and LJM2 Co-Investment LP. Following the announcement, Enron's shares fell more than 20%, closing at $20.65, down $5.40. The SEC inquiry, described as informal, originated from the Fort Worth regional office's enforcement arm.

The disclosure came after Enron's previous week's announcement of a $1.01 billion third-quarter write-off resulting in a $618 million loss, along with a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity tied to unwinding the Fastow-related partnerships and repurchasing 55 million shares. Chairman and CEO Kenneth Lay stated the company would cooperate fully with the SEC.

Analysts raised concerns about Enron's transparency, the valuation of assets in the partnerships, and potential dilution risks from other financing vehicles such as Marlin Water Trust II and Whitewing (Osprey Trust), which could require Enron to issue additional stock if its credit rating falls below investment grade. Moody's placed Enron's debt on review for possible downgrade. Jeffrey Skilling had resigned as president and CEO in mid-August. Multiple shareholder lawsuits, including a class action filed by Milberg Weiss, were initiated against Enron. Janus Capital Corp. was the largest institutional holder of Enron shares as of June 30, 2001.
