Observations of 14 out of 16 dwarf galaxies orbiting the elliptical galaxy Centaurus A, 13 million light-years away, show they move on a common plane, contradicting predictions from the lambda cold dark matter model. That model suggests satellite galaxies should orbit randomly in a spherical cloud. Similar planar orbits have been seen around the Milky Way and Andromeda, but this is the first observation outside the Local Group.

Study author Marcel Pawlowski suggests scientists may need to consider alternative models or revise existing ones. However, other astrophysicists, such as Mike Boylan-Kolchin, argue the standard model should not be abandoned, proposing the observations may be a statistical fluke or explainable by large-scale dark matter filaments. Researchers agree further observations of distant galaxies are needed.

Offensive corner kicks are planned restarts involving a set play, designated target, and proper service by a corner taker. The main types, classified by target area, include:

- **Far Post Corner**: Directed outside the Goal Area but inside the Penalty Area, aimed at the team's best header, using a lofted instep drive that may swing in or out.
- **Near Post Corner**: A waist-high, straight ball sent two yards inside the near post, allowing the receiver to volley, head on goal, or redirect.
- **Medium Corner**: Lofted kicks aimed at points in front of the goal (6, 12, or 18 yards) to challenge central defenders or the goalkeeper.
- **Top-of-the-Arc Corner**: A driven ball to the edge of the Penalty Area, exploiting undefended space.
- **Short Corner**: A pass to a nearby teammate to draw defenders out before crossing.
- **Skip Header Corner**: A flat ball flicked on by a near-post teammate toward the back post.
- **Direct Score (Olympico) Corner**: A bending kick intended to enter the goal directly.

Coaches should select kickers based on accuracy and distance, and targets based on heading ability and aggressiveness. Training should progress from no defenders to game-like conditions. Additional considerations include wind, goalkeeper ability, rules preventing the kicker from touching the ball twice, timing runs, and preparing for defensive clearances or counterattacks.

Researchers developed and validated a Fluorescent Immuno-Lectin Assay (FILA) using five lectins (MGL, SNA, MAA, PNA, Gal-3) to analyze glycoforms of lubricin, a heavily O-glycosylated protein involved in joint lubrication, in plasma and synovial fluid (SF) of osteoarthritis (OA) patients and controls. The FILA assay was benchmarked against quantitative SRM mass spectrometry and showed good agreement.

Lubricin concentrations were 1-3 orders of magnitude higher in SF (>100 μg/ml) than plasma (<10 μg/ml). Plasma lubricin displayed higher sialylation and lower Tn-antigen content than SF lubricin, suggesting different tissue origins, with plasma lubricin potentially secreted by the liver.

Comparing 183 OA patients with 41 controls, only SNA-binding glycoforms (6-linked sialic acid) were significantly decreased in OA plasma (p=0.0023). BMI positively correlated with sialylation (MAA, SNA) and complexity (Gal-3) of plasma lubricin, while age negatively correlated with sialylation (MAA, SNA) and positively with Tn-antigen (MGL).

The authors conclude that plasma and SF lubricin have distinct glycosylation profiles, and plasma lubricin glycosylation is altered by age, BMI, and OA, potentially reflecting metabolic syndrome and systemic inflammation.

Streptococcus pneumoniae is a respiratory pathogen primarily transmitted by children, though some vaccine serotypes persist in adults despite pediatric pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) programs. This study investigated pneumococcal carriage and transmission among community-dwelling older adults to evaluate whether adult PCV vaccination could reduce transmission.

Using a longitudinal household design, 121 adults aged 60+ from 61 households were enrolled across the 2020/2021 and 2021/2022 autumn/winter seasons. Saliva samples were collected every two weeks for six visits and tested via qPCR for pneumococcal genes (piaB, lytA, SP2020) and 36 serotypes, with urine samples tested at the final visit.

Overall, 4.8% of samples tested positive for pneumococcus (piaB), with 22.3% of individuals colonized at least once. Carriage rates were consistent across seasons despite COVID-19 restrictions easing. Mean time to acquisition was 358 days, and mean colonization duration was 17.7 days. Only 4.2-6.8% of households had both members carrying pneumococcus, with no clear evidence of adult-adult transmission.

Contact with children strongly influenced carriage, particularly children under 5 (14.8%) and aged 5-10 (14.1%). Daily contact with children increased acquisition risk six-fold. Many published serotyping qPCR assays showed non-specificity due to non-pneumococcal Streptococci.

The authors conclude that adult PCV immunization primarily benefits adults directly exposed to children rather than reducing adult-to-adult transmission. Limitations include a demographically skewed sample and incomplete serotype resolution. More sensitive and specific pneumococcal surveillance methods are needed.

On June 10, 2015, Tesla Motors, Inc. and its subsidiary Tesla Motors Netherlands B.V. entered into an ABL Credit Agreement with Deutsche Bank, Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo and Credit Suisse. The agreement provides a senior secured asset-based revolving credit facility of up to $500.0 million, expandable by an additional $250.0 million subject to conditions, and includes a $100.0 million letter of credit subfacility and a $40.0 million swingline loan subfacility. Proceeds may be used for working capital and general corporate purposes, with the facility terminating on June 10, 2020. Availability is based on borrowing base certifications tied to inventory, accounts receivable, and equipment. Interest accrues at floating rates with a 1.0% margin for LIBOR loans, and an unused commitment fee of 0.25% applies. The Borrowers provided guarantees and security interests in various assets. The agreement contains customary affirmative covenants, restrictions on dividends, debt, liens, and stock repurchases, and customary events of default.

Michael Barnard argues that politicians will eventually be held accountable for climate change denial. He contends that the 2017 hurricane season and western wildfires will shift voter attitudes, making more people accept climate change as real and serious. Migration from affected areas like southern Florida and Houston will relocate voters outside denial-supporting communities, exposing them to different information sources. Barnard predicts this will reduce Republican popular vote support and disrupt gerrymandered districts. He notes that since 2000, only one Republican presidential term had popular vote support, and while the electoral college is flawed, growing vote shifts will overcome it. He suggests current denialist efforts reflect cognitive dissonance following recent hurricanes, and unless Republicans change their stance, they will eventually lose power.

Europe is launching Sentinel-3B on Wednesday, the seventh satellite in the Copernicus Earth monitoring constellation since April 2014. Operating alongside Sentinel-3A at over 800 kilometres altitude, it will monitor oceans, coastal areas, sea level, pollution, sea ice, rivers, lakes, and wildfires, delivering data within three hours continuously. The 1,250-kilogramme satellite will launch on a Russian Rockot from Plesetsk Cosmodrome at 1757 GMT. Funded by the EU and ESA, Copernicus has a 2008-2020 budget of approximately 7.5 billion euros and provides free data. Brexit creates uncertainty about Britain's future EU-linked participation, though it intends to remain in ESA, where UK companies hold significant contracts.

Crews in Gainesville, Florida began removing the Confederate statue "Old Joe" from outside the Alachua County Administration Building on Monday, returning it to the local United Daughters of the Confederacy chapter that erected it in 1904. The removal had been planned for months, though it was unclear if violent protests in Charlottesville, Virginia hastened the process. Meanwhile, in Tampa, someone splashed red paint and scrawled derogatory comments on a Confederate memorial on private property, according to Hillsborough County sheriff's officials. Hillsborough County commissioners voted on July 19 to remove a separate monument in downtown Tampa and are scheduled to discuss its relocation on Wednesday.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on April 24, 2019. The filing reports that Microsoft issued a press release announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2019, included as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

The Triangle & Two defense uses three players in a triangle zone and two "Chasers" who deny passes to strong shooters. The "Double Stack" offense counters this by positioning both posts at mid-post with shooters behind them, giving shooters space along the baseline and an advantage over stationary defenders.

Key options include:
- **Pop out**: Shooter comes off the post's screen for a jump shot.
- **Curl**: Used when the Chaser trails late over the screen.
- **Fade**: Used when the Chaser cheats over the screen; shooter V-cuts to the corner.
- **Back Cut**: Alternative when the Chaser cheats over.
- **Switch counter**: Screener posts up against the smaller defender.

Additional entries include cross, fake cross, and single/double screen actions. The offense can flow into base screen or side screen continuity options.

Successful implementation requires execution of double screens, base screens, post-ups, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, and timing. Recommended teaching uses the Whole-Part-Whole method with 4-on-4 shell drills and scrimmaging. Game strategies emphasize scouting opponents, varying alignments, and attacking weaker defenders.

The GHCB/VMGEXIT protocol enables communication between SEV-ES/SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors. The guest #VC handler disables preemption/interrupts, sets the GHCB physical address in an MSR, populates required fields, and triggers VMGEXIT. The hypervisor processes the exit based on SW_EXITCODE and resumes the guest. Because SEV-ES guests encrypt memory by default, guests must determine the encryption bit position (via CPUID function 0x8000_001f) before establishing the GHCB.

The SEV-SNP Secrets Page includes a 96-byte Guest Reserved Area (offsets 0x00a0–0x00ff) for communicating VMPL message sequence numbers and AP jump table addresses between operating environments. An EFI configuration table GUID communicates secrets and CPUID pages to the OS.

Non-Automatic Exits (NAE) generate a #VC exception; the guest populates the GHCB, invokes VMGEXIT, and inspects results. The VALID_BITMAP tracks valid fields. Supported NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV Doorbell Page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC, and Termination Request.

SMP booting under SEV-ES requires alternate methods since hypervisors cannot modify measured vCPU registers. SEV-SNP allows AP creation via VMSA pages marked with RMPADJUST. An AP jump table enables control transfer between environments (e.g., UEFI to OS). SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported. Debug register virtualization is supported on capable hardware.

Restricted Injection uses a #HV doorbell page with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields to deliver interrupts and non-maskable events while preserving APIC semantics. Guests must atomically exchange values when acknowledging interrupts and validate vectors against expected interrupts, as non-cooperative hosts can cause denial of service but not state corruption.

The AEGEAN study randomized 1162 subjects with atrial fibrillation to either Primary Standard of Care (SOC) (n=583) or an Additional Educational Program (n=579) group to evaluate apixaban adherence. At 24 weeks, 1054 subjects completed the visit, with 108 (9.3%) discontinuing, primarily due to withdrawal of consent, adverse events (AEs), serious AEs, and death. In Part 2, 524 subjects were further randomized to Secondary SOC (n=263) or Continued Additional Educational Program (n=261) groups, with 1003 completing the 48-week visit.

Baseline characteristics were comparable across groups. Median age was 74 years, 59.9% were male, and 96.4% had atrial fibrillation. Mean CHADS2 score was 2.1, and 63.8% were VKA-naïve.

For the primary efficacy endpoint, mean adherence at 24 weeks was 91.64% (Primary SOC) versus 91.88% (Additional Educational Program), with no significant difference (p=0.8117). Adherence declined significantly between Week 12-24 versus first dose to Week 12 in both groups. At 48 weeks, adherence was similar across all three groups (~87-88%). Persistence was also comparable between groups at both 24 and 48 weeks.

Predictors of non-adherence included lower MMSE scores, alcohol consumption, permanent atrial fibrillation, and certain occupational categories in the Primary SOC group.

Safety outcomes were similar across groups. Before Week 24, AEs occurred in 51.2% (Primary SOC) and 52.0% (Additional Educational Program), with major bleeding in 0.7% and 1.1%, respectively. A total of 24 deaths were reported, with no pregnancies and no concerning hepatic or renal signals.

The study concluded that apixaban demonstrated high adherence and persistence up to 48 weeks, and the proactive educational program provided no additional benefits.

A phase 2 clinical trial presented at the American Society of Hematology Annual Meeting found that adding the drug Abatacept to standard treatment nearly eliminated severe acute graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) in stem cell transplant patients. In patients receiving mismatched unrelated donor transplants, grade III-IV acute GvHD dropped from 32 percent to 3 percent. Acute GvHD, caused when donor T cells attack the recipient's organs, is the deadliest complication of stem cell transplantation, affecting up to 80 percent of unrelated donor recipients.

Principal investigator Dr. Leslie Kean explored abatacept based on its success in rheumatoid arthritis, where it inhibits T-cell activation. The trial enrolled patients across 18 sites, with 43 patients receiving abatacept alongside a calcineurin inhibitor and methotrexate, compared against national database controls. At one year post-transplant, abatacept patients showed 85 percent overall survival and 79 percent disease-free survival, with no increase in infection or disease relapse. A second cohort of 140 matched-donor patients is expected to report data within six months.

Stoke City defender Geoff Cameron has emphasized the need to end their five-game winless streak when they host Hull City on Saturday. Stoke sit 13th, eight points above relegation, while Hull are 17th. Cameron called it a "must-win game," noting Hull's fight for position. Hull have won three of their last five but have not won away in the league since August.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2015, with 468,762,005 shares of common stock outstanding as of October 14, 2015.

Total net sales reached $25.4 billion in Q3 2015 (up 23% year-over-year) and $71.3 billion for the nine-month period. Net income was $79 million for Q3 2015, compared to a $437 million loss in Q3 2014. Operating cash flow for the trailing twelve months was $9.8 billion, and free cash flow was $5.4 billion.

Beginning Q1 2015, Amazon reorganized reportable segments into North America, International, and AWS. Q3 2015 segment operating income was $528 million (North America), $(56) million (International), and $521 million (AWS). AWS sales grew 78% year-over-year to $2.1 billion.

Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $14.4 billion as of September 30, 2015. Long-term debt face value was $8.3 billion, with an additional $2.0 billion undrawn credit facility. The filing disclosed ongoing legal proceedings, including patent infringement suits, copyright tariff disputes in Europe, and tax matters with the IRS (seeking approximately $1.5 billion in additional federal tax) and the French Tax Administration (€196 million assessment). The European Commission is investigating Luxembourg tax arrangements. Tax contingencies totaled $895 million.

Amazon changed its annual goodwill impairment testing date from October 1 to April 1; no impairment was identified.

President Obama addresses Americans on Syria, describing how peaceful protests against Assad's regime evolved into a civil war killing over 100,000 people. He focuses on the August 21st chemical weapons attack that killed over a thousand people, including children, and presents evidence implicating Assad's regime, including preparation by chemical weapons personnel, rocket launches from regime areas, and positive sarin tests.

Obama argues inaction would embolden Assad, other dictators, and terrorists to use chemical weapons, threatening allies and emboldening Iran. He determined a targeted military strike was in U.S. national security interests but brought the debate to Congress.

Addressing public concerns, he pledges no ground troops, no prolonged campaign, and no regime change, only a limited strike to deter chemical weapons use. He dismisses retaliation fears and argues inaction would strengthen extremists.

Obama notes encouraging diplomatic developments: Russia's willingness to push Assad to surrender chemical weapons, and Assad's admission of possessing them. He has asked Congress to postpone the authorization vote while pursuing diplomacy, sending Secretary Kerry to meet Russian counterparts and working with allies on a U.N. Security Council resolution. Military pressure will be maintained.

He concludes by appealing to both political sides and emphasizing America's role in enforcing international norms against chemical weapons.

President Trump addressed senior military leadership, thanking Secretary Hegseth and General Caine and praising the U.S. military. He highlighted the renaming of the Department of Defense to the Department of War and the renaming of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America, noting both changes faced little resistance.

Trump claimed credit for settling seven wars during his nine months in office, including conflicts between India-Pakistan, Rwanda-Congo, and Azerbaijan-Armenia, with a potential Middle East deal pending Hamas agreement. He stated the Russia-Ukraine war remains unresolved, blaming Biden's Afghanistan withdrawal for enabling Putin's invasion.

He announced over $1 trillion in military spending for 2026, record-high recruitment numbers across all branches, a 3.8% pay raise, development of the F-47 sixth-generation fighter, Golden Dome Missile Defense Shield construction, and expansion of the Navy by 19 ships. He mentioned deploying nuclear submarines near Russia in response to nuclear threats.

Trump emphasized restoring merit-based standards following a Supreme Court decision, and criticized political correctness. He discussed using the military domestically to address crime in cities like Washington D.C., Chicago, and Portland, and to combat drug cartels, citing strikes on Venezuelan boats.

He referenced a B-2 bomber strike on Iranian nuclear facilities, NATO members increasing defense spending to 5% of GDP, and $17 trillion in investment flowing into the U.S. He announced a "Board of Peace" for Gaza, which he will chair, and concluded by praising military heritage and leadership.

On New Year's Eve around 11:00 p.m., a woman named Melissa on Milwaukee's east side experienced an attempted break-in when suspects kicked in her front door while she was home watching TV. Her alarm scared the suspects off, and she overheard them say they had the wrong house. Police told her they had received similar calls on her street that night. The door sustained enough damage to require boarding up, and blood was left behind, suggesting the suspects may have been injured. Melissa plans to upgrade her home security.

Biogen fell $8.05 to $253.37 after its CFO departed for Alexion Pharmaceuticals. H&R Block rose $2.14 to $29.13 on a better-than-expected fourth quarter. Childs Farm Baby Moisturiser, a £3.99 cream made by a small business and sold at Boots and Asda, has been praised online as a treatment for eczema and psoriasis. Laura Gray reported on Facebook that her psoriasis cleared within 24 hours of use. Paige Sweeney shared before-and-after images of her three-year-old daughter Evie-Rae, whose eczema improved within days after other treatments had failed; her post was shared over 40,000 times. Joanne, mother of one-year-old Kelisha, said the cream cleared her daughter's severe eczema after four weeks of use. Dermatologist Dr Jennifer Crawley noted that regular moisturising is crucial for managing eczema, as it soothes and hydrates dry, cracked skin.

This study examined whether the 2021 CKD-EPI equation, which removed the race adjustment, reduced diagnostic disparities for chronic kidney disease (CKD) between Black and non-Black patients compared to the 2009 equation. Using Truveta electronic health record data from over 8 million adult patients with serum creatinine lab results between January 2016 and September 2023, researchers calculated GFR using both equations and assessed discordance in CKD staging and timing of diagnosis.

Of the patients analyzed, 15.3% met criteria for CKD stages 3a–5. The 2021 equation identified CKD earlier in 24% of Black patients versus 0.7% of non-Black patients. Significant discordance in staging was observed, particularly for Black patients in earlier disease stages; nearly 50% of Black patients staged as 3a by the 2021 equation did not meet CKD criteria under the 2009 equation. Multivariate logistic regression found Black patients were 126 times more likely to experience an increased CKD stage under the 2021 equation. Included social determinants of health factors were not significantly associated with staging differences.

The authors conclude the 2021 equation enables earlier CKD identification for Black patients, potentially improving treatment access, though limitations include reliance on EHR data and use of unvalidated comorbidity weighting. Further evaluation of race removal from GFR estimation is warranted.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on April 28, 2021, reporting under Item 2.02 that it had issued a press release regarding its financial results for the second fiscal quarter ended March 27, 2021. The press release was attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing lists Apple's registered securities, including common stock traded on Nasdaq under the symbol AAPL and various notes due between 2022 and 2042. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The speaker reflects on reaching a decisive final game, stating home ice advantage is not a major factor and emphasizing the team's ability to bounce back throughout the year. He stresses focusing on the upcoming game rather than previous series, noting his team earned their playoff spot. He describes the mental exhaustion players face and the importance of rest. He expresses surprise at his team's uncharacteristic penalties, attributing them to frustration from opponents' on-ice provocations. Regarding a player's status, he says questions will be answered after rest. He considers the growing hatred between teams a normal byproduct of long series that fuels good competition.

Legal experts Shane Kilcommins and Eimear Spain from the University of Limerick have criticised the Government's draft Communications (Retention of Data) Bill 2017, which responds to the Murray Report. While the bill requires district court authorisation for state agency requests for communication data, it omits two key Murray recommendations: specific protections for journalists' sources, including High Court authorisation for such requests, and an independent, resourced body to monitor service providers. Kilcommins noted that journalistic sources are a recognised category of privileged communication under European and Irish law. Spain also criticised the bill's retention of retrospective High Court reviews, previously described by the Irish Human Rights and Equality Commission as "light touch, and not human rights compliant," though she acknowledged the bill expands requirements for prior judicial authorisation.

New oral GLP-1 drugs, including orforglipron from Eli Lilly, could expand weight loss treatment options. Unlike current GLP-1 injections, which require refrigeration and needles, pills would not. Recent clinical trials indicate that orforglipron and another oral drug aid weight loss in people with obesity.

Deanna Conley, 77, of Florissant, suffered nearly 40 years of chronic back pain despite x-rays, scans, and five spinal fusion surgeries, leaving her isolated and reliant on a walker or wheelchair. Dr. Michael Bottros at the Washington University Pain Management Center recommended a spinal cord stimulator implant, in which insulated wire leads placed in the epidural space pulse electrodes to block pain signals to the brain. After a one-week trial, patients can receive a permanent implant with a battery placed under the skin near the buttocks, rechargeable via a pad and adjustable with a wireless controller. Conley reported dramatic improvement, calling it a miracle. Dr. Bottros said the epidural space is a relatively low-risk "safe zone," and of the 40 to 50 patients he has implanted in the past year, nearly all have seen remarkable results. Data suggests effectiveness continues at five years, with longer-term outcomes still being studied.

Rory McKelvie, a 19-year-old from Biggar, Lanarkshire, has been found dead at an address in his hometown, with his death not being treated as suspicious. In the weeks before his death, he shared his mental health struggles on social media, stating that his doctor had told him he "wasn't bad enough yet" for help and to return when closer to breaking point. He also revealed someone had stopped him from committing suicide in November and urged others to talk to friends and family. His mother Sharryn announced his death online, saying he passed away in his sleep. Tributes have been paid by his girlfriend Caitlin Brigham, and Mirror Online has contacted NHS Lanarkshire for comment.

Donald Trump posted a tweet defending his writing abilities that contained misspellings and grammatical errors, including using "poured" instead of "pored" and "bestselling" instead of "best selling." In the tweet, he criticized the "Fake News" media for scrutinizing his tweets and explained he capitalizes words for emphasis. Tony Schwartz, ghostwriter of Trump's book The Art of the Deal, responded that Trump cannot write or even read a book. J.K. Rowling also mocked the tweet. Separately, Trump faced criticism from Annapolis, Maryland's mayor for initially denying a request to lower flags after a newsroom shooting, though he later reversed the decision.

Clinton County was ranked among the "Top 100 Micropolitans" in the U.S. by Site Selection magazine, tying for 64th place. Ohio led all states with 16 Top 100 micropolitans in 2017, followed by Georgia with 14. The magazine's annual ranking evaluates regions based on new investment and job creation, with qualifying projects needing to meet criteria such as creating 20+ jobs, adding 20,000+ square feet of space, or involving $1 million+ in capital investment. Clinton County submitted four projects through the Clinton County Port Authority, representing $70 million in new investment, 150 new jobs, and 400 retained jobs. Submissions were vetted by JobsOhio and Site Selection staff. CCPA Executive Director Dan Evers credited collaboration among local governments, the Dayton Development Coalition, and JobsOhio. A micropolitan is defined by the Census Bureau as an urban cluster with 10,000 to 50,000 residents, with 550 recognized nationwide.

Enron Corp. faces imminent bankruptcy after Dynegy Inc. withdrew from a $9 billion merger and credit agencies downgraded Enron's debt to junk status. The collapse has triggered widespread consequences:

**Trading Suspensions:** Enron has been barred from multiple exchanges, including the Australian wholesale electricity futures market, Nord Pool, UK Power Exchange, and European Energy Exchange. The Amsterdam Power Exchange continues to allow trading pending monitoring.

**European Impact:** Enron Europe entered administration under PricewaterhouseCoopers, with 6,800 employees facing likely job cuts. The company held roughly 20% of Europe's $100 billion electricity-trading market. Potential buyers for assets include Royal Bank of Scotland (Wessex Water), Innogy (Teesside power station and Enron Direct), and HSBC (metals-trading).

**Financial Exposure:** Insurers may absorb over $3 billion in losses. European banks including Abbey National, ABN Amro, and Credit Lyonnais face significant exposure. Most individual utility exposures are under $50 million.

**Dynegy Dispute:** Dynegy plans to acquire Enron's Northern Natural Gas pipeline on December 12 through preferred stock rights tied to a $1.5 billion ChevronTexaco-backed investment. Enron may sue to block the transfer. Fitch kept Dynegy on Rating Watch Negative.

**Investigations:** The SEC promised a swift probe, while federal prosecutors in Texas and New York seek to monitor the investigation for potential criminal charges. The Senate Energy Committee plans hearings.

**Partnership Concerns:** An Enron-affiliated partnership (JEDI) lost $50 million in bankrupt Costilla Energy, a transaction Enron did not fully disclose in SEC filings. Enron used over 30 partnerships to move assets off its books.

**Operations:** The Teesside power station continues operating normally. Enron failed to deliver natural gas to German utilities. Overseas assets in Brazil, India, and Japan remain uncertain.

Arsene Wenger aims to fit all his attacking players—Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang (signed for a record £56million), Henrikh Mkhitaryan, Mesut Ozil (new £350,000-a-week contract), and Alexandre Lacazette—into Arsenal's starting XI, citing attacking football as the club's DNA. Wenger acknowledged the need to improve Arsenal's defensive record and find balance. He defended Ozil's new three-year contract as the cheapest option compared to buying a replacement of similar calibre. Wenger feared the Aubameyang transfer could collapse as Borussia Dortmund awaited a replacement. Lacazette is not guaranteed to start against Everton due to illness, and Wenger will not offer him reassurances about his place.

Edmonton police charged 62-year-old blogger Barry Kent Winters on June 1 with wilfully promoting hatred, a rare charge under the Criminal Code with only three such cases in Alberta over the past six years. Winters' blogs, the Baconfat Chronicles and Baconfat News, contained racist, misogynist, homophobic, and otherwise bigoted content targeting numerous groups and public figures, including Jesse Lipscombe, Wab Kinew, Justin Trudeau, and Rachel Notley. The blogs also harassed the late Rehtaeh Parsons and accused her father, Glen Canning, of molestation. Rather than making direct threats, the posts described violent fantasies. After a 13-month investigation, charges were laid with the consent of Alberta's deputy attorney general, and Winters was ordered to remove the blogs. Constitutional law professor Eric Adams noted the tension between criminalizing offensive speech and preserving free expression. Columnist Paula Simons expresses concern that prosecution may amplify Winters' notoriety, referencing the Jim Keegstra case.

The Strategic National Stockpile is a $7 billion U.S. government repository of medicines and supplies stored in secret warehouses for use during bioterrorism attacks, pandemics, or other public health emergencies. It contains antibiotics, vaccines, antivirals, nerve agent antidotes, and over 1,000 categories of items, with capacity to deploy "12-hour push packages" of 50 tons of materiel to affected regions.

Created in 1999 to address terrorism threats, the stockpile's mission has expanded to include natural disasters and infectious diseases. It has been managed primarily by the CDC, but the Trump administration plans to shift oversight in October to the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response (ASPR), led by Robert Kadlec, to create efficiencies and streamline decision-making.

Critics, including some public health officials and bipartisan members of Congress, worry the change could disrupt relationships with state and local distribution partners, politicize purchasing decisions, and favor expensive specialized drugs over broadly useful medications. Proponents argue it will improve coordination and advocacy for funding. Lawmakers have urged HHS to maintain a central role for the CDC.

The Larisons appealed summary judgment granted to Public Water Supply District #1 of Andrew County in a personal injury action. Mrs. Larison was injured when she stepped backward onto a water meter lid while mowing, causing the lid to slide and her leg to fall into the well. The incident occurred nine days after a Water District operator had read the meter.

The Larisons claimed their action fell within the dangerous condition exception to sovereign immunity under Section 537.600, alleging operator negligence, constructive knowledge by the Water District, and res ipsa loquitur.

The court held that a genuine issue of material fact existed regarding operator negligence, because the operator's credibility about following his routine was a jury question, and circumstantial evidence could support an inference of negligent replacement of the lid. Summary judgment on this claim was reversed.

However, the court affirmed summary judgment on the claim that the Water District knew or should have known of the dangerous condition, finding only speculation supported the assertion that a mower caused the lid to loosen.

The court also affirmed dismissal of the res ipsa loquitur claim, holding the Water District did not have exclusive control over the meter lid, which was accessible to tampering between monthly readings.

This Australian study investigated the association between COVID-19 vaccinations and audiovestibular conditions (hearing loss, vertigo, tinnitus) using two methodologies: analysis of spontaneous reports from the SAEFVIC database and a self-controlled case series (SCCS) analysis of general practice data from the POLAR platform, covering January 2021 to March 2023.

The study reviewed 45,350 SAEFVIC reports and 4,940,000 general practice presentations in adults aged 18-65 years. Vertigo was the most frequently reported condition, followed by tinnitus and hearing loss.

Key findings included:
- Increased relative incidence of tinnitus following both adenovirus vector and mRNA vaccines
- Increased relative incidence of vertigo following mRNA vaccines
- No increased incidence of hearing loss following any COVID-19 vaccine
- Higher spontaneous reporting rates following adenovirus vector vaccines compared to mRNA vaccines
- Higher reporting rates after dose 1 than dose 2 for adenovirus vector vaccines
- Higher reporting rates in females in SAEFVIC data, though SCCS showed negligible sex differences

Limitations included potential COVID-19 infection as a confounder, incomplete vaccination records in the POLAR dataset, and inability to stratify SCCS analyses by dose. The authors concluded that healthcare providers should be aware of these potential adverse events to appropriately counsel patients.

This lecture on the Higgs mechanism explains how gauge bosons acquire mass. While gauge invariance is a guiding principle of Lagrangian theory, it forbids explicit mass terms for spin-one gauge fields. This problem is resolved through spontaneous symmetry breaking.

In a toy model using a complex scalar field with a potential where mu squared is less than 0, the vacuum state itself breaks the symmetry, with a minimum at v over square root 2 (v being the vacuum expectation value). Expanding around this minimum produces a mass term for the gauge field proportional to the coupling strength times v, along with a massive scalar field. The Goldstone boson is eliminated via a gauge transformation, described as being "eaten" by the longitudinal polarization of the gauge boson.

Generalizing to the Standard Model's SU(2) × U(1) gauge groups, a complex scalar doublet with four components is introduced. Spontaneous symmetry breaking yields masses for the W+, W−, and Z bosons, proportional to the couplings and vacuum expectation value, while the photon remains massless. The weak mixing angle relates the W and Z masses.

In summary, three Goldstone bosons are absorbed by the W and Z bosons, and one additional scalar—the Higgs boson—remains, which was experimentally discovered in 2012.

Education groups in China address disparities in basic education caused by the "siphon effect," where quality resources and talent concentrate in affluent areas. These groups pair prestigious "core schools" with "ordinary" branch schools, sharing administrators, teachers, and resources.

Benefits include: improved overall educational quality through unified resources and curriculum coordination; enhanced teacher job satisfaction and professional competence via peer exchanges and anchor teacher mentoring; comprehensive student development through shared philosophies, diverse learning modes, and inter-school activities; and reduced public anxiety over "school picking."

However, challenges exist: core school culture may overwrite non-core schools' unique identities; ordinary schools struggle to apply prestigious schools' advanced pedagogies due to ability gaps; and core school leaders face resource strain and evaluation pressures that dampen motivation.

Recommended improvements include establishing equal, democratic relationships among member schools through standing committees; strengthening team building via teacher rotation, incentives, and online resource-sharing platforms; and securing government policy and financial support, including operational funding and rewards for dedicated teachers and principals.

Education groups represent a "deep cooperation" model, though further study is needed to balance collaboration with preserving individual school identity.

Fire Departments across the state are holding education sessions during October for Fire Prevention month, with this year's theme being "Every Second counts – know two ways out." The GHCB (Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block) protocol defines how SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests negotiate and communicate with hypervisors. During negotiation, the hypervisor sets VMCB offset 0x00a0 with protocol version and encryption bit information, which the guest reads to configure page tables and establish the GHCB page as shared.

For VMGEXIT handling, the guest #VC handler disables interrupts, sets GHCB fields, and issues VMGEXIT; the hypervisor processes the exit based on SW_EXITCODE and resumes the guest. Non-Automatic Exits (NAE) trigger #VC exceptions, requiring the guest to set SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, SW_EXITINFO2, and VALID_BITMAP fields.

Specific NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV Doorbell Page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SEV-TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC, and Termination Request.

SMP booting challenges under SEV-ES/SNP are addressed through AP Reset Hold mechanisms or, for SEV-SNP, the AP Creation NAE event using RMPADJUST-marked VMSA pages. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

For SNP Restricted Injection, a doorbell page communicates PendingEvent (vector and non-maskable events) and NoEoiRequired fields, emulating APIC behavior. The guest must atomically exchange these fields when acknowledging interrupts or performing EOIs, while the host schedules #HV delivery for new interrupts or non-maskable events.

The Appellate Court affirmed the judgment convicting defendant of three counts of first-degree robbery. Defendant's claim that the prosecutor discriminated in exercising a peremptory challenge was unpreserved, and the court declined discretionary review.

The officer's initial questioning of defendant, who had brought his wounded brother to the hospital, did not constitute unlawful detention. The suggestion that defendant wait in a family room and the later request to return to the emergency area did not amount to forcible detention. Once another officer arrived with information about a nearby robbery and homicide, police had reasonable suspicion justifying continued detention for a showup identification and questioning.

This study investigated perivascular space (PVS) burden, a component of the brain's glymphatic waste clearance system, across epilepsy subtypes. Researchers analyzed 3T T1-weighted MRI scans from 467 epilepsy patients at Hospital das Clínicas, Unicamp, Brazil, including those with temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis (TLE-HS, n=267), MRI-negative temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE-NEG, n=71), extratemporal focal epilepsy (ETLE, n=65), and idiopathic generalized epilepsy (IGE, n=64), compared with 473 healthy controls. The PINGU deep-learning algorithm segmented PVS in white matter (WM) and basal ganglia (BG), with volume fractions analyzed via general linear models adjusting for age and sex.

All epilepsy subtypes showed significantly enlarged PVS volume fractions in the BG compared to controls (101–140% increase, effect sizes 0.95–1.37, p<1.33x10⁻¹⁵), while WM showed no significant differences. TLE-HS patients displayed PVS asymmetry favoring the contralateral side, particularly in the temporal lobe, unlike other groups. No association was found between PVS measures and illness duration.

The authors discuss possible mechanisms, including impaired glymphatic clearance of excitotoxic substances, seizure-generated byproducts taxing the system, or shared upstream causes such as astrocyte or blood-brain barrier dysfunction. Limitations include the cross-sectional design and age differences between groups. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify whether PVS enlargement precedes or results from seizures.

On June 16, 2016, David M. Shannon, NVIDIA Corporation's Executive Vice President, Chief Administrative Officer and Secretary, announced he will retire at the end of the calendar year. The passage presents a correct-by-construction approach for designing a fault-tolerant voter unit that selects input for a control system from N redundant input units measuring the same physical quantity synchronously.

The voter unit addresses measurement noise, transient faults (e.g., from cosmic radiation), and permanent hardware faults. In each cycle, it selects a prime input unit, produces an output with reliability parameters, and preserves data across cycles to distinguish transient from permanent faults.

The authors formulate a consistent set of functional requirements in three categories: fault identification, isolation of permanently faulty units, and output generation. They establish theoretical limits for soundness and completeness of fault identification, proving their algorithm matches these limits. Key definitions include miscomparison (deviation exceeding 2δ between measurements), a simultaneous fault hypothesis limiting concurrent new faults, and a minimum surviving units assumption.

To prolong operational life, the design avoids misclassifying healthy units as permanently faulty through finer partial fault identification. A risky_count tracks consecutive faulty cycles, with units isolated when it reaches persistence_lmt.

The voter is modeled as a state transition system with five states (S0–S4), capturing normal operation, transient faults, isolation events, unidentifiable conditions (un_id), and invalid states. Output age is bounded by 2*(persistence_lmt−1).

Implementation uses the Rocq theorem prover, leveraging higher-order logics and dependent types to embed proof terms within definitions. Verification takes approximately 23 seconds, and the extracted OCaml code (362 lines) executes one cycle in about 3 milliseconds. Future work includes extensions to hierarchical and asynchronous fault-tolerant systems.

Dr. Thomas Wilson Ikubese, a 2019 presidential aspirant and convener of the YesWeFit Revolution, has joined the Alliance for New Nigeria (ANN) to pursue his presidential ambition. His move followed the Nigerian Intervention Movement's (NIM) adoption of ANN as its party on May 29, 2018. Since YesWeFit is part of NIM, Ikubese aligned with the decision. He is urging other young presidential aspirants to unite under NIM to challenge President Buhari's administration. The Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) Operations Guide describes AMD's optional extensions to SEV and SNP firmware that facilitate page migration between memory tiers of differing performance. TMPM enables software to move frequently accessed data into faster memory while transparently updating IOMMU virtual-to-physical mappings. It requires IOMMU enablement and supports two capabilities unavailable to standard x86 or I/O devices: migrating pages that are concurrent DMA targets, and migrating SNP-protected guest pages.

TMPM provides commands including PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO (for hypervisor-owned pages with concurrent DMA), PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST (for SNP guest pages), and PM_NOOP. A new Pre-Migration RMP state supports SNP guest page migration. Commands may batch up to 128 pages, with best performance achieved at 128 pages per command.

Commands are submitted via a ring buffer interface controlled by a driver, using mailbox registers for communication. System physical addresses must be 4K-aligned (except 8-byte aligned host PTE addresses and 2M-aligned 2M pages). The driver handles initialization, shutdown, pause/resume, and six interrupt sources.

Firmware can be reloaded via a PSP mailbox protocol when operations are paused and the ring buffer is torn down; reload requires equal or greater firmware version. Errors are reported through command status fields, migration list entries, the PM_STATUS register, or Machine Check Architecture, with some hardware errors potentially rendering affected pages unrecoverable.

Doctors in India have emphasized the need for greater awareness about eye cancer, noting that most cases are detected at late stages, complicating treatment. Bikramjit Pal, an Ocular Oncology expert at Sankara Nethralaya, stated that while eye cancer is not very frequent, it can cause blindness or death if not detected early. He highlighted that specialised treatment facilities and trained ocular oncologists are scarce in India, with only 10-11 such specialists nationwide and no dedicated institutes in western and central India. Pal mentioned that Retinoblastoma, the most common eye cancer in children under five, affects one in 20,000 kids and is curable if detected early.

Education encompasses formal, non-formal, informal, and random learning, with digitalization transforming these processes through personalization and online platforms. Since World War II, technological advancements have digitized educational materials, enabling online archives, hybrid education, and intelligent learning environments. The internet facilitated distance and online education, which expanded significantly during the COVID-19 pandemic through synchronous and asynchronous formats.

In design education, digital tools have enhanced creativity, problem-solving, and collaboration. Online informal education, including workshops and courses in computational and parametric design, supplements formal curricula by offering personalized learning opportunities.

This study analyzed two examples of online informal design education: the "Introduction to Computational Design" workshop by Driven by Volumes and the "Sustainability through Computational Design" course by Rethinking the Future. Using a literature review and case study methodology, the research evaluated their structures, methodologies, and outcomes.

Findings indicate that online informal education offers advantages such as short-term applied learning, multidisciplinary engagement, discussion environments, and open access. However, limitations include unequal certification, competitive pressures, resource accessibility issues, and lack of integration into formal education transcripts.

The study concludes that while online informal education fosters personalized learning and collaboration, it also intensifies competition and excludes economically disadvantaged individuals. Integrating informal programs into formal education could enhance personalized learning, though structural differences currently hinder this integration. The research recommends experimental studies with student and professional groups to provide objective quantitative insights into informal design education's impact.

This research develops an integrated environmental education model based on multiple intelligences theory for students in expanded educational opportunity schools in Nakhon Pathom Primary Education District 2, Thailand.

The study was conducted in three phases: investigating environmental education conditions via questionnaires, performing SWOT analysis, and evaluating model effectiveness through action and developmental research. Samples included 364 junior high students, 44 teachers, and three school directors.

Findings revealed community pollution issues primarily from agricultural chemicals affecting soil (48.60%), water (32.70%), and air (35.20%), alongside waste pollution from indiscriminate disposal (49.50%) and cultural problems from technological advancement (40.10%). Students showed the lowest learning levels in environmental awareness (X̄=3.79), participation (X̄=3.90), and skills (X̄=3.96), while teachers demonstrated excellent learning levels (X̄=4.48).

The developed integration model achieved efficiency of 81.51/82.11, exceeding the 80/80 criterion. Content validity (X̄=4.60) and construct validity (X̄=3.97) were high. Post-learning achievement scores (X̄=24.63) significantly exceeded pre-learning scores (X̄=5.90) at the 0.05 level, with students reporting high satisfaction (X̄=3.83).

The researchers recommend promoting environmental education through integrated, holistic teaching approaches connecting classroom theory with real-world problem-solving for sustainable development.

A seven-judge Supreme Court Constitution Bench, headed by CJI T.S. Thakur, ruled that re-promulgation of ordinances constitutes a fraud on the Constitution and subverts democratic legislative processes. The ruling arose from cases involving successive Bihar ordinances appointing school teachers who were not regularised after the ordinances lapsed.

The majority judgment, authored by Justice D.Y. Chandrachud, held that the satisfaction of the President under Article 123 and the Governor under Article 213 is subject to judicial review, and courts may examine whether it constitutes a fraud on power or was motivated by oblique reasons. The power to issue ordinances is legislative and conditional, exercisable only when the legislature is not in session.

The majority deemed it mandatory to lay ordinances before the legislature, enabling it to assess their necessity, validity, and approval. Justice Madan B. Lokur disagreed, while the CJI left the question open. The court also ruled that salaries already paid to the teachers should not be recovered.

A University of Surrey study reports that solar energy has become the world's cheapest power source, costing as little as £0.02 per unit in sunny regions and undercutting coal, gas, and wind. Global installed solar capacity surpassed 1.5 terawatts in 2024, doubling since 2020. An 89% drop in lithium-ion battery prices since 2010 has made solar-plus-storage competitive with gas plants. However, researchers warn that grid congestion, as seen in California and China, poses a challenge. They emphasize that smart grids, AI forecasting, innovations like perovskite cells, and sustained policy support—such as the US Inflation Reduction Act, EU's REPowerEU, and India's Production Linked Incentive scheme—are essential to accelerate the clean energy transition.

The passage contains two documents. The first is an anonymous notice from 1893 by Mr. Kung-i of Pai-ling Shan attacking foreign religions. It claims the Eastern land has long been a Kingdom of propriety, while foreign creeds disguise rebellion as reverence and deception as love. It denounces beliefs in heaven and hell, abandonment of ancestral sacrifice, and "universal love." It accuses religious leaders of insincerity, neglecting parents, immoral marriages, greed, bribing converts with education promises, and using preaching as pretext for sightseeing and book sales. It threatens an attack on the 7th of the third moon if they do not depart.

The second document is a dispatch from Mr. Heard to Mr. Gresham reporting that Confucian followers in Seoul petitioned the King to suppress the Tong Hâk religion for corrupting the people. Concerns that Western religion would also be attacked proved unfounded. His Majesty replied that the Government would handle the matter and urged petitioners to focus on their own studies.

A non-inverting comparator with hysteresis uses a two-resistor network and a voltage reference (VREF). When VIN is below VREF, the output is low and must rise above threshold VIN1 (Equation 4) to switch high. When VIN exceeds VREF, the output is high and must drop below VIN2 (Equation 5) to switch low. Hysteresis is the difference between VIN1 and VIN2 (Equation 6).

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on January 26, 2015, announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2014, via a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing, signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer, specifies that the information is furnished rather than filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act.

The bull market signal strategy identifies the end of a bear market when the S&P 500 closes above its 200-day SMA for 18 consecutive days. Backtested from 1927 to present on the S&P 500, the strategy sells when the index drops 20% from its all-time high and buys upon the signal's trigger. It generated 12 signals, aligning with 12 historical bear markets. On average, the market rose 9.54% six months after and 21.84% one year after each signal. Compared to the Golden Cross strategy, which produced 49 signals in the same period, this strategy avoids false signals, though it is not superior on a risk-adjusted basis. The most recent signal occurred on February 15, 2023.

St. George, Utah welcomed an 11-member delegation from its sister city Ibigawa, Japan, continuing a nearly three-decade tradition of cultural exchange. The delegation, which includes four runners competing in the 41st annual St. George Marathon, was received by Mayor Jon Pike and other officials at a reception, a City Council meeting, and an international luncheon. Top Japanese runners include Kenji Miyazaki and Mitsue Tomita, both ranked among the race's elite entrants. Ibigawa Vice Mayor Sunao Isaji expressed gratitude for the relationship, and Pike announced that St. George will send its own delegation to compete in the Ibigawa Marathon on Nov. 12. During their five-day visit, the delegates will tour local attractions including Dixie Rock, Dixie State University, Tuacahn, and Zion National Park.

Commuters in Delhi-NCR may face difficulty hiring taxis on Tuesday as drivers of Ola and Uber have threatened a one-day strike over low fares. However, the Delhi High Court on Monday restrained two taxi-driver unions from disrupting Ola and Uber services in NCR, with Justice Rajiv Sahai Endlaw issuing a permanent injunction. The Sarvodaya Drivers' Association, claiming to represent 1.25 lakh app-based taxis, demands fare hikes from Rs 6 to Rs 20 per km and abolition of the 25 per cent commission charged by companies. Vice-president Ravi Rathore said a protest march will be held to the CM's residence, and an indefinite strike may follow if demands are ignored. Delhi Autorickshaw Sangh and Delhi Pradesh Taxi Union have declined to participate. A previous strike in February lasted 13 days.

Rain Bird's new 9v WPX battery operated controller is designed for situations where mains powered irrigation controllers are impractical. IP 68 compliant and fully submersible, it is suitable for installation in valve boxes and use in wet or muddy conditions. Models are available for 1, 2, 4, or 6 zones, with programming accessed via an LCD screen. Features include Contractor Rapid Programming™, which copies start times and watering days from the first zone to others, and automatic zone-stacking. The controller operates for approximately one year on a single 9v battery, or up to two years with two.

Brad May was changing lines when Matt moved the puck out to Teemu, who passed to the speaker coming off the bench. The speaker returned the puck to Teemu, drove to the net, and scored on an open net. May became his winger after the line change. The player stated the mood was less emotional than expected, noting the team had a strong second period, stayed disciplined in the third, and secured the goal to finish the game.

A study published in Nature Ecology & Evolution found that birds and mammals adapt to temperature changes 2-3 times faster than reptiles and amphibians. Lead author Jonathan Rolland and colleagues analyzed 300,000 million data points across 11,500 species over 270 million years. Endotherms' ability to regulate body temperature and warm their developing young likely contributes to faster adaptation, allowing them to inhabit colder regions.

However, it remains unclear whether this advantage will help birds and mammals survive current climate change, which is occurring far more rapidly than historical shifts. Rolland notes that pollution, hunting, habitat loss, and invasive species pose greater immediate threats. Species are disappearing up to 10,000 times faster than normal, with 25% of mammals and 12% of birds threatened with extinction. Rolland hopes his research will help link macroevolution with current microevolution to predict future adaptation.

The SNP Run VMPL NAE event lets guests request the hypervisor to run a vCPU at a different VMPL level, with each level requiring a unique VMSA and optionally a GHCB.

SEV-TIO enables guests to bind to trusted devices in their private address space. SNP TIO Guest Request is similar to SNP Guest Request but requires unencrypted data including Guest PCI ID, MMIO range, and TDISP status. Data pages return measurements, certificates, and TDISP attestation reports, and must be guest-contiguous and hypervisor-assigned. The hypervisor validates sufficient pages before proceeding.

Secure AVIC manages guest-owned APIC state for SEV-SNP guests via per-vCPU backing pages. Guests use REGISTER_BACKING_PAGE and UNREGISTER_BACKING_PAGE actions to notify the hypervisor.

The termination request NAE event lets guests request termination with a reason code in SW_EXITINFO1 and details in SW_EXITINFO2. Unsupported NAEs trigger a VMGEXIT with an "Unsupported Event" code.

Guests identify SEV-ES support via CPUID properties. SMP booting under SEV-ES/SNP requires new methods since register values cannot change after measurement. Examples include using the reset vector or predetermined CS/IP locations. Control transfer between environments (e.g., UEFI to OS) uses an AP jump table communicated via SW NAE events or the SEV-SNP Secrets Page. vCPU hotplug is unsupported in SEV-ES.

The SEV-SNP AP Creation feature (VMGEXIT 0x8000_0013) lets guests create/update vCPU state using RMPADJUST-marked VMSA pages, supporting vCPU hotplug.

For NMIs, the hypervisor intercepts #DB (not IRET) and uses "NMI Complete" messages. Hardware debug register virtualization requires "DebugVirtualization" support; otherwise DR7 access is intercepted and cached. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

SNP-isolated guests run with RestrictInjection, limiting host notifications to #HV doorbell exceptions. The doorbell page contains a PendingEvent field (vector, NMI, #MC, NoFurtherSignal) and NoEoiRequired flag, aligned with APIC behavior. The page must be host-owned and accessed with C=0. Configuration uses VMGEXIT 0x8000_0014 with GET, SET, and QUERY actions.

Guests should execute HLT with interrupts disabled; hosts re-enter immediately if events are pending. Hosts emulate APIC interrupt lifecycle, writing vector numbers to PendingEvent and setting NoEoiRequired when possible to avoid explicit EOI exits. Guests atomically exchange PendingEvent to acknowledge interrupts and must validate vectors against non-cooperative hosts. Non-maskable events are dispatched even when interrupts are disabled. EOI is completed by clearing NoEoiRequired or via explicit X2APIC MSR writes.

Kuwait will complete cleaning up a crude oil spill in its southern Gulf waters this week, according to Oil Minister Essam al-Marzouq, as quoted by al-Rai newspaper. Marzouq said no additional oil patches have been found, with remaining efforts focused near the shore. The cause of the spill was not disclosed, though it occurred near Ras al-Zour, where KNPC is constructing a major refinery. The Khafji Joint Operations (KJO), a venture between Kuwait Gulf Oil Co and Saudi Aramco subsidiary AGOC, stated its facilities were unaffected and attributed the spill to an oil tanker per media reports. KJO activated an emergency plan and will conduct an aerial survey. The Khafji and Wafra oilfields have been shut since 2014 and 2015, respectively.

The invention relates to an augmented reality tracking system for image-guided surgery. A first healthcare professional wears a head-mounted device with a display and a tracking device (typically a single camera) that images a patient marker and tool marker to determine their locations and orientations relative to the head-mounted device.

The patient marker includes an array of elements with a unique appearance at each viewing angle, allowing position determination without triangulation. A computer processor generates an augmented reality image combining a virtual tool and virtual patient anatomy overlaid on the patient's body, with acceptable misalignment typically under 2-3 mm.

When the patient marker and tool are both within the first tracking device's line of sight, the image is generated using only data from the first tracking device. When line of sight is lost or obstructed, the processor incorporates data from an additional tracking device, which may be mounted on a second head-mounted device worn by another healthcare professional or disposed in a stationary position (ceiling, wall, or stand).

Several fallback display modes are described, including showing the second professional's view, displaying only the virtual image, or continuing to show a virtual image based on the last known position with updates from the secondary tracker. An inertial measurement unit may supplement tracking when the marker is obscured.

Investors, after a year of ignoring geopolitical and economic risks in favor of strong corporate profits and Trump's tax and regulatory policies, have become nervous. Stocks fell over 2 percent Friday, marking the worst week in two years, triggered by a jobs report suggesting rising wages and potential inflation. The deeper concern is that cheap money from global central banks may end sooner than expected. Since 2009, low interest rates set by central banks encouraged investment in stocks and bonds rather than safe government bonds, aiming to stimulate economic growth and hiring.

Market corrections of 10% or more have occurred roughly once a year since 1900, with the average correction being a 13.5% decline lasting 54 days. Fewer than 20% of corrections escalate into bear markets (drops over 20%). Bear markets have historically averaged a 33% decline, with over one-third exceeding 40%. The 14 U.S. bear markets over the past 70 years lasted an average of about a year. Despite frequent intra-year declines averaging 14.2% from 1980 to 2015, the S&P 500 posted positive annual returns in 27 of those 36 years. Selling during downturns often locks in losses before rebounds. Warren Buffett maintains confidence in America's long-term economic growth, citing population growth and productivity gains. Investors, not the market, determine their financial outcomes through their decisions.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises radiation-hardened current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies including buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. Devices feature primary switching outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) with ~150-mA peak current capability, requiring external gate drivers. The TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP allow programmable dead times (TDSP, TDPS) via resistors on PS and SP pins, while leading edge blank time is programmable on most devices through the LEB pin. Maximum duty cycle is configurable (50%, 75%, or 100%) via the DCL pin, with only TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP supporting 50%. Pulse skipping prevents minimum on-time issues during high-frequency operation. Current sensing and overcurrent protection use the CS_ILIM pin with a 1.05-V threshold triggering hiccup mode, controlled by a capacitor on HICC. The FAULT pin enables external protection, and thermal shutdown activates at 175°C. Slope compensation is programmable via RSC, and Type 2A or 2B frequency compensation can be used. A design example demonstrates a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter with 5-V output, detailing component selection for the transformer, FETs, output filter, compensation, and protection. Layout guidelines emphasize minimizing noise coupling, separating analog and power grounds, and proper placement of bypass and compensation components.

Congress is pursuing moderate reform, rejecting both reactionary and extremist positions, including government ownership of railroads. The government should supervise, not conduct, business to ensure it serves the national interest and provides equality of opportunity. Current laws prohibiting all combinations of capital are flawed; combinations are necessary in modern industry and should be distinguished as beneficial or harmful rather than uniformly banned. Railroad agreements, for example, should be permitted if approved by the Interstate Commerce Commission and made public. The Commission has noted that existing law, as interpreted by the Supreme Court, cannot be fully enforced without harming business, and amendment is recommended.

On taxation, local taxes like those on real estate and state franchises belong to localities and states, while other taxes are best levied federally to prevent evasion. Beyond tariffs and excise taxes, a graduated inheritance tax and, if possible, a graduated income tax should be imposed. The wealthy owe greater obligations to the state, though such taxes must be implemented justly and moderately, treating rich and poor equally.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q with the SEC for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2018, as a large accelerated filer with approximately 4.92 billion shares outstanding as of April 20, 2018.

For Q2 2018, Apple reported net sales of $61.1 billion (up 16% year-over-year) and net income of $13.8 billion, with diluted EPS of $2.73. Six-month net sales were $149.4 billion with net income of $33.9 billion. Gross margin was 38.3% for the quarter. Growth was driven primarily by higher iPhone, Services, and Other Products sales, with all geographic segments showing year-over-year increases.

Total assets were $367.5 billion, with $45.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Long-term debt stood at $101.4 billion, with total term debt of $111.1 billion.

The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, enacted December 22, 2017, lowered Apple's U.S. statutory federal rate from 35% to 21% and imposed a deemed repatriation tax. Apple recorded a $2.6 billion provisional tax charge, including $1.8 billion for deferred tax remeasurement and $800 million for repatriation tax, replacing a $36.1 billion deferred tax liability with a $38.0 billion tax payable.

Apple spent $23.5 billion on share repurchases and $3.2 billion on dividends in Q2 2018. On May 1, 2018, the Board authorized a new $100 billion share repurchase program.

Ongoing matters include the European Commission State Aid Decision (estimated recovery of €13 billion plus €1 billion interest) and VirnetX patent litigation with verdicts totaling $440 million and $503 million, both under appeal.

Two teenagers were arrested and a third remains at large following a police pursuit in Frankston. Around 12.20am, road workers reported a speeding car through roadworks to police via Peninsula Link staff. Somerville Highway Patrol pursued the black Subaru, which had stolen numberplates, until it was abandoned in a Bayswater car park. A 17-year-old girl and 18-year-old man from Mill Park were arrested, with the man hospitalised after a police dog bite. Both are assisting inquiries.

Saudi Arabia Gas Initiative Awards:
Saudi Arabia announced selections of international oil companies for three natural gas core ventures requiring approximately $25 billion in combined investment, marking the kingdom's biggest opening to foreign investment in 25 years. ExxonMobil, Royal Dutch/Shell, BP, and Phillips Petroleum won Core Venture 1 (the $15 billion South Ghawar project). ExxonMobil will lead Core Venture 2 (Red Sea project), with Enron and Occidental Petroleum taking smaller stakes. Shell, TotalFinaElf, and Conoco were awarded Core Venture 3 (Shaybah project). Leaders for Ventures 1 and 3 will be announced by June 5. The U.S. Energy Department welcomed the decision, aligning with the Bush administration's energy plan.

California Power Contracts:
According to a San Jose Mercury News article, California risks losing over 40% of its long-term power contracts after Republicans opposed a $12.5 billion bond deal. Forward power prices in the western U.S. have declined since Governor Davis announced $43 billion in purchases in March, with contract values estimated to have dropped 15%, or $6.5 billion. Companies like Calpine, Dynegy, and Enron benefited from the state's buying. The state reduced electric usage 9% through conservation and economic slowdown.

Options Market:
Options volatility fell further on Expiration Friday, with investors selling options amid expectations of a flat market. Enron's June options were active as an institutional investor bought over 5,000 June 55 calls and sold a similar number of June 50 puts, reflecting bullish sentiment. Enron stock rose $2.02 to $54.24.

FTX, a crypto exchange founded by Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF) and Gary Wang in 2019, collapsed into bankruptcy on November 11, 2022. At its peak in early 2022, FTX was valued at $32 billion and was the second-largest crypto exchange globally. SBF, an MIT graduate and adherent of effective altruism, had previously co-founded the crypto trading firm Alameda Research in 2017.

FTX specialized in crypto derivatives and leveraged products prohibited in the U.S. and operated from the Bahamas. It issued its own token, FTT, which was largely held by FTX and Alameda. In November 2022, a leaked Alameda balance sheet revealed heavy reliance on FTT, prompting Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao to sell his FTT holdings. This triggered a customer run, with $6 billion withdrawn in 72 hours. A Binance rescue deal fell through, and FTX filed for bankruptcy.

Investigations revealed FTX diverted billions in customer funds to Alameda for investments, real estate, and political donations, granted Alameda special privileges, and lacked basic corporate controls. SBF was charged with eight criminal counts and pled not guilty. Executives Caroline Ellison, Gary Wang, and Nishad Singh pled guilty to related charges. Singh admitted writing code enabling the fund diversion and inflating FTX's 2021 revenues.

The collapse raised questions about the roles of investors, auditors (Prager Metis and Armanino), regulators, celebrity endorsers, and employees who failed to prevent or expose the fraud.

Penn State University will no longer allow its nearly century-old Outing Club to organize student-led outdoor trips starting next semester, citing safety concerns. The Nittany Grotto Caving Club and Nittany Divers SCUBA Club have received similar directives. Club leaders said the decision followed a two-month review conducted without consulting them. University spokeswoman Lisa Powers said the activities were rated high risk due to remote environments, poor cell service, and distance from emergency services, and noted the assessment was proactive rather than based on past injuries. Penn State will continue offering a university-operated outdoors program, though club president Richard Waltz said it is more expensive for students. Incoming president Christina Platt acknowledged the university's concerns about litigation following past scandals. Staff are meeting with student leaders about the transition.

Android 8.0 Oreo, released in August, introduces several under-the-hood refinements including Picture-in-Picture (PiP) Mode, Notification Dots, Smart Text Selection, Notification Snoozing, and Autofill Framework. Unlike Nougat's split-screen feature, PiP Mode is implemented at the OS level, though it must be enabled by app developers. Currently supported apps include Google Chrome, Google Duo, Google Play Movies & TV, Google Play Services, Google Maps, WhatsApp, YouTube, and VLC. YouTube's PiP requires a YouTube Red subscription, which is unavailable in countries like India.

To use PiP via Chrome, open YouTube in Desktop mode, play a video in full-screen, then tap the home button to shrink it into a floating window that can be moved, paused, closed, or expanded. If PiP doesn't work, it can be enabled via Settings > Apps & notifications > Advanced > Special app access > Picture-in-picture.

Thomas Henderson sued Alexander Beaton and others in trespass to try title and for partition of an undivided half of a league of land in Navarro County, originally granted to Mastin Latham in 1835. Henderson's claim derived from an 1839 instrument by which Latham conveyed half the league to William F. Henderson in consideration of locating, surveying, and paying government dues on the land, with a provision for equal division. The defendants contended the instrument was an executory contract, unfulfilled and abandoned, and pleaded stale demand and statutes of limitation of three, five, and ten years.

The court held the instrument was an absolute warranty deed, not an executory contract, as its language conveyed title in the present tense and the recited services referred to past, executed consideration, corroborated by William F. Henderson's testimony and the fact that the original grant had been perfected four years earlier. The partition provision was not a condition precedent or subsequent that could defeat the estate; even if treated as a condition subsequent, no entry or election to forfeit had been made by the grantor, and the right could not be assigned to strangers.

Because the deed was executed rather than executory, stale demand did not apply. The five-year limitation failed for lack of evidence of tax payment. The three- and ten-year limitations failed because the occupants held as Latham's tenants, whose possession was adverse to, not under, the chain of title Beaton relied upon (from Latham through Ferguson to Wood's heirs). Naked possession cannot be joined with subsequently acquired title to establish limitations, and privity was not shown for the ten-year bar. The deed from Wood's heirs was also defective regarding the married woman grantor.

The judgment was reversed and the cause remanded.
