The lecture concludes the topic of Markov chains and introduces dynamic programming, an algorithm historically significant in control and operations research from 1960-1990.

The professor reviews eigenvalues and eigenvectors, demonstrating that for a unit chain with block upper diagonal structure, the determinant of (P - λI) equals the product of determinants of transient and recurrent submatrices. Consequently, the eigenvalues of P are the combined eigenvalues of P_t and P_r, and this holds regardless of the transition probabilities from transient to recurrent states. Left eigenvectors of recurrent submatrices extend to eigenvectors of P by prepending zeros.

The concept of rewards (or costs) is introduced, where each state i has an associated reward r_i. The expected aggregate reward over n steps can be calculated using transition probabilities. For ergodic unit chains, rewards approach a steady-state gain per step independent of starting state.

A key application is computing expected first-passage time to a state, achieved by converting the target state into a trapping state with zero reward, producing a solvable linear equation with a unique solution.

The lecture then addresses dynamic programming, where a decision maker chooses among alternatives at each state, each with its own reward and transition probabilities. Using a two-state example, the professor distinguishes stationary policies (optimal for infinite horizons) from dynamic policies (optimal for finite horizons). Bellman's algorithm solves the finite-horizon problem by working backward: solving the one-step problem first, then the two-step problem, etc. The optimal decision at each time depends only on the current state, enabling recursive computation. Bellman's main contribution was formulating the problem correctly; the algorithm itself follows naturally. The next lecture will cover renewal processes.

The application relates to information transmission in communication systems, particularly addressing maximum power exposure (MPE) issues in 5G millimeter wave communication. It provides information sending and reception methods, apparatuses, communication nodes, and storage media.

A first communication node sends report information to a second communication node (e.g., base station), containing first type power parameter information and/or uplink channel state information. The power parameter information may include maximum power reduction (MPR), remaining/accumulated energy values, uplink duty cycle, alert identification, power backoff, or power headroom. The uplink channel state information may include reference signal information, antenna group information, path loss values, or quasi co-location information.

The report enables the base station to determine maximum power reduction and effectively schedule the first communication node to minimize human body exposure while optimizing uplink transmission performance. The power headroom may be real or virtual, with virtual power headroom triggered when P-MPR exceeds thresholds. Reports may be periodic, semi-persistent, or aperiodic, and triggered based on threshold conditions or timer overflow.

The apparatuses include sending, reception, association, scheduling, and configuration modules implemented via processors and storage devices storing executable programs.

The power play is a gap run scheme favored by many offensive line coaches, featuring a backside guard pulling to block a linebacker, a kick-out block, and back blocks to create angles at the point of attack. It can be run from various formations and personnel groups.

Its main strength is concentrating multiple blockers at the point of attack, creating double teams and angles that allow even smaller offensive lines to succeed. Double teams can be vertical (suited for powerful lines) or horizontal (suited for undersized lines).

The primary weakness is backside pursuit and penetration, particularly through the gap left by the pulling guard. This is especially problematic against odd fronts, where the center must make a correct "point call" to identify the first linebacker.

Against a 3-4 odd front, blocking assignments include a tackle-tight end combination block, a center back block, a guard down block, a guard skip-pull to the playside linebacker, and a fullback kick-out. Against a 4-3 even front, assignments are similar but adjusted for the defensive alignment.

Variations include the Diamond Fullhouse, where an F-back arcs to occupy the overhang defender, and the Gun Same-Side Power RPO, which incorporates a tight end one-on-one block and gives the quarterback pre- or post-snap throwing options based on the defense.

Bill Purswell was convicted of unlawfully transporting intoxicating liquor and sentenced to one year in the penitentiary. Officers hiding in a field on McElvain's property observed appellant, a guest at a social gathering, carrying a jug that was found to contain whiskey when he was arrested.

Appellant objected to the officers' testimony, arguing the arrest and search were illegal because officers lacked a warrant. The court held that the right to challenge an illegal search is personal to the owner of the premises, and since the property belonged to McElvain, appellant could not raise this objection. Additionally, the statute permits warrantless arrest when a felony is committed in an officer's presence, and the search was justified by probable cause.

Appellant's general objection to the court's charge was insufficient because the statute requires specific exceptions. 

On rehearing, appellant argued jury misconduct based on his own affidavit claiming the jury considered his failure to testify. The court held this unsupported hearsay averment was insufficient to show misconduct, and since evidence was heard on the motion but not brought forward, it was presumed to justify the trial court's ruling.

The judgment was affirmed and rehearing denied.

Dairylea Cooperative appealed an order denying its application to quash a subpoena duces tecum issued by the New York Attorney-General, which required production of corporate records before a Grand Jury. Dairylea argued the Attorney-General lacked authority to issue the subpoena and that its scope was burdensome. Special Term found merit only in the latter argument and denied the motion after the Attorney-General agreed to limit the subpoena's scope. On appeal, the court first determined an appeal was permissible, rejecting the State's cited precedents as outdated. On the merits, the court found that subdivision 3 of section 63 of the Executive Law authorized the subpoena, as the Commissioner of Agriculture and Markets had made the requisite request. The order was affirmed.

Texas Monthly's November 2001 article "How Enron Blew It" by Mimi Swartz chronicles the rise and decline of the Houston-based energy company. Enron transformed from a struggling pipeline company in 1985 into a trading powerhouse, with stock rising 1,700 percent and revenues growing from $40 billion to $100 billion by 2000. The transformation was largely driven by Jeff Skilling, hired by CEO Ken Lay in 1985, who created the "Gas Bank" concept and shifted Enron toward trading energy commodities rather than producing them.

Skilling built an aggressive corporate culture that recruited elite graduates, offered lavish perks, and rewarded bold risk-taking with uncapped bonuses. The Performance Review Committee, nicknamed "rank and yank," forced out 15 percent of employees yearly. Enron used mark-to-market accounting and front-loaded profits, practices some analysts questioned.

By 2000, Enron was trading commodities ranging from coal to bandwidth and weather. Skilling pushed out rival Rebecca Mark, whose asset-heavy international projects, including a troubled India plant, conflicted with his vision. He became CEO in February 2001.

Problems quickly emerged: the California energy crisis damaged Enron's reputation, the telecom division collapsed with the tech bubble, the Blockbuster deal failed, and analysts questioned accounting practices. Executives sold significant stock, and share prices fell from $80 in January to around $35. Skilling abruptly resigned after six months, citing personal reasons, and Lay returned as CEO, promising reforms.

The South Dakota Board of Regents has directed staff and officials from the state's two largest universities to prepare a plan for closing the jointly operated Capital University Center (CUC) in Pierre. The plan is expected at the board's next meeting on Oct. 3-5 at Dakota State University. The decision emerged from a three-day planning meeting, with regents John Bastian and Kevin Schieffer advocating for decisive action on the matter.

Firefly Aerospace's stock fell nearly 21% after its Alpha Flight 7 rocket exploded during a first-stage test flight at its Briggs, Texas facility. The company stated safety protocols were followed and all personnel were safe, with no impact to other facilities. Firefly debuted on the Nasdaq last month, raising $868 million at a $6.3 billion valuation, but shares have since dropped more than 50%. The company, which makes rockets, space tugs, and lunar landers, competes with firms like SpaceX. Its sixth Alpha rocket failed in April, and the FAA recently cleared Firefly to continue testing Alpha rockets.

The passage describes transmitting devices and methods for radio resource selection and sensing procedures in mobile communication systems, particularly for vehicular (V2X) communication based on 3GPP LTE frameworks.

The background covers LTE architecture, including eNodeB functions, MME, SGW, component carrier structure, carrier aggregation in LTE-Advanced supporting up to 100 MHz bandwidth, MAC/RRC/physical layer protocols, uplink access schemes using SC-FDMA, L1/L2 control signaling via PDCCH, and semi-persistent scheduling (SPS) for predictable traffic like VoIP.

The passage details LTE Device-to-Device (D2D) Proximity Services (ProSe), including direct discovery, layer-2 link establishment over PC5, and two resource allocation modes: Mode 1 (eNB-scheduled) and Mode 2 (UE-autonomous). It describes ProSe identities, network architecture with ProSe functions and application servers.

For V2X services introduced in Release 14, the passage covers V2V, V2P, V2I, and V2N communication types, including Cooperative Awareness Messages (CAMs) transmitted at 1-10 Hz intervals and event-triggered DENM messages.

The disclosure addresses problems with existing sensing mechanisms, including inaccurate energy predictions, increased latency, interference from preemption, and missed sensing opportunities during half-duplex transmissions.

The proposed solution involves a transmitting device performing continuous resource sensing to acquire information about future radio resources. When data arrives for transmission, the device performs autonomous radio resource allocation within a transmission window, distinguishing between primary subframes (where complete sensing information was acquired) and secondary subframes (where sensing was not performed due to the device's own transmissions). Resources in primary subframes are preferred over secondary subframes, with candidates ranked by time delay and energy predictions. Similar procedures apply to scheduling assignment transmissions, with resource reservations indicated in scheduling assignments to inform receiving entities of future reserved resources.

The Arctic is a dynamic, interconnected system where environmental, geopolitical, economic, and sociocultural factors interact, producing cascading effects across domains. Traditional, siloed, and linear educational approaches fail to capture this complexity, risking unintended consequences in security decisions.

Systems thinking offers an alternative framework that emphasizes holistic analysis, recognition of patterns and feedback loops, and identification of leverage points where small interventions yield significant impact. Applied to Arctic security education, it fosters interdisciplinary learning, complex thinking skills, and anticipatory rather than reactive decision-making.

The proposed Systems Thinking Education Model consists of three components: core principles (interdisciplinary, interconnected analysis), leverage points (shifting mental models, improving information flows, adapting governance, behavioral shifts, and technological integration), and learning and assessment strategies (concept mapping, simulations, wargaming, role-playing, interactive case studies, scenario-based problem-solving, reflective analysis, and competency-based metrics).

This framework bridges the gap between theory and operational reality and is well-suited to online graduate education, where asynchronous modules, simulations, and collaborative tools support interdisciplinary, self-directed learning. Adopting systems thinking prepares security professionals to navigate the Arctic's unique legal, environmental, and geopolitical interdependencies and to develop sustainable, adaptive strategies.

Enron Corp.'s shares fell to seven-year lows after Moody's Investors Service downgraded its senior unsecured debt to Baa2, two notches above junk status, with warnings of further potential downgrades to both long-term debt and commercial paper ratings. The company announced it was in talks with banks, including Citigroup and J.P. Morgan Chase, to secure an additional $1-2 billion credit line, following its drawdown of $3.3 billion from existing credit lines the previous week. Analysts characterized the move as a sign of weakness rather than strength.

The stock decline followed disclosures about off-balance-sheet partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, which prompted an SEC inquiry and resulted in $1.2 billion in lost shareholder equity. Enron lost approximately $14 billion in market value over two weeks.

European energy companies began restricting or freezing trading with Enron due to credit concerns. Analysts suggested Enron may need to reconsider its asset-light strategy, as trading gross profits had declined significantly since 1998. At least five shareholder class-action lawsuits were filed, naming Ken Lay, Jeff Skilling, and Fastow as defendants, focusing on the partnership transactions.

Separately, Moody's reported broader U.S. corporate credit quality deterioration, with downgrade reviews outpacing upgrade reviews by a 5.5-to-1 ratio in the third quarter.

The course focuses on cellular materials—porous structures with low solid volume fractions (typically under 30%)—including honeycombs, foams, medical materials like trabecular bone and tissue engineering scaffolds, and natural materials such as wood and bamboo. Instructor Lorna Gibson outlines that the class will cover processing, structure, and modeling of these materials, beginning with honeycombs due to their simple analyzable unit cells, then progressing to foams and applications including energy absorption, sandwich panels, osteoporosis, and cell-scaffold interactions.

Students complete a project in pairs on any cellular materials topic. Past projects have included negative Poisson's ratio honeycombs, elephant skull acoustics, tissue engineering scaffolds, and food foams like bread and meringue. Two reference textbooks are available through the library.

Gibson references Robert Hooke's 1600s observation of cork cells as the foundation of materials science—linking structure to properties. She presents examples including engineering honeycombs (aluminum, paper, ceramic catalytic converters), various foams (polymer, metal, ceramic), trabecular bone showing osteoporotic degradation, tissue engineering scaffolds, and natural structures like wood, cork (with zero Poisson's ratio), parenchyma, sponges, bird skulls, palm stems, bamboo, and animal quills.

The lecture then covers processing methods. Honeycombs are made via expansion (glued stacked sheets pulled apart, yielding walls of thickness t and 2t), corrugation (rolling sheets through shaped wheels, mainly for metals), extrusion (for ceramics), 3D printing, laser sintering, casting, and bio-carbon templating from pyrolyzed wood.

Polymer foams are produced by introducing gas via mechanical stirring, physical blowing agents, or chemical blowing agents, with cell structure determined by rheology and surface tension. Syntactic foams use bonded hollow spheres, and structural foams have integral skins forming sandwich panels.

Metal foams, primarily aluminum, are made through methods including stirring with silicon carbide stabilizers, titanium hydride decomposition in powders or melts, polymer foam replication, vapor deposition (used for nickel), entrapped gas expansion, hollow sphere bonding, and fugitive phase techniques using leachable salts.

Gibson concludes with personal background: she grew up in Niagara Falls, studied civil engineering in Toronto, completed her PhD on cellular solids at Cambridge, briefly worked in Calgary's oil industry, taught at the University of British Columbia, then joined MIT's civil engineering department before transitioning to materials science.

Anecdotal evidence suggests goals in soccer are scored more frequently during certain five-minute segments: the opening five minutes of each half, the five minutes after a goal, penalty kick (saved or missed), or dangerous foul, the five minutes before halftime and at the end of the match (including added time), and the start and near-end of extra time.

These trends are attributed to team and player psychology, including excitement at kickoffs, mental unpreparedness, post-goal overconfidence or complacency, frustration after conceding, and urgency as time runs out. The most significant factor is the let-down following a goal. Coaches are advised to prepare players to avoid overconfidence after scoring and discouragement after conceding, commonly reminding them, "No letdown!"

Municipal bonds are considered a safe asset class and flight-to-quality product. The Federal Reserve reduced short-term interest rates in September, citing slowing job growth and mixed inflation data. Numerous municipalities have received credit upgrades due to improved reserves, reflecting better budgeting or economic and population growth. This quarter may mark a shift in muni credit quality.

Job hunting in an unfamiliar country can be emotionally challenging, but preparation helps. Ivy Chiu of RBC recommends building a network before beginning the search. Suggested tips include: starting the job search online before arriving in Canada; attending free workshops offered by newcomer associations like ACCES Employment in Toronto for resume, skills, and interview support; pursuing internships and volunteer roles to gain experience and explore career paths; verifying whether credentials need updating for the Canadian market; and improving English or French proficiency through language courses, noting that business acumen differs from language skills.

Treetops, built in 1992 near Keynsham town centre, provides accommodation for elderly people with dementia across three family-sized units, each with a lounge and dining room. Residents and families are encouraged to contribute to care planning, supported by a family group. Each resident has a named carer, and activities are organised by an activity therapist and care staff.

Trump's first meeting with Trudeau indicated US trade concerns with Canada are "much less severe" than with Mexico, with only tweaks planned rather than an overhaul. USD/CAD fell to 1.3060 despite a 2% drop in crude prices. The positive trade assessment reduces a key CAD risk, opening the way for a test of 1.3000. A New York Fed survey showed inflation expectations rising to 3% from 2.8%, ahead of Yellen's semi-annual testimony. Upcoming events include Chinese January CPI (forecast to rise to 2.4%) and PPI (forecast 6.5%), plus a Kuroda speech amid speculation he may shift away from yield curve control.

The Supreme Court heard arguments on whether Delaware's procedural requirements limiting medical malpractice litigation should apply in federal court. Justice Elena Kagan strongly opposed the Delaware rules, arguing they contradict the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure's notice pleading system by forcing plaintiffs to prove their case before it begins. Justices Ketanji Brown Jackson and Sonia Sotomayor identified specific conflicts, including requirements for initiating lawsuits and filing answers. Frederick Yarger, representing the defendants, argued federal courts needn't ignore an entire state statute over partial conflicts, but Justice Neil Gorsuch questioned the authority to selectively apply portions of Delaware law. Chief Justice Roberts and Justices Thomas and Alito said little, making the overall outcome uncertain.

CoachingAmericanSoccer.com's American Soccer Player's Creed outlines tactical and behavioral principles for players. Key points include: maintaining constant awareness of the ball and teammates, communicating with coaches and teammates, and self-reporting injuries or concussions. Players should avoid putting down teammates, reacting to opponents' taunts, or committing unnecessary fouls. The creed emphasizes intelligent movement, creating passing opportunities, protecting possession, and giving full effort. Players should not retaliate after fouls, anticipate referee calls, or stop play before the whistle. They should learn from mistakes, play as a team, know the Laws of the Game, and demonstrate fair play and sportsmanship on and off the field.

The DAWN-PLASMA study is a phase 2, randomized, open-label, multicenter clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of convalescent plasma combined with standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adult COVID-19 patients. Participants were randomized 2:1, with the plasma group receiving 800-1000 mL divided into 4 doses, requiring neutralizing antibody titers of at least 1/160. The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15, with secondary endpoints including clinical status, time to improvement, thromboembolism incidence, and safety measures. Key exclusion criteria included prior mechanical ventilation, severe plasma allergy, and recent anti-CD20 therapy. The study followed ICH-GCP guidelines and the Declaration of Helsinki, with IEC approval and informed consent obtained. Six patients were replaced after early withdrawal or screen failure, with no loss to follow-up. The trial statistician remained blinded until database lock.

This study investigates the usability of e-business websites in Saudi Arabia, an emerging online market. Using a cross-sectional survey, two groups of trained student evaluators (26 and 39 participants) assessed eight business websites—four retail and four reservation sites—through a questionnaire covering navigation, design, and content.

Findings from both groups were largely consistent. While most usability aspects received positive ratings, several weaknesses were identified: poor internal page navigation, missing or misleading links, orphan pages, inconsistent Arabic-English language interfaces, inconsistent font sizes, unlabeled icons, simplistic layouts, missing contact information, absent sitemaps, and undisclosed update dates.

The study concludes that Saudi e-business portals need improvements in navigation, design, and content to enhance customer engagement and retention. Recommendations include employing ethnographic studies, participatory design, and user-centered approaches. Limitations include a small sample size, suggesting further qualitative research is needed to measure usability improvements' impact on customer behavior.

The Blair school district's $250,000 transportation bond issue failed Tuesday's election, receiving 58.76 percent approval (111-80) and falling short of the 60 percent super-majority required by state law. The bond would have funded three 72-passenger buses to replace leased ones. Other Southwest Oklahoma elections included municipal races in Altus and Walters, and school board races across Caddo, Comanche, and Cotton counties.

Bank of Canada senior deputy governor Carolyn Wilkins told a parliamentary committee she expects Canada's household debt-to-disposable-income ratio to gradually stabilize, citing slowing credit growth for mortgages and other debt, along with rising labour income. The latest ratio stands at 170.4 per cent, slightly below the previous quarter's record 170.5 per cent. Wilkins noted the debt buildup, ongoing since the early 2000s, included asset purchases that boosted Canadians' net worth. Some experts argue the ratio alone is insufficient and debt composition matters. The Bank of Canada, which has raised rates three times since July, considers household debt a top concern. Governor Stephen Poloz stated high debt has made households 50 per cent more sensitive to interest rate changes.

The speaker emphasizes that scoring requires battling to reach the net and getting pucks into key areas, since opposing teams are limited in what they can do under the rules. Regarding the opposing goalie, he describes him as big, noting he plays back and deep, and says the team needs to get shots and pucks up on him. He also reflects on the two-day break following a disappointing loss, mentioning they practiced yesterday to prepare and are ready to try to score first tonight.

In a May 1980 interview with the Wall Street Journal, Ronald Reagan criticized President Carter's handling of the Iranian hostage situation and expressed concern about Soviet influence in Iran, citing propaganda broadcasts and the Iranian Communist Party. Reagan stated that Iran moving into the Soviet camp would be a serious threat to the Middle East and U.S. security.

On July 17, 1980, Reagan accepted the Republican presidential nomination in Detroit. In his speech, he stressed that ensuring national safety against hostile powers would be his top priority. While affirming America's peaceful nature and reluctance to use force, he argued that war occurs when freedom's defenders are weak, and pledged to restore national strength to preserve peace.

In another address, Reagan praised veterans for supporting military preparedness, asserting that peace is not preserved through weakness and quoting Will Rogers: "I've never seen anyone insult Jack Dempsey."

Effective press breaks require anticipation, analysis of the press type, and exploitation of its weaknesses. Teams should spread the floor, use short crisp passes, maintain a slow-to-quick tempo, and work the ball into the middle before attacking. Advancing the ball relies on teamwork rather than a single point guard, using formations like the 2-1-2 rather than set plays. Key don'ts include receiving with back to basket, dribbling up the sideline, one-handed passes, and bounce passes when inbounding.

Coaches should assign clear player roles, run the press break after every made shot, and use the "Whole-Part-Whole" teaching method with progressive breakdown drills. Practice should occur against strong defense at game speed. Coaching objectives include developing poise, quick ball advancement, attacking outnumbered situations, combating double teams, and flowing into early offense. Scouting opponents and recognizing defensive changes are essential game strategies.

This study investigates coherent control of 15N nuclear spins adjacent to negatively charged boron vacancy (V−B) centers in isotopically enriched hexagonal boron nitride (h10B15N). Using electron-nuclear double resonance (ENDOR), the authors selectively address the four nuclear spin states of the three identical spin-1/2 nitrogen nuclei neighboring the V−B center.

The researchers performed optically detected magnetic resonance measurements at 212 mT, revealing a characteristic four-peak hyperfine structure. Through pulsed ENDOR, they identified three distinct transition energies (α, β, γ), with inequivalence arising from perpendicular hyperfine components (~100 MHz) that induce mixing between electron spin states. Measurements across 169-240 mT enabled accurate determination of hyperfine tensor values (Ax = −61.3 MHz, Ay = −121.6 MHz, Az = −63.7 MHz).

Key findings include:
- Nuclear resonance linewidths as narrow as 1.2 MHz
- Nuclear Rabi frequency enhanced by ~116 times compared to isolated 15N spins, due to hyperfine-induced electron-nuclear state mixing
- Rabi coherence time exceeding 10 μs (approximately two orders of magnitude longer than electron spin T2)
- Unexpected fast nuclear spin depolarization (within 1 μs) under optical pumping, tentatively attributed to the 3E″ excited state

Experiments used h10B15N crystals grown by the atmospheric pressure high temperature method, exfoliated onto coplanar waveguides, and implanted with 2 keV He ions. Measurements were conducted using a home-built confocal microscope with 488 nm excitation under ambient conditions. Numerical simulations solved the Liouville–von Neumann equation using ab initio hyperfine parameters.

The authors conclude that strongly coupled nuclear spins in hBN provide a controllable quantum resource with potential applications in quantum memories, sensing, and integration with van der Waals heterostructures.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court affirmed the Commonwealth Court's decision holding that the Nonpublic Elementary and Secondary Education Act ("Act 109") is constitutional and enforceable as applied to nonsectarian nonpublic schools. The First School, a nonsectarian nonpublic school, had been denied aid under Act 109 by the Department of Education, which argued the Act was wholly invalidated by Lemon v. Kurtzman.

The Court rejected the Department's four contentions. First, it held that Lemon I and Lemon II invalidated Act 109 only as applied to sectarian nonpublic schools, not in its entirety. Second, the Court found Act 109 severable, relying on Pennsylvania's general policy favoring severability, the Act's explicit severability clause, and the fact that the Act's secular legislative purpose of enhancing nonpublic education can be effectuated when applied solely to nonsectarian schools. The Court noted it was not bound by the U.S. Supreme Court's severability determinations in Sloan and Meek, as severability of a state statute is a question of state law.

Third, the Court held Act 109 was not impliedly repealed by subsequent legislation (Acts 89, 90, and 195), finding these acts did not cover the Act's entire subject matter and merely provided alternative or additional aid. Finally, the Court held that distinguishing between sectarian and nonsectarian schools does not create excessive government entanglement with religion, comparing the inquiry to tax exemption determinations upheld in Walz v. Tax Commission. Justice Eagen dissented.

Amid Jake Browning's inconsistent play for the Bengals, Andy Dalton has been floated as a potential quarterback option. Writer John Breech listed Dalton, currently with the Panthers through 2026, among five possible targets. Dalton previously started 13 games under Zac Taylor in 2019, giving him familiarity with the offense despite being benched by Taylor that year. Browning has thrown for 506 yards, three touchdowns, and five interceptions in three games filling in for Joe Burrow.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2018, reporting 169,793,685 shares of common stock outstanding as of April 30, 2018. Total revenues were $3.41 billion, up from $2.70 billion year-over-year, while net loss attributable to common stockholders was $709.6 million ($4.19 per share) compared to $330.3 million ($2.04 per share) in Q1 2017. Total assets were $27.27 billion and total liabilities were $21.55 billion as of March 31, 2018.

Tesla operates in two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. On January 1, 2018, the company adopted ASC 606 (new revenue standard) using the modified retrospective method, resulting in a $623.2 million decrease to beginning accumulated deficit. Under the new standard, most vehicle sales with resale value guarantees are now recognized upon delivery as sales with a right of return, rather than as operating leases.

Key debt activities included issuing $546.1 million in Automotive Asset-backed Notes (Series 2018-A), repaying $453.6 million under Warehouse Agreements, and converting $5.2 million of 2018 Notes. Total debt was $10.47 billion.

In March 2018, stockholders approved the 2018 CEO Performance Award granting Elon Musk 20,264,042 stock options vesting in 12 tranches based on market capitalization milestones (starting at $100 billion) and operational milestones tied to revenue or Adjusted EBITDA targets. Tesla recorded $6.7 million in related stock-based compensation for the quarter, with $766.2 million unrecognized for probable milestones.

The socket base and cover are made of Liquid Crystal Polymer (LCP) with a 94 V-0 flammability rating. The cover thickness must not exceed 1.17 mm, and flatness must stay below 0.25 mm before and after SMT reflow and testing. A removable overlay facilitates pick-and-place operation without outgassing or residue.

Required markings molded on the cover include "SOCKET 940," lock/unlock directional designators, a triangular A01 orientation symbol, the supplier's UL symbol, and a lot traceability number.

Contacts use high-strength copper alloy plated with minimum 1.27-µm nickel, with mating areas additionally plated with 0.76-µm gold. Tin/lead (63/37) solder balls of 0.76 mm diameter attach the socket to 0.64 mm PCB pads, with 0.20 mm co-planarity required. A solder barrier prevents wicking.

A stainless steel actuation lever enables toolless operation. Insertion/extraction forces must not exceed 2 kgf when open; extraction force must be at least 0.013 kgf per pin when closed. Lever actuation force must be under 3.6 kgf, and pin displacement during actuation under 1.0 mm. The socket must withstand 50 actuation cycles.

Visual inspection requirements prohibit missing/damaged solder balls, contacts, plating, cover, base, latch, or lever.

Electrical specifications: 1.5 A current rating per contact with under 30°C temperature rise; initial and final LLCR must not exceed 25 mΩ per contact with Kovar pins; partial self-inductance under 4 nH; loop inductance 3 nH ±10%; capacitance under 1 pF; differential impedance 100 Ω ±10%; propagation delay skew under 10 ps (plus 3 ps error); dielectric withstanding voltage minimum 650 Vac; insulation resistance minimum 1000 MΩ.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2016. As of July 29, 2016, there were 148,692,605 shares of common stock outstanding. The company designs, manufactures, and sells electric vehicles and energy products, operating through subsidiaries in North America, Europe, and Asia.

In May 2016, Tesla completed a public offering of 7,915,004 common shares, raising approximately $1.7 billion. On July 31, 2016, Tesla entered a definitive agreement to acquire SolarCity Corporation, with each SolarCity share to be converted into 0.110 shares of Tesla common stock, subject to stockholder and regulatory approvals.

Total Q2 2016 revenues were $1.27 billion, up from $955.0 million in Q2 2015, driven by higher vehicle deliveries including Model X. Gross margin decreased to 21.6% from 22.3%. Net loss was $293.2 million ($2.09 per share) versus $184.2 million in Q2 2015. Six-month net loss was $575.5 million. Total assets grew to $11.87 billion from $8.07 billion at year-end 2015, with cash and equivalents at $3.25 billion.

Tesla produced 18,345 vehicles in Q2 2016 and targets approximately 50,000 deliveries in the second half of 2016, with Model 3 volume production planned for late 2017 and a 500,000-vehicle annual production target by 2018. Planned 2016 capital expenditures are approximately $2.25 billion, supporting Model 3 tooling, Gigafactory cell production, and retail/service expansion. Operating expenses are expected to grow about 30% in 2016. Tesla had $678.0 million outstanding under its Credit Facility (repaid in July 2016) and received conversion notices on approximately $411 million principal of its 2018 Notes after quarter-end.

The passage contains two distinct parts. The first describes the electronic edition of the Foreign Relations of the United States (FRUS) series, released by the Office of the Historian at the U.S. Department of State in May 2018. The ebook offers portability, full-text search, and offline access while maintaining fidelity to printed editions, recommending document numbers over page numbers for citations.

The President recommends prohibiting corporations from contributing to campaign expenses and granting the Government the right of appeal in criminal cases on questions of law. He cites conflicting court rulings on rebate conspiracy indictments and a decision leaving railway employees without remedy, arguing that without appeal rights, the Government cannot effectively pursue justice against wealthy wrongdoers or challenge a single district judge's constitutional rulings.

The ADS868xW device uses two separate power supplies: AVDD for internal circuits and DVDD for the digital interface, each independently configurable within the permissible range.

Power supply decoupling requires 10µF and 1µF capacitors on AVDD, with the 1µF placed close to supply pins, and a 10µF capacitor near DVDD. Proper decoupling improves the power-supply rejection ratio (PSRR).

The device offers two low-power modes for reduced consumption at lower throughput rates:
- NAP mode: Entered by unlocking RST_PWRCTL_REG (writing 69h to address 05h), setting the NAP_EN bit, and holding CONVST/CS high. A falling CONVST/CS edge exits NAP mode, with a tNAP_WKUP wait before new conversions.
- Power-Down (PD) mode: Entered by unlocking the register and setting the PWRDN bit. Analog blocks power down while the interface and register contents remain active. Clearing PWRDN exits PD mode, requiring a tPWRUP wait.

PCB layout recommendations include separating analog and digital sections, using X7R ceramic bypass capacitors near AVDD and DVDD pins, decoupling REFCAP with 1μF and 10μF capacitors (ESR under 0.2Ω), and decoupling REFIO with a minimum 4.7μF capacitor when using the internal reference.

After a 38–10 loss to Clemson, North Carolina coach Bill Belichick accepted responsibility for mistakes, citing early big plays, three illegal formation penalties, and a secondary that allowed 399 passing yards. Quarterback Max Johnson went 26-for-42 for 213 yards with no touchdowns, and UNC converted just 2-of-11 third downs. Belichick declined to assess the program's rebuild but praised his team's effort and vowed to keep improving.

Russia denies involvement in the poisoning of former spy Sergei Skripal and his daughter Yulia, with Putin calling accusations "nonsense" and claiming Russia destroyed its chemical weapons in 1992. However, UK Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson stated there is evidence Russia has been producing and stockpiling the nerve agent Novichok over the past decade, and investigating its use for assassinations. Russia's EU ambassador suggested Britain's Porton Down facility could be responsible. The passage argues the West should respond with stronger sanctions targeting assets held by Putin's associates abroad, noting that Trump signed a law last fall to identify hidden assets, though further legal changes may be needed in the UK and US to close money-laundering loopholes.

The passage investigates the braiding of topological edge state pairs protected by two symmetries—time-independent inversion symmetry and time-dependent interchain symmetry—in coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chains.

In a double-coupled SSH chain system, the authors demonstrate a twisted energy spectrum and braiding structure of edge state pairs, arising from the swapping property of the time-dependent interchain symmetry operator's eigenvalues. They achieve symmetry-protected adiabatic evolution, enabling high-fidelity, ratio-tunable topological transport of particles from one chain end to both ends of another chain, controlled by an accumulated dynamical phase.

Extending to a triple-coupled SSH chain, the authors realize non-Abelian braiding of three pairs of edge states. They demonstrate two key signatures of non-Abelian behavior: operation-sequence-dependent topological transport and non-Abelian Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference. The latter generates spatially entangled two-particle NOON states, with the recipient chain determined by the braiding sequence.

The authors note that unlike time-independent symmetries, adiabatic evolution protected by time-dependent symmetry requires sufficiently long (but finite) evolution times. They suggest adiabatically modulated photonic waveguide arrays as a feasible experimental platform for testing the protocol.

Speedy, a leading hire services company that floated on the stock market in 1999, has been led by chief executive Russell Down since summer 2015. Down joined as group finance director but was promoted three months later following a profit warning. He inherited operational challenges including unreliable IT data, a loss of focus on smaller customers, and equipment availability issues caused by relocating testing from local depots to regional super stores, leaving over 50% of products unavailable by September 2015.

Under Down's leadership, profits rose 58.8% to £10.8m in the six months to September, with reduced net debt and improved Return on Capital Employed. He refocused the company on customers, introduced customer surveys (150,000 sent) and reinstated an annual staff survey, which showed rising engagement.

Speedy recently acquired Prolift Access Limited (south west, 770 platforms, 72 staff) and Platform Sales & Hire Limited (Midlands-based, 850 platforms, 64 staff) to expand in the powered access market, anticipating revenue and cost synergies.

Clark County schools are determining how to use funds from Nevada's new weighted funding formula, which allocates $1,200 per student for children scoring in the bottom 25 percent on state tests who are learning English or living in poverty, provided their school does not already receive Zoom or Victory funding. Unlike those schoolwide programs, weighted funding targets specific students. Garside Junior High School received over $450,000 for 378 qualifying students. Teacher Kimberly Ivanick suggested expanding after-school tutoring and providing technology. Clark County received over $34 million of the $36 million statewide allocation. Spending will be tracked separately and analyzed for its impact on student achievement.

Bovine mastitis, the dairy industry's most costly disease, damages mammary tissue and is typically treated with antibiotics, which kill bacteria but do not regenerate tissue. Researchers at Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine, led by Gerlinde Van de Walle and Daryl Nydam, published a March 16 paper in Scientific Reports examining secretions from bovine mammary stem cells as an alternative therapy. They are the first to detail what these stem cells secrete. The secreted factors promote blood vessel formation, cell migration, protect epithelial cells from bacterial toxins, and contain antimicrobial peptides. They were more effective against gram-negative bacteria, complementing FDA-approved antimicrobials that target gram-positive bacteria. The researchers plan to test the secretome in cows with mastitis.

Hyundai Motor Co. and Kia Motors Corp. have installed a vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication system along a 14-kilometer road with seven intersections in Hwaseong, south of Seoul, to advance their autonomous driving technology. The system enables real-time information exchange between vehicles, roads, signals, and pedestrians, addressing limitations of onboard sensors in poor weather. Using signal relay stations and CCTVs, the setup follows an agreement with Hwaseong City reached late last year. The carmakers plan to collect data through year-end to refine the system, aiming to make it operational for a government infrastructure project enabling highway vehicle communication in 2020.

A treaty of annexation concluded on February 14, 1893, between U.S. Secretary of State John W. Foster and five commissioners representing the Hawaiian Government is transmitted to the Senate for ratification. The treaty leaves detailed questions arising from annexation to future adjustment by the United States.

The Administration states it previously supported an independent Hawaiian government but asserts the monarchy's overthrow was not promoted by the U.S. Rather, it originated from Queen Liliuokalani's policies, which endangered U.S. and foreign interests. Restoration of the Queen is deemed undesirable or impossible.

Two options are presented: a U.S. protectorate or full annexation. Annexation is chosen as best serving Hawaiian and U.S. interests, including preventing acquisition by other powers. No foreign government has protested, and all foreign representatives in Honolulu recognized the provisional Government.

Prompt Senate action is requested. Existing laws would maintain order until Congress legislates a permanent government, which should be just and liberal toward natives, residents, and foreigners. Accompanying correspondence provides further facts.

Caitlin Bassett, a 29-year-old international netballer, says the lead-up to Saturday's Super Netball grand final between Sunshine Coast Lightning and Greater Western Sydney at Brisbane Entertainment Centre has been unlike anything in her 12-year career. Having never played in a national grand final previously, Bassett has leaned on experienced team-mates Geva Mentor and Laura Langman for guidance. Mentor, the goal keeper, faces the challenge of containing the Giants' 196cm goal shooter Kristina Brice, and has prepared by training against 215cm Queensland men's player Junior Levi.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI), developed by Welles Wilder in 1978, is an oscillator measuring the magnitude of gains and losses over n days, ranging from 0 to 100. It identifies overbought (high readings) and oversold (low readings) conditions in mean-reverting markets.

Backtesting over 20 years confirms RSI works reasonably well on stocks and stock indices, but requires additional filters or indicators for effectiveness. A 2-day RSI strategy on the S&P 500 (buying below 15, selling above 85) performed similarly to buy-and-hold from 1993-2020, with less market exposure (42%) and lower drawdowns (33% vs. 55%). A 10-day RSI produced weaker results.

Research indicates short time frames (2-6 days) and daily bars work best, particularly on stocks rather than commodities or forex. Divergences between price and RSI are difficult to quantify and offer limited practical use. Combining RSI with other tools, such as the Internal Bar Strength Indicator, can enhance performance.

Variations include Connors RSI and Cutler's RSI. A Nasdaq 100 backtest yielded a 71% win rate across approximately 300 trades, with average gains of 0.82% per trade. RSI 14 offers quicker signals for short-term traders, while RSI 21 suits longer-term trends.

When a defending team sends the ball over its own end line, play restarts with a corner kick by the attacking team. Though goals from corner kicks are statistically rare at higher levels, they remain valuable scoring opportunities as set plays near the opponent's goal.

To introduce corner kick offense to young players, coaches should follow a progression: explain Law 17, demonstrate fundamental skills, show right-footed and right-side kicks, introduce a play with designated positions, rotate players through positions, demonstrate left-footed and left-side kicks, and assign specific players to positions.

Coaches should clarify terminology (end-line/goal line), demonstrate when a ball is out of bounds, show proper ball placement in the corner arc, and mark the corner with a flag or substitute. They should demonstrate a proper instep drive kick with a 45-degree run-up, contrasted with improper technique.

The basic play uses three positions: corner taker, receiver (5 yards into the field), and cover man (5 yards from the arc, inside the end line to prevent mis-kicks going out). The receiver turns toward goal while the taker and cover man run forward for possible passes.

Four kicking options exist combining left/right foot with left/right corner arc, with ball placement varying accordingly. Coaches can later add passive then active defenders, additional passing options, offside instruction, and longer lofted kicks. Referees indicate the correct corner, and kickers must await referee acknowledgment.

The Supreme Court's upcoming case, Landor v. Louisiana Department of Corrections and Public Safety, addresses whether the Religious Land Use and Institutionalized Persons Act (RLUIPA) authorizes money damages against government officials. Damon Landor, a Rastafarian, had his dreadlocks forcibly shaved by prison officials despite legal precedent protecting his religious practice. A lower court ruled RLUIPA does not permit money damages, but the author argues Landor should win, citing prior unanimous Supreme Court precedent regarding the related Religious Freedom Restoration Act.

The author contends the case challenges several common misconceptions about religious freedom jurisprudence: that such cases are always polarized and partisan, that protections primarily benefit religious majorities, and that claimants are merely conservative culture-war combatants. The author notes many religious-liberty rulings have been unanimous or near-unanimous, and that historical claimants have frequently come from minority faiths including Jehovah's Witnesses, Sikhs, and Native Americans. Most religious-freedom disputes involve low-profile accommodations rather than contentious social issues. The author frames Landor as a reminder that religious freedom is a fundamental right belonging to all persons.

A San Diego police pursuit of a shooting suspect ended Sunday in City Heights after the suspect crashed into fences at Central Elementary School and San Diego Fire-Rescue 17. The chase began around 12:30 p.m. on Fairmont Avenue when officers tried to stop the suspect. After crashing, the armed suspect fled on foot but was arrested a block away near 41st Street and University Avenue.

A retrospective analytical study examined 671 patients (212 women, 459 men) hospitalized for traumatic brain injury (TBI) between July 2017 and December 2018 to identify frequently reported risk factors. Data were analyzed using T test, ANOVA, and Pearson correlation via Statistica software.

The mean patient age was 46.016 years, with hospitalization averaging 12.75 days. Most patients lived in cities (78.09%). The leading cause of TBI was domestic accidents (43.81%), followed by alcohol-related injuries (20.71%) and motor vehicle injuries (16.54%). Surgical treatment was required in 39.91% of cases, most commonly surgical debridement of wounds.

Key findings included: village residents were at higher TBI risk (p<0.002); men were hospitalized longer than women (p<0.024); men were affected at an earlier age (44.41 vs. 49.50 years, p<0.0004). Domestic accidents were the most frequent cause in both genders (37.47% of men, 57.54% of women). Age correlated directly with hospitalization duration in both groups.

The study concluded that domestic accidents are the leading TBI cause for both sexes, men are affected earlier in life, village residents face higher risk, and gender influences TBI severity and outcomes. Study limitations included the absence of a control group.

The passage documents U.S. foreign policy actions and Department of State organizational changes in late 1945. Key personnel changes included Edward Stettinius's resignation as Secretary of State (June 27), James Byrnes's appointment (July 2), Joseph Grew's resignation as Under Secretary (August 16) replaced by Dean Acheson, Patrick Hurley's resignation as Ambassador to China (November 27), and George C. Marshall's appointment as personal envoy to China. Cordell Hull received the Nobel Peace Prize on December 10.

Two major functions were transferred to the Department of State: Executive Order 9608 (August 31) moved international information functions from the Office of War Information, and Executive Order 9621 (September 20, effective October 1) transferred the Office of Strategic Services' Research and Analysis and Presentation Branches, abolishing the O.S.S. President Truman directed the Secretary of State to lead development of a coordinated foreign intelligence program across federal agencies.

The Blackwell GPU architecture introduces several power management and rendering advancements. Advanced power gating reduces latency between power states, with new clock gating that can shut off entire clock trees, including the memory clock tree for the first time. A separate voltage rail for GPU cores and memory allows independent voltage control per workload. Accelerated frequency switching adjusts clocks 1000x faster than previous architectures, and Blackwell enters its deepest sleep state 10x faster than Ada, yielding up to 50% power savings in some workloads.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three additional frames per rendered frame using a model that is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than its predecessor. Enhanced Flip Metering shifts frame pacing to the display engine. DLSS also transitions from CNN-based to transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving stability, detail, and lighting quality.

Blackwell emphasizes neural shaders, enabled by the new Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, which allows Tensor Core access from any shader type. Key features include RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (over 3x memory savings), Neural Radiance Cache for indirect lighting, RTX Skin (subsurface scattering), and RTX Neural Faces using generative AI.

The Blackwell GPU family includes the GB202 (flagship, 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA Cores) powering the RTX 5090; the GB203 (45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA Cores) powering the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti; and the GB205 (31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA Cores) powering the RTX 5070.

Sodium cumenesulfonate is a hydrotope compound with hydrophilic and hydrophobic parts, available in powder and liquid forms. It increases solubility of organic matter, lowers cloud points, improves ingredient compatibility, and moderates viscosity. Applications include wax cleaners, drilling fluids, detergents, metal processing, and oilfield uses. Market growth is driven by industrialization and household detergent use in emerging economies, while raw material price volatility, health hazards from exposure, and declining research activities may hinder it. By form, liquid dominated the market in 2015. By application, the household segment held the largest share in 2015, with industrial and institutional use also growing.

U.S. stocks fell approximately 2 percent on Monday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropping nearly 400 points, driven by a selloff in technology stocks. Facebook shares tumbled 7.1 percent following reports that a political consultancy improperly accessed data on over 50 million users, raising broader data privacy concerns. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.09 percent and the S&P technology index dropped 2.5 percent. Other FAANG stocks—Amazon, Apple, Netflix, and Alphabet—declined between 1.7 and 7.2 percent. All 11 major S&P sectors were lower, and the CBOE Volatility index rose 5.86 points.
