Frost Brown Todd and Gibbons plan to merge in January to form FBT Gibbons, a law firm with 800 lawyers across 25 offices. The merger expands Frost Brown Todd's presence into the Northeast, including New York and New Jersey, supporting its goal of becoming a national firm serving the middle market. Robert Sartin will chair the merged firm, with Adam Hall and Peter Torcicollo serving as co-managing partners. Frost Brown Todd reported $336.5 million in gross revenue, while Gibbons reported $115 million. Merger talks began after leaders met at a Zeughauser Group retreat, and additional mergers may follow.

Stephen Hawking, the renowned theoretical physicist, has died, according to a family spokesman. His children Lucy, Robert, and Tim described him as "a great scientist and an extraordinary man." Diagnosed with ALS at 21, Hawking lived with the illness for over 50 years, using an electronic voice synthesizer to communicate after a 1985 pneumonia attack. As Lucasian Professor of Mathematics at Cambridge University, he sought a "unified theory" reconciling Einstein's General Theory of Relativity with Quantum Mechanics, though he later suggested such a theory might not exist. His book "A Brief History of Time" became an international bestseller, followed by "The Universe in a Nutshell" in 2001. Hawking made cameo appearances on "The Simpsons" and "Star Trek," and his life was depicted in the 2014 film "The Theory of Everything," for which Eddie Redmayne won the best actor Academy Award. His achievements demonstrated that severe disabilities need not prevent a fulfilling life.

The 1854 treaty, which included annuities and statehood provisions, failed after Kamehameha III's death and his successor's opposition. An 1855 reciprocity treaty negotiated by Marcy and Judge Lee also failed ratification. In 1863, U.S. diplomatic representation was elevated to minister resident, with James McBride appointed. The Civil War delayed further reciprocity discussions. In 1867, Mr. McCook and Mr. Harris concluded a new reciprocity treaty at San Francisco, approved by the President but rejected by the Senate in 1870. Correspondence between Seward and McCook indicated that annexation was preferred over reciprocity if the two policies conflicted. The presence of the U.S.S. Lackawanna in Hawaiian waters, commanded by Capt. Reynolds, caused concern for the King and delayed Hawaiian ratification, which occurred July 30, 1867.

The President begins by taking the oath of office and invoking divine guidance, noting that he will not seek reelection. He reflects on the recent peaceful Presidential contest as evidence of American self-government.

On slavery in the Territories, he endorses Congress's application of majority rule, stating that residents should decide the question themselves. He considers the timing of this decision a judicial matter pending before the Supreme Court, whose ruling he will accept. He affirms that slavery within existing States lies beyond federal power and hopes the prolonged agitation over slavery will end, as it has endangered the Union.

He warns against those who calculate the material value of the Union, arguing that free trade across the country and shared prosperity make disunion ruinous. He stresses preserving government from corruption, noting the unprecedented Treasury surplus encourages extravagant spending. He recommends applying surplus funds to paying the public debt and strengthening the Navy, and supports a modified tariff that collects only necessary revenue.

He urges preserving public lands for actual settlers at moderate prices and welcomes immigrants as equal citizens. He endorses strict construction of the Constitution, but argues the war-making power permits Congress to fund a military road to defend the Pacific Coast.

On foreign policy, he advocates peace, commerce, frank diplomacy, non-interference, and avoiding entangling alliances. He notes America has acquired territory only through fair purchase or voluntary union, and defends future expansion if conducted justly.

He concludes by proceeding to take the oath.

On February 16, 2016, Apple Inc. entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co., Deutsche Bank Securities Inc., J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, and Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Incorporated for the issuance of $12 billion in notes. The offering included two series of Floating Rate Notes (due 2019 and 2021) totaling $1 billion, and seven series of Fixed Rate Notes with interest rates ranging from 1.300% to 4.650% and maturities between 2018 and 2046. Interest on the Floating Rate Notes will be paid quarterly beginning May 23, 2016, while Fixed Rate Notes will pay semi-annually beginning August 23, 2016. The Notes, issued under a 2013 indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company as trustee, will be senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with Apple's other unsecured, unsubordinated debt.

Synaptics Incorporated announced plans to mass produce "Clear ID," an optical in-display fingerprint sensor embedded under a phone's screen. The company claims it is twice as fast as 3D facial recognition and requires only one touch. The technology is designed for bezel-less smartphones and allows unlocking from any angle. According to Synaptics SVP Kevin Barber, consumers prefer front-facing fingerprint authentication, making in-display placement ideal as the industry shifts to OLED infinity displays. While Synaptics is not the first to develop this technology, it aims to compete with major companies. It remains unclear when this technology will appear in smartphones.

The Bemidji Lumberjacks (14-6) defeated Thief River Falls 77-45, led by Caden Rolfes (18 points), Linaes Whiting (17), Caleb Carlson (14), and Jeremy Beberg (10). Bemidji led 45-25 at halftime. Coach Travis Peterson praised the team's sustained effort, calling it a significant improvement over their narrow 56-51 win against the Prowlers three weeks earlier. BHS next plays at Fergus Falls on Feb. 18.

Containers define APIs that include parameters, external service calls, and traditional interfaces. Maintaining stable APIs is critical for sidecar modularity, as even subtle changes (like altered parameter formats or units) can break consumers. Documentation is essential for reusable containers; since formal tools are limited, best practices include using Dockerfile directives like EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL, with label names drawn from the Label Schema project for shared tooling compatibility.

The sidecar pattern augments application containers with added functionality. The ambassador pattern brokers interactions between an application container and external services, enabling modularity and reuse. Examples include sharded services (e.g., sharded Redis using twemproxy), service brokering for portability across environments, and request splitting for experimentation (e.g., nginx routing 10% of traffic to a test version).

The adapter pattern modifies a container's interface to match a standardized one, useful for monitoring (e.g., Prometheus exporters for Redis), logging normalization (e.g., fluentd plugins), and health checks (e.g., custom MySQL health adapters). This promotes modularity and community sharing.

Multi-node distributed patterns are loosely coupled via network APIs. Microservices architectures offer reliability, agility, independent scaling, and team decoupling, but increase debugging and design complexity.

Replicated load-balanced services handle stateless workloads, requiring at least two replicas for high availability and readiness probes for proper load balancing. Session-tracked services route users consistently using hashing. Caching layers (e.g., Varnish) improve performance, and SSL termination (e.g., nginx) secures traffic.

Sharded services distribute data across replicas when state exceeds single-machine capacity. Sharded caches increase memory utilization but are vulnerable to shard failures impacting hit rates. Replicated sharded caches add resilience. Sharding functions must be deterministic and uniform, with appropriate key selection; consistent hashing minimizes remapping during resizing. Hot sharding dynamically rebalances loads.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing across leaves, merging partial results at the root. It can use replicated or sharded leaves (e.g., distributed document search). Performance is limited by overhead and straggler nodes, where 99th-percentile latencies dominate. Replicating shards improves reliability and scale.

Function-as-a-service (FaaS), or serverless computing, handles short-lived, event-driven workloads.

Florida State University President John Thrasher has appointed a 15-member committee, chaired by Renisha Gibbs, to review the university's policies on campus names, markers, and statues. The panel was formed following a nationwide movement to remove Confederate designations and will seek community input on naming criteria. The campus chapter of Students for a Democratic Society has called for removing a statue of Francis Eppes, a founder of FSU's predecessor institution, citing his history as a slave owner and Confederate supporter. The committee's meetings will be open to the public.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture and fabricated on TSMC's 7nm N7 process, is NVIDIA's 8th generation data center GPU, containing 54.2 billion transistors on an 826 mm² die. It builds on the Tesla V100, delivering significant performance gains for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads.

Key features include:

- **Third-Generation Tensor Cores**: Support new data types (TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, Binary), with TF32 running 10x faster than V100 FP32 (20x with sparsity), and FP64 Tensor Core operations 2.5x faster than V100.
- **Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity**: A 2:4 sparsity pattern doubles Tensor Core throughput with minimal accuracy loss.
- **Multi-Instance GPU (MIG)**: Partitions a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, improving utilization for cloud and multi-tenant use cases.
- **Memory**: 40 GB HBM2 with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (1.7x V100) and a 40 MB L2 cache (nearly 7x larger than V100), with L2 residency controls and Compute Data Compression.
- **Third-Generation NVLink**: 600 GB/sec total bandwidth (2x V100) via 12 links at 50 Gbit/sec per signal pair.
- **PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV**: Doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth to 31.5 GB/sec.
- **Additional features**: Asynchronous copy and barrier instructions, hardware JPEG decode (NVJPG), five NVDEC units, optical flow accelerator, improved atomics, and enhanced error detection/isolation.

The A100 contains 108 SMs, 6912 FP32 CUDA Cores, and 432 Tensor Cores, delivering up to 312 TFLOPS of mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance. CUDA 11 adds programming support for these features, including Task Graph acceleration and Cooperative Groups enhancements. The A100 powers the NVIDIA DGX A100 system, which delivers 5 PFLOPS of AI performance using eight A100 GPUs connected via six NVSwitches.

The government shutdown has placed federal aviation safety workers, including air traffic controllers and TSA agents, in the position of working without pay. The FAA had announced plans to furlough 11,300 workers before the shutdown, and some projects have stopped due to absent colleagues. Employees interviewed by WIRED maintain that air travel remains safe, though they expect increased delays and cancellations as the shutdown continues, particularly given existing air traffic controller staff shortages.

Workers expressed anxiety over missed paychecks and fears that the Trump administration may use the shutdown to justify mass firings or undermine public sector unions. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy suggested on Fox Business News that controllers who don't report to work could be fired. The FAA stated that safety-critical positions would be exempt from reductions in force, and that air traffic will be slowed at impacted airports if staffing issues arise.

Unions, including the National Air Traffic Controllers Association, have discouraged coordinated sick-outs, which could jeopardize bargaining agreements. The Trump administration previously attempted to rescind TSA workers' collective bargaining agreement in March, a move preliminarily halted by a court in June. Union leader Johnny Jones noted employees may still need to call out if they cannot afford to commute.

The 23rd BMO Okanagan Marathon in Kelowna expects close to 3,000 participants. The Boston Marathon-qualifying course runs along Okanagan Lake and includes marathon, half marathon, 10 km, and 5 km events, plus children's activities. New this year are a timed 5 km event and an adult beverage garden. Notable participants include Team "Special Addition," supporting a lung transplant recipient, and Olympic race walker Mat Bilodeau. The event's official charity is The Sunshine Foundation of Canada. Saturday activities begin with a Running Room Free Friendship Run at 9 a.m., followed by the 5 km and kids' events. Sunday features the marathon, half marathon, and 10 km races, all staged from City Park with over 300 volunteers.

The disclosure describes devices, systems, and methods for surgical procedures, particularly robotic-assisted and navigation-assisted placement of implants such as pedicle screws within vertebrae during spinal fusion.

The system includes a robotic manipulator, a navigation system with a localizer, and a tool assembly. The tool assembly comprises a drive coupler removably coupled to an input device (manual handle, powered robotic device, or freehand powered device) and interchangeable working tools including scalpels, depth probes, burs, drills, taps, dilator probes, and tap inserters. The drive coupler features mating and locking features enabling quick tool interchange without decoupling from the input device, with indicia indicating tool depth.

A second drive coupler variant permits translational and rotational movement of the working tool relative to the input device, enabling semimanual incision and dilation while the manipulator constrains movement along a planned insertion trajectory.

An elongate sleeve positioned coaxially around the working tool retracts tissue to create a working channel. The sleeve may include a movable feature at its distal end (flexible tabs optionally connected by frangible material) that remains closed during insertion to prevent tissue ingress, then opens when the working tool advances through it. Bone-penetrating spikes at the distal end may anchor the sleeve to bony anatomy. Some sleeve embodiments have varying inner and outer diameters with tapering sections.

The workflow involves incising soft tissue, dilating, creating a pilot hole with a bur, and inserting a tap marker into the pedicle. The drive coupler can be decoupled from the working tool while the tool remains secured in bone.

For relocalization, working tools may include navigation features (divots) touchable by a digitizing probe, or a removable tracking device with markers. One tracking device embodiment includes a ratcheting mechanism providing unidirectional rotation of markers relative to the working tool, accommodating vertebral movement during discectomy and cage placement.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on January 27, 2022. The filing reported that Apple issued a press release on the same date regarding its financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 25, 2021, attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report lists Apple's securities registered under Section 12(b), including common stock (AAPL) and multiple notes due between 2022 and 2042, all registered on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Anjuna police registered two unnatural death cases on Sunday involving tourists, with drug overdose not ruled out. Pravin Sundaram, 28, from Tamil Nadu, collapsed in a Vagator parking area after reportedly attending a rave party with friends and was declared dead at a private hospital. In a separate case, a Kerala native named Abdul died after being brought to a private hospital by an unidentified person. Both bodies were sent to GMC Bambolim for autopsy, with viscera preserved to determine cause of death. Police Inspector Rahul Parab stated investigations are ongoing, including recording statements and tracing the person who brought Abdul to the hospital. The Water Resource Minister and Siolim MLA called the deaths unfortunate, urged stopping outdoor music parties linked to drug cases, and spoke to the North Goa SP about curbing such activities.

A New York Drug Utilization Review Board unanimously recommended that the state Medicaid program pause coverage of Sarepta Therapeutics' Duchenne muscular dystrophy treatment, Elevidys, following a safety controversy. The board advised waiting for the FDA to update the product labeling with safety and clinical trial data, and for evaluation of a forthcoming regimen to mitigate liver failure risk. However, New York will still cover some patients under 21 through the Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic and Treatment Medicaid benefit on a case-by-case basis. Other states may monitor the outcome.

The St. John's Edge defeated the London Lightning 123-110 in Game 4, tying the best-of-seven National Basketball League of Canada Central Division final 2-2. The Lightning played with little focus or intensity, were outscored 50-38 in the paint, and missed 13 free throws. Coach Keith Vassell accepted blame, saying he failed to prepare his team adequately. Tension arose when Royce White and Ryan Anderson tugged at each other near the officials at the end of the third quarter. Edge coach Jeff Dunlap adjusted by starting Alex Johnson, and Charles Hinkle and Coron Williams each scored 28 points, while Ryan Reid added 22. White led the Lightning with 32 points and Anderson added 21. Vassell again used a short bench. Separately, NBL deputy commissioner Audley Stephenson confirmed an official complaint alleging White used a homophobic slur during Game 3, though accounts of the incident differed. Game 5 is scheduled for Thursday in St. John's, with Game 6 set for Sunday in London.

The speaker reflects on playing hockey in various casual settings and expresses optimism about an upcoming Wednesday game, despite a prior loss. He emphasizes the team's strength as a road team, their ability to focus on one game at a time, and describes this as the biggest game of their careers.

Key tactical points include maintaining forecheck pressure, getting pucks deep, closing gaps in the defensive zone, and being physical with opponents. He acknowledges that the previous game was competitive at five-on-five, praising both goaltenders, particularly expressing confidence in "Binner."

The speaker values the travel days before the game for preparation and relaxation. He highlights the importance of a returning teammate who contributes physicality and scoring. He stresses sticking to a consistent road-game approach, noting the home crowd was supportive but the focus now is business as usual. To score, he suggests directing players and pucks toward the net.

A Carpool Karaoke-style video featuring mothers and their children with Down's syndrome signing Christina Perri's "A Thousand Years" in Makaton has been viewed over 600,000 times. Created for World Down's Syndrome Day on March 21, the video was inspired by a SingingHands clip and conceived by Coventry mum Becky Carless, whose son Archie has Down's syndrome. The mothers belong to the "DesignerGenes" Facebook support group for parents of children born in 2013 and 2014. Perri granted permission within an hour, and James Corden praised the video on Twitter. Participants filmed themselves separately, with a father from the group editing the final version.

This study examines Turkish teachers' experiences with distance education and technological tools used during the COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey. Using a qualitative case study approach, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 20 Turkish teachers in Hazro district of Diyarbakır province, with data analyzed through descriptive analysis.

Key findings include:
- 45% of participants believed education progressed during the pandemic, while 25% found progress insufficient and 20% thought education did not progress.
- 70% considered distance education not efficient enough, while 30% found it completely inefficient; none found it fully productive.
- Target behaviors and achievements were only partially achieved, primarily due to lack of internet infrastructure and materials (phones, tablets).
- Major problems identified: students' lack of equipment, multiple school-age children per household, infrastructure issues in rural areas, and student absenteeism.
- For Turkish lessons specifically, students needed reading books and dictionaries (35%), technological materials (25%), both (20%), and practice activities (20%).
- Phones (65%) were the most-used communication tool, and WhatsApp was the most preferred application, followed by Zoom and EBA.
- Required teacher qualifications included subject knowledge, communication skills, technological proficiency, and activity-oriented teaching.

Recommendations include resolving infrastructure problems, providing equal access to materials, continuously updating the EBA platform, maintaining distance education as support for face-to-face learning, offering professional development courses for teachers, and restructuring curricula to account for pandemic-era learning gaps.

Topshop has recalled all till display stands nationwide after 10-year-old Kaden Reddick from Reading died from serious head injuries sustained in an incident involving a store display barrier at its Oracle shopping centre branch on Monday afternoon. Thames Valley Police and Reading Borough Council are investigating the circumstances. Kaden's parents paid tribute on social media. The incident follows a 2013 case in which a four-year-old boy was killed by a falling mirror in a Bicester Village shop changing room.

This inaugural address frames the moment as a historic opportunity for America to lead the world toward peace. The speaker notes that converging forces, including global desire for peace and fear of war, make progress possible. He acknowledges American achievements in science, industry, civil rights, and economic management, but identifies a current crisis of spirit marked by division, war, and discord despite material wealth.

He calls for lowering rhetoric, listening to overlooked voices, and continuing government efforts in employment, housing, education, and urban renewal, while recognizing government's limits and the need for citizen involvement. He emphasizes racial unity, stating laws must now be given life.

On foreign policy, he announces a shift from confrontation to negotiation, pledging open communication, peaceful competition with adversaries, cooperation in arms reduction and space, and maintained strength. Drawing on his international experience, he commits his office to peace among nations, seeking not victory but healing.

Referencing the Apollo astronauts' view of Earth and Archibald MacLeish's reflection on shared human destiny, he closes by urging Americans to move forward with faith, purpose, and confidence.

The FDA announced a crackdown on illegal sales of Juul e-cigarettes to minors, including a nationwide undercover operation targeting stores and online retailers. Juul devices, which resemble flash drives, are popular among teens and contain nicotine levels equivalent to a pack of cigarettes per cartridge. Since March, FDA compliance checks found 40 violations, resulting in 40 warning letters. The agency also had eBay remove Juul listings and requested documents from Juul's manufacturer to understand the product's appeal to youth. Dave Dobbins of the Truth Initiative urged the FDA to act faster and remove youth-enticing flavors. The FDA plans further enforcement against misleading marketing and will educate youth on tobacco dangers.

Diana Beresford-Kroeger lives on a 160-acre property near Merrickville with her husband Christian, where she cultivates a rare arboretum and organic garden called Carrigliath. Born in Ireland and orphaned at 11, she was raised by families who taught her ancient Irish traditions and the laws of nature. She earned degrees in botany and medical biochemistry from University College, Cork, and later pursued doctoral studies at Carleton University and cardiovascular research at the University of Ottawa. Her gardening passion grew after receiving trees as a wedding gift, leading her to classify and preserve local flora. She has authored books and delivered lectures worldwide. Her latest project is a Canadian-made feature film, "Call of the Forest: The Forgotten Wisdom of Trees," based on her book "The Global Forest," addressing deforestation and climate change. She developed the Bioplan, proposing that each person plant one tree annually for six years to reduce atmospheric carbon dioxide. The film has attracted large audiences and received nominations at the Paris Science Awards.

Ravita Meghwar, a 16-year-old Hindu girl from Pakistan, reportedly converted to Islam and married a Muslim man. Her family alleges abduction and forced conversion, while she claims she eloped willingly. Such cases, predominantly reported in Sindh province—home to most of Pakistan's Hindu minority (about 2% of the population)—have alarmed the Hindu community. Activists say conversions are often organized, backed by shrines, seminaries, clerics, and politicians, who offer money and housing to converts. Lower-caste Hindus, often economically dependent on landowners, are particularly vulnerable. In 2012, the high-profile case of Rinkle Kumari reached the Supreme Court, which ruled in favor of the Muslim husbands. In 2016, Sindh's legislature passed a bill banning forced conversions and conversions before age 18, but opposition from hardline religious groups, including Jamaat-ud-Dawa, led the governor to refuse to sign it. Lawyers now rely on laws against underage marriage, though judges often rule in favor of the marriages. Activists trace the organized nature of conversions to the Islamization policies of General Zia-ul-Haq's regime. Many Hindu families are reportedly leaving their villages for cities within Sindh or migrating to India, with one estimate citing 5,000 departures annually.

The speaker describes the coach as tough but fair, honest, and hardworking. He acknowledges the opposing team's strong defense and depth, presenting a challenge. After waiting years for this opportunity, he intends to enjoy the moment while recognizing the hard work ahead. He praises Canadian hockey fans, recalling an intense atmosphere in Edmonton, and expects Ottawa's crowd to be similar. On goaltenders, he notes they remain large and skilled, requiring precise shots. He credits his team's success to forward depth, with younger lines and Pahlsson's line contributing significantly. On age, he says he mostly feels like his younger teammates. He suggests Giguere is underrated due to playing in a small market rather than a place like Toronto.

The author, a high school senior in Las Vegas, shares how employment transformed his academic trajectory after two disengaged years of high school. He cites that 42,000 youth in southern Nevada are classified as NEETs (not in education, employment, or training), with Nevada having the second-highest rate of young male NEETs in the country at 19%. Outcomes for NEETs include higher incarceration rates, isolation, and addiction.

After getting a summer job following his sophomore year, the author maintained a 4.0 GPA while working 20+ hours weekly. He argues that jobs connect classroom learning to real-world applications, build durable skills, and provide confidence and purpose. Research cited indicates youth employment programs reduce delinquency, improve academic performance, increase college enrollment, and enhance social development.

The author notes that internships and jobs remain rare, with only 5% of students accessing apprenticeships or internships, and youth unemployment at 10.5% (over 14% for African American youth). He advocates for government incentives for businesses to hire young people, referencing tax credit programs in some states and a failed Nevada bill that would have provided $15 million for NEETs. He concludes that expanding work opportunities benefits entire communities.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on August 1, 2017, reporting its financial results for the third fiscal quarter ended July 1, 2017. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and a related data sheet (Exhibit 99.2). The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The speaker reflects on the Dallas Stars' recent playoff loss, emphasizing that the team "ripped their own hearts out" through self-inflicted critical errors in the third period, particularly puck support mistakes that created odd-man rushes for New Jersey. He stresses these mistakes are correctable and expresses confidence the team will respond.

He praises New Jersey's commitment to defending with speed and size, noting their passion to defend has exceeded Dallas's in recent games. He highlights several Devils players including Malakhov, Gomez, Rafalski, White, and Madden, and credits coach Larry Robinson and Fetisov's influence on the defense.

The coach distinguishes New Jersey's "speed without the puck" from Colorado's "speed with the puck." He emphasizes that at this playoff stage, emotion and leadership must come from within the dressing room, with captains taking responsibility for passion while coaches handle tactics.

He notes Dallas must eliminate easy odd-man rushes, stay within their system rather than trying to "hit home runs," and raise their level of play. He points to Modano as an example of a player who tried too hard to force offense. He acknowledges facing elimination but believes the team wants to keep playing and can force a return game. Regarding Carbonneau, he notes the series hasn't suited his defensive role since Dallas has been chasing games.

Saturday night has historically been a key ratings battleground between BBC1 and ITV, with success in this slot demonstrating the BBC's commitment to entertainment and offering rare family co-viewing opportunities. Launching new shows in this competitive slot is difficult, so schedules rely on long-running favourites like Strictly Come Dancing and The X Factor. Few entertainment programmes have historically succeeded on Saturday nights, and almost none created in the last decade, with The Voice UK as a possible exception. When Blind Date declined, Strictly and The X Factor revived the slot, but both will eventually fade as formats grow stale. Although financial rewards for new hit formats are substantial—the BBC has earned millions from Strictly—most new shows fail, leaving controllers to rely on instinct, producer track records and luck. The piece is written by Greg Dyke, former LWT chief executive and BBC director-general.

Combination defenses aim to limit touches by standout offensive players or serve as a surprise tactic, with timing and surprise being critical to their success. The Box & One, the most common, uses four defenders in a box zone while a "Chaser" denies passes to a top scorer. The Diamond & One similarly targets a single scorer, matches up against a one-guard front, and shuts down the middle but leaves the corners open. The Triangle & Two is effective against two strong scorers, as a surprise change, or when an opponent is stalling late in the game.

A study by Patrick D. Quinn of Indiana University found that pre-existing psychiatric and behavioural conditions, along with psychoactive medication use, are associated with a higher risk of long-term opioid use. While about 1.7 percent of patients with opioid prescriptions become long-term users (six months or more), the risk increased 1.5 times for those on ADHD medications, three times for those with prior substance use disorders, and nearly nine times for those with prior opioid use disorders. Harmful outcomes such as depression, self-injury, and motor vehicle accidents also predicted long-term use. Quinn suggested mental health assessments should accompany long-term opioid therapy. Published in PAIN, the study examined 10.3 million patients with opioid prescription claims from 2004 to 2013.

German Chancellor Angela Merkel has agreed to a deal to close asylum transit camps along three Austrian borders, tightening migrant entry into Germany. The move came after Interior Minister Horst Seehofer, leader of Bavaria's CSU, threatened to resign unless granted powers to expel migrants, including asylum applicants. Seehofer's pressure is reportedly linked to the rising support of the far-right AfD in Bavaria, which threatens Merkel's three-party governing coalition with the CSU and SPD. Under the deal, rejected asylum seekers will be held at transit centers and returned to their countries via negotiation, or to Austria if no agreement is reached. However, the SPD opposes the transit centers, and Austria has refused to accept returned refugees, with Chancellor Sebastian Kurz threatening reciprocal expulsions that could collapse the EU's open-border system. Italy has also refused migrants under its new far-right government. Germany, which took in 1.4 million refugees in 2015, now accepts around 10,000 monthly. The Czech Republic, Poland, Hungary, and Slovakia also reject EU immigrants.

The passage presents a lecture on binary detection theory in communication systems. The professor explains the approach of simplifying complex problems into "toy problems," referencing advice from Claude Shannon, who demonstrated that understanding simple cases first enables solving more complex ones.

The lecture focuses on binary detection where a single bit (plus a or minus a) is transmitted through a channel with Gaussian noise, and the receiver must guess the input from a one-dimensional output value, v. The detector uses a known probability model and applies Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) decoding to minimize error probability, making detection, hypothesis testing, and decoding equivalent concepts.

Key concepts introduced include: a priori probabilities (before observation), a posteriori probabilities (after observation), and likelihood ratios. The MAP decision rule compares the likelihood ratio to a threshold equal to the ratio of a priori probabilities (p1/p0). Binary MAP tests are always threshold tests, and the likelihood ratio serves as a sufficient statistic.

For 2PAM (antipodal signaling) in Gaussian noise with variance n0/2, the likelihood ratio simplifies to an exponential function of the observation. Taking the log likelihood ratio yields a simple decision rule. The probability of error depends on the ratio of signal amplitude to noise standard deviation, expressed as Q(√(2Eb/n0)), where Eb is energy per bit.

Non-antipodal signaling produces the same error probability based on the distance between points but wastes energy (e.g., 3 dB loss when sending a pilot tone). For antipodal vectors in white Gaussian noise, the inner product of v and a becomes the sufficient statistic, implementable via a matched filter. Geometrically, decision regions become perpendicular planes bisecting the line between signal points, reducing the vector problem to the one-dimensional case.

The NPD Group has identified five trends expected to shape Britain's £57 billion foodservice industry in 2018:

1. **Click & collect**: Smartphone-based ordering will reduce wait times and boost sales, requiring operators to improve efficiency and possibly reconfigure layouts.

This patent application describes systems and methods for creating arbitrarily-shaped ion energy distribution functions (IEDFs) using shaped-pulse bias in plasma processing chambers.

Background: In Reactive Ion Etch (RIE) chambers, an RF bias generator supplies voltage to a power electrode, creating a self-bias voltage that determines ion energy and etch anisotropy. Traditional RF bias produces a two-peak IEDF, which can cause feature bowing in high-aspect-ratio etching. A shaped-pulse bias scheme was previously developed to maintain nearly constant sheath voltage for ~90% of each cycle, producing a single-peak (mono-energetic) IEDF.

The disclosed methods create customized IEDF shapes through three approaches:

1. **Amplitude modulation**: Applying shaped pulse bias while modulating the negative voltage jump (V_OUT) amplitude. The relative number of pulses at each amplitude determines the ion fraction at that energy. Bursts of pulses at varying amplitudes can create multi-peak IEDFs (e.g., "HHHL" produces a two-peak IEDF with 75% high-energy and 25% low-energy ions).

2. **Overcompensation**: Creating a voltage ramp during the ion compensation phase with a more negative slope than needed for constant substrate voltage, producing a wider, double-peaked IEDF.

3. **Undercompensation**: Using a less negative slope than needed, producing a wider, single-peaked IEDF.

The system includes a substrate support assembly with a power electrode, a ceramic layer, and a bias supply with memory and processor for executing control programs. These techniques enable precise IEDF shaping for applications like hard-mask opening and high-aspect-ratio etching.

The Princeton Offense is an unstructured, motion-based style of play developed by Pete Carril, relying on constant player movement, precise spacing (12-15 feet), and defensive reads rather than set plays. Its signature is the back door cut, set up by ball control and strong outside shooting.

Key requirements include team commitment, player versatility (shooting, passing, driving with either hand), unselfishness, patience, and superior conditioning. All five players are equally involved, making it adaptable against any defense.

The offense typically begins in a 2-3 high post alignment and progresses through three phases:
1. **Entries** – triggered by passes or dribble penetration (e.g., Off Guard Rub, Point Rub, Mid Screen, Dribble Clear, Zipper, High Post).
2. **Exchanges** – constant ball and player movement via wing exchanges, down screens, back cuts, and base crosses.
3. **Post Action** – high post basket cuts flowing into a four-out alignment, with post-ups used mainly to collapse the defense and kick out to shooters.

Additional tactics include dribble penetration, dribble weaves, misdirection dribbles, drive-and-kick actions, quick-hitting set plays (e.g., high post splits, guard lobs, weakside skip passes), and prepared press breaks.

Psychologically, the offense pressures opponents through low-possession games, exploits weak defenders, induces fatigue and rushed shots, and remains consistent regardless of shooting performance.

The case involves an appeal from a District Court decision dismissing plaintiffs' petition to recover on a foreign judgment against James E. and Elizabeth Siver, and to enjoin allegedly fraudulent conveyances to their sons. The Sivers counterclaimed, alleging that the original New York property exchange with Secor, which led to the deficiency judgment, was induced by fraudulent representations regarding the farm's condition, orchard, sawmill, pasturage, and value.

On appeal, appellants argued that testimony from James E. Siver and his wife was inadmissible under Code Section 4604, which prohibits parties from testifying about personal transactions or communications with a deceased person against the administrator.

The court held that objections to witness competency must specifically state the grounds of incompetency; general objections that a witness is "incompetent and unqualified" are insufficient. The court also held that an objection referencing "personal transactions" does not necessarily cover "personal communications," as the terms are not equivalent. The witnesses were found competent to testify regarding property descriptions, values, reliance on representations, and property conditions.

The court affirmed the lower court's decree, finding sufficient evidence that defendants were defrauded in the original transaction. The court also denied defendants' cross-appeal seeking to tax costs against the administratrix individually.

Justices Ladd, Salinger, and Stevens dissented, arguing the objection adequately covered communications and that the testimony related to inseparable transactions involving both spouses and the deceased.

The lecture reviews Wald's identity and sequential hypothesis testing before introducing martingales. Wald's identity, applied to a random walk with thresholds alpha and beta, yields an upper bound on the probability of crossing the positive threshold via the Markov inequality, with r* being the critical parameter for threshold problems.

For hypothesis testing, the likelihood ratio serves as a sufficient statistic, and the MAP rule reduces to a threshold test. The log-likelihood ratio creates a random walk, with r* always equal to 1 in hypothesis testing contexts. Fixed-sample tests trade off error exponents between hypotheses (Neyman-Pearson principle), while sequential tests continue observations until a threshold is crossed, guaranteeing error probability bounds via preset procedures rather than unethical data manipulation.

Taking derivatives of Wald's identity at r=0 yields Wald's equality (first derivative) and a variance relation (second derivative). Applied to a simple symmetric random walk, expected stopping time equals |beta|·alpha.

A martingale is a sequence where E[Zn | Zn-1,...,Z1] = Zn-1, generalizing to E[Zn | Zi,...,Z1] = Zi. Examples include zero-mean random walks, sums of dependent zero-mean random variables, products of unit-mean independent variables, and sign-randomized sequences. The double-or-nothing game illustrates that limits and expectations cannot always be interchanged: E[Zn]=1 for all n, but Zn→0 with probability 1.

Submartingales and supermartingales use inequalities instead of equality. Jensen's Inequality states that for convex H, H(E[Z]) ≤ E[H(Z)].

Socket 940 must have specific markings molded into its cover, including the socket identifier, lock/unlock directional designator, pin A01 orientation triangle, UL symbol, and a lot traceability number, all positioned to remain visible post-assembly.

The contact base is high-strength copper alloy, plated with a minimum 1.27 µm nickel, with the mating area receiving an additional 0.76 µm gold plating. The socket attaches to the PCB via SMT using 0.76 mm tin/lead (63/37) solder balls on 0.64 mm pads, meeting a 0.20 mm co-planarity requirement. Contacts include a solder barrier to prevent wicking.

A stainless steel actuation lever on the right side enables toolless operation. Package insertion/extraction force must not exceed 2 kgf when open, and extraction force must be at least 0.013 kgf per pin when closed. Lever actuation force must be under 3.6 kgf, with pin displacement under 1.0 mm. The socket must withstand 50 actuation cycles.

Visual inspection (1X magnification) requires no missing/damaged solder balls, contacts, or lever, and no cracks on the cover or base.

Electrical requirements include: 1.5 A current rating per contact with under 30°C rise; initial and final LLCR not exceeding 25 mΩ per contact (measured across 200 daisy-chained pairs with Kovar pins); partial self-inductance under 4 nH; loop inductance of 3 nH ±10%; capacitance under 1 pF; differential impedance of 100 Ω ±10%; propagation delay skew under 10 ps (+3 ps error); dielectric withstanding voltage minimum 650 Vac; and insulation resistance minimum 1000 MΩ.

This command moves contents of SNP guest pages within system physical address space as a faster alternative to SNP PAGE_MOVE. For 2M pages, constituent 4k pages must be physically contiguous and 2M aligned; non-contiguous 2M pages are not directly supported. DMA to migrating pages is unsupported and may be aborted, and the CPU must be prevented from accessing them, typically via non-present host page table entries.

Source pages must be in Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state, and destination pages in Pre-Migration state. After migration, destinations inherit the source state, and sources become Pre-Migration.

Firmware processes each migration entry sequentially, validating RMP_ENFORCE, page states, GCTX_PADDR, guest context, exclusive RMP access, matching page sizes, and required source/destination states, returning specific error codes on failure. It then issues TLB invalidate and sync, copies data, and updates both RMPs.

A separate command marks the end of migration command strings and can trigger interrupt-on-completion.

Errors in command format, content, or migration list entries are reported in commands/entries and may yield partial success. Ring buffer errors appear in PM_STATUS. Hardware errors surface via command status or MCA; timeouts require client-side MCA logging and recovery decisions. Batches process up to 128 pages, and hardware errors may render all batch pages unrecoverable, potentially leading to eventual system failure.

European and Polish qualification standards require higher education to deliver knowledge, skills, and social competences, yet contemporary challenges—such as broad access to online databases and the rise of knowledge-based societies—demand innovative teaching methods. Gamification, the purposeful application of game mechanics to non-game contexts, offers a way to increase student motivation, engagement, and retention by leveraging positive emotions, clear goals, feedback, and competition.

The paper discusses four gamification projects conducted at the Institute of Pedagogy, University of Wrocław (2014–2015):

1. **Kulturalny Wrocław** – A location-based game where students located cultural sites in Wrocław, solved riddles, and completed a crossword. Students rated it highly for socialization, experiential learning, and knowledge retention, though some questioned its efficiency compared to traditional lessons. It proved low-cost and easily repeatable.

2. **Gamification in Career Management** – A five-day seminar framed as a science-fiction space mission, with missions, point systems, badges, and prizes. Students absorbed significant content, integrated quickly, and scored highly on the final game-exam. However, instructors reported that preparation was extremely labor-intensive and only viable if repeated multiple times.

3. **Entrepreneurship Location-Based Game (Zostań przedsiębiorcą)** – Teams named after famous entrepreneurs completed quests around the city, earning money and managing props representing business obstacles. Participants praised its socializing nature, dynamism, and development of soft skills and teamwork, though competition, weather, and unfamiliar terrain were viewed ambivalently.

4. **Learning through Games (LARP: Spell of the Black Magic Master)** – A fantasy role-playing game for 12 participants playing adventurer roles. Students with prior RPG experience adapted better; novices struggled with complex rules and role-assumption. Participants developed negotiation, communication, and creativity skills, though preparation was time-consuming.

**Conclusions**: Location-based games have strong potential in academic education, especially when simple, clearly ruled, and integrated with ICT. Longer, complex games suit supplementary, funded programs and benefit from preparatory socializing and tutorials. Game design must balance student experience, topic, time, and cost to avoid diminishing satisfaction.

The New Jersey Supreme Court reviewed consolidated appeals challenging the Chancery Division's denial of costs and counsel fees sought by appellants under N.J.S. 2A:15-53 of the Anti-Injunction Act.

In the strike case, United States Pipe and Foundry Co. obtained temporary restraints and an interlocutory injunction against mass picketing by Steelworkers Union members during a 1959 strike. The Appellate Division reversed the injunction on procedural grounds—primarily the trial court's delayed decision—while concluding that defendants' conduct substantively justified injunctive relief.

In the arbitration case, the company sought a declaratory judgment that a discharged striker's grievance was not arbitrable under the new collective bargaining agreement. The Appellate Division reversed and directed summary judgment for the union.

The Court held that counsel fees under Section 53 are mandatory only when a suit falls within the Anti-Injunction Act and injunctive relief is denied on the merits, citing Westinghouse Electric Corp. v. Local No. 449. The arbitration case was deemed outside the Act's scope, being essentially a declaratory judgment action rather than an injunction suit targeting coercive labor activity.

Regarding the strike case, the Court determined that because the suit was not "wrongfully brought" and defendants' conduct substantively warranted an injunction—with reversal based solely on procedural violations not attributable to plaintiff—costs and counsel fees were properly denied.

The Chancery Division judgments were affirmed, with costs awarded to respondent only in the arbitration case. Appellants were granted leave to reapply for statutory trial court costs in the strike case.

The Turing architecture introduces a new SM design with two SMs per TPC, each containing 64 FP32 Cores, 64 INT32 Cores, eight Tensor Cores, and one RT Core. Turing enables concurrent execution of FP32 and INT32 operations, delivering approximately 36% additional throughput. A unified architecture for shared memory, L1, and texture caching doubles L1 hit bandwidth per TPC compared to Pascal, achieving 50% performance improvement per CUDA core.

Turing Tensor Cores add INT8 and INT4 precision modes, enabling real-time deep learning in gaming. The Tesla T4, the first Turing-based inferencing GPU, includes 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores, delivering up to 40X higher inference performance and 50X higher energy efficiency than CPUs.

Turing is the first GPU to use GDDR6 memory at 14 Gbps with 20% better power efficiency than GDDR5X, and features larger L2 caches and improved compression, yielding 50% higher effective bandwidth. The display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60Hz, HDR, and VirtualLink for VR headsets. NVLink replaces SLI bridges for GPU-to-GPU transfers.

RT Cores accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing via hybrid rendering (combining rasterization and ray tracing). NVIDIA NGX uses Tensor Cores for AI features including DLSS, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

Additional features include Mesh Shading for handling complex geometry, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering supporting up to four views per pass. The TU104 and TU106 GPUs share Turing's architectural features, with varying configurations for different products. The RTX-OPS metric measures hybrid rendering workloads combining Tensor, CUDA, RT, and INT32 operations.

This retrospective cohort study investigated whether perinatal mood disorders are associated with peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) and other adverse cardiac events. Using the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project National Inpatient Sample (HCUP-NIS) database from 2017-2019, researchers analyzed over 2.2 million hospitalizations of pregnant and postpartum patients, of which 168,729 (7.4%) had an ICD-10 diagnosis of a mood disorder (depression, bipolar, anxiety, or other).

Patients with mood disorders were more likely to be non-Hispanic white, obese, use tobacco, have diabetes, chronic hypertension, asthma, or anemia, be publicly insured, deliver earlier, and undergo cesarean delivery. The incidence of PPCM was higher among those with mood disorders (0.12% vs 0.05%), as was the composite of adverse cardiac events (0.36% vs 0.14%). After adjusting for confounders, mood disorders remained independently associated with PPCM (aOR 1.36), composite adverse cardiac events (aOR 1.57), and pulmonary edema (aOR 1.62). No significant association was found with maternal mortality.

The authors conclude that perinatal mood disorders represent a modifiable risk factor for PPCM and cardiac events, suggesting implications for mental health screening and care during pregnancy and postpartum. Study limitations include reliance on ICD-10 codes, inpatient-only data, and lack of long-term follow-up.

In card identification mode, the host resets cards, validates operating voltage, identifies cards, and assigns a Relative Card Address (RCA) individually per card via the CMD line, using the identification clock frequency.

CMD0 (GO_IDLE_STATE) is a software reset that moves cards into Idle State, except those in Inactive State. After power-on or CMD0, CMD lines enter input mode, and cards initialize with RCA=0x0000, 400KHz clock, and default driver strength (DSR-specified for 3.3V; type B for 1.8V). In UHS-II Mode, CMD0 does not clear the RCA.

Since the host and card may not initially know the supported voltages, CMD8 (SEND_IF_COND), introduced in Physical Layer Specification Version 2.00, verifies operating conditions. The VHS field indicates supplied voltage (only one bit set), with CRC and a check pattern validating communication. A compatible card echoes back the voltage and check pattern; an incompatible card gives no response and remains idle. CMD8 must be issued before the first ACMD41 to initialize SDHC or SDXC cards and signals to the card that the host supports Version 2.00 or later.

A University of Rochester Medical Centre study published in Scientific Reports found that low levels of alcohol consumption may benefit brain health. Led by Dr Maiken Nedergaard, the research on mice examined the glymphatic system, which clears waste including proteins linked to Alzheimer's and dementia. Mice given the equivalent of about 2.5 drinks daily showed reduced brain inflammation and improved glymphatic function compared to teetotal mice, performing equally on cognitive and motor tests. In contrast, intermediate doses (7.9 drinks daily) and high doses (21 drinks daily) decreased glymphatic function, though effects from chronic moderate drinking were reversible within 24 hours. High chronic exposure also caused inflammation and impaired cognition. Nedergaard said the findings align with the J-shaped model of alcohol's health effects and may explain why low-to-moderate drinking is associated with reduced dementia risk while heavy drinking increases cognitive decline.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers support three oscillator modes: internal, external synchronization, and primary-secondary. In external synchronization mode, RT is left floating while a clock (200 kHz–4 MHz, 40–60% duty cycle) at twice the switching frequency is applied to SYNC. In primary-secondary mode, the primary device's SYNC output drives the secondary's SYNC input, enabling synchronized independent converters or interleaved parallel converters, with a 90° or 270° phase shift between outputs.

The controllers feature single or dual primary outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and optional synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB), each with ~150 mA peak current requiring external gate drivers. OUTB and SRB are only active when DCL is tied to AVSS for a 50% duty cycle limit (TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP only). Dead times (TDSP, TDPS) and leading edge blank time are programmable via resistors to AVSS on the TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP, while TPS7H5003-SP has fixed 50 ns values. Pulse skipping prevents minimum on-time issues during high-frequency operation.

Maximum duty cycle is configurable (50%, 75%, or 100%) via the DCL pin, depending on the device. The CS_ILIM pin handles current sensing and PWM generation with a 1.05 V current limit threshold triggering hiccup mode, controlled by a capacitor on HICC. The FAULT pin enables external protection with a 0.6 V threshold. Slope compensation is set via RSC, and Type 2A/2B frequency compensation is supported through the COMP pin. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C with restart at 160°C.

A design example details a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull converter with 5 V output using GaN FETs, covering component selection for the transformer, switching FETs, RCD clamp, output inductor/capacitance, current sense, hiccup capacitor, compensation, and slope compensation. Layout guidelines emphasize separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switch node area, short high-current traces, close placement of bypass and compensation components, and routing noise-sensitive signals away from switching traces.

Modern offensive trends like RPOs and Air Raid concepts have pushed defenses toward "match coverage" and "middle of the field open" looks, which affects run fits. Coaches must translate terminology into executable schemes, recognizing that run fits vary by talent and philosophy.

Run fits stem from two influences: front spacing (even or odd) and coverage behind the fit. Even spacing leaves the B gap open; odd spacing leaves the C gaps open. What matters is the post-snap front, not the pre-snap alignment.

Spacing is further categorized by the number of box defenders versus 12/21 personnel:

- **7-man spacing**: Defense is "out-gapped" with a light box, typically paired with middle-of-field-open coverage. Tools include 2-gapping linemen or stunts. Linebackers often play "stack-track-fallback" versus zone and "spill-overlap" versus gap scheme.

- **8-man spacing**: "Gapped-out" with equal box numbers, typically using middle-of-field-closed coverage (Cover 1 or 3). Defenders play one-gap fits. Common tools include "indicator fitting" versus zone and "lever-spill-lever" versus gap scheme.

- **9-man spacing**: "Maxed out" with an extra box defender, using Cover 0 or Narduzzi-style quarters where safeties are force defenders. Allows aggressive one-gap play with an additional overhang defender.

These concepts apply to 3-4 defenses as well, where Tite/Mint fronts represent odd spacing and function like pre-exchanged even fronts. Overhangs may be taught "fill or freeze" based on the running back's alignment.

The lecture's main topic is forward and futures contracts. Lo explains that these are tools for hedging risk, particularly useful for companies exposed to currency or commodity price fluctuations (e.g., Caterpillar's foreign sales). He discusses debates on whether firms should hedge, citing examples like Homestake Mining (no hedging), American Barrick (full hedging), and Battle Mountain Gold (partial hedging).

A forward contract is a customized, binding agreement between two parties to transact a specified commodity at a set price on a future date. At inception, the contract has zero value because the forward price is set so neither party gains an advantage. Forwards are traded over-the-counter and carry illiquidity and counterparty risk.

Futures contracts address these problems through standardization, exchange trading, daily mark-to-market settlement, and a Futures Clearing Corporation that acts as intermediary. Daily mark-to-market means gains and losses are settled each day, limiting counterparty exposure to one day's price movement. Traders must post initial margin and maintain a minimum maintenance margin, or positions are closed out.

Lo notes forwards remain popular in certain markets like currencies, while most futures contracts are cash settled rather than involving physical delivery.

The lecture focuses on understanding light forces, particularly the stimulated force, through the dressed atom picture, which atomic physicists commonly use when lasers drive atoms.

Key points covered:

1. **Dressed atom picture basics**: The atom interacts with both the vacuum (spontaneous emission) and a laser field. Diagonalizing the two-by-two matrix yields dressed states as linear superpositions of bare states (ground/excited) with sine/cosine theta amplitudes.

2. **Mollow triplet and rate equations**: In the strong Rabi frequency limit, the Optical Bloch Equations decouple into separate equations for populations and coherences, with different relaxation times explaining the different widths of central and sideband features.

3. **Spontaneous emission pictures**: The bare basis describes antibunching (temporal view), while the dressed basis describes alternation between blue and red detuned sidebands (spectral view). These are complementary.

4. **Stimulated/dipole force**: Atoms in the two dressed levels experience opposite forces. Population imbalance creates net force—attractive for red detuning, repulsive for blue detuning.

5. **Cooling via time lag**: Non-adiabaticity creates friction. For blue-detuned light, the population lag causes extra force opposing motion, producing "blue molasses" cooling.

6. **Heating**: Force fluctuations when atoms switch dressed levels cause momentum diffusion, dominant over photon recoil in strong fields.

7. **Sisyphus cooling**: In a blue-detuned standing wave, atoms preferentially emit at potential hilltops and land at valleys, continuously climbing hills and losing kinetic energy.

8. **Perturbative limit**: Simple derivations yield the friction coefficient, diffusion coefficient, and the key result that minimum temperature equals lattice depth—preventing localization of two-level atoms in optical lattices via laser cooling alone.

9. **Dipole potential interpretations**: Can be derived from Optical Bloch Equations, dressed atom picture, AC polarizability, or macroscopic refraction (applicable to optical tweezers in biology).

Russ Tedrake's lecture introduces trajectory optimization as an extension of policy search methods, focusing on open-loop control policies parameterized by vectors of control actions.

The lecture covers two main approaches:

**Shooting Methods**: These simulate the system forward from initial conditions and iteratively adjust parameters. Two gradient computation techniques are presented:
- Back-propagation through time (BPTT)/adjoint method: simulates forward, then backward, carrying a vector the size of x
- Real-time recurrent learning (RTRL): only simulates forward while carrying a matrix of partial derivatives (∂x/∂α)

The trade-off is that BPTT carries less data but requires forward-backward passes, while RTRL works forward-only but carries a larger matrix.

**Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP)**, specifically SNOPT, is recommended over simple gradient descent because it eliminates learning rate tuning, offers faster convergence, and efficiently handles constraints.

**Direct Collocation (DIRCOL)**: Augments the parameter vector with state variables, adding explicit constraints ensuring consistency between states and dynamics. This avoids explicit simulation, enables efficient gradient computation, and allows strategic initialization to escape local minima. Its main drawback is reliance on fixed-step integration, reducing accuracy compared to shooting methods.

Demonstrations with pendulum, acrobot, and a path-planning problem illustrate the methods. Local minima exist but Tedrake argues they are typically not problematic for most applications.

Upcoming topics include trajectory stabilization via LQR, iterative LQR methods, and possibly discrete mechanics approaches.

This retrospective study analyzed 377 percutaneous tracheostomies performed on intubated COVID-19 patients at Jaber Al Ahmad Al Sabah Hospital in Kuwait between March 2020 and March 2022, reportedly the largest single-center series of its kind. The department chose the percutaneous bedside technique over open tracheostomy to reduce staff exposure, cross-contamination, and the need for patient transfer. Procedures were generally performed after 7 days of intubation, under bronchoscopy guidance with a team of up to five staff members using full personal protective equipment.

Patients had a mean age of 56.2 years and mean BMI of 31.3, with 59% male. Common comorbidities included diabetes (50%) and hypertension (48%); 29% were on ECMO and 23% on dialysis. The mean interval from intubation to tracheostomy was 17.4 days. Complications occurred in 23% of cases, most commonly minor bleeding (14%), followed by tracheo-esophageal fistulae (2%) and peristomal infections (2%). Post-tracheostomy, 54% of patients were weaned from sedation (mean 7.5 days) and 41% from mechanical ventilation (mean 12.9 days). Overall mortality was 63%, all attributed to COVID-19 complications rather than the procedure; hypertension and age over 65 were significantly associated with increased mortality risk.

The authors conclude that percutaneous tracheostomy can be performed safely in COVID-19 patients and recommend performing it soon after the 7th day of intubation, though the optimal timing remains debated. Limitations include the absence of a comparison group undergoing open tracheostomy, lack of long-term follow-up, and absence of PCR testing to confirm staff safety.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition device. It is powered down via the PWDN pin or by writing 11b to the PD_CH field, and reset via the RESET pin or RESET field. After power-up or reset, the device requires an initialization sequence of register writes with a free-running sampling clock connected.

The device supports a speed-boost mode allowing up to 8MSPS for a user-selected analog input channel pair, while the other six channels remain idle. Registers are organized in three banks, addressable via 8-bit addresses, with bank 0 always accessible. Register writes require selecting a bank (via address 0x03) then writing data, while reads require enabling SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE bits.

Multiple devices can be connected in a daisy-chain topology, sharing CS and SCLK, with SDI/SDO connected sequentially. Daisy-chain operations require N × 24 SCLKs per frame, where N is the number of ADCs.

The ADS9803 has three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence, and offers low-noise (22.7kHz) and wide-bandwidth (700kHz) modes. Post-calibration TUE is 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. Layout recommendations include using 0.1μF bypass capacitors near supply pins and keeping analog signals away from digital lines.

Yale-New Haven Hospital brought three collection actions against Mitchell and Wilczynski for unpaid medical services. The defendants raised special defenses and counterclaims alleging violations of the Hill-Burton Act and Connecticut's hospital bed funds statute, and asserting CUTPA claims based on those violations. The hospital moved for summary judgment, arguing the defenses were legally invalid and no private cause of action existed under either statute.

The court denied the motions, holding that indigent patients have a private right of action under the Hill-Burton Act and may raise noncompliance as a special defense in collection suits, finding cases such as Euresti v. Stenner and Hospital Center at Orange v. Cook more persuasive than Yale-New Haven Hospital v. Matthews. Applying the Cort v. Ash test, the court also found a private right of action under the hospital bed funds statute.

The court further held that CUTPA claims can be based on violations of statutes lacking private causes of action, citing Mead v. Burns and Conaway v. Prestia, and that factual issues regarding unfair practices precluded summary judgment. The court rejected the claim that the Hill-Burton Act preempts CUTPA.

The NHS offers cancer screening to detect early signs of cancer in people without symptoms, which Cancer Research UK estimates has saved around 90,000 lives in the past five years. Dr Alexandra Moorhouse explains that the UK has three main screening programmes:

- **Cervical screening**: Offered every five years to women and people with a cervix aged 25–64, testing for high-risk HPV strains linked to cervical and other cancers.
- **Breast screening**: Offered every three years to women aged 50–71 using a mammogram. Those over 71 can self-refer, and younger people with concerns should consult a doctor.
- **Bowel screening**: Offered every two years to people aged 50–74 via a home FIT kit that detects blood in stool samples. Positive results lead to a colonoscopy referral.

Screening can detect cancer or pre-cancerous changes early, improving treatment success and survival rates, particularly for breast, bowel, and cervical cancers. Invitations are sent automatically by post when eligible, and missed letters can be followed up through local services.

People with conditions like Neurofibromatosis type 1 may qualify for earlier screening (e.g., mammograms from age 40). Private screening is available for those outside NHS eligibility criteria or with family history concerns. Individuals worried about symptoms should consult their doctor without waiting for routine invitations.
