The report outlines the United States' longstanding policy opposing foreign aggression in Hawaii and considering annexation as a contingent necessity. Key developments include: Lord Palmerston's 1850 suggestion of U.S. protectorate or annexation; an 1851 contingent deed of cession signed by the Hawaiian king; Mr. Marcy's 1854 draft annexation treaty, defeated by Kamehameha III's death; Mr. Seward's 1867 instructions favoring annexation over reciprocity; President Johnson's 1868 anticipation of voluntary Hawaiian application for Union admission; President Grant's 1871 Senate inquiry on annexation; and Mr. Fish's 1873 directive encouraging annexation sentiment. After the 1875 reciprocity treaty, U.S. policy defended exclusive commercial rights and supported the Hawaiian Government. In 1881, Mr. Blaine emphasized Hawaii's strategic importance, pledging an "American solution" if benevolent neutrality became impracticable. The report, submitted by John W. Foster on February 15, 1893, accompanies Andrew H. Allen's report on U.S.-Hawaiian relations beginning with John C. Jones's 1820 appointment as commercial agent.

Which? argues that official mpg figures cannot be trusted, as the current New European Driving Cycle (NEDC), unchanged since 1997, contains numerous loopholes. These include no sustained motorway driving, tests conducted with ancillary loads off, permitted removal of parts, unrestricted tyre pressures, allowed use of eco modes, no policing body, and a 4% reduction applied to results. From September 2017, the tougher Worldwide-harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) will replace the NEDC, with full compliance required by September 2018.

Which? uses the WLTP in its own lab tests, running cold, hot and motorway cycles with realistic conditions—default driving mode, air conditioning on, standard tyre pressures, and no result adjustments. Hybrid and plug-in hybrid cars are tested using adapted procedures. Air-polluting emissions (NOx, CO, HC, PM) are also measured, and suspicious results trigger additional on-road testing using a Portable Emissions Measuring System (PEMS) to detect cheating, following the 2015 Volkswagen scandal. Which? has reviewed over 700 vehicles, testing around 120 new cars annually.

Anthurium, originating from South America, is a flowering plant that filters ammonia and xylene from indoor air. Its red, pink, or white heart-shaped blossoms have earned it the nickname "tongues of fire," though its sap and leaves can trigger allergies. The plant thrives in bright, indirect light and damp conditions, ideally near a window at 18–21°C. It requires leaf misting in winter and annual repotting in a pot with a drainage hole, reduced to every two years as it matures.

The COVID-19 pandemic prompted widespread business and school closures globally. While many U.S. colleges reopened in fall 2020 with in-person, online, or hybrid teaching plans, concerns arose about virus transmission from campuses to surrounding communities, despite students' lower death rates. This study uses a quasi-experimental approach to examine how teaching modality impacts COVID-19 cases and deaths in neighboring areas, matching similar colleges that chose different modalities. Results indicate that in-person reopening increases COVID-19 cases and deaths over time.

Prior research largely focused on K-12 school closures with mixed findings. Unlike earlier studies using difference-in-difference methods, this study addresses endogeneity issues—teaching modality choices were often influenced by pre-existing COVID rates. The authors leverage varied reopening dates and cellphone mobility data, using methods that re-weight samples based on modality selection probability. Outcomes are measured at the county level, reflecting concerns about transmission to non-students and vulnerable populations.

Austria-Hungary faces serious post-war economic risks, including demobilization and financial burdens. In Bulgaria, satisfying her claims—now that Russian occupation of Constantinople is no longer a threat—could prevent her exploitation, aided by the influence of the Russian revolution. In Turkey, Allied military successes and Turkey's economic weakness are key assets. German colonies and exclusion from the Pacific and Americas offer bargaining material. The Russian revolution poses dangers to German domination through anti-capitalist, religious, and nationalist sentiments, and acts as a dissolving example elsewhere. The Vatican, though pro-German in neutrality, could be leveraged with skilful handling. American manpower and resources guarantee eventual military victory. Intangible assets include the universal desire for peace, rejection of old diplomacy, hope for a league of nations, and fears of social revolution tied to war debts. German policy, having shifted from Italy to Constantinople and now eastward following Russia's collapse, may lead Germany to accept concessions elsewhere to secure Russian opportunities.

The paper presents a hierarchical Bayesian multinomial modeling approach for estimating competing viral variant dynamics and relative fitness advantages, addressing limitations of standard regression methods when genomic data are sparse or geographically uneven. Analysis of GISAID data showed that 10% of countries contributed 90.3% of SARS-CoV-2 sequences, with sequencing of emerging variants concentrated in high-capacity countries. By pooling information across countries and variants, the model produces country-specific and global estimates of variant proportions, growth rates, and fitness advantages, with shrinkage reducing overfitting to noisy emergence data. Applied to Omicron sublineages, the model estimated BA.5 as having the highest global fitness advantage relative to BA.2, followed by BA.4 and BA.2.12.1, while BA.1 was less fit. Retrospective validation using BA.5 emergence in Portugal showed the multicountry model produced more stable estimates and lower Brier scores than single-country multinomial regression, particularly early after variant emergence. The authors note assumptions including random sampling, accurate lineage assignment, and constant relative fitness over the modeled period. The method is extensible to other pathogens and sub-national scales, complementing sequencing capacity investments.

President Johnson announces the appointment of a special Advisory Commission on Civil Disorders, chaired by Governor Otto Kerner, to investigate the origins of recent urban riots and recommend preventive measures. He condemns the looting, arson, and violence as crimes unrelated to civil rights protests, stating that offenders must be punished. He has directed the Secretary of Defense to issue new riot control training standards for the National Guard.

Johnson argues that lasting peace requires more than force; it demands attacking root conditions like poverty, discrimination, slums, and unemployment. He cites past legislative achievements, including the Voting Rights Act, Model Cities Act, Medicare, and education bills, while criticizing Congress for rejecting funding for rat control, model cities, and other urban programs.

He emphasizes that most Americans, Black and white, live peacefully, and that law-abiding Black families have suffered most from the rioting. Johnson announces a national day of prayer on July 30 and calls on citizens, officials, and community leaders to reject violence, support peaceful change, and work toward better jobs, housing, and education.

The paper studies Gorenstein-projective modules over the ring Z[ε] of dual integers (Z[T]/(T²)), focusing on finitely generated right modules since full classification is infeasible.

The category G-proj Z[ε] is shown to be equivalent to several categories: torsionless Z[ε]-modules, perfect differential structures of abelian groups, and orbits of bounded complexes of free abelian groups. It lacks the Krull-Remak-Schmidt property.

The main result (Theorem 1.2.1) establishes equivalences between: the stable category G-proj Z[ε], the stable category sub(Z[ε]) of submodules of free Z[ε]-modules modulo projectives, the orbit category Db(Z)/[1], the homotopy category of perfect differential structures, and the stable category of perfect differential structures. The result extends to any principal ideal domain.

These categories form a chain connected by dense functors, starting from bounded complexes of free abelian groups Cb(F) and ending at finite abelian groups. Three functor types are involved: modulo shift (σ), modulo projectives (π), and modulo stalk-factoring maps (ϕ). Their compositions yield a cube with commutative square faces.

Thiel's views trace back to an Austrian theologist influenced by Nazi-era legal theorist Carl Schmitt. Critics note the irony given Thiel co-founded surveillance company Palantir.

Reporter Aarian Marshall found Tesla is prompting drowsy drivers to engage Full Self-Driving mode, despite the manual requiring drivers to remain alert. This contrasts with Tesla's prior safety efforts and comes after a Florida jury found the company partly liable for a fatal 2019 crash.

Science reporter Emily Mullin reported that scientists created human eggs from skin cells and formed embryos, potentially offering an IVF alternative, though bioethicists warn of embryo farming concerns.

The main story covers OpenAI's launch of Sora 2, a TikTok-like social app featuring only AI-generated videos. Users verify their identity to create digital avatars. Guardrails block nudity and unauthorized likeness use, though copyright enforcement appears inconsistent.

Vodafone Ghana staff member Eunice Ampomah-Manu is credited with saving the life of customer Andrew Kufuor, a cousin of former President J. A. Kufuor. During a routine customer check-up call, Mr. Kufuor suffered an attack and told Eunice he was dying. She kept him on the line for about ten minutes, obtained his wife's number, and called her. His wife rushed home and took him to a clinic for treatment. Mr. Kufuor later visited Vodafone's headquarters to personally thank Eunice. CEO Yolanda Cuba stated that providing exceptional customer experience is central to the company's values.

Australia faces the United States in a Davis Cup quarter-final in Brisbane, with Nick Kyrgios drawn to play John Isner in singles, following Jack Sock's match against Jordan Thompson. Kyrgios and Isner are tied for third on the ATP aces leaderboard with 218 this season. Sam Groth and John Peers will play Sam Querrey and Steve Johnson in Saturday's doubles. Isner leads Kyrgios 2-1 in past meetings, while Sock has never faced Kyrgios. Thompson replaces Bernard Tomic, who declined to play. Between them, the countries hold 60 Davis Cup titles, though neither has won recently.

Advances in information technology have expanded usage scenarios in industrial development and manufacturing. Over half of surveyed industrial decision makers use simulation, modeling, and virtual prototyping, while 42% use high-performance data analytics. Digital twins, IT-based design optimization, and digital verification and validation enable faster development and feedback loops between physical and digital processes.

Key technology trends include data visualization via cloud-based engineering workstations, digital twins for monitoring and simulating scenarios, and integration of multiple IT solutions to support diverse workloads.

Industrial simulation relies on complex calculations, often creating trade-offs between speed and accuracy. Currently, 8% of respondents report high demand for high-performance calculations, rising to nearly 50% in two years. Half report that calculations take too long.

81% of respondents view HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation. HPC enables complex calculations, improves quality and intensity of use, unlocks new scenarios, and increases agility. Over a quarter of surveyed enterprises already use professional HPC infrastructure, with 39% piloting deployment.

Challenges include security concerns (72%), high energy consumption (58%), costs, computing power limitations, availability issues, and expertise shortages (42%). Most HPC users (87%) prefer external HPC infrastructure, while 74% use colocation datacenters.

Cloud-based HPC architectures, particularly public and hybrid clouds, are expected to dominate. HPCaaS offers cost flexibility, scalability, modernity, and supports new business models. 81% of current HPC users intend to implement HPC-based business models.

IDC recommends establishing virtual development processes, creating a holistic data strategy with a single source of truth, evaluating suitable HPC operating models, prioritizing scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise.

The findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 decision makers from industrial enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on January 25, 2022, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2021. The press release is included as Exhibit 99.1. Microsoft, incorporated in Washington and headquartered in Redmond, has common stock and two sets of notes (3.125% due 2028 and 2.625% due 2033) registered on NASDAQ. The report was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for demonstrating quantum effects in an electric circuit during the 1980s. Using a Josephson junction chilled to very cold temperatures, they showed quantum tunneling and energy quantization involving billions of electrons, challenging the notion that such effects occur only at atomic scales. Their work forms the foundation for superconducting qubits used in quantum computers. The three share the 11 million Swedish kronor prize. Martinis later led Google's quantum computing effort, which in 2019 claimed to have performed a calculation beyond traditional computers' reach.

Enron shares fell to eight-year lows after Moody's downgraded the company's long-term debt rating to Baa2, two notches above junk status, and placed its commercial paper rating under review. The decline followed Enron's disclosure of $1.01 billion in third-quarter losses, a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, and an SEC inquiry into off-balance-sheet partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, who was ousted and replaced by Jeff McMahon. Enron was seeking additional credit lines after tapping $3.3 billion previously. Insurance premiums on Enron bonds doubled, and utilities including AEP, Exelon, and Northeast Utilities said they were monitoring their trading exposure.

In a prior interview, McMahon discussed Enron Industrial Markets' forest products trading, noting newsprint volumes grew from under 5,000 tons in January to 60,000 tons in July, with expectations of 120,000 tons by year-end. Enron spokesperson Karen Denne said the forest products venture would continue despite company struggles.

U.S. stocks also slumped broadly after consumer confidence dropped to a seven-year low. Separately, Germany's cartel office threatened legal action against four utilities over balancing energy charges affecting competitors including Enron Capital & Resources.

The passage details design considerations for a push-pull converter using the TPS7H500x-SP controllers.

Section 9.2.2.8 describes selecting an 80-V GaN FET for synchronous rectification, with a parallel Schottky diode to reduce soft-start current and reverse conduction losses. Section 9.2.2.9 explains an RCD clamp circuit to limit switch node voltage, using KCLAMP to define overshoot tolerance. Section 9.2.2.10 targets 40% ripple current, selecting a 0.47 μH output inductor. Section 9.2.2.11 describes calculating output capacitance based on load transients and voltage ripple, requiring at least 1.3 mF; 2.3 mF total was used to mitigate radiation-induced single event transients. An optional secondary output filter can further reduce noise.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting activates at ~35 A, with a 7.5-Ω RCS resistor selected. Section 9.2.2.13 uses a 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor. Section 9.2.2.14 uses Type 2A compensation targeting 10 kHz crossover, with RCOMP = 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP = 15 nF, and CHF = 47 pF. Section 9.2.2.15 sets slope compensation via a 102 kΩ resistor on RSC.

Power supply recommendations specify a 4–14 V input with a minimum 0.1 µF bypass capacitor. Layout guidelines emphasize routing feedback away from noise sources, minimizing switch node area, separating analog and power grounds, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, and filtering the CS_ILIM signal. The document also includes package, orderable, and revision history information.

The MSPM0 G-Series 80MHz microcontroller integrates multiple functional units. The Power Management Unit (PMU) regulates core supplies, monitors VDD, and includes brown-out reset and parity-protected trim. The Clock Module (CKM) provides oscillators (LFOSC, SYSOSC, LFXT, HFXT, SYSPLL) and distributes clocks like MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, and others to peripherals.

The DMA controller supports 12 channels for memory transfers without CPU intervention, with configurable triggers and transfer sizes up to 128-bit. The Event manager routes digital events between peripherals, DMA, and CPU.

Memory includes dual-bank flash (up to 512kB) with ECC, and 128KB SRAM split into two 64kB banks with optional ECC. GPIO supports up to 93 pins with wake functionality, configured via IOMUX.

Analog peripherals include two 12-bit ADCs (4Msps), a temperature sensor, VREF module, comparators, and a 12-bit DAC. Security features include AES-128/256, TRNG, Keystore (4 keys), CRC, and firewalls. The MATHACL accelerates 32-bit math functions.

Communication peripherals include UART (with LIN support), I2C (up to 1Mbit/s), SPI (up to 32Mbit/s), and CAN-FD (up to 5Mbit/s). The LFSS contains RTC_B and IWDT_B for low-power timekeeping and watchdog functions. A separate WWDT provides windowed watchdog capability. General-purpose (TIMGx) and advanced (TIMAx) timers support PWM, quadrature encoding, and fault handling.

Debug uses a serial wire interface, while the bootstrap loader (BSL) enables UART/I2C programming with password protection. Factory constants provide device identification and trim data. Typical applications require decoupling capacitors, NRST pullup, and a VCORE tank capacitor.

The Open Source Definition (OSD) was published approximately twenty years ago, establishing a framework for open source software development. The Open Source Initiative dates its inception to February 3, 1998, when Christine Peterson proposed the term "open source" during a meeting prompted by Netscape's decision to release its source code. The term was chosen as an alternative to "free software," which required clarification that "free" meant liberty, not price. Other suggested terms included "sourceware" and "freely distributable." Bruce Perens, who drafted the Debian Free Software Guidelines that became the OSD, dates the movement to February 9, 1998. Perens described open source as a way to promote free software concepts to business audiences. Major technology companies including Apple, Amazon, Facebook, Google, and Microsoft now rely on open source software. Microsoft's embrace is notable given former CEO Steve Ballmer's 2001 comparison of Linux to cancer. Red Hat's Tim Burke stated that open source has shifted from cloning proprietary software to leading innovation.

Ambassador Bernstorff informed the recipient that Germany's blockade would end if a conference could be arranged on reasonable terms. Ambassador Gerard reported that Zimmermann delivered a submarine note and memorandum, urging President Wilson to remain inactive for two months while Germany used submarine warfare to force England to seek terms. Zimmermann warned of an exhausted Europe facing Japan and other "yellow races" if peace failed. Minister Droppers reported Greek developments regarding Entente concessions on victuals and rifle accounting. Gerard later reported German peace terms including retention of guarantees in Belgium, French frontier adjustments, partial return of Serbia, Bulgarian control over Romania, and indemnities to Germany. Ambassador Penfield transmitted a message from Austria-Hungary's Foreign Minister stating they sought a defensive war and "peace without victory" per Wilson's proposal, but could not discuss peace while the Entente aimed at dismembering Austria-Hungary. Modification of submarine warfare was deemed impossible due to allied consultation requirements and submarines already deployed being unreachable. The Minister urged Wilson to pressure the Entente to accept his proposed peace basis.

Storage, particularly batteries, has been promoted as a way to integrate renewable energy into electricity grids. Storage systems involve capital and running costs, and must deliver savings exceeding these costs to be economical. Various technologies exist, each suited to different applications: lithium ion batteries for small-scale distributed use, pumped hydro for large-scale grid management, and flywheels for voltage and frequency control.

Lithium ion battery costs have halved in five years to US$600 per kWh. For a home with rooftop PV and variable tariffs, batteries need to cost around A$1,000 per kWh to break even; current costs are A$1,000-3,000 per kWh. If retailers flatten tariffs in response to losing market share, batteries would need to drop to around A$300 per kWh. Claimed network savings from reduced peak demand only apply where demand is growing, which is not the case in Australia's National Electricity Market since 2009.

Pumped hydro is cheaper at around A$100 per kWh, with 1,500 MW already operating in the market. Although pumped hydro is more economical, distributed lithium ion batteries may prevail due to human behaviour rather than economics.

The article reflects on a photograph of Ernest Walton, joint winner of the 1951 Nobel Prize for physics, taken in a lab at Trinity College Dublin. Part of an Irish Times Portrait Gallery series, the unsigned feature described Walton as a quiet, shy man in his early 50s who declined opportunities abroad due to his fondness for Ireland. The piece briefly referenced his achievement of splitting the atom at Cambridge's Cavendish Lab in the 1930s, noting its complexity for laypeople. Jack McManus's accompanying photograph gives equal prominence to Walton and his equipment, with the scientist appearing guarded. The author contrasts this understated tone with contemporary coverage of Cern's Higgs boson research.

On August 3, 2020, Apple Inc. filed an amendment to its Restated Articles of Incorporation with the California Secretary of State, increasing authorized common stock shares from 12,600,000,000 to 50,400,000,000. The amendment also provided for a four-for-one stock split, effective at 5 p.m. Pacific daylight time on August 28, 2020, occurring automatically without action by shareholders. The Form 8-K was signed by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary, on August 7, 2020.

Bitcoin futures trading was set to launch on Cboe Global Markets' Cboe Futures Exchange, offering a regulated way to bet on or hedge against the cryptocurrency's price swings. The cash-settled contracts are based on bitcoin's auction price on the Gemini Exchange. The launch has fueled bitcoin's price surge, which nearly doubled since December despite sharp volatility. Reception among US banks and brokerages is mixed: Interactive Brokers will offer access with restrictions, while Charles Schwab and TD Ameritrade will not initially allow trading. JPMorgan and Citigroup will not immediately clear bitcoin trades, while Goldman Sachs plans to clear futures for certain clients. Analysts suggest futures may eventually reduce volatility and improve price discovery, but warn of risks including inaccurate pricing, systemic risk to clearing houses, and potential market manipulation.

The Korean Diet (K-Diet) is based on traditional Korean eating habits, focusing on whole, unprocessed foods, fresh vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and fermented foods like kimchi. It is low in sugar, unhealthy fats, and dairy, with smaller portion sizes than Western diets.

Permitted foods include rice, barley, noodles, various vegetables, fermented products (doenjang, gochujang, miso), and seasonings like soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger. Processed foods, sugary drinks, and unhealthy fats are minimised.

According to nutrition experts Dr Nilda Abellera and Bharathi Ramesh, benefits include weight loss support, improved digestion from probiotics, and antioxidants from plant-based ingredients. The diet can be adapted for vegan, low-carb, or gluten-free lifestyles.

Drawbacks include high sodium content from fermented foods, low calcium due to minimal dairy, and high carbohydrate levels, which may affect people with high blood pressure, digestive issues, or blood sugar concerns. Portion control and sodium monitoring are recommended.

New soccer players require guidance on general team tactics, including positioning, ball work, and team functions. CoachingAmericanSoccer.com provides General "Rules of the Road" for on-field play, intended for both new players and coaches. The list complements instruction on positions and positioning and can be adapted to suit a coach's personal preferences and style.

The manual explains how to use the Sansa® Fuze™ player, covering file transfers, playback, settings, and support information.

**Transferring Files:** Music can be transferred via drag-and-drop through Windows Explorer or using Windows Media Player (WMP), which requires adding files to the library and creating playlists for synchronization. Audible.com files require Audible Manager. Photos and videos must be converted and transferred using the Sansa Media Converter software, downloadable from SanDisk's website. Photos and videos should not be converted simultaneously.

**Playback:** The player supports MP3, WMA, secure WMA, and Audible formats for music, audiobooks, and podcasts. Users navigate via the Home button, thumbwheel, and Submenu button to play content, adjust volume, skip tracks, and access options like Repeat, Shuffle, MusicEQ, Go Lists, and Delete. Videos and photos are accessed similarly, with options to bookmark, rate, adjust brightness, and create slideshows with music, shuffle, loop, and adjustable slide duration.

**FM Radio and Recording:** The integrated FM radio (region-dependent) allows tuning, storing up to 30 presets, auto-preset scanning, and recording. The built-in microphone enables voice recording for personal use.

**Deleting and Settings:** Content can be deleted directly from the player or via computer. System Settings allow customization of wallpaper, backlight timer, power saver, language, date/time, brightness, volume, USB mode (Auto Detect, MTP, or MSC), and factory reset. Formatting deletes all content.

**Support:** Troubleshooting tips cover supported bit rates (32–320 Kbps MP3, 32–256 Kbps WMA), firmware updates, microSD/microSDHC compatibility, and power reset (hold power button ~10 seconds). SanDisk offers a one-year limited warranty to original purchasers, excluding damage from misuse or unauthorized repair. The software is licensed under restricted terms governed by California law, with disclaimers on warranties, liability limits, and prohibitions on reverse engineering, transfer, or use in high-risk applications.

The speaker expresses concern for Mr. Horton and Aaron, hoping Horton makes a full recovery, while noting the team must move on. They reference a tough loss in Chicago during the first round and emphasize their mentality of focusing on the next game. Despite a strong first period, the opponents got lucky bounces, including a goal after a stick broke, leading to easy goals. The speaker states a few things need to change but dismisses the series as nothing unusual, noting all three series played have been hard fought.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition device supporting a speed-boost mode that enables up to 8MSPS sampling on a user-selected analog input channel pair, while the other six channels remain idle.

Register access uses 16-bit configuration registers grouped in three banks addressable by 8-bit addresses. Writes require selecting a bank via register 0x03 (except bank 0), then writing to the target register. Reads require setting SPI_RD_EN=1 and SPI_MODE=1, followed by two 24-bit SPI frames.

In daisy-chain topology, multiple ADCs share CS and SCLK, with SDI/SDO chained sequentially. Daisy-chain mode is enabled via the DAISY_CHAIN_LEN register, and register operations require N×24 SCLKs per frame.

The device includes registers for data format, averaging, test patterns, gain error correction, bandwidth selection, common-mode range, and PGA initialization. It has three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence, and offers low-noise (22.7kHz) and wide-bandwidth (700kHz) modes. Post-calibration TUE is 0.0015% at 25°C, suitable for ATE applications.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K Current Report with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on October 28, 2021. The filing reported that Apple issued a press release regarding its financial results for the fourth fiscal quarter ended September 25, 2021, attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report lists Apple's common stock and various notes registered on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC. The filing was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

This retrospective study analyzed 109 patients who underwent aneurysm obliteration treatment following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) at Kaohsiung Veterans General Hospital between January 2013 and October 2021, aiming to develop a predictive model for shunt-dependent hydrocephalus (SDHC).

Patient data including age, gender, BMI, treatment modality, neurological deficits, laboratory values (eGFR, NLR, PLR, PNR), aneurysm location, Fisher grade, and Hunt and Hess scale (HHS) were analyzed. All patients received external ventricular drainage (EVD) and underwent an EVD challenge 1–4 weeks after aSAH; those who failed or developed hydrocephalus after removal received ventriculoperitoneal shunts.

Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified three significant risk factors for SDHC: age ≥65 years (OR 3.94), surgical clipping versus coiling (OR 4.36), and HHS ≥3 (OR 3.59). The predictive model had an AUC of 0.753. Fisher grade, aneurysm location, and inflammatory ratios were not significant predictors in this cohort; the authors attribute the Fisher grade finding to universal EVD placement.

A nomogram incorporating these three factors was developed to estimate individual SDHC risk. Study limitations include its retrospective design and limited sample size, requiring prospective validation.

Nike reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $11.72 billion, a 1% increase year-over-year, surpassing Wall Street expectations and its own projection of a mid-single digit decline. However, net income fell 31% to $727 million, and gross margin dropped 3.2 percentage points to 42.2%, reflecting ongoing efforts to clear old inventory through discounting.

CEO Elliott Hill highlighted progress in wholesale (up 7%), running, and North America (up 4% to $5.02 billion). Nike direct sales fell 4%, and China revenue dropped 9%. CFO Matt Friend cautioned that "progress will not be linear."

Hill's turnaround strategy includes inventory clearance, restructuring teams by sport rather than demographic, and expanding female customers through partnerships like NikeSKIMS, which launched recently.

Miami Dolphins wide receiver Tyreek Hill dislocated his knee during Monday night's game against the Jets and was carted off the field after his left leg twisted under him following a 10-yard reception in the third quarter. He is undergoing further tests and will remain hospitalized overnight. Hill had 67 receiving yards on six catches before the injury and entered the game leading the Dolphins with 198 receiving yards. According to coach McDaniel, Hill was in good spirits and told the team to secure the win, which was their first of the season. Since entering the NFL in 2017, Hill has 11,363 receiving yards, the most in the league, along with 819 catches and 83 touchdown receptions.

An international team of scientists is studying live specimens of Kuphus polythalamia, a giant shipworm found in a Philippine lagoon on an abandoned log farm. Though known for centuries, live specimens had been difficult to obtain. Published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the research examines microbes in the bivalve's single gill in hopes of discovering new antimicrobial substances. Unlike related species that consume rotting wood, K. polythalamia burrows into mud and consumes hydrogen sulfide, which its microbes convert to carbon. Researchers, including Margo Haygood, Marvin Altamia, and Daniel Distel, note uncertainty about the animal's life cycle and age. Its tusk-like shells can reach five feet in length. Distel believes the giant shipworm evolved from wood-eating ancestors.

The DAX 40 is Germany's main stock market index, comprising 40 blue-chip companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, founded in July 1988 with a $1,250 billion market capitalization. Since inception, it has returned 5.36% annually. U.S. investors can access the German market via the iShares MSCI Germany ETF (EWG), which holds large and mid-size German companies and charges a 0.50% expense ratio.

Historical monthly returns of EWG since 1996 show the final quarter as the best-performing period, while the rest of the year trades sideways. Based on this, a seasonal strategy was developed that invests only during the last three months of each year. Backtesting with dividend- and split-adjusted data since EWG's inception showed the strategy outperformed buy-and-hold.

Climate change is warming high-altitude streams in the northern Rocky Mountains, threatening native cutthroat trout. Previously, cold water protected cutthroats from rainbow trout, which prefer warmer conditions. Now, rainbows are invading cutthroat habitats and interbreeding with them, producing weaker hybrid offspring. Ecologist Clint Muhlfeld of the U.S. Geological Survey, writing in Global Change Biology, reports widespread hybridization across hundreds of sites, especially where rainbow trout were introduced by fish and game departments. Some states are removing rainbows to preserve cutthroats, which Muhlfeld warns could otherwise go extinct permanently.

Christian Nwosu, a former INEC Administrative Secretary in Kwara state, has told a Lagos Federal High Court that EFCC operatives coerced him into admitting he received N30 million from former Petroleum Minister Diezani Alison-Madueke. Testifying before Justice Mohammed Idris, Nwosu alleged that operative Usman Zakari threatened him with detention unless he wrote a statement dictated by him, claiming another officer, Adedoyin, had admitted to collecting N28 million and been released. Nwosu said he was escorted by the operative and armed police to a bank, where he issued drafts totaling N5 million to the commission, and was also made to surrender property worth N30 million. He further alleged that EFCC prosecutor Rotimi Oyedepo advised him to cooperate to avoid litigation, conviction, and imprisonment.

A nationwide study published in the October 1, 2025 issue of the American Academy of Neurology's medical journal links long-term outdoor exposure to trichloroethylene (TCE) with increased Parkinson's disease risk in older adults. TCE is an industrial solvent used in metal degreasing and dry cleaning that persists in air, water and soil across the U.S.

Researchers led by Brittany Krzyzanowski of Barrow Neurological Institute used Medicare data to identify 221,789 people over 67 newly diagnosed with Parkinson's between 2016 and 2018, comparing them with over 1.1 million people without the disease. TCE exposure was estimated using EPA data and participants' ZIP+4 locations two years before diagnosis.

After adjusting for factors including age, smoking, and particulate pollution, those in the highest TCE exposure group had a 10% increased Parkinson's risk versus the lowest. Geographic hot spots were identified, particularly in the Rust Belt. The study shows association, not causation. Limitations include focus on Medicare-aged individuals and reliance on 2002 outdoor air estimates.

State Street Corporation, the firm that commissioned the "Fearless Girl" statue on Wall Street, has agreed to pay $5 million to settle U.S. Department of Labor claims that it paid 305 female employees and 15 black vice presidents less than their male and white counterparts in equivalent positions. The settlement includes approximately $4.5 million in back pay and $500,000 in interest. State Street denies the allegations but stated it is committed to equal pay practices. The "Fearless Girl" statue was installed in March opposite the "Charging Bull" to promote State Street Global Advisors and a gender diversity stock index called SHE. Sculptor Arturo Di Modica had complained that "Fearless Girl" distorted the bull's intended message.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis have been awarded the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for demonstrating quantum effects in an electric circuit, achieving these effects at a scale previously considered impossible.

A swimming advisory was issued Friday for Little Beach in Port Stanley due to high bacteria levels and remained in effect Monday. According to Cathie Walker of the Elgin St. Thomas Health Unit, an advisory warns of potential health risks such as gastrointestinal illness, but does not close the beach, as the bacteria threshold for closure has not been met. Swimming remains a personal choice. Beachgoer Terrie Vergiris said she did not notice the signs and continued to let her children swim, believing Little Beach is safer than the main beach. Advisories are posted on the health unit's website.

Sir John Deane's sixth form college held its fourth annual Evening of Jazz and Soul at the Macdonald Portal Hotel, Golf and Spa in Tarporley. Directed by Timothy Murphy, the 35-strong jazz collective performed 60s soul and classic swing pieces. Head of performing arts Alison Richards praised the vocalists and instrumentalists, noting they had only been performing together for a few months. The college's next event, an evening of classical music featuring 14 students, will take place at Arley Hall on February 9, with tickets priced at £8 (£6 concessions).

Norwich children Evan and Brynn Meek, ages 10 and 6, traveled to New York City on August 6 and distributed 220 bagged lunches to homeless people in Manhattan after being moved by their mother Stephanie's account of homelessness there.

In a separate story, Norwich Police Department officer Thomas Miller, an eight-year veteran, was sworn in with the Syracuse Police Department on August 10. During his tenure, Miller and his K9 Nitro participated in numerous community events. Miller personally funded Nitro's training and food until Vance offered to supply her food.

Additionally, Tracy A. Price, 31, of Norwich, was arrested August 16 on a warrant for torturing, injuring, and neglecting a dog, and was granted $750 bail.

Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden have used machine learning and computer simulations to reveal the low-temperature structure of formamidinium lead iodide, a halide perovskite material considered promising for efficient, flexible, and lightweight solar cells. Although the material has excellent optoelectronic properties, its instability has limited its use, and mixing it with another halide perovskite may solve this issue. By combining standard methods with machine learning, the team ran simulations thousands of times longer and with millions of atoms, identifying that formamidinium molecules become stuck in a semi-stable state during cooling. The findings were validated experimentally with collaborators at the University of Birmingham and published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society.

A 36-year-old New York man, Reinaldo De Jesus Henao, was arrested at the Coachella Art and Music Festival on suspicion of stealing over 100 cellphones. Victims used the "Find my iPhone" feature to track him, and some followed him until security detained him. Police recovered the phones from his backpack, returning some to owners and placing the rest in lost and found. Henao faces grand theft and possession of stolen property charges. Indio Police recommended concertgoers secure valuables in front pockets, use elastic bands, carry "dummy wallets," and spread valuables across locations.

Wafa Yahia, the 52-year-old Syrian mother-in-law of Honolulu imam Ismail Elshikh, arrived in Honolulu on Saturday after receiving US government approval weeks earlier. Elshikh is a plaintiff in Hawaii's lawsuit challenging President Trump's travel ban on six mostly Muslim countries, which argued the ban prevented Yahia's visit. A federal appeals court in Seattle will hear the government's appeal of a July ruling permitting grandmothers and other family members to enter the US. The Supreme Court previously allowed a scaled-back ban, exempting applicants with a "bona fide" relationship with a US citizen or entity, and will hear the case in October. Hawaii Attorney General Doug Chin stated the visa approval does not affect the lawsuit. Two of Elshikh's five children had never met Yahia, who last visited in 2005.

Cuba commemorated the 58th anniversary of its revolution on Jan 2 with a military parade at Revolution Square in Havana, also paying tribute to Fidel Castro, who died on Nov 25 at age 90. Unlike previous years, soldiers marched without military equipment. Tens of thousands participated, some carrying banners and photos of Castro, despite his request against a personality cult—a wish reinforced by a recent law banning monuments and infrastructure named after him. Cuba faces challenges in 2017, including a shrinking economy impacted by Venezuela's crisis, Raul Castro's planned 2018 departure, and potential threats to US-Cuba relations from President-elect Donald Trump. Student leader Jennifer Bello affirmed Cuba would not abandon its principles and described normalising US ties as a lengthy process.

A study published in the Journal of Experimental Psychology identifies effective methods for recovering from a breakup. According to co-author Sandra Langeslag, general distraction—such as taking up hobbies, returning to school, or exercising—can boost mood in the short term, though it should be used sparingly as a form of avoidance. Another suggested technique is focusing on the negative aspects of the former partner and relationship to move on more quickly.

The author describes discomfort sleeping during pregnancy, as lying on the back after five months can reduce circulation, stomach-sleeping becomes impossible, and only left-side sleeping is recommended. After researching online, she purchased a U-shaped Leachco pregnancy pillow, recommended over the J-shaped version because it doesn't need to be moved when flipping. She found it greatly improved her comfort, allowing side-sleeping and easing congestion. Downsides include its large size, a scratchy cover (replacements sold separately), and disruption to blankets. She recommends it for pregnant women and others seeking comfort.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on July 27, 2021. The filing reports that Microsoft issued a press release on the same date announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2021, furnished as Exhibit 99.1. Microsoft's securities registered under Section 12(b) include common stock and three series of notes (2.125% due 2021, 3.125% due 2028, and 2.625% due 2033), all listed on NASDAQ. The report was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

Vale SA's stock conversion plan received backing from 84.4 percent of preferred shares, exceeding the 54.09 percent minimum threshold, CEO Fabio Schvartsman announced. The company may list on São Paulo Stock Exchange's Novo Mercado as early as this year, rather than 2020 as originally planned. CFO Luciano Siani said Vale is not considering cash incentives for investors who did not swap shares. Merging share classes into a single common stock aims to attract Asian investors and specialized mining investment firms. The plan limits political involvement, though the government retains a golden share to block hostile takeovers. Vale's common shares rose 2 percent to 31.40 reais. Vale will absorb its former controlling entity, Valepar SA, as part of a reorganization toward dispersed share ownership.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, in-person education was suspended in Turkey and replaced with virtual education through platforms like EBA TV, Zoom, and WhatsApp. Students with disabilities, most of whom receive education in inclusive settings, were significantly affected. This phenomenological study examined primary school teachers' perspectives on the participation of students with disabilities in inclusive virtual education during the pandemic.

Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 general education primary school teachers in Turkey's Marmara region, each having at least one student with a diagnosed disability. Data were analyzed through content analysis, yielding six main themes and 15 sub-themes.

Findings revealed that teachers used varied approaches, including contacting parents, teaching via EBA and Zoom, and trying hybrid models. Student participation varied: those with parental support attended regularly, while others could not attend due to illiterate parents, technology issues, or reliance on rehabilitation center services. Teachers reported challenges including crowded classrooms, limited student engagement, socialization problems, students keeping cameras off, difficulty tracking homework, lack of engaging content, and insufficient parent cooperation. Some teachers reported no problems, attributing success to daily parent communication and EBA's tracking features.

Applied solutions included hybrid scheduling, flexible support sessions, and video-based feedback with families. Suggested solutions included providing devices and internet support, supporting students' social development, keeping schools open for students with disabilities, utilizing EBA support points, and coordinating with rehabilitation centers.

The study concludes that parental involvement is crucial in virtual education and recommends informing stakeholders, improving technological infrastructure, and designing accessible content suited to students with disabilities.

This paper argues for adopting cooperative education (co-op) in Nigeria to address youth unemployment and improve school-to-work transitions. Using UN definitions, youth refers to persons aged 15-24, and skills development encompasses both hard and soft skills.

Nigerian youth unemployment has historically been lower than other regions but has risen sharply in recent years, now exceeding most regions. Youth unemployment is at least double the total unemployment rate, and employment-to-population ratios remain low. Informality, gender disparities, and higher unemployment among educated youth characterize the labor market.

Co-op, originating in industrialized countries and practiced in some SSA nations like South Africa and Namibia, integrates academic study with workplace experience through alternating or parallel models. Literature from developed countries indicates co-op benefits students (higher earnings, employability), employers, institutions, and society, though costs exist and are typically shared among stakeholders.

Nigerian government responses include SIWES, SURE-P, and N-SIP (including N-Power), which have shown mixed results due to funding and implementation challenges. SIWES resembles apprenticeships more than integrated co-op.

The authors recommend a federally championed co-op initiative using the alternating model, integrated with existing programs like SIWES and N-Power, leveraging government-industry partnerships and offering tax credits or grants to mitigate costs. Further research is needed on management structures, appropriate models, and applicability to non-tertiary education.

The Omicron variant (B.1.1.529), first identified in Botswana and South Africa in November 2021, was designated a Variant of Concern on 26 November 2021. Following its first confirmed case in England on 27 November 2021, Omicron BA.1 spread rapidly, peaking first in Greater London in mid-December before reaching northern regions in early-to-mid January 2022.

A phylodynamic analysis of 115,622 global SARS-CoV-2 genomes (42% from England) identified at least 6,455 independent introduction events into England, with 69.9% being singletons. The 8 largest transmission lineages, mostly imported before travel restrictions, accounted for over 60% of sampled English genomes. Early travel restrictions on southern African countries were largely ineffective, as importation sources shifted to the US, whose weekly importation intensity was roughly four times that of South Africa during the restriction period. Approximately 80% of reported BA.1 infections in England stemmed from the ~6% of introductions occurring before 15 December 2021.

Phylogeographic reconstruction showed Greater London as the predominant source of viral dissemination during the expansion phase, with gravity model dynamics driving spread. Long-distance movements increased in early December, primarily from London to the Midlands and North West. Post-expansion, aggregated mobility became more influential, and dissemination shifted toward LTLAs with later peak times.

Statistical modeling indicated that human mobility declined in response to rising local case numbers: trips between "home" and "hub" LTLAs decreased by approximately 12% per unit increase in weekly cases per 100 people, with shorter-distance movements more affected than longer ones.

The authors note limitations including potential underestimation of introductions and residual sampling biases, and emphasize the need for better understanding of behavior-transmission interactions and coordinated global genomic surveillance for future variants.

The TLV321/2x comparator family consumes 40uA per channel with 40ns propagation delay. The TLV321x has a push-pull output, while the TLV322x has an open-drain output pullable up to 5.5V independent of supply voltage.

Input voltage range extends 200mV beyond V- and V+, with current limited to 10mA via series resistance. Unused inputs should not be tied together; instead, connect to voltages providing at least 50mV differential. The family includes 1.8mV of internal hysteresis, characterized by VTH, VOS, and VHYST components.

Push-pull outputs should never connect to another output or be shorted to supply rails. Unused push-pull outputs must be left floating. Open-drain outputs support logical OR'ing and level translation, with recommended pull-up currents between 100uA and 1mA. Unused open-drain outputs can float or tie to V-.

Internal ESD protection clamps exist on inputs/outputs. A Power-On Reset circuit activates for up to 32us after VPOR of 1.65V is crossed, holding output low during this period.

Applications include basic comparators, configurations with external hysteresis (inverting and non-inverting), and low-side current sensing. Design recommendations include 0.1µF ceramic bypass capacitors near supply pins, minimizing output-input coupling, and optionally adding <100Ω series output resistors to dampen ringing.

The NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture GPU features SMs with 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation Ray Tracing Core, and 128 KB of L1/Shared Memory. The full GA102 GPU includes 168 FP64 units, twelve 32-bit memory controllers with 6144 KB of L2 cache, and 112 ROPs now integrated into the GPC for improved raster performance.

The GA10x SM doubles FP32 throughput over Turing by enabling FP32 on both datapaths, with one datapath also handling INT32 operations. L1 cache capacity grew 33%, and shared memory bandwidth doubled. Ampere GPUs are up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection testing and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit, accelerating ray-traced motion blur up to eight times faster than Turing. GA10x supports concurrent RT Core, graphics, and compute workloads. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 support and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, doubling throughput.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, delivering up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth at 19.5 Gbps. NVIDIA RTX IO, paired with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, enables GPU-based decompression, improving I/O by up to 100x.

Additional features include enhanced DLSS for 8K gaming, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a, HDCP 2.3, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode, seventh-generation NVENC, and Error Detection and Replay (EDR) for GDDR6X overclocking. The NVIDIA A40 and RTX A6000 are data center and workstation GPUs based on GA102, with 48GB memory expandable to 96GB via NVLink.

Justice Barrett's book defends originalism as the correct method of constitutional interpretation, based on the premise that constitutional text is binding law whose meaning must reflect what lawmakers understood it to be. Applying originalism to Louisiana v. Callais—a case challenging Louisiana's majority-Black congressional district—reveals problems with the Shaw v. Reno line of precedent.

The Shaw doctrine, which subjects race-predominant districting to strict scrutiny under the 14th Amendment's equal protection clause, cannot be justified on originalist grounds. The subsequent adoption of the 15th and 19th Amendments demonstrates that the equal protection clause was not originally understood to constrain state election regulations. Section 2 of the 14th Amendment explicitly contemplates states restricting voting rights. Justice O'Connor's Shaw opinion did not attempt an originalist defense.

Reconstructing Shaw under the 15th Amendment also fails, because Shaw claims involve no vote dilution—only the separation of voters by race. The 15th Amendment's text prohibiting denial or abridgment of voting rights cannot plausibly reach such claims.

While originalists can respect stare decisis, precedents that prove unworkable or inconsistent with other law warrant reconsideration. The Shaw "racial predominance" test is notoriously difficult to apply and conflicts with Section 2 Voting Rights Act jurisprudence. A principled originalist would resolve this tension by jettisoning Shaw, preserving congressional authority to address vote dilution, rather than curtailing the VRA. Congress retains power to outlaw racially motivated districting legislatively if it chooses.

The Investors Intelligence Sentiment Index, developed by AW Cohen in 1963, is a contrarian indicator that surveys over a hundred independent market newsletters weekly, categorizing each author's stance as bullish, bearish, or expecting a correction. It also reports the percentage of stocks above their 10-week and 30-week moving averages, useful for identifying short-term and major market turns respectively.

Originally intended to signal bullish conditions as buying opportunities, it was found that advisors were typically wrong at turning points, leading the investment community to adopt it as a contrarian tool. Bullish readings above 55% suggest excessive optimism (negative for markets), while readings below 35% indicate pessimism (positive). Weekly figures above 70% suggest overbought conditions, and below 30% suggest oversold.

Investor sentiment refers to the general mood of investors, assessed through price activity or indicators. The AAII Sentiment Survey, established in 1987, surveys individual investors about the next six months, whereas the Investors Intelligence Index focuses on professional advisors and commentators. The Investors Intelligence index is published by Chartcraft and available via subscription on its website.

Employees at the Department of Education (DOE) reported that their automatic out-of-office email replies were changed without consent to include partisan language blaming Senate Democrats for the government shutdown, according to sources who spoke to WIRED. Some employees who reverted the message to neutral language found it changed back again. The original HR-suggested language had been neutral, but the altered version referenced HR 5371 and blamed Democrat Senators for blocking its passage. Sources and screenshots indicate the Department of Labor received similar suggested partisan language. Experts, including University of Michigan professor Don Moynihan, suggest this could violate the Hatch Act, which limits political activity by government employees and can result in fines or job loss. The DOE's press line responded to WIRED's request for comment with the same partisan message.

Afghanistan's ban on girls' secondary education illustrates the limitations of the "out-of-school children" (OOSC) indicator, which measures only formal school enrollment. This policy brief advocates replacing OOSC with an "out-of-education children" (OOEC) indicator that includes formal, informal, and non-formal educational pathways.

The OOSC indicator privileges formal schooling as the only legitimate pathway, delegitimizing alternatives like madrasas, community-based education (CBE), and technology-based systems. It also fails to account for chronic absenteeism, ghost schools, and marginalized populations such as displaced children and pastoralists. Globally, 251 million children are reportedly out of school, with the highest concentrations in Sub-Saharan Africa and Central/Southern Asia.

Afghanistan's education history reveals ongoing ideological contestation between formal schooling and traditional systems like madrasas. Despite enrollment growth from 500,000 in 2000 to 10 million by 2021, millions remained excluded due to geographic disparities, nomadic lifestyles, child labor, and disabilities. The Taliban's 2021 return left 80% of school-aged girls out of school.

The OOEC indicator offers three advantages: broadening perspectives on educational challenges, fostering culturally relevant transformation, and reimagining education as an interconnected ecosystem. Implementation requires evolving data systems to capture diverse pathways, developing credentialing systems to validate non-formal learning, fostering collaboration among education actors, and reallocating resources equitably. This shift is essential for achieving SDG 4 and ensuring inclusive education for all learners.

Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) is an AMD firmware feature that allows datacenter operators to apply patches for high-priority system issues without rebooting.

Successful SFS deployment changes three version numbers: the SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), which identifies the currently applied package and must monotonically increase to prevent rollback; individual firmware component and Security Patch Level (SPL) versions; and the System Patch Level (SYSPL), which tracks run-once code modifying registers and SRAM outside versioned components.

AMD cryptographically signs all SFS packages, and customers may optionally co-sign them for approval control by providing a public key (2048-bit or 4096-bit RSA) to the AMD Security Processor (ASP) during early boot. The ASP serves as root of trust for detection, while OEM/ODMs retain root of trust for update. BIOS enables SFS via APCB tokens, with both SFS and co-signing off by default.

SFS updates are non-persistent across reboots and must be reapplied after each reset. In multi-socket systems, the first socket's ASP receives and distributes patches. Updates must be applied sequentially in numerical order.

Commands require 2MB-aligned memory pages and use a TEE Extended Command Buffer sent via the TEE mailbox interface. Key commands include GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO (retrieving firmware versions and patch levels) and UPDATE_FW (loading and executing update packages). The ASP verifies signatures, protects memory from x86 access, executes patches, and updates patch level information.

Packages are named using family, AGESA release, and an incrementing integer. Updates typically run in parallel with x86/DMA traffic with minimal performance impact, though SEV/ES virtual machines must restart for SEV firmware updates (SEV/SNP VMs can continue operating). Reverting SEV updates requires a system reboot.

Passport applicants must take an oath of allegiance to the U.S. Government and submit a physical description including age, stature, and facial features, along with a witness certificate verifying identity. Native citizens need only provide the basic information. Those born abroad to a native-citizen father must document the father's birth, residence, and citizenship at the time of applicant's birth. Naturalized citizens must submit their naturalization certificate and details of emigration, arrival, residence, and naturalization. Unmarried women must state so; wives or widows of citizens must provide their husband's citizenship details. Children claiming citizenship through a naturalized parent must submit the parent's certificate and related facts. Residents of U.S. insular possessions must affirm sole allegiance to the United States, supported by two witnesses. Passports expire after two years, with old passports acceptable in lieu of naturalization certificates for renewals. A single passport may cover a wife, minor children, and servants if specified. Professional titles are excluded. Chief executives of insular possessions may deny passports for improper purposes or noncompliance. The document is signed by Theodore Roosevelt, dated July 19, 1902, and lists fees totaling $2.00.

Archaeologists from the Great Mayan Aquifer Project, led by Guillermo de Anda, will begin excavating a sealed tunnel beneath the El Castillo pyramid at Chichen Itza in Mexico. The goal is to reach a hidden cenote — an underwater cavern — detected two years ago by scientist Rene Chavez Segura. Cenotes were Mexico's Yucatan state's only fresh water source and were considered entrances to the underworld in Mayan cosmology, sometimes used for human sacrifice to appease the rain god Chac. The team previously explored passageways from the Ossuary pyramid but found them intentionally blocked. De Anda believes the hidden cenote may represent the "axis mundi," or center of the world, as known cenotes lie to the north, south, east, and west of El Castillo. Excavation is expected to take three months. De Anda's prior analysis of sacrificial remains showed roughly 80 percent were malnourished children aged 3 to 11, possibly from lower social strata.

The European Union has announced a €545 million ($636 million) investment package to support renewable energy and electrification projects across Africa, including initiatives in Côte d'Ivoire, Cameroon, Lesotho, and Madagascar. The funding is part of the EU's Global Gateway program, launched in 2021 to build global infrastructure and counter China's Belt and Road Initiative, which has invested over $1.3 trillion in more than 100 countries. The EU estimates its investments could create 38 million green jobs in Africa by 2030.

Africa is strategically important due to its deposits of critical minerals such as cobalt, lithium, copper, and manganese. China has been heavily investing in African clean energy, exporting 15GW of solar panels to Africa in the year leading up to June 2025. The United States launched a similar initiative, the Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment, which includes the Lobito Corridor railway project connecting Zambian and Congolese mines to Angola's Atlantic coast. Nearly 600 million Africans currently lack electricity access.

The COVID-19 pandemic forced educational systems worldwide, including Greece, to shift to distance education. This research, conducted during 2020-2021 in the Region of Epirus, Greece, investigated kindergarten teachers' views on distance education implementation in preschool settings.

Using a quantitative approach with a web-based questionnaire, the study sampled 82 kindergarten teachers (96.3% women). Most participants held a bachelor's degree (75.6%), had 15-25 years of service (55.6%), and possessed basic ICT certification (Level A).

Key findings revealed that over 75% of teachers were little or not at all familiar with distance education before its mandatory implementation. More than 90% had never integrated distance learning before the pandemic. Synchronous education tools were preferred (64.6%), with Webex being the most used platform (88.9%), likely due to free state provision.

Teachers expressed predominantly negative views about integrating distance education in kindergarten. Approximately 90% reported that it reduces psychomotor activities and requires adult supervision. About 86% considered it less effective than conventional education for developing social skills. Additional concerns included inadequate digital infrastructure (65%), limited internet access (73%), and young students' difficulty using technology independently (78%).

Statistical analysis showed teachers with Level B ICT certification had significantly higher familiarity with distance education than those without certification. No significant relationship existed between years of service and ICT literacy.

The study concludes that successful integration requires state investment in school infrastructure, teacher training in distance education strategies, interactive resources suitable for young children, and support systems for families. However, the authors caution that preschool children's young age remains a fundamental factor potentially exacerbating digital inequality. Results are limited to the Epirus region and cannot be generalized nationally.

A take a knee chart helps football coaches decide when the offense can kneel down to run out the clock at the end of a game while preserving a lead. The offense uses a "victory formation" to minimize turnover risk, and the quarterback kneels immediately after the snap, counting as a run play that keeps the clock running. The chart shows player positioning and movement order for executing the play.

Clock management is considered a primary responsibility of head coaches, and practicing end-of-game scenarios is valuable. High school football rules now largely mirror college football, including the 40-second play clock, though neither has a two-minute warning like the NFL. Coaches must avoid incomplete passes when running out the clock, as these stop the clock and can give opponents time to score.

ML²B (Multilingual Machine Learning Benchmark) is the first benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) on generating complete machine learning pipelines from multilingual natural language descriptions. It comprises 30 Kaggle competitions (24 public, 6 private) translated into 13 languages, yielding 390 evaluation instances across tabular, text, and image modalities in 12 domains. The benchmark includes structured metadata, human-reviewed task descriptions, and standardized data cards to prevent information leakage. Its architecture features a main pipeline, Docker runtime, and a code grader supporting two submission formats (single-function and modular) to reduce preprocessing leakage. Translations were generated using GPT-4o and validated by native-speaker annotators with computer science backgrounds. Evaluation uses percentile-based ranking on Kaggle leaderboards. Testing five LLMs across AIDE and ML-Master frameworks revealed 15–45% performance degradation on non-English tasks, with English as the strongest anchor language and low-resource languages (Kazakh, Belarusian, Romanian) showing systemic weaknesses. No single model proved universally optimal; hybrid stacks partially mitigated cross-lingual gaps. Static analysis identified potential data leakage in roughly 5.9% of modular submissions.

Amazon.com, Inc., incorporated in Delaware with headquarters in Seattle, Washington, filed its Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2018. The company operates through three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS), serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators.

In 2018, Amazon reported net sales of $232.9 billion (31% growth), operating income of $12.4 billion, and net income of $10.1 billion. North America sales grew 33%, International 21%, and AWS 47%. The company employed approximately 647,500 full-time and part-time employees and had 491,202,890 shares outstanding as of January 23, 2019.

Amazon identified numerous risk factors, including intense competition, rapid expansion, international operations, fulfillment network optimization, seasonality (with Q4 generating 31% of 2018 revenue), foreign exchange exposure, data security, intellectual property, tax liabilities, and regulatory changes such as the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017.

Operating cash flow reached $30.7 billion in 2018, with cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities of $41.3 billion. Capital expenditures totaled $11.3 billion, largely supporting fulfillment and AWS infrastructure. The company included Whole Foods Market results since its August 2017 acquisition and announced additional headquarters in New York and Arlington, Virginia. Jeffrey P. Bezos served as President, CEO, and Chairman.
