The 9 EMA trading strategy is a technical analysis approach that uses the 9-period exponential moving average to generate buy and sell signals for short-term trend identification. A buy signal occurs when price moves above the 9 EMA, and a sell signal when it moves below. The strategy can be applied to stocks, forex, commodities, and crypto.

Backtesting shows mixed results. On Bitcoin, a basic crossover system produced 284 trades with an average gain of 2.65% per trade, though with a maximum drawdown of 83%. Applied to the S&P 500/SPY, the strategy performed poorly due to stocks' mean-reverting nature. Adding a 200-day moving average trend filter improved Bitcoin's results to 153 trades with a 4% average gain, but the S&P 500 results remained untradable.

The strategy can be combined with indicators like RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and candlestick patterns for confirmation. Risk management techniques include stop-loss orders, position sizing, and diversification. The 9 EMA works best in trending or momentum-driven assets and is generally unsuitable for mean-reverting markets.

A class action complaint filed in the Superior Court of California, County of San Diego, by plaintiff Pamela R. Gordon against wholesale electricity generators and traders including Reliant Energy, Southern Company, NRG Energy, Dynegy, AES Corporation, Williams Energy, and Duke Energy North America. The complaint alleges that, beginning around May 22, 2000, defendants unlawfully manipulated California's wholesale electricity market, resulting in inflated prices. Alleged tactics include improperly using confidential real-time generator and transmission data shared via the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) in violation of ISO Tariffs, withholding generating capacity from forward markets, parking power with out-of-state affiliates for resale at higher prices, scheduling unplanned plant outages, and creating transmission congestion.

The complaint cites findings from FERC (November 1, 2000), the CPUC, and the CAISO that Summer 2000 prices were "unjust and unreasonable" and resulted from the exercise of market power, with the CPUC estimating over $4 billion in overcharges. The class includes approximately 1.2 million SDG&E retail customers who purchased electricity through the California Power Exchange during the Class Period. Causes of action include violations of California's Cartwright Act (antitrust), Unfair Trade Practices Act, Consumers Legal Remedies Act, and unconscionability. Plaintiff seeks class certification, treble damages, restitution, disgorgement of profits, injunctive relief, and attorneys' fees. The complaint was forwarded by Mark Palmer to Enron executives, noting a reporter's indication that Enron's anticipated suit would be similar.

GOLDWOOD is recognized as a premium quality brand committed to delivering results without compromise. The company operates on principles of mutual trust, transparency, and intellectual honesty, including timely delivery. It aims to reshape the wood panel industry's approach to quality. GOLDWOOD prioritizes sustainable development alongside profits, focusing on quality manufacturing, people growth, and environmental safety. GOLDWOOD PLY, based in Yamunanagar, Haryana, is a leading plywood manufacturer offering products such as Block Boards, Flush Doors, and Plywood across India.

The passage argues that law enforcement effectiveness often depends on less publicized legislation, which interested parties actively seek to defeat. The government has shifted toward criminal proceedings in trust and interstate commerce cases, achieving successes that deter wrongdoing through fines and imprisonment.

Judge Holt's decision is cited as exemplifying appropriate severity toward such offenders. In the case described, a railroad granted illegal rebates exceeding one-fifth of the tariff rate, potentially driving competitors out of business. Holt characterized the crime as deliberate, premeditated, and more serious than common crimes, committed by educated businessmen on behalf of a railroad corporation holding public privileges and obligations. Despite the Interstate Commerce Act's passage in 1887 and widespread rebate complaints, proof difficulties made this the first such prosecution in his court. Holt concluded the penalty should primarily fall on the corporation rather than the traffic manager, who acted on his employer's wishes.

The Missouri Student Union held its annual Veterans Day wreath laying ceremony, participating in the National Remembrance Day Roll Call where names of MU student veterans killed in service were read. Keynote speaker Col. Roderik Cox, an MU alumnus with over 12 years of combat and peacekeeping experience, defined a veteran as anyone who swore an oath to defend the Constitution. Speakers included leaders from MU's Student Union Programming Board, Student Veterans Association, and Military Science department. Robert Ross, director of the MU Veterans Center, which supports over 400 student veterans, expressed hope for future world peace. Cox and attendee David Emily, a former Navy servicemember, challenged Hollywood stereotypes, emphasizing that veterans are ordinary people in various professions. A reception followed at Bengal's Lair in Memorial Union.

The Konektadong Pinoy Act, signed into law on August 24, 2025, aims to remove barriers to competition in the Philippine telecommunications market. The law could reshape the industry by enabling Virtual Network Operators to compete with PLDT, a leading Philippine telecom company. This added competition coincides with PLDT's declining profitability and slowing growth. Applying Capital Cycle analysis, the act may introduce excess capital into an already mature, highly penetrated industry, further reducing profitability. Despite PLDT's attractive valuation, the author views the threat of new entrants as sufficient reason to avoid the stock.

Passports expire two years after issuance, requiring a new application for renewal. A single passport may cover an applicant's wife, minor children, and servant if ages and allegiance are stated; others need separate passports. Professional titles are excluded. A $1 fee, payable by currency or postal money order to the State Department's disbursing clerk, is required. The Department does not obtain foreign visés and provides blank forms only to applicants, not commercial agents. Communications must go to the Passport Bureau with a return address. The Secretary of State may reject applications suspected of unlawful purposes or noncompliance.

Under Section 4075 of the Revised Statutes, as amended June 14, 1902, President Theodore Roosevelt prescribed rules on July 19, 1902, for issuing passports in U.S. insular possessions. Applications are made to the possession's chief executive, or abroad to a diplomatic or consular officer. Passports cannot be issued to non-citizens, including those who have only declared intent to naturalize. Applicants must submit a sworn written affidavit stating birth date and place, occupation, permanent residence, and intent to return to the U.S. or its possessions.

Joy Williams, BSN, RN, has been welcomed into the International Nurses Association and will be featured in the Worldwide Leaders In Healthcare publication. Based in Louisiana, Williams has over seven years of nursing experience across agency and hospital settings. She earned her Diploma of Practical Nursing from Nunez Community College in 2009 and her Bachelor of Science in Nursing from Dillard University in 2016. She maintains memberships with the National Black Nurses Association and the National Student Nurses Association, and credits her daughter Londen as her inspiration.

Small group differentiation is a pedagogical strategy that tailors teaching methods, content, and assessment to address diverse student needs in elementary and higher education. Increasing diversity in U.S. schools—including racial, linguistic, and ability-based differences—makes differentiation increasingly relevant. Grounded in Constructivism and Sociocultural Theory, differentiation emphasizes student-centered learning, scaffolding, and collaboration.

Effective differentiation requires understanding student profiles, forming heterogeneous groups, and using instructional-level materials. Its five principles include flexibility, ongoing assessment, respectful challenges, collaboration, and student autonomy. Implementation differs between elementary settings, where teachers guide foundational learning, and higher education, where independence and self-directed learning dominate.

Small group instruction boosts engagement, accountability, peer interaction, and relationship-building, while supporting struggling learners and culturally diverse students. However, challenges include time-intensive planning, large class sizes, inadequate administrative support, and accommodating students with disabilities under IDEA.

Limitations include insufficient empirical research comparing small group instruction's effectiveness across settings. Future research should include longitudinal studies tracking differentiated instruction's long-term impact and evaluating outcomes across various learning styles.

The Atlas of Human-AI Interaction is a framework that uses large language models to map empirical findings from over 1,000 human-AI interaction research papers into a structured knowledge graph. Through a five-stage pipeline—abstract collection, findings extraction, triplet formation, semantic clustering, and graph construction—the system organizes research into [cause, relationship, effect] triplets, producing 1,310 nodes and 3,908 edges.

The Atlas offers three visualization modes: a 3D Graph View for landscape exploration, a Cause-Effect View (Sankey diagram) for tracing relationships, and a Paper View for detailed study examination. Analysis identified 24 thematic clusters across human, AI, and concept categories, and network analysis revealed structural holes around LLMs, generative AI, trust, chatbots, and agents as opportunities for cross-community research integration.

A user study with 20 expert researchers found the tool effective for identifying research gaps, validating relationships, and exploring cross-disciplinary connections, though participants noted limitations in information depth, temporal analysis, and applicability to technical domains. The authors position the Atlas as a complement to traditional literature reviews, with future directions including continuous data updates, expanded relationship types, refined extraction methods, and deeper connectivity analysis.

The 4-3 defense, popularized in the NFL by Tom Landry and modernized by Jimmy Johnson, consists of four defensive linemen, three linebackers, and four defensive backs. It typically uses two 5-technique ends, a 1-technique nose guard, and a 3-technique tackle, with the latter considered the most critical position. Linebackers decrease in size from the Sam (strong) to the Mike (middle) to the Will (weak).

The defense's strengths include strong run defense with seven defenders in the box, clear gap assignments, and coverage flexibility. Its weaknesses include struggles against modern spread offenses, which pull linebackers out of the box, and vulnerability to edge runs, often forcing teams into nickel personnel.

Common blitzes include the Will Edge Blitz and zone blitzes featuring a defensive end dropping into coverage. Typical coverages include the Tampa 2, where the Mike drops into the deep middle, and Cover 3.

Notable users include the early 2000s Tampa Bay Buccaneers, featuring players like Warren Sapp and Derrick Brooks; the 2006 Chicago Bears under Lovie Smith with Brian Urlacher; and Montini Catholic High School in Illinois, which won multiple state titles under Mike Bukovsky.

Google has launched Gemini Enterprise, an AI platform for business customers offering access to Gemini Ultra models alongside tools for data governance, security, and regulatory compliance. Positioned between consumer and research-tier products, it allows firms to customise AI applications on Google Cloud using proprietary data with built-in explainability and access controls.

The launch intensifies Google's competition with Microsoft, Amazon, and OpenAI in the enterprise AI market, with Google emphasising transparency, traceable outputs, and compliance features for regulated industries such as finance, healthcare, and manufacturing. Integration with Google Workspace and third-party software may support wider adoption.

The platform reflects Google's shift from AI model development toward enterprise deployment and monetisation. Its success will depend on demonstrating reliability, measurable returns, and seamless integration into corporate systems.

Ray Dalio's All Weather Portfolio, developed by Bridgewater Associates, is designed to perform across all economic environments—inflation, deflation, or stagflation—by diversifying across stocks, bonds, and commodities. The portfolio heavily allocates to bonds, with smaller portions in stocks and commodities, prioritizing reduced drawdowns over maximum returns through a risk parity approach.

Backtests from 2007 onward show a CAGR of approximately 4.5%, underperforming the S&P 500's 6.7% but with significantly smaller drawdowns. During the 2008/09 financial crisis, Covid-19 in 2020, and the 2022 bear market, it outperformed stocks with maximum drawdowns of 17%, 6%, and 12%, respectively. Leveraging the portfolio 1.5x raised returns to match the S&P 500 with lower drawdowns.

The strategy suits risk-averse investors, retirees, and FIREs, and should be rebalanced one to four times yearly, preferably in tax-deferred accounts. Retail investors can replicate it using five ETFs. However, it typically underperforms during bull markets, as seen in 2022 when bonds also declined.

In this dissolution appeal, the mother challenged a trial court judgment awarding her $31 per month in child support for each of the parties' two children, and objected to the abatement of child support during the father's visitation periods. The father, a law firm partner, and the mother, a school librarian, share a visitation arrangement resembling joint custody, with children in the father's care approximately half the time. While the court agreed that the father's visitation expenses should factor into his support obligation, it found the awarded amount insufficient. Citing difficulty in applying the formulas from Smith v. Smith and Belt and Belt due to uncertainty about the father's future income, the court modified the judgment to require $65 per month per child.

Please, Continue (Hamlet), a theatrical work by Yan Duyvendak and Roger Bernat, stages a fictional trial of Hamlet for the murder of Polonius using real lawyers, judges, and a jury selected from the audience. Premiered in Switzerland in 2011, it has been performed in 12 countries, adapting each time to the local legal system, and is only staged in jurisdictions with jury trials. The project was inspired by the creators' shock at the Guantanamo trial transcripts and their interest in how justice systems operate. The case blends Shakespeare's plot with details from a real 2010 case involving a young man accused of killing his girlfriend's father, shared by a lawyer friend of Duyvendak. The creators themselves disagreed on the real defendant's guilt, which motivated them to design a performance allowing audiences to grapple with similar complexity. Duyvendak reports that audience members and jurors often shift their opinions during the show and gain a more nuanced view of justice. Performances run under four hours, and Duyvendak serves as master of ceremonies.

This study conducts a systematic review and bibliometric analysis of 270 Scopus-indexed journal articles published between 2015 and July 2024 on the metaverse in education, using PRISMA methodology and VOSviewer software.

The analysis addressed three research questions concerning publication trends, influential journals/articles, and prominent research topics. Findings reveal that research on the metaverse in education began in 2020, coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic, rising sharply in 2022 and peaking at 131 publications in 2023. South Korea, China, the United States, and the United Kingdom emerged as the most productive and cited countries, attributed to their advanced technology sectors and investments in 5G and AI.

"IEEE Transactions on Learning Technologies" published the most articles, while "Sustainability (Switzerland)" received the most citations. The most influential article was by Dwivedi et al. (2022). Co-occurrence analysis of keywords revealed that research primarily focuses on virtual reality, augmented reality, and artificial intelligence.

Two prominent research areas were identified: (1) using the metaverse to create virtual educational environments, particularly in medical education, and (2) examining students' and teachers' perceptions toward metaverse adoption, which are largely positive due to immersive and engaging experiences.

The study identifies gaps, including the lack of longitudinal studies and limited geographic diversity, recommending future research explore long-term impacts and cross-cultural adaptability of metaverse-based education.

In Jones v. Dow, the Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department, issued a per curiam decision on December 10, 1912, affirming the order with $10 costs and disbursements. Justice Thomas dissented, arguing the order was entered ex parte and deprived the plaintiff of a statutory right to reply to the answer. Justice Carr did not vote.

Michigan State Police, Emergency Management and Homeland Security are asking residents to join a voluntary statewide tornado drill at 1 p.m. Wednesday during Severe Weather Awareness Week. Capt. Chris A. Kelenske emphasized preparedness due to tornadoes' unpredictable nature and short 10-to-15-minute average lead time. Recommendations include identifying safe shelter locations, conducting drills, monitoring broadcasts, understanding watch-versus-warning distinctions, recognizing warning signs, and preparing 72-hour emergency kits. If severe weather occurs April 19, the drill will move to Thursday at 1 p.m.

Transition defense requires deliberate practice, not just verbal reminders. Good offense—ball care, shot selection, offensive rebounding, and defensive balance—is the foundation. The "Twelve Musts" include taking care of the ball, sprinting back while maintaining ball vision, forcing multiple passes before shots, and defending outnumbered situations.

Key principles include "Seek the Level of the Ball," staying ahead of the ball, and never running side-by-side with opponents. Bigs have specific responsibilities: the first covers the basket, the second shadows to prevent dribble penetration.

Defending outnumbered situations (break-aways, 2-on-1, 3-on-2) requires buying time, pressuring the ball, forcing extra passes, and preventing easy shots. On missed field goals, the closest defender jams the rebounder while another denies the outlet pass to the primary ball handler; remaining defenders sprint back. Five methods disrupt outlet passes: attacking, denying, taking a charge, forcing a premature pass, or trapping.

Similar principles apply after missed free throws, turnovers, and blocked shots, emphasizing that defensive stops after these events are "Really Big Plays." Made baskets allow setup of full or half court pressure.

Game strategies include scouting opponents and substituting players who don't sprint back. Teaching uses the "Whole-Part-Whole" method with breakdown drills, recognizing that offseason pickup games create bad habits requiring correction.

The passage specifies requirements for the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB), used for secure communication between guests and hypervisors.

Guests and hypervisors must set appropriate bits in the VALID_BITMAP field for GHCB fields. At minimum, guests set SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2 bits; hypervisors set SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2 bits. The VALID_BITMAP must be reset before each NAE event. Bit positions are calculated from field byte offsets.

Non-Automatic Events (NAEs) are generally handled via a standard method, with exceptions documented separately. Software must disable interrupts and preemption when invoking VMGEXIT. Hypervisor errors are communicated via SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2, with non-zero values indicating errors or requested exception injection.

Specific NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access (#NPF), Page State Change (supporting private/shared transitions and PSMASH/UNSMASH hints), SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request (returning certificates), AP Creation (for SEV-SNP), #HV doorbell page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request (for trusted device binding), Secure AVIC backing page management, and Termination Request.

The specification addresses guest SEV-ES identification via CPUID, SMP booting challenges (requiring AP Reset Hold or SNP AP Creation), NMI handling using #DB intercepts, debug register virtualization, and exclusion of SMM and nested virtualization.

The #HV Doorbell Page provides host-to-guest notifications when Restricted Injection is active. It contains a PendingEvent field (including interrupt vectors and non-maskable event flags) and a NoEoiRequired field for EOI optimization. The host emulates APIC interrupt lifecycle behavior, while guests must atomically exchange fields when acknowledging interrupts or performing EOIs. Guests must validate vectors due to potentially non-cooperative hosts, and specific conventions govern HLT behavior with interrupt shadows.

The Navy's Pier Pressure mobile app, part of the Keep What You've Earned campaign, helps Sailors evaluate their drinking habits during Alcohol Awareness Month and year-round. According to NADAP Deputy Director LaNorfeia Parker, the free app combines interactive gaming with practical tools. Features include a calorie counter showing drink calories and equivalent pushups needed to burn them, plus integration with Uber and Lyft for safe rides home. The app has been played over 30,000 times and is available on iTunes and Google Play.

The Dow Jones industrial average dropped 424.56 points (1.74 percent) on Tuesday, closing at 24,024.13, while the S&P 500 fell 1.3 percent and the Nasdaq composite declined 1.7 percent. Caterpillar's stock fell 6.2 percent after its CFO Bradley Halverson described the first quarter as "the high-water mark for the year." 3M dropped 7 percent after lowering its profit forecast, and Alphabet fell 5 percent despite reported profit gains. The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note surpassed 3 percent for the first time in four years, raising concerns about potential Federal Reserve monetary tightening and higher borrowing costs.

Appellee Florence O. Summers sued appellants Clennon C. Hemsell and Columbian Fuel Corporation on behalf of herself, her three minor children, and the deceased's mother, for damages arising from the death of J. W. Summers in an automobile collision with Hemsell, who was allegedly acting as an employee of Columbian Fuel Corporation. A jury awarded appellees $30,890, and appellants appealed.

The Court of Civil Appeals found several reversible errors in the trial court's charge to the jury. First, the court's instructions on special issues Nos. 54 and 55 improperly assumed the life expectancies of the deceased husband (34½ years) and his surviving mother (20.2 years), removing these fact questions from the jury. Mortality tables are not conclusive, and the stipulation regarding the American Experience Table of Mortality did not constitute an absolute agreement on life expectancy.

Second, the instruction on issue No. 54 erroneously directed the jury to consider the manner in which the wife expected to be cared for, rather than the pecuniary benefits she reasonably expected to receive.

Third, on issue No. 56, the court erred in instructing the jury to consider "loss of love and care and fatherly advice," as emotional elements like society, companionship, and natural affection are not recoverable, being incapable of pecuniary evaluation.

Fourth, the instruction on issue No. 57 regarding contributions to a college education was on the weight of the evidence and unsupported by sufficient testimony.

Fifth, the court should have instructed the jury to exclude consideration of sorrow and grief.

The court found no error in refusing requested issues on sole proximate cause or new and independent cause. Finally, appellees' counsel's argument criticizing appellants for introducing admissible divorce evidence was improper and inflammatory, and the trial court erred in failing to instruct the jury to disregard it. The judgment was reversed and remanded.

Security researcher Michael Myng discovered a keylogger pre-installed in Synaptics touchpad drivers affecting hundreds of HP notebooks, tablets, and other devices. The keylogger is disabled by default but could be enabled via a registry change, allowing a malicious actor with administrative privileges to monitor keyboard activity. After Myng reported the issue, HP confirmed the finding—describing it as a debug trace—and released software patches in a November 7 security update covering more than 450 products, including HP Notebook, EliteBook, Mobile Thin Client, ProBook, Spectre Pro, and ZBook Mobile Workstation models. HP stated that neither it nor Synaptics had access to customer data. This is the second such incident in 2017; in May, Modzero researchers reported a similar keylogging vulnerability in Conexant audio drivers on HP laptops, also attributed to leftover debugging code.

Chinese police shot dead three knife-wielding attackers who killed five people and injured 10 in Pishan County, Xinjiang, on Tuesday evening. Authorities called the assailants "thugs" but did not disclose ethnic backgrounds. Xinjiang is home to the predominantly Muslim, Turkish-speaking Uighur minority. Beijing frequently blames exiled Uighur separatist groups for attacks in the region, while some foreign-based Uighurs allege a crackdown on the minority. Previous incidents include the killing of three "rioters" last month, 28 alleged terrorists in November 2015 following an Aksu colliery attack that killed 16, and a 2014 Kunming train station attack that killed 31.

Philadelphia Union's Borek Dockal, a 29-year-old Czech import, recorded a goal and two assists in a match against Chicago, extending Philly's unbeaten streak to four matches. Dockal averages 2.4 key passes per game. In the same match, Ilsinho scored a notable goal after beating Bastian Schweinsteiger inside the box. In another match, Josef Martinez scored against New England despite questionable defending from Antonio Delamea Milnar, though a late Teal Bunbury penalty secured a 1-1 draw for New England.

Johnny Juzang is making a case for a roster spot with the Minnesota Timberwolves, potentially replacing Nickeil Alexander-Walker, who left in the offseason. Though on a non-guaranteed training camp contract, Juzang scored 20 points in 14 minutes during a preseason game Tuesday and has made 9-of-15 three-pointers this preseason. Over the past two seasons, he has shot over 38% from three. The 24-year-old former third-team All-American fits Minnesota's playing style as an outside shooter. The Timberwolves would need to determine how to retain him.

Researchers from Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine and the Mayo Clinic have published a guideline in JAMA Internal Medicine recommending the elimination of creatine kinase-myocardial band (CK-MB) blood testing for evaluating suspected heart attacks. Citing prior statements from the American College of Cardiology and peer-reviewed studies, the report concludes CK-MB offers no additional diagnostic value beyond cardiac troponin testing, which is more sensitive and a better predictor of mortality. Despite these findings, a 2013 survey found 77 percent of U.S. labs still use CK-MB. The researchers estimate heart attack blood tests cost $416 million annually.

The report is the first in a series from the High Value Practice Academic Alliance (HVPAA), a coalition of over 80 academic institutions. It outlines four implementation steps: hospitalwide education, partnering with clinical stakeholders to remove CK-MB from order sets, creating IT alerts for CK-MB orders, and measuring outcomes. Future guides will address transfusions, routine lab tests, antibiotics, C. difficile testing, and cardiac telemetry.

Dynamical evolution in molecular clouds occurs over millions of years, making direct observation of stellar collapse impossible. Redshifted self-absorption in molecular line profiles is commonly used to identify gravitational collapse and estimate infall velocities, often via the Myers et al. (1996) analytical method, though its simplicity limits accuracy for non-uniform velocity profiles.

This study combined smoothed-particle hydrodynamic simulations of a collapsing 5 M⊙ Bonnor-Ebert sphere with time-dependent chemistry (uclchem) and radiative transfer modelling (radmc3d) to produce synthetic line observations. The J=1-0 transitions of C18O, N2H+, HCO+, and H13CO+, and J=2-1 transitions of CS and C34S were modelled at two timesteps (0.81 and 0.87 Myr) and two aperture radii (0.05 and 0.2 pc).

Results showed that infall velocities calculated via the Myers method fell significantly below true mass-weighted values (0.153 and 0.228 km/s). CS-derived values reached about half the true velocity, while HCO+ underestimated by an order of magnitude. The discrepancy arises because self-absorption features in optically-thick lines originate in outer core regions with lower velocities, rather than reflecting peak infall rates.

The authors conclude that commonly-used techniques systematically underestimate true infall velocities and mass accretion rates, potentially by an order of magnitude. They suggest intrinsic velocity dispersion from optically-thin lines may provide better estimates in simple collapsing cores, though this may not apply to turbulent environments.

Dr Sachiendra Amaragiri, an Indian-origin surgeon, has been struck off the UK's medical practitioners' register after a Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service hearing found he abused his professional position by writing a love letter to a female patient, referred to as Patient A, whom he had treated for a stomach complaint. The letter, which also invited her for coffee, distressed the patient and prompted her to contact police. Amaragiri, 59, who worked at Russells Hall Hospital in Dudley, denied taking advantage of the patient, calling it a "moment of madness," and has apologised. He intends to appeal the decision.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC reporting that, effective March 11, 2021, Jerome Guillen transitioned from President, Automotive to President, Tesla Heavy Trucking. In his previous role since September 2018, Guillen oversaw Tesla's vehicle programs, supply chain, and service infrastructure. He will now lead the Tesla Semi program, including its charging and servicing networks, as Tesla enters the heavy trucks market. The report was signed by CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn on March 12, 2021.

Sony has launched a rebate and trade-in promotion in the United States, running through September 30, 2017. Customers can receive up to $300 in instant savings on select Sony cameras, plus an additional $500 for trading in an interchangeable lens camera. Savings of up to $200 are available on A7 cameras and up to $100 on select full-frame lenses and accessories. All offers include free U.S. shipping. Discounted items include various Sony Alpha a7R II and a7S II kits, as well as select Sony lenses.

Compass Minerals International (CMP) is rated a "Buy" due to attractive valuation and operational improvements. Revenue and volumes in salt and plant nutrition are increasing, while cost-cutting measures are boosting cash flow and EBITDA. Although CMP has higher net debt and leverage than peers, it trades at lower multiples, suggesting upside potential. Management anticipates further revenue growth in 2025, but leverage concerns prevent a "Strong Buy" rating.

The CANSLIM method, developed by William O'Neill and detailed in his book *How To Make Money In Stocks*, uses seven criteria to identify strong-performing stocks. The acronym represents factors including quarterly earnings, annual earnings growth, new products/management, supply and demand, leadership status, institutional sponsorship, and market direction.

Backtests indicate the strategy has outperformed the S&P 500 since 2003, with one report showing 18% CAGR versus 9%. However, this outperformance comes with higher volatility and larger drawdowns, partly attributable to its small-cap bias. The method has underperformed in recent years.

Investors' Business Daily publishes the IBD 50, a computer-generated list of top stocks meeting CANSLIM criteria, available to subscribers. Exposure can also be gained through the Innovator IBD 50 ETF. The method is considered suited for long-term investing and is difficult to backtest due to its combined fundamental and technical requirements.

The speaker expresses satisfaction with a recent win, crediting Rucchin's two goals and Jiggy's strong play. He acknowledges contributing offensively after a slow start in the finals and emphasizes the team's consistent preparation under Mike's guidance. He describes himself as a lead-by-example player rather than a vocal one. Regarding a hit from Scott, he says it's in the past and he would make the same plays again. He attributes the two losses in New Jersey to the team lacking energy, but expresses confidence in their road performance. He discusses the importance of the Stanley Cup, his ability to sleep well, and the need to tighten up defensively. He recalls being checked by a doctor after a hard stick hit and returning to play. He describes the rivalry as intense competition rather than hate, and fondly recalls a past comeback win involving Rucchin.

Peter Crouch made a joke on Twitter following the birth of the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge's third child, referencing his own height of 6ft 7inches. The tweet received over 22,000 retweets. His wife, Abbey Clancy, responded with a brief reply that drew significant attention and amusement from users. Earlier, Crystal Palace's official Twitter account had also posted a joke, playing on an AFP news announcement about the birth as though it revealed the baby's name. The Duchess delivered the 8lbs 7oz boy at St Mary's Hospital, Paddington, on St George's Day, with Prince William present.

Mark Jackson and Jeff Van Gundy, both former NBA coaches and current ESPN analysts, express concern about the Golden State Warriors' tendency to fall behind early and rely on comebacks, despite their talent. The Warriors led the NBA in third-quarter scoring and overcame large deficits in Games 6 and 7 of the Western Conference finals against the Houston Rockets. However, this strategy failed in Games 2, 4, and 5. Jackson warns that consistently digging such holes will eventually catch up with the team. The passage compares the Warriors' comeback style to racehorse Silky Sullivan, runner Dave Wottle, and the early-2000s Oakland A's.

Investors are purchasing closed-end equity mutual fund schemes on stock exchanges, where existing investors sell them at discounts to their net asset values (NAVs) due to poor liquidity. Buyers benefit because redemption at maturity occurs at NAV, making the discount a profit. Examples include Reliance Close Ended Mutual Fund Series A Growth (10% discount) and HDFC Equity Opportunities Fund (6% discount). The discount depends on time remaining until maturity and tax implications—shorter timeframes typically yield higher discounts due to short-term capital gains tax. Anup Bhaiya of Money Honey Financial Services advises focusing on schemes with assets exceeding Rs 250 crore, as larger funds are more likely to see trading activity.

Airbus is developing Project Vahana, an autonomous flying car designed as a helicopter-style vehicle to transport multiple passengers as an airborne taxi service. CEO Tom Enders announced the initiative at the DLD digital tech conference in Munich, stating the technology is now available to move urban transport skyward. Airbus aims to use clean technology and reduce infrastructure costs, with a functional prototype targeted for 2017 and short-haul service by 2021. Other companies pursuing flying vehicles include Uber, Urban Aeronautics (which developed the Cormorant passenger drone), and AeroMobil. Investors like Skype's co-founder and Google's Larry Page have also funded flying car projects.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael Ben'Ary of the Eastern District of Virginia was fired during his prosecution of a suspect in the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing, according to a letter bearing his typed signature taped to his door. The letter claimed his termination resulted from a false social media post and criticized DOJ leadership for prioritizing punishment of perceived Trump enemies over national security.

The firing followed a social media post by commentator Julie Kelly, who suggested Ben'Ary was allied with former Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco and part of internal resistance to indicting former FBI Director James Comey. Comey was indicted by Ben'Ary's new boss, interim U.S. Attorney Halligan, who replaced the previous U.S. Attorney after Trump pressured him to indict Comey.

The passage describes a light emitting diode (LED) device and its manufacturing method, aimed at providing a reliable connection structure between luminous bodies and their electrodes.

The LED device comprises a thin film transistor substrate with multiple light emitting areas, first and second diode electrodes, a first passivation pattern positioned between the electrodes, multiple micro light emitting diodes (NLDs) on the passivation pattern, and first and second bridge patterns that electrically connect the diode electrodes to the micro LEDs. A key structural feature is that the sidewalls of each micro LED align on the same plane with the sidewalls of the first passivation pattern, minimizing steps that could break the bridge patterns.

Each micro LED has a cylindrical shape with a light emitting material (inorganic crystal structure containing p-type semiconductor, intermediate layer, and n-type semiconductor) surrounded by a protective insulating layer. The first and second sidewalls expose the p-type and n-type semiconductors respectively, contacting the corresponding bridge patterns.

The device also includes a display architecture with a luminescent panel of light emitting units driven by scan drivers, data drivers, a power supply, and a timing controller. Each light emitting unit contains three thin film transistors and a capacitor.

The manufacturing method involves forming the passivation patterns and micro LEDs through a single mask process with two etching steps. The first etching is more anisotropic and longer; the second is more isotropic, shorter, and uses an oxygen-containing additive gas. Micro LEDs are aligned by applying voltage between the diode electrodes to create an electric field.

Thursday marks win-or-go-home Game 3s in the MLB wild-card round, only the second time in baseball history that three decisive playoff games occur in one day. The Tigers must improve their conversion of scoring opportunities, having gone 3-for-38 with runners in scoring position across recent elimination games. The Padres-Cubs matchup features starters Yu Darvish and Jameson Taillon, with bullpen depth likely decisive. For the Yankees-Red Sox game, Boston's bullpen is taxed after Alex Cora used six relievers in Game 2, making starter length critical.

Aspen, Colorado, is replacing its traditional Fourth of July fireworks with a 15-minute drone show due to wildfire risks amid drought conditions. Organised by the Aspen Chamber Resort Association in Wagner Park, 50 drones will display patriotic colours set to music. The decision follows strict fire restrictions across western Colorado. Spokeswoman Melissa Wisenbaker said alternatives were needed given increasing annual fire dangers. The event may have been inspired by the 2018 Winter Olympics opening ceremony in Pyeongchang, which featured 1,218 drones forming the Olympic rings, though that display was later revealed to be pre-recorded due to weather concerns.

The US national debt surpassed $21 trillion on Friday, exceeding the size of the US economy. The debt grew by $73 billion in a single day, $215 billion in February, and over $1 trillion in the past six months, despite no major economic crisis. Debt growth is outpacing GDP growth: while the economy grew 4.4% last year including inflation, the national debt grew 6%. Over the past decade, the economy grew 36% while the national debt grew 123%, from $9.4 trillion to over $21 trillion. The author argues the debt matters, as defaulting on obligations to Social Security, US banks, or the Federal Reserve would cause severe financial consequences. The author categorizes people into three groups: those who ignore the debt, those who believe it doesn't matter, and those who rationally prepare for potential consequences.

Jio announced new offers on the Samsung Galaxy J2 2018 and Galaxy J7 Duo under the Jio Galaxy Club. Both smartphones, priced at Rs 8,190 and Rs 16,990 respectively, will come with an instant cashback of Rs 2,750 in the form of 55 vouchers of Rs 50 each. Galaxy J2 2018 buyers using a Jio SIM will receive an additional 100GB data on Rs 198 and Rs 299 plans, bringing the effective price to Rs 5,440. Galaxy J7 Duo buyers get doubled daily data on the same plans. The offer is valid until September 30. The Galaxy J2 2018 features a 5-inch qHD display, Snapdragon 425, 2GB RAM, and a 2600mAh battery, while the Galaxy J7 Duo has a 5.5-inch HD display, Exynos 7 processor, 4GB RAM, and a 3000mAh battery.

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) finalized rules requiring payday and auto title lenders to verify borrowers' ability to repay loans within 30 days, and limiting lenders' ability to repeatedly debit borrowers' accounts. CFPB Director Richard Cordray said the rules prevent lenders from trapping borrowers in unaffordable loans. A 2014 CFPB study found over 80 percent of payday loans are rolled over or followed by another loan within two weeks.

The Financial Services Association of America argues the rule would devastate the $39 billion industry, which serves 30-40 million customers annually, and push borrowers toward unregulated lenders. The CFPB estimates loan volume could be halved, affecting many of the 16,000 payday lender stores across 35 states. Fifteen states have already banned such lenders.

The rule would not take effect until 2019 and could be rolled back by Congress. The CFPB has faced opposition from the Trump administration and Republican lawmakers, including legislative efforts to cut its funding and weaken the Dodd-Frank Act. A Pew Charitable Trusts poll found 70 percent of surveyed American adults want more regulation of payday lenders.

This study investigated predictive biomarkers for immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) response in sarcomas by analyzing pre-treatment biopsies from 67 patients across three ICI clinical trials, with validation in 190 TCGA samples.

Using RNA-seq-based immune deconvolution (MCP-counter) and hierarchical clustering, tumors were classified into two distinct groups: "immune-hot" and "immune-cold." Immune-hot tumors showed significantly greater abundance of immune cell populations, lower tumor purity, and elevated expression of immune checkpoint genes (CD274, CTLA4, LAG3). These classifications aligned with previously described sarcoma immune classes (SICs).

Clinically, immune-hot tumors had higher overall response rates (30% vs. 8.1%) and longer progression-free survival (3.65 vs. 1.7 months) compared to immune-cold tumors, independent of sarcoma subtype.

Lasso logistic regression identified transposable elements (TEs) and the transcription factor IKZF1 as predictive of immune type. Signature TEs included MER57F, MER45A, Tigger17a, MER61F, LTR104_Mam, and HERVL74.int. A combined TE score and IKZF1 expression correlated positively with immune pathways (cGAS-STING, type I/II interferon, antigen-processing, CD8+ T cell effector) but not non-immune pathways. High TE scores and IKZF1 expression were associated with prolonged progression-free survival.

Conditional independence analysis suggested IKZF1 regulates TE expression, which determines immune type. Findings were replicated in the TCGA validation cohort, where immune-hot classification, high TE score, and high IKZF1 expression correlated with improved overall survival.

Limitations included small sample size, sarcoma heterogeneity, variable ICI regimens, and polyadenylated transcript selection. The authors propose IKZF1 expression and TE score as potential predictive biomarkers for ICI response and suggest pharmacologic de-repression of TEs as a therapeutic avenue to convert immune-cold tumors to immune-hot phenotypes.

Meagan Holt participates in a writing program at Seattle Children's Hospital to help cope with her 3-year-old daughter Madeline's terminal illness, Zellweger Syndrome. The program, offered by the Pediatric Advanced Care Team (PACT), encourages parents to journal as a way to express emotions. Consultant Julie Arguez states the practice empowers parents and brings calm, relief, and acceptance. Holt says writing provides an outlet and helps her stay strong. The program is funded by donations.

Happy Home Furnishers is closing its Neath store after 33 years, with managing director Mike Semmens citing anti-social behaviour, rising business rates, and lack of free parking as reasons. Semmens described staff encountering fights, vomit, blood, and drug needles near the store, blaming a bench installed outside a nearby shop, which took years to remove. Other local traders confirmed anti-social behaviour, particularly in summer, though some said it was manageable. Semmens also criticised wide pavements replacing parking spaces, arguing free short-stay parking would attract shoppers. Neath Council stated the street improvements benefited the town, the bench was removed about a year ago, and it is working with police to tackle anti-social behaviour. The council highlighted a new 600-space multi-storey car park with free parking after 3pm. The Welsh Government noted business rates relief schemes supporting small businesses. Happy Home Furnishers continues trading at other locations and may seek a new Neath site.

This study explores physics teachers' perspectives on physics education research, focusing on potential scepticism regarding its practical value. The research addresses a notable gap, as teachers' attitudes towards educational research are known to influence whether scientific findings are implemented in practice.

Using a two-step mixed-methods approach, the researchers first conducted interviews with 13 German physics teachers, then surveyed 174 teachers from Germany and Austria. The interviews identified seven main attitudes—both sceptical and non-sceptical—including views that research findings play a minor role compared to personal experience, cannot be implemented in practice, and that research-practice cooperation is poor.

Exploratory factor analysis of the survey data revealed four dimensions of science scepticism: (1) relevance for the individual teacher, (2) feasibility of findings for practice, (3) relevance for teaching practice in general, and (4) cooperation between research and practice. Latent profile analysis identified four teacher profiles: The Sceptical Ones (14%), who reject research value entirely; The Uncertain Ones (27%), with neutral views; The Undersupplied Ones (41%), who value research but find it impractical; and The Research Advocates (18%), who hold the most positive views.

Multinomial logistic regression showed that among tested variables (teaching experience, teacher education, school type, doctoral degree, journal reading frequency), only the frequency of reading instructional journals significantly predicted profile membership.

The authors conclude that while physics teachers are not generally sceptical, meaningful scepticism exists, particularly regarding research-practice cooperation. They recommend better integration of research into teacher education and closer collaboration between researchers and practitioners. Limitations include small and convenience samples, potential Hawthorne effects, and measurement challenges regarding journal reading frequency.

The Baltimore Ravens traded pass rusher Odafe Oweh and a 2026 fifth-round pick to the Los Angeles Chargers for safety Alohi Gilman. Oweh, 26, recorded 10 sacks last season but none in his first five games this year, with his playing time dropping to 45% of defensive snaps. The trade frees approximately $8 million in cap space for Baltimore, which also signed safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson to its practice squad. The Ravens (1-4) have allowed the most points in the NFL (35.4 per game) and rank 31st in pass defense. Gilman, 28, was a key part of the Chargers' top-ranked defense last season. For the Chargers, Oweh provides edge depth while Khalil Mack recovers from an elbow injury.

At the 18th Forum for VAT Administrators in Africa (VADA) in Lilongwe, Malawi's Secretary to the Treasury, Ben Botolo, urged African countries to adopt modern technology to address tax non-compliance. He noted that electronic fiscal devices are critical for optimizing tax revenue, but many African nations remain cash-based economies, complicating collection. Botolo stated Malawi has progressed in electronic tax monitoring and is developing a Tax Administration Act. VADA Chairperson Henry Saka emphasized formalizing regulatory strategies and designing African solutions to tax evasion. VADA has 10 member countries and provides technical support to 12 non-members, convening to share compliance challenges and propose interventions.

The lecture reviews properties of the propagator G(x, x'), interpreted heuristically as a transition amplitude between spacetime points or as a correlation function between field values. The Feynman (time-ordered) propagator G_F combines G+ and G- depending on time ordering.

The propagator's integral expression has poles on the real axis at ω = ±ω_k. Different contour choices around these poles produce the retarded (G_R), advanced (G_A), Feynman (G_F), and anti-Feynman propagators. A convenient alternative is the epsilon prescription, which slightly shifts pole locations rather than deforming contours, making calculations more tractable.

For free theories, n-point vacuum correlation functions factorize into sums of products of two-point functions, since creation and annihilation operators must pair. Composite operators (products of fields at the same point) generally yield divergences requiring renormalization, a recurring theme in quantum field theory.

The lecture then introduces interactions via adding a λφ⁴/4! term to the free Lagrangian. The resulting nonlinear equation of motion cannot be solved exactly, necessitating perturbative expansion in small λ.

Interactions are probed experimentally through scattering, characterized by the S-matrix, defined using idealized initial and final states at t = ±∞ where particles are infinitely separated and non-interacting. The S-matrix is written as S = 1 + iT, where T captures interactions. Momentum conservation allows extracting a delta function, defining the scattering amplitude M_αβ. The S-matrix is unitary and respects symmetries of the Hamiltonian.

The LSZ theorem (stated without proof) relates scattering amplitudes to time-ordered correlation functions in the interacting vacuum. The next lecture will introduce the path integral approach.

The President writes to the Senate to clarify potential misunderstandings of a prior message and protest sent on the 17th (15th). He affirms that the message was not intended to deny the legislative branch's authority to provide by law for the custody, safekeeping, and disposition of public money and property.

He acknowledges the constitutional power of the Legislature to designate where public funds are deposited and to regulate their custody and removal. He disclaims any executive right over public property or treasure except as granted by law, and disclaims authority to supervise persons entrusted with such property unless they are officers appointed by the President, alone or with the Senate, for whom he bears constitutional responsibility.

He requests that this communication be entered on the Senate Journal as part of the original message to prevent misattribution of views or claims of power not granted by the Constitution and laws.

The speaker discusses the team's preparation for upcoming games against Philadelphia, emphasizing the importance of staying focused and winning away games. He notes that several players, including Vernon, Murphy, and Kocur, have prior experience in similar situations. Regarding goaltender Mike, the speaker praises his resilience and confidence, citing strong performances against Grant Fuhr and Patrick Roy.

The speaker addresses penalties taken during the previous game, stating they weren't foolish, and commends the team for not retaliating. He comments on a missed scoring play, believing the right decision was made despite the outcome.

On team chemistry, he highlights successful defensive pairings: Fetisov with Konstantinov, and Murphy with Lidstrom, noting Murphy's puck-handling experience. Reflecting on a past series loss to the Devils, he acknowledges their defensive strength and Neal Broten's contribution.

He also discusses Kirk Maltby's transition to left wing due to the team's surplus of right wingers, mentioning prior trades of Ray Sheppard and Dino Ciccarelli. The team plans to stay away from the arena the night before the game, as has been their playoff routine.

This patent application describes a sidelink positioning method and apparatus for improved terminal device positioning accuracy. Existing positioning technologies rely on core network control and reference signal measurements between network devices and terminal devices, where positioning errors increase with distance, making them unsuitable for high-accuracy scenarios.

The proposed solution uses sidelink signals between terminal devices to determine relative or absolute positions. The method involves:

1. A network device sends sidelink positioning configurations to a first and second terminal device, potentially after receiving a position information request from the first terminal device.

2. The first terminal device sends a first sidelink positioning reference signal to the second terminal device, which measures it to obtain a first measurement value (including Rx–Tx time difference and/or angle of arrival).

3. Optionally, the second terminal device sends a second sidelink positioning reference signal to the first terminal device, generating a second measurement value.

4. Measurement values are exchanged via Uu interface (to network device) or PC5 interface (between terminal devices).

5. The first terminal device's position is calculated based on these measurement values and the second terminal device's position, either by the first terminal device itself or by the network device.

Because measurements use nearby terminal devices as references rather than distant network devices, positioning accuracy is improved. Additionally, measurements bypass the core network, reducing positioning latency. The solution also accommodates terminal devices that don't support sidelink reference signal measurement by allowing another terminal device to perform measurements on their behalf. The application is applicable to various communication systems including LTE, 5G NR, V2X, and IoT networks.

The passage describes figures illustrating two embodiments of an analytical instrument design, including perspective, front, back, side, top, and bottom views of each. Features shown in broken lines are not part of the claimed design.

Marcel Strigberger, a retired Toronto lawyer, describes decluttering his home by discarding his McGill University law schoolbooks purchased over 50 years ago. He reflects on each book before disposing of it, including a contracts text by Cheshire and Fifoot featuring memorable cases like the Carbolic Smokeball case and an 1860s ruling involving a carriage owner and a prostitute deemed unenforceable on public policy grounds. He also tossed a property law book by Magarry and Wade, noting concepts like "fee simple" and "fee tail" rarely arose in his 42-year practice, though he later saw a used copy listed on Amazon for over $1,000 Canadian. He discarded a book referencing the Wagon Mound cargo ship case as well. All books went into the recycling bin, except one thick volume he kept to use as a reading stand.

In June 2014, analyst Abby Devins read that Hertz Global Holdings would have to restate three years of financial results due to widespread accounting problems, causing its stock to drop 9%. Devins questioned whether the issues related to Hertz's large rental fleet.

The U.S. car rental industry generated roughly $36 billion in 2013, dominated by Enterprise, Avis Budget, and Hertz, which together held 71% market share. Founded in 1918 by Walter Jacobs and later sold to John Hertz, the company changed ownership multiple times before being taken public again in 2006. By 2013, Hertz operated nearly 12,000 locations across 145 countries with over 700,000 rental cars, reporting record revenue and EBITDA driven by acquisitions like Dollar Thrifty and Donlen, and expansion into China.

Revenue earning equipment comprised over 50% of Hertz's assets, making depreciation significant. Depreciation requires estimates of useful life and residual value, typically applied via the straight-line method. Hertz reassessed depreciation rates quarterly based on market conditions. Its fleet included program cars (with manufacturer repurchase guarantees) and non-program cars (subject to residual price risk). Over 2006–2013, Hertz extended the useful life range for cars from 5–16 months to 4–36 months, while program car purchases in the U.S. declined sharply. Devins compiled depreciation data comparing Hertz with Avis Budget to assess the potential role of depreciation in Hertz's accounting issues.

AI, particularly LLMs, has the potential to augment human cognition, learning, and creativity, but also poses risks including over-reliance and limited internalization of skills. Mitigation requires avoiding passive learning, fostering critical thinking, and designing AI as an enhancer rather than replacement of human intelligence.

AI may reshape the social division of labor by reducing knowledge scarcity and blurring job boundaries, potentially shrinking the traditional middle class. Foreseeable changes include the rise of the gig economy, which offers flexibility but lacks labor protections, and new forms of global collaboration based on dynamic, network-based partnerships. Managing these shifts requires regulations, evolved welfare and education systems, and cross-sector cooperation.

In social sciences, LLMs offer opportunities to synthesize research data, automate analysis, and explore novel theories, though challenges include biases, ethical concerns like misinformation, and questions about originality. Human-AI collaboration is essential to maintain rigor.

Regulatory frameworks face challenges including inconsistent international standards, gaps between industry and government, and difficulty identifying risks promptly. Responsible AI development requires forward-looking, top-down and bottom-up governance, partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers, and mechanisms for timely regulatory updates.

The TLV32xx comparator family requires unused inputs to be tied to a voltage within the input range with at least 50mV differential, rather than tied together, to prevent high-frequency chatter. The devices have 1.8mV of internal hysteresis, with a transfer curve defined by VTH, VOS, and VHYST.

The TLV321x offers a push-pull output that can sink and source current, must never be shorted to a supply rail or connected to another output, and unused outputs should be left floating. The TLV322x offers an open-drain output that can be pulled up to 5.5V independent of V+, with recommended pull-up currents between 100µA and 1mA. Both include ESD protection and a Power-On Reset circuit that holds output low for up to 32µs after V+ crosses 1.65V.

In application, the comparator outputs high or low depending on whether VIN exceeds VREF, with propagation delay influenced by overdrive voltage. External hysteresis can be added via resistor networks in inverting or non-inverting configurations to prevent output chatter. Example applications include low-side current sensing.

Proper layout requires low-ESR 0.1µF bypass capacitors near the supply pin, minimized coupling between inputs and outputs, and treatment as high-speed logic devices. The devices support split or single supplies.

Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike, during a courtesy visit by US Ambassador to Nigeria William Symington, called on the US Government to establish a Visa Office in Port Harcourt to serve the South-South and South-East regions, stating it would create opportunities for the people.

Wike described the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) as a fundraising body for politicians seeking elections, alleging that it funded APC's rerun elections in Rivers State and that its Managing Director is accumulating wealth to contest the Akwa Ibom governorship election. He claimed the NDDC failed to act on a 2016 list of beneficial projects submitted by the state and reneged on its N900 million counterpart funding for the Mother and Child Hospital, despite the state paying its N800 million share. The state has since taken over the hospital's construction.

Wike also called for the clean-up of Ogoni land, expressed interest in partnering with the US in agriculture, oil and gas, and industrialization, and urged government focus on governance rather than the 2019 elections. Ambassador Symington stated his visit aimed at engaging with the state's people.

Coach Vigneault acknowledges he has not personally spoken to Dan but notes his assistants and teammates have, describing a bad puck bounce as something to move past. Reviewing game footage, Vigneault emphasizes the opponent is exceptionally strong and the team cannot win without every player bringing their "A game," as their "B game" will not suffice. He felt the first period was competitive but the third period was inadequate against the opponent's strong push.

On personnel, he praises Johnny's consistent play among the six defensemen and Rafa's contributions. He describes the opponent as experienced, structured, skilled, and physical, executing their game plan without deviation, making it difficult to exploit weaknesses. He contrasts them with previous opponents: Philadelphia (physical), Pittsburgh (skilled with edge), and Montréal (structured).

Vigneault states the team must focus on the next game with adjustments, emphasizing compete level, execution, and sticking to the plan. He commends Rick for strong, competitive play and defensive contributions, expecting his scoring chances to convert. He stresses playing to the team's strengths, particularly speed, and praises a key defenseman's improving stamina and two-way play throughout the playoffs.

The lecture addresses pathways to nuclear war, proliferation, the Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), and prospects for abolition. The speaker contrasts nuclear war, which has low daily but catastrophic probability, with climate change, which is near-certain but gradual.

Debates persist over whether nuclear weapons deter war or whether non-use since 1945 reflects luck or taboo. Key pathways to nuclear war identified include accidental launches between the US and Russia (via early warning malfunctions or cyber attacks) and escalation from conventional conflict between India and Pakistan, with Pakistan's aggressive deployment posture and delegated command raising particular concern. North Korea is considered a lesser but special risk.

The speaker traces the post-WWII arms buildup, noting that early scientists like Franck, Bethe, and Weisskopf predicted arms races if no agreement was reached. Stockpiles grew into tens of thousands before declining through treaties, though roughly 1,000 weapons remain on hair-trigger alert on each side.

The NPT is described as effective in limiting proliferation but undermined by nuclear states' failure to disarm under Article VI. The 2015 review was expected to be contentious. Regarding Iran, the speaker supports the interim agreement, citing rigorous IAEA inspections and Iran's stated rejection of weapons.

Obama's record is called mixed: the Prague speech and New START Treaty were positive, but modernization programs, hair-trigger alerts, and disengagement from North Korea are criticized. US policy toward India is faulted for aggravating Pakistan tensions through nuclear and military deals.

The speaker argues deterrence is overrated, requires rationality, enables brinkmanship, and fails against terrorists. Abolition, while unlikely soon, should be pursued as risk minimization. Conventional precision weapons increasingly substitute for nuclear deterrence, blurring future arms control boundaries.

The passage advocates for the creation of a Cabinet-level secretary of commerce to address growing issues of labor, capital, and corporate oversight, citing support from commercial bodies. It discusses plans to submit a reciprocity treaty with Cuba to the Senate, arguing that Cuba's political ties to the U.S. under the Platt amendment warrant economic integration and friendly relations with sister republics. A reciprocal trade convention with Great Britain regarding Newfoundland has been concluded. The passage praises The Hague international tribunal, noting the U.S. and Mexico were the first to use it, and encourages arbitration over war where possible. It also commends the Hawaiian fire claims to Congress and supports building an isthmian canal, preferably at Panama, pending negotiations with Colombia, describing it as a major engineering endeavor to continue across administrations.

The Council for the Protection of Rural England Bedfordshire (CPRE) has criticised Central Bedfordshire Council's (CBC) claim that 44,000 to 55,000 new homes are needed over 20 years. A Freedom of Information request revealed that 60% of these homes would be for people moving into the area, with only 41% meeting the needs of current residents. The 2017 'Initial Strategic Housing Market Assessment' identified an Objectively Assessed Need of 32,000 dwellings for 2015–2035, to which CBC added 7,400 homes for Luton residents and up to 20% contingency. CPRE argues the scale is unsustainable and threatens countryside, while CBC states it is legally required to plan for migration trends using a government-mandated formula.

President Andrew Johnson transmits to the House of Representatives further correspondence regarding General Grant's vacation of the War Office. In a letter dated February 10, 1868, Johnson responds to Grant's letter of February 3, which characterized Johnson's earlier correspondence as containing "many and gross misrepresentations." Johnson encloses statements from five Cabinet members (Welles, McCulloch, Randall, Browning, and Seward) who were present at the January 14 Cabinet meeting, all substantially corroborating Johnson's account.

Johnson argues that Grant admitted accepting the Secretary of War ad interim position with the intent to circumvent the President's purpose of keeping Stanton out of office and forcing a judicial test of the Tenure of Office Act. Johnson contends Grant had promised either to retain the office pending court proceedings or to resign in time to allow appointment of a replacement, but instead surrendered it to Stanton without notice.

Johnson also addresses Grant's refusal to obey a written order of January 29 directing him to disregard War Department orders purporting to come from the President unless personally authorized by the Executive. Johnson asserts Grant has taken an insubordinate position by deferring to Stanton over the Commander in Chief.

In a February 11 response, Grant denies intending to disobey legal presidential orders, explaining his interpretation was based on being the only subordinate instructed to disregard Stanton's authority, while other departments continued recognizing Stanton as Secretary of War. Supporting correspondence from the Treasury and Post Office Departments is included.

Woodstock grief specialists Vicki Travnicek and Nicole Bruder of the Surviving Suicide Grief Support Group offer strategies for coping with loss during the holidays. These include limiting events, having an exit plan, being honest with hosts, feeling emotions, sharing memories, practicing self-care, and creating new traditions while maintaining some old ones. Travnicek, who lost two brothers to suicide, noted the group has operated for 20 years and has met at Smith Leroy since May 2017. Facilitated by trained peer volunteers, it meets twice monthly, resuming in January. Additional grief programs include "Understanding Your Grief," starting April 4 in Woodstock, and an eight-week "Healing Journey Through Grief" program in Ingersoll from Feb. 1 to March 22.
