The study employed a single-group posttest experimental design to evaluate an eight-week activity-based guitar lesson plan for five beginner volunteer students (ages 18-33) with no prior guitar training. Online one-on-one lessons of 50 minutes each were conducted, covering scales, chords, and arpeggios.

The lesson plans followed a 3E model (introduction, development, evaluation) adapted from the 5E model. Topics included major scales (C, G, F), minor scales (A, E, D in natural, harmonic, and melodic forms), open and barre chords, and arpeggio techniques.

Assessment combined a theoretical knowledge test (40% weight) and performance test (60% weight), evaluated by three field experts using Albuz's (2001) performance scale with criteria including pitch accuracy, tempo, technique, and musicality.

Results showed theoretical test scores averaging 92 points. Individual overall achievement scores were 91, 89.2, 95.5, 93.6, and 98.8, with a class average of 93.6. All students completed the chapter with a "very good" grade.

The findings align with prior research indicating activity-based instruction enhances student engagement, listening skills, and academic achievement, supporting its effectiveness in amateur guitar education during the Covid-19 pandemic.

The Digital Business Ecosystem (DBE) results from the co-evolution of Business and Digital Ecosystems, with its lifecycle consisting of formation, evolution, and dissipation phases. The formation phase is critical, with negotiation being its most important activity. The Contract Net Protocol (CNP), later extended by FIPA, is a widely used negotiation protocol that decomposes the process into sequential steps with defined message formats.

This paper proposes an extension called Contract Net with Quality Protocol (CNQP), which introduces quality evaluation stages during negotiation. Specifically, it adds time slice tq1 for participants to evaluate the announcer's quality and tq2 for the initiator to evaluate participants' quality. Quality is assessed through a Quality Backbone Engine (QBE) and encompasses reliability, trust, and reputation.

While CNQP increases negotiation time, it reduces uncertainty and risk during contract execution, improving overall transaction performance. Future work will apply the protocol to negotiations on service level parameters.

Offensive tackles are crucial but often unrecognized members of the offensive line, tasked with blocking opposing pass rushers and defensive linemen one-on-one. They line up as the outermost linemen on both sides of the formation, filling 2 of the 5 offensive line positions. Their responsibilities include executing run or pass blocking schemes while reading pre-snap defensive looks, requiring high football IQ, athleticism, agility, and strength.

The position's name traces back to early football, when edge defenders frequently tackled ball carriers on outside runs. Common abbreviations include OT and T, with nicknames like "Hogs" and "Big Uglies."

NFL offensive tackles typically stand 6'3"–6'8" and weigh 300–340 pounds, combining size with lateral movement skills. The left tackle is especially valued for protecting the quarterback's blind side. Notable tackles include Jonathan Ogden, Anthony Munoz, and Joe Thomas.

The task force will combine prosecutors from the department's criminal division with U.S. attorneys' offices in Houston, New York, and San Francisco. Legal experts noted that such a task force for a single corporate investigation is unprecedented. Enron attorney Robert Bennett viewed the consolidation positively, as it reduces the burden of dealing with multiple investigating entities.

In separate proceedings, U.S. District Judge Lee Rosenthal declined to freeze over $1 billion in assets from 29 Enron executives and directors named in a shareholder lawsuit, though she confirmed she had authority to do so.

The White House disclosed that Vice President Dick Cheney or his aides met with Enron representatives six times in 2001 while drafting national energy policy, with the last meeting occurring October 10, days before Enron's financial troubles became public. Comptroller General David Walker indicated he would decide within a month whether to sue the White House over access to energy task force records. Education Minister Mitzie Hunter recently wrote a letter to the editor claiming the Ontario government remains committed to rural students, citing $1,000 more in per-pupil spending for rural students, new school construction, and renovations. She criticized Conservative leader Patrick Brown's call for a moratorium on school closings, arguing it would limit local school boards' decision-making power. A new study analyzing data from 1,856 adults with a lifetime history of psychosis found that cannabis use among this population rose nearly 10% five years after states legalized recreational marijuana, with the largest increase tied to commercialization in retail shops. Study co-author Andrew Hyatt, a psychiatrist at Cambridge Health Alliance, noted that THC can induce and worsen psychosis, particularly in high-potency forms. Research links cannabis use to earlier onset and worse prognosis of psychosis, including more severe symptoms and higher medication needs, according to psychiatrist Matthew Large. Despite these risks, only two states require warnings about high-potency cannabis and psychosis, per a 2024 study. Researchers suggest potency caps and health warnings could reduce harm. Limitations of the study include an overrepresentation of women and self-reported diagnoses. The biological mechanism linking cannabis and psychosis remains unclear, and researchers call for additional datasets to examine the impact of high-potency products.

The passage describes several distributed system design patterns using containers and FaaS.

The **adapter pattern** uses a sidecar container to modify an application's interface to conform to a standard one, enabling consistent monitoring, logging, or health-checking across heterogeneous applications. Examples include using Prometheus exporters for Redis metrics, Fluentd plugins for normalizing logs, and adapter containers for MySQL health checks. This approach promotes modularity and reuse without modifying original application containers.

**Multi-node distributed patterns** include microservices, which decouple applications into independently scalable services communicating via APIs, improving agility but complicating debugging.

**Replicated load-balanced services** handle stateless workloads, requiring at least two replicas for high availability and readiness probes for proper load balancing. Session-tracked variants use consistent hashing to route users to specific replicas. Caching layers (e.g., Varnish) and SSL termination (e.g., nginx) can be added as separate replicated tiers.

**Sharded services** distribute data across replicas when it exceeds single-machine capacity, commonly used for stateful services and caches. Sharding functions must be deterministic and uniform, often using consistent hashing to minimize remapping during resizing. Replicated sharded caches add resilience, and hot sharding handles uneven load.

**Scatter/gather patterns** parallelize request processing across leaf nodes, combining partial results at a root node. Performance is limited by overhead and the "straggler" problem, where the slowest leaf determines overall latency. Sharding and replication improve scale and reliability.

**FaaS/event-driven patterns** simplify deployment but face challenges with debugging, background processing, in-memory data, and cost at scale. The decorator pattern transforms requests/responses (e.g., adding defaults), while event handlers process asynchronous events like two-factor authentication.

Researchers from the University of Exeter claim to have refined James Lovelock's 1970s 'Gaia' hypothesis, which proposed Earth is a self-regulating living organism where life interacts with inorganic processes to maintain planetary conditions despite threats like solar brightening, volcanoes, and meteorite strikes.

According to Professor Tim Lenton, the original hypothesis could not explain how Earth developed stabilising properties over geological timescales through natural selection. The researchers propose that 'sequential selection' is key: destabilising situations are short-lived and lead to further change until a stable state emerges and persists. Once stable, the system gains time to acquire additional stabilising traits through 'selection by survival alone'.

Co-author Dr James Dyke noted the mechanisms could help estimate the likelihood of complex life elsewhere and understand Earth's response to human-caused climate change and extinction events. The paper, "Selection for Gaia across multiple scales," was published in Trends in Ecology and Evolution.

Hard-to-borrow stocks in the US underperform over 3-, 6-, and 12-month periods, while this pattern does not hold in Japan and Europe, according to Verdad Research's analysis of nearly 30,000 stocks from 2005 to 2023. Despite this negative edge, a profitable short-selling strategy is unlikely because obtaining a short locate is difficult.

Short selling requires borrowing shares through a broker, who facilitates lending from other clients. Selling without a locate constitutes illegal naked short selling. Stocks become hard to borrow due to limited supply, high demand, regulatory restrictions like Regulation SHO, elevated stock loan fees (ranging from 1% to 50%), and locate requirements.

Borrowing costs depend on stock size, stability, liquidity, and volatility. Large, stable, liquid stocks have lower fees, while small, volatile, illiquid stocks cost more. Fees can fluctuate dramatically; for example, GameStop's short-borrow fee jumped from around 1% in January 2019 to 34% in January 2021 during its short squeeze. Short selling carries unlimited potential losses.

The lecture continues the discussion of numerical optimization methods. The instructor advises students to prioritize numerical techniques over chemical engineering definitions when solving assignment problems.

Steepest descent is reviewed as a method that follows the negative gradient downhill toward local minima, with optimal step sizes derived from a quadratic Taylor expansion. The method runs perpendicular to contour lines but struggles on flat landscapes or functions without a bottom.

Linear equations Ax=b can be reformulated as optimization problems by minimizing a quadratic functional, provided A is symmetric and positive definite. The conjugate gradient method improves upon steepest descent by choosing descent directions that preserve minimization from previous steps. Directions are chosen to be conjugate (p transpose A p = 0), allowing convergence in n steps for n-dimensional problems. It only requires matrix-vector products, making it suitable for large systems, and represents the state of the art for iterative linear solvers.

Newton-Raphson applied to grad f = 0 uses the Hessian as the Jacobian, converging quadratically and exactly in one step for quadratic functions. However, it seeks any critical point (not specifically minima) and fails when the Hessian is singular or has negative eigenvalues.

Trust-region methods combine steepest descent and Newton-Raphson heuristically. A trust-region radius Ri defines where the quadratic approximation is reliable. Newton-Raphson steps are preferred when they fall within the region and reduce f; otherwise steepest descent is used. The radius grows or shrinks based on how well the quadratic approximation predicts actual function values. Matlab's fsolve and minimizers use a dogleg variant of this approach, initializing Ri at 1.

The lecture introduces modern portfolio theory, building on the bullet-shaped curve representing risk-return trade-offs for portfolios of multiple securities. Andrew Lo argues that rational investors, who prefer higher returns and lower risk, will choose portfolios on the upper branch (efficient frontier), meaning no one should hold 100% of a single stock. Adding more securities to a portfolio cannot make an investor worse off, since unwanted stocks can be given zero weight, and generally shifts the efficient frontier northwest, improving risk-return trade-offs.

When a riskless asset (T-Bills) is combined with risky portfolios, the result is a straight line. The optimal line is tangent to the efficient frontier, touching it at the "tangency portfolio." All rational mean-variance investors, regardless of risk preferences, will want to be on this tangency line, differing only in how much they allocate between T-Bills and the tangency portfolio. The slope of this line is the Sharpe ratio, measuring expected excess return per unit of risk.

Lo contrasts this approach with Warren Buffett's stock-picking, noting the difficulty of identifying mispricings or finding negatively correlated stocks with positive returns. Correlations among stocks exist due to macroeconomic conditions and psychological factors.

Building on Markowitz's work, Bill Sharpe showed that if all investors hold the tangency portfolio, it must equal the market portfolio—all assets weighted by market capitalization (approximated by indices like the S&P 500). This equilibrium result yields a linear relationship between expected return and risk for efficient portfolios.

Sharpe extended this to any asset through the Capital Asset Pricing Model: an asset's expected return equals the risk-free rate plus beta times the market risk premium, where beta is the covariance of the asset with the market divided by the market's variance. This provides the appropriate discount rate for capital budgeting and financial decisions, measuring risk through covariance with the market rather than standalone volatility.

President Ford addressed Congress on combating inflation, calling it the nation's "public enemy number one." Citing recommendations from the Conference on Inflation, he outlined a 10-point program for joint executive-legislative action:

This paper addresses memory management challenges in long-running Low-Code/No-Code (LCNC) AI agents, specifically memory inflation and contextual degradation caused by finite LLM context windows. Central to the system is an "Intelligent Decay" mechanism that assigns each memory entry a Utility Score based on recency, relevance, and user-assigned utility, determining whether memories are retained, discarded, or consolidated. The AP Creation NAE event enables SEV-SNP guests to create, destroy, or modify vCPU register states at specified VMPL levels, providing an alternative AP boot method. Create/Add operations require the guest to issue RMPADJUST against the target VMSA page beforehand, and can either defer activation until INIT-SIPI or activate immediately.

The #HV doorbell page NAE event lets SEV-SNP guests register a doorbell page for hypervisor injection exceptions when Restricted Injection is enabled, supporting GET_PREFERRED, SET, QUERY, and CLEAR actions. The #HV Send IPI NAE event permits IPI delivery between vCPUs using x2APIC ICR format. The #HV Timer NAE event provides emulated APIC timer functionality via SET and GET actions.

The APIC ID List NAE event returns associated APIC IDs to the guest, useful for booting APs without broadcast INIT-SIPI sequences. The SNP Run VMPL NAE event allows running vCPUs at different VMPL levels, each requiring a unique VMSA.

SEV-TIO enables guests to bind to trusted devices, with SNP TIO Guest Requests handling device info, interface reports, MMIO, and IOMMU configuration. Returned data includes certificates, measurements, and TDISP attestation reports identified via GUID tables.

Secure AVIC manages guest-owned APIC state through REGISTER_BACKING_PAGE and UNREGISTER_BACKING_PAGE actions. Termination Request NAE events allow guests to request shutdown with reason codes.

SMP booting under SEV-ES/SNP requires special handling since hypervisors cannot modify measured/encrypted register state. Solutions include reset-vector polling or predetermined locations, with AP jump tables communicated between UEFI and OS via NAE events or the SEV-SNP Secrets Page. The SNP AP Creation feature simplifies this and supports vCPU hotplug. NMI handling requires #DB interception and "NMI Complete" messages. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

The #HV doorbell page contains PendingEvent (16-bit) and NoEoiRequired (1-byte) fields aligning with APIC behavior. The host presents interrupts by writing vector numbers, sets NoFurtherSignal for non-maskable events, and uses NoEoiRequired to optimize EOI cycles. Guests must atomically exchange these fields when acknowledging interrupts or completing EOIs, validate vectors against expected interrupts, and execute HLT with interrupts disabled when entering halt states.

NVIDIA's Turing GPU architecture introduces several advancements over the prior Pascal generation. Turing supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink, a new standard providing power, display, and data to VR headsets through a single connector. TU102 and TU104 GPUs use NVLink instead of MIO/PCIe for SLI, offering significantly higher bandwidth and enabling new display topologies, though only two-way SLI is supported.

Turing enables real-time ray tracing on a single GPU through dedicated RT Cores, which accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, freeing SMs for other work. Turing delivers over 10 Giga Rays/sec, roughly 10x faster than Pascal.

NVIDIA NGX uses Tensor Cores for AI-based features including DLSS (which matches or exceeds TAA quality with improved performance), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Additional features include Mesh Shading (eliminating CPU draw-call bottlenecks), Variable Rate Shading (enabling content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering), Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering supporting up to four views per pass.

The TU104 (used in RTX 2080, Tesla T4, Quadro RTX 5000) contains 13.6 billion transistors, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores. NVIDIA introduces RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric combining tensor, CUDA, RT core, and integer operations weighted by usage.

This study conducted a problem-based political economy analysis of medical oxygen access in Peru, combining 13 key informant interviews with reviews of academic literature, grey literature, and policy documents. This regulation concentrated market control among six companies, predominantly two business groups supplying 92.6% of government contracts between 2008-2020.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, Peru experienced the highest excess mortality rate globally in 2020 (413.4 per 100,000). The fragmented, decentralized health system and lack of a national oxygen strategy led to severe shortages, particularly in Andean and jungle regions where production and distribution infrastructure were limited. Lowering the purity standard to 93% required seven months and multiple legal instruments. An informal market emerged with inflated prices. Civil society groups, notably Respira Perú led by the Catholic Church, helped procure and donate oxygen plants when government response proved slow. The 2021 Oxygen Law established RENOXI, a national registry, though its data reliability has been questioned.

Post-pandemic, nearly 200 of 496 installed oxygen plants are unused or abandoned due to lack of maintenance planning, legal clearance delays, insufficient trained personnel, and possible corruption. Interviewees indicated Peru remains unprepared for future pandemics and emphasized the need for a National Oxygen System encompassing supply management, maintenance, training, and equitable distribution, aligning with WHO recommendations on pandemic preparedness.

This scoping review examined methods for measuring socio-economic status (SES) in health-related studies in sub-Saharan Africa, following the Arksey and O'Malley framework. Searches across five databases (January 2012–June 2024) yielded 19,669 publications, with 65 articles ultimately included.

Studies spanned 22 countries, with South Africa (13.4%), Kenya (11%), and Ghana (9.8%) most represented. Publications peaked in 2020 and 2022. Cross-sectional studies (52%) and cohort studies (23%) predominated, and maternal/child health and SES assessment were the most common themes (31% each).

The review identified 41 SES measures across 11 categories. Asset-based wealth indices were most common (61.9%), with the Wealth Index and its variants accounting for 28.6%. Indices based on education, health, and living standards (e.g., Multidimensional Poverty Index) represented 16.7%. Principal Component Analysis was the predominant analytical method (57.7%), sometimes combined with other approaches such as Multiple Correspondence Analysis.

The authors note methodological heterogeneity limits cross-study comparability and recommend moving toward standardized SES measurement approaches in Africa while allowing for local contextual adjustments.

This study developed and tested a Maternal Vulnerability Segmentation Tool (MVST) to identify pregnant women at risk of not utilizing essential maternal health services in Oromia, Ethiopia. Despite progress in reducing maternal mortality, Ethiopia still faces disparities in health facility delivery and antenatal care use, particularly among disadvantaged women.

Using baseline data from a 2024 quasi-experimental study, researchers screened 1,189 pregnant women using a 20-item questionnaire covering economic, social, and service-access drivers. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses identified four items relevant for urban-rural settings (rural residence, housing type, mobile phone ownership, distance to health facility) and six items for rural settings (adding women's and husband's education and household mobile phone ownership), each with acceptable reliability (Cronbach's alpha = 0.60).

Results showed that higher vulnerability scores were significantly associated with lower health facility delivery and fewer antenatal care visits (p<0.001). Mediation analysis confirmed that vulnerability affected facility delivery partly through reduced antenatal care utilization.

The authors conclude that the MVST is a practical, low-literacy tool suitable for frontline health workers to identify underserved pregnant women and enable targeted interventions. Limitations include context-specific applicability, the static nature of the assessment, and focus on service utilization rather than health outcomes. Further validation across diverse settings is recommended.

Statistical analyses will be presented through tables, listings, and figures (TLFs) following ICH numbering conventions. Testing will be 2-sided at a 0.05 significance level, performed using SAS 9.4 or higher and Phoenix WinNonlin 6.4 or higher for PK/PD analyses. Continuous variables will be summarized with standard descriptive statistics; categorical variables with counts and percentages.

Treatment groups include dasiglucagon, GlucaGen, and placebo. Analysis sets include the Safety set, Full Analysis Set (FAS), and Per Protocol Set (PPS). The primary efficacy analysis uses the FAS, with safety analyses on the Safety set.

Demographics, baseline characteristics, diabetes history, concomitant medications (coded via WHODrug), and medical history (MedDRA v22.0) will be summarized by treatment group.

The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery (≥20 mg/dL increase within 45 minutes), analyzed via stratified log-rank test and Kaplan-Meier estimates, with sensitivity analyses including Cox proportional hazards modeling. Secondary endpoints address plasma glucose recovery and changes from baseline at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes, tested hierarchically to control type I error.

PK parameters will be derived via non-compartmental analysis. Safety analyses cover exposure, local tolerability, treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), laboratory parameters, vital signs, ECGs, and immunogenicity (ADA). No interim analyses are planned. The share of young Americans aged 22-27 without college degrees who are working or seeking work has declined in recent decades, according to a Goldman Sachs analysis. The percentage of disconnected youth—those not in school, working, or job-seeking—reached about 12% as of May, higher than any year between 1989 and 2009, per Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas data.

Workforce experts cite several factors. Zachary Mabel of Georgetown University said many young non-graduates can find jobs but choose not to take available roles, partly because well-paying jobs are increasingly concentrated among degree holders and a cultural stigma has developed against blue-collar work. Carol Graham of the Brookings Institution pointed to mental health challenges, isolation, and substance abuse as contributing factors. Extended financial dependence on family and the rise of gig work, which may not be captured in labor statistics, are also cited.

Proposed solutions include education models combining schooling with apprenticeships and campaigns to reduce stigma around non-degree careers. Both experts suggested change is more feasible for younger children than for those already in their 20s or 30s.

The SPREAD Offense is a 3-2 no-post motion offense requiring all five players to be skilled passers and ball handlers, as all are involved in the continuity.

Basic Cuts & Continuity: O1 passes to O2 and cuts to the basket, clearing to the opposite corner if no pass is received. O3 replaces O1 in the middle. O2 passes to O3, cuts to the basket, and clears to the same-side corner if no pass comes, while O4 replaces O2 on the wing. O3 then assumes a triple threat position with passing options to O5 or O4.

Back Cut Counters: Overplayed players should immediately back cut rather than fight defensive pressure, clearing to the same-side corner if no pass is received.

Dribble Penetration: Ball handlers assume a triple threat position. When overplayed, they have a "Green Light" to drive. If defenders sag to help, the handler kicks the ball out and clears to the opposite corner.

Back Door Option: When a wing is overplayed or the shot clock is low, a corner player can break into the middle to execute a back door play, feeding a cutter to the basket on either side.

Deepa Das Acevedo, a legal anthropologist and associate professor of law at Emory University, argues in her book "The War on Tenure" that attacks on tenure are intentional, strategic efforts that began decades ago through state legislation and university policies. She contends tenure serves two enduring purposes: providing in-kind compensation through employment security and protecting academic freedom.

Das Acevedo challenges common arguments against tenure. The claim that tenure de-incentivizes work, she says, misunderstands academic socialization and lacks empirical support; available data on faculty productivity shows only a slight pre-tenure ramp-up. Regarding bad actors, she notes tenure is a just-cause employment contract that permits termination for misconduct, including academic integrity violations; whether action is taken depends on institutional willingness, not tenure itself.

Following the killing of Charlie Kirk, at least five tenured faculty were terminated or placed on leave over social media posts, sometimes within 24 to 72 hours. Das Acevedo argues this demonstrates that while tenure provides legal just-cause protections, the procedural details—including faculty input before termination—depend on universities' willingness to honor them, and institutions are increasingly disregarding these processes.

Research from Ben-Gurion University, published in Social Psychological and Personality Science, found that using smiley emojis in work emails can harm career prospects. Based on experiments with 549 participants from 29 countries, the study revealed that virtual smileys do not increase perceptions of warmth and actually decrease perceptions of competence, unlike real smiles in photographs or face-to-face interactions. Recipients also shared less detailed information in response to emails containing smileys. Additionally, senders using smileys were more often assumed to be women when gender was unknown. Dr Ella Glikson advises avoiding smileys in initial professional interactions.

A qualitative study was conducted as part of a quality improvement project to explore perspectives on regional teaching for Stage 1 anaesthetic trainees in a UK deanery, following a 2021 curriculum change that extended training and introduced variability across five hospital trusts. Six trainees and eight trainers participated in semi-structured focus group interviews, analysed thematically.

Three main themes emerged. First, Stage 1 training was considered complicated due to curriculum newness, heavy demands including the primary FRCA examination, and heterogeneous trainee needs. Second, implementation challenges included siloed hospital practices, disparities in teaching quality and trainer compensation, unhealthy inter-hospital competition, and logistical issues regarding location, funding, rota organisation, and quality control. Third, despite concerns, participants saw value in a regional programme for improving fairness, standardising teaching, supporting smaller hospitals, developing educators, and fostering networking.

Trainers and trainees broadly supported developing a regional teaching programme, recognising it could address curriculum demands and site disparities. The study highlighted that teaching is undervalued and that GMC survey data alone is insufficient for identifying solutions. Findings informed subsequent project actions, including trainee surveys and engagement with deanery leaders. Limitations included small trainee numbers and potential interviewer bias.

A genome-wide association study (GWAS) of neonatal jaundice was conducted using nearly 30,000 parent-offspring trios from Norway, with replication in two Danish cohorts. The study identified two loci reaching genome-wide significance in the discovery dataset: UGT1A* and CHRDL1.

A missense variant at UGT1A4 (rs6755571) was associated with a five-fold lower risk of neonatal jaundice, with effects limited to transmitted alleles, indicating a neonate-only effect. Colocalization analysis suggested this variant may regulate UGT1A1 expression in the colon rather than the liver. The protective effect was not modified by maternal-fetal ABO incompatibility but was stronger in full-term and post-term neonates.

A maternal GWAS identified three loci, including one at the ABO gene region (rs687621), which reflected maternal-fetal ABO blood group incompatibility. An X chromosome locus near CHRDL1 was also associated with jaundice risk.

Comparisons with adult bilirubin GWAS revealed distinct genetic architectures. The top adult bilirubin SNP was not associated with neonatal jaundice, and SLCO1B1 variants (strongly linked to adult bilirubin) showed minimal association. A polygenic score for adult bilirubin predicted neonatal jaundice only when chromosome 2 was included.

The findings suggest intestinal UGT1A1 may be a primary factor in neonatal bilirubin metabolism, highlighting context-specific genetic mechanisms distinct from adult bilirubin regulation.

Larry O'Neal, 44, a U.S. Border Patrol agent in Houlton, was indicted on Feb. 15 on a federal felony charge of possessing child pornography and pleaded not guilty on Feb. 22 in U.S. District Court in Bangor. Homeland Security agents began investigating him in January after tracing a downloaded file to an IP address at his home. A Jan. 19 search of his residence and vehicle uncovered a computer and external drive containing explicit images of girls aged approximately 12 to 14. O'Neal reportedly admitted to Special Agent Edward Ainsworth that he downloaded the material using search terms including "young," "rape," and "teen hardcore." No evidence indicated he used government property to store the material. CBP spokeswoman Stephanie Malin said the agency is cooperating with the FBI and DHS Office of the Inspector General. O'Neal was released on bail and is scheduled to appear in court on June 6. If convicted, he faces up to 10 years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000, and mandatory sex offender registration.

The patent application describes a hard-sided, collapsible shelter or camper designed to balance portability with protection. Unlike fabric shelters that offer limited security or rigid shelters that lack portability, this invention provides a rigid, lockable, weather-tight enclosure that collapses into a low-profile case.

Key features include:
- Rigid walls, floor, and roof made from composite materials (fiberglass, carbon fiber) with insulated cores
- Bi-fold or multi-fold side wall panels that fold parallel to the floor when collapsed
- Front and rear wall panels hinged to the roof or floor
- Transportability via roof rack, truck bed, trailer, or attached wheels, suitable for vehicles ranging from bicycles to trucks
- Weather stripping and gaskets at joints for a weather-tight seal
- Lockable in both expanded and collapsed configurations

Optional components include solar panels, batteries, climate control, plumbing, lighting, kitchenette, bathroom fixtures, and a movable bed platform that can be raised to allow standing room below or lowered for sleeping.

Multiple embodiments are described, including shorter versions for sleeping only and taller versions with multiple stacked bi-fold wall panels connected by a mid-section connector, enabling over six feet of interior standing height. The shelter can be opened and closed manually or mechanically using cranks, pulleys, pistons, or motorized hinges, and accommodates standard mattress sizes.

On January 26, 2016, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC reporting its financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 26, 2015. The filing included a press release (Exhibit 99.1), a related data sheet (Exhibit 99.2), and supplemental materials (Exhibit 99.3). The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The article examines pivot points trading strategies, defining pivot points as the average of the previous day's high, low, and close prices, from which support and resistance levels are derived. The authors note that despite frequent references to pivot points in trading media and their historical use by traders like Lewis Borsellino, little backtesting has been done.

The authors tested six pivot point strategies on 1-minute futures data from 2010 onward for the S&P 500, Nasdaq, Russell 2000, and USD/CHF markets. Results showed that none of the strategies were consistently tradeable, though a few produced notable outcomes, such as the first strategy on NQ with a 62% win rate and 0.16% average gain per trade.

The article outlines the pivot points formula, different types of pivot points, and pros (simplicity, objectivity, versatility) and cons (lagging price, low win ratio). The authors conclude that pivot points appear overhyped but suggest a few ideas may warrant further research for day trading strategies.

RWE Supply & Trading, the trading arm of Germany's RWE AG, may double or triple its LNG derivatives trades in 2018 from 1.5 million tonnes in 2017, according to Javier Moret, global head of the unit's LNG division. The increase is driven by Asia's potential shift from oil-linked prices and risk management for physical cargoes. The company traded 6 million tonnes of physical LNG last year, up from 4.5 million tonnes in 2016. Fragmented demand from new buyers like Bangladesh, Vietnam, the Philippines, and China is boosting short-term trading. RWE has traded 7 to 10 physical cargoes on Platts' JKM index so far this year, matching all of 2017's volume.

The lecture introduces the stress-energy tensor, a central object for describing matter in relativity. Beginning with a dust cloud of identical particles, the instructor shows that energy density transforms with a factor of gamma squared between frames, indicating it is neither a scalar nor a four-vector component, but rather a component of a rank-2 tensor. The stress-energy tensor T^(αβ) is defined as the flux of momentum component α in the β direction, with components representing energy density (T^00), energy flux/momentum density (T^0i), and momentum flux/stresses (T^ij).

A key example is the perfect fluid, which has no energy flow or lateral stresses in its rest frame, characterized only by energy density and isotropic pressure. Dust is a pressureless special case. The tensor is symmetric, motivated by a torque argument showing that asymmetry would cause unphysical angular accelerations as volume shrinks.

The instructor argues that Newton's field equation (Poisson's equation with mass density as source) must be generalized because density is only one tensor component; the full stress-energy tensor must source gravity in relativity, meaning pressure also generates gravity. Conservation of energy and momentum is expressed covariantly as the vanishing spacetime divergence of T^(αβ).

Additional examples include the stress-energy tensor for a point particle (using a Dirac delta function) and for electromagnetic fields (built from the Faraday tensor), which yields familiar energy densities, the Poynting vector, and anisotropic pressures.

The lecture concludes by transitioning toward curvature, introducing flat spacetime in curvilinear (polar) coordinates as preparation. In such coordinate bases, basis vectors are not constant and need not be normalized, and transformation matrices between coordinate systems can have components with differing dimensions—features that will become important for general relativity.

Lawton High School unveiled the second panel of its Wolverine mural in the cafeteria, created by art teacher Kenneth Hobbs. Funded by the class of 2014, the 10-by-three-foot panel depicts the school's front and south side, the "Hanta Yo!" sign, and a Wolverine breaking through a pixilated frame. It complements the first panel, funded by the class of 2006 and unveiled in 2010, which shows the school's three historic buildings and a timeline of state championships, including the 1927 National Women's Basketball Team. The new panel's timeline begins with the 1993 National Wrestling Champions and their coaches.

Minority children in U.S. schools have been widely characterized as overrepresented in special education, prompting federal legislation and policies—such as requiring local educational agencies to report overrepresentation and allocate 15% of Part B funds toward early intervening services—to address this perceived disparity. However, a study analyzing longitudinal, nationally representative data found no evidence of overrepresentation. After adjusting for confounding factors like socioeconomic status, academic achievement, and behavioral functioning, racial, ethnic, and language-minority children were significantly less likely than comparable White, English-speaking children to be identified as having disabilities including learning disabilities, speech or language impairments, intellectual disabilities, health impairments, or emotional disturbances. This underrepresentation persisted across elementary and middle school. The findings suggest schools identify disabilities based on academic achievement and behavior, and that federal efforts to reduce minority representation in special education may reduce access for children who could benefit from services.

The speaker disagrees with Curtis, believing the key to shutting down the opponents is limiting their puck time and keeping play out of their own end, as the opponents forechecked effectively. Mental health services are available in over 80% of Minnesota's public school districts, supplemented by nonprofit programs offering specialized support. Know the Truth, an offshoot of Minnesota Adult and Teen Challenge, provides peer recovery services and substance use prevention through people who have completed addiction treatment. Tiffany White, a youth peer support specialist with the organization, draws on her own recovery from alcohol addiction to connect with students in three Twin Cities schools, offering individual meetings, support groups, and outside-school contact. She emphasizes harm reduction and a nonjudgmental approach, though federal funding cuts recently eliminated her contract at Hastings High School.

Restoration for All, founded by Nigerian immigrant Tolulope Ola, supports the mental health of Minnesota's African immigrant and refugee youth. The organization trains school staff on cultural context, including trauma from refugee camps, to prevent misinterpretation of student behavior. Coordinator Ruth Ezeagwula notes that immigrant families often discourage mental health discussions at home, creating tension for students. A 2023 four-year, $400,000 Minnesota Department of Health grant funds services including therapy, suicide monitoring, and culturally grounded mind-body practices, with additional grants supporting work in Twin Cities, St. Cloud, and Rochester schools.

South Korea's spy agency suspects two female North Korean agents assassinated Kim Jong Nam, the estranged half-brother of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, in Malaysia, according to South Korean lawmakers. U.S. government sources also believed North Korean assassins murdered Kim, who died Monday en route to a hospital from Kuala Lumpur International Airport. South Korean intelligence believed he was poisoned, and said Kim Jong Un had issued a "standing order" for his half-brother's assassination, with a failed attempt in 2012. Kim Jong Nam, 46, held a passport under the name Kim Chol and had been living with his second wife in Macau under Beijing's protection. He had publicly opposed his family's dynastic rule. Malaysian police confirmed a woman was involved based on CCTV footage, and an autopsy was being performed. South Korean Prime Minister Hwang Kyo-ahn condemned the killing if confirmed as North Korean-directed. Malaysia maintains close relations with North Korea, allowing visa-free travel between the countries.

A Salvadoran woman fled her country with her common-law husband after two of her children disappeared, fearing gang members wanted to kill the entire family. They were caught shortly after crossing into Texas and she was deported back to El Salvador on Thursday with about 100 other migrants, while her partner remained detained.

Thousands of Central Americans fleeing gang violence in El Salvador, Honduras and Guatemala are being returned under the Trump administration's zero-tolerance policy. Although Trump has claimed illegal immigrants "infest" the U.S. like MS-13, U.S. Customs and Border Protection statistics show only 0.09 percent of 310,531 people detained in fiscal year 2017 belonged to Central American gangs. In 2017, nearly 163,000 migrants caught at the border were from El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras, compared to 128,000 Mexicans.

In El Salvador, MS-13 and Barrio 18 control neighborhoods, extort businesses, kill those who refuse to pay, and force young women into sexual slavery. El Salvador's defense minister said in 2015 there were 60,000 gang members versus 50,000 combined police and army personnel. Security forces are estimated to be responsible for 10 to 15 percent of threats and violence. According to priest Mauro Verzeletti, 90 percent of deportees attempt to migrate again within days.

The October 12, 2000 edition of "Inside UT Football" newsletter by Chip Brown of The Dallas Morning News addresses the Texas Longhorns' upcoming game at Colorado following their loss to Oklahoma. Colorado has won six straight against Texas, and UT has not won in Boulder since 1941.

Coach Mack Brown named Major Applewhite the sole starting quarterback, ending the rotation with Chris Simms, who will only play on a "need-to-win" basis. B.J. Johnson and Roy Williams were promoted to starting receiver positions, and running back Kenny Hayter is expected to see more carries.

Brown answers reader questions about coaching decisions, predictable play-calling, and the team's lack of offensive leadership. Brown notes that Texas's recent losses have come against opponents with greater motivation, and suggests Mack Brown must find ways to equalize that incentive factor.

Brown states the Colorado game is critical for Big 12 South title hopes, but a loss would not set the program back significantly if the team responds. Travis Phippen, a Valencia man wounded in the October 1 Las Vegas mass shooting in which his father John Phippen was killed, has filed a civil lawsuit against the estate of gunman Stephen Paddock. Scale AI billionaire Alexandr Wang, 28, advises 13-year-olds to spend their time "vibe-coding"—using AI to generate software through natural language prompts—arguing that 10,000 hours of practice with AI tools could yield a career-defining advantage. Wang became the youngest self-made billionaire in 2022 and now leads Meta's AI superintelligence team as its first chief AI officer. Alyn Family Doctors has proposed closing its Gresford Health Centre branch and merging patients with its Llay and Rossett surgeries, citing insufficient manpower to operate three sites. The practice has applied to Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB) for approval. An online petition opposing the closure has gathered over 600 signatures, with patients raising concerns about travel difficulties, appointment availability, and added pressure from proposed housing developments of 365 homes in Llay and 132 in Rossett. Three other Wrexham surgeries have returned their contracts in the past two years. BCUHB stated it is supporting the practice and gathering patient feedback via forms, post, or email.

During a penalty kick in the normal run of play, the ball is live once kicked, so the defending team must be prepared to react to rebounds or blocks. Under Law 14, all players except the kicker and goalkeeper must stand at least 10 yards from the penalty mark, behind it, inside the field, and outside the penalty area. Defenders should take standard perimeter positions and may not enter the area or arc until the ball is touched and moves forward; premature entry results in a retake or goal.

When the ball rebounds or is blocked, defenders must sprint to win it before attackers, turn away from their goal, and clear it. If secured, the team transitions quickly to attack using a designated outlet player. A rare "tap" penalty kick allows the kicker to nudge the ball for an onrushing teammate to shoot.

Coaches should practice positioning, boxing out attackers without jostling, responding to rebounds, and outlet passing. The article distinguishes in-game penalty kicks from shoot-outs, which do not allow follow-ups, and warns defenders against being deceived by stutter-steps.

The present disclosure describes a gaming machine, control method, and program that synchronizes the display timing of in-game events with the beat of background music (BGM). The gaming machine includes a display, speaker, storage device, and controller. The storage device stores sound data of the BGM and tempo data containing beat information. The controller outputs BGM through the speaker while displaying game progression, determines event display timing based on the tempo data, dynamically configures animation data to display events at the determined timing, and shows the animation on the display.

Embodiments include determining event timing based on player operation of an operation unit, randomly determining event content, outputting event sounds synchronized with event timing, and using rhythm pattern data to sequentially display multiple events. The gaming machine may provide slot games with symbols arranged in a grid, where reel spin and stop operations serve as events synchronized to the BGM beat. Illumination may also be lit at the determined timing.

The tempo data includes timing information for beats, loop start/end points, and may be converted into frame counts matching the animation frame rate. The system uses a game application and system application implemented on an operating system, with middleware modules for animation, sound, timer, and network functions. Methods described include synchronizing reel stops to on-beat frame counts, applying rhythm patterns to sequential reel stops, and synchronizing bonus game animations with the BGM beat.

This qualitative study used an interpretive phenomenological approach to explore stakeholder perspectives on metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for infectious disease diagnostics (IDD). Ten UK-based participants, including clinicians, scientists, and academics, were interviewed via Microsoft Teams between July and November 2021.

Five themes emerged: diagnostic choice, infrastructure, open data sharing, COVID-19, and communication. Participants viewed mNGS as a valuable addition to existing diagnostic tools rather than a replacement, but identified cost and speed as major barriers. Funding disparities between smaller and larger hospitals created inequitable access, and centralised sequencing models delayed turnaround times. Infrastructure challenges included limited bioinformatics training, inadequate staffing, accreditation difficulties with "research use only" reagents, and insufficient data storage systems.

Open data sharing was seen as beneficial for surveillance but conflicted with patient privacy. COVID-19 was cited as proof of concept, demonstrating sequencing's public health value and expanding manufacturing capacity. Communication gaps within hospitals, between hospitals, and with commercial partners were identified as obstacles to implementation.

The study concluded that cost, speed, and infrastructure are key considerations for integrating mNGS into routine clinical use, with COVID-19 serving as a model for advancing genomic diagnostics. Limitations included lack of representation from Southwest and Northeast England.

Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi have won the 2025 Nobel Prize in chemistry for developing metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), molecular structures containing gaps that can store gases and chemicals in large quantities. Applications include harvesting water from air, capturing greenhouse gases, and extracting forever chemicals.

In the late 1980s, Robson of the University of Melbourne discovered that combining copper ions with organic compounds created a diamond-like crystalline structure full of useful holes. Kitagawa of Kyoto University later developed MOFs that could absorb gases like methane, nitrogen and oxygen. In 1999, Yaghi of UC Berkeley created a material where a sugar-cube-sized amount contained thousands of square meters of surface area.

The three scientists share the 11 million Swedish kronor prize. Yaghi, whose Palestinian refugee parents moved him to the U.S. from Jordan as a teenager, credited the U.S. public school system for his success.

NHS workers at Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals Trust have recreated a 1927 photograph to mark the health service's 70th anniversary. The original image, showing a matron, her assistant and nurses in old-fashioned caps, was taken at what was then Hallam Hospital in West Bromwich. Fourteen staff members posed in the same spot for the recreation. The old photographs were discovered in a broom cupboard by ward service officers and given to Sue Woodcock, an electronic patient record systems trainer. The images will be displayed at Sandwell Hospital during a tea party celebrating NHS70.

Professor Andrew Lo opens the lecture by discussing a prior auction where an iPod sold for $45 and a book for $60, illustrating how lack of information affects valuation. He connects this to current events, specifically the federal government's takeover of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, government-sponsored entities that purchased mortgages from banks to expand credit availability in housing and consumer markets. As the housing market declined, these institutions could not meet their obligations, prompting Treasury intervention to prevent wider financial collapse. Lo notes the government guaranteed their debt, with potential inflationary and taxpayer consequences.

Lo then transitions to the main lecture on present value. He defines an asset as a sequence of current and future cashflows at a given point in time, regardless of whether tangible or intangible (e.g., patents, trade secrets, brand reputation). He introduces the value operator V sub t, which converts a cashflow sequence into a number, with market prices serving as one source of valuation.

Assuming no uncertainty, Lo explains that cashflows at different times are like different currencies and cannot be added without conversion via exchange rates (discount factors), obtained from the market. Net present value (NPV) sums cashflows converted to today's dollars. He introduces the opportunity cost of capital, r, where $1 today grows to $(1+r)^T in year T, and the discount factor is 1/(1+r)^T. This framework allows valuation of any certain cashflow. Future lectures will address annuities, perpetuities, compounding, inflation, and uncertainty.

The Avontuur, a 97-year-old two-masted schooner, has arrived at the busy port of Puerto Cortés in northern Honduras. Unlike the typical cargo ships that rely on bunker fuel, the Avontuur is powered by wind through its canvas sails. A small crew sailed it from Europe across the Caribbean, collecting and delivering cargo along the way. Sergio Romero boards the vessel, which stands in contrast to the modern freighters, containers, and cranes surrounding it.

Title IX staff ensure compliance with federal nondiscrimination regulations in higher education. Since 2020, Title IX rules have been significantly amended under both Trump and Biden administrations, creating complex compliance requirements for institutions.

A CUPA-HR poll found most Title IX staff are housed in Human Resources (29%) or Student Affairs (28%), followed by Compliance and DEI offices (11% each).

Analysis of CUPA-HR survey data (2019-20 to 2023-24) shows the percentage of institutions with at least one dedicated full-time Title IX position grew from 33% to 43%, with total Title IX staff increasing by 38%. However, 56% of institutions still lack a dedicated full-time Title IX position, often integrating these duties into broader roles.

Heads of institutional Title IX compliance remain the most common position (31% of institutions), while deputy heads (12%) and investigators (16%) are growing faster. Doctoral institutions are most likely to have dedicated Title IX staff (64%) and multiple positions (36%).

Women hold 77% of Title IX positions, with Black women notably represented (13%). Unlike other higher ed roles, Title IX staff are compensated equitably, with women and people of color earning salaries comparable to or exceeding White men.

The report recommends institutions reassess Title IX officer responsibilities, increase staffing where needed, and prepare for regulatory changes under the incoming Trump administration.

The speaker believes effort is consistent but the team hasn't played cohesively, expressing dissatisfaction with the last game and emphasizing the need to act rather than just talk. They note that injuries shouldn't prevent players from pursuing their goals at this stage. Key injuries during the season forced other players to step up, and while they hope for the return of certain teammates, others are capable of filling in if needed.

Berkshire Hathaway sold its 10.6 million-share stake in General Electric during the second quarter of 2017, valued at approximately $315 million as of June 30. Berkshire had acquired most of the shares after lending GE $3 billion during the 2008 financial crisis, ultimately generating over $1 billion in profit. The sale coincided with GE's leadership change, as Jeff Immelt was replaced by John Flannery. GE shares have fallen nearly 20% this year. Berkshire also bought shares of Synchrony Financial, Bank of New York Mellon, and Apple. Kindergarten teachers view visual arts as essential for children's holistic development, including creativity, imagination, expression, social skills, and intellectual growth. A survey of 65 pre-school teachers in the Municipality of Piraeus, Greece, examined their perceptions, teaching approaches, and challenges regarding visual arts integration.

Findings showed 56.9% considered visual arts crucial in early childhood education, while 89.2% observed benefits to imagination and creativity. Demographic factors (gender, age, education, specialization) did not significantly influence views. Notably, 89.2% lacked specialized training in visual arts.

Teachers preferred free approaches (33.1%) and experimentation with varied materials (30.7%). The main challenges identified were classroom management (86.1%) and external factors like time constraints and limited resources (10.7%). Solutions included individualized guidance, positive feedback, and flexible teaching methods.

The study concludes that while teachers value visual arts, targeted professional development and improved resources are needed to support effective implementation. Limitations include reliance on electronic questionnaires and lack of qualitative interviews for deeper insight.

SOS "On Ball" switching operates under two scenarios based on ball position relative to the free throw line.

**Below Free Throw Line:** When O5 sets a side screen and O3 is below the free throw line extended, X5 traps O3 with X3 before the screen is set. Other defenders rotate into "I" positions or denial/front positions on offensive players. If the ball is passed out of the trap—to O1, O2 (skip pass), or O5 in the post—defenders close out, push ball handlers to designated checkpoints, and assume snuggle denial or helpside positions accordingly.

**Above Free Throw Line:** An aggressive contact switch is used. X4 bumps the screener and hedges into the ball handler's path, while X3 forces the screener through his body. X4 then forces the ball handler toward a checkpoint and assumes a smother position, while X3 moves into a snuggle or front position. Other defenders take weakside "I" positions.

**All Out SOS Disruption:** The defense traps the point guard before any screen occurs, forcing the offense into freelance play. X1 and X5 double-team O1, while X4 covers the post roll and X2/X3 take helpside positions. On passes out of the trap, defenders rotate using the near-player concept.

**Secondary Trap:** If O1 passes to O5 on the base roll, X5 and X4 trap O5 on the baseline. Subsequent rotations depend on O5's pass, with defenders applying standard SOS principles, "Base Go" scenarios, or post traps as needed.

All rotations occur as the ball leaves the passer's hands.

The passage describes a display device designed to detect defects such as cracks in a display panel. The device includes a substrate with a display area containing pixels, a pad area with input pads, and a circuit area between them containing a crack sensing circuit. A crack sensing line extends around the display area, with a first end connected to an input pad and a second end connected to a static electricity discharge element within the crack sensing circuit.

The static electricity discharge element, typically a capacitor, is positioned in the center area of the circuit area, while switching elements connecting test data lines to data lines are positioned outside this center area. The discharge element may connect between test data lines or between a connection wire and a test data line, and can comprise multiple sub-capacitors corresponding to sub-wires.

Without the discharge element, crack sensing lines could act as antennas, accumulating static electricity and causing leakage current in switching elements, leading to erroneous defect detection during testing. The discharge element stores or discharges static electricity, preventing damage to switching elements and improving defect detection accuracy.

The passage also describes bending areas, bending crack sensing lines, the layered cross-sectional structure (including conductive layers, insulating layers, pixel electrodes, emission layers, encapsulation, and touch sensors), and testing methods where voltage differences reveal cracks through visible white lines in pixel columns.

Foreign Relations series editors have full access to Department of State records, including central files, lot files, Executive Secretariat files, and overseas post files from 1981–1989, which will eventually be transferred to the National Archives after declassification. Research also draws on restricted documents at the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library and materials from the Remote Archive Capture (RAC) project, which coordinates declassification across Presidential libraries. Due to RAC scanning methods, editors sometimes cannot confirm whether attachments were physically attached, noting such cases as "Not found attached."

Regarding editorial methodology, documents appear chronologically by Washington, DC time, with memoranda of conversation dated by the conversation itself. Original texts are reproduced faithfully, preserving spelling, capitalization, punctuation, abbreviations, and underlining (rendered as italics), while silently correcting obvious typos and using bracketed insertions for other corrections. Editors supply headings for each document. Bracketed insertions also mark unrelated or still-classified omitted text, with the extent of withheld material noted. The disclosure relates to systems and methods for indicating wireless channel status in 5G New Radio (NR) systems operating at high frequencies, where beamforming is used to overcome significant pathloss. The disclosure addresses issues that arise when beam failure occurs and quasi-co-located (QCL) configurations for PDCCH or PDSCH become unusable before transmission configuration indication (TCI) states are updated.

Two primary example embodiments are presented. In the first, after beam failure recovery, the UE assumes a QCL relationship between a newly selected beam and the downlink reference signal (DMRS) of PDCCH or PDSCH, using the new beam's spatial domain receive filter until an updated QCL configuration is received. In the second embodiment, the UE assumes no QCL relationship exists post-recovery and relies solely on the DMRS of PDCCH or PDSCH for detection and decoding until TCI states are updated.

The disclosure describes various implementation scenarios, including cases where TCI fields are present or absent in downlink control information (DCI), procedures for access nodes updating TCI tables, and DCI selection procedures. These techniques aim to reduce signaling overhead and improve system performance following beam failure recovery.

Many children respond to adults' questions with brief or vague answers, and students often hesitate to ask questions in class. This reluctance can lead to disengagement or willful ignorance in adulthood. The author offers five strategies for parents and caregivers to foster better conversation and curiosity in children:

1. Ask specific, open-ended questions rather than routine ones.
2. Engage genuinely with children's questions instead of dismissing them, and model curiosity by asking questions aloud.
3. Demonstrate how to find answers using resources like glossaries, manuals, or multiple internet searches, rather than just saying "I don't know."
4. Model active listening by repeating what was said and highlighting meaningful parts of their responses.
5. Avoid multitasking when children approach with questions; give full attention.

The author argues that encouraging curiosity while respecting children's limitations helps build their confidence to ask and answer questions.

This cross-sectional study investigated the relationship between self-esteem and physical activity among 10th and 11th grade students at Capa Science High School in Istanbul during the 2022-2023 academic year. Data were collected from 225 students (80.93% of the targeted population) using a questionnaire containing sociodemographic questions, the International Physical Activity Questionnaire Short Form (IPAQ-SF), and the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (ROSE). BMI was calculated from self-reported height and weight.

Results showed that males reported higher self-esteem and higher MET scores than females. Students who exercised regularly had higher ROSE scores than those who did not. Positive correlations were found between ROSE scores and height, as well as between ROSE and MET scores. Students reporting higher school success had higher ROSE scores. No significant differences in ROSE scores were found between BMI categories. Among participants, 23% were classified as inactive, 61.70% as minimally active, and 15.30% as HEPA active.

The authors concluded that higher physical activity correlated with higher self-esteem, noting that the study was conducted in a specific, high-achieving population, which may limit generalizability. The causational relationship between physical activity and self-esteem requires further investigation.

The ADS868xW features a user-programmable input alarm with adjustable high/low thresholds and hysteresis, illustrated through an NTC thermistor temperature-sensing application. Since NTC resistance changes inversely with temperature, a voltage divider produces an output voltage used to detect over- or under-temperature conditions. Hysteresis is applied to prevent false alarm triggering caused by ambient noise near threshold limits, improving noise immunity.

The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, each set independently within permissible ranges. Decoupling AVDD with 10µF and 1µF capacitors (1µF placed close to supply pins) and DVDD with a 10µF capacitor improves PSRR performance.

Two low-power modes reduce consumption at lower throughput rates:
- NAP mode: Entered by unlocking RST_PWRCTL_REG (write 69h to 05h), setting NAP_EN to 1b, and holding CONVST/CS high. A falling edge exits NAP mode after tNAP_WKUP.
- Power-Down (PD) mode: Entered by setting PWRDN to 1b, powering down analog blocks while retaining register contents and interface activity. Exited by clearing PWRDN; new conversions begin after tPWRUP.

PCB layout recommendations include separating analog and digital sections, using X7R ceramic bypass capacitors close to supply pins, decoupling REFCAP with 1µF and 10µF capacitors (ESR <0.2Ω), and decoupling REFIO with at least 4.7µF when using the internal reference.

Canadian researchers at the University of Toronto, led by nutritional science professor Ahmed El-Sohemy, analyzed blood samples from nearly 2,800 people in Toronto to study celiac disease prevalence. Celiac disease is a genetic autoimmune condition where gluten triggers intestinal damage, causing symptoms like abdominal pain, diarrhea, and nutrient deficiencies. Experts note diagnosis is difficult because symptoms overlap with other conditions, and patients must consume gluten during testing to avoid false negatives. El-Sohemy, who founded Nutrigenomix Inc., also noted gluten-free foods are costlier and sometimes less nutritious. The research was funded by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research.

The disclosure describes a device and method for optimizing basal insulin dosages for diabetic users, particularly those using automated insulin delivery (AID) systems. The device includes a processor, memory, wireless communication capability, and an artificial pancreas application.

The processor calculates the total insulin delivered over a predetermined time period, which combines basal and bolus dosages. It then determines the proportion of total insulin attributed to basal dosages and compares it to a threshold (e.g., 70%). If the threshold is exceeded, the processor calculates an average basal dosage approximately equal to the threshold and generates instructions to actuate a pump mechanism to deliver a modified basal dosage.

The ideal distribution is 50% basal and 50% bolus, though variations occur due to user physiology, diet, behavior, or activity levels. The threshold may be adjusted based on user activity or hypoglycemia history. Insulin delivered shortly after bolus doses may be omitted from calculations. Clustering algorithms can establish time-dependent basal profiles across segments of the day.

The drug delivery system comprises a wearable drug delivery device, a blood glucose sensor (continuous glucose monitor), a personal diabetes management device, and optionally a smart device, communicating via wireless links such as Bluetooth or Wi-Fi. The system may utilize cloud-based services for data storage and processing.

Plaintiffs, alien enemies during World War I, filed a bill in equity in 1931 seeking to recover property seized by the Alien Property Custodian under the Trading with the Enemy Act. The District Court dismissed the bill based on Public Resolution No. 53 (1934), which postpones deliveries of money or property while Germany remains in arrears on certain obligations.

The Court of Appeals affirmed, holding the case is governed by Cummings v. Deutsche Bank, in which the Supreme Court held that the original grant to alien enemies to recover seized property was made as a matter of grace and subject to withdrawal by Congress. Appellants' attempt to distinguish their case on the ground that their property was illegally seized was rejected, as the Deutsche Bank case similarly involved allegations of unlawful conduct by the custodian, and the Supreme Court found such conduct immaterial given the resolution's broad terms.

According to Jay Owen, SVP of Schneider Electric's North American IT Division, the module helps customers standardize distributed edge endpoints for consistent efficiency and reliability.

The passage describes boot configuration terminal functions for a Texas Instruments device, detailing pins multiplexed between ARM Cortex-A8 boot mode and General-Purpose Memory Controller (GPMC) peripheral functions.

Key points:
- BTMODE[10] is sampled at reset when XIP bootmodes are selected, to choose GPMC pin muxing options A or B. After reset, this pin functions as GPMC_D[10].
- BTMODE[9:8] pins are sampled at reset when EMAC bootmode is selected, determining Ethernet PHY Mode selection.
- Reserved boot pins function as GPMC_D[7:5] after reset.
- BTMODE[4:0] inputs are sampled at reset to determine ARM boot configuration; these pins function as GPMC_D[4:0] after reset.

Abbreviations defined include I/O states (I, O, Z, S, GND, A, MM, DSIS) and internal pull states (IPD, IPU, DIS), representing default states during and after reset.

Tail risk, or "fat tails," refers to the increased probability of rare, extreme events in financial markets compared to a normal distribution. Nassim Taleb popularized the concept, arguing such events occur more often than statistical models suggest. Negatively skewed strategies, which produce many small gains but occasional catastrophic losses, are particularly vulnerable.

Investors hedge against tail risk to limit losses, survive market downturns, and avoid behavioral mistakes like panic-selling during crashes. Six main hedging approaches are discussed: buying out-of-the-money put options, diversifying into foreign assets, holding cash, investing in tail risk ETFs like Cambria's TAIL, adopting Ray Dalio's All Weather Portfolio, and using trend-following strategies.

Meb Faber's research shows tail risk hedging (e.g., 10% in puts, 90% in bonds) outperforms during crises but reduces overall returns in rising markets. Backtests combining SPY with TAIL confirm smaller drawdowns at the cost of lower long-term returns. The author's personal experience with put-option hedging in 2019 highlights the psychological difficulty of enduring continuous small losses while awaiting rare payoffs.

Ultimately, tail risk hedging involves trade-offs between protection and return, and may be more suitable for investors nearing retirement than younger investors with long time horizons.

The thesis analyzes web services in event management and explores digitized event organization, including the development of a mobile application to enhance attendee experience.

The paper outlines the evolution of e-business since 1995, distinguishing it from e-commerce and digital business (d-business). It discusses negative aspects such as business consolidation and internet security risks, and protective measures including antivirus software, firewalls, encryption, and digital certificates. Key technologies associated with e-business include cloud computing, Web 2.0, the Internet of Things, and mobile technology.

The research analyzed 200 event management websites (17 Croatian, 183 foreign) from August-September 2017 using 103 Boolean-scored criteria across five categories: website content, social networks/Web 2.0, public relations/user support, multimedia/mobile technologies, and user experience/technical specification.

Results showed foreign websites focus more on user experience and less on bureaucratic information than Croatian ones. Facebook (90%), Twitter (92%), and LinkedIn (81%) were the most used social media. All analyzed sites used photos and HTML, most had blogs, and newsletters were common (83%). Croatian organizations ranked poorly, with the first appearing at position 40 and the last at 200.

The conclusion emphasizes that Croatian event organizations need improvement in user experience, social media presence, mobile applications, and multimedia content to remain competitive. A limitation noted is the restricted country sample; future research should examine customer perspectives.

Artificial intelligence has advanced significantly and is transforming the legal profession. AI simulates human intelligence in machines and has existed in basic forms like spellcheck for years. Modern discussions typically focus on generative AI, which creates content based on existing data (e.g., ChatGPT4), and agentic AI, which focuses on decision-making by analyzing data to provide insights and recommendations.

AI is useful but not suitable for every task. Practical applications in law include document review, legal research, and client communication. Tasks requiring nuanced judgment may still be best handled by humans.

Recommended AI tools include Vincent AI for legal research, Copilot for drafting and workflows, ChatGPT as a general-purpose tool, built-in AI features in existing legal software, and custom tools tailored to specific firm needs. For example, Palace Law uses an AI chatbot to assist injured workers.

Part 2 will address effective AI use, integration into practice, and future expectations.
