He praises a defenseman's mobility, puck-moving, and offensive instincts, and notes Rusty's speed, compete level, and confidence contributing to his scoring. Chris is described as most effective when physical and proactive. Ovechkin expressed gratitude for receiving an award, thanking his teammates, coaching staff, and family. He described the past year as difficult due to a mid-season switch from left wing to right wing, crediting coach Adam Oates for guiding him through the transition. He credited the coaching staff and teammates for making the position change work on the power play.

Peter Marks, the former top vaccine regulator at the FDA, has joined Eli Lilly to oversee molecule discovery and infectious diseases. Marks was forced to resign from the FDA in March by health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. He expressed enthusiasm about advancing infectious disease products for public health.

The "Triangle Rotation" offense targets the triangle zone of the Triangle & Two defense, which is typically weaker than its skilled pass-denial chasers. It uses simple clockwise and counter-clockwise three-player rotations, with two shooters activated if initial inside rotations fail.

Key actions include the point guard dribbling to an elbow, a post player popping out, a baseline cut, a weakside lob option, and side screens initiated when passing to the wing shooter.

Successful implementation requires simplicity, practice against Triangle & Two defenses, and mastery of zone-attacking fundamentals, including defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, and timing.

Recommended game strategies include scouting opponents, preparing players for defensive reads, monitoring adjustments after substitutions or timeouts, varying alignments, and targeting weaker defenders.

Two U.S. government studies that exposed rats and mice to high doses of cellphone radiation found a weak link to rare heart tumors in male rats, but no significant effects in female rats or mice. Lead researcher John Bucher noted the exposure levels far exceeded typical human use, and the FDA maintained that current cellphone safety limits adequately protect public health. The American Cancer Society's Dr. Otis Brawley said the findings would not change his advice, as evidence linking cellphones to cancer remains weak. Earlier preliminary results suggesting increased brain tumors in male rats were not confirmed in the final report, which cited only "equivocal evidence" of DNA damage and some cancers. Critics like David Carpenter argued the studies were too small to detect rare problems. Prior large-scale studies, including a 2010 13-country analysis and a Danish study, found little evidence of cancer risk from cellphone use. California has issued guidance on reducing radiofrequency exposure for concerned users.

Michael Johnson has been named president of John Carroll University, becoming the first lay leader in the institution's 131-year history. Currently provost and marketing professor at Babson College, Johnson, 61, will begin his five-year term on July 1 following board approval on Dec. 6. He replaces retiring Rev. Robert Niehoff, with Jeanne Colleran serving as interim president. Johnson holds degrees from the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Chicago, and previously taught at the University of Michigan and served as dean at Cornell's School of Hotel Administration. He will also join JCU's faculty and has received endorsement from the Society of Jesus's USA Midwest Province.

This study systematically reviews the accuracy and validity of ChatGPT responses in education. Since its November 2022 release, ChatGPT has rapidly gained users and influenced education, generating both enthusiasm and concerns about plagiarism, cheating, and critical thinking.

Using PRISMA guidelines, the author searched Google Scholar, Web of Science, and EBSCO, ultimately analyzing 18 empirical, peer-reviewed studies across fields including medicine, business, chemistry, physics, writing, and programming.

Two main categories emerged: ChatGPT's writing quality and its performance as a learner. Findings indicate ChatGPT produces coherent, well-structured, precise text, sometimes exceeding high school students' writing quality and functioning effectively as an advisor. However, responses often lack depth, argumentation, and higher-order thinking.

As a learner, ChatGPT passed many undergraduate exams, including business, law, and some medical tests, but struggled with complex scientific problems, calculations, and analytical reasoning. It sometimes produced hallucinations, false information stated confidently, repetitive answers, or inconsistent responses to identical prompts. Its training data ending in 2021 limits reliability.

The author recommends validating ChatGPT content, carefully structuring text prompts, redesigning assessments to prevent dishonest use, developing institutional policies, and training students in constructive use. An "ABCD framework" is proposed for adoption.

The study concludes that ChatGPT shows educational potential but requires improvement for scientific and computational tasks. Collaboration between institutions and developers to create education-specific versions is suggested. Limitations include restricted databases and search dates; future research should examine AI's effects on student learning and innovative evaluation frameworks.

This cross-sectional study conducted at Hemen Medical Center in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, from June to August 2024, assessed awareness and attitudes toward labor epidural analgesia (LEA) among 230 third-trimester pregnant women. Data were collected via self-administered questionnaires and analyzed using SPSS with logistic regression.

Results showed that 78% of participants had heard of LEA, primarily from previous users (27%), family/friends (24%), and the internet (19.6%), with only 6.5% citing healthcare providers. While 47% believed LEA was effective for pain relief, only 14.3% were willing to use it. Concerns included side effects for mother and baby, interference with labor, and cost.

Multivariable analysis identified education level, monthly family income, perceived fetal risk, and perceived pain-relief effectiveness as significant factors influencing the decision to use LEA. Women with higher education and income above 25,000 ETB were more likely to consider LEA.

Limitations included single-center design, inability to assess prior epidural experience, and the cross-sectional approach. The study concludes that despite general awareness, hesitancy persists due to insufficient counselling from healthcare providers, highlighting the need for improved antenatal education to address misconceptions about LEA.

A King's College London study analysing data from 49 studies involving 266,939 people found that regular physical activity reduces the risk of developing depression across all age groups, continents, and regardless of factors like BMI, smoking, and physical health. Co-author Dr Brendon Stubbs emphasised prioritising physical activity throughout life. Researchers plan further studies on activity types and dosages. Co-author Dr Simon Rosenbaum called for policy changes to enable everyone, including vulnerable groups, to engage in physical activity.

The "Four Down" offense is primarily used for taking the last shot in a period but can function as a spread offense for teams with a skilled ballhandler. Signaled by the ballhandler pointing four fingers downward, it positions four non-ballhandlers along the baseline with top shooters in the corners, creating space for one-on-one play similar to Dean Smith's "Four Corner" offense.

Basic reads include driving to the basket, pulling up for jumpers, drop passes to posts when baseline defenders help, or kick-outs to corner shooters. For continuity, if the ballhandler faces pressure or the five-second rule, corners pop out for release passes and may assume the isolation role.

Crunch-time specials include:
- **Mid Screen**: A post sets a mid screen for O1, enabling drives, pull-ups, rolls, or kick-outs.
- **Triple Base Screen**: O3, O4, and O5 set staggered baseline screens for shooter O2, ideally with four seconds remaining.
- **Misdirection Double**: O1 executes a dribble hand-off with O2 while O3 and O5 set a weakside double screen for O4, creating multiple scoring options.

The 2-3 zone is the most common zone defense, strong at protecting the basket and defending dribble penetration, but vulnerable to good outside shooting. It is typically used by teams at a disadvantage in quickness or skill, though quick players can make it aggressive and trapping.

Alignment places two guards above the free throw line, a post in front of the basket, and two baseline defenders outside the lane near the blocks. Defenders shift based on ball position, with outside guards covering sideline to sideline, the post fronting or denying the low post, and baseline defenders alternating between on-ball and weakside rebounding roles.

Variations include wing defenders either denying corner return passes or dropping to help on dominant posts. On ball reversal, the baseline defender temporarily "shows" until the guard recovers. The 1-1-3 tandem variation matches the point defender on the ball handler while the wing guards the first pass.

Advanced options include corner traps, surprise point traps, and automatic wing traps to pressure star shooters. Against dominant post players ("Footers"), adjustments create double and triple teams by fronting the post with backside and topside support from surrounding defenders.

Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, is investing $2 billion in cash into prediction market platform Polymarket, valuing the startup at $9 billion. As part of the deal, ICE will distribute Polymarket's data, and the two firms will collaborate on tokenization initiatives. CEO Shayne Coplan called the partnership a step toward bringing prediction markets into mainstream finance.

Founded in 2020 and built on blockchain technology, Polymarket gained prominence during the 2024 U.S. presidential election, with trading volume peaking near $400 million in November. Daily volume has since fallen to between $40 million and $80 million in early October. Competitor Kalshi previously raised $185 million at a $2 billion valuation and is reportedly in talks for a new round valuing it at nearly $5 billion.

The UC1825B-SP controller operates from a 10-30 V input supply and supports topologies including push-pull, forward, half-bridge, and full bridge. A sense resistor detects ripple current and triggers shutdown when peak current exceeds the limit, with a CS pin voltage threshold of approximately 1 V.

Layout recommendations include:
- Using low-EMI ferrite closed-core inductors, with stick cores avoided.
- Routing feedback traces away from inductors and noisy power traces, ideally on the opposite PCB side with a ground plane separating them.
- Placing ceramic input capacitors, feed-forward capacitors, and compensation components close to the IC, preferably surface-mount.
- Making power traces short, direct, and at least 15 mils per Ampere, with output components placed close together.
- Employing ground planes on both PCB sides; multilayer boards should separate power and signal planes.
- Arranging components so switching current loops curl in the same direction to reduce EMI.

Each output driver handles 2-A peak currents, requiring a dedicated power ground section for high di/dt currents connected to PGND. VCC and VREF should be bypassed with low ESR/ESL 1-mF ceramic capacitors, and the output clamped with a Schottky diode to VCC and PGND.

California faces a major electricity supply shortfall for summer 2001, with demand potentially exceeding supply by 2,000 MW or more during heat waves. Critics argue Gov. Gray Davis is focusing on utility solvency and power-line purchases rather than addressing the supply-demand imbalance through rate increases that would reduce demand.

Most Western states face similar power shortages, having failed to match electricity production with rapid population growth. Leaders across the West are seeking to renegotiate longstanding arrangements under which California draws power from out-of-state plants, with Utah already recalling some capacity.

Construction of 29 small "peaker" plants intended to help California through summer has been delayed by the Department of Water Resources' efforts to revise existing contracts originally signed with Cal-ISO.

A National Federation of Independent Business survey found 40% of small companies have a dimmer view of California's business climate due to the crisis, though 69% have no plans to relocate.

After early criticism of inaction, Davis has shifted to a high-profile role, touring plants and announcing agreements, including a framework deal to buy Southern California Edison's transmission lines for $2.76 billion. The broader $7.5 billion plan to purchase utility transmission lines faces skepticism from legislators and consumer groups.

Despite perceptions, California ranks 49th in per-capita electricity consumption, aided by mild climate, less heavy industry, and conservation standards.

Western spot power prices declined February 26 as several major plants returned to service amid mild temperatures and lighter loads.

Community Board 7 of Manhattan brought an Article 78 proceeding challenging the New York City Department of City Planning's denial of its Freedom of Information Law (FOIL) request for documents related to the proposed "Trump City" development. The Supreme Court and Appellate Division ruled in favor of the board, finding it had standing to sue.

The Court of Appeals reversed, holding that the board lacked capacity to maintain the proceeding. The Court distinguished between "standing" and "capacity," explaining that capacity concerns a litigant's power to appear in court and that governmental entities created by statute have no inherent right to sue; such authority must derive from enabling legislation either expressly or by necessary implication.

Applying this standard, the Court found that the New York City Charter neither expressly authorizes community boards to sue nor implies such authority. The enabling legislation denies community boards the power to retain independent counsel or subpoena documents, and the legislative history shows that recommendations to grant boards the power to sue were rejected during the 1975 Charter revision. Because community boards serve a purely advisory role under the Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP), the power to sue cannot be inferred as necessary to their functions.

The Court concluded that FOIL's broad standing provisions do not override the capacity requirement for governmental entities, and accordingly dismissed the petition.

Cboe Global Markets' CEO Ed Tilly said the smooth launch of bitcoin futures could pave the way for additional cryptocurrency-related products, including options and ETFs. Cboe became the first U.S.-based traditional exchange to offer bitcoin futures, with nearly 3,700 contracts traded by early Monday afternoon and roughly 20 trading firms participating. The contract showed significant volatility, surging enough to trigger a five-minute trading halt, though Tilly said markets resumed in an orderly fashion.

Following the launch, fund managers REX Shares, Van Eck Associates, and First Trust Advisors approached the SEC seeking permission to launch bitcoin ETFs, though the SEC has previously rejected or tabled such proposals. Cboe plans to wait for a couple of one-month futures settlements before introducing new crypto-derivative products. Tilly also indicated futures on other cryptocurrencies could follow. Cboe's website briefly went down due to traffic six times higher than an average weekday.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition device that can be powered down via the PWDN pin or PD_CH register. After power-up or reset, it requires an initialization sequence of register writes with a free-running sampling clock connected. A speed-boost mode supports up to 8MSPS for a user-selected channel pair, while the remaining six channels are idle.

The device uses a configuration SPI interface with three register banks accessed via an 8-bit address. Register bank 0 is always accessible, while banks 1 and 2 are selected via REG_BANK_SEL. Writes use two 24-bit SPI frames, and reads require setting SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE bits. Multiple devices can be connected in a daisy-chain topology, configured through the DAISY_CHAIN_LEN register, requiring N × 24 SCLKs per SPI frame.

Registers control functions including data format, averaging, test patterns, gain error correction, analog input bandwidth, common-mode range, channel power-down, output lane count, and internal/external reference selection.

The ADS9803 achieves 0.0015% TUE at 25°C post-calibration and offers low-noise (22.7kHz) and wide-bandwidth (700kHz) modes, with the latter settling to 99.95% FS in 7.5µs. It uses three power supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence, and recommends 0.1μF decoupling capacitors near supply pins.

Premium Subscription features include: the Lex Column, providing daily commentary on companies, markets, and investing theory since the 1930s from specialists in London, New York, and Hong Kong; Editor's Choice, a weekly newsletter from FT editor Lionel Barber; FT Newsmine Blog, a weekly email summarizing macroeconomic data; and Martin Sandbu's Free Lunch, a daily column on global economics.

The ADS868xW device supports an external reference mode, enabled by setting the INTREF_DIS bit, allowing a 4.096V external reference at the REFIO pin. The REFCAP pin requires a 10µF and 1µF decoupling capacitor. The internal buffer has stable performance from –40°C to +125°C with typical 0.5ppm/°C drift.

The device supports single-ended and differential inputs in bipolar and unipolar ranges, with straight-binary output format and LSB equal to FSR/2^16.

Alarm features include input alarms (user-programmable thresholds) and AVDD alarms (fixed at 4.7V low, 5.3V high), readable via the ALARM pin, ALARM_REG register, or appended data output.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI and source-synchronous protocols, with single or dual SDO options. Devices can be connected in daisy-chain topology. Three operational states exist: RESET, ACQ, and CONV, controlled by RST and CONVST/CS signals.

Nine configuration registers control device ID, reset/power, SDI/SDO protocols, data output, range selection, alarms, and thresholds. Commands include read/write operations for bytes or half-words.

Low-power modes include NAP (between conversions) and power-down (PD). Power supplies AVDD and DVDD require decoupling capacitors. Application examples include an 8-channel analog input module for PLCs using the MUX36D08 multiplexer, with the input alarm useful for thermistor-based temperature monitoring with hysteresis to prevent false triggering.

The paper addresses challenges posed by Europe's ageing population, focusing on Finland where 22% of the population will be 65+ by 2020. The authors propose digital wellness services delivered via mobile smartphones for the "young elderly" (ages 60-75) as a proactive, preventive intervention to reduce future health and social care costs for the 75+ age group.

The research, conducted through the BeWell program (2014-2016) led by Tieto Group with 10 companies and 4 research partners, addresses four questions: whether young elderly are a relevant user group, whether they find wellness important, how services should be designed, and what environment can sustain wellness routines.

The authors advocate a four-dimensional wellness framework (intellectual, physical, social, emotional) where deficiencies in one dimension can be compensated by others. Services are developed using action design research (ADR) with users rather than for them, built on the Wellmo omnivore platform (connecting 100+ devices and applications) with backend support from Tieto's cloud analytics platform.

A survey of 101 young elderly in the Åland Islands (26.6% response rate) found that approximately 73% use smart mobile phones, 72.9% use mobile apps, and respondents rated mobile apps highly for usefulness and ease of use. Intellectual challenges and physical health were deemed important for wellbeing. Statistical analysis revealed significant differences based on education, age, employment status, and income regarding attitudes toward mobile apps and wellness.

The authors conclude that young elderly are a viable user group, wellness services can feasibly be delivered via mobile platforms, and sustainable commercial ecosystems are required. If adopted widely, such services could potentially save billions of euros annually in EU health and social care costs.

Patrick Kane, Brent Seabrook, and Bryan Bickell discussed their team's performance after evening up the series. FreeNAS has released version 11, following the troubled version 10 ("Corral"), which was downgraded to a tech preview after users experienced significant issues. Developed by iXsystems, the new version is based on FreeBSD 11-STABLE and includes the bhyve hypervisor for hosting virtual machines. Docker support from Corral has been postponed to a future release, though FreeBSD jails remain available. New features include compatibility with AWS S3 object storage, integration with messaging tools like Slack and HipChat, and the ability to choose which services start at boot. A new Angular-based GUI is included but remains in beta. Feedback from testers of the release candidates has reportedly been largely positive.

The study examined the spatiotemporal evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Alpha and Delta variants in Vietnam during 2021. After successfully controlling community transmission in 2020 through border restrictions, contact tracing, and quarantine measures, Vietnam experienced a major nationwide outbreak in 2021, with over 1.7 million infections and 32,000 deaths.

Researchers sequenced 1,303 genomes from nasopharyngeal swabs collected at two tertiary hospitals in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. The Delta variant accounted for 93.8% of sequences, with AY.57 being the dominant lineage (99.2% of Delta sequences). The Alpha variant (5.7%) was introduced multiple times between January and May 2021 but did not sustain community transmission due to strict containment measures.

Phylogeographic analysis indicated that AY.57 was first introduced into the Northeast region around March 2021, later spreading to southeastern provinces, which then reseeded the virus back across Vietnam. Strict lockdowns between July and September 2021 limited inter-provincial dispersal, resulting in distinct localized clusters. Genetic diversity increased sharply between April and August 2021, coinciding with the outbreak's escalation in a largely unvaccinated population. The estimated evolutionary rate was 5.29x10-4 substitutions per site per year, with weak purifying selection overall.

The authors conclude that rigorous public health measures contained the Alpha variant, but the highly transmissible Delta AY.57 lineage caused an explosive outbreak in an immunologically naïve population, underscoring the importance of genomic surveillance.

Ostersunds, a Swedish club formed after September 1996, will face Arsenal in the Europa League last 32. Managed by English coach Graham Potter, the club has earned three promotions since 2011 and qualified for European competition by winning their domestic cup. They finished second in Group J after three qualifying rounds. The tie marks Arsenal's first European meeting with a Swedish side since 1999-2000. Borussia Dortmund, Atletico Madrid, Celtic, and Napoli, having dropped from the Champions League, will face Atalanta, Copenhagen, Zenit, and RB Leipzig respectively.

Cannabis sativa contains approximately 500 bioactive compounds, including the non-psychoactive CBD and psychoactive THC. Globally, cannabis is the third most used psychoactive substance, with increasing use among older adults following medical legalization. Cannabinoids exhibit anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive properties, and interact with the gut microbiome through the gut-brain axis.

This systematic review, registered on PROSPERO (CRD42022354331), followed PRISMA guidelines and searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases through July 20, 2022. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. From 4,022 identified articles, 9 studies were included (1 case-control, 6 cohorts, 2 clinical trials), involving 2,526 participants aged 17–101 across the USA, Iran, Israel, and UK. Most participants were women, and 76.6% of patients had cognitive impairment.

Findings indicated that marijuana or endocannabinoid supplements (2-AG, AEA, OEA, PEA) altered microbiota in patients with HIV, obesity, oral disease, musculoskeletal pain, systemic aspergillosis, and inflammation. MJ use in HIV patients correlated with increased Fusobacterium and Anaerotruncus and decreased Dorea. In musculoskeletal pain patients, medical cannabis increased S. mutans and Lactobacilli. OEA supplementation reduced energy and carbohydrate intake and increased A. muciniphila in obese participants. Endocannabinoid increases correlated with higher SCFA-producing bacteria and reduced proinflammatory cytokines. Reported adverse events included coughing, wheezing, drowsiness, and night sweats, which resolved after cessation.

A meta-analysis could not be performed due to heterogeneous conditions. The review concludes that both cannabis use and gut microbiota contribute to various clinical manifestations, warranting further research.

Chinese textile firms are increasingly using North Korean factories for cheaper labour, with garments labelled "Made in China" and exported worldwide, according to traders in Dandong. UN sanctions on North Korea do not ban textile exports, which were the country's second-largest export in 2016 at $752 million. Chinese suppliers send raw materials to North Korean factories, where manufacturers can save up to 75 percent on production costs. North Korean factories are reportedly fully booked, with workers producing 30 percent more daily than Chinese counterparts at significantly lower wages. Chinese firms also employ North Korean workers in China, earning about half the Chinese average, with a portion of wages going to North Korean government handlers. Recent UN sanctions prohibit increasing the number of North Korean labourers working abroad.

Glenner Town Square, opened in April 2018 in Chula Vista, is an 8,500-square-foot daycare facility for Alzheimer's and dementia patients designed as a 1950s-style downtown with 13 interactive storefronts intended to trigger long-term memories. Activities include watching old movies, dining in a retro diner, browsing a library, working on a 1959 Ford T-Bird, and visiting a simulated hospital nursery. Glenner also operates centers in Hillcrest and Encinitas, which will be converted into Town Square projects. The passage additionally lists other licensed adult day programs for cognitively impaired individuals throughout San Diego County, including facilities in Clairemont, College Avenue, Mira Mesa, Logan Heights, Bankers Hill, Rancho Bernardo, San Marcos, and Fallbrook, each offering varying therapeutic, social, and health services.

The speaker expresses strong desire to win the championship after reaching the finals three times with three different teams. They note that losses provide learning opportunities and renewed enthusiasm. They praise the city as a true hockey town, citing sold-out games and passionate fans throughout the season. Having signed with Chicago as a free agent, they credit the team's success to hard work rather than luck. They anticipate a tight series against the experienced Flyers, emphasizing that winning the trophy is most important.

President Reagan delivers the State of the Union address, reporting that America has improved after overcoming the crisis of the 1970s. He cites reduced inflation (from 12.4 to 3.2 percent), tax cuts, deregulation, four million new jobs in 1983, and restored military strength.

He outlines four major goals:

1. **Economic growth**: Reduce federal deficits by limiting government size rather than raising taxes. He proposes bipartisan talks with congressional leaders on a $100 billion deficit reduction "down payment," a line-item veto, a balanced budget amendment, and tax code simplification (with recommendations due December 1984).

2. **Developing the space frontier**: He directs NASA to build a permanently manned space station within a decade and invites international participation. He also addresses environmental priorities, including Chesapeake Bay cleanup, hazardous waste, acid rain research, and Superfund extension.

3. **Strengthening traditional values**: He advocates educational excellence, tuition tax credits, school prayer, anti-abortion measures, stronger crime enforcement, and enterprise zones.

4. **Building peace**: He seeks stable U.S.-Soviet relations, nuclear arms reductions, and peacemaking in Lebanon, Central America, and elsewhere. He addresses the Soviet people directly, stating nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.

Reagan closes by honoring Sergeant Stephen Trujillo (Grenada), Father Ritter, and Dr. Charles Carson as examples of American heroism, expressing confidence in America's future.

Ben Rice, born and raised in Cohasset, Massachusetts, became the Yankees' first baseman after Anthony Rizzo's 2024 injury. Despite growing up near Boston, Rice was a Yankees fan who admired Derek Jeter. He attended Noble and Greenough School in Dedham, initially focusing on hockey before shifting to baseball.

Rice played college baseball at Dartmouth, but accumulated only 110 plate appearances due to the COVID-19 pandemic and a cancelled 2021 Ivy League season. The Yankees drafted him in the 12th round of the 2021 MLB Draft based on a strong summer league performance.

In 2025, Rice hit 26 home runs over 138 games, playing catcher, first base, and designated hitter. He hit a 2-run home run in Game 2 of the Wild Card Series against the Red Sox. Rice turns 27 on February 22 and is under team control through 2030.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate for the third consecutive quarter to a range between 1 percent and 1.25 percent, citing continued job growth and moderate economic expansion, according to Binyamin Appelbaum of The New York Times. The Fed acknowledged weakening inflation, lowering its 2017 forecast from 1.9 percent to 1.6 percent while maintaining a 2 percent prediction for next year. Some officials now anticipate unemployment could drop below 4 percent.

The study evaluates the effectiveness of a screening-isolation strategy for controlling infectious diseases in a semi-isolated community when vaccines and medications are unavailable. Researchers developed a simplified compartmental mathematical model based on the SIR framework, incorporating factors such as contagious capacity, recovery/death rate, screening efficiency, time lag, and external influx of infection.

Theoretical analysis revealed that the time lag between infection and isolation is critical, while improvements in screening efficiency contribute only weakly to control robustness. Computer simulations tested scenarios with varying basic reproduction numbers (R0), screening frequencies, efficiencies, and influx rates.

Key findings include:
- With R0=3.0 and daily screening (efficiency 0.9), infections were well controlled; the strategy also worked at R0=6.0 but failed at R0=8.0.
- Screening every 3 days maintained control, while weekly screening performed worse, and biweekly screening failed regardless of efficiency.
- Higher screening efficiency significantly reduced cumulative infections.
- Infection size increased proportionally with influx rate, highlighting the necessity of strict border control.

The discussion notes that PCR-based tests are promising candidates for mass screening, outperforming traditional methods like fever screening. The authors acknowledge model simplifications and suggest further research on operational and psychological challenges.

The study concludes that regular, periodic community-wide screening, combined with border control, can effectively limit disease transmission in semi-isolated communities during pandemics when medical interventions are unavailable.

Tom Brady's agent, Don Yee, confirmed the 40-year-old quarterback intends to return to the New England Patriots in 2018 and play into his mid-40s, unless his performance drops below a championship level. Brady has two seasons left on his contract, earning $14 million plus a $1 million roster bonus annually. Despite missing voluntary offseason workouts and retirement rumours, Yee said Brady continues to train and customise his preparation each season. Patriots owner Robert Kraft stated there is no issue with Brady's current contract and the team is not focused on negotiating a new deal.

MultiChoice's DStv service has been affected by Netflix's growing presence in South Africa, with Premium subscribers declining by 41,000 and average revenue per customer dropping from R353 to R344 monthly. CEO Calvo Mawela expressed concern over Netflix's "unfair advantage" and noted that customers who switch to streaming rarely return to broadcast TV. As a solution, MultiChoice is working towards a standalone DStv streaming service, separate from Showmax, though securing streaming rights remains a challenge. The company has also urged ICASA against over-regulating pay-TV, warning it could lead to job losses to international streaming competitors.

CoreWeave (CRWV) has rebounded amid strong AI sentiment and new deal announcements, including a $22.4B agreement with OpenAI and a $14.2B deal with Meta, which help diversify its customer base beyond Microsoft. However, concerns remain about revenue concentration, aggressive capex, debt-funded growth, and a high forward revenue multiple. With optimism appearing fully priced in, shares may face a cooling-off period despite recent momentum.

Joppatowne High School held its 45th commencement ceremony at Harford Community College, graduating more than 130 seniors. According to Principal Pamela Zeigler, about 95 percent of the 138-member class will pursue college, technical school, the military, or law enforcement. Graduate Amya Hill, 17, who plans to study nursing at Albany State University, was celebrated by family members traveling from Colorado and Georgia. Classmate Zachary Wagmun plans to attend Harford Community College for an electrician's apprenticeship. Valedictorian Kacey Lebrun and class president Breea Stevenson addressed the seniors, with Stevenson sharing three life lessons. The class also heard from Board of Education Member Robert Frisch, state Sen. Robert Cassilly, Del. Kathy Szeliga, County Executive Barry Glassman, and County Councilman Mike Perrone. Cassilly referenced fallen officer Amy Caprio and Sgt. Eddison Hermond as examples of sacrifice.

The speaker declines to analyze the previous game publicly, stating it will be discussed with the team. He notes players were fatigued from a long flight but will recover by tomorrow. He emphasizes the pressure is on Calgary, not Tampa, since Calgary is expected to win with the Cup in their building and all of Canada watching. Tampa's focus is simply on extending the series.

The team will stay in Calgary after the game rather than travel, to maximize rest. He praises a Calgary player as a top player in the league, acknowledging both teams rely on big players making key plays.

He rejects suggestions his players lacked effort last night, suggesting instead they struggled mentally by anticipating winning the Cup. He expects Calgary may face similar mental challenges in an elimination game at home.

Michael Ben'Ary, an assistant U.S. attorney in the Eastern District of Virginia, was abruptly fired while prosecuting a terrorism case related to the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing. A letter bearing his typed signature, taped to his door, claimed his termination followed a false social media post by pro-Trump commentator Julie Kelly, who suggested he was an ally of former Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco and had resisted the indictment of former FBI Director James Comey. The letter stated that DOJ leadership was prioritizing punishing the president's perceived enemies over national security, and warned that removing career officials from U.S. attorney's offices and the FBI was making America less safe. Ben'Ary's firing occurred under interim U.S. Attorney Halligan, who replaced the previous U.S. attorney after Trump pressured for Comey's indictment.

The study investigates an intervalley superconducting phase in approximately 2°-twisted bilayer MoTe2 at hole filling νh = 3, using exact diagonalization on a continuum model of half-filled second moiré bands with both valleys and screened Coulomb interactions.

By tuning the effective screening length d, the phase diagram reveals three regimes: a ferromagnetic Chern insulator at small d, a non-Abelian fractional spin Hall insulator at large d, and an intermediate paramagnetic superconducting phase. The superconductivity is identified through negative binding energy, a dominant eigenvalue in the pair density matrix, finite superfluid stiffness, and abrupt changes in intervalley entanglement entropy. The pairing is time-reversal symmetric, extended nodal s-wave, occurring between holes of opposite spins and valleys at opposite momenta.

The transition between the superconductor and fractional spin Hall insulator is continuous, with simultaneous changes in topology and symmetry, described using a U(2)2,−4 × U(1)8 Chern-Simons field theory where condensation of a matter field reduces the Pfaffian × anti-Pfaffian topological order to a superconductor. Non-uniform quantum geometry is shown to be crucial for stabilizing the intermediate phase. The authors suggest the screening length could be experimentally tuned via gating or substrate engineering to access this superconducting phase.

Over-the-counter (OTC) trading involves direct transactions between two parties without a centralized exchange, conducted electronically through networks of market makers and dealers. OTC markets trade various instruments, including stocks, bonds, derivatives, and commodities, and are regulated by FINRA, though less stringently than formal exchanges.

Unlike exchanges, OTC markets are decentralized, less transparent, and have fewer reporting requirements. Stocks traded here typically belong to small companies unable to meet exchange listing requirements, though some foreign companies trade via American Depository Receipts (ADRs). Risks include counterparty default, market manipulation, lower liquidity, and fraud schemes like "pump and dump."

The OTC market enables unlisted companies to raise capital and offers customizable derivative contracts for hedging. However, OTC stocks have historically shown negative average returns; one study of 10,000 OTC stocks (2001-2010) found an average loss of 27% and median loss of 37%. Over 90% of penny stocks fail, and fewer than 1% transition to major exchanges.

Cryptocurrency trading occurs on both exchanges and OTC desks, with OTC used primarily for large off-market deals. Due to poor performance, high slippage, and scam risks, both investing and day trading in OTC markets are generally discouraged.

"Brainsaver" classes, offered by OptumCare in the Valley, are part of a 12-week course focused on brain health through physical exercise, stress reduction, cognitive exercises, education, socialization, and nutrition, with the aim of reducing the risk of Alzheimer's Disease. Instructor Ben Brock describes the program as a holistic approach. Students, ranging from their mid-50s to late 80s, report noticeable benefits. Classes are held at three locations: Deer Valley, Goodyear, and Chandler.

Following a White House meeting between President Trump and congressional leaders, a federal government shutdown appears likely. Vice President JD Vance blamed Democrats, while Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer cited "very large differences" between the parties. Republicans seek a stopgap bill maintaining current funding levels until late November, while Democrats demand the inclusion of an extension of enhanced Obamacare tax credits set to expire at year's end. Republicans accuse Democrats of "hostage taking" by refusing a clean resolution, while Democrats say they were excluded from drafting the bill. Earlier short-term funding bills failed in the Senate, where 60 votes are needed to overcome the filibuster.

Moina Shaiq, a Muslim mother and grandmother in Fremont, California, launched the "Meet a Muslim" program after placing a newspaper ad inviting questions about her religion. Around 100 people attended her first event at a coffee house last year. Since then, she has spoken at libraries, churches, coffee shops, and private homes across the San Francisco Bay Area, Arizona, and Atlanta, addressing topics such as the hijab, differences between Sunnis and Shias, women's rights in Islam, and American Muslim life. Similar initiatives emerged after 9/11 and have resurged amid rising anti-Muslim incidents, including arson, vandalism, harassment, and a deadly May attack in Portland, Oregon. Shaiq herself received a threat in Atlanta. Zainab Arain of the Council on American-Islamic Relations supports such efforts amid heightened fear and references to President Trump's travel ban targeting six Muslim-majority countries. Critics like Detroit activist Asha Noor argue the focus should instead be on policy change. Shaiq says her goal is to educate Americans that Muslims share the same needs as others.

The application is a continuation of multiple prior U.S. applications and claims priority from Korean and U.S. Provisional Applications. It relates to wireless communication, specifically methods and devices for transmitting/receiving a sounding reference signal (SRS) in NR systems.

The disclosure proposes methods for configuring and/or indicating a guard period (Y symbols) for SRS transmission/reception when adjacent to other uplink transmissions such as PUCCH or PUSCH. A UE receives configuration information from a base station including SRS resources and usage information, then transmits the SRS accordingly. When the guard period overlaps with a specific uplink channel transmission, the priority between them is configured identically to the priority between the SRS and that channel.

Key embodiments include: configuring the guard period for antenna switching usage; handling PUCCH for CSI reporting or beam failure recovery; determining guard period symbol count based on subcarrier spacing (typically one or two symbols); and configuring guard period information per SRS resource set via higher layer signaling, including starting position index and number of symbols.

The First Embodiment describes methods for configuring guard periods considering PUSCH/PUCCH-SRS relationships, including joint-encoding of position and number of symbols, implicit beam assumptions, explicit beam designation via SRI/TPMI, and collision resolution rules.

The Second Embodiment addresses collisions between guard periods and SRS resource sets, proposing priority rules, SRS group definitions, reconfiguration methods, and slot-shifting approaches.

These methods aim to enable efficient uplink transmission and prevent distortion from SRS resource collisions during antenna switching.

Turing Tensor Cores are specialized units for tensor/matrix operations used in Deep Learning, offering speed-ups for neural network training and inferencing. Enhanced for inferencing, they add INT8 and INT4 precision modes. They enable new AI capabilities on GeForce and Quadro systems, including Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS), which uses a neural network to combine details from multiple frames into a high-quality image with fewer input samples than techniques like TAA.

Zsolt Lakatos, 31, was sentenced to 13 years in prison in his absence on February 6 after being found guilty of wounding with intent for violently shaking his four-month-old son. Lakatos failed to appear at the end of his trial and hid at an address in Litherland for eight days before being arrested. He admitted breaching bail and received an additional 10 days imprisonment. His defence stated he had panicked over the prospect of a lengthy sentence. The child, now 22 months old and in foster care, suffered catastrophic brain injuries, fractured ribs, a fractured shin, and retinal haemorrhaging after being shaken on two occasions. He will require lifelong nursing care and medication. Lakatos initially lied to police but admitted shaking his son vigorously out of frustration when the baby would not stop crying.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, reporting an event dated January 3, 2016. The filing addresses Item 2.02 (Results of Operations and Financial Condition) and Item 7.01 (Regulation FD Disclosure), referencing a press release issued by Tesla on January 3, 2016, attached as Exhibit 99.1. The information is furnished rather than filed under the Exchange Act. The report was signed by Todd A. Maron, General Counsel, on January 4, 2016.

Coach Quenneville discusses his consistent approach with the Blackhawks, emphasizing accountability, open communication, and the leadership of core players. He addresses the goaltending situation, noting healthy competition between Crawford and Darling, and explains that Crawford's return to the net was based on Darling's performance rather than poor play.

He comments on a player's improving performance, particularly in faceoffs and offensive contributions, and stresses the importance of not being overconfident and treating every game as a must-win. He discusses line combinations featuring Kane, Richards, Hossa, and others, noting improvement throughout last night's game.

Quenneville praises Kane's evolution toward a shooting mentality, explaining that overlooking shots for perfect plays leads to turnovers. He describes how trust in players is earned through defensive play, positional awareness, and puck protection.

He speaks highly of a rookie player who exceeded expectations early in the season before being injured, noting his upside and the benefit of learning from top players. Quenneville reflects on the team rising to challenges as series progress, acknowledging the opponent's speed, and praises a player's playmaking ability, patience, and imagination during the playoffs.

Cover 0 is a man-to-man defensive coverage with no safeties providing deep help. Every non-lineman defender is either covering an offensive player one-on-one or blitzing, typically allowing the defense to rush up to six players.

Strengths include clear assignments, easy adjustments to motion, strong run defense, and effectiveness against Run-Pass Options, short routes, and screens. The heavy pressure also limits the quarterback's time to throw.

Weaknesses include vulnerability to big plays if a defender is beaten, since there is no deep help. It can struggle against draw plays, quarterback scrambles, pick plays like the mesh concept, and deep throws down the middle, which remains open. Al Davis reportedly banned his Raiders coordinators from using it.

Typical assignments place cornerbacks on outside receivers, safeties on the tight end and slot, and a linebacker on the running back, while other linebackers blitz. Variations include "Rat" coverage, where one defender is freed to watch crossing routes and the quarterback, and schemes dropping a defensive lineman into coverage.

Astronomers at the University of Toronto, led by Alan Jackson, report that Oumuamua — the first confirmed interstellar object in our solar system — likely originated from a binary star system and was ejected during planet formation. Discovered in October by a Hawaiian observatory, the reddish, cigar-shaped asteroid is estimated at 1,300 feet long and is moving away from Earth at over 16 miles per second. A separate team led by Wesley Fraser found it is tumbling through space, possibly due to a collision. Researchers suggest close binary systems may produce most interstellar objects.

This study examines holistic education within Indian higher education, identifying its core dimensions through a twofold literature review: a comprehensive review and a PRISMA-guided systematic literature review (SLR) using Scopus and Semantic Scholar databases.

The comprehensive review traced education's etymology to Latin roots 'educere' (to draw out) and 'educare' (to train/mold), contrasting contemporary materialist education with the holistic visions of Indian sages-thinkers such as Tagore ("universal man"), Osho ("Zorba the Buddha"), Vivekananda (man-making through svadharma), and Sri Aurobindo (integral education). These align with modern policies like India's NEP 2020 and UN SDG 4.7, which emphasize human-centered, sustainable learning.

The review identified Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) as a bridge between academic and human development. Among evaluated SEL frameworks, the LIBRE/EMC² framework—developed in India and endorsed by UNESCO MGIEP—emerged as culturally grounded, integrating four dimensions: empathy, mindfulness, compassion, and critical inquiry through "whole brain learning."

The SLR analyzed eight articles using MAXQDA, validating two thematic clusters: (1) foundational themes supporting holistic competence in higher education, and (2) dimension-specific themes confirming the LIBRE/EMC² components. Empathy reflected interpersonal and cultural awareness; critical inquiry involved analytical and reflective thinking; mindfulness encompassed self-awareness and resilience; and compassion related to moral and relational development.

The discussion connects these dimensions to Indian philosophical traditions and contemporary policies, proposing a feedback model linking classroom assessment to institutional and policy reform. Limitations include reliance on two databases. Future research should develop culturally sensitive assessment tools and explore implementation across diverse educational contexts.

Soybean May futures rose as supplies declined while crushing demand remained steady, supported by soy meal exports. Per Agmarknet, soybean arrivals during April 1-15 were 97,040 tonnes, down from 1,64,286 tonnes in the same period in March. Prices are expected to trade higher on strong crusher demand amid falling supplies. Refined Soy oil and CPO may rise on technical rebound, though ample supplies and cheap imports could pressure prices, while domestic demand offers support.

A University of Maryland study found that young adults who regularly consume caffeinated energy drinks may face a higher risk of alcoholism and drug abuse later in life. Researchers surveyed 1,099 college students at intervals, tracking energy drink consumption and drug use. Participants with a "persistent trajectory" (51.4 per cent), who sustained consumption over time, were significantly more likely to use cocaine, non-medically use prescription stimulants, and be at risk for alcohol use disorder at age 25. Those in the "intermediate trajectory" group (17.4 per cent) also showed increased risk for cocaine and stimulant use compared to non-users (20.6 per cent). The "desisting trajectory" and non-use groups showed no elevated risk. Researchers controlled for demographics, sensation-seeking, other caffeine consumption, and prior substance use at age 21. The findings were published in Drug and Alcohol Dependence.

Consumer advocates reported glitches during the final days of Affordable Care Act enrollment, including an erroneous message on HealthCare.gov telling some Illinois applicants that no plans were available in their area. An administration official said the issue was resolved, though advocates said the problem persisted. Friday, Dec. 15, is the deadline to enroll for 2018 coverage in 39 states served by HealthCare.gov, after the Trump administration halved the sign-up period to 45 days. Residents of hurricane-affected areas can get extensions until Dec. 31. An estimated 9-10 million people currently have ACA marketplace coverage, and many eligible for subsidies may pay lower premiums in 2018. It is unclear whether the Trump administration will allow grace-period extensions as the Obama administration did. Most states running their own exchanges have later deadlines, with California and New York accepting enrollments through Jan. 31.

Following a joint Congressional resolution declaring war between the United States and the Imperial German Government, President Woodrow Wilson issued this proclamation on April 6, 1917, invoking Sections 4067-4070 of the Revised Statutes concerning alien enemies.

The proclamation defines alien enemies as male natives, citizens, denizens, or subjects of Germany aged fourteen and older residing in the United States who have not been naturalized. Wilson directed officials to exercise vigilance and called on citizens to support the war effort.

Alien enemies conducting themselves lawfully would be permitted to pursue their lives peacefully, while those violating regulations faced restraint, removal, or other penalties. The proclamation established twelve regulations prohibiting alien enemies from:
- Possessing firearms, explosives, or munitions
- Possessing aircraft, wireless devices, signaling equipment, or cipher materials
- Approaching within half a mile of military or munitions facilities
- Publishing attacks against the U.S. government or officials
- Aiding enemies of the United States
- Residing in presidentially designated prohibited areas
- Departing or entering the United States without a permit

Violators were subject to seizure of property, relocation, registration requirements, summary arrest, and detention. The regulations applied to all territory under U.S. jurisdiction.

The Washington Nationals signed veteran Jeremy Hellickson to a minor league contract, adding him to a fifth starter competition with A.J. Cole and Erick Fedde. Hellickson would receive $2 million if added to the 40-man roster, plus potential $4 million in bonuses. General manager Mike Rizzo indicated Hellickson may stay in minor league camp to build arm strength, citing past issues rushing players through spring training. His contract includes a delayed opt-out clause. Early-season off days could allow Washington to skip the fifth starter initially. Manager Dave Martinez announced Max Scherzer as the opening day starter, followed by Stephen Strasburg, Gio Gonzalez, and Tanner Roark. Cole is expected to make the team regardless, while Fedde will likely go to the minors. Hellickson, the 2011 AL Rookie of the Year, went 8-11 last season and struggled after being traded to Baltimore. Rizzo said adjustments have been made to Hellickson's delivery. Shortstop Trea Turner left to address an ingrown toenail.

Tesla announced two more affordable vehicles on Tuesday: the Model 3 Standard at $36,990 and the Model Y Standard at $39,990, with the latter offering 321 miles of estimated range. The Standard models omit features such as Autosteer, LED lightbars, adaptive high beams, and FM/AM radio, and save buyers $5,000–$5,500 compared to Premium variants. Availability is estimated for November-January. Tesla's stock closed down 4.45% following the announcement. New York buyers may access additional state rebates. The release follows the end of the $7,500 federal EV tax credit. CEO Elon Musk had teased a $25,000 EV since 2018 but missed deadlines, later calling the endeavor "pointless."

The November 14, 2000 edition of VentureWire, published by Technologic Partners, reports on private company business news. Top stories include Apax Partners merging its European and Israeli units with a $600 million pledge for Israeli investments, New Edge Networks laying off 135 employees, KSolutions receiving $50 million in first-round funding from Great Hill Equity Partners, and Cisco Systems acquiring wireless chip firm Radiata for $295 million in stock.

The issue details numerous funding rounds across sectors including energy, wireless, optical networking, e-learning, and B2B marketplaces, with amounts ranging from roughly $1 million to $80 million. Notable raises include PhotonEx ($80 million), StorageApps ($50 million), and Equator Technologies ($40 million).

Bad news items cover executive departures at Buzz MSP, the closure of eSociety, and layoffs at iExplore. Several companies announced name changes, including Wapmagic to AtoBe and Radix Wireless to BeamReach Networks. M&A activity includes iKnowMed's acquisition of CancerSource.com and USBX's purchase of BizQuest.

The newsletter also reports new board appointments, CEO hires at eOriginal, Codeon, Lendx, Agillion, Solution.com, and Switch & Data Facilities, and VC personnel updates at Horizon Ventures and St. Paul Venture Capital. Murphree Venture Partners held a first close on a new fund targeting $150–$200 million.

In People v. Ortiz, the defendant appealed his conviction of simple assault following charges of assault with a deadly weapon. The defendant, having followed his wife and found her with Albert Donaso at his home, entered through a window and engaged in a struggle with Donaso, cutting him repeatedly with a pocket-knife. The defendant claimed self-defense.

On appeal, the court found no error in the trial court's rulings. It held that the district attorney's request for the defendant to illustrate how he drew and opened his pocket-knife was proper cross-examination, given the self-defense claim. The court also held that evidence regarding whether defendant had written threatening letters was a collateral issue, as the central question was whether the cutting was done in self-defense. The judgment was affirmed.

The Blackwell GPU architecture introduces enhancements to ray tracing and AI-driven rendering. Ray Reconstruction (RR) uses a transformer model trained on NVIDIA supercomputers to generate higher-quality pixels and reduce denoising artifacts, while DLAA applies DLSS Super Resolution technology for native-resolution anti-aliasing.

Blackwell is designed to advance neural shaders, which use trained AI models to approximate complex shader computations. Through the new Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, developed with Microsoft, Tensor Cores become accessible to any shader type. Combined with Slang's differentiable shading features, this enables technologies including:

- **RTX Neural Materials**: Approximates multi-layered materials for film-quality assets at real-time frame rates.
- **RTX Neural Texture Compression**: Reduces memory usage significantly (e.g., 1110 MB down to 333 MB in one demo) using neural networks, supported by Stochastic Texture Filtering.
- **Neural Radiance Cache**: Infers multi-bounce indirect lighting from limited ray data, trained live during gameplay.
- **RTX Skin**: Brings ray-traced subsurface scattering to real-time rendering.
- **RTX Neural Faces**: Uses a generative AI model to produce realistic faces from rasterized input and pose data.

The evolution of shaders progressed from fixed-function pipelines through vertex, pixel, geometry, compute, mesh shaders, and RTX ray tracing, culminating in Blackwell's unified AI and traditional shaders with SER 2.0 scheduling.

The Blackwell family includes:
- **GB202** (flagship): 92.2B transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA Cores — powers the GeForce RTX 5090.
- **GB203**: 45.6B transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA Cores — powers the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti.
- **GB205**: 31B transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA Cores — powers the RTX 5070.

Devanna Cornitcher, 25, was found stabbed to death in a Chester, Pennsylvania apartment on Friday night. Her 6-year-old daughter told police that her mother's boyfriend, Alonzo Carter, 25, killed her. Police found Carter bloodied near the body, with a kitchen knife on the floor. Carter was arrested on charges including murder and reportedly confessed, claiming self-defense. Cornitcher's 6-year-old daughter and the couple's 3-year-old son were present during the killing. Carter is being held without bail at George Hill correctional facility.

Archibeque sued Miera before a justice of the peace for damage caused to his wheat field by Miera's cattle, and obtained judgment. Miera appealed to the district court, where the case was tried de novo. Miera's motion to dismiss based on errors in the justice's transcript was overruled, and plaintiff was allowed to file his account.

The court held that under the organic act, only the supreme court has appellate jurisdiction; the district courts, probate courts, and justice courts are courts of original jurisdiction. The legislature cannot confer appellate powers on district courts. On appeal from a justice of the peace, the district court tries the case de novo on its merits, using the transcript only to verify that the case originated in the justice's court and was properly appealed. Parties may file accounts and set-offs as if the case originated in the district court.

At trial, the jury returned a verdict for Miera, and plaintiff's motion for new trial was denied. On appeal, the court noted discrepancies in witness testimony regarding the number of cattle and timing, and evidence that plaintiff's own animals and others had been in the field. Weighing such testimony is the jury's province. Motions for new trial based on verdicts against evidence are within the court's discretion and should be denied unless the verdict is clearly against the weight of evidence. Finding no clear preponderance against the verdict, the court affirmed the judgment.

Between January and March 1945, the United States consulted with the United Kingdom, Soviet Union, China, and France on unresolved Dumbarton Oaks questions and Yalta Conference decisions, reviewed views from American Republics, other governments, Congress, and the public, and extended conference invitations to 39 United Nations governments. At a December 29 meeting, the Secretary of State and American Republic Heads of Mission discussed a compilation of Dumbarton Oaks memoranda from nine governments, noting that a forthcoming Conference of American Republics would strengthen cooperation ahead of the general international organization conference.

Early-game power plays and penalty kills are challenging without proper warm-up. The home crowd has been a strong point all season and will be important for winning more games in the series. The opposing team has talented goal scorers, and J.S. is among the best penalty killers. Frustration exists over recent performance, but with two home games coming up, the team expects to turn things around. The opponents have strong defensemen, and in the first two games, the team gave up possession too easily. Holding onto the puck slightly longer is an area for improvement.

This study applied machine learning (ML) to predict depressive symptom severity (DSS) from sleep quality, anxiety, and brain measures across three independent cohorts: HCP-Young (primary, n=1101), HCP-Aging (n=378), and eNKI (n=334 cross-sectional, n=66 longitudinal).

Using ensemble decision tree models with nested 10-fold cross-validation, researchers trained predictive models on the HCP-Young dataset and validated them on the other cohorts without retuning. Features included 19 PSQI sleep items, anxiety scores, and whole-brain gray matter volume (GMV) from 473 parcels. Complementary analyses examined functional brain measures (ReHo, fALFF), lifetime depression history, reverse-direction prediction, and mediation effects.

Key findings:
- Sleep quality predicted DSS in HCP-Young (r=0.43), HCP-Aging (r=0.57), and eNKI (r=0.50).
- Adding anxiety improved predictions substantially (r=0.67, 0.72, and 0.66, respectively).
- GMV and functional brain features neither predicted DSS nor improved models.
- The reverse direction (predicting sleep from DSS) was weaker (r=0.33).
- Anxiety mediated 52.6% of the sleep–DSS association; GMV showed no mediation.
- In longitudinal eNKI data, baseline sleep and anxiety predicted future DSS (r=0.66), but predictions failed for participants who received neurofeedback therapy between visits.
- Sleep-related daytime dysfunction, sleep disturbance, and subjective sleep quality were the most important predictors.

The authors conclude that poor sleep and anxiety robustly predict depressive symptoms across cohorts, while brain structure/function play minimal roles, supporting the importance of screening sleep and anxiety to reduce depressive burden.

The Base Cross Offense is a successful basketball strategy in which a smaller player sets a baseline screen for a bigger player to create mismatches. The point guard initiates the action with a pass to the wing and a "Give & Go" cut, then sets a baseline screen for the post, who comes off for a shot or post-up. Variations include Pass, Dribble Clear, UCLA, and Hawk entries.

Execution of the baseline screen is critical, with specific counters based on defensive reads: back cuts against trailing defenders, going over or under based on post defender positioning, screen-and-pop or slip cuts against switches, and lob passes against fronting defenders.

If no shot is available, the offense flows into ball reversal options with weakside down screens, mid screens, or side screens. Back cuts counter reversal pass denials.

Successful implementation requires mastery of screens, post moves, defensive recognition, communication, and timing. Coaches should scout opponents, vary entries, and attack weaker defenders. Teams should also prepare to defend against this commonly used offense.

Kirkpatrick argues that the Carter administration, in 1979, facilitated the replacement of friendly moderate autocrats with hostile extremist regimes in Iran and Nicaragua, and risks repeating this pattern in countries like El Salvador, Guatemala, Morocco, and Zaire. She contends that U.S. foreign policy lacks a realistic approach to non-democratic allies threatened by Soviet-backed subversion, driven instead by a bias favoring leftist challengers over rightist autocracies.

Kirkpatrick asserts that traditional authoritarian governments are less repressive, more open to liberalization, and more compatible with American interests than revolutionary autocracies. She cites Vietnam, Cambodia, China, and North Korea as examples of revolutionary regimes being more repressive than their predecessors or counterparts. While acknowledging both types can produce brutal rulers, she argues traditional autocrats preserve existing social structures and customs, whereas revolutionary autocracies actively create inequities and disrupt familiar ways of life, generating refugees.

Des Moines Public Schools Superintendent Ian Roberts resigned effective immediately after being detained by ICE on Friday during a "targeted enforcement operation." ICE alleges Roberts, a Guyana citizen who entered the U.S. on a student visa in 1999, evaded arrest and had a handgun, hunting knife, and $3,000 in his vehicle. The agency stated an immigration judge issued a final removal order in May 2024.

Roberts' attorney, Alfredo Parrish, said Roberts believed his immigration case had been closed based on a letter from a prior attorney, and his firm is filing a motion to reopen the case and has requested a stay in Omaha federal immigration court. Roberts is held at Woodbury County Jail.

The Iowa Board of Educational Examiners revoked Roberts' license, and questions have emerged about DMPS's vetting process. The National School Board Coalition claimed background-check consultant Baker-Eubanks did not perform I-9 verification, with CEO Kim Cockerham stating such verification is not a service offered. U.S. Rep. Zach Nunn criticized the hiring, citing the final removal order confirmed via FOIA inquiry.

Markets shifted to risk-off last week after a series of catalysts clouded by controversy and contradiction. Q2 2025 earnings were strong, with 82% of S&P 500 companies beating EPS estimates and global upward revisions hitting a 43-month high, yet stocks sold off on the news. GDP grew 3%, exceeding expectations, but tariff-related import distortions muddied interpretation, and personal spending showed weakness.

The FOMC held rates with two dissents, but markets now price over 75% odds of a September cut and three cuts by January. Bond ETFs showed bullish breakouts. Major indexes formed a bearish engulfing pattern at all-time highs, volume turned negative, and nearly all sectors declined, signaling a potential tactical pullback.

A two-hour police pursuit through Kansas and Missouri ended with the arrest of a motorist driving on four flat tires. The chase began in Atchison County, Kansas, when officers tried to stop a pickup truck over felony warrants. After the suspect drove into Missouri, St. Joseph police used a spike strip to deflate all four tires. The pursuit ended when the vehicle veered into a ditch in Savannah, Missouri. Officers recovered drugs and three loaded weapons. The suspect was hospitalized on suspicion of ingesting methamphetamine and will be jailed following evaluation.

The NHS Constitution, also known as the Patient Charter, outlines the legal rights of patients, the pledges made by the NHS, and patient responsibilities. Key patient rights include:

- **Access**: Free care at the point of use (with some exceptions), equal access regardless of personal characteristics, and waiting time standards.
- **Quality and safety**: Treatment by qualified staff in clean, regulated settings, monitored by bodies like the Care Quality Commission.
- **Treatments**: Access to NICE-approved medicines, with local funding decisions required to be evidence-based and explained.
- **Consent and privacy**: The right to accept or refuse treatment, receive clear information, and have personal data kept confidential.
- **Choice and information**: The ability to choose a GP, be involved in treatment decisions, and be informed openly when something goes wrong (duty of candour).
- **Complaints**: The right to have complaints investigated, escalate to the Ombudsman, and seek compensation for negligence.

Patient responsibilities include maintaining personal health, respecting staff, following treatment plans, and participating in vaccination and screening programmes.

The Charter emphasises the NHS as a partnership requiring mutual trust and shared responsibility, particularly amid current pressures such as waiting lists and staff shortages.

A study by Alexandra Tinnermann and colleagues at the University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf found that the nocebo effect—negative side effects from sham treatments—is stronger when a treatment appears more expensive. Participants were given fake creams, presented as either expensive or generic, and told they might increase pain sensitivity. When exposed to heat, those using the expensive-looking cream reported nearly 30 percent more pain, compared to just 3 percent for the generic version. fMRI scans showed varying activity in the prefrontal cortex and periaqueductal gray, both linked to pain and placebo pathways. The findings, published in Science, could help healthcare providers communicate with patients to reduce nocebo effects.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-K annual report for fiscal year ended January 28, 2018. The Delaware-incorporated company, headquartered in Santa Clara, California, is a large accelerated filer trading on NASDAQ under NVDA, with approximately 605 million shares outstanding as of February 26, 2018.

NVIDIA invented the GPU in 1999 and introduced CUDA in 2006, extending its focus to artificial intelligence, virtual reality, and high-performance computing. The company operates two reportable segments: GPU (including GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, GRID, DGX brands) and Tegra Processor (including DRIVE and SHIELD). It serves four primary markets: Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter, and Automotive, with over 320 companies using its DRIVE platform for autonomous vehicles.

NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on suppliers such as TSMC and Samsung for wafer fabrication. The company has invested over $15 billion in R&D since inception, with fiscal 2018 R&D expenses of $1.80 billion. As of January 28, 2018, it had 11,528 employees, including 8,191 in research and development. Revenue from outside the United States and Other Americas accounted for 79% of total revenue in fiscal 2018. Cash and marketable securities totaled $7.11 billion at fiscal year-end 2018.

The report identifies competitors including AMD, Intel, Qualcomm, and Samsung, and outlines risks including competition, manufacturing dependencies, cybersecurity, international operations, intellectual property, and regulatory compliance including GDPR. In November 2017, NVIDIA increased its quarterly dividend to $0.15 per share and paid $341 million in dividends during fiscal 2018. The company plans to return $1.25 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2019 through dividends and share repurchases, with $1.82 billion remaining under its repurchase authorization through December 2020.

Being "goal side" in soccer means a defender positions themselves on an imaginary line between the goal they are defending and their opponent. Coaches can teach this concept to youth by instructing them to "get in the way" of opponents or keep them "in front of them."

To practice, defenders should move out from their goal toward forwards near midfield, stopping before reaching them. Defenders caught behind opponents must sprint past and turn around to regain goal side position. Each defender should learn positioning for right, center, and left locations, adjust to opponent movement, and glance back at the goal or use Penalty Area markings for reference.

Drills should progress from forwards moving without a ball at half-speed, to adding a ball, then increasing speed. Defenders must also learn not to approach forwards with the ball too closely. Unlike basketball or football defenders, soccer defenders cannot block opponents or extend their arms.

James F. Robertson III, an inmate acting pro se, petitioned the Court of Civil Appeals of Alabama for a writ of mandamus ordering the Escambia Circuit Court to enter a default judgment in his divorce action against Cynthia D. Robertson.

After the wife could not be served at the address provided, the husband filed an affidavit under Rule 4.3(d)(1), Ala. R. Civ. P., and the trial court clerk arranged for notice to be published in The Atmore Advance for four consecutive weeks. The husband later moved for a default judgment, alleging the wife failed to respond within 30 days of service by publication. The clerk returned the motion, citing the absence of proof of publication in the file. The husband resubmitted the motion without additional proof, and the trial court denied it for failure to comply with Rule 4.3. A motion to reconsider was also denied.

The court denied the petition, citing the standard from Ex parte Integon Corp., 672 So.2d 497 (Ala.1995), because the husband failed to establish that the affidavit required by Rule 4.3(d)(5) had been filed with the trial court.

The United States appealed the appraiser's valuation of imported fishing equipment at Seattle. The defendant-importer conceded that outside packing charges of 50 yen and 4 yen, initially deducted as nondutiable, were actually dutiable. The Government challenged a 26.557 yen deduction on one invoice, but offered no evidence showing the deduction was improper. The court found the merchandise values on the export date to be the appraised values less shipping, consular fee, insurance, and petties charges, and, for consular invoice 3806, the 26.557 yen deduction.
