Lecture 18 of 14.13 addresses gender, discrimination, and identity. Four reasons are given for studying gender differences: fairness, efficiency, understanding preference formation, and equal reward for equal work.

Claudia Goldin's research shows that while female labor market outcomes have improved over the past half-century due to education gains, technological innovations, labor demand shifts toward services, and reduced discrimination, a gender wage gap of 20-30% persists even controlling for work hours and education.

Goldin and Rouse found that blind auditions in orchestras increased female representation, though results were mixed due to sample size and selection effects across audition rounds. Bertrand and Mullainathan (2004) showed callback rates for white-sounding names were 50% higher than African-American-sounding names, illustrating both taste-based and statistical discrimination.

This manifests in fewer such marriages forming, more divorces, and women reducing labor supply while doing more household work.

Kleven et al. showed women face a roughly 20% long-run "child penalty" in earnings after the first child, while men are unaffected. Supposedly gender-neutral tenure clock policies have actually worsened outcomes for women while helping men. Bursztyn et al. found single female MBA students downplay ambition when observed by male peers.

Vesterlund et al. showed women are more likely to volunteer for non-promotable tasks, more likely to comply when asked, and consequently more likely to be asked—amplifying gender inequality in task allocation.

The device transitions from ACQ to CONV state on the rising edge of CONVST/CS, ignoring further transitions during conversion (tconv). It features nine configuration registers and supports data write and read operations.

Data transfer frames begin with CONVST/CS falling edge and end with its rising edge. Frames with exactly 32 SCLKs are optimal; shorter frames are treated as NOP commands for writes but valid for reads, while longer frames use the last 32 bits as the command.

The device supports HWORD (16-bit) and byte commands for register operations, including CLEAR, READ, WRITE, and SET variants. Output data can include conversion results, register data, or fixed patterns, with optional flags for device address, alarms, range, and parity.

The multiSPI interface supports four legacy SPI protocols (SPI-00-S through SPI-11-S) for configuration, plus single/dual SDO-x and source-synchronous (SRC) protocols for reading. Default on power-up is SPI-00-S.

Configuration registers control device ID, reset/power, SDI/SDO protocols, data output, input range, and alarm thresholds/hysteresis. The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated AFE and reference, suitable for industrial analog input modules supporting ±2.5V to ±10V and current ranges.

Power supplies AVDD and DVDD require decoupling capacitors for optimal PSRR. NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput. Proper PCB layout separates analog and digital sections with appropriate bypass capacitors near supply and reference pins.

The SPY and TLT rotation strategy tactically switches between the S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and the 20-year Treasury bond ETF (TLT) based on monthly momentum, rotating into whichever performed best the prior month. Backtested from 2003, the strategy achieved a 9.2% CAGR with dividends reinvested. Maximum drawdown was 22% before 2022, rising to 41% during that year's bond decline. Momentum strategies generally perform best on timeframes of 1 to 12 months but carry risks of large drawdowns and survivorship bias.

This study, part of the NIHR STIMULATE-ICP project, used a co-produced community-based active case finding approach to identify people with probable Long Covid who lacked a formal clinical diagnosis, in order to explore barriers and stigma in accessing care. Twenty-three semi-structured interviews were conducted across Camden, Merton, and Derbyshire, England, with participants recruited via leaflets distributed through community organisations. A Community Advisory Board including patients, healthcare professionals, and stakeholders informed the study design.

Thematic analysis identified four themes: (1) uncertainty and limited Long Covid awareness, including self-doubt; (2) barriers to healthcare engagement, such as hesitancy, perceived NHS strain, and difficulties presenting multi-system symptoms; (3) experiences and perceptions of enacted, anticipated, and internalised stigma, including ageism, gender discrimination, dismissal by healthcare professionals, and shame; and (4) sources of support, including alternative therapies, private care, peer and social support, and desired improvements to NHS services.

Findings align with epistemic injustice frameworks, encompassing both testimonial and hermeneutical injustice. The authors recommend raising awareness, mitigating stigma, listening to lived experiences, and improving signposting to support. Limitations include the absence of participants under 29. The co-produced design is highlighted as a strength.

The 3 Days Down Overnight Trading Strategy targets the S&P 500 (SPY), entering a trade at the close after three consecutive down days and exiting at the next day's open. Backtesting from 1993 shows 661 trades, a 65% win rate, 8% maximum drawdown, and an average gain of 0.13% per trade.

A further modified version, introduced in March 2022, reduced market exposure and drawdowns. In the 2022 bear market, it produced 35 trades with a 0.3% average gain.

The double-down trading strategy involves adding another position of the same size to a losing trade, aiming to lower the average entry price so that a partial price recovery achieves breakeven. It differs from the Martingale strategy, which doubles position size after each loss, and from the repair strategy, which uses call options.

Backtests on SPY (a mean-reverting asset) show that doubling down improved performance, increasing the average gain per trade from 0.56% to 0.97%, though with fewer trades. In contrast, backtests on HYG (a trending junk bond ETF) showed worsening results, with average loss per trade increasing from 0.19% to 0.22%.

The strategy tends to work for mean-reverting assets but not trending ones. It carries significant risk, as continued declines can cause major losses, and is often driven by trading bias rather than a rational plan.

A low-side current sensing circuit uses an amplifier to amplify the voltage drop across a shunt resistor, with a high-speed comparator changing state when the output exceeds the over-current threshold (1.1V in this design).

The device can operate with split supplies ((V+) and (V-)) or single supplies ((V+) and GND), with input signals kept within the recommended range.

To prevent oscillations, coupling between outputs and inputs should be minimized by avoiding parallel traces without a (V+) or GND trace between them. Series input resistors should be placed close to the device, and a low-value (<100Ω) series output resistor can dampen ringing on long traces. Controlled impedance traces with back-terminations are recommended for long-distance routing.

Summary:

The Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming the digital economy, driving new business models and revenue opportunities while raising concerns about a new "productivity paradox"—a lag between technology investment and measurable productivity gains. This paradox builds on earlier ICT-related debates, beginning with Solow's observation and later analyses by Brynjolfsson and others, which found that Internet-driven free culture, consumer surplus, and disruptive innovations generate value not captured by GDP statistics. This unmeasured value is termed "uncaptured GDP."

An empirical analysis of 500 global ICT firms (2005–2016) shows that high R&D-intensive firms have fallen into a trap where dramatic Internet advancement lowers ICT prices, reducing marginal productivity. In response, leading firms activate self-propagating functionality development by harnessing soft innovation resources, including consumer preferences for supra-functionality, sleeping/untapped resources, trust, past experiences, memory, and vision.

Review of seven leading ICT firms (Samsung, Intel, Google, Microsoft, Huawei, Apple, Amazon) demonstrates successful transformation through ICT-driven disruptive business models incorporating these soft resources. Key findings suggest firms must shift from traditional ICT-driven strategies to digital business strategies, recognize uncaptured GDP's implications, and adopt trust-based disruptive business models addressing consolidated social demand. Future research should explore additional soft innovation resources, Amazon's unique model, and the limitations of GDP measurement in the digital economy.

This video from course 8.701 discusses nuclear binding energies. It begins by noting the uneven distribution of nuclear abundances in the solar system, with hydrogen dominating and a peak around iron.

The binding energy is calculated by summing the masses of constituent protons, neutrons, and electrons, then subtracting the nucleus's mass. Neutrons are slightly heavier than protons and can decay within a nucleus, while free protons do not decay. Average binding energy per nucleon ranges from 7.5 to 9 MeV, peaking at iron, which enables energy release through fission (heavier elements) and fusion (lighter elements).

The Weizsäcker semi-empirical mass formula, also called the liquid-drop model, parameterizes binding energy with five terms:
1. Volume term: dominates at ~16 MeV per nucleon, proportional to mass number A, indicating a short-range nuclear force.
2. Surface term: reduces binding energy for surface nucleons, proportional to A^(2/3).
3. Coulomb term: accounts for proton repulsion, proportional to charge squared over radius.
4. Asymmetry term: based on the Pauli exclusion principle, favoring equal neutron and proton numbers.
5. Pairing term: favors even numbers of protons and neutrons.

Central nuclear density is about 0.17 nucleons per cubic femtometer, with nucleons spaced roughly 1.8 femtometers apart.

The overlap in soccer involves a wing fullback sprinting from the back into the attack, running past and beyond a midfielder along the sideline to become an unmarked attacker. If a defender picks up the overlapping player, another attacker is left free. The maneuver requires space, so it is typically performed near the sideline, though it can occur anywhere in the attacking end. The overlapping player usually receives the ball and crosses toward the end-line, or passes back to the midfielder if covered.

A related move, the underlap, involves the fullback running inside the midfielder toward the middle, often resulting in a shot on goal. After either play, the defender returns to their original position. Coaches are advised to vary between overlaps and underlaps, but should not use the tactic if it disrupts an already effective attack. The term "overlap" can also be used as verbal communication between players, and a back heel pass can facilitate an overlap.

In Nelson v. John (1906), the Washington Supreme Court affirmed a judgment dismissing an action for specific performance of an 1892 contract by which Puyallup Indian John Salerhand agreed to convey allotted reservation land to plaintiff Ross Nelson.

The land had been allotted under the 1854 treaty and patented to Salerhand in 1886, subject to restrictions on alienation until the state legislature, with Congressional consent, removed them. The court rejected appellant's three arguments:

1. The restriction on alienation was not void as repugnant to the grant, because federal policy treated Indians as wards of the government, justifying such restrictions.
2. The Bland Act conferring citizenship on Puyallup Indians did not impliedly repeal the alienation restrictions.
3. The Washington legislature's 1890 act and the Congressional Act of March 3, 1893, did not validate the 1892 conveyance, as the state act required prior Congressional consent, and the 1893 Wilson Act prohibited alienation for ten years after its passage.

The court held that contracts conveying Puyallup allotted lands made before the restrictions were lifted are void.

The passage presents an SEIR-like compartmental model with nine compartments (susceptible, exposed, vaccinated, asymptomatic, mildly, severely, and critically infectious, recovered, deceased) to describe SARS-CoV-2 spread, incorporating a time-dependent transmission parameter. The authors analyze both the direct and inverse problems associated with this model. For the direct problem, they establish well-posedness, proving the existence of a unique non-negative solution on [0,T] under the assumption that parameters are continuous and strictly positive, extendable to [0,∞) if parameters are bounded. They define a parameter-to-solution map J that associates the transmission parameter β to the model solution, and demonstrate its key regularity properties: the domain is closed, convex, and weakly closed; the map is well-defined, injective, continuous in the H¹-norm, sequentially closed under weak topologies, and Fréchet differentiable in the interior of its domain. These theoretical results provide the foundation for applying Tikhonov-type regularization to estimate time-dependent transmission parameters from reported infection data.

Neural Radiance Cache (NRC) uses a neural shader to cache radiance information, inferring multiple light bounces after one path-traced bounce, improving performance and indirect lighting quality while training on live game data.

RTX Skin adapts film subsurface scattering techniques for real-time ray-traced translucent materials. RTX Neural Faces uses a generative AI model, trained on thousands of images and optimized with TensorRT, to produce more natural-looking faces from rasterized input and 3D pose data.

The Blackwell family includes:

Researchers at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis have identified a secondary heat-production system in brown fat that could help the body burn more calories. While brown fat's heat generation has traditionally been attributed to mitochondria using a molecule called uncoupling protein 1, the new study in mice shows that peroxisomes—cellular structures that process fats—can also produce heat, particularly when mitochondrial heat production is impaired.

The team found that a protein called acyl-CoA oxidase 2 (ACOX2) drives this process. Mice lacking ACOX2 in brown fat had lower cold tolerance, reduced insulin sensitivity, and gained more weight on high-fat diets, while mice engineered to produce extra ACOX2 showed improved heat production, cold tolerance, insulin sensitivity, and weight control.

According to senior author Irfan Lodhi, the relevant fatty acids metabolized by ACOX2 are found in dairy products, breast milk, and are produced by some gut microbes, suggesting potential dietary, probiotic, or drug-based interventions. Prior research has linked higher levels of these fatty acids to lower body mass indices in humans, though further studies are needed to confirm causation.

The S&P 500 Equal Weight Index (EWI), created by Standard & Poor's in January 2003, contains the same 500 companies as the traditional S&P 500 but assigns each stock an equal weight (0.2% at quarterly rebalancing) rather than weighting by market capitalization. As a result, sector weights depend on the number of companies in each sector.

Two ETFs illustrate the difference: Invesco's RSP tracks the EWI, while State Street's SPY tracks the market-weighted index. Although they hold the same companies, RSP requires rebalancing to maintain equal weights and offers more protection when large tech stocks decline.

Historically, the equal-weight index has outperformed the market-weight index, though not in the last decade. A $10,000 investment in RSP in 2004 grew to $60,000 after 18 years, compared to $55,000 for SPY, despite RSP's higher expense ratio (0.2% vs. 0.0945%). Return differentials widen during turbulent periods like 2008 and 2020.

The outperformance is attributed to the small-cap effect: smaller companies tend to grow faster than larger ones, and equal weighting gives them greater influence in the index.

Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) linked to core-collapse supernovae may fail to break out of massive progenitors with hydrogen-rich envelopes, producing "choked" GRBs. Although suppressed in gamma rays, these events are candidates for high-energy neutrino production and may explain the lack of observed neutrino-GRB correlations and the diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux detected by IceCube.

This work investigates jet propagation in Blue and Red Supergiant (BSG/RSG) progenitors using relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) simulations with the PLUTO code. The authors model stellar density profiles, estimate breakout and choking times through 39,000 1D numerical integrations yielding linear scaling relations, and develop a shock-finding algorithm based on convergence, pressure jumps, gradient alignment, and Mach number criteria.

Preliminary results from a BSG simulation (R*=50 R☉, M*=15 M☉, L_jet=10⁵¹ erg/s, Γ₀=7, engine time 5 s) reveal a cocoon, termination shock, and collimation shock during injection. After engine shutdown, the collimation shock disappears while the cocoon shock accelerates down the density gradient, with jet choking occurring within about a minute. Future work will expand the parameter space to predict neutrino and electromagnetic signatures.

This lecture continues a discussion of the massive Sudakov form factor in Soft-Collinear Effective Theory (SCET), focusing on rapidity divergences in SCET_2 that require an additional regulator (nu) beyond dimensional regularization.

Key points covered:

1. **Two-dimensional renormalization group**: Because of dual cutoffs (mu and nu), the renormalization group operates in a two-dimensional space. Both running directions are needed to sum large logarithms. Hard modes depend only on mu, while soft and collinear modes occupy specific points in the mu-nu plane.

2. **Path independence**: Since mu and nu are independent parameters, evolution paths between points yield identical results, expressed through commuting derivatives and relations between anomalous dimensions.

3. **Counter terms and anomalous dimensions**: The lecturer derives z-factors, mu anomalous dimensions, and nu anomalous dimensions, showing how 1/epsilon poles cancel to yield finite results.

4. **Physics examples**: 
   - **gg → Higgs (pt distribution)**: Involves transverse-momentum-dependent PDFs with rapidity divergences
   - **e+e- → dijets (jet broadening)**: Another SCET_2 example
   - **Drell-Yan (pp → l+l-)**: Discussed in four kinematic regimes—q_perp measurement, inclusive, endpoint (tau → 1), and isolated

5. **Drell-Yan factorization theorems**: Each kinematic regime produces a distinct factorization theorem. The isolated case, measuring hemisphere plus-momenta, introduces **beam functions**—matrix elements of chi-bar chi operators measuring both large and small momenta, combining features of jet functions and PDFs.

6. **Beam functions** factorize perturbatively into matching coefficients convolved with standard PDFs and appear generically in processes with specified jet numbers and initial-state radiation.

The lecture reviews decoder design principles, noting that minimum probability of error, maximum a posteriori, and maximum likelihood rules are equivalent under equiprobable signals, and equivalent to minimum distance decoding under AWGN. The union bound estimate is introduced as a practical approximation for error probability.

Effective coding gain (gamma_f) is defined as the gap between a signal set's performance and baseline 2-PAM at a fixed bit error probability (10^-5). It is distinct from nominal coding gain (gamma_c = d_min²/4Eb). A rule of thumb states effective coding gain ≈ nominal coding gain (dB) - 0.2 log2(K_b), where each doubling of nearest neighbors costs 0.2 dB.

Examples show 2-PAM and 4-QAM yield 0 dB effective coding gain, while a 4-point subset of a 3D cube achieves ~1 dB gain. Orthogonal signal sets asymptotically approach the Shannon limit (11.2 dB effective coding gain) as M increases, but suffer from vanishing spectral efficiency and exponential decoding complexity. Simplex signal sets (orthogonal minus mean) and bi-orthogonal signal sets are briefly introduced.

For the bandwidth-limited regime, analogous expressions are derived using SNR_norm, with a similar rule of thumb.

A preview of Chapter 6 introduces binary block codes, where K bits map to N bits then through simple binary signaling (0→α, 1→-α). This coding/modulation separation is near-optimal for power-limited regimes, losing at most 0.2 dB compared to unconstrained signaling.

This study, part of the PSY-COVID project, analyzed predictors of intention to comply with COVID-19 preventive measures among 15,131 Spanish adults during the first wave lockdown (May-June 2020). Using an anonymous online survey, researchers examined sociodemographic, personality, behavioral, cognitive, and social variables across Spanish regions.

Results showed generally high adherence to preventive behaviors and strong trust in scientists, contrasted with low trust in government. The strongest predictors of future compliance were self-efficacy, outcome expectations, general adherence to preventive behaviors, information level, previous experience, perceived vulnerability, and social norms. Adherence to prevent infection and perceived vulnerability of others were moderated by perceived pandemic severity. Region of residence had a minor but significant influence, with Canary Islands residents showing the highest intention and Aragón and Balearic Islands residents the lowest.

Limitations included online-only data collection, non-probabilistic sampling, low Cronbach's alpha for some ad-hoc measures, and exclusive focus on Spain. The authors recommend public health strategies that promote self-efficacy, ensure consistent communication, and address regional disparities to improve compliance with preventive measures in current and future health crises.

Markov cohort-state-transition models (MCSTMs) rely on transition probability matrices (TPMs), which are often difficult to estimate due to data limitations, unequal observation intervals, and missing transitions. Craig and Sendi previously proposed a uniformly weighted expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm to address these issues, but this may increase within state-transition variance and affect probabilistic sensitivity analysis. This paper proposes an optimized, weighted version of the EM algorithm, motivated by best linear unbiased estimator theory, where weights are determined via a computational grid search to minimize variance of a chosen function of the TPM.

The method was demonstrated using a 3-state Markov model comparing a fictitious treatment "SuperDrug" to placebo, using 1-, 2-, and 3-month transition count matrices reflecting missing-at-random reporting. A grid search over the 3-simplex of weights was used to minimize ICER variance across 5,000 bootstrap samples.

Results showed a 15.2% reduction in ICER variance and a 3-percentage-point increase in the probability of cost-effectiveness at £20,000/QALY, with similar ICER means. The authors note the method requires similar data sources to avoid bias, and recommend a stepwise approach including feasibility checks, comparison with the original method, and expert validation. Further research using real-world clinical data is needed.

AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine is an optional extension to the SEV and SNP Firmware ABI that facilitates page migration between memory tiers of differing performance. Tiered memory systems optimize performance by relocating frequently accessed data to faster memory while keeping less-used data in slower memory. TMPM off-loads page migration, supports pages actively targeted by DMA, and can migrate pages owned by SNP-protected Guests. IOMMU enablement is required.

Key commands include PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO (migrates Hypervisor-state or default pages, including those undergoing concurrent DMA) and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST (migrates SNP Guest pages, requiring destination pages in a new Pre-Migration state). Up to 128 pages may be moved per multi-page command via a Page Migration List, with per-page status reporting. PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking individual entries; PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE allows retry.

Performance is best with 128-page commands, consistent queue filling, and limited interrupt requests. Certain structures (IOMMU data, vIOMMU buffers, ring buffers) cannot be migrated. Host software must avoid concurrent modifications to referenced IOMMU host page table entries during TMPM operations.

Blackwell was designed to advance neural shaders as the dominant shader technology, with architectural improvements aimed at boosting their performance and efficiency. Shaders are GPU programs controlling graphics rendering, calculating light, darkness, and color in 3D scenes. Shader technology evolved from non-programmable fixed-function pipelines, limited by GPU hardware, to programmable forms: GeForce 3 introduced vertex shaders, HLSL enabled pixel shading, DX10 added geometry shaders, DX11 added compute shaders, and a DX12 update delivered ray tracing using BVH acceleration structures. Blackwell's launch introduces developer-created neural shaders, some compatible with prior generation GPUs.

Emergency Medical Service (EMS) response times, largely determined by ambulance driving times, are critical for survival chances. The Ambulance Location Problem (ALP), a variant of the Maximum Covering Location Problem (MCLP), has been widely studied but tends to favor densely populated urban areas over rural ones. This paper presents a real-world case study conducted for two German district councils in Rhineland-Palatinate, which needed to relocate 11 obsolete ambulance stations across three study areas.

The authors propose a multi-criteria integer programming model that simultaneously maximizes population reachability within two response time radii (r1 = 5 minutes and r2 = 10 minutes), while ensuring full coverage within the legally mandated r3 = 15 minutes. Unlike prior grid-based studies using Euclidean distance, this approach uses a detailed OpenStreetMap road network with ambulance-specific speed profiles across 29 road classes.

One study area was presented in detail, involving 17 potential sites (4 to be selected), 13 fixed adjacent stations, 20,444 weighted road segments, and over 450,000 inhabitants across 764 km². Using Gurobi and the ε-constraint method, 16 Pareto-optimal solutions were identified.

Results show a clear trade-off: optimizing for 5-minute coverage concentrates stations in urban centers, while optimizing for 10-minute coverage distributes them evenly, including rural areas. The Pareto curve indicates that small losses in one objective can yield significant gains in the other. The identified solutions served as a first stage in decision-making, later refined through discrete event simulation.

The authors conclude that station placement depends on weighting short versus longer response times, and this moral choice rests with decision-makers. Future extensions include incorporating investment costs, multiple coverage by different stations or vehicles, and simultaneous optimization of location and vehicle provision.

A short squeeze occurs when a heavily shorted stock's price rises instead of falling, forcing short sellers to buy back shares at higher prices to cover their positions, which further drives up the price. Unlike price declines capped at zero, price increases have no theoretical limit, making short selling risky.

Short squeezes are rare and typically last 2-4 weeks. Their duration depends on factors like shorted share volume, short interest ratio, daily trading volume, and broker actions. Notable examples include Volkswagen (2008) and GameStop (2021), where the stock rose from $17 to $483 within a month.

In the U.S., short squeezes may be illegal if they involve price manipulation, and naked short selling is prohibited. The opposite of a short squeeze is a long or bear squeeze, where short sellers sell at lower prices to cut losses.

Backtesting short squeeze strategies is impractical due to the lack of precise rules. High short interest does not reliably predict squeezes; in fact, high short interest stocks tend to underperform. Exit strategies involve monitoring price movements and using stop-loss or trailing stop orders.

The lecturer explains that a new problem set (problems 1-7 and 26) will be due October 14th, then transitions to discussing Riemann versus Lebesgue integration. He argues that understanding Lebesgue integration, though mathematical, simplifies work with Fourier series and random processes in communication theory.

Riemann integration quantizes the time axis and approximates function values within intervals, failing for wild functions. Lebesgue integration instead quantizes the function's value axis and measures the set of times where the function falls within each slice, introducing measure theory. Whenever a Riemann integral exists, the Lebesgue integral gives the same value, and familiar integration rules still apply.

Lebesgue defined the measure of an interval [a,b] as b-a, and the measure of a countable union of disjoint intervals as the sum of their measures. Sets coverable by intervals of arbitrarily small total measure have measure zero. Examples include the rationals between 0 and 1 (countable, measure zero) and an uncountable Cantor-like set of ternary expansions without 1's (also measure zero).

A function is measurable if the set of times where it falls within any interval is measurable. For non-negative measurable functions, the Lebesgue integral always exists as either a finite number or infinity. Weird sets of measure zero simply don't contribute to integrals, eliminating issues like discontinuities in Fourier series.

L1 functions have finite integral of their magnitude; L2 functions have finite integral of magnitude squared (energy). Over finite intervals, L2 implies L1. For L2 time-limited functions, Fourier coefficients always exist and are finite, and partial Fourier sums converge to the function in energy (mean-square) sense, denoted l.i.m. Given any square-summable coefficients, a corresponding L2 function exists.

Arbitrary L2 functions can be segmented into intervals of width T and expanded in Fourier series per segment, as done in voice compression (typically 20ms segments). This gives a double orthogonal expansion. Next class will cover the Fourier integral, which freezes time unlike the segmented approach that better matches intuitive notions of changing frequencies.

The VNAU algorithm computes least general generalizations, captures difference information, and is parametrized by a rigidity function controlling granularity. The paper proves termination, soundness, and completeness properties. Code clones are classified into four types (Type-1 through Type-4), ranging from identical fragments to semantically equivalent ones with different syntax.

BG Group PLC agreed to purchase Enron's offshore Indian oil and gas assets for $388 million, including a 30% stake in the Tapti gas field and Panna/Mukta oil and gas fields, plus a 62.64% interest in the CB-OS/1 exploration license. Analysts considered the price, roughly $2.30 per barrel of oil equivalent, a bargain. The deal requires approval from the Indian government and existing partners, including state-owned ONGC, which is seeking operatorship. BG Chief Executive Nigel Shaw stated BG would withdraw if not granted operator status. The acquisition excludes Enron's 65% stake in the troubled Dabhol Power Project, which Enron is separately seeking to exit following a payment dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board. Enron's Dabhol Power Co. also defaulted on a $24 million interest payment to Indian lenders.

In related news, U.S. technology stocks led a major market rally, with the Nasdaq rising 5.93% and the Dow gaining 1.93%. Enron shares rose 9.4% to $33.49. Separately, Southern California Edison reached a settlement with the state Public Utilities Commission to repay over $3 billion in debt by maintaining higher rates through 2003, prompting consumer advocate criticism. Additionally, Army Secretary Thomas White, a former Enron Energy Services vice chairman, was named the Defense Department's top official for homeland security.

The S&P 500 closed July up 2.2% (7.8% YTD), marking the third month above its 10-month moving average, though it fell 1.6% on the first day of August. US large-caps ranked third in monthly returns, trailing Frontier Markets, while global stocks lead year-to-date amid an ongoing global rotation. This archive log from Enron's Steven Kean folder documents discussion threads spanning September 2000 through July 2001, primarily concerning the California energy crisis. A Chino vehicle code violation stop on Feb. 4 led to the arrest of Mark William Ellis, 36, on suspicion of grand theft and vehicle theft, San Bernardino County sheriff's officials announced. Investigators recovered more than $200,000 in stolen items from six storage units in Montclair, with thefts dating back at least 12 years. Ellis allegedly stole from vehicles, homes, businesses and schools across multiple California cities and Las Vegas, taking firearms, electronics, tools and gym equipment. Approximately $63,000 in property has been returned to victims, including several schools and gyms. Authorities confirmed over 50 vehicle burglaries with 40 identified victims. Ellis, who worked cleaning parking lots, has pleaded not guilty and is being held without bail. He returns to court March 21.

Centana Growth Partners, a New York-based limited partnership founded in 2015, has raised $250 million for its first fund to invest in financial services startups. The firm has already invested in four companies, including One and Jumio, and plans to allocate $5 million to $30 million per investment. Founding partner Ben Cukier stated the firm aims to back practical, innovative financial companies, saying they want to invest in "workhorses, not just the unicorns." Centana was founded by Eric Byunn, Steven Swain, and Cukier, with offices in New York and Palo Alto.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, advances GPU capabilities for AI and HPC workloads through enhanced GEMM operations on third-generation Tensor Cores. Each A100 SM contains four redesigned Tensor Cores delivering 1024 FP16 FMA operations per clock, and the full GPU with 108 SMs provides 312 TFLOPS of mixed-precision performance—2.5x that of the V100.

A100 Tensor Cores support expanded data formats including FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary. TF32 enables automatic AI training acceleration without code changes, while FP64 Tensor Cores deliver 2.5x V100's FP64 performance for HPC applications such as iterative refinement solvers.

A100 introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using a 2:4 pattern that doubles Tensor Core throughput with minimal accuracy loss. Other improvements include a combined 192 KB L1/shared memory per SM, 40 GB HBM2 memory at 1555 GB/sec, a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100) with residency controls and compute data compression, and simultaneous FP32/INT32 execution.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions an A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, enabling multi-tenant use cases with guaranteed QoS. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth (12 links), and PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV is supported.

Additional features include hardware JPEG decoding (NVJPG), five NVDEC units, an Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomics, and enhanced error detection. CUDA 11 supports new capabilities including asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, accelerated CUDA Task Graphs, L2 residency controls, and expanded Cooperative Groups. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs via NVSwitch, delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance.

Obamacare has affected nearly all Americans, not only the 20 million enrolled through exchanges or Medicaid expansion. President-elect Trump and congressional Republicans have pledged to repeal it, starting with provisions affecting spending and revenue.

For Medicare's 57 million beneficiaries, repeal would likely raise premiums, deductibles, and cost-sharing, increase Medicare spending by $802 billion over 10 years per CBO estimates, eliminate free preventative screenings, and restore the prescription drug "donut hole." Higher-income enrollees, however, could benefit financially.

For the 150 million workers with employer-sponsored insurance, repeal would end the employer mandate requiring companies with 50+ employees to cover staff working 30+ hours weekly. Free contraceptives and preventative screenings, bans on annual/lifetime benefit limits, and coverage for children up to age 26 (which Trump may retain) could end. Employees at smaller companies could lose protections regarding pre-existing conditions, required benefits, and age-based premium limits.

In the individual market, Obamacare required coverage of pre-existing conditions, banned benefit caps, mandated essential benefits, limited premium variations, and created subsidized exchanges covering 10.4 million people, with 6.9 million more buying individual policies outside exchanges.

Medicaid expansion added nearly 17 million people across 31 states and D.C., with the federal government covering 100% of expansion costs initially, decreasing to 90%. Repeal would leave millions uninsured and eliminate the individual mandate penalty ($695 per adult or 2.5% of income in 2016).

The passage is a transcript from an MIT OpenCourseWare lecture on holographic duality delivered by Hong Liu. The lecture begins with logistical information: there is no textbook, no recitation, and grading is based on five problem sets (75%) and a final project (25%), with no exams.

The academic content introduces holographic duality, noting that while electromagnetic, weak, and strong interactions are understood as gauge theories in fixed spacetime, gravity remains poorly understood at the quantum level. A 1997 proposal established that quantum gravity is equivalent to field theories on a fixed spacetime, representing a form of unification where both sides describe the same quantum system differently.

The lecture discusses the emergence of gravity from non-gravitational systems, referencing Sakharov's 1967 ideas and parallels between Einstein's equations and hydrodynamics. It presents the Weinberg-Witten theorem (1980), which contains two parts: theories with Lorentz-covariant conserved currents cannot have charged massless particles with spin greater than 1/2, and theories with Lorentz-covariant conserved stress tensors cannot have massless particles with spin greater than 1.

The theorem is shown to be compatible with QED, Yang-Mills theory, and general relativity due to specific exceptions. Crucially, the theorem has a hidden assumption that emergent particles live in the same spacetime as the original theory—an assumption that holographic duality circumvents by placing gravity in higher dimensions. The lecture concludes with a detailed proof of the Weinberg-Witten theorem using Lorentz symmetry and rotation operators.

The BioRecall study is a cross-sectional pilot protocol designed to collect comprehensive lifestyle and environmental data from biobank donors and combine it with existing genetic, biological, and clinical data to better understand non-communicable diseases (NCDs). Conducted at the Central Finland Biobank in collaboration with the University of Jyväskylä and the Finnish Biobank Cooperative (FINBB), the pilot will invite 1,386 genotyped donors diagnosed with type 2 diabetes who have consented to recontact.

Participants will complete a 30–40 minute electronic questionnaire via the MyBiobank portal, covering physical activity (using GPAQ with novel strength and balance questions), diet (Healthy Diet Index), anthropometrics, weight loss history, smoking, medical history, sleep, work characteristics, emotional states, and residential environment. Postal code data will be linked to open-source geospatial and socioeconomic datasets. Automated feedback on lifestyle habits is provided to improve engagement and response rates.

The study received ethical approval from the University of Jyväskylä and Central Finland Biobank. Data collection begins February 2025, with potential expansion to other Finnish biobanks. Strengths include its low-cost, scalable electronic design and broad exposome approach. Limitations include a small pilot sample, a single biobank, and the absence of wearable data.

The Supreme Court's second week of its new term produced several notable denials of certiorari. The court declined to review cases involving ineffective appellate counsel in a death-penalty matter, Seventh Amendment incorporation, a school district's alleged concealment of students' transgender identities from parents, and Section 230 immunity, though several justices filed separate opinions expressing concerns.

Nine newly relisted cases fall into three groups:

**Second Amendment and controlled substances:** Following *New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen*, the Fifth and Eighth Circuits held 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(3)—which bars firearm possession by unlawful drug users—unconstitutional as applied. The government seeks review, arguing the law parallels historical restrictions on "habitual drunkards." The petitioner contends no genuine circuit split exists.

**Judicial estoppel in bankruptcy:** In *Keathley v. Buddy Ayers Construction*, the Fifth Circuit barred a personal injury suit because the plaintiff failed to disclose it in his bankruptcy filings. Keathley argues the Fifth and Tenth Circuits' categorical rule conflicts with other circuits' intent-based approach. The author views this case as a serious candidate for review.

**Prisoner petitions:** Four pro se petitions, mostly handwritten, raise procedural and statutory claims, including one questioning whether Elon Musk can be prosecuted for drug transactions on Twitter.

Sony, under CEO Sir Howard Stringer, prepared to launch the PlayStation 3 (PS3) on November 17, 2006, amid intense competition from Microsoft's Xbox 360, released a year earlier with nearly 4 million units sold, and Nintendo's Wii, priced at $249.99, half the PS3's $599 cost. The PS3 also served as a vehicle for Sony's Blu-Ray format, which competed against Toshiba and Microsoft's HD-DVD.

The video game industry, generating $10.5 billion in U.S. revenue in 2005, had evolved significantly since Atari's 1977 console dominance and subsequent 1983 collapse. Nintendo revived the market in the 1980s through strict quality control and licensing, capturing 90% of the U.S. market by 1990. Sony entered in 1994 with the 3D PlayStation using CD format, achieving 60% U.S. market share by 1999. The PS2, launched in 2000 with DVD capability, held 55% market share by 2006.

Consoles were typically sold at a loss, with profits derived from software royalties of $5-$7 per unit. The industry shifted toward independent developers and publishers, with consolidation accelerating as publishers acquired studios to control talent and intellectual property.

The Xbox 360 launch marked the first console generation centered on Internet connectivity, with Microsoft's Xbox Live offering unified online experiences and new revenue streams. Sony's PlayStation Network and Nintendo's Virtual Console followed different approaches. While Sony and Microsoft targeted core male gamers, Nintendo pursued broader audiences with intuitive controls.

The industry also faced public concerns about violence, leading to the ESRB rating system, though critics questioned its accuracy. Legislative attempts to restrict violent game sales were largely struck down as First Amendment violations. Industry analysts projected the PS3 would capture over 50% of next-generation console market share through 2010.

The Chicago Cubs defeated the Pittsburgh Pirates 7-0, but the game was overshadowed by a controversial slide by Anthony Rizzo into catcher Elias Diaz during the eighth inning. Rizzo's slide, which took out Diaz's legs after a force out at home, caused a wild throw allowing two runs to score. Rizzo and Cubs manager Joe Maddon defended the slide as legal, while Diaz and Pirates manager Clint Hurdle, who was ejected after arguing the upheld call, disagreed. Diaz remained in the game.

Spot starter Mike Montgomery, filling in for injured Yu Darvish, retired the first 13 batters and allowed only two singles over 5 2/3 innings. Rizzo hit a solo home run in the first, and Addison Russell added a pinch-hit two-run homer in the seventh. The Pirates fell to 2-8 in their last 10 games. Cubs' Jon Lester and Pirates' Nick Kingham are scheduled to pitch next.

The MSPM0C1105/C1106 microcontroller integrates multiple subsystems. The Power Management Unit (PMU) regulates core supplies, provides a bandgap reference, brown-out reset monitoring, and parity-protected trim. The Clock Module (CKM) includes LFOSC, SYSOSC, LFXT, and HFXT oscillators, distributing clocks such as MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, MFCLK, LFCLK, ADCCLK, CLK_OUT, HFCLK, and HSCLK across operating modes.

The DMA_B controller supports two full-feature channels and one basic channel with triggers from ADC, UART, SPI, and timers, enabling transfers up to 64k of various data sizes. The event manager routes events between peripherals, DMA, and CPU.

Memory includes flash with 1KB sector sizes (up to 100,000 cycles on first 32KB) and zero-wait-state SRAM retained across low-power modes. Peripherals include up to 45 GPIOs, IOMUX, a 12-bit 1.6-Msps ADC, temperature sensor, VREF (1.4V/2.5V), comparator, CRC-16, UART, I2C (up to 1Mbps), SPI (up to 16Mbit/s), IWDT, WWDT, RTC_B, and general-purpose and advanced timers (TIMx).

Debugging is provided via the Arm SWD interface and DEBUGSS subsystem. Factory constants store device identification and trim data. Typical applications require decoupling capacitors, NRST pullup/pulldown, and crystal bypass capacitors. The September 2025 revision removed the DGS32 package and updated multiple specifications.

DNA origami is a method that uses base-pairing between DNA strands to self-assemble complex nanostructures, with applications including functional nanomachines. A team led by Ralf Jungmann at LMU Munich has reported, in Nature Communications, a super-resolution microscopy technique called DNA-PAINT that can individually visualize all strands within these nanostructures.

In DNA origami, a long "scaffold" strand is folded by shorter "staple" strands into predefined shapes, such as a flat rectangle. DNA-PAINT uses short dye-linked "imager" strands that bind transiently to complementary sites, producing a blinking signal. By analyzing these signals, researchers can precisely determine strand positions and assess assembly quality.

The study found that assembly is robust across varied physical conditions, but strand incorporation efficiency depends on the target sequence's position within the structure. Not all available sites are occupied in every nanoparticle, even when using excess staple strands. The authors recommend adding components in large excess and selecting modification positions based on their incorporation-efficiency mapping. They also suggest DNA-PAINT has potential in quantitative structural biology for measuring labelling efficiencies of antibodies, proteins, and nucleic acids.

This paper studies modal extensions of lattice-based semantics, examining how modal sentences can characterize algebraic properties of lattices. Building on Kripke semantics, the authors consider alternatives to the two-valued Boolean algebra, such as Łukasiewicz, Belnap, and n-valued Boolean algebras, where lattices interpret conjunction and disjunction while their order structure naturally supports the necessity operator as the greatest lower bound of values in accessible worlds.

After introducing lattice semantics and defining regular modal extensions (where necessity means truth in all accessible worlds, NAW), the authors prove that a normal modal valuation yields a unique regular modal extension if and only if the set of designated values F is a filter containing its own meet. For finite lattices, this reduces to F being a filter; for infinite lattices, NAW may fail, as shown with fuzzy and classical logic examples involving non-principal ultrafilters.

The paper then characterizes lattice properties via modal formulas. Key results include: (1) F is implicative if and only if every frame satisfies (□φ ∨ □ψ) → □(φ ∨ ψ); (2) under strictly deductive implication, a lattice is linear outside the filter if and only if axiom K holds on every frame; (3) under regular implication (a ⊃ b = −a + b) with anti-monotone, involutive, down-distributive lattices, implicativeness corresponds to K's validity.

An example using twist algebras derived from Boolean algebras illustrates these results, recovering the filter used by Carnielli and Coniglio for paraconsistent semantics.

The authors conclude by noting the relevance of shared order relations for cross-logical communication between worlds and express interest in investigating finite-model properties for computational applications.

Gaussian Process Dynamic Mode Decomposition combines transfer operator theory with reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces to model noisy, nonlinear dynamical systems. Dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) discretizes the Koopman operator via eigenvalue decomposition of a linear regression model, while Gaussian process (GP) regression offers non-parametric, probabilistic function approximation. The authors develop a Bayesian interpretation of the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator, extending Extended DMD (EDMD) to construct models from noisy data with uncertainty estimates for multi-step predictions. Their approach applies the variational free energy method to kernel Koopman operators, addressing EDMD's limitations regarding hyperparameter optimization, sparse dictionary learning, measurement noise, and computational complexity.

The team performed well, with linemates Ron Francis and Sami Kapanen having exceptional games and strong goaltending from Arturs. Bob Jones, a serial entrepreneur and MIT Sloan graduate, delivered a lecture on identifying customers as the foundation of a successful business. He argued that the only non-negotiable requirement for business success is having customers, and that entrepreneurs must determine who will actually pay for a product, what problem it solves, and how to reach those buyers.

Jones illustrated his points with two contrasting product launches. The first, Regain, was a nutrition bar for dialysis patients. Despite positive feedback from clinicians, the launch failed because he surveyed the wrong audience—patients themselves could not afford the product, did not like its taste, and retail pharmacies demanded costly slotting fees.

The second venture, NiteBite, targeted people with diabetes at risk of nighttime hypoglycemia. By consulting patients and parents directly, Jones learned they wanted a discreet, non-medical product. The company marketed it as "peace of mind," built demand through Certified Diabetes Educators and direct consumer outreach, and leveraged that demand to enter retailers and wholesalers without paying slotting fees. The business was eventually sold to a large pharmaceutical firm.

Key lessons included: correctly identifying the paying customer, selling benefits rather than features, segmenting markets by motivation, focusing on those experiencing the most pain, and building minimum viable products to test demand before scaling. Jones emphasized talking directly with customers rather than relying solely on surveys or emails.

The American Indian College Fund announced a two-year study, funded by a $600,000 grant from Strada Education Network, to assess the economic and social impact of five tribal colleges and universities (TCUs) in North Dakota. Researchers developed a machine learning interatomic potential for YBa2Cu3O7−x (YBCO) based on the Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) method, trained on density functional theory (DFT) data that included defect configurations of all species. The potential was designed to overcome limitations of previous classical potentials, particularly the Buckingham+Coulomb (B+C) potential of Gray et al., which fails to reproduce the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal structural transition in YBCO.

The training dataset comprised 1368 configurations, including defect-free structures, vacancies, interstitials, amorphous-like configurations, oxygen Frenkel pairs (FPs), and approximate transition-state geometries. The ACE potential achieved RMSEs of approximately 10 meV/atom for energies and 70 meV/Å for forces.

Validation showed the ACE potential accurately reproduces the DFT equation of state, lattice parameters across a wide volume range, and oxygen FP migration barriers within 20 meV of DFT values, significantly outperforming the B+C potential.

NPT molecular dynamics simulations with approximately 25,000 atoms reproduced the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition at around 800 K, compared to the experimental value of approximately 1000 K. The transition was identified as an order-disorder process driven by oxygen migration from O1 and O4 sites to O5 interstitial sites in the basal plane. Analysis indicates the transition is entropy-driven, facilitated by decreasing FP formation energy at thermally expanded lattices. The discrepancy with experimental transition temperature is attributed partly to oxygen degassing in experiments, which is not captured in the fixed-composition simulations.

This non-empirical research investigates the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on inclusive education through a literature review, addressing a gap in studies explicitly examining this relationship.

The literature review establishes that inclusive education upholds equity and accommodates all students regardless of background, ability, or disability. Barriers to inclusion include inadequate educator training, overcrowded classrooms, insufficient infrastructure, poor communication among stakeholders, and student labeling. AI, defined as problem-solving through STEM-integrated technologies, is increasingly used in education and supports inclusion by enhancing teaching, learning, and non-teaching functions.

AI benefits include assistive features (text-to-speech, grammar checkers), personalized learning, immediate feedback, raised awareness of diversity, automation of administrative tasks, and continuous student evaluation. However, AI cannot replace human educators due to its lack of consciousness and emotional understanding.

Methodology followed PRISMA guidelines, searching Web of Science, Science Direct, and IEEE Xplore from September 2023 to March 2024.

Limitations of AI include potential data bias, job loss risks, high costs, over-reliance on technology, privacy concerns, and diminished human interaction. Physical harm from prolonged use and the need for pre-training were also noted.

The discussion recommends an inclusive syllabus featuring screen-reader capabilities, assistive technologies, and Universal Design for Learning approaches. Tools like Calendly, text-to-speech software, and shared documents support diverse learners.

Study limitations include reliance on literature rather than empirical data and exclusion of minority-specific analysis. The conclusion affirms that AI supports inclusive education, with recommendations for educators and policymakers to integrate AI, promote child-centered learning, provide professional development, and foster awareness of inclusion.

The lecture compares ion traps to neutral atom traps, noting that ions experience much stronger confinement via Coulomb forces (up to 10,000 K trap depths) compared to neutral atoms (microkelvin to kelvin range). Both systems are used for clocks, quantum information, and quantum simulation, though ions have historically dominated quantum computing applications.

Ions cannot be confined in stationary electric traps due to the divergence of the electric field being zero, requiring dynamic trapping. Two main approaches exist: Penning traps (using electric fields plus a magnetic field to create cyclotron motion) and RF/Paul traps (which alternate between confining and anti-confining potentials). The Paul trap works analogously to combining convex and concave lenses separated in space, producing net focusing. The trapping force arises from rectification: micromotion at the drive frequency combines with the oscillating force to produce a time-averaged attractive force (via a cosine-squared term).

The lecture then explains the Cirac-Zoller quantum gate for two-ion quantum computation. Single qubit operations use Rabi oscillations, while two-qubit gates require a mechanism for ions to interact. The Cirac-Zoller scheme uses the ions' common center-of-mass vibrational motion as a "data bus." The procedure involves: (1) cooling the center-of-mass motion to its ground state, (2) swapping qubit information from one ion into the phonon state via a sideband pi pulse, (3) performing a controlled phase gate on the second ion using an auxiliary state (where a 2π Rabi oscillation produces a -1 phase shift), and (4) swapping the phonon information back into the first ion.

Limitations of this gate include the requirement for ground-state cooling and slow gate speeds limited by the center-of-mass vibrational frequency. Alternative gates (geometric, Sorensen) avoid these issues, but the Cirac-Zoller gate remains pedagogically important.

On May 29, 2018, following the arrest of two Black men at a Philadelphia Starbucks, The Black Star Project is organizing "National Eat at a Black Coffee Shop Day." The event coincides with Starbucks closing over 8,000 U.S. stores for diversity training. More than 400 Black-owned coffee houses are expected to participate, aiming to gain market share and promote economic development. Chairman Phillip Jackson stated the initiative is part of a broader "Circulate Black Dollars in the Black Community" campaign, seeking to increase Black consumer spending within Black communities from 2 percent to 10 percent. Some shops will also host evening "Black Economic Empowerment Forums."

Cadillac sold 35,020 units globally in September 2017, marking 16 consecutive months of growth. Year-to-date sales reached 256,613 units, up 44,336 from 2016. U.S. sales rose 1.1 percent year-over-year, while China sales grew 37.6 percent. The XT5 leads brand sales with 103,645 units delivered worldwide in 2017. President Johan de Nysschen attributed growth to attracting younger buyers and new technologies like Super Cruise on the 2018 CT6. The brand's average U.S. transaction price remained around $54,000.

On November 29, 2016, NVIDIA Corporation's Board of Directors amended and restated the company's Bylaws to implement proxy access and modify advance notice provisions for stockholder proposals and director nominations. Under the new Section 5(h), a stockholder or group of up to 20 stockholders holding at least 3% of NVIDIA's voting stock continuously for three years may include director nominees in the annual meeting proxy materials, up to the greater of two directors or 20% of the Board. Beginning with the 2018 annual meeting, stockholders nominating directors outside of proxy access must provide written notice 90 to 120 days before the anniversary of the previous year's annual meeting, shortened from the former 120-to-150-day window. Adjusted timing applies if the meeting date shifts by more than 30 days. The Restated Bylaws took effect immediately upon adoption.

This study investigated race differences in the relationship between blood pressure (BP) and longitudinal cognitive performance in older Black and White adults. Data were drawn from 2,284 participants across three harmonized cohort studies (MARS, MAP, and Black Clinical Core), who were categorized into six groups based on race and BP status (normal, high, or variable). Participants completed annual cognitive assessments across five domains: episodic memory, semantic memory, working memory, processing speed, and visuospatial ability.

Linear mixed effects models revealed no racial differences in cognitive decline among individuals with normal BP. However, White adults with high BP declined faster than Black adults with high BP in global cognition, perceptual speed, semantic memory, and working memory. White adults with variable BP exhibited significantly faster decline than Black adults with variable BP across all cognitive domains.

The authors suggest these disparities may relate to autonomic nervous system functioning and allostatic load, proposing that greater lifetime exposure to stressors in Black individuals may reduce the cognitive impact of stress-induced physiological changes like elevated BP. Limitations include not accounting for medication adherence or comprehensive medication history. The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions addressing racial disparities in cognitive health related to BP.

AMD shares rose over 20% in premarket trading following the announcement of a multiyear AI chip supply agreement with OpenAI. Under the deal, AMD will provide high-performance AI accelerators, beginning with its MI450 series, while OpenAI will receive warrants for up to 10% of AMD's equity upon meeting certain milestones. The partnership positions AMD as a competitor to Nvidia in the AI chip market and could generate tens of billions in revenue. The agreement coincides with AMD's $6 billion share buyback plan. Analysts caution that execution risks, supply chain challenges, and sustained demand will determine whether AMD can meet heightened expectations.

Judges are fining attorneys for submitting legal briefs containing faulty case citations likely generated by AI. In Puerto Rico, Chief U.S. District Judge Raúl Arias-Marxuach ordered solo practitioners Ibrahim Reyes and Jose R. Olmo-Rodriguez to pay $24,492 in legal fees to firms including Paul, Weiss and Sidley Austin after their motions contained at least 55 defective citations. The lawyers denied using AI, but the judge found the volume of errors suggested otherwise. The firms had initially requested nearly $88,000.

In California, attorney Amir Mostafavi was sanctioned $10,000 for including AI-generated fake quotes and irrelevant cases in appellate briefs. The Second Appellate District directed the payment to the court rather than opposing counsel, who failed to detect the errors. Mostafavi stated that lawyers cannot realistically stop using AI but must exercise caution while the technology still produces inaccurate information.

Following the death of President Franklin Delano Roosevelt, the speaker addresses Congress, acknowledging the loss while emphasizing the need to continue forward. He affirms America's commitment to the war effort, demanding unconditional surrender from Germany and Japan, and pledges to punish war criminals.

The speaker states that lasting peace requires law, justice, and international cooperation rather than geographical barriers. He confirms that military strategy will continue unchanged under current commanders and that the San Francisco Conference will proceed as planned.

He argues that hope alone cannot prevent war; peace-loving nations must unite and be willing to defend one another. While great powers bear special responsibility for enforcing peace, their role is to serve rather than dominate. He appeals for bipartisan support in building a United Nations Organization.

The speaker emphasizes that America's leadership extends beyond military power to include trade and cooperation with other nations for mutual benefit. He closes with a prayer from King Solomon, asking for wisdom to serve the people faithfully.

Several manufacturers have discontinued manual transmission options in South Africa. Audi scrapped the manual A4 1,4T FSI, making the range entirely dual-clutch. BMW removed manual versions of the 120i, M140i, 220i, 230i and M240i, while retaining manuals for the 118i, 120d, 220d and M2. Volkswagen ended manual versions of the Polo GTI, Scirocco 2,0TSI Highline and Jetta 1,6TDI Comfortline. Volvo discontinued the manual S60 T3 Kinetic. Manufacturers cite low demand as the reason. The cast of Stranger Things is reportedly receiving significant pay raises ahead of the third season, according to The Hollywood Reporter. Series regulars have been divided into three salary tiers: adult stars Winona Ryder and David Harbour will earn $350,000 per episode; younger actors Finn Wolfhard, Gaten Matarazzo, Caleb McLaughlin, and Noah Schnapp will receive $250,000; and teenage cast members Natalia Dyer, Joe Keery, and Charlie Heaton will get $150,000. Contracting parties acknowledged the potential need for development work to increase Congo product supplies, with Belgium agreeing to facilitate such activity. Day reported that a complete commodities list for negotiations on Belgian Congo civilian requirements would be forwarded by August 10, with full survey requiring six additional weeks.

The Secretary of State instructed Ambassador Winant to inform the Belgian Government that the Combined Raw Materials Board and Combined Production and Resources Board in Washington would allocate Congo supplies, requesting that data be sent simultaneously to the Foreign Office and the Department of State. Hull also suggested considering a provision preventing increases in Congo export duties during the agreement's term, following recent increases on palm nuts and geranium oil. The Department accepted postponement of the tripartite Belgian agreement signing, with retroactive application to the prior Anglo-Belgian agreement's expiration.

Negotiations continued through 1942–1943 without agreement and were discontinued by mutual consent. An Office of Economic Warfare mission visited the Congo in 1943, and an informal Tripartite Supply Committee was established.

Dr Chris Bradley of the University of Birmingham has supported Birmingham City Council's view that drainage was not responsible for recent flooding in the city, attributing it instead to the extreme volume of rainfall. The council stated drains are checked periodically, with extra attention during weather warnings, and noted some areas received a month's rainfall in an hour. A yellow weather warning has been issued for Birmingham and the West Midlands for Thursday, with the Met Office predicting thunderstorms, potential torrential rain of 30-40mm per hour, frequent lightning and large hail.

The article presents an ETF momentum rotation strategy using monthly data for SPY (S&P 500), TLT (20-year Treasury bonds), and EEM (MSCI Emerging Markets). These ETFs were selected for their importance, low correlation, and safe-haven qualities, respectively. The strategy ranks the three ETFs by the previous month's performance and holds the best performer for one month before repeating.

Backtested over two decades without slippage or taxes, the strategy outperformed buy-and-hold with lower drawdowns until 2022. CAGR since inception is 11%, but while maximum drawdown was 22% before 2022, the portfolio dropped 41% from its peak that year. The strategy is best suited for tax-deferred accounts due to frequent rotation and has underperformed in the last 5-6 years.

Charlie Javice, founder of the fintech startup Frank, was sentenced to seven years in prison for defrauding JPMorgan Chase, which acquired her company in 2021 for $175 million. A jury found Javice and chief growth officer Olivier Amar guilty on three counts of fraud and one count of conspiracy. Prosecutors had sought 12 years. Javice expressed remorse in court, while Judge Alvin Hellerstein cited the need for deterrence. She was also ordered to pay $22.36 million in forfeiture and $287 million in restitution, and will remain on bail pending appeal. Though Frank claimed over five million student customers, it had fewer than 300,000 real users, with the rest being synthetic identities. Javice had directed employees to fabricate users before the acquisition. JPMorgan failed to verify the customer base before purchasing the company.

The Forties Pipeline System in the North Sea, operated by Ineos, has been shut down due to a widening hairline crack, with repairs potentially taking weeks. The 450,000-bpd pipeline carries nearly 40 percent of the UK's North Sea oil production and connects 85 offshore oil fields to the mainland, with more than 80 platforms expected to shut down as a result. The outage caused Brent crude prices to spike nearly 2 percent, surpassing $64.50 per barrel—a two-year high. Analysts note the closure is significant because the Forties system underpins the Brent benchmark, which influences global prices. A three-week shutdown could disrupt up to 10 million barrels of supply, tightening the Atlantic Basin market. The outage has also widened the Brent-WTI price gap to nearly $7 per barrel, which could boost U.S. crude exports and accelerate inventory drawdowns. The situation parallels the recent Keystone pipeline spill, though the Forties outage may have broader global implications.

At the Scripps National Spelling Bee, 113 spellers are returning for at least a second time, including Erin Howard, 13, Cameron Keith, 12, and Naysa Modi, 12, all of whom advanced to the final round. After misspelling "Klydonograph" last year, Erin now studies three to four hours on weeknights and up to eight hours on weekends, sacrificing social events. In Wiechmann v Wiechmann, the Michigan Court of Appeals affirmed a trial court's divorce judgment that split physical custody of four children between the parents, with the father receiving custody of the two older children and the mother receiving custody of the two younger twin boys. The parties shared legal custody.

The defendant mother appealed, arguing the trial court abused its discretion by not granting her custody of all four children and keeping the siblings together. The custody specialist had recommended all four children be placed with the defendant.

The Court of Appeals held that while maintaining sibling bonds is an important consideration under the best interest factors of MCL 722.23; MSA 25.312(3), the best interests of each individual child ultimately control custody decisions. Although keeping siblings together is typically preferable, it may be overridden when contrary to an individual child's best interests. The court found the trial court properly reviewed the statutory factors, found the parties essentially equal except for factor (d) which slightly favored the plaintiff, and did not palpably abuse its discretion or commit legal error in separating the children.

Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) is an AMD firmware feature enabling non-persistent, runtime updates to firmware and settings without requiring BIOS reflash or system reset. SFS addresses high-priority runtime issues affecting AMD-provided binary firmware components in AGESA releases, but does not patch x86 code such as SMM, AGESA, UEFI, or run-once code like ABL. Updates do not persist across reboots and serve as interim fixes between BIOS releases.

Successfully applying an SFS package can change three version numbers: the SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), individual firmware/Security Patch Levels (SPL), and the System Patch Level (SYSPL) for run-once code. All version numbers increase monotonically to prevent rollback.

AMD cryptographically signs all SFS packages, and customers may optionally co-sign them using RSA 2048-bit or 4096-bit keys provided during early boot. The AMD Security Processor (ASP) serves as the root of trust for detection, while OEMs/ODMs remain the root of trust for update. BIOS developers enable SFS via APCB tokens; both SFS and co-signing are off by default.

SFS commands are issued through the TEE mailbox interface with specific memory alignment requirements. A customer-provided SFS Deployment Agent handles communication with the ASP via the PSP/ASP driver. The ASP verifies signatures, executes the patch, and updates patch level information.

In multi-socket systems, the first socket's ASP receives the patch and coordinates application. Multiple updates must be applied sequentially. Updates run in parallel with x86/DMA traffic with minimal performance impact, though SEV/SEV-ES virtual machines must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates (SEV/SNP VMs can continue).

Package names follow the format fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg.

The Covid-19 pandemic necessitated a shift to distance education worldwide, highlighting the need for alternative educational methods. This literature review explores artificial intelligence (AI) as a tool in distance education. AI systems, enabled by machine learning and deep learning, can perform complex tasks and are increasingly used in education through Intelligent Education Systems (IES), which include domain, pedagogy, and learner models.

Three AI-based education types are proposed: AI-supported face-to-face education, face-to-face education delivered by AI, and simulation-based education with AI. These can operate through supervised algorithms or unsupervised deep learning. Simulation education may use intermediary tools like VR devices or, potentially, direct neural integration such as Neural Link technology.

Potential benefits include efficiency, cost reduction, personalized learning, elimination of classroom discipline issues, and access to immersive experiences. However, concerns include privacy risks, cyber-attacks, social isolation, teacher unemployment, psychological effects, adaptation difficulties, and fears of AI controlling humans.

The authors conclude that while computers have not reached human mental capacity, rapid advancements suggest AI will play a growing role in education, warranting serious philosophical and practical discussion.

The Seattle Mariners defeated the Texas Rangers 2-1 on May 28, 2018, marking their ninth win in ten games and 16th one-run victory of the season, the most in the majors. Starter Marco Gonzales pitched 6 2/3 innings without allowing an earned run, extending his streak to 19 1/3 innings. FCA data from its 2017 Financial Lives Survey reveals that up to 70 per cent of customers planning to access their defined contribution pensions within two years have not been asked by providers how they intend to do so. Only 20 per cent said all their providers had contacted them about options, while 2 per cent said some had. Sixty-seven per cent had not received advice from an adviser at their pension provider. Among those not taking advice, 40 per cent felt capable of deciding alone and 10 per cent cited cost. When asked about their largest expected retirement income source, 33 per cent named the state pension, 21 per cent their DC pot, and 15 per cent a final salary scheme. On anticipated annual retirement income, 44 per cent had a good idea, 28 per cent had little or none, and 17 per cent did not know.

El neuromarketing, definido como la aplicación de técnicas de neuroimagen para comprender la conducta del consumidor, se ha incorporado al sector audiovisual desde los años noventa. Empresas como Viacom, Cartoon Network y ESPN ya lo utilizan para testar contenidos, promociones y bloques publicitarios.

En España, esta disciplina es emergente. Una investigación basada en 18 entrevistas a consultoras, representantes del sector audiovisual, neurocientíficos y académicos permitió contrastar seis hipótesis, confirmándose todas ellas.

Los principales resultados indican:
- La investigación neurocientífica del consumidor audiovisual es viable, aunque presenta limitaciones éticas, interpretativas y muestrales.
- Se requieren equipos multidisciplinares (neurocientíficos, expertos en marketing, ingenieros biomédicos), sin existir un profesional integral.
- La introducción es incipiente por desconocimiento, desconfianza, mala praxis, falta de innovación y precio.
- Las consultoras dedican en promedio un 33% de su trabajo al sector audiovisual, con crecimiento exponencial reciente.
- Atresmedia y Mediaset España son los principales clientes, usando estas técnicas para testar contenidos de ficción y bloques publicitarios. TVE abandonó su línea por motivos económicos.
- Las productoras cinematográficas muestran interés pero carecen de recursos para invertir.

Se prevé una evolución favorable, condicionada al desarrollo tecnológico, mejor interpretación de datos, abaratamiento y demostración del retorno de inversión.

Research suggests that improving air quality in schools through air filters and better ventilation can significantly enhance student outcomes at low cost. A study by economist Michael Gilraine following the 2015 Aliso Canyon gas leak found that schools receiving air purifiers saw math and English test scores rise by roughly three months of learning—gains comparable to those from major class-size reductions, but at a fraction of the cost (about $30 per student versus $7,000).

Additional studies link air purifiers to reduced absenteeism, fewer illnesses, and improved test scores. Benefits are attributed to three factors: direct cognitive improvements from reduced particulate inhalation, better health and attendance, and mitigation of inequities, since low-income students often attend schools with worse air quality.

Implementation requires minimal administrative effort compared to other interventions. The author recommends schools reactivate existing devices, pilot and expand programs, and aim for specific Clean Air Delivery Rates. Philanthropists, advocates, and researchers are encouraged to support funding, standards, and further trials.
