Research published in Nature Climate Change identifies multiple Australian ecosystems undergoing sudden, catastrophic shifts due to the combined stress of gradual climate change ("presses") and extreme weather events ("pulses"). Australia's average temperature has risen about 1°C since the 19th century, bringing longer heatwaves, extended fire seasons, altered rainfall, and severe droughts, with shorter intervals between events.

Six case studies of ecosystem collapse include kelp forests shifting to seaweed turfs, Gondwanan refugia destroyed by wildfire, Murray River floodplain forest dieback, alpine forest converting to shrubland, arid zone boom-bust cycles, and mangrove dieback in the Gulf of Carpentaria. Most affected areas had little prior human disturbance, indicating undisturbed systems are not inherently more resilient.

Collapses affect fisheries, forests, carbon storage, tourism, and water supply. Targeted interventions such as reseeding and assisted recolonisation are costly and become less likely to succeed as extreme events grow more frequent. The authors suggest inaction risks may increasingly outweigh intervention risks.

This retrospective cohort study used the All of Us Research Program dataset (v7) to develop machine learning models predicting healthy aging from social determinants of health (SDOH) in adults aged 50 and older. Healthy aging was defined by a composite score based on comorbidities (modified Charlson Comorbidity Index), cognitive conditions, and mobility function. Three algorithms—logistic regression, multi-layer perceptron, and XGBoost—were trained, with a primary cohort of 99,935 participants (44.1% classified as healthy aging) and a secondary cohort of 62,475 (10.6% healthy aging) using a stricter age threshold.

XGBoost with random oversampling performed best (AUROC: 0.793), outperforming the other models, and demonstrated predictive parity across race and sex groups. SHAP analysis identified health insurance type as the strongest predictor, followed by employment status, substance use, and health insurance coverage. Top predictors aligned with prior socioeconomic findings, though substance and alcohol use showed unexpected positive associations with healthy aging, possibly due to selection bias, the Hawthorne effect, or age-related overdose patterns.

Limitations include the lack of a universal healthy aging definition, potential selection bias from volunteer participants, and unmeasured confounders such as early-life exposures. The authors conclude that health insurance access plays a pivotal role in healthy aging and should be integrated into public health strategies.

This study simulates the transition from internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles to Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs) using one year of telematics data from UnipolTech, covering 10,441 users and over 10 million trips in Asti, Italy. The authors replicated each user's trips across four BEV models (Fiat 500e, Renault Megane E-Tech, Tesla Model 3, Audi A6 e-tron) and four charging scenarios: workplace daytime AC charging, low-SoC AC charging, overnight AC charging, and low-SoC fast DC charging.

Unlike prior research, this work applies vehicle- and road-type-specific energy profiles, updates state-of-charge per trip, and accounts for seasonal and spatial variations. The authors measured feasible trip percentages, monthly charging sessions, and average post-trip SoC.

Results show Scenario 1 (workplace charging) performs worst, while Scenario 4 (fast DC) performs best, enabling 72% of users to complete 100% of trips with the Audi A6 e-tron. Scenario 3 (overnight) yields the highest post-trip SoC (above 70%). Scenarios 2 and 4 require roughly half the charging sessions of Scenario 3. At least 35% of users could adopt BEVs with overnight charging and a Fiat 500e, but 5% remain unserved even under optimal conditions.

Limitations include assumptions of constant consumption and charging power, universal charger availability, and exclusion of cost analysis.

Former Maui County Councilmember Mike Victorino, who plans to run for Maui County mayor in 2018, was confirmed as the driver in an April 13 collision that struck two pedestrians, aged 18 and 15, on West Papa Avenue around 9:30pm. According to police and Victorino's wife Joycelyn, alcohol and speeding were not factors, with the vehicle traveling no faster than 25 mph. Victorino stopped and waited for authorities, and both young men sustained nonlife-threatening injuries. Police stated the pedestrians were not in a crosswalk, though the mother of the older victim said her son reported they were.

Linebackers require toughness, athleticism, and intelligence to play their position, which involves organizing the defense, stopping the run, and defending against the pass. Positioned 3-5 yards behind the defensive line, they often relay coaching calls and serve as the "Quarterback of the defense." The name derives from their alignment behind the defensive line. Individual linebacker positions include Sam, Mike, Will, and Jack. Key skills include vision, agility, tackling, and block shedding, with typical heights of 5'10"-6'5" and weights of 215-255 pounds.

Notable linebackers include Ray Lewis, Chuck Bednarik, and Lawrence Taylor, all Pro Football Hall of Fame inductees with multiple championships and accolades. While the value of inside linebackers has declined due to offenses shifting toward passing attacks, 3-6 linebackers are still typically drafted in the first round. Versatile linebackers capable of rushing the passer, covering man-to-man, and playing zone remain valuable for creating mismatches and disrupting offenses at any level of football.

The Canadian dollar is caught between the Bank of Canada, which favours a low loonie to aid exporters, and markets pushing it higher based on economic strength. The loonie reached nearly 75.50 U.S. cents Wednesday, up 2 per cent from the previous week, after hitting a year-to-date low of 72.73 cents on May 4. According to CIBC economist Andrew Grantham, the loonie's movements reflect oil prices and the Canada-U.S. interest rate gap, both of which have pressured it downward. Oil fell below US$45, and the U.S. Federal Reserve raised its rate to 1.0-1.25 per cent, while Canada's remains at 0.5 per cent. However, strong economic data, including 3.7 per cent first-quarter growth, and recent signals from Bank of Canada officials have led CIBC to forecast a Canadian rate hike in the fourth quarter, earlier than its previous 2018 expectation.

The Colorado State University Board of Governors received feedback on the first two games at the new on-campus stadium. ASCSU President Josh Silva noted challenges with student awareness of the tailgating lot, as many students used it only for parking. ASCSU plans rebranding and pre-game programming to boost engagement. Athletics Director Joe Parker reported 37,583 attendees at the first game and 27,038 at the second, with queuing and concession issues improving by the second game. Roughly 50 vehicles were towed from gameday lots each weekend, with a similar number towed from surrounding neighborhoods. Alternative transportation exceeded expectations, with 7,000 patrons using gameday transit versus a predicted 5,000, and post-game traffic flowed smoothly, aided by the MAX system.

This study investigated whether role-taking and literacy-based interventions could reduce the influence of demographic and appearance-based cues (age, gender, ethnicity, attire) on trust and risk-taking in social engineering contexts. Using a 4×2 mixed factorial online experiment, 139 Arab participants were assigned to one of four groups: Persuader, Persuadee, Literacy, or Control. Participants evaluated 16 personas before and one week after the intervention, rating trust and willingness to accept a stranger's mobile hotspot offer.

Repeated Measures ANOVAs revealed no significant changes in trust or risk-taking across persona factors or roles, with Bayes Factors supporting the null hypothesis. A significant effect was only observed for Issue of Involvement, which decreased post-intervention. Qualitative feedback indicated participants found the intervention engaging and reflective, though behavioral change was limited.

The authors conclude that short-term interventions may raise awareness but are insufficient to alter deeply ingrained cognitive biases and heuristics. Limitations include reliance on imagined scenarios, static comic-based simulations, and potential overconfidence from increased awareness. Future research should explore longer-term, immersive approaches such as gamified or virtual reality methods.

District and Sessions Judge Nasir Khan Yousafzai in Zhob sentenced four convicts in separate murder cases. Brothers Ajab Khan and Fateh Khan were each given 25 years' imprisonment and fined Rs. 200,000. Dilbar Khan was also sentenced to 25 years' imprisonment and fined Rs. 105,000. Allen Iverson, discussing his new memoir "Misunderstood" on ESPN's "First Take," told Stephen A. Smith that the lowest point of his life was his 2013 divorce from Tawanna Turner, which coincided with his retirement from the NBA. Iverson said seeing "Iverson vs. Iverson" on the divorce papers prompted deep self-reevaluation. He and Turner have since reconciled. Germany's strategy to dominate Middle Europe depends on controlling four groups: Poles, Czechs, South Slavs, and Bulgaria. The United States should not oppose economic unification in Central Europe itself, but rather the imperialistic control exercised by ruling powers in Berlin, Vienna, Budapest, Sofia, and Constantinople. These powers are bound by shared interests in subjugating minorities, maintaining German-Magyar ascendency, exploiting Bulgaria's grievances from the Treaty of Bucharest, preserving Turkish integrity, and postwar debts owed to Germany.

American assets to counter this include:

1) Economic leverage: Control over raw materials, markets, and trade routes can pressure Germany, threatening demobilization and raising revolution risks among ruling classes, commercial interests, the army, and poorer populations.

2) Assets within Austria-Hungary: Nationalist discontent among Czechs and South Slavs, potential Polish statehood disrupting coalitions, and Austria-Hungary's desire to preserve its territory, leading it to support no-annexation policies, disarmament, and a league of nations.

US policy should stimulate nationalist unrest while stopping short of dismembering Austria-Hungary, pressuring it toward independence from Berlin.

Texas has passed a law (HB 8) replacing the STAAR standardized test with three shorter exams administered at the beginning, middle, and end of the school year, set to launch in 2027-28. The law bans practice tests and requires results to be released within two days so teachers can adjust instruction. However, parents, teachers, and education experts worry the changes may increase student stress rather than reduce it, as the end-of-year test will still heavily influence school accountability ratings. A TEA study on reducing testing's weight in ratings is not due until 2029-30 and is not required to be implemented. Critics argue the new system largely codifies what many districts already do. Some educators hope the approved assessment menu includes MAP tests, which adjust difficulty based on student responses and are reportedly less stressful than STAAR. Supporters, including bill architect Sen. Paul Bettencourt, say the overhaul will reduce testing time and pressure, though comparisons to Florida's similar 2022 reform suggest testing minutes could increase. LAPIS is a compiler framework addressing two challenges: enabling performance, portability, and productivity in a single framework, and bridging C++ simulation codes with Python-based ML codes. Built on MLIR and inspired by Kokkos, LAPIS contributes: (1) a custom Kokkos dialect representing Kokkos constructs in MLIR; (2) mapping of Kokkos Kernels linear algebra operations to sparse/dense tensors; (3) lowering passes supporting accelerators; (4) a Kokkos-inspired memory reference model including DualView; and (5) an emitter that converts mid-level Kokkos IR to C++ source code.

LAPIS accepts input conforming to the linalg-on-tensors dialects, supporting torch-mlir and MPACT frontends. The kokkos dialect provides parallel loop operations (range_parallel, team_parallel, thread_parallel), synchronization operations (single, team_barrier), and linear algebra operations (gemm, gemv). The kokkos-loop-mapping pass translates scf.parallel loops to Kokkos loops based on nesting depth (up to three levels), estimates parallelism for vector length tuning (e.g., in CSR traversal patterns), and inserts synchronization. Performance is demonstrated on AMD MI300A and NVIDIA H100 GPUs and Intel Granite Rapids CPUs, matching hand-optimized implementations for sparse and dense linear algebra and coupling CSE with AI/ML use cases.

Pseudorandom unitaries (PRUs) are efficiently computable unitaries indistinguishable from Haar-random unitaries by quantum polynomial-time adversaries with oracle access. They generalize t-unitary designs and have applications in black-hole physics, quantum benchmarking, learning theory, and cryptography.

Prior work established PRUs from one-way functions, culminating in Ma and Huang's adaptively secure construction. Separately, researchers have investigated pseudorandomness in idealized models, particularly the quantum Haar random oracle model (QHROM), where parties access a Haar-random unitary U and its inverse U†. Previous results include pseudorandom function-like state generators in QHROM and PRUs in the weaker inverseless QHROM (iQHROM), but the feasibility of PRUs in the full QHROM remained open.

Studying the QHROM is motivated by modeling random circuits used in quantum benchmarking and black-hole dynamics, and by implications for plain-model cryptography, such as transforming PRUs to have shorter keys.

This work proves that strong pseudorandom unitaries exist in the QHROM. The construction is GU(1^λ, k) := X^k3 · Uλ · X^k2 · Uλ · X^k1, using two queries to the Haar random oracle and O(log^(1+ε)(n)) bits of randomness, achieving security against poly(n)-query adversaries.

The security proof extends Ma-Huang's path-recording framework, replacing Haar-random unitaries with path-recording isometries and defining an approximate isometry S that merges independent databases while simulating keys. The analysis uses a query-by-query progress measure, leveraging the unitary invariance of the Haar measure, working with non-norm-preserving operators, and decoupling registers to simplify computations. The proof proceeds through a sequence of hybrids bridging the real and ideal experiments.

Chipotle released a new queso dip on Sept. 12, priced at $2.95 alone, $3.95 for a small order with chips, and $6.25 for a large order with chips. Chipotle spokesman Chris Arnold stated that 63% of test market customers said the queso would make them visit more often, and confirmed there are no plans to reduce the price because it is made with real, whole ingredients. The State Bar of Michigan e-Journal for May 23, 2001 contains case summaries across practice areas including Bankruptcy, Civil Rights, Constitutional Law, Criminal Law, Employment & Labor Law, Family Law, Insurance, Litigation, Municipal, Negligence & Intentional Tort, and Real Property. Energy Central's Deregulation Public Forum email, forwarded by Peggy Mahoney on August 28, 2000, poses a new question about whether policy changes should encourage natural gas exploration on federal lands and the continental shelf, given that 95% of planned power plants will be gas-fired while supply shortages are predicted to drive winter gas prices to record highs.

The bulk of the message presents selected responses to the previous question: whether power generators are deliberately manipulating wholesale markets in San Diego and whether price caps should be imposed. Respondents express diverse views:

- Many industry professionals argue generators are not manipulating the market but responding to supply-demand imbalances caused by hot weather, rising natural gas prices, reduced hydro output, and insufficient new generation capacity.
- Several blame California's flawed deregulation design, regulatory neglect, and NIMBY opposition to new plants.
- Most respondents oppose price caps, arguing they discourage new generation investment, mask true costs, and could cause shortages or blackouts.
- A minority support price caps or re-regulation, citing collusion, monopolistic market structures, and the inability of commodity markets with high fixed costs to remain competitive.
- Proposed solutions include removing barriers to new generation, demand-side management, robust bilateral markets, and cost-of-service-based pricing.

The email concludes with subscription, submission, and copyright information for the Energy Central service.

CEMEX, a Mexico-based cement company, grew from a small domestic firm into one of the world's largest building materials suppliers between 1992 and 2007, culminating in the $15.3 billion acquisition of Australia's Rinker Group. Under CEO Lorenzo Zambrano, who assumed leadership in 1985, the company prepared for globalization by divesting non-core assets and investing in communication systems like CEMEXNET.

CEMEX's international expansion progressed through four stages: Laying the Groundwork, Stepping Out (beginning with Spain in 1992), Growing Up (acquisitions across Latin America and Asia), and Stepping Up (major deals including Southdown, RMC, and Rinker). Central to its success was the "CEMEX Way," a standardized approach combining best practices from across the corporation while learning from acquired companies. This post-merger integration (PMI) process, refined over time, reduced integration periods from 25 months for Spain to under five months for Southdown.

The CEMEX Way emphasized knowledge management, standardized processes, IT implementation, and innovation, with middle managers playing key roles in diffusing practices. The approach delivered significant cost savings, including over $200 million in synergies from the RMC acquisition within one year. Despite shareholder rewards through 2007, CEMEX's share price fell sharply in 2008 due to the global downturn and debt from the Rinker deal.

Paul Clement is set to be named Swansea manager after Bayern Munich granted permission for talks. He will replace Bob Bradley, who was dismissed following a 4-1 loss to West Ham on Boxing Day. Clement is expected to sign a deal until 2019 and receive a £30million transfer budget. Owners Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan have indicated willingness to invest, with Swansea currently 19th in the Premier League. Clement joined Bayern in the summer as Carlo Ancelotti's assistant, having previously worked with him at PSG and Real Madrid. His prior managerial role at Derby ended after eight months. Swansea's Neil Taylor expressed support for Clement's potential appointment.

Following localized uprisings in East Berlin (1953) and Poznań (1956), a nationwide revolt erupted in Hungary in 1956. After World War II, Hungarian Communists led by Mátyás Rákosi had consolidated power and implemented collectivization and industrialization. Discontent grew due to irresolute leadership, a failing economy, repressive measures, and encouragement from Poland's political changes in October 1956, where Władysław Gomułka's appointment suggested national Communism might be tolerated.

A student rally in Budapest on 22 October produced a manifesto demanding reforms. The next day, a peaceful rally turned violent when state security police fired on crowds. Revolutionary councils emerged nationwide, demanding nationalism, neutrality, and Soviet troop withdrawal. Imre Nagy was reappointed prime minister, and Soviet tanks entering on 24 October were met with resistance. Soviet envoys Mikoyan and Suslov initially appeared conciliatory, announcing respect for Hungarian sovereignty on 30 October.

However, this was a deception. While the Suez Crisis diverted international attention, 250,000 Soviet troops and 2,500 armoured vehicles surrounded Budapest, striking on 3/4 November. Despite courageous Hungarian resistance, fighting largely ended by 14 November, with all resistance crushed by 30 November. Approximately 25,000 Hungarians and 7,000 Soviet soldiers died.

A federal judge dismissed Drake's defamation lawsuit against Universal Music Group over Kendrick Lamar's 2024 song "Not Like Us," which labeled Drake a "certified pedophile." U.S. District Judge Jeannette A. Vargas ruled that Lamar's lyrics constituted "nonactionable opinion" delivered during a heated rap battle featuring incendiary language from both sides. Drake's suit had alleged a "defamation-for-profit strategy," including the song's promotion and Lamar's 2025 Super Bowl performance, and included claims of defamation, harassment and deceptive acts. Springfield, Massachusetts police officer Conrad Lariviere faces disciplinary action after commenting "Hahahaha love this, maybe people shouldn't block road ways" on Facebook in response to a story about Heather Heyer, who was killed when a car struck counter-protesters at a white nationalist rally in Charlottesville, Virginia. Police Commissioner John Barbieri initiated an internal investigation, and Mayor Domenic Sarno denounced the comments. Lariviere later apologized, told Masslive.com he is not racist, and called himself "a good man who made a stupid comment." The DAWN-plasma study is a phase 2, randomized, open-label, multicenter clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of convalescent plasma combined with standard of care (SOC) versus SOC alone in hospitalized adult COVID-19 patients. The researchers hypothesized that administering high-volume convalescent plasma with high neutralizing-antibody-titers early in hospitalization would reduce the proportion of patients requiring mechanical ventilation.

The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints included clinical status, time to improvement, mortality, venous thromboembolism incidence, transfusion-related side effects, and quality of life.

Participants were randomized 2:1 to receive SOC with convalescent plasma or SOC alone. Eligible patients were adults ≥18 years with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and radiographic or clinical evidence of illness. Key exclusion criteria included prior mechanical ventilation, severe plasma allergy, treatment restrictions excluding ventilation, and recent anti-CD20 therapy.

Patients received 800–1000 mL of plasma in four doses, with the first dose within 12 hours of randomization. Only plasma with neutralizing antibody titers ≥1/160 was permitted. The study followed ICH-GCP guidelines and the Declaration of Helsinki, with IEC approval and informed consent obtained. Five patients withdrew consent and one was a screen failure before intervention; all six were replaced.

Williams & Connolly has confirmed a cybersecurity incident in which hackers accessed a small number of its attorney email accounts through a zero-day attack, which exploits a security vulnerability before it is patched. The firm stated there is no evidence that confidential client data was extracted from other parts of its IT system or from client file databases. The hackers are believed to be affiliated with a nation-state actor linked to recent attacks on law firms and companies. A Mandiant warning last month indicated hackers tied to the Chinese government have targeted law firms and technology companies seeking information on U.S. national security and international trade.

Coppin State, a historically Black university in Maryland, has more than quadrupled out-of-state enrollment over two years through its Expand Eagle Nation program, which offers in-state tuition to students from 41 states and territories without an HBCU, plus D.C. In 2024, qualifying-state enrollment rose from 81 to 195, and this fall, 416 of 1,000 incoming students came from those areas. Overall enrollment increased 26 percent.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers feature an EN pin that can be activated via VLDO connection, external signal, or a two-resistor divider configured for UVLO, with recommendations to keep UVLO at approximately 75% or less of input voltage. The devices include a 1.23-V internal bandgap reference, a transconductance error amplifier (1800 µA/V), and programmable output voltage via a resistor divider to a 0.613-V reference. Soft-start timing is set by a capacitor on the SS pin. Switching frequency (100 kHz to 2 MHz) can be configured through internal oscillator, external synchronization, or primary-secondary modes. Features include programmable dead time, leading edge blank time, duty cycle limits, current sensing with hiccup mode protection, external fault protection, slope compensation, and thermal shutdown at 175°C. The controllers support buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. A design example demonstrates a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter using GaN FETs with 5-V output, detailing component selection for the transformer, FETs, output filter, and compensation network. Layout guidelines emphasize separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switch node area, and proper bypass capacitor placement.

A change of government has occurred, with Democrats now controlling the House, Senate, Presidency, and Vice-Presidency. This shift reflects the Nation's desire to reinterpret its plans and viewpoint, not merely a party victory.

The Nation is great in material wealth, moral force, and governmental structure, but evil has accompanied the good. Resources have been squandered, industrial achievements have come at great human cost, and government has been used for private and selfish purposes.

The duty now is restoration: to cleanse and correct evils without impairing what is good. Key items needing alteration include the tariff, the banking and currency system, the industrial system, agricultural activities, and the neglect of natural resources. Government must also safeguard the health and rights of citizens as a matter of justice, not pity, through sanitary, food, and labor laws.

This work must be done without partisanship, ignorance, or haste. The goal is to restore, not destroy, guided by justice. This is a day of dedication, summoning honest and forward-looking people to support this high enterprise.

The passage introduces LG-CD, a Language-Guided Change Detection model for remote sensing change detection (RSCD) tasks. Traditional RSCD methods relying on thresholding, morphological analysis, and image algebra are sensitive to environmental interference. Deep learning approaches using CNNs and Vision Transformers improved accuracy but face challenges including data scarcity, annotation costs, and limited multimodal integration.

LG-CD addresses these issues by combining visual and textual information. It uses a pre-trained SAM2 encoder with lightweight multi-layer adapters to extract and fine-tune multi-scale features from bi-temporal remote sensing images, and CLIP to encode textual prompts into word-level and global embeddings. A Text Fusion Attention Module (TFAM) aligns textual and visual features using multi-head cross-attention, while a visual-semantic fusion decoder generates accurate change detection masks.

The main contributions are: (1) integrating natural language cues to guide attention toward target regions; (2) leveraging SAM2's generalization capability with multi-layer adapters for fine-tuning; and (3) designing the TFAM and visual-semantic fusion decoder to produce high-precision change masks.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture by Will Ma focuses on post-flop poker strategy. Key concepts covered include:

**Continuation betting**: The preflop aggressor typically gets checked to because their range is stronger (more likely to have premium hands). Bets should generally be 50-100% of the pot, with increasing percentages from flop to river. Small bets are strictly worse than checking since they give opponents free options to check-raise.

**Fundamental Theorem of Poker**: Bets should either be value bets (with strong hands, to get worse hands to call) or bluffs (with weak hands, to fold out better hands). Middle-range hands should be checked.

**When to raise**: Generally requires two-pair or better when stacks are deep (40+ big blinds). With shorter stacks (25 big blinds), top pair can be sufficient to go all-in. Position, stack size, and cards all matter.

**When to call vs. fold**: New players tend to call too often. Most missed flops should be folded. Calling is preferred over raising in "way-ahead, way-behind" situations where opponents will only continue with hands that beat you.

**Leading**: An advanced play used when the flop favors your range better than the preflop raiser's, typically in shallow-stacked situations.

**Implied and reverse implied odds**: Hands like suited connectors have good implied odds (can win big pots when hitting draws), while weak hands like 7-2 offsuit suffer from reverse implied odds even with correct preflop equity. Set mining exemplifies implied odds play.

**Bluffing epiphanies**: (1) When bluffing, what matters is how many outs you have against calling ranges, not current hand strength—draws are ideal bluffing hands. (2) Consider what strong hands you could credibly represent; abandon bluffs when the board doesn't favor your perceived range.

Multiple news articles from July 18, 2001 address California's energy crisis:

Prof. Cyril Dim, a lecturer at the University of Nigeria, explains that cervical cancer is a malignant condition of the neck of the womb, caused almost entirely by the human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly oncogenic types like HPV 16 and 18, which are sexually transmitted.

Cervical cancer progresses through a pre-cancer stage (precancerous lesions), an early stage, and a late stage. Precancerous lesions have no symptoms but can be detected via pap smear and treated to prevent invasive cancer. Early symptoms include post-coital bleeding, later progressing to foul-smelling vaginal discharge and abnormal bleeding. Late-stage symptoms include weight loss, anaemia, pelvic pain, and incontinence.

Diagnosis requires tissue biopsy and histology. Men face no harm from sex with affected women, though they can transmit HPV. Survival depends on stage: early-stage cancer can be cured, while late-stage cases have poor outcomes.

Cervical cancer is largely a disease of developing countries due to lack of structured screening. Globally, about 500,000 new cases and 200,000 deaths occur annually, with 80% of deaths in developing nations. Nigeria records about 15,000 new cases and 10,000 deaths yearly. Treatment includes radical surgery or radiotherapy for early stages, and radiotherapy with chemotherapy for late stages. Some attribute the disease to witchcraft due to misunderstanding.

U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin ruled on Tuesday that the 1991 Nirvana album cover depicting a naked baby underwater reaching for a dollar bill does not constitute child pornography. The judge dismissed a 2021 lawsuit filed by Spencer Elden, who was photographed at 4 months old and sued under a federal law providing civil remedies for minor victims of certain crimes. Olguin evaluated factors including the focus on genitalia, sexual suggestiveness of the setting, nudity, and intent to elicit a sexual response, concluding that only the nudity factor applied. He compared the image to a family photo of a nude child bathing and found it insufficient to support a finding of lasciviousness.
I am unable to summarize this passage.

The Ottawa coach acknowledges his team has been outplayed in two games against Anaheim but believes they are a better team and must prove it at home. Key issues include losing faceoffs at center ice, turnovers, attempting long stretch passes against Anaheim's defensive system, and failing to establish puck possession and forecheck. Pahlsson's line has dominated physically, while Alfredsson and other forwards haven't created plays. Chris Neil is absent as his wife is having a baby. The coach praised their young goaltender's performance and spoke highly of Rob Niedermayer. He plans to use the fourth line more and expects an energetic home crowd to boost the team.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) has grown in presence across many contexts, including education, particularly following the COVID-19 pandemic. Its introduction in education aims to develop 21st-century skills based on learning, self-correction, and reasoning. Higher education institutions have been impacted by AI across multiple dimensions: teaching-learning, research, organizational management, and external relationships.

Li and Yang (2023) identify differences between traditional and AI-oriented higher education regarding evolution pace, governance, training models, and research approaches. AI offers advantages such as personalized learning, automated grading, data analysis, plagiarism detection, virtual assistants, and predictive analytics (Zentner, 2022). Aldosari (2020) outlines ten areas where AI can transform education, including automating tasks, redesigning programs, and changing teachers' roles.

However, challenges include equity of access, ethical and privacy concerns, teacher training, financial costs, organizational resistance, and AI's limitations regarding emotions and creativity. Integration is hindered by traditional pedagogical practices and may create anxiety about de-professionalization.

To enhance AI use, stakeholders should develop AI literacy beyond digital literacy. Teachers need specific competencies, and the process should be participatory, potentially through action-research. The teacher's role must be reshaped alongside the development of soft skills to adapt to AI-driven changes.

A player expresses surprise and gratitude at being put back in the lineup by coach Pat after a two-week absence, noting he was nervous but wanted to contribute. He reflects on winning three cups in nine years, calling it special, and describes the season as the most difficult, citing the loss of Holik and the addition of Madden and Marshall. He credits Pat's no-nonsense, focused coaching style for keeping the team from becoming complacent, describing him as one of the toughest coaches he's played for but worth it.

An analysis of campaign contributions by lawyers and staff at the 100 top-grossing law firms and 50 larger plaintiffs-side firms found that 92.45% of contributions in 2023 and 2024 went to Democrats, a roughly 12-1 ratio. This marks a shift from the 6-1 ratio identified in a 2021 analysis covering 2017-2020. Conducted by University of Notre Dame Law School professor Derek Muller, the analysis showed about $52 million went to Democratic-affiliated groups versus $4 million to Republican-affiliated groups. Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton had the highest percentage of Democratic contributions (99.7%), while Nelson Mullins Riley & Scarborough had the lowest (66.4%), though still favoring Democrats.

The lecture discusses discrete symmetries in quantum field theory: parity (P), time reversal (T), and charge conjugation (C).

For a complex scalar theory, these symmetries are implemented through unitary operators at the quantum level, except time reversal which requires an anti-unitary operator. An anti-linear operator satisfies aC = C*a, which is necessary for UT to properly reverse time in the Schrödinger equation. The adjoint definition is modified for anti-linear operators with a complex conjugate.

Each symmetry transformation can include a phase factor (eta_P, eta_T, eta_C). Since P² must return the system to itself, eta_P must be ±1, distinguishing scalars (+1) from pseudoscalars (-1). The transformations act on creation/annihilation operators by flipping momentum for P and T, while C exchanges particles with antiparticles.

For Dirac fields, transformations require a matrix D acting on spinor space because components can reshuffle. For parity invariance, D must commute with gamma^0 and anti-commute with gamma^i, giving D proportional to gamma^0. For charge conjugation, a matrix C exists satisfying -gamma^μT = C^(-1) gamma^μ C, guaranteed by the equivalence of gamma matrix representations. Time reversal uses DT = C^(-1) gamma^5 transpose.

Parity and time reversal are independent discrete transformations not related by Lorentz boosts.

The lecture then introduces path integrals for fermions. Feynman couldn't extend path integrals to fermions for about 15 years until Berezin introduced Grassmann variables—anti-commuting numbers where θ² = 0. Functions of Grassmann variables have finite power series expansions. Differentiation direction (left vs right) matters due to anti-commutation.

Integration rules require linearity and that total derivatives vanish, leading to ∫dθ = 0 for constants and ∫dθ θ = 1 (by convention). Remarkably, integration equals differentiation for Grassmann variables. Change of variables gives the inverse Jacobian compared to ordinary calculus: dθ' = (1/a)dθ when θ' = aθ.

U.S. stock index futures rose on Thursday, supported by a strong start to earnings season and rebounding oil prices. However, U.S.-North Korea tensions and the upcoming French election limited risk-taking. Of the 57 S&P 500 companies that have reported earnings, 75.4 percent beat expectations, above the 71 percent four-quarter average. The system synchronizes data collection between a rotating LIDAR sensor and one or more cameras. The LIDAR emits light pulses and detects reflections while rotating about an axis. The cameras provide rows of sensing elements aligned parallel to the LIDAR's rotation axis, operating in a rolling shutter mode. A controller obtains a sequence of image pixel rows, where each row measures external light during respective exposure periods that may partially overlap. The order and timing of image pixel capture can be matched to the LIDAR's light beam emission order, rotation direction, rotation rate, and pointing direction, improving alignment between image pixels and LIDAR detections in both time and viewing direction. Cameras may be arranged in a ring formation with partially overlapping fields-of-view, and sensing elements may be mounted on a curved surface. The combined data can generate 3D representations, colored point clouds, or depth-enhanced images of the environment.

Quantbot Technologies LP increased its position in Zoe's Kitchen by 114.5% during the second quarter, owning 17,056 shares worth $203,000, representing approximately 0.09% of the company. Other institutional investors, including American International Group, FMR LLC, Teachers Advisors, California Public Employees Retirement System, and Massachusetts Financial Services, also adjusted their holdings during the first quarter. The defendant appealed two judgments from the Supreme Court, Queens County: a 2008 conviction for second-degree murder, criminal possession of a weapon, reckless endangerment, and endangering the welfare of a child following a jury verdict, and a 2009 conviction for second-degree murder following a guilty plea.

The court affirmed both judgments. It found the defendant's claims regarding a detective's testimony about locating him and the jury charge on consciousness of guilt to be unpreserved and, regardless, meritless, as the testimony supported the consciousness-of-guilt argument and the charge was warranted and correct. The court rejected the claim that the prosecutor altered the prosecution's theory during summation, noting the theory that the defendant was the gunman remained consistent and that principal versus accomplice status does not affect the theory of liability. As no independent claim was raised regarding the second indictment, that judgment was affirmed alongside the first.

Darren Osborne, 48, was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum term of 43 years at Woolwich Crown Court for driving a van into a crowd outside Finsbury Park mosques in London last June, killing Makram Ali and injuring nine others. Osborne was found guilty of murder and attempted murder and reportedly shouted "I want to kill all Muslims" after the attack. The prosecutor said Osborne had been "brainwashed" into Islamophobia after watching a BBC drama about a Muslim grooming gang. Ali's family expressed being "pleased" with the verdict. Several prominent hedge funds reduced their healthcare holdings in the second quarter as the sector outperformed the broader U.S. stock market, rallying amid failed Republican efforts to repeal the Affordable Care Act. Facebook is launching a "Trending News" section for its iOS and Android apps, according to TechCrunch. The feature aggregates news stories from various sources, ranking them by how many publications share each story. Users can access it via the "Explore" tab, where tapping a story reveals headlines, videos, photos, and top Facebook posts on the topic. The patent describes an electronic smoking device (e-cigarette) with a coil-less atomizer comprising one or more woven fiber tubes serving as both heating element and wicking element. The housing contains a battery, control electronics, optional airflow sensor, LED, liquid supply, and atomizer. The woven fiber tube has an electrically conductive heating section connected to two leads or electrical contacts, with end sections in contact with the liquid supply. The tubes can be shaped as U, C, or L forms, and may be made of carbon fibers, nickel-chromium, steel, titanium, ceramic fibers, or composites woven from multiple materials for combined electrical resistance and capillary properties. Liquid travels through the hollow interior via capillary action and through the porous fiber wall. Multiple tubes of same or varying diameters can be arranged parallel or in contact to enhance liquid transport or provide staged aerosol delivery. Sections of the tube may be coated or modified to create differential electrical resistance, with the heating section typically having 3-5Ω resistance. Manufacturing involves masking part of the tube and sputtering conductive material onto unmasked portions. The design eliminates the need for separate heating wires and porous wicks, enabling miniaturization.

The U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Massachusetts addressed remaining issues in litigation between Access Cardiosystems, Inc., its investors (Moriarty, Connolly, Zimmel, and Radley), and Access's founder Randall Fincke. The Court had previously found Fincke liable for breaching fiduciary duties and violating Massachusetts General Laws ch. 110A, § 410(a)(2) based on a false statement in an October 2002 Business Plan claiming Access's patent counsel had advised that its product did not infringe on any known patents.

The Court denied Fincke's Motion to Reconsider the § 410(a)(2) liability ruling, finding the statement was objectively false and material regardless of whether investors understood it as a formal or informal opinion.

Regarding damages, the Court found the Investors' testimony that they relied on the Business Plan for all subsequent investments was not credible, noting inconsistencies and contrived delivery. Applying an objective analysis of the nexus between the misstatement and specific securities transactions, the Court concluded that only Zimmel's October and November 2002 stock purchases totaling $1,500,000 were made "by means of" the misstatement. Subsequent investments, including the April 2003 Transaction, resulted from separate negotiations and a new Company Overview document, not the Business Plan.

The Court entered judgment against Fincke for $1,500,000 plus interest in favor of Zimmel, and $281,534.62 plus interest in favor of Access for fiduciary duty breaches.

The BIRDS workshop aims to bridge the gap between digital library domain experts, who possess deep collection knowledge but often lack technical resources, and computer science researchers, who have computational expertise but limited awareness of real-world library challenges. The Ohio Supreme Court considered the constitutionality of the first sentence of R.C. 3105.03, which requires a divorce plaintiff to have been an Ohio resident for at least one year before filing. Appellant did not meet this requirement at the time of filing.

Citing Shapiro v. Thompson and Dunn v. Blumstein, the court acknowledged that durational residency requirements penalizing the right to interstate travel must satisfy a "compelling state interest" test. However, the court distinguished divorce from welfare and voting, noting that divorce is not a basic need and is a creature of state statute.

The court held that R.C. 3105.03 does not penalize the right to travel, as it does not prevent persons from moving to Ohio and exempts alimony-only actions. The state has a compelling interest in regulating marriage and ensuring its divorce laws apply only to residents who intend to make Ohio a permanent home. Because residency intention is subjective, the one-year requirement is the least restrictive means of verifying domicile.

The judgment was affirmed. Justice Schneider concurred based on the particular facts, noting the grounds for divorce arose in New York, but suggested the decision might warrant re-examination if grounds arose after establishing Ohio residency.

On August 17, 2022, Apple Inc.'s Compensation Committee approved the Apple Inc. Executive Cash Incentive Plan, under which eligible executive team members, including named executive officers, may receive cash incentive awards based on the achievement of performance goals over Committee-established performance periods. Released on December 11, 1987, less than two months after the Black Monday stock market crash, Oliver Stone's Wall Street has remained the preeminent film about finance for 30 years. The film succeeds not through realism or market explanation, but by combining a rags-to-riches narrative with a Hero's Journey, following Bud Fox (Charlie Sheen) as he rises from low-level broker to wealth under the mentorship of Gordon Gekko.

The film also captures the excess of 1980s Wall Street, including junk bonds, corporate raiders, and yuppie culture, before Dodd-Frank regulations. Its central strength is Michael Douglas's Oscar-winning performance as Gordon Gekko, a character modeled on figures like Ivan Boesky, Michael Milken, and Carl Icahn. Douglas was cast after Warren Beatty and Richard Gere declined the role. Stone and Douglas report that finance professionals still cite Gekko as career inspiration. Unlike later finance villains, Gekko targets corporations rather than everyday people, and his monologues prevent the film from becoming a simplistic moral lecture. Phrases such as "Greed is good" remain recognizable cultural touchstones.

The Simons Observatory has deployed over 67,000 transition-edge sensor (TES) detectors across four telescopes in Chile's Atacama Desert to measure the cosmic microwave background (CMB). These detectors are read out using microwave frequency multiplexing via SLAC microresonator radio frequency (SMuRF) electronics and universal focal-plane modules (UFMs), achieving a multiplexing factor near 1,000 per RF transmission line pair.

For the Large Aperture Telescope (LAT), SMuRF electronics are mounted directly to the receiver, exposing RF transmission lines to diurnal temperature swings that can cause systematic phase drifts mimicking TES signals. To characterize this effect, researchers analyzed off-resonance tones during a 22.6-hour observation period. They found phase drifts correlated with ambient temperature, but only at the picosecond level over a day-night cycle.

Using analytical conversions based on measured SQUID curves and calibration parameters, the inferred noise contribution from this phase drift was shown to be a minor component of on-sky detector noise, falling within the readout noise budget and not expected to impact the telescope's mapping speed.

The Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian describes electron-photon interactions in optical cavities, where molecular electronic structures are altered by quantized electromagnetic fields. Standard quantum chemistry methods are unsuitable for this context, and computational tools are scarce. The electron-photon coupling term is non-local, weak, but long-range, requiring a precise basis set. The sinc basis set is orthonormal, systematically improvable, and converges to the complete basis set limit. However, it has an O(N⁴) computational cost for two-electron integrals, though sparse or low-rank approximations can reduce this scaling. In cavity QED, single-mode optical cavity photon fields are modeled as quantum harmonic oscillators.

The DAWN-Plasma trial was a randomized, multicenter, open-label phase II study evaluating the efficacy and safety of convalescent plasma combined with standard of care (SOC) versus SOC alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH-GCP guidelines, the study was approved by Independent Ethics Committees, and informed consent was obtained from all participants.

Between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized 2:1 to receive either 4 units (800-1000 mL) of convalescent plasma with high neutralizing antibody titers (≥1/160, with 80.7% ≥1/320) plus SOC, or SOC alone. Eligible adults had confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and were not on mechanical ventilation at randomization.

The primary endpoint—proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation at Day 15—showed no significant difference between groups (83.7% plasma vs. 84.1% control; OR 0.99, p=0.976). A significant interaction with age was observed in subgroup analysis. No secondary endpoints, including mortality and Day 30 outcomes, showed statistically significant differences.

Safety outcomes were comparable between groups, with similar rates of adverse events (28.13% vs. 30.06%), serious adverse events (20.63% vs. 20.86%), and fatal AEs (10.31% vs. 9.82%). Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 6.0% of plasma recipients, with no TRALI cases. Higher baseline and Day 6 neutralizing antibody titers correlated with better outcomes, independent of plasma intervention.

The study concluded that early high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma transfusion did not alter the clinical course of hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

This study analyzed NHANES data (2009-2020) from 32,498 US adults to identify empirical dietary patterns and their associations with cardiovascular disease (CVD), social determinants of health (SDOH), and Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) participation. Using principal components analysis, researchers identified four dietary patterns: American (least healthy, HEI-2020 score 42.4), Prudent (58.2), Legume (55.0), and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy (healthiest, 62.0).

The American pattern was most common overall (33.7%) and more prevalent among individuals with CVD, higher SDOH scores, and SNAP participants or income-eligible non-participants. Higher SDOH scores and SNAP participation were associated with lower alignment with the Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy patterns, but greater alignment with the Legume pattern. Most associations were consistent across racial and ethnic groups, though some variation was observed, particularly among Hispanic individuals.

The authors conclude that dietary patterns vary by cardiovascular health and socioeconomic vulnerability, and that nutrition interventions, including "Food is Medicine" approaches and SNAP-related policies, should account for these naturally occurring patterns. Study limitations include cross-sectional design, self-reported data, and reliance on two 24-hour dietary recalls.

The Wham play is a complementary run concept similar to Trap, but uses a Tight End or Fullback to kick out a Defensive Lineman instead of a Guard.

Its main strength is creating favorable, unexpected running angles, since defenses spend little practice time on it. Its weaknesses include complex installation requirements and the need for a physically strong blocker to execute the kickout.

Against a 3-4 Odd front, assignments involve double teams on the Nose Tackle, climbing linemen to linebackers, and a Fullback motioning to kick out the first Defensive Lineman outside the Center. Against a 4-3 Even front, assignments are similar, with adjustments for the different alignment.

Variations include the Gun H-Back Wham RPO, where the Center releases and the Fullback kicks out the Nose Tackle while the QB reads a flat defender, and the Shotgun Influence Wham, which uses a pulling Guard to bait a 3-tech into being trapped by the Fullback.

Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection is a major global public health concern, with approximately 170 million infected worldwide and a 4% prevalence in Rwanda. This descriptive cross-sectional study, conducted at CUSP in Huye district, aimed to evaluate whether horizontal household transmission contributes to increased HCV prevalence. The study included 148 household members from 30 families of HCV-positive patients, screened using HCV Ab rapid tests with ELISA confirmation.

Results showed an HCV prevalence of 10.8% (16 positive cases) among participants. Statistically significant risk factors included HBV co-infection (p=0.001), HIV co-infection (p=0.001), and unprotected sex (p=0.016). Blood transfusion (p=0.058) and awareness levels (p=0.079) showed no significant correlation. Unprotected sex emerged as the most prominent transmission factor, while 93.9% of participants demonstrated poor awareness of HCV transmission.

The study concluded that household members living with HCV-positive individuals have elevated infection risk. Limitations included the cross-sectional design, which prevented determination of infection origin. Recommendations include educating family members, improving follow-up by the Ministry of Health, and conducting broader phylogenetic and countrywide studies.

The Construction Defining Functionality (CDF) framework is introduced as a formal model for analyzing computational problems through a tripartite architecture consisting of syntactic (Ssyn), semantic (Ssem), and logical (Slog) spaces, connected by structural mappings αf, βf, and γf.

Unlike classical set theory, CDF interprets intensionality as internal generative rules and extensionality as observable outcomes, representing different levels of abstraction. Semantics is built on propositional logic, where syntactic complexity can cause exponential growth in semantic interpretations—a phenomenon termed semantic explosion.

CDF classifies problems based on mapping behavior: ComCDF (compositionally coherent with stable αf), ExpCDF (explosive or incoherent), and Semi-ExpCDF (intermediate). This classification aligns with the P versus NP distinction. The framework treats the diagram as a bridge between potentiality (generative possibilities via αf and βf) and actuality (realized computation via γf).

Applied to Boolean satisfiability, 2SAT clauses decompose into local binary implications, yielding stable, polynomial-time reasoning. In contrast, 3SAT clauses create non-local, ternary dependencies that cannot be decomposed, producing exponential semantic growth (O(2^n)). This explosion is structurally intrinsic to 3SAT's definition and cannot be eliminated without transforming the problem itself, explaining its NP-completeness as a consequence of syntactic non-locality rather than algorithmic limitations.

Patents grant inventors temporary monopolies, after which inventions become publicly available. Scott Crump's 1992 FDM patent led to today's affordable desktop 3D printers, while his company Stratasys still sells industrial machines for up to $400,000. HP's Jet Fusion 4200 enables mass production without molds.

Applications include NASA propulsion components and GE's LEAP engine nozzles, which are lighter and longer-lasting. GE also consolidated 900 parts into 16 for a helicopter engine. As industrial patents expire, these technologies become accessible to consumers. The Wohlers Report, priced near $500, provides comprehensive annual industry information.

At the UN Climate Summit, Chinese President Xi Jinping reaffirmed China's commitment to the clean energy transition, positioning the country as a global leader as the US and EU step back. An open-label randomised controlled trial was conducted in Kampong Speu province, Western Cambodia, between November 2021 and February 2024 to compare the efficacy of 3·5 mg/kg versus 7·0 mg/kg primaquine (both over 14 days) in preventing Plasmodium vivax recurrences. P. vivax-infected patients over 15 years old with uncomplicated malaria were treated with 7-day artesunate and relocated to a non-endemic area for 90 days to prevent reinfection. G6PD normal patients were randomised (2:2:1) to low-dose primaquine, high-dose primaquine, or no primaquine, while G6PD deficient patients received no primaquine.

Of 156 enrolled patients, recurrence rates within 90 days were 81·4% (no primaquine), 24·4% (low dose), and 4·7% (high dose). The hazard ratio for high versus low dose primaquine was 0·17 (p=0·0229). Both primaquine regimens were well tolerated, though methaemoglobin increases were more frequent with high-dose primaquine.

The authors conclude that 7·0 mg/kg primaquine is more effective than 3·5 mg/kg in preventing P. vivax relapses in Cambodia, with comparable safety in G6PD normal patients, and recommend policy changes in Cambodia and likely other Southeast Asian countries. Limitations include small sample size, single-centre design, and inability to definitively distinguish relapses from recrudescence.

Bollinger Bands, developed by John Bollinger in the 1980s, are a technical analysis tool measuring price volatility. They consist of a middle band (typically a 20-period simple moving average) and two outer bands placed two standard deviations above and below the middle band. The bands expand during high volatility and contract during low volatility.

Several trading strategies use Bollinger Bands, including:
- **Bollinger Band Squeeze**: Identifies low-volatility consolidation periods that may precede breakouts.
- **Bollinger Band Breakouts**: Trades price breaks above or below the bands as bullish or bearish signals.
- **Bollinger Band %B**: Quantifies price position relative to the bands to identify overbought/oversold conditions.
- **Bollinger Band Walks, Bounce, Double Bands, Width, RSI Divergence, Pinch Play, Reversal, Volatility Contraction, and Triple Strategy**: Various approaches using the bands in different configurations.

Prices generally stay between the middle and upper band in uptrends, and between the middle and lower band in downtrends. Touching the upper band suggests overbought conditions; touching the lower band suggests oversold conditions.

Settings like the moving average period and standard deviations can be adjusted for different timeframes. Shorter timeframes produce more signals but more false positives; longer timeframes yield more reliable signals.

Limitations include delayed signals, equal weighting of older data, and potential false overbought/oversold indications during strong trends. Bollinger Bands should be combined with other indicators like RSI or MACD and proper risk management.

Testing suggests Bollinger Bands show some profitability in mean-reverting stock markets and as a breakout indicator in gold, though they did not prove useful for stock indices in the author's tests.

The holiday effect is a well-known stock market anomaly where returns tend to increase around holidays, potentially due to lower liquidity, lack of macro news, or pre-holiday risk reduction. This article backtests seven US holiday effects on the S&P 500 (using SPY and ^gspc data).

Results by holiday:
- Martin Luther King Day: negligible effect (average -0.05%, profit factor 0.9)
- President's Day: absent effect (average -0.24%, profit factor 0.77)
- Memorial Day: small to non-existent (average 0.18%, profit factor 1.17)
- Independence Day: strong (average 1.01%, profit factor 2.97, 68% win rate)
- Labor Day: poor results (average 0.11%, profit factor 1.14)
- Thanksgiving: strong (average 0.82%, profit factor 2.72); retail sector performs even better
- Christmas/End-of-year rally: strongest (average 1%, profit factor 4.8, 2.9% max drawdown)

Only Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas show tradeable effects. A post-holiday backtest found that holding over the holiday produced no gains, but the second day after the holiday delivered good returns (profit factor near 2). A refined post-holiday overnight strategy achieved a 71% win ratio and profit factor of 4 across 100 trades. The effects are small but real, and similar patterns have been documented internationally.

The SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) Specification defines how SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests communicate with hypervisors while protecting VM register state from hypervisor access.

The document begins with a Specification Agreement governing use of the document, including restrictions on duplication, disclaimers of warranties, export compliance requirements, and California governing law.

Key technical content includes:

**GHCB Overview**: A 4KB decrypted page that enables guest-hypervisor communication during Non-Automatic Exits (NAE). The format mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save state area.

**Version 2 Enhancements**: Introduces SEV-SNP support, hypervisor feature advertisement via a FEATURES bitmap, and multiple revisions (2.01–2.04) adding capabilities like VLEK certificates, APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL support, SEV-TIO (trusted IO), and Secure AVIC.

**GHCB Establishment**: Uses an MSR protocol (MSR 0xc001_0130) for initial negotiation before the GHCB page is available, including CPUID requests, SEV information exchange, and GHCB GPA registration (mandatory for SEV-SNP).

**Guest Exits**: Classified as Automatic Exits (AE) requiring no register exposure, or Non-Automatic Exits (NAE) where guests control exposed state via VMGEXIT.

**NAE Event Handling**: Covers IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Requests (standard, extended, TIO), SNP AP Creation, #HV Doorbell/IPI/Timer for Restricted Injection, APIC ID List, Run VMPL, Secure AVIC backing page registration, and Termination Requests.

**SMP Booting**: Describes challenges of booting APs under SEV-ES/SNP (since register state cannot be modified after measurement) and solutions including AP Reset Hold, AP Jump Tables, and the SNP AP Creation feature.

**Additional Topics**: NMI handling using #DB interception, debug register virtualization, and SNP Restricted Injection with a #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields.

SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

This study introduces Doublethink, a Bayesian model averaging method that simultaneously controls the Bayesian false discovery rate (FDR) and frequentist familywise error rate (FWER) for identifying direct non-genetic risk factors in biobank-scale data. Unlike genome-wide association studies, systematic identification of non-genetic risk factors is complicated by mediation, confounding, and pervasive correlation between variables.

The authors applied Doublethink to 1,912 variables in UK Biobank to identify direct risk factors for COVID-19 hospitalization, using 1,917 cases and 200,000 controls. Rather than filtering correlated variables, they tested groups of variables both a priori and post-hoc to recover signals diluted by correlation.

The analysis confirmed established risk factors including age, sex, obesity, socioeconomic deprivation, smoking, lung disease, alcohol intake, general comorbidity, kidney disease, and educational attainment. However, commonly analyzed factors such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and hypertension showed no significant direct effects, possibly because their influence is mediated through general health decline. The method also highlighted underexplored factors like psychiatric disorders, infection, dementia, and aging.

Theoretically, the work demonstrates that Bayesian posterior odds thresholds constitute a closed testing procedure controlling FWER, and provides analytic interconversion between posterior odds and adjusted p-values. Limitations include high computational cost (3,500 CPU hours), reliance on large-sample asymptotic approximations, sensitivity to prior choice, and inability to assess total (versus direct) effects.

The passage traces the evolution of software patterns and their application to distributed systems, particularly container-based architectures.

It begins with a historical overview: Donald Knuth's 1962 work formalized algorithms as reusable concepts, the 1990s introduced object-oriented design patterns (notably the "Gang of Four" book), and the late 1990s/2000s saw open source development emphasize software as a community endeavor.

Patterns for distributed systems provide general blueprints rather than specific technologies. Their value lies in enabling learning from others' mistakes, creating shared vocabulary, and building reusable components.

The text then describes single-node container patterns:
- **Sidecar pattern**: A secondary container augments an application container (e.g., adding HTTPS to a legacy service, synchronizing configurations). Sidecars should be parameterized, have stable APIs, and be documented.
- **Ambassador pattern**: A container brokers interactions between the application and external world (e.g., client-side sharding with twemproxy/Redis, service brokering, request splitting for experiments).
- **Adapter pattern**: Modifies an application's interface to match standardized conventions for monitoring (e.g., Prometheus), logging (e.g., fluentd), or health checks (e.g., MySQL).

Multi-node distributed patterns address microservices architectures, which offer reliability, agility, and independent scaling but complicate debugging and design.

Key multi-node patterns include:
- **Replicated load-balanced services**: Stateless services replicated behind a load balancer, requiring readiness probes. Can include session tracking, caching layers (e.g., Varnish), rate limiting, and SSL termination (e.g., nginx).
- **Sharded services**: Each replica serves only a subset of requests, used for stateful services where data is too large for one machine. Sharded caches increase effective cache storage but create dependencies on specific shards. Replicated sharded caches combine both approaches for resilience.

Teams should prepare for three jump ball situations: defensive (opponent has advantage), even (equal chances), and offensive (team has advantage).

For defensive jump balls, early rotation and preparation are encouraged, especially when opponents have a height or jumping advantage. Players should watch the jumper's eyes and hands, as jumpers typically telegraph tip direction—right-handed jumpers tip forward-left, left-handed jumpers tip forward-right. Box and Diamond alignments use various defender rotations to contest the tip, while the "Y" alignment positions two defenders back to prevent easy shots when facing superior jumpers.

Even jump balls require boxing out, establishing inside position, and rotating clockwise or counter-clockwise based on predetermined signals (e.g., hand placement).

Offensive jump ball plays are effective with a 6"+ height advantage, generally tipping forward to the tallest player while maintaining defensive balance. Documented plays include: Possession, Double Tap, Post Split (Diamond and Box), Jumper Fly, Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem, and Loop. Each involves specific tipping, screening, cutting, and defensive balance assignments, with several plays executable on either side of the court. If a good shot is unavailable after possession, teams should flow into a set or motion offense.

Baseline out of bounds situations give the defense a 5-on-4 numerical advantage, yet most coaches neglect them and assume standard half-court defense applies. Defending the ball behind the basket differs from defending it in front, and errors typically yield easy baskets. Zones are vulnerable to the screens and overloads common in such plays.

Four effective defensive options are:

1. **Jam**: Defenders sag to protect the middle, then aggressively smother opponents without switching, disrupting screens and forcing five-second violations or charges.

2. **Jump Switch**: Defenders aggressively switch screens while denying passing lanes, useful with limited clock time. Switching without aggressive denial is discouraged.

3. **Trap**: After the inbounds pass, the inbounder's defender follows to double-team the receiver, with others rotating into helpside positions.

4. **Combination Defenses**: Box & One, Diamond & One, or Triangle & Two alignments can surprise the offense, using chasers to face-guard key players while others form a zone.

All options begin with sagging off to protect the basket before the ball is handed in, then transition to standard defensive rules once inbounded.

This study investigated the molecular signature of neuropathic pain using Morton's neuroma as a model of human peripheral nerve injury. Researchers performed RNA sequencing and immunohistochemistry on nerve samples from 22 patients with Morton's neuroma and 11 control participants.

Differential gene expression analysis identified over 3,349 differentially expressed genes between groups. Gene Ontology and Weighted Gene Co-expression Network analyses revealed overrepresentation of biological processes related to immune/inflammatory response and nervous system development (including myelination and axon guidance). Deconvolution analysis showed increased macrophage and memory B cell proportions in Morton's neuroma, with macrophage proportions correlating with paroxysmal pain severity.

Three genes (MARCO, CD163, STAB1) characteristic of the M(GC) glucocorticoid-induced macrophage subset were upregulated, with MARCO expression correlating with paroxysmal pain. Immunohistochemistry confirmed demyelination, increased T-cell density, and elevated CD163+MARCO+ macrophage density in Morton's neuroma samples. CD68+ macrophage density correlated with burning pain.

Limitations included variable control nerve locations, sex imbalance between groups, small sample size, and inherent human tissue variability.

The findings indicate that neuroinflammation persists in chronic human peripheral neuropathic pain, long after initial nerve injury, potentially reflecting failure of inflammation resolution. The M(GC) MARCO+ macrophage subset may be particularly relevant to paroxysmal pain and could represent either a failing reparative response or a pro-fibrotic population preventing return to tissue homeostasis.

Diffusion models and flow matching are two generative modeling approaches used for high-fidelity generation of images, videos, audio, and text. Both can be viewed as special cases of learning stochastic dynamics between distributions, formalized as the Schrödinger bridge (SB) problem. One computational method for solving SB is the iterative proportional fitting (IPF) algorithm, which updates forward and reverse processes until they become time reversals of each other. Existing IPF variants require samples from both marginal distributions and cannot handle cases where marginals are given as unnormalised densities.

The authors extend IPF to settings where one or both marginals are unnormalised densities (energy functions), building on off-policy reinforcement learning losses and stabilisation techniques for diffusion samplers. Their contributions include: (1) demonstrating that data-to-energy and energy-to-energy IPF learn stochastic bridges with low transport cost comparable to data-to-data IPF; (2) showing existing data-to-data IPF can be improved by learning the diffusion coefficient alongside the drift; and (3) applying data-to-energy IPF to translate prior distributions to posteriors in generative model latent spaces, enabling scalable data-free image-to-image translation.

The passage also provides background on the SB problem, framing it as a KL-divergence minimization between processes with fixed marginal constraints, and relates it to entropy-regularised optimal transport. It introduces the IPF recursion, initialised with a reference process, which iteratively solves half-bridge problems.

Overnight trading involves buying at the close and selling at the next day's open or close. The overnight edge in the stock market is well-documented, as the average gain from open to close over the past 30 years has been zero, making overnight holds more profitable.

Several overnight trading strategies can be developed around specific patterns, including the Turnaround Tuesday effect, holiday seasonality, end-of-month effect, weekday effects, mean reversion, and options expiration week. Backtests using SPY since 1993 show average gains per trade ranging from 0.2% to 0.55%, with win ratios between 57% and 70%.

Combining these strategies into a portfolio produces strong performance metrics. The strategies were developed in 2017, with live trading beginning in 2021. Commissions are minimal and slippage is smaller than commonly believed.

Key principles for portfolio construction include:
- Using uncorrelated strategies across different asset classes and time frames
- Avoiding overlapping trades, as most global indices correlate strongly with SPY
- Mixing mean-reverting, trend-following, and seasonal strategies
- Including short strategies for risk mitigation, despite their typically weaker standalone performance
- Avoiding large drawdowns to benefit from compounding

Trend-following strategies are difficult due to low win ratios. The author emphasizes that trading many sub-optimal strategies is preferable to relying on a few "perfect" ones. Overnight trading's short holding period allows traders to capture brief bursts of market movement and improve risk-adjusted returns.

Small sided games (SSGs) in soccer involve two teams with fewer than 11 players on a reduced field, used for either practice or competition. The main goal is to increase individual ball touches.

In practice, SSGs range from 3v3 to 9v9, address specific tactical themes (such as attack, defense, passing, or goalkeeping), and use restricted spaces to improve technique. Field size and complexity increase with age progressions (U6 through U16).

In August 2017, U.S. Soccer issued Player Development Initiatives (PDIs) establishing standards for competitive youth SSGs for players U-6 to U-12. These use smaller fields, goals, balls, and shorter game times to suit younger players' physiological needs and promote development. Standards will be implemented nationally by all U.S. Soccer youth member organizations.

Additional rule changes include build-out lines starting at U-9 to encourage possession, no offside before U-9, offside only beyond the build-out line, and bans on headers, punts, and goalkeeper drop kicks.

The analyte monitoring system uses a sensor applicator containing a sensor control device with an electronics housing, a sensor, a sharp hub, and a sharp. A cap coupled to the applicator contains a collimator defining a sterilization zone that receives the sensor and sharp. During preparation, the sensor and sharp undergo radiation sterilization while the collimator prevents radiation from damaging electronic components in the housing.

Traditional analyte monitoring systems require separate sterilization of sensors (via radiation) and electronics (via gaseous chemical sterilization like ethylene oxide), since each method damages the other component. This typically necessitates a two-piece architecture requiring user assembly, introducing potential for error.

The disclosed one-piece architecture eliminates this issue through focused sterilization. The collimator, made of material with mass density typically greater than 0.9 g/cc (such as polyethylene, metals, or high-density polymers), focuses radiation through a passageway onto the sensor and sharp while blocking radiation from reaching sensitive electronics. Additional shields within the electronics housing can further protect components like data processing units. Seals create a sterile region encompassing the sterilization zone and portions of the housing interior. External collimators may also be used alongside or instead of internal collimators during manufacturing sterilization.

These MADF emitters exhibit both singlet and triplet excitons, yielding unity internal quantum efficiency and short lifetimes. The triplet state is localized on the benzo-imidazo-phenanthridine portion, while singlet energy can be reduced by extending conjugation with minimal effect on triplet energy. The small singlet-triplet energy gap allows thermally assisted delayed fluorescence while remaining triplet excitons emit via phosphorescence. Implementations include light-emitting diodes and lighting devices incorporating these complexes. The lecture constructs Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments (SNARGs) using two building blocks: Batch Arguments (BARGs) and Somewhere Extractable Hash functions (also called Somewhere Statistically Binding hashes).

A BARG for an NP language consists of Gen, Prover, and Verifier algorithms, where the proof size depends polylogarithmically on the number of instances k. BARGs satisfy semi-adaptive soundness: a cheating prover must commit to the index i where cheating occurs before seeing the CRS, because switching the CRS in analysis might change the cheating location, and language membership cannot always be efficiently checked.

A Somewhere Extractable Hash consists of Gen, Eval, Open, Verify, and Extract algorithms. It satisfies completeness, index hiding (hash keys hide the bound index), and somewhere statistical binding (even unbounded adversaries cannot open the bound location two different ways). Repeating l times yields binding on l locations while preserving hiding on unrevealed indices.

The hash is constructed using Fully Homomorphic Encryption in a Merkle-tree style, where each node decrypts children ciphertexts and re-encrypts under a fresh key to ensure well-formed ciphertexts along opening paths.

The SNARG construction: the CRS contains a hash key and a BARG CRS. The prover computes all circuit wires, hashes them using the somewhere extractable hash, and provides a BARG proving that every gate is satisfied (valid openings of input and output wires respecting the gate) and the output wire equals 1. The verifier only checks the BARG. Because the BARG statements form an index language, verification runs in polylogarithmic time in the circuit size.
