The Simons Observatory (SO) is a cosmic microwave background project in the Atacama Desert, consisting of three small-aperture telescopes (SATs) and one large-aperture telescope (LAT). It observes six spectral bands (30–280 GHz) using three types of dichroic, polarization-sensitive TES detector arrays: Low-Frequency, Mid-Frequency, and Ultra-High-Frequency (UHF).

This work reports the pre-deployment laboratory characterization of 25 production-design UHF detector modules, from which 19 will be installed in SO instruments. Each module contains 1756 TESs read out via a microwave SQUID multiplexing architecture with SMuRF electronics. Testing involved measuring I-V curves across varying bath and cold-load temperatures to determine critical temperature, saturation power, optical efficiency, and noise-equivalent power (NEP).

Results showed an average operable TES yield of 83%, median Tc of 163 mK, and median Psat of 24–26 pW. Optical efficiencies were 0.62–0.63, and approximately 89% of detectors met NEP requirements. Resonator yield averaged 86% after all cuts, with readout noise peaking at 35 pA/√Hz. Module "Uv63," which underwent re-annealing, showed degraded optical efficiency and will not be deployed. Thirteen UHF modules have been deployed to the LAT and a SAT, with six more planned for an LAT upgrade.

The lecture presents a cell probe lower bound proof for dynamic connectivity, demonstrating that insert, delete, and connectivity query operations require Ω(log n) time per operation, even when connected components are paths, and even for amortized and randomized algorithms. The proof, from a paper by Patrascu and Demaine, applies to both RAM and pointer machine models, showing that link/cut trees and Euler tour trees achieve optimal bounds.

The proof constructs a √n by √n grid graph where columns are connected by perfect matchings representing permutations. Block operations include updates (setting an entire permutation) and verify sum queries (checking if a composition of permutations equals a given permutation). The bad access sequence follows the bit-reversal sequence, with alternating verify sum and update operations.

A balanced binary tree is built over the access sequence, exploiting the interleaving property between left and right subtrees. The key claim is that for each node v with l leaves, Ω(l√n) cell probes must read cells last written during the left subtree. Summing across all nodes yields the log n factor.

The proof uses an information-theoretic argument: random permutations require l√n log n bits to encode. If the claim fails, a smaller encoding could be constructed, creating a contradiction. For verify sum, the decoding simulates queries for all possible permutation arguments, using a separator family (based on perfect hash functions) to distinguish memory access cases. The final bound considers two cases based on whether total reads/writes or the intersection of read/written cells dominates, both yielding the required lower bound.

Vernon Clausing, an osteopathic physician whose license was revoked for improperly prescribing Soma and Nubain, continued operating his clinic by hiring licensed physicians while personally filling prescriptions for these drugs. Following a sting operation in which Clausing delivered drugs to a former patient, police searched his premises and found large quantities of legend drugs. He was charged with multiple counts including unlawful delivery and possession with intent to deliver legend drugs under RCW 69.41.030, and was ultimately convicted on all counts after two trials.

On appeal, Clausing argued that jury instructions 17 and 25 misstated the law by requiring that legend drugs be dispensed by a licensed practitioner. The court rejected this argument, holding the instructions accurately reflected chapter 69.41 RCW when read with chapter 18.64 RCW, because nonpractitioners cannot dispense legend drugs even though unlicensed persons may physically deliver them to patients with valid prescriptions.

The court also rejected Clausing's claims that the charging document was defective, that instructions 18, 21, and 12 misstated the law or lessened the State's burden, that testimony from the Board of Pharmacy's executive director was improperly admitted, and that the prosecutor committed misconduct in closing argument. The convictions were affirmed.

In a cash sale where no payment terms are specified, title does not pass to the buyer who obtains possession without payment, and trover may be used to recover the goods. In 2015, PayPal, under CEO Dan Schulman, adopted a mission to democratize financial services. In 2019, an internal assessment revealed 65% of entry-level and hourly employees ran out of money between paychecks, contradicting the company's mission. In response, PayPal launched a four-point Employee Financial Wellness Initiative in late 2019: raising wages where appropriate, reducing healthcare premiums by 60% for U.S. employees in grades 15-19, granting stock awards to previously uncovered employees, and providing financial education and coaching.

The initiative aligned with PayPal's broader stakeholder capitalism approach, prioritizing employees alongside customers, regulators, investors, and communities. PayPal also achieved gender and ethnic pay equity, established a $5 million emergency relief fund, and committed $535 million to racial equity and $100 million to women's economic empowerment.

Early results showed improvements: customer service turnover dropped from 19.4% in 2019 to 7.3% in 2020, engagement scores rose, and financial wellness survey responses improved. By 2021, PayPal had 426 million active accounts and expanded its wellness efforts with on-demand pay tools and additional equity grants during COVID-19.

Schulman sought to build a broader movement, partnering with Financial Health Network, Good Jobs Institute, and Just Capital to launch the Worker Financial Wellness Initiative. By end of 2021, 11 companies had joined, including Chobani, Verizon, and Chipotle.

The passage describes a study investigating deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the ventral intermediate nucleus (VIM) of the thalamus, a surgical therapy for tremor in essential tremor, multiple sclerosis, and Parkinson's disease. Current DBS systems are open-loop, and developing closed-loop systems requires identifying neural biomarkers correlating with tremor control using the same lead as stimulation.

Researchers recorded local field potentials (LFPs) and accelerometer-based tremor data from 34 patients undergoing DBS surgery. They found moderate correlation between tremor and low-frequency LFP spectral power (alpha and theta bands), but strong correlation between tremor and peak LFP-acceleration coherence. Postural tremor was decoded from LFP signals with an AUC of ~0.7. High-frequency DBS (~130 Hz) reduced low-frequency spectral power.

Methods included intraoperative LFP recording via externalized leads, DBS artifact removal, spectral and coherence analyses, and statistical modeling (RMANOVA, GLM, ROC). Electrode locations were mapped using pre-op MRI and post-op CT.

A computational model of the thalamus with 5000 thalamocortical relay neurons across VC, VIM, and VOP regions simulated LFPs under different tremor cell distributions (normal, clustered, uniform). Simulated low-frequency LFP power varied with electrode location, tremor cell distribution, and tremor-to-non-tremor cell proportion, potentially explaining inter-patient variability.

This paper studies the popular dimension in matching markets, motivated by the nonexistence of popular matchings. A popular winning set is a collection of matchings M such that no alternative matching is strictly preferred by a plurality of (weighted) voters over M. The popular dimension is the minimum cardinality of such a set.

The authors examine three classical matching problems—house allocation, marriage, and roommates—across four variants: unweighted/weighted agents with strict/tied preferences.

Main results:
- For the house allocation problem, the popular dimension is exactly 2 in all four cases.
- For the marriage problem with unweighted agents and strict preferences, the popular dimension is 1 (following from Gale-Shapley and Gärdenfors).
- For the roommates problem with unweighted agents and strict preferences, the popular dimension is exactly 2.
- For the marriage and roommates problems with weighted agents or ties, the popular dimension is between 2 and 3.

The authors provide polynomial-time algorithms to construct these popular winning sets. Their results also imply that the Condorcet dimension conjecture of Lassota et al. holds for these three matching problems. Closing the gap between 2 and 3 for the weighted/tied cases remains open; the authors conjecture the marriage problem has popular dimension exactly 2.

This study examines how climate change affects the education of internally displaced K-12 learners in lower- and middle-income countries (LMICs), addressing a research gap where educational needs have been overlooked in climate change dialogues. Using an integrated framework combining the Human Rights-Based Approach (HRBA) and Education in Emergencies (EiE) research, the author conducted a literature review of 73 documents.

Findings reveal that climate change restricts educational access and quality through direct physical barriers, socioeconomic pressures, and environmental conditions affecting learning capacity. Rapid-onset disasters destroy infrastructure, while slow-onset disasters create economic hardship forcing school withdrawal. Higher temperatures correlate with reduced schooling years and learning outcomes. Displaced learners face additional challenges in new destinations, including financial barriers, administrative hurdles, discrimination, and inadequate distance learning solutions. Climate-related stressors also impair children's neurodevelopment, mental health, and academic performance.

Girls face compounded barriers, as families prioritize boys' education during financial constraints, and girls assume expanded household responsibilities when parents migrate. Cultural norms increase risks of early marriage and dropout.

The study recommends scalable financial support, simplified administrative processes, gender-sensitive policies, and robust data collection. It identifies research gaps including limited focus on climate-related displacement in EiE, insufficient long-term outcome studies, and reactive rather than proactive policy responses, advocating for climate-specific education frameworks integrated with adaptation strategies.

The passage introduces two all-optical thermometry methods using fluorescent microdiamonds containing silicon-vacancy (SiV) centers to measure micro/nanoscale temperatures. The methods employ multi-feature regression (MFR) and two-stage multi-feature regression (2SMFR) algorithms that combine photoluminescence from SiV centers with Raman signals from the diamond host, tracking up to nine temperature-dependent features including intensity, peak position, and FWHM values.

The models were trained and tested on eight diamonds across temperatures of 25–85 °C. Unlike conventional methods, performance was evaluated on unseen test data to produce generalized accuracy and resolution metrics. The MFR model includes explicit feature selection that automatically identifies optimal feature combinations, while the 2SMFR uses Lasso regression with implicit feature selection.

Results show the MFR model achieves 1.7 K accuracy and 1.2 K·Hz⁻¹/² resolution with only 3–4 training diamonds, representing a 26% improvement over single-feature (SF) models. The 2SMFR model, trained with seven diamonds and seven temperature set points, achieves 0.7 K accuracy, 0.6 K·Hz⁻¹/² resolution, and 0.04 K⁻¹ sensitivity—improvements of approximately 3×, 2×, and 7× respectively over the best SF model. Performance improves with more training data, with the greatest gains occurring at smaller training set sizes.

The authors conclude that multi-feature approaches provide a flexible, data-efficient framework applicable to any optical sensor with at least two temperature-dependent observables.

Mock v. Watson et al. addressed whether a widow's interest in her deceased husband's real estate is subject to the estate's debts. The plaintiff widow petitioned to have her interest in her late husband's land set apart to her. The defendant heirs objected, arguing the estate's debts must first be paid from the land. The trial court sustained the widow's motion and ordered her interest set apart; defendants appealed.

The court, per Beck, J., held that although the Code abolished dower and created a new estate, the widow's interest attaches upon the concurrence of the husband's seizin and the wife's coverture, becoming vested upon his death. Unlike the heirs' interest under § 2453, the widow's interest is not made subject to charges against the estate. Sections 2387 and 2391, permitting sale of real estate to pay debts, refer only to the estate's interest, not the wife's vested portion. Section 2441 merely prevents the widow from receiving more than her statutory one-third, and § 2451 protects a homestead acquired with her share from her own debts, not her husband's. The order was affirmed.

OPEC indicated readiness to boost production to stabilize prices. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission ordered heightened security at all 104 U.S. nuclear reactors, and oil refineries tightened access.

Foreign energy companies operating in South Asia, particularly Pakistan, reviewed security arrangements amid concerns of U.S. retaliation against targets in Afghanistan. The quarterback is considered the most important position in football, serving as the offensive leader and team face. Quarterbacks touch the ball every play, taking snaps from the center, throwing passes, and occasionally running. At higher levels, they call plays, communicate with teammates, identify defensive coverages, and call audibles when needed. This requires extensive study of playbooks, scouting reports, and opponent film.

The term "quarterback" originated from early formations where the player stood a "quarter back" from the running back. Other names include Signal Caller, Field General, Gunslinger, and QB. Body types have evolved from traditionally tall and strong to include smaller, more athletic players.

Key skills include football IQ, decision-making, accuracy, leadership, footwork, athleticism, and arm strength. Accuracy enables receivers to maintain momentum and avoid injury, while leadership involves setting examples in preparation and practice.

Notable quarterbacks include Otto Graham, Peyton Manning, Dan Marino, Joe Montana, and Tom Brady, who has won the most Super Bowls. The quarterback's importance stems from his involvement in every offensive play and his role in the offense's overall success.

Josephine Slosson, a New York resident, died in 1918. Her father's will had established a trust paying her income for life, with the principal to be distributed according to her will, or, in default, to those entitled under intestacy laws. Josephine exercised this power of appointment by bequeathing $5,000 to her husband (who predeceased her), $500 to Margaret Gillesse, directing payment of her debts from the trust, and leaving the balance to her surviving issue per stirpes. Her three children sought to take under their grandfather's will instead.

The court held that Josephine validly exercised the power of appointment, making the beneficiaries' interests subject to transfer tax. The children could not take under their grandfather's will because the contingency triggering that alternative—their mother's failure to validly dispose of the property—never occurred. Since the children did not renounce their legacies, taxation under renunciation was not addressed. Debts paid from the trust fund ($24,840) were taxable. However, $682.04 advanced by legatee Alice Slosson to pay creditors (to whom decedent was not actually indebted at death) was improperly included in her taxable interest. The order was modified to deduct this amount and otherwise affirmed.

Carol Christ, 73, has become the first woman to serve as chancellor of UC Berkeley, taking the role after previously retiring as president of Smith College in 2013. A Victorian literature scholar, Christ first came to Berkeley nearly 50 years ago after earning her Ph.D. at Yale, later serving as English department chair and then vice chancellor and provost before leaving for Smith. She assumes leadership during a turbulent period marked by sexual assault scandals, a $110 million budget deficit, a student housing shortage, tense relations with Sacramento following a state audit revealing $175 million in undisclosed funds, and national debate over free speech on campus.

Christ has identified several priorities: increasing the low percentage of Black students (about 3 percent), addressing sexual assault, and designating 2017-18 a "free speech year" featuring point-counterpoint debates. She plans to partner with Berkeley and Oakland on housing, pursue private philanthropy and administrative cuts to halve the deficit, and strengthen UC's presence in Sacramento. Earning nearly $532,000 annually, Christ will not reside in the official chancellor's house but will use it for school functions. She views restoring campus community as her greatest challenge.

A penalty kick in soccer is a restart awarded when a defender commits a direct-free-kick foul inside their own penalty area. Taken from 12 yards, it pits the kicker against the opposing goalkeeper alone.

Law 14 governs penalty kicks, specifying ball placement, player positioning, goalkeeper restrictions (remaining on the goal line until the kick), and rules about replaying the ball. Coaches must teach these rules and train designated kickers, called "penalty kick specialists," chosen for skill, composure, and success rate.

Successful penalty kicks require a consistent routine covering ball placement, starting position, run-up, plant foot, and strike. Kickers should practice regularly, manage nerves through techniques like visualization and controlled breathing, and avoid giving "tells" to the goalkeeper. 

The three main kick types are inside-of-the-foot, instep drive, and instep-face. Preferred targets are the lower corners, though upper corners, side netting, and even the center can be effective. Accuracy outweighs power.

Advanced techniques include scouting goalkeepers, developing multiple kicks, feinting during the run-up (not after), changing kickers, and the rare "tap" penalty kick. Feinting after completing the run-up results in a caution.

Coaches should simulate game conditions, involve goalkeepers in practice, and pre-designate kickers and alternates. Kickers uncomfortable with taking a kick should inform the coach without shame. After the kick, the ball remains live; the kicker may replay a goalkeeper rebound but not one off the posts or crossbar until another player touches it.

Options expiry is the time at which an options contract becomes void. In the US, the expiration date is the third Saturday of the expiration month at 11:59 a.m. EST, with the last trading day typically the preceding Friday. The third week of the month is known as the options expiration week, during which large-cap stocks with actively traded options tend to show higher average weekly returns (the OPEX effect). Quad witching weeks occur four times yearly when stock options, stock index futures, and stock index options expire simultaneously.

Backtests of expiry trading strategies show positive results: SPY averaged 0.3% per week during expiration weeks, with only January and July negative. A healthcare ETF (XLV) strategy averaged 0.7% per trade, an SPY overnight strategy averaged 0.46%, and a short day-trading strategy on SPY averaged 0.18% per trade across 306 trades. Volatility was found to be slightly higher on expiry days, especially quad witching days.

Developing options strategies involves researching models, backtesting them over at least 15 years across market cycles, and forward-testing them.

The UC1825B-SP PWM controller is designed for high-frequency switched mode power supplies, featuring minimized propagation delays and high error amplifier bandwidth. It supports current-mode or voltage-mode systems with input voltage feed-forward. Protection includes a 1-V current limit comparator, TTL shutdown port, soft start/duty-cycle clamp, latched logic, and undervoltage lockout with 800 mV hysteresis. Totem pole outputs handle high peak currents for capacitive loads like power MOSFET gates.

Chenai Mathabire, a 35-year-old Zimbabwean nurse and epidemiologist, received an International AIDS Society prize for research showing that a rapid tuberculosis test could be implemented at health centers in Malawi and Mozambique. Working for Doctors Without Borders since 2008, Mathabire has diagnosed malnourished children, supported HIV-positive pregnant women, and treated war injuries in South Sudan. Her two-year study found the rapid TB test, which analyzes urine with a paper strip, delivers results in under an hour, compared to days or months for traditional cough tests or X-rays. This is critical because TB is the leading killer of HIV-positive patients, and HIV is the top cause of death in Malawi and Mozambique. Staff could be trained quickly, and patients welcomed the method. The findings have prompted some health centers to adopt rapid TB testing. Mathabire recently moved to Sweden to marry an infectious disease specialist.

The speaker reflects on a strong first period performance, noting the team kept shots down despite three opposing power plays, and scored a late goal. He discusses being traded from Toronto to Detroit before the deadline, crediting Jimmy Devellano and Scotty Bowman for the opportunity. He describes the championship as a total team effort, highlighting the contributions of the five Russian players in critical situations. While he did not predict a four-game sweep, he states Detroit was clearly the best team in the league, outplaying every opponent regardless of size or strength.

Kennedy accepts the Democratic nomination for President, thanking Stevenson, Johnson, and other party figures for their support. He endorses the party platform, particularly its focus on civil and economic rights, and addresses concerns about his Catholic faith, asserting that his policy decisions will be independent of religious influence.

He criticizes Republican nominee Richard Nixon, arguing Nixon cannot match Eisenhower's stature and that the country needs strong Democratic leadership after years of stagnation. Kennedy outlines challenges facing America: shifting global power, Communist expansion, nuclear weapons, agricultural and urban changes, civil rights struggles, inadequate elder care, automation, and moral decline.

He calls for a new generation of leadership and introduces the concept of the "New Frontier"—not a set of promises, but challenges requiring sacrifice, courage, and innovation. Kennedy frames the election as a choice between public interest and private comfort, between progress and mediocrity. He asks Americans to join him as pioneers addressing unsolved problems in science, peace, poverty, and prejudice, concluding with a call for renewed strength to meet the test ahead.

A new study published in The American Journal of Psychiatry suggests that one hour of exercise per week can help prevent depression. Researchers tracked 33,908 Norwegian adults over 11 years, accounting for variables such as socio-economic background, substance use, BMI, social support, and physical illness. Participants who did not exercise were 44 percent more likely to experience depression than those who exercised one to two hours weekly. The study also found that small amounts of exercise could have prevented 12 percent of reported depression cases. Lead author Professor Samuel Harvey noted the potential for integrating exercise into mental health plans and public health campaigns.

Irish soccer player Megan Connolly, who plays for the Republic of Ireland National Team and Florida State University, posted a viral Twitter video of her reaction to an amusement ride during a trip to Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. The clip features her FSU teammate Dallas Dorosy laughing at Connolly's reaction, with the Fray's "How To Save A Life" playing in the background. Fellow Irish footballer Sophie Perry responded to the viral post.

Google's Project Fi has added three new compatible phones: the $199 Moto G6, the $740 LG G7 ThinQ, and the $899 LG V35 ThinQ. Launched in April 2015, Fi is an MVNO that uses T-Mobile, Sprint, and U.S. Cellular networks, plus Wi-Fi, charging $20 monthly for unlimited calls and texts and $10 per gigabyte of data, with refunds for unused data. The service's portfolio remains limited, notably lacking iPhones and Samsung devices. Analyst Roger Entner says the limited handset selection halves its market and suggests the service is not growing due to minimal advertising. Google has not disclosed user numbers but claims a "healthy user base."

BC NDP Premier John Horgan attributes a nine-cent overnight rise in gas prices to gouging and profits by companies, not taxation. He said he has raised the issue with the federal government and pointed to supply concerns, suggesting more domestic refining rather than exporting raw materials would benefit Canadian consumers. Liberal leader Andrew Wilkinson blamed Horgan, calling the increase a "tax grab" and urging the government to lower the gas tax to ease costs for drivers.

The Texas Court of Civil Appeals affirmed a trial court judgment denying appellants recovery for damages from a head-on collision on a three-lane highway in May 1955. Based on jury findings, the collision occurred in the western lane, and Wilson's act of driving into that lane was found to be negligent and the sole proximate cause of the collision, while appellee King was found not negligent.

On appeal, appellants raised six assignments of error concerning the court's failure to submit certain special issues, the submission of others, and improper argument by opposing counsel. The court held these objections were waived because appellants failed to timely object to the charge, did not submit requested issues to opposing counsel as required under Rules 272 and 273 of the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure, and did not object to the allegedly improper argument when it was made. The court noted that the argument complained of could have been cured by a trial court instruction, and objections raised for the first time on appeal are not preserved.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K Current Report with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on October 27, 2022. The filing reported Apple's financial results for its fourth fiscal quarter ended September 24, 2022, with a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report lists Apple's securities registered under Section 12(b), including common stock traded on Nasdaq under the symbol AAPL and multiple note series maturing between 2022 and 2042. Madhav Godbole, chairman of the Maharashtra government-appointed committee renegotiating the power purchase agreement (PPA) with Enron-promoted Dabhol Power Company (DPC), resigned on May 23, 2001, in protest against remarks by NCP chief Sharad Pawar, who had alleged the negotiating team had a "negative approach." Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh refused to accept the resignation, while Pawar later claimed he had been misquoted and was not speaking for the state government. A scheduled renegotiation meeting was cancelled following the resignation.

The development followed DPC's May 19 preliminary termination notice (PTN) to the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) over unpaid bills, giving six months to resolve the dispute. Enron indicated it may seek $3.5–5 billion in termination damages. The Maharashtra government considered issuing its own termination notice, and MSEB employees planned protests at Dabhol on June 5.

Indian financial institutions, including IDBI, ICICI, and SBI, faced potential losses of Rs 5,255 crore, with their stocks declining. Unlike foreign lenders, Indian FIs are not covered by counter-guarantees. Indian power companies, including Tata Power and Reliance, ruled out buying DPC due to high tariffs. Enron reportedly appointed Arthur Andersen and Jones Lang La Salle to value its Indian assets, suggesting a possible exit. The Centre adopted a wait-and-watch approach. Coach Bylsma brought renewed confidence to the team after the coaching switch, marking a turning point along with a successful five-game road trip and trades for Billy and Adams. The speaker would appreciate a ring over other mementos. Sid's leadership shows through his on-ice play, system discipline, and two-way performance rather than just vocal leadership. Jordan is recognized as a skilled, responsible two-way forward. Certain talented players can turn a game around in minutes with their effort and skill. North Tyneside Mayor Norma Redfearn stated that councils south of the Tyne could join the North of Tyne devolution deal at a later date, after the council's cabinet unanimously approved moving ahead with it. The deal, announced in November 2017 following the collapse of a seven-council agreement, involves Newcastle, Northumberland and North Tyneside, and will bring £600m over 30 years and 10,000 jobs. The combined authority is set to be established in summer 2018, with mayoral elections in May 2019. Newcastle City Council leader Nick Forbes rejected claims the authority would be "under-powered," noting it included health, disability and housing components, and offered greater per-head investment than other deals. Liberal Democrat councillor Greg Stone expressed concerns about its scale compared to Greater Manchester and other regions. A vote to split the existing North East Combined Authority was postponed to mid-April.

NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture introduces power savings of up to 50% for small language model inference through performance improvements, power gating, and faster sleep state entry.

DLSS 4, powered by GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs and fifth-generation Tensor Cores, introduces Multi Frame Generation (MFG), which generates up to three additional frames per rendered frame. The new AI model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than its predecessor. Blackwell's enhanced Flip Metering shifts frame pacing to the display engine for smoother output.

DLSS 4 also transitions from CNN-based to transformer-based neural networks for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, using 2x more parameters to improve temporal stability, lighting detail, and motion detail.

Blackwell enables neural shaders via the new Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, allowing Tensor Cores to be accessed through any shader type. Neural shader applications include:
- RTX Neural Materials: renders film-quality multi-layered materials in real time
- RTX Neural Texture Compression: reduces memory usage (e.g., 1110 MB to 333 MB in a demo)
- Neural Radiance Cache: infers multi-bounce indirect lighting from limited ray data
- RTX Skin: introduces real-time subsurface scattering
- RTX Neural Faces: uses generative AI to produce more natural-looking faces

The Blackwell GPU family includes:
- GB202 (flagship): 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA Cores, used in GeForce RTX 5090
- GB203: 45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA Cores, used in RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti
- GB205: 31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA Cores, used in RTX 5070

Plymouth Studio School, a sports-focused free school on the Plymouth Marjon University campus, is set to close at the end of the summer term 2018, just three years after opening. Tory MP Johnny Mercer said the £4.2million school, built for 300 pupils but holding only 155, was operating at 50 per cent capacity and was not financially viable. The closure, which requires Government approval, was announced ahead of an Ofsted report rating the school "inadequate". Mercer said he was "deeply disappointed" and focused on ensuring no interruption to pupils' education. It will be the 19th studio school to close since the model began.

Assembly Republican Leader Chad Mayes faces intense backlash from California Republicans after supporting the extension of the state's cap-and-trade climate program, alongside seven other GOP lawmakers. Critics, including RNC representative Shawn Steel and county GOP leaders, accuse Mayes of betraying party principles and aiding Democrats, pointing to photos of him with Gov. Jerry Brown after the vote. The state party's board is expected to vote on the matter, and Mayes faces a leadership challenge from Assemblyman Jay Obernolte. Other Republicans who supported the bill, including Marc Steinorth and Devon Mathis, have also encountered hostility. Meanwhile, Assemblywoman Melissa Melendez, who resigned as deputy caucus leader in protest, was relocated to a smaller office. Supporters argue the vote showed Republicans addressing climate issues important to Californians and prevented stricter regulations. The dispute highlights ongoing tensions between minority-party relevance and conservative orthodoxy.

This email from David I. Levine to students outlines mandatory and optional readings for the following week.

**Mandatory reading:** Students must read Mankiw chapter 10 and complete Homework #4, which covers how monetary and fiscal policy shift IS and LM curves, finding a newspaper article illustrating such a shift, analyzing recommended shifts during the Southeast Asia aggregate demand decline versus IMF recommendations, and textbook problems. Class discussion will focus on IS & LM shifts in the EC, US, Japan, and Indonesia during the 1997-98 crisis.

**Optional readings** include three articles:

1. "A French Paradox at Work" (NYT) describes France's 35-hour workweek law, passed in June 1998, requiring companies with 20+ employees to adopt the shorter week by 2002. While intended to create up to a million jobs, experts doubt its job-creation effectiveness but note it is modernizing workplaces. Results are mixed: some businesses like the Beyer jam factory and Packard Bell benefit through reorganization, while service industries struggle. Public support has declined, with unions and businesses protesting.

2. "Latin American markets rally" (San Jose Mercury News) reports stock market rallies in Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, Chile, and Colombia, driven by reduced expectations of US interest rate hikes and optimism about 2000 regional growth (projected at 3.2% versus a 0.4% contraction in 1999). Chile and Mexico show particular promise, while Brazil's currency strengthened after IMF flexibility was granted.

3. "Getting to the Bottom of Japan's Economic Blues" (Japan Echo) by Kojima Akira analyzes Japan's economic decline in the 1990s, attributing it to the late-1980s bubble collapse and subsequent policy failures, particularly inadequate handling of nonperforming bank loans. Structural factors include completing the catch-up with the West, globalization pressures, rapid population aging, and a technology paradigm shift. The Bank of Japan became a "lender of first resort," and massive fiscal stimulus was deployed. The author argues systemic reforms are essential to avoid a "lost decade."

The 2017 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons (ICAN) for its efforts to highlight the humanitarian consequences of nuclear weapons and to achieve a treaty banning them. Nobel committee president Berit Reiss-Andersen cited rising tensions over North Korea and the modernization of nuclear arsenals. ICAN, a coalition of NGOs in 100 countries, was recognized as a key force behind the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, adopted on July 7 with support from 122 nations. The treaty's negotiations were not attended by the five permanent UN Security Council members. ICAN chief executive Beatrice Fihn said the prize was important for raising awareness and signaling that nuclear weapons are unacceptable.

The TPS7H500x-SP push-pull converter design uses GaN FETs with approximately 25 ns dead time, implemented via 20.5 kΩ resistors for RPS and RSP, to minimize reverse conduction losses. Leading edge blank time was set near 50 ns using a 49.9 kΩ RLEB resistor, with a 33 nF soft-start capacitor yielding ~7.5 ms soft-start time.

The transformer design targets a 35% duty cycle limit (below the 50% controller limit), resulting in a 2.5 turns ratio. Primary inductance was calculated at 33 μH but 40 μH was used. Primary GaN FETs were rated 170 V (for 36 V max input), while synchronous rectifier FETs were rated 80 V, with optional parallel Schottky diodes to reduce reverse conduction losses.

An RCD clamp limits switch node overshoot. The output inductor was 0.47 μH (40% ripple target), and output capacitance required at least 1.3 mF, though 2.3 mF (7 × 330-μF polymer tantalum) was used to mitigate radiation-induced single event transients. An optional secondary LC filter can further reduce ripple.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting triggers at ~35 A using a 7.5-Ω RCS resistor with a 1:100 current sense transformer. A 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor was used. Type 2A compensation (RCOMP = 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP = 15 nF, CHF = 47 pF) targets a 10 kHz crossover, with slope compensation set via a 102 kΩ resistor on RSC.

Layout guidelines emphasize separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switch node copper area, routing feedback traces away from magnetics, placing bypass capacitors close to the controller, and using wide traces for high-current paths. The controller operates from a 4–14 V supply requiring at least 0.1 µF ceramic bypass capacitance.

Pragyan '18, held from March 1, 2018, was inaugurated at Barn Hall with aerospace engineer Dr BN Suresh as Chief Guest. The four-day fest featured guest lectures by speakers including Casey Handmer, Meher Pudumjee, Shivshankar Menon, Kevin Grazier, and Robert Metcalfe, along with workshops on deep learning and armoured fighting vehicles. The 2025 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine was awarded to Shimon Sakaguchi, Mary Brunkow, and Fred Ramsdell for their discoveries regarding regulatory T cells (T-regs), which prevent the immune system from attacking the body. Sakaguchi identified T-regs in 1995, while Brunkow and Ramsdell discovered a mutation causing fatal autoimmune disease in mice, later linked to similar disorders in humans in 2001. Research on T-regs is now being applied to treat autoimmune diseases, cancer, and other immune-related conditions. The prize is worth over $1.1 million.

The defendant moved to dismiss a bigamy indictment, arguing his second marriage was void under subdivision 5 of section 11 of the Domestic Relations Law because it was performed by a Justice of the Peace when he was 19 years old. Grand Jury minutes showed the defendant's first marriage in 1954 was still valid when he married a second time in 1955, and he admitted both marriages upon arrest.

The court examined conflicting case law on whether subdivision 5 merely prohibits a Justice of the Peace from solemnizing such marriages or renders them void. Caplan v. Caplan and De Martino v. De Martino held such marriages invalid, while Andrews v. Andrews and Graves v. Graves held the prohibition affected only the officer, not marriage validity.

Favoring the reasoning in Caplan and De Martino, the court granted the motion to dismiss the indictment.

Christmas Day became a US federal holiday in 1870 and is not a trading day, though surrounding days may be, depending on the weekday. Backtests confirm a Santa Claus rally in stocks, with the second half of December showing strong performance.

Testing the S&P 500 from 1960 onward produced 0.7% per trade, a 66% win ratio, and a profit factor of 2. Extending the holding period improved results to 1.6% per trade with a 72% win ratio. Entering after December 20th and exiting on the first trading day of the new year yielded 1% average gain and a 67% win ratio.

Possible causes include mutual fund rebalancing, limited macro news, and holiday optimism, alongside the turn-of-the-month effect.

European indices also showed the effect: EWG (German stocks) produced 2.1% per trade with an 81% win ratio, while Euro Stoxx 50 (FEZ) gained 1.5% per trade. Emerging Markets (FEMKX) showed 2.7% per trade, and India's NIFTY 50 showed 1.2% per trade, though recent returns have weakened across markets.

The University of Maine cancelled its annual American Floating Offshore Wind Technical Summit (AFLOAT), which its Advanced Structures and Composites Center had hosted since 2020, citing changing federal policies and priorities. While Maine's state energy plan includes offshore wind as central to renewable energy goals, the Trump administration suspended a $12.5 million grant to the university's floating offshore wind program this spring, though the university proceeded with launching an experimental floating wind turbine. The university has no plans to revive AFLOAT but intends to hold private meetings with industry, research, and government leaders regarding its technology.

Darfon America Corp. is presenting upgraded energy storage products at Intersolar North America 2018, including the H200 and H300 hybrid energy storage systems and the H5001 hybrid inverter. The H200 now offers Panasonic LNMC and Dragonfly LFP battery options, relocated wiring terminals, and expanded battery storage up to 30kWh. The H300, a wall-mounted solution, is now available in a 10kWh configuration. The H5001 features a lockable distribution box, lockable external PV disconnect, laser-cut conduit knockouts, and an easier-to-remove access cover. All three models have upgraded fans for temperature control, improved in-rush overload handling on 120V circuits, and an optional generator start-up kit.

Drew Doughty commented on his team's performance in a series, stating they are not discouraged despite being down, having faced adversity against top conference teams earlier. He noted the opponent is executing better, requiring adjustments. Doughty emphasized crashing the net to score on rebounds against an aggressive goalie, and said goals will come from persistent chances. He acknowledged players were distracted by family and the Cup's presence in earlier games, but the coach has refocused the team. Doughty expressed confidence despite recent losses, citing adrenaline and motivation. He also praised his strong on- and off-ice relationship with defense partner Rob, highlighting communication as key to their success.

The Federal Reserve raised short-term interest rates by a quarter point, its third hike since December, placing the key rate between 1% and 1.25%. Fed chair Janet Yellen cited economic progress, and the Fed upgraded its forecasts for U.S. growth and unemployment. Unemployment fell to 4.3% in May, the lowest since 2001, though inflation projections were lowered to 1.6%. The Fed also plans to begin selling off $10 billion monthly from its $4.5 trillion in holdings later this year. Most Fed officials anticipate at least one more rate hike in 2017. Mortgage rates are not expected to rise immediately.

The speaker expresses excitement about playing in their hometown but emphasizes treating it like any other road game to stay focused on finishing the job. They credit their team's strong performance for their confidence at the net and avoid overthinking during play. They note being surrounded by supportive teammates and enjoying the experience.

The ARM Cortex-A8 Subsystem integrates the ARM Cortex-A8 processor, targeted at multi-tasking applications requiring memory management, high performance, low die size, and low power. It features a Harvard architecture with NEON SIMD, VFPv3 coprocessor, separate L1 instruction/data caches, and a 128-bit interconnector. It supports ARM debug architecture and connects to an Embedded Trace Buffer with 32KB memory. The AINTC prioritizes service requests and generates IRQ or FIQ interrupts, though General-Purpose devices do not support FIQ generation. A PLL Controller generates subsystem clocks, and the processor connects to a 128-bit DMM port for DDR access and a 64-bit L3 interconnect port for other modules.

The DSP Subsystem features a C674x CPU combining C64x+ performance with C67x+ floating-point capabilities, including eight functional units, two register files with 32 32-bit registers each, 32KB L1 program cache with EDC, and 256KB unified L2 with ECC. Enhancements include SPLOOP, compact instructions, exception handling, privilege modes, and a time-stamp counter.

The System MMU remaps C674x MDMA accesses to physical addresses, protecting ARM memory regions. The device also includes a Media Controller managing HDVPSS and ISS, an HDVICP2 video encoder/decoder supporting multiple codec standards, a Face Detection module for QVGA images, a Spinlock module with 128 hardware semaphores, and a Mailbox module for inter-processor communication with four-message FIFO queues.

The device uses a unified memory map across bus masters, with separate L3, C674x DSP, L4 Fast, and L4 Slow peripheral memory maps, plus TILER extended addressing. Terminal function tables describe pin multiplexing, types, internal pull resistors, supply voltages, and functions for boot configuration, camera interface, DCAN, DDR2/DDR3 controllers, EMAC, GPIO banks, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, reset/JTAG, SD/MMC, SPI, oscillator/PLL, timers, UART, USB, video input/output, and power supplies.

Volkswagen's U.S. unit has asked a Virginia judge to delay consumer fraud trials over diesel emissions cheating for at least six months, arguing that comments by Michael Melkersen, a lawyer representing over 300 VW diesel owners, would prejudice juries. In a Netflix documentary, Melkersen criticized VW-sponsored tests exposing monkeys to diesel fumes and alluded to Hitler and the Holocaust. VW's lawyers said linking the company to Hitler is irrelevant to consumer fraud claims. Melkersen dismissed the motion as a delay tactic. VW has agreed to spend over $25 billion in the U.S. to address emissions claims, though about 2,000 owners opted out of the 2016 settlement and are pursuing additional compensation. The first trial was scheduled for February 26.

President Madison returns the bill "An act to set apart and pledge certain funds for internal improvements" to the House of Representatives unsigned, citing its incompatibility with the Constitution. He argues the power to fund roads, canals, and waterway navigation is not among Congress's enumerated powers in Article I, Section 8, nor justified by the "necessary and proper" clause. He rejects interpreting the commerce clause or the "common defense and general welfare" clause to authorize such projects, warning this would render enumerated powers meaningless, grant Congress unlimited legislative authority, override state laws, and exclude judicial review. State consent cannot supply the missing power. While acknowledging the potential benefits of internal improvements, Madison insists the proper remedy is constitutional amendment.

NATO's 2017 annual report indicates upward trends for the alliance, according to Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg. In response to Russian actions, NATO deployed four multinational battle groups to the Baltic states and Poland, increased its presence in the Black Sea region, strengthened cyber defenses, and welcomed Montenegro as its 29th member. Since the 2014 Wales summit, European and Canadian defense spending has risen for three consecutive years, totaling $46 billion, with $18 billion spent on major equipment. NATO deployments grew from 18,000 troops in 2014 to over 23,000 by end of 2017.

Stoltenberg condemned the nerve agent attack in Salisbury, attributed to Russia, calling it the first offensive use of a nerve agent on alliance territory. He cited a pattern of Russian aggression, including actions in Georgia, Crimea, and Eastern Ukraine, along with election interference and nuclear modernization. While rejecting a new Cold War, he affirmed NATO would maintain conventional and nuclear deterrence.

NATO's Resolute Support mission in Afghanistan expanded from 13,000 to approximately 16,000 personnel, and the alliance supports Afghan-led peace efforts. NATO also joined the anti-ISIS coalition, training Iraqi forces and planning a new training mission in Iraq, with expanded support for Jordan and Tunisia.

Scalping is a trading style aiming to profit from small price changes within very short time frames, from seconds to minutes. The article argues scalping is a waste of time because most scalpers lose money. Scalpers compete against better-equipped participants like banks, hedge funds, and high-frequency traders who have superior software, capital, and proximity to exchanges.

Profitable scalping opportunities are rare, and most strategies shared online are anecdotal rather than backtested. Backtests on short time frames are unreliable due to noise, randomness, and underestimated transaction costs. Commissions and especially slippage erode theoretical profits, and free commissions often encourage overtrading.

Scalping also causes significant stress and requires automation, which introduces risks like execution errors. One real-world example describes a trader who invested heavily in infrastructure but was outpaced by faster competitors and eventually quit.

The author recommends focusing on longer time frames, where profit potential per trade is greater and backtests are more robust. Stocks and indices are considered easier markets than forex. Long-term investing in mutual funds is suggested as a more reliable alternative for most people.

MAX phases are ternary compounds (Mn+1AXn) combining metallic and ceramic properties, with applications in high-temperature coatings, catalysis, and as MXene precursors. Out-of-plane ordered o-MAX phases exhibit superior mechanical performance. This study uses DFT calculations (CASTEP code with GGA-PBE and GGA-PBEsol functionals) to investigate three novel o-MAX phases, Mo2A2AlC3 (A = Zr, Nb, Ta), examining their structural, electronic, mechanical, thermodynamic, and optical properties.

The compounds crystallize in a hexagonal P6₃/mmc structure and demonstrate chemical, dynamic, and mechanical stability, confirmed by negative formation energies, positive phonon frequencies, and satisfied elastic stability criteria. Electronic analysis reveals metallic behavior with mixed ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding, dominated by Mo-4d states. The materials are brittle and anisotropic, with Vickers hardness values of 6.02–6.27 GPa. Mo2Nb2AlC3 shows the highest stiffness and crack resistance, while Mo2Zr2AlC3 exhibits higher damage tolerance.

Thermal properties include Debye temperatures of 525–634 K, low minimum thermal conductivities (0.74–0.90 W/m·K), melting temperatures of 2064–2237 K, and thermal expansion coefficients of 9.90–11.47 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹, suggesting suitability as thermal barrier coatings. Reflectivity exceeds 44% across IR, visible, and mid-UV ranges, indicating potential for solar heat-shielding applications.

Becton, Dickinson and Company (NYSE:BDX) has paid dividends since 1962, with 12 of the past 13 years showing double-digit dividend growth averaging 16.3% since 2004. The company projects 2017 GAAP diluted EPS of $7.90 to $8.00, a 78% increase over 2016, partly due to a favorable antitrust ruling in Q1 2017. The 2015 $12.2 billion CareFusion merger temporarily reduced profit margins through 2016 due to acquisition costs and higher interest expenses, but 2017 is expected to approach record profits. The dividend payout ratio fell to 59% of GAAP diluted EPS in 2016 and could drop to 37% in 2017. Risks include manufacturing issues, rising interest rates, and competing products. The author is long BDX.

QuantifiedStrategies.com offers trading resources including backtested strategies, articles, videos, and courses. The site covers topics such as trading strategies, indicators, backtesting, seasonal strategies, risk management, trading psychology, and candlestick patterns. Content emphasizes data-driven analysis using numbers, facts, and statistics rather than opinions. Resources include over a thousand free articles, daily YouTube videos, trading courses for beginners, and customer testimonials.

Celtic's victory at Ibrox demonstrated their superiority over Rangers, according to the author. Celtic have accumulated significant Champions League revenue and stand to gain more from future player sales like Moussa Dembele. The article criticises Rangers chairman Dave King for failing to deliver on promises of £30million in transfer spending, leaving manager Mark Warburton without adequate backing. Warburton's signings, including Joey Barton and Joe Garner, are described as disappointing, while Rangers rely heavily on veteran players Clint Hill (38) and Kenny Miller (37). The author suggests Rangers' Scottish Cup semi-final win last season prompted Celtic owner Dermot Desmond to implement major changes, leading to the signings of Dembele and Scott Sinclair. Manager Brendan Rodgers is urged to strengthen the squad further to compete in Europe, as previously achieved under Martin O'Neill. The author argues Celtic should use their financial advantage to distance themselves permanently from Rangers, an opportunity missed when Rangers went bust in 2012.

This paper examines how generative AI can be ethically integrated into educational contexts, drawing on philosophical traditions to propose a practical framework for classroom use.

The authors review key philosophical perspectives: Gunther Anders's concept of "Promethean discrepancy"—the gap between what technology can produce and what humans can comprehend—and his call for critical reflection on technology's role in shaping humanity. Michel Foucault's "regimes of truth" is applied to analyze how AI-driven corporations influence knowledge and epistemology, particularly given AI's documented hallucinations, biases, and inconsistencies across platforms like ChatGPT and Gemini. Paulo Freire's concepts of humanization and conscientization are presented as ethical guides, suggesting technology can benefit learners if used critically to promote dialogue and agency.

The paper combines Bloom's Revised Taxonomy (RBT) with Hannah Arendt's hierarchy of labor, work, and action. While RBT helps classify cognitive tasks AI can perform, the authors argue it is insufficient for addressing ethical concerns. Arendt's framework adds directionality, prioritizing "action"—meaningful human engagement in public life—over mere labor and consumption.

The resulting framework presents a spectrum from consumptive labor to humanizing action, helping educators assess whether AI use promotes meaningful learning or merely replaces human thought. The authors provide guiding questions and two sample lesson applications—community-based political action and Socratic dialogue for individualized research—demonstrating how AI can streamline labor while students focus on evaluation, personal perspective, and community engagement.

The authors conclude that AI is permanently embedded in education and requires reimagining pedagogy to foster student agency and humanization, calling for further research into ethical gray areas.

The application describes methods and apparatus for handling reduced processing time in low-latency cellular systems using configurable or short transmission time intervals (sTTIs). A wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) determines its processing capabilities (PC), reports them to an eNodeB, receives a PC configuration, and limits applied timing advance or Rx-Tx time difference based on TTI length.

The WTRU may measure a processing value, calculate headroom relative to its PC, and report it conditionally. Processing capabilities can include timing advance limits, Rx-Tx time difference limits, processing time, TTI length, transport block size, or scheduling/HARQ timelines, determined from criteria such as TTI length, symbol count, TBS, channel type, or transmission parameters.

For uplink grants, the WTRU determines available processing time between the end of downlink control information and the start of scheduled transmission, transmitting only if processing time meets a threshold based on its PC. Similarly, for HARQ-ACK feedback on downlink transmissions, the WTRU determines start time and available processing time before transmitting.

The application also addresses exception handling when processing capabilities are exceeded, including capping values, suspending or dropping transmissions, flushing HARQ buffers, or sending error reports. Embodiments are applicable across LTE, LTE-A, NR, and related radio access technologies within described WTRU, RAN, and core network architectures.
