Jimmie Johnson's longtime sponsor Lowe's announced in March it will leave NASCAR after 18 seasons, creating what Johnson calls a "golden opportunity" for a replacement sponsor of the No. 48 Hendrick Motorsports team. Johnson, 42, indicated he has "a handful of years" left in Cup racing and suggested the new sponsor could accompany him to the end of his career. Beyond NASCAR, Johnson expressed interest in racing the 24 Hours of Le Mans, the Rolex 24 at Daytona, and possibly the Indianapolis 500 if IndyCar adopts Formula One's halo cockpit protection.

The 5-Day Low Overnight Trading Strategy targets the S&P 500 when it opens at a 5-day low but closes higher than the open. Traders enter at the close and exit at the next day's open.

Overnight trading in the S&P 500 historically yields an average return of 0.04% from close to next-day open, supporting mean reversion strategies. Testing from 2005 onward, the strategy produced an average profit of 15.93% and 0.26% per trade, or 0.17% excluding the largest winner (6% in October 2008). Backtesting used the SPY ETF from 1993 to the present.

The disclosure presents an image processing method, apparatus, electronic device, and computer-readable storage medium for placing objects such as advertisements into videos.

The method involves obtaining a to-be-processed video containing m frames (m≥2), placing a target three-dimensional model (e.g., a cube) on a target plane of the first frame such that feature points of the model surface fall on the target plane. Three-dimensional coordinates of these feature points in a world coordinate system and their pixel coordinates on the first frame are determined. Using these coordinates, the pose of the camera coordinate system relative to the world coordinate system is calculated for the first frame. For subsequent frames (second through m-th), poses are determined by tracking the target plane and computing homography matrices relative to the first frame. The target three-dimensional model is then replaced with a target model (e.g., a three-dimensional advertisement), which is projected onto each frame to generate the target video.

The target plane may be identified using a neural network model (such as Mask R-CNN) trained on labeled sample pictures, or selected manually. The model's pose can be adjusted by dragging vertices, rotating, sliding, or tilting, or automatically via AI. The camera intrinsic parameter may be obtained through deep learning if unknown, and the PnP algorithm may be used to calculate camera pose.

The approach does not rely on feature point calculation across images or require large-parallax videos, resulting in reduced computation, faster speed, and higher accuracy. Data may be stored using blockchain technology.

New York's Excelsior Scholarship, introduced in 2017, offers tuition-free education at SUNY and CUNY schools for students from families earning under $110,000, creating challenges for private colleges competing for in-state students. The program covers only tuition ($6,670) after other aid is applied, and the state has budgeted $118 million for an estimated 27,000 students.

Highly selective private institutions like Cornell and Columbia are less affected, but smaller regional private colleges have responded with new initiatives. Canisius College launched its "Excellence Within Reach Initiative," cutting tuition by about $8,000. Roberts Wesleyan introduced a "Four-Year Promise" guaranteeing on-time graduation plus an $8,000 minimum annual merit award. Le Moyne College unveiled "Promise NY," offering a $10,000 scholarship, guaranteed four-year graduation, and internships. St. Bonaventure increased scholarships by up to $4,000 per student annually.

St. John Fisher and Nazareth College report strong recent enrollments without dramatic strategy shifts. Private college leaders suggest expanding the state's existing Tuition Assistance Program would have been preferable to Excelsior, and question the sustainability of free tuition. The Commission on Independent Colleges and Universities reports private institutions enroll about 52 percent of New York undergraduates and employ roughly 180,000 people.

Text messaging has become a dominant form of communication, with various apps offering alternatives to traditional texting. Music Messenger lets users send songs to convey moods. WhatsApp, originally an iPhone alternative to Blackberry's free international messaging, now works on any smartphone and supports video, photos, sound clips, and emoticons. Facebook Messenger integrates with Facebook and offers media sharing, HD video chats, sound bites, group chats, customizable emojis and text colors, and is free without advertising.

The Federal Reserve has proposed easing the Volcker Rule, which bars banks from making risky trading bets using depositors' money. The rule, a key part of the 2010 Dodd-Frank law, was created to prevent another financial crisis like the 2008 meltdown. The proposed changes would apply the strictest rules only to banks doing the most trading. This follows other regulatory rollbacks, including legislation signed by President Trump easing oversight for small and mid-sized banks, and reduced enforcement at the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau under Mick Mulvaney. Consumer advocates warn that weakening the rule allows banks to gamble with others' money, while industry attorneys note proprietary trading desks have largely disappeared. Fed Chairman Jerome Powell and board member Randal Quarles support improving, but not scrapping, post-crisis regulations.

Lotte Group plans to list its Malaysian petrochemical unit, Lotte Chemical Titan Holding, on Bursa Malaysia in the third quarter of 2017, according to a Korea Exchange filing by Lotte Chemical Corp. Sources say the IPO could raise $1-1.5 billion, potentially making it Malaysia's largest listing since Astro Malaysia Holdings' $1.5 billion IPO in 2012. Lotte Chemical plans to offer up to 740.48 million shares, with an over-allotment option of 55.54 million shares. Proceeds will fund a naphtha cracker in Indonesia, a polypropylene plant in Malaysia, and expansion of its Malaysian cracker facility. Originally planned for last year, the IPO was postponed amid fraud investigations into Lotte Group. Maybank Investment Bank, Credit Suisse, and J.P. Morgan are joint global coordinators, with CIMB, HSBC, and Nomura as joint bookrunners.

The offside trap is a defensive soccer maneuver in which defensive backs move upfield in unison just before an opponent passes to a leading striker, placing the striker in an offside position. If the striker receives the ball, the officials should call a violation of Law 11, awarding an indirect free kick to the defenders.

Introduced in the 1900s, the trap was widely adopted mid-century but has become riskier due to changes in offside interpretation and the rise of short-passing tactics. If the trap fails—often because a defender moves late or an attacker stands still—the goalkeeper is left exposed.

Coaches must assess whether players are mature enough to execute the trap and whether opponents are vulnerable, particularly those relying on through balls. Flat-back-four formations suit the trap better than stopper-sweeper alignments. The trap can be used during normal play or on free kicks.

All back defenders must align in a straight line parallel to the halfway line, move as one unit, and communicate constantly. Only one designated defender, typically a center-back, calls the trap using a unique verbal or non-verbal signal. Execution requires a quick three-to-five-yard sprint forward at the moment of signal.

The trap requires extensive practice, should be used sparingly to avoid predictability, and is unsuitable for unfocused defenders. Overuse leads to the saying, "Live by the trap, die by the trap."

Gary Gensler introduces an MIT lecture on the technical foundations of blockchain technology, framed through Bitcoin as its first use case. He explains that understanding blockchain requires familiarity with its core design features, even without mastering the underlying algorithms.

The lecture reviews prior material on money as a social construct and ledgers as record-keeping systems, then identifies key blockchain design features: cryptographic hash functions, timestamped append-only logs, block headers and Merkle trees, asymmetric cryptography and digital signatures, Bitcoin addresses, proof-of-work consensus, nodes, networking, a native currency, and transaction inputs/outputs.

Gensler focuses primarily on two cryptographic primitives. Hash functions map inputs of any size to fixed-size outputs, are deterministic, efficient, preimage-resistant (one-way), and collision-resistant, making data tamper-evident. Bitcoin uses SHA-256, and security is described as infeasible rather than impossible to break. Merkle trees compress thousands of transactions into a single root hash stored in block headers, which also contain the version, previous block hash, timestamp, difficulty target, and nonce.

Asymmetric cryptography uses mathematically linked public/private key pairs generated from random numbers. Digital signatures allow a sender to sign a message with a private key, which recipients verify using the corresponding public key. Bitcoin addresses are derived by hashing public keys twice for added security.

Gensler notes Stuart Haber's 1991 timestamped hash chain as a blockchain precursor, discusses Bitcoin's roughly 10-minute block time, mining economics (currently 12.5 bitcoins per block), mining pool concentration in China and Russia, and the difficulty of updating decentralized software. Upcoming lectures will cover consensus protocols and transactions.

SunPower, founded in 1987 by Stanford professor Richard Swanson, became a leading producer of high-efficiency solar cells following a 2001 partnership with Cypress Semiconductors and a 2005 IPO. By 2006, CEO Tom Werner faced strategic questions about sustaining competitive advantage in a rapidly growing solar industry.

Global interest in solar power was driven by environmental concerns, particularly rising CO2 levels and climate change warnings from the IPCC. Over 1,000 pro-solar policies worldwide, including California's Million Solar Roofs initiative and renewable portfolio standards, supported demand, though solar remained two to three times more expensive than conventional electricity.

The industry's value chain included silicon production, wafer manufacturing, cell and module production, and system installation. A silicon shortage drove prices from $32/kg in 2004 to over $200/kg on short-term contracts in 2006. Japan, Germany, and China led global production, with China surpassing the U.S. in 2006.

SunPower produced the most efficient commercial solar cells (20.7%), using a differentiated back-contact design. The company integrated across the value chain, securing silicon supply through DC Chemical, entering ingot manufacturing via a Chinese joint venture, and acquiring installer PowerLight in December 2006. Revenues grew from $6 million in 2004 to a projected $220 million in 2006.

Competitors included Sharp Solar (market leader), Q-Cells, REC Group, First Solar (thin film), SunTech, and newcomer Citizenre. Werner faced decisions about module pricing versus process improvements to maintain SunPower's advantage.

A failed North Korean missile launch on Sunday from near Sinpo may have involved a new, undeveloped system, according to weapons expert John Schilling of the 38 North monitoring group. The Pentagon has not identified the missile, while the White House described it as medium-range. Anonymous US officials told Fox News it was a new Scud variant called the KN-17. Schilling suggested it could be a design displayed at Saturday's Pyongyang military parade. Susan Thornton, acting assistant secretary of state, said the rocket's quick failure limited available information. Some observers speculated US cyber sabotage contributed to the failure, though Schilling said North Korean missile technology is too primitive to hack. Separately, Pentagon chief Jim Mattis ordered a review of America's nuclear deterrent.

The speaker discusses Jim Dowd from Brick, New Jersey, noting he played for the Brick hockey club growing up and heard about Dowd's work ethic. He describes participating as a one-time opportunity he couldn't pass up, praising the players and the exciting game, though he would have preferred overtime to a shootout. He plans to stay to prepare for his goal of playing in the NHL. He chose New Hampshire over Michigan due to proximity to home and is excited to play there next year. His father, Frans van Riemsdyk, is with him.

The lecture provides an overview of equity valuation. Equity represents ownership in a corporation, providing value through dividends (cash or stock) and capital gains. Unlike bonds, equities are residual claimants—they receive assets only after bondholders are paid—but have unlimited upside potential. Key features include limited liability, which caps losses at the amount invested and encourages entrepreneurship and innovation, along with voting rights, access to public markets, and the ability to short sell, which helps incorporate information into prices.

Equity markets consist of primary markets (new issuances) and secondary markets (trading of existing securities). Technological innovations like the internet and electronic communication networks (ECNs) have dramatically increased trading volume and reduced costs.

The Dividend Discount Model values stocks as the present value of all expected future dividends, discounted at a risk-adjusted rate. This rate reflects both the riskiness of cash flows and market conditions, and is determined by the market, not the company. Two simplifications include: the perpetuity formula (P = D/r) for constant dividends, and the Gordon growth model (P = D/(r-g)) for dividends growing at rate g, where r must exceed g for sustainability. Rearranging yields r = D/P + g, showing that required return equals dividend yield plus growth rate—highlighting that growth opportunities, not just current dividends, drive value. This helps explain phenomena like the technology bubble.

Practical application is difficult because forecasting dividends and discount rates far into the future is highly inaccurate. Companies typically avoid changing dividend policies, as cuts signal trouble, though exceptions occur during cash crunches or windfalls. Understanding the cost of capital is essential for both corporate decision-making and investor evaluation.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated analog front-end, programmable gain amplifier (PGA), second-order low-pass filter, and precision reference. Analog inputs present ≥1MΩ impedance and feature internal overvoltage protection withstanding ±20V when powered (AVDD=5V) or ±15V when AVDD is floating. External protection is recommended for surges, ESD, and EFT.

The PGA adjusts gain via RANGE_SEL[3:0] bits, supporting multiple bipolar and unipolar input ranges. The antialiasing LPF has a 500kHz cutoff. The internal 4.096V reference is factory-trimmed and temperature-compensated (–40°C to +125°C), but may shift due to solder reflow stress. An external reference option is available via the INTREF_DIS bit.

Output is in straight-binary format. Alarm features monitor input signals against programmable thresholds (with hysteresis) and AVDD against fixed 4.7V/5.3V limits, with active and tripped flags.

The device uses a multiSPI interface supporting standard SPI, daisy-chain, dual SDO, and source-synchronous protocols. It operates in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states, controlled via CONVST/CS and RST pins. Data transfers use 32-bit frames with read/write commands (byte or half-word).

Nine configuration registers control device ID, reset/power, SDI/SDO protocols, data output, range selection, and alarm thresholds. Low-power NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput. Separate AVDD and DVDD supplies require decoupling capacitors. Applications include industrial analog input modules (PLCs, DCS, DAS) measuring voltage/current inputs up to ±10V, often paired with multiplexers like the MUX36D08.

This protocol outlines a systematic review examining how Rapid Response Team (RRT) services are implemented or redesigned in hospitals, and how implementation success is measured.

RRTs, originating from the Medical Emergency Team concept introduced in 1990 at Liverpool Hospital, Australia, aim to identify and treat deteriorating patients to reduce cardiac arrests, mortality, and emergency ICU admissions. Nomenclature, team composition, funding, and calling criteria vary widely across services, with over 30 different calling criteria in use. Given this heterogeneity and lack of unifying guidance, the review aims to clarify available evidence and identify gaps.

The review will include prospective and retrospective observational cohort studies, following Cochrane Handbook recommendations and PRISMA reporting standards. Searches will be conducted across Medline, CINAHL, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar, supplemented by manual reference searches and expert contact. Non-English studies will be excluded.

Two independent reviewers will screen records via COVIDENCE, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Extracted data will cover study characteristics, team characteristics, implementation methods, and outcome assessments. Risk of bias will be assessed using the JBI critical appraisal checklist. Analysis will be primarily narrative with simple statistics.

The primary outcome is describing RRT implementation methods; secondary outcomes include reasons for change, timeframes, and success measures. Ethical approval is not required. Limitations include study heterogeneity and potentially limited available literature on service implementation.

Asia-Pacific equities extended gains in April, driven by increased risk appetite following French election results, reduced North Korea concerns, and strong Q1 earnings. MSCI's Asia-Pacific index (excluding Japan) neared a two-year high, up over 15 percent year-to-date. Indian stocks led with 20 percent gains, while Chinese stocks trailed at 2.5 percent. New Zealand and Indian equities had the highest valuations, while South Korean and Hong Kong stocks were cheapest. Samsung Electronics, CITIC Securities, and TSMC reported strong first-quarter results.

Enron Corp. replaced Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow with Jeff McMahon, former treasurer and head of Enron's industrial markets group, after the company's stock fell 17% to $16.41 on October 24, 2001. CEO Kenneth Lay stated the change was necessary to restore investor confidence, reversing his prior-day defense of Fastow.

The shake-up followed a Securities and Exchange Commission informal inquiry into two partnerships, LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment, run by Fastow, which cost Enron $35 million in third-quarter losses and led to a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. Reports indicated McMahon had previously raised concerns about conflicts of interest regarding Fastow's partnership role while serving as treasurer.

Enron shares had fallen roughly 50% over the previous week, dragging down stocks of other energy-trading companies, including Dynegy and Aquila. Prudential Securities analyst Carol Coale downgraded Enron to "sell," and Banc of America cut its rating to "market perform." Analysts remained concerned about undisclosed liabilities, potential credit downgrades, possible equity dilution, and other off-balance-sheet partnerships such as Marlin and Whitewing. Shareholder lawsuits, including one alleging insider trading by executives, were filed against the company.

Containerization is an intermodal transportation process where goods remain in containers during transit, and it is also performed by air for faster delivery. Commercial airlines and military forces use custom-made containers, carried on lower decks of passenger aircrafts and both decks of cargo aircrafts. Market growth is driven by demand for rapid global transportation and technological advancements producing lightweight containers compliant with IATA standards. Restraints include the global economic slowdown, reduced GDP in regions like Asia Pacific, Latin America, and the Middle East, and rising aviation fuel costs limiting cargo flight hours. Future opportunities stem from increasing commercial airlines and defense sector demand. The market is segmented by container type (refrigerated and non-refrigerated), aircraft type (narrow body, wide body, very large, military), end user (commercial airlines and defense forces), and geography. Major vendors include Nordisk Aviation Products, Zodiac Aerospace, VRR Aviation, Satco, Cargo Composites, Granger Aerospace, Chicago Metal Fabricators, PalNet GmbH, ACL Airshop, and DoKaSch Temperature Solutions.

China's former one-child policy led families to spoil children and prioritize academic grades over moral and character development, creating societal problems. To improve family education, several approaches are suggested. First, education should liberate children's individuality rather than stifle them through examination-oriented discipline, as surveys show many Chinese children lack life skills and suffer emotional issues. Second, children should be taught to give unselfishly rather than focus solely on high marks. Third, connecting with nature benefits psychological well-being. Fourth, moral behavior education should take precedence over scientific knowledge, as illustrated by the Yao Jiaxin case; traditional Chinese moral teachings emphasizing virtue, filial piety, and unity of knowing and practicing remain valuable. Fifth, joint parent-child activities such as outings, travel, and entertainment help bridge generation gaps. Sixth, religious beliefs, particularly Buddhism, provide values and standards for distinguishing right from wrong. Finally, mothers' status and conduct significantly influence children, so women's role in family education deserves attention. Overall, family education should integrate morality, humanity, parental guidance, and traditional moral wisdom.

A comprehensive geoarchaeological study of Egypt's Karnak Temple complex near Luxor, led by Dr. Angus Graham of Uppsala University with researchers from the University of Southampton, has provided new insights into the site's 3,000-year history. The team analyzed 61 sediment cores and thousands of ceramic fragments to map landscape changes around the temple.

Findings indicate the site was uninhabitable before approximately 2520 BCE due to Nile flooding, placing the earliest occupation in the Old Kingdom period (2591-2152 BC). Karnak was founded on an island of high ground formed as river channels cut beds to the east and west. Researchers discovered the eastern channel was more defined than previously assumed. Over time, diverging channels created space for expansion, and Egyptians reshaped the river by dumping desert sand to create building land.

The team suggests the temple's location may reflect an Egyptian creation myth in which a creator god emerged as high ground from primeval waters. Further research is planned across the Luxor floodplain.

Microsoft's voice assistant Cortana, comparable to Apple's Siri, has evolved with Windows 10 updates. It is now compatible with desktops, laptops, and tablets, and works alongside the Edge browser. Cortana can locate files across hard drives and cloud storage, and some manufacturers offer dedicated activation buttons. Originally exclusive to Windows, Cortana is now available on Android and iOS, though less efficiently. It features personalized voice recognition, can tell jokes and sing, and provides location-based reminders.

The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card is a no-annual-fee credit card designed for people seeking to pay down debt or finance large purchases. Its primary benefit is a 0% intro APR for 21 months from account opening on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, with a variable APR of 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74% applying thereafter.

The card requires a good to excellent credit score (670-850) for consideration. Additional features include up to $600 in cell phone protection against damage or theft (subject to a $25 deductible, usable twice yearly) when the monthly phone bill is paid with the card, and access to personalized merchant deals through My Wells Fargo Deals.

Drawbacks include the lack of ongoing rewards after the intro period, a 5% balance transfer fee (minimum $5), and a 3% foreign transaction fee. Applying involves submitting personal and financial details and awaiting approval. The card received Motley Fool Money's Best 0% Intro APR Card of 2025 award.

Former Ford CEO Mark Fields stated that US automakers overestimated consumer demand and "went full bore" into EV production without adequately considering what would drive consumers to buy them. The TPS7H500x-SP controllers are radiation-hardened PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. Output voltage is set via a resistor divider to VSENSE, referenced to 0.613 V. A soft-start capacitor controls startup timing using a 2.7 µA charging current.

The controllers support three switching frequency modes (100 kHz–2 MHz): internal oscillator (set by RT resistor), external synchronization (clock applied to SYNC at twice the switching frequency), and primary-secondary mode for synchronizing two controllers.

Devices include primary outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) with ~150 mA peak drive capability, requiring external gate drivers. Programmable dead times, leading-edge blank times, and duty cycle limits (50%, 75%, or 100%) are available depending on device variant. Pulse skipping prevents issues from minimum on-time during high-frequency operation.

Protection features include cycle-by-cycle current limiting via CS_ILIM (1.05 V threshold), hiccup mode controlled by a HICC capacitor, external fault input (FAULT pin), and thermal shutdown at 175°C. Slope compensation is set via an RSC resistor to prevent subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle.

A transconductance error amplifier supports Type 2A or 2B compensation. A design example demonstrates a 500 kHz synchronous push-pull converter with 5 V output using GaN FETs, detailing transformer, inductor, capacitor, and compensation component selection. Layout guidelines emphasize minimizing noise coupling, separating analog and power grounds, and placing bypass capacitors close to the controller.

The article tests trend following and momentum strategies on Bitcoin (BTC-USD) using free Yahoo Finance data from 2015 to April 2021, excluding commissions, slippage, and taxes.

Bitcoin's volatility and large price swings resemble commodities markets, making it suitable for trend following and momentum strategies. Although Bitcoin has suffered drawdowns up to 82%—comparable to the Nasdaq after the dot-com bubble—it has historically recovered more quickly.

Three strategies were tested:
1. A short 20-day exponential moving average, with optimization showing best results using five days (CAGR of 145%).
2. Two simple moving averages (100-day and 250-day crossover), producing a CAGR of 115% versus 94% for buy and hold, with a 65% max drawdown.
3. A momentum strategy comparing the close price to 25 days prior, which also beat buy and hold despite a low win ratio.

All three strategies outperformed buy-and-hold (HODL) while reducing drawdowns. The author concludes these strategies should continue working as long as Bitcoin remains volatile, and notes that logarithmic charts are necessary when analyzing such high-growth assets.

Engineers at UC San Diego have developed ultrasound-powered nanorobots capable of removing bacteria and toxins from blood. The nanorobots consist of gold nanowires coated with a hybrid of platelet and red blood cell membranes, enabling them to bind pathogens like MRSA and neutralize their toxins simultaneously. The gold body responds to ultrasound, allowing rapid movement without chemical fuel, while the membrane coating prevents biofouling.

The technology combines work from Joseph Wang's team, which developed the ultrasound-powered nanorobots, and Liangfang Zhang's team, which created the cell membrane coating method. The nanorobots, 25 times smaller than a human hair, travel up to 35 micrometers per second in blood. In tests, blood samples contaminated with MRSA showed three times less bacteria and toxins after five minutes of treatment.

The research, published in Science Robotics, is at an early stage. Future plans include testing in live animals and replacing gold with biodegradable materials. The ultimate goal is general detoxification of biological fluids rather than treating specific infections.

In Oxley et al. v. Oldden, the case had been referred, and the referees examined evidence with both parties present and agreed upon their report, signing it the day before delivery to court. About an hour before the report was delivered, the defendant obtained a rule to show cause why the reference should not be stricken. No irregularity or partiality was alleged against the referees. After argument, the rule was discharged. Chief Justice McKean stated the motion was too late, as the referees had investigated the matter, agreed on their report, and faced no imputation of misconduct or refusal to hear testimony.

Katalin Karikó won the 2023 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine for her mRNA research, joining an elite group of laureates. Named for Alfred Nobel, the prizes were first awarded in 1901 and quickly gained worldwide prestige. However, the Nobels recognize only narrow areas of science, excluding fields like ecology, oceanography, climate and geology. Prizes are limited to three recipients, leaving many collaborators unrecognized.

Winners are predominantly white men from wealthy regions, particularly the United States and Western Europe. Only 13 women have received the physiology or medicine prize, and just one Black scientist, W. Arthur Lewis, has won a science-related Nobel. Sociologist Harriet Zuckerman notes that women and people of color face barriers to reaching prize-worthy positions. Nominations also typically take decades.

Victor Ambros, 2024 co-winner for microRNA discoveries, noted his wife and lab partner Rosalind Lee contributed equally but was excluded. The Nobel Foundation is bound by Alfred Nobel's will, limiting changes. Despite criticisms, supporters argue the prize valuably celebrates and publicizes science.

The application is a continuation of prior U.S. applications and claims priority to multiple provisional applications filed in 2017 and 2018 related to deep learning-based splice site classification and aberrant splicing detection using convolutional neural networks. Numerous PCT and U.S. patent applications and thirteen technical documents describing neural network architectures are incorporated by reference.

The disclosed technology relates to artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep convolutional neural networks for genomic analysis. It uses atrous (dilated) convolutions, which apply kernels over areas larger than their length by skipping input values according to a dilation factor, enabling large receptive fields with few parameters and incorporation of long-range contextual dependencies.

The technology trains an atrous convolutional neural network (ACNN), termed "SpliceNet," on at least 50,000 donor splice site examples, 50,000 acceptor splice site examples, and 100,000 non-splicing site examples, with target nucleotides flanked by context nucleotides. Variants include SpliceNet80, SpliceNet400, SpliceNet2000, and SpliceNet10000, differing in flanking context length (40 to 5000 nucleotides on each side), groups of residual blocks, convolution window sizes, and atrous convolution rates. Unlike prior architectures, atrous convolution rates progress non-exponentially and window sizes vary between residual block groups.

The ACNN outputs triplet scores classifying each nucleotide as donor splice site, acceptor splice site, or non-splicing site. For aberrant splicing detection, reference and variant sequences are processed through the ACNN, and differences in splice site scores are compared position-wise. When differences exceed a predetermined threshold, the variant is classified as causing aberrant splicing and therefore pathogenic. Applications include identifying variants causing autism spectrum disorder and developmental delay disorder.

The system may be deployed across training and production servers, uses one-hot encoding of sequences, and may alternatively be implemented using a standard convolutional neural network (CNN) with similar training examples and classification functions.

Kickers are specialized football players responsible primarily for kicking extra points and field goals, with NFL expectations of roughly 80% accuracy on field goals and 90% on 33-yard extra points. They also handle kickoffs, aiming for touchbacks or directional kicks, and execute situational plays like onside kicks. Typically smaller and slimmer than other players (5'10"-6'2", 180-210 pounds), kickers require accuracy, lower body power, consistent technique, and flexibility. Notable kickers include Justin Tucker (most accurate all-time, holds 66-yard field goal record), Morten Andersen (2nd all-time in field goals, HOF 2017), and Adam Vinatieri (all-time leading scorer with 2,673 points). Kickers significantly influence coaching decisions and game outcomes, particularly in close games, making them a valued specialty despite typically receiving minimal pay and recognition.

North Carolina regulators are considering testing backyard garden vegetables near a Chemours plant in Fayetteville for GenX, an industrial compound produced at the facility for years, state waste management director Michael Scott announced. The discussions follow a Dutch study that found GenX and related chemicals in about 40 percent of food samples collected within 2.5 miles of a Chemours factory in the Netherlands, though the crops were deemed safe to eat. North Carolina agencies have not yet decided whether or how to test gardens, with initial focus on home gardens in response to neighbor concerns about health risks. Fish tests from nearby waterways are expected within months. GenX, used since 2009 to replace PFOA, has shown toxic effects in animals, but its effects on humans are unknown, and no federal health standards exist. The chemical has been detected in drinking water serving 200,000 people in Wilmington, 100 miles downstream. Chemours did not respond to requests for comment.

High-κ materials are critical for electronic and energy storage devices, with HfO₂ currently favored over SiO₂ and perovskite oxides, though limitations remain. Machine learning (ML) offers promise for discovering new materials, but prediction accuracy for ionic dielectric constants (εion) has been poor.

This work develops a high-accuracy ML framework that separately predicts Born effective charges (BECs) using an E(3)-equivariant graph neural network (EGNN) and phonon properties using pretrained machine learning potentials (MLPs), then analytically combines them via the standard εion equation. Trained on 928 oxides spanning 45 elements, the BEC model achieved R² = 0.982. Among four MLPs tested, SevenNet-MF-ompa performed best. The joint model (R² = 0.843) significantly outperformed direct prediction (R² = 0.418).

Virtual screening of 8,717 oxides from the Materials Project database identified 38 novel high-κ oxides with figure of merit (FoMDDH) ≥ 350, a fourfold increase over the training set. Twelve candidates surpassed KTaO₃, the best training oxide. Ten identified oxides have been experimentally synthesized, with five showing confirmed high dielectric constants. Most candidates contain d⁰ transition metals (Ti⁴⁺, Zr⁴⁺, Nb⁵⁺, Ta⁵⁺, etc.) and feature oxygen octahedral networks such as perovskite-related frameworks. LiBi₄Nb₃O₁₄ and LaYO₃ are highlighted as experimentally accessible, unexplored candidates. Future directions include extending to non-oxides and incorporating finite-temperature effects.

The higher highs and higher lows pattern signals an uptrend, but backtesting across three asset classes (S&P 500, gold, and long-term Treasuries) suggests weak short-term gains following the pattern.

The strategy entered trades after two consecutive daily bars showing higher highs and higher lows, exiting after 1-10 bars. In the S&P 500, returns were minimal, with a two-week average gain of 0.23%, about half of random two-week returns. Gold showed similarly poor returns, underperforming random periods. Long-term Treasuries produced negative short-term returns despite a favorable interest rate environment.

Extending the pattern to three or four consecutive days did not improve results, and the pattern also failed as a short strategy. The findings indicate it functions as a short-term reversal pattern but is not strong enough to serve as a standalone trading signal.

Scoring combines judges' input and audience votes equally. Judges Derek Hough, Carrie Ann Inaba, and Bruno Tonioli each award 1–10 points, totaling up to 30. Each couple's score is converted into a Judges' Score Percentage, calculated against the night's total points. Audience votes are similarly converted into a Public Vote Percentage, then combined with the judges' percentage.

Viewers can vote online via ABC's website, the Disney+ app, or text message during the live ET/CT simulcast, typically from 8:00 p.m. ET until after the final dance. NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture and fabricated on TSMC's 7nm process, is NVIDIA's 8th generation data center GPU featuring 54.2 billion transistors and 108 SMs. It delivers significant performance improvements over the Tesla V100 for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads.

Key features include third-generation Tensor Cores supporting new data types (TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, Binary) with up to 2.5x mixed-precision performance over V100, and a new Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity feature that doubles throughput. The A100 includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth and a 40 MB L2 cache (nearly 7x larger than V100).

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology allows partitioning a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, benefiting Cloud Service Providers with improved utilization and fault isolation. Third-generation NVLink doubles signaling rates and provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth via 12 links. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, improved error detection, asynchronous copy/barriers, task graph acceleration, L2 cache residency controls, hardware JPEG decode (NVJPG), five NVDEC units, and an optical flow accelerator.

The NVIDIA DGX A100 system combines eight A100 GPUs via six NVSwitches, delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and supporting up to 56 MIG instances, serving as a building block for large-scale AI infrastructure like DGX SuperPOD.

Medora Brown, appointed communications manager at Sanergy in April 2015, faced the task of developing a social media strategy for the Kenya-based sanitation company. Sanergy, founded in 2011 by three MIT Sloan MBA students, addressed Kenya's sanitation crisis through its non-profit Fresh Life brand, which franchised hygienic toilets in Nairobi slums, and its for-profit Farm Star brand, which converted human waste into Evergrow organic fertilizer.

By 2015, Fresh Life had franchised 615 toilets serving 32,000 people, with a goal of 36,000 toilets by 2020. Farm Star sold 118 tons of fertilizer in 2015, aiming for 2,000 tons annually by 2018.

Kenya, known as "Silicon Savannah," had a growing middle class, 55% internet penetration, 82% mobile phone penetration, and rising social media usage—primarily on Facebook, Twitter, and LinkedIn. However, slum dwellers and franchisees rarely used social media, and Kenyan culture emphasized trust built through personal contact.

Brown needed to craft strategies for three brands with distinct audiences: Fresh Life (entrepreneurs and slum customers), Farm Star (farmers, where early Facebook efforts generated leads at $7 each), and Sanergy corporate (investors and donors). She had to determine appropriate platforms, create efficient content workflows, and measure social media's ROI, while questioning whether social media could build the trust Kenyan business relationships required.

University of Edinburgh researchers analyzed DNA from over 52,000 middle-aged men in the UK BioBank study and identified 287 genetic signals linked to male pattern baldness, publishing their findings in PLoS Genetics. Notably, 40 of these genes were found on the X chromosome, which men inherit from their mothers. Participants were categorized by hair loss severity, and those with more baldness-related genes were more likely to experience hair loss, though predictions remain imprecise. Among men with the top 10 percent of baldness genes, 58 percent had some hair loss. Researchers say the findings improve understanding of hair loss genetics but do not yet allow accurate individual predictions.

Mercy University's School of Education has received several grants to enhance educator preparation and support diverse learners.

The GRAD-PRO Grant, a 5-year, $2.8 million award from the U.S. Department of Education (2023), supports Hispanic and underrepresented graduate students across health sciences, education, business, and faculty mentoring. It has hosted events on mental well-being in schools and established a Faculty Mentoring Fellowship.

The BRANCH-ED Grant (2023), a three-year award, focuses on strengthening teacher preparation through district partnerships, curriculum reviews, and biweekly coaching. Mercy achieved a 100% success rate in Year 1, becoming the first institution to complete the Transformation Center process with such distinction.

The MISTI Program, funded by the NSF since 2013, prepares science and math teachers for high-need middle and high schools through observations, coursework, student teaching, and ongoing mentorship.

The NSF Master Teaching Fellowship (2019-2024) supported 14 PK-12 teachers in developing as STEM leaders through graduate coursework and leadership projects, resulting in new STEM programs, published articles, and conference presentations.

The CR-ITI/ESOL Program, a $687,500 NYSED award (2023-2028), prepares ESOL teachers through clinical practice and school partnerships, leading to an Advanced Certificate in TESOL.

U.S. mortgage application activity fell 0.8 percent for a second consecutive week, according to Mortgage Bankers Association data released Wednesday, despite a sharp drop in borrowing costs. The average interest rate on 30-year fixed-rate conforming mortgages dropped to 4.33 percent from 4.46 percent, the largest decline since early January. The decrease in rates followed a fall in U.S. Treasury yields amid doubts about the Trump administration's ability to deliver tax cuts and infrastructure spending. Refinancing applications fell 2.9 percent, while purchase applications rose 1.2 percent.

A CORAF report details outcomes from the "Improving and Scaling up the System of Rice Intensification in West Africa" (SRI-WAAPP) project, described as the largest SRI project globally. Spanning three years, it involved over 50,000 farmers across 13 West African countries and was coordinated by Mali's National Center of Specialization on Rice with Cornell University.

SRI is an adaptable methodology that reduces input needs while increasing yields. An independent evaluation found yield increases of 54 percent for irrigated, 65 percent for rainfed lowland, and 153 percent for rainfed upland systems, with farmers' incomes rising 41 percent on average. The 2015-2016 season produced over 20,000 additional tons of milled rice, valued at about US$10 million.

Authors Styger and Traoré advocate expanded adoption, noting SRI's principles must be adapted to local conditions. Concerns include potential increased labor burdens on women; the team adopted a weeding technology from India to address this. The project's regional scope facilitated cross-border collaboration among researchers, extension staff, and farmers.

Retired lawyer Marcel Strigberger describes decluttering his home by discarding his McGill University law schoolbooks, purchased over 50 years ago. He reflects on each book before disposing of it, recalling notable cases from his contract law text by Cheshire and Fifoot, including the Carlill smokeball case and an 1860s case involving an unenforceable contract between a carriage owner and a prostitute. He also reviews his property law book by Magarry and Wade, noting concepts like fee simple and fee tail that never arose in his 42 years of practice, though he later discovered a used copy sells for over $1,000 on Amazon. He also discarded a book containing the Wagon Mound cargo ship case. All books were placed in the recycling bin, except one thick volume he kept to use as a reading stand.

Estonia's Minister of Education and Research, Mailis Reps, has signed a directive to establish two state-run upper secondary schools in Viimsi and Rapla, set to open on September 1 next year. Hiring for leadership positions has begun, with the ministry seeking candidates capable of developing and implementing an ambitious vision. Construction is in its second phase, with Novarc AS and Kamp architects handling the Viimsi school, and Salto architects designing the Rapla school.

Five days after Stephen Paddock killed 58 people and wounded hundreds at a Las Vegas country music festival, investigators say they still have no clear motive despite following 1,000 leads. The FBI announced billboards appealing for public tips. Authorities are examining Paddock's finances, politics, mental health, possible radicalization, and social behavior, but have found little. Investigators are looking into his interactions with prostitutes, his cruises abroad including one to the Middle East, and a cryptic note with numbers left in his hotel room. Officials said Paddock planned meticulously, stockpiling 23 guns, setting up cameras, and purchasing 1,000 tracer rounds from a Phoenix gun show. He also booked rooms overlooking festivals in Chicago and near the Las Vegas Strip earlier. His girlfriend, Marilou Danley, told the FBI she noticed no warning signs. Undersheriff Kevin McMahill said investigators don't believe Paddock had an accomplice in the shooting.

This systematic literature review examines trends in robotic coding studies in science education published between 2015-2022. Using the WOS and Scopus databases and following PRISMA guidelines and Petticrew and Roberts' (2006) five-step method, 15 peer-reviewed empirical articles were selected based on predetermined inclusion criteria.

The analysis revealed three main themes in study results: cognitive skills (21st-century and computational thinking skills), applications in robotic coding teaching (primarily in science and engineering using Arduino and tablets), and affective variables (interest, motivation, opinion). Suggestions from reviewed studies focused mainly on applications—particularly integrating robotic coding into various fields, subjects, and teacher training—and future research, including large-scale studies and diverse data collection tools.

The review recommends further studies addressing additional 21st-century skills, integration of robotic coding into technology, engineering, and mathematics, use of alternative coding tools beyond Arduino, exploration of diverse affective characteristics, inclusion of psychomotor domain, curriculum development, and in-service teacher training. The study is limited to 15 articles and suggests future meta-syntheses or meta-analyses across different fields and periods.

System Management Arts Incorporated ("Smarts") moved under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 54(b) to revise the court's prior opinion (Smarts I) denying partial summary judgment against Avesta Technologies and David Zager. Smarts had sued for patent infringement concerning Avesta's "Trinity" program, and defendants claimed the patents were invalid because Morgan Stanley's "Delphi" program constituted prior art. In Smarts I, the court found a triable issue of fact on Delphi's status as prior art, partly based on corroborating testimony from Igor Klener.

Smarts based its revision motion on newly-discovered evidence from Klener's deposition, which revealed Klener had been invited to invest in Avesta before its IPO and was friendly with Avesta executives, allegedly showing bias.

The court held the Rule 54(b) motion was procedurally proper and timely due to the newly-discovered evidence. However, it denied the motion on the merits, ruling that an interested corroborating witness's testimony is not per se insufficient under the "rule of reason." Bias is a credibility issue for the jury, not grounds for disregarding testimony as a matter of law. The court distinguished Woodland Trust and found that Klener's alleged bias and the passage of time did not eliminate genuine issues of material fact. The motion was denied.

1515 Broadway Associates, a Delaware limited partnership that owned a New York City office building, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October 1990 after financial projections proved overly optimistic and debts mounted. A Plan of Reorganization was confirmed on December 13, 1991, which settled outstanding lawsuits, required Equitable to provide additional funding, reorganized the partnership structure, and allowed for potential sale or foreclosure of the Building in 1995 or 1996.

The New York City Department of Finance and New York State Department of Taxation and Finance appealed, contesting tax exemptions under 11 U.S.C. § 1146(c). The appellees moved to dismiss the appeals as moot, arguing the Plan had been substantially consummated without a stay being obtained.

Judge Sweet denied the motion to dismiss in part and granted it in part. Applying the AOV standard, the court held that appeals are moot only where relief would harm non-party creditors or impact the reorganized debtor. The court ruled:

1. The reorganization of the general partnership into a limited partnership was moot, as it was central to the Plan and within the bankruptcy court's jurisdiction.

2. The City's challenge regarding possible future foreclosure was not moot, since the transaction had not yet occurred and funds remained available.

In a 1947 letter to Norbert Wiener, mathematician Warren Weaver described translating Russian as merely decoding English written in strange symbols. While tools like Google Translate are practically useful, they lack understanding, focusing on decoding rather than meaning. This raises the question of whether high-quality translation is possible without genuine comprehension of language, which the author explores through experiments.

The @YesYoureRacist Twitter account, which gained 271,000 followers over the weekend, has been identifying participants of the Charlottesville, Virginia protest where mostly men marched with tiki torches alongside posters supporting the Nazi Party and KKK. The anonymous moderator has invited followers to send names and profiles of marchers to make them "famous." One identified participant, Cole White, was fired from Top Dog restaurant in Berkeley, California, with the owners stating they do not support the actions in Charlottesville. Another identified man, Peter Cvjetanovic, defended his participation as promoting "white European culture" but expressed upset at being labeled "angry torch guy" online. James Allsup, a Washington State University student and College Republicans president, was also identified, prompting followers to contact the university's president. The account was featured on Good Morning America and credited with identifying the driver who killed a protestor.

Software engineering is a systematic approach for developing and maintaining software efficiently. Requirements, which define services and constraints of a software system, are classified as functional (describing actions the software must perform) and non-functional (defining characteristics such as usability, security, and reliability). Non-functional requirements (NFRs) add qualities without altering functionality and play a critical role in client and user evaluation.

Automatic document classification has gained importance, with methods including K-NN, Naïve Bayes, Decision Tree, and Support Vector Machine classifiers, each with specific advantages and limitations.

Related works explored model-driven generation of Domain NFRs, prioritization techniques, effort estimation using Use Case Points, interplay among NFRs across software projects, and reuse of NFR knowledge through ontology-based tools.

The proposed methodology identifies potential NFRs by clustering semantically similar words extracted from functional requirements, using measures like Normalized Google Distance and Average Linkage clustering. A decision tree classifier is applied with an NFR matrix to classify null and non-null functions from an IVR dataset.

Results show that the proposed method, combining NFR matrix with decision tree classification, achieves higher accuracy and lower execution time compared to the existing method using only the NFR matrix. Implementation was performed in Python.

Turing GPUs introduce hybrid rendering, combining rasterization and ray tracing to enable real-time ray-traced effects in games and professional applications. Dedicated RT Cores accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, offloading work from the SM and delivering approximately 10x faster ray tracing than Pascal GPUs.

NVIDIA NGX leverages Tensor Cores for AI-based features including Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS), which produces high-quality images at lower shading costs than TAA, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Turing also introduces Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh Shaders) to reduce CPU draw call bottlenecks, Variable Rate Shading (VRS) for fine-grained shading control enabling content adaptive, motion adaptive, and foveated rendering, Texture Space Shading (TSS) to decouple shading from screen-space pixels, and Multi-View Rendering (MVR) supporting up to four views per pass.

VR enhancements include USB-C/VirtualLink support, MVR for wider FOV headsets, foveated rendering via VRS, and RT Core-accelerated VRWorks Audio. The TU104 and TU106 GPUs share Turing's architecture, powering products like the GeForce RTX 2080/2070, Quadro RTX 5000, and Tesla T4.

The RTX-OPS metric measures hybrid rendering performance by weighting Tensor, CUDA, RT Core, and INT32 operations based on typical usage. Ray tracing with denoising improves shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections over traditional rasterization techniques, as demonstrated in Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider.

PML-N leader Dr Rana Muhammad Tariq Khan, speaking at a prize distribution ceremony at Government Girls High School, Liaquatabad in Lodhran, described students as the nation's most valuable assets. He referenced his late brother Rana Muhammad Aslam Khan's vision of providing basic facilities to Lodhran's educational institutions and urged civil society to support government school students. Dr Tariq announced the installation of a water pump and provision of furniture for the school, pledging ongoing support. Deputy District Officer Education (Secondary) Muhammad Aslam Qaisrani highlighted the Punjab government's provision of qualified teachers, infrastructure, free education, and a Rs1,000 monthly stipend per student.

Smoky River FCSS is seeking parents with babies aged 2-4 months in October to participate in the Roots of Empathy Program during the 2017-2018 school year at schools in the Smoky River region. Created in 1996 by Mary Gordon, this Canadian program aims to develop empathy in children through classroom visits featuring a baby. Students engage in guided observations to identify and reflect on emotions. Participating schools reportedly see increased positive social behaviors and decreased aggression. Interested families can contact Crystal at 780-837-2220 or youthsrfcss@live.com, or visit www.rootsofempathy.org.

This study addresses sex differences in Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses of sleep phenotypes and cardiovascular disease (CVD) outcomes, particularly when female sample sizes are limited, as in the Million Veteran Program (MVP) where only 10% of participants are female.

The authors developed a semi-empirical Bayesian framework that calibrates sex-specific variant-exposure effect estimates by borrowing information across sex groups. Two shrinkage estimators are derived: the fixed-effects meta-analysis (FE meta) estimator and a novel adaptive posterior mean (APM) estimator, which incorporates sex-difference strength into its prior variance. These estimators are used as inputs to existing two-sample MR methods.

Simulation studies across three scenarios (fixed, random, and OSA-guided sex differences in variant-exposure effects) showed that APM and adaptive weight (AW) estimators improved causal effect estimation efficiency for the smaller female population, regardless of sex-difference magnitude, with MR-RAPS performing best among MR methods.

Applying the method to MVP sleep GWAS data (OSA, insomnia, short/long sleep, daytime sleepiness) and All of Us CVD outcomes (atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, heart failure, hypertension, type 2 diabetes), the authors identified several sex-specific causal associations: insomnia increased CKD risk in females, long sleep increased hypertension risk in females, short sleep increased CAD risk in males, and OSA showed significant effects on multiple CVD outcomes in males. A significant sex difference was found for OSA's effect on CKD.

Limitations include reliance on a lenient p-value threshold (10⁻⁵) for IV selection, restriction to European ancestry, and use of conventional t-tests for sex-difference testing. Code and harmonized summary statistics are available on GitHub.

Markets shifted to risk-off last week following a confluence of muted or contradictory catalysts. Q2 earnings were strong, with 82% of S&P 500 companies beating EPS estimates and upward revisions reaching multi-month highs, yet stocks sold off on the news. GDP came in at 3% versus 2.5% expected, though distorted by tariff-related trade volatility and weak personal spending. The July jobs report missed expectations at 73,000 versus 100,000, with the largest non-pandemic two-month downward revision since 1979. Markets now price over 75% odds of a September rate cut and three cuts by January. Bond ETFs showed bullish breakout patterns as rates declined. Major indexes formed a bearish engulfing pattern at all-time highs, with nearly all sectors declining, volume weakening, volatility surging, and market internals flipping negative across most timeframes.

President Bush addresses Congress, outlining a budget plan with four features: addressing urgent priorities, investing in the future, reducing the deficit, and no new taxes. He projects $80 billion in new revenues from economic growth, enough to increase modest spending while cutting the deficit by 40% to meet Gramm-Rudman-Hollings targets.

Bush proposes budget process reforms including two-year budgets, a line-item veto, and a balanced budget amendment. His investment priorities include $2.2 billion for the National Science Foundation, a permanent R&D tax credit, $2.4 billion more for NASA, a capital gains tax cut, and urban enterprise zones.

On education, he proposes merit school rewards, Presidential teacher awards, National Science Scholars, magnet schools, and alternative certification. He requests nearly $1 billion more to combat drugs, supporting treatment expansion, border protection, tougher prosecution, and the death penalty for drug kingpins. He also requests $1.6 billion for AIDS.

Environmental proposals include a new Clean Air Act addressing acid rain, clean coal technology, ocean protections, and postponing three offshore lease sales. Social initiatives include Medicaid expansion, a child care tax credit, adoption deductions, full Social Security funding, and homeless assistance.

Bush supports a Puerto Rico referendum, savings and loan reform, nuclear weapons plant cleanup, and a one-year defense freeze. On foreign policy, he advocates SDI, banning chemical weapons, nonproliferation, supporting Central American democracy, and strengthening alliances.

A University of Copenhagen study published in Cyberpsychology, Behaviour and Social Networking found that excessive social media use can harm emotional well-being. Surveying over 1,000 mostly female participants, researchers identified "lurking" or passive browsing as particularly damaging, often triggering envy and mood decline due to unrealistic social comparisons. A separate 2015 Ontario study linked more than two hours of daily social media use among teens to higher risks of mental illness, though such platforms can also deliver mental health services. Researchers recommend limiting social media use or quitting it entirely, noting that heavier users benefit most from cutting back.

The passage introduces a dynamically-controllable x-ray interferometer for Mössbauer science that addresses limitations of traditional crystal-based x-ray interferometers. The setup uses two α-iron targets enriched in 57Fe placed inside a high-purity polarimetry setup, operating in a "dark-fringe" mode where the empty interferometer ideally transmits no x-rays. The interfering pathways differ in polarization rather than spatial separation, and radiative couplings between targets cancel, leaving only two pathways corresponding to polarization-changing scattering in either target. By mechanically displacing one target using a piezoelectric transducer, the authors dynamically control the relative phase between pathways. They experimentally demonstrate nanosecond-scale control of transmitted x-ray intensity and measure target displacements at x-ray wavelength and nanosecond scales by observing mechanical wave propagation over 10 µs durations.

HARMONY is introduced as an entropy-based metric for auditing benchmark reliability from a distributional perspective. Benchmarks form a feedback loop with model development, and their reliability is essential to ensure reported gains reflect genuine capabilities. Prior work has identified structural issues like redundancy and uneven data distributions in popular benchmarks.

The HARMONY pipeline: (1) partition a benchmark into semantic clusters representing subdomains, (2) gather per-cluster model performance, and (3) measure the uniformity of performance distribution across subdomains. High HARMONY indicates aggregate metrics reflect broad competence, while low HARMONY obscures model strengths and weaknesses, potentially favoring specialist models over generalists.

Formally, given a benchmark B partitioned into subsets via a semantic similarity function, HARMONY quantifies uniform performance across subsets using size weights, a weighted mean, and Gaussian kernel proximity scores.

Contributions include introducing the HARMONY metric and providing an empirical mapping of 19 MCQA benchmarks across five model families, revealing a spectrum of benchmark reliability. The authors recommend reporting HARMONY alongside accuracy.

Iain Stewart's lecture continues the discussion of the weak Hamiltonian, derived from the Standard Model by removing the top, W, Z, and Higgs, focusing on the process b → c ū d with two four-fermion operators and their Wilson coefficients.

The lecture derives anomalous dimension equations for Wilson coefficients by exploiting the mu-independence of the Hamiltonian, which means coefficient and operator mu-dependence must cancel. Working in the plus/minus basis (linear combinations of operators O1 and O2), the coupled differential equations are solved by changing variables from mu to alpha using the beta function, yielding solutions of the form (alpha at one scale / alpha at another scale) raised to a power.

This procedure sums leading logarithms (LL) of Mw/Mb, treating alpha times large log as order one. The physical picture involves matching at scale mu_w ~ Mw, then renormalization group evolution to scale mu_b ~ Mb, where matrix elements are evaluated without large logs. Notably, the coefficient C2, zero at tree level, becomes nonzero (~ -0.3) at leading log.

Higher-order improvements (NLL, NNLL) require one-loop matching plus two-loop anomalous dimensions, etc. The running order is always one higher than matching order. An application discussed is B → Dπ decay.

Comparing full-theory and effective-theory calculations: full-theory diagrams (triangles, boxes) are UV-finite due to conserved currents, while IR divergences (logs of p²) agree between theories, confirming correct effective-theory degrees of freedom. The difference determines one-loop matching coefficients.

Key observations: Mw is replaced by the cutoff mu in the effective theory; mu-dependence cancels between coefficients and operators order-by-order; effective theory calculations are simpler (single-scale) and encode higher-order logs through renormalization alone.

On scheme dependence: while one-loop anomalous dimensions and leading-log results are scheme-independent, at NLL the quantities B1, gamma1, J, C, and O are individually scheme-dependent. However, specific combinations (B1 + J, and C times O) are scheme-independent, ensuring physical observables remain well-defined. Users must maintain scheme consistency across matching, running, and matrix elements.

Subtleties in full calculations include the proper treatment of gamma_5 in dimensional regularization and evanescent operators (Dirac structures that vanish as epsilon → 0 but are needed in d dimensions).

Patient advocacy groups have asked the U.K.'s antitrust regulator to investigate major drugmakers and their U.K. lobbying organization over alleged coordinated efforts to raise medicine prices. The request follows a dispute between the pharmaceutical industry and the U.K. government regarding mandatory rebates that cap brand-name drug costs for the National Health Service, which spent $18.6 billion on such treatments in 2023-2024. After rebate rates increased from 10% to 23%, AstraZeneca, Merck, and Eli Lilly halted or canceled U.K. expansion plans totaling $2.6 billion.

The U.S. Department of State's Office of the Historian has released an ebook edition of the Foreign Relations of the United States (FRUS) series, established in 1861. The ebook edition preserves the full content of printed volumes while enabling search, bookmarking, and offline access. Readers are advised to cite document numbers rather than page numbers for accuracy.

The preface, referencing President Roosevelt's 1942 address to Congress, frames the publication of official American records from the 1919 Paris Peace Conference as timely during wartime planning for a post-war settlement. It notes that no government represented at Paris had previously released a substantially complete record, though extensive unofficial literature exists, including memoirs, document collections, and bibliographies by authors such as David Hunter Miller, Ray Stannard Baker, Robert Lansing, David Lloyd George, and H. W. V. Temperley. This FRUS volume aims to fill that gap by providing authoritative information on the peacemaking of 1919.

Systems evolved from purpose-built machines to general-purpose programmable machines running multiple programs via time-sharing. Networking led to client-server architectures, where clients made requests and servers serviced them. In the early 2000s, the internet and large-scale datacenters of networked commodity computers enabled distributed systems, where multiple applications across machines communicate to implement systems like web-search or retail platforms.

When properly structured, distributed systems are more reliable and scalable, but they are harder to design, build, and debug, requiring greater engineering skills. Despite this, demand for them grows, along with the need for supporting tools and practices. Containers, container images, and container orchestrators have emerged as foundational building blocks, enabling reusable patterns and components for building reliable distributed systems.

Lansdowne High School students produce morning announcements from the school's television studio, led by teacher Brandon Nicklas, who joined in 2005. The broadcasts are streamed throughout the school, and students also produce "The Lansdowne Show" for the Baltimore County Public Schools cable channel and YouTube.

According to Alex Wolf of the school system's Office of Digital Learning, about 100 of the 161 county schools have studios, with roughly half being digital. Studios have been included in construction and renovation projects for nearly 20 years. Wolf said students develop teamwork, communication, and public speaking skills. Expanding digital studios to all schools depends on funding, which comes from individual school operating budgets. Basic live-streaming setups cost about $400, while full digital studios cost $15,000 to $18,000.

This year, "broadcast production facilitator" was added to the union-negotiated extra-duty activities list, compensating advisers $2,005 or $3,004. Sheila Wells of Wide Angle Youth Media and Jason Loviglio of UMBC noted that media production skills foster critical thinking and are increasingly valuable as online video grows.

Hillcrest Elementary launched a studio last month under librarian Jacqueline Schoen, and Arbutus Middle School principal Michelle Feeney established one using extra equipment, with secretary Matthew Moser running it.

Researchers at Penn Medicine identified brain circuits affected by psilocybin, the active compound in psychedelic mushrooms, suggesting potential new treatments for chronic pain and mood disorders. In mice with nerve injury and inflammatory pain, a single dose reduced pain and anxiety/depression-like behaviors for nearly two weeks by activating serotonin receptors (5-HT2A and 5-HT1A) like a "dimmer switch." The effect originated in the anterior cingulate cortex, not the spinal cord. Lead author Joseph Cichon notes psilocybin is non-addictive, though further research is needed on dosing, safety, and long-term effects. Findings may also inform therapies for addiction and PTSD.

The eighth annual Regional Theatrical Youth Camp will run June 19-30, 2017, ending with a ticketed production of "Bye, Bye Birdie, Jr.," with a second show added July 2. The camp offers Level I for ages 5-8 and Level II for ages 9-18, which includes 50 hours of training and a guaranteed role. Directed by Cindy and Kenny Brown and sponsored by Oliver Companies, the program has grown in regional participation over the years.

Different urinary proteomics profiles were identified among type 1 HAE, type 2 HAE, and healthy controls. Several biological processes were enriched in HAE, including complement and coagulation cascades, cell adhesion molecules, immune response, proteolysis, and bradykinin catabolism. A urinary biomarker panel (C1-INH, KNG1, and EGF) shows promise as a noninvasive diagnostic tool for HAE.

Hereditary angioedema (HAE) is characterized by recurrent subcutaneous and submucosal swelling. Classic HAE results from SERPING1 gene mutations causing C1-INH deficiency, subdivided into type 1 (decreased C1-INH levels) and type 2 (normal levels but dysfunctional C1-INH). Type 1 predominates in China, with type 2 representing less than 5% of cases. HAE has an estimated prevalence of 1/50,000 and is often misdiagnosed, with diagnostic delays of 8–13 years. Laryngeal edema-induced asphyxiation is the main cause of death, with mortality rates between 11% and 40%.

Urine is an attractive, noninvasive sample source for biomarker research because it accumulates systemic changes without homeostatic control. No urine biomarkers are currently available for HAE diagnosis or monitoring. In this study, data-independent acquisition (DIA)-based proteomics was applied to characterize urinary protein profiles in HAE patients, followed by bioinformatics analysis and validation of candidate biomarkers using parallel reaction monitoring (PRM)-based targeted proteomics in an independent cohort.

In the discovery phase, 20 HAE patients (15 type 1, 5 type 2) and 29 healthy controls were recruited at Peking Union Medical College Hospital. The validation phase included 24 type 1 HAE patients and 18 healthy controls. Midstream first morning urine samples were collected, centrifuged, and stored at -80 °C. Samples were prepared using a filter-aided method, reduced, alkylated, precipitated with acetone, digested with trypsin, and analyzed via LC-MS/MS.

A hard ferromagnetic sphere (radius ~24–30 µm) is levitated in a superconducting lead trap at 4.2 K, with motion detected via a dc SQUID and driven by synchronous feedback coils. Meissner repulsion confines translational motion, while a residual horizontal field creates librational trapping in the azimuthal angle. Synchronous driving spins the magnet beyond the librational barrier into free rotation, reaching a maximum of 2.3 MHz for a 30 µm magnet.

Spin-down follows exponential decay governed by gas damping, with rate γ proportional to pressure. Experimental measurements yield γ/P = (11.6 ± 0.2) (s·mbar)⁻¹, matching theoretical predictions. The rotor functions as a cryogenic pressure sensor across 10⁻³ to 10⁻⁸ mbar, with a minimum damping rate of 4.75×10⁻⁷ s⁻¹ (Q = 1.33×10¹³). A secondary low-frequency peak was identified as precession, following fl = fx²/fs.

This represents the fastest magnetically levitated rotor demonstrated, requiring no active stabilization and producing minimal heating. Potential applications include gyroscopes, gravimeters, magnetometry for dark matter detection, collapse model tests, and investigations of rotational quantum effects.

Researchers at Columbia University, led by Michal Lipson, have developed a silicon chip that converts a single laser into a "frequency comb," producing dozens of evenly spaced, high-power light channels simultaneously. The discovery occurred accidentally during LiDAR research when the team noticed high-power chips generating frequency combs. Using a multimode laser diode combined with a locking mechanism, the researchers purified the laser's noisy output into a stable, coherent beam, which the chip's nonlinear properties then split into multiple colors.

Traditionally, frequency combs require large, expensive lasers and amplifiers. By miniaturizing this capability, the technology could replace racks of individual lasers in data centers, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing in compact systems. Potential applications include more efficient data centers, portable spectrometers, optical clocks, quantum devices, and advanced LiDAR. The work was conducted with collaborators including Andres Gil-Molina, now at Xscape Photonics.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on October 22, 2015, announcing its third quarter 2015 financial results. The filing includes two exhibits: Exhibit 99.1, a press release detailing the financial results, and Exhibit 99.2, providing information regarding non-GAAP financial measures. Uber board member David Bonderman resigned after making a comment during a Tuesday meeting suggesting that adding more women to the board would lead to "more talking." The remark was made while fellow board member Arianna Huffington discussed the addition of Wan Lang Martello as the second woman on Uber's board. Bonderman called his comment "careless, inappropriate and inexcusable." The meeting was held to share findings from an investigation led by former Attorney General Eric Holder into Uber's workplace culture, prompted by sexual harassment allegations from former engineer Susan Fowler. Paul Tudor Jones, founder of Tudor Investment, said conditions are in place for a major stock market rally before a "blow off" top ends the current bull market. He compared today's environment to the lead-up to the 1999 dot-com bubble, citing tech rallies and speculative behavior, and expressed unease about circular deals in the AI sector. Jones noted a key difference: the Federal Reserve is easing rates and the U.S. has a 6% budget deficit, versus rate hikes and a budget surplus in 1999. He said the biggest price gains typically occur in the 12 months before a market top, requiring investors to time entries and exits carefully. Jones expects further gains driven by retail buying and broader participation, and said he would hold gold, cryptocurrencies, and Nasdaq tech stocks through year-end. The Nasdaq Composite has risen 55% from its April low to recent record highs.
