Scientists have documented the first modern case of "river piracy," attributing it to global warming. In May 2016, meltwater from Canada's Kaskawulsh glacier abruptly rerouted from the Slims River to the Alsek River, redirecting flow from the Bering Sea to the Pacific Ocean. A 30-metre canyon formed at the glacier's edge caused the change, which occurred in roughly one day. Researchers, led by Dan Shugar of the University of Washington Tacoma, found the once deep and swift Slims River reduced to shallow, still water, while the Alsek grew deeper and faster. Typically, river piracy takes tens of thousands of years. The Kaskawulsh glacier, covering 25,000 square kilometres, has retreated significantly since 1899. Scientists calculate only a one in 200 chance the event is unrelated to human-caused climate change. The study was published in Nature Geoscience.

The NRST reset pin requires a pullup to VDD, typically via a 47kΩ resistor with a 10nF pulldown capacitor. The SYSOSC frequency correction loop requires an external 100kΩ (0.1% tolerance, 25ppm/C TCR) resistor between ROSC and VSS when enabled; otherwise PA2 may be used as digital I/O. A 0.47µF tank capacitor is required on VCORE. 5V-tolerant open drain I/Os require pullup resistors for output high and are fail-safe.

TI assigns prefixes to MSP MCU part numbers: "X" for experimental prototypes (not recommended for production) and "MSP" for fully qualified production devices. Device suffixes indicate temperature range, package type, and distribution format.

TI offers development tools including LaunchPad kits, MSPM0 SDK, TI Resource Explorer, SysConfig, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, Code Composer Studio, IAR Embedded Workbench, Keil MDK, TI Arm-Clang, and GNU Arm Embedded Toolchain.

The revision history (November 2024 to April 2025) documents numerous updates including PSA-L1 certification targeting, clarified peripheral quantities in low-power modes, added package variants (100_nFBGA_ZAW and 42_DSBGA_YCJ), updated electrical characteristics (absolute maximum ratings, supply current, POR/BOR thresholds, ADC, temperature sensor, VREF, comparator, SPI), flash memory sector flexibility for high-endurance operation, and various section updates (DMA, SRAM, security, keystore, UART, SPI, LFSS, timers).

Automotive-qualified versions (MSPM0G3518-Q1, MSPM0G3519-Q1) are available.

Fort Bend ISD maintenance crews worked to repair air conditioning issues at Quail Valley Elementary School and Marshall High School, which malfunctioned following a three-day weekend and high temperatures. Contractors and district crews fixed the elementary school's AC overnight, and Marshall's AC was also repaired overnight. Students at Marshall reported unusually hot conditions, with some relocating to the cafeteria for cooler air and fans being used in hallways. By the following day, the AC was functioning at Marshall, and students noted that with only a day left of school, they managed despite the heat.

Since 1993, all gains in the S&P 500 have occurred overnight (from close to next open), with daytime trading yielding zero returns. A similar overnight bias exists in gold (GLD) and gold miners (GDX), where daytime holding produces negative returns. Night trading involves holding positions from market close to the next open, distinct from after-hours trading. The average overnight gain in the S&P 500 is 0.04%, which alone is insufficient to cover slippage and commissions, requiring developed strategies. Possible reasons for the bias include inflation, earnings growth, and compensation for overnight risk. The author references published strategies, including a 2014 overnight strategy that continues to perform well, and 24-hour variations with an average gain of 0.33% per trade.

AT-752 is an orally available guanosine nucleotide prodrug inhibitor of the dengue virus (DENV) polymerase, which is metabolized to the active triphosphate AT-9010 targeting the NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase of DENV1–4. This first-in-human Phase 1, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluated the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics (PK) of single ascending doses (SAD; 250–1500 mg) and multiple ascending doses (MAD; up to 750 mg three times daily [TID]) of AT-752 in 65 healthy subjects.

AT-752 was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events or discontinuations. Treatment-emergent adverse events were mild-to-moderate, most commonly headache, nausea, and vomiting. In SAD cohorts, plasma exposure increased approximately dose-proportionally, no PK ethnic sensitivity was observed in Asian participants, and a high-fat meal had limited impact on total exposure, indicating AT-752 can be taken with or without food. In MAD cohorts, the 750 mg TID regimen rapidly achieved and maintained plasma AT-273 levels exceeding the target EC90 for DENV inhibition. These findings support further clinical development of AT-752 for dengue treatment.

California Governor Gray Davis announced progress in negotiations to rescue Pacific Gas and Electric Co., with the state potentially paying at least $7 billion for PG&E's transmission lines, though PG&E may seek up to $10 billion. El Paso Energy shut down six cogeneration plants in the San Joaquin Valley due to non-payment from PG&E.

The state Department of Water Resources has spent $3.2 billion on electricity purchases, with disputes ongoing over reimbursement. Davis signed 40 long-term power contracts averaging $69 per megawatt-hour, but confidentiality agreements kept details private, drawing criticism from consumer advocates. Wall Street analysts questioned whether Davis's approach addresses the underlying imbalance between wholesale and retail rates.

Legislation to reduce payments to alternative energy generators stalled amid concerns about preferential treatment. The Sacramento Municipal Utility District and other smaller utilities sought to opt out of rolling blackout agreements with PG&E. The PUC considered whether to allow PG&E and Edison to lay off thousands of workers to cut costs.

Experts warned that up to 43 percent of California's summer power needs might come from the volatile spot market, risking blackouts and high costs. Contra Costa County supervisors voted to explore sites for new power plants, drawing resident opposition. State energy officials approved a temporary 51-megawatt "peaker" plant at San Francisco International Airport.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Davis's plan to issue $10 billion in bonds faces obstacles, as legislative formulas may only support approximately $1 billion based on current rates, potentially leaving the state financially exposed without rate increases.

Two new oral GLP-1 medications can help people with obesity lose weight, according to studies published September 16 and 17. Currently, most GLP-1 drugs, which mimic gut hormones to curb appetite and control blood sugar, are injectable and require refrigeration.

In one trial, more than 300 participants taking 25 milligrams of oral semaglutide lost nearly 14 percent of body weight over 64 weeks. In another trial of Eli Lilly's orforglipron, a small-molecule drug, over 3,000 participants on the highest dose lost about 11 percent of body weight over 72 weeks.

Researcher Sean Wharton noted that pills are easier to manufacture, distribute and take, potentially lowering costs and improving accessibility. Side effects included nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and constipation, but no liver toxicity was observed, unlike in some earlier small-molecule GLP-1 drugs discontinued by Pfizer. Endocrinologist Daniel Drucker said longer-term studies are still needed. Wharton hopes both drugs will be available by 2026, pending FDA approval.

The 9.0-magnitude earthquake that struck Japan on March 11, 2011, along with a tsunami and nuclear meltdowns at Fukushima Dai-ichi, caused over 25,000 casualties and approximately ¥16.9 trillion in economic damage. The Japanese auto industry was severely disrupted, with 80% of plants suspending production and annual production falling 9%. Exports and overseas plants dependent on Japanese components were also affected.

Nissan, which suffered damage to six plants and around 50 critical suppliers, was prepared due to a risk management philosophy developed after its near-bankruptcy and 1999 alliance with Renault. Unlike Toyota's tightly controlled TPS, Nissan used a decentralized, flexible supply chain with strong central crisis coordination, a simplified product line, and a mix of build-to-stock and build-to-order strategies.

Nissan's pre-existing earthquake response plan prioritized human life, disaster prevention, business continuity, and community support. After the disaster, its Global Disaster Control Headquarters convened within 15 minutes, and a Recovery Committee coordinated global actions by: sharing information across regions, allocating constrained supplies to highest-margin products, managing production around bottlenecks, and empowering rapid decision-making.

Nissan recovered more effectively than Honda and Toyota, which faced greater supply chain constraints. In 2012, Nissan announced plans to increase localized production in the Americas from 70% to 90% by 2015, reduce Japanese-sourced components by 50% by fiscal 2013, and strengthen business continuity planning for lower-tier suppliers.

Ashley Leger, a paleontologist contracted by Los Angeles transportation officials, monitors construction of a subway extension for fossil discoveries. Since work began in 2014, crews have uncovered Ice Age remains including rabbit, mastodon, camel, bison, and horse fossils. About a year ago, Leger's team excavated an intact skull of a juvenile Columbian mammoth, named Hayden, now housed at the La Brea Tar Pits and Museum. Assistant curator Dr. Emily Lindsey called it remarkable, noting only about 30 mammoths have been found in Los Angeles, and this skull is rare for having both tusks attached. California's environmental laws, enacted in the early 1970s, require paleontologists at certain construction sites, and similar discoveries have occurred in San Diego and Boston.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on January 29, 2020, reporting that it released its financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended December 31, 2019. The results were posted as the Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2019 Update on Tesla's website and attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

The provisional government in Cuba will end following peaceful elections. The United States urges Cubans to maintain order and justice, warning that failed elections or continued insurrection would force another U.S. intervention, as the U.S. has assumed sponsorship for Cuba's independence before the world.

The Third International Conference of American Republics was held in Rio de Janeiro from July 23 to August 29, following arrangements made by the Bureau of American Republics' governing board. The conference addressed trade, communication, and international cooperation, producing resolutions and proposed conventions to be presented later. Compared to the lengthy first two conferences in Washington (1889) and Mexico (1901–2), the Rio Conference concluded efficiently within six weeks.

The Secretary of State attended the conference as an honorary president and accepted invitations to visit Brazil, Uruguay, Argentina, Chile, Peru, Panama, and Colombia, delivering a message of friendship. Paraguay, Bolivia, and Ecuador were omitted due to travel constraints. He was warmly received throughout.

Wall Street stocks declined in early Tuesday trading, led by healthcare companies and banks. Goldman Sachs fell 3% after earnings missed forecasts due to a trading business shortfall, reducing the Dow by about 50 points. Johnson & Johnson dropped 2.7% on weak revenue, while Cardinal Health plunged 10.6% after a weak forecast. The S&P 500 fell 0.2% to 2,343, the Dow lost 0.4% to 20,563, and the Nasdaq slipped 0.2% to 5,846. The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 2.21%.

This study demonstrates that a simple annealing treatment can decouple carrier and phonon transport in Se-alloyed n-type Bi2Te3 (BTS) thermoelectric materials, significantly enhancing performance. N-type BTS traditionally lags behind p-type counterparts due to stronger crystallographic anisotropy and higher intrinsic point defect concentrations, while existing texturing methods face scalability challenges.

The researchers synthesized Bi2Te3−xSex samples via a melting-hot pressing (MT-HP) route, identifying Bi2Te2.6Se0.4 as the optimal composition. Subsequent annealing at 723 K induced Te(Se) volatilization, forming cation vacancies (V'''Bi) and antisite defects that reduced carrier density while increasing carrier mobility. After 100 hours of annealing, the sample achieved a carrier mobility of 295.97 cm²V⁻¹s⁻¹, a room-temperature power factor of 27.65 μW cm⁻¹K⁻², and a lattice thermal conductivity as low as 0.48 W m⁻¹K⁻¹.

SEM and EDS analyses confirmed increased porosity and element depletion after annealing, correlating with enhanced phonon scattering. The atomic-scale defects intensified phonon scattering while preserving high carrier mobility, enabling synergistic optimization of transport properties.

The optimized sample achieved a peak ZT of 1.06 at 373 K and an average ZT of 0.99 between 300–423 K, among the highest reported for n-type Bi2(Te,Se)3 alloys. This scalable post-synthesis annealing strategy offers a practical pathway for developing high-performance n-type BTS materials suited for thermoelectric cooling applications in advanced electronics.

NTT Docomo has installed smartphone wipes in restrooms at Tokyo Narita International Airport, available until March 15. The company released an instructional video on using Japanese toilets and the wipes. The wipes also advertise NTT's wifi service and a travel guide app with voice translation. A 2012 Wall Street Journal study found poop germs on all eight cellphones tested, and a University of Arizona study found phones are 10 times germier than toilet seats.

The Supreme Court ruled that Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook may remain in her position pending oral arguments scheduled for January 2026 regarding President Trump's attempt to fire her. Trump cited alleged mortgage fraud as cause for removal, though Cook has not been charged and denies wrongdoing. The case is viewed as a potential landmark on Fed independence from political interference. The ruling allows Cook to vote at upcoming Federal Open Market Committee meetings, including those expected to approve additional interest rate cuts. Cook's lawyers welcomed the decision, while the White House expressed confidence in prevailing at oral arguments.

The passage addresses limitations in ISO 25023's "Accessibility" subcharacteristic evaluation, which lacks methodologies for determining key parameters in its quality attributes "Accessibility for users with disabilities" and "Supported languages adequacy."

The study focuses on users with visual impairments and develops a classification and mathematical model that introduces four subproperties: perceptiveness, operability, understandability, and localization. Each subproperty includes specific quality attributes with defined formulas, such as alternative text, color contrast, subtitles and audio descriptions, keyboard navigation, structured navigation, clear instructions, input assistance, and correct input support. Weighting coefficients are applied to calculate integrated accessibility measures.

The methodology was tested on the Vasyl Stefanyk Precarpathian National University website, using tools like Image Alt Checker and WCAG Contrast Checker. The overall accessibility score of approximately 0.68 was classified as "excellent" on a Fibonacci-based quality scale, though weaknesses were identified in subtitles, input assistance, and alternative text attributes.

The scientific novelty lies in developing evaluation methods with new subproperties and quality attributes adapted to visually impaired users. The practical significance includes enabling objective accessibility assessment aligned with ISO 25023 and WCAG standards.

This systematic review protocol aims to identify implementation determinants, implementation strategies, and adjunctive interventions relevant to structural interventions for HIV evidence-based interventions (EBIs) in the U.S., addressing disparities affecting minoritized populations identified by the CDC as key populations.

The authors searched multiple databases (Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, Web of Science, Sociological Abstracts, Google, ProQuest) for literature from 2000-2024, yielding 8,098 articles. Natural language processing (NLP) was used for preliminary screening across five domains, followed by manual title/abstract and full-text review in COVIDENCE by trained investigators, with disagreements resolved by senior team members.

Inclusion criteria require a U.S.-based HIV focus, implementation or hybrid implementation-effectiveness study design, original behavioral/social science research, and at least one implementation outcome. Extracted data will be coded using established frameworks: CFIR 2.0 for determinants, ERIC for implementation strategies, and TDF/COM-B for adjunctive interventions. Structural interventions will be categorized using the Sipe et al. taxonomy.

Analysis will tabulate and stratify findings by setting, priority population, study method, intervention type, and outcomes, using NLP for thematic analysis. Results will be disseminated through two primary papers, conference presentations, and an online literature review dashboard. Title/abstract review is underway, with full-text review beginning January 2025 and dissemination through Fall 2026. The review seeks to support the Ending the HIV Epidemic initiative by informing policy, programs, and future research.

The Supreme Court agreed to hear oral arguments this winter on several cases, including a challenge to a 2023 Hawaii law criminalizing the carrying of handguns on private property open to the public without the owner's explicit permission, and banning firearms in "sensitive places" like parks and beaches. The 9th Circuit upheld the law, and challengers argue it effectively nullifies the right to public carry established in New York State Rifle & Pistol Association v. Bruen. The court also took up two cases involving Cuba's 1960 property confiscations under the Cuban Liberty and Democratic Solidarity Act of 1996: Exxon Mobil's suit against state-owned Cuban companies, and Havana Docks Corporation's suit against four cruise lines for dock usage between 2016-2019.

Another case addresses whether federal law preempts state negligence claims against brokers for selecting motor carriers.

This study examined relationships between mentalization, attachment, and personality pathology within the DSM-5 Alternative Model of Personality Disorders (AMPD) framework, distinguishing between self-oriented and other-oriented mentalizing.

The sample included 109 participants (60 psychiatric inpatients and 49 community members), aged 18-47, with 54% meeting criteria for a personality disorder. Measures included the SCID-5-PD, MASC (other-mentalizing), RFQ-8 (self-mentalizing), SIFS (Criterion A), PID-5 (Criterion B), and ECR-R (attachment).

Regression analyses revealed that self-mentalizing deficits strongly predicted both self- and interpersonal functioning impairments (Criterion A) and all five maladaptive traits (Criterion B), explaining 18-55% of variance. Other-mentalizing had more specific associations, with correct other-mentalizing predicting only interpersonal functioning.

Moderation analyses showed attachment anxiety predicted all personality pathology dimensions, while avoidance predicted Criterion A dimensions and Detachment. Self-mentalizing moderated the relationship between anxious attachment and both Negative Affectivity and Detachment. Other-mentalizing moderated the relationship between avoidant attachment and Detachment, and between anxious attachment and interpersonal functioning.

The authors conclude that self-mentalizing plays a broad, foundational role in personality pathology, while other-mentalizing specifically addresses interpersonal dimensions. They suggest prioritizing self-mentalizing in therapeutic interventions, with other-mentalizing targeted for interpersonal difficulties. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, small sample size, and different assessment methods for self- versus other-mentalizing.

Public lands suitable for agriculture should be reserved strictly for actual home builders and settlers. Laws such as the desert-land law, timber and stone law, and homestead commutation clause have been misused to acquire large tracts for non-settlers. Grazing regions require different acreage allowances than arable land, since 160 acres of dry pasture cannot support a family. Illegal fencing of public lands by non-titleholders will now be stopped. A commission of experts is recommended to investigate these issues.

Alaska, owned for 35 years, lacks adequate laws despite its mineral, fishery, fur, forest, and agricultural wealth. It needs liberal land laws encouraging permanent settlement, forest and game protection, regulated timber use for settlers, salmon fishery protection under the Commission of Fish and Fisheries, and a congressional Delegate.

Regarding Indians, the goal is eventual absorption into the general population, though at varying paces depending on each tribe's advancement and living conditions. Land allotment suits some tribes, while those on arid prairies should be encouraged toward pastoral village life rather than forced isolation.

The Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST), a 6-meter telescope being constructed for the CCAT Observatory in Chile, will use the Prime-Cam receiver with seven instrument modules populated with superconducting microwave kinetic inductance detectors (KIDs). Mod-Cam is the single-module precursor and first-light instrument for FYST, serving as a testbed for the 280 GHz module.

This paper characterizes Mod-Cam's thermal performance, which is critical because KIDs are sensitive to operating temperature fluctuations. Measurements were conducted using a cold load configuration to isolate the system from external radiation, with the detector stage servo-controlled at 100 mK via a PID loop.

Key results include:
- RMS temperature fluctuation of 3.2 × 10⁻⁵ K at the 100 mK stage over 8 hours
- Median thermal responsivity of 1.995 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹ for aluminum detectors and −6.081 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹ for titanium-nitride detectors
- Equivalent optical power fluctuations of 0.20 fW (Al) and 0.11 fW (TiN) at a 5 pW optical load, representing fractional noise contributions of only 0.0040% and 0.0023% respectively

The authors conclude that thermal fluctuations contribute negligibly to the noise budget, validating Mod-Cam's cryogenic design for achieving background-limited sensitivity on FYST.

The lecture introduces 6.851 Advanced Data Structures, taught by Erik Demaine, covering topics such as temporal data structures, geometry, dynamic optimality, memory hierarchy, hashing, integer data structures, dynamic graphs, strings, and succinct data structures. Course requirements include lecture attendance, weekly problem sets, and scribing lectures, with optional open problem sessions.

The lecture focuses on temporal data structures using the pointer machine model, which consists of nodes with a constant number of fields containing pointers or data. Two types of time travel are introduced: persistence (covered in this lecture) and retroactivity (next lecture).

Four levels of persistence are defined:
1. Partial persistence: updates only on the latest version; versions are linearly ordered.
2. Full persistence: updates on any version; versions form a tree.
3. Confluent persistence: versions can be combined; forms a DAG.
4. Functional: nodes can never be modified, only created.

For partial and full persistence, Driscoll, Sarnak, Sleator, and Tarjan (1989) showed any bounded-degree pointer machine data structure can be made persistent with constant amortized overhead. The technique uses back pointers and modification records (mods) stored in each node, with node-splitting when full, analyzed via the potential method.

Full persistence requires linearizing the version tree using order maintenance data structures (covered in lecture 8) to handle ancestor queries in constant time.

Confluent persistence is harder. Fiat and Kaplan (2003) achieved overhead proportional to "effective depth" (log of number of paths to a version), which can be linear. A 2011/2012 result achieves O(log n) overhead in the disjoint case using link-cut trees and fractional cascading.

Functional data structures include balanced BSTs via path copying (O(log n)), deques with concatenation in constant time, and tries for implementing version-controlled directory trees like Subversion. Constant-time split for lists remains an open problem.

The Missouri Supreme Court will hear two cases addressing whether the Missouri Human Rights Act prohibits discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, despite those terms not appearing in the act. Lower courts have been divided on the issue.

The first case involves R.M.A., a transgender teenager who sued the Blue Springs R-IV School District after being denied access to the boys' locker room and restrooms. His attorneys argue gender identity falls under sex discrimination, while the district contends gender identity is not mentioned in the Act and that school districts cannot be sued as "people." Lower courts ruled for the district.

The second case involves state employees Harold Lampley and Rene Frost. Lampley, a gay man, alleged sex discrimination based on not conforming to male stereotypes, while Frost claimed retaliation over her friendship with him. The Human Rights Commission classified it as sexual orientation discrimination and denied the claims, but an appeals court reversed. The state argues the Act does not cover sexual orientation.

Several organizations, including the ACLU of Missouri and the American Medical Association, have filed briefs supporting the plaintiffs, while the Alliance Defending Freedom supports the school district.

According to Finder.com's America's Biggest Money Mistakes survey, 78.3% of Americans admit to having made a financial mistake. The most common mistake, cited by nearly 64% of respondents, was overspending on fun activities like shopping, vacations, and dining out. Women (66.2%) were more likely than men (58%) to admit overspending and were also more likely to regret letting partners control finances. Men reported greater regrets over bad investments (24.5% vs. 11.4%) and gambling (14.7% vs. 6.3%).

About 20% of both sexes regretted dropping out of college. BLS data shows college dropouts earn a median $774 weekly versus $1,173 for bachelor's degree holders, with higher unemployment rates. Consumer Advocate Jennifer McDermott recommends researching career paths, gap years, or internships before committing to a major.

Generationally, millennials (78.9%) and Gen X-ers (79.1%) admitted mistakes at similar rates, while baby boomers were lowest at 74.1%. Millennials most often regretted overspending on fun (70.8%), while boomers more frequently regretted bad investments (26.6%). Other regrets included expensive weddings, online scams, and having children—with child-rearing costs estimated at over $233,000 through age 17, per the USDA.

An experiment with 6-year-olds found that children performed repetitive tasks with greater effort and focus when they pretended to be someone else, such as Batman or Dora the Explorer. Children who focused on themselves took more breaks.

Denmark's Systemic Risk Council has recommended tightening mortgage rules for highly indebted households in Copenhagen and Aarhus to safeguard financial stability. The proposal would bar most borrowers with debts exceeding 400 percent of pretax income from taking interest-only or variable-interest loans, with only 15 percent of loans exempt. The government has three months to adopt the recommendation or publicly justify rejecting it. The council, formed in 2013 after the financial crisis, cited rising household debt amid a booming urban property market. Denmark's covered bond market totals about 2.8 trillion crowns ($402 billion).

Generative AI (GenAI) models are increasingly used in computational screening workflows for scientific discovery, but they often produce nonsensical candidates and suffer from model decay during iterative retraining. This work proposes a queue prioritization algorithm that combines GenAI with an active learning (AL) model using a custom acquisition function to prioritize promising candidates and filter unreasonable ones.

The approach is demonstrated on a workflow for discovering metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for carbon capture, using a DiffLinker diffusion model to generate organic linkers paired with zinc metal atoms. An XGBoost surrogate model predicts internal strain (SIS), while additional scoring functions assess synthesizability (SSAScore) and similarity to known HMOF linkers (Tanimoto distance).

Experiments show that AL prioritization mitigates model decay, particularly when fine-tuning on large fractions of generated candidates. Multi-objective acquisition functions combining stability, synthesizability, and similarity produced effective results, while upper confidence bound (UCB) acquisition with weak exploration (λ=0.1) outperformed pure exploitation or exploration strategies. Out of 1000 generated candidates, the workflow with AL produced an average of 604 high-performing candidates versus 281 without AL, with less than 1% computational overhead.

The speaker describes their status as doubtful for the night's game due to an injury sustained two weeks prior against Ottawa. Markets face pressure from seasonal weakness observed over the past 35 years, reduced liquidity, thin volume, and institutional tax-loss selling and rebalancing. In a discussion with Maggie Lake, the author noted that yields have topped and could drop further, while TLT rallied to the July 6-month calendar range high before selling off after an auction. The Real Motion Indicator showed a mean reversion sell signal, though a bullish divergence exists with price above the 50-DMA but below the 200-DMA.

The dollar's rally to the 80-month moving average represented a technical bounce into resistance; a break below 98 would suggest further declines, which would be bullish for commodities and energy. A weakening dollar, lower yields, and rising gold prices typically indicate risk-off conditions. The divergence between growth and value continues to widen, with key levels identified for monitoring market direction.

Professor Noelle Selin delivers a lecture on mercury regulation, focusing on the Minamata Convention, the first new global environmental treaty in over a decade, signed in October 2013. She explains that mercury is a global concern because emissions travel through the atmosphere for six months to a year, mixing globally before depositing into ecosystems where it converts to methyl mercury, a neurotoxin that bioaccumulates in food chains and causes neurological and cardiovascular harm.

Major mercury sources include coal combustion, artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM), and various products like thermometers, batteries, fluorescent lamps, and dental amalgam. Selin traces the treaty's history, noting that US participation shifted under the Obama administration, enabling negotiations to begin in 2010. The US ratified quickly because existing domestic laws already aligned with the treaty.

The convention uses a "negative list" approach, banning mercury in specified products by 2020 with exemptions (e.g., vaccine preservatives). Scientific analysis primarily informed the decision to act, while specific provisions resulted from political negotiation rather than technical assessment. The EU has become the leading global standard-setter for chemicals regulation, with many developing countries adopting EU or German standards due to limited technical capacity.

For ASGM, the treaty emphasizes capacity building and formalization rather than elimination, as mining supports many livelihoods. Selin notes that negotiations move slowly due to interpretation requirements, delegation size disparities, and last-minute compromises. Her analysis suggests the treaty will prevent increases in environmental mercury rather than reduce current levels, making its importance primarily legal and political—signaling that mercury use is globally discouraged.

Jim Cramer has reversed his positive stance on Snap, roughly two months after comparing it to early Facebook following its strong fourth-quarter earnings. Cramer now cites Snapchat's December redesign, which separated media and celebrity content from personal contacts, as a significant concern. The redesign drew criticism from celebrities including Kylie Jenner, whose tweet contributed to a 7% share decline. Cramer worries advertisers may leave if user engagement drops and considers the stock too expensive currently, though he indicated he would buy at a lower price. Snap reports first-quarter results on May 1, with Wall Street expecting an adjusted loss of $0.17 per share on $243.85 million in revenue.

Researchers led by Dr. Shinichi Furuya of the NeuroPiano Institute and Sony Computer Science Laboratories scientifically confirmed that pianists can alter piano timbre through touch, resolving a century-old question. Using a proprietary sensor system (Hackkey) to measure all 88 keys at 1,000 fps and 0.01 mm resolution, the team analyzed performances by 20 pianists intending various timbres. In psychophysical experiments, 40 listeners—both pianists and non-musicians—consistently perceived the intended timbres, even when volume and tempo were controlled, though pianists discerned differences more sensitively. Linear mixed-effects analysis identified specific movement features, such as escapement acceleration and hand synchronization deviation, as causal factors. The findings, published in PNAS, may inform music education, neuroscience, rehabilitation, skill transfer, and human interface design.

The ambassador pattern enables service brokering by separating application logic from service discovery logic. The application connects to a localhost service while an ambassador container introspects the environment and brokers the appropriate connection. This pattern also supports request splitting for experimentation, where nginx can be configured (using IP hashing and weight parameters) to route a percentage of traffic to experimental versions while maintaining consistent user experiences.

The adapter pattern modifies an application container's interface to conform to predefined standards for monitoring, logging, or health checks. Examples include using Prometheus exporters to standardize metrics from services like Redis, fluentd plugins to normalize log formats, and adapter containers to implement rich health checks for databases like MySQL without modifying the original container. This modular approach enables reuse and community sharing.

Multi-node distributed patterns include microservices architectures, which offer reliability, agility, and independent scaling but complicate debugging and design. Replicated load-balanced services use identical stateless replicas behind a load balancer, requiring readiness probes and often adding caching (e.g., Varnish) and SSL termination (e.g., nginx) layers for performance and security.

Sharded services distribute data across replicas when state exceeds single-machine capacity. Sharding functions require determinism and uniformity, typically using hash functions with modulo operators. Consistent hashing minimizes remapping during resharding. Replicated sharded caches provide resilience, while hot sharding dynamically scales shards experiencing disproportionate traffic.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing across leaf nodes, with a root combining partial results. Increased parallelism has diminishing returns due to overhead and straggler problems, where slow nodes delay overall responses.

Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) provides event-driven, serverless computing that simplifies deployment but complicates debugging, is unsuitable for background processing or memory-intensive applications, and becomes costly at scale. The decorator pattern using FaaS transforms requests or responses, such as adding default values to API calls.

The ADS868xW device uses a multiSPI digital interface for data communication between the device and host controller, supporting multiple data transfer protocols. The interface module contains shift registers, configuration registers, and a protocol unit, functioning as a 32-bit input-output shift register.

Host-to-device connection topologies include single device configurations (standard SPI or all multiSPI options) and multiple devices in daisy-chain topology. In daisy-chain mode, devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK signals, with SDI/SDO pins connected sequentially, requiring 32×N SCLK edges per optimal frame.

The device operates in three functional states: RESET, ACQ, and CONV. The RST pin supports either application reset or power-on reset (POR), determined by the RSTn_APP bit. The device acquires signals in ACQ state and performs conversions in CONV state using an internal clock.

Data transfer frames begin with a CONVST/CS falling edge and end at the rising edge. Frames with exactly 32 SCLKs are optimal; shorter frames are treated as NOP commands, while longer frames use the last 32 bits as the command. The device supports byte and half-word read/write commands, with HWORD commands ignoring the LSB of the 9-bit address.

Data read protocols include legacy SPI-compatible (single or dual SDO-x) and source-synchronous (SRC) protocols, where the RVS pin provides an output clock synchronous with data.

The device features nine configuration registers controlling device ID, reset/power control, SDI/SDO protocols, data output, input range, and alarm thresholds with hysteresis. Two low-power modes (NAP and power-down) reduce consumption at lower throughput rates. The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, requiring proper decoupling capacitors for optimal PSRR performance.

OSCAR (One-Shot multi-label Causal AutoRegressive discovery) is introduced as a method for causal discovery in high-dimensional event sequences, addressing limitations of existing approaches that are computationally intractable with thousands of nodes. The method is fully parallelised, making its per-batch complexity independent of event and label cardinality, and it produces a causal indicator quantifying whether events promote or inhibit labels.

The approach relies on assumptions including causal sufficiency, temporal precedence, bounded lagged effects, and oracle-quality density estimators. Under these, the authors prove Markov Boundary identifiability.

Evaluated on a vehicular dataset with 29,100 event types and 474 labels across 50,000 samples, OSCAR achieved 55.26% precision, 31.37% recall, and 40.02% F1-score in 11.7 minutes, while competing local structure learning algorithms (IAMB, CMB, MB-by-MB, PCD-by-PCD, MI-MCF) failed to complete within a 3-day limit.

The lecture addresses iterative methods for solving large sparse matrix equations (Ax = b), where direct elimination is too costly in time and storage. Since multiplying a sparse matrix by a vector is fast, iterative methods aim to approach the solution quickly rather than exactly.

A key decision is choosing a preconditioner P, a matrix similar to A but simpler. The iteration is framed as Px_{k+1} = (P-A)x_k + b. Convergence is governed by the iteration matrix M = I - P⁻¹A, specifically its spectral radius (largest eigenvalue magnitude), which must be below 1.

Several preconditioner choices are discussed:
- Jacobi: P is the diagonal of A
- Gauss-Seidel: P is the lower triangular part of A, allowing back substitution
- Successive Overrelaxation (SOR): weighted combinations
- Incomplete LU (ILU): approximate LU factors that limit fill-in

For the standard tridiagonal matrix (2s on diagonal, -1s off), eigenvalues of A fall between 0 and 4. Jacobi's method produces eigenvalues of M equal to cos(jπ/(n+1)). The largest eigenvalues, near ±1, correspond to the lowest and highest frequency eigenvectors, slowing convergence. Convergence requires roughly n² iterations to reduce error meaningfully.

Two error measures are distinguished: the solution error (e_k) and the residual (r_k = Ae_k). Residuals shrink faster than solution errors because A⁻¹ amplifies low-frequency components.

Weighted Jacobi (with ω = 2/3) eliminates the high-frequency problem but low frequencies persist. Gauss-Seidel effectively squares Jacobi's eigenvalues, doubling convergence speed per step, but remains insufficient. These limitations motivate multigrid methods, covered in subsequent lectures.

A Reversal Day refers to a day when a stock or market index changes direction significantly, either upward (Bullish Reversal Day/Selling Climax) or downward (Bearish Reversal Day/Blowoff), often after an extended trend and accompanied by high trading volume.

Reversals can be caused by shifts in market sentiment, economic conditions (such as interest rate, inflation, or GDP changes), company-specific news, and technical analysis patterns. Different markets, including stocks, forex, commodities, and bonds, are prone to reversals for varying reasons.

Traders identify Reversal Days through trend changes, heavy trading volume, technical indicators (moving averages, RSI, Bollinger Bands), support and resistance levels, and divergences with RSI or MACD.

Backtests on gold (GLD) using Amibroker showed that the Bullish Reversal Day strategy produced positive average gains across 1–25 day exits, with the highest average gain (2.02%) at 24 days, though trade frequency was low. The Bearish Reversal Day strategy produced losses, partly attributed to gold's overnight upward drift.

This cross-sectional study investigated burnout prevalence, associated factors, and coping strategies among 243 prison officers (POs) at Nsawam Medium Security Prison in Ghana, using the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey, Work Environment Scale, and Coping Methods Checklist.

The overall burnout prevalence was 9%, lower than rates reported in many other studies. While 42% of officers showed high emotional exhaustion and 68.7% reported low personal accomplishment, depersonalization was more evenly distributed. Officers perceived irregular shifts (71.6%), heavy workload (49.0%), and lack of training opportunities (47.7%) as primary causes of burnout. Over half disagreed their workplace had a supportive culture, though many took pride in their work and felt accepted by colleagues.

Logistic regression identified sex and education as significant factors associated with burnout. Female officers were more likely to experience burnout than males, and officers with diplomas/certificates had lower odds than those with postgraduate degrees. Junior officers experienced more depersonalization than senior officers, and main-shift officers reported higher emotional exhaustion.

The most common coping strategies were talking to colleagues (62.5%), anticipating off-duty time (60.1%), and talking to family (54.3%); alcohol use was least reported (29.2%).

The study concludes that addressing irregular shifts, workload, and training opportunities is necessary to reduce burnout among POs.
