StockX, the Detroit-based "Stock Market of Things" marketplace, has added BAPE and Palace to its streetwear category, which launched in October 2017 with Supreme. CEO Josh Luber cited the expansion as evidence of growth across the company's sneakers, watches, handbags, and streetwear categories. Scotty Newman, formerly of 3peatLA, leads the BAPE team, while Kenny Locklier manages PALACE. At launch, StockX will offer over 4,000 BAPE products and more than 3,000 PALACE products. BAPE, founded in 1993 by NIGO, was acquired by I.T. Group in 2011. PALACE, a British skateboard brand, was launched by Lev Tanju in 2010. StockX, founded by Luber, Greg Schwartz, and Dan Gilbert, has over 200 employees and generates more than $2 million in daily sales.

Vertigo, an iOS app, has become the first to integrate both Apple Music and Spotify Premium, enabling cross-platform music-sharing between subscribers of either service. Users can import playlists, discover music, and share songs that friends can play through their own subscriptions. Beyond sharing, Vertigo offers "live sessions," allowing users to live-stream listening experiences with video, photos, real-time chat, or audio commentary, shared with individuals, close friends, or the whole community. CEO Greg Leekley emphasized that users shouldn't have to choose between platforms. Vertigo pays royalties to rights holders for shared songs and requires paid subscriptions, likely facilitating its API access. The app could address Apple Music's limited social features, as Apple has de-emphasized its Connect social network.

Glen Campbell, a country music legend, is in the final stages of Alzheimer's disease, according to a People magazine interview with his family. Despite his condition, music remains a comforting presence in his life. His daughter Ashley shared that he sometimes smiles and sings along to unknown tunes. Campbell's final album, "Adios," recorded in 2012, was released on June 9. Ashley noted that Alzheimer's did not take away his voice or his soul in music.

Current cytogenomic approaches for hematological malignancies (karyotyping, FISH, chromosomal microarray, and NGS) have limitations in resolution, subjectivity, labor requirements, and comprehensive variant detection. Optical Genome Mapping (OGM) is emerging as an alternative technique that combines optical analysis of ultra-high molecular weight DNA with high-throughput molecular approaches to detect structural rearrangements and copy number variants.

This study extended a framework by the International Consortium for OGM in Hematologic Malignancies by implementing an analysis and reporting workflow using Variant Intelligence Applications (VIA) software. Ten retrospective myeloid malignancy cases (9 AML, 1 MDS) were analyzed 5-6 times each by independent technologist-director teams to assess efficiency and reproducibility.

OGM via VIA identified all variants detected by standard of care (SOC) testing, including fusions such as BCR::ABL1, CBFB::MYH11, RUNX1::RUNX1T1, and KMT2A::MLLT10, which were unanimously classified as Tier 1A. OGM additionally revealed variants missed by SOC in five of six positive cases, including large copy number losses, trisomies, and complex rearrangements. Technologist review averaged 25.2 minutes for negative cases, 28.5 minutes for simple cases, and 47.3 minutes for complex cases, representing approximately a 50% time reduction compared to Bionano Access alone.

The authors conclude that OGM analysis using Bionano Access and VIA provides a streamlined, efficient, and objective approach for interpreting and reporting cytogenomic variants in hematological disorders, with potential to standardize variant analysis and reduce labor demands in clinical laboratories.

A reporter traveled across Germany, Austria, Italy, and Switzerland in October 2022 using a $477 Eurail pass, taking eight train rides between six cities over seven days. With upgrades to business class and overnight sleeper bunks, the total cost was $560. The reporter found train travel more comfortable, scenic, and sustainable than flying, citing easier boarding, no ear-popping or dehydration, lie-flat sleeping options, and better views. Although a comparable 2025 flight itinerary would cost about $440 in economy, the reporter prefers trains for future European travel.

Brazilian stocks rose on Thursday, driven by Vale SA shares, which climbed up to 4.9 percent after the miner reported a record first-quarter iron ore output for the period, up 11.2 percent year-on-year. Itaú BBA maintained an "outperform" rating on Vale. Steelmaker Usiminas also gained after reversing a first-quarter loss. The Brazilian real fluctuated alongside other Latin American currencies amid geopolitical tensions in North Korea and Syria, and election uncertainty in France and the UK. Polls showing Emmanuel Macron leading Marine Le Pen eased some investor concerns.

The 2018 Livestock Judging Season ended for the Rio Blanco 4-H senior team at Colorado State University's 73rd annual Colorado 4-H June conference. Macy Collins, Jilly Bumguardner, Marryn Shults, and Tatumn Kennedy competed for RBC. Collins finished as the third high individual overall, while Shults placed seventh. Collins competed individually because her national qualifying eligibility was used in 2015 with the state champion team.

The contest includes twelve livestock classes and six sets of oral reasons over a 15-hour day. In beef, Shults placed fourth and Collins fifth; in swine, Collins was third; in sheep/goat, Collins was fourth and Shults fifth. Shults scored 572 of 600 possible points; Collins scored 570. In oral reasons, Collins finished third with 281 points and Shults 12th with 270.

Collins made the Colorado State 4-H Livestock All State team and will attend Hutchinson Junior College on a full scholarship. She was part of RBC's first State Champion Team in 2015 and competed in multiple states.

U.S. President Donald Trump warned Iran against restarting its nuclear program while meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron, who sought to preserve the 2015 nuclear accord. Trump criticized the deal as "terrible" for not addressing ballistic missiles or Iran's regional involvement, though he said an agreement with Macron could be reached soon. Iran indicated it may expand its nuclear program or exit the nuclear non-proliferation treaty if Trump withdraws from the accord. A U.S. withdrawal could heighten regional tensions and complicate negotiations with North Korea. Macron's visit also addressed European steel tariff exemptions, the Paris climate accord, and U.S. troop presence in Syria. The Trumps were set to host the Macrons at a state dinner.

The holder assists the kicker on field goals and extra points by catching the snap and placing the ball precisely for the kick. The position requires soft hands, quick and consistent ball placement, and the ability to rotate the laces away from the kicker. Holders must work in sync with the long snapper and kicker to create a reliable routine. On fake field goals, holders may throw, run, or flip the ball. Any body type can play the position, and in the NFL, punters often serve as holders, while high school and college teams may use backup quarterbacks or receivers. No holding statistics are tracked, and there is no consensus on the best holders ever, but great kickers often credit their holders for their success. Although overlooked, the holder's precise execution can determine whether a scoring opportunity is converted or missed.

The Daily Examiner is transitioning from a metered digital subscription model to a premium model, where some stories will be subscriber-only, marked with a PLUS symbol. Essential public safety information will remain freely accessible. Existing subscribers are unaffected and retain unlimited access to the site and other News Corp publications including The Courier-Mail, The Daily Telegraph, and Herald-Sun. Subscriptions include newspaper delivery options, app access, a daily email newsletter, and breaking news alerts. Sign-up is available online or by phone.

Thailand recorded 390 road deaths during the seven-day Songkran new year period, an 11 per cent decrease from the previous year, following a junta campaign to reduce accidents. Since taking power in 2014, the junta has approved harsher penalties for drink driving, seized vehicles, and required offenders to visit mortuaries, though earlier campaigns yielded no reductions. Junta chief Prayut Chan-O-Cha said he was not satisfied with the results. Drunk driving caused 28 per cent of this year's Songkran accidents, with authorities seizing 5,600 motorbikes and 1,800 cars. According to a 2015 WHO report, Thailand has the world's second most dangerous roads per capita. Speeding and non-helmet use are also cited as major factors. Neighbouring Myanmar reported 285 road deaths during the same period.

The European Union plans to urge multilateral development banks (MDBs), including the World Bank, to align financing with the Paris Agreement and prioritise climate action, according to a draft policy seen by Reuters. The proposal seeks to shift lending from fossil fuels toward low-carbon projects, improve transparency, offer local currency financing, and attract private investment.

Led by Germany and France, the initiative will be featured at upcoming World Bank and IMF meetings. The EU argues MDBs must expand beyond poverty reduction to address climate costs. The United States opposes the plan, warning it could detract from core development goals.

In 2024, MDBs directed a record $137 billion into climate projects, though European leaders consider this inadequate. If adopted, the proposal could reshape international development finance, but U.S. resistance may hinder consensus.

The Supreme Court of Canada unanimously ruled that records documenting abuse claims from former residential school students can be destroyed after 15 years. The decision upheld a lower court ruling and addressed the tension between victim privacy and historical documentation. The records stem from an independent assessment process, established under a 2006 settlement agreement, which provided compensation to Indigenous people who attended residential schools. The court determined that negotiators intended the process to be confidential, and both claimants and alleged perpetrators relied on those assurances. Participants disclosed personal narratives and signed confidentiality agreements before private hearings. Over 37,000 claims were filed under the process.

Eric Thames hit a two-run homer in the fifth inning to lead the Milwaukee Brewers past the Minnesota Twins 2-0 on July 3, 2018. The homer, off Jake Odorizzi, followed a walk and steal by pinch-hitter Nate Orf. Thames now has 12 home runs on the season, with eight opening scoring for Milwaukee.

Brewers starter Junior Guerra pitched five shutout innings, allowing two hits with eight strikeouts. Josh Hader added three hitless relief innings, and Corey Knebel struck out the side for his ninth save. Odorizzi allowed two runs over five innings with nine strikeouts.

The Twins dropped to 1-7 on their road trip. First baseman Joe Mauer recorded no putouts or assists, a rare occurrence. An umpiring delay in the ninth prompted an argument from Twins manager Paul Molitor. Jose Berrios is scheduled to start the series finale against Chase Anderson.

A McKinsey memorandum dated December 6, 2000, provides a periodic update on international electric power sector privatization and restructuring activity from June to November 2000. The report notes that privatizations and restructuring continue globally, with governments opening generation markets to foreign investors, state-owned utilities unbundling, and competition being introduced at wholesale and retail levels.

In Europe, the EU Directive has spurred competition, with mergers, alliances, and consolidation dominating the market. Country-specific updates cover Austria, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the UK, detailing their market opening schedules and restructuring progress. Central and Eastern European countries, including Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Hungary, Moldova, Romania, Russia, Slovak Republic, Turkey, and Ukraine, are pursuing privatization to attract capital, often motivated by EU membership aspirations.

In Asia-Pacific, economies are recovering from the economic crisis, with governments resuming unbundling plans, though IPPs face ongoing issues with PPAs and government guarantees. Updates cover Australia, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, New Zealand, Pakistan, Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam.

Latin American countries have postponed some privatizations due to inflation and currency fluctuations, though transmission system privatizations are increasing. The region's heavy reliance on hydropower has caused shortages during droughts. Updates are provided for Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Jamaica, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, Venezuela, and the Virgin Islands.

African and Middle Eastern governments are increasingly opening power sectors to foreign investment, primarily through IPPs, with regional transmission links emerging as a notable trend. Updates cover Algeria, Ghana, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Tunisia, and the United Arab Emirates.

Every Inauguration Day since 1789, Americans renew their dedication to the nation. Washington's era focused on creating the Nation, Lincoln's on preserving it from internal disruption, and the present on protecting it from external threats.

Nations are measured by the endurance of their spirit, not years. Though some believe democracy is fading before tyranny, Americans reject this. Eight years ago, amid crisis, the country acted decisively, achieving greater security while preserving the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, the separation of powers, and free elections.

Democracy endures because it relies on individual initiative, enlists people's will, enables progress, and continues spreading worldwide.

Like a person, a Nation has a body, a mind, and a spirit—the last being most vital. America's spirit was shaped by immigrants seeking freedom and is rooted in documents from the Magna Charta to the Gettysburg Address. Despite progress, work remains to address poverty and expand opportunity.

Without its spirit, America would perish. That spirit speaks through government at all levels and from other nations. Quoting Washington's 1789 Inaugural on liberty's "sacred fire," the passage warns against letting doubt extinguish it. Protecting democracy justifies sacrifices for national defense, and Americans will move forward in service to country.

Former CIA case officer Kevin Mallory, 60, is on trial in Alexandria, Virginia, accused of providing classified information, including details about human assets, to a Chinese spy for $25,000. Prosecutor Jennifer Gellie said Mallory was caught after customs agents found $16,500 in undeclared cash at O'Hare Airport in April 2017. During a subsequent interview, a Samsung phone given to him by the Chinese revealed text exchanges with a Chinese recruiter, and computer discs found at his home contained secret documents.

Defence attorney Geremy Kamens argued Mallory was a loyal American feeding the Chinese phoney documents to expose their operation, noting Mallory contacted CIA colleagues in February 2017, before the Shanghai trip. Two CIA witnesses confirmed the February contact. The trial is rare for the Eastern District of Virginia, and Mallory, charged under a statute last used in 2003, faces up to life in prison.

Olean's Common Council unanimously authorized Mayor Bill Aiello to apply for the state Downtown Revitalization Initiative, which will award $10 million each to 10 communities statewide. If awarded, it would be among the largest grants the city has received. Mary George, community development program coordinator, prepared the application in three weeks. The proposed area extends from Olean General Hospital to the Allegheny River and from Franchot Park to Seventh Street. Project ideas include redeveloping the former Manufacturers Hanover building, funding business incubators, expanding downtown theater options, improving access to Lincoln Park, and creating a park near Olean General Hospital. Aiello noted the city could also qualify for over $2 million through the Buffalo Billion initiative. John Sayegh of JCC's Cattaraugus County Campus supported the application and offered collaboration on upgrading the Cutco Theater.

Industrial enterprises face challenges including geopolitical uncertainties, energy prices, supply chain disruptions, and sustainability demands, while digitalization transforms manufacturing. IDC's December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers from manufacturing enterprises (500+ employees) in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland examines IT-based simulation, modeling, and data analysis use.

Simulation and modeling support product development, production planning, and quality management, with deployment expected to reach 90% within two years. Three-quarters of respondents view innovation as the top business goal, while 57% cite quality improvement. Integrated data strategies creating a "single source of truth" are essential to overcome data silos.

IT advances enable virtual prototyping, digital twins, design optimization, and high-performance data analytics (used by 42%). However, 42% of respondents use outdated simulations, and half report calculations take too long.

High-performance computing (HPC) is viewed as a game changer by 81% of respondents (96% among current HPC users). HPC enables complex calculations, higher quality, new usage scenarios, and increased agility. Over a quarter of enterprises use professional HPC infrastructures, with 39% planning deployment.

Challenges include security (72%), energy consumption (58%), costs, computing power limits, and expertise shortages (42%). Most users prefer external HPC infrastructures (87%) or colocation (74%) over on-premises solutions (6%).

Cloud-based HPC and HPC-as-a-Service (HPCaaS) offer scalability, cost flexibility (OPEX vs. CAPEX), modern technology access, and support for new business models. Public and hybrid cloud architectures are projected to dominate. 81% of HPC users intend to implement HPC-based business models.

IDC recommends establishing virtual development, holistic data strategies, evaluating suitable HPC operating models, prioritizing scalability/security/energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise.

The AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 Specification Update documents multiple hardware issues and their resolutions:

**PIC Interrupt/Clock Gating**: Edge-configured PIC interrupts may be missed if the interrupt source remains high when the Local bus clock gates off, potentially hanging the system. Resolution: disable automatic clock gating.

**ATAC/ACC PRD Prefetch**: Non-8-byte aligned PRD tables may cause prefetch errors during UDMA/audio operations. Resolution: ensure PRD tables are defined before operations start or kept two tables ahead.

**UDMA Write CRC Corruption**: After device termination following a prior UDMA read with host termination, CRC errors occur. Resolution: use UDMA I/O blocking via ATAC Error MSR.

**ATAC SSMI, Main GLIU Clock, PMC Register Access**: Various issues with SSMI blocking, ASMI wakeups, and byte/word accesses to PM1_EN/PM1_STS/PMC registers causing hangs or corruption. Resolutions include avoiding features, disabling clock gating, or using SMI I/O traps.

**KEL Emulation**: HceStatus CmdData bit does not distinguish Port 060h/064h writes, and Snoop mode incorrectly modifies HCE registers. Resolutions use ASMI trap information and software state save/restore.

**PCI/Timing Issues**: Possible memory read failure on back-to-back fetches (no real-world impact); IRDY#/DEVSEL# violate tVAL minimum (add capacitors if needed); SSMI may not be synchronous with simultaneous IRQ (use processor SSMIs instead).

**UDMA/ATAPI/IDE**: PIO after bus master enable fails; ATAPI packet command after bus master enable can hang; tACK bits don't affect UDMA timing; ATAC hangs with non-DWORD aligned PRDs. Resolutions: use normal UDMA procedures and DWORD alignment.

**ACPI S3 Wakeup**: GPIO[27:24] don't wake from S3. Resolution: use PWRBTN# with external OR circuitry.

**RTC/LPC/USB/SMB**: RTC CMOS RAM read errors after extended port writes; LPC I/O fails during block/demand DMA (use single transfer mode); USB clock gating unreliable (disable it); LPC aborts on certain SYNC patterns (use PLD workaround); SMB NEGACK bit behaves incorrectly (write twice to clear).

**GLPCI/GPIO/Power Management**: Retry counter counts all PCI retries; GPIO High Bank atomic writes fail after suspend (use Read-Modify-Write); SMBus hold time too short; LOWBAT_FLAG missing after abnormal standby; SLEEP_X/Y not deasserted if delays exceed PM_SED.

Uber has launched a nationwide panic button feature, announced in April following reports of alleged sexual assaults. The button enables riders to call 911 directly from the app's home screen, displaying their real-time location in most cities. In a pilot program across seven cities, including Denver, Louisville, and soon Nashville, the app automatically sends location and vehicle details—color, make, model, year, and license plate—to emergency dispatchers. CEO Dana Khosrowshahi and Safety Products Director Sachin Kansal emphasized the goal of providing quick, accurate assistance during emergencies.

The speaker discusses a game against Scotty Bowman's defensively sound team. They acknowledge being unhappy with not generating chances and having no immediate answer. Early nerves led to conceding goals, but aside from ten minutes, the game was even. Giving Detroit a two-goal lead was costly, especially given current trends where two goals is significant. The power play underperformed, and the speaker admits not playing their best, wanting better results and more contribution.

In the spring of 1953, the free world weighs the chance for a just peace, recalling the similar hope of 1945 that faded as the U.S. and Soviet Union took divergent paths after World War II. The United States pursued peace guided by principles: no people is an inherent enemy, security requires cooperation, nations have the right to self-determination, no nation should dictate to others, and peace rests on just relations rather than arms races. The Soviet Union instead sought security through force, subversion, and power superiority, prompting free nations to arm themselves defensively while remaining open to genuine peace.

The cost of this arms race is immense, diverting resources from human needs—each weapon representing schools, hospitals, homes, and food foregone. With Stalin's death and new Soviet leadership, an opportunity has emerged to change course.

The United States proposes concrete steps: an honorable armistice in Korea, ending attacks in Indochina and Malaya, concluding an Austrian treaty, unifying Germany through free elections, ending Europe's division, and reducing armaments through limits on military forces, strategic materials, atomic energy (controlled internationally for peaceful use), and other destructive weapons, all enforced by U.N. inspection.

Savings from disarmament could fund world aid and reconstruction, helping develop underdeveloped areas and stimulate trade. The U.S. asks whether the Soviet Union will support genuine peace in Asia, allow free choice of government in Eastern Europe, and agree to disarmament with U.N. oversight. Only deeds, not words, can prove sincerity, offering humanity a chance at a golden age of freedom and peace.

Digitalization is essential in modern business, facilitating supply chain activities and influencing brand image through digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth. This study examined how digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth affect sustainable supply chain performance through brand image and supply chain image in Indonesian ICT companies.

Data were collected from 315 valid responses out of 568 distributed questionnaires among ICT company employees across 10 randomly selected clusters in Indonesia. Analysis was conducted using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM).

Seven hypotheses were developed and tested. Results confirmed that digital customer experience (t=3.086) and electronic word of mouth (t=11.084) positively influenced brand image. Brand image positively affected supply chain image (t=25.167), which in turn positively influenced sustainable supply chain performance (t=84.298). Mediation effects of brand image and supply chain image were also supported. The model explained 82.3% variance in sustainable supply chain performance.

The findings suggest Indonesian ICT companies should enhance brand image through digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth via e-commerce practices to strengthen supply chain performance.

The patent describes a hybrid gas turbine electric propulsion system and method for operating it during descent. The gas turbine engine includes a core with compressor and turbine sections connected via shafts, along with an electric motor coupled to the low-speed shaft. The motor functions as a generator during certain operational modes, storing electricity in an energy storage system.

The engine is undersized relative to takeoff or climb thrust requirements, with peak efficiency designed for cruise rather than takeoff. During descent mode, the core is effectively shut off or maintained at a minimum temperature to prevent thermal cycling. Aircraft systems, such as environmental controls, are switched to electric operation, powered by stored energy and supplemented by an electric compressor replacing engine bleed air.

Optionally, the fan is allowed to windmill during descent, rotating the low-speed spool and driving the motor as a generator. Alternatively, stored energy can power the motor to rotate the spool, generating thrust sufficient to overcome engine drag or match conventional descent thrust. This approach reduces fuel burn and emissions by decoupling aircraft system operation from engine operation during low-power modes.

On February 8, 2021, Apple Inc. issued and sold $14 billion in senior unsecured notes across six series: $2.5 billion of 0.700% Notes due 2026, $2.5 billion of 1.200% Notes due 2028, $2.75 billion of 1.650% Notes due 2031, $1.5 billion of 2.375% Notes due 2041, $3 billion of 2.650% Notes due 2051, and $1.75 billion of 2.800% Notes due 2061. The issuance was conducted under an underwriting agreement dated February 1, 2021, with Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, and Morgan Stanley as representatives. Interest will be paid semi-annually on February 8 and August 8, starting August 8, 2021. The Notes rank equally with Apple's other unsecured, unsubordinated debt.

Cloud providers offer continuously evolving HPC technologies, with 52% of respondents valuing fast access to cutting-edge analysis methods and hardware as core to HPCaaS innovation. Beyond faster calculations, new data processing methods enable novel digital products, services, and business models central to digital transformation.

Industry leaders highlight cloud-based HPC benefits: Hexagon's Mahesh Kailasam notes energy efficiency and sustainability gains, while Bridgestone's Luigi Lobello cites agility and cost-effectiveness advantages over on-premises limitations like peak capacity, hardware freshness, and upfront investment costs. Bridgestone is taking a gradual cloud transition approach. Notably, 81% of current HPC users intend to implement further solutions.

IDC concludes that IT-based simulation, modeling, and data analytics are key enablers for manufacturers facing disruptive change, supporting product development, supply chain optimization, sustainability, and digital business models. HPC is becoming prerequisite technology, with public cloud and HPCaaS offering significant potential alongside traditional architectures. Success depends on integrating data across the value chain as a single source of truth.

Recommendations include: establishing virtual product development, creating a holistic data strategy, evaluating the best HPC operating model (on-premises, HPCaaS, or hybrid), prioritizing scalability/security/energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise.

The findings derive from a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and departmental decision-makers at industrial enterprises with over 500 employees across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended October 30, 2022. As of November 11, 2022, 2.46 billion shares of common stock were outstanding.

Third-quarter revenue was $5.93 billion, down 17% year-over-year and 12% sequentially. Net income was $680 million ($0.27 diluted EPS), compared to $2.46 billion a year earlier. Gross margin fell to 53.6% from 65.2%, primarily due to a $702 million inventory charge largely tied to weaker Data Center demand in China. Operating expenses rose 31% to $2.58 billion.

By segment, Compute & Networking revenue grew 27% to $3.82 billion, while Graphics revenue declined 48% to $2.12 billion. Data Center revenue rose 31% year-over-year, Gaming fell 51%, Professional Visualization dropped 65%, and Automotive increased 86%.

In February 2022, NVIDIA and SoftBank terminated the Arm acquisition due to regulatory challenges, resulting in a $1.35 billion acquisition termination charge. During the third quarter of fiscal 2023, the U.S. government imposed new export license requirements affecting sales of A100 and H100 products to China and Russia.

NVIDIA held $13.14 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities as of October 30, 2022. The company repurchased $3.65 billion of shares and paid $100 million in dividends during the quarter, with $8.28 billion remaining under its repurchase authorization through December 2023. Total long-term debt was $9.70 billion across notes maturing from 2023 to 2060.

A federal judge ruled Tuesday that Nirvana's 1991 album cover depicting a naked baby swimming toward a dollar bill does not constitute child pornography. U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin dismissed the lawsuit filed in 2021 by Spencer Elden, who was photographed at 4 months old and sued under a federal law providing civil remedies for child crime victims. Olguin evaluated factors including genitalia focus, sexual suggestiveness, nudity, and intent to elicit sexual response, finding only nudity applied. He compared the image to a family photo of a nude child bathing, deeming it insufficient to establish lasciviousness.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation in the 2014 murder of Dan Markel, a Florida State University law professor and her former son-in-law. Before sentencing, Adelson maintained her innocence, claiming a lack of evidence, prompting Judge Stephen Everett to warn her about her "utter lack of remorse." Prosecutors said the motive stemmed from the Adelson family's desire to relocate Markel's ex-wife, Wendi Adelson, and their children to South Florida. Her son Charlie Adelson, his girlfriend Katherine Magbanua, and one hit man were convicted of murder; a second hit man pleaded guilty to second-degree murder. Donna's husband, Harvey Adelson, defended her innocence in court.

Myrna LaPlante, a Saskatoon woman whose aunt Emily Osmond went missing in 2006, opposes the Assembly of First Nations' December 7 vote (48-15) calling for chief commissioner Marion Buller's resignation from the National Inquiry into Murdered and Missing Indigenous Women and Girls. LaPlante said families were not consulted before the vote and stated she would withdraw her family's story if the commission were reset. She supports extending the inquiry's deadline by two years beyond November 2018, arguing the original mandate was insufficient. However, other Saskatchewan families back Buller's resignation. Lillian Ewenin of Kawacatoose First Nation cited poor communication and scheduling issues at November's Saskatoon hearings. Danielle Ewenin criticized the commission for lacking a holistic approach to community trauma.

With 30-year fixed mortgage rates near 5 percent, Scott Sheldon outlines ways to boost mortgage borrowing power. Paying off debt lowers the debt-to-income ratio, since lenders evaluate minimum payments rather than interest rates; exceeding a 50 percent ratio creates borrowing challenges. Adding a co-signer shares borrowing ability and liability, removable only by refinancing or selling. Switching loan programs, such as Freddie Mac to Fannie Mae or conventional to FHA, can affect approval. Larger down payments help but less than paying off debt. Changing jobs within the same field before applying may also help, but requires loan officer guidance.

Singapore, a densely populated multiethnic city-state that gained independence in 1965, has developed into a globally recognized economic and educational hub. Its success is attributed to leadership under the People's Action Party, a merit-based ethos, and investment in human capital.

The evolution of special education in Singapore is divided into pre- and post-2004 periods. Before 2004, special education operated separately from mainstream schools, primarily run by voluntary welfare organizations, with integration rather than inclusion as the goal. In 2004, Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong's call for inclusive education marked a turning point, leading to Enabling Masterplans, ratification of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (2013), and the Compulsory Education Act (2019).

Teacher preparation expanded through the National Institute of Education (NIE), which introduced programs including the Diploma in Special Education (DISE), Advanced Diploma (ADISE), Certificate in Special Needs Support for mainstream teachers, and training for Special Educational Needs Officers (SENOs). The number of students with disabilities in mainstream schools grew from 2,500 in 2005 to 35,500 currently, with 80% served in mainstream settings.

Key issues remain: special schools operate under social service agencies rather than the Ministry of Education, resulting in lower teacher salaries; there is a limited continuum of special education options for students with higher support needs; and special education teacher preparation is less comprehensive than mainstream programs, with no undergraduate degree offered. Singapore's education system is shifting toward holistic, inclusive development through the "Learn for Life" movement.

An email from Jean Munoz distributes IEP news summaries for July 31, 2001, covering California's energy crisis. Key stories include:

- A Los Angeles Times commentary by Kathleen Connell and Peter Navarro criticizing Governor Davis' $43 billion long-term power contracts as overpriced and burdensome to California's economy.

- Reports that the SEC launched a preliminary inquiry, requested by Secretary of State Bill Jones, into whether Davis' energy consultants used inside information to trade power company stocks. Five consultants were fired for possible conflicts of interest.

- Davis' press secretary Steve Maviglio disclosed purchasing $12,000 in Calpine Corp. stock and owning Enron shares, denying any conflict of interest.

- Consultants Chris Lehane and Mark Fabiani agreed to forgo over $50,000 in state payments following a taxpayer lawsuit over their concurrent work for Southern California Edison.

- A Salon.com article discussing Davis' struggle to orchestrate a bailout of Southern California Edison, which contributed over $350,000 to his campaign.

- San Francisco voters will consider two November ballot measures to establish public power systems, opposed by PG&E.

- California's potential FERC refunds were reduced to under $4 billion, less than half of what the state requested.

- Texas began its deregulated electricity pilot program, with officials promising to avoid California's problems.

- Maryland regulators reviewed BGE's proposed split from Constellation Energy Group.

Sony has released a firmware update for its A7Riii camera, primarily addressing an issue with the 'Set File Name' function and improving overall camera stability. While the update is minor, Mac users running macOS 10.13 (High Sierra) are unable to install it, as the update only supports Mac OS X 10.10–10.11 and macOS 10.12. This incompatibility stems from High Sierra, which has caused issues with various third-party software. Workarounds include using an earlier Mac OSX version or running Windows to install the update.

The lecture covers partial differential equations (PDEs) and introduces probability. Regarding homework 7, students must solve a drug patch diffusion problem using both COMSOL and their own finite volume code. The problem has a very small characteristic length and a large Peclet number, creating sharp concentration gradients that require careful mesh selection and verification of convergence.

The finite volume method treats each mesh element as a small CSTR with uniform concentration, computing exact fluxes across boundaries. Boundary conditions can be handled using direct flux calculations or "ghost volumes" with linear interpolation. For solving the resulting sparse linear system, options include backslash, fsolve, or for large 3D problems, iterative solvers like BiCGSTAB (conjugate gradient).

The CFL number (Δt·u/Δx), from a 1928 paper, must be ≤1 for time-dependent PDEs to avoid unphysical results where material convects across multiple mesh points per time step. Smaller Δx requires smaller Δt, substantially increasing computational cost.

For probability, the professor emphasizes that real-world measurements always involve fluctuations, both from measurement instruments and intrinsic system variability. Continuum equations represent averages over ensembles, while reality involves discrete molecules and quantum probability distributions.

Key probability concepts introduced include joint probabilities P(A and B) = P(A)·P(B|A), Bayes' theorem P(A|B) = P(B|A)·P(A)/P(B), and probability densities for continuous variables. Probability densities must be multiplied by a differential to yield actual probabilities, and cumulative distribution functions F(vx) give the probability of values below a threshold.

On February 14, multiple developments emerged regarding the Trump administration. The New York Times reported U.S. agencies intercepted 2016 calls between Russian intelligence and Trump campaign members, including former chairman Paul Manafort, though no evidence of election-related collaboration was found. The FBI interviewed ousted national security adviser Michael Flynn about his contacts with a Russian official. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called for an independent investigation into Flynn and urged Attorney General Jeff Sessions to recuse himself. Labor secretary nominee Andrew Puzder faced growing Republican skepticism, with five GOP senators, including John Thune, withholding support ahead of his confirmation hearing over his employment of an unauthorized housekeeper. Meanwhile, Linda McMahon was confirmed as Small Business Administration head in an 81-19 vote, and David Shulkin was unanimously confirmed as Veterans Affairs secretary.

A 1968 study by Lew Goldberg examined how consistently doctors diagnosed ulcers from x-rays. Doctors were shown 96 ulcers twice, without knowing duplicates were included, and asked to rate malignancy on a seven-point scale. The doctors disagreed with each other, and each doctor contradicted his or her own previous diagnosis at least once. Researchers then asked the doctors how they made diagnoses and built a simple algorithm based on their answers. The algorithm outperformed even the best doctor. Michael Lewis, recounting this in The Undoing Project, concluded that an equation based on doctors' stated methods could beat the doctors themselves. The author questions how the algorithm handled disagreements and accessed image data in 1968, suggesting a human likely coded the images. The author reflects on implications for expertise and the growing role of artificial intelligence in generating diagnostic rules.

Research by Which? suggests lenders have been quicker to raise mortgage costs than savings rates following the Bank of England's November base rate increase from 0.25% to 0.5%. Of 327 variable instant access savings accounts and ISAs examined, 48% saw no rate change in the five weeks after the rise, while only 21% received the full 0.25% increase. Just 10% of 95 instant access savings providers applied the full rise to all their accounts. For mortgages, 53% of standard variable rate providers increased rates for existing borrowers by the end of 2017, and average rates on two-, three- and five-year fixed deals rose between October and December. Gareth Shaw of Which? accused some institutions of "double standards" and urged fairness ahead of any future rate rise. UK Finance responded that rates are influenced by multiple factors beyond the base rate, most borrowers are on fixed deals, and switching has become easier for customers.

The United Way of Northwest Illinois is launching the Imagination Library in Carroll County on March 28, 2018, at the Mt. Carroll Township Public Library. The program provides books to children ages 0-5 to help prepare them for kindergarten. Created by Dolly Parton in 1996 in Sevier County, TN, the initiative has expanded to over 1,300 communities worldwide. United Way has partnered with the Morse Group and other supporters for the Carroll County launch. Registration and sponsorship information is available at https://www.uwni.org/imaginationlibrary.

Professor Hong Liu discusses the mass and dynamics of D-branes in string theory. The mass of a D-brane is defined as the vacuum energy of open strings living on it, calculated via Euclidean path integrals summing over surfaces with boundaries weighted by g_s^(-χ), where χ is the Euler number. This yields a D-brane tension proportional to 1/g_s in weak coupling.

An alternative calculation considers gravitational interaction between two D-branes via closed string exchange, which can equivalently be viewed as a one-loop open string diagram. This "channel duality" is presented as the string theory origin of holographic duality.

The low-energy effective action for massless modes on D-branes can be summed into the Dirac-Born-Infeld action, describing relativistic motion of p-dimensional objects. The massless scalar fields φ^a are identified as Goldstone bosons from spontaneously broken translation symmetry.

The open string coupling relates to closed string coupling as g_s ∝ g_o².

When N D-branes coincide, each string excitation carries two indices (IJ), forming N×N matrices. String interactions naturally produce matrix products, and the worldsheet global symmetry becomes a U(N) gauge symmetry in spacetime. The low-energy theory becomes U(N) Yang-Mills coupled to adjoint scalar fields, with g_YM² ∝ g_s (αʹ)^((p-3)/2).

Separating branes breaks U(N) gauge symmetry via the Higgs mechanism, as strings stretched between separated branes acquire mass proportional to separation distance times string tension. Diagonal φ configurations satisfying [φ^a, φ^b]=0 correspond to brane locations, with separation into stacks breaking U(N) → U(n₁)×U(n₂)×...×U(n_k).

Residents of Bristol observed an unusual cloud formation on Monday morning, sharing images on Twitter. According to Met Office meteorologist Emma Sharples, the wave-like clouds appear to be Asperitas, a new supplementary feature added to the International Cloud Atlas this year and the newest cloud type classified in over 50 years. The clouds resemble a rough sea surface when viewed from below. Their formation remains unclear, though theories link them to post-thunderstorm conditions or changes in wind direction. The clouds were spotted by the Filton-based NPAS helicopter in Monmouthshire, as well as in Thornbury and Filton.

The Low-Frequency Sub-System (LFSS) combines peripherals clocked by the 32kHz LFCLK, including a Real Time Clock and asynchronous IWDT. The VREF module provides 1.4V/2.5V internal references or external reference support. The COMP comparator offers 6 blanking sources, wake-up capability, and an 8-bit reference DAC. Security features include firewalls and CRC-16. The CRC module supports CRC16-CCITT with bit reversal.

UART peripherals support asynchronous communication with programmable baud rates and LIN mode. I2C supports 7/10-bit addressing up to 1Mbps (Fm+) with SMBus 3.0. SPI supports up to 16Mbits/s with configurable controller/peripheral modes and 4-16 bit data frames.

The IWDT is an independent 25-bit watchdog with LFOSC clock generating POR resets. The WWDT supervises code execution with selectable periods. RTC_B operates on 32kHz, providing calendar functions, alarms, and calibration up to ±240ppm.

Timers include general-purpose (TIMGx) with 16-bit counters and QEI support, and advanced (TIMAx) with dead-band insertion and fault handling. The IOMUX manages digital IO peripheral selection. SWD provides debug access via the DEBUGSS subsystem, supporting security features. Factory constants are stored in a read-only memory region.

Typical applications require decoupling capacitors, NRST pullup/pulldown components, and pullup resistors for 5V-tolerant open drain IOs. TI offers development tools including LaunchPad, MSPM0 SDK, SysConfig, and Code Composer Studio.

The Hickory Tussock Moth caterpillar, found in the Belleville area from July to September, has venomous hairs that serve as a defence mechanism. According to John Cannan of Hastings Prince Edward Public Health, the white, fluffy caterpillar with black markings grows to about 4.5 centimetres and feeds mainly on hickory, walnut, and oak trees. Contact with its hairs can cause reactions ranging from mild skin redness to burning, swelling, headaches, nausea, or allergic responses. Cannan recommends washing the affected area and applying calamine lotion or cortisone, and seeking medical attention for severe reactions. David Bree, a naturalist at Presqu'ile Provincial Park, notes that younger children may react more strongly, but the caterpillars pose no threat if left alone. Bree observes that sightings and discussion of the species have increased in recent years.

Options trading in META is a form of derivatives trading where investors purchase contracts giving them the right to buy (call) or sell (put) an underlying asset at a predetermined price by a specified date. Investors can trade options on META stock, as well as other stocks, indices, commodities, and currencies.

Opening an account requires a minimum deposit of $100, though this may vary by broker. Leverage up to 1:100 is available, and the minimum trade size is one contract. While META charges no commissions, brokers may apply financing charges, slippage, and inactivity fees. Margin requirements match those of other single-stock options.

Brokers provide risk management tools like stop losses and trailing stops, plus charting tools, technical indicators, and educational resources including demo accounts. Strategies include buying calls/puts, writing covered or naked calls/puts, straddles, strangles, and spreads.

Options trading carries high risk due to leverage and speculation, and can result in significant losses, particularly when shorting options. Backtesting options strategies is difficult due to varying strikes and expirations.

The passage describes a classical mean reversion trading strategy for the S&P 500 (SPY), backtested since January 2000 with an initial equity of $100,000 and 100% compounding allocation per trade, excluding taxes. The strategy uses Internal Bar Strength (IBS) and Relative Strength Index (RSI) criteria to generate trading signals. Performance is evaluated through metrics such as win rates, drawdowns, and annual returns. The passage also examines how the strategy performs when its parameters are inverted. Amibroker and Tradestation code for this and 70+ other strategies are referenced as available via external links.

The note traces how U.S. jobs came to be categorized by skill level and questions whether low wages reflected actual value. In 1917, Alba Edwards formalized an occupational classification system with six Social Economic Groups, reserving "skill" for manual work and labeling laborers and servants as "unskilled." By 1930, 28% of the workforce held "unskilled" jobs, disproportionately filled by African Americans, immigrants, women, and children.

Four main "unskilled" categories—farm labor, factory labor, servant/service occupations, and other labor—persisted into the 21st century with evolving demographics. Farm work shifted to rely heavily on foreign-born, often undocumented workers. Manufacturing employment declined 67% between 1965 and 2020 due to automation and offshoring, while service jobs like retail, fast food, and home health care grew, becoming the dominant employment for non-college-educated workers. New gig economy roles and warehouse jobs emerged with low wages and difficult conditions.

Three stakeholders influenced wages and conditions: government regulations (FLSA, NLRA, minimum wage laws), labor advocates (strikes, unions, new worker organizations like CIW and NDWA), and employers (Ford's wage increases, Toyota's production system, and "Good Jobs Strategy" companies like Costco). Union membership declined from 34.8% in 1954 to 6.2% in 2020.

The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted that nearly 70% of essential workers held "unskilled" jobs. MIT and California commissions identified job quality, not automation, as the primary challenge. The note concludes by questioning how society should reconsider work, workers, and pay for historically "unskilled" jobs now recognized as essential.

The Nuclear Medicine Market report offers a competitive outlook, including market share and profiles of key participants such as GE Healthcare, Bracco Imaging, Mallinckrodt, Lantheus Medical Imaging, and Bayer. The market grew at an average annual rate of 6.27%, from $3,500 million in 2013 to $4,200 million in 2016, and is projected to reach $5,890 million by 2021. The report covers manufacturer data, regional development (Europe, North America, Middle East, China, Japan, Southeast Asia), and segmentation by product type (Tc-99, I-123/131, In-111, Xe-133, Th-201), industry (Diagnostic, Therapeutic), and channel (Direct Sales, Distributor). It also analyzes price, cost, gross margins, consumption figures, SWOT analysis, and investment feasibility.

Eric Hirsch, founding CEO of EdReports, will step down at the end of the school year, with the board beginning a search for his replacement. Since 2014, Hirsch has led the organization in reviewing instructional materials using a Consumer Reports-style approach, completing over 1,100 reviews that many states and districts now rely on for curriculum decisions.

His departure coincides with organizational changes, including a revised scoring process, expansion into pre-K material reviews, and updated ELA review tools emphasizing phonics and fluency. EdReports has faced criticism for being slow to adapt to reading reforms and for overemphasizing standards alignment. Alternative review organizations have also emerged.

Expert Devon Gadow said the next leader should understand the intersection of AI and curriculum. Hirsch noted research showing that adopting strong curricula alone hasn't significantly improved student achievement, citing mismatches between curriculum, training, and assessment.

The Gann Fan is a technical analysis tool invented by W.D. Gann that uses diagonal lines drawn from significant highs and lows to identify potential support and resistance levels. It consists of nine angled lines fanning from a selected swing point, with the main 45-degree line (1:1) representing equal price and time movement. Other lines follow ratios such as 2:1, 3:1, 4:1, 8:1, and their inverses. According to Gann's theory, prices above the 1:1 line indicate a bull market, while breaks below suggest bearish conditions.

Unlike the Fibonacci fan, which uses Fibonacci ratios, the Gann fan is based on price-time relationships. The tool is not always accurate since price movements can be random, and traders are advised to combine it with other indicators and risk management techniques.

The author states that a meaningful backtest of the Gann fan strategy is not possible due to its subjective nature and the excessive rules required, and suggests traders avoid strategies that cannot be objectively backtested.

Cover 1 is a man-to-man defense where every receiver is covered individually, with a free safety playing deep zone in the middle of the field, sometimes supplemented by a "low hole" player to stop short-intermediate routes. Defenses use it to stop the run, blitz the quarterback, and force vertical throws.

To beat Cover 1, offenses should attack the perimeter, away from the free safety's help. Effective strategies include:
- Pick plays, where receivers cross paths to create collisions between defenders
- Double moves (e.g., Sluggo, Stutter routes) that exploit defensive backs breaking quickly on the ball
- Routes that get receivers the ball on the move (deep crossers, wheels, outs) to maximize YAC

The passage provides five example plays from Ohio State, Oklahoma, Georgia, and a red zone concept illustrating these principles.

Christine Milligan was surprised when hospital staff asked if she wanted to revoke her daughter Cassidey Ouellete's organ donation decision after the 19-year-old was declared brain dead following a car accident near Peterborough, Ontario. Ouellete had signed her donor card at 16, and her family honoured her wishes.

Ontario's Trillium Gift of Life Network says families overruled loved ones' donation decisions in about 10 per cent of cases in 2016, down from 21 per cent in 2015. CEO Ronnie Gavsie says the option exists in case donors express regret before death, and noted families are often exhausted during end-of-life decisions.

Milligan wants to revive a 2012 private member's bill introduced by her brother, former PC MPP Robert Milligan, which proposed that only donors could revoke their registration and that all Ontarians be automatically registered with an opt-out option. Gavsie is skeptical, citing a 2015 Ipsos poll showing two-thirds of Ontarians prefer an opt-in system, and said research found no evidence presumed consent increases donors. Milligan hopes future legislation will be named after her daughter.

S&P Global Platts will launch new low-sulphur marine gasoil and diesel oil price assessments at several Asian bunkering ports starting June 1, 2017, according to a subscriber note. The move responds to rising sales of the fuel in Singapore, where volumes grew nearly six-fold over three years to a record 1.14 million tonnes in 2016, and to anticipated tightening of global sulphur limits. The new assessments will reflect fuels with a maximum sulphur content of 0.1 percent and be published alongside existing marine gasoil and diesel prices. Low-sulphur marine gasoil prices will cover Singapore, Fujairah, Hong Kong, Shanghai and South Korea, while low-sulphur marine diesel prices will cover Tokyo Bay and West Japan.

The Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card is highlighted as a top no-annual-fee credit card offering unlimited 2% cash rewards on purchases. New cardholders can earn a $200 cash rewards bonus after spending $500 in purchases within the first 3 months. The card includes a 0% intro APR for 12 months from account opening on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 18.99%, 23.99%, or 28.99%.

Additional benefits include up to $600 in cell phone protection (with a $25 deductible) when paying the cell phone bill with the card, and access to a 24/7 Visa Signature® Concierge. Approval typically requires a good-to-excellent credit score (670-850).

The passage also briefly compares two other cards: the Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card, which offers 1.5% cash back and a $300 welcome bonus, and the Citi Double Cash Card, which offers up to 2% cash back (1% when buying, 1% when paying) and an 18-month 0% intro APR on balance transfers.

Misunderstanding has existed in South America regarding U.S. intentions under the Monroe Doctrine, which was wrongly perceived as implying superiority or a protectorate. Secretary Root's mission sought to dispel this impression. In a July 31 address at Rio, Root affirmed that the U.S. seeks no territory or sovereignty beyond its own, respects the equality of all American Republics, and desires mutual prosperity rather than gain through others' ruin. He called for all American nations to be represented at The Hague as equal sovereign states, to aid weaker republics, and to create an all-American public opinion to prevent war and international wrongs. His words were reportedly well received in South America. Former Argentine foreign minister Doctor Drago characterized U.S. policy as opposing European control without asserting superiority. Buenos Aires honored figures including Monroe, Adams, Clay, and Rush, and Brazil named its conference building "Palacio Monroe." The passage also references a prior December 5, 1905, message concerning foreign nations forcibly collecting contract debts from American republics.

The speaker praises a teammate's defensive skills and expresses satisfaction with living in the Carolina area, noting his family's enjoyment and growing local fan support, especially after Christmas. He acknowledges that Canadian fans will likely rally behind Edmonton in upcoming games. He emphasizes the importance of selling hockey in southern markets, citing increased youth participation after Tampa Bay's championship, and hopes a Carolina win would similarly grow the sport. He mentions coaching kids in Tampa during the lockout. The speaker hopes to finish his career in Carolina, which he previously identified as having hidden depth and potential to challenge for a championship.

Steve Mitchell, a fifth-generation farmer at Boglily Farm near Kirkaldy, runs The Buffalo Farm with a focus on innovation and digital engagement. He uses social media to promote deals, share farm life, and build brand awareness, successfully marketing buffalo meat's health benefits to health-conscious customers. The Buffalo Farm won the Meat category at the 2016 Scotland Food & Drink Excellence Awards for its buffalo fillet steak, which Mitchell says boosted credibility and opened doors with larger clients. Entries are now open for the 2018 awards.

A white van drove onto the sidewalk on Yonge Street in Toronto, striking multiple pedestrians between Finch and Sheppard avenues. Witnesses, including Yang, Ham Yu-Jin, Amir Bahmeyeh, and Ali Shaker, described the driver zigzagging on the sidewalk at high speed, deliberately hitting people. Witnesses reported seeing bodies, severe injuries, and people performing CPR along several blocks.

The driver and van were taken into custody. In arrest footage, the suspect reportedly said "kill me" and appeared to threaten the officer with what seemed to be a weapon. Police Chief Saunders established a hotline (416-808-8750) and web portal for witness information.

Sunnybrook hospital received 10 patients—two pronounced dead, five critical, three serious—while North York General received four. Three injured were Seneca College students. Toronto Police Association president Mike McCormack called it unprecedented "carnage for blocks."

Public Safety Minister Ralph Goodale stated there was no indication of a change in risk level or connection to national security, noting the incident occurred during a G7 ministers' meeting in Toronto. The TTC suspended subway service between Finch and Sheppard, later partially restoring it. The city opened Mitchell Field Community Centre for emergency social services.

Chemical engineer Arthur Potts cautioned Edmonton city council that its road salting pilot program, which used liquid calcium chloride, should not yet be declared successful. While the city reported $4.2 million in operating savings and a 68 per cent reduction in sand use, Potts argued the cost to private vehicle owners could be ten times that amount, as calcium chloride remains liquid longer, penetrating vehicles and damaging concrete by attacking its binding agent. Residents have reported increased rust on vehicles and bikes. Potts criticized the city for not testing the chemical locally before deployment. Officials want to continue the program and purchase new equipment, with funding to be discussed in fall budget debates. Environmental impact data and collision statistics comparing treated and untreated routes were not yet available.

Researchers developed an AI tool called Waldo that scans social media posts to identify harmful side effects of cannabis use. In an experiment published September 30, 2025, Waldo reviewed over 430,000 Reddit posts and flagged more than 28,000 as potentially describing adverse effects. When researchers verified 250 of the flagged posts, 86 percent represented genuine problematic experiences. The tool outperformed ChatGPT, which produced 18 times more false positives, but did not surpass human reviewers. Experts note that agencies like the CDC do not monitor social media, where people share experiences freely. Researchers suggest tools like Waldo could help public health workers identify side effects, particularly in countries lacking robust drug monitoring systems, though ethical and privacy considerations would be necessary. It remains unclear whether Waldo would perform equally well for other products.

The U.S. has withdrawn from United Nations negotiations on the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration, citing concerns about national sovereignty and immigration enforcement. Secretary of State Rex Tillerson stated the process could undermine U.S. authority over its borders and laws.

The U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops expressed disappointment, urging reconsideration. Archbishop Timothy Broglio and Bishop Joe Vásquez emphasized that Catholic teaching respects national sovereignty but also requires protections for vulnerable migrants. Pope Francis supported the Puerto Vallarta conference, calling for welcoming and integrating migrants.

Bill Canny of the USCCB noted the framework addressed migrant education, humanitarian assistance, and preventing labor exploitation. Supporters of the withdrawal, such as the Center for Immigration Studies, argued the compact's language was too broad and threatened U.S. law. U.N. officials maintained that implementation would remain consistent with member states' sovereignty.

An anonymous analyst warned that U.S. absence could lead to more liberal refugee policies. The bishops' 2014 document affirmed that border control is not absolute and wealthy nations have greater obligations. Vincent Rougeau of Boston College Law School stressed that global migration requires international cooperation.

King Edward VI Grammar School in Louth finished second in the national schools University Challenge. The team—Rowan Roddick, Jack Leeming, Fraser Whittock and Ben Jeffrey—defeated previous winners St Ivo School and Nottingham High School to reach the finals at the University of Lincoln. Of the 10 finalist teams, most were from the independent sector. King Edward's scored 280, losing to Southend High School for Boys, who scored 315. Headmaster James Lascelles praised the team's performance and development in public speaking.

Indian Railways has introduced a policy stating "if no bill, your food is free" to curb overcharging on trains where food costs are not included in ticket fares. Railway Minister Piyush Goyal directed that all such trains display this message by March 31. IRCTC is publicising the policy on its website and has deployed 120 inspectors, with plans to add more, to ensure fair pricing and proper billing. Between April and October last year, over 7,000 overcharging complaints were recorded. Officials note vendors often refuse bills using various excuses. Previously, Railways cancelled two caterers' contracts and fined vendors around 5,000 times. A CAG report had recommended measures against overcharging, attributing it partly to unchanged food tariffs over five years.

The U.S. government shutdown is worsening a long-standing air traffic controller shortage, with staffing reportedly down 50% in some areas as controllers work without pay. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy noted the impact, while airports nationwide face delays. As of early this year, 91% of U.S. air traffic control facilities fell short of FAA staffing targets, and safety experts link the shortage to a rise in "near misses," including 1,757 runway incursions in 2024.

The shortage stems from lengthy, costly training—16 months to several years—with roughly a third of trainees washing out. Pandemic-era training pauses and retirements worsened the gap. The FAA requires applicants to be U.S. citizens under 31, and mandatory retirement is at 56. Fewer than 10% of applicants are accepted.

Despite demanding conditions, controllers earn an average of $144,580 annually, and the profession is projected to grow 3% between 2023 and 2033, with 2,200 openings yearly.

Hascall Steel Company, based in Grandville, is a US steel service center with over 45 years of experience. It partners with local and foreign producers to maintain a diverse inventory, including cold reduced steel, blanked steel, slit steel, and flat-rolled steel coils. The company processes inventory according to customer specifications, evaluating gauge, width, and chemical properties. Trained technicians operate the machinery, and an in-house laboratory conducts multipoint testing to ensure steel meets client composition requirements. Hascall aims to shorten lead times, reduce supply chain costs, and provide quality assurance.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, introduces several advancements over the V100. The Tensor Core Accelerated Iterative Refinement Solver (TCAIRS) in cuSOLVER leverages mixed-precision Tensor Cores for HPC applications, with TF32 delivering a 2.0X geomean speedup over FP64 solvers, outperforming FP16 and BF16 modes.

A100 introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using a 2:4 sparse matrix pattern, doubling compute throughput for deep neural networks with minimal accuracy loss. Sparse MMA instructions skip zero-value computations for 2x speedup.

Memory improvements include 192 KB/SM combined L1/shared memory, 40 GB of HBM2 with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth (1.7x V100), and a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x V100) with residency controls and Compute Data Compression.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions an A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated SMs, cache, and memory, supporting multi-tenant use cases with QoS guarantees.

Third-generation NVLink doubles per-signal data rate to 50 Gbit/sec with twelve links per GPU providing 600 GB/sec total bandwidth. A100 supports PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV.

Additional features include hardware JPEG decoding (NVJPG), five NVDEC units, an Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomics throughput, and enhanced error detection and isolation.

CUDA 11 supports new capabilities including Task Graph acceleration, asynchronous copy operations bypassing the register file, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, and expanded Cooperative Groups APIs.

The NVIDIA DGX A100 system contains eight A100 GPUs delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, interconnected via six NVSwitches with 4.8 TB/s bandwidth, and scales via Mellanox ConnectX-6 HDR InfiniBand adapters for large AI clusters like DGX SuperPOD.

SanDisk provides a 1-year limited warranty to the original purchaser, covering product defects but excluding third-party software, misuse, unauthorized repairs, or damage. Remedies are limited to repair, replacement, or refund, and SanDisk is not liable for lost data or consequential damages. The End User License Agreement grants a limited, non-exclusive license to use the bundled software on a single device, prohibiting modification, reverse engineering, or redistribution. The agreement is governed by California law, and violations may result in termination. Users must also comply with U.S. export regulations and properly dispose of the device through local waste authorities rather than household waste.

On February 28, 2019, Tesla announced the availability of the standard Model 3 at $35,000, offering 220 miles of range, and the Model 3 Standard Range Plus at $37,000 with 240 miles of range. To support these prices, Tesla is shifting global sales to online-only and winding down many physical stores, while retaining some as galleries. Customers can return vehicles within 7 days or 1,000 miles for a full refund. Tesla plans to expand its service system and has announced firmware upgrades that increase range, top speed, and peak power for Model 3 vehicles. Tesla stated it does not expect profitability in Q1 2019 but anticipates likely profitability in Q2 2019.

Researchers have developed nanoscale synthetic packets that release their contents when exposed to specific wavelengths of light and reseal when the light is removed. The packets consist of two polymer layers—a water-soluble outer rind of polyethylene oxide and a rigid inner glassy layer of polylactic acid—connected by a light-responsive linking molecule. When illuminated, the molecule changes shape, softening the glassy layer and allowing contents to escape. Potential applications include targeted drug delivery and releasing chemicals into soil. Both polymers are biocompatible. The team is exploring additional trigger mechanisms such as pressure and chemical cues. The findings appear in Nature Chemistry.

The judgment in Schildkraut v. Paino was reversed on the law and facts, with a new trial granted and costs to abide the event. The court found that the judgment could not be sustained in its present form because no decision was rendered, citing Civil Practice Act sections 440 and 441 and related case law. The plaintiff had established a prima facie case for an accounting based on oral testimony and documentary proof, but the trial court unduly restricted the scope of his proof. A new trial was ordered before another Special Term justice to determine credibility and make appropriate findings.

A training intervention study was conducted in Palghar District, Maharashtra, India (2019-2022) to build a sustainable cadre of local master trainers (MTs) for maternal and newborn health (MNH) using a Training of Trainers (TOT) model. This scale-up followed a pilot project in Pune District (2017-19), with virtual support from UK-based obstetricians and pediatricians during the COVID-19 pandemic.

The intervention had two phases. Phase 1 involved selecting eight Core Trainers (CTs) from Pune and preparing them through refresher and virtual learning sessions. Phase 2 developed Palghar MTs through a six-step approach: (1) pre-TOT screening of 48 candidates, selecting 32; (2) TOT with pre/post assessments; (3) staggered induction pairing intermediate-scoring MTs with higher-scoring ones; (4) continuous support from Pune CTs during trainings; (5) virtual quality assessments by UK experts; and (6) virtual refresher training via the ECHO platform.

The 32 Palghar MTs trained 505 health providers across multiple cadres over 18 months. Mixed-methods evaluation showed significant improvements in trainees' post-training scores for clinical knowledge and skills (abdominal palpation, newborn resuscitation, eclampsia management). Qualitative data indicated three key gains for Palghar MTs: increased clinical competency and application of evidence-based practices (including DR ABC and SBAR approaches), enhanced confidence as trainers using adult-learner-centric pedagogy, and career recognition and motivation.

The study demonstrates that a methodical TOT approach with extended timeframes, hybrid delivery platforms, and supportive supervision can effectively build sustainable training capacity within public health systems. The authors recommend recognizing training as a career path, integrating it into systemic mechanisms, and providing enabling ecosystems. Further research on long-term retention of competencies and cost analysis is warranted.

T-Tamer is a theoretical framework for managing bi-objective trade-offs (e.g., accuracy vs. latency) in cascaded inference, where multiple sub-models of varying complexity are invoked adaptively. The framework formalizes routing and termination as a costly exploration problem over directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), where nodes represent sub-models and edges encode precedence and performance dependencies.

The authors distinguish between no-recall strategies (which must use the last consulted model) and with-recall strategies (which may return any previously inspected model). They prove an information-theoretic impossibility result: no-recall strategies cannot achieve any constant-factor approximation to optimal utility, even in simple two-model cases. This reveals fundamental limitations of confidence-threshold heuristics commonly used in early-exit models.

For with-recall settings, the authors develop a dynamic indexing strategy computed via dynamic programming. The strategy is proven optimal for three DAG topologies: directed lines, their transitive closures (allowing skips), and directed trees. All variants run in polynomial time, with O(n) inference time per input.

Experiments on synthetic data and real-world vision (VGG models on video streaming datasets) and NLP (BERT, GPT-2 on IMDB and Amazon Review) classification benchmarks demonstrate favorable accuracy-latency trade-offs, with latency reductions up to 90% in some cases.

The S&P 500 closed near record highs at 6,715, with valuations surpassing pre-2000 levels and prompting debate over whether the rally is reaching bubble territory. Futures remained steady as tech weakness, Federal Reserve policy, and government shutdown concerns tempered upside momentum, while the index held above 6,620 support.

The ESCAPE Dark Matter Test Science Project (TSP), supported by the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC), provides a FAIR platform for dark matter research, combining tools and data from particle physics and astroparticle experiments including ATLAS, DarkSide, Fermi LAT, KM3NeT, and CTA. The TSP hosts reproducible workflows on the Virtual Research Environment (VRE) to produce dark matter summary plots, reinterpret searches, and share common tools like the Baler data compression software.

This review, aimed at astronomers, outlines how astrophysical observations—such as gravitational lensing of galaxies and quasars, and gamma-ray emission from dwarf spheroidal galaxies—can constrain dark matter models including CDM, WDM, and SIDM. It also highlights software tools like pyHalo, lenstronomy, GAMBIT, AxionLimits, and the Dark Matter Limit Plotter, which could be integrated into the VRE.

The authors encourage astronomers to use ESCAPE services to incorporate astronomical dark matter searches, bridging the gap between astronomy and particle physics communities.

At a town hall meeting in Charlestown, Nevis on February 13th, 2017, Minister of Foreign Affairs Mark Brantley highlighted the Team Unity Government's achievements since taking office in February 2015 under Prime Minister Timothy Harris. Brantley stated that before Unity, the St. Kitts-Nevis Sugar Industry Diversification Foundation (SIDF) spent $95,474,153 in 2013, none of which reached Nevis. Under Team Unity, Nevis received $62.2 million from the SIDF for projects including a pier, sporting facilities, geothermal work, an athletic track, airport upgrades, hospital funding, and a generator. Additionally, the Nevis Island Administration received $51.16 million in budgetary support from passport processing fees, compared to $17.3 million received between 2006 and 2015. Brantley commended Premier Vance Amory and emphasized the government's commitment to equal access to national resources for all citizens.

The speaker describes him as a classy, intelligent, and helpful individual who works harder than younger players to stay in top shape. The United States and Imperial Russia agreed, via notes dated September 8, 1900, to arbitrate claims for indemnity concerning four American vessels: the Cape Horn Pigeon, James Hamilton Lewis, C. H. White, and Kate and Anna. The U.S. contends that Russian agents' arrests and seizures of these vessels violated international law, treaty rights, and personal rights of citizens, with crews from three vessels held as prisoners. The U.S. also claims interest on the indemnity, arguing that awarding only the principal would not constitute full restitution. Numerous precedents are cited, including arbitrations under the 1794 and 1871 treaties with Great Britain, the Alabama claims, Chinese indemnity, Costa Rica Packet, and 1897 Bering Sea seizures, where interest was granted. In Case No. 1, the Cape Horn Pigeon, an American whaling bark registered in New Bedford, Massachusetts, was seized on September 10, 1892, by Russian authorities in the Okhotsk Sea while whaling, taken to Vladivostok, detained until the season's end, and released without trial.

The team conceded two goals and managed only one despite applying pressure and having late scoring chances to equalize. The Delhi High Court sought responses from the Centre and Jammu and Kashmir regarding whether judges of the J&K High Court take oath of allegiance to the Indian Constitution. The query arose during a PIL filed by advocate Surjeet Singh, whose counsel alleged that J&K High Court judges do not appear obligated to uphold the Indian Constitution. The petition challenges the Constitution Order 1954, which added a proviso to Article 368 stating that constitutional amendments do not apply to J&K unless ordered by the President under Article 370. The petitioner argues this proviso is an unconstitutional encroachment on Parliament's amending powers and seeks its quashing.

Progressive advocates gathered at Wells Fargo's annual shareholders meeting in Des Moines, Iowa, demanding the bank reform its investments and business practices, with some calling for the CEO and board to resign. Organized by People's Action, demonstrators criticized the bank for alleged racially discriminatory consumer practices, backing private prisons and the gun industry, foreclosures, and funding fossil fuel projects including the Dakota Access Pipeline. The meeting followed a $1 billion fine from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau for predatory mortgage practices. According to the Banking on Climate Change report, Wells Fargo invested over $4.6 billion in fossil fuel projects between 2015 and 2017.
