The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC device supporting standard SPI and daisy-chain topologies. In single-device SPI mode, CONVST/CS, SCLK, SDI, and SDO-0 form the SPI port. In daisy-chain topology, multiple devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, with SDO-0 of each device connecting to SDI of the next. Optimal data frames require 32×N SCLK edges for N devices.

The device operates in three states: RESET, ACQ, and CONV, determined by CONVST/CS and RST signals. The RST pin supports either application reset or power-on reset based on the RSTn_APP bit.

The device features nine configuration registers and supports data read/write operations via a multiSPI interface. Data frames begin on CONVST/CS falling edge and end on its rising edge. Frames with exactly 32 SCLKs are optimal; shorter frames are treated as NOP, longer frames use the last 32 bits as commands. Four SPI protocols (SPI-00-S through SPI-11-S) are supported, along with source-synchronous (SRC) protocols using internal or external clocks, with single or dual SDO output options.

Registers control device ID, reset/power, SDI/SDO configuration, data output, input range, and alarm thresholds with hysteresis. Power-saving NAP and power-down modes are available.

Application examples include industrial analog input modules for PLCs, measuring voltage/current ranges up to ±10V across eight channels using the MUX36D08 multiplexer. The device includes input and AVDD alarms useful for temperature sensing. Recommended layout separates analog and digital sections with proper decoupling capacitors on AVDD, DVDD, REFCAP, and REFIO pins.

Knees are subject to lifelong wear and tear, with many people over 50 requiring knee surgery. Healthy lifestyle choices can reduce the risk of injury and the need for surgery.

Hila Glick of Onestep recommends staying active, strengthening leg and body muscles, and maintaining flexibility. Strength training can improve bone density by up to 3% and slow age-related bone and muscle loss. Danielle Wills suggests targeting hamstrings, quads, glutes, and hip flexors, while gradually increasing weight.

Stretching improves range of motion, balance, and reduces injury risk. Low-impact cardio, such as cycling and swimming, maintains circulation to knee ligaments and cartilage without jarring impact. Maintaining a healthy weight reduces joint stress and lowers osteoarthritis risk.

Common knee injuries vary by area, severity, and physical background. Physiotherapy can diagnose issues and provide tailored exercises—such as quad strengthening, bridges, wall squats, calf stretches, and knee-to-chest stretches—to restore mobility and potentially avoid surgery. Glick advises against ignoring pain and recommends staying active. Online physiotherapy platforms offer convenience.

Most knee replacements are performed on people over 50, with osteoarthritis being the leading cause. Genetics also play a role. Around 160,000 knee and hip replacements occur annually in England and Wales. Surgery carries risks including infection and deep vein thrombosis. Dr Sarah Jarvis notes that over 80% of total knee replacements and 70% of unicondylar replacements now last 25 years. Physiotherapy also aids post-surgery recovery.

The disclosure pertains to absorbent hygiene products, specifically an absorbent core for articles such as diapers, incontinence products, sanitary napkins, and panty liners. The absorbent core comprises a front portion, back portion, and crotch portion with a longitudinal axis, featuring one or more substantially interconnected channels extending through the crotch portion. These channels, preferably forming a U-bend closed end and funnel-shaped open end, distribute fluid faster than surrounding absorption structures comprising three-dimensional absorbent material and superabsorbent polymers, enabling tri-stage fluid distribution at varying speeds.

The channels are formed by two nonwoven webs bonded with adhesive in zones of varying bonding strength, allowing separation upon wetting in weaker zones while stronger central zones maintain channel integrity. The channels remain visible before and after use, becoming more visible after use.

The core may be combined with an acquisition and distribution layer (ADL), with preferred arrangements where channel extremities extend beyond the ADL edges to maximize fluid flow.

The manufacturing process involves a mold with a 3D insert (inverse shape of desired channels) connected to an under-pressure source. A first nonwoven web, three-dimensional absorbent material, and second nonwoven web are applied sequentially, with vacuum forcing material around the insert to form channels substantially free of absorbent material. This process produces channels free of absorbent material, unlike embossing or material-removal methods.

The UK Government has launched a six-week consultation on proposals to update the Package Travel Regulations, aiming to extend protections to an additional 10 million package holidays booked online each year. The revisions are intended to reflect the shift from high street travel agents to internet bookings, ensuring online customers receive equivalent rights. Proposed changes include clearer information about refund rights and making the business that assembles the package responsible for the entire holiday, even when third parties fulfil parts of it. Consumer minister Margot James said regulations must be updated to match changing booking habits. Consumer group Which? supports the proposals, urging the Government to address gaps in protection.

Japan's GDP grew at an annualised 4 percent in the second quarter, exceeding the 2.5 percent economists expected and marking 18 months of continuous expansion. However, Japanese data is volatile and frequently revised, and the Topix stock index fell 0.8 percent on Monday. This represents Japan's longest growth streak in over a decade, suggesting increased resilience under Prime Minister Shinzo Abe's reforms, alongside a stronger global economy and the Bank of Japan's easy policies. The 22nd District Agricultural Association board unanimously rejected construction bids for remodeling Surfside Race Place at the Del Mar Fairgrounds, citing a $4 million funding shortfall. Sector trading involves buying and selling securities within a specific economic sector, carrying higher risk than broad market investing. Based on JP Morgan's 2015 research analyzing Russell 3000 components from 1980-2015, the worst sectors to invest in are information technology, energy, utilities, and materials, due to their low median returns.

JP Morgan measured sector performance using two methods: catastrophic losses (declines of 70% or more with recoveries under 60%) and excess returns versus the Russell 3000. Telecom, information technology, and energy suffered the most catastrophic losses, while utilities, financials, and consumer staples had the fewest. By excess returns, utilities ranked worst, followed by energy and materials. Overall, 40% of stocks experienced catastrophic losses.

Utilities are stable but deliver poor long-term returns due to heavy regulation. Despite many underperforming stocks, the Russell 3000 generated positive returns because a minority of stocks produced spectacular gains, while the median stock had negative lifetime returns.

The article references Charlie Munger's inverse thinking and Charles Ellis's "Loser's Game," suggesting investors may benefit from identifying and avoiding poor-performing sectors rather than focusing only on winners. S&P divides the stock market into 11 sectors.

The AMD Security Processor (ASP) serves as AMD's root of trust for detection, verifying AMD signatures on firmware retrieved from ROM and on SFS update packages at runtime. System designers (OEM/ODM) own the firmware root of trust for updates, and may optionally co-sign SFS packages by providing a public RSA key (2048 or 4096-bit) to the ASP during early boot before BOOT_DONE.

SFS updates are applied at runtime and do not persist across reboots. BIOS developers enable SFS via APCB tokens (disabled by default), with options for requiring co-signing. In multi-socket systems, the first socket's ASP receives patches and distributes as needed. Multiple updates apply sequentially.

Update packages check existing patch levels and firmware versions for compatibility, and can patch registers, replace firmware images, or update firmware components. SEV updates auto-commit and prevent rollback without reboot; SNP-enabled systems require HV-FIXED pages.

Applying an update requires a 2MB-aligned TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER, with the update package appended along with any co-signing header and signatures. Commands are sent via ASP TEE registers. The ASP protects the DRAM region, verifies customer and AMD signatures, executes the patch, and updates patch level information.

The GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO command returns current patch levels and firmware versions. Package names follow the format fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg. Updates run in parallel with x86/DMA traffic with minimal performance impact, though SEV/SEV-ES VMs must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates (SEV/SNP VMs do not).

The passage introduces the empirical Stochastic Inverse Problem (eSIP), a statistical framework for inferring probability distributions of unknown parameters in complex systems from experimental observations. Unlike classical Bayesian inverse problems, the eSIP addresses cases where parameters vary stochastically across trials rather than having a single "true" value corrupted by noise.

The authors formulate the problem using a measurable parameter space Λ, observation space D, and a Quantity of Interest (QoI) map Q that is generally not one-to-one, reflecting information loss in observations. Because multiple parameter values can yield identical observations, the solution relies on disintegration of measures rather than Bayes' Theorem directly.

Four main results are presented: (1) under general conditions, a unique posterior distribution solves the Stochastic Inverse Problem (SIP) with an explicit density formula; (2) this density is continuous almost everywhere; (3) the uniform prior yields maximum entropy solutions; and (4) a numerical importance-sampling estimator is asymptotically unbiased and strongly consistent.

The paper illustrates concepts through examples including exponential decay models and discrete probability spaces. Applications span epidemic forecasting, groundwater contamination, hydrodynamics, black hole mergers, and nuclear reactor analysis. The authors distinguish their approach from related methods like Bayesian computer model calibration, 4D-VAR, and ensemble Kalman filtering, noting that the eSIP targets parameter distributions rather than point estimates. The paper establishes theoretical foundations, including structural properties of generalized contours, conditional density formulations, and continuity conditions dependent on boundary behavior of Λ.

Vijay Mukhi, a pioneer of the Indian IT industry, claims that Bitcoin exchanges, particularly in tax haven countries, are becoming a platform for concealing black money of HNIs, businessmen, and tax-evading criminals. Mukhi advised the government against banning cryptocurrency, suggesting demonetization 2.0 instead to curb black money flow into Bitcoin.

AMD reserves the right to modify unpublished internal procedure names, and only published entry functions are guaranteed stable. The document describes AGESA™ software procedures for processor initialization across boot phases:

**Initialization procedures:**
- **AmdInitReset**: Performs minimal processor initialization after system reset, including HyperTransport link initialization and execution cache allocation (up to three regions, subject to alignment and boundary rules).
- **AmdInitEarly**: Establishes the boot environment, configures platform-specific characteristics (VRM, C-State, CPB, P-States, GPU, PCIe), and performs full HyperTransport initialization.
- **AmdInitPost**: Initializes main system memory, handles DRAM configuration (interleaving, ECC, refresh rates), and transitions from pre-memory to post-memory phase.
- **AmdInitEnv**: Transfers HOBs/artifact data to host-controlled memory using AgesaAllocateBuffer.
- **AmdInitMid**: Performs graphics display hardware configuration after PCI enumeration.
- **AmdInitLate**: Generates informational tables (ACPI, DMI, WHEA, CRAT, CDIT, IVRS) for the OS.
- **AmdInitRtb**: Saves processor context at Ready-To-Boot for S3 suspend.
- **AmdInitResume/AmdS3LateRestore/AmdS3FinalRestore**: Restore silicon state during resume.

**Required call-outs** (host must implement): AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer, AgesaRunFcnOnAp, AgesaReset, AgesaLocateBuffer, and AgesaReadSpd.

**Optional call-outs** provide hooks for memory training, voltage adjustments, and platform-specific customizations.

**Customization mechanisms** include: <Plat>Options.c build configuration, wrapper interaction after AmdCreateStruct, IDS controls, and defined call-outs. Build options (BLDOPT_*) remove unused code (DIMM types, memory types, ECC, specific processor families/sockets, S3 support) to reduce ROM size. Build configuration elements (BLDCFG_*) define VRM capabilities, CPU frequency limits, MMIO settings, ACPI table content, C-States, CPB, and core leveling without affecting code size.

All procedures require a pre-established stack, and most require coordination between BSP and AP cores. MTRR settings apply to x86-64 architecture only.

The Denver Broncos defeated the Cincinnati Bengals 28-3 on Monday night at Empower Field at Mile High, snapping a two-game losing streak. Quarterback Bo Nix had his most complete game of the season, throwing for 326 yards, his first 300-yard passing performance of the year. The Broncos' defense dominated against a Bengals offense missing injured quarterback Joe Burrow. Denver also ended a 37-game regular-season streak without a 100-yard rusher. However, the Broncos committed seven penalties for 72 yards and had offensive drops, including by tight end Evan Engram, who has yet to have a breakout game.

The Bengals were outscored 55-6 in the first halves of their last two games and gained just 21 yards on 18 plays across five drives in the middle of Monday's game. Cincinnati faces Detroit and Green Bay next.

Isaiah Silva, the former husband of Frances Bean Cobain, is suing Courtney Love and others, alleging they conspired to murder him to recover Kurt Cobain's 1959 Martin guitar. Silva received the guitar, played during Nirvana's 1993 MTV Unplugged performance, as part of his divorce settlement. The lawsuit, filed in Los Angeles, accuses the group of crimes including burglary, kidnapping, attempted murder, and extortion. Silva claims that on June 3, 2016, Love's manager Sam Lutfi, actor Ross Butler, and Yan Yukhtman attempted a home invasion, impersonating police officers. Love has not yet responded to the complaint.

Research presented at the American Physiological Society annual meeting suggests that low mental energy may influence walking patterns in older adults more than physical fatigue. Clarkson University researchers observed adults averaging 75 years old performing a six-minute walking test before and after cognitive tasks involving math and number identification. LED sensors measured gait speed and stride length, while participants self-reported mood, motivation and energy. While gait was unchanged in the first 30 seconds of the follow-up walk, walking speed and stride length later decreased significantly in those reporting cognitive fatigue, but not physical fatigue. Researchers noted further study is needed to understand why physical energy levels did not correlate with gait.

WWE announced five-year deals to distribute "Raw" on USA Network and "Smackdown Live" on Fox, but remains open to streaming its shows on digital platforms like Amazon and Facebook in the future, according to chief brand officer Stephanie McMahon. While WWE currently prioritizes linear TV for its large reach, digital platforms could help WWE reach younger viewers, as the median age of pro wrestling TV viewers rose from 28 in 2000 to 54 in 2016. Digital distribution could open new sponsorship opportunities, drive traffic to WWE's Instagram and YouTube channel, and attract subscribers to WWE Network, its OTT service with 2.1 million subscribers.

A report by the Education and Training Inspectorate (ETI) found that some schools in Northern Ireland are excluding pupils from overall exam results to improve their standing in media-published league tables. Pupils can be ruled ineligible for reasons including illness, welfare issues, or withdrawal from school. In 2015-16, around 2,900 pupils were deemed ineligible, comprising 7% of year 12 pupils at GCSE and 8.8% of year 14 pupils at A-Level, with the majority attending non-grammar schools. HF-band RFID enables wireless communication and power transfer from reader to transponder, with Near Field Communication (NFC) being one application used in mobile devices. However, NFC increases battery drain, with measurements showing smart phones consume 50% more power when NFC is active without a transponder, and up to 107% more when reading a transponder.

This article presents three investigations on magnetic field strength scaling in HF-Band RFID-Systems to reduce energy consumption: (1) field strength scaling during card detection phase, (2) dynamic scaling during communication to account for changing distances and operations, and (3) scaling for multiple transponders in range.

The proposed PTF-Determinator method determines the Power Transfer Function by gathering parameters from reader and transponder, approximating the physical relation factor (distance) during runtime, and integrating into the existing communication flow. Required parameters are distributed between reader and transponder, with the reader serving as the central computation unit.

A case study reading digital business cards validated the method through simulation and hardware measurement. Simulation results showed up to 80% transmission energy savings in close distances, while measurements demonstrated 26% energy reduction compared to simple card detection. When exceeding maximum transmission distance, power cutoff saved 75% of transmission energy. Applied to state-of-the-art smart phones, this translates to approximately 13% battery drain reduction in real environments, and up to 39% when distance limits are exceeded.

Future work will focus on improving the physical relation factor approximation and verifying the other investigations through simulation and measurement.

U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin ruled that the 1991 Nirvana album cover depicting a naked baby underwater reaching for a dollar bill does not constitute child pornography, and dismissed a 2021 lawsuit filed by Spencer Elden, who was pictured as a 4-month-old. Elden had sued under a federal law providing civil remedies for victims of certain crimes committed against minors. Olguin evaluated factors including whether the image's focal point was the child's genitalia, whether the setting was sexually suggestive, and whether it was intended to elicit a sexual response. He concluded that only the child's nudity weighed toward the statute's definition, comparing the image to a family photo of a bathing child.

Jeane Kirkpatrick argued in a November 1979 Commentary article that the United States need not adopt a posture of self-abasement toward the Third World or forswear military force, asserting that liberal idealism is compatible with defending freedom and national interest.

On November 12, 1979, Ronald Reagan taped a television address announcing his candidacy for the 1980 Republican presidential nomination, broadcast the following evening. Reagan described the U.S. as a forward-looking nation and rejected the view that it had reached the peak of its power or must accept decline. He attributed the country's crisis to a failure of leadership rather than of the American spirit, and pledged to set a new agenda if elected.

Addressing foreign policy, Reagan warned that the 1980s would test the U.S. and its allies, particularly given potential Soviet nuclear superiority. He emphasized commitment to allies, rejected appeasement, and argued that the U.S. must continue accepting the responsibilities of global leadership to ensure its own survival.

Singapore's Smart Nation vision, launched in 2014 by Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong, aims to enable citizens to live technology-enhanced lives and solve problems independently. Numerous initiatives have been introduced, including the Smart Nation Sensor Platform (SNSP) to network 110,000 lamp posts, the reorganisation placing GovTech under the Prime Minister's Office, the launch of SGInnovate to support start-ups, and programmes like Tech Silver to help the elderly adopt technology.

However, these efforts lack a clear success story for the general public, with many initiatives being infrastructural, administrative, or targeted at specific demographics, leading to public disengagement. Estonia is cited as a successful example, where citizens use a state-issued digital identity for travel, banking, voting, and taxes. China's widespread cashless payments via QR codes is another example.

In Singapore, PayNow was launched in July by the Association of Banks in Singapore, followed by QR code payments from DBS and OCBC, but adoption has been slow due to abundant payment choices. The author suggests automatically enrolling bank customers into PayNow with an opt-out option to drive adoption and create demand among retailers, potentially providing the tangible benefit needed to advance the Smart Nation vision.

The World Bank has raised China's 2025 GDP growth forecast from 4.5% to 4.8%, citing economic resilience from government stimulus and modest export recovery. The upgrade reflects strength in domestic investment, industrial output, infrastructure spending, and manufacturing support, which have offset weaknesses in property and private consumption.

However, growth remains below pre-pandemic levels, with structural challenges including local government debt, demographic pressures, and declining productivity. The World Bank expects momentum to ease in 2026 due to narrowing fiscal space and global trade uncertainties.

Looking forward, China is expected to shift gradually from state-led investment toward consumption-based growth, supported by green industries and digital innovation, though careful policy balancing will be required to avoid financial risks.

The speaker reflects on their time as captain in Edmonton, comparing it to the current team's unity, while crediting Rod as the face of the franchise. They express excitement and nerves about returning to Edmonton, where they spent eight and a half years. The speaker praises young teammates like Cam, Justin Williams, Andrew Ladd, and Eric for playing beyond their years, particularly Eric's performances in big games. Regarding the finals, they believe the two best and most deserving teams are competing, predicting loud atmospheres, physical play, and great hockey, while expressing confidence their team can win.

The speaker emphasizes focusing one game or period at a time rather than looking at the bigger picture, which can be overwhelming given the sacrifices made. To cope with the mental strain, they suggest getting away from hockey, reading, and spending time with family, though it is difficult to stop rehashing games. They note that leads are never safe, so the team must avoid emotional extremes, having already faced ups and downs in the playoffs, and simply focus on playing their best in the next home game.

The U.S. Department of Energy has awarded the University of Wyoming nearly $10 million to study whether 50 million tons of carbon dioxide can be stored underground north of Gillette. The research will examine capturing the gas from coal-burning plants. Wyoming's Powder River Basin supplies about 40 percent of U.S. power plant coal, but regulations and shifting customer preferences threaten the industry's future.

The Trump administration's "Make Our Children Healthy Again Strategy" report aims to increase U.S. breastfeeding rates through WIC and other policies, but does not mention federal paid parental leave. Experts say structural reform and financial investment are needed. While 84 percent of U.S. parents initiate breastfeeding, fewer than 40 percent of infants still receive human milk at one year, and 60 percent of parents stop sooner than planned.

Researchers, including Rafael Pérez-Escamilla of Yale and Cecilia Tomori of Johns Hopkins, point to structural barriers rather than lack of desire. A National Academies of Sciences report recommends coordinated postpartum services, breastfeeding training for medical professionals, and expanded insurance coverage. The U.S. is the only high-income country without federally mandated paid maternity leave, and studies show paid leave increases breastfeeding initiation and duration.

Lower breastfeeding rates affect Black, Native American, Alaska Native, low-income, rural, and younger mothers, who often lack paid leave. Advocates like Inimai Chettiar and Dawn Huckelbridge call for federal paid leave, enforcement of existing protections, and addressing racial health disparities. Concerns remain about cuts to SNAP and Medicaid. The report also supports expanding safe donor human milk supply, which Lindsay Groff notes can help premature infants and support later breastfeeding.

Document 31 (Jan 27, 1942): Minister Schoenfeld reports that former Finnish Foreign Minister Erkko believes most Finns favor withdrawal from the war, but the timing depends on external circumstances favorable to both Russia and Germany. Erkko stressed that Finnish security from Russia remains paramount, and that overseas supplies would be needed if Germany retaliated. He noted growing friction between Finnish and German troops and dissatisfaction with German military performance.

Document 32: Secretary Hull instructs Schoenfeld to formally raise with the Finnish Government U.S. concerns over German forces using Finnish territory as a base of operations, unopposed by Finland. An internal memo notes the telegram aims to document German use of Finnish territory in case of future Allied operations and to warn Finland against prolonged association with Germany.

Document 33: Finance Minister Pekkala inquired about U.S.-Finnish relations. Schoenfeld replied that Finland's position required clarification, especially after Japan's attack on the United States.

President Trump announced a deal with Pfizer on Tuesday in which the company agreed to offer lower drug prices to Medicaid and directly to patients, and to launch new medicines at prices comparable to those in other countries. In exchange, Pfizer will be exempt from certain pharmaceutical tariffs for three years, provided it continues U.S. manufacturing investments, including a $70 billion commitment.

Americans will be able to purchase many Pfizer products at 50% or more off list prices through a forthcoming Trump-branded purchasing platform. Specific drugs like Duavee, Eucrisa, and Toviaz will see discounts of 80% or more. The full details remain confidential, and Pfizer did not disclose revenue impacts.

Trump indicated similar deals with other drugmakers, including Eli Lilly, are forthcoming, and threatened tariffs on non-compliant companies. The announcement follows letters sent to 17 major drug companies demanding pricing changes by September 29. Health policy experts suggested the deal's impact may be smaller than described, as affected drugs represent a small fraction of U.S. prescriptions. Pfizer's stock rose 6.8%. Industry group PhRMA also announced aligned initiatives, including a direct-purchase website launching in January.

The 4-2-5 defense combines elements of the 4-3 and 3-3-5 defenses, featuring 4 down linemen, 2 linebackers, and 5 defensive backs. It maintains 6 defenders in the box for run defense while using 5 defensive backs for pass coverage, making it effective against modern spread offenses.

The defense's key position is the "Sam" or "Rover" linebacker, a hybrid player who must cover receivers, take on blockers, and rush the passer. The scheme favors athletic, sometimes smaller personnel to generate pressure.

Strengths include versatility in coverage, ability to defend both run and pass, and flexibility in blitz packages. Weaknesses stem from its unbalanced alignment—the Sam creates an overhang on one side, leaving the opposite side vulnerable, particularly for the weak safety. Bigger offensive lines can also exploit its smaller personnel.

Offenses typically attack the weak side away from the Sam, using plays like buck sweeps or outside zones. Common blitzes include the 6 Man Cover 0 Blitz and 6 Man Cover Zero Field Blitz. Common coverages include Cover 4 and Cover 3 Sky, both run from a 2-high safety shell.

Gary Patterson, formerly of TCU, is the most prominent 4-2-5 coach, leading the nation in defense five times. Greg Etter also used the scheme successfully at Carthage College and other programs.

The author describes touring Otago schools and community events to speak about mental health, despite lacking professional qualifications in the field. He explains he is motivated by having personally experienced depression, by New Zealand's mental health crisis, and by concerning youth suicide statistics. He believes society shares responsibility for raising awareness and that open conversation is the most effective approach.

His goal is to convey to young people that discussing mental health is acceptable and that help is available. He argues mental illness draws its power from silence, stigma, and isolation, and weakens when people speak openly about it.

The author acknowledges others who have shared their experiences, including Zac Guildford and Zac Franich, and expresses hope that the 2010s will be remembered as the decade New Zealand addressed mental health stigma and reversed declining mental health trends.

The passage concludes with a list of helplines and emergency contacts for those seeking mental health support.

This study evaluated a mobile app sleep psychoeducation module as part of a broader chronic disease self-management intervention for adults aged 40 and older with chronic health conditions and low health literacy. Sleep problems are common, particularly among older adults with chronic conditions, minoritized groups, and those with low socioeconomic status or health literacy, and are linked to poor health outcomes and disparities.

The app featured tailored content at varying reading levels (3rd, 6th, and 8th grade), developed using cognitive load theory and multimedia learning principles. Conducted in Fort Lauderdale and Atlanta, the study recruited participants through clinics, churches, and referrals. Assessments occurred at baseline, post-intervention, and three months later, using measures including the Insomnia Severity Index, PSQI, and FLIGHT/VIDAS health literacy scale.

Of 286 participants, 195 had insomnia-level ISI scores; most were BIPOC, low-income, and showed elevated stress and depression scores. Sleep disturbance was significantly related to hypercholesterolemia, depression, bipolar disorder, and other nervous conditions. Mixed effects models showed that SES, health literacy, and number of health conditions were significantly associated with sleep quality, and the intervention produced a statistically significant small-to-medium improvement in PSQI scores (d = 0.40).

Compared to prior CBT-I studies, this intervention showed smaller effects but included participants often excluded elsewhere. Limitations include reliance on self-report, the multi-topic nature of the broader intervention, and limited generalizability. The authors conclude that a brief, tailored digital sleep intervention may modestly improve sleep and warrants further development, potentially as part of a stepped-care approach.

The speaker praises a player's puck handling, skating, and physicality, noting he proved himself in the last game. The goalie has earned player trust and is expected to gain media recognition, having handled Detroit's pressure well. Playing in Pittsburgh is difficult due to the loud atmosphere, requiring a strong, patient road game. Repeating as champions is harder than winning initially, with Hossa's determination driving the team. Discipline, managing the puck, and playing between whistles are emphasized. The team values character over personal stats. Momentum from previous games is dismissed as irrelevant. One key player is lauded as among the world's best two-way players, capable in all situations, including matching up against Crosby.

This MIT lecture by Erik Demaine focuses on pleat folding origami, particularly the hyperbolic paraboloid model made from concentric squares with alternating mountain and valley folds, plus diagonals. The paper forms a saddle-like 3D shape through "self-folding," where physics finds an equilibrium between creased regions (which want to stay bent due to plastic deformation) and uncreased regions (which want to stay flat).

Demaine describes simulations developed with Jenna Fizel and John Ochsendorf that recreate these forms virtually, enabling physical "origami skeletons" built from 3D-printed spheres and aluminum rods. He also discusses hyperhedra sculptures combining multiple hyperbolic paraboloids into polyhedral forms, and curved-crease sculptures in MoMA's collection, including glassblowing collaborations.

A central theorem presented: the standard concentric-square crease pattern cannot actually fold into a non-flat proper shape (where every crease is folded between 0 and 180 degrees). Real paper models work because additional hidden creases exist. Adding diagonal triangulations makes folding possible, which Demaine proves using interval arithmetic in Mathematica, verified up to 100 rings. The resulting shape closely approximates but isn't exactly a hyperbolic paraboloid.

The proof relies on differential geometry concepts including Gaussian curvature (preserved under folding per Gauss's theorema egregium), ruled surfaces, and torsal ruled surfaces. Key results proven: straight creases remain straight in proper foldings, and polygonal boundaries force planar interiors. Together these imply interior faces must remain rigid, making the untriangulated pattern impossible to fold.

The lecture concludes with related topics: the tea bag problem (maximum volume of inflated pillows, still open), inflation of convex polyhedra via "karate chops" to edges, and David Huffman's curved-crease origami work, which Demaine is recreating with Huffman's family and Duks Koschitz to document his mathematical methods.

The Houston area is experiencing severe weather on the first Monday of the new year, with a system capable of producing large hail, damaging winds, and isolated tornadoes. A Severe Thunderstorm Warning is in effect until 9am for counties north of Houston, including parts of Liberty, San Jacinto, Montgomery, and Polk counties. According to ABC13 Meteorologist David Tillman, the main threats are damaging winds, quarter-size hail, and heavy rain, with concern focused on areas from Conroe to Wharton, as well as Angleton, Beaumont, Galveston, and Lake Jackson. The storms are expected to move quickly east of Houston by 9am.

Adoree' Jackson told reporters after Sunday's game that the Titans had not practiced the final offensive play, on which a pass was thrown to him. Head coach Mike Mularkey contradicted this, stating the team had practiced the play previously, though not during the past week. According to Cameron Wolfe's reporting, Jackson said he was only told his route. Jackson, a rookie cornerback, has no career receptions. The play occurred on fourth down at a critical point in the game.

Max Correa, an Appalachian State freshman majoring in biochemistry, has announced his candidacy for governor of Kansas, despite having no ties to the state. Kansas and Vermont are the only states without age requirements for gubernatorial candidates. Correa acknowledges his youth as a weakness but believes it allows him to bring fresh perspectives. His campaign targets younger voters and incorporates Jewish concepts such as tikkun olam and kibbutz-inspired communal settlements to help fund college tuition. If elected, Correa plans to leave App State, move to Topeka, and enroll part-time at the University of Kansas. He intends to address the opioid crisis by offering state-owned properties to pharmaceutical companies to reduce Narcan production costs. Political science professor William Hicks, who Correa says influenced his decision, supports young people's involvement in politics.

Algoma Public Health, celebrating its 50th anniversary, has partnered with Healthy Kids Community Challenge Sault Ste. Marie to launch 'Get Active Algoma,' a contest encouraging community engagement away from screens. Participants download the GooseChase app, join the game, and earn points by completing missions and uploading photos/videos. Running from March 19 to May 31, 2018, the contest offers a $600 bike voucher as the first prize, along with secondary and bonus prizes. Winners will be contacted via their registered email.

Micro E-mini futures, launched by the CME Group in 2019, are contracts that are 1/10th the size of E-mini futures. They trade on the CME Globex electronic platform and were created to make futures markets accessible to retail traders with smaller capital. Initially covering major indexes (S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq 100, Russell 2000), they now extend to assets like bitcoin, copper, crude oil, Treasury yield, and FX futures. Most contracts are financially settled, as retail traders typically do not seek physical delivery.

A Micro E-mini futures strategy involves techniques for trading these contracts, often incorporating technical and fundamental analysis for timing, position sizing, and risk management. Strategies can be used for speculation, diversification, or hedging. Backtesting is recommended before live trading.

Trading hours for the Micro E-mini S&P 500 run Sunday to Friday, 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET, with a one-hour daily break. Contracts are listed quarterly (Mar, Jun, Sep, Dec) for five consecutive quarters, with trading terminating at 9:30 a.m. ET on the 3rd Friday of the contract month. Trading requires a futures broker to access the exchange clearinghouse, though CFDs tracking these contracts are an alternative. The main risk is adverse price movement amplified by leverage. Seasonality and price-affecting factors vary by underlying asset.

NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU architecture introduces several new rendering technologies. Stochastic Texture Filtering (STF) adds randomness to texture sampling to reduce artifacts, running efficiently on Blackwell GPUs. Neural Radiance Cache (NRC) uses a neural shader trained on live game data to infer multi-bounce lighting from path-traced rays, improving performance and indirect lighting quality. RTX Skin brings film-rendering subsurface scattering to real-time path tracing for translucent materials. RTX Neural Faces uses a generative AI model, trained on offline-generated images and optimized with TensorRT, to render more natural-looking faces in real time.

The Blackwell family includes multiple GPUs:
- GB202: 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, 768 Tensor Cores; used in the GeForce RTX 5090.
- GB203: 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA Cores; used in the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti.
- GB205: 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA Cores; used in the RTX 5070.

All GPUs include Blackwell's fourth-generation RT Cores, fifth-generation Tensor Cores, and support DLSS 4.

Napheesa Collier, Minnesota Lynx star and WNBA Players Association vice president, criticized WNBA leadership in an exit interview, calling commissioner Cathy Engelbert's governance "negligent." Collier cited failures in addressing officiating, player compensation, and the league's overall product. She alleged Engelbert said in private conversations that Caitlin Clark "should be grateful" to the WNBA and that players "should be on their knees" for the media rights deal. Collier also claimed Engelbert dismissed officiating concerns by saying "only the losers complain about the refs."

Engelbert responded that she was "disheartened" by Collier's characterization but maintained respect for her. Collier's comments come as players negotiate a new collective bargaining agreement, with a potential work stoppage looming in 2026. Collier, also co-founder of Unrivaled, missed Game 4 of the Lynx's elimination loss to Phoenix due to an ankle injury. Coach Cheryl Reeve, who was ejected and suspended during the series, supported Collier's remarks. The league announced a multiyear media rights deal with USA Network the same day.

Daniel Jones, a 31-year-old British expatriate, received a one-year suspended prison sentence in Cambodia for using "pornographic" images to promote a pool party in Siem Reap. He was among 10 foreigners arrested in January after a police raid on a private villa. Jones denied any sex or nudity occurred at the event, which he advertised on Facebook with the tagline "Let's Get Wet," and apologised. Prosecutors argued images encouraging sexual activity violate Cambodian culture. Having already served nearly two months on remand, the remainder of his sentence was suspended. His lawyer indicated a possible appeal.

President Van Buren transmits to the House of Representatives further correspondence between Secretary of State Forsyth and British minister Fox regarding Alexander McLeod, imprisoned in New York on charges of murder and arson for his alleged role in the 1837 destruction of the steamboat Caroline.

Fox expresses regret that the President declined to release McLeod and has forwarded the correspondence to Her Majesty's Government. He protests characterizations of the Caroline's destruction as an outrage, asserting it was an act of self-defense against a hostile vessel engaged in piratical war, carried out because New York authorities could not prevent hostilities from its territory.

Forsyth replies that evidence has been submitted to Britain with a demand for redress, making further discussion improper, and suggests Fox's opinions would differ had he reviewed the collected testimony.

Kay Frazier, a 50-year-old grandmother from Wigan, died from a blood clot, an inquest heard. She had married American prisoner Gary Frazier in his Nebraska jail cell after exchanging around 12,000 letters, and regularly flew to visit him. In May, she was hospitalised with severe headaches caused by a thrombosis blocking blood to her brain. Radiologist Toby Williams told the inquest a risky thrombectomy was necessary, as she would otherwise die. During surgery, she suffered a ruptured artery and died two days later at Salford Royal Hospital. The cause of the clot is unknown. Gary Frazier, 37, is serving 49 years for shooting two people. The coroner has yet to return a verdict.

Retired lawyer Marcel Strigberger describes decluttering his home by discarding law school textbooks purchased over 50 years ago from McGill University. He reflects on each book before disposal, including a contracts textbook by Cheshire and Fifoot containing memorable cases, and a property law book by Magarry and Wade covering concepts like fee simple and fee tail that he rarely used in 42 years of practice. He notes with regret that one discarded book sells used on Amazon for over $1,000 Canadian. He also tossed a book containing a cargo ship explosion case. All books went into the recycling bin, except one thick volume he kept for use as a reading stand.

The speaker expresses frustration with opponents' aggressive tactics, including intentionally falling on him and pushing teammates onto him while he was down, calling it dangerous. He believes his teammates should be more aggressive in front of the net (Eddie) but not retaliate with dangerous plays. He expects similar treatment in upcoming games and wants referees to call penalties on intentional falls and pushes. At home, he plans to play the puck more aggressively, noting Buffalo's ice and boards allow pucks to bounce farther from the boards, making puck-handling easier than in Dallas. He reports feeling good physically, with no groin issues. The team intends to remain aggressive but play smarter.

The President assumes office amid industrial and financial difficulties, pledging to rely on God and the support of citizens. He identifies key priorities:

**Finance and Currency:** The financial system needs revision to ensure stable money value under government supervision. He supports creating a bipartisan commission to examine coinage, banking, and currency laws. International bimetallism will be pursued through cooperation with other commercial powers, while maintaining parity between gold and silver.

**Economy and Revenue:** Strict economy in government spending is required. Revenues must cover expenditures, including pensions for soldiers, sailors, and their families. Deficits should be addressed through increased revenue rather than loans.

**Tariffs:** Revenue should come primarily from tariffs on foreign imports to protect American industries and labor. He urges reenactment of the reciprocity principle from the 1890 law to expand foreign markets.

**Domestic Issues:** Agriculture and labor have suffered; manufacturing revival will help. He condemns lynchings, insisting courts enforce law. Naturalization and immigration laws should be improved, illiteracy eliminated, and civil service reform continued genuinely. Trusts and combinations restricting trade will be opposed.

**Merchant Marine and Foreign Policy:** The American merchant marine must be restored. Foreign policy will follow Washington's non-interference tradition, avoiding territorial conquest and favoring arbitration. He urges Senate ratification of the arbitration treaty with Great Britain.

**Extra Session:** Due to Treasury conditions, he will convene Congress in extraordinary session on March 15, 1897.

He concludes by celebrating national unity across former sectional divides and pledges to uphold his oath to preserve the Constitution.

Both teams are evenly matched with similar styles, and an emotional game was expected. The speaker acknowledges past errors and lack of intensity, emphasizing the need to correct them with better effort. A fortunate break was capitalized on. Away from the rink, time with family and friends provides enjoyment, though focus returns before games. In the last seven minutes, the team began creating chances, winning battles, and getting the puck to the net. The strategy is to stay poised rather than play defensively, maintaining the same approach to generate scoring opportunities by involving the defense and driving to the net.

An international team of physicists from Leiden, Beijing, and Hangzhou has confirmed that large quantum systems genuinely follow quantum mechanics using Bell's test, developed by John Bell. The test determines whether a system truly uses quantum effects or merely mimics them.

Rather than measuring Bell correlations directly, the researchers focused on energy minimization. They created a quantum state with 73 qubits in a superconducting processor, measuring energies far below classical possibilities, with a 48 standard deviation difference. They also certified genuine multipartite Bell correlations—where all qubits must be involved—in states of up to 24 qubits.

The study demonstrates that deep quantum behavior can be certified in large systems at an unprecedented scale. The findings could advance quantum communication, cryptography security, and the development of new quantum algorithms.

Advanced attacking runs in soccer require offensive players to make conscious decisions to create opportunities several passes or minutes ahead. They fall into three categories: individual, planned, and supporting runs.

Individual runs include blind-side runs (behind an inattentive defender), drawing defenders out, inverted runs (opposite of expected direction), overlap/underlap runs (moving beyond a teammate without switching positions), third-man running, late runs, and deep-lying runs by back players.

Planned runs are designed by coaches for set plays and include designated routes, runs to receive specific passes like crosses, and fast breaks—typically involving a target midfielder and a sprinting attacker exploiting sudden possession changes.

Supporting runs help maintain possession and include back-pass options (10+ yards behind the ball carrier), square-pass options (parallel to the halfway line), and swinging the ball between defenders to switch fields.

Key considerations include avoiding offside positions, proper timing (including patience), and unpredictability to prevent defenders from anticipating runs. Only one run receives the pass, but all runs must be completed. Players should also scout opposing defenders' tendencies.

Medical student mistreatment remains prevalent, affecting approximately 38% of graduating students according to the 2023 AAMC Graduation Questionnaire, yet only 26.9% of mistreated students report incidents. Mistreatment is associated with anxiety, depression, burnout, decreased empathy, and career regret. To investigate motivations for reporting, researchers conducted peer-to-peer, semi-structured interviews with 21 medical students at a single urban academic institution in the southern United States between April-May 2019. Participants described 34 mistreatment incidents, of which 12 were reported.

Using inductive analysis based on grounded theory, four overarching factor groups influencing reporting decisions emerged: personal, situational, structural, and climate. Personal factors included concern for repercussions (e.g., grades, career), a sense of justice toward protecting others, and lack of personal motivation. Situational factors involved ambiguity in defining mistreatment, severity of the incident (with race-based mistreatment viewed as more reportable), input from confidants, bystander inaction, and perceptions of the perpetrator. Structural factors included doubt that action would be taken, logistical barriers, and lack of communication about outcomes. Climate factors reflected the hierarchical culture of medicine, where mistreatment was perceived as expected and reporting as futile.

Only personal and situational factors motivated reporting; most identified factors discouraged it. The authors recommend mitigation strategies including transparent, easy-to-use reporting systems, publicized de-identified data, anonymous retaliation reporting, bystander training targeting those higher in the hierarchy, and top-down cultural change led by educational leadership. Limitations include single-site sampling, self-selection bias, higher-than-average reporting rates, and focus on clinical settings. Future research should develop validated measures of mistreatment climate and further examine the role of witnesses.

A research paper published in Climate Change suggests that the Eldgjá volcanic eruption, which occurred from spring 939 CE to at least autumn 940 CE, may have encouraged Icelanders to adopt Christianity. The eruption, the largest known lava flood of the Common Era, devastated the newly settled Iceland by blocking sunlight, lowering temperatures, and hindering agriculture. Researchers argue that the Völuspá, a 10th-century poem from the Poetic Edda, references the eruption in its depiction of the end of the Norse gods, suggesting it was used to promote Christianisation. Iceland's official conversion date is 999/1000 CE. The 13th-century Kristni saga also links the conversion to a volcanic eruption, supporting the researchers' conclusion that the Eldgjá eruption acted as a catalyst for cultural change.

Huawei's subsidiary Honor launched the Honor 9i in India on October 5, marking its third anniversary. The device is a rebranded version of Huawei Maimang 6 and Nova 2i, and is described as the world's first smartphone with a FullView display and four cameras. It features a uni-body metal design, a 5.99-inch full HD+ IPS LCD with 18:9 aspect ratio, and 13MP+2MP front and 16MP+2MP rear dual cameras with Bokeh effect. It runs on a HiSilicon Kirin 659 octa-core processor with Android Nougat-based EMUI, 4GB RAM, 64GB storage, and a 3,340mAh battery. Priced at Rs. 17,999, it targets the mid-range segment.

The Nation should not alienate its remaining coal lands. The President has temporarily withdrawn lands identified by the Geological Survey as containing coal, but legislation is needed to withdraw them from sale or entry. Ownership should remain with the United States, with private individuals permitted to work them under a royalty system, with government oversight ensuring fair prices to consumers. Rates charged by common carriers transporting coal must also be supervised to prevent favoritism. This approach parallels the withdrawal of forest lands from settlement.

Congress has advanced National Government supervision of interstate corporations through the railway rate bill, pure food bill, and beef-packing inspection provisions. These laws have proven effective; the interstate commerce law has coincided with increased railroad earnings and an unprecedented number of voluntary freight and fare reductions. Further measures, such as dating labels and charging inspection costs to packers, may be advisable.

Progress must continue in expanding National Government control over interstate capital, including enlarged powers for the Interstate Commerce Commission. State-level regulation has proved chaotic and ineffective for interstate corporations. A national license law or similar mechanism should prevent overcapitalization and require disclosure of stockholders, properties, and business dealings. The goal is supervising consolidation rather than preventing it. Remedying genuine abuses is the best method for countering socialistic agitation and calls for government ownership of railways. Proper regulation would not suppress individual initiative; unregulated competition itself can eliminate competitors and mirror effects attributed to socialism.

This weekly job announcement email, distributed to Haas School alumni on October 19, 2000, lists 14 job opportunities from various companies. Positions include Senior Business Analyst at Kaiser Permanente (Oakland), Controller at University of Michigan, Development Officers and Writer/Communications Director at United Nations Foundation (Washington, DC), Associate at Micron Technology (Boise), Product Marketing roles at Informatica (Palo Alto), multiple finance and analyst positions at PG&E Corporation (San Francisco), Analyst at Blue Shield of California, business development roles at ePocrates (San Carlos), Director of Strategy at an online shopping service (New York), Business Development and Finance directors at iVenturi (San Francisco), multiple marketing positions at Extensity (Emeryville), Economist at Fremont Group (San Francisco), and Market Research Analyst at Research Dog. Most positions prefer or require an MBA. Each listing includes contact information for applications. The bulletin is supported by the Haas School Annual Fund and notes that companies have not been vetted by the school.

Delta Air Lines reported record revenue and beat earnings forecasts, driven by strong premium and corporate travel demand. CEO Ed Bastian projected full-year adjusted EPS near $6. Premium seat sales are expected to overtake main cabin sales in 2026, a year earlier than previously forecast. Premium revenue rose 9% to $5.8 billion, while main cabin sales fell 4% to $6 billion. Corporate travel grew 8%. President Glen Hauenstein noted premium products, once loss leaders, are now highest-margin. The trend aligns with U.S. wealth concentration, where the top 10% of households accounted for nearly 50% of consumer spending in Q2 2025. Delta's shares rose up to 6% following the release, lifting the broader airline sector. Hauenstein highlighted growth opportunities in Los Angeles, Boston, New York, and Seattle, plus investments in Delta One lounges.

The January 24, 2002 Energy Central Daily News edition covers top stories in electric power and gas industries. Key electric power headlines include congressional subpoenas issued to Arthur Andersen witnesses regarding Enron's document destruction, Long Island opening its power market to retail competition, pressure on Florida Power to cut rates, and NRC's revised standards for a U.S. nuclear waste site. Enron-related coverage dominates, including Democratic pressure over Bush administration meetings, an auditor refusing to testify, a Senate request for Enron's tax returns, federal authorities taking over Enron's Houston headquarters, and creditor requests for outside supervision. Other topics include California's energy crisis, competition and deregulation developments, power plant projects by Calpine and Endesa, renewable energy news, nuclear plant issues, and fourth-quarter financial results from Dynegy, DPL, Northeast Utilities, Progress Energy, and Hydro-Quebec. International coverage addresses European power market liberalization, Taiwan's energy sector opening to foreign investment, and Andersen's potential loss of UK audit contracts.

This paper presents research conducted on D'harawal Country in south-west Sydney, where Indigenous community members were asked to envision what education could look like when grounded in Indigenous knowledges. Written by Michelle Bishop, a Gamilaroi woman, the research responds to documented harm caused by mainstream schooling to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students and rejects school reform in favour of envisioning Indigenous education sovereignty.

The study involved 35 anonymous online survey respondents and face-to-face yarns with over 15 participants of varied ages, roles, and educational backgrounds. To protect anonymity, exact participant numbers and demographic tables are withheld—an intentional act of refusal grounded in relational accountability.

Methodologically, the paper draws on Indigenous futurities, futurisms, and resurgence, alongside envisioning as a decolonising process that creates space to imagine futures beyond colonial constraints. The author applies a concept called "layering the vision," which accepts multiple truths and weaves participant contributions into a collective vision.

Findings are re-presented through story, an Indigenous knowledge-transmission practice that protects anonymity while amplifying participant voices. The paper concludes with the story "Our Education, Our Way," in which an Aunty, community members, and young people yarn about the failures of current schooling and imagine an Aboriginal-controlled education grounded in Country, Elders, culture, language, belonging, and identity. The story incorporates 58 direct and indirect quotes from anonymous participants, with characters intentionally amalgamated to safeguard identities.

Darren protected Nick respectfully without causing harm to Rod Brind'amour. Crystal Palace came from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 with Leicester City, with goals from Yohan Cabaye and Christian Benteke cancelling out strikes by Robert Huth and Jamie Vardy. The result put Palace on 35 points from 32 games, two behind Leicester. Palace manager Sam Allardyce praised his players' fightback, while Vardy expressed disappointment ahead of Leicester's Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid.

Meb Faber's 2012 paper in the Journal of Wealth Management proposed a simple trend-following strategy for the S&P 500: buy when price crosses above the 200-day moving average and sell when it crosses below. The strategy ignores news, earnings, and sentiment, focusing solely on price. Paul Tudor Jones has also endorsed the 200-day moving average as a defensive tool to avoid major losses.

Backtesting from 1960 to present shows the strategy largely avoided the 2008/09 Global Financial Crisis, exiting in December 2007 and re-entering in June 2009. During COVID-19, it experienced a 19% maximum drawdown. Using monthly data with a ten-month moving average, $100,000 invested in 1960 grew to $4.7 million (excluding dividends), with a CAGR of 6.3% versus 7% for buy-and-hold, and a maximum drawdown of 26% during the 1987 crash. The 200-day moving average is described as a simple but effective trend-following tool.

Congress has made no appropriation for better enforcement of the antitrust law, though more could be accomplished with a special appropriation directed by the Attorney-General. Reducing the tariff as a means of addressing trust-related evils would be ineffective, as many large corporations would be unaffected except through general economic harm. Lowering the tariff would damage weaker competitors and disadvantage domestic products. Trust regulation should be treated separately from tariff revision.

Economic stability is essential, and the protective-tariff principle has brought prosperity; radical or frequent changes are undesirable. Tariff matters should be considered based on business needs rather than partisanship, with periodic reapplication of principles to shifting national conditions. Any changes must maintain equality with foreign interests, cover labor cost differences, and protect American wages.

Adjustments can be achieved through reciprocity treaties to expand markets and lower unnecessary duties, or, failing ratification, through direct legislation. Where reciprocity is unsuitable, duties may be lowered outright after expert review. A commission of business experts could be appointed to examine schedules scientifically and recommend changes that preserve prosperity and fixed economic policy.

Elmatica, a Printed Circuit Broker, is establishing operations in South Africa due to increased business and customer demand for closer technical assistance. According to CEO Didrik Bech, sales in South Africa grew 245 percent compared to 2016. The company plans to create a permanent team in the country to provide access to technology, processes, and compliance knowledge. Swedish Country Manager Mikael Jansson has been temporarily relocated from Stockholm to South Africa.

The binary image build model funnels all interface call-out functions through a single portal, with the host environment implementing a router function that translates function numbers into execution addresses. The router exists external to the AGESA™ software binary module in 32-bit protected mode flat addressing.

The UEFI BIOS environment offers four execution stages (SEC, PEI, DXE, RTP) across three modes. AGESA™ core files are organized into three libraries, with four additional UEFI libraries. Development uses MASM 6.15 for 16-bit SEC, and specific Microsoft Macro Assembler and C/C++ compiler versions for 32-bit and 64-bit phases.

The SEC phase establishes the C programming environment. PEI drivers include modules for processor initialization (AmdProcessorInitPeim) and post-reset initialization, publishing PPIs such as AMD_PEI_INIT_RESET_PPI, AMD_PEI_INIT_EARLY_PPI, and AMD_PEI_INIT_POST_PPI. A reset coordination PEIM manages warm reset requests from multiple AMD PEIMs.

The DXE driver performs late initialization and publishes the AgesaDxeProtocol. Additional drivers like AmdGpuVgaControlDxe handle VGA resource decoding.

Key entry procedures include AmdInitReset (minimal processor initialization), AmdInitEarly (full processor configuration), AmdInitPost (memory initialization), AmdInitEnv (transitions to post-memory), AmdInitMid (graphics configuration), AmdInitLate (generates ACPI/DMI tables), and AmdInitRtb (saves state for suspend). Resume procedures (AmdInitResume, AmdS3LateRestore, AmdS3Save) restore processor state.

Required host call-outs include AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer, and AgesaDoReset. Service functions like AmdCreateStruct, AmdReleaseStruct, and various identification/configuration routines support host operations. Stack management uses AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK and AMD_DISABLE_STACK macros for x86-64 APUs; AArch64 APUs with Platform Security Processor do not use these stack macros.

This paper examines how English as a Second Language (ESL), Bilingual Education (BE), and World Languages (WL) developed as separate U.S. educational domains shaped by distinct sociopolitical histories, including settler colonialism, Americanization campaigns, and English-only policies. The authors apply Valdés' (2018) framework of language curricularization to analyze how theories, ideologies, and policies shape language teacher education across these fields.

Drawing on their work at a Hispanic-Serving Institution in Chicago, the authors describe a three-phase curricular innovation for ESL and BE methods courses serving future WL and Chinese bilingual teachers. Phase 1 shifted the ESL methods course from sheltered instruction to translanguaging pedagogy, revising learning outcomes and assessments to serve diverse educators. Phase 2 created a combined ESL and WL Methods course focused on Chinese, emphasizing multilingual approaches, cultural learning, and varied program models. Phase 3, a planned future redesign of the BE methods course, will prioritize documenting candidates' linguistic repertoires, building critical consciousness through drama-based pedagogy, and conducting critical curricular analysis of BE programs.

The authors identify enabling factors (cross-program collaboration, external review, guiding frameworks) and constraints (non-sequenced enrollment, limited field experience oversight). They emphasize modeling for candidates the practices they should use with emergent bilingual learners. Rather than merging language teacher education into one path, the authors advocate bridging fields through historical awareness, heteroglossic views of language, and culturally responsive pedagogy attentive to minoritized learners.

Construction on the $1.8 billion Las Vegas stadium project has exceeded minority hiring goals since beginning in November. According to Lynn Littlejohn of general contractor Mortenson Construction, 54 percent of the 80,000 work hours completed between November and March were performed by minorities, women, and veterans, surpassing the 38 percent goal. Of $509 million in subcontracts awarded, $91 million (18 percent) went to 32 small-business-enterprise companies, exceeding the 15 percent goal set by Senate Bill 1. About 225 workers have been hired, expanding to 500 by fall. Raiders President Marc Badain said the 65,000-seat stadium remains on schedule for summer 2020 completion. The seven-member Community Benefits Oversight Committee, chaired by Ken Evans, held its inaugural meeting Monday and will meet quarterly to monitor the Raiders' community benefits plan and philanthropic efforts.

The company operates through Devices and Consumer and Commercial segment groups and faces ongoing litigation including antitrust matters, patent disputes with Motorola and others, and a China SAIC investigation.

The professor introduces course 6.451, Principles of Digital Communications II, describing it as fundamentally a coding course within a communications framework, focused on achieving channel capacity on the additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel.

Logistical details covered include: the course will be videotaped for OpenCourseWare; teaching assistant Ashish Khisti will lecture during the professor's absence; weekly problem sets are due Wednesdays; the midterm is scheduled for March 16 (worth 1/3 of the grade) and the final is worth 1/2. The prerequisite 6.450 is enforced for mathematical sophistication rather than content.

Topics to be covered include algebraic block codes, convolutional codes, tail-biting codes, capacity-approaching codes, low-density parity-check codes, lattice codes, trellis coded modulation, and their decoding algorithms. The course aims to provide more time on capacity-approaching codes and potentially band-limited channel codes.

The professor illustrates the design framework using example channels: the deep space channel (power-limited) and telephone line channel (bandwidth ~3700 Hz, SNR ~37 dB). AWGN channels are characterized by power P, noise spectral density N_0, and bandwidth W, combined into signal-to-noise ratio SNR = P/(N_0·W).

Shannon's capacity theorem establishes C = W·log₂(1+SNR) bits per second as the maximum achievable rate with arbitrarily low error probability, achieved through coding that introduces constraints over long sequences. Reaching this limit practically took roughly 50 years.

The professor advocates using decibels (dB) as a convenient logarithm system and provides a reference table of common values.

Chapter 2 demonstrates converting continuous-time AWGN channels to discrete-time equivalents via orthonormal PAM, preserving SNR and information. Bandwidth W Hz corresponds to 2W real symbols per second. Spectral efficiency ρ = R/W is defined as bits per second per Hertz, or equivalently bits per two dimensions in discrete time.

The article compares dollar-cost averaging (DCA) and lump-sum investing strategies, examining how sequence of returns risk affects outcomes. DCA involves investing gradually in installments, while lump-sum investing deploys capital all at once.

According to a Morningstar study, lump-sum investing outperforms DCA about 90% of the time over 10-year periods. Despite this, DCA helps reduce behavioral biases and fear-driven decisions that cause many retail investors to underperform.

Using S&P 500 data from 2000-2019, the article presents three backtests starting with $60,000:
- Lump-sum investment grew to $193,157 (CAGR 6.02%) despite a 55% drawdown in 2008.
- DCA produced a CAGR of 5.5%.
- When the return sequence was reversed (2010-2019 returns first), lump-sum CAGR only slightly dropped to 5.93%, but DCA's final value fell to $87,396, with CAGR dropping to 1.9%.

The article concludes that lump-sum investing is generally preferable because DCA is heavily influenced by the sequence of returns and randomness.

The Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card is highlighted as a top no-annual-fee credit card offering unlimited 2% cash rewards on purchases with no categories to track. New cardholders can earn a $200 welcome bonus after spending $500 within the first 3 months. Weber State University canceled its 27th annual Unity Conference, themed "Redacted: Navigating the Complexities of Censorship," on October 1, two days before it was scheduled to begin. The cancellation followed a directive requiring presenters, including associate professor Sarah Herrmann and her student, to remove mentions of "DEI," "diversity," "equity," and "inclusion" from their materials. Multiple faculty withdrew rather than censor their work.

The conference, formerly called the Diversity Conference, is sponsored by the Student Access and Success division, making it subject to Utah's HB 261, which restricts DEI-related content in non-academic programming. Academically sponsored events are exempt from the law. Vice President Jessica Oyler explained that presentations could not describe legislation as "harmful" or partisan, or suggest individuals are inherently privileged or oppressed based on identity.

A university spokesperson acknowledged communication issues and said officials are still interpreting the legislation. The faculty and staff union held an alternative event on Friday attended by about 50 people. The Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression criticized Weber State for overinterpreting the law. The university is considering restructuring future conferences under Academic Affairs to exempt them from HB 261. Political science professor Richard Price noted recent state budget cuts led to the closure of programs including queer studies, ethnic studies, and women's and gender studies minors.

Winter fishing will feature sailfish, dolphin, wahoo, and kingfish offshore. Anglers should head south and drift north with the stream, targeting 160' depth off the Dodge Wall for sails and 90' for kings. Live bait, available from bait boats monitored on VHF 68, is essential. Kite fishing, flat lining, and deep rods all work, and wire trace leaders are recommended for wahoo or king.
