A study published October 8 found that ChatGPT generates resumes depicting female candidates as younger and less experienced than male candidates, then ranks them as less qualified. Researchers led by Douglas Guilbeault of Stanford University analyzed nearly 1.4 million online images and videos, conducted text analysis, and ran a randomized experiment with over 450 participants. Coders consistently rated women in online images as younger than men, with the bias strongest in prestigious occupations like doctors and CEOs. Text analysis linked less prestigious jobs with younger females and prestigious roles with older males. The experiment showed that viewing online images influenced participants' age estimates for occupations. The findings do not reflect U.S. Census data, which shows male and female employees are roughly the same age. Researchers suggest these biases may help explain the persistent glass ceiling for women and argue that addressing single biases in isolation overlooks intersecting forms of discrimination.

Michael Gayed's paper proposes a weekly rotation strategy between SPY (S&P 500) and XLU (Utilities) based on past performance. Rotation systems switch between assets to exploit varying sector performance, often used in trend following and seasonality strategies.

Gayed argues utilities are distinctive due to risk-aversion, low beta, and interest rate sensitivity, outperforming during falling rates and underperforming during rising rate expectations. For instance, during the 2008 crash, XLU's drawdown was -45.2% versus SPY's -54.61%.

Gayed's backtest since 1929 showed 13.1% annual compounding. A backtest from 1999 shows the strategy returned 6.7% annually versus 4.6% for buy-and-hold until the paper's 2014 publication. Since then, it has lagged SPY (5.1% vs. 10.4% annually), never recovering from the 2020 COVID crash. Its maximum drawdown since 2021 (-23.6%) is similar to SPY's (-23.9%). While underperformance is notable, it may be too early to declare the strategy ineffective.

Researchers are exploring ways to repurpose grape pomace, a waste product from winemaking, into a renewable resource for antioxidants, oils, and dietary fibers. Presented at the 255th National Meeting of the American Chemical Society, Changmou Xu's team notes that the global wine industry produces about 14 million tons of pomace annually, which can pollute water, acidify soil, and spread disease. Pomace contains natural antioxidants such as proanthocyanidins, anthocyanins, and ellagic acid. Xu's team is identifying technologies to extract nutrients and remove pesticides for commercial use. Collaborations have examined pomace's effects against foodborne pathogens and on piglet health. The researchers added phenolic compounds to fatty foods like mayonnaise, finding they inhibited lipid oxidation and extended shelf life. A previous study reduced acrylamide in potato chips by 60 percent. The team aims to match the performance of the artificial antioxidant EDTA, offering consumers a natural-ingredient alternative.

Game is selling an Xbox One S (500GB) bundle for £249.99, which includes Forza Horizon 3, Tekken 7, Halo 5, and Gears of War 4. Purchasing these items individually on Amazon UK would total £297.10, representing a £47.11 saving.

The Xbox One S received a 4/5 review, with praise for its smaller size, 4K upscaling, HDR gaming compatibility, and affordability as a UHD Blu-ray player—a feature the competing PlayStation 4 Pro lacks.

The included games also scored well in reviews: Forza Horizon 3 (5/5), Tekken 7 (4/5), Halo 5 (4/5), and Gears of War 4 (4.5/5).

The BNT162b2 COVID-19 vaccine study ran from 29 April 2020 to 10 February 2023 at 153 locations across 6 countries, enrolling healthy participants aged 12 and older without prior COVID-19 infection or vaccination. Initial doses were observer-blinded, while booster doses were generally open-label.

Phase 1 included 195 participants (ages 19–82), while Phase 2/3 enrolled 46,406 participants (ages 12–91). An additional 333 participants received BNT162b2SA in Phase 3.

Key efficacy results showed BNT162b2 (30 µg) was 95% effective in preventing COVID-19 from 7 days after Dose 2, regardless of prior infection status. Immune responses after a BNT162b2 booster matched those after Dose 2, and BNT162b2SA produced comparable responses against the Beta variant.

Common side effects included injection site pain, tiredness, and headache, mostly mild to moderate and short-lived. Phase 1 participants showed temporary lymphocyte count drops that resolved within 6–8 days. The 100-µg BNT162b1 dose was discontinued due to reactions.

Serious medical problems were rare (less than 1%) and mostly deemed unrelated to the vaccine. No deaths were attributed to BNT162b2. Researchers concluded the vaccine was well tolerated and effective.

NASA's Cassini spacecraft completed the first of five close flybys of Saturn, marking the end of its 20-year mission. The probe skimmed Saturn's clouds at an altitude of 1,010-1,060 miles on August 14, becoming the first Saturn atmospheric probe. Depending on atmospheric density, the team may perform a "pop-down" maneuver to bring the craft 120 miles closer on the second pass, enabling data collection on temperature, auroras, vortexes, and chemical composition. The team also hopes to determine the length of a Saturn day, currently estimated at 10.5 hours. Cassini has spent 13 years at Saturn, including 127 Titan flybys. Due to low fuel and concerns about crashing into Titan or Enceladus, the mission will end with Cassini's descent into Saturn on September 15, following a final Titan farewell on September 11.

The application claims priority to numerous U.S. patent and provisional applications filed between 2017 and 2018, all incorporated by reference, concerning surgical network systems, smart energy devices, and interactive surgical platforms.

The disclosure provides methods for characterizing an ultrasonic device's end effector, which includes an electromechanical ultrasonic system with a transducer coupled to an ultrasonic blade. The methods involve applying power to the transducer, measuring its impedance, comparing it to a stored reference value, classifying the impedance, and adjusting power based on characterizations of: (1) the end effector's state, (2) its function, or (3) the tissue in contact with it.

The system encompasses a computer-implemented interactive surgical platform featuring surgical hubs that communicate with cloud-based servers, visualization systems, robotic systems, and handheld intelligent instruments. A modular hub enclosure accommodates interchangeable components including generator modules (integrating monopolar, bipolar, and ultrasonic capabilities), smoke evacuation modules, suction/irrigation modules, imaging modules, and communication modules via docking stations with aligned power and data contacts.

The surgical data network connects modular devices through network hubs, switches, and routers to cloud computing resources, enabling real-time data collection, processing, and manipulation to improve surgical outcomes. Imaging devices may utilize multi-spectral monitoring, CCD or CMOS sensors, and modular light sources replaceable during procedures. The visualization system coordinates information flow between sterile and non-sterile field displays under hub guidance.

Jack Hare introduces a course on plasma diagnostics, explaining that diagnostics are tools used to indirectly gain knowledge about plasmas since their properties cannot be measured directly. He compares this to familiar instruments like thermometers but notes plasma measurements often rely on less intuitive physical effects, such as light polarization indicating magnetic fields. The prerequisite is course 22.611, with strong plasma physics background assumed.

Hare emphasizes diagnostics' historical importance, citing the ZETA experiment, where inadequate diagnostics led UK researchers to mistakenly attribute neutron bursts to fusion rather than MHD instabilities. This failure spurred the development of Thomson scattering, later used to confirm Soviet tokamak temperatures, transforming fusion research globally. Similarly, the National Ignition Facility initially lacked proper diagnostics, delaying understanding until improved diagnostics enabled ignition.

Diagnostics matter to experimentalists (for understanding measurement uncertainty), computational researchers (for code validation), and theorists (for designing testable predictions).

Ideally, researchers would know every particle's position and velocity, but in practice they measure moments like density, average velocity, and magnetic fields. Real diagnostics are limited: measurements are sparse in space and time, often line-integrated (especially for light-based techniques), filtered by instrument response functions, and dependent on imperfect physics models like atomic data for spectroscopy.

The course, following Hutchinson's textbook, focuses on enduring principles rather than changing practical implementations. Students then introduced themselves and mapped their plasmas onto a temperature-density-magnetic field chart, covering devices including tokamaks (DIII-D, HBT, ASDEX Upgrade, SPARC), NIF, Z machine, C2W, CNT, Hall thrusters, helicon plasmas, and plasma wakefield accelerators, using diverse diagnostics such as Langmuir probes, Mirnov coils, bolometers, neutron spectrometry, Thomson scattering, interferometry, Faraday rotation, and spectroscopy.

The Rams have requested permission to interview Doug Marrone for their head coaching vacancy, per Adam Schefter. Marrone went 1-1 as the Jaguars' interim coach, with the team defeating the Titans 38-17 in Week 16 and losing 24-20 to the Colts. Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q with the SEC for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2015. The company is a Delaware-incorporated large accelerated filer with 465,680,957 shares of common stock outstanding as of April 15, 2015.

For Q1 2015, Amazon reported total net sales of $22.7 billion, up 15% from $19.7 billion in Q1 2014, with foreign exchange reducing sales by $1.3 billion. Income from operations rose to $255 million from $146 million, though the company posted a net loss of $57 million compared to net income of $108 million a year earlier. Operating cash flow for the trailing twelve months was $7.8 billion, and free cash flow reached $3.2 billion.

Beginning in Q1 2015, Amazon restructured its reportable segments into North America, International, and AWS. North America sales grew 24% to $13.4 billion with operating income of $517 million; International sales declined 2% to $7.7 billion with an operating loss of $76 million; AWS sales grew 49% to $1.6 billion with operating income of $265 million.

Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $13.8 billion at quarter-end, down from $17.4 billion. Long-term debt face value was $8.4 billion, primarily from senior notes issued in 2012 and 2014. The company also maintains a $2.0 billion unsecured revolving credit facility with no outstanding borrowings.

Amazon acquired companies for an aggregate $341 million during the quarter. The company is contesting IRS transfer pricing adjustments that could result in approximately $1.5 billion in additional federal tax, and faces a French tax assessment of approximately $250 million, along with various patent infringement lawsuits and a European Commission investigation into Luxembourg tax arrangements.

Tesla, founded in 2003 and led by CEO Elon Musk since 2008, grew into the leading EV manufacturer, launching the Roadster (2008), Model S (2012), Model X (2015), and Model 3 (2017). The company went public in 2010, raising $226.1 million, and by April 2017 became the most valuable U.S. automaker by market capitalization. Tesla expanded beyond vehicles into battery gigafactories with Panasonic, the Powerwall home battery, and acquired SolarCity in 2016 for roughly $2.1 billion.

Despite its rising valuation, Tesla consistently failed to generate profits or positive operating cash flow, requiring repeated equity and debt offerings that nearly doubled shares outstanding and pushed long-term debt above $10 billion by 2017. The Model 3 launch intensified financial strain, as production repeatedly fell short of the 5,000-cars-per-week target needed to achieve positive cash flow. Analysts, including Goldman Sachs, projected Tesla might need over $10 billion in additional capital by 2020. Musk publicly denied the need for further fundraising in 2018, leaving Tesla's survival dependent on balancing capital needs against investor willingness to continue funding the company.

NVIDIA's Turing GPU architecture introduces significant advancements across memory, display, rendering, and AI capabilities. Turing is the first GPU architecture to use GDDR6 memory, delivering 14 Gbps signaling and 20% improved power efficiency over GDDR5X. Combined with larger L2 caches and enhanced compression, Turing achieves 50% higher effective bandwidth than Pascal.

The new display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K resolution at 60 Hz, HDR processing, and includes an improved NVENC encoder supporting HEVC 8K at 30 fps. Turing GPUs include hardware support for USB-C and VirtualLink, simplifying VR headset connectivity, and replace SLI bridges with NVLink for higher GPU-to-GPU bandwidth.

Turing introduces real-time ray tracing through dedicated RT Cores that accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, enabling hybrid rendering that combines rasterization and ray tracing. Ray tracing performance is roughly 10x faster than Pascal.

NVIDIA NGX leverages Turing's Tensor Cores for AI-based features including Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Additional new features include Mesh Shading (Task and Mesh Shaders) for efficient geometry processing, Variable Rate Shading (VRS) for dynamic shading rate control, Texture Space Shading (TSS), and Multi-View Rendering (MVR) supporting up to four views per pass.

The Turing family includes TU102, TU104 (used in GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, Quadro RTX 5000), and TU106 (GeForce RTX 2070). NVIDIA introduces RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering, with the RTX 2080 Ti rated at 78 RTX-OPS. Ray tracing applications include physically correct shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, demonstrated in games like Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider.

Hurricane Harvey, which struck the Texas Gulf Coast with 120-mph winds and heavy rainfall, may have damaged up to a dozen critical wildlife habitats. According to Ryan Fikes of the National Wildlife Federation, Texas Parks and Wildlife and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service are conducting initial damage assessments, with detailed monitoring to follow. Aransas National Wildlife Refuge's salt marshes, used by endangered whooping cranes, were damaged. Attwater Prairie Chicken National Wildlife Refuge received 50 inches of rain, and only about 10 of its 60 endangered prairie chickens are believed to have survived. Fikes said the National Wildlife Federation attributes the increased intensity of recent storms to climate change. Shrimp and crabs appear to have survived, but oyster beds suffered losses, and bottlenose dolphins may have been harmed by freshwater inflows.

This study introduces a method for analyzing the hierarchy of public transit modes based on actual passenger travel patterns using smart card data, addressing the gap between planner-designed hierarchies and real-world usage. The approach classifies trip segments into "ascending" and "descending" phases based on half of the total travel distance, then constructs transfer rate matrices to quantify hierarchical differences between modes. Unlike prior studies, it does not assume spatial homogeneity, enabling analysis of localized modes and multi-zonal systems through interzonal and intrazonal trip chains.

Applied to T-money transit card data from the Seoul Metropolitan Area (November 12, 2019), covering 10,264,700 trip chains across six modes (walking, community bus, urban bus, intercity bus, light rail, metro), the analysis found consistent hierarchical ordering between ascending and descending phases within Seoul: walking, community bus, urban bus, light rail, and metro. For interzonal trips involving Gyeonggi and Incheon, the intercity bus held the highest hierarchical position, and the inclusion of intercity bus lowered the relative hierarchy of other modes. Regional variations were observed, with metro ranking higher in Seoul due to denser station distribution, while intercity bus was more prevalent in Gyeonggi and Incheon. Urban bus also held a lower hierarchical position outside Seoul.

A 16-year-old driver, Bradd Rudolph, drove through a "T" intersection in Morehouse Parish and into Bayou Bartholomew, drowning two backseat passengers, including 15-year-old Michael Hill. Hill's father sued the Morehouse Parish Police Jury and its insurer, alleging inadequate warning signs at the intersection. The trial court found the police jury knew of the intersection's danger—a known teenage gathering route—and had previously posted double arrow signs that had been knocked down or stolen and not replaced for approximately three months before the accident. The court allocated 20% fault to the police jury and 80% to Rudolph, awarding $31,587.53 to plaintiff.

On appeal, the Second Circuit affirmed the finding of liability, holding the trial court's factual findings were not manifestly erroneous. The court determined the police jury had actual notice of the defect and failed to remedy it, and that the absence of a double arrow sign was a substantial factor in causing the harm. However, the court found the fault allocation unreasonable and reallocated it to 65% for Rudolph and 35% for the police jury. The $150,000 general damage award was affirmed as not an abuse of discretion. Judges Norris and Price concurred with reasons, and rehearing was denied.

This study examined the potential of green open access (OA) self-archiving to broaden access to clinical trial results publications from German university medical centers. Using the IntoValue cohort, 1,897 trial publications published between 2010 and 2020 were analyzed with Unpaywall to determine OA status and Shareyourpaper to identify self-archiving permissions.

Results showed 54% of publications were openly accessible, while 46% (871) were closed-access. Of the closed-access publications, 85% (736) had permission to self-archive either the accepted or published version in an institutional repository, typically with a 12-month embargo. Realized green OA was estimated at 16%, indicating a substantial gap between self-archiving opportunity and practice.

The authors attribute this gap partly to limited awareness, few institutional self-archiving mandates in Germany, and unresolved legal disputes regarding secondary publication rights. They conclude that compliance with WHO guidelines recommending open access for clinical trial results remains low, despite available self-archiving pathways. The automated approach combining Unpaywall and Shareyourpaper is proposed as a scalable tool for libraries and institutions to identify publications eligible for self-archiving and support interventions to improve research discoverability.

Natural gas closed at $3.27/MMBtu, remaining within a descending wedge pattern that has limited gains since March. While Europe's shift to LNG has increased U.S. exports, North American oversupply continues to pressure domestic prices. Seasonal softness and Canadian supply disruptions contribute to ongoing volatility.

U.S. markets fell sharply Tuesday, while Canada's main stock index was partially cushioned by gains in precious metals and materials. The S&P/TSX composite closed down 75.06 points at 15,477, while the Dow dropped 424.56 points to 24,024.13. According to Luc de la Durantaye of CIBC Asset Management, the U.S. selloff was driven by the 10-year Treasury yield reaching three per cent and concerns about companies like Alphabet, whose shares fell nearly five per cent. Barrick Gold shares rose over three per cent on strong quarterly earnings and its decision to stop selling assets to reduce debt. The Canadian dollar traded at 77.95 cents US, gold rose US$9 to US$1,333 an ounce, and copper gained three cents to US$3.14 per pound.

Ontario Premier Kathleen Wynne stated at Humber College that if young people and minorities don't vote, older white people will. The article criticizes this comment as ageist and racist, arguing it presumes different demographics have opposing interests. It suggests both old and young, white and minority voters may share concerns about employment, hydro rates, and manufacturing jobs after 14 years of Liberal government. Commentator Ali Taghva accuses Wynne of playing identity politics, while labour lawyer Sunira Chaudhri notes such a statement in a workplace would prompt Human Rights Tribunal complaints. The article contends that while voter participation varies by age and ethnicity, demonizing one group to boost another's turnout is irresponsible, and contrasts Wynne's comments with her rhetoric about inclusivity.

Global stock markets rose on Wednesday after Federal Reserve chair Janet Yellen told a Senate committee that the U.S. central bank could raise interest rates as soon as next month, citing a strengthening job market and modest inflation. European indices including Britain's FTSE 100, France's CAC 40, and Germany's DAX posted gains, while most Asian markets, such as Tokyo's Nikkei 225 and Hong Kong's Hang Seng, also finished higher. Analyst Jingyi Pan described Yellen's comments as surprisingly hawkish. Meanwhile, Chinese consumer and wholesale inflation rose, though UBS economists reported no meaningful monetary tightening. The dollar gained against the yen, and crude oil prices declined.

Gary Gensler, a Senior Lecturer at MIT Sloan and advisor at the MIT Media Lab, introduces course 15.S12 on blockchain and its intersection with finance and money. He surveys the class, noting about 45% have owned cryptocurrency and roughly a third have worked on blockchain projects.

Gensler traces the history of the internet (ethernet, TCP/IP, HTTP) and cryptography, noting that early digital currency attempts failed until Satoshi Nakamoto's 2008 peer-to-peer electronic cash system solved the problem of moving value online without a centralized intermediary. He defines blockchain as time-stamped append logs secured by cryptography, hash functions, digital signatures, and consensus protocols, noting blockchain predates Bitcoin (Stuart Haber, early 1990s).

The lecture covers money's roles (medium of exchange, store of value, unit of account) and finance's role in moving, allocating, and pricing money and risk. Gensler outlines financial sector challenges including crises, fiat instability, centralized intermediaries, legacy payment systems, and 1.7 billion unbanked people. He discusses blockchain's limitations: scalability (Bitcoin's 7 transactions/second versus Visa's 20,000-70,000), privacy, interoperability, and governance.

He distinguishes permissioned blockchains (favored by financial institutions like the Australian Stock Exchange) from permissionless ones like Bitcoin. Crypto finance is approximately $200 billion, modest compared to global capital markets. Public policy concerns include illicit activity, financial stability, and investor protection.

The course covers fundamentals, economics, and financial use cases, emphasizing critical reasoning over hype. Requirements include class participation (30%), two individual write-ups, and a team project. Gensler shares his background at Goldman Sachs, the US Treasury, and the CFTC, and fields questions before concluding.

Digital laggards tend to restrict data access, treating data as a source of power and storing it in departmental silos. They often favor a "culture of genius," where decisions rely on leadership expertise rather than data, which is used mainly to justify pre-made decisions. In contrast, 88% of digital leaders have standardized APIs enabling cross-departmental data flow, compared to 27% of laggards.

Digital leaders encourage extensive data collection to set and measure ambitious, realistic goals. Employees track progress via data-driven metrics and 360-degree reviews. Rather than creating rigidity, this measurement focus fosters flexibility, innovation, and risk-taking. A case study describes a retail company that, after acquisition, implemented real-time sales dashboards, enabling faster data-driven decisions.

Laggards set aspirational goals disconnected from data, leading employees to avoid measurement and default to qualitative, process-focused practices that stifle innovation.

Digital leaders use transparent, data-driven objectives as coordinating tools, aligning teams around a shared "North Star" through combined top-down and bottom-up processes. However, over-reliance on analysis can slow simple decisions. Laggards struggle to connect goals to strategy, causing misalignment.

Data culture aligns organizations vertically (individuals to company goals) and horizontally (cross-team collaboration). Digital leaders treat data culture as central, with consistent beliefs, values, and behaviors. Laggards show gaps between stated values and actions due to entrenched habits and skill gaps.

Transformation is possible. Organizations typically fall into four patterns: data novices, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant—each requiring targeted actions to build a strong data culture.

Keystone Strategy, which produced the research, is a consulting firm specializing in technology-led strategy and digital transformation for major clients.

Recent years have seen renewed interest in the therapeutic potential of psychedelics, including tryptamines, ketamine, and phenethylamines like MDMA, enabling a new paradigm of drug-facilitated psychotherapy. A pooled analysis of six Phase II trials found 54% of patients no longer met PTSD criteria after MDMA-assisted therapy (MDMA-AT), leading the FDA to designate it a breakthrough therapy. A subsequent Phase 3 multisite study confirmed MDMA-AT's safety and efficacy, showing significant reductions in PTSD symptom severity compared to placebo with therapy.

Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Ireland's economy is highly sensitive to exchange rate movements, particularly against the dollar and sterling. The weak euro-dollar rate has boosted American tourism, while a weak sterling has reduced UK visitors. Since the Brexit referendum, sterling has fallen from 76 to 91 pence against the euro, while the euro has strengthened against the dollar from $1.05 to $1.18, driven by expectations of ending quantitative easing and rising eurozone interest rates. This appreciation likely exceeds ECB preferences, as low rates support export-driven recovery. If the euro returned to its historical mean of $1.35, it could reach parity with sterling. Impacts vary by sector: tourism firms have limited hedging options; UK importers benefit and should lock in gains; the car industry suffers from cheap UK second-hand imports; and exporters to the UK require hedging strategies, ideally incurring costs in sterling.

Browns coach Kevin Stefanski declined to commit to rookie Shedeur Sanders as the team's backup quarterback following the trade of Joe Flacco to the Cincinnati Bengals. The trade, which sent Flacco and a 2026 sixth-round pick for a 2026 fifth-round pick, leaves Sanders and fellow rookie Dillon Gabriel as the only quarterbacks on Cleveland's active roster. Stefanski said he would let the week play out before deciding, citing concerns about young player development. Sanders, the 144th pick in the 2025 draft, had previously been inactive as the No. 3 quarterback but was listed as QB2 on the unofficial depth chart. Stefanski also would not confirm whether Bailey Zappe would be signed to the active roster. Gabriel made his first start in a 21-17 loss in London. Deshaun Watson remains on the PUP list rehabbing an Achilles injury.

A University of Michigan study of over 2,000 older Americans found that 21% of women and 10% of men aged 50 to 64 meet criteria for ultra-processed food addiction, compared to 12% of women and 4% of men aged 65 to 80. Researchers used the modified Yale Food Addiction Scale 2.0 to measure addiction based on substance use disorder criteria applied to foods like sweets, fast food, and sugary drinks.

The higher rates in middle-aged adults may stem from growing up during the proliferation of ultra-processed foods, including the 1980s marketing of "diet" products to women. Addiction was strongly associated with being overweight, poor mental or physical health, and social isolation. Women describing themselves as overweight were 11 times more likely, and men 19 times more likely, to meet addiction criteria than those reporting normal weight.

Senior author Ashley Gearhardt warned that children today consume even higher proportions of ultra-processed foods, potentially leading to greater addiction rates in future generations. The study was funded by the National Science Foundation and the National Institute on Drug Abuse.

The Bank of England will keep the £5 polymer note in circulation and issue the new £10 polymer note in September as planned, despite concerns over trace amounts of tallow used in production. Alternatives such as destroying or reprinting notes were deemed costly and would compromise anti-counterfeit measures. Following a petition signed by over 134,000 people, the Bank has delayed supply contracts for the 2020 £20 note to consider plant-based substitutes like coconut or palm oil. A public consultation will inform a final decision by summer 2017.

A massive rock formation called "Qarlinngua," meaning "like pants" in Inuktitut, stands in salt water on the Brodeur Peninsula of Baffin Island, roughly 80-90 kilometres from Arctic Bay, Nunavut. After CBC North shared a photo submitted by local hunter Max Kalluk, many online viewers believed it was fake, including tourism staff in Iqaluit who later confirmed its existence.

Geologists identified it as a sea arch formed through erosion. John England, a University of Alberta professor emeritus, said he had never seen anything like it in the Arctic. He explained that in areas where land is sinking relative to the sea, wind and water erode coastal cliffs to form arches. Linda Ham of the Canada-Nunavut Geoscience Office noted the horizontal layering indicates sedimentary sandstone, with the standing portion likely containing erosion-resistant quartz. The rocks are Paleozoic, aged 250-600 million years.

Kalluk, who first saw it as a child, estimates it stands over 50 metres tall and is accessible only by a four- to five-hour boat ride during a brief summer window. Arctic Bay Adventures is the only tour company visiting the site. Nunavut's tourism director Nancy Guyon said the government plans to promote the formation to tourists. England estimated the arch could collapse within decades, though other geologists suggested thousands of years.

This study examines career transitions of lecturers and education personnel (civil servants) in Indonesian higher education institutions using a grounded theory approach. Previous research has largely focused on organizational rather than individual perspectives, and has not adequately addressed career transition adaptation in higher education contexts.

Using Schlossberg's transition theory and Schein's anchor career theory as lenses, the research employed qualitative methods, including in-depth interviews with six key informants (lecturers and education staff) selected through snowball sampling across three types of state universities. Data were analyzed using NVIVO 12 Pro through open, axial, and selective coding.

Findings identified four new dimensions within Schlossberg's 4 S factors (situation, self, support, strategies) and revealed that these factors have reciprocal relationships during adaptation. Contrary to Schein's theory of a single career anchor, the study found lecturers and education staff use two anchors—competence and managerial—during transitions.

Career transitions produced changes in behavior, roles, learning, and perception. Dual roles forced informants to sacrifice one role, often prioritizing organizational responsibilities over individual performance, resulting in declining performance in primary positions.

Managerial implications suggest extending Schlossberg's theory to other campus groups and carefully managing bureaucratic simplification programs by prioritizing competence and education when assigning functional positions.

Limitations include the qualitative nature preventing generalization, narrow focus on intra-institutional transitions, exclusion of demographic characteristics, and potential researcher bias as the researcher belongs to the education personnel group studied.

Regarding a recent loss, he cited execution issues and lack of passion, including a missed overtime power play opportunity. He emphasized the team must play harder with a chance to win the Stanley Cup on home ice.

The case involves The Mayor of the City of New York v. Collis P. Huntington, with Charles W. Tweed representing the defendant and E. S. Lacombe as counsel for the plaintiff. This bibliometric analysis examines mathematics anxiety research in mathematics education from 2013 to 2023 using data from the Scopus database, analyzed through VOSviewer and Biblioshiny software. After filtering, 324 journal articles were analyzed to address three research questions regarding prevailing topics, influential journals and authors, and international collaborations.

Key findings include:
- Publications on mathematics anxiety have generally increased yearly, peaking in 2022 with 56 documents. The topic is studied across multiple fields, predominantly social sciences (35.1%) and psychology (30.7%).
- Network visualization revealed seven clusters connecting mathematics anxiety to variables including gender, self-efficacy, motivation, skills, and technology.
- Frontiers in Psychology published the most research on this theme (55,251 citations, Q2 quartile).
- Garcia-Santillan (Mexico) was the most productive author with 10 publications, while Pekrun Reinhard had the highest citation count (985).
- The United States led in publications (62 documents) and international collaboration, while Germany received the most citations. The University of Barcelona was the most relevant affiliate with 23 publications.

Limitations include reliance solely on the Scopus database and restriction to article-type documents. The study suggests researchers can use these findings to identify key studies, authors, and journals relevant to mathematics anxiety research.

North Korea warned the United States it is prepared to respond to nuclear attacks and all-out war, as stated by Choe Ryong-hae, the country's second most powerful official. The company paid $197 million in dividends during the first half and had $7.24 billion remaining under share repurchase authorization through December 2022.

The filing also disclosed ongoing securities class action and derivative litigation, and noted potential COVID-19 impacts on supply chain and demand.

This patent application describes a detection model training method, apparatus, and terminal device, primarily applied to detecting target objects such as lesions (e.g., colorectal polyps) in medical images.

The method involves determining an initial training model comprising an initial detection model and an adaptive model. The initial detection model includes a feature extraction module and a detection and classification module, while the adaptive model includes a domain classification module and optionally a gradient inversion module.

Training samples include two types of data: source domain data with a plurality of first images labeled with identifiers indicating whether a target object is present and the domain they belong to, and target domain data with second images labeled only with a domain identifier (no target object labels).

During training, the initial detection model determines whether target objects are present in first images, producing a detection result. The adaptive model determines which domain each image belongs to, producing a domain classification result. A loss function value is calculated based on these results and the identifiers, combining a detection loss function and an adaptive loss function. Parameter values in the model are adjusted according to the loss function until stop conditions are met (convergence or maximum iterations).

The gradient inversion module creates an adversarial relationship between the feature extraction module and the domain classification module, enabling extraction of domain-invariant features. This allows detection capabilities learned from labeled source domain data to be applied to unlabeled target domain data.

The approach addresses the problem of domain migration when medical detection systems are deployed across different hospitals with different equipment, reducing the need for expensive expert labeling of training data while maintaining detection accuracy. After training, to-be-examined images can be processed by the final detection model to identify target objects and their types and locations.

Teams should prepare for three jump ball situations: defensive, even, and offensive. In defensive jump balls, where the opponent has a height or jumping advantage, players should rotate early, watch the jumper's eyes and hands for tip direction (right-handers typically tip left, left-handers tip right), and maintain contact with the jumper. Defensive alignments include Box, Diamond, and "Y" formations, the latter placing two defenders back against superior jumpers to prevent easy shots.

For even jump balls, players box out, anticipate, and rotate clockwise or counter-clockwise based on predetermined signals to crash open spots.

Offensive jump ball plays are used when a team has a 6" or greater height advantage, generally tipping to the tallest player while maintaining defensive balance. Specific plays include Possession, Double Tap, Post Split (from Diamond or Box alignments), Jumper Fly, Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem, and Loop, each involving coordinated tips, screens, cuts, and receiver movements. If a good shot isn't available after possession, teams should transition into a set or motion offense.

Apple has removed multiple ICE-tracking apps from its App Store, including ICEBlock, Eyes Up, and DEICER, following claims from US Attorney General Pam Bondi that such tools endanger ICE officers. Apple justified at least one removal by citing a developer guideline prohibiting "mean-spirited content" toward targeted groups, with Google similarly classifying ICE officers as a vulnerable group. Developers including Joshua Aaron and "Mark" say they will appeal and continue fighting the bans, noting their apps remain available on Google Play and their websites.

Legal experts told WIRED the apps constitute protected First Amendment speech, publishing truthful information about public events. Similar law enforcement-reporting features exist in apps like Waze, Apple Maps, and Google Maps. Critics, including Stanford policy researcher Riana Pfefferkorn, characterized Apple's actions as CEO Tim Cook "kowtowing" to the Trump administration, noting Cook donated $1 million to Trump's inauguration. The Trump administration previously threatened to prosecute Aaron.

Digital rights researchers argue the removals highlight risks of centrally controlled platforms, particularly Apple's closed ecosystem, which—unlike Android—does not permit sideloading. Security researcher Will Strafach noted the situation demonstrates the problem of Apple serving as a "single point of failure."

NASA's Terra satellite captured an image of the remnants of Tropical Depression 02W over the South China Sea on April 17, 2017. The depression made landfall on the eastern Visayas on April 15 with maximum sustained winds near 25 knots, prompting the Joint Typhoon Warning Center to issue its final bulletin. It weakened to a remnant low as it crossed the Eastern Visayas, Bikol, and Mimiropa regions before entering the South China Sea. On April 17, the remnant was located about 230 nautical miles west of Manila, moving west with a compact closed circulation. JTWC indicated that wind shear and drier air would prevent re-intensification.

Rocky View County faces a $1 million transportation shortfall following the passage of Bill 1, which eliminated school bus fees for students living 2.4 kilometres or more from their designated school. Alberta's Education Minister David Eggen indicated the province may allow parents to pay bus fees despite the legislation. Rocky View Schools, which serves nearly 24,000 students, surveyed parents on potential solutions, including changing bell times, extending rural commutes, and relocating urban bus stops. Board chair Todd Brand said many parents preferred paying the previous transportation fee. The shortfall was attributed to insufficient provincial grants, a $360,000 carbon levy, and Bill 1. Administration will contact the Ministry of Education, and the April 12 decision deadline may be extended.

The Supreme Court is considering whether the double jeopardy clause prohibits separate firearm convictions and sentences under 18 U.S.C. §§ 924(c) and 924(j) for the same conduct. Section 924(c) covers firearm use in violent or drug-trafficking crimes, while 924(j) applies when such use causes death.

The parties agree that double jeopardy generally bars simultaneous convictions for a crime and its lesser-included offense, unless Congress clearly indicates otherwise. They agree Congress provided such indication for 924(c) and its underlying offense, but dispute whether similar clarity exists for 924(c) and 924(j).

Justice Kavanaugh highlighted Section 924(c)(1)(D)(ii), requiring consecutive sentences "notwithstanding any other provision of law." Justice Jackson questioned whether this provision presupposes a separately established offense. Barrett's attorney Matthew Larsen and the federal government argued this language is insufficient.

Aimee Brown, for the government, pointed to 924(c)'s "in addition to" language, which refers only to underlying violent or drug crimes, not 924(j). Charles McCloud, defending the lower court ruling, argued congressional intent can be shown through statutory structure and purpose, not magic words.

Justice Gorsuch raised unbriefed questions about the justification for requiring clear congressional indication.

Schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD) affects approximately 1% of the global population and lacks objective biomarkers for diagnosis. While resting-state functional connectivity (rs-FC) MRI classifiers are emerging, they face challenges including accuracy, generalisability, across-session variability, and specificity.

This research pursued two aims: (I) developing a clinically applicable SSD classifier using a harmonized multi-site dataset, a customized LASSO sparse learning algorithm, a voting method, and spatial averaging of 100 classifiers; and (II) exploring whether the diagnostic biomarker could function as trait, state, and staging markers.

Two independent datasets were used: a discovery dataset (1,015 participants) and a validation dataset (683 participants). Mass univariate analysis showed significant correlation of FC diagnostic effects between datasets (r=0.597). LASSO classifiers achieved 79.6% accuracy (AUC=0.876) in the discovery dataset and 77.3% accuracy (AUC=0.824) in the validation dataset, with site-level variation. Performance was lower at the JHU site, where early-stage SSD patients fell between chronic SSD and HC distributions.

Forty-seven important FCs were identified, with 44 maintaining consistent HC-SSD relationships across datasets. Voting classifiers showed significantly higher sensitivity than LASSO classifiers. Classifier performance varied with disease severity, being highest in the marked PANSS subgroup. Seven ROIs appeared significantly frequently among important FCs, showing laterality imbalance between hemispheres except in the cerebellum.

Amazon's mobile accessory kit allows third-party wearables to integrate Alexa, with the Jabra Elite 65t ($170) among the first earbuds to use it. Testing revealed significant limitations compared to Alexa on smart speakers. The earbuds currently work with Alexa only on Android, with iOS support forthcoming.

Music streaming is restricted to Amazon Music, excluding Spotify and other services, and voice commands cannot pause or skip tracks. Alexa cannot place calls, send text messages, or use Drop In, though it can answer calls. Reminders are not supported, and timers and alarms lack auditory notifications. Navigation is unavailable, requiring users to rely on their phones. Voice shopping, however, works well, leveraging Amazon's order history.

The Elite 65t offers strong sound quality, comfortable fit, and a HearThrough ambient sound feature. Downsides include 15 hours total battery life (versus 24 for Pixel Buds and AirPods) and no tracker for lost earbuds.

By comparison, Google Assistant and Siri offer more robust notifications, messaging, and navigation, while Pixel Buds support translation across 40 languages. Amazon plans future feature updates, but currently the Alexa-in-earbuds experience lags behind that of smart speakers.

Shohei Ohtani is making his first postseason pitching appearance in Game 1 of the 2025 NLDS between the Dodgers and Phillies at Citizens Bank Park on October 4, with first pitch at 6:38 p.m. ET. Ohtani pitched in 14 games during the 2025 season, going 1-1 with a 2.87 ERA and 62 strikeouts in 47 innings. Manager Dave Roberts hopes Ohtani can pitch into the seventh inning. He faces Phillies ace Christopher Sanchez, who went 13-5 with a 2.50 ERA. In the first inning, Ohtani struck out Trea Turner and retired Schwarber and Harper. The game airs on TBS and truTV, and streams on HBO Max.

Following the Las Vegas mass shooting at the Route 91 Harvest festival, which killed 58 and injured over 500, country musician Charlie Daniels shared his perspective in a phone interview. Daniels called the incident an anomaly and the shooter a "nut," stating that fear would mean "the bad guys have won." The shooting sparked debate about gun control and country music's role, given the NRA's ties to the industry through N.R.A. Country. While Rosanne Cash urged country musicians to oppose the NRA in a New York Times essay, Daniels said he supports regulating "bump stock" devices but opposes stricter gun laws. He criticized politicians for lacking knowledge about firearms and cited Chicago's strict laws and high violence as evidence such measures would leave people defenseless. Daniels will headline a show at Cary's Booth Amphitheatre on Oct. 21.

Digital leaders view sensible risk-taking and experimentation as essential strategies in rapidly changing competitive environments. They consider themselves learning organizations that value data and continuous feedback, believing experiments yield knowledge even when goals aren't met. While avoiding overly costly risks, they emphasize thoughtful planning. They also prioritize long-term individual development, investing in training for critical thinking skills like problem solving, statistics, and design thinking, despite delayed payoffs.

Willis Eschenbach analyzed solar radiation data from the Mauna Loa Observatory (MLO), which has recorded direct solar radiation minute by minute since 1980. He found that, apart from periods following the El Chichon and Pinatubo volcanic eruptions, atmospheric clarity at MLO has remained unchanged since 1980.

Examining the two-year periods after each eruption, Eschenbach observed nearly identical reductions in maximum and average solar radiation, despite differences in the volcanoes' size and location. Average downwelling solar radiation dropped by about 24.5 W/m2 during volcanic periods. However, he noted that clouds appeared to rearrange to offset some of this loss, increasing solar radiation by roughly 7 W/m2 compared to what would have occurred had cloud patterns remained unchanged.

Despite the 25 W/m2 reduction over two years, temperature records at MLO and four other Hawaiian stations (Hilo, Molokai, Barber's Point, and Lihue) showed no corresponding cooling. Eschenbach suggests this supports his theory that the climate system responds to forcing changes in ways that restore prior conditions, consistent with the Constructal Law and Le Chatelier's Principle. He acknowledges he does not definitively know why temperatures were unaffected and invites alternative explanations.

The speaker expresses enthusiasm about Winnipeg receiving an NHL team, praising the passionate fans and the organization under Mr. Chipman. He recalls playing at the old Winnipeg Arena during its final games, including a whiteout against San Antonio, and later at the MTS Centre. He prefers smaller, full arenas over larger, emptier ones like Atlanta's. Regarding the Sedin twins, he distinguishes them by facial features and speech, noting Henrik is more vocal as captain. On facing goalie Thomas, he emphasizes doing homework, getting shots through, and choosing spots carefully, acknowledging Thomas's skill despite his unconventional style.

Energy sector trading involves gaining exposure to multiple energy stocks for diversification and profit, either through ETFs like XLE or VDE, or by building a stock portfolio. The S&P 500 energy sector includes companies in oil and natural gas exploration, refining, distribution, and related services. As of July 2022, the sector returned 52.81% over one year, compared to the S&P 500's -9.28%, offering diversification benefits.

The article presents two XLE trading strategies. Specific strategy details are not disclosed.

The energy sector is considered difficult to trade because oil prices depend on unpredictable macro factors, but it offers diversification value.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's financial sector declined in March and April, with Canada's big five banks dropping between 4.6% and 7.5% from February highs. Several small-cap lenders saw larger declines, including Home Capital Group (-28%), First National Financial, and Equitable Group (both -15%).

Comparing the big five banks to five small-cap lenders using five criteria—beta, earnings yield, dividend yield, payout ratio, and dividend history—the author ranked each stock. MCAN Mortgage Corporation ranked first overall, followed by Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and Atrium Mortgage Investment Corp. Equitable Group ranked last due to high volatility and low dividend yield.

Advantages of small-cap lenders include higher dividend yields and smaller price swings. Disadvantages include lower liquidity and less diversified business models. The author discloses long positions in AMIVF, CM, TD, and BNS.

The Hawk Offense combines a wing isolation, high post shuffle cut, and weakside post up, resembling the UCLA Offense. Defending it requires fundamentals against dribble penetration, shuffle cuts, and low post play.

The Basic NBA Show & Recover approach avoids switching on the high post rub. In Phase 1, weakside defenders sag to help against wing isolation, recovering when the ball stops. In Phase 2, the cutter is forced behind the high post screen, with a weakside defender showing before recovering. In Phase 3, defenders show and recover on down screens, finishing with pass denial and helpside positioning.

The All Out "SOS" Disruption traps the ballhandler on the sideline wing. Phase 1 uses a trap by the on-ball and high post defenders, with rotations following the near player concept on pass-outs. Phases 2 and 3 employ contact switches on shuffle cuts and down screens. Once matched up, standard SOS principles apply, with "Base Go Red" or "Post Trap" rotations triggered by baseline drives or post passes.

AMD has released two new high-end graphics cards, the Radeon RX Vega 64 and Vega 56, to compete with Nvidia's GTX 1080 and GTX 1070 respectively. AMD has stated the Vega 64 is not intended to beat the GTX 1080 Ti. Madison Snap and William Francis were convicted and fined fifty dollars each for unlawfully and wantonly shooting and wounding a mare that was trespassing in an oat field belonging to one of them, protected by an insufficient fence. Snap shot the mare under Francis's direction, wounding her flank. Their motions to quash and for a new trial were overruled. On appeal, Chief Justice Catón held that shooting or wounding trespassing stock violates both the statute and common law. A landowner may expel trespassing animals using necessary force or impound them damage feasant, but may not inflict unnecessary injury. While the animal's owner may be liable for damages, the injured party cannot retaliate. The judgment was affirmed.

Brits have less than a month to spend old paper £10 notes, which cease to be legal tender on 1 March. After this date, outdated notes can be exchanged for new polymer versions at banks, building societies, post offices or the Bank of England, potentially requiring ID.

The new £10 polymer note, featuring Jane Austen, entered circulation on 14 September 2017. It is expected to last around five years, has enhanced security features to deter counterfeiting, and includes a tactile feature to assist blind and partially-sighted users. The design was unveiled on 18 July 2017, the 200th anniversary of Austen's death.

A 12-sided £1 coin launched in March 2017, and a plastic £20 note is planned for 2020. There are no current plans to update the £50 note.

The safety is a defensive back positioned deepest on the field, serving as the last line of defense against big plays. There are traditionally two types: the free safety, who roams the middle of the field without a specific assignment and relies on speed, and the strong safety, who is stockier, plays closer to the line of scrimmage, and focuses more on run defense and tackling. Safeties may also be called "Rover" or "Star," while older terms like defensive fullback and halfback persist in Canadian football.

Safeties must cover receivers and tight ends, tackle effectively, and communicate well, having the best view of the field. As football has become more pass-oriented, their coverage skills have improved.

The Pro Football Hall of Fame includes 17 safeties, such as Troy Polamalu, Ed Reed, Ken Houston (record 12 Pro Bowls), Ronnie Lott, and Sean Taylor, whose career was cut short by his death.

A great safety boosts defensive confidence, creates turnovers, limits the quarterback's options, and supports cornerbacks. Mistakes are costly, making leadership, communication, and versatility highly valued.

Researchers published in Nature Geoscience found that Australia's Great Barrier Reef (GBR) has recovered from near-extinction five times over the past 30,000 years, shifting seaward or landward in response to changing sea levels at a rate of 20 cm to 1.5 metres per year. Co-author Jody Webster of the University of Sydney warned, however, that current rates of sea surface temperature rise and ocean acidification likely exceed anything the reef has previously endured. Studying fossil data from 16 drilled ocean-floor sites, the team identified die-offs caused by exposure to air, sea level rise, and sediment dumping. Webster noted the reef may die again naturally in coming millennia, but whether human-induced climate change will accelerate this is unclear. A separate April study reported nearly a third of the reef's coral died during a 2016 heatwave.

Following the 2024 Arab Summit in Bahrain, an initiative was launched to ensure free education for Arab children, prompted by a UNESCO report that over 10 million Arab children aged 5-15 are out of school. Authors Jaber Mustafa and Younis Bukhari developed the "Hope" initiative to address this crisis, using the Syrian conflict as a case study.

Over two million Syrian children lack education, and nearly 400,000 Syrian refugee children in Turkey are out of school. Quality suffers from untrained teachers, resource shortages, and fragmented curricula, while trauma impairs cognitive and emotional development.

The methodology used triangulation design combining interviews and surveys. A case study of Ahmed, a Syrian child, revealed inadequate learning spaces, limited materials, and lack of infrastructure. Interviews with a parent confirmed destroyed schools, scarce resources, untreated PTSD, and dedicated unpaid teachers.

Proposed solutions include immediate remedial measures (emotional and academic support) and proactive sustainable solutions through the "Hope Initiative," an organization providing structured short and long-term educational responses to conflict zones.

Residents of San Andrés Hueyapan in Morelos, located 18 kilometers from the Popocatépetl volcano, are experiencing heightened stress due to the combination of volcanic activity and the September 19 earthquake. Sean "Diddy" Combs, 55, was sentenced to four years and two months in prison and fined $500,000 by US District Judge Arun Subramanian for two counts of transporting sex workers across state lines for drug-fueled sexual events he called "freak offs." The sentence was less than the 11 years prosecutors sought but more than the 14 months his defense requested. A jury had convicted him on Mann Act charges while acquitting him of sex trafficking and racketeering conspiracy, which could have carried a life sentence.

Backtests show that both DAX 40 and Euro Stoxx 50 perform better during futures expiration week than during a random week. DAX 40 futures expire on the third Friday of March, June, September, and December, with an average expiration-week gain of 0.39% and a 57% win ratio, versus 0.12% for a random week. December is the strongest month, possibly due to the Santa Claus Rally.

The week after DAX 40 futures expiration performs poorly, averaging a 0.1% loss with a 47% win ratio. September is the worst month, profitable only 25% of the time. Defendant Samuel Israel III appealed his conviction from the Southern District of New York, raising two main arguments. First, he contended that Judge McMahon should have recused herself. The Second Circuit found no basis to question her impartiality, noting her explanations regarding duty station changes, a docketing error, and her recusal from a related bankruptcy case did not indicate bias. The UC1825BEVM-CVAL uses an RCD clamp (resistor, capacitor, and diode) to limit switch node voltage overshoot. Starting component values can be calculated after determining allowable overshoot. The clamp voltage is found via Equation 30: Vclamp = Kclamp × Nps × (Vout + VDiode), with Kclamp recommended at 1.5 to permit about 50% overshoot. Initial resistor and capacitor values can then be derived using the transformer's parasitic inductance and permissible clamp voltage variation per switching cycle.

This patent describes methods for producing elastomeric compositions containing dispersed carbon black (CB) particles within a silicone matrix. The method involves: (a) treating hydrophilic CB particles with a dispersant that is miscible in a curable hydrophobic silicone pre-polymer and has CB-affinic moieties (amino, acrylate, or epoxy) with affinity to the hydrophilic CB surface; (b) mixing the treated particles with the pre-polymer; and (c) addition-curing or condensation-curing to form the elastomer.

The treated CB particles may be size-reduced to achieve a Dv90 of 0.10 to 5 μm. The hydrophilic CB particles are characterized by specific properties including pH (≤5.0), volatile matter content (≥1.5%), oxygen content (≥1.0 wt%), acid value (≥0.05 mmol/g), negative surface zeta potential, and I_D/I_G Raman ratio ≥0.8.

Suitable dispersants are siloxane-containing or siloxane-based branched molecules, including amino-silicones (with amine numbers typically 3-75), silicone-acrylates, and silicone-epoxy types. The dispersant at least partially envelops the CB particles, rendering hydrophilic particles compatible with the hydrophobic silicone matrix through non-covalent interactions.

The cured compositions may contain platinum or tin catalysts, retardants, cross-linkers, and 3D network formers like hydrophobic fumed silica. CB concentration typically ranges from 0.01% to 30% by weight. Applications include intermediate transfer members for printing systems and UV-absorbing sealants.

The ADS8860 ADC application uses three filters in the PGA848 front end: an EMI/RFI input filter, a feedback filter (CFB = 75pF yielding a 318kHz cutoff), and a charge reservoir RC filter at the ADC inputs for sample-and-hold settling and THD performance. The nominal f–3dB bandwidth is 318kHz, with –0.1dB flatness to 41kHz. The PGA848 REF pin is set to 2.5V via a REF6250 5V reference through a precision voltage divider buffered by an OPA192 op amp in a dual-feedback configuration, providing 86° phase margin.

Power supplies are specified at ±15V, with output stages clamped within input-stage supply levels. Voltages above ±20V cause permanent damage.

Layout recommendations include symmetrical input paths, low-ESR 0.1µF bypass capacitors near supply pins, separation of input from supply/output traces, minimizing leakage and parasitic capacitance on DA_IN± pins, reducing thermal junctions, and keeping distance from heat sources.

Supporting tools include PSpice for TI and the free TINA-TI simulation software. Related documentation covers instrumentation amplifiers, the ADS8860 ADC, REF62xx voltage reference, and OPAx192 op amp.

In Brooks v. Missouri Pacific Railroad Co., the petitioner was hired as an apprentice machinist in 1951, drafted into military service, and later resumed his apprenticeship at different locations, ultimately completing it in North Little Rock, Arkansas in 1958. He sought a seniority date of November 3, 1955, at North Little Rock, arguing he would have completed his apprenticeship then but for his military service. The railroad offered this date only for the Monroe location. The District Court ruled in petitioner's favor, finding promotion was automatic and he would have been employed at North Little Rock. The Court of Appeals reversed, citing uncertainty in workforce supply and demand. The Supreme Court reversed the Court of Appeals, relying on its decision in Tilton v. Missouri Pac. R. Co., holding that such possibilities do not defeat a veteran's seniority rights, and remanded the case.

U.S. equities rose Monday, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq leading gains driven by technology and semiconductor shares, while the Dow also edged higher. Russian journalist Arkady Babchenko, 41, appeared alive at a news conference less than 24 hours after Ukrainian police reported he had been shot dead at his Kiev apartment. Babchenko, a Kremlin critic who fled Russia in 2017 after death threats, apologised to his wife and mourning friends, saying law enforcement had known of the contract on his life for two months and approached him a month ago. Ukrainian prosecutor general Yuri Lutsenko criticised politicians who had accused the government of permitting contract killings.

Americans spent over $100 billion on summer vacations last year, and while travel offers health benefits, it can be costly. Experienced travelers recommend several money-saving tips: create a budget using tools like Excel, TripAdvisor, Priceline, Orbitz, or Gasbuddy, starting with your bank account to avoid overspending. Use online travel sites such as Travelocity, Expedia, Travelzoo, and Skyscanner to find bargains. Use credit cards without foreign transaction fees and carry a backup card. Monitor cell phone roaming charges abroad. Travel during the offseason, book early, and consider trip insurance. Sign up for airline newsletters to catch brief deals, and search for local discounts through information centers, hotels, and city passes.

Miami-Dade Mayor Carlos Gimenez announced study results showing PortMiami is the top revenue-generating operation in the county and state, with an economic impact exceeding $41 billion, an increase of $12.8 billion. The port contributed $288 million in state and local taxes in 2016 and has added 116,000 jobs since 2012, totaling 300,000 jobs. A $247 million Royal Caribbean terminal project is expected to generate $500 million in annual economic impact.

The ARM Cortex-A8 Microprocessor Unit (MPU) Subsystem provides master control over the device, managing configuration of subsystems, peripherals, and external memories. It features ARMv7 ISA with Thumb2, JazelleX, and Media Extensions, along with an ARM Cortex-A8 Interrupt Controller (AINTC).

The ARM Cortex-A8 processor, a general-purpose microprocessor with Harvard architecture, targets multi-tasking applications requiring memory management, high performance, small die size, and low power. It supports ARM debug architecture and includes:
- NEON 64/128-bit Hybrid SIMD Engine
- Enhanced VFPv3 Floating-Point Coprocessor
- Separate Level-1 Instruction and Data Caches
- 128-bit Interconnector to memories and peripherals

For real-time trace, it offers an embedded trace module (ETM) interface with a trace port and triggering facilities. The trace port connects only to a system-level Embedded Trace Buffer (ETB) with 32KB memory, requiring ETB-enabled debug tools to interpret trace data.

The National Weather Service San Diego issued a zone forecast on July 4, 2018 for Extreme Southwestern California. An Excessive Heat Watch is in effect from Friday morning through Saturday evening across all zones, and a High Surf Advisory is in effect from Wednesday evening to Friday evening for Orange County and San Diego County coastal areas.

Temperatures peak Friday, with highs reaching 85–90°F at beaches, 99–112°F in inland valleys and the Inland Empire, 97–116°F in mountain and desert areas, and up to 117°F in the Coachella Valley and San Diego County Deserts. Following a joint resolution by Congress requesting a day of public humiliation and prayer, the third Thursday in August is recommended as a day for religious observance. It asks for protection of the American people, blessings on their military, inspiration of justice among nations, and a swift restoration of peace. Issued by James Madison on July 9, 1812.

The University of Virginia School of Medicine's Blue Ridge Poison Control Center is preparing for increased calls as warmer weather approaches. The center warns of poisonous plants, mushrooms, black widow spiders, and snakes. Director Dr. Chris Holstege advises against self-treatment methods like tying off limbs or sucking out venom, noting they often cause more harm. The center recommends protective clothing, checking boots, and staying aware of surroundings.

ESPN, once dominant as the centerpiece of the cable television bundle with over 100 million subscribers paying monthly fees, faced significant challenges by 2024 due to streaming disruption. Cable subscribers declined to approximately 70 million, while live sports rights costs continued rising and competition intensified from streaming platforms like Netflix, YouTube, and Amazon.

Founded in 1978 by Bill Rasmussen and his son Scott, ESPN went through multiple ownership changes before Disney acquired 80% through its 1996 merger with Capital Cities/ABC. Hearst Corporation has retained 20% since 1990. ESPN's growth was driven by affiliate fees (introduced in 1983), NFL rights deals, the emergence of direct broadcast satellite competition, and the creation of additional channels like ESPN2 and ESPNEWS.

To adapt to streaming, Disney acquired BAMTech in 2017 and launched ESPN+ in 2018, reaching 25 million subscribers at $6.30 average revenue per user. In 2023, CEO Robert Iger confirmed the flagship ESPN network would go direct-to-consumer in 2025. In February 2024, Disney, Warner Bros. Discovery, and Fox announced Venu Sports, a joint sports streaming venture launching fall 2024.

The competitive landscape included incumbent media companies, technology companies (Amazon, YouTube, Apple, Netflix), sports properties with rising rights fees, cable/satellite operators shifting focus to broadband, and fans facing increased choice, fragmentation, and costs. ESPN's Q2 FY24 showed $3.866 billion in domestic revenue (up 4%) but operating income declined 9% to $780 million. ESPN faces the challenge of transitioning from a B2B to B2C model while managing rising rights obligations exceeding $10 billion annually against uncertain subscription revenue.

IEX, a stock exchange that promised to disrupt common stock trading, has underperformed with less than 3% market share. The author argues IEX suffers from a split identity: "IEX One" exploits the SEC's National Market System (NMS) through its speed bump, which subsidizes buy-side traders at the expense of sell-side traders, functioning as an implicit fee. "IEX Two" aspires to be a broader market disruptor serving all traders equally. The author contends the speed bump depends on NMS barriers rather than challenging them, and that the NMS protects exchanges from competition based on service quality. To achieve market dominance, IEX must bypass the NMS, balance buy-side and sell-side interests, and deliver liquidity, with support from brokers and traders.

The U.S. economy added 200,000 jobs in January while unemployment remained at 4.1 percent, according to federal economists. Average hourly wages rose 2.9 percent year-over-year, suggesting wage gains may be accelerating as the labor market tightens. Economist Kate Bahn attributed the pay increase partly to minimum wage hikes in 18 states, affecting 4.5 million workers. Job growth under President Trump (2.1 million in 2017) has been similar to growth under President Obama (2.2 million in 2016). African-American unemployment rose to 7.7 percent in January from 6.8 percent in December, though it has declined steadily since 2010. Economist Michelle Holder noted the declining unemployment trend preceded Trump's presidency. Analysts caution against drawing conclusions from single reports, citing a margin of error of about 100,000. December's estimate was revised up to 160,000 jobs, while November's was revised down to 216,000.

IT buyers comparing data warehouse systems often evaluate Oracle's Exadata against Hewlett Packard Enterprise's Vertica, according to IT Central Station. Exadata users praise its "smart scan" feature, while Vertica users appreciate its columnar storage for faster access to "hot data." However, users note areas for improvement: Exadata's patching process and Vertica's documentation. Coronation Street recently portrayed a storyline involving the suicide of character Aidan, played by Shayne Ward, prompting renewed discussion of the topic. Competitive Capabilities International (CCi) and R&G Global Consultants have partnered to develop Stable Operations TRACC, a data-driven solution aimed at scaling predictable and stable manufacturing operations. According to CCi CEO Glenn Leask, the product can increase capacity by 15 to 20 percent within six months of implementation. Cargill was the first client to deploy it and helped facilitate the partnership. The solution addresses challenges such as capacity utilization, supply chain service delivery, and CAPEX avoidance, and includes blended learning modules for training. R&G Managing Partner Aart Willem de Wolf stated the partnership strengthens implementation support for their global clients.

This study examines problems and challenges facing women's education in rural areas of Pakistan and Azad Jammu Kashmir, where female literacy stands at only 40.8%, compared to a national female literacy rate of 51.9% and male literacy of 73.3%.

Using a quantitative approach, researchers surveyed both illiterate and literate women through two separate questionnaires. Thematic analysis identified several key barriers: management problems (workload, time, resources), patriarchal culture and family/society barriers, motivational issues stemming from illiterate family environments, financial constraints due to poverty and inflation, insufficient schools and infrastructure, inadequate teacher training, early child marriages, curriculum issues (lengthy syllabus, English language challenges), and restrictive religious interpretations. Literate women additionally reported technical issues and family pressure regarding subject selection.

The study concludes that despite government efforts, significant challenges remain. Recommendations include conducting monthly seminars on women's education involving parents and females, leveraging media platforms to promote awareness, enacting legislation for compulsory women's education, and utilizing open and distance education to improve female literacy.

The Pakistan Super League (PSL) will allow franchises to draft replacement players if contracted international stars decline to play the March 5 final in Lahore due to security concerns. Around 30 foreign players, including Chris Gayle, Shane Watson, and Eoin Morgan, are contracted to the five teams, with most matches held in the UAE. Qamar Javed Bajwa has offered full support. Pakistan has not hosted major test-playing nations since the 2009 attack on the Sri Lankan team in Lahore.

After a 20-year marriage ended, the author, who had been a stay-at-home mom, realized she knew little about the family's finances or accounts. Interior Secretary Ryan Zinke is visiting Maine to review the Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument, an 87,000-acre privately donated wilderness in northern Penobscot County, accompanied by a $40 million private endowment for maintenance. Content-based image retrieval is considered a promising approach to address the botanical taxonomic gap, with growing interest from the multimedia community. The ImageCLEF/LifeCLEF plant identification task, organized since 2011, aims to evaluate and improve identification tools under realistic conditions. The 2014 edition introduced multi-image queries, user ratings metadata, a new "Branch" view type, and expanded coverage to 500 species.

The PlantCLEF 2014 dataset contained 60,962 pictures from 19,504 observations collected by 1,608 contributors, covering trees, herbs, and ferns from a European region centered on France. Each image belongs to one of seven view types (entire plant, fruit, leaf, flower, stem, branch, leaf scan) and includes metadata such as observation ID, species, location, date, and user quality ratings.

The task evaluated plant species retrieval based on multi-image observation queries using a score inverse to the rank of the correct species, averaged per author to avoid bias. A secondary metric evaluated image-level predictions.

Of 74 registered groups, 10 submitted runs. Participants used various approaches including Fisher Vectors, Bag-of-Visual-Words, Convolutional Neural Networks, matching methods, and shape descriptors. The IBM AU team achieved the best results using Fisher Vector encoding combined with CNN and segmentation. Pure CNN approaches underperformed due to insufficient training data and the prohibition on external training resources. Combining multiple images per observation consistently improved results. LeafScan and Flower categories yielded the best identification scores.

The task demonstrated progress in scaling plant recognition to real-world applications, with a possible 2015 extension to around 5,000 species covering the entire French flora.

Offensive switches in soccer are tactical position exchanges between two attacking teammates intended to beat defenders. They can be "called" (using oral communication) or "natural" (performed during normal play), and may occur with or without the ball.

In a basic or lateral/horizontal switch, two teammates run diagonally in opposite directions forming an "X," exchanging roles and responsibilities until returning to original positions. A vertical switch involves players exchanging positions back-to-front or front-to-back, and differs from an overlapping run because positions are actually swapped.

The objective of any switch is to free a runner for a pass by forcing defenders to choose whom to cover or by causing confusion about marking assignments. Lateral switches are particularly effective against offside traps. Once the switch is complete, players should verbally signal "Switch back" when returning to original positions.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC reporting that, effective September 25, 2022, Joseph Gebbia was appointed to Tesla's Board of Directors. This paper introduces MatterMech, a benchmark comprising 4,800 questions across 8 nanomaterial synthesis subdomains (metal, biological, compositional, carbon, ceramic, semiconductor, polymer, and photocatalytic/energy) designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to hypothesize physicochemical principles in materials synthesis.

The benchmark was developed through four phases: (1) collecting ~17,000 domain-specific academic papers via Semantic Scholar API; (2) generating multiple-choice questions (MCQs) using Claude-3.5-Sonnet, validated through a multi-agent system (Worker, Reviewer, Critic) to reduce hallucinations; (3) transforming MCQs into text-infilling (TIF) questions; and (4) human quality assurance using a 5-point Likert scale. The authors also released MatterDB, a dataset of 31,735 papers paired with extracted synthesis mechanisms.

Evaluation of 14 LLMs (including Qwen, Llama, and reasoning-focused models) revealed that Qwen-Max led MCQ performance (61.99% accuracy), while Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct led TIF performance (35.25% similarity). Reasoning-specialized models performed well on MCQs but weaker on TIF tasks, indicating a trade-off between logical inference and precise terminology reproduction. Performance followed a logarithmic scaling law with model size, and principle-guided prompting outperformed traditional Auto-CoT in accuracy while reducing output tokens.

Key findings: LLMs struggle to simultaneously handle conceptual understanding and principle-based reasoning; larger models and principle-guided approaches improve performance; and critical limitations exist in LLMs' comprehension of materials synthesis mechanisms. Limitations include lack of human expert annotation and the benchmark's static nature.

The Covid-19 pandemic forced a rapid shift from face-to-face to distance education worldwide, exposing unpreparedness in many countries.
