The Executive submits to Congress extracts from a report on the condition of Texas, but has taken no steps toward recognizing its independence. Prior resolutions from both Houses indicated that recognition should occur once Texas demonstrated a functioning independent government.

Recognizing a new state that has separated from another is a delicate matter, and premature recognition can be viewed as hostile. The United States has historically treated such questions as matters of fact, waiting until independence is clearly established before acknowledgment, as was done with Mexico and various South American states.

While Texas has expelled Mexican authority and defeated its army, Mexico retains greater physical force and threatens reinvasion, leaving Texan independence suspended. The document specifies the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) standard for AMD's SEV-ES and SEV-SNP virtualization features, which protect guest register state from the hypervisor.

When SEV-ES/SNP is enabled, VMEXITs are classified as Automatic Exits (AE) or Non-Automatic Exits (NAE). For NAE events, guests selectively share register state with the hypervisor through the GHCB, a 4KB decrypted page mapped between guest and hypervisor.

The GHCB must be page-aligned and accessed via MSR 0xc001_0130. A GHCB MSR protocol uses the lower 12 bits to request actions before the GHCB page is available, supporting functions such as protocol negotiation, CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration, page state changes, VMPL switching, and termination requests.

Version 2 introduces SEV-SNP support and hypervisor feature advertisement via a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap. Subsequent revisions add: VLEK certificate support, expanded error codes, APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL support, SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob EFI Protocol, SEV-TIO (trusted IO with TDISP), and Secure AVIC.

Key NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access via #NPF, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV Doorbell Page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, and Termination Request.

SMP booting differs from traditional INIT-SIPI-SIPI since hypervisors cannot modify measured/encrypted vCPU registers. Solutions include AP Reset Hold NAE events, AP Jump Tables, and the SNP AP Creation feature (which also enables vCPU hotplug).

NMI handling requires the hypervisor to intercept #DB (not IRET), with guests signaling "NMI Complete" when ready. Debug register virtualization is supported on capable hardware. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

For SNP Restricted Injection, a #HV doorbell page communicates pending events (interrupt vectors, NMIs, #MC) and an EOI assist field to the guest, with the host emulating APIC behavior for interrupt lifecycle management.

On Hasek, the speaker argues that when the puck is loose, it belongs equally to their team, and if Hasek ventures out, he risks being hit. However, when he has the puck, he shouldn't be physically challenged. His stick outside the crease is considered fair game.

Regarding the Buffalo series, Satan and Sanderson have contributed defensively rather than offensively, with Curtis Brown being a key player. The speaker praises Marshall, Hogue, and potential replacements Sim and Gavey. Sydor could be moved to forward if Hull cannot play.

The team killed critical penalties in the first period, energizing them after a previous confidence-losing loss. A wrist brace helped an injured player, though he struggled with faceoffs on one side. Nieuwendyk's mindset has shifted from dreading extended playoff runs to embracing them. The team played passionate defense knowing they had two rest days ahead. The speaker emphasizes that age is irrelevant, praising Skrudland's fierce pride and heart.

A study by Ian Stephen of Macquarie University found that women preferred the body odor of men who ate more fruits and vegetables, while men who consumed more carbohydrates produced less appealing smells. Researchers assessed men's skin using a spectrophotometer to measure carotenoid levels, had them complete food questionnaires, then asked women to rate the scent of their sweat after exercise. Meat consumption made odor more intense but not more or less attractive. A 2006 study similarly found women preferred the odor of men on non-meat diets. George Preti of the University of Pennsylvania notes the diet-odor link is indirect: body odor arises when skin bacteria metabolize sweat compounds. The study did not examine same-sex couples.

Maya Kodes, billed as the world's first interactive real-time virtual pop star, is a hologram created by Montreal's Neweb Labs. Developed over 18 months by Yves St-Gelais, she has released a song on iTunes, performed 30 concerts, and gained 5,500 Facebook followers. Kodes performs at the custom-designed Prince Theatre and will launch her first EP, The New Kode Vol. 1, via a 360-degree livestream on June 13. A Toronto performance and world tour are planned.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on January 26, 2017, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2016. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. Per General Instruction B.2, the information is not deemed "filed" under Section 18 of the Exchange Act. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

Mac Otakara, a Japanese Apple blog, reports that the upcoming iPhone—possibly called "iPhone Edition"—may take design cues from the Apple Watch. The device is rumored to feature a polished stainless steel frame sandwiched between front and rear glass plates, with a Touch ID sensor embedded under the display. It is also expected to include vertically positioned dual cameras capable of taking VR or augmented reality shots. The blog claims this information came from engineering and design verification documents, though the rumors remain unverified.

This study evaluates fine-tuning strategies for Universal Interatomic Potentials (UIPs) applied to material surface systems, addressing the limitation that UIPs trained on bulk data tend to underestimate surface energies. Using MACE-MP-0a-small as the foundation model, the authors compared four approaches: training from scratch (TS), zero-shot prediction (ZS), fine-tuning (FT), and multi-head fine-tuning (MHFT) across three surface systems of increasing complexity: unary gold (Au), binary ruthenium oxide (RuO2), and ternary bismuth vanadate (BiVO4).

Key findings include:

1. FT models consistently outperformed TS models across all three systems, achieving comparable accuracy with significantly less training data (as few as 40–200 configurations versus 2,000).

2. FT models produced more physically realistic diatomic potential energy curves, while TS models exhibited unphysical behaviors such as spurious local minima and incorrect long-range interactions.

3. Prediction performance declined as system complexity increased due to more intricate interactions among elemental species.

4. For BiVO4, FT models better handled high-force outliers by leveraging the foundation model's prior knowledge.

5. Conventional FT can cause catastrophic forgetting and poor generalization to out-of-domain systems. MHFT, which trains simultaneously on original bulk data and new surface data, effectively mitigated this, improving predictions on related noble metal surfaces (Ag, Cu, Pt, Ir) at the cost of roughly 100× longer training time.

6. MHFT requires careful alignment of computational conditions between pre-training and fine-tuning datasets, whereas FT is more tolerant of such discrepancies.

The authors recommend fine-tuning as an efficient strategy for extending UIPs to surface systems with limited first-principles data, with MHFT preferred when preserving bulk predictive performance is important.

Human rights education (HRE) is integrated across all levels of learning but remains largely confined to law schools in higher education, despite its relevance across disciplines. Existing HRE models predate contemporary threats such as climate change, AI, digital misinformation, and refugee crises, and often avoid politically sensitive content. Given that over half of UK university students have experienced adverse childhood events, HRE risks retraumatising learners without a trauma-informed approach.

Trauma-informed HRE (TIHRE) applies pedagogies grounded in dignity, respect, and inclusion to mitigate retraumatisation and empower learners as survivors and advocates. Drawing on the SAMHSA framework (safety, trustworthiness, peer support, collaboration, empowerment, and cultural recognition), this article offers three key recommendations based on a structured literature review.

First, educators should clarify their values and cultivate an authentic, self-aware teaching persona, "locating" themselves to identify unconscious biases and build trust through rapport, such as learning students' names.

Second, trauma-informed principles should be embedded in course design using the UN's tripartite framework (learning about, through, and for human rights). This involves co-creation with students, project-based learning, skills development, content warnings, wellbeing check-ins, and reflective exercises (e.g., Gibbs' Cycle), while avoiding "trauma porn" and romanticised resilience narratives.

Third, dialogic teaching should underpin TIHRE, reimagining student-teacher power dynamics through horizontal, respectful dialogue. Incorporating guest speakers, including survivors and practitioners, bridges theory and practice while building advocacy skills.

Ultimately, TIHRE seeks to empower learners and educators as catalysts for hope, healing, and reconciliation, centring wellbeing, agency, and dignity.

Industrial enterprises face challenges including geopolitical uncertainties, energy prices, supply chain disruptions, and sustainability demands, while digitalization transforms manufacturing. IT-based simulation, modeling, and analysis, supported by high-performance computing (HPC), are key tools for optimizing processes and driving innovation.

An IDC survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers from manufacturing enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland found that 64% plan to invest in modern simulation, modeling, and high-performance data analytics. Three-quarters view these tools as essential for innovation, while 57% see them as important for quality improvement. Deployment in product development, production planning, and quality management is expected to reach 90% within two years.

Applications include virtual prototyping, digital twins, design optimization, and high-performance data analytics (used by 42%). Data silos and the lack of unified information bases remain obstacles. Demand for high-performance calculations is projected to grow significantly, with 81% of respondents viewing HPC as a game changer for innovation. HPC enables complex calculations, improves quality, unlocks new usage scenarios, and increases agility.

Currently, 27% of enterprises use professional HPC infrastructures, with 39% piloting deployment. Most prefer external HPC infrastructures (87%) or colocation (74%) over on-premises options due to cost and agility concerns. Key challenges include security (72%), high investment and licensing costs, and energy consumption and sustainability (58%).

This paper investigates whether textual content of earnings press releases predicts earnings announcement day stock returns, using over 138,000 press releases from 2005-2023. The authors apply five NLP techniques—including Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), BERT, MPNET, and FinBERT—within a rolling window framework to avoid look-ahead bias.

Key findings include:
1. Soft information from press releases explains stock price reactions as much as earnings surprises (hard information), with FinBERT performing best and LDA providing interpretability.
2. Topic analysis reveals a self-serving bias: managers frame internal factors (financial performance) positively and external factors (sector/macro conditions) negatively.
3. Trading strategies executed at market open yield no abnormal returns, supporting market efficiency.
4. However, if press release content is leaked in advance (as in documented hacking cases), combining hard and soft signals raises Precision@10 for identifying top/bottom performers from 0.25-0.36 to 0.44-0.52.

The authors conclude that press releases contain substantial return-relevant information that is rapidly incorporated into prices, emphasizing the importance of cybersecurity for newswire services.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter-point to a range of 1 percent to 1.25 percent, its fourth hike in 18 months, with one more expected this year. The increase will raise costs for credit card holders, adjustable-rate mortgages, and home equity lines of credit, but fixed mortgage and auto loan rates have barely changed, as they track other factors like the 10-year Treasury yield. Consumers with poor credit may face higher borrowing costs, particularly on used car loans. Savers may see modest gains, mainly through smaller banks offering higher CD and savings rates, while larger banks have not adjusted. Internationally, higher U.S. rates attract overseas investment, strengthen the dollar, and can pull capital from developing countries, complicating their dollar-denominated debts. Financial planners advise fixed-income investors to maintain balanced bond portfolios rather than shift strategies.

A UCLA study by professor Gregory Okin, published in PLOS One, found that meat-based food consumed by U.S. dogs and cats, along with their waste, produces roughly 64 million tons of carbon dioxide annually—equivalent to 13.6 million cars. Pets account for 25-30 percent of the environmental impact of U.S. meat consumption. Okin does not advocate vegetarian pet diets but wants owners to consider climate impacts, especially with the shift to premium high-protein foods. UC Davis professor Frank Mitloehner noted most pet-food meat comes from rendered livestock byproducts that would otherwise be wasted. While Humane Society lobbyist Jennifer Fearing reported success with a vegan dog diet, many veterinarians warn against plant-based diets, particularly for cats, which need taurine from meat. A 2015 study found most vegetarian pet foods tested failed to meet industry labeling standards, with some lacking critical amino acids.

U.S. government bond yields rose after Friday's jobs report, with the 10-year Treasury yield climbing to 2.370% and the two-year to 1.511%, marking four consecutive weeks of increases. The Labor Department reported the economy lost 33,000 jobs in September—the first monthly decline since 2010—while unemployment fell to 4.2% and average hourly earnings rose 2.9%. Traders attributed job losses to recent hurricanes and focused on wage gains as potentially inflationary. Fed-funds futures indicated an 88% chance of a rate increase by December, up from 73% a week earlier. Some analysts cautioned that the wage data may be skewed because absent hourly workers earn less than salaried employees. Yields were also pressured by three upcoming Treasury debt auctions.

The Wall Street Journal reports that three small black entrepreneurs—Lance Stroud, Renard D. Euell, and Ronald Peek—were named winning bidders for oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve alongside major oil companies. The Department of Energy had waived its usual financial guarantee requirement, giving bidders five days to produce letters of credit equal to the oil's market value. Stroud and Euell failed to secure the necessary financial backing by the deadline, with Euell blaming Enron for missed deadlines after negotiations with the company fell through. Only Peek succeeded, transferring his interest in three million barrels to Hess Energy Trading Co.

The Washington Post reports that Rockville-based Artesia Technologies secured $26 million in its second funding round, led by Warburg Pincus Ventures with strategic partners including Enron Broadband Services, Vignette, and others. The digital asset management company plans to use the funding for international expansion, particularly in Europe, and to expand its sales and marketing staff.

The Houston Chronicle examines a November 7 referendum on publicly financing a new downtown basketball arena for the Houston Rockets. Under the proposal, the Harris County-Houston Sports Authority would sell bonds covering the $175 million construction cost, while owner Leslie Alexander could gain $30–45 million in additional annual revenue. Supporters, including Enron's Ken Lay as co-chairman of the pro-arena campaign, argue the arena would spur downtown development and strengthen Houston's economy, citing 18 projects worth $700 million developed around Enron Field. Critics call it corporate welfare, arguing taxpayers would fund between $125–175 million while benefits accrue primarily to the team's owner. A comparative study found four of seven recently built NBA arenas used less public money than Houston's proposal, though some cities offered alternative incentives such as land condemnation for private development. The Chronicle editorial board endorsed the referendum.

The Vegas Golden Knights will finalize their inaugural roster through the NHL expansion draft next week. Existing teams must submit protection lists by Saturday, choosing either to protect 11 players (seven forwards, three defencemen, one goalie) or nine players (eight skaters, one goalie). Teams must expose at least two forwards, one defenceman, and one qualifying goalie, while players with two or fewer seasons are exempt. Vegas will select one player from each of the 30 teams, with picks announced June 21. Readers are invited to submit their own protected list for the Calgary Flames.

The University of Notre Dame received two gifts totaling $205 million within two weeks. Alumnus Matthew Walsh and his wife Joyce donated $150 million to the School of Architecture, which will be renamed the Matthew and Joyce Walsh School of Architecture. Walsh, a 1968 Notre Dame graduate, is co-chair of Walsh Construction, founded by his grandfather in 1898.

A second gift from Francis and Kathleen Rooney will endow an institute originally established in 2008 as the Rooney Center for the Study of American Democracy, which promotes scholarship and dialogue on American democracy. Francis Rooney, former CEO of Rooney Holdings Inc., served as ambassador to the Holy See and as a Florida congressman. University president Robert Dowd praised the Rooneys' generosity, noting it will allow students and scholars to engage with political challenges through democratic principles and Catholic social teaching.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting the results of its Annual Meeting of Shareholders held on February 13, 2018. Shareholders voted on six proposals: (1) elected eight directors, including Tim Cook, Al Gore, and Bob Iger; (2) ratified Ernst & Young LLP as the independent registered public accounting firm for 2018; (3) approved an advisory resolution on executive compensation; (4) approved the amended and restated Non-Employee Director Stock Plan; (5) rejected a shareholder proposal on Proxy Access Amendments; and (6) rejected a shareholder proposal for a Human Rights Committee. The report was signed by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President and General Counsel.

The author argues that Apple should enable Siri to learn from users directly, starting with basic features like teaching it custom pronunciations, nicknames, and new vocabulary. Currently, Siri has only limited learning capabilities, such as storing nicknames in the user's own contact entry, but cannot naturally assign nicknames to others or adapt to individual speech patterns. The author suggests that allowing users to teach Siri words like "photobomb" or alternative pronunciations would improve interactions, and aggregated input could enhance Siri through machine learning. The piece also proposes letting users redefine Siri's functional commands, and criticizes Apple for prioritizing superficial product features over meaningful improvements to Siri.

Students returned to North Park Elementary School in San Bernardino, California, a week after a shooting in a special education classroom. Police said Cedric Anderson killed his estranged wife, teacher Karen Smith, and 8-year-old Jonathan Martinez before fatally shooting himself. Another student, 9-year-old Nolan Brandy, was wounded and later released from the hospital. Superintendent Dr. Dale Marsden praised faculty for supporting students and said reopening the school was a step toward healing. Security was tightened, counselors were made available, and a memorial with flowers and candles was placed outside the school.

Amsterdam's Buiksloterham district is undergoing an experimental docklands regeneration rooted in sustainability and circular economy principles. At its centre is De Ceuvel, a ten-year temporary co-working hub built from renovated houseboats placed on a former shipyard, surrounded by plants designed to draw toxins from polluted soil.

The site minimises waste through wormeries, composting toilets, a struvite reactor that converts urine into fertiliser, and an aquaponics system that supplies the cafe. Energy comes from solar panels on each boat, supported by insulation and heat exchangers. A local cryptocurrency called Jouliettes rewards energy-efficient occupants and may become a wider solar-based currency.

The approach offers an alternative to conventional dockland redevelopment, which typically requires costly soil removal and results in luxury housing that displaces locals. Following the financial crisis halting earlier plans, Buiksloterham adopted this inclusive, lower-cost model, aiming to become Europe's most sustainable neighbourhood.

Kilauea volcano has been erupting for 27 days in Hawaii's Big Island, and volcanic haze has now drifted 4,000 miles to Guam, prompting health warnings for residents with respiratory issues. On the island, fast-moving lava from Fissure 8 threatens the communities of Leilani Estates and Lanipuna Gardens, advancing at 600 yards per hour, with lava fountains reaching over 200 feet. Officials warn of falling volcanic glass fibers called "Pele's hair," which can cause skin and eye irritation. Residents of Kapoho are being evacuated to avoid being trapped. Since May 3, approximately 22 fissures have opened, at least 40 homes destroyed, over 2,000 acres covered by lava, and 200 people are in emergency shelters. The USGS also humorously advised against roasting marshmallows over volcanic vents due to toxic gases.

Peel Regional Police are investigating a March 13 attack in which three men assaulted a 29-year-old autistic man at Square One mall's bus station in Mississauga. The surveillance video has been viewed over 300,000 times. Investigators now believe the suspects are originally from British Columbia's lower mainland and recently travelled to the GTA. Insp. Norm English is asking media and residents in areas like Vancouver, Surrey, Abbotsford, and Richmond to review the footage. All three suspects are described as South Asian, 5-foot-10, wearing black clothing. The victim remains shaken. Tips can be directed to Peel police or Crime Stoppers.

The RSI indicator shows mixed results when applied to cryptocurrency trading. As a mean reversion indicator (buying low RSI and selling high RSI readings), it proved ineffective on Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Dogecoin, unlike its performance on US equities. Testing on Bitcoin from January 2015 to September 2021 yielded weak results with too few trades to be reliable.

However, RSI performs well as a momentum indicator in crypto markets. Using a strategy of buying when the five-day RSI crosses above 50 and selling when it crosses below 50 produced a CAGR of 122% compared to 101% for buy-and-hold, with significantly lower drawdowns (39% vs 83%). Similar positive results occurred with Ethereum and Dogecoin. Overall, RSI works on crypto when used as a momentum indicator rather than a mean reversion tool.

One of eight Arkansas inmates facing execution had a last meal Monday as courts decided his fate. After the Arkansas Supreme Court stayed two executions, Attorney General Leslie Rutledge asked the US Supreme Court to overturn the ruling. If she prevails, Don Davis could be executed first, as Bruce Ward has another stay in place. Separately, the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals overturned a federal judge's Saturday ruling that had halted all eight executions on grounds the lethal injection method was likely unconstitutional, stating the use of midazolam did not create undue severe pain.

The manuscript illustrates the value of critical approaches to quantitative research, advancing epistemological and methodological considerations for scholars in education. It targets researchers, faculty, students, institutional staff, and methods instructors.

The authors share their positionalities, arguing that quantitative research is never truly objective and that researchers' identities and biases shape their scholarship. Jay, a white cisgender queer scholar, studies queer and trans collegians using quantitative methods. Jimmy, a Vietnamese-Chinese American institutional researcher, emphasizes disaggregating data and minimizing harm.

Quantitative criticalism combines methods with critical epistemologies, challenging post-positivist assumptions and advocating for social justice. Scholars must embed criticality throughout the research process, from question formation to implications, while building community and partnering with those being studied.

The authors identify key tensions: statistics' white supremacist and cisheteropatriarchal origins (e.g., Galton, Pearson); the undefined "threshold of criticality"; difficulties operationalizing identity variables; limited analytical power for multiply minoritized populations; underuse of nonparametric tests; individualistic framing that blames marginalized communities; and conflicts between generalizability and community-specific nuance.

Four example studies demonstrate applications: Sablan (2019) applied QuantCrit using Yosso's community cultural wealth model; Garvey (2017) used queer theory to advocate including "queer" as a survey category despite categorization tensions; Szymanski and Lewis (2016) and Wilson and Urick (2022) used intersectionality through interaction effects and latent class analysis, respectively.

Implications emphasize that authors' intentions matter alongside methods, that criticality exists on a continuum without a universal threshold, and that incremental change can reinforce white supremacy. The authors pose reflective questions about intentions, the possibility of liberation through historically oppressive methods, and personal thresholds of criticality, urging scholars to move beyond objectivist approaches.

SpinGPT is an LLM-based poker agent designed for the Spin & Go three-player tournament format, addressing limitations of prior approaches that focused mainly on two-player cash games. Built on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, it uses a two-stage training pipeline: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on 320,000 decisions from professional hands played between 2018–2020, followed by offline Reinforcement Learning with the ORPO algorithm on 270,000 solver-generated hands mixed with 50,000 human hands to prevent catastrophic forgetting.

The SFT version achieved 80% exact accuracy and 86% macro F1 on professional data, producing few illegal moves. Against the benchmark Slumbot (after a heuristic patch correcting deep-stack all-in errors), SpinGPT-SFT won 13.4 ± 12.9 BB/100 over 30,000 hands. The final SpinGPT model beat SpinGPT-SFT by 13.2 ± 7.24 BB/100 over 10,000 hands, confirming the value of the RL phase.

Limitations include lack of evaluation against Slumbot for the final model, format mismatches, and typical LLM errors such as numerical mistakes. Future directions include stronger base models, retrieval-augmented GTO charts, chain-of-thought reasoning, opponent-adaptive training, explainability features, and hybrid LLM-solver systems.

A global learning crisis, worsened by pandemic closures, climate change, conflict and economic slowdown, costs an estimated US$129 billion annually. Youth unemployment nears 30 percent in lower-income countries, and 20 percent of youth globally are not in employment, education or training, two-thirds of whom are women. Nearly 40 percent of employers report skills shortages, and 39 percent of current job skills are expected to transform by 2030.

The Global Partnership for Education (GPE) supports lower-income countries in building education systems that deliver foundational learning (literacy, numeracy, socio-emotional) and 21st century skills such as critical thinking, creativity, collaboration and problem solving. Through policy dialogue, financing and public-private partnerships, GPE helps align curricula with labor market needs.

Examples include Lesotho, where private and philanthropic partners unlocked over $6 million via the GPE Multiplier, and Ghana, where a $40 million partnership supports foundational learning. In 2024, 20 active GPE grants focused on employment-readiness skills. Kenya is implementing a competency-based curriculum, while El Salvador prioritizes socio-emotional skills and teacher training. GPE also supports assessment tools through the A4L Initiative and KIX.

Common weight-loss mistakes include: drinking from plastic bottles, which leach fat-storing Bisphenol-A; completely eliminating sweets, carbs, or fats instead of replacing them with healthier alternatives; emotional eating; consuming store-bought protein bars and energy drinks containing artificial sweeteners; and drinking calories rather than eating meals.

Other errors involve being a perfectionist, surrounding yourself with unsupportive people, relying on weighing scales, and using meal-replacement supplements that increase cravings. Insufficient sleep, eating too little while over-exercising, and repeating the same workout routine also hinder progress, as the body adapts or enters starvation mode.

Additionally, being too restrictive too quickly or copying another person's weight-loss plan is ineffective, since routines should be tailored to individual body type, metabolism, and health status.

The MACD-histogram trading strategy is a mean-reversion system that identifies momentum changes and reversal points. Tested on a portfolio of 77 liquid ETFs, it generated 6,669 trades, performing better on long positions than short. Entry occurs at the close, with exit on the first day the close exceeds the prior day's close.

When backtested on QLD (2x Nasdaq 100) from 2007, the strategy produced 85 trades with a 2.2% average gain, 10.4% annual returns, and a 19% max drawdown, while invested only 5% of the time. The MACD histogram visually represents the difference between the MACD line and signal line, with bars above zero indicating bullish momentum and below indicating bearish momentum.

NVIDIA's Turing GPU architecture introduces significant advancements in display, video, and rendering technologies. The display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, enabling 8K resolution at 60Hz, HDR processing with tone mapping, and an enhanced NVENC encoder supporting HEVC 8K at 30fps with improved bitrate savings. Turing GPUs include hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, a new standard that delivers power, display, and data to VR headsets through a single connector. NVLink replaces MIO and PCIe for SLI data transfers in TU102 and TU104 GPUs, providing higher bandwidth for advanced display topologies.

Turing enables real-time ray tracing through dedicated RT Cores, which accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing. A hybrid rendering approach combines ray tracing with rasterization for optimal performance. NVIDIA NGX leverages Tensor Cores for deep learning-based features including DLSS (Deep Learning Super-Sampling), InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

New shading capabilities include Mesh Shading (introducing Task and Mesh Shaders to eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks), Variable Rate Shading (VRS) for adjusting shading rates across 16x16 pixel regions, Texture Space Shading (TSS) for decoupling visibility and appearance sampling, and Multi-View Rendering (MVR) supporting up to four views per pass.

Turing improves VR through VirtualLink, MVR, Foveated Rendering via VRS, and ray-traced audio. The TU104 and TU106 GPUs share Turing's core features with varying configurations. The RTX-OPS metric measures hybrid rendering workloads by combining tensor, CUDA, RT core, and INT32 operations based on typical usage ratios. Ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections provide significant visual improvements over traditional rasterization techniques, demonstrated in games like Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider.

Nokia's announcement of an updated 3310 has generated interest in feature phones, which are popular as secondary devices or alternatives to smartphones. Several options are available: the Nokia 216 (Rs 2,536) offers a camera, MP3 player, and long battery life; the Samsung Metro 350 (Rs 2,780) has a 2MP camera and larger screen; the Nokia 230 (Rs 4,799) is a premium choice; the Intex Yaari (Rs 799) is the cheapest; the upcoming Nokia 3310 is expected around Rs 4,000; the Micromax X408 (under Rs 1,000) offers dual SIM; the Samsung Guru E1200 (Rs 1,200) is a basic backup option; and the Nokia 105 (Rs 1,310) is durable and available in three colours.

Onesmo Rupil, 23, of Mwanza, began using drugs at 17 and was later expelled from the University of Dodoma in 2013 due to poor performance linked to substance abuse. He now manages Philimisana Foundation Sober House, which rehabilitates about 30 young people, mostly marijuana users. Onesmo began using drugs in A-Level school in Moshi, attributing his vulnerability partly to limited parental contact from early boarding school. He progressed from marijuana to heroin, spending over Sh100,000 on daily doses and stealing laptops at Udom to fund his addiction. He was arrested in 2015 for stealing over 200 laptops and detained at Isanga Prison for six months, later undergoing rehabilitation in Dar es Salaam.

According to Dr Kassian Nyandindi of Muhimbili National Hospital, 2014 research showed 550,000 people affected by drug abuse in Tanzania, with 25,000 addicts nationwide and only 3,500 receiving methadone treatment in Dar es Salaam. HIV infection among drug users is 20–50 percent. He explains marijuana's THC damages the corpus callosum, causing mental disorders often misattributed locally to superstition. A UN report identified marijuana as the world's most widely produced and used drug in 2010, with 119–224 million adult users globally.

This study developed and validated an automated system for monitoring clinical practice guideline adherence in intensive care units, combining Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) for computer-interpretable guideline representation with the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) Common Data Model for patient data standardization.

Six COVID-19 and ARDS-related recommendations were selected from intensive care guidelines and encoded in FHIR using the CPG-on-EBMonFHIR Implementation Guide. The system's execution engine interprets these recommendations and queries OMOP CDM databases to assess applicability and adherence. It was deployed across five German university hospitals, covering 82,015 intensive care episodes from January 2020 to May 2023.

A validation study in three hospitals compared the system against seven intensive care physicians, using ground truth established by supervising physicians. The system achieved 97.0% accuracy, significantly outperforming human reviewers (86.6%; p < 0.001). Over 80% of discrepancies stemmed from human error, while system errors primarily resulted from data stored in unstructured free-text fields not transferred to the OMOP CDM. The system processed over 2,000 patient days per second, compared to approximately 30 seconds per patient-day for human reviewers.

Adherence rates across recommendations ranged from 10–60%, with variability attributed to newly introduced guidelines, incomplete documentation, and imprecise recommendation formulations. The authors recommend that guidelines explicitly define tolerance ranges, deviation limits, and timing requirements to enable reproducible adherence monitoring.

Limitations include retrospective validation, potential bias in expert assessments, and limited scope of evaluated recommendations.

The speaker acknowledges the Colorado series was tough and emphasizes that New Jersey presents an equally difficult challenge in the finals. He rejects tiredness as an excuse, attributing the tight play to both teams' styles. He describes the opposing line as balanced with strong chemistry, good defensive play, and quick transitions, requiring careful containment. A paper by Nicholas Lewis and Judith Curry, published in the Journal of Climate, concludes that high estimates of future global warming from most computer climate simulations are inconsistent with observed warming since 1850, implying future warming will be 30–45% lower than IPCC projections.

Using IPCC AR5 forcing estimates extended to 2016, with revisions to greenhouse gas, ozone, and aerosol forcing, the study derives a median equilibrium climate sensitivity (ECS) of 1.66°C (5–95%: 1.15–2.7°C) and transient climate response (TCR) of 1.33°C, compared to 3.1°C and 1.9°C respectively for 31 CMIP5 models. The estimates are insensitive to the analysis period chosen.

The paper examines potential biases from forcing-efficacy effects, sea-surface warming patterns, and temperature estimation, concluding these are minor when using globally-complete temperature data. It also addresses criticisms regarding time-varying climate feedbacks, finding them immaterial to median ECS estimates.

The Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) describes analyses for trial ZEA-DNK-02170 evaluating dasiglucagon versus placebo.

Plasma glucose concentrations and pharmacodynamic metrics will be summarized by treatment group and time point, with mean and individual concentration curves plotted.

Safety analyses, based on the safety set, cover:
- Extent of exposure: insulin administration prior to hypoglycemia induction, the induction procedure, trial medication administration, and post-treatment rescue glucose infusion, including time to first IV glucose infusion.
- Local tolerability at the injection site at 30, 120, and 300 minutes post-dose.
- Adverse events: restricted to treatment-emergent AEs (TEAEs), coded via MedDRA v21.0+, summarized by causal relationship (related/not related) and severity (mild/moderate/severe). Overview tables include AESIs, injection site reactions, study drug-related TEAEs, SAEs, and deaths.
- Laboratory parameters (hematology, biochemistry, coagulation, urinalysis, pregnancy, alcohol tests), vital signs, physical examinations, and ECGs (including categorical QTcF analysis at >450/480/500 ms thresholds).
- Immunogenicity: ADA incidence including treatment-induced and treatment-boosted patients.

Changes from the protocol include reworded primary efficacy analyses with added sensitivity/supportive analyses and revised terminology for secondary endpoints.

Appendices specify presentation rules, SAS programming QC requirements, and a list of planned tables, figures, and listings.

Former Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen stated that gradual interest rate hikes are necessary to prevent the U.S. economy from overheating while allowing inflation to reach the Fed's 2 percent target. Speaking in Philadelphia, she suggested a sustainable monthly job growth pace of 90,000 to 120,000, compared to February's 313,000. Yellen warned of risks in tightening too slowly or too quickly. She left the Fed after being passed over for a second term by President Trump, who appointed Jerome Powell, expected to continue gradual rate increases. During Yellen's tenure, unemployment fell from 6.7 to 4.1 percent without triggering above-target inflation.

Arizona has been a leader in school choice, becoming the first state to enact Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) vouchers in 2011 and the first to make them universal in 2022, despite voters rejecting a capped expansion in 2018. The state provides over $1 billion annually in private education subsidies with limited accountability.

ESA enrollment grew from 144 students in FY2012 to 87,602 by Q2 FY2025. Voucher amounts equal 90% of charter school funding, though awards for students with disabilities can exceed $30,000. In FY2023, approximately $304 million was spent, with $173 million going to private schools—51% to religious schools (86% Evangelical Christian and Catholic) and 44% to special needs schools. Less than 40% of ESA students used funds for private school tuition, suggesting significant use for homeschooling or extracurriculars. Unspent balances accumulated to an estimated $360 million by end of FY2024.

Zip code analysis shows ESA users primarily come from higher-income areas, though income disparities have narrowed over time. The Grand Canyon Institute estimates nearly three-quarters of universal ESA participants never attended district or charter schools, though about 90% of new FY2025 entrants did. GCI calculates the universal voucher program creates net costs to the state's general fund of at least $330 million in FY2024 and $350 million in FY2025, contradicting claims that vouchers save money.

Mega Geometry is an RTX technology that increases geometric detail in ray-traced applications, enabling engines like Unreal Engine 5's Nanite to ray trace at full fidelity. It addresses two challenges: cluster-based LOD updates through new Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS), which reduce BVH build processing by two orders of magnitude, and high object counts via Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures (PTLAS), which update only changed partitions. Mega Geometry also enables real-time ray tracing of subdivision surfaces. It is supported on DirectX 12, Vulkan, and OptiX 9.0, and runs on all RTX GPUs from Turing onward, with Blackwell's 4th generation RT Cores offering up to 2x ray-triangle intersection rates.

Blackwell introduces Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) for hair and strand rendering, offering 2x faster performance and 5x less VRAM than Disjoint Orthogonal Triangle Strips. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 doubles reorder efficiency. The AI Management Processor (AMP), a RISC-V-based scheduler, offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU.

Blackwell adds 4:2:2 chroma hardware encode/decode support, ninth-generation NVENC with 5% BD-BR PSNR quality gains for AV1/HEVC, sixth-generation NVDEC with 2x faster H.264 decoding, and DisplayPort 2.1b with up to 80 Gbps bandwidth supporting 8K@165Hz and 4K@480Hz.

Max-Q power efficiency improvements include advanced power gating, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, accelerated frequency switching (1000x faster clock adjustments), and low-latency sleep (10x faster sleep entry than Ada), yielding up to 50% power savings in some workloads.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three additional frames per rendered frame, 40% faster and using 30% less VRAM than prior methods. It uses enhanced Flip Metering for frame pacing. DLSS 4 also transitions from CNN to transformer-based models with 2x more parameters, improving Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA quality.

Neural shaders, accessible via the new Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, enable technologies like RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression (up to 7:1 VRAM compression), Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin (subsurface scattering), and RTX Neural Faces (generative AI-based face rendering).

The Blackwell GPU lineup includes the GB202 (RTX 5090) with 92.2 billion transistors and 24,576 CUDA Cores; GB203 (RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti) with 45.6 billion transistors and 10,752 CUDA Cores; and GB205 (RTX 5070) with 31 billion transistors and 6,400 CUDA Cores.

Education programs encompass formal and non-formal activities designed to help students achieve learning goals, with curriculum serving as a plan outlining objectives, content, methods, and evaluation. Curriculum evaluation, the final step of curriculum development, is essential for identifying and correcting weaknesses. Teachers' views are particularly valuable in this process.

This study aimed to determine pre-service teachers' opinions on the Physical Education and Sports Curriculum (grades 5-8) regarding objectives, content, learning-teaching processes, and assessment practices. Using a quantitative scanning model, a researcher-developed questionnaire was administered to 100 students from Bayburt University's Faculty of Sports Sciences, with 25 students drawn from each of four departments via cluster sampling.

Results showed that pre-service teachers generally held positive views about program objectives, finding them appropriate, understandably expressed, and well-organized, though many were undecided about scientific accuracy. Regarding content, most participants were undecided about scientific accuracy, age appropriateness, and compatibility with other countries' programs, though 80% agreed the content was meaningfully arranged. For learning-teaching processes, 56% found activities enriching and 61% acknowledged use of concrete materials, but 60% disagreed that different methods and techniques were used. For assessment, participants agreed varied forms were used but indicated alternative measurement methods were lacking.

The study concludes that pre-service teachers lack sufficient information about program content and recommends increasing research, seminars, and curriculum review courses in teacher training.

The present invention relates to methods for forming 3-dimensional vertical NOR-type memory string arrays. The method uses damascene local vertical bit lines and etches local word lines in two steps to reduce aspect ratio during patterning, thereby improving structural stability of word line stacks and avoiding "ribboning"—a stress-induced deformation of microscopic rectangular features occurring at high aspect ratios.

The fabrication process begins with a memory structure formed on global interconnect lines over a semiconductor substrate, comprising multiple layers of silicon nitride and silicon oxide. A first set of trenches is etched and filled with sacrificial dielectric material. A second masking layer is then patterned to create a second set of trenches, forming narrow word line stacks. The silicon nitride layers are selectively removed, creating cavities that are filled with metal (such as TiN, W, or Mo) to form word line strips.

Vias are then etched through the structure, and layers are conformally deposited: tunneling dielectric, charge storage, blocking dielectric, channel, liner, and sacrificial dielectric. Shafts are subsequently filled with doped semiconductor material to form common source and drain regions for thin-film transistors. A second set of global interconnect lines is added above to contact drain layers. Word line connections are made through a staircase structure with vertical conductors.

Alternative embodiments include using dielectric pillars for mechanical support of high aspect-ratio word line strips, and employing stacked masks with different pitches to define word line stacks.

InnerDancer Performing Arts, a nonprofit founded in 2009 by former professional dancer Caroline Bossmeyer, hosts monthly dances for teens and adults with developmental disabilities at the Gloria McClellan Adult Activity & Resource Center in Vista. Digital Ecosystems are proposed as software systems that mimic biological ecosystems to address the growing complexity of software development and automated service composition. Unlike existing uses of the term "digital ecosystem" (which often lack ecological properties), these systems aim to exploit properties like self-organisation, scalability, and robustness found in nature.

Key design considerations include: fitness landscapes that are complex and dynamic (unlike static genetic algorithm landscapes); agents that reproduce, vary, interact, move, and die; spatial dynamics through distributed networks that maintain diversity; and a balance between self-organisation and user-driven constraints. As Complex Adaptive Systems, they offer scalability but pose prediction challenges, requiring tradeoffs between diversity and efficiency, and between stability and adaptability.

The proposed Ecosystem-Oriented Architecture uses a two-level optimisation: a decentralised peer-to-peer network of agents feeding an evolutionary algorithm operating on local habitats. It differs from traditional island-model distributed evolutionary computing by evolving populations for similar (not identical) requests and using Hebbian learning to dynamically reconfigure habitat connectivity based on successful agent migrations, producing small-world network topologies resembling the user base.

Simulations modelled a business ecosystem of 100 users (SMEs) who deployed agents and submitted requests represented as semantic descriptions. Habitats instantiated evolving populations with dynamic population sizes, using fitness functions derived from user requests to evolve optimal agent-sequences.

The lecture discusses effective field theory (EFT) with fine tuning in the context of two-nucleon scattering. Fine tuning here means an operator appears irrelevant under dimensional power counting but is actually relevant, requiring expansion around an interacting fixed point rather than a trivial one.

Because nucleons are non-relativistic (P much less than M pi), the theory reduces to contact interactions with derivatives, allowing calculation of all loops. The professor demonstrates that using only the HQET-style kinetic term produces a pinch singularity, so the kinetic energy term (P²/2M) must be kept as relevant. A nucleon field scaling analysis shows loop and tree-level diagrams both scale as 1/M.

Summing the geometric series of bubble diagrams reproduces the effective range expansion (P cotangent delta as a Taylor series in P²), proving this quantum mechanics theorem within EFT without specifying a potential.

However, experimental scattering lengths (23 fm for 1S0, 5 fm for 3S1) are unnaturally large, indicating fine tuning in C0. MS-bar scheme fails here; offshell momentum subtraction and the Power Divergence Subtraction (PDS) scheme—which subtracts poles at D=3 to track power-law divergences—promote C0 to a relevant coupling scaling as 1/(Mμ).

The beta function reveals three fixed points (a=0, ±∞), with nature sitting near the interacting fixed points. These exhibit conformal and SU(4) spin-isospin symmetries, and a pole in the amplitude corresponds to the deuteron bound state. The renormalization group equations propagate the fine-tuning enhancement to all higher operators, determining the correct power counting throughout the theory. This framework has practical applications, including precision deuteron physics calculations.

Coral Davenport, a New York Times reporter, explains how Russell Vought, director of the Office of Management and Budget, plans to bypass Congress's budgetary powers to advance the Trump administration's agenda.

President Trump described the government shutdown as an "unprecedented opportunity" to cut federal agencies and Democratic priorities. His administration froze roughly $18 billion for New York City infrastructure projects and canceled $8 billion for climate projects in Democratic-leaning states, both announced by OMB Director Russell Vought, a Project 2025 author. Trump plans to meet with Vought to determine which agencies to cut and whether cuts will be temporary or permanent. White House officials indicated federal layoffs, potentially in the thousands, could begin within days.

The shutdown began Wednesday after Congress failed to pass a funding bill. Republicans sought a stopgap maintaining current funding until late November, while Democrats demanded an extension of enhanced Obamacare tax credits set to expire at year's end. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said no agreement on ACA credits would be reached. Competing Senate bills failed Wednesday, with the next vote scheduled Friday due to Yom Kippur.

Shieldalloy Metallurgical Corporation challenged the NRC's transfer of regulatory authority over nuclear materials to New Jersey under 42 U.S.C. § 2021, arguing the state's program was incompatible with the federal scheme and that the transfer was arbitrary and capricious. Shieldalloy had spent a decade seeking NRC approval for a plan to decommission its Newfield, New Jersey facility with on-site disposal of radioactive byproducts. Shortly after the transfer took effect in September 2009, New Jersey rejected Shieldalloy's decommissioning plan.

The court found the NRC's response to Shieldalloy's comments on criterion 25 (regarding uninterrupted processing of license applications) inadequate. The NRC dismissed Shieldalloy's suggestion of a partial transfer excluding the Newfield site, despite precedent from the Oklahoma transfer allowing limited agreements for discrete subcategories of materials. The NRC failed to explain how Shieldalloy's decommissioning could proceed without interference or why partial transfer was not a viable alternative.

Because the NRC's explanations lacked a rational connection between facts and decision, the court granted Shieldalloy's petition, vacated the transfer, and remanded for further proceedings.

The Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) Operations Guide describes AMD's optional extensions to the Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) and Secure Nested Paging (SNP) APIs for facilitating page migration between memory tiers. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement and offloads page migration to address two challenges: pausing DMA traffic during migration and migrating pages owned by SEV/SNP-protected guests.

Key commands include PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO (migrating pages during concurrent DMA by coordinating with IOMMUs), PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST (migrating SNP guest pages), PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, and PM_NOOP. A new Pre-Migration RMP state facilitates SNP guest page migration. Commands can process up to 128 pages per batch, with optimal performance achieved at 128 pages.

Software interacts with TMPM through a ring buffer interface using mailbox registers. The driver must initialize the device by verifying ENGINE_READY, configuring the ring buffer, and setting DRIVER_INITIALIZED. Six interrupt sources share a single x86 signal, including error indicators and queue status flags.

System physical addresses must be 4K-aligned (except 8-byte aligned host page table entries). SMEE-enabled systems encode encryption information in SPAs. TMPM firmware can be reloaded via a PSP mailbox protocol when no operations are in flight, with EPYC Family 19h identified by FW_VER_Major value 71.

Errors are reported through command status fields, the PM_STATUS register, or Machine Check Architecture, with some hardware errors potentially rendering affected pages unrecoverable.

This paper investigates whether large language models (LLMs) can autoformalize physics problems into differential game logic (dGL), preserving continuous dynamics and discrete transitions of cyber-physical systems.

The authors propose 20 benchmarks derived from undergraduate kinematics problems and develop an autoformalization pipeline with two LLM query types: Propose Formalization and Revise Formalization. The pipeline uses few-shot prompting, KeYmaera X parser feedback for syntax repair (up to three iterations), and a semantic checker that performs symbolic execution to verify equivalence with the expected solution and ensures sufficient variable mutations.

Evaluation compared GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, and OpenAI o3 with zero-shot and multi-shot prompting, sampling five times per benchmark. Few-shot prompting substantially improved all models, with o3 achieving a 70% top-5 success rate, versus 45% for GPT-4.1 and 20% for GPT-4o.

Six problems were unsolved by all models, categorized as optimization problems, non-polynomial continuous dynamics, and complicated dynamics. The authors suggest improvements through extending solvers (e.g., continuous invariant generation) and guiding LLMs toward better abstractions. Future work includes multimodal autoformalization from vision and sensor data for runtime use by autonomous systems.

Depression and anxiety disorders affect over 300 million people globally, with diagnosis complicated by symptom overlap and comorbidity. Digital phenotyping and large language models (LLMs) offer potential for quantitative psychiatric assessment, though LLMs remain underutilized for producing objective digital biomarkers, and most studies rely on social media or structured clinical reports with limited data.

To address these gaps, researchers at the Shanghai Mental Health Center (SMHC) collected over 15,000 minutes of speech recordings from 1,160 outpatients with 25 diagnoses between August 2023 and January 2024. Participants, aged 12-80 and fluent in Mandarin, were diagnosed using ICD-10 criteria. Recordings were transcribed, anonymized, and analyzed using a pre-trained LLM fine-tuned with psychiatrist annotations to identify clinical entities based on diagnostic criteria, complaints, mental status evaluations, and assessment scales. Linguistic and acoustic features were also extracted. An ensemble machine-learning pipeline combining these modalities predicted diagnostic groups and symptoms with moderately high accuracy, suggesting potential to improve psychiatric diagnosis efficiency.

Cover 0 is an all-out man-to-man blitz defense designed to pressure the quarterback quickly, but it leaves defenders isolated and the middle of the field vulnerable. Offenses counter it with quick-hitting man-beater concepts, particularly slants, crossing routes, and pick/rub plays that create natural collisions between defenders. Examples from college offenses include:

1. **Double Slants (Ole Miss)** – Mirrored slants allow the QB to choose the best matchup.
2. **Full-Slide Fade-Out/RB Seam (Oregon)** – A gadget play where the RB fakes blitz pickup before slipping uncovered upfield.
3. **Trips Bunch Jerk Route (Michigan)** – Bunch releases create natural picks, especially effective in the red zone.
4. **Slant-Rub (Wake Forest)** – A slot route rubs off a defender to free the Z receiver near the goal line.
5. **Jerry Rice Motion Slant-Flat (Dixie State)** – Pre-snap motion helps the slot receiver separate from his defender.

Personnel advantages on the perimeter increase an offense's success against Cover 0.

This study analyzed Demographic and Health Survey data from Benin (2017-2018) and Cameroon (2018) to assess awareness of cervical cancer and screening among women aged 15-49. A total of 21,322 women were surveyed about cervical cancer awareness, with 7,010 additionally asked about screening awareness.

Awareness of cervical cancer was considerably lower in Benin (9.5%) than in Cameroon (46.1%). Among women aware of cervical cancer, approximately half knew about cervical screening in Benin (51.4%) and Cameroon (59.7%).

Multivariate logistic regression found that older age, higher educational attainment, and frequent internet use were significantly associated with increased cervical cancer awareness in both countries. Greater wealth was additionally associated with awareness in Cameroon, while Muslim women had reduced odds of awareness compared to Christians in both countries.

For cervical screening awareness, older age, higher education, and frequency of radio and internet use were significant factors. Women aged 25-34 in Benin and 45+ in Cameroon had the highest screening awareness.

As of 2021, neither country had a national HPV vaccination or cervical screening programme. The authors recommend strengthening awareness programmes through stakeholder engagement, public enlightenment via media, targeting younger women with age-appropriate information, and addressing socioeconomic inequalities in access to cervical cancer information and screening.

Limitations include the cross-sectional design, potential sampling and recall bias, and inability to adjust for unmeasured confounders.

SARS-CoV-2, the RNA virus causing COVID-19, is shed in feces and detectable in wastewater, making wastewater monitoring a key COVID-19 surveillance tool. Processing typically requires concentrating virus from 50-250 mL samples via methods like membrane filtration, PEG precipitation, skim milk, ultracentrifugation, or ultrafiltration, often requiring centrifuges unavailable in resource-limited labs.

Nanotrap particles are porous hydrogel particles that capture, concentrate, and preserve analytes including viruses from complex mixtures, and have been used to detect SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory viruses in wastewater.

Three sampling approaches exist: grab (limited snapshot), composite (representative but costly), and passive sampling (e.g., Moore swabs, low-cost alternative). The authors used Moore swabs in institutional buildings and grab samples from manholes, applying membrane filtration to grab samples and skim milk concentration to higher-turbidity Moore swab samples.

This study evaluated how pH, temperature, incubation time, volume, RNA extraction method, and one-step versus two-step concentration methods affect SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection. Secondary aims compared automated versus manual Nanotrap processing of small (10 mL) volumes and compared Nanotrap methods to membrane filtration (150 mL grab) and skim milk (250 mL Moore swab) methods, to ensure sensitivity is maintained.

Wastewater samples were collected weekly from Atlanta community manholes (Moore swabs, 24-hour deployment) and wastewater treatment plant influents (500 mL grab samples) from June–August 2021.

Kratom, derived from Mitragyna speciosa leaves, produces stimulant-to-opioid-like effects and is illegal in Wisconsin, though use still occurs. Researchers analyzed Wisconsin Poison Center (WPC) data from January 2010 to September 2022 to characterize kratom-associated adverse events.

WPC recorded 59 kratom-exposure calls, with frequency generally increasing over the period, peaking at 15 in 2020. Most exposed persons were male (62.7%), with a mean age of 35.3 years. Three exposures involved infants under 2 through unintentional ingestion. Calls were concentrated in southeastern Wisconsin, with Marinette County reporting the most (10). Approximately 55.9% reported kratom alone; the most common co-substances were alcohol and benzodiazepines. Common symptoms included agitation (39%), tachycardia (35.6%), confusion (23.7%), and CNS depression (22%). Of calls with known outcomes, 38% had moderate or major effects, and 7 required critical care, including two women in their 70s (one died with kratom identified as contributory) and two weightlifters who co-ingested phenibut.

The authors note polysubstance use complicates understanding kratom's effects and recommend clinicians caution against concurrent substance use, particularly among older adults, pregnant individuals, and parents of young children. They emphasize kratom can act as a stimulant at lower doses, evidenced by frequent agitation. Continued research, improved clinical data collection, and public education are recommended.

This randomized, open-label clinical trial studied 1112 subjects treated with apixaban for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation over 48 weeks. Subjects were randomized 1:1 to receive standard of care (SOC) information or an Additional Education Program. After the 24-week primary endpoint, the education group was re-randomized 1:1 to continue the program or revert to SOC. Adherence was measured via an electronic monitoring device, with an interim analysis at 24 weeks.

A unit of adherence was defined as a 24-hour window where treatment was taken as prescribed (one tablet twice daily); missing one dose still qualified. Non-adherence was defined as missing two consecutive doses within 24 hours. Periods when apixaban was withheld by the investigator were excluded from adherence assessment. Discontinuation exceeding 30 consecutive days was considered permanent.

The application, a continuation of prior U.S., international, and Chinese patent applications, relates to wireless communications, specifically a communication processing method and apparatus for managing information in a duplication mode.

In wireless systems, data is transmitted between terminal devices and radio access networks across protocol layers including PHY, MAC, RLC, PDCP, and RRC. With 5G technology, duplication mode allows data from a PDCP entity to be duplicately transmitted on multiple RLC entities, improving transmission stability but requiring information management solutions.

The first aspect provides a method where a terminal device determines that a data volume report is needed for one of two paths (first and second) in a radio bearer operating in duplication mode, triggers the report indicating data volume on that path, and sends it to the radio access network. This reduces signaling overhead compared to reporting all paths. The path may be indicated by the radio access network or selected by the terminal based on priority or data volume.

The second aspect provides a method where the terminal receives a first indication message from the radio access network indicating whether to activate or deactivate the duplication mode, then acts accordingly. Various message structures using fields and bits are described for indicating activation status and corresponding radio bearers or paths.

Additional aspects cover communications apparatuses containing processing, sending, and receiving units (potentially implemented as processors, transmitters, receivers, or chips), computer storage media with program code, and apparatuses with processors and memory for implementing these methods.

The embodiments support carrier aggregation and dual connectivity scenarios, with configurations for primary/secondary cells, master/secondary cell groups, and primary/secondary radio access devices. The system handles activation/deactivation decisions based on channel quality, cell load, or measurement reports, manages duplicated data discarding when modes are deactivated, and addresses scenarios where RLC entities reside on different physical devices (DU/CU architectures).

Microsoft Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2020. The COVID-19 pandemic boosted cloud, Surface, and Gaming demand while reducing Search advertising revenue and transactional licensing.

A special weather statement was issued for Edmonton and surrounding areas on Wednesday afternoon due to conditions favourable for funnel cloud development. The passage describes a data intake and query system for processing machine-generated data in IT environments. It claims priority to prior U.S. patent applications and references related patents incorporated by reference.

The system addresses challenges of analyzing large volumes of unstructured machine data from sources such as servers, sensors, routers, and IoT devices. Rather than pre-processing and discarding data, it stores minimally processed machine data as time-stamped "events" for later retrieval, enabling flexible analysis.

Key components include forwarders (which receive, annotate, and route data), indexers (which parse data into events, determine timestamps, apply transformations, and optionally build keyword indexes), and search heads (which execute queries). Events are stored in data stores organized into buckets by time range, with hot, warm, cold, frozen, and quarantine bucket types managed across directories of varying storage speeds.

The system uses a late-binding schema, applying extraction rules (often regular expressions) at search time rather than ingestion time, allowing ongoing refinement. A common information model enables unified field references across disparate data sources.

The system can be deployed on-premises or as a cloud-based service, and supports searching external data collections (virtual indices) through External Result Provider (ERP) processes that operate in streaming mode, reporting mode, or mixed mode.

Inverted indexes store token entries and field-value pair entries with event references, supporting filter criteria (indexes, hosts, sources, sourcetypes, time ranges, keywords) and categorization criteria for grouping search results.

Melissa Jennings, a former member of the UNC women's soccer team dismissed in May 1998, brought suit against UNC, head coach Anson Dorrance, assistant coach William Palladino, and several university officials. Her claims were based on sexually-themed comments allegedly made by Dorrance during team warm-ups, two direct inquiries into her personal life, and a meeting where Dorrance allegedly asked about her sexual activity while discussing her poor grades.

The court addressed three motions. Plaintiff's Motion to Strike the Amended Answer and enter default judgment was denied, as Dorrance's deposition statement was not clearly inconsistent with the Amended Answer and showed no bad faith. Plaintiff's Motion to Strike Exhibits C through H of Dorrance's affidavit was denied because the exhibits were properly authenticated and qualified as Records of Regularly Conducted Activity under the hearsay exception.

Defendants' Motion for Summary Judgment was granted on all claims. On the Title IX claim, the court found the alleged conduct was not sufficiently severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive to deprive Jennings of educational opportunities, considering the social context. On the §1983 claims, the court found no violation of Jennings' privacy rights, as she was never forced to disclose information; the sexual harassment claims failed for the same reasons as the Title IX claim; and supervisory liability claims failed because no underlying constitutional violation occurred. The state common law invasion of privacy claim failed because the two inquiries did not constitute egregious conduct or physical/sensory intrusion under North Carolina law.

Treasury minister Mel Stride assured Parliament that Britain's fish fingers would be "safe in the hands" of the Government during Brexit negotiations. The integration of Information Technology (IT) into language education in Indonesia, accelerated by Education 4.0 and the COVID-19 pandemic, presents both challenges and opportunities. This qualitative study used descriptive analysis, comparative analysis, and framework development, drawing from 151 relevant Scopus articles to examine IT and management strategies in language education.

Key challenges include teachers' limited technological proficiency, difficulties maintaining student engagement in virtual settings, unequal resource availability, and complications in remote assessment. University students face additional obstacles such as the digital divide, reduced self-regulation, and loss of social interaction. Global responses vary, with wealthier nations leveraging advanced tools like AI and VR, while developing regions rely on basic technologies.

Technological innovations supporting language learning include Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), which provides real-time pronunciation feedback, alongside task-based and game-based learning that enhance vocabulary acquisition and engagement. Other tools include AR, VR, IoT, AI, LMS, gamification, blockchain, cloud computing, and robotics.

Effective management strategies involve integrating digital learning platforms, investing in teacher professional development, providing language support tools, facilitating global collaborations, adopting cloud-based infrastructure, utilizing mobile learning, applying data-driven decision-making, and establishing inclusive IT policies.

Student attitudes toward IT in language education parallel those in STEM, generally positive but affected by resource inequity and resistance. Successful IT integration requires addressing pedagogical approaches, equitable access, teacher support, and collaborative learning opportunities.

SA58 Nasal Spray, a broad-spectrum anti-COVID-19 monoclonal antibody developed by Sinovac Life Sciences, was evaluated as post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) in a randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial during an Omicron BF·7 outbreak in Beijing from November 26 to December 9, 2022. The study enrolled 1,222 healthy adult workers at 21 construction sites within 72 hours of contact with SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals, randomized 3:1 to SA58 (n=901) or placebo (n=321).

In the efficacy analysis of 1,123 SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR-negative participants, symptomatic COVID-19 occurred in 7 of 824 SA58 recipients versus 14 of 299 placebo recipients, yielding a treatment efficacy of 80·82% (95%CI 52·41%-92·27%). Efficacy against SARS-CoV-2 infection was 61·83% (95%CI 37·50%-76·69%). All 21 sequenced samples were Omicron BF·7.

Adverse events were reported by 25% of SA58 and 22% of placebo recipients, all Grade 1, with no SAEs or AESIs. Common events included nasal mucosal dryness, runny nose, and headache.

Limitations included early study termination, a young healthy population, and short follow-up. The authors recommend further evaluation in high-risk populations.

A medical system assists rescuers during endotracheal (ET) tube intubation procedures, including rapid sequence intubation (RSI). The system includes airflow sensors (oxygen, flow, or capnography) that detect airflow in the patient's airway, physiological sensors (capnography, impedance, acoustic, pulse oximeter, ECG, or blood pressure sensors) that monitor airflow in the patient's lungs, and a patient monitoring device with a processor, memory, and user interface.

The processor receives airflow data, determines airflow presence, initiates a timer (typically 5-15 seconds, default or user-defined), evaluates whether the ET tube is properly placed based on physiological data, and displays results on a user interface.

Proper placement determinations may rely on ETCO2 values, transthoracic impedance, or acoustic spectral patterns meeting predetermined criteria such as thresholds, trends, or deviations from initial or dynamic baselines (moving averages of measured values after tube placement).

The patient monitoring device may be an automated external defibrillator or professional defibrillator with a touchscreen display and various inputs (softkeys, buttons, knobs, switches). It may connect with portable computing devices (tablets, smartphones, laptops) for transmitting patient information (height, weight, gender) and accessing central facilities for additional data.

The system automatically detects RSI steps—Preparation, Preoxygenation, Pretreatment, Paralysis, Positioning, Placement with Proof, and Post-intubation management—based on changes in intubation parameters (gas, physiological, positioning). It provides context-sensitive feedback, alarms for hypoxemia, drug dosage calculations, event markers, and verification that positive pressure breaths reach the lungs. Wrist-worn devices and heads-up displays may provide additional visual, audible, or haptic feedback to rescuers.

California Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 53, a landmark AI safety law requiring major AI companies to publicly disclose plans for mitigating risks from advanced AI models. Authored by State Sen. Researchers at the University of California, Irvine and other institutions have developed a new satellite-based drought severity index using data from NASA's Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) mission. Unlike conventional tools that primarily track precipitation, the GRACE-DSI incorporates terrestrial water storage, including groundwater, to assess drought conditions. According to UCI professor Isabella Velicogna, the index enables accurate, continuous, and globally consistent drought monitoring, even in regions where ground-based readings are difficult to collect. The twin GRACE satellites observe a large area of Earth's surface, allowing both regional and global-scale monitoring, and the index tracks groundwater changes that affect soil moisture and drought recovery. The dataset currently covers 2002 to 2014 and will be extended through the ongoing mission and a follow-on mission scheduled for launch in early 2018. Evaluations in the continental United States showed significant agreement with established indices such as the Palmer drought severity index. Findings were published in the Journal of Hydrometeorology and presented at the American Geophysical Union fall meeting.
