WIRED reviews white noise machines for adults, children, and pets. The article explains that "white noise" and "sound machine" are used interchangeably, though noise comes in different "colors" (white, pink, brown) corresponding to sound spectrum ranges, with pink and brown being less grating.

Top picks include the LectroFan Classic (compact, multiple fan and color noise options, up to 85 decibels), the Snooz (simple fan-generated white noise), the Hatch Restore 3 (sunrise clock with 58 sounds, subscription-based), the Hatch Rest 2nd gen (night-light and sound machine for children), the Babelio mini (suitable for pets), the Yogasleep Dohm (a reliable option since 1962), and portable options from Momcozy and ErgoPouch. Google and Alexa smart speakers can also function as sound machines.

For children, machines should play below certain volumes and be placed at least 6.5 feet away. Buyers should verify whether machines run continuously or on timers. Fans can substitute for white noise machines. WIRED donates tested products to local communities.

The Inverted Hammer is a bullish reversal candlestick pattern forming at the bottom of a downtrend, characterized by a small body at the lower end, little or no lower shadow, and a long upper shadow. It signals that buyers are gaining momentum against sellers, potentially indicating an upward price reversal.

The pattern should not be used alone but combined with other tools like trendlines, support levels, moving averages, and momentum oscillators for confirmation. Traders commonly use it for swing trading in uptrends or mean reversion strategies in oversold conditions, with proper risk management including stop-losses and position sizing.

Backtests on the S&P 500 show 132 occurrences since 1993, with win ratios of 53-65% when exiting after 1-10 days, and an average gain of 0.36% per trade. It ranks 11th in frequency among 75 candlestick patterns. The pattern tends to be bearish in overbought conditions and bullish in oversold conditions. It differs from the Shooting Star, which forms at the top of uptrends. Disadvantages include subjectivity, potential false signals, and unsuitability across all timeframes.

President Trump is set to direct U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer to determine whether to investigate Chinese trade practices that force U.S. firms to transfer intellectual property, according to senior administration officials. The move could eventually result in tariffs on Chinese goods under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the president to impose trade restrictions unilaterally. Officials said the trade probe is unrelated to ongoing diplomacy over North Korea, though Trump had postponed the announcement earlier while seeking Beijing's cooperation on Pyongyang. Any investigation could take up to a year, and the issue may be resolved through negotiation. Concerns about Chinese intellectual property theft have also been raised by the EU, Japan, Germany, and Canada.

Violet Brown, a 117-year-old woman from Duanvale, Jamaica, is believed to have become the world's oldest living person following the death of Italy's Emma Morano. According to Robert Young of the Gerontology Research Group, Brown, born March 10, 1900, is the oldest person with credible birth documentation, verified through a British colonial-era birth certificate. Guinness World Records has not yet officially declared her the title holder, stating its verification process is complex and ongoing. Brown, who lives with her 97-year-old son and two caregivers, is hard of hearing but responsive. A former sugarcane farmer, she attributes her longevity to hard work and her Christian faith.

A University of California, Davis study published in Annals of Epidemiology reviewed 50,921 California firearm deaths from 2000 to 2015, finding gun homicides declined from 4.19 to 3.13 per 100,000 people, largely due to reduced gang violence in Los Angeles County. Gun homicides of black men fell 32 percent from their 2005 peak, while Hispanic male homicides dropped 38 percent. Rates for White and Asian men remained steady. Researcher Veronica Pear hopes the study serves as a template for other states. Federal gun-violence research has been restricted for 30 years following NRA lobbying, though California funded UC Davis's program with $5 million, and Kaiser Permanente pledged $2 million for related research.

Digital laggards set aspirational goals that lack grounding in data, leading employees to avoid measurement and default to qualitative, process-focused approaches that stifle innovation. They also struggle to connect goals with strategy, resulting in organizational misalignment exacerbated by a "culture of genius."

In contrast, digital leaders use data-driven objectives as coordinating functions, developed through transparent, combined top-down and bottom-up methodologies that align teams around a shared "North Star" vision. However, even leaders risk over-relying on data, potentially bogging down simple decisions in exhaustive analysis.

Data culture aligns organizations both vertically (linking individuals to company goals) and horizontally (enabling inter-functional collaboration). Digital leaders treat data culture as central, ensuring consistency between leadership beliefs, stated values, and employee behaviors. Laggards often recognize the importance of data culture but fail to align behavior with ambitions due to entrenched habits and insufficient focus.

Organizations typically fall into four patterns based on culture and technical sophistication: data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant. Each can target specific actions to build a stronger data culture, as laggards are not doomed—many leaders have successfully transformed.

NVIDIA's A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture and built on TSMC's 7nm process, is the company's 8th generation data center GPU, containing 54.2 billion transistors on an 826 mm² die. It builds on the V100 with 108 SMs, third-generation Tensor Cores, and support for new data types including TF32, BF16, FP64, and INT8, delivering up to 20x faster performance than V100 for certain workloads. Key features include a new Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity capability that doubles throughput, 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache (nearly 7x larger than V100), and third-generation NVLink providing 600 GB/sec total bandwidth. The new Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) feature allows partitioning a single A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, benefiting Cloud Service Providers by improving utilization and providing fault isolation. The A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, asynchronous copy and barrier instructions, and enhanced error detection. CUDA 11 provides programming support for these features, including Task Graph acceleration and L2 cache residency controls. The A100 powers the NVIDIA DGX A100 system, which delivers 5 PFLOPS of AI performance using eight A100 GPUs connected via NVSwitches.

This study presents an ion-sensitive field-effect transistor (ISFET) Lab-on-Chip (LoC) device for detecting circulating nucleic acid biomarkers in prostate cancer (PCa) patients. Current PCa diagnostics rely on PSA testing (with up to 47% false positives), mpMRI, and invasive biopsies, creating a need for rapid point-of-care alternatives. The researchers targeted three biomarkers: YAP1 nucleic acid, full-length androgen receptor (AR-FL) mRNA, and AR-V7 mRNA variant, using reverse transcriptase pH-sensitive loop-mediated isothermal amplification (RT-pHLAMP).

After optimizing RNA extraction using TRIzol LS reagent, the team tested blood plasma from 13 PCa patients. YAP1 nucleic acid was detected in 62% of samples via RT-qPCR, with 92.3% concordance with benchtop RT-pHLAMP results. LoC detection occurred within approximately 10 minutes, compared to 2.5 hours for RT-qPCR. AR-FL mRNA amplification and AR-V7 mRNA were observed only in high-risk and metastatic patients. YAP1 nucleic acid presence significantly correlated with more advanced cancer staging (p=0.043) and higher initial PSA levels (p=0.035).

The device achieved 100% concordance with benchtop RT-pHLAMP assays for both YAP1 and AR-FL detection and successfully performed simultaneous multiplex detection using a dual-well manifold. This represents the first ISFET-based biosensor capable of detecting endogenous nucleic acids from cancer patient blood, offering potential for rapid, minimally-invasive PCa prognostics at point-of-care.

Mark Schroeder responds to Steven Kean regarding a forwarded McKinsey memo on international power sector restructuring. Schroeder notes the EU summary provides a useful overview but contains errors: the Spanish pool is not mandatory for those owning generation in-country, Denmark has more than two generators due to municipal ownership, and transitional anti-competitive arrangements in the Netherlands are not addressed. He also points out that Poland, the most progressive former Communist country in terms of reform, was omitted from the Central and Eastern Europe discussion.

The forwarded McKinsey memo, authored by Carol B. White and Pru Sheppard, provides a June-November 2000 update on global power sector privatization and restructuring. Key themes include: governments opening generation markets to foreign investors, unbundling of state-owned utilities, introduction of wholesale and retail competition, and some international players retreating to less risky markets. The memo details country-by-country developments across Europe, Central/Eastern Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and the Middle East/Africa, covering market opening timelines, privatization progress, mergers and acquisitions, regulatory changes, and IPP activity. Regional trends noted include EU Directive-driven competition in Europe, recovery-driven restructuring in Asia, postponed privatizations in Latin America due to currency issues, and growing IPP activity and regional transmission links in Africa and the Middle East.

European shares rebounded on Monday following their worst weekly losses of the year caused by US-North Korea tensions. The STOXX 600 rose 0.7 percent, with banking leading gains at 1.4 percent. RWE jumped 3 percent after targeting the top end of its 2017 profit forecast. Danone gained 2 percent on bid speculation, while Standard Life Aberdeen rose 2.7 percent on its first trading day. Ladbrokes Coral fell 2.7 percent after a Credit Suisse downgrade. With 82 percent of MSCI Europe quarterly results reported, energy and basic materials outperformed, while consumer cyclical and industrial companies missed expectations.

Compass Minerals International, led by CEO Michael Ducey, prepared for its IPO on December 12, 2003, led by Goldman Sachs. The company had been acquired by Apollo Management from IMC Global in 2001, with Ducey joining in April 2002.

Salt, historically valuable and used as currency, is produced through three main methods: rock salt mining (cheapest dry form, 45-65% recovery), mechanical/vacuum pan evaporation (purest and most expensive), and solar evaporation. Brine is the cheapest overall form. U.S. salt is primarily used for highway deicing (about one-third of consumption), chemicals, food processing, water treatment, and agriculture.

The U.S. salt industry has consolidated significantly, from 160 establishments in 1900 to 66 establishments owned by 29 firms in the early 2000s. Production is capital-intensive with high transportation costs, making location critical. Historical attempts at price coordination frequently collapsed into price wars. Total U.S. production averaged 40 million metric tons annually since the 1970s, with prices around $25/metric ton.

Environmental concerns were growing, as road salt caused rising chloride concentrations in freshwater systems, damaging plants and aquatic life. Though unregulated in the U.S., Canada was considering regulation.

Compass Minerals' subsidiary, North American Salt, was the third-largest U.S. salt producer. General trade salt comprised over 50% of its revenue, with highway deicing at about 40%. The company operated mines and plants across North America and the U.K., employed 1,541 people (37% unionized), and emphasized safety, workforce training, and execution.

Ducey considered how to position the company for investors amid regulatory threats but strong demand and few substitutes, while exploring new uses for salt mines including storage and nuclear waste disposal.

In his sixth and final State of the Union address, the President reviews past achievements and outlines unfinished commitments. He cites accomplishments including Medicare, voting rights legislation, federal education aid, Head Start, job training for five million Americans, land conservation, and an unemployment rate of 3.3 percent.

He urges Congress to fund ongoing commitments, including the model cities program, 500,000 homes under the Housing Act of 1968, and the creation of an urban development bank. He recommends a 13 percent increase in Social Security benefits, expanded medical care for mothers and children, and protection against catastrophic illness costs. He calls for continuing the antipoverty program, extending the Voting Rights Act, enforcing the Fair Housing Act, funding the Safe Streets Act, and passing firearms licensing and registration.

He proposes postal reorganization based on the Kappel report, modified salary increases for Congress ($42,500), and a random-selection draft system. He reports a projected $2.4 billion surplus for fiscal year 1969 and a $3.4 billion surplus for the next fiscal year, noting President-elect Nixon's support for continuing the surtax.

On foreign policy, he urges Senate ratification of the nonproliferation treaty, resumed arms talks with the Soviet Union, adequate foreign aid, support for European unity, and continued efforts toward peace in Vietnam and the Middle East.

He concludes with personal reflections on his 38 years in the Capitol, acknowledges colleagues from both parties, and urges support for President-elect Nixon.

A study by Rand Corporation, Harvard Medical School, and UCLA surveyed 3,066 American workers in 2015 about their workplace conditions. One in five reported a hostile or threatening social environment at work, with women citing unwanted sexual attention and young men reporting verbal abuse. Two-thirds frequently work under tight deadlines, one in four feels they lack time to complete their job, and over half face unpleasant or hazardous conditions. However, four out of five find their work meaningful, and more than half describe their boss as supportive.

Buyers in online secondary markets for expiring items (e.g., event tickets) strategically delay purchases anticipating price reductions, while sellers face time pressure as unsold items lose all value at expiration. This paper addresses the optimal pricing policy for a monopolist selling a single expiring item to strategic buyers arriving stochastically.

The authors formulate a Stackelberg game in which a time-sensitive seller commits to a pricing schedule, and time-neutral buyers, whose valuations and arrival times are private, choose purchase times. Their contributions are twofold. First, they develop a tractable framework using Value-Based Threshold strategies, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for equilibrium existence under continuous valuation distributions—extending prior work limited to discrete valuations. Second, they derive near-optimal closed-form pricing schedules for two stylized regimes: a constant price in thin markets (low arrival rates) to prevent delay, and a linear discounting schedule in thick markets (high arrival rates) where competition induces myopic buyer behavior.

Numerical simulations confirm these policies' near-optimality and reveal that optimal schedules transition from end-loaded to flat to front-loaded as seller time sensitivity increases. Unlike prior literature assuming buyer impatience, the model assigns time-dependent disutility solely to the seller, better reflecting expiring-item markets.

The toss play is a widespread outside run where the quarterback tosses the ball to a running back aiming for the edge of the defense. Hall of Fame runners like Walter Payton, Barry Sanders, and Marcus Allen frequently used it.

Strengths include its simplicity, ease of teaching and installation, and efficiency in getting the ball to the perimeter. Its primary weakness is dependence on a fast tailback and athletic offensive line; without them, the play suffers. It is also vulnerable to edge blitzes.

Against a 3-4 defense, blocking involves reach and combination blocks, with the tight end sealing the edge, the fullback leading on the nearest unblocked defender, and receivers handling safeties and corners. Against a 4-3 defense, similar combination reach blocks are used across the line.

Variations include the Flexbone "Rocket Toss," where a motioning wingback receives the toss while the fullback serves as a decoy, and the Single Back Toss G Pull, where the playside guard pulls as lead blocker instead of a fullback. The common goal is delivering the ball to the edge before the defense can react.

The speaker observes that opponents are playing the neutral zone differently, with forwards backchecking hard, leaving little space. They acknowledge the need to try something different to get back in the series. While the power play has scored frequently, it underperformed in the last game and requires review and adjustments. The speaker expresses frustration over trailing in the series but notes they have not played many poor games in the playoffs and hopes to return to previous form and tie the series.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting the results of its 2019 Annual Shareholders Meeting held on December 4, 2019. Of 7,632,138,696 shares eligible to vote, 6,610,123,128 were voted. Shareholders elected all thirteen director nominees, approved executive officer compensation on an advisory basis (76.69%), and ratified Deloitte & Touche LLP as the independent auditor for fiscal year 2020 (96.48%). Two shareholder proposals—one concerning a report on employee representation on the Board and another on gender pay gap—were rejected. The report was signed by Keith R. Dolliver, Assistant Secretary, on December 5, 2019.

Diane David appealed a trial court's order dissolving her marriage to Joseph David, challenging the award of the marital residence (a 50-acre farm) to Joseph, the noncustodial parent, and the court's failure to make an equal property division or consider tax consequences of liquidating retirement funds awarded to her.

The parties, married in 1980, separated in 1995 after an incident involving a broken gun cabinet. They stipulated to joint legal custody with Diane having primary physical custody of their two daughters. Both wanted the farm, valued at $96,500. The court awarded Joseph the farm, equipment, cattle, and truck, and awarded Diane Joseph's pension ($28,309) and 401(k) ($22,875). The court declined to equalize the distribution based on Diane's $27,130 separate Public School Retirement System account.

The appellate court held that § 452.330 does not require awarding the marital residence to the custodial parent, and found no abuse of discretion given Joseph's farming use of the tillable acreage. The court rejected Diane's claim that the parties stipulated to equal division, finding no meeting of the minds. Regarding the teacher retirement account, the court distinguished Mallams v. Mallams because Diane could also draw social security from Joseph's account. The tax consequences issue was not preserved for appeal.

However, due to a mathematical error showing Diane's assets as $62,781 instead of $59,182, the case was remanded for reconsideration of the property distribution.

Copper is often considered a leading indicator for stocks because it is used across most economic sectors, so rising demand and prices may signal economic growth, while falling prices may indicate slowdown. The S&P 500 has reached 1,526 all-time highs from 1950 to 2022, averaging nearly 21 per year, or about 8.3% of trading days. Despite spending 91.7% of the time below its peak, the index has compounded at 7.67% CAGR (excluding dividends). A tested strategy buys the S&P 500 when within 5% of its all-time high and sells when it falls more than 5% below. Mean reversion is a statistical and financial concept where asset prices tend to revert to a moving average over time, with abnormal rises and falls correcting themselves. The article presents three free mean reversion strategies applied to the ETFs XLP (consumer staples), FXI (Chinese ETF), and the S&P 500, each with backtested equity curves showing decent returns.

Mean reversion contrasts with trend-following: it typically produces many small winners with occasional large losses. These strategies work best in stocks rather than commodities, partly due to futures arbitrage and the continuous interaction between buyers and sellers.

Counterintuitively, mean reversion performs best during bear markets due to heightened volatility, with long positions often outperforming short ones. Data from the 2008/09 financial crisis showed numerous explosive up days despite the overall 50% decline, making buying weakness profitable. Volatility, illustrated by events like the GFC and 2011 euro crisis, provides the opportunities short-term traders need.

This study examined associations between unintended pregnancy and children's psychosocial problems from preschool age through adolescence, using data from the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development (ABCD) birth cohort (n=7,784). Pregnancy intentions were measured as a multidimensional construct (mistiming, unwantedness, unhappiness), and outcomes were assessed via the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire at ages 5-6, 11-12, and 15-16.

Using Structural Equation Modelling, researchers found that dimensions of unintended pregnancy were associated with more internalizing and externalizing problems in children at preschool age, with small effect sizes. Pregnancy mistiming predicted both problem types, while unwantedness predicted internalizing problems. These associations were largely mediated by maternal bonding problems and, for mistiming, maternal psychosocial distress. No significant associations were found in early or middle adolescence, including in sensitivity analyses using child-reported outcomes.

The authors note that findings differ from prior studies conducted in contexts with restrictive abortion laws, as highly unwanted pregnancies in the Netherlands may have been terminated and excluded from the sample. Limitations include potential selection bias from dropout, reliance on maternal reporting, and absence of paternal data. The authors conclude that maternal mental health and bonding, rather than pregnancy unintendedness itself, should be the focus for supporting children's psychosocial outcomes.

- Each curved data line may include first and second straight line portions connected by a curved portion, either integrally formed at the same layer or at different layers connected through contact holes in an insulating layer.

The "Box and One" is a common combination defense featuring four defenders in a box zone and one "Chaser" in aggressive full pass denial against the opponent's star player. Baseline defenders (X4, X5) shift like a 1-2-2 zone, while outside defenders (X1, X2) shift like a 2-3 zone.

The Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) Specification describes AMD's mechanism for updating firmware without system reboots.

**Co-Signing and Keys**: Customers must provide an RSA public key (2048 or 4096-bit) during early boot via SET_CUST_SFS_SIGNATURE, before BOOT_DONE, and cannot update it afterward. Customers co-sign update packages using RSA-PSS (SHA256 for 2048-bit, SHA384 for 4096-bit keys).

**Update Packages**: Packages are non-persistent across reboots and can patch registers, firmware images, or components like drivers. SEV updates auto-commit and require reboot to revert. SNP-enabled systems require HV-FIXED pages via RMPUPDATE. Each package validates firmware versions before applying, and partial application is avoided to prevent forced resets.

**Command Process**: SFS commands require 2MB-aligned TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER in DRAM. The deployment agent appends co-signing headers, AMD update packages, and signatures, then communicates via the TEE mailbox interface. Software checks bit 3 (SFS_ENABLED) of the ASP Feature Register, polls the Ready flag, writes the buffer address, and issues the command.

**ASP Processing**: The ASP protects DRAM from x86 access, verifies customer and AMD signatures, executes the patch, and updates patch level information.

**Version Information**: GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO returns current SFS patch level, System Patch Level, and firmware version triplets (type, version, SPL) using two contiguous pages.

**Package Naming**: Follows format fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg.

**Performance**: Updates run parallel to x86/DMA traffic with minimal impact. SEV/SNP VMs continue operating across SEV firmware updates, while SEV/ES VMs must stop and restart.

Dane Gudauskas, interviewed after returning from Fiji, described riding what may be the best wave of his life during the XXL Cloudbreak swell. Despite challenging weather and wind conditions that made many surfers hesitant, Gudauskas decided to paddle out after watching Shaun Lopez tow in. On his third wave attempt, he caught a massive left, eventually getting wiped out and breaking his board—a 8'6" Channel Islands quad, the same board used during his 2016 Cloudbreak ride. He noted this swell had significantly more power and speed than the 2016 event, and admitted he felt undergunned, preferring a board over 9 feet in hindsight. Gudauskas called it the most intense surf experience of his life, praising the water safety crews from Tavarua, Namotu, and the mainland. He plans to recover by longboarding at San Onofre.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2022. A 20-for-1 stock split was effected on May 27, 2022, with 10,201,654,176 shares outstanding as of October 19, 2022. Effective January 1, 2022, the company extended the useful lives of servers from four to five years and networking equipment from five to six years, reducing Q3 2022 depreciation by $882 million. Total net sales rose 15% to $127.1 billion in Q3 2022, while operating income fell to $2.5 billion from $4.9 billion. Net income was $2.9 billion in Q3 2022, but a net loss of $3.0 billion was reported for the nine months, impacted by a $10.4 billion valuation loss on the Rivian equity investment. Amazon acquired MGM Holdings for approximately $6.1 billion in March 2022 and announced agreements to acquire One Medical ($3.9 billion) and iRobot ($1.7 billion). Long-term debt totaled $58.9 billion, including $12.8 billion in notes issued in April 2022. The company repurchased $6.0 billion of common stock under a $10.0 billion authorization. Segment results showed North America and International operating losses, offset by AWS operating income of $5.4 billion on sales of $20.5 billion. Ongoing legal and tax matters include antitrust litigation, patent disputes, and a Luxembourg state aid case.

Mr. Heard reports to Mr. Gresham on conditions in Korea. In the first dispatch, he notes that Seoul remained quiet after April 20, and communications with Captain Dayton of the Petrel and Commander Book of the Alert led both vessels to depart by late April. Investigators sent to southern provinces, including a Christian traveler and Roman Catholic priests, reported no evidence of Tong Hâk assemblages, though discontent due to official exactions was expected to produce continued rumors.

In the second dispatch, Heard reports that thousands of Tong Hâk had gathered at Po-eun in Ch'ung ch'ong Do, drilling and displaying a flag reading "Down with the Japanese and foreigners! May the right flourish!" They refused to disperse when a government officer remonstrated. On May 15, 800 troops with three Gatling guns were sent toward Suwen and possibly Chong-ju. Heard believed the Tong Hâk themselves were not dangerous but had attracted discontented people, and suspected an unknown political party directed the movement. The Alert remained at Chemulpo as a precaution.

Biocon India, founded in 1978 by Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, grew from an enzyme manufacturer into a pharmaceutical firm with 800 employees and $75 million in revenue by 2003. Following an "earn as you learn" philosophy, Biocon expanded into generic drugs and established Syngene, a contract research organization (CRO) serving global pharmaceutical clients.

India's pharmaceutical industry benefited from 1970 regulations permitting generic reproduction of patented drugs, a large pool of low-cost English-speaking scientists, genetic diversity for trials, and government support for biotech. Global pharmaceutical firms increasingly outsourced R&D, clinical trials, and manufacturing to India to reduce costs.

In 2000, Biocon launched Clinigene to enter clinical trials, aiming to become a fully integrated drug discovery and development company. Clinigene initially focused on lab services, bio-equivalence/bio-availability studies, and hospital partnerships.

Mazumdar-Shaw faced several concerns about Clinigene: uncertain market positioning against foreign CROs and in-house centers of major pharmaceutical firms, potential disruption of Biocon's collaborative culture if Clinigene grew rapidly, and ethical and publicity risks associated with conducting trials on Indian subjects for Western firms. She had to decide whether to aggressively expand Clinigene, limit it to safer low-value services, or acquire an existing CRO.

The Friday seasonality strategy in crude oil trading involves buying oil assets on Thursday's close, anticipating a price rise on Friday. It performs better when Thursday is a down day, particularly when USO falls at least 0.75 times the 25-day average of high minus low. Historical data from April 2006 onward shows a P/L of 56.96% across 98 trades, with 60 winners and an average profit per trade of 0.58%. Other weekdays display more random patterns.

Virtual machines use architectural APIC for interrupt delivery, including synthetic host messages. The #HV doorbell page aligns with APIC behavior to reuse guest interrupt logic. It contains two fields: a 16-bit PendingEvent field (bytes 0-1) and a NoEoiRequired EOI assist (byte 2). Bytes 3-63 are reserved for future use, while the remainder is unspecified and available for the virtualization stack's message formats. The doorbell page must be backed by a host-owned physical page (not assigned with RMPUPDATE), and guest accesses must use C=0.

The ADS868xW is a family of single-channel, 16-bit data acquisition devices with a successive approximation register (SAR) ADC and analog front-end circuit. Operating on a 5V supply, they support bipolar and unipolar input ranges up to ±12.288V and feature high input impedance (≥1MΩ), a programmable gain amplifier, a second-order low-pass antialiasing filter, overvoltage protection up to ±20V, and a 4.096V internal reference.

The devices use a multiSPI interface supporting legacy SPI and source-synchronous protocols, with single or dual SDO configurations and daisy-chain capability. Nine configuration registers control device operation, including input range selection, reset/power control, data output formatting, and alarm thresholds. Input and AVDD alarm functions with programmable thresholds and hysteresis are provided.

The devices operate in RESET, ACQ, and CONV states, and offer NAP and power-down modes for reduced consumption. Applications include programmable logic controllers and data acquisition systems, with recommended decoupling capacitors on AVDD, DVDD, REFCAP, and REFIO pins.

On Aug. 6, Dylan Kennedy, 19, was stopped for speeding and cited for marijuana possession and drug paraphernalia after officers spotted a jar of suspected marijuana in his vehicle. On Aug. 5, Caton Preston, 18, was charged with underage alcohol possession and third-degree forgery for producing a fake license. Police collected 75 pounds of unused prescription drugs for incineration. Three children received trespassing warrants at Falls Hole restaurant on Aug. 5, and a smashed mailbox on Topstone Road is being investigated. Total calls logged: 204.

The President reports that the United States continues to grow rapidly in population and territory, with eleven new states admitted and strong bonds between national and state governments. Foreign relations are generally friendly. The 1822 navigation convention with France remains in force, though indemnity claims for spoliations are unresolved. Commercial relations with Britain continue under the 1815 convention, but West Indies trade and boundary disputes from the Treaty of Ghent remain unsettled. A convention with Britain to suppress the slave trade by declaring it piracy was signed in March 1824 but faces ratification obstacles. Reciprocity agreements exist with Sweden, Russia, the Netherlands, Prussia, and others. A convention with Russia concerning the Northwest coast was signed in April. Relations with new South American republics and Brazil are friendly.

Treasury receipts for the year will exceed $18.5 million. Loans at 4.5% were authorized to refinance war debt and fund Florida treaty awards. The public debt, estimated at $79 million (excluding bank stock), could be discharged within ten years.

The military academy is functioning well, and artillery training has been centralized at Old Point Comfort. Coastal fortifications and Navy augmentation continue. A board is surveying potential roads and canals per the April 30 act. Relations with most Indian tribes are peaceful, though hostilities continue on the Missouri and Upper Mississippi; 32 schools serve 916 Indian students.

Naval squadrons operate in the Mediterranean, Gulf of Mexico (suppressing piracy), and Pacific. General Lafayette arrived in August and was warmly received; the President recommends compensation for his services.

The President recommends reorganizing the Supreme Court to exempt justices from circuit duties, developing a plan to relocate and civilize Indian tribes in territory west of current states, establishing a military post at the Columbia River, and improving Washington city. He concludes by expressing gratitude for public confidence during his service.

Mali's gold exports are declining as legacy mines wind down, and the future of the Sadiola mine hangs on stalled negotiations over a $380 million investment to extend its life by 10 years and access 3.4 million ounces of reserves. Sadiola, a joint venture between IAMGOLD (41%), AngloGold Ashanti (41%), and the Government of Mali (18%), has been operating for 20 years but is depleting its soft-rock deposits. The proposed investment would modify the plant to process hard-rock sulphides beneath.

Two other legacy mines—Morila and Yatela—are closing or depleted. Industrial gold production is projected to fall to 45 tonnes in 2017, with no new mines expected until 2018. Gold accounts for 25-30% of government revenues, and Sadiola employs around 1,000 people, 93% Malian. Expansion would preserve and expand jobs, connect the mine to Mali's power grid, and potentially aid local villages.

With elections in 2018, the government faces uncertainty that could affect mining deals and the broader investment climate. IAMGOLD CEO Stephen Letwin emphasized the company's continued commitment to Mali but did not comment on rumors of a deadlock.

NVIDIA RTX IO improves game loading and frame rates by enabling fast data streaming from SSDs directly to the GPU, with GPU-based lossless decompression. It integrates with Microsoft's DirectStorage API, reducing CPU load and improving I/O performance significantly. RTX IO also benefits professionals working with large datasets, such as CAD models and 3D visualizations.

The NVIDIA A40, based on the GA10x Ampere architecture, is designed for data center visual computing. Compared to the Quadro RTX 6000, it offers up to 2X FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 10X AI training performance. It features 48GB of memory (scalable to 96GB via NVLink), PCIe Gen4, three DisplayPort outputs, and supports NVIDIA vGPU software and the EGX Platform.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz displays via DisplayPort 1.4a and are the first discrete GPUs with HDMI 2.1 support (48 Gbps bandwidth), along with HDCP 2.3.

The fifth-generation NVDEC decoder supports hardware-accelerated decoding for various codecs, including AV1—GA10x being the first GPUs with AV1 hardware decode, capable of 8K60 HDR playback with minimal CPU usage. The seventh-generation NVENC encoder enables high-quality video encoding up to 4K (H.264) and 8K (HEVC).

The GA10x Ampere architecture delivers up to 2X performance in shading, ray tracing, and AI, featuring second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with sparsity support, and first-ever GDDR6X memory (up to 19.5 Gbps, 936 GB/sec in RTX 3090).

The GeForce RTX 3090 includes 82 SMs, 10496 CUDA Cores, and 24GB GDDR6X, delivering 1.5X the performance of Titan RTX. The RTX 3070 uses the GA104 GPU with GDDR6, outperforming the RTX 2080 Ti.

Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology on GDDR6X helps overclockers identify memory limits through performance plateauing instead of crashes.

The NVIDIA RTX A6000 features a GA102 GPU with 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 48GB GDDR6 (scalable to 96GB via NVLink), offering significant performance gains over the RTX 6000 in rendering, HPC, and deep learning workloads.

This study presents near-infrared (NIR) spectral measurements of water ice, epsomite, and halite, along with their mixtures, at cryogenic temperatures relevant to Europa's surface. The authors developed the CRONOS facility at Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory, using a nitrogen-purged glove box to prepare and measure discrete grain mixtures across four grain size bins (<63 µm, 63-250 µm, 250-500 µm, >500 µm) at temperatures of approximately 100-120 K. Unlike previous studies using frozen salty aqueous solutions, the authors mixed discrete grains to better represent Europa's radiolytically desiccated surface.

The laboratory spectra were compared with both linearly-mixed and intimately-mixed models generated using Hapke radiative transfer theory and published optical constants. Key findings include: (1) linearly- and intimately-mixed models of water ice produced comparable fits to laboratory data, generally within 10% reflectance; (2) smaller grain sizes disproportionately influence mixture spectra; (3) halite-water ice mixtures were nearly indistinguishable from pure water ice; and (4) published "cryogenic" epsomite optical constants appear to have been recorded at ambient conditions, causing significant discrepancies with laboratory data.

The authors conclude that quantitative spectral mixture analyses using optical constants are necessary for accurate compositional and grain size determinations, particularly in preparation for NASA's Europa Clipper (MISE) and ESA's JUICE (MAJIS) missions. They recommend both linear and intimate unmixing approaches to assess abundance uncertainty and note that updated epsomite optical constants are needed in future work.

The Sri Lankan rupee declined for a third session on Wednesday, closing at 158.60/75 per dollar, as importer dollar demand exceeded remittance inflows. Dealers attributed emerging market currency pressure to rising Fed rates, the US-China trade war, and higher oil prices. The rupee has fallen 3.4% this year, hitting a record low of 160.17 on June 20. Moody's warned that a strengthening dollar has increased credit risk and could reduce foreign reserves in countries including Sri Lanka. Pressure eased somewhat after a $584 million payment from China Merchants Port Holdings for the Hambantota port deal. The IMF cautioned that Sri Lanka's economy remains vulnerable due to public debt. Foreign investors sold a net 3.5 billion rupees in government securities in the week ending June 27.

An Uzbek court convicted Zokir Aliyev, a 46-year-old Uzbek-born U.S. citizen, of publicly calling for the government's overthrow and participating in an extremist group, but fined him only $67 due to the offences dating from December 1999. Detained on June 16 by Uzbekistan's state security service on suspicion of belonging to the Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan (IMU), Aliyev was released after six days. Authorities said he had been on their wanted list since 2005 and suspected he trained with IMU fighters in Afghanistan. Aliyev denied IMU involvement, stating he only attended Uzbek opposition meetings in Turkey in the 1990s. The U.S. embassy declined to comment.

The President responds to a Senate resolution regarding a forcible resistance to U.S. law enforcement in Boston. He describes the incident as an unexpected violation of federal authority, contrary to the general sentiment of Massachusetts citizens, and attributes it partly to negligence and lack of preparation.

He cites congressional resolutions from 1789, 1791, and 1821 regarding the use of state jails for federal prisoners, and notes that Massachusetts' 1843 law prohibited state officials from enforcing the federal Fugitive Slave Act of 1793 and denied use of state jails for fugitive slave detention. Though such state laws create difficulties, they cannot override federal constitutional obligations. The marshal of Massachusetts was empowered to hire a temporary jail but apparently did not do so.

Regarding enforcement authority, the President explains that the Constitution places the Army and Navy under executive control, while the militia can only be called forth per congressional authorization. He references the 1795 and 1807 acts and suggests Congress modify the proclamation requirement, as advance notice could undermine arrests. He also raises whether marshals may summon organized militia as posse comitatus.

The President pledges to faithfully execute the laws and suppress forcible opposition.

A separate April 25, 1851 proclamation warns citizens against joining military expeditions to invade Cuba, a Spanish colony at peace with the U.S. Such expeditions violate federal law, carrying fines up to $3,000 and imprisonment up to three years. Participants forfeit government protection, and officials are directed to arrest offenders.

Options trading in NVDA is an investment strategy that allows investors to leverage small investments for potentially large profits, with losses on long options limited to the premium paid. Available options include calls, puts, straddles, strangles, spreads, and collars, each with distinct risk-reward profiles.

Option prices in NVDA depend on the underlying stock price, time to expiration, implied volatility, market sentiment, and dividends. Rising stock prices generally increase call values and decrease put values, while dividends have the opposite effect. Implied volatility, often calculated via the Black-Scholes model, is a key premium determinant.

NVDA options are typically liquid. Margin requirements are lower for buying than writing options. Risks include adverse price movement, time decay, volatility, and liquidity. Strategies to manage risk include stop-loss orders, protective puts, hedging, diversification, and position sizing. Returns can be maximized through leverage, deep in-the-money options, covered calls, and bullish spreads.

Effective analysis combines quantitative and qualitative methods. Options trading is generally subject to capital gains tax. The article emphasizes that options are complex and require both theoretical understanding and practical experience.

The 2018-19 Union Budget, presented by Finance Minister Arun Jaitley, lacks a dedicated section for women, unlike previous Budgets. Economists offer mixed views on its impact on women. Dr. Jayati Ghosh and Dr. Ratna Sudarshan argue the Budget reinforces traditional gender roles without addressing barriers women face. The National Health Protection Scheme, offering Rs 5 lakh insurance to 10 crore families, is viewed positively by Dr. Devaki Jain and Dr. Sudarshan for improving women's healthcare access, though Dr. Reetika Khera questions its effectiveness based on its predecessor, RSBY. Dr. Ghosh criticizes the lack of budgetary allocations for major promises, noting only a 2.7% increase in health allocations and cuts to the National Health Mission. MSME tax cuts may benefit women-employing small industries. However, maternity entitlement funding was reduced to Rs 2,400 crore against a required Rs 8,000 crore, and the Ujjwala LPG scheme's expansion ignores affordability issues preventing refills. Overall, experts see the Budget as largely a continuation of existing approaches rather than transformative for women.

The speaker expresses happiness about playing near Quebec after eight months away, noting family members who have supported his career will attend the game. He attributes the team's success to hard work, preparation, and efforts made since last summer's training camp, adding that luck in hockey is created through hard work. He acknowledges the opposing team will be tough to beat at home and emphasizes matching their intensity, taking it one game and shift at a time. He states his team is comfortable playing both home and away, citing their size, toughness, and skating ability. He anticipates a loud, exciting atmosphere and stresses the importance of the first ten minutes to quiet the crowd and execute their game plan.

USB technology remains widely used but has become increasingly complex. USB-C and USB-A refer to connector shapes, with USB-C being smaller, reversible, and more capable than USB-A, which has a 5-volt power limit. Older connector types like USB-B and Micro-USB still exist on some devices.

USB specifications, managed by the USB Implementers Forum, determine data transfer and power capabilities. In any connection, speed defaults to the slowest component. USB4, introduced in 2022, supports 20–40 Gbps and is exclusive to USB-C; USB4 Version 2 can reach 120 Gbps but isn't widely adopted. USB 3.0 branding is inconsistent, so checking actual speed ratings is recommended. USB-A maxes out at 20 Gbps.

USB Power Delivery (USB-PD) charges devices, with USB-PD 3.1 supporting up to 240 watts. DisplayPort Alt Mode transmits audio and video via USB-C, with capabilities depending on the DisplayPort generation used.

Thunderbolt, an Intel standard using the USB-C connector, enforces stricter certification. Thunderbolt 4, built on USB4, guarantees 40 Gbps, 100-watt power delivery, and dual 4K displays. Thunderbolt 5, emerging in 2025, offers 80 Gbps bidirectional bandwidth (up to 120 Gbps unidirectional), supports higher-resolution displays, and delivers up to 240 watts.

To ensure proper performance, users should use cables provided with devices or check listed speed and wattage ratings rather than relying on USB version names.

The speaker argues that the nation has entered its fifth year under a policy intended to end slavery agitation, which has instead intensified. He contends the country cannot remain permanently half slave and half free; it must become one or the other.

He traces a sequence of events—the Nebraska bill repealing the Missouri Compromise, the "squatter sovereignty" argument, the delayed Dred Scott decision, and presidential endorsements—suggesting these fit together too precisely to be coincidental, implying coordinated design among figures like Stephen (Douglas), Franklin (Pierce), Roger (Taney), and James (Buchanan).

He identifies three working points of the Dred Scott decision: denying citizenship to Black people, prohibiting Congress or territorial legislatures from excluding slavery, and leaving to slave states the question of whether slavery persists when a slave enters a free state. He warns a future decision may forbid states themselves from excluding slavery, making it lawful everywhere.

The speaker rejects the idea that Senator Douglas is a suitable ally, arguing Douglas does not oppose slavery's expansion and has reduced slavery to a property question. He concludes that the cause must be led by committed Republicans, who, though gathered from diverse elements, will ultimately succeed if they remain firm.

Henry J. Adams III participated in an October 2012 bank robbery as a lookout and recruited a friend to drive a getaway car. After pleading guilty to armed bank robbery, he received an above-guidelines sentence of 140 months' imprisonment. On appeal, Adams argued he should have received an offense-level reduction as a minor participant and that the district court abused its discretion in imposing an above-guidelines sentence.

The Tenth Circuit affirmed. The court held Adams was not entitled to a minor-participant reduction because he helped plan the robbery, served as lookout, provided transportation, and expected compensation. Citing Lockhart and persuasive decisions from other circuits, the court found his role comparable to defendants denied such reductions.

Regarding the sentence, the court determined it was a variance rather than a departure, based on the district court's explicit reliance on § 3553(a) factors and its Statement of Reasons. This rendered most of Adams's arguments—which relied on departure law—inapplicable. The court found the variance substantively reasonable given Adams's extensive criminal history, which included 50% more points than needed for category VI and repeated reoffending. The court rejected Adams's disparity argument comparing his sentence to codefendant Nixon's, noting § 3553(a)(6) concerns nationwide disparities.

Chelsea and Real Madrid are reportedly attempting to outbid Tottenham for Ajax defender Davinson Sanchez, valued at £40m. The 21-year-old was dropped at the weekend after telling staff he wasn't mentally ready to play. According to The Daily Mail, Tottenham plan to hold talks on Monday, offering an initial £28m. Chelsea and Real Madrid are preparing counter bids that could exceed Tottenham's offer. Sanchez reportedly wants to leave Ajax to play in the Premier League and Champions League. Tottenham have yet to sign anyone this transfer window.

The stick concept is a quick-game passing play used in West Coast and Air Raid offenses, designed for fast QB decisions. It features five eligible receivers releasing downfield, with the tight end typically serving as the primary target on an adjustable "stick" route.

The concept performs well against man coverage, Cover 3, and Cover 4, but struggles against Cover 2, where the cornerback becomes the flat defender and can undercut the arrow route. Against Cover 2, the "hole shot" throw to the Z receiver becomes an option, though it requires a strong-armed, anticipatory QB.

Route assignments differ between man and zone coverage, particularly for the TE, who runs a speed-out against man and settles in zone voids against zone. Pre-snap, the QB identifies the flat defender and throws based on that defender's post-snap movement—to the arrow if the defender honors the TE, or to the stick if the defender widens.

Variations include a 2x2 condensed formation read outside-in, and "Sticko," a counter using double moves where the TE fakes the stick before going vertical, paired with a delayed slant and backside sluggo.

President Bush addresses Congress on the state of the Union, outlining domestic and foreign priorities. Domestically, he proposes making income tax reductions permanent, eliminating double taxation of dividends, limiting federal spending growth to 4%, and allowing younger workers to invest in retirement accounts. He calls for Medicare reform with $400 billion over a decade, medical liability reform, and opposes nationalized health care. He proposes a hydrogen fuel research initiative, Clear Skies legislation, and a Healthy Forests Initiative. Compassion initiatives include a Faith-Based Initiative, $450 million for mentoring disadvantaged youth, and $600 million for drug treatment. He asks for bans on partial-birth abortion and human cloning.

Internationally, Bush announces the Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief, committing $15 billion over five years to combat AIDS in Africa and the Caribbean. On terrorism, he reports over 3,000 suspected terrorists arrested and proposes Project BioShield ($6 billion) and a Terrorist Threat Integration Center. He identifies Iran, North Korea, and Iraq as threats involving weapons of mass destruction. Citing Saddam Hussein's failure to account for biological, chemical, and nuclear materials, obstruction of inspectors, and alleged ties to Al Qaeda, Bush announces Secretary Powell will present evidence to the U.N. Shares of Walgreens Boots Alliance, CVS Health, and Rite Aid fell on Friday following reports that Amazon.com is considering entering the online drug retail market. According to Leerink analyst Ana Gupte, Amazon is in talks with mid-market pharmacy benefit managers and hiring staff to evaluate the sector, with entry likely within two years. CNBC reported Amazon would decide before Thanksgiving whether to sell prescription drugs online. Amazon declined to comment. Walgreens shares closed down 5.8 percent, while Rite Aid and CVS Health each fell 4.9 percent.

This study examines the value loads conveyed through words in reading texts of 2nd, 3rd, and 4th grade Turkish primary school textbooks published by Turkey's Ministry of National Education (MoNE).

Values are defined as principles desired in society that influence behavior, decision-making, and character development. Since values are acquired through experience rather than innately, values education plays a critical role in schools. The MoNE curriculum identifies ten root values, including justice, friendship, honesty, respect, and responsibility, all carrying positive value loads.

Using corpus-based methodology, researchers analyzed 88 prose reading texts (excluding 1st grade and poems) from textbooks available on the MoNE's online platform. Text processing software (ABBY Fine Reader, Text Mate, Text Wrangler) was used to clean and tokenize the data, resulting in a database of 3,637 unique words. Three applied linguistics PhD experts classified each word's value load as positive, negative, or neutral using introspection and dictionary comparisons.

Findings showed that 172 words (4.72%) carried positive value transfer, 159 (4.37%) negative, and 3,306 (91.43%) neutral. Results were similar across grade levels, with no observable relationship between grade level and value transfer.

The authors conclude there are no established standards for value education in word selection for textbooks. They recommend using corpus-based methods in textbook preparation, increasing the distribution of positive-value words, and digitizing printed textbooks to enable further diachronic research in the Turkish context.

This passage introduces MIT course 18.217 on combinatorial theory, graph theory, and additive combinatorics, taught by Yufei Zhao. The course connects extremal graph theory with additive combinatorics, demonstrating common themes between the two areas.

The lecture begins with Schur's theorem (circa 100 years ago), which arose from Schur's failed attempt to prove Fermat's Last Theorem via modular arithmetic. Schur showed that for every n, non-trivial solutions to Fermat's equation exist mod p for sufficiently large primes p. This was deduced from his combinatorial result: any finite coloring of positive integers contains a monochromatic solution to x + y = z. The theorem is presented in both infinitary and finitary forms, which are shown to be equivalent via diagonalization. Schur's theorem is proved using Ramsey's theorem for triangles, illustrating how moving to graphs provides flexibility through induction arguments.

The second half surveys modern additive combinatorics milestones: Van der Waerden's theorem (1927) on arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions; the Erdős-Turán conjecture (1936) about positive density sets; Roth's theorem (1953) for 3-term APs using Fourier analysis; and Szemerédi's theorem (late 1970s) proving the full conjecture. Later approaches include Furstenberg's ergodic theory proof, Gowers' higher-order Fourier analysis, and hypergraph regularity methods.

Extensions discussed include multidimensional Szemerédi's theorem (Furstenberg-Katznelson), the polynomial Szemerédi theorem (Bergelson-Leibman), and the Green-Tao theorem on arithmetic progressions in primes.

The lecture concludes by previewing upcoming topics: Mantel's theorem on triangle-free graphs, and the graph-theoretic question about maximum edges where every edge lies in exactly one triangle, which connects to Roth's theorem. Current bounds for Roth's theorem remain a significant open problem.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired via email during Rosh Hashanah after conservatives surfaced past blog posts attributed to him that criticized President Trump. Commentator Natalie Winters cited posts from his "Hosts of Error" blog calling Trump "mentally unfit" and "an institutional terrorist," allegedly written while Rosenzweig was at Kobre & Kim before joining the U.S. attorney's office in September 2020.

According to the Miami Herald, Rosenzweig is among dozens of federal prosecutors dismissed by Trump's Justice Department. Three other Southern District of Florida prosecutors who worked with former special counsel Jack Smith—Brooke C. Watson, Michael Thakur and Anne McNamara—were also fired. Smith recently spoke at George Mason University, expressing concern over the dismissal of career public servants and attacks on the rule of law. Separately, U.S. Attorney Erik S. Siebert left his position after Trump pressured him to indict Letitia James and James Comey.

The weekly trading strategy focuses on weekly price action and can take various forms, including position trading, trend-following, range trading, or weekly swing trading. It typically trades less frequently than daily strategies but may offer larger gains.

Most weekly chart traders are long-term position traders holding trades for 6-12 months, with range trading being more common than trend-following. Some traders use the weekly chart alongside the daily chart to gain a broader market view and identify key support/resistance levels for entries, stop losses, and profit targets.

Common weekly strategies include:
- Range trading using reversal candlestick patterns or oscillator signals at support/resistance levels
- Trend following, which may require holding trades for years
- Swing trading weekly highs and lows on lower timeframes like H4, using breakout or reversal approaches

Choosing between weekly and daily charts depends on trading style. Position trading suits the weekly chart, while day trading requires lower timeframes. Backtesting across timeframes is recommended to determine optimal results.

Stocks can be traded weekly. Day traders in the US must comply with FINRA's pattern day trader rule requiring a $25,000 minimum balance, while swing traders are not subject to this rule.

A backtested sector rotation strategy ranking four ETFs weekly produced 15.1% annual returns with a 43% max drawdown across 728 trades. A monthly version generated 12.1% annual returns with 21% max drawdown.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed the district court's grant of summary judgment to AMCO Insurance Company on Morello's claims for breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing, intentional infliction of emotional distress, unfair business practices, and Unruh Act violations.

The court found no genuine issue of material fact that AMCO conducted an unreasonable investigation, as it pursued information diligently and employed experts. AMCO reasonably relied on Dr. Soong's expert opinion, which was corroborated by Nurse Powell and Dr. Strassberg, and no evidence showed bad faith. Because a genuine liability dispute existed, AMCO did not unreasonably withhold benefits. The expert reports from Corridan and Kornblum were conclusory and rebutted by the record.

Since the bad faith claim failed, the related claims also failed. The court also upheld the denial of Morello's reconsideration motion, finding no clear error or intervening change in controlling law.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended May 2, 2021 reports revenue of $5.66 billion, up 84% year-over-year, with net income of $1.91 billion ($3.03 per diluted share). Growth occurred across all market platforms, with Gaming up 106% and Data Center up 79%, the latter driven partly by the Mellanox acquisition completed April 27, 2020. Gross margin was 64.1%, down 100 basis points year-over-year due to Mellanox-related intangible amortization. Operating expenses rose 63%, reflecting the Mellanox acquisition and employee growth.

NVIDIA operates two segments: Graphics ($3.45 billion revenue) and Compute & Networking ($2.21 billion revenue). The pending $40 billion acquisition of Arm Limited from SoftBank, announced September 13, 2020, is expected to close in the first quarter of calendar 2022, pending regulatory approvals.

As of May 2, 2021, NVIDIA held $12.67 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, with $6.96 billion in outstanding notes. The company paid $99 million in dividends and had $7.24 billion remaining in share repurchase authorization. On May 21, 2021, the Board declared a four-for-one stock split, contingent on shareholder approval. The COVID-19 pandemic continued to affect demand and supply, with supply constraints expected into the second half of the fiscal year.

The PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO command processes 1-128 migration entries to move page contents in both SNP-enabled and non-SNP-enabled systems, restricted to Hypervisor-owned pages in SNP systems. It can migrate pages actively used by DMA devices and updates IOMMU host PTEs to new physical locations. Software must prevent CPU access to pages being moved and handle ATS invalidations for non-secure ATS devices. 2M pages must be smashed into 4K pages before migration. Firmware performs validation checks, TLB invalidations, data copying with encryption preservation, and PTE updates, returning status codes for each entry.

The PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST command serves as a faster replacement for SNP PAGE_MOVE, migrating SNP guest pages. It does not support concurrent DMA or non-contiguous 2M pages. Source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, while destination pages must be in Pre-Migration state. After migration, destinations adopt source states, and sources return to Pre-Migration state. Firmware validates pages, obtains exclusive RMP access, performs TLB invalidation, copies data, and updates RMPs.

A separate command marks the end of migration command sequences and can trigger completion interrupts.

TMPM errors include command format errors (rejected), migration list entry errors (partial success possible), ring buffer errors (reported in PM_STATUS), and hardware errors (reported via command status or MCA). Batch processing of up to 128 pages may result in unrecoverable pages if hardware errors occur, potentially requiring system reboot.

Under the GST regime effective July 1, e-way bills are mandatory for transporting goods consignments exceeding Rs 50,000 in value to curb tax evasion. The GST Council on August 5 exempted 153 items from this requirement, including LPG, PDS kerosene, jewellery, currency, live animals, fresh produce, milk, honey, cereals, khadi, puja samagri, hearing aids, human hair, contraceptives, and postal baggage. Exemptions also apply to goods moved by non-motorised transport and from international to hinterland ports. The provision will take effect once the NIC's software is ready, likely by October. E-way bills require details of goods, transport mode, and parties involved, though conveyance details are not needed for intra-state transport under 10 km.

School districts across the U.S. are increasingly equipping buses with advanced technology, including GPS tracking, live cameras, turn-by-turn navigation, and student check-in systems. Kansas City Public Schools, for example, signed a $100 million, five-year contract with Zum to modernize its fleet. Vendors like Transportant and Transfinder provide similar services to districts nationwide, offering parent apps, route optimization, and on-board cameras.

Proponents say the technology improves student safety, helps recruit and retain drivers amid a national shortage, creates route efficiencies, and reduces parent calls to dispatchers. Live video feeds also allow quick responses to behavioral incidents.

However, advocates such as the Parent Coalition for Student Privacy warn about risks tied to collecting large amounts of student data, including GPS locations and video footage. School officials and vendors say they encrypt data, store it securely, and routinely delete videos. Costs vary, with some districts paying thousands per bus upfront plus annual subscription fees.

The Infiniti Q Inspiration concept, unveiled earlier this year, will inspire a new electrified vehicle platform supporting up to five models over the next five years. These vehicles will be manufactured in China at an undetermined location and are likely to be sold globally. While the concept itself is a four-door coupe, not all five upcoming electric models will share this body style. According to Infiniti Executive Design Director Karim Habib, the concept evolves traditional sedan architecture through more compact powertrains, enabling flowing designs and balanced proportions.

SOS pressure defense relies on drills, practice, and positive coaching to develop tough man-to-man defensive habits. It uses two sets of three actions, on-ball and off-ball, to proactively control offensive players.

On-ball actions:
- **Set**: A semiflexed stance forcing the ballhandler to dribble rather than shoot or pass, guiding them toward a sideline or baseline.
- **On**: Dogging the dribbler with quick slides toward a checkpoint, using "Sprint and Recover" if beaten.
- **Smother**: Crowding with arms raised to pressure a ballhandler who has stopped dribbling.

Off-ball actions:
- **Snuggle**: A pass-denial stance one pass away from the ball, including a full Post Front when defending the low post.
- **Off**: Jumping to the ball to deny give-and-go cuts, then reestablishing a Snuggle position.
- **Strike**: A weakside position between opponent and passer, providing help defense, rebounding, and lob coverage.

A closeout transitions the defender from Strike to Set when the ball is passed crosscourt.

Fiat Chrysler (FCA) has reportedly rejected a merger offer from an unidentified Chinese automaker, believing the financial terms were insufficient. FCA has historically pursued mergers, previously targeting General Motors and Volkswagen, though CEO Sergio Marchionne recently stated he was focusing on the company's finances. Several Chinese carmakers, including joint venture partner Guangzhou, have shown interest in FCA. According to Automotive News, Chinese interest is driven by the government's "China Outbound" initiative, which encourages manufacturers to acquire foreign assets. FCA's established distribution network, product line, and U.S. presence make it appealing to Chinese automakers seeking entry into the American market. Marchionne has indicated he prefers partnerships over being acquired, though he previously suggested China was more likely to buy FCA than partner with it.

Xiaomi is preparing for a major 2018 launch event featuring the Mi 8, Mi 8 SE, Mi Note 5, and Mi Band 3. According to a Digit report, a Xiaomi spokesperson stated that no phone called the Mi A2 exists, though the company plans to launch more Android One devices. The Mi A1, launched in India last year, was the company's first stock Android phone and a rebranded Mi 5X. The anticipated Mi 6X may launch in India under a different name. Xiaomi is also preparing to launch the Redmi S2/Y2, its most affordable dual camera smartphone, which will compete with the Realme 1, Honor 7A, and Honor 7C.

In Givens v. Missouri-Kansas-Texas R. Co. of Texas, the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals reviewed a case where a brakeman sustained frostbite injuries after being ordered to flag the rear of a train that broke down in zero-degree weather near Hewitt, Texas, on January 31, 1949. The breakdown occurred when a driving wheel tire came off and others slipped. The plaintiff sued under both the Federal Boiler Inspection Act and the Federal Employers' Liability Act.

The jury, responding to special issues, found the breakdown was a proximate cause of plaintiff's injuries and awarded $12,000 in damages, but also found the locomotive was safe to operate and that the incident was an unavoidable accident not caused by negligence. The district court entered judgment for the defendant.

On appeal, the court held that the Boiler Inspection Act imposes an absolute and continuing duty on carriers, not based on negligence. The court ruled that the locomotive's breakdown while in service established a violation of the Act as a matter of law, since a locomotive that cannot operate is not in proper condition. Because the jury found the breakdown was a proximate cause of plaintiff's injuries, and plaintiff was not at fault, he was entitled to recovery. The judgment was reversed with instructions to enter judgment for plaintiff in the amount of $12,000.

North American markets closed the week with significant losses. The Dow Jones fell 666 points (2.5 per cent) to 25,520.96, its biggest decline in two years, while the S&P 500 dropped 2.1 per cent to 2,762.13 and the Nasdaq fell two per cent to 7,240.95. Both the Dow and S&P had their worst week since January 2016. Losses deepened after jobs data showed the strongest annual wage growth since 2009, with 200,000 jobs added in January and unemployment at 4.1 per cent, raising concerns about inflation and interest rate hikes. Rising bond yields and weak earnings from Exxon Mobil, Chevron, Alphabet, and Apple also weighed on markets. The Canadian dollar fell to 80.78 US cents. The S&P/TSX Composite lost 255 points (1.6 per cent) to 15,606.03, hurt by falling oil and gold prices and declines in marijuana stocks, with Canopy Growth down 12.5 per cent.

This study analyzes the integration of AI ethics into computing education across India's top 100 NIRF-ranked engineering institutions, examining 3,395 syllabi. Only 2.21% (75 courses) included AI ethics content, with 60% covering it in a single session and just 7% dedicating an entire course to the topic. Most courses were undergraduate-level (92%), and AI ethics was typically embedded within broader technical courses rather than taught as standalone subjects.

Common themes included privacy and data governance (42%), accountability and policies (32%), ethical frameworks (24%), human-AI interaction (24%), algorithmic bias (18%), AI safety (16%), generative AI concerns (11%), and social justice (8%). Over 90% of syllabi lacked dedicated ethics textbooks, relying instead on general AI/ML resources, and no courses documented assessments specifically targeting AI ethics.

Findings align partially with the ACM/IEEE/AAAI CS2023 curriculum but reveal gaps in addressing generative AI ethics, sustainability, and India-specific issues like caste-based bias and biometric systems. Fewer than half of the institutions had publicly accessible curricula, limiting transparency. The authors call for standardized learning objectives, open educational resources, context-specific materials, and faculty development to meaningfully integrate AI ethics into computing education.

Mazabuka, a Zambian town nicknamed "Sweet Town" for its sugar industry, became a hotspot for HIV/AIDS due to an influx of migrant workers and an accompanying sex trade. Zambia was among the world's hardest-hit countries, with 70,000 deaths annually at the epidemic's peak in 2003. The situation has improved through a campaign by local NGO DAPP, which uses a military-style "Total Control of the Epidemic" strategy, involving door-to-door testing, condom distribution, and outreach to truckers, sex workers, and chiefs. The approach, which began in Zimbabwe in 2000 and reached Mazabuka in 2006, has contacted over 1.5 million Zambians. According to UN figures, new infections have dropped 27 percent since 2010, and AIDS-related deaths have fallen 11 percent. Officials, including District Commissioner Protacia Mulenga, credit DAPP's reach and advocate expanding the model to other countries.

The FBI arrested 23-year-old Jerry Drake Varnell of Sayre, Oklahoma, for allegedly attempting to detonate what he believed was an explosives-laden van outside an Oklahoma City bank. According to a federal complaint, the FBI learned in December of Varnell's intent to bomb a building, prompting an undercover agent to pose as an accomplice. Varnell initially targeted the Federal Reserve Building in Washington, D.C., with a device similar to the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing. He faces a federal charge of attempting to use explosives to destroy a building in interstate commerce.

Heart attacks and strokes have decreased by 30% in the UK over two decades, partly due to cholesterol and blood pressure medicines. Statins are commonly prescribed, and studies show reported side effects are largely due to the nocebo effect. Other lipid-lowering options include newer injectable medicines targeting a specific protein, reducing LDL cholesterol by around 50%, though reserved for high-risk patients.

Lifestyle changes also help. Quitting smoking improves cholesterol, with NHS support available. Exercise, combining aerobic and resistance training for 30 minutes five days a week, lowers LDL and raises HDL. Oily fish and plant sources provide heart-healthy omega-3s. Soluble fibre, found in oats, fruits, vegetables, beans, nuts, and seeds, reduces fat absorption.

Cooking from scratch avoids hidden salt and sugar. Replacing sodium with potassium-based salt substitutes could cut early deaths by 12%. Plant stanols and sterols, found in fortified foods and soya products, also help lower cholesterol.

Judge Royce C. Lamberth of the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia ordered the Trump administration to reverse layoff notices sent to nearly all remaining Voice of America employees. The ruling accused Trump officials of violating his April order requiring the news organization to serve as a reliable news source. Kari Lake, who leads the U.S. Agency for Global Media, had moved to lay off 532 staff in August, keeping programming minimal. Lamberth has threatened to hold Lake in contempt for noncompliance and failing to maintain broadcasting as required by Congress.

American Football, credited to Walter Camp as its creator in the late 1870s and early 1880s, evolved from rugby and soccer. Camp introduced key elements like 11-man teams, the line of scrimmage, the quarterback position, and the scoring format. The sport is not currently in the Olympics, though flag football may debut in 2028. Games consist of four 15-minute quarters (12 minutes in high school) with 11 players per side on a 100-yard field.

Scoring includes touchdowns (6 points), extra points (1), two-point conversions, field goals (3), and safeties (2). Common penalties include offsides, encroachment, false starts, pass interference, holding, personal fouls, roughing the passer, and illegal formations, with varying yardage penalties.

Key concepts include the line of scrimmage, neutral zone, downs (four attempts to advance 10 yards), the red zone (inside the 20-yard line), and audibles (play changes at the line). Turnovers include interceptions, fumbles, and turnovers on downs. Special teams handle kicking plays.

Notable players cited as among the greatest include Tom Brady, Jerry Rice, Jim Brown, and Lawrence Taylor.

CBS's new legal drama "Doubt," premiering February 15, stars Katherine Heigl as Sadie Ellis, a defense attorney at a small New York firm led by Isaiah Roth (Elliot Gould). Sadie falls for her client Billy Brennan (Steven Pasquale), a pediatric surgeon accused of a murder committed 24 years earlier. The supporting cast includes Dulé Hill as associate Albert Cobb and Laverne Cox as a transgender lawyer, marking the first time a transgender actor plays a transgender regular on broadcast TV. Created by "Grey's Anatomy" alums Tony Phelan and Joan Rater, the show balances Billy's ongoing case with weekly cases and reveals Sadie's backstory, including her imprisoned mother. The reviewer finds the series formulaic with occasionally overly cute dialogue and logic lapses, but praises its likeable cast and evenhanded treatment of real issues.

Police have seized a white Holden Commodore as part of the investigation into the murder of Aaron Marks, who was found fatally injured on a Ballina footpath earlier this month. Detective Chief Inspector Cameron Lindsay said forensic officers are examining the vehicle for biological material, fingerprints, DNA, and items such as blood. The driver is assisting police, who are now calling on passengers from the car to come forward. Chief Insp Lindsay declined to say whether Mr Marks provided details of the incident before his death but thanked the public and media for their assistance.

Callum Knott, 21, of Worksop, took his aunt's car from her Ollerton address on November 20 and was seen by her driving it on Walesby Lane. He abandoned the vehicle when the battery died. At Mansfield Magistrates Court, he admitted taking a vehicle without consent and driving without a licence or insurance. His solicitor said he acted because he was "young and stupid." Probation officer Sarah Phillips noted Knott had previously driven the car with permission, has ADHD, and is remorseful. He received a 12-month community order with 80 hours of unpaid work, a four-month driving ban, and was ordered to pay £85 costs and an £85 victim surcharge.

Cover 2 is a widely used 5-under, 2-deep defense designed to stop quick passes and deep throws, with cornerbacks acting as flat defenders. Despite its effectiveness, offenses can exploit it in several ways: high-low stretching the corners using concepts like smash or fade-out; attacking the middle linebacker with dig/seam combinations from 3-receiver surfaces; using vertical concepts like 4 verticals from 2x2 formations to strain the two deep safeties; and attacking the open middle with post routes while widening safeties. Example plays from Ohio State, Oregon, Michigan, Ole Miss, and TCU illustrate these tactics, including corner-flat combinations, snag-and-go, fade-out, RB pop passes off run action, and jet sweep verticals.
