This paper presents a methodology for studying the dynamics of a digital business ecosystem (DBE), defined as a closed or semi-closed system of small and medium enterprises interacting through buyer-seller relationships in cyberspace. The authors aim to determine which companies are likely to prosper or be suppressed under static, closed conditions.

Because interactions between companies are asymmetric, Markov random fields are unsuitable. Instead, the authors adapt a model from biological neural systems, producing coupled non-linear differential equations that govern each company's "fitness" value.

The methodology involves two components. First, a simulated DBE is constructed with companies assigned SELL, WANT, TRUST, and MISTRUST lists, using statistical properties derived from real DBEs. The psychophysical Weber-Fechner law is applied to convert qualitative trust categories into numerical weights (0.14, 0.29, 0.57 for undesirable, indifferent, and desirable partners).

Second, a self-organizing neural network models competitive co-existence, where each company's fitness evolves based on: self-excitation, excitatory signals from companies whose products match its WANT list, inhibitory signals from competitors selling similar products, external input, and background economic conditions. Trust weights modulate excitatory signals.

Preliminary experiments show the system's behavior under varying parameters, including scenarios producing monopolies. The authors acknowledge that further refinements are needed, particularly modeling inhibition from shared demand in closed environments and associating model parameters with measurable real-world quantities.

Lung cancer remains a leading cause of death, with most cases diagnosed at late stages when survival is poor. While low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening has reduced mortality, adherence rates are low and false-positive rates high, indicating a need for complementary blood-based biomarker tests.

The MOSAIC study, an observational case-control study of 2,513 subjects enrolled across 77 US clinical sites, collected blood samples for lung cancer biomarker discovery. Researchers applied an untargeted multi-omics approach integrating proteomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics, and targeted immunoassays, analyzing over 750,000 molecular features. Data from 1,225 subjects were used to train a machine learning-based (XGBoost) classifier, with 398 subjects held out for validation.

The multi-omics classifier achieved an AUC of 0.96 for all-stage lung cancer and 0.93 for stage I, outperforming both a baseline clinical-variable classifier (AUC 0.78) and a proteomics-only classifier (AUC 0.91). In the validation set, specificity was 89% and sensitivity was 89% across all stages, with stage I, II, and III-IV sensitivities of 80%, 88%, and 99%, respectively.

The final model included 682 features representing 149 proteins, 346 genes, and 77 metabolic pathways, with no single ‘omics type dominating. Approximately 60% of features were significantly associated with cancer stage. Limitations include the need for validation in a prospective high-risk screening population. The authors conclude that this multi-omics platform shows promise for early lung cancer detection and may extend to other clinical applications.

The Camarilla pivot point, introduced in 1989 by Nick Scott, is an extension of the classical pivot point that provides day traders with four support and four resistance levels, totaling nine price levels. It uses the previous day's closing prices to compute key intraday support and resistance levels, helping traders identify entry points, exit points, and manage risk.

Unlike Camarilla, the Fibonacci pivot points strategy uses Fibonacci retracements and extensions (such as 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, 127%, and 161.8%) to determine key price levels.

A backtest of ordinary pivot points did not reveal significant profits, and the author suggests Camarilla would likely perform similarly. Readers are encouraged to backtest their own strategies, as historical performance provides useful insight.

The Trump administration, led by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and NIH Director Jayanta Bhattacharya, is targeting the academic publishing industry, citing concerns about research fraud, pharmaceutical industry influence, bias, and high costs. Kennedy has proposed barring government-funded scientists from publishing in major medical journals and suggested launching a government-run journal. Bhattacharya has emphasized reproducible research and pledged to cap article processing charges (APCs).

While some scientists acknowledge genuine problems in academic publishing—including "publish or perish" culture and industry ties—critics like Luís Nunes Amaral, Ivan Oransky, and former NEJM editors warn that the administration's actions may worsen issues rather than reform them. Former NEJM editors noted that NIH budget cuts will exacerbate dependence on pharmaceutical funding. Others, including Meagan Phelan and Jennifer Trueblood, argue that capping APCs or expanding open access alone won't restore public trust or fix incentive structures, which require reform led by scientists and academic institutions. Concerns also exist that Bhattacharya's new journal, The Journal of the Academy of Public Health, could platform dubious research.

He emphasizes the importance of puck possession, stating the team is playing a system they've been comfortable with all year, and acknowledges fortune in winning a close Stanley Cup Finals game on a shot from Sammy Pahlsson.

He notes that directing pucks at the net is a universal goal, and that adjustments—like the opposing team breaking up their top line—are expected at this stage. He attributes the regular season's competitiveness to the salary cap creating a level playing field.

Regarding an injured player with pins in his hands, he says it's too early to comment until doctors clear him. He explains that morning skates are optional and describes the team's playoff routine of hotel check-ins, meals, and pregame naps.

He denies publicly criticizing Getzlaf, calling his comments minor. He praises a defenseman acquired at last year's trade deadline for his size and net-front presence. He cites health as the reason for limiting the fourth line's minutes and being cautious with young players Carter and Motzko.

Finally, he references the loss to Edmonton in last year's conference final as motivation to avoid mediocrity, highlighting the acquisition of Chris Pronger and roster continuity as key to the team's progress.

Lookout security researchers have identified a spyware family called SonicSpy in over a thousand apps on Google Play. The malware can record audio, take photos, make calls, send texts, and retrieve call logs, contacts, and Wi-Fi information, responding to more than 73 remote commands via a command and control server. A recent example, Soniac, was marketed as a messaging app using a customised version of Telegram while secretly stealing data. Upon execution, SonicSpy hides its launcher icon, connects to C2 infrastructure, and installs a custom Telegram version. The account behind Soniac, iraqwebservice, previously posted two other SonicSpy samples, now removed. Lookout analyst Michael Flossman warned the malware poses risks to enterprises, particularly employees travelling abroad who rely on messaging apps.

The Supreme Court, in an unsigned order, paused a federal judge's ruling that had barred Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem from terminating Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Venezuelan nationals. This marks the second time the court has intervened on the issue, following a similar May order.

TPS allows designated foreign nationals to remain and work in the U.S. when they cannot safely return home. Venezuela was designated under the program by former DHS Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas in 2021, redesignated in 2023, and extended through October 2026 in 2025. Noem terminated the 2023 designation and 2025 extension in February.

U.S. District Judge Edward Chen initially blocked the termination in March and issued a final ruling on Sept. 5 finding Noem acted unlawfully. After the 9th Circuit declined to intervene, Solicitor General D. John Sauer appealed to the Supreme Court.

Justices Sotomayor, Kagan, and Jackson dissented. Jackson wrote a solo dissent criticizing the order as a "grave misuse" of the emergency docket, noting lower courts had ruled against the termination five times and arguing the government had not shown a time-sensitive need for intervention.

Manjot Kalra scored an unbeaten century in the 2018 ICC Under-19 World Cup final, earning the Player of the Match award as India claimed its fourth U19 World Cup title. Though overshadowed before the final by teammates Prithvi Shaw, Shubman Gill, Kamlesh Nagarkoti, and Shivam Mavi—who fetched higher IPL bids—Kalra, bought by Delhi Daredevils at his base price of Rs 20 lakh, became central to India's win. He joins Unmukt Chand, Brett Williams, Stephen Peters, and Jarrad Burke as batsmen who scored centuries in U19 World Cup finals, though none of the other four played for their senior national teams. From Virat Kohli's 2008 U19-winning squad, only four players went on to represent India, and none from Chand's 2012 team. Head coach Rahul Dravid expressed hope that the victory would not define the players but be surpassed by greater achievements in their careers.

The severance packages are available to workers aged 55 and older with at least 10 years at the company. These are the insurer's first buyouts since the late 1980s.

The invention relates to dynamic graphics rendering based on saccade detection. A saccade is a rapid eye movement between fixation points during which the brain masks visual signals (saccadic masking), lasting approximately 100-200 ms including pre- and post-movement masking periods.

The system includes a processor, memory, display, and sensor configured to detect eye movement. Sensors may include cameras, optical sensors, EMG sensors, Doppler sensors, range sensors, or microphones. EMG sensors placed near eye muscles can detect saccade onset before eye movement begins.

The method comprises: rendering a computer simulated scene (e.g., VR/AR content), detecting saccade onset through sudden changes in eye direction, speed, or acceleration exceeding a threshold, and reducing computing resources during the saccade duration. Resource reduction techniques include skipping frames, repeating frames, reducing rendering detail or resolution, or adjusting variable frame rates.

Saccade duration may be predicted based on eye movement models and onset magnitude. The system may include calibration processes comparing predicted versus measured saccade durations to refine the eye movement model for individual users.

Saved computing resources can be reallocated to low-frequency calculations like complex lighting, used by other processes, or conserved to reduce power consumption. The technique can be combined with foveated rendering and implemented in head-mounted displays for AR or VR applications.

Microsoft Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended December 31, 2017. As of January 26, 2018, approximately 7.70 billion shares of common stock were outstanding.

For the three months ended December 31, 2017, total revenue was $28.9 billion (up from $25.8 billion), with operating income of $8.7 billion. A net loss of $6.3 billion ($0.82 per share) resulted from a $15.5 billion income tax provision tied to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA), enacted December 22, 2017. For the six-month period, revenue was $53.5 billion and net income was $274 million.

Total assets were $256.0 billion, with cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments of $142.8 billion. Long-term debt was $73.3 billion, and stockholders' equity totaled $78.4 billion.

Microsoft recorded an estimated $13.8 billion net TCJA charge, including $17.8 billion for the transition tax on deferred foreign income, partially offset by $4.0 billion from deferred tax remeasurement. The blended U.S. federal statutory rate for fiscal 2018 was 28%.

The company early-adopted new revenue recognition and lease accounting standards effective July 1, 2017, restating prior results. Windows 10 revenue is now primarily recognized at billing/delivery rather than ratably.

Microsoft completed the $27.0 billion LinkedIn acquisition on December 8, 2016. The company repurchased $3.4 billion in shares during the first half of fiscal 2018, with $33.4 billion remaining under its $40 billion repurchase authorization. Quarterly dividends were $0.42 per share. Ongoing litigation includes patent, antitrust, product liability, and employment discrimination matters.

Students in Max Hayes High School's Auto Collision Repair program spent a year and a half repairing a Cleveland police cruiser damaged during the 2016 Cavaliers championship celebrations, when fans jumped on it near Quicken Loans Arena. Teacher Greg Boykin initiated the project after seeing the vehicle on the news. Students dismantled and rebuilt the cruiser, replacing its roof, hood, and side panels using donated materials from companies including Sherwin Williams and Safelite Auto Glass. The city had considered the vehicle a total loss, and the students' work saved approximately $10,000. Division of Motor Vehicle Maintenance Commissioner Jeff Brown said the cruiser will return to service as a zone car.

This article demonstrates how to build an RSI-based trading strategy in TradingView using Pine Script, applied to DOT on a 5-minute timeframe with a 14-period RSI and 65/35 overbought/oversold levels.

TradingView is a widely used technical analysis platform offering charts, indicators, backtesting, and community features, available free with limitations. Users can add the RSI indicator via the Indicators search and adjust parameters in the Settings window. The RSI measures price movement strength, oscillating between 0 and 100, with values above 70 typically indicating overbought conditions and below 30 indicating oversold.

To build the strategy, users open the Pine Editor, select the Strategy template, and rename it. The RSI is coded using "ta.rsi" with Source and Length parameters. Long conditions trigger when RSI exits the oversold zone; short conditions trigger when it exits overbought. Positions close when RSI crosses 50. Orders use strategy.entry and strategy.close commands within IF statements. User inputs can be added for adjustable parameters.

After adding the strategy to the chart, TradingView displays the equity curve, net profit, drawdown, and win rate, though free accounts have limited historical data. Pro accounts enable deep backtesting across all available historical data. The Performance Summary provides metrics like Sharpe Ratio and R:R, while the List of Trades shows individual trades (CSV export requires a paid account).

The article notes RSI alone does not perform consistently and works best combined with other indicators.

Nannette Perkins, 40, was arrested on April 16, 2017, at her Taylorsville home after Salt Lake City police received a tip about her identity. She is suspected of committing at least six bank robberies in the Salt Lake City area, including five within two hours on Saturday morning. According to Unified police Lt. Brian Lohrke, the robber wore pajama bottoms, eyeglasses, and a blue bandanna while robbing banks in Cottonwood Heights, Salt Lake City, Sandy, Holladay, and West Valley City. Perkins is being held at Salt Lake County jail pending an initial court appearance.

Student newsrooms function like local news for university communities, keeping students informed about campus events and issues. America is experiencing a rise in news deserts, which former Rocky Mountain News editor John Temple argues deprives locals of the ability to make informed decisions about local government. Most popular news outlets are controlled by roughly six powerful corporations, limiting news diversity. Removing student news would leave students uninformed about pertinent issues, unable to learn peers' perspectives, and lacking content that challenges their beliefs. Since students represent the next generation of American workers, maintaining student journalism is essential to producing an educated public.

This research employed a Research and Development (R&D) methodology to investigate strategies for achieving excellence in vocational education management within institutions under Thailand's Office of Vocational Education Commission. The study was conducted in two phases: investigating foundational data and needs, and developing a strategic framework.

Phase 1 involved analyzing current and desired conditions through a questionnaire distributed to 206 respondents from 424 institutions, supplemented by structured interviews at three exemplary vocational colleges. Results showed current conditions were at a high level while desired conditions were at the highest level, with an overall Priority Needs Index (PNImodified) of 0.179. Curriculum Development ranked highest in necessity, followed by Collaboration Networks and Personnel.

This study evaluates the maturity of AI in healthcare publications from 2019-2021 using a BERT-based classifier applied to PubMed articles, supplemented by manual annotation of data types, model types, and geographic origin.

Of 7,062 publications reviewed, only about 5% (385) were classified as mature. Maturity rates were 6.01% in 2019, 7.7% in 2020, and 1.81% in 2021. Radiology consistently had the most mature models, followed by Pathology, Ophthalmology, and Gastroenterology. Only 4% and 1.6% of COVID-19-related publications in 2020 and 2021 were mature.

Geographically, the United States and China dominated mature publications, while South America, Eastern Europe, and Africa were underrepresented. Image data was used in roughly 88% of mature publications across all three years, while tabular data use declined and text data use increased. Deep learning, particularly CNNs, was the most common model type (62-71%), followed by classical machine learning.

The authors note that readily available CNN algorithms and large imaging repositories enabled image-based specialties to produce more mature publications. Limitations include reliance on PubMed and English-language sources. The study highlights the need to leverage diverse datasets and models globally to advance AI in healthcare.

The London breakout strategy is a forex day trading strategy that attempts to trade the upward or downward breakout of the Asian session's trading range, which typically occurs within the first three hours of the London session. Traders go long on upside breakouts and short on downside breakouts.

The London session (8:00 AM–5:00 PM GMT) overlaps with the Asian and New York sessions and has the highest liquidity and volatility. The Asian range can be defined using either the high-low method (including wicks) or the open-close method (candle bodies only). A London breakout indicator is a custom tool that identifies breakout opportunities and provides entry, stop loss, and take profit levels, typically generating one signal per day.

Backtesting on the EUR/USD pair showed the strategy loses money on upside breakouts, while downside breakouts produced near-zero average gains. MnBi₂Te₄/(Bi₂Te₃)ₙ superlattice crystals were grown using the Inverted Vertical Bridgman Method (IVBM) to investigate how growth dynamics influence structural and magnetic properties. Four samples taken along an ingot revealed distinct stacking sequences and Mn concentrations, characterized by TEM, EDX, SQUID magnetometry, and magnetic resonance.

Four growth stages were identified: (i) turbulent flow producing pure MnBi₂Te₄; (ii) rapid MnTe precipitation reducing melt Mn content from ~14 at.% to ~7 at.%, initiating MnBi₂Te₄/Bi₂Te₃ mixed phases; (iii) stationary flow enabling ordered QL/SL assembly; and (iv) cessation of flow causing Mn depletion and structural disorder.

An inverse relationship between septuple layer (SL) spacing and MnTe supersaturation was established, explained by diffusion-limited competition between SLs following combined Chernov and van der Eerden models. Magnetically, samples with closely spaced, compositionally complete SLs exhibited antiferromagnetic ordering (TN = 26 K and 13.5 K), while samples with larger SL separations (4–5 or 7±2 QLs) and Mn-deficient SLs showed ferromagnetic behavior (TC ≈ 9–11 K). Sample C displayed stronger magnetic anisotropy (μ₀HA ≈ 460 mT) than the more disordered Sample D (~370 mT).

The findings demonstrate that controlling melt composition and flow dynamics enables tuning of layer spacing and magnetic properties in bulk magnetic topological insulators.

Young African entrepreneurs are using new technologies to transform agriculture and address climate change, as showcased at the MasterCard Foundation's Young Africa Works Summit 2017 in Kigali. Rwanda's Jean Bosco Nzeyimana runs Habona Ltd, which converts organic waste into fuel briquettes and fertiliser. Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) is an autosomal dominant hereditary cancer syndrome comprising MEN1, MEN2, and MEN4 subtypes, caused by mutations in the MEN1, RET, and CDKN1B genes respectively. Despite high penetrance, MEN remains understudied in India.

This study classified variants in the RET, MEN1, and CDKN1B genes from the IndiGen, ClinVar, and Mastermind datasets using ACMG/AMP guidelines. A total of 1,324 unique variants were classified, and combined with expert-panel classifications to form the MAPVar database containing 3,280 variants (1,094 Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic, 1,591 Benign/Likely benign, and 595 VUS).

Using IndiGen data, the authors estimated that approximately 1 in 341 Indians is a likely carrier of MEN-linked pathogenic RET mutations. Comparison with 18 global datasets showed significantly different allele frequencies in Indians. The database was validated using the GUaRDIAN rare disease cohort, identifying pathogenic variants in seven patient cases.

The authors also developed a multiplex NGS primer panel covering all coding regions of the three genes (38 amplicons, 33 exons, 65kb), which successfully diagnosed three cases from a 72-patient endocrine cohort.

The MAPVar database, accessible at https://clingen.igib.res.in/MAPVar/, along with the NGS panel, aims to facilitate cost-effective genetic testing, early diagnosis, and variant interpretation for MEN in clinical and research settings.

Bar Harbor Bankshares reported $14.9 million in net income for 2016, consistent with the prior year, despite $2.7 million in charges related to the Lake Sunapee Bank Group acquisition and a core system conversion expected to complete in Q2 2017. The Supreme Court heard arguments in a case examining whether the U.S. Postal Service and federal government can be sued for intentionally failing to deliver mail. The case was brought by Lebene Konan, a Texas landlady who alleged postal workers deliberately withheld mail from her property as part of racial harassment. The Federal Tort Claims Act waives sovereign immunity in some cases but includes a "postal exception" for claims involving "loss, miscarriage, or negligent transmission" of mail. A district court dismissed Konan's case, but the 5th Circuit reversed in part, ruling that intentional nondelivery isn't covered by those terms.

During arguments, several justices, including Chief Justice Roberts, questioned the government's broad definition of "loss." Justices Kavanaugh and Alito appeared more sympathetic to the government, with Alito warning of a surge in lawsuits. Government attorney Frederick Liu argued a ruling for Konan could quadruple USPS lawsuits, while Konan's attorney Easha Anand countered that such long-term mistreatment is rare. Justices Sotomayor and Jackson noted plaintiffs would still face a high bar. A decision is expected by early July.

At the Silverbluff Audubon Center in remote Aiken County, S.C., staff are rooting for the Philadelphia Eagles in the Super Bowl because the center is home to bald eagles, including a nesting pair present since 1994. Christa Goldblatt of Crossborder Energy distributed the rebuttal testimony of R. Thomas Beach, filed before the California Public Utilities Commission (I. 99-07-003) on behalf of Indicated Electric Generators in support of the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement.

Beach's testimony responds to the Southern California Generation Coalition (SCGC) and The Utility Reform Network (TURN) Post-Interim Settlement Agreement (PISA), arguing it fails to unbundle intrastate transmission on the SoCalGas system. Key points include:

1. **PG&E vs. SoCalGas comparisons**: Beach contends SCGC/TURN exaggerate differences between the two systems, arguing both have faced similar access and conflict-of-interest problems, and that SoCalGas's backbone facilities can be unbundled similarly to PG&E's under the Gas Accord.

2. **City-gate benefits**: Beach asserts the PG&E Gas Accord city-gate market has delivered $0.05–$0.11 per Dth savings for electric generators without requiring them to hold capacity or pay demand charges.

3. **Cost/benefit analysis**: Beach argues SCGC/TURN overstate demand charge impacts, citing unrealistic assumptions in their study (e.g., generators over-contracting for capacity, ignoring secondary markets, interruptible service, and city-gate purchases). He recalculates that interruptible service would raise generators' fixed costs by only 0.6%.

4. **Settlement benefits**: The Comprehensive Settlement reduces EG rates by $3 million annually, shifts 100% of backbone cost recovery risk to SoCalGas shareholders, uses embedded cost pricing through 2006, and limits any one party from holding more than 40% of intrastate capacity from any receipt point.

5. **Reliability concerns**: Beach dismisses SCGC/TURN's warnings of plant closures and blackouts, noting that any price pressure would likely increase Reliability Must-Run contracts rather than cause outages.

VOT broadcasts via shortwave on three frequencies: 11.510 mHz (25m band), 9.510 mHz (31m band), and 15.565 mHz (19m band), with varying times for Tibet, India, and Nepal. U.S. higher education institutions increasingly emphasize global competencies, yet only about one percent of students participate in study abroad programs, largely due to financial and logistical barriers. While virtual alternatives exist, immersive travel offers unique benefits in intercultural understanding, language skills, and personal growth. This article presents a structured methodology for developing sustainable business models for faculty-led education abroad programs, drawing on the authors' two decades of experience.

The framework identifies three interdependent drivers: curricular logistics, operational logistics, and financial logistics. Curricular considerations include learning outcomes, elective versus required participation, credit structure, assessment methods, strategic alignment with host institutions, competitive positioning, location selection, engagement modalities (site visits, coursework, research, service-learning, design-build projects), and program duration. Operational logistics encompass risk management, program leadership, travel timing, flights, lodging, partner coordination, local transport, communication, meals, entertainment, emergency preparation, student preparation, wellbeing, and problem support. Financial logistics address program expenses (faculty, staff, external parties, projects, coordination), income sources (tuition, fees), internal and external funding, and budget distribution including scholarships.

The article outlines twelve business model types grouped into three categories: external party-led programs (run by organizations like CIEE or IES Abroad), faculty-led programs (driven by student payments, revenue, corporate donations, or grants), and student-led programs (typically non-credit, club-based, funded through donations and student activity fees).

Key principles for sustainability include leveraging community engagement revenue or corporate sponsorships, utilizing dedicated staff support, and delegating responsibilities to students. The authors emphasize that models should be adapted to each program's unique objectives, constraints, and resources to create impactful and financially viable global learning experiences.

A UCLA study led by Susanne Henning found that black tea, like green tea, may promote health and weight loss, though through a different mechanism. While green tea polyphenols are absorbed into the blood and tissue, black tea works through the gut microbiome by altering bacterial ratios—increasing microbes linked to lean body mass and decreasing those tied to obesity. Both teas act as prebiotics. In the study, mice were divided into four groups with varying diets, including high-fat, high-sugar diets supplemented with either green or black tea extract. Since black tea works in the gut and green tea works in both the liver and gut, combining the two may offer the greatest benefits.

Developments in technology have significantly impacted education, particularly distance education in higher education institutions. This study evaluates how advanced technologies—artificial intelligence, metaverse, brain-computer interfaces, blockchain, brain chips, and virtual reality—will influence digital transformation in open and distance education from a managerial perspective.

Using a qualitative case study approach, researchers conducted semi-structured interviews with four academics having at least 20 years of experience in open and distance education at Anadolu University. Data were analyzed using content analysis via Nvivo software, with researcher triangulation ensuring validity.

Findings reveal that advanced technologies will impact education through technology investment, educational processes, services, and content, while managerial impacts include management, employment, economy, and socio-cultural change. Experts predicted AI would occupy managerial positions, augmented reality would support practice-based learning, and blockchain would enable centralized control and prior learning recognition. Socio-culturally, experts noted potential increases in laziness, psychological problems, virtual addiction, decreased physical communication, and emergence of "meta-culture."

Recommendations include developing AI assistants and managers, implementing blockchain-based certification, creating adaptive synthetic content, configuring metaverse teaching systems, and researching brain-computer interfaces in educational and managerial processes. The study suggests larger-scale research across different geographies and institutions.

A 179-megawatt utility-scale solar project, consisting of Switch Station 1 and Switch Station 2, was commissioned on December 11, 2017, at the Apex Industrial Park near Las Vegas. Hartman analyzes the Andropov regime and recommends U.S. policy direction. He concludes Andropov offers no foreign policy shift from Brezhnev, pursuing internal discipline and maintaining hard lines on Afghanistan, Poland, and Southern Africa, with possible acceleration of overtures to China. Despite this, Soviet relations with the U.S. remain a Soviet priority.

Hartman argues U.S. policy should return to first principles, with security and reducing nuclear war risk as paramount. He urges heightened emphasis on arms control, particularly INF, as the only available catalyst for improving relations and countering Soviet exploitation of European public opinion.

He recommends abandoning the zero-zero INF position, noting the Soviets aim to prevent U.S. deployment without affecting their own by gradually softening their negotiating stance to appeal to Europeans. Hartman recalls that the 1979 NATO decision to deploy 572 GLCMs and Pershing-IIs was primarily political—to assure Europeans of U.S. commitment—rather than military, and the specific numbers were not sacrosanct.

Bank analysts and KGI Securities' Ming-chi Kuo anticipate that the Apple Watch Series 3 will include an LTE-capable modem. The passage describes a continuation patent application relating to medical devices for neural modulation, particularly Spinal Cord Stimulation (SCS).

The system includes electrodes on leads, a neural modulation generator, and a programming system that determines electrode fractionalizations based on a target multipole. The target multipole uses at least three target poles that directionally and progressively stack fractionalizations to produce a linear electric field over a tissue volume.

In various examples, the target multipole includes a center point with target anodes on one side and target cathodes on the opposing side, which may be in-line. Poles farther from the center may have higher fractionalization percentages. Additional flanking anodes, cathodes, and opposite-polarity flanking electrodes may be included for edge guarding and current steering. Some embodiments use directional electrodes extending less than 360 degrees around the lead circumference.

The programming system may include a user interface allowing adjustment of the multipole's angle, focus (field length), and spread (field width). It may accept user-drawn regions or identified pain areas to automatically determine the multipole, display gradient controls for therapy strength, automatically move the multipole within the electrode array, and implement search heuristics to optimize pole distance, amplitude, number, orientation, focus, and spread.

The method involves programming modulation parameters based on the target multipole and delivering energy through active electrodes to produce the linear electric field.

The technology aims to selectively modulate dorsal horn (DH) or dorsal root (DR) tissue over dorsal column (DC) tissue, potentially providing sub-perception pain therapy without paresthesia. The linear field design maximizes the electric field (activating DH fibers) while minimizing the second-order voltage derivative (reducing DC fiber activation). The field may be delivered at various frequencies, duty cycles, and pulse widths, and can be implemented with percutaneous leads, paddle leads, or multiple leads in various configurations.

A Senate committee on legal and constitutional affairs released a report criticizing the Supreme Court of Canada's 2016 "Jordan" ruling, which imposed 18-month trial deadlines in provincial courts and 30-month deadlines in superior courts. John Bryant, a pro se inmate at Sing Sing, filed a Section 1983 complaint against the New York State Department of Correctional Services (DOCS), Sing Sing Correctional Facility, and Officer Hanser Hernandez, alleging constitutional violations stemming from a "Code Blue" lockdown from December 1999 to January 2000. The lockdown, prompted by Hernandez's later-discovered false report of hidden ammunition, allegedly subjected inmates to 24-hour cell confinement, denial of showers, mail, recreation, hot meals, religious services, and non-emergency medical care. Bryant also alleged inadequate inmate wages and inability to bargain collectively.

DOCS moved to dismiss under Rule 12(b) for lack of subject matter jurisdiction based on Eleventh Amendment immunity. Magistrate Judge Maas recommended granting the motion. Judge Berman, conducting de novo review, adopted the Report, holding that New York has not consented to suit and Congress did not abrogate immunity through Section 1983. State agencies like DOCS are not "persons" under Section 1983. The court sua sponte dismissed claims against Sing Sing on the same grounds. The action against Officer Hernandez was permitted to proceed, with Bryant directed to report on service status by June 29, 2001.

The Government is launching a consultation on new measures to hold company directors accountable following large-scale insolvencies such as Carillion and BHS. The Grand River Conservation Authority is undertaking a $1.8-million, five-year project to create digital floodplain maps using LiDAR technology, which uses airborne laser beams to produce detailed 3D maps. The new digital maps will integrate with U.S. Army Corps of Engineers forecasting software to provide real-time flood predictions, helping identify at-risk properties and notify emergency coordinators. Penn State engineers have developed an optical technique to rapidly analyze the structural properties of proteins, including within living bacteria, as reported in the journal Analyst. Led by Melik C. Demirel, the team seeks to identify both natural and synthetic semicrystalline proteins with specific mechanical properties, characterized by their crystalline structure. Because standard flow cytometry lasers generate heat that alters crystalline structures, the researchers used femto and pico-second lasers in a process called time-domain thermo-transmission, which screens proteins in milliseconds without killing cells. The team studies natural proteins like silk and synthetic proteins adapted from squid ring teeth, which retain strength in water. Demirel received a Defense University Research Instrumentation Program grant to scale up the method. The work was supported by the Army Research Office and involved collaborators from Penn State, the University of Virginia, and Washington University.

The speaker discusses the importance of kids enjoying ice time when players aren't skating. The paper addresses risk analysis in e-commerce interactions within digital business ecosystems, where a trusting agent initiates interactions with a trusted agent. The authors argue that trusting agents should analyze potential risk beforehand by determining the probability of failure and its consequences.

The authors propose a methodology using the metrics 'FailureLevel' (FL) and a 'Failure scale' to quantify the probability of failure. Since risk is dynamic, the total time space is divided into non-overlapping time slots across two phases: pre-interaction and post-interaction.

In the pre-interaction phase, the trusting agent determines the Previous FailureLevel (PFL) either from past interaction history or by soliciting recommendations, considering trustworthiness, time, and criteria. In the post-interaction phase, the Future FailureLevel (FFL) is predicted using Gaussian Distribution applied to prior FailureLevels, calculating the probability of each failure level occurring.

The methodology is demonstrated with an example comparing two probable trusted agents, where the level with the highest probability of occurrence is taken as the FailureLevel for subsequent time slots. Determining the consequences of failure is identified as future work.

Iowa State, ranked 14th and previously unbeaten, lost 38-30 to Cincinnati in week 6, with Cincinnati building a 31-7 halftime lead. The study evaluates disabled education within inclusive education quality during distance learning in Kazakhstan, based on special education teachers' perspectives. Using a qualitative case study design, researchers conducted semi-structured interviews with ten special education teachers instructing students with hearing, visual, or mild intellectual disabilities across grades 5–8. Data were examined through thematic analysis.

Findings revealed teachers primarily used online lessons, video sharing, homework, online activities, and mobile applications. Seven of ten teachers preferred formal education over distance learning, and six found distance education insufficient for meeting students' individual learning needs. Teacher–student and peer interaction was described as weak, time-limited, unqualified, and disorganized.

Recommendations include diversifying technology-based methods, developing individualized learning content, organizing online seminars for families, and creating social activities to strengthen interaction among teachers, students, and peers.

This study analyzed high-throughput transcriptomic data from three Alzheimer's disease (AD) cohorts (Knight ADRC, MSBB, and ROSMAP) to investigate the molecular connection between AD and epilepsy. Researchers focused on a previously identified AD subtype associated with synaptic plasticity dysfunction (SPD), which correlates with more severe cognitive decline.

From a list of 105 epilepsy-causing genes, 16 were consistently dysregulated across all three cohorts in the SPD profile. Fifteen genes were downregulated (including ARHGEF9, GABRA1, GABRB3, GABRG2, GRIN2A, HCN1, SCN1A, and SCN8A), while only CERS1 was upregulated. Many of these genes were highly expressed in neurons and involved in synaptic function.

Pathway analyses revealed enrichment in epilepsy-related pathways, including glutamatergic, GABAergic, and dopaminergic synapses, as well as ion channel activity and synaptic transmission processes. The dysregulation of epilepsy-causing genes was observed in both early and late AD stages, with stronger effects at later stages.

The findings support a bidirectional relationship between epilepsy and AD, suggesting shared genetic pathways and pathophysiological mechanisms. The authors propose that disrupted GABAergic and glutamatergic neurotransmission, along with altered ion channel function, contributes to cognitive decline in both conditions. These results highlight potential therapeutic targets and support the need for personalized treatment approaches addressing shared genetic vulnerabilities in patients with both disorders.

The Tax Court considered whether noncharitable gifts made by check from decedent Elizabeth C. Dillingham were complete for federal gift and estate tax purposes upon delivery of the checks in December 1980, or upon payment by the drawee bank in January 1981. The outcome determined whether the gifts qualified for the $3,000 annual exclusion and whether certain limitations periods applied.

Petitioner argued the "relation back doctrine" applied, making payment relate back to delivery. While this doctrine has been applied to charitable gifts (Estate of Spiegel; Estate of Belcher), the court previously reserved judgment on its application to noncharitable gifts.

The court declined to extend the relation back doctrine here because petitioner failed to prove unconditional delivery of the checks, noting the 35-day delay in cashing, lack of evidence regarding sufficient funds, and unclear donative intent.

Applying Oklahoma law, the court found that a check does not operate as an assignment of funds until accepted by the drawee bank, and donees who gave no consideration were not holders in due course and would be subject to a stop-payment defense. Therefore, the decedent retained dominion and control until the bank paid the checks in 1981, making the gifts complete then.

This prospective single-site observational cohort study of 103 cerebral cavernous malformation (CCM) patients investigated the predictive capacity of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in PTPN2, VDR, and FCGR2A genes, along with plasma cytokine levels, in relation to aggressive CCM behavior.

Blood samples were collected, genomic DNA extracted, and SNPs genotyped via allelic discrimination. Plasma cytokines were measured using a multiparametric immunoassay. Statistical analyses included logistic regression, ROC curves, propensity score matching, and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.

Key findings include:
- PTPN2rs72872125 CT and VDRrs7975232 CC genotypes were associated with asymptomatic phenotype and altered cytokine levels (higher IL-10, lower IL-18, IFN-γ, IL-27, IL-23).
- A weighted biomarker combining PTPN2rs72872125 CC genotype and GM-CSF levels served as a diagnostic indicator for symptomatic phenotype, with strong accuracy in familial and infratentorial cases.
- FCGR2Ars1801274 GG genotype functioned as a prognostic biomarker, predicting symptomatic events during follow-up with high accuracy. In silico analysis showed the H131R substitution is conserved among higher primates.
- VDRrs731236 AA and VDRrs11568820 CC genotypes correlated with timing of first symptomatic event.

The authors propose a new paradigm incorporating both hemorrhage and epilepsy as components of aggressive CCM behavior, and hypothesize an inflammatory cascade triggering autoimmune-like responses against CCM lesions, potentially opening avenues for immunomodulatory interventions.

Methane (CH4) gas bubbles in shallow muddy aquatic sediments pose environmental, climatic, and mechanical risks. These bubbles nucleate under supersaturated conditions, grow beyond pore scale by displacing sediment, and form disc-shaped cavities. Their growth is governed by coupled mechanical and biogeochemical processes, accurately described by Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics (LEFM) theory, which treats large bubbles as Mode I tensile gas-filled cracks.

The model simulates bubble growth beginning with a 3D penny-shaped seed embedded in a symmetry plane of a sediment box, continuing until a "mature" inverted tear-drop configuration develops. Outside the bubble, dissolved methane transport follows a solute conservation equation with uniform concentration boundaries, while solid mechanics uses a Force Equilibrium Equation under a Kelvin-Voigt framework where elastic behavior dominates at longer timescales. Methane conservation within the bubble integrates flux across its surface, with Henry's Law governing equilibrium between gaseous and aqueous concentrations, and ideal gas law determining inner bubble pressure.

Fracture modeling uses the Displacement/Stress Extrapolation Method to calculate Mode I stress intensity factors (SIF), with the Strain Energy Density Criterion determining crack propagation direction. Cracks propagate when maximum SIF exceeds the sediment fracture toughness, with increments largest at the bubble's head. The model is implemented in COMSOL Multiphysics using FEM with adaptive meshing.

Simulations use parameters from Eckernförde Bay summer conditions. Validation against analytical solutions for bubble semi-height and crack opening displacement showed good agreement across varying fracture toughness values, with lower toughness producing smaller, flatter bubbles and higher toughness producing larger, more inflated bubbles. The model is limited to individual bubbles and requires future upscaling methods for broader applications in remote sensing and geohazard assessment.

This study addresses the challenge of improving teacher education students' (TESs) ability to diagnose student learning problems and design effective instructional activities.

**Literature Review:** Effective teaching requires diagnosing student learning through observation of behaviors reflecting cognitive processes. Collaborative inquiry—involving lesson preparation, teaching, observation, and post-lesson discussion—helps teachers link instructional activities to student outcomes. However, TESs often lack diagnostic observation skills and struggle to collect sufficient evidence. Panoramic cameras offer a potential solution by capturing multi-angle classroom recordings for review.

**Methodology:** A "Professional Teaching Practicum" course (September 2022–January 2023) was implemented with 22 TESs divided into five groups. The course comprised two stages: a five-week preparation phase covering collaborative inquiry concepts, lesson planning, observation training, and panoramic camera use; followed by a 12-week collaborative inquiry cycle in which TESs alternated between teaching and observing in junior high classrooms, using panoramic cameras to supplement observation records. Data were collected via an Observation Record Form (scored using a three-rank checklist) and a 12-item questionnaire on perceived instructional design capabilities, analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.

**Results:** Observation report scores improved across four cycles (averages rising from 0.47 to 1.88 out of 2), indicating enhanced diagnostic capabilities. Questionnaire results showed statistically significant improvements (p < 0.05) across all three facets: lesson preparation (Z = -4.025), linking student learning with observation (Z = -3.535), and adjusting lesson plans post-discussion (Z = -3.536).

**Conclusion:** Integrating collaborative inquiry with panoramic cameras effectively enhanced TESs' diagnostic abilities and instructional design capabilities. The approach improves upon traditional mentor-guided observation by providing concrete evidence for reflection. A limitation is the difficulty in verifying the effectiveness of proposed instructional strategies due to TESs' limited teaching experience. The model may also apply to other professional education fields.

Amazon has received a patent for a "directed fragmentation" system for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) used in deliveries. The drone would use terrain topology data to identify safer drop locations, such as bodies of water, forests, or open fields, while avoiding buildings, roads, and populated areas. Components could be released via latches, hooks, springs, small explosive charges, or compressed gas. The order of release would consider factors like replacement cost, weight, and purpose of each component.

The patent, applied for in June 2016, does not guarantee implementation, and the system appears unsuitable for urban areas.

Social media platforms are increasingly using artificial intelligence to moderate content that violates community standards, such as hate speech and extremism. A.I. can recognize offensive language across multiple languages and identify images, including symbols like swastikas, but its accuracy is inconsistent. Notable failures include Google Photos tagging dark-skinned people as "gorillas" and Twitter suppressing LGBT-related hashtags due to an outdated algorithm.

A.I. systems are inherently biased because they are trained on human-tagged data, and shared training sets can spread these biases across multiple programs. Additionally, A.I. cannot determine intent, leading to mistakes like Facebook removing anti-hate posts containing swastikas or historic photographs.

Consequently, human moderators remain essential. Facebook is doubling its review team to 20,000. A.I. helps by screening and prioritizing content for human reviewers, improving efficiency—such as identifying suicidal posts. Industry experts emphasize that A.I. is not close to full automation and warn that ethical considerations are lagging behind technological advancement, suggesting a growing need for employees with humanities or ethics backgrounds.

This patent application describes a method and system for manufacturing orthodontic appliances through digital treatment planning. The method involves measuring a patient's tooth positions, receiving tooth movement constraints, and measuring elements of dental malocclusion. Multiple treatment plans are generated in parallel, each branching into additional plans based on treatment decisions such as bicuspid extraction, molar and canine relationship corrections, overjet correction, and interproximal reduction.

The process evaluates malocclusions including openbite, molar class problems (I, II, III, or mixed), posterior crossbite, canine class problems, bi-protrusion, and overjet. At each decision point, treatment plans branch based on measured thresholds (typically 2-3 mm for root apical movement or overjet) and clinical settings. Each branch inherits previous corrections and continues through subsequent steps, generating many clinically distinct plans.

A dental professional selects one plan from the generated options, after which instructions are output to fabricate appliances for each treatment stage. Appliances can be produced via direct fabrication (stereolithography, selective laser sintering, fused deposition modeling, 3D printing) or indirect fabrication (thermoforming over molds). The system includes processors, memory, scanners, and fabrication machines, potentially distributed across networked locations. This parallel evaluation approach aims to produce improved treatment outcomes with shorter treatment times and less invasive procedures compared to traditional linear planning methods.

This study evaluated the effect of COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) in patients with hematological malignancies and COVID-19, enrolled in a French monitored access program between May 2020 and April 2021. The CCP cohort included 112 patients (83 with B-lymphoid neoplasm, 19 with multiple myeloma, 10 with myeloid neoplasm), who received four ABO-compatible CCP units with verified anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody content. A subset of B-cell neoplasm patients was compared to 120 non-CCP-treated patients using propensity score and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) analyses to limit indication and immortal time biases.

CCP transfusion was well tolerated and associated with significant decreases in temperature, CRP, ferritin, and fibrinogen, along with increased PCR cycle thresholds at day 7. The 90-day overall survival was 64.9% overall and 77.5% in B-lymphoid neoplasm patients, but only 20% and 36.8% in myeloid and plasma cell neoplasm patients, respectively. In multivariable analysis, age over 70, high blood pressure, and COVID-19 severity were associated with higher mortality, whereas prior anti-CD20/CD19 therapy was associated with better survival. IPTW analyses showed CCP reduced death risk by 40–63% in anti-CD20 pre-exposed B-cell neoplasm patients.

Limitations include the retrospective design, lack of viral strain data, and absence of vaccinated patients. The authors conclude CCP is beneficial for B-cell lymphoid malignancy patients pre-treated with anti-CD20 antibodies, who respond poorly to vaccination, pending confirmation by randomized trials and consideration alongside anti-spike monoclonal antibodies.

The passage lists known silicon issues for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Revision A3, including problems with PMC sleep clock control, GLIU errors, UART register access during DMA, DMA memory writes, I/O addressing above 10000h, PIC interrupt handling, UDMA CRC corruption, ACPI register access, USB clock gating, LPC aborts, and GPIO register writes after suspend.

- PIT deviates from standard by not cancelling uncompleted latch commands upon read-back, though impact is negligible.
- The GLIU debug port hangs when used; workaround is to avoid it since internal traffic is already externally visible via PCI.

- DMA rotating priority mode does not rotate correctly, but transfers still complete, with minimal practical effect.
- Thermal alarm recovery is impaired because the alarm resides in the Work domain, though the system cycles through standby until the condition clears.
- Disabling the Sleep Clock affects other optional sleep features; it should always be enabled in the PMC register.

Electric Resistance Welding (ERW) is used for transporting vapor and liquid substances like petroleum and gas under varying pressures. Welded pipes include submerged arc welded steel pipes (marked SC for water/gas), thinner line pipes (marked T for threading), and ERW high-frequency resistance welded pipes. ERW offers high efficiency, low cost, and material savings, and is used across multiple industries. Modern ERW production ensures quality seaming, with internal burr removal controlled to 0.2–0.5 mm. Made from hot-rolled coil with wall thickness controlled to ±0.2mm, ERW pipes follow API or GB/T9711.1 standards and are widely used in urban gas pipe networks.

This patent application, a continuation of multiple prior applications dating back to 2015, relates to media playback systems and methods for identifying audio content facilitated by a playback device.

The disclosure describes a playback device configured to: (i) receive digital data representing audio content, (ii) send at least a portion of the digital data to an identification system that identifies the audio content, (iii) receive information associated with the audio content from the identification system, (iv) forward that information to a control device, and (v) play the audio content through connected speakers. Using the playback device rather than the control device for identification is described as more efficient, since the playback device already receives and processes the digital data, avoiding the need for microphone capture and analog-to-digital conversion by the control device.

The system operates within a media playback environment (exemplified by Sonos systems) featuring multiple networked playback devices across zones that can play synchronously or independently, controlled via software on smartphones, tablets, or computers.

Additional described features include: sending digital data portions at periodic intervals, detecting discontinuities (such as silence) to trigger re-identification, sample rate conversion, decoding, dynamically changing the audio pipeline extraction point, segregating data by frequency range, and retrieving metadata from a curating device using identifiers. The control device can display retrieved metadata (track title, artist, album) and request refreshed information when existing metadata is incomplete.

This disclosure describes a directional display device comprising an imaging directional backlight with a waveguide, a transmissive spatial light modulator, input and output polarisers, at least one additional polariser, and at least one retarder. The retarder may include passive retarders (such as crossed A-plates, C-plates, or O-plates) and a switchable liquid crystal retarder controlled by applied voltage.

The waveguide images light sources in a lateral direction, directing output light into optical windows based on input positions. The additional polariser may be reflective and positioned on either the input or output side, with parallel electric vector transmission to the adjacent polariser to maintain head-on efficiency.

The device enables switching between wide angle and privacy modes, reducing off-axis luminance visible to snoopers while maintaining luminance for primary users. The switchable liquid crystal retarder may use homeotropic alignment with correcting passive retarders (negative C-plates or crossed positive A-plates) having specified optical thicknesses. Independently addressable regions allow variable privacy levels, and camouflage patterns may be implemented via patterned electrodes.

A control system synchronizes the spatial light modulator, light sources, and retarder voltage, optionally displaying primary images to primary observers and obscuring secondary images to snoopers through temporal multiplexing. Snooper location detection can adjust applied voltage accordingly. Applications include automotive displays mounted beneath transparent windows to reduce reflections. Additional embodiments include multiple stacked switchable liquid crystal retarders with various alignment configurations, and non-directional backlight variants providing wide viewing cones in wide angle mode.

A Deloitte study reveals growing consumer confidence in autonomous vehicles, with only 49% now viewing them as unsafe, down from 73% last year. Trust in traditional car manufacturers (51%) significantly outweighs trust in technology companies (21%) to develop the technology, with 53% of respondents citing brand trustworthiness as a reason for confidence. In contrast, electric vehicles remain unpopular, with 73% preferring engine-powered cars and only 2% choosing electric, citing concerns over driving range, price, and charging infrastructure. Customer service also ranked highly, with 71% considering it important. Despite increased consumer trust in driverless cars, the UK government is launching a safety inquiry ahead of their anticipated roll-out.

The Presidential Election Cycle theory, formulated by Yale Hirsch in the 1967 Stock Trader's Almanac, asserts that U.S. stock market performance follows a predictable four-year pattern tied to presidential terms. Based on historical data, the market performs worst in the first two years and best in the last two, peaking in the third year. Since 1952, the S&P 500 has averaged 12.5% gains in election years with an incumbent running, 6.7% in all election years, and -1.5% when no incumbent runs. Midterm election years, particularly the second year, tend to be the weakest until the fourth quarter, with increased volatility.

Certain sectors, such as healthcare and energy, experience heightened volatility around elections due to policy differences between parties. Analysts note that equities and bonds typically underperform in the year preceding a presidential election, while the S&P 500 performs better after midterms. Consistency in these trends holds except during major shocks like recessions. Experts attribute the patterns to election-related uncertainty and suggest investors focus on policy impacts, maintain diversified portfolios, and rebalance regularly rather than react to election-driven volatility.

Intel has embedded a microcontroller called the Management Engine (ME) in its CPUs for over a decade. The ME is connected to storage and network interfaces, remains active even when the computer is off, and runs the Minix operating system. Researchers Mark Ermolov and Maxim Goryachy recently presented an exploit at BlackHat Europe enabling arbitrary code execution on the ME, though it requires physical access via USB.

Because Intel kept the ME closed-source, security researchers previously could not assess its vulnerabilities. Mitigation options are limited: System76 released firmware to disable the ME, and Dell offers a laptop with ME disabled by default. Intel provides a detection tool, but disabling methods vary by motherboard manufacturer. A computer lacking valid ME firmware shuts down after 30 minutes, but the me_cleaner tool tricks the ME into appearing functional while disabling it.

The current exploit requires physical access, but a remote network-based exploit remains the ultimate concern. The article frames the ME as validation of long-standing warnings about hidden hardware surveillance.

New Jersey Governor Chris Christie signed legislation strengthening legal protections for people with developmental disabilities and increasing family involvement in their care. The bill was prompted by the 2007 death of 22-year-old Stephen Komninos in a Haddonfield group home, whose family alleged caregiver neglect. The law allows state inspectors to make unannounced visits to group homes twice a year, authorizes the Department of Human Services to hire additional staff, requires operators to notify parents or guardians within two-to-eight hours of a patient injury, and mandates biannual family meetings. Christie stated the measure is not an indictment of caregivers but aims to ensure quality care.

This paper presents a philosophical analysis of Mortimer J. Adler's perennialism and its application to Christian education and global education management. Using qualitative literature review methodology with Adler's books as primary sources and international journals as secondary sources, the researchers examine how Adler's perennialist philosophy—which emphasizes eternal, sustainable values over instant achievement—applies to contemporary educational challenges, including posthumanism.

The researchers explore Adler's concepts of docility and obedience as enduring educational values, arguing these represent not slavery but intellectual postponement of judgment toward trusted authority. They critique Adler's failure to differentiate between male and female educational participants, noting women require prior support due to historical subordination.

Regarding posthumanism, the paper questions human identity amid technological developments like AI and humanoid robots, examining how humans coexist with non-human entities and technology. The researchers review multiple studies on Christian-based education management across contexts including family meals, spirituality and health, cross-cultural student participation, Christian business families, institutional transformation in Kenya, disaster response in New Zealand, and investor identity diversity.

The researchers conclude that a just educational society requires empowering women and avoiding forcing children toward adult expectations. They argue failures in education should not scapegoat children but prompt teachers, parents, and governments to reorganize educational praxis. Teachers' responsibilities extend beyond classrooms, and Adler's perennialist framework directs educational management toward deeper engagement with learners rather than administrative concerns or instant achievement, with relevance to Indonesia's independent curriculum.

The Cleveland Browns have not eliminated Oklahoma quarterback Baker Mayfield as a possibility for the No. 1 pick in Thursday's NFL draft, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. General manager John Dorsey has stated he remains open to "all options" for the No. 1 and No. 4 picks, while head coach Hue Jackson indicated all four top quarterbacks—Sam Darnold, Josh Allen, Mayfield, and Josh Rosen—are under consideration. Nicola Sturgeon has criticised Theresa May's call for a snap general election on 8 June, describing it as an "extraordinary U-turn" and a "huge political miscalculation". The MSPM0C1105/C1106 MCU integrates an Arm Cortex-M0+ CPU (up to 32MHz) with pre-fetch logic, I-cache, SysTick timer, and NVIC. It supports five operating modes (RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN) across two power domains (PD1, PD0) for optimized power consumption.

Key subsystems include a PMU with BOR supply monitoring, a clock module with multiple internal/external oscillators, and a DMA controller with 3 channels supporting various transfer modes. The device features an event manager for routing digital events between peripherals, CPU, and DMA.

Memory includes flash (with up to 100,000 program/erase cycles on select sectors) and SRAM with write protection, retained in all modes except SHUTDOWN. Peripherals include up to 45 GPIOs, a 12-bit ADC (1.6-Msps), temperature sensor, VREF, comparator, CRC-16, UART, I2C (up to 1Mbps), SPI (up to 16Mbits/s), IWDT, WWDT, RTC_B, and general-purpose/advanced timers.

Security features include firewalls and CRC. Debug is supported via a two-wire SWD interface through the DEBUGSS subsystem. A memory-mapped FACTORY region stores device identification and trim data. The document also covers application schematics, package information, and development tool support.

Lawyers for Venezuelan citizens have asked the Supreme Court to leave in place a San Francisco federal judge's order that temporarily bars the Trump administration from ending their Temporary Protected Status (TPS). The TPS program, created by Congress in 1990, allows the DHS Secretary to designate citizens of certain countries as eligible to remain and work in the U.S. due to conditions in their home country.

Former DHS Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas designated Venezuela for TPS in 2021, redesignated it in 2023, and extended it through October 2026. After taking office, DHS Secretary Kristi Noem ended both the 2023 designation and the 2025 extension. The National TPS Alliance and Venezuelan TPS holders challenged the termination, arguing it violated federal administrative law and was motivated by racial animus.

On March 31, Judge Edward Chen temporarily blocked Noem's action. The Supreme Court paused Chen's order on May 19, with only Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson dissenting. On September 5, Chen issued a final ruling that Noem acted unlawfully, stating the Supreme Court's earlier order did not bar a final judgment on the merits. The 9th Circuit declined to pause this ruling, prompting Solicitor General D. John Sauer to return to the Supreme Court on September 19.

The challengers argue the Supreme Court's prior limited stay did not foreclose further litigation, noting Chen's recent ruling relies on different statutory authority, addresses a new claim, and is based on a more developed record.

The invention relates to an optical waveguide display apparatus and method for enhancing the field of view (FOV). In prior art waveguides, light is injected via a Bragg grating and propagates by total internal reflection (TIR), but the FOV is limited by TIR angular constraints and varies with wavelength, causing colour-dependent losses.

The invention addresses this by coating the external waveguide surfaces, against which light reflects internally, with a material (e.g. a meta-material) having a refractive index substantially equal to or less than 1.0 at optical wavelengths. This reduces the critical TIR angle, allowing light from a wider input FOV to be retained and guided along the waveguide.

The apparatus comprises an optical waveguide with a first diffractive part to receive and diffract display light for TIR propagation, and a second diffractive part to diffract light out for viewing. The diffractive parts may be Bragg gratings, optionally surface-profile gratings, and may be mutually conjugated to reduce geometric distortion and chromatic dispersion.

The meta-material may consist of periodic unit cells containing a magnetic resonator (e.g. alumina between silver plates) sandwiched between conductive meshes, or parallel conductive nanowires. Geometric parameters can be optimised to achieve refractive index values between 0 and 1.

Multi-layered slab waveguides are described, where component waveguides tuned to different colours are joined by an intermediate meta-material layer, optionally with outer protective plastic layers. The coating protects exposed gratings and waveguide surfaces from damage and contamination while enhancing TIR performance and enabling wider FOV multi-colour displays.

The lecture reviews three major theorems for renewal processes: the strong law for renewals (sample path time average), the elementary renewal theorem (expected rate of renewals approaches 1/x-bar), and Blackwell's theorem (which addresses limitations of expected values). Blackwell's theorem applies differently to arithmetic and non-arithmetic renewal processes.

The professor then examines age and duration at specific time t for arithmetic renewal processes. By defining q sub j as the probability of arrival at time j, the joint probability of age and duration asymptotically depends only on the inter-renewal interval, not on age. This provides a precise mathematical foundation for the "random incidence" concept. The expected duration equals E[x²]/E[x], and expected age is E[x²]/(2E[x]), with the factor of 1/2 arising from integer-versus-continuous time considerations.

The lecture transitions to countable-state Markov chains, where recurrence requires careful definition. Using a Bernoulli process model and birth-death chains as examples, the professor shows that probability distributions spread out over time (variance grows with n), meaning steady-state probabilities can be zero even when returns occur with probability 1.

First passage time probabilities f_ij(n) are defined, with recursion relations relating them to transition probabilities p_ij(n). A state j is recurrent if f_jj(∞) = 1, making returns to j a renewal process. States in the same class are either all recurrent or all transient. Null recurrent states have infinite expected return time (and zero steady-state probability), while positive recurrent states have finite expected return time.

The author recounts developing sepsis in 2015 after scratching their hand on a nail, falling into a three-month coma, and taking a year to recover. Sepsis affects over 30 million people annually and kills around 6 million, including nearly 2 million children. Of survivors, 40% experience post-sepsis syndrome with lasting symptoms.

Sepsis is triggered by the body's uncontrolled response to an infection, leading to rapid organ failure. Symptoms include pale or mottled skin, severe breathlessness, shivering, muscle pain, lack of urination, and vomiting. Anyone can develop sepsis, though vitamin D deficiency may increase risk.

There is no specific cure, but new research indicates metformin may reduce sepsis's impact, and gene therapy targeting the NF-kB protein shows promise. Public awareness remains low—40% in Australia, 14% in Brazil, and over 60% in the UK and Germany, though knowledge of symptoms is limited. Efforts to improve healthcare worker education include the Sepsis6 protocol. Greater awareness is considered the most effective current defence.

This paper presents a face anonymization system for scientific experimental education within AIED (Artificial Intelligence in Education). The system addresses a key challenge: anonymizing student faces while preserving visibility of experimental instruments and operational techniques needed for evaluation.

The authors identify limitations in existing methods: multi-object tracking, K-same clustering, and GAN-based approaches are not tailored for experimental education contexts, where instruments often include fine structures (wires) or transparent objects (beakers) that traditional blurring obscures.

The proposed solution includes two main innovations:
1. **MSFF-YOLOv8 (Multi-Scale Feature Fusion YOLOv8)**: An enhanced YOLOv8 architecture with additional feature connection paths between shallow and deep layers, improving small object detection and adding a semantic segmentation branch.
2. **CAOR (Contour-Adaptive Occlusion Refinement)**: A data preprocessing module that dilates occlusion mask edges outward from the face center, preventing instruments near facial contours from being misclassified and blurred.

The authors created a specialized dataset of 51 experimental videos with manual annotations (7,590 face labels, 5,240 instrument labels, 1,530 pose labels). They introduced two evaluation metrics: SOBA (Sensitivity of Blur Accuracy) and OBR (Over Blur Rate).

Experimental results show the system achieves 96.02% accuracy (SOBA) with a low 0.0159 OBR at 22.67 fps on 1080p video, outperforming SAM, Edge-SAM, and standard YOLOv8. CAOR reduced the over-blur rate by approximately 10%.

The system successfully balances privacy protection with experimental detail preservation across physics, biology, and chemistry settings. Future work will focus on improving real-time edge classification during inference.

A trade deficit reduces domestic demand, shifting it abroad and potentially increasing unemployment, though this can be offset by budget deficits or economic bubbles. The claim that the dollar's reserve currency status forces trade deficits is flawed, as the dollar is one of several reserve currencies, and countries like China and South Korea hold excess reserves deliberately to maintain a trade advantage—a policy that could be challenged. Regarding Samuelson's criticism of China coercing technology transfers from foreign companies, firms like Boeing and Apple voluntarily chose to invest in China under those conditions, as they were better positioned than individual workers to protect their interests.

The RSI is a mean-reversion indicator used on stock indices like QQQ. This article tests an RSI 2 trading strategy on QQQ, where positions are entered when the two-day RSI is below a low threshold.

Using an RSI 2 reading below 10, the strategy returned 10.01% compared to 6.39% for buy and hold, and performed well during four bear markets (2000-2002, 2008/09, 2018, and March 2020). Lowering the threshold to 5 increased average gain but reduced total return due to fewer trades.

Adding a second indicator while keeping RSI(2) below 10 improved results: a CAGR of 12.7%, 14% time in market, 232 trades, 75% winners, profit factor of 3, max drawdown of 19.5%, and Sharpe Ratio of 2.85. The code is available for purchase or via subscription. The RSI 2 reportedly works better on QQQ than on the S&P 500.

SD Memory Cards are designed for audio and video consumer electronics, offering security, high capacity, and performance. They employ a content protection mechanism compliant with SDMI standards, using mutual authentication and a new cipher algorithm, while also permitting non-secure access to user content. A secondary security system based on standards like ISO-7816 may be supported for mobile e-commerce and digital signature applications.

Separately, SDIO Cards, defined in the "SDIO Card Specification," provide interfaces between I/O units and an SD Host and may also include memory storage. SDIO cards are mechanically, electrically, and software-compatible with SD Memory Cards, aiming to deliver high-speed I/O with low power consumption. When inserted into non-SDIO aware hosts, the card is ignored without causing damage.

SD Memory Card communication uses a 9-pin interface (Clock, Command, 4xData, 3xPower), operating at up to 208 MHz within a low voltage range.
