Researchers conducted repeated cross-sectional SARS-CoV-2 serosurveys among 9,221 pregnant women attending first antenatal care (ANC) visits in four Zambian districts (Chadiza, Chipata, Chongwe, Lusaka) from September 2021 to September 2022, spanning the Omicron wave and early COVID-19 vaccine rollout. Using a multiplex bead assay detecting nucleocapsid and spike antibodies, 63.8% of 8,304 valid samples were seropositive. Seroprevalence rose over time, approaching 100% in Lusaka, Chipata, and Chongwe by August 2022, while peaking at 77.2% in rural Chadiza in April 2022 before declining. Most antibodies were infection-induced (77.7%); only 1.6% were vaccination-only, and 20.6% reflected hybrid immunity, which produced the strongest anti-RBD responses. Vaccination coverage among participants rose from 4.4% to 26.6%, with Janssen the most common vaccine. COVID-19 vaccination was associated with higher seropositivity across all districts, while age, education, occupation, and HIV status showed district-specific associations. Ratios of seroprevalence to reported cumulative incidence ranged from 29:1 to 92:1, indicating substantial case underreporting. Limitations include non-representative sampling, restriction to women aged 15–49, potential antibody waning, and early termination of Chadiza surveillance. The study demonstrates the feasibility of using ANC clinics for SARS-CoV-2 serosurveillance and supports subnational, tailored COVID-19 mitigation and vaccination strategies.

Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) has a 5-year survival rate of approximately 14%, creating a need for biomarkers to monitor disease progression. This study evaluated the clinical relevance of circulating tumor cell (CTC) genomic variation in mCRC using whole-exome sequencing data from CTC pools collected from 29 patients.

Blood samples were processed using the Parsortix® platform to enrich CTCs, while peripheral blood mononuclear cells served as healthy controls. Whole-genome amplification was performed on CTC pools, and both CTC pools and PBMC samples underwent whole-exome sequencing. Somatic variants, copy number alterations, microsatellite instability status, and mutational signatures were identified. Genomic diversity was measured using 15 metrics, including mutational burden, proportion of aberrant genome (PAG), and mutant allele tumor heterogeneity (MATH) score.

One patient exhibited microsatellite instability and was excluded from downstream analyses. CTC pools showed high genomic variation, with recurrent mutations in CRC driver genes including ARID1A, BCL9L, BIRC6, and KMT2C. Multivariate analysis revealed that high MATH scores (HR=5.0, p=0.008) and non-silent BCL9L mutations (HR=5.6, p=0.009) were significantly associated with poorer overall survival. Patients with low MATH scores had a median survival of 52.9 months versus 18.3 months for high MATH scores. BCL9L-mutated patients survived 14.5 months compared to 34.2 months for unmutated patients.

A custom 55-gene panel (CRC-P55) produced MATH scores strongly correlated with whole-exome results and retained prognostic value, while two commercial panels did not. The authors note that small sample size limits generalizability and that larger cohorts are needed for validation. This represents the first study linking CTC genomic diversity to cancer outcomes in mCRC.

BerkeleyGW achieves exascale performance for quantum many-body materials simulations, demonstrating portability across AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA GPU architectures on Frontier, Aurora, and Perlmutter supercomputers. The software implements the GW approximation and GW perturbation theory (GWPT) to compute electronic quasiparticle excitations and electron-phonon coupling beyond the limitations of density functional theory.

Key innovations include: directive-based OpenACC and OpenMP models for portability; hardware-optimized kernels using HIP, SYCL, and CUDA; a fast full-frequency GW method using static subspace approximation; and a mixed stochastic-deterministic pseudobands algorithm that reduces scaling. Optimized kernels for diagonal and off-diagonal self-energy matrix elements employ techniques including memory coalescing, block size tuning, loop unrolling, and ZGEMM reformulation.

Performance results include 1.069 ExaFLOP/s on Frontier's full machine (75,264 GPUs, 59.45% of theoretical peak) and 707.52 PetaFLOP/s on 90.4% of Aurora (115,200 GPUs, 48.79% of attainable peak) in double precision. The system enables calculations on materials with up to 17,574 atoms, including silicon and lithium hydride defects and BN moiré superlattices, advancing predictive modeling of complex quantum materials for electronic, optical, and quantum device applications.

The ASP Process of SFS involves checking DRAM address protection, verifying customer and AMD signatures, loading and running the executable patch, updating patch level information, and returning status to the software agent. The ASP interface provides base firmware and patch levels for microprocessors.

The GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO command uses two 4096-byte pages sent to the ASP interface to check firmware versions, with output initialized to C7h. SNP systems require HV-FIXED pages. Output includes API version, current SFS patch level, system patch level, and firmware version entries (type enum, version, and Security Patch Level). Unsupported items show 0000_0000h.

The SFS sub-command instructs the ASP to load, verify, and execute the package, applying updates only after full validation. SFS packages are binary objects aligned to AGESA releases, named as fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg. Platform providers coordinate releases through AMD customer channels.

Update packages must match specific firmware and system patch levels on the target system. Updates run parallel to x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact, ideally requiring no OS quiescing. Few operations require quiescing; for example, SEV/ES virtual machines must restart for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating through such updates.

This paper introduces ABXLAB, an open-source man-in-the-middle framework that modifies real-world web content in real-time to study LLM agent decision-making under controlled behavioral manipulations. The authors evaluated 17 state-of-the-art language models across over 80,000 trials in a consumer shopping environment, testing sensitivity to product ratings, prices, presentation order, and persuasive nudges (authority, social proof, scarcity, negative framing, incentives).

Results show that LLM agents exhibit systematic biases far exceeding human susceptibility, with effect sizes up to 90+ percentage points compared to modest human responses (4-10pp). Agents displayed hypersensitivity to ratings (30-80pp shifts), strong price preferences (intensifying when ratings were matched), inconsistent order effects across models, and substantial responsiveness to nudges (10-60pp shifts). The Wirecutter authority nudge had the largest impact.

When given explicit user preference profiles, agents behaved like categorical switches, with stated preferences dominating decisions and suppressing competing attributes. The authors conclude that agents employ simplistic, hierarchical decision rules and release ABXLAB to support further behavioral research on AI agents.

First Solar, a thin-film cadmium telluride (CdTe) photovoltaic manufacturer, faced significant challenges in 2011. After becoming the first PV manufacturer to produce panels below $1/watt in 2009, the company reported its first year-end net operating loss ($39 million) in seven years, with revenue growth slowing to 8%. Senior VP Tymen deJong confronted eroding competitive advantages caused by subsidized Chinese crystalline-silicon manufacturers flooding the market, declining European subsidies following the 2008-2009 financial crisis, and falling silicon prices that benefited competitors.

The PV industry featured two main technologies: dominant crystalline silicon (85% market share) and thin-film. First Solar controlled proprietary CdTe technology developed through substantial R&D investment, operating 36 production lines across Ohio, Germany, and Malaysia. The company pursued vertical integration, acquiring system integrators to expand into utility-scale projects, growing systems sales from 5% to 25% of revenue between 2009-2011. It maintained a conservative financial strategy with lower debt than competitors.

Chinese manufacturers, supported by government subsidies for demand and supply, grew from under 1% to nearly 60% of global PV production by 2012. A Department of Energy study found Chinese producers had an 18-20% cost advantage, partly from subsidies. Industry consolidation resulted in bankruptcies including Evergreen Solar, SpectraWatt, and Solyndra.

First Solar controlled 41% of the U.S. market, with SunPower holding 38.5%. DeJong needed to evaluate whether First Solar's competitive edge was sustainable, how to counter Chinese competition, and whether its systems acquisitions were strategic assets or distractions.

Alabama held off Vanderbilt 30-14 after Vandy turnovers in the red zone, while Miami defeated Florida State, which committed three turnovers. In the Big 12, Texas Tech dominated Houston, Cincinnati upset Iowa State, and BYU, Baylor, TCU, and Kansas also won.

In this lecture, Alan Oppenheim demonstrates sampling, aliasing, and properties of discrete time linear systems using a programmable digital filter. The filter setup consists of a sampler, C-to-D converter, digital filter, D-to-C converter, and a smoothing low-pass filter.

First, using the digital filter as an identity system, Oppenheim illustrates aliasing. When a sinusoidal input's frequency exceeds half the sampling frequency, the output frequency decreases rather than increases, due to aliases falling within the low-pass filter's passband. A beating phenomenon also occurs near half the sampling frequency because real low-pass filters are non-ideal.

Next, a symmetric linear-phase low-pass digital filter with a cutoff of pi/5 is inserted. The equivalent continuous-time frequency response has the same shape as the digital filter's response but with a rescaled frequency axis, where 2 pi corresponds to the sampling frequency. Thus, the effective analog cutoff frequency equals one-tenth of the sampling frequency.

Demonstrations show the symmetric impulse response, the boxcar output before smoothing, and the filter's frequency response via sinusoidal sweeps. Changing the sampling frequency proportionally changes the effective cutoff frequency, demonstrated by sweeping sinusoids and filtering live audio at sampling rates from 40 kHz down to 2.5 kHz.

Tesla filed an 8-K announcing that Deepak Ahuja, who served as Chief Financial Officer since 2008 (with a 14-month gap), intends to retire. He will remain CFO briefly and then serve as an advisor to facilitate the transition. Tesla plans to appoint Zachary Kirkhorn, currently Vice President of Finance, Financial Planning and Business Operations, as the new CFO. Kirkhorn joined Tesla in March 2010 and contributed to programs including Gigafactory 1 and the Model X and Model 3 launches. CEO Elon Musk and both executives provided statements regarding the transition and Tesla's financial position.

Sun Waa, a Chinese takeaway in Oaklands Avenue, Littleover, Derby, received a food hygiene score of one from Derby City Council inspectors in November 2017. Inspectors found rice left at room temperature for six hours, a wash basin obstructed by a wok and utensils, food debris on work surfaces and behind appliances, a sink used for both raw meat and ready-to-eat foods, bleach being used on food preparation surfaces, insect webbing on a storeroom light bulb, and a non-functioning probe thermometer. On TripAdvisor, Sun Waa averages 3.5 stars from six reviews, and on Just Eat it has 5.5 out of 6 stars.

Tarren Joseph Titus, 23, of Sarnia received three months of house arrest and one year of probation after pleading guilty to possession of hydromorphone and two probation violations. Police found Titus attempting to escape during a June 2017 raid where the painkiller and drug paraphernalia were discovered. Justice Deborah Austin called his transformation "outstanding," imposing only a curfew during house arrest and requiring continued counseling. Prosecutor Michael Robb, who had sought six months of house arrest, expressed being impressed by Titus's progress. Defence lawyer Robert McFadden noted Titus had been exposed to drug culture from a young age. Titus has attended daily sobriety meetings for eight months.

Jonathan Toews stated that the team views winning the Stanley Cup at home or on the road as equivalent, and plans to focus on playing well despite surrounding excitement. He described the playoff journey as fast-paced and memorable, and noted his family finds watching more stressful than he finds playing. Toews said the team tends to improve as a series progresses and played well in the previous game but must improve further.

Brad Richards commented that the core group's past championship experience makes preparation easier, reducing the need for speeches. Toews credited coach Joel Quenneville with adjusting matchups and lineups effectively and enabling individual performance.

Kris Versteeg acknowledged Tampa Bay's skill and expected close games. Toews dismissed a comment about an opponent, describing him as a strong two-way player. Toews also attributed the team's health to player preparation and recovery habits.

Versteeg expressed excitement about his new line's chemistry. Toews reflected on the team's ability to return to the Finals despite roster changes, noting league-wide parity. Versteeg emphasized staying ready when not in the lineup.

Richards warned against complacency, stressing patience against a talented opponent. He praised a teammate's all-around play, defensive work, and leadership, citing his multiple Finals appearances.

Researchers Michelle Munson (NYU) and Sarah Narendorf (University of Houston) have spent a decade studying "mental health narratives"—how young adults perceive and interpret their mental health conditions. Their work, published in the American Journal of Orthopsychiatry and forthcoming in the Journal of the Society for Social Work and Research, focuses on marginalized youth, defined by the Institute of Medicine as those facing added challenges like poverty, disabilities, and reliance on safety-net systems.

The researchers argue that understanding a young person's own interpretation of their condition—its causes, management, and treatment—is essential to effective care. Unlike physical illness narratives, mental health narratives involve stigma and shame. The researchers use in-depth, open-ended interviews analyzed through qualitative methods.

They contend that a collaborative approach between provider and patient yields better outcomes than expert-driven diagnosis alone. Their current NIMH-funded project, "Just Do You," conducted in Brooklyn and the Bronx, tests whether narrative types generalize and evolve over time. They are also developing technology-based interventions with the Jed Foundation. Munson and Narendorf warn that many marginalized young adults don't seek help because they feel unheard by providers, emphasizing the need for cultural humility in mental health care.

Murad Rahimov, a 16-year-old Uzbek immigrant who became a U.S. citizen in January, received a private tour of NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center after an NPR listener, Aaron Schnittman, heard a story about his passion for space and connected him with his brother Jeremy Schnittman, an astrophysicist at Goddard.

Murad, who has dreamed of becoming an astronaut since age three, visited the facility with his mother, Limara. Jeremy Schnittman showed them the clean room, cryo-vac chamber, acoustic chamber, and laser lab, and discussed his black hole research and topics like time travel.

The Rahimov family immigrated from Uzbekistan in 2010. Murad, now entering his junior year of high school on an accelerated track, plans to attend Cal Tech and hopes to lead a Mars mission. His mother said citizenship made her feel more rooted in the U.S. Murad also planned to watch the upcoming total solar eclipse from Kansas City.

BBC presenter Anita Anand was removed from presenting Radio 4's Any Answers edition scheduled to discuss the corporation's gender pay dispute, because she had publicly supported the equal pay campaign on social media. She was replaced by Julian Worricker and is expected to return next week. Tory MP Andrew Bridgen criticised the decision, comparing it to Soviet-era practices and arguing it implied women journalists cannot be impartial. The BBC stated editors must decide case-by-case whether campaigning presenters can cover related topics. The dispute intensified after former China Editor Carrie Gracie revealed she earned less than male colleagues.

YETI coolers responded to an NRA claim that the company had cut ties with the organization. On April 20, the NRA sent a letter to members stating YETI refused to do business with the NRA Foundation without explanation. YETI countered on Twitter, saying it had notified the NRA Foundation and other groups that it was eliminating outdated discounting programs, while offering an alternative customization program available to the NRA Foundation and others. Some NRA supporters responded with boycotts, and one South Carolina man, Bryan Atkinson, shot a YETI cooler filled with explosives, sparking the #YetiCoolerChallenge trend. This benchmarking study evaluates 15 summary-level data-based Mendelian randomization (MR) methods for causal inference using real-world genetic datasets. The evaluation focuses on three aspects: type I error control under confounding scenarios (population stratification, pleiotropy, and family-level confounders), accuracy of causal effect estimates, and replicability/power.

The authors analyzed over 1,000 exposure-outcome trait pairs, including negative controls, six same-trait pairs with known causal effects of one, and a positive control case (LDL-C and coronary artery disease) using six LDL-C GWAS datasets. They also varied IV selection thresholds from 5×10⁻⁸ to 5×10⁻⁵.

Key findings indicate that MR-APSS, Egger, Weighted-mode, and CAUSE performed better in type I error control, though CAUSE showed deflated p-values. Most methods exhibited inflated type I errors under population stratification. Family-based GWAS data effectively controlled type I errors across all methods. MR-APSS demonstrated the highest accuracy in causal effect estimation and robustness to weak IV bias. CAUSE and MR-APSS showed strong replicability in the LDL-C/CAD analysis. IV selection thresholds significantly influenced method performance, with looser thresholds generally increasing bias.

The authors recommend using negative controls, multiple IV selection thresholds, and data from multiple independent sources to improve MR analysis reliability. Limitations include challenges in isolating specific confounders, indirect power assessment, and exclusion of individual-level MR methods.

Several foods are rich in folate (vitamin B9). Boiled asparagus provides 33% of the daily recommended folate per cup, while broccoli offers about 14% per cup. Citrus fruits, particularly oranges (50 mcg each), along with papaya, grapefruit, grapes, banana, and strawberries, are high in folate. Legumes such as beans, peas, and lentils meet most daily folate needs in a small bowl. Avocado contains 110 mcg per cup (28% of daily needs), and lady's finger provides 103 mcg per half cup cooked. Nuts and seeds, including sunflower and flax seeds, peanuts, and almonds, are also rich sources. Cauliflower offers 55 mcg per cup (14%), beetroot provides 14% per cup, raw carrots give 5% per cup, and cooked corn supplies 34 mcg per cup.

Zita Kovács began winemaking seven years ago, when few women worked in the field and she was often mistaken for a hostess; she now designs labels and names wines, and feels respected as a winemaker. Zsófi Laposa notes the profession was previously male-dominated due to physical demands, but technological advances have opened it to women. After studying in California, Burgundy, and Bordeaux, she earned a Master's in wine production in Bordeaux and believes women have invigorated the community. Krisztina Csetvei founded her winery in Mór in 2011 and balances winemaking with raising her daughter Panna, who attends tastings and harvests; their wine "Panna Rose" is named after her. Andi Gere co-manages the Gere Attila winery with her father, and believes feminine elegance complements the stronger style of men's wines.

This application relates to articles exhibiting structural color through optical elements, where color is produced by physical interaction of light with micro- or nano-features rather than dyes or pigments. The optical element can be used alone or combined with a textured surface and/or primer layer to impart structural color to articles such as footwear, apparel, sporting equipment, containers, electronics, and eyewear.

The optical element includes at least one optical layer (e.g., multilayer reflector or filter) and can be disposed on a component's surface. Structural colors may be single-hued, multi-hued, iridescent, or limited iridescent, and can be characterized using CIE 1976 (L*a*b*) or CIELCH color spaces measured at observation angles between -15 and +60 degrees.

The optical layers typically contain 2-20 layers of materials such as silicon dioxide, titanium dioxide, zinc sulfide, magnesium fluoride, tantalum pentoxide, or aluminum oxide, with thicknesses of 10-500 nanometers and differing refractive indices. Layers can be formed through various deposition techniques including physical vapor deposition, chemical vapor deposition, and sputtering.

Textured surfaces contain profile features (projections or depressions) ranging from 10 nanometers to 500 micrometers, which affect light scattering, diffraction, reflection, and interference. The optional primer layer (3 nanometers to 200 micrometers thick) can include paint, ink, metal, or oxide layers, typically in dark colors to enhance structural color appearance.

The polymers used can be thermoplastic or thermoset, including polyurethanes, polyesters, polyethers, polyamides, and copolymers, with specified melting temperatures, glass transition temperatures, and mechanical properties.

Several mining deals announced Monday suggest an uptick in mergers and acquisitions among junior mining companies, particularly in gold. Thus far in 2018, Canada has seen only six metals and mining mergers, compared to 19 at the same point in 2017, according to Financial Post data.

The largest deal is Hecla Mining Co.'s proposed US$462 million cash-and-share acquisition of Klondex Mines Ltd., which would give Hecla three Nevada gold mines producing 150,000 ounces annually, raising Hecla's gold production to 370,000 ounces. The speaker describes Detroit as the strongest team faced so far, citing their offensive firepower and elite goaltender. MSPM0C1105/6 are 32-bit ultra-low-power MCUs based on the Arm Cortex-M0+ core, operating up to 32MHz, with temperature ranges of -40°C to 125°C and supply voltages of 1.62V to 3.6V. Pusa, 63, a sitting All India Congress Committee member, has died, leaving behind his wife, two sons, and a daughter. He served as Nagaland's Minister for Veterinary and Animal Husbandry (1998-1999) and Minister for Roads and Bridges (2000-2003) under the SC Jamir-led Congress Government, and was an opposition Assembly member for two terms (2003-2013). India's 21 state-run banks posted a combined loss of 853.7 billion rupees ($12.65 billion) in fiscal year 2017/18, their largest ever, according to Reuters data. The losses followed the Reserve Bank of India's February withdrawal of loan restructuring schemes and imposition of stricter rules, which increased bad-loan provisions. Fourth-quarter losses totaled 626.81 billion rupees, with only Indian Bank and Vijaya Bank posting profits. Gross non-performing loans rose 15 percent quarter-on-quarter to 8.96 trillion rupees, with IDBI Bank recording the highest bad-loan ratio at 27.95 percent. New Delhi has announced a 2.11 trillion-rupee recapitalization plan, though concerns remain about banks' growth capacity after meeting Basel III requirements by March 2019.

A Zillow analysis found that U.S. homes with air conditioning sold for 2.5 percent more than homes without it, a premium of approximately $5,500. San Antonio had the highest premium at 5.8 percent, followed by Cincinnati at 5.7 percent, with Detroit, Indianapolis, and Las Vegas each at around 5 percent.

According to the 2017 Zillow Group Consumer Housing Trends Report, 62 percent of buyers listed air conditioning as a required feature, compared to 48 percent for private outdoor spaces. Nationally, 66.1 percent of homes sold in the past year had air conditioning, with near-universal presence in hot markets like Las Vegas (99.1 percent) and Phoenix (97.9 percent).

Renters paid a 2.8 percent premium (about $40 monthly) for rentals with central air conditioning. The New York, Las Vegas, and Phoenix metros had the highest rent premiums. Options trading in IWM involves buying and selling call and put options, giving buyers the right to buy or sell shares at an agreed price before expiration. It offers leverage, hedging, and speculation benefits but carries risks, including potential total loss or unlimited risk on short calls.

Available order types include market, limit, stop, and trailing stop orders. Strategies include buying calls or puts based on price predictions, selling covered calls, and buying protective puts. Traders should use technical indicators like moving averages, RSI, and Bollinger Bands, and backtest strategies before committing funds.

Requirements include a margin account and sufficient funds, with minimum balances typically around $2,000. Short selling and margin trading are allowed but risky. Taxes apply to profits, with rates depending on holding period. Fees vary by broker.

Investors should research underlying assets, select contracts based on length, expiration, and strike price, and allocate no more than 10% of their portfolio to options. Beginners are advised against options trading, and backtesting is strongly recommended.

Governor Kay Ivey announced the voluntary Alabama Sentry Program, which permits trained administrators in schools without a school resource officer to store a firearm in a safe on campus for use during active shooter situations. Participants must complete training and obtain approval from the local superintendent, school board, and county sheriff. Sentries or their boards of education must supply an approved weapon, ammunition, and bullet-proof vest. Ivey described the program as a temporary measure until more School Resource Officers can be added. Alabama Secretary of Law Enforcement Hal Taylor and Superintendent of Education Dr. Eric Mackey expressed support for the initiative.

This patent application describes a system and method for tracing cryptocurrency transactions and managing blockchain transaction risk using artificial intelligence and machine learning. The system receives blockchain transaction data and intelligence labels containing behavioral characteristics of entities associated with blockchain addresses. Users can input trace parameters including directional settings, tracing constraints, and transaction filters based on timestamps and assets transferred. An AI graph search algorithm determines auto-traced paths of digital assets, generating reports with summary statistics and identifying suspicious addresses.

Key components include a digital asset intake engine, entity knowledge base, risk classification engine with machine learning, risk scoring regression engine, risk policy engine, and security control system. When suspicious addresses are detected, the system can alert users, flag illicit transactions, or suspend transactions. Risk scores range from 0-100, categorized as Safe, Legitimate, Unknown, Suspicious, or Risky.

The machine learning models include AutoML pipelines, decision trees, and regression models that analyze feature categories such as statistics, topology, temporal patterns, linkage, and sequential behaviors. Applications include anti-money laundering, cybersecurity blockchain forensics, investigation, and fraud detection, supporting regulatory compliance across multiple blockchains including Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Monero.

The Bank of England has warned that the rally in AI-related stocks may be unsustainable, raising the risk of a sharp market correction. Its Financial Policy Committee report compared current AI sector valuations to those of the dot-com bubble and flagged risks from gains concentrated in U.S. tech giants such as Nvidia, Microsoft, and Meta.

The BoE identified potential bottlenecks in power supply, semiconductor capacity, and data infrastructure that could limit AI expansion. While the UK financial system remains stable, its openness exposes it to shocks from U.S. equity markets. The International Monetary Fund has raised similar concerns, and the BoE urged investor caution, warning that a correction could be swift and extend beyond the technology sector.

Plum School District officials began early 2018-19 budget discussions Tuesday, hoping to avoid a third consecutive tax increase. The district enters the school year roughly $4 million in debt after approving a $66 million budget in June that included a 0.866-mill tax hike and a 12-year, $5.6 million bond. Board president Kevin Dowdell and finance chair Michelle Stepnick support starting budget talks earlier than the usual October timeline. Plans for 2018-19 include recruiting tuition-paying Chinese students, with Superintendent Tim Glasspool scheduled for a September recruitment trip. Additional discussion items include elementary construction, redistricting, and initiating the process to close Regency Park Elementary School, which requires state notification and public hearings.

A survey of 100 financial services professionals by Infosys Finacle found that over 80% of global bankers expect commercial blockchain adoption by 2020, with more than half of financial institutions investing or planning to invest this year. Average investment is projected at $1 million, with only 4% spending over $10 million. Half the banks are collaborating with fintech start-ups or technology companies. Priority use cases include cross-border payments, digital identity management, clearing and settlement, letters of credit, and loan syndication. Private blockchains were preferred by 69% of banks, hybrid/consortium models by 20%, and public blockchains by only 10%.

Pump and dump schemes involve promoters acquiring shares, typically in thinly traded penny stocks, then artificially inflating prices through false or misleading information before selling to latecomers, causing prices to crash. These schemes exploit the fear of missing out (FOMO) and are largely illegal on regulated exchanges, though common in OTC markets and the unregulated crypto market, where low-volume coins are targeted, often organized via platforms like Telegram.

A notable case involved a 16-year-old promoter who earned nearly a million dollars between 1999 and 2000 before settling with the SEC. A German study found about 6% of sampled investors participated in at least one such scheme, with average returns of -28%. Wikipedia reports pump and dumps account for 15% of spam emails.

Investors are advised to avoid these schemes, be cautious with OTC stocks, and pursue systematic, long-term trading or investing strategies instead.

The disclosure relates to wireless communications, specifically a method, apparatus, and system for transmitting paging information in next-generation wireless systems operating at high frequency bands (e.g., 28 GHz, 45 GHz, 70 GHz).

In such systems, beamforming limits single transmit port coverage to narrow angles, preventing the network from identifying which beam covers a UE in IDLE state. Applying the LTE paging DRX mechanism is problematic because paging information must be loaded within subframes corresponding to each beam, and IDLE UEs cannot predict beam/port scheduling.

The disclosed method involves a first communication node (e.g., base station) calculating a time domain position of a paging occasion (PO) for a second communication node (e.g., UE), then transmitting paging information within that PO. The PO contains a group of paging resources for transmission on multiple preset beams or ports, and corresponds to a synchronous signal (SS) burst set or sweeping resources.

The time domain position is calculated using PO determination parameters: DRX cycle (T_DRX), paging transmission interval (T_paging), number of transmissions (N), device ID, and PO offset (t_offset). Multiple formulas are provided for calculating the starting radio frame number (SFN).

Paging information includes paging downlink control information (DCI) and/or paging messages. The disclosure also addresses quasi-co-location relationships between paging signals and other sweeping signals (SS, DMRS, BRS, MRS, CSI-RS) to help the UE determine reception parameters.

The disclosure includes corresponding apparatus, systems, base stations, terminal devices, and computer-readable storage media implementing these methods.

Orbital ATK reported Q2 2017 sales of $1.12 billion, up 3% year-over-year and slightly above estimates. Adjusted earnings of $1.56 per share beat expectations by $0.13, though GAAP profits fell 3% as operating margins dropped 140 basis points to 12.2%. Free cash flow swung from $107.2 million positive to $55.8 million negative.

Management remains optimistic, citing $1.4 billion in new orders and a book-to-bill ratio of 1.45. Backlog grew 10% year-over-year. Orbital raised full-year guidance to sales of $4.6-$4.65 billion and EPS of $5.95-$6.25, while maintaining free cash flow projections of $250-$300 million.

Argus Research upgraded the stock from hold to buy with a $120 price target, citing expected milestone achievements and increased defense spending. Under Director Jill Medvedow, who arrived in 1998, Boston's Institute of Contemporary Art (ICA) underwent a significant transformation from a marginal institution with 25,000 annual visitors, no permanent collection, and a cramped Boylston Street location into a major cultural destination. Historically, Boston had struggled to support contemporary art due to a weak arts ecosystem, limited public and private funding, and proximity to New York.

Medvedow, trained as an art historian and experienced in public arts projects, was hired for her vision of making the ICA relevant, public, and non-elitist. She assembled a business planning group that recommended growing the audience, expanding education, considering a permanent collection, and relocating. Targeting a waterfront site, she secured Parcel J on Fan Pier in November 1999 after a competitive process, aided by advocate Gloria Larson and support from local political leaders.

Medvedow then hired Paul Bessire as development director, launched a $50 million (later $62 million) capital campaign, and recruited new board members from business sectors. After a public, transparent architect selection process, the ICA chose New York firm Diller + Scofidio, despite their limited building experience, over more established candidates like Peter Zumthor.

Despite obstacles—numerous regulatory approvals, the Pritzker family's withdrawal from surrounding development, and construction delays requiring a contractor change—the new $51 million building opened in December 2006 to over 8,000 visitors. The ICA surpassed its fundraising goal, raising over $75 million, and welcomed more than 280,000 visitors in its first year. Unlike many new museums, the ICA sustained attendance, drawing over 450,000 combined visitors in 2008 and 2009, including 130,000 for Shepard Fairey's 2009 "Supply and Demand" exhibition.

This study introduces "whole human pedagogy," a novel decolonial framework for education abroad built on four tenets: embodiment, emotions, belonging, and becoming. Drawing on hooks (1994), Thompson (2016), and decolonial theory, the framework addresses gaps in alternative pedagogies literature for education abroad and critiques Euro-U.S. epistemological dominance by valuing diverse forms of knowledge.

Using purposive and snowball sampling, the qualitative study conducted 60-90 minute semi-structured virtual interviews with 17 U.S.-based education abroad practitioners in Fall 2023, analyzing data inductively in NVivo.

Findings showed participants embraced all four tenets: embodiment through physical, place-based immersion; emotions through culture shock normalization and reflection; belonging through non-hierarchical, reciprocal relationships and learning communities; and becoming through transformation and self-knowing. Most participants described multiple tenets without prompting.

The discussion affirms whole human pedagogy as a compelling framework centering collaboration, presence, and wellbeing while destabilizing dominant Euro-U.S. educational values. Its significance lies in offering a holistic, decolonial model for program development, professional development, and future research on education abroad praxis.

Sean "Diddy" Combs, 55, was sentenced to four years and two months in prison and fined $500,000 for transporting people across state lines for sexual encounters. Having already served a year, he is expected to be released in about three years. Convicted in July under the Mann Act, he was acquitted of sex trafficking and racketeering charges. U.S. District Judge Arun Subramanian cited Combs' power and resources as reasons the conduct persisted. In a plea for leniency, Combs apologized for his actions and asked for a chance to be a father again. Trial testimony included accounts from former girlfriends describing beatings, coerced sex with strangers, and drug-fueled "freak-offs." Six of his seven children addressed the judge, requesting mercy.

Amazon held a fall hardware event in New York City, where senior vice president Panos Panay announced several new products powered by the Alexa+ assistant.

New Echo devices include the Echo Dot Max, Echo Studio, and updated Echo Show 8 and 11 models. These use Amazon's new AZ3 and AZ3 Pro chips, feature Omnisense technology for contextual awareness, and support Alexa Home Theater. Alexa+, which uses a large language model, is rolling out in waves in the US and is free for Prime subscribers or $20/month otherwise.

Three new Kindle Scribe tablets were unveiled, including the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft—the first Kindle with writing capability and a color screen. Features include Quick Notes, Kindle Workspace, AI-powered search, and reading tools like Story So Far and Ask This Book.

Amazon introduced new Fire TVs, a $40 Fire TV Stick 4K Select, and a new operating system called Vega, replacing the Android-based Fire OS on some devices.

Ring founder Jamie Siminoff announced new 2K and 4K cameras using Amazon's Retinal image processing system. New features include Familiar Faces, Alexa+ Greetings, and Search Party for locating lost pets. Ring has also reinstated law enforcement footage requests. Blink released new 2K cameras and an Arc accessory enabling 180-degree footage from two cameras.

The sidecar pattern pairs a container with an existing application to add functionality without modifying it. Examples include adding HTTPS via an nginx sidecar to a legacy HTTP service, synchronizing configuration files dynamically, and providing reusable introspection tools like topz. Sidecars can also implement complete logic, such as a simple PaaS using Git synchronization. Effective sidecars require parameterization (typically via environment variables), stable APIs, and documentation through Dockerfile directives like EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL.

The ambassador pattern uses a container to broker interactions between an application and external systems. Applications connect to localhost while the ambassador handles routing, such as client-side sharding (e.g., twemproxy for sharded Redis), service brokering for portability across environments, and request splitting for experimentation (e.g., using nginx to route 10% of traffic to a test service).

The adapter pattern modifies an application's interface to conform to a standard. Examples include using Prometheus exporters for monitoring heterogeneous applications, normalizing logs with fluentd plugins, and adding rich health checks (e.g., MySQL queries) without altering the original container.

Multi-node distributed patterns support microservice architectures, which offer scalability, agility, and decoupling but complicate debugging and design. Replicated load-balanced services handle stateless workloads, requiring readiness probes and optional session tracking via consistent hashing. Caching layers (e.g., Varnish) and SSL termination (e.g., nginx) can be added as additional replicated tiers.

Sharded services distribute state across replicas, each handling a subset of requests. Sharded caches improve memory utilization but introduce failure sensitivity; replicated sharded caches add resilience. Sharding functions require careful key selection (balancing specificity and generality) and benefit from consistent hashing to minimize remapping during resizing. Hot sharding dynamically scales shards based on load.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing across many leaves, with a root distributing work and combining partial results to reduce response time for computationally intensive requests.

Mr. Stevens's March 8, 1892 communication reported that revolutionary plans in Hawaii were restrained only by a U.S. naval presence, with hostility toward the "half English" heir and growing support for U.S. annexation. Dissatisfaction with the Queen's reliance on Marshal Wilson persisted, and after a cabinet deadlock, a no-confidence vote occurred October 17. In November, Stevens recommended either annexation or a customs union with a cable, cession of Pearl Harbor, and an implied American protectorate. Naval reports corroborated his accounts until news arrived January 28 of a peaceful revolution and the Queen's dethronement.

The report characterizes U.S. policy toward Hawaii from 1820 to 1893 as one of friendship and protection, resistant to foreign intervention, with annexation considered at times—notably under President Pierce. The appendix offers selected correspondence rather than full documentation, omits private claims, and notes three unperfected treaties (1849, 1855, 1867) held by the Bureau, with additional materials available in Navy Department archives.

Seven months after the Trump administration cut U.S. Department of Education staff, contracts, and grants, researchers express cautious optimism about the future of federal education research. The department plans to reinstate 20 of more than 100 canceled research contracts and 10 regional education labs, and is seeking public input on modernizing the Institute of Education Sciences (IES).

Tabbye Chavous of the American Educational Research Association rated IES at 3 or 4 on a 10-point scale, down from 10 before DOGE cuts, citing ongoing staff shortages and data quality concerns. Secretary McMahon appointed Amber Northern from the Thomas B. Fordham Institute to lead IES reform through December, which researchers view positively.

IES has begun hiring for high-level assessment positions at the National Center for Education Statistics (NCES), whose staff was reduced from roughly 100 to three. Concerns remain about NAEP's reporting capabilities, a mandated admissions data collection effort, and the broader research infrastructure. Department spokesperson Madi Biedermann stated the administration is committed to supporting national education research and protecting NAEP, saying NCES and IES needed reform.

Theratechnologies Inc. has entered into an agreement with underwriters led by RBC Capital Markets to sell US$50,000,000 in convertible unsecured senior notes, due June 30, 2023, at US$1,000 per Note. Underwriters have an over-allotment option for an additional US$7,500,000. The Notes bear 5.75% annual interest, payable semi-annually, and are convertible into common shares at US$14.85 per share. The Notes are not redeemable before June 30, 2021, after which they may be redeemed under specified conditions. Proceeds will fund US$23,850,000 in payments under the EMD Serono Termination Agreement, Trogarzo™ commercialization in Europe and elsewhere, and general corporate purposes. Closing is expected around June 19, 2018, pending regulatory approvals.

NGC 5949 is a dwarf galaxy located about 44 million light-years from Earth, captured in a NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image. With a mass roughly one-hundredth that of the Milky Way, it is a relatively large dwarf galaxy, classified as such due to its small number of stars, and also categorized as a barred spiral due to its loosely-bound spiral arms. Its proximity allowed William Herschel to discover it in 1801 using a small telescope. Dwarf galaxies like NGC 5949 present cosmological challenges, including the "cuspy halo" problem regarding dark matter distribution and the "missing satellites" problem, as simulations predict more dwarf galaxies than are observed.

The Ultimate Oscillator (UO) is a momentum indicator developed by Larry Williams in 1976 and popularized in 1985. It measures price momentum across three timeframes (7, 14, and 28 periods), generating a weighted average where shorter timeframes carry more weight (4:2:1 ratio). This multi-timeframe approach reduces volatility and false signals common in single-timeframe oscillators.

Calculation involves determining Buying Pressure (BP), True Range (TR), and averages across the three periods, producing values between 0 and 100. Levels below 30 indicate oversold conditions, and above 70 indicate overbought. Trading signals are generated through price-indicator divergences meeting specific criteria.

Backtests on SPY using default settings (buy below 40, sell above 50) yielded poor results. However, optimization testing showed strong performance, with most simulations producing profit factors above 2. One example achieved a 2.5 profit factor across 355 trades, a 78% win rate, 0.77% average gain per trade, and 25% maximum drawdown, with only two losing years. The indicator proved consistent as a mean reversion tool across various settings.

The Supreme Court dismissed Varun Thakur's plea seeking cancellation of the interim bail granted to the Pinto family, owners of Ryan International School, in connection with his son Pradyuman's murder. The Punjab and Haryana High Court had granted them anticipatory bail on November 21, barring them from leaving the country. Pradyuman was found dead on September 8 with his throat slit. While Gurugram Police initially arrested bus conductor Ashok, the CBI later cleared him and held a class 11 student responsible. Pradyuman's family alleges the Pinto family's complicity.

Automation threatens millions of jobs, including the 3.5 million U.S. truck drivers, as companies worldwide invest in autonomous vehicles and AI enters fields like law, hospitality, and journalism. The World Economic Forum predicts over five million jobs will be eliminated in five years. To remain competitive, humans may need augmentation.

Brain augmentation, such as Elon Musk's proposed "neural lace," could enhance cognitive abilities. Harvard researchers have already developed an injectable electronic mesh for mice brains, blurring lines between electronic and neural circuits.

Body augmentation through exosuits is being developed by Hyundai, Harvard, and the U.S. Army. Hoomayoon Kazerooni's SuitX produces medical and industrial exoskeletons that reduce physical strain. Harvard's Biodesign Lab creates soft exosuits showing 23% reduced walking effort, with potential applications for soldiers, factory workers, and delivery personnel.

Tom Davenport, co-author of "Only Humans Need Apply," recommends workers develop non-codifiable skills like creativity or learn to maintain machines. He is more optimistic about knowledge workers than physical laborers, though general AI could change everything.

President Trump disputed a New York Times article on Twitter, denying its claim that he watches four to eight hours of television daily, often starting with CNN or MSNBC. Times spokeswoman Danielle Rhodes Ha defended the article, citing interviews with 60 sources. Trump's response followed a weekend of posts criticizing media outlets for "fake news."

A fast-moving lava flow from Hawaii's Kilauea volcano crossed Highway 132, destroying power lines and cutting electricity to coastal neighborhoods. The Hawaii County Civil Defense Agency confirmed 71 homes have been destroyed since the eruption began May 3, with more expected. Over 400 utility poles have been lost, and residents in Kapoho-area neighborhoods were told to evacuate. A new fissure brought the total to 24, and lava has covered two wells at a geothermal plant, though officials said they remain stable. Explosions at the summit have sent volcanic ash up to 15,000 feet, prompting health warnings.

Meb Faber's Tactical Asset Allocation is an active trend-following strategy using market timing across five categories: U.S. stocks, foreign stocks, U.S. bonds, U.S. REITs, and world commodities, with 20% allocated to each. It can be implemented via five diversified index ETFs, avoiding individual asset selection. Unlike passive strategies, investors enter and exit based on signals, staying in cash otherwise.

Faber, co-founder and CIO of Cambria Investment Management, authored multiple books and white papers. Stocks historically offer the highest returns; bonds reduce volatility and drawdowns; REITs and commodities improve diversification due to low correlation with traditional assets.

Backtesting over 16 years showed a maximum drawdown of only -13.24%, significantly lower than passive portfolios, which often exceed -40%. The timing model is universal and applicable to various portfolios.

Richard Berg appealed a Minnesota trial court's amended judgment increasing his child support obligation from $145 to $258 per child per month, bringing it to the guideline level of 30% of net income. The parties divorced in 1981, with Nancy Berg receiving custody of three children. The trial court found appellant's net income had increased 34.5% since the original decree, making the original terms unreasonable and unfair. The Court of Appeals found the support amount within the trial court's discretion but held the findings inadequate under Moylan v. Moylan, which requires specific findings justifying support increases based on factors in Minn.Stat. §§ 518.17, 518.551, and 518.64. The case was remanded for further factual findings.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2017. As of October 18, 2017, 481,872,175 common shares were outstanding. The company reported Q3 2017 net sales of $43.7 billion (up 34% year-over-year) and net income of $256 million, with nine-month net sales of $117.4 billion and net income of $1.2 billion. Operating cash flow for the trailing twelve months was $17.1 billion, while cash and marketable securities totaled $24.3 billion as of September 30, 2017.

Key developments included the August 28, 2017 acquisition of Whole Foods Market for approximately $13.2 billion (net of cash acquired) and the May 2017 acquisition of Souq for $579 million. In August 2017, Amazon issued $16.0 billion in unsecured senior notes across seven tranches (2020-2057) to fund the Whole Foods acquisition and for corporate purposes, and assumed $1.0 billion in Whole Foods notes.

Amazon operates three segments: North America, International, and AWS. AWS sales grew 42% to $4.6 billion in Q3 2017. The company recorded a Q2 2017 valuation allowance charge of $600 million against Luxembourg deferred tax assets. Ongoing legal matters include an IRS transfer pricing appeal (potentially $1.5 billion), a French tax assessment of €196 million, and an October 2017 European Commission state aid decision requiring Luxembourg to recover approximately €250 million plus interest.

Other analysts have issued varying ratings, with KeyCorp and Northland Securities maintaining "buy" ratings at $25.00 and $23.00 price targets respectively, Zacks downgrading to "sell," and Susquehanna and UBS upgrading to "positive" with $20.00 targets. A senior Iranian Revolutionary Guards commander, Major-General Qassem Soleimani, stated on Wednesday that the Guards were prepared to block regional oil exports if the United States bans Iranian oil sales. His remarks supported President Hassan Rouhani's apparent threat to disrupt neighbouring countries' oil shipments if Washington pursues its goal of halting all Iranian oil purchases. Iranian officials have previously threatened to block the Strait of Hormuz in response to hostile U.S. actions.

The University of Agriculture Faisalabad (UAF) approved non-development accounts of Rs3.28 billion for 2015-16 during its 44th Senate meeting, chaired by VC Dr Iqrar Ahmad. He stated UAF launched 48 new degree programs, with enrolment rising from 16,000 in 2013 to over 25,000, and financial assistance exceeding Rs700 million. He noted the research portfolio surpassed Rs2.5 billion. Dr Iqrar criticized Pakistan's 0.1 percent GDP spending on agricultural research compared to India's, and urged increased investment. He recommended reducing wheat irrigation from five to three applications, claiming water savings equal to Tarbela and Mangla storage. He highlighted that 40 percent of Pakistanis face malnutrition and post-harvest losses account for 40 percent of total losses, advocating modern techniques.

Photographer Richard Mosse's project Heat Maps documents the refugee crisis across Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East using a military-grade thermal telephoto camera. The camera, designed for surveillance and weapons targeting, renders human figures as translucent grey forms without identifiable features. Mosse intends the work to challenge Western perceptions of refugees and implicate viewers in their governments' policies. The large-scale images are composed of nearly a thousand smaller frames stitched together, evoking Bruegel paintings. Mosse gained access to locations like Berlin's Tempelhof Airport camp because subjects' identities remained intact. The three-year project faced logistical challenges, including difficult border access and complex equipment. Mosse employs a Brechtian distancing effect, previously used in his Infra series on the Democratic Republic of Congo. Heat Maps is displayed at NYC's Jack Shainman Gallery until March 11.

India has called on the UN Secretariat to disclose information about crimes and misconduct by UN staff and the use of immunity to block prosecutions. Yedla Umasankar, legal advisor at India's UN Mission, told the General Assembly's legal affairs committee that the UN appears reluctant to waive immunity even in serious misconduct cases, damaging the organisation's credibility. He requested data on the number of misconduct cases, instances where immunity was not waived, and host country requests for waivers. Umasankar noted accountability remains elusive due to jurisdictional complexities and varying national capabilities to prosecute. Although the UN adopted a zero-tolerance policy following sexual misconduct allegations against peacekeepers and began publishing related data in 2015, it has not released a comprehensive roster of misconduct cases across the UN system.

President Trump announced that the U.S. will impose an additional 100% tariff on Chinese imports and export controls on "critical software" starting November 1, 2025. The move retaliates against China's new export controls on rare earth minerals, of which China supplies roughly 70% globally. These minerals are critical for automobiles, defense, and semiconductors. Trump criticized China's actions as "extraordinarily aggressive" and suggested canceling a planned meeting with President Xi Jinping at an upcoming summit in South Korea. Chinese imports currently face an effective tariff rate of 40%. China's new rules, effective December 1, require foreign entities to obtain licenses to export products containing over 0.1% Chinese-sourced rare earths.

The double bottom chart pattern is a price action formation consisting of two swing lows at approximately the same level with a swing high between them, forming a support level and a neckline resistance. Appearing in downtrends, it is considered a bullish reversal pattern, signaling potential upward price movement once the price breaks above the neckline.

Traders approach the pattern differently: aggressive traders enter at the second low using reversal signals like bullish candlesticks or RSI indicators, while conservative traders wait for a confirmed neckline breakout with increased volume. Profit targets are typically measured by the pattern's size projected upward from the neckline, with stop losses placed mid-pattern or below.

The pattern is difficult to quantify and backtest due to numerous required rules. Thomas Bulkowski's research, published in 2000, studied 500 stocks over 5 years and found 68% of double bottom formations reached their targets—nearly twice the rate of double tops. However, the study may suffer from survivorship bias, covered only a bull market period, and relied on manual pattern identification. The author prefers fully quantified rules over human interpretation for reliable trading.

Emperor penguins are classified as "near-threatened" by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, with a 2014 study projecting a 19 percent population decline by 2100 due to rising temperatures. A new monitoring system, detailed in the Journal of Applied Physics, uses a time-lapse camera positioned near colonies along with weather data to track penguin behavior, with information accessible online. The system revealed that penguins huddle in warmer conditions, suggesting reduced body fat and possible food shortages linked to sea ice loss affecting plankton and fish. Researcher Zitterbart attributes food scarcity to global warming, while ecologist David Ainley suggests commercial fishing may be responsible. Rod Downie of the World Wildlife Fund praised the system as cost-effective for research in Antarctica's harsh conditions.

A class action complaint filed in the Superior Court of California, San Diego County, by plaintiff Pamela R. Gordon against Reliant Energy, Southern Company, NRG Energy, Dynegy, AES Corporation, Williams Energy, and Duke Energy North America. The suit alleges that from May 22, 2000 onward, the defendants manipulated California's wholesale electricity market by misusing confidential real-time generator and transmission data obtained through the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC), withholding generating capacity, parking power with out-of-state affiliates for resale at inflated rates, and scheduling outages to exacerbate supply shortages.

The complaint cites findings by FERC, the CPUC, and CAISO that summer 2000 prices were "unjust and unreasonable," with the CPUC estimating over $4 billion in overcharges. It claims these practices violated CAISO/FERC Tariff confidentiality provisions and tripled SDG&E customer bills. The suit asserts five causes of action: violations of the Cartwright Act (antitrust), two counts under the Unfair Trade Practices Act, violation of the Consumers Legal Remedies Act, and unconscionability. Plaintiffs seek class certification, treble damages, restitution, disgorgement of profits, and injunctive relief.

The document was forwarded by Mark Palmer of Enron, who noted that a reporter indicated Enron's forthcoming suit would resemble this one.

The court fined defendant Pomeroy $6,000 and the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad Company $108,000 for six offenses each. The speaker criticizes the practice of overturning lower court judgments on technicalities unrelated to case merits and proposes legislation preventing judgments from being set aside unless errors caused a miscarriage of justice.

Regarding injunctions, the speaker opposes abolishing them in labor cases, arguing such a law may not survive judicial review and that injunctions are necessary against mob violence. However, the power requires careful exercise. Judges should enjoin violence and intimidation but must not forbid peaceful labor activities or aid corporate aggrandizement. Improperly granted preliminary injunctions in labor disputes can cause irreparable harm and may effectively settle disputes. Careless injunction use threatens the process's existence by fueling calls for its abolition.

The speaker praises judges who disregard public sentiment or powerful interests when justice requires it, while arguing that criticism of judges who act timidly or unjustly should be permitted, since judges hold power subject primarily to public opinion.

UDMA write operations may produce CRC errors following a device termination, but only when preceded by a UDMA read operation that experienced a host termination near its end. During a UDMA write device termination, the ATAC correctly passes the CRC for the first termination but fails to restart the CRC for subsequent portions, causing errors. A host-initiated IDE I/O between events can reset the CRC, but this is unreliable. As a result, UDMA writes are generally unusable. The resolution is to use the UDMA I/O blocking feature tied to bit 8 of the ATAC Error MSR.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed the district court's dismissal of an antitrust suit brought by Sea Breeze Salt, Inc. and Innofood, S.A. de C.V. against Mitsubishi Corporation and Exportadora de Sal, S.A. de C.V. (ESSA), a Mexican salt producer 51-percent owned by Mexico. Plaintiffs alleged ESSA breached distribution contracts to resume selling salt exclusively to Mitsubishi.

The court held the act of state doctrine barred the suit because: (1) ESSA's decisions constituted official acts of the Mexican government performed within Mexican territory, as Mexico's Constitution vests ownership of sea salt in the nation, making its exploitation a sovereign function; and (2) the requested relief would require a U.S. court to invalidate Mexico's sovereign decisions about distributing its natural resources.

The court found the Sabbatino factors supported applying the doctrine, noting no international consensus condemns such arrangements and significant foreign relations implications exist. The court declined to decide whether a commercial exception to the doctrine exists, finding it inapplicable because the challenged conduct involved powers peculiar to sovereigns. The court emphasized its holding is narrow and limited to the specific facts involving Mexico's policy decision regarding its entire salt output.

Interferometric second-harmonic generation (SHG) polarimetry is presented as a non-destructive optical method for assessing crystalline quality in CVD-grown 2D hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). Conventional probes like TEM, STM, LEED, and Raman spectroscopy cannot reliably detect antiparallel domains, which form due to hBN's threefold rotational symmetry on sixfold symmetric metal substrates. By combining polarization-resolved SHG with interferometric detection, the authors optically resolved antiparallel domains and boundaries across ten types of CVD-grown hBN samples, finding such domains pervasive even in apparently unidirectional films. SHG intensity varied by three orders of magnitude among samples, while Raman intensity varied only fourfold. A mixed-domain numerical model showed this large SHG variation results from destructive interference between antiparallel domains and scales with domain size. Correlating SHG intensity, Raman intensity, linewidth, and orientational spread (measured against mechanically exfoliated references) provides a quantitative framework for structural assessment. The method is applicable to other non-centrosymmetric 2D materials such as transition metal dichalcogenides.

This study used untargeted metabolomics to investigate metabolite changes in 22 cirrhotic patients undergoing transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) placement, a procedure that reduces portal hypertension but increases the risk of hepatic encephalopathy (HE). Blood samples were collected from peripheral and hepatic veins before and after TIPS, and patients were monitored for HE up to one year post-procedure.

Key findings include:

1. The peripheral vein (PIV) metabolome changed significantly pre- to post-TIPS, while hepatic vein (HV) changes were minimal, suggesting pre-existing intrahepatic shunting in many patients.

2. Patients who developed more severe HE showed greater dissimilarity in their pre- to post-TIPS HV metabolome, suggesting less intrahepatic shunting prior to TIPS predisposes patients to HE.

3. Bile acids were the primary metabolites driving post-TIPS changes. Three conjugated hydroxylated bile acids decreased more substantially in patients who developed higher-grade HE, implying a potential protective role.

4. Two readmitted patients showed bile acid fluctuations consistent with HE exacerbation and recovery following treatment.

5. Chemical proportionality analysis identified fluctuations in glycerophosphocholines and bilirubins (particularly biliverdin oxidation-reduction) associated with HE severity.

The authors propose that measuring intrahepatic shunting pre-TIPS could help risk-stratify patients, and that specific bile acids may serve as biomarkers or therapeutic targets for HE. Limitations include limited metabolic coverage, reliance on spectral library annotations, small sample size, and absence of microbiome correlation data.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on February 14, 2019, announcing its financial results for the fourth quarter and fiscal year ended January 27, 2019. The filing includes a press release (Exhibit 99.1) and CFO Commentary (Exhibit 99.2) from Colette M. Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. The CFO Commentary was to be posted on NVIDIA's investor website. The report was signed by Kress on behalf of the company.

This specification update document details known issues (errata) in the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device, Silicon Revision A3. Key issues include:

- **UART/DMA conflicts**: UART registers cannot be accessed during legacy block or demand DMA cycles; single byte transfer mode should be used instead.
- **8237 software DMA**: Memory writes from LPC fail, but with no operational impact.
- **I/O addressing**: I/O cycles at address 10000h or higher hang the system; LBARs allow illegal values at these addresses.
- **USB over-voltage**: The CS5535 does not meet USB 1.1 over-voltage protection requirements; external circuits are needed.
- **PIC issues**: Edge-configured interrupts may fail if automatic clock gating is enabled; Polling mode is not supported.
- **PRD/DMA errors**: ATAC and ACC prefetch issues occur with non-8-byte-aligned PRD tables.
- **UDMA problems**: CRC corruption after device termination; failures when PIO commands follow bus master enablement; ATAC hangs with WORD-aligned PRDs.
- **ACPI/PMC registers**: Byte access to PM1_EN/PM1_STS fails; WORD/BYTE writes may corrupt PMC registers.
- **KEL emulation**: CmdData bit incorrect; Snoop mode requires software workarounds; AuxOutputFull bit improperly cleared.
- **Power management**: Most wake events (GPIO[27:24]) don't work from ACPI S3 state; LOWBAT_FLAG not set after abnormal standby; SLEEP_X/Y deassertion issues.
- **Other issues**: RTC CMOS RAM access errors, LPC I/O blocking during DMA, USB clock gating failures, SMB NEGACK bit issues, PCI timing violations, SSMI synchronization problems, and SMBus hold time below specification.

Resolutions typically involve software workarounds, avoiding specific modes/features, or external hardware additions.

Monitoring and Logging with Adapter Patterns

Prometheus is an open-source monitoring aggregator that collects metrics into a time-series database, but requires containers to expose a specific API. The adapter pattern allows incompatible services like Redis to be monitored by deploying an adapter container (e.g., a Prometheus exporter) alongside the application. Similarly, adapters can normalize heterogeneous logging formats, redirecting output to stdout or transforming data for log aggregators. Using adapters instead of modifying application containers enables modularity, reuse, and easier maintenance. Tools like fluentd, with community plugins, can adapt logs from Redis (SLOWLOG) or Apache Storm. Adapters can also add rich health checks (e.g., running queries against MySQL) without altering the database container.

Microservices and Distributed Patterns

Microservices break applications into small, independently deployable components communicating via APIs, improving reliability, agility, and scalability, though complicating debugging and design. Distributed patterns help standardize these architectures.

Replicated Load-Balanced Services

Stateless services are replicated behind load balancers for redundancy and scale, requiring readiness probes to signal when instances can serve traffic. Session-tracked services route a user's requests consistently to one replica, often via consistent hashing. Caching layers (e.g., Varnish) improve performance, and SSL termination can be handled by nginx. Kubernetes Deployments and Services implement these layers.

Sharded Services

Sharded services distribute data subsets across replicas, enabling storage beyond a single machine. Sharded caches improve memory utilization but risk outages if a shard fails; replicated sharded caches add resilience. Sharding functions, typically using hash and modulo operations, must be deterministic and uniform. Consistent hashing minimizes remapping during resizing. Hot sharding dynamically replicates overloaded shards.

Scatter/Gather

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing across leaf nodes, which return partial results combined by a root node. It suits embarrassingly parallel problems and can shard data across leaves. Drawbacks include per-node overhead, the "straggler" problem (slowest leaf defines latency), and amplified tail-latency effects. Replicating shards improves reliability and scale.

Functions and Event-Driven Processing (FaaS)

FaaS (serverless computing) simplifies deployment and scales automatically but complicates monitoring, is ill-suited for background processing or memory-heavy tasks, and becomes costly at sustained high request volumes. Running FaaS on container orchestrators like Kubernetes (e.g., Kubeless) can mitigate costs. Key FaaS patterns include the decorator pattern (transforming requests/responses, e.g., adding defaults), event handling (e.g., two-factor authentication), and event-driven pipelines (e.g., new-user signup flows with required and optional actions).

Wall Street rose on Thursday, led by financial shares, after data showed stronger-than-reported U.S. economic growth in the fourth quarter, with GDP increasing at a 2.1 percent annualized rate. The Nasdaq set a record closing high for a fifth straight session. The energy sector gained for a third consecutive day, supported by higher oil prices and an 8.8-percent rise in ConocoPhillips following an asset sale agreement. The President addresses Congress, expressing his profound anxiety at being summoned from retirement to assume an office for which he feels inadequately prepared, despite his dedication to duty. He offers fervent supplications to the Almighty, asserting that the United States' progress toward independence has been marked by providential agency, and that the peaceful establishment of its new government warrants gratitude.

Rather than recommending specific measures, he expresses confidence in the talents, rectitude, and patriotism of the assembled representatives, trusting they will avoid local prejudices and party animosities while grounding national policy in private morality. He emphasizes the indissoluble link between virtue and happiness, noting that the fate of republican government rests on this American experiment.

Regarding the Fifth Article of the Constitution, he defers to Congress's judgment on amendments, urging balance between preserving effective government and honoring the rights of freemen.

Addressing the House of Representatives, he declines any personal financial compensation beyond actual expenditures, consistent with his prior practice during the struggle for liberty.

He concludes with another appeal for divine blessing on the new government's deliberations and measures.

James T. Hodgkinson, 66, shot Republican Rep. Steve Scalise and several others at an early morning baseball practice in Alexandria, Virginia, before being fatally shot by police. Authorities say Hodgkinson had been living out of a white cargo van since March after leaving his Illinois home and was frequently seen at a nearby YMCA overlooking the field. Witnesses described him as quiet and solitary. He had expressed online grievances about President Trump and Republicans, though a motive has not been confirmed. Armed with a handgun and rifle, Hodgkinson died from multiple gunshot wounds. A congressional aide, two Capitol Police officers, and a former aide were also injured. Hodgkinson previously ran a home-inspection business, supported Bernie Sanders, and wrote letters to his local newspaper complaining about income inequality. He had a record of minor offenses, a dismissed 2006 battery charge, and was questioned in March for firing a rifle near homes, though no charges were filed.

Ari Guiragos Minassian, the only Armenian school in Orange County, held its 31st Annual Banquet on April 1, drawing over 250 guests. The President transmits to Congress a letter from the governor of Texas, dated June 14, and the response made to it. The governor states that Texas dispatched a commissioner to extend state jurisdiction over four counties east of the Rio Grande, including Santa Fe, but that U.S. military officers at Santa Fe opposed these efforts. The Texas legislature has been convened to assert this claim by force.

The President notes that the territory in question has historically been part of New Mexico, conquered from Mexico during the late war. Under the Constitution, the President is Commander in Chief and must ensure faithful execution of the laws. Acts of 1795 and 1807 authorize him to call forth the militia and employ military forces to suppress combinations obstructing federal laws.

While Texas may enforce its laws within its own boundaries, its authority cannot extend beyond them. If Texas militia enter another state or U.S. territory to enforce Texas law and obstruct federal law, the President is constitutionally bound to act.

The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, part of the supreme law of the land, guarantees liberty, property, and religious rights to Mexicans residing north and east of the treaty's demarcation line. Until Congress establishes a definitive boundary, the territory possessed as New Mexico at the treaty's date must be regarded as such, and its inhabitants protected.

The executive cannot establish civil or military government in the territory—that power belongs solely to Congress. The President urges Congress to promptly settle the Texas–New Mexico boundary dispute, preferably through legislation with Texas's assent, possibly including a reasonable indemnity to Texas. Judicial proceedings or commissions would cause undue delay. Resolving this question is essential before any government can be established for New Mexico and would promote national harmony.

James D. Rone, a line foreman employed by Dan Raymond Construction Company, was injured at a sewer construction site in Hobart, Indiana, when his hand was caught in a back hoe cable, severing fingers on both hands. The back hoe was operated by an employee of Boncar Construction Company, which had formed a joint venture with Raymond. Rone filed a three-count complaint: Count I alleged violation of the Illinois Structural Work Act, Count II alleged negligence under the Indiana Dangerous Occupation Act, and Count III alleged willful and wanton negligence. The trial court struck Count I, finding the Illinois Act inapplicable to out-of-state accidents. A jury returned a verdict for Boncar on Count II, and Count III was dropped.

On appeal, the court held Rone waived his right to appeal Count I's dismissal by failing to perfect his earlier appeal. The court found that questions of negligence, proximate cause, and contributory negligence were properly submitted to the jury. It ruled the Indiana Employers Liability Act inapplicable and distinguished Testa v. Kaluzny Bros. on its facts. The court also found no error in refusing Rone's tendered jury instructions. The judgment was affirmed.

The AEGEAN study evaluated apixaban adherence in subjects with atrial fibrillation, comparing a Primary Standard of Care (SOC) group with an Additional Educational Program group, with a second study part adding a Secondary SOC and Continued Additional Educational Program group.

Exposure to study drug and dose distribution (predominantly 5 mg BID, ~87%) were comparable across groups at 24 and 48 weeks. Compliance exceeded 94-95% throughout.

For the primary efficacy endpoint, mean adherence at 24 weeks was 91.64% (Primary SOC) versus 91.88% (Additional Educational Program), with no significant difference. Adherence declined significantly from Week 12 to Week 24 and from Week 24 to Week 48 in both groups, but remained comparable between groups. Mean adherence from first dose to Week 48 was 89.52% (Primary SOC) and 90.93% (Educational Program).

Persistence at 24 weeks (~91%) and 48 weeks (85-88%) showed no significant differences between groups. The percentage of fully adherent subjects was also similar across groups.

Logit models identified predictors of non-adherence including alcohol consumption, technical occupations, and permanent atrial fibrillation in the Primary SOC group, while MMSE score was inversely associated. Few predictors emerged in the Educational Program group.

Safety endpoints were similar across groups at 24 and 48 weeks, including adverse events, serious adverse events, bleeding events, and major bleeding. A total of 24 deaths were reported. No pregnancies occurred, and no hepatic or renal safety signals were identified.

The study concluded that adherence and persistence were high through 48 weeks, and the proactive educational program provided no additional benefit.

Opening range breakout (ORB) strategies, popularized by Tony Crabel's 1990 book, involve trading when price breaks above or below a defined opening range (e.g., the first 5 or 30 minutes of a session). Backtests on S&P 500 futures and other contracts (Nasdaq, gold, silver, oil) show these strategies no longer perform well, with minuscule average gains and low win rates in both long and short variations.

Reasons for diminished effectiveness include frequent false breakouts, overnight gains capturing most of the movement, algorithmic competition, and the tendency for daily highs and lows to occur near the open and close.
